I had a couple of tech issues and professor was quick to respond and help.

reviews.comment: Prof. Awad is really an exceptional professor for BIOCHEM. I did a lot of research before deciding to take the course through UCSD Extension, and with Prof. Awad. I was most appreciative that she has minimal work due each week, but is clear about her expectations with each assignment (a discussion board and a quiz). She also offers extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Highly recommend this online Biochemistry course! Dr. Awad was a great instructor and guided the class with ease. If anyone is looking to take this course post-grad as well, 100% worth your time.

reviews.comment: If I wrote a review when I first entered college, I probably would've given Professor Nandi a 3 at most. However, after taking other math courses, I've realized that Nandi's way of teaching is very thorough and really helps students learn the topics. While his homeworks are difficult, I think they're relative to the course's advertised difficulty.
he's chill but his tangents during lectures sometimes confused me, he mumbles a bit too but its cool. a bit hard
Harsh grader

The exams were not particularly difficult and were mostly based on the material we had learned in class. There were also bonus points available on the test. The professor is very sociable and clearly very knowledgeable. Attendance is not required for in-person lectures, as all classes are recorded and made available for later viewing.

hard but educational
makes you learn but in a good way
chill vibe
He is a bit tough to get along with, but he is brainy and knowledgeable about the material.

Never take this professor even if he is the last prof. He abruptly changed his grading policy after making a mistake himself and forgetting to specify that midterm attendance is compulsory and their grade can't be compensated. After that, he is very hard to communicate with.

Often went on tangents during lecture, commonly moved class to online with short notice or canceled class, saying there would be a posted lecture but it never happened. Handwriting is not legible, only writes on chalkboard. Homework was never graded in a timely manner and midterm reviews had no posted keys. Overall grade curve was generous

reviews.comment: Its a proofs class. You pretty much need to understand everything. It gets hard around chapter 14 or week 7. Has a bad time with releasing recorded lectures on time and has a hard time explaining harder subjects. Overall, would still take if doing pass no pass, but not sure about letter grade. I believe he will curve though

Grades inaccurately. Doesn't lecture, only writes on blackboard. Practice exams are nothing like the actual exam. Actual exam difficulty is much worse than lecture problems/homework problems. Take any other Math 109 professor...
He skips lectures without prior announcement. He also says he'll post the lectures he missed but never posts them. The midterm also had two whole problems with wrong numbers that left me confused.

This class is no walk in the park. Make sure to attend every lecture and take notes or you will suffer because most of this stuff will not come intuitively. The teacher has no slides he goes to the chalkboard and writes the whole time. Midterms + final = 80% of the grade. His accent isn't too bad though.

The professor cares about the student's understanding when he explains things in class and explains concepts/train of thought mostly clearly. Sometimes goes on side tangents which are unrelated to course material, and occasionally makes mistakes on the board. Also, as one review said, he promises video lectures but ends up not recording them.
He often announces that lectures will turn online before 10hrs lec begin, and delay to post online records. He has no class notes, and even a clear Midterm syllabus is inaccessible.

Pros: Clear and logical board work. Very responsive to students outside of class and actively adopts our suggestions. Homework is well-targeted and helpful. Generous implicit curve. Nice taste in sunglasses😎

Cons: He has an accent, and sometimes it feels like he is mumbling or talking to himself during lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Cogs 1 is a great class to take for an intro to cogs material. The lectures were all online and the quizzes were open note at home and on canvas. I would recommend this course to anyone in any major.

I heavily recommend going to every single lecture to take as detailed notes as possible because that's what the open note quizzes, exams, and discussion activities will be based on! Great course to see all the Cog Sci professors and  department faculty.

Dr. Kiyonaga was pretty cool, and she created a fairly easy class format. Lectures were all extra credit, discussions were not mandatory and you could get extra credit for working with other people, and tests were take home. Because the tests were take home, they were a little harder but nothing to complain about. I think I got a B on every test.

attendance not mandatory but EC is given if attended, weekly quizzes + section assignments. all quizzes + midterms are based on guest speakers' lecture so pay attention. quizzes are open note and collaborative. no "final", it was just a third midterm & not cumulative. Midterms are weighed 10/20/30%, 10% being ur worst score.

Had a different guest lecturer every lecture. The tests were based on what these guest lecturers said. So u needed to memorize every word they said to do well on the tests. Totally killed my interest in the course material because I couldn't just pay attention to what the lecturer was saying, I was too busy furiously typing everything they said.

Class is based on a lot of group work. We had to work with the same group all quarter. Wednesday lab time was spent doing group labs and Fridays were journal clubs (where we had to discuss articles with our groups). There was a group presentation at the end of the quarter. Lectures were interesting, but I wish more time was spent on them.

The class involves multiple guest speakers within the cog sci department, weekly quizzes and DI activities, 3 tests total that are weighted 30/20/10 = 60% and are based on performance. overall a really easy and interesting class

guest speakers each lecture. 6 weekly quizzes, 6 discussion assignments, 3 exams. Many hard/ trick questions but no textbook or attendance, & all quizzes/exams are online open note & non-cumulative. extremely fair in my opinion, but don't expect 100% on quizzes(it's hard). discussion attendance only required 6 times. lowest quiz/ discussion dropped
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's GOATED

The class was mostly pre-recorded guest lectures, and there are TONS of extra credit opportunities that you probably won't need. Section is for lecture review and collaborative quizzes, but you can go to any section you want which is nice since some TAs are better.

COGS 1 had new guest lecturers each lesson, so Prof Kiyonaga was more of a moderator. She, however, did a great job facilitating questions between students and lecturers and her class was very organized. You don't have to necessarily go to the section you were assigned. You can go to another TA's. My personal favorite was Pamela Riviere.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The quizzes were collaborative, the section work was easy, and the midterms were 3 hours and open notes. All you have to do to pass is watch the lectures, but if you wanted a guaranteed A, read the textbooks, especially for the third midterm. Overall, very great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Although a little strict with grading, she's very approachable outside of class, and provides fair alternative solutions without violating the university's standard grading policies. A fair and honest professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Kiyonaga's class is graded on weekly section activities, quizzes, peer discussions, and 4 midterms. It's not difficult to get 100% on the weekly requirements and midterms aren't difficult. Although she tells you to do weekly reading, reading the textbook is not necessary as long as you listen and take detailed notes on lectures.

Professor Kiyonaga is an amazing professor who truly cares about her students. She always looks for ways to improve her lectures and is open to criticism. Her tests aren't too difficult and questions can be answered from readings or lectures. The structure of the class does a fair job in not being weighted heavy by any particular assignment.

She knows her material very well, fMRI is not a simple concept to grasp but she managed to teach it well. Quizzes are collaborative and a little bit hard. The only problem with her is she is unorganized, and the project that is over 40% of our grade is quite unorganized too. Shes fairly new at teaching and still learning the road.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Before taking COGS 17 I was really scared since everyone said it was a really hard class. I began with Johnson and then moved to Kiyonaga. She's the best professor out there and the class became one of the easiest classes to get an A. If you are doubting between Kiyonaga and Johnson, pick Kiyonaga and you'll learn a lot and enjoy the class way more

I would've given it a rating of 5 but the professor didn't include A+ as an option in the grading scheme. She also did not tell students at the beginning of the quarter that an A+ is unavailable in her course. Many hard-working students who aimed for an A+ ended up getting A unexpectedly. If you are aiming for an A+, go for another professor.

Asynchronous lectures with live discussion, but you can go to any section you want. Lectures are short and hit the main points, but you'll really want to read to get the maximum out of the class. Very manageable, almost no homework. Easy to pass: quizzes and exams are open book, open notes, open Internet; quizzes can be collaborative too.

Absolutely loved Dr. Kiyonaga's class and it made me more interested in learning about the human brain. Tests are very fair, 20 questions, 3 hours, open note. Quizzes are collaborative and section activities are pretty fun to do. She's really good at dissecting the material and posts additional TED talks and 2-minute neuroscience videos.

Professor Kiyonaga is a really sweet woman who tried her best to make distance learning achievable for us. 4 exams, lowest grade can be dropped, 3 hours for 20 questions (whole course open book). There is a bit of reading but I reccomend watching lectures BEFORE reading (helps solidify + gives an overview). Tests are very critical thinking heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: First quarter at UCSD and I really enjoyed her class: -thorough lecture vids (10-20 mins) -3 hr tests for 20 questions (plenty of time) -she only grades 3/4 test (drops lowest score) -easy weekly discussion posts -reading textbook helps but not necessary -offers test corrections! -extra credit opportunities You learn a lot and an easy A! 10/10

I absolutely love Dr. Kiyonaga! She is such a passionate teacher who clearly cares about not only her students but also the subject. Her exams and quizzes are fair, and she provides external resources for students to understand the concepts being taught in class. As long as you pay attention to the lectures, you're going to do well in her class:)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I really liked her! Her teaching model was very fair, she gave many small weighted assignments instead of only a few big assignments to determine the grade which made the class less pressure while also I feel facilitating more learning. i learned a good bit of interesting material in her class. Watch her lectures & take good notes, no txtbk needed

Test questions aren't difficult, as long as you pay attention in lecture and memorize certain terms you'll be good to go. She assigns readings but personally I never read and passed the class with an A+. All I did was watch all the lectures + review notes before the exams. Office hours always available, she's a new professor and is wonderful!

The seminar consists of Monday lectures, Wednesday journal discussions and Friday group project works. While she did make an effort to improve, it's still pretty obvious that she's inexperienced in teaching. The grading rubric is unclear and not much help is offered toward the group project that takes up 40% of the grade. Very approachable though.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: She relied on the book versus herself. Her lectures were prerecorded, short, and had extra videos for clarity. We had four unit test, no final, and she'll drop the lowest test score. Discussions are useful to complete section work, but not required after Week 6. Online discussion posts and weekly ungraded quizzes were easy points. Easy A w/ effort
It is good for pilot studies and more suitable for continuing ed. It is OK if you want to improve you GPA.

Really awesome prof, extremely long lectures. Gave us resources to explore more artsy films regarding topics within lecture and TA's were extremely helpful with projects. Likes more experimental work, though enough effort on your own projects will let you achieve a higher grade. Great class to start exploring who you are as an artist !

I agree with those saying that a class like this counts more for continuing education than for credit. But I am more traditional, and am not into these postmodern projects that have no beginning, no middle and no end. Hard to know the direction of a subfield that is not really scholarly. Look for something that has substance.

The material is not up to college level. It is interesting for undergrads, who like the fun of it, but there is no way to review. The prof. has no doctoral degree or publications that verify his credibility as a well-rounded scholar.

I'm not sure what other students are saying by tests, when I took it spring 23, we only had a screenplay, midterm and final project...And honestly they were easy to work on. The TA's were inspirational too and gave good feedback. The lectures are a bit long in my opinion, but informative if filmmaking is what you're into.

The guest lectures were informative and interesting but there is a lot of squandered time that can be used for review. In a class like this, it is difficult to know how to study for a test because the final grade is permanently posted on your record. The way it is structured counts more for continuing education than for academic credit.

Like guest speakers once in a while, but think that the class could be more cohesive if he picked up the thread of the syllabus, if any. Studying for test is hard though at the end U may end up with an A. Would be good to have the feedback from publications whether in pdf format or books. Would be more motivated to continue with a class like this!!

Very much an icon regarding their own art and history with art. Lectures are long but has good material in, and with many guest speakers coming in, lectures give really good advice and techniques for the class regarding what the projects will ask of you. Discussion and grades are done by TA, but lecture is great and he is accommodating.
She always read off slides and notes!

I love Amy! She is so smart and quirky and inspiring as a teacher. She makes you want to participate with the types of lectures she has. She really is a free form type of teacher and allows a lot of freedom for you to be creative.
It was a very stimulating class. But get ready to work a lot!

left out concepts in lectures

no never again.

reviews.comment: Bad teacher. Do not choose him if you want to keep your gpa

Genuinely bad teacher. Every other teacher gave students extra resources to pass. No curve, no cheat sheet, no uploaded notes, no recorded lectures, no study guide, nothing. Yaps a lot and still falls behind in content and expects you to know it for the exams.
Lectures were not mandatory but did not post slides. All the discussion worksheets were representative of the test. There were 2 midterms and a final with homework. Adds 5% weight to best midterm.

He was a cool guy but distant and the lectures were so bad. He rushes through everything at an insane speed and didn't actually explain anything, just read the problem and solve it himself. Basically had to self teach

I love MATH 4C with Professor Aycock! He is the best Maths Professor I had. He gives great lectures and is always happy to answer questions during class. The homework assignments are graded, but you can always get additional support during office hours if you have trouble with any questions. Highly recommended!

You can tell Jon Aycock is passionate about math, it shows through his lectures. He's an amazing professor. His humor made lectures entertaining at times. For this course, you do not need the textbook. Attendance is not mandatory, but he does not record lectures, so you basically have to go to each lecture to not miss out on what is covered.

He was very funny and included a lot of humor in his lectures making it easy to pay attention. Lectures are not recorded and notes aren't posted so if you don't want to rely entirely on the textbook attendance is critical. The homework is very helpful when studying for tests, as they are pretty much the same questions with different numbers.

All content is learned in the lecture, however he doesn't podcast even though there's no attendance. He writes everything on a chalk board and takes his time. Midterms and final are COMPLETELY based on homework, so practices those questions the most.

- textbook is optional, not required
- funny dude, down to earth
- office hours are helpful, allow for more personalized help
- homework on Macmillan Learning (it's like $60 for access) weekly 
- NO RECORDED LECTURES meaning attendance is basically mandatory 
- he provides a cheat sheet of formulas for midterms
- no calculator on exams, paper only

He is a nice professor who is not very strict in attendance, however, his class is fairly disorganized and you're not sure if you're completing the homework correctly as it takes the TAs a while to grade them. Homework is worth the greatest portion of this class, making this slow grading horrible for your grade. Exams aren't hard but vague.

I already took pre-calc in high school but I bombed the MPE so I had to take his class. I would say he's a fine lecturer, he went over things pretty clearly and always encouraged people to ask questions, but we didn't get to some things labeled in the course (ex. conic sections and vectors). Exams were all online and very fair & simple.

Started off the quarter pretty solid. Explained concepts that were confusing from 103a is a clear way.  Towards the end of the quarter he started slipping, taking longer to post things. mandatory attendance that contributes to grade, professor goes really fast compared to other professors in other sections.
