reviews.comment: grades based on attendance, otherwise would be 5 stars
You'll do fine if you follow and take notes in the lectures. Midterms and final were online and open note. Gives plentiful examples during his lectures.

All exams are remote and fairly easy, if you understand the hw you'll be good for the exams. He gives a lot of examples during lecture but they can be confusing at times since he writes long paragraphs. His teaching style can be better but overall an okay professor. Going to office hours might help if you're struggling in the course.

7/9 dicussions are mandatory. All midterms and final are remote. He gives good examples in class. If you have no background knowledge of pre-calc you might struggle in the class but should be fine if you study on your own. He's not a bad teacher, it's just hard to understand the subject if you've never learned anything like it. He seems caring.

TOOK HIM FOR MATH4C but doesnt let me pick. Class is SUPER easy he's just bad at teaching. Hw assignments once per week on Gradescope, 2 midterm & final exam are remote. Lecture not mandatory (dont bother going youtube taught me more) Discussion mandatory. Hate him bc he wants to be an English prof so bad & always puts everything into paragraphs...

When I took 103A it was very hard for me, but 103B with Prof. Aycock was so much better. Lectures are super clear and 2 homework problems every day. (I took it for Summer Session 2 so it might be different during normal school year) 3 midterms based on hws, and if you miss < 5 lectures and discussions, you get to drop your lowest midterm.

Jon sure as hell knows how to teach. He holds multiple office hours a week. Lowest exam and 2 quizzes are dropped. He tries to be funny during class. Great story teller. His class and Edfinity covers real world applications. He allows infinite attempts on every question on Edfinity.

Great professor. Understands the material very well but also understands students' struggles. When students have a ton of question, he tells them to see him in office hours to avoid slowing down the pace of the course. I will be taking Prof Aycock again.

Other things: lectures weren't mandatory, but discussion sections were. Reading not required.

Prof. Aycock is an amazing professor. Attendance is not mandatory. His slides are clear and it is easy to understand the material being taught. Out of all my professors, Prof. Aycock seemed the most approachable. He was very friendly and he is not overly "formal" when he teaches, which makes the class seem more casual and enjoyable.

Professor Jon A. taught this course very well, despite the fact that the entire course was coordinated through another professor. All exams open note, & very generous dropping two lowest quizzes & lowest exam out of four. Extremely helpful in office hours, so if you don't understand something go! Would take again in the future. Very good professor!

Very focused on lecture, got through the class with minimal reading only for the assignments. Two assignments (SWOT memo and LQ Shift-Share analysis), one midterm and one final. Great lectures, although a bit sleep inducing at times. Great class that got me into USP department, and a very caring professor.

While a lot of people in the RED major give him a hard time for being a slow lecturer who gets off topic, Anderson is an extremely competent teacher who gives very useful commentary and interesting insight from his ample experience. Midterm is easy econ, projects are easy, and he is very sweet

Amazing professor with decades in the industry and a lot of experience, also loved to help with students about inquiries into non-class related opportunities. Assignments were mainly handled by TA, and readings were assigned (I got by without reading). Go to lectures, study the section material, and it's an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The only assignments throughout the quarter were readings and memos. This is a pro and a con as your grade only relies on these + the midterm/final. The lectures can feel boring as he speaks about his life story at times. He's a nice guy and genuinely seems like he cares about his students. Not a bad class, but don't know if I would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is a little boring at times, but he means well and genuinely cares about his job. As long as you watch the lectures and stay on top of the material, you'll do fine. He's a sweet guy who wants his students to succeed. The TA was incredible too! Plenty of time to complete HW assignments. (three of them), the rest of the grade mid/final

Professor Anderson uses a lot of stories as examples for concepts and terms, his class is podcasted, and the only homework was an Excel project, writing a short essay, and optional reading from a textbook. The only con I can think of is he put a few tricky questions on the midterm/final, but the exams overall were reflective of what was taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's a fairly easy class. Every exam is multiple choice. There are only 4 HWs assigned every 2-3 weeks and they're not difficult either. Discussions are mandatory though as part of your grade. You don't need the textbook for this class, so don't forget to opt out of it

She has organized lectures and provides non-graded quizzes at the end of some of the lectures. A majority of the questions appearing on the final exam and she goes over them after. Homework is easy and straightforward. Lectures are recorded and slides are posted.

Professor Schartup is a very organized and knowledgeable lecturer who's passionate about what the material. Class is split between exams, homework (which is easy to do), and discussion attendance. She wanted every student to succeed and offered extra credit and a curve for the class. She is also clear about what information will be tested on exams.

Shes a nice person and her slides are very organized and clean. When it comes to answering questions, she doesn't answer and tells you to go watch the lecture. That quickly changed tho when a lot of students complained. She is nice and always willing to listen and adapt to students needs

Prof. Shartup is very passionate about what she teaches while also caring for her students. She tries her best to make sure everyone does well in the class and is relatively accessible. While she does require a textbook, readings weren't required and midterm questions could be answered without reading the textbook.

if you get points off in the quizzes, its kinda over. the essay had to be an exact word count? got docked off sm points bc of it. the finals and midterm was on canvas: i watched every movie and i still only got an 80%, never knew anyone who got higher: questiosn are odd. prof is funny

The prof gives extra credit for submitting the essay early, which I recommend because the quizzes and bring your grade down if you don't do well. There were weekly quizzes, 1 midterm/final that was open-note and multiple choice (a lot of the questions come from the textbook). The last half of the class was online lectures.
Super chill and very easy A
Great professor, super easy. Be serious with writing the essay, and you will get an A.

Class was almost all attendance reading quizzes that were super easy. Highly recommend taking his classes because the subject matter is really interesting and professor havis is really knowledgeable about the material.
The guy knows his stuff. The newer films fit the class better.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor has questionable integrity because he structures the class as pay to win. The midterm and final questions are based on stuff from a textbook that HE wrote that costs 30 dollars. Plus, he offers extra credit if you buy tickets to a play. I dont think this professor cares about his students and only wants people to buy his textbook.

Class was easy but extremely boring and annoying, and professor Havis is lowkey a horrible professor and might I say a con artist too. He wants you to buy his textbook that he wrote and a lot of the quiz and final questions were dependent on the textbook. Horrible in lectures, can't understand him, class is boring and a waste of my time, NOT FUN.
hes super nice
hes nice but its a lot of work for a fine arts
Would do magic tricks at the start of the class. Classes are very relaxing and entertaining.
Amazing professor, he was very entertaining and his classes were very relaxing.

Really easy class. One paper you can turn in early for extra credit, plus extra credit for attending a UCSD play. Quizzes are straightforward from readings and lecture. Attendance isn't required but helps a lot. The take-home MCQ midterm was manageable. Havis is funny and genuinely cares about getting students into theatre and film.

Had him for TDGE 125 and 127 over summer. His Canvas went down in the last few hours when the final exam was due, but he was very considerate and responded to everyone's concerns. He's also really passionate about the films he talks about, and the work isn't difficult at all. Film selection is good too, lots of great films to watch!

Professor Havis was really engaging and charming, and I loved the selection of films we watched. Lecture is long, but worth it to learn/see the films. A couple of exams that were a bit difficult, you just have to actually study some of his textbook and pay attention to his lecture before the film. Final paper was long, but was not difficult.

Chill prof and class. Your enjoyment will depend a little on if you like Spike Lee's movies. Attendance isn't mandatory, but he will give answers to the quizzes and tests in class, so it's worth going. There are weekly readings you have to do, and you do need to know what they talk about for the paper and tests. Just skim them and you'll be fine.

ehh, mid film class for my GE. quiz on the movies to make sure u act watch them, pretty boring some times, but easy A if u try, not trying to make this class impossible which is really nice, would recommend.

He did magic tricks in class lol. Attendance not taken but go to lecture because quizzes/midterm/final are based on lots of lecture materials (still very easy), & take notes as most lectures aren't recorded. Interesting movies but some you could skim through, such as King Kong. I watched a cut version on 2x speed & passed w/ flying colors.
A professor that 'gets it'. Engaging, funny, kind, passionate, and informed. This is my first day in his class and nothing but good things to say so far.

It's really not a difficult class at all. Graded by 1 paper, 10 (4Qs) quizzes based on lecture and film material. 30Qs midterm, 30 Qs final. He's super interactive during in person lectures, He's pretty funny. Definitely take it if you want/need to with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The guideline for the big essay is incredibly vague, get 4/20 points taken off for things didn't mention (but extra credit gave 4 points back for submitting early). The midterm is incredibly hard, but there are 7 extra points given out (not sure how they are counted) if you finish the class and go see his movie (free). Overall not too bad.

Really tough grader on the paper, changed my grade 3/20 points lower from what the TA first graded for just missing minor detail. Forces you to buy his book, all the answers to the quiz are in the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures have no visual guides and are not based on slides/power points, so it's essentially him talking at you for an hour. Quizzes are based on very specific details that he mentions in lecture or in his book. Class goes through a lot of old movies and silent films which can be a hard watch if you're not interested.
Films are good on Spike Lee's career. Textbook not great. Not bad. Kind of dense for grad student BS

He makes you buy a $40 book full of his personal opinions, we had to write an essay and I got docked 12% for not mentioning a minor detail briefly discussed in class. The quizzes are difficult and graded for correctness. I don't understand how his reviews are so good, he is the worst professor I have had at ucsd.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ingmar Bergman films, Swedish, classic black and white movies 50 years old all term, bleak and brutal, but powerful themes and meaningful.  Worth the effort
Easy class, but he's insufferable. Forced us to buy his $40 textbook that's filled with his opinions on the films discussed in class (which were horrid btw).

Would be smoother sailing if he had PowerPoints. Take notes on his essay tips; he only discusses it once. He only recorded lectures when we shifted to zoom. Most stuff from his quizzes comes from the lecture itself and not the movie, so attendance is important. I found the class boring, but he cared for his students and gave us all 4 points boost.

This professor knows the topic very well and is very charismatic. Lectures are not mandatory but he talks about things that will be on the quiz. He is an unconventional lecturer meaning he just talks at you about the director/film. Questions on quizzes and exams can be confusing sometimes.

Just get the book. Most of the answers are in the book he MAKES you buy. It's not cheap, especially for a book you will never use again. Take all the quizzes; none are dropped. Listen to the lectures; gives hints of quiz answers. No lecture slides for the class= hard to follow. Watch the films for the quiz/exam/assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do not miss a quiz. All answers are either given in class lectures or easy to pick out in the films. Missing a quiz will significantly drop your grade. Super funny guy, and easy to approach about questions and content.

Allan was a fun professor but you have to attend the classes in order to do well. If you miss one question in his 4 question quizzes, your grade drops. I had a hard time keeping up with the lectures cause there were no visuals. The class essay was fun I enjoyed it. Midterm dropped me hard. Final failed me. Please go to all classes. Read the book.

Prof. Havis is an awesome and chill Prof. Took him for TDGE 127, which consists on watching a movie once a week, followed by a quiz for attendance. There is one midterm, one final, and one paper (extra points for submitting early). The class overall was easy but also very interesting. Prof. Havis is very chill and passionate about what he teaches.
He has a veryyy cute dog!!!!! And a cat, but we don't see the cat often. I love this class and Prof Havis is great. Just pay attention to the lecture and watch those movies you would be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was an easy A, but Havis never really discussed the performances and our quizzes were all trivia that he sometimes doesn't even mention in lecture. Also he wrote the required textbook and its bad and expensive.

Weekly movies, weekly quizzes (based on lecture, readings, and movies), a midterm, an essay, and a final. To do well on the quizzes, take detailed notes during lecture, watch the movies, and read the assigned readings. You actually have to pay attention during the movies and what is said in the readings. Lectures are more entertaining than usual.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Havis is great! His lectures are a bit slow (you can tell the online format is out of his comfort zone). Each week has an assigned film to watch before lecture, the lecture, and a short 4 question quiz on topics explicitly discussed in lecture. Midterm paper is very easy with EC for turning it in early. MC final/midterm were not hard.

A very erudite professor who is really passionate about his field. Don't hesitate to pick his class. Listen to his lectures, take good notes, watch the movies and read the books: that's what all you need.

Weekly quizzes were based on lectures that can be seen live or pre-recorded. Prof shows interest in theater. Lectures went a bit slow so I would watch at 2X speed. Midterm and final was based on films one would need to watch. The readings would come from the prof own book and were quick and short. Good easy class, took for GE yet nice experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Havis is amazing and really cares about the material. His class is extremely easy as long as you listen to the lecture and read the 3 to four pages of the book he asks you to. As well as watch the movie. The TA is amazing and does all the grading along with random graders.

I took the Cult Films seminar with him and it was really interesting. Great films covered, though the discussion portion wasn't as strong, mainly owing to the online format. Still a fun class, though.

Dr. Havis is definitely knowledgeable in the films that he lectures about. However, to be honest, I don't think I learned too much from his class at all. It's so hard to stay attentive during his lectures. This is not a hard class, but it's just so boring.

I can tell Professor Havis has a passion for films and knows a lot of background information on them, but I do not recommend this class for someone who has little to no interest in films. I joined because I love movies but this class focuses on the background of films rather than the story itself. The lectures are heavy and sometimes unorganized.

I don't think anyone takes this class expecting to learn much. It's primarily for GE requirements. I personally found the class to be an easy A. Really easy quizzes every week, one 6 page essay, one midterm, and one final. Since the class was open book this quarter, literally every question can be looked up. There is no reason not to do well.

His class isn't necessarily hard, but I feel like I barely learn anything from him. This class is about great performances, yet he barely talks about the performances and just summarizes the movies in a redundant and useless way. Also, he makes the textbook mandatory for his students, and it is the most useless book I have ever read.

Professor Havis's lectures were very long and not terribly interesting, but he's very knowledgable on the subject and what he's teaching. The class was graded off of weekly quizzes, a 6 page paper, a multiple choice midterm, and a final.

I didnt buy the book because you dont really need it. The class itself is easy: you just watch films and take tiny quizzes. But the multiple choice midterm is very hard, with specific questions about names and dates. Maybe it wouldve helped if I bought the book, but there wasn't anything specific given to me to study. Final essay is not hard.

Professor Havis is entertaining and seems to be really passionate about theatre & film. The class is pretty easy because your grade will only be based on weekly quizzes and a final paper. The quizzes are simple and the essay is straight forward.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Fun professor who usually does magic tricks before lecturing the class. There is a quiz at the end of every class, a midterm with some difficult questions, and a final 6 page paper. The extra credit opportunities should be able to secure you an A in the class - don't make my same mistake.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 1 midterm, 1 paper, 1 quiz at the end of every lecture. I didn't really care too much about the course, took it for an easy A. A little more work than I was told by peers but very doable. He gives extra credit to boost your grade by 1-2 letter grades so do that. The final paper was very ambiguous in terms of what was expected of us though.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Professor Havis during the summer session and was in his TDGE 10 class. This class was super interesting and you will watch some great movies. It is a very easy class as long as you pay attention during his lectures and the movies. When he says to read a chapter in his book, I definitely would as it helps for the tests and his papers.

TDGE 10 is very little work. But, you're graded by only a few things, and there really is no way to "study" to pull up your grade. Everyone said the midterm was easy, but the info on the test was super specific with names and dates. Highly recommend using the Quizlets online to study. Prof is cool, though his oral lectures are not very structured.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Havis is awesome. Hes always very caring of his students. Go to class, take notes and youll be fine. The midterm is just on the movie lists that he assigns and its easy. Essay is 6 pages but theres plenty of information he gives in class necessary for a quality paper.
Go to this class, and you will be crazy in theater. The professor  is very kind and knowledgeable. Wonderful experience!
Go to this class, you will be crazy in theater.  By the way,  the professor is very kind and knowledgeable.

Quizzes every lecture so it is mandatory. One midterm and one final paper. Prof. Havis is an amazing lecturer and is extremely knowledgeable and funny! Great prof. but his 6-page paper was a bit hard to write, but that is my own opinion.  Great class overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class is manageable. There are 1 midterm and 1 final paper. You need to pay attention to what he says in lecture and the films that are shown in class because there are quizzes (4 questions true or false) every day. The quizzes are pretty easy and they count toward your class attendance. He also sometimes does cool magic tricks in class.

Easy class. Gives quizzes based on the movies watched/lectures at the end of lecture and as long as you pay some attention you should easily get 100%s. Midterm was super easy. Only complaint was for the final paper; was super vague about it and kept changing his answers on what he "wanted from us". Ex: something that he approved is suddenly not.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is such an amazing professor. TDGE 10 was my stress reliever. 1 midterm based on director names, movie dates, success/failures, and other details. It is curved. One 6 pg ppr (EC if turn in early). There is a quiz everyday (mostly for attendance), but it is super easy if you are awake in class. Not much reading at all. Easy and fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof. Havis is pretty awesome. He does magic tricks and doesn't hold back politically. His interpretations of the films we watch during class can be quite interesting. The grading consists of one midterm and the final (6 page paper). Pretty straightforward prompt, gives extra credit for turning it in early.

He's funny and his lectures don't even feel like lectures. We just watched films and he would tell us interesting facts about the director or the movie. The midterm was easy as long as you watched the movies. We didn't even have a final, we just had to write a 6-page paper that he warned us about at the beginning of the course so we had time.

Absolutely loved this class! Took it during second summer session and loved getting to watch films and find the theatricality in them. He started every class with a magic trick, and although I found myself checking the clock often because some movies were boring, the class as a whole was phenomenal. Take him if you can!
Smart lecture notes on very old movies  mixing with newer movies.  Harold and Maude hilarious
Cool film seminar.  Horror films without gore. Sharp funny  comments.  Uses his own text book.

Honors seminar on the New York Times and current journalism standards.  We tracked key topics like ebola virus, political scandals, and general news hype.  We got a free online subscription to the Times.   Great seminar - everyone talked.
You watch entire films in class and some are very weird.

It's an easy class but it gets pretty boring. Prof. Havis is very knowledgeable and interesting, but prepare to be kept waiting for him to come back to class after the film is done. It was kind of annoying how he would leave during class while the film played, and he was never on time coming back as we waited to take our daily quiz.

This class is so relaxing. It's fun to go to this class and watch 50 minutes of a movie - which is all we did each class. Profesor Havis' pre-movie commentary is comical and enjoyable. There's a 2 page paper at the end and it'll be the easiest thing you'll ever write at UCSD. And the 'final exam' is common sense if you payed attention to the movies
Coolest class you ever take, you can totally enjoy this class
Film 87. One of the coolest classes you will ever take. there is a quiz, but it is so easy. it is based on the movies you watch.

films we watched were pretty entertaining. there's a multiple-choice midterm that focuses on the lectures/films, and a couple of questions from the book. final is a paper. he gives extra credit for going to his plays! i got an A! great professor.
Awesome professor, period!

While he's a smart guy, he comes off as somewhat arrogant. He's unreachable outside of class, and doesn't seem to know how to connect with students. He's not a difficult teacher, but why take a prof who's simply mediocre???

This freshman seminar is probably my all time favorite class! The science fiction movies were interesting and there was one 2 page paper due at the end of the quarter which was super easy.  There was also a short quiz at the end of the quarter which was also easy.

I took his FILM 87 Film Studies Seminar on Fantasy/Sci Fi films. It was so relaxed and VERY EASY. We had like one miniquiz that was easy if you attended and watched all the movies. There is one light reading assignment, and you write one two page paper that will probably be the EASIEST paper you will write at UCSD!

This class (cult films) was great. Easy reading, easy weekly 5 pt. quizzes, and an easy M/C, TF midterm. The 6 page final paper was the only difficult part of the class but it is do-able. Havis is very funny, although he is not very accessible out of class or via email. Overall, the class is a definite "must take", even for non-theatre majors.

Allan Havis was one of the folks who got me through the MFA program at UCSD. His friendship and support kept me in school at a time when I'd almost certainly have left without it. He's a caring, kind human being and also a good supervisor for graduate work.

While the class was easy, Havis was of no help to anyone, especially concerning the final paper. I didn't learn anything in this class and all he talked about was how stupid the people in the "red states" are. For a "openminded" UCSD professor I found his tirades very ignarant and condescending and harmful to the tolerant liberal cause.
Perfect class for me because I love movies. I would have liked more earlier films but overall I give the class and the prof. an A.

Allan's suggestions were not very helpful.  I felt like he tried to steer my writing in a way that did not reflect my original concept/idea/creation.  His lectures reflect his knowledge of writing though, which was very helpful/interesting.  His ideas/attempts to counsel me with my writing, were not helpful.

I loved this class! Professor Havis is a nice, humorous man. This class opened my eyes to a different style of film and an understanding and appreciation of it. There was reading (1 article per class), weekly quizes (easy), a midterm (easy), and a paper (most difficult). TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

Easy film class. Watch a movie or two every week and take a MC test to make sure you were in class. Midterm was MC (also easy). Most of the grade comes from a final paper, which is easy to complete if you actually went to class.
I scored a 99 percentile in the biology section of MCAT. I am grateful for this course.

I truly appreciate her knowledge and support toward her students. 100% would recommend her as an instructor. Her support provided me with the confidence to effectively present my PowerPoint on the cardiovascular system. Her encouragement when expanding our knowledge is also much appreciated and is an attribute that not many professors have.

This class came directly after a class that the instructor was highly difficult. Nidhi's positive encouragment made a difference for my learning experience. Being in this class refreshed me and made me excited to learn! Instructors make a huge impact on learning experiences and I am so glad I had Nidhi!
I thought the instructor was very honest with her grades. I appreciated the feedback I received each week from her.

Her grading is iffy, deducted points on discussion boards no matter what. Does not reply to messages to ask why you received a certain grade, intro bio course which should be easy is made difficult. Never got a 100% on anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: As a full time working professional, I appreciate how organized the course was. Multiple reminders that I received throughout the week were helpful too. Fast responses were an added plus!

Spent a lot of time on this class. Grading felt arbitrary & nitpicky. Points deducted without feedback, making it hard to learn. When I asked for clarification, I was met with more questions instead of answers, which felt unhelpful. I didn't feel supported in understanding the material or improving.
Instructor's positive encouragement really makes the course engaging and enjoyable.

Professor Ahuja is an exceptional master teacher. Her in-depth knowledge is excellent. She effectively communicated complex anatomical physiological concepts so they are easily understood and presented the course material in engaging, creative ways. Her ability to incorporate real-life examples and case studies was fantastic. She's an inspiration.
I enjoyed the enthusiasm that she has for teaching. I did well in the class. I usually repeat science classes, but this time, it will be only once, thanks to the professor.
The instructor did a great job at pushing our discussion posts to be engaging and meaningful to the course and our learning

This professor's teaching is incredibly challenging, lacking consistency and clarity. Her grading feels arbitrary, causing constant uncertainty. Email communication is unhelpful, often with ignored questions. The absence of detailed grade explanations makes improvement difficult. reconsidering my academic path I advise against enrolling.

i can tell prof ahuja cares about her students. Given that physio was an online class, all communication is via email with her. Each exchange was respectful & accommodating. She is a pleasant person in general and try to work with you case by case. there are weekly discussion posts, lengthy labs and quizzes but she isn't nitpicky about her grading

I took Physiology w/ lab from UCSD Ext. You will get to choose from 2 professors: nidhi ahuja and praveen kumar. TAKE W/ NIDHI AHUJA DO NOT TAKE W KUMAR. they are both responsive to emails but kumar is unaccommodating and snarky w/ his responses. ahuja is pretty accommodating and flexible. Your life will be much easier with professor nidhi ahuja
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I was nervous about this being online and my knowing very little about the school, professor, and subject. Her consistent, clear, and encouraging communication with the class via canvas announcements has been helpful and I love how the modules are set up. As long as you follow the process and do the reading and activities, you can't fail!
Expectations were high, and from my interactions with the professor, I could tell that she really cares for the students
I really enjoyed taking this course!
I am really glad I took this course- Definitely recommending to y'all
I enjoyed this class very much-- Easy A
Labs were online, relevant and very interesting.
I loved how the course was structured. It was my favorite course this term.
The course was easy to understand and navigate. I learned a lot of useful information.
The labs are pretty cool with hands on experience!
No final exam; Excllent projects

This Professor is tough and very demanding. Her quizzes are hard to pass because only gives you one minute for each question. As much as I tried l could not finish the quizzes with more than a C. Her labs will take you 10 hours to complete, for each of them, and she wants you to know every tiny detail. I had to give up in the fourth week.
The class was perfect, and the professor made sure that we understand the material each week before we moved on.

I really enjoyed this professor and thought the lecture material was very well laid out and easy to understand. She's also extremely responsive to emails. The lab part was terrible though to complete during a pandemic. I recommend you take this class but the lab elsewhere! UCSD made a poor choice in using this type of lab software.
Lecture is boring… Huge amount of homework to do
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For the love of god do not take her class.

Sometimes the professor spoke too softly. Lots of reading in the class, but if you put in just a little thought into the analysis of the works assigned, you'll be fine. The final was not a test, but a mock exhibition/write up and depending on the T/A, graded very lightly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Soooooooooo boring, hard to stay awake. Lots of reading and weekly assignments. Not the worst but I did not have fun, she means well, but I don't like her lecture style. beware. be alert.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: she means well but she is really boring. lectures are very content heavy and it's ok for a ge requirement, but no one was interested.

The professor is very nice. Fulfilling class content with clear logic of lecture arrangement. It's an introduction if you're into serious media studies, but could also be a way too boring academic conversation if you know nothing with no interest in this field. It's fine taking for GE since lenient grading though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Media and art isn't for everyone, however, if you are someone interested in this field, the course was interesting and provided historic and relevant context to film, media, video, art, etc. Lectures can get boring, DIs can be interesting, NO Midterm, Final is a straightforward project, discussion boards do matter + readings, and weekly worksheets.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Class was easy and fairly manageable, but lots of reading. No final or midterm (only a final project). Lectures could be a bit of a drone at times. Super nice professor though.

It's a really easy class and she has good intentions. It's just extremely boring is the only problem. Lots of readings but you can get by reading nothing. No final or midterm, just a project that you technically could not do and still get an A.

Readings can be a lot, but you can get away with skimming them just enough to answer the canvas discussions and weekly worksheets. There is no midterm or final exam, with only a final project which isn't that hard and are given ample amount of time to do. Not a terrible class if you don't want to stress about an additional midterm or final.

Nice woman, good intentioned, but holy moly she literally assigns so much reading. In week 8 and it's literally been like this the whole quarter. Really easy assignments but like... not if you didn't do the readings which are like 60 pages every two days. Just too much work, not trying to be lazy but yea. Wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
I'm in VIS 85A
She is such a nice professor who gives charitable grades. She doesn't have any tests; all of the grades are covered by assignments and a final project, which is not so strict.

If you want to cover your GE, this will be fine for you.

Weekly workload depend heavily on the articles and essay she gave, for now experiencing like hundred page of reading every week. Minimum time to complete her weekly assignment around 12 hours, attendance taken in iCloud which located your location through GPS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I'm taking VIS85A right now, and her lectures are really boring, with a lot of tedious stuff. She assigns a lot of homework, and her attitude toward students when judging their work is disrespectful. Do not take her class. There is a reason why her class is the only one with extra slots among all other GEs.

Great professor! Grades come from weekly discussion posts, reading quizzes, and take-home midterm & final exams. Lectures aren't recorded, but slides are available. The required readings are lengthy but necessary for quizzes (2 attempts for each). Online exams are open-note with multiple choice and 1 short answer. Fun class; I highly recommend it!

During lecture on Day 1, she kept writing things on the chalkboard that did not align at all with the Powerpoint right in front of her. Then on the next lecture she states she did ALL mechanisms wrong, and blames this on a "cold" instead of taking accountability like a good professor would. Unorganized, seems lost in her own world, just bad

Probably the worst lecturer I've ever had. Her lectures are extremely unorganized. She would ramble about things that are not important to the class and she would forget names of important proteins and other mechanisms. You're better off just reading the textbook instead of going to lectures. She is really nice though

The worst professor of the entire series. She is the best when it comes to kindness and understanding students, but her lectures are extremely confusing and make no sense. The HW does not help with the exams. Practice midterms are posted but conflict with HW and the answers are not completely posted. Horribly organised class.
This is the best biochem professor. She is extremely kind. If you get a chance sign up for her class. Its still hard but she is by far the most empathetic and reasonable professor you will get.

This was the professor's first time teaching the class. But I do not feel like she prepared enough for it. There were continuous technical difficulties with podcast and she refused to switch to Zoom lectures. Barely explained bioinformatics and expected us to do HW on it. Exam gradting criteria was not clear. She does have enthusiasm for subject.

One of the most disorganized professors I have ever seen. Lectures are a mess since she is not confident in the material herself, so she literally makes mistakes every lecture. I do not recommend this professor to anyone.

Professor Komives seems like a wonderful person but this class has been a horrible experience. Since biochemistry is my major I thoroughly enjoyed 114A and 114B and the professors that taught them, but this has been an awful experience. She doesnt even seem confident in the material, and the lectures are all over the place.

I don't know if its her teaching style or the fact that she's not tech savy, but there is not one lecture I can clearly understand what's going on. The lecture video is always kinda blurry and the audio cuts out a lot. I really don't understand why she choose to do podcast instead of a zoom lecture. The tests were hard and so are the homework.

8 weeks in and we still have terrible lecture videos. Can't even understand what is going on in the lecture because of MAJOR technical difficulties. Midterms are also unreasonably difficult for this class. She's told us repeatedly this is her first time teaching yet her exams are on a completely different level compared to her lectures.

the quarter is almost over and she still has not produced one understandable lecture. she makes mistakes in every single lecture and expects us to go out of class time to fix the errors. hw isn't related to the actual course or tests. she was so unprepared and gave unreasonable tests that weren't representative. i really wish i was exaggerating.

Boomer professor who refuses to fix her online lectures, despite 80% of them having either an audio problem or visual problem, or both. Records her lectures inside of a lecture hall through the UCSD podcast system, so the camera and audio doesn't always track on her. Uses the excuse that we are "learning under adversity" by recording these lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This class was honestly a mess. Tests were on concepts beyond what we learned in class, she was always unprepared and didn't know the concepts she was teaching. She would make a lot of mistakes and had to correct herself later on. Homework was on bioinformatics and not even helpful to know for the class itself. Just all over the place

Amazing prof, very passionate about chemistry, will keep you engaged in lectures, will give you knowledge that will help in your future and isn't just stuff pulled from the textbook. Very funny and will tell cool stories. Her tests were very fair imo, as long as you took good notes and spent time studying.

I loved learning biochemistry from her all quarter, she's one of those professors that were just made to teach the world. She knows what she's doing and she's always there to cut around the bs. That being said I'm lowkey sad about winter quarter finals being caught in the middle of the pandemic cause that final was a big oof. Take her if you can

TAKE HER CLASS IF YOU CAN! The class is video-casted now so you don't need to go to lecture, but it really is worth the time to go to lecture. She's funny and very animated and she also lightens the load of the class. Goes over mechanisms in great detail which were really helpful for the 2 midterms and final. 100% would retake. Definitely take her!

GO TO LECTURE. Everything important (mechanisms) is on the blackboard which isn't podcasted bc ucsd is far behind its time. She's a great lecturer, funny, loves what she does and teaches. The class can be difficult if you don't practice the mechanisms and understand all the steps of the diff cycles, so you really just need to put the work in.

The best professor in the Chemistry department! She is fun and super enthusiastic about teaching and also about the subject; she has a lot of experience in the field and with other scholars but is one of the few who also cares a lot about her students. The class is extremely mechanism-heavy, which she emphasizes and goes over in lectures.

she really cares about her students. Her office hours are helpful with solving the HW she assigns which could be a little bit challenging sometimes. The midterm was fair, very similar to the HW and practice midterm. The final was a little bit harder, but everything that was on the final was covered in the lecture. could not recommend her enough.

She is the best professor I have had so far at UCSD. She explains her lecture on the board so you need to attend lecture. she assigns HW from the book. she could help you on the HW if you go to her office hours. her midterm is very similar to the practice midterm and the HW. practice the mechanism daily until you can not forget them. Must take her.

Clear lecture. Book is not necessary. Study the mechanisms by keep drawing them till you can draw them without checking notes. She writes everything on blackboard, so go to lecture is kinda necessary. Need to work for it to get A, but it's definitely doable. One midterm one final, MC and short answers(mechanisms based). 8 HWs. Class based on curve
Professor Komives is great.  Very friendly, upbeat, and funny - makes lectures go by very fast.  A third of your grade is turning in HW, so it's not tough to get a good grade.  Mechanism-heavy class.

She is a great professor. She knows the material really well and her explanations are very clear. And she is entertaining. I recommend going to lectures, because she writes down mechanisms on the board and knowing the mechanisms is a major part of the exams. Make sure to pay attention to the details that she emphasizes.

She is very funny. She is clear on what she wants for tests. Attend her review. Super helpful. She has podcast but come to class for stuff on the board. Her test was fair and reflect on what focus on. HW is 30% of overall grade.

33% homework, 33% midterm, 33% final. You don't need the textbook (homework posted on TED). She really enjoys what she teaches and you can tell because she's always happy during lecture and loves to answer questions. Her exams were difficult but very fair without any surprises. They look just like practice exams LOTS OF MECHANISMS! Good curve.
This is an interesting course.  She is a great professor with broad knowledge.  Plus, very intelligent... Recommend to everyone.
she's a great lecturer. she knows her material really well, but the class is hard. really mechanism based. know the ones she emphasizes and you can do well. she's quite the character too
She has good days and bad days. I wish she prepared the class better, instead of filling the time with other topics.
SO COOL but homework blows and vague outlines for exams in general bah humbug I say

Her class is beyond fair because the grade is based on either 100pts mid-term, 200 pts final, and 100 pts problem sets or she sets these 3 categories as out of 300 points. She is very enthusiastic about teaching metabolic chemistry class. You should take her notes, redo her problem sets,  and read her lecture notes, and practice mechanisms
The class was disorganized. She expects you to go to office hours, instead of teaching during the class. She should prepare the lectures better.

Dr. Komives is by far one of the most interesting profs i have had. She presents the material well and definitely displays a true passion for the subject. The tests are definitely fair but difficult because of the volume of memorization involved because of the mechanism-heavy nature of the course. I would highly recommend taking her. She's great!

Komives really fueled my passion for learning biochemistry. Prior to this class, everything seemed overwhelming but she made this class extremely enjoyable. As long as you pay attention to her during lecture as well as her notes (especially points she emphasizes) you will do great!
So, so class. Professor yells and laughs all the time while she goes on and on with her explanations. Her exams are easy compared to the irrelevant details of the class.

Prof Komives is fantastic.  She challenges students to learn the material and use it in a meaningful way.  The material is tough and there IS a large amount of memorization, but you don't have to know the details of EVERY pathway & mechanism. 1 midterm, 1 final, graded HW each count for ~1/3 of your grade. It's totally possible to get an A (I did!)

Great professor. She understands that no one has all the metabolic pathways memorized so she only tested us on the material she emphasized in lectures (don't memorize the whole pathway, just the key step!). Despite it being a mechanism-heavy course, she manages to make lectures interesting with her off-topic stories and passion for biochemistry.

Awesome professor, really passionate about the topic and cares a lot about her students; tests are representative of the material she goes over in lecture but covers a wide range of information so it does require a lot of memorizing and keeping up, she doesn't test about the small details. Definitely one of the best, most interesting professor ever

One of the best BioChem Professors are UCSD. I did all my studying when I went to her class, that is how well she taught. She explain everything in a clear manner that enable you to memorize & understand the concepts without having to study for long hrs.
She can be a good teacher, but if you happen to be born in the wrong group you and your grade will suffer.

She can teach well or she can make up answers that she doesn't know. I felt I didn't know what to believe at the end. She seems to always have the answer, but then you figure out that it was misleading. Her out-of-the-blue laugh scares me.

A lot of articles to read, but read enough to do problem sets. Take very good notes and study them to do well on her final. The final was very hard, but it's good that she's generous. She is very fun during lecture, more enthusiastic than any other chem professor.
She is a wonderful professor. Very helpful. Definitely go to lectures and her office hours. YOU CANNOT FAIL THIS COURSE. She'll even write rec letters for you!

Make sure to attend office hours and all lectures and suck up there and get clues to homeworks and final (don't have to think on your own, and you automatically get higher grades). Bodily presence in office hours and lectures influences grades. So it's not just that you studied very hard and did well on assignments that gets you an A. Just be there

Betsy's awesome. She wants you to learn and appreciate the subject, not to memorize. Her "stories" are always hilarious and it's wonderful to have a professor who knows so much about the field. This class was meant to teach us to challenge scientific literature - even published ones. It's a healthy skill to learn, even for an undergrad.

She's a good professor to have, if only to challenge your perception of science textbooks and to give you a healthy dose of skepticism.  Her tests are a lot of rxns and somewhat difficult.  Nice professor.

Somehow i lost any remaining passion for biochemistry taking this professor's class. Class not exciting, though she knows her subject well. Of 114A-C series this was the worst quarter. Tests stess detail and memorization.

Friendly teacher with rather funny laughter. Her handwritting and organization need a little improvement. Test are essay-style quesitons where she focuses on mechanisms of rxns that students have to memorize. Homeworks are a breeze.

Genuinely the worst professor I had ever had . He accused me of using AI with no evidence , academic integrity dismissed my case because there was no proof AND he had encouraged me to stop going to class which academic integrity said was not okay for him to say, felt super unfair to work hard just to get accused of AI for NO reason
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I agree with a mix of what I see on this site: he's probably harder than any other Muir Prof. And if he even suspects AI, he's gone come down on you.  I know his sense of humor might rub people the wrong way. But he's super smart. I learned more from him than I have in many upper divisions classes in my major (poli sci).
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very stressful to take. If you're good at writing, obviously you're gonna do good in any writing class. If you are a developing writer that needs assistance and support for your peers, you likely wont get that because of how he operates his class. Snarky, blunt, mistaken, and he's hard to talk to so if you are having any sort of trouble, good luck.

Don't trust the haters on this site. A few of my friends have had him and it's pretty simple: if you work hard, you're going to do well. If you think MCWP should be easy, or you were looking for an easy prof, or you use AI, you'll hate it and hate him. But the guy is fair and brilliant and funny. At least I think he is. Very cool dog.

I regret taking this professor, especially after hearing that friends in MCWP 50 with other instructors are earning A's while I am not because of how rigorous his grading is. Many people say MCWP is difficult, but it doesn't seem that way unless you take a professor like Jason Bartulis.

Couldn't tell if he was making fun of me or not, but always mispronounced my name. Extremely difficult grading criteria. Better off taking another professor as it'd be easier to get an A with anyone else other than Jason Bartulis.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I quickly lost motivation because he graded drafts harshly, even though they were meant to be based mainly on completion. This made earning an A feel nearly impossible unless you were acknowledged by him. He also seemed to expect students to write at a level comparable to the authors in the articles he gave us.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was often delayed in grading drafts and provided feedback only after we were already well into the assignments. Many of his comments suggested revisions that were difficult to implement since earlier drafts had already passed. His lack of transparency was disappointing, and he frequently overcomplicated assignment prompts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very straight forward when it comes to content. Despite from what I see, he tries to be very reasonable when it comes to work. I personally did not use AI so I can't vouch for the comments regarding his stance on AI. There were definitely plenty of opportunities to seek help via office hours.  Its a hard class, but he makes it a bit better.
I hoped my throat would close any time I was in this class. I lost 4 pounds from stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Don't listen to bad reviews, bro. I had him for both 40 and 50, and would soooo take him again. He's SUPER clear about what he expects, gives feedback, is patient, and takes his time answering questions. I think the reason why students say he doesn't help is bc they don't ask questions, so user error ig. He also brings his dog (I miss the dog).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I've never met a professor who's found as many ways to take points off assignments as Bartulis has
Accuses people of using AI given that turnitin is not always accurate  even with proof with AI wasn't used, gives no useful feedback and expects drafts to be near perfect,

NOT good and not helpful at all. Gives minimal insight and expects you to understand what he wants. Gives low grades for assignments that aren't hard, his expectations are high. Compared to other MCWP teachers, he pretty much is the worse. Also he likes to accuse of the use of AI, so watch out for ANY minor thing that could give that away.
If you use AI at all, even a little, he will probably catch you and give you an F. Pretends to be nice and understanding about it but he's not.

I think Bartulis gets a bad wrap from some because he's hard and expects real work. There are easier 50 teachers for sure so if you aren't interested in politics or art or don't like jazz, I'd avoid him. He's sarcastic and that can offend some people. But he's a great professor and I'd take any class he taught outside of Muir. Muir writing stinks.

The difference btw a good and bad MCWP professor is how much responsibility they are willing to take for their students. A good MCWP teacher (from students perspective) will be considerate, lenient, and understanding. Bartulis is none of these, and comes off like he's itching to make your life worse while blaming the department's strict criteria.

I'm taking him for 50. I don't know have any idea about my grade. But Jason might be the best prof I've had at UC. He's a little scary but funny and makes fun of himself. I think people don't like him because they think MCWP should be easy and he's not. But I've learned a tone from his lectures about political issues. Don't believe the haters.
Strict about assignment expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very pragmatic, respectful, logical professor who adds nice elements to class at times with his jokes, background, even his dog. Clear grading criteria that he elaborates on extensively, and he is very open to questions, comments, etc. regarding clarification. Physical copies of the textbooks are required and cost money which is unfortunate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Fr don't listen to any of the bad reviews. Caring prof, and I'm taking him again for 50. He's VERY clear about what he expects and gives GOOD feedback, so as long as you follow that, you'll be fine (he legit had a whole lecture dedicated to answering questions, idk what ppl are on abt him not helping). 10/10 easy A. Funny, sassy, and brings his dog
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very clear about grading criteria, which I appreciate, but he does follow it pretty strictly and can be insistent on specific things, so be careful about that. MCWP 40 is a pretty weirdly structured class overall but he tries to make things as clear as possible. Really nice, although a little bit sassy but I love his energy.

Amazing professor, course was hard but that's just the department's fault not necessarily his. Office hours were a life savior in this course. He was intimidating week 1 but if you just talk to him he's a great guy and is willing to hear your questions. Very friendly! You'll struggle for sure if you're not willing to put in the work/effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jason could be a good professor if he actually tried caring a bit more and helping each student more. He is very passive agressive and not welcoming.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is a little condescending in class and when asked questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: rigid grading and captious about any speculations without evidence.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jason is funny and super smart and is very helpful in office hours. The class can be confusing at times. But I'm not sure it's him or that Muir changed a lot of the assignments. He's clear about what he expects but there is a lot of independent work required

Jason is a really nice guy and very well articulated in class. He knows what he's talking about and engages the class well! He cares a lot about making sure that we really understand the prompt before writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dismissive and deflective of all punitive responsibility to the MCWP department. Plays the "good cop" when exacting punishment, acting like his actions were completely out of his own hands– no accountability. Came off as condescending on the first day, which unfortunately never changed. Do not take if you do not absolutely have to.
The professor grades so strictly. I don't know why he give me a bad grade for an assignment that is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mandatory class and I think his 50 topic is really hard compared to others I've heard about. But he's super funny and gives great feedback and is very passionate. He's a little  intimidating in class but he's actually very friendly in office hours so I'd recommend going to see him. Don't yawn with your mouth open. He's very strict about that.

Was a bit moody/snappy at times, and is quite strict. He gives good feedback, and tells you what it takes to get an A, though it means you have to always be on top of things (I wasn't). He wasn't a very fun teacher imo. Not the best MCWP professor, not the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I'm not sure if Professor Bartulis is really hard or if it's just MCWP 40. But the class is a tone of work. There are so many drafts. I've heard people complain about him but it's probably because they just didn't want to do all the work. He's actually super smart and funny but the class is not easy. He was my favorite professor freshmen year.

This writing program itself is sucked for everything, and he was very focused on FOLLOWING these criteria, even if we weren't able to learn anything. He is a tough grader, can't have a good grade unless we completely meet his expectations. He didn't do a good job of reminding us what assignments and drafts were due.

MCWP honestly sucks as a whole, the grading criteria makes it almost impossible to get an A or above. Professor isn't super organized + doesn't really remind anyone on what things are actually due even if he changes some parts of the bundle. Very strict grading, I'm still not sure why I got the score I got for the last paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class as a whole kinda sucks but that's not the Prof's fault. I ended up slacking a bit at the end and it really hurt me due to the grading of the course. Also make sure you check his slides often to keep track of hw and due dates b/c he doesn't post them on canvas super well.

Had to take MCWP 40 which is sorta lame. Tone of drafts. Not a tone of time to discuss the actual material. But that's not really his fault, just Muir. If you miss even one class, you miss a lot. He's a hard grader but he does tell you exactly what he expects. He's very brilliant and very funny. I wish he was teaching courses outside of Muir.

MCWP40 is boring itself but he does try doing his best in entertaining you. He cracks some jokes during class making it better. At times he also pushes deadlines or tries giving you less work if possible. Will def be taking again for MCWP50 if I can!

The format of MCWP is terrible generally, however, Jason tries his best to help giving advice and extremely helpful feedback. He has funny and sarcastic humor which makes up for how boring the class is. He was also able to move due dates to a later time. He is a tough grader, however he does sometimes provide leeway. Will be taking him again for 50

This was his first quarter at UCSD. The class is really lame, there are a tone of drafts. But he was great. Could be very dry and very sarcastic. He's hard and expects a lot.  He's obviously very brilliant and he cares about what he's teaching and works hard to get the best out of you.

This class has a ton of reading and homework, but that is MCWP's decision, not Jason's. He made the classes fairly fun despite the course itself being pretty annoying and boring, so I would definetly recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He respects students and is very understanding. I'm between a 3 and 4-star review. MCWP 40 is an annoying class but he does his best to make it a little better. He is very talkative and can be a little intense/indifferent at times. Can disorganized at times. He tries to minimize hw as much as possible. Gives good feedback and responses quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: He's a very talkative professor, sometimes he can go on and on with talking. Kind of bad with time management., during the classes, students wanted to fall asleep. Challenging to keep focus in the class.

New to UCSD but hes pretty great for how bad the Muir Writing program is. He is very understanding but does follow the rules pretty strictly because he is new. Good prof though. Will be taking him for MCWP 50.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: He was a fair grader who provided feedback. Would take again
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took his online asynchronous course through UCSD extended studies. Professor Barbaro was approachable, clear in his grading system, and thorough with his material content. We had weekly quizzes and one discussion post per week with due dates on Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday. The schedule each week was the same so it was easy to keep track!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very well put together course.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mr. Brett Barbaro is an excellent professor who genuinely cares about his students. I took this course online, and I appreciated that his assignments really encourage critical thinking. He allows students to create their own discussion questions, which makes the coursework much more engaging. He is a very fair grader and gives extra credit.

Very knowledgeable professor, and very caring and wants his students to succeed! He would weekly send email updates to make sure we knew what was due and the material that was being covered that week. His lectures that were uploaded had subtitles making it easy to take notes and follow along. Would take another class with him if possible!

He did a relatively good job of making difficult concepts clear and when there was confusion over the lecture slides, it could be easily understood by reading the book. Also extra credit is offered which helps augment the difficulty of the tests.

Great professor. Understanding and willing to set time aside for students if needed. Lecture and textbook heavy but the lectures are thorough on what you need to focus on. Discussion post and response every week with a quiz between 20-40 questions open book/notes. Great for people who go to school full time or work full time.
Always available for questions and teaches difficult material in a way that's easy to understand with lots of videos and examples. Awesome class!
great experience!

Very knowledgeable professor, and very caring. He did weekly emails to update us on the material and whats due. His lecture videos also came with lecture slides that had subtitles, making it easier for note taking. Theres 10 quizzes, 10 discussions, one final exam and optional extra credit assignments. Would take a class with him again if I could!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I personally appreciated the .pdf files with Brett's subtitles on them because he provides such great insight and a great deal of information on every slide. Brett Barbaro, along with others did an outstanding job in putting this course together, and it motivated me to learn and ultimately do well in the course.

Great professor, gives good feedback on discussion posts and requirements. Some test questions and answers were worded in a difficult way but he made the material easy to understand overall. I would definitely take a class of his again if needed.
Very knowledgeable professor checks in every week and is there to help you with whatever you need. I wish he taught more sciences. Def take him

Great professor. Loves to break things down. Super clear language when he speaks, meaning he explains everything and stays on topic. Lectures had clear structure making the textbook readings easy to navigate and study. 10 quizzes, 10 discussions, and 1 final. Multiple extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is the best Biochemistry proffessor you can imagine of
He was very knowledgeable and was always willing to help. I'd take his class again!
Dr. Barbaro is clearly passionate about his field and explains concepts very clearly in his lectures.
Dr. Uranga, is an excellent professor, she was always very clear and responsive with her instructions and always willing discuss any material in class.

Dr. Barbaro did a fantastic job with communication and organization. His course was fast-paced, but he had material available ahead of time and responded promptly to questions or concerns. I appreciated that the coursework overlapped with some of the work he has done in the real world. Without a doubt, I enjoyed learning more about biochemistry.

This was a well-organized course. I work full-time and the requirements around this course was very flexible for me taking it online. The professor was passionate about teaching, engaged, checked in weekly, and had accessible office hours. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Bárbaro was a good instructor. The class made an extremely complicated topic very approachable, and it was designed by him. I don't think there is a better class for the price accessibility and quality of instruction. Every thing is very, clear I recommend this professor
Lectures were great and easy to follow.
Professor Barbaro was amazing! He always provided clear feedback and there was opportunity for extra credit as well.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This course was extremely beneficial as I was able to successfully grasp the concepts of life at a molecular and atomic level. The course was intriguing and well-paced. I, along with others in the course, took this with the hopes of checking off a prerequisite for PA school and this discussion heavy course helped me on my path to a practicing PA!

Professor teaches with exceptional clarity and engagement: the concise video lectures distill complex biochemistry into digestible concepts, while  and extra-credit research tasks push students to apply theory critically. The rigor balanced support, offering timely guidance that deepens comprehension and fosters genuine enthusiasm for the material.

Professor posted lectures that he narrated which helped to understand difficult material. The weekly discussion posts were helpful in understanding new material. He was understanding and always available to answer any questions!!

I was nervous to take this class at first but this professor made the class very enjoyable. You can tell he really cares about his students doing well as the grading criteria is very straightforward and he leaves comments on every submission as to how to improve or to keep up the good work. His lectures are concise and he offers extra credit!

Great professor, you can tell he wants his students to succeed despite difficulty of the course. You can also tell he pays attention to each student as everything graded provides insightful feedback. This class does require a textbook but the lessons personally were more helpful and helped retain the information better!

You can definitely succeed in this course if you keep up with the weekly material and take advantage of the extra credit offered. The lectures are interesting and not overly long. Notes with transcripts of the lectures and powerpoints are provided. I found this course to be so enjoyable and I am no fan of chem! Easy to do while working FT. 10/10!

Dr. Barbaro was awesome! His lectures were clear and easy to understand, which is helpful for such heavy material that is covered. Just make sure you study for the quizzes a.k.a. tests every week, and you will crush this class. If he taught other classes I need, I would absolutely take him again.
Take Prof Barbaro for Biochemistry! He is super nice and understanding. He gives great lectures and the quizzes matches with lectures well. Overall, I truly recommend him for Biochemistry.

As an online biochemistry course, the structure was well paced and the course guidelines for each week are clear. Since it is a 10 week course and week 11 is the final, it is lecture heavy with weekly quizzes, discussion posts and responses. reviews.comment: Dr. Barbaro gave us illuminating lectures. Our textbook was extremely difficult and he told us what he wanted us to study. Thank heavens. He offered a lot of extra credit and dropped our lowest quiz score. No final. If anyone could get me through this class it was him. Thank you!

Brett is incredibly passionate about Biochemistry and it shows when he is teaching. It was engaging to have a professor so excited about the smallest molecules and their reactions. He also was very flexible to student needs and taught to different learning styles, video, lecture, picture, etc... Also good time management with a large amount of info

You don't have to buy any textbook or pearson for homework. The textbook is available online and the homework is embedded in canvas. The lectures are clear and the tests mimic things you see during discussion. Discussion attendance and lecture attendance are not mandatory. He is good at explaining things and pretty funny.
His lectures are straightforward and exams are very fair and similar to the review. As long as you go to lecture and do the homework youll be fine

Explained everything very clearly and homework is extra credit for the weekly quiz category. Discussions are also extra credit for the final. The midterms were pretty easy but you definitely have to put in a lot of work to do well on the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I'm like less than 1% away from the next grade and he's refuses to round my grade up. He's also rude in his reply.

The professor is a great lecturer. However, there is no cheat sheet or equation sheet on exams, and the grading can get harsh. You can get extra points on your test if you go to discussion and do the homework.

I loved the structure of this class. I recommend printing the lecture notes and following along. He's really organized, and posts all of the lecture notes, quiz solutions, exam solutions, etc. This class can be hard but he made it feel easy.
No cheat sheet. No extra credit. No curve. No thank you.
Good teacher overall, his lectures are clear and works through tons of examples. Still a difficult class but he does what he can to make it managable.

Lwk goated prof. Lectures are useful, but homework is the key to learning. Midterms were fair and reasonable. As long as you understand how to do the problems from the homework without help, the class is easy.
Exams are very hard. Run. Save yourself.

professor was nice and very funny, but lectures were sometimes unclear. i learned more by doing the homework/going over notes on my own. that being said, going to office hours helped a lot. concepts could be hard to understand but once you get it, it's pretty easy
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing prof who I would recommend for any class he teaches lectures were easy to digest and left me feeling prepared for any future classes that might require this material also very sweet and more than happy to help with any issues that may arise.
Super nice guy, I love his deadpan style of humor, he's great at using analogies to make complex math concepts easier to fully digest

All his exams are FRQ. 2 midterms and he has a grading system which allows you to drop a midterm if your final grade with the better midterm score and your final score is higher than your grade with both the midterms inputted into the gradebook. Practicing the problems from the notes and discussion is enough to be ready for the exams.
Great lecturer! Straightforward and easy to follow. Exams are easier than the homework problems, so as long as you get in the practice you'll do fine in the class.
This professor is the best. I got an A+!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Bach taught the subject well. I believe that if you really pay attention, you could pass with an easy A. Don't end up playing catch-up, as I did. The tests were fair and reflected the content covered in class. He was also pretty funny during the lectures and made the class more enjoyable.

On exams in totality, I made one very large mistake, two large mistakes, and four small mistakes, with room only to make one more small mistake to keep my A. 20E is a difficult class and it took a ton of studying to limit my mistakes to just these, but Bach is an amazing teacher, and the discussion worksheets and example/note packets saved me.

Very engaging and thorough professor. He is very detailed during lectures and explains all the parts of the problem without skipping steps. Helps students understand all the problems conceptually, too. Homework and worksheets prepare you very well for the exams and the exams are very fair and cover exactly what was reviewed in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bach's exams are not difficult, but all of them are FRQs, so be aware of procedure points. As he said, as long as you understand the examples he went over lectures, follow his suggestions for review, and check each knowledge point on the exam study guide he posed before the exam, your grade will be well.

I never spoke to the guy and never went to office hours but he is very accessible and always willing to help. He has a clear outline what is expected of you on exams. His exams are accurate to what he teaches and very fair. Overall a great dude and professor who seems to love his job.

This guy is the goat and he teaches very thoroughly and ensures the students pick up the material. My favorite part was the way he creates visualizations of the content, which helped me the most in interpreting all the material. I don't think the class in general is very difficult, but Bach grades fairly and has clear expectations on tests.

professor bach is a gem of the math department 
he is very caring about his students understanding and explains concepts thoroughly w. many examples, which made his lecture very helpful. he sets up the class with the students success in mind and has answered questions during/after lectures, would recommend!
Goated professor. Engaging lectures that made me understand the material. Tests are fair and stem from the homework and discussion worksheets.
shout out to prof. bach for making his lecture podcasts public!!! Very helpful for classes ive taken with different professors

Dr. Quang was by far the best math professor I've ever had. He gladly helped me with practice problems during his office hours for the entire quarter: 2 hours a day, 4 days a week! (Class met everyday during summer session I.) Great lecturer and gives a strong conceptual grounding of the material. He changed my perception of my ability to do math.

He was a great professor. He'll pause multiple times during lecture to ensure students understand. Exams are truly reflective of the teachings. His office hours are helpful. The class did not feel difficult because of him. Wish I could take him for 10B. Great professor!
