He genuinely cares about his students, but his humor makes lectures painful sometimes. It sometimes feels like he is trying too hard. He is good at explaining difficult concepts in easier ways to grasp.

The class grading was based entirely off you remembering a tiny detail he included in a lecture 4 weeks ago. He never told you what you should put on your lab report and graded you based off including some minute ridiculous keywords in your lab report. Rubric was based around penalizing on as many things as possible. Horrible professor & uncaring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I heard that Professor Leigh was a bad professor before I took this class, but I actually really enjoyed it. Professor Leigh wants his students to do well and provides a lot of important information in lecture, you probably just have to rewatch it to make sure you absorb/understand it all. He is funny and very clearly states what he expects

Imagine someone chronically on reddit (which is funny) and then have them teach CHEM lab to a bunch of undergrads. Class was more busy work than understanding the fundamentals imo, and grading rubrics/criteria is often unclear for lab reports. Great guy, hate the class though.

lectures were explained very poorly making me more confused about the material that i had previously learned in high school. exams were nothing like the homework questions or practice problems in the lecture slides. exam questions were poorly written, so many students were confused on what the question was asking. do not take this prof.

We had 5 lab reports and two exams, all of which were ridiculously challenging and didn't reflect lectures/labs. You needed to state absolutely everything in the lab report despite the page/word limit. He seemed like he was genuinely excited when he talked about students failing his exams. Grades do not reflect effort or competency in lab.

Excellent professor! Chem 7L is my first lab course in ucsd. To be honest, it is not easy, it is time-consuming to writer the reports. But Brian makes lectures very interesting! Funny memes, well prepared lectures, guest professors... He is very patient and accessible! Take his course!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Love this guy. Likes to joke around but knows his stuff and teaches it well. Don't mess up your lab reports, go to his office hours, and quadruple-check your calculations. Midterm was easy if you study and final is easy if you know everything CONCEPTUALLY. Don't memorize, understand. Good at getting you to learn, not memorize. Wonderwoman superfan.
Soooo vague in lab reports

I honestly have no idea why his rating is so high. Gives you a template for lab reports which helps but on the same note the labs are graded so meticulously. Not very accessible outside class and definitely not empathetic towards students, sometimes insults passive aggressively.

Professor Leigh is tough but fair. He encourages you to figure stuff out instead of having him tell you. Lab reports are decent as he gives a template providing much of the work. Just follow the guidelines in the template without overthinking it and you'll get a good grade. Final is tough though as it covers every lab in detail.

Professor Leigh is a very caring professor. His class definitely is rigorous, but that has nothing to do with him, but rather that is how the class as a whole is designed. Brian keeps lectures interesting with memes and jokes, but can come off slightly condescending towards students asking questions. I do believe he genuinely wants you to succeed.

I have never felt so unsupported by a professor. He made a lab report (which btw are graded so harshly and so tedious) the day before a final, and has made 0 accommodations for his students. Extremely condescending and expects us to know everything. I have literally had a mental breakdown over this class every day and genuinely think I will fail
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DON'T take his class EVER.

Professor Leigh is the least empathetic professor I've ever had. He refused to make any accommodations to his class after the TA strike. The lab reports are needlessly hard and tedious and graded insanely harshly. Leigh is extremely condescending and passive aggressive to his students and it seems like he does not want his class to succeed.

Grades very difficult with no clear rubric. Didn't give helpful feedback either, so I felt very discouraged. He doesn't answer emails either and was pretty hard to reach. He was also rude and sarcastic when students came for help and I sometimes just felt ridiculed. I would try to avoid if you can :/
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Leigh is overall a very good lecturer; the material he presents in class is clear and outlines the details of the labs well. However, the grading criteria and grade distribution make it difficult to do well in the class. I was often discouraged from the amount of work that had to be done outside of the class with little reward.

A huge amount of points were taken off the lab report despite working really hard to perfect it. If you want us to put every specific info on the report then stop putting word limits on it :) and stop telling us that "as long as you follow what the instruction says for every section you would get all the credit" because that is just not the case :D

Avoid. Condescending to students when they ask clarifying questions. It just feels like his heart isn't really in it. His labs are graded very harsh, and he admits in lecture that he expects students to do poorly on upcoming assignments and that they were "designed that way". I have put in a lot of time and work into this class, yet am struggling.

Lab reports were graded so harshly it was hard to succeed after spending hours and hours perfecting them. There is a midterm and a final for this lab class on paper, which is kind of odd and extra for all the constant work there is for the class. He was an okay professor, but I think the pacing was too fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Condescending, tries to be funny when he's not, and a harsh grader. I would work my ass off in lab and for my lab reports and literally get C's and one D on the reports. It's really unfair to get a non-passing grade when you go to every lab and really try on the lab reports. Definitely seems like he gets a kick out of having power over students.

Of course this class had to get standardized the quarter I take it. I tried to hard to run away from any chem class taught by stallings or schurmier but obviously I got caught up in it again. All the tests and lecture and entire class format is based on stallings'. Which is literally horrible. Tests are only multiple choice, final worth 70% ofgrade

Dr. Leigh is my favorite professor at UCSD. He genuinely cares so much for his students learning. He sets aside a lot of time to help students and is very reachable. He is very proficient in the material and tries to teach the subject in a very understandable and easy manner. I definitely recommend.

I think I would have really enjoyed this class if it wasn't standardized to every other chem class. If you find out your class is standardized, look at Schurmeier's rating to see what you're getting into. In terms of Leigh as a professor, he was pretty good. He moves a mile a minute, but he has a sense of humor, so he has that going for him.

Prof Leigh is SO MUCH FUN. Having come over from 7L he made lecture so much fun, and lectures in a very understandable manner. Discussion problems and homework isn't the EASIEST but the tests compensate by making them extremely straightforward and similar to lecture problems. If you understand the basic content, you will perform well in this class.

Professor Leigh was definitely a nice guy but this class is much harder than it needs to be. Contents are all easy but lab reports and oral quiz are so harshly graded. Went to tons of office hours and help rooms but still don't know what they expect me to write in those reports and got points knock off everywhere.

Dr. B is a very caring and accessible prof, but he makes the class more difficult and tedious than it needs to be. There is no clear grading criteria for lab reports and the final exam is difficult. It is possible to succeed in this class by working hard and completing all assignments to the best of your abilities. Overall would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Leigh's lectures are very interesting, and they are helpful to get ready for the exams. The exams themselves are very intensive, but he gives a generous curve. The lab reports are not very forgiving, so you need to write as many words as possible to hit his rubrics. The oral quizzes are hard, so taking online doesn't mean a lot easier.

awful person and professor. lectures are confusing and assignments are way too harshly graded. hes the type of professor to think his class is the only important class in the world. he's also the type of professor that literally doesn't care what issue your going through because his lab reports mean more.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor overall is a nice guy, but the strict grading and lack of preparation for tests makes it difficult for a high grade. The labs themselves are difficult, then the lab reports you have little to no guidance when meeting their expectations, so it is very easy to loose a lot of points. Tests he says you are expected to fail, but a big curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Midterm and final extremely difficult. Lab reports are graded extremely hard, but that being said Professor Leigh is a great guy and an understanding professor. The class has a big curve. Expect to spend 10-15 hours per week in this class tho, but I think its probably the same for other profs anyway.

Go to lectures and all but still do terrible on the midterms, follow exactly what they want for the lab report and the Tas that grade it are still so nitpicky and give you a low score. Almost impossible to exceed in this class. Professor himself is kind and funny but the class needs more structure for the grading scene with the TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do not ever take this class with Professor Leigh. While he is a nice person, he and his TA's are the by far the hardest graders I've ever experienced. Grading is very inconsistent and it's impossible to get a decent grade on lab reports because they find the smallest thing missing and dock a ton of points for it. Tests are very hard as well.

He is amazing in delivering the material for the most part. He is funny and really inspires students in doing chem. YOU SHOULD KNOW: The lab reports are graded by TA's, not him. So the guidelines are by the department. Accept it and try to learn from it (go to Gradescope and read every comment, submit a regrade request if you feel like it)

Professor Leigh acts like a cool guy, only for the labs to be graded harshly and the midterm and finals extremely hard. He is aware that people will get low grades on the exams, but he does curve them. Lectures are not mandatory, but he does walk through what to write on lab reports so watch the recordings when the time comes. Not my favorite prof

Professor Leigh is generally a very nice person willing to help those that ask for help, but this class was extremely difficult with him as the professor. I genuinely tried very hard to meet and exceed what was expected for lab reports, but was unable to get the grades I wanted on them. He is a great person, but not the best professor :(
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Leigh is a pretty tough professor.

This was the hardest class I've ever taken. Professor Leigh seems like a great person, he is funny and is passionate about chemistry, but I did not find him as a great professor. His grading is very specific and sometimes seems impossible. I genuinely felt like I tried my best and I still did bad on labs even afters spending DAYS on them.

Amazing professor, best Ive had in the chemistry department, and though I had him for CHEM7L during the pandemic (so online class), it doesnt make him any less proficient at what he does. He truly cares and has inspired me to do a lot more than what I initially intended at university in terms of research. Very easy to reach out to..

Professor Leigh is genuinely a great professor and shows substantial compassion for students and their progress. Being a lab class, grading criteria is tough and be prepared to work hard on assignments. However, Professor B does a great job making time and availability for extra help and supplemental instruction.

Dr.B is an amazing professor! He's very knowledgeable, funny and honest. His lab is very difficult, but if you watch the lectures and pay very close attention to what you're doing in the lab reports you'll be fine. Labs are mandatory and study for the post lab quizzes. Overall, I'd highly recommend this class even during remote learning.

Professor Leigh is one of the most caring and enthusiastic professors I've ever had. He's very passionate about teaching and cares deeply about students learning and success. This class is hard, but he provides a ton of resources and support which helps. He was always enthusiastic in OH and never made me feel dumb or silly for any questions I asked

Professor Leigh is a great person. He gave meaningful lectures in this class and the TA's were the sweetest. All of my peers had something nice to say about him. He appreciates participation and loves to hear our opinions on his lectures. Can't wait to have him again for CHEM 7L in the Spring!

He is almost impossible to reach outside of class. His TAs are the hardest graders on planet earth. I would often get 100% on the data input and 50% on the template for reasons I never really understood after looking at rubric. Good professor but that harsh grading REALLY messed up my grade
Do not take this class over zoom or with Professor Leigh. Although he knows his content this clasS was the worst experience I have had so far at UCSD due to his teaching and grading style.

Professor Leigh really seems to care about students. He tries to keep lectures entertaining even online. He's accessible outside of classrooms and is approachable during office hours. The course itself is very doable and the grade cutoffs/curves are generous.
Amazing professor! He is very understanding of the COVID situation and how it has affected us as students. Would definitely recommend.

Great overall Professor! His lectures are a mix of humor, science, and real life thoughts. I would advise you to read the lab manuals very carefully before doing the labs. Hes not an easy grader. Also, make sure to send him an email well before you need a response because he probably wont answer you within a few days. Took him for 7L

He is a really really good professor. He is the only prof I have seen at UCSD that actually has a sense of humor. He is really responsible and good at teaching. He holds lots of extra Office hour which benefits student a lot. However his final is extremely hard and he cancel midterm as well which put big proportion of grade on final. Final is horri

This is a hard class, but Leigh helps make it better. He's super funny, cares a lot about the students, and does his best to make his expectations clear. Very very caring in the time of COVID-19. Final was a group project presentation, which I didn't mind. If you pay attention to the lectures, you've got this class in the bag. Take notes!

Professor Leigh really cares about teaching you chemistry and is always very available, answering emails on holidays and weekends. This dedication is uncommon and he has a great sense of humor. Don't miss out on this chem teacher he is a true gem.

He really tries to make the lectures interesting with jokes and memes! He's also easy to talk to if you have any questions about the lab or think you were graded wrong. For online classes, his lab videos are helpful for the quizzes and reports but they are long.

Dr. Leigh really knows his stuff and is willing to help students with any problems that may arise. Lab reports are challenging (grading criteria isn't super clear) so make sure to utilize the help room and watch his help videos linked on BB. Overall a great prof. that will push you to think and inquire (fitting for a lab course!).

Lab reports are a pain because they provide you no specific rubric to help you format your writing. Prof. Leigh has a great sense of humor for putting a lot of memes on his lecture slides. I'd recommend trying taking this class with another friend that work together on lab reports to catch each other's mistake. Prof. Leigh grades very harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Leigh did a great job of adapting to an online format. Lectures were funny and informative. Discussions were CRUCIAL to passing. As long as you read the manuals, take good notes, record your data, and go to/watch lecture you'll be great! Really REALLY loved this class.

Professor Leigh makes learning such a pleasure. I personally hate chemistry, but I'm so glad I had him. He was always willing to help students and you can tell he wanted us to learn. I also appreciate how great my TA was. I took this course remotely due to the COVID-19 situation. He gives you what you need for lab reports for the most part.
All around a great guy. He will make you enjoy doing chemistry lab. He pushes you but all the resources are there for you to be successful. Fantastic freshman lab experience.

Professor Leigh is extremely clear on what he expects from our assignments and he made 5-7 help videos on YouTube that took us through the lab reports. Hes funny and you know that he likes to teach. I would recommend taking him if you ever get a chance! My favorite quote from him: Any pizza is a personal pizza if youre brave enough

If you have the chance to take him, please do. He's very inspiring and you can tell he really cares about his students. I took him for Chem 7L. I am not a chem person, but his lectures were amazing and he has a good sense of humor which made me never miss a class even though the course was podcasted and not mandatory.
The lab was pretty easy, and I did alright with all the experiments. His exams are written as though he's never been to this class, though, which isn't ideal.

Dr. Leigh was amazing. He is hilarious and tries his best to make Chem 7L both interesting and as easy as possible for his students. His sense of humor makes waking up early worth it. I would definitely take him again!

Literally the best chem prof I've ever had. He makes lecture easy to understand. It's absolutely necessary to do the suggested homework problems, but he posts videos working out the solutions which is amazing and super helpful. Doing all the homework is really the only studying you need, quizzes and tests are very fair.

Without a doubt the best chemistry professor I've had at UCSD. Dr.B is always trying his best to help his students learn chemistry and makes it fun aswell. Homework is is straight from the textbook and he posts his own solution videos which are very helpful. Homework isn't graded but quizzes are very similar to the homework.

Just do ALL the homework he gives you and really try to understand it. Go to his office hours for extra help, he's a really cool person that knows a lot about everything. Do your homework, attend class, and you will pass.
Great professor. You can tell he cares a lot about his students. Exams and quizzes have questions similar to the suggested homework problems so make sure to do them.

Brian Leigh is a great professor who truly cares for his students. He is extremely caring and makes himself incredibly accessible outside of class. He goes to the help room to help students in addition to his office hours (going to these saved my grade). Only downside is that the midterm/final was kind of confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Leigh is by far one of the most helpful professors I have had. He spoon feeds you large portion of the work for the class (esp. the lab reports). But with all that being, you still need to work hard to do well. The final was tough, but thanks to the podcasts, lab manuals and office hours, I was able to review enough to do well.

Funny professor and overall great guy. Class is podcasted and slides are posted online. He has review sessions for midterms and final. He'll tell you pretty much how to do the lab report (especially for sources of error). Midterm wasn't too bad, but the final was HARD. Still a fantastic professor, and probably my favorite professor at UCSD.

Professor Brian is really caring outside out class. Not only that, he always have science related memes on his lecture slides as well as on the midterm and final (YES, on the exam paper). He always threw in puns and jokes while lecturing and that really kept me awake for a 9:00 a.m. class. There are help videos on tritoned so you won't get a F.

Prof Leigh starts every lecture with some chemistry memes pertaining to the material of the day and throws in hilarious quips and puns to keep the class interested. He's very knowledgeable and gives in-depth examples of lab calculations on the class website. Take his class!
Prof is funny and cares about our progress. Lab reports graded by TAs. Final worth a small portion of class. Final was fair and not hard

Leigh is an amazing professor. I took his his class mostly because I didn't have other choice. However, his lectures are clear and inspiring, and he would give a lot of examples. Textbook and homework are important for you to get an A. He curves the grade. In all: not very hard, amazing demos could happen.

Professor Leigh is an amazing professor. He truly cares about his students and he makes class interesting by doing demonstrations during class and making jokes. He does not use clicker; however, we did have in class quizzes every Thursday. You definitely have to work hard if you want an A in the class but it is not impossible.

Good professor and a great lecturer. Goes through plenty of examples in class but some test questions come out of nowhere making the exams challenging. You need to be naturally talented at chemistry for an A in this class.

I only took chem just for a GE and I was hardly interested in it before I had Leigh. He doesn't bore you in lecture and he doesn't use iclickers so there wouldn't be a reason to go but his lectures are helpful when taking the class. He makes taking the exam somewhat more bearable.
He's a really funny chem teacher that has great demonstrations during class.  He explains things step by step so that it is easy to understand.  One of my best profs yet!
One of the few math professors that make me understand what he is talking about. Lectures gives a thorough understand of the concepts and exams are mostly discussed problems.
Hard to make out what he's saying during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are very clear and organized, although a bit slow. He's very knowledgable on the topic and has written a whole textbook on it.
Super solid professor. He was funny in class, and his lectures provided good intuition about the subject. Probably the easiest professor for Math 140. Definitely take his class if you see him!

Don't be intimidated by his Asian name! He has no accent at all and is a great lecturer and an awesome teacher! The 140 series is literally one of the hardest series in UCSD math major, but he taught it in a way that is much easier to understand than any other professor here. I have experienced 3 professors in the 140 series and he teaches the best
Do NOT MISS this WONDERFUL professor because of this rmp grade for him. The 2.8 is WAY TOO LOW for this good man
The course content is significantly less difficult than the simple act of understanding this man's lectures

His lecture style is not for everyone and he has trouble explaining concepts concisely sometimes. But he is very accessible outside of class and answers homework questions in office hours. His tests are also quite fair and are similar to the practice problems he gives. Overall a solid professor in my opinion.

I never watched his prerecorded lecture and rarely showed up during his office hours/actual lectures, but if you do the homework and practice midterms and attend his additional office hours before the exams, you should be fine. He gives a lot of hints on what he will put on the exams. He is a generous professor and is willing to curve for student.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's a very knowledgeable mathematician, but it doesn't make him a great professor. He always leaves out chunks of concepts and tells the students to do it themselves because "it's rather trivial". He never gives the full picture of the material, and his lectures are all over the place. Only 15 kids attend his 100 person lecture, so it shows.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Just don't take his lectures. If you could understand all the material he gives as homework, tests are easy.

He made his own homework problems but he went over the problems in class. And he helped to solve the homework in his office hour. The exams were based on in-class review and homework problems. If you understand the homework problems perfectly and study hard the in-class review, it is easy to get A.
I can get A/A+ in exams. I can do the homework without much trouble. However, I dont know what he is talking about in lectures.

He explained all the concepts fairly clearly during lectures except for occasional calculation errors. There was a lot of homework for the course and the final was not easy, but overall, he is a great professor to choose.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I first did not like his way of teaching because he sometimes doesn't give you enough details during lecture, but because he wrote his own homework, made me work for it to solve it, instead of copying from a solution from online. If you spend time to do his hw then you'll be okay on the exams. He prepared me for upper division proof base classes.

He focuses on theoretical concepts of calculus rather than only applying it for which I respect a lot. He also tries to connect Linear Algebra to Calculus, which is interesting. The boundary of exam is clearly stated, with bunch of former exam examples, which if you take will make you get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His lecture is very confusing and he writes on the board very unorganized. People gradually left the room after the beginning of the class. His final is way harder than the midterm.

Professor Chow is a zero effort professor. Skipping lectures actually helped in this class since he only confused me. He wouldn't even prepare a lecture and would simply try to teach from the Math 20C class that had the room before us. However, I got a B without learning any of math 20C so there's that
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He mumbles a lot to himself and talks to the board instead of to his students. Instead of doing specific examples he makes up problems in his head that usually confuse himself and uses a lot of theoretical explanations. His lectures always end early and he never seems prepared for class. His lectures confuse me and I feel like I haven't learned.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lots of homework and usually spend 7-8h finishing it without doing any other thing. You have no idea what he says during the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: An interesting professor who is funny at times and has exceptional handwriting. These positives are overshadowed however by the disjointed way he moves through the 20C topics, picking the topics based on how he feels, not what makes the most logical ordered sense. Homework is challenging Tips: work with your peers to understand all topics in depth.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Chow is completely lost. He began by reading what the professor before him (also 20C) wrote on the board and said something like "you all get this right? If you get this raise your hand"... then, no one would raise their hand because he hadn't even grazed that topic before... "ok perfect" and began to prove some theorem no other class was taught.

The midterms were easy to get full score, but then comes the finals and you have no idea how to do many of the problems! Overall, the lectures are useless. Just do the homework and borrow another classs notes to self study. I skipped most of the classes but attended TA office hours and it proved to be right.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Chow gives pretty clear exam range. Unlike other professors, chow focuses more on proving and understanding concepts. Hes always passionate during class. Great overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The best math teacher everrrr. His tests are so easy that are just from homework.

I find it adorable that he knows so much about pop culture and has tons of jokes on it. theres a lot of hw but math takes practice anyway. the exams are fair and we are allowed a cheat sheet. lecture is not mandatory but if you dont attend and dont read the books, its gonna be hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The final was so hard; a lot of students say that they just have no idea  what happen with the questions.

So by past finals he posted and the midterm, I expected that most of the problems would be similar to the homework and lecture problems with a few of them being extra difficult.  I'm not sure what happened this time around but the final was ridiculously difficult with only a few similar to class problems. Prof did not prepare us for final at all...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures: Often very unorganized, although informative if able to follow along. HW: (20%) Followed mainly from book, and some from lectures. Midterm: (30%) Probs followed HW mainly, some lecture. Final: (50%) Only 1/4 probs followed HW/Lecture, 3/4 DID NOT!!! Most probs overly difficult/not covered directly.  DO NOT rec prof for final alone!!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof Chow is a fine choice for MATH 109. Although he covers much more materials, his tests are very fair, and most of the problems were similar to past exams and sample problems covered in lecture. However, he often makes mistakes, so you should definitely asked whenever in doubt.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Chow is not very engaging in his lectures and tends to make everyone fall asleep. But aside from that, judging from his explanations, the guy knows his stuff down to pat. If you have any questions about pretty much anything, shoot him an email or visit his office hours to explain a question/proof. His exams and HW were easy as well.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Initially I didn't like him. However, his way of teaching grew on me as I became more adjusted. He curves extremely generously. The class itself is hard so watch out for that. He's definitely not the worst choice out there for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Ben Chow isn't a good professor by any means for math 109, he does have practice exams available but those only help so much. In class he often dwelled on very conceptual proofs which he got lost in. The class introduces a new way of thinking mathematically but Chow does a poor job of delivering these important concepts. A nice guy, but stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Chow is a pretty cool professor. He makes the material clear and understandable. Homework is mandatory but a top of 20 or less problems per assignment. There are two midterms and one final. You are allowed a page of notes for each exam with is awesome. He is corky and fun to learn Math from. I would highly recommend him.

Had him for summer session 1.  Lectures are pretty easy to follow and his handwriting is extremely clear. Midterms and finals are fair if not easy, especially if you have already had calculus AB before.  Very nice guy as well- he is always willing to answer any questions you have.  His practice midterms & final were also really helpful - use them!
He has a clear handwriting, and that's it.

I love Chow. His tests were pretty easy and he was enthusiastic in class. He makes jokes and it's easy to pay attention to him. His writing is super neat and I think his lectures were clear, though they did lack a little in material.

He's a nice guy, but truly his teaching is impossible to follow. I sat in the front, went to every lecture, and read the book before class and still found my friends and I looking at each other after each class asking "what was he talking about?" Maybe it's because he's so tight about keeping schedule that he rarely finishes a subject..
Really nice and always crack jokes during lecture. His midterms are very straightforward from homework assigned! Definitely a great teacher.
He is a nice person, but dont understand what he is teaching about, maybe too deep for me. The only thing I can do is to read textbook by my own in order to pass this class.

He is a nice guy. And that's about the only good thing i can say. His lectures often leave me lost and the online homework is a pain to say the say the least. His tests are outright ridiculous. You are expected to answer roughly 5 questions that each require at least a page worth of work in just a 50 minute period. AVOID HIS CLASS!

He is a nice guy and a pretty easy professor. Don't rely on him explaining stuff to you in class, it doesn't help and the book is trash too. The online homework can be a pain at times. Recommend a lot of self studying and if possible, attend another profs lecture.
Probably the easiest math professor I've had at UCSD. There are a lot of professors worse than him (in terms of difficulty) so if you have trouble with Prof. Chow, I suggest you study better.
Nice professor and well prepared.
Nice guy, well-prepared. Exams are more challenging now.

He has the easiest quizzes. They are always homework problems. This quarter, his exams were pretty hard. The first exam was easy. By the final, many students were having A LOT of difficulty. He is a huge fan of arbitrary variables. His questions on the final seemed a little too involved for a basic level of understanding. Be ready!!!

He's a nice guy, but is extremely unfocused and does not relate topics together. Half way through the course he began rambling and lectures rarely reflect course work. Easy midterms though so far, the class average was an A- on the first one.

Most unclear, unfocused lecturer ever. While his speech is clear and his handwriting is practically computer type, he only lectures by proofs, introduces nothing before he starts it, and can hardly communicate what the whole point of an exercise is. His midterms tend to be pretty easy, though I haven't taken the final yet. AVOID or learn from book.
Clear lecturer, makes math interesting.

His quizzes and tests are really easy--quizzes are homework problems and he basically tells you exactly what's on the test. He has really neat handwriting and he tries to crack jokes every once in a while. He's a really easy teacher!

Chow is a very nice, very neat guy. He is genuinely funny and while he can indeed be a little scatterbrained in his lectures he shows a clear approach to solving almost all types of problems in the homework. His review sessions for midterms and finals are extremely helpful. He taught us how to make pot pies.

avoid this teacher at all costs! his lectures suck and you'll leave super confused. the good things about him:his quizzes are just homework problems. if you are one of those people who can teach themselves from a book be my guest.
The only good thing about this professor is that he has very neat handwriting....

Easy. He doesn't go as indept as other 20C profs. Midterms and finals are just like the homeworks, basically--same kinds of problems. Straight foward stuff, no tricks. Homework is easy too, by the by. Refreshing way to end the 20 series, if you're not a Chem/Phys/Engineer/Math/CogSci mayjor.

i hated this class he couldnt teach without his colored chalk so he said but to me he wasnt teaching students but rather talking to the board very hard class and tests, well since i didnt learn anything... but somehow came out with a C not a C- a C

He constantly screws up his examples which only ends up confusing you and makeing you learn how to do things the wrong way. He is very unprepared for lectrures. On the bright side the midterms are not to hard although the final is difficult.

He writes clearly but that's the only part of lectures worth anything.  He's scatterbrained and not very clear about the topics he lectures about.  I guess it could be worse.  My suggestion, take 20A and 20B when everyone is on the same schedule and takes the same test.

Guy below me should change majors. Very organized notes and clear lectures, but they are entirely out of the book. Not much point in attending lecture if the textbook is good. Reasonable length on the hw assignments and the tests are very easy to do well on with studying. So-so.
This guy sucks. Do not take him EVER! Avoid him at all costs. And this is coming from a math major. He is never prepared for class and he is HORRIBLE at explaining important concepts.

Lectures are completely pointless. He doesn't have an accent, and his writing is neat and organized, but what he says is irrelevant. Just read the book and complete (and memorize) all of the assigned homework problems and you'll do fine.

not the greatest teacher ive encountered. makes mistakes on the board a lot and even though it might seem like he's using simple phrasing, he often ends up confusing both the student body and himself.  also, i emailed him several times and never received replies. don't go to lecture; go to sections.

MATLABs suck, but all 20D professors are required to use them.  Material itself is not too difficult, but I took Oasis with it.  Professor isn't that bad, i've definitely had worse.  Nice guy :) Writing is super neat.  I love his colored chalk!!

Absolutely the WORST teacher I have encountered at UCSD. He confuses himself in lecture and often makes mistakes on the board. His examples are unclear and often difficult to understand. The book itself is quite confusing and MATLAB work is time consuming. If at all possible do not get him as a prof

He is hard to follow, and his lectures were all over the map. Homework and labs are time-consuming.  Book is pretty useless.  I recommend OASIS with Dante...I think I learned it all there rather than in lecture.
just study the book. don't go to lecture or you'll be confused out of your mind, even if you already know how to do it. I had a good t.a. though. he was clearer. teacher makes mistakes a lot.

try not to take his class, extremely confusing teacher.  Never introduces what hes trying to do, just does some weird stuff on the board.  Only option to learn is out of the book, which is almost as confusing.  Plus Side: his practice midterms are almost exactly like the real midterms (40% of class)
Here is some excellent advice: Dont go to lecture and just study the homework and the text, and you will do fine!!!!!!!!

Do not take a math class with Ben Chow. It will be painful and you will want to cry in class.  He confuses himself and the class in his lectures.  The book is no help, it is almost as confusing as the teacher.

He is SOOOO confusing, but luckily if you can learn from the book it'll be ok. But then again, differential equations is rather a confusing subject.. but still. He is always late for class too, I call him the "master & commander" cause its funny to see him mess up.

I hate this guy SO MUCH.  Worst lecturer of all time, has no idea how to teach.  I seriously want to kill him.  The book (Conrad) was horrible too, almost impossible to learn from.  We ended up buying a different book to learn the stuff.  This guy is a complete moron, AVOID TAKING HIM AT ALL COSTS.

Absolutely horrible lecturer. If you can't learn out of the book, avoid at all costs. Unorganized. Will stop mid-example and do other sub-examples and get entirely off-topic trying to prove obscure points. His English is clear, but that's about the only plus. Leaves out all the helpful details.
Not hard or tricky at all

Chow was totally unprepared for the class, and didn't make much sense up on the board. His midterms were realistic (just like the practice problems). The final was EXTREMELY difficult (he grades on a curve.) He's not bad, just don't expect a great prof.

I think I learned more from the book than from Chow's lectures, which I did not go to half the time but still managed a decent grade.  His midterms are pretty simple and easy.  The final is definitely harder than the midterms.

this guy is an ****, he really doesnt care about his students.  i went to his office hours before a midterm and he was on the fone and told me to get out so he could finish his conversation... he is totatlly unprepared.. i hated him for wastin our time
Gives fair midterms and final. That's all I know considering that I didn't go to many of his lectures.

Chow has the neatest handwriting ever.  He is very clear and speaks in english, unline 99% of the math department.  I've been to a total of 4 classes this quarter and I've got over 90% on both midterms.  Tests are a cinch.  I reccomend Chow.
He's adorable and he color-codes his work on the board. His hand writing is easy to read, but he erases half of the stuff he writes. He tries to make math interesting.

His lectures were really easy to read. But the book and the material made the class impossible. I don't blame him for it though. If I want to solve a diff eq, I'll just look it up in a book. Chow always looks lost outside of class.
I liked him so much for 20B that I rearranged my schedule to take him again.  BIG MISTAKE...don't take him for 21D!  The midterms are easy but the finals are substantially harder.
Awesome guy, rather down-to-earth, very reasonable course work n such. I'd take him again if i needed to.

Good, clear speech and jealousy-inducing handwriting.  Unfortunately, it took him about 6 weeks to do an actual practice problem...he seems to have some obsession with doing proofs...but then again, which math professor isn't?
Very nice handwriting and fair exams including the finals.  His lectures can be a bit boring...but he tries to make MATH interesting. =]
GOod hand writing, lectures are helpful... and tests were pretty easy... well except the final, i thought it was hard...
Good handwriting, clear voice, manageable class.

3 lecture videos (sometimes 2, sometimes 4) per week w/ 2 mcq inside each lecture. There is also a 20 question quiz with each lecture. Discussion every Wed but you only need to go to 3 of them for full credit. No final exam, instead there are two projects, a writing assignment and a creative project. Really chill class.

took this class through uc online and it was very chill. 3 lecture videos every week with quizzes. final project was a creative/concert project and a short essay. lectures were very interesting, would recommend!
3 lectures a week which are recorded like edpuzzle (2 mcq per video), each lecture comes with 20 quiz questions. Attend 3 discussion zooms for full participation credit.

He is very intelligent and listens to music uploaded on YouTube created by him. I love his band and the Music. The course is pretty light and I would recommend taking his course if you can. Thank you Professor Borgo, music is very interesting thanks to you!
Easy class with lecture videos and four short writing assignments making up the entire grade. Great way to fulfill the fine arts GE requirement!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Class is fully remote and attendance is based on completing lecture video quizzes (2 true or false questions per lecture). Grade is ONLY based on 'attendance' and 4 writing assignments sprinkled throughout the course. This class is extremely manageable and the concepts are genuinely super interesting. He gives extra credit for attending discussion.

Took MUS20R as to complete my DEI requirement. Amazing class! Lectures were interesting and the four writing assignments that he gave were doable. TA's were also amazing! (shout out to Daniel) If I have to take a music class in the near future I would definitely take with him. Seats do fill up quick so might as well take it when available.

His lectures were very digestible and the coursework isn't demanding. Pulled content and readings that was interesting enough that it made me explore more about the topics, studies, etc. mentioned in them outside of the class. The guidelines for writing assignments are described super well--I never had to ask for any clarification about them.

Prof Borgo is a kind and intelligent guy, highly recommend him. I took MUS20 as a GE -very low maintenance and interesting. 3 in-class writing assignments (that you get the questions for in advance), 1 discussion presentation and attendance grade (easy if you go to most lectures). Went to prof. Borgo's jazz concert for credit which was super cool.

This course was entirely online, just watching previously recorded lectures of Professor Borgo. His lectures were interesting and not too long so it was very manageable, and he put real effort into them. There are lots of papers that you need to write but they are not too difficult, just time consuming and you need to pay attention to lecture.

MUS126 w Prof. Borgo was one of the easiest classes I've ever taken. This course is about the blues which is intrinsically tied with African-American history so there is a lot of color to the class. On average I spent 1-2 hours a week on the class. Super easy and interesting class. Clearly is passionate and brings on a lot of cool guests.

I took MUS126 as a GE and it was honestly one of the easiest classes I have taken. I learned a lot about the blues and professor Borgo honestly seems to passionate about what he is teaching. There is a little bit of writing assignments, but they are pretty simple. Attendance was never mandatory and the final exam was relatively simple as well.

Mediocre teacher who mostly reads copy and pasted quotes on his insipid PowerPoint presentations. Has a ridiculous participation grading policy that accounts for 25% of your total grade, so if you deal with introversion or social anxiety get ready to see your grade fall down considerably. This was one the worst classes and instructors I've ever had
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the most tedious and boring classes I have ever taken. What is this even about? Don't take this if you're not into the music. This Professor talks a lot without saying much of anything.

Easiest course I've done at UCSD. The professor delivers good lectures, covers the history and current development of Blues music, but sometimes lacks some unique personal thoughts on these topics. There are five writing assignments and two take-home midterms with loose grading criteria.

MUS 43 is the required music department seminar. It's pass or no pass - literally just a cool presentation every week. Attendance is taken but you can miss one or two if necessary. I found it to be a lot of fun! Great way to ask professionals questions and watch cool performances.

Cool guy, just had a very boring class. He pulled out a saxophone the first day but after that everything was dull and boring. Lectures felt like the same repetitive boring stuff and the TAs for it were very late grading papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Borgo's class gets boring after the first two weeks. Outside of watching music videos, Borgo goes on and on about the same two topics every week. Though the class is relatively easy (as long as you do the writings), the grading is all up to the TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Essays are 300-500. For my class, we only had one big essay and a sound recording project which requires some sort of audio editing. Other than that, there is not a lot of work to even do. I personally have only read the readings before essay(only the one big essay requires reading). Only problem: the classroom is cold and materials are boring.
100+ pages of reading in one week. Quiz includes memorization of 35 songs and their respective performers. Are you kidding me? None of my major classes are even this hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He is a great professor but his lectures could get boring at times. He definitely encourages class participation but the class would rarely talk. If you have good a TA, this class should be an easy A since they do most of the grading and lead discussions.

Great Professor who cared about getting student feedback. Assignments were doable and interesting. Reading got a little tedious but not a big deal. It was an interesting class and easy to get a good grade if you put effort in doing the assignments. He gives surprise in class assignments based on the reading. Grade also mostly depends on your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Would take again

reviews.comment: In every lecture he included something funny or interesting that related to the topic which was awesome when you're trying not to fall asleep.  Difficulties you have with the assignments and/or papers will all depend upon you TA.  They are mostly very helpful, but some are tougher graders than others. Make sure to utilize your resources!

I didn't particularly enjoy lecture as sometimes it seemed a bit tedious. However, the class was very reasonable and Professor Borgo is very caring and passionate about his field. His enthusiasm made the class nice. The class was reasonable in that he only required weekly journals which is not a stressful assignment

Way more interesting than any of the other CAT teachers. Would definitely recommend. The readings aren't bad, and the final project is actually really engaging if you pick a good topic. I thoroughly enjoyed his class.

He is a funny and quirky professor. He plays his saxophone on the first day of class, which kinda sets the tone for the rest of the quarter. Lectures can be interesting, but are not really related to the assignments, which are pretty easy for the most part. Your grade is based on your TA so hopefully you get a good one. Would definitely recommend

Required attendance in CAT 1. Lectures were boring and confusing, so many didn't pay attention. Discussions and essays had nothing to do with lecture material. Speaking of essays, he assigned several and each of them was graded quite harshly, so that getting an A would require a lot of time and effort on them.
Amazing professor.  Has a lot of passion for music, and it really shows.  Made the content really interesting and engaging.  Often asks for opinions and thoughts from the class.
You get only 4 essays the year, but they're all piled together so it's slightly hectic at times. If you like musicthe arts, this class will be fun. If you don't, good luck.

Overall I thought that David Borgo was well informed about the topic. You don''t need to read because he thoroughly goes through the book through his lectures. He gives quite easy take home quizzes and the essay topics are not bad at all.

Best professor ever! I highly recommend Professor Borgo. Out of all the CAT 1 classes, his class was the best. Just 4 moderately easy essays. No final exam. Weekly quizzes, but since they are online, they are not too hard. I did not do any of the readings and still managed to get an A. His lectures and readings are pretty interesting. Take Borgo!

BEST TEACHER EVER! started off the first day of class by playing the saxophone! He always goes over the readings in class and clarifies confusions. The TAs take attendance so make sure to go! His weekly tests are easy points and super short. The only problem that I found with his class is that the essay prompts are very vague. GREAT PROFESSOR!
Interesting class. Great guy. Just make sure you do the reading so you have material to go off of in your papers.

His class isn't the easiest music class. Weekly online quizzes that were pretty easy if you skim the readings and pick out the answers. Exams were fair (listening,short answers, short essays). Overall a really great professor that opened my ears towards Jazz.

Assigns a lot of reading, doesn't take attendance but gives weekend quizzes and gives out the quiz password on the last day before weekend, also gives "attendance quizes" which is just free points in the quiz category if you show up. Good lecturer
Amazing Professor. His lectures go beyond the slides (which he posts on TED), and he is really engaging! His assignments are also fun as well!

The assignments includes 3 1-2 paged essays and  two 5 paged essay on technology and for the final. You can relate to the course easily because it is based on how you use music and see it as an identity to yourself. Compared to the other CAT classes I heard, this is the most fun,which makes it made it easy.
Really cool guy, class is pretty easy. Lectures sort of boring. He shows lots of viedos though which makes it fun. If you get the chance take him.

If you want to do well you have to attend class, do the readings and listen to the music on DAR. Listenings are really important...be able to relate musicians and compositions with their historical context. He changed the format of tests from T/F to Blue Book short essay and listening identification. Extra credit is given freely.Great TA's!

Don't be fooled by previous ratings, this class is NOT an easy A! However, Prof. Borgo is really nice, a talented musician, and he genuinely wants his students to do well. His lectures can be somewhat confusing but it helps to outline them to get the "big picture" before the midterm and final. Good luck!

Easy class, but not a super easy A. Borgo is not the most stimulating instructor, but he's definitely a nice guy. If you go to lectures, study, and do well on the online quizzes, you can definitely get an A. The quizzes are what killed me.

The class isnt too hard,  but it's not an easy A class. He's not that great at lecturing bc you wont absorb anything from lectures. To do well on exams, you must do the hard work on your own. He also changed the test format, which consists fill in the blank, free response & essays. Weekly online quizzes are open book, but the ?s are worded tricky.

Great professor. Really wants students to do well. Mus 126 with him was one of the easiest classes I have ever taken and he made it really interesting. The final is not cumulative, and both the midterm and final are half multiple choice and half T/F. I definitely recommend him.

I took a year long of jazz history classes with him. A very upbeat & easy going professor. Tests are super easy. The essays are leniently graded. I learned & appreciate jazz a great deal now. Plus, he performs live in class!! or invites live performers which is pure joy to watch.
Did you ever think you could take an upper div final with 40% true or false? Borgo says YES YOU CAN!

Borgo was a tight cat. His tests are VERY easy, lectures are pretty chill if you just pay attention you'll do fine. Do his review sheets. Phil is an awful TA to grade though, but Borgo's performances are incredible. Overall easy class!

Eeasy easy easy. Nothing to it. Kinda wish I had taken it for a letter grade now. No need to read those longgg papers he assigns, cuz he tests mostly from lectures. The essays r graded pretty easily. He's not the most interesting prof, but lectures aren't extremely boring.
Great professor. you can tell he's really interested in what he's teaching. I feel like he deserves more respect than he gets from the class. Go to lectures and you'll do fine on exams.
Cake. If you pay attention in class and listen to the music a few hours before, the A is yours.  You can sleep through the rest.

This is an incredibly easy class if you spend a couple hours before the tests listening to the music. Borgo brings in fun musicians a couple of times during the course, and offers extra credit for going to other musical events. You don't really need to do any of the reading if you go to class. The projects are easy too.

He seemed to lack enthusiasm and knowledge of the subject, which made class uninteresting. I also could not stand his glued grin or why, on the first day of class, came with his sax and played a little ditty w/o any explanation. Overall, the class was easy as long as you did some extra credit, went to class everyday, and studied the notes.

i dont think he is a good professor. he is not good at teaching at music all....his lecture is so boring...and a ot of stiff to memerize...itz not a easy professor at all... if you just want to pass his class...then you can take his class...but itz so diff to get an a in his class.

Borgo's enthusiasm for the subject is cute, but his constant smiling can get a bit creepy. The class is easy if you go to every lecture and listen to the music samples before midterms/finals. The writing assignments are a piece of cake if you know how to regurgitate key facts from readings and lectures. Highly recommended course!

Well I lvoe African Music so the class was a blast but a huge part of that was Professor Borgo. He knows amazing musicians and we constantly had really cool performers. He responds promptly to emails and he just grins happilty throughout lecture, and its obvious he adores the subject (he even made a jazz tribue cd to South African Protest Music!)

Very fun and easy class! Exams were representative of the material and you can easily get an A in the class by either reading the material or attending the lectures. Professor enjoyed what he was teaching and brought in live performers to play for the class.
Lectures were really boring, too much powerpoint.  For a musician very monotone.  Tests were easy if you did the work, which meant a lot of reading.
Ugh. Prof Borgo knows crap about Jazz. He spent all of his time letting rude ppl in the "audience" make their comments. I learned nothing new in this class. And he plays like crap.
very knowledgable about S. African music but totally killed the class. its way too long and he is mind numbingly dull.
Borgo is awesome.  I have had him for both blues and jazz now.  The tests are easy, and the essays are graded easy.  Anyone can get an A.
Essays are easy! Exams are Easy! Music is awesome! Class goes by fast! Funny, this girl in class volunteered with a live band and sang blues FREESTYLE! Very impressive! FUN CLASS!!
One of the best classes I've ever taken at UCSD and it was easy in addition to being fun. Having live music in class, performed by local groups, was the best experience.

Borgo is a good professor and he is receptive to students needs. go talk to him and he will be nice and help you out. the tests are easy and you dont need to do the readings at all to still get an A. the essays are even easier.

Lectures are very helpful, though he goes through his slides too fast. Essays are pretty easy, but the readings are necessary for the midterms. Questions on the midterms can be very specific, but you'll pass as long as you keep up with the material.
He has a pretty limited blues knowledge, he actually seemed to pull all of his course material from a set of PBS documentaries.  He has no passion for the music whatsoever.
What a great professor!  What an awesome class!
Borgo is a cool professor.  His grading is very cool especially on his essay grading.
Great hands-on class. His explanations are very clear and he is almost always available after class. Two hours goes by too quickly.

Excellent professor with decades of meaningful experience bolstering every course concept he teaches. But, then he will assign as much ineffective, time-disrespectful busywork as he feasibly can. Dr. Chapman's lecturing quality is in direct contrast to the thought that was put into the kind of work he expects from students. Easy, but disengaging.

Dr. Chapman is amazing. His lectures are thoughtful, he is funny but also professional, and he starts every class by playing music (which is awesome). Keep up with his online textbook assignments. They will usually require you to access them more than once before the due date to complete them (which actually helps content stick). 10/10. Easy A.
Best instructor ever. TAKE HIM!

Loved Dr Chapman. Lectures are fairly informative but the real value is in Dr Chapman's professional insight. He is clearly very experienced and has an answer for everything and is not afraid to dispel false information. Endless opportunities to engage with the lectures which I appreciated. Very easy class, most points are essentially free.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Chapman is very blunt and has a dry sense of humor, which I grew to really enjoy. I learned so much in his classes. He's SO intelligent and passionate about psych.

Dr Chapman was my favorite professor during my time at UCSD, I took multiple classes with him and enjoyed learning under his guidance. Just make sure to stay organized and on top of deadlines, also class attendance is mandatory as he does class codes to input into attendance quizzes.

TAKE HIS CLASS! Professor Chapman has been the most inspirational educator that I've ever met. I loved his course and I plan to take more during my time at UCSD. Pay attention to his lectures and review the slides for his exams and you'll do well.

Dr. Chapman was my favorite professor throughout my tenure at UCSD. I took 3 courses with him and would have taken more if I could! He genuinely cares about the relevance, relatability, and understanding of his courses. You can tell he is passionate about what he does and excited about impacting the next generation of psychologists. Funny too!

Entire course is basically just Achieve work, 3 credits of psych study work, and 1 hr of reflection circle. Very easy and doesn't take up much time if you manage your time correctly. Very interesting class would recommend.
I cannot recommend Professor Chapman enough! I have taken 3 courses with him and his classes are some of my favorite classes I have ever taken.

I have taken two classes with Professor Chapman and both were fairly easily. Lots of homework on Mindtap but very easy and straightforward. No midterm and the multiple choice final is focused on vocab. The free response portion of the final exam is not too bad either.

Cannot believe he does not have a 5/5, he is simply amazing. Great lecturer, may come off cold, but honestly think this is more his professionalism. Gives very clear guidelines of what is due. You do not have to attend lectures as they are all online. Have to do Mindtap/launchpad assignments, simple project & final! i took him 3 times, TAKE HIM!!!

Professor Chapman is very knowledgeable. He used Mindtap for homework/textbook engagement. There was a textbook chapter, a learning section, and 1-2 quizzes per week. There was no midterm, only a final. I really appreciated his lecture style. He gives lots of examples, which is super helpful. The only thing I didn't love was the online format.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very easy A as long as you complete the work. Weekly online module homework (with as many attempts as you need), SONA study participation, and a two part final. As he tells you at the beginning, the course is set up for you to succeed - idk how anyone doesn't pass.

Interesting professor--as a practicing clinical psychologist, he has a lot of information about the field. However, lectures were straight from the book. Most learning was through interactive textbook--do not put these off until end! Tons of memorization. Final exam is closed notes despite being online, so be prepared to study.
The lectures relied a lot of participation, probably would have been better in an in person setting. The class was very vocab heavy.

I think many students focus on memorization rather than fully understanding the concepts, which can make the questions feel more challenging. The professor is very supportive—her office hours are especially helpful. I would take this course again; it was enjoyable and more engaging than other lab courses.

The professor's test were not reasonable. The test felt like they were made to make you fail. The lectures and homework were nothing like the exams. The TAs were often either unhelpful or were unsure of what to do.
The course was challenging, and at times the grading felt unclear due to her vague expectations!! Lectures were very difficult and did not always align closely with exams.

Get ready for very challenging exams, difficult lab reports, and two finals in the last week worth almost 50% of your grade. She is not very supportive of students without a strong molecular biology background. Homework questions are extremely hard and you lose points often. I would take this class with anyone but her.

Class is very hard and concept is not easy to follow. She expects student to know a lot of details about molecular biology. Exams are super hard and she does not care about class average and wants to challenge students. TAs are not good and helpful and they do not answer questions. They are very fake.

Wonderful prof who not only knows her stuff, but cares about you actually learning it. You get a lot of review/practice material that help solidify the content. Really doable class for anyone and she's super accessible and will help you learn the material.

the BEST bild 1 prof. SO sweet and genuinely wants her students to succeed. 3 midterms (drops lowest) and a final. tests were difficult but you're allowed a study sheet. lectures are mandatory but very engaging! pay attention in class and have a good study sheet and this class will be a breeze.

She was an amazing and concise lecturer, the course itself had lots of reading if you are not familiar with bio. Exams were exactly what to expect as she gave a very descriptive study guide and practice exam before each exams. Three midterms, lowest gets dropped, and one final. Discussions are group work for worksheets. She is very understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment:
Very enthusiastic and fairly engaging, but testing style is fairly difficult, with harder protein structure / cellular respiration topics than AP Bio imo. A lot of which of the following is *not* true questions or drawing something with unclear grading schema.

Getting an A seems very attainable given the amount of extra credit (1%) and weighting.

Her lectures are easy to follow and are podcasted so you could go back to them if you want. Lecture participation is required as she uses learning catalytics for attendance. There are three midterms and the final, lowest midterm gets dropped and final is cumulative, one study sheet for each midterm and you can do two for the final.

I really suck at tests but on MC tests she at least gives partial credit for the best wrong answer. None of her exams are worth a crazy amount of your grade. She really cares about me and wants all of her students to be successful in life. HW is a fair amount of our grade. Take this professor, trust me. I didn't even pay attention in her class.

3 midterms, lowest was dropped. Lots of opportunities for extra credit and points back on exams. Learning catalytics (like clickers) used in class, so attendance is mandatory. Discussions are optional, can do the assignments asynchronously.

Shes actually really nice but the lectures were very boring and the class overall takes up so much time.
- Uses a clicker system(not iclickers) to grade attendance and participation
- super boring lectures
- Questions on exams were always super unclear even the TAs admitted it

Prof Meaders is one of my fav profs. Take her if you can! She is so caring and really wishes for her students to succeed. There are lots of chances to boost your grade with extra credit. The grading on the midterms was very forgiving, since there is a lot of partial credit given. Homework every week, three midterms, lowest midterm is dropped.
super caring, records lectures that are super helpful because class is pretty fast paced

love her!!! my queen!! fairly difficult course and very conceptual, but she explains really well and is quite thorough. she teaches a little fast so if you comprehend a little slower it might be tough to fully grasp ideas in class (but she acknowledges this). allowed one double sided crib sheet for midterms, weekly hw but sufficient time given.

Excellent lectures motivate students to get engaged and be involved with the material, as do the TAs. It was not an easy class, but we had cheat sheets for every quiz and final, which was extremely helpful. Overall, it was a fulfilling class experience, so I would definitely recommend it!

This class has been my favorite since it combined concepts from past courses into one lab class. Given that it is a lab, attendance is mandatory. The IAs and the professor made this class fun and understandable. You are more than set if you form a tight and understanding group in lab. Meaders cares and is always willing to help.

Taking BILD 1 with Meaders was a great experience.She is a very understanding professor who actually cares about your learning and grades. There were many opportunities to learn the material inside/ outside of class, as well as opportunities to bump your grade up (ex cred). Attendance was recorded via clicker questions, but in the end helpful

Prof Meaders is so inspirational/kind, but her class is pretty difficult! Lots of studying. She provides 1 double-sided Cribb sheet on 3 exams, and 2 double-sided sheets on Final. To pass exams, you need to understand and actually APPLY knowledge, memorization won't get you far (reason why she's generous w/ cribb sheets). Go to office hours!

Not only is prof Meaders so incredibly sweet and smart, she also makes this class really easy to do good in and keeps the information interesting. I learned so much and would take her for everything if I could. There are 3 tests: best grade is worth the most, middle is worth less, and lowest is dropped. The homework is also so incredibly easy.

OMG I loved Meaders. Her lectures were very concise and she elaborated on concepts really well. Her exams are a little difficult, but if you study and understand the concepts, they aren't that bad. If you missed points, she lets you get some back through a reflection. Her grading scheme was also very generous. She slayed!!

You can go to any discussion section which was very convenient, you get basically infinite tries for homework, exams are very fair (we take 3 midterms and she drops the lowest score), and all the TAs were really helpful! Lecture is mandatory (we do learning catalytic which are helpful), but you can miss 6. Taking Dr. Meaders is a no brainer imo!!

Nicest professor ever!! She would go around labs and ask students how they are doing. Very caring, offers 1-to-1 student office hours, offers career/academic/life advice. Very clear grading criteria, assignments are grade buffers, offers ec opportunities, 3 exams (2 count, which the highest worth more %), final is a writing project (summary of labs

Prof Meaders was really good. Lectures are mandatory, tracked by a clicker equivalent, but the lectures were super helpful for the midterms. Offers extra credit and your lowest midterm (out of 3) is dropped and the next lowest is worth less than your highest midterm. She's super sweet. Homework is kinda tough, but you have unlimited attempts.

The class was fast-paced and hard to follow at times. Lectures are detailed and podcasted. Professor Meaders herself was super kind and wanted all students to succeed but tests were very hard and lecture-heavy. Weekly homework was very easy and manageable. Grading is the reason I passed, three midterms (lowest dropped)

Amazing professor! Super nice and understanding. She does go a little fast for someone who takes hand written notes. But puts lecture slides in advance so you can prepare. There are weekly chapter readings and questions. She does drop multiple assignments to make sure your life isn't too hard. Extra credit is given. Interesting lectures TAKE IT!!!

Dr.Meaders is the best professor I have had thus far at UCSD. She gives so many extra credit opportunities. Discussions aren't mandatory but you have to submit the discussion assignment if you don't go. Amazing lectures and as long as you study and attend lectures, you will do amazing. Office hours helped a lot!

One of the nicest professors at UCSD, she really cares about her students and how they are learning. You are allowed a double sided cheat sheet on each midterm and two on the final. She teaches understanding rather than memorization, which I liked a lot. Would 100% recommend, take her if you have the chance.

I do not recommend this class. I usually do really well in all my classes with regular studying (average A/A+) but this class really made me work hard. Like someone else mentioned, she requires a full understanding of the concepts because the exam questions require you to know them completely also explain your answers. She is nice but no thank you.
favorite prof at ucsd easily. extremely nice, very good teacher, and tests are entirely reflective or lectures.

Really great prof, attendance is mandatory, the textbook readings are optional. Gives tons of extra credit and has you talk through the participation questions with partners for understanding. You don't have to go to discussion, if you don't you will need to submit a worksheet. Tests are really hard at times it requires you to apply topics learned

Her lectures are easy to understand and straightforward. Exams might be difficult because they require us to think through and connect different concepts of the class. One thing good about this class is that textbook readings are optional, and she explains those concepts in class pretty well and they are way easier than I thought at first.

Dr. Meaders is supportive and caring. Her lectures combine conceptual information and examples. The questions in her lecture are to check students' understanding of the concepts. However, her tests are challenging. She requires you to understand the concepts and be able to apply these concepts to real-world's scenarios.

Professor Meaders is truly a great professor but her class, BILD 1 is the toughest class I have taken at UCSD. I took her based on RMP rating and had an extremely tough time in class. Her lectures are participation based and exams are very very different from lecture slides.

Yes she's nice. That said, the exams were a lot harder than the practice exams or other study info provided, non-STEM students beware. Her questions require DEEP understanding of the concepts she's teaching so if you think you can just cruise through the class by just reading the book and attending lectures, you have another thing coming.
one of the best professors i've ever had at this university easily.
Great Professor. Really understanding and patient. Prioritizes student learning and seeks constructive feedback. Focuses on applied learning instead of simply memorizing facts.

Meaders is one of the best professors I've ever taken. She really built up my confidence in biology. The content is usually clearly explained in class, but she also makes an effort to be available for office hours. Discussion is mandatory, but also very helpful.
Most definitely the best professor i've ever had, she truly cares about her students and gives many opportunities for extra credit!

Dr. Meaders is a blessing of a human! Shes very smart and cares deeply about her students and their learning. Tests are challenging, but she has a lot of failsafes built into her grading policy (i.e. extra credit, dropping assignments). She also asks students for their opinions and feelings about their learning experiences. Cant recommend enough!

FAVORITE TEACHER EVER. She most understanding and kind prof you will ever have. YOU NEED TO TAKE HER if you are taking BILD 1. Her remote tests were hard - not in notes and a lot of applying. The concepts are hard and you have to study. However, 50% grade is homework. and she weights the midterms based on how well you do (drops 1/3).

She is a PERFECT professor and person!!! She truly wants us to succeed, loves what she is teaching, gives us so many opportunities for extra credit for 5% after each exam and does not take into account our lowest grades in each category (such as hw and midterms). She teaches biology in an extremely interesting and simplified way, truly AMAZING.

Tests pulled directly from lectures. Specific questions, but tests were open note so you can refer to them. Lectures recorded and participation recorded through Pearson questions open until Saturday. Super accessible, responds to questions within the day. Drops one midterm, weights next highest score 18% and middle score 12%. Homework super easy
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is truly one of the sweetest most caring professors ive ever had. She cares about her students and is passionate about the subject. She provided every resource available. I felt the class itself was relatively easy- but I struggled with the exams and felt that they required some outside knowledge I didnt have yet.

Definitely one of the best professors I've ever had at UCSD. Lectures, assignments, exams, office hours, grading policy... I would say everything is basically perfect.
