I particularly love that she sends out messages to encourage and congratulate you for your performances in exams. 100% recommended.

Professor Meaders loves what she does and it is very evident in her teaching. Not only does she offer almost every source available to succeed, but she is also incredibly quick to respond to emails. She is an incredibly caring teacher and I would recommend her to anyone.

amazing professor. lots of extra credit, exams are fair. she really cares about her students. make sure you complete all of her assignments every week and stay on top of the lectures. the TAs are super helpful as well, attend their discussions for participation points and as a good resource for extra help/review stuff.

Her lectures are reflected on her exams, so it is not too difficult. She clearly explains the material and answers questions you may have. There are also extra credit opportunities after every midterm. Overall, I feel that she genuinely cares for her students and wants them to succeed.

Professor Meaders makes the material super easy to understand. She teaches it in a way that is engaging and isn't boring. Additionally, she has such a sweet vibe to her and her grading system is very forgiving. Three midterms, but you drop the lowest. Also able to add up to 5% to every midterm by post- reflection. Definitely recommend her 100%!
I had her for bild 1. She does an amazing job teaching and is very inspiring. Really easy to study for and tests are not bad. Offers a lot of extra credit. Overall 5 stars

One of the best professors I've ever met in UC San Diego. She is always cheerful, caring, respectful, and knowledgeable. If you want an easy A, her class might not be a good fit for you, because you still need to put in time and effort. But if you really want learn something, improve your skills, she's the best choice.

Dr. Meaders  BIO DEPARTMENT's GOAT Take her if you can-you won't regret it. She offers a lot of ec opportunities and I can tell that she and the IAs really care about the students. Her classes always fill up super quickly. She is very knowledgeable and accessible. JUST AMAZING.

Professor Meaders is the best professor for Biology. You will be challenged but for a good reason! Exams are really based on conceptual learning and mostly check whether you can apply your knowledge to the real world examples. Overall amazing intructional team. The good thing is there is a lot of extra credit opportunity. Definitely take this prof!

She is perfect! She really cares about students and often asks students what they think about the class. If you took AP Bio in high school, this class will be a review class for you. But if you only took bio in high school, it's all good. Her lecture makes everything clear. She has extra credit and you can get them easily.

Professor Meaders is awesome! There is clear guidleines for her class and she is very approachable. I love her! The exams are hard and require lots of studying but she is very accomodating and offers extra credit opportunties.

Professor Meaders is an absolute gem and truly cares about her students. I don't think I have ever had a professor that I loved more. This class is A LOT of work, don't get me wrong. But the take-home exams, mini-quizzes, lab notebooks, and the write-ups are leniently graded as long as you read the rubric. Overall, TAKE HER IF YOU CAN!!

Dr. Meaders is a GEM! She truly cares for all her students and always asked for feedback and suggestions to accommodate to our needs. Best biology classroom experience! There are three exams (including the finals) which I found to be very fair. She also gave extra credit after each exams if you did the exam reflection. Take her if you can!!

Professor Meaders is by far my favorite professor! She is super caring and accommodating for her students! Her lectures are very informative where she has quick questions in between to keep you engaged. There are 3 midterms, but if you study the study guide that she provides you, you will earn the grade that you studied for! I highly recommend her!

She is truly the BEST professor I've ever had at UCSD. She is extremely accommodating, understanding, and friendly. She is super caring and takes the time to get to know her students and develop meaningful connections with them. She is an amazing lecturer and engaging, which made learning intro bio very fun. Don't hesitate to take her class. 100/10

Take Dr. Meaders as many times as you can! She cares so much about her students. Her lectures are easy to understand and she offered open OH 3 days a week, as well as private scheduled OH if you need extra help, career advice, etc. If you stay on top of everything, you should get an A. Lectures were asynchronous but lab session was synchronous.

If you check Professor Meaders CV, you will find out how successful she has achieved academically. Meanwhile, she truly cares about her students and trying her best to help students. At the beginning of class, she talked about growth mindsets, women in academic and first-generation college student. A wonderful professor+human being

Would take this class again!! I gained strong foundational knowledge for future HDS courses. Lectures were lengthy and featured multiple presenters, which could be challenging to follow, but discussions were very helpful. Study based off TA slides and you will be set. Exams allow cheat sheets.

The class is mainly guests who come and lecture instead of the professor. Grading really depends on the TA. She allows a cheatsheet only on the front side. My suggestion if you take this class is to pay attention during discussions because most of the midterm questions are from the discussions, but are more in-depth.

super easy class and an amazing professor. there are weekly hws which are based on lectures. reading is given out but no one does it and honestly you don't need to finish hws and tests. hws are graded on completion not accuracy so just make sure to answer all parts of the question. dr. reese is so nice and just wants respect for guest speakers.

She mostly had guest lecturers come in to teach different lessons, which can be really interesting! There are weekly homework assignments that are graded by completion, so your grade mostly depends on the midterm and final. She is a pretty chill professor and cares about her students.

Almost ALL guest lecturers & most of the info is useless for exams as it's to see if you're interested in their topic (gets boring). only important info is on the weekly hw. Prof. also yelled at students multiple times abt respect for talking/doing something for another class during lecture, which i thought was unnecessary. readings are optional
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The course is mainly guest lectures. The midterm and final exam is free response but it's fairly easy. I highly recommend using the discussion slides to study!! Also she gives you a cheat sheet (1 side for midterm and 2 sided for the final).

HDS 1 with Professor Reese was my favorite course this quarter. She is very kind and makes lectures fun and entertaining. As long as you go to lecture and pay attention you will get an A. And you get to learn some pretty cool stuff and learn how to increase your lifespan! I would take this class again and again if I could. Take this class!

This class lives up to its reputation as the most difficult class in the major, but I've never had a class with such real life benefits. It's a research class, but with a big professional component (some classmates even got jobs). Dr. Reese cares a lot about her students and is always there as support, but you need to go to her when you need it.

Prof seems caring except that she doesn't teach because it's all guest lectures. Your grades depend heavily on your TA and they all grade differently. Unfortunately, my TA (Isabel) grades based on wording choice so I couldn't get full points in most exam questions despite addressing every part of it. Makes you feel like it's not even possible

- all guest lectures
- one homework assignment per week graded by completion, discussed during section
- midterm & final are free response but pretty easy, just study the discussion slides

osrs this class was not difficult if you put in enough effort and go to discussion section since the actual lectures didnt really matter. the worse part of the class imo is the professor because she doesnt teach her own class and is lowk passive aggressive. i also didn't like how she yelled at students in class during week 4 about respect
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not gonna lie, people aren't joking when they say this is the hardest class in HDS. It will take up a lot of your time and energy. I feel like I learned a lot in a short period of time. I went to office hours and my writing and project are a lot better. Pay attention, ask questions, be respectful. All that will go a long way in succeeding in 191.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: she doesn't even teach the class besides week 1 or 0 depending on the quarter. Homework doesn't even help because it's all graded on completion so you don't know what is right or wrong. Final is worth 42.5% of your final grade and midterm is worth 28%. She offers extra credit but doesn't it doesn't even do that much to help your grade.

If I could give this professor a 0/5 I would. Avoid this class if you can because its genuinely one of the worst UCSD classes I've ever taken. Prof has a bad attitude and doesn't teach ONLY guest lectures. Treats everyone like a kid then goes on to say "we're all adults". Class is so bad I had to write this review during Week 6 before the midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pay close attention to the syllabus and rubric, and you should be okay. This is a very high-stress class; it consumed literally all of my time and I would only recommend taking it with other easy classes so you can dedicate your time. Structured to be the hardest course within HDS, spent the whole quarter not knowing if I would pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Go to OH. Read the syllabus. There's something due every week so you can't get behind in this class but make use of the materials she provides as they will help and I can't emphasize enough to go to OH as you will get more constructive feedback then
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Every lecture except 1 was given by a guest lecturer. The content was interesting and not very conceptually difficult. There was one homework assignment per week that was graded on completion, not accuracy.

5-question weekly homework, 1 midterm (one-sided cheat sheet), 1 final (2-sided cheat sheet), content based on lecture material. Dr. Reese doesn't teach except for one lecture at the beginning. She invites guest lecturers - some of them go fast but the midterm and final are based off of the material you need for the homework

Lectures are mandatory to come to, you use iClicker to check in. Homework was a bit challenging, but it's graded based one completion and not correctness. You are allowed a handwritten cheat sheet for the midterm and final. Use the slides from the TA discussion sections for your cheat sheet!!!

This was a very interesting class. Professor Reese lectured about once, and the rest were guest lectures. There were readings for each lecture, but no one does them. The homework is just based on completion. The tests do require you to know not just the topic but actually how to apply it, so don't think you know something because it's logical.

Beware of prof Reese. She will put the spotlight on you, and depending on the status of your project, get ready for some berating. Her class structure is also not the best; you should honestly start researching for your topic week 1 or 2 and start your project earlier. Create a group chat with the class so y'all can be confused together

I'm an A student except for this class. So frustrating bc the grading for exams is all memorization based and no leeway. They dgaf if you can apply ideas on your own sadly, they want you to memorize the examples on the slides and leave no room for interpretation so why make exam questions open ended?? Clarissa is condescending too, so discouraging.

I LOVE PROF. REESE!! If you're an HDS major, you'll probably take her at least once, and she is quite lovely. Her classes are challenging but great for the first few quarters of college. Attendance matters, but her lectures are quite engaging, and often there are guest lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Reese is super caring and funny but doesn't lecture. Every class is a different subtopic within HDS so you can explore all aspects. Discussion sections really help with digesting the material and homeworks are short and relatively easy. My TA (Jose) was really quick at responding, was understanding, and overall did a great job!

Strongly recommend HDS1! Professor Reese is humorous/understanding. She only taught the 1st lecture; every other class featured guest lecturers from other fields (which was interesting too). Attendance is mandatory and discussions narrow long lectures into key points. It's easy to succeed in this class. I just wish she taught more lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: To try to express how I feel towards this professor in the few characters allowed is nowhere near enough, but to sum up the course in adjectives it was miserable, agonizing, pointless, passive aggressive, and demeaning. If I could do college all over again, I would switch majors to avoid her. Apologies to future HDS majors who have to take her.
booooooooo
Great class to take for a GE. Topics were very interesting and can be applied to a lot of other classes in whatever field you choose to go into.
this class was the perfect introduction to HDS

I took her in my fall quarter, she didn't teach, and had guest lectures. Once a week homework assignment that gets discussed in discussion section. Her midterm and final are pretty easy, some questions are confusing tho.

This professor actually does not teach a single class herself. TA Isabelle was horrible in her grading, she marked me down over a wording choice. Your entire grade is two exams with not enough time to complete and when you rush you will probably miss all the points for that question because Isabelle will nitpick and the teacher allows it.

I was excited since Dr Reese was very funny the first few days of class, however she was never teaching and had all guest lecturers. Some lectures are boring and my grade went down to a A- (93%) despite getting an A on the final. TA Isabel just repeats information and her discussions are useless. Reese seems a good prof, yet minimal interaction.

Only 2 tests that dictate your entire grade and some lectures are straight boring. They try to make themselves feel important by dedicating classes to things that they reiterated at the very beginning of the class. One of the TAs tries to be the teacher by copying her dress style and mannerisms. Grade inflation is ridiculous and you learn nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Reese doesn't even teach she just gets other lecturers to come and speak. 2 out of the 5 TA's actually care and are willing to help (Jovana & Marco). The other TA Isabel acts like she's an actual teacher and teaches like she is a PhD candidate (which she's not). Only 2 tests and the grade inflation is insane I had an A until the final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grading depends on the TA you get. Isabel is an extremely tough grader and will dock points for the smallest things. For example, I didn't specify that you needed a human brain to learn language on the midterm and was docked 5 points. Obviously, you need a human brain!!! Lots of guest lectures so I'm unsure of Dr. Reese's quality of teaching!

Dr Reese knows a lot about research and expects your knowledge to be at the same level as hers. Although she claims to respond to emails quickly, she doesn't. The best way to ensure you will get a question answered is to go to her office hours. She often sounds condescending. David (TA) is AWFUL! He offers more confusion than support

Reese is really caring but HEAVY on guest lecturers. Each lecture gives a lot of information. Attendance mandatory. Weekly homework based on lectures- graded for completion. Grades mainly made up of midterm and final. Post: lecture slides after class. Make sure to pay attention and you should be good

She herself seemed like a cool professor but I wouldn't know because this class was entirely guest lectures. Honestly a very boring class and only really learned something from discussions where the TA would reteach the subjects. Midterm/Final is free response (no MCQ). Grade depends on your TA and they all grade differently

Not very good at getting her ideas across and it's very heavy on guest lectures. Would not recommend because your grade basically depends on the TAs you get and they all seem to be doing it on different criteria.

good person and she seems to care about her student's success (in theory) but she is condescending at times and she does not teach at all. Grading depends on TA and they are very tedious on what they want you to write for exams. Kind of misleading "easy" class where students end up more confused and lost than actually learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The 191 course is objectively difficult but Dr. Reese really wants you to succeed and she cares about you and your wellbeing. My best advice is plan ahead and make sure you don't fall behind in the course busywork, course assignments, or site observation hours. If you come to class, participate, and do what is expected of you, you'll be fine

Professor Reese is very caring and wants all her students to succeed. Has guest lecturers and exams are based on lecture material and are very fair. Weekly homework assignments are also based on lectures and answers are given during sections. Would totally recommend her!

Exams are heavily based on lectures but it's nothing one can't teach themselves without a little extra studying/research. You don't really see her because it's a bunch of guest lecturers from other departments. Content is very easy and somewhat self-explanatory. You go over homework in Discussion.

Took Prof. Reese for both HDS 1 and 191 and you get to interact with her more intimately in 191. 191 was very time intensive and challenging. A lot of the "homework" is busy work. The main grading/focus is on your research project/final paper/field notebooks. Go to her OH for help! But I learned a lot from this class and Prof. Reese.

This class gave students the opportunity to hear from different experts and their knowledge on specific hds fields therefore professor Reese rarely lectured. Going to lecture or at least reviewing lecture slides is crucial for completing homework and doing well on the midterm and final. Homework is given every week but is fairly manageable.

Professor Reese is AMAZING. She is a wonderful, humorous individual. For HDS 1, each lecture was performed by a different guest speaker with different expertise. Discussions connect learned material (because lectures can be a lot of info) and exams are fairly graded. This course and Professor emphasize understanding, not memorization.

Dr. Reese is sarcastic and a little condescending. She swears by her syllabus and the setup of the class, indicating that everything is "clear". However, we get mixed messages and most students end up confused. If we show any sign of confusion or misunderstanding, she gets frustrated/annoyed pretty easily. Good professor, bad attitude.

Prof. Reese is a really nice lady. But if you're taking HDS 1, you'll probably only hear one lecture from her plus a few review sessions. I can't really say much about her teaching style specifically but she does care that you know the material and is very big on giving feedback. Grading heavily relies on your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She has guest lecturers every class, which are recorded and posted on zoom. I absolutely loved my TA and if you can't attend your discussion you can switch to another. Weekly homework that's relatively short but I always had to rewatch the lectures to get the correct answer. There are reading assignments but I don't do them and I'm doing just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's kind and makes lame jokes. This course is taught mainly by other professors so they can teach about their fields relating to HDS. Online you could choose to go to lecture or watch the recording. Discussions are mandatory, but you have the option to change your TA if you tell them ahead of time. Homework is really useful for midterm and final.

She doesn't lecture and has different experts come in for each topic to give the lectures. Grade is based only on attendance to section, hw, midterm and final which were all easy. If you pay attention during lecture and study well before your exams you're good to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Reese goes above and beyond to help the students who make the time to go to office hours. She requires all of her students to attend office hours at least once, and more people need to take advantage of her fountain of knowledge. She will challenge you and do everything in her power to help you grasp the concepts and excel in her class.
Very scary and sarcastic. Not easy going at all. Can be rude. Takes this class way to seriously.
She was fantastic! A lot of work, but you learn a lot.

Dr. Reese is a wonderful professor. She actually cares about her students. There is a method to the madness in this course, literally. Go to office hours and put effort into assignments and you'll do great.

This class is a TON of work. Dr. Reese knows her stuff & really pushes you to your limit. There are assignments due almost every class, put time into them because it'll help in the end. Dr. Reese is really helpful with feedback & guiding you in the right direction. Put in the work & when it comes time to write the final paper, you'll be set.
No Comments
No Comments
If you have previous chemistry experience (such as AP Chem) this class will easier to manage. If not try a diff prof

I enjoyed his lectures as he's very knowledgeable about chemistry. He didn't provide lecture slides, but podcasted so slides can be found there afterwards. His review material wasn't identical to test content, so you need a thorough, conceptual understanding of the science, not just the math. Prior knowledge (AP Chem for me) helps a lot.

Professor Kubiak is very knowledgeable and passionate about chemistry! It is inspiring how he incorporates facts beyond the textbook when explaining concepts. Although the lectures can be fast-paced at times, attending weekly discussions and reading the textbook beforehand make the course manageable. Special thanks to the TAs!

Not a great lecturer, so you might as well just watch the podcasts on 2x speed. The tests are also nothing like what is learned in the course, and they are 80% of your grade. He also doesn't share the lecture slides with students. The only positive was his generous curve.

This professor is the absolute worst I've ever had at UCSD. I need a lecturer who can teach and provide clear expectations; he does not meet that need. If you're looking to ruin your GPA, this is the professor for you. I spent 20+ hours a week studying to get the median score or below (Median was rouhghly 50%).

Reads off his slides super quick during lecture. Refuses to give students his slides. Exams are insanely challenging and do not match with the examples he goes over during class. Provides a cheat sheet with half of the necessary charts/information missing. Midterms averaged around a 60. DO NOT TAKE KUBIAK.

There were no slides, no practice final, and no cheat sheets, which made studying more difficult than it needed to be. The practice midterms didn't reflect the actual exams at all the actual midterms were much harder. The midterm averages were very low, which wasn't surprising. Genuinely triggered a autoimmune disease because of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but wow, this class is extremely difficult, way more difficult than it should be. No slides posted, no practice final, averages for midterms are below 60%. The actual midterms are not even remotely similar to the practice midterms. Just imagine the practice midterm but make the questions 10x harder and introduce a bunch of extra steps.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy but for a gen chem class he made it way too difficult to get by. Graded mostly on exams that are multiple choice (no cheat sheet, not even remotely similar to the practice exam). still don't have the midterm 2 grade and its finals week. Exams are so hard the averages have been around 50%. And doesn't post lecture slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor definitely understand the content, but he assumes we just finished getting our PhDs and speeds through the lecture slides. Content isn't easy, tests are incredibly difficult, averaging 60%, discussion helps a LOT though, but overall: Do not recommend unless you have to (hes a nice guy though)

Seems like a nice guy, but lectures weren't very helpful. I don't think he normally teaches this course. No notes posted on Canvas, best option was the podcasts because he speeds through slides. Tests are all multiple choice, graded really poorly, likely screwed over my grade. Don't take unless you have to.
super smart guy, very passioante about the class

He's a nice guy but his lectures are not at all engaging nor helpful, basically you self learn the entire course. Doesn't post lecture slides, speeds through content and spends more time making side comments than doing examples or explaining them clearly. Graded on 2 midterms, final, and weekly hw (achieve). I'd say avoid him if you can.

he seems very knowledgable + is a kind person, however as a professor, he doesnt rly teach + reads off the slides, doesnt post lecture slides, i thought his exam was fair game (it's a little similar to the problems in lecture) but i also had to teach myself a lot

I hate this class. Surprisingly he talks super slow but zooms through the lecture. I hate that we don't get cheat sheets or at least one midterm dropped. This class is way too hard and I have to teach myself since he doesn't post the slides. TAs just sit and flirt with each other all lecture they're lowkey careless but hey I get it

Try to avoid him if you can. During his lectures, he zooms past slides without fully explaining them. I believe this happens because he has taught the honors section of Chem 6C and other higher-level chemistry classes. He expects you to have some knowledge going into his lectures, and he does not release the lecture slides.

doesn't post lecture slides at all. lectures are just him reading off the screen. midterm 1 median score was despicable. good luck if you take him youre just gonna be learning the whole course by yourself.

He's nice but only knows how to teach 6CH. Lecture was him reading off the slides. The first midterm was bad because no one (including the professor and TAs) knew the right answers until 4 weeks after. A lot of midterm scores dropped by more than a letter grade after they got the key straight. Would be cool to talk to outside class

Really knowledgeable and fun professor! He saves time at the end for fun class problems with the TA. Class is tough, and the lectures aren't entirely based of the TB, so attendance is key. Only criticisms are that the hw covers concepts not yet covered by lecture, and there is no answer key as well. Not curved. He does interesting research too.

Main complaint: The homework for the chapter is due after we take the midterm for the chapter
Minor: No solutions posted of homework or midterms. Luckily I have grad students who have TAed this class, I was able to ask them...

Awesome lectures on his own research- chemical reduction of CO2... as an organic chemist this is high impact research.

Prof. Kubiak is very inspirational as well as resourceful, and is a great lecturer. He is good at explaining those deep concepts and interacting with students. Some advice: Things covered in class (sometimes) are not found in the textbook and theres no podcast. So do the readings & homework before going to lectures.

Kubiak is passionate about teaching and is excited about the material, which is great. His research ties closely to the subject matter so he's always ready with real world examples. MAJOR issue was that some of the stuff he taught was straight up wrong, especially with semiconductors. Just memorize what he says and regurgitate it on the tests.

A fun easy going professor.  Lectures are simple and easy to follow, uses blackboard and teaches at a nice relaxed pace.  Tests are very reasonable, study the notes and the things he tells you to study.  The class, CHEM 6CH was overall much less pressure than AH or BH.  Textbook only really used for Homework Assignments.

Really cares about his students and is clearly passionate about the material. Pretty reasonable overall. Study hard and definitely interact with him as much as possible at office hours, he definitely favors students he knows.
fantastic professor, very interesting class. If you're interested in chem, you'll love it.

Great professor. He's very approachable, cares deeply about his students' learning, and teaches the material well. The class material can get difficult, but it's interesting, and doable if you put a little elbow grease into  learning it.

I'm surprised and dismayed to see that Prof Kubiak has such low ratings. He was my favorite professor for the honors series. He's very friendly, lively, funny, and helpful. His grading is fair and straightforward (no curve). Only thing I didn't like was he taught some material not in the book, which made it hard to study for.

My favorite out of the honors series prof's. His humor is a little weird but definitely entertaining. Respects the students' intellect, teaches interesting aspects of chemistry. Grading is fair: homework 100pts, 3xmiderms 100pts each, final 200 pts, drops a midterm or half final.
horribly bad teacher

If you're the type of person who can't pick up on material within the first time it's mentioned (which accounts for most people), don't take his class. 3 midterms, 100 points each, and 1 final. Test questions greatly reflect his lecture material, so if you take his class, GO TO LECTURE AND TAKE NOTES. If you love your GPA, don't take him.

He is a typical nerd type teacher. Makes weird jokes and laughs by his jokes. His lectures are hard to understand but the exams are basically on his lecture notes and study guide he makes. If you know somebody who took his class, ask them for past exams. It helps you a lot.

This professor cannot teach. His lectures or study guides are random and does not really help out with the midterms. The book does not really help either. The midterms are not that difficult but it is very random. He does not really help you that much either.

Horrible professor for 6c. Does not explain the course material at all, flies through what he explains. Makes learning incredibly difficult. Not conducive to note-taking. Exams are random and hard to predict. The only plus is that he's relatively funny. If possible take another professor for Chem 6c, then you'll actually be able to learn something.
3 midterms. 20 questions. all multiple choice so no partial credit. miterm questions are hard to predict and confusing at times. funny professor though. homework is recommended.
No comment
He's the department chair. How easy can he get? There is no curve or extremely small curve. MOstly Multiple choice on exams.
Favorite Chem 6 professor! Extremely helpful, and the tests were strait forward. Do the study guides, they are very representative. His office hours are great, really cares about teaching!
No Comments

I was nervous about this class, but it ended up being easy. You gotta put in effort because there is a lot of content but as long as you keep up, you'll be fine. rewatching lectures and reviewing slides will help you with tests because it's all from lecture but the textbook can help if you're having a hard time understanding things. Great class!

Professor Walker is great. Her class was easy. 2 midterms and a final that is cumulative. If you do better on a midterm section of the final, she replaces your midterm grade. She was extremely clear and only tested on things from her slides. People complaining are likely the problem themselves. I was taking 4 classes and hers was a breeze.
Professor walker was not clear about wha we needed to know for tests and they were not well explained

Professor Walker is one of the best professors I've had. Her lectures are really good and her slides are helpful if you actually listen and take your own notes. Her exams are fair and based on lecture. I definitely recommend her, just know it's an upper division class so it will be reasonably challenging. (PS. best way to study is to watch record..

Her exams are way too difficult and content dense for the material she covers in lecture as it is directly lecture related yet she does not put enough information on her slides. Exams make up most of the grade with other assignments not making a dent in your grade. Avoid unless you want a GPA tank for a course that should be easy not this difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved Dr Walker! Engaging lectures and she clearly cares about her students. Lots of helpful TA's/UGIA's, and multiple extra credit opportunities. 2 midterms, the final was cumulative but tests were only from lecture, not the textbook at all. Really enjoyed the subject matter :)

Professor Walker is such a great lecturer and is very understanding! Attendance wasn't mandatory since she does podcast, but she does do participation questions for lectures which are due at the end of the week. Overall, her course wasn't difficult, midterms are multiple choice, would definitely take her again!

Whoever said she's hard or this class is hard is genuinely tripping. She's the best and the class was incredibly easy so long as you went to lectures, which I did because she is funny and engaging. Since I went to lectures the exams were straightforward and easy. Great class, great prof.
Emailed her and never emailed me back. When she did it was a rude response.

Caren is an amazing lecturer, as well as an attentive listener to ideas and questions during office hours. Tests are exceptionally easy and anyone can score high on the exams if they attend and pay attention in lecture. I barely supplemented with the readings- she tells you everything you need to know. Generous extra credit. Easiest A+ ever

This was my favorite class this year...maybe ever. Professor Walker's lectures are super engaging and makes you feel like she is in conversation with you. She is really funny and open. The exams can be hard, but they are fair, and she gives credit back when too many students get a question incorrect. If you pay attention in class, you'll be fine!

One of my favorite professors so far at UCSD. Great lecturer who cares about keeping her students engaged and involved with the material. Super organized Canvas, manageable workload, exams are based off slides which are also well organized. Exams are usually curved a few points, SONA is extra credit. Podcasts lectures too. Highly recommended!

I really like the way she teaches. If you pay attention and make sure you somewhat understand the material and experiments the youre totally fine. She is super sweet and accessable and makes class really fun.

I really enjoyed taking Psych 101 with Professor Walker. She helps you understand the material by using lots of examples, most are videos of studies done on babies which are adorable. She does have a textbook, but she has said no questions on the midterms will be based on the textbook. The workload wasn't too bad I highly recommend it.

I loved her. Exams are difficult, BUT! The questions are focused on the slides and the little details she adds while going over them, so if you pay attention to literally every word she says, you'll do just fine. And listening to her is fun, she's got the sweetest energy. Also tons of extra points.
The best professor I've ever had in my life! So caring and understanding; she is truly amazing. Pay attention to her lectures and take notes during her podcasts and you'll be set!

Great Prof, not the greatest class! Don't expect fast email responses from her/TA's (Almost 2 weeks in my case)! Easy assignments. Good EC. Exams could have been easier if we were given less complex questions that did not have double negatives. However, tests was curved! Overall, class is def doable, just be prepared for low quality exam questions!
A sweet person who gives hard and sometimes bad exam questions. Be PREPARED if you take her.

amazing prof. lecture attendance not mandatory, theres a participation q but its in the podcast. I loved going to lectures, super engaging, amazing prof. Would take again 100%. super knowledgable and passionate, very nice outside of class too.
Another stupid lecturer. She gives extra credit and participation points but in an inconsistent manner. Nothing inspirational matters or learned from her lectures.

Surprised she has a 5. tests are heavily reliant on the application of what we have learned.  you have to know not what the experiment is, but what is does and the effects. "make sure you come to lecture, that's how you get a good grade,"not true. BEWARE, go with someone else if you can! Most of the grade is the tests. She's nice, but hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very interesting class and sweet teacher! mini essays and participation points are easy, exams are quite tough you will have to pay attention to the small details, and take detailed notes to understand material. Take this class if you are interested in it and are going to putting in effort and work. (do not recommend for those that want an easy A)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Walker is caring & pushes students to learn material, as her exams are difficult, but fair. Go to lecture & pay attention, she leaves clues on what to focus on. Very receptive to feedback & can tell she wants everyone to succeed & be excited about the material. Tons of cute baby vids & chances to earn padding points to the 2 midterms & 1 final

my class was fully online so can't speak for in-person. Test Qs were ambiguous, difficult, and heavily based on lecture; very tricky. LOTS of textbook reading. Overall, class required a lot of effort but she ended up curving exams. Pay very close attention to lectures- some test questions from things she said in passing or other student questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's such a caring human being! She's one of those professors who definitely puts her heart and soul into teaching and even though I never spoke personally, I can see how much she cares about her students. Two midterms, a final, and three short reading responses. She also takes attendance randomly so don't skip. Lectures are super interesting.

This was honestly the best course I have taken at UCSD. The class is based on discussion of articles and I learned so much this way - even though it was super challenging. She gets to know all of her students, and lets you pick your final project topic. Wish I could take the class again!
Professor Walker clearly cares about her students. I am definitely going to take more classes with her.

This was the best class I have taken at UCSD, and it was my first Psychology course. Dr. Walker inspired me to seek out additional courses in the department - and I am even considering making it my major. I loved this class.

She's considerate and concerned about her students' grades. She's pretty helpful during office hours and always show cute baby videos during class to explain concepts. It's also helpful that she allows 3 mins of break for an hour class so that we can relax a bit. There are 2 midterms and 1 cumulative final, they are all multiple choice.

She's a fantastic lecturer and makes it fun to come to class even though she podcasts and attendance isn't mandatory. Study her slides and read to do well, but the class is easy if you give a little effort. Offers extra credit for CAPE eval and participating in psych studies

Professor Walker is such a sweetheart. Her tests are pretty difficult; you cant just look for key words or else youll end up missing concept question. Did poorly on the first two midterms because of that. She really cares about students grades and is willing to go over any confusing concepts individually. Reading definitely helps you ace tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Walker is super nice and a very good lecturer. She makes the topics more interesting with video examples, and explains everything really well. She does talk a bit fast, so her class isn't conducive to heavy note-taking, but she gives you lecture slides you you don't really have to take extensive notes. Take her!

Dr. Walker has interesting lectures and is always available if you have questions. She also podcasts so you can review the lectures which is great. The class itself is pretty standard, grades based on 2 midterms and a final plus some extra credit options. Tests are neither hard nor easy, all multiple choice questions. I would recommend this class

Professor Chapman is one of the best professors I have had here at UCSD. Her lectures were engaging and well planned. I also had some issues come up in my personal life, and she gave me a one week extension on the final. It is clear she really cares about her students!

Took her class online over the summer. 4 very easy quizzes and a couple of discussions per week, which are graded on completion. She gives out extra credit, which can boost your grade by up to 10%. There's a final paper at the end of class, which is also graded on completion. An easy class that fills the DEI requirement. Grades were given out late.
Really enjoyed professor Chapman's CRT class, she was very insightful and explained content well! I recommend her to anyone!

She was so great! I really enjoyed her. She was so powerful in the way that she carried herself, and her style of teaching was really a conversation with her students. The assignments were really reflective and made us challenge our current views on urban education. She's super approachable as well and is so funny!
Long PAs and zybook readings, but other than that quizzes and exams are pretty straight forward.

Good prof who knows the content. PAs are most of your grade and can take a long time, but they do help you learn the data structures. 3 quizzes with redos, a midterm, and a final. Lots of previous tests to study with. Only scary part is needing above 55% for the coding portion of the final. If you study well, it is a breeze. Mandatory attendance

Cao is a great teacher. His lectures were very easy to follow, and you can tell he cares about his students learning. Practice exams were very similar to real tests. The class teaches you a lot, and is very fair.

Good prof, good notes/lectures. But the class has a 55% requirement on the coding portion of the final to pass or else its an auto-fail, so be super careful of that. Prepare to invest time since the weekly hw projects are long.

Definitely knows what he's doing. He lectures from a note outline, which he fills out during the lectures, which honestly isn't my cup of tea, but it's alright. Attendance is graded, but two weeks of attendance are dropped, so there's room for error. He provides past midterms, finals, and quizzes, which are really useful for study and practice.
Good teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Definition of average teacher. Lectures feel random sometimes. Programming HW is painful, taking 6+ hours weekly, literally left me with sore fingers. Small accent and monotone speaker. Requires iClicker participation (~$25) Literally made me reconsider CS and life as a whole multiple times. Tests are fair but don't take with another hard class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: He's a fair professor, but not ideal for beginners. Lectures cover the basics, but assignments go much deeper. Tests are fair, and practice exams are helpful and similar to the real ones. Programming assignments are fun but time-consuming, so don't procrastinate. He does a lot of iClicker practice problems during lectures so attending is important!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Solid prof for this class. It's a pretty foundational class for CSE and he did a great job sort of orienting his students. Lectures were helpful, with clicker questions to check your understanding, weekly quizzes so you can be kept up to speed with the content of the class, and fair PAs. Good. (Though I do believe he is better for CSE 12 than 30)

Professor Cao made a somewhat boring subject, interesting. He clearly was knowledgeable in the subject and cared about the class. The PAs for CSE11 are long and tedious towards the end so definitely start ahead of time, but for exams, Cao gives ample studying material.

Cao is solid, he knows what he's talking about and will answer questions in and outside the class. took this class with just AP comp sci principles knowledge and felt like most people were way ahead of me but was able to catch up! don't be afraid of imposter syndrome and if you do bad in the midterm, it can be replaced by a portion of the final

The class itself is hard but that's to be expected for programming. With respect to the professor, do NOT take this professor if you have sound sensitivity issues. He constantly sucks on mints (?) and clicks his mouth, it even comes through in the podcasts. As someone with auditory sensory issues, I left every class feeling like I wanted to cry.
His courses often at 8 am. There is no way I can get participation point:(

Very clear and pretty fair professor. I am not very good at coding, but I learned a lot in this class. His lectures are very good and he makes note-taking very easy. PAs can be long and tests/quizzes can be kind of hard, but you basically have a second try at everything in the class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures are a little dull and not recorded, but extremely helpful. The readings he assigns aren't that helpful, more like busy work. The class is more homework focused than test focused. Very accessible office hours/tutor hours and overall a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
The best way to describe Paul is fair. 

He does nothing too exciting or special, but he does his job well in trying his best to explain harder concepts clearly through repetition and answering questions. He also always gives second chances in class to do better.

Expect an average Asian dad teaching and you won't be surprised.

In general CSE 30 is a terrible class and it wasn't helpful that the class is extremely test heavy, but Cao made most of the topics digestible. The class itself is extremely challenging, but Cao was patient and went over most topics multiple times when students were confused. I would recommend him for the class.

DO NOT TAKE if you need to fulfill your graduation req. Lectures do not prepare you at all for the exams or PAs which are the most important part of your grade. If you have no background to programming, this class & prof are not for you. Save time & money and sign up for something like COGS 18 or CSS 1. He also does not care if you fail or not.

Cao is a really good professor. His tests were very fair (they were all MCQ). His lectures are good, covering the basics but you need to read the textbook and do some research on your own so you can complete the PAs. The PAs varied in difficulty based on the topic they were covering. Come in with previous coding experience it definitely helps.

Fun professor. Lectures are helpful and mandatory with iClickers. Programming assignments were easy and dealt with subjects relating to lectures. Midterm and Final were easy, Final lets you make up your midterm grade. Quizzes are surprisingly hard, but if you study you should be ok.

Honestly I thought he was really good, his lectures are mandatory but the PAs are very reasonable, always relevant to what we're learning in class. We get a lot of opportunities to make up for bad scores, and you really learn a lot from him.

He was good for a CS professor. Attendance is mandatory, using the iClickers, but the questions during class were actually helpful. The PAs were super boring and sometimes confusing, but relevant to what we learned. He gives opportunity to fix your PAs for credit back, make-up quizzes, and make-up for the midterm. Basically, you get second chances.
The course was challenging and the quizzes were mostly trick questions. A lot of reading set for every lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Cao gives very light lectures and then gives EXTREMELY difficult assignments. Prepare to spend the entire week dedicated to this class and no other class. You will spend most of your time with tutors if you take Paul Cao. If you are taking any other difficult course, expect to see your grades drop from the time commitment in this course.

While his lectures are clear, they have nothing to do with the assignments. He teaches you to do the most basic code for a section and then makes the assignments as hard as humanly possible. Like yeah sure you explained how to set up a for loop in class but not how to implement it in anything practical like you asked for in the assignment
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Take good notes, the professor sometimes would go fast during lectures. PAs some of them are hard but some are easy so go to tutoring early because the queue can get really long. There is a quiz with each PA and if you don't pass the final with a 55% or more you automatically fail the class so really take good notes.

If you listen and make notes while his lectures, you're sorted for the Quizzes and PAs.
His PA's are kind of long and is one of those professors who like to mess with your grade by not dropping scores, and taking averages of a test and its make-up.

Don't take this class. Currently we are remote, and UCSD uses the quarter system. He goes too fast through the materials and you have to go to tutoring hours to get help. The tutors are terrible at explaining and make you feel stupid. They don't understand that coding is hard and not everyone can grasp it immediately. Save yourself the stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: she is not a bad prof, just expects wayyy too much. has lectures for you to watch before you go into class ontop of readings. attendance isnt taken but you will need to particpate in class for points. so many moving parts in this class, i suggest taking this while you have some other easy class so you wont be too stressed.

I would avoid this teacher at all cost, if you're taking this course for credit sorry to break it to you but she's the only one that teaches this class. No room to breath you have a quiz everyday starting the second week. In class essays after ai essays were caught, no notes either. Required debate and participation matters.

This is the most unnecessarily challenging management class I've taken. Two quizzes a week requiring scantrons, pre-recorded lectures to watch before class, in-person essays, mandatory debates, a no-technology policy (everything handwritten), and lectures that always run late. If it's not a major requirement, avoid this class at all costs.

Tons of work and quizzes which make the class annoying if you have other difficult classes. If you're like me and just looking to pass the class you're fine. She has lots of lectures to watch before class but I didn't watch them or study and I was good. The curve she offers is huge, over a whole letter grade. Just put in effort and you'll be good.

This class could be so much fun but she literally makes it so hard for no reason. Easy subjects, wildly confusing test questions and you will never receive a perfect grade on the essays. Everyone I have asked taking this class hates the professor because she gives quizzes every single day. She canceled class for a week and made us suffer bc of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Boring lectures, even worse understanding of business. In fact in my review her suggestion could hurt the business in the example. Some assignments shouldnt be timed but are. Quiz every week. Essays are hard to get good grades on, and the content can make it harder to get good grades on. Participation mandatory and hard to score if introvert.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great Professor, best professor Ive had so far. He really tries to connect with his students in order to make the environment more welcoming and accessible. Grading was very fair. I will say, discussion sections are not mandatory, but definitely recommended in order to be ahead/caught up.

He's not a hard professor, it's just that ochem itself is hard. He's pretty funny and tries to bond with us using gen-z slang and really does try to get to know as many students as he can through lecture participation and midterm/final reviews. He really makes the effort to know your name and to guide you to the right answer with no judgment.

Loved this class much more than general chemistry, and I believe the professor played a key role in that. Exams were fair and straight to the point, and the problems sets were extremely helpful for studying to exams. Offers extra credit, and overall one of the best professors in this university. Thx a bunch - Stefan

really amazing professor. exams were all fair and the lectures were engaging. i found the textbook provided easy enough to follow along. i went to his review sessions every exam and found them really helpful and detailed. he's clearly passionate about teaching and his students. would love to take any of his classes

Midterms were simpler than textbook practice problems while the final was a bit harder but fair and only on lecture content. Problem sets are quite difficult though so make sure you go to office hours. TA's were super helpful!

Provides an amazing introduction to ochem. Lecture pace is good and he encourages student engagement. He provides extra resources for practice questions on difficult units or review material for older chemistry concepts. He makes an effort to learn peoples names which is very uncommon at this school, especially in classes of 200+ people.

The course was fast paced however, the professor was very clear with conveying the course content and material. Exams were reflective of the slides in lecture. Prof also gave ample extra credit and took the class to UCSD basketball events for bonding.

I was worried about taking organic chemistry but Cohen made the class very manageable! The tests were reflective of the homework and felt very fair. I also appreciate the effort he puts to get know people in the class.

Cohen is the goat, no doubt. His interest in organic chem turned a supposedly scary class into one of my favorite and interesting classes I ever had. His TAs were the best ever, and discussions were the most productive classes ever. I liked how he remembered kid's names and handed out gifts. His tests are fair and only cover material from lecture
Seth Cohen is one of the best professors at UCSD I have had so far. Great lecturer, wants you to succeed in the class, and you can tell he is passionate about the subject.

I was really scared for this class but Professor Cohen made it really manageable. He genuinely makes an effort to learn names in a lecture hall of 300 students, which is really impressive. His review sessions were incredibly helpful and the grading criteria was very straightforward. He's passionate about chemistry and teaching and it comes through.

His lectures are engaging and straightforward (although sometimes being kinda slow at the beginning and rushing thru the end). He calls on students during class and remembers our names. His TAs are also amazing. They are just so passionate about chemistry. Prof Cohen made me wanna change my major into chem

He is very knowledgeable and brings unique real-world experience. What truly sets him apart is how much he cares about students beyond academics, like sharing networking resources, career advice, and genuine mentorship. He's also fun and approachable, often sharing movies and places to explore in the new city with the class.

Professor Cohen was a good professor and lecturer. The exams were a little long but fair. Discussion section is not mandatory but definitely recommend to attend. Also, going to office hours and his review sessions were very helpful. O-chem is hard regardless of the professor, you just have to put in the work and you will be fine.

Professor Cohen is truly the best professor I have had at UCSD. It is clear how passionate he is about Chemistry, and his teaching style reflects that. His lectures are engaging, and he allows many opportunities for participation throughout the course. His exams are fair, and if you go to lectures and follow his advice, you will do well!

Prof Cohen genuinely cares about his students & puts in the time/effort to make Ochem click. Its a hard subject (you're gonna have to accept that) but he makes it manageable and even kinda fun. I used to hate chemistry, but he really did change my perspective. Plus he puts consistent effort towards learning everyone's names, which is really sweet!

One of the greatest professors I've had so far. Very passionate about the subject and makes an effort to get to know his students. He shares a lot of analogies and uses his molecular model kit to simplify hard concepts which helps a lot. He also holds exam review sessions that are helpful and exams are pretty reflective of problem sets.

Prof Cohen is an amazing lecturer and genuinely made one of the hardest subjects easy to understand. Super approachable and really cares about his students. Exams were all FRQ w/ no crib sheets which was tough, but I believe it was for the better bc it forced me to actually learn the material. 80% of your grade is 2 midterms and a final, though

Professor Cohen is a committed and caring professor! Of course, Ochem is tough, but he really puts in the effort to explain concepts clearly and the tests were very much reflective of what he teaches. He was out of town for one day and a different Ochem professor subbed in for him, and I realized that compared to other profs, he's much better.

BEST PROFESSOR FOR CHEM40A! Prof. Cohen truly cares about his students and he delivers his lectures in a clear and engaging way. He willingly re-explains concepts when asked. Practice problems done in class, office hours, and review sessions really help for the exams. Exams fairly assess the knowledge gained from the course. Highly recommend!!

He's one of my favorite professors I've taken here at UCSD. There are 15-point graded problem sets every week (half of the problems are graded for completion and half graded for correctness) which reflect the midterms and final very well and they're good practice. He's funny and keeps the audience engaged and overall a great lecturer

Excellent professor with good lectures and plenty of extra material, but it heavily depends on how much effort you put in. If you are just taking the course for credits, the lectures and homework is not enough to prepare you for the exams. If you utilize the extra material and speak to him, he's very approachable and you'll learn a lot more.

Takes the time to know students + make them laugh; homework is very representative of the tests; homework is digestible, weekly, and not overwhelming; multiple review sessions + office hours a week (both himself and TAs); uses free textbook PDF + not mandatory; clearly communicates

overall chill dude + extra points for bringing dog to the final.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great teacher, covers all the material well, very funny. As long as you put in the effort you'll get an A.

midterms based on lectures, accesible outside of class, and in all honesty really cares for his students success. he also tries to get to know you by reserving seats in basketball games. very friendly and he also tries to learn gen z slang and use it at least once a week during lectures which makes many of us laugh.

These reviews don't do him justice. He's a very lively and funny professor who always brings snacks and prizes to students who answer his questions in class! He's very good at teaching and always gives demos in class. His tests are kind of hard, but if you study and practice the material and textbook questions, you'll be fine.

Professor Cohen had pretty bad reviews on here so I was nervous going into the class, but these reviews were  from a misunderstanding and glitch in the grade system. He is a really caring professor and the first one I met that actually went out of his way to learn our names, invite us to go to basketball games with him so he could get to know us.

Great teacher, engaged with students, actually taught the material and explained why concepts were important. Included relevant examples to the content and prepared students for the test. Genuinely demonstrated passion for teaching chemistry and offered as much as help as possible. Would take a course with this professor in a heartbeat.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Cohen was the best Ochem teacher I have taken. Tests were very fair and reflected what we did in class and the problem sets. He was also a very chill and nice professor. I definitely recommend for chem40A.

Good lecturer, mentions real life applications of everything which makes the class interesting, gets to know students, nothing on the test should come as a surprise. However, did not curve his class whatsoever which is pretty standard for a class like ochem, esp. when many people got their final graded wrong with no test correction petitions.

Free textbook, optional mediocre lectures, tests are easy because nobody understands the content.

He makes an effort to learn the names of students who go to class, but it seems that if he doesn't know you, he has certain presumptions about you (lazy, unmotivated, more likely to cheat, etc). If you need accommodations, make sure to befriend him.
I was tentative as well but he is very kind, tries to connect with his students, and is very helpful. his exams are not too tough either, and are very representative of the things taught in class
I had Cohen for 40A, ochem for life sciences, and honestly thought he was pretty good. Lectures were organized and he answers questions quickly and is available a lot outside of class.

He must've changed as a prof since 2018 because he has been a great lecturer and very friendly. He even reserved sections for a couple of the UCSD basketball games to get to know his students more. Grading for tests is tough but w/ enough studying you can do well. 50% of the points for each hw was graded only on completion, the rest on accuracy.

Was scared to take his class because of such negative reviews but he is not bad at all! Very good lecturer, he makes the class interesting from a bio perspective.  Homework and exams are extremely similar. Fair grader, just practice a lot. Overall, he is a strict old school professor who is kind and wants his students to succeed
Im still in his class but he doesn't teach us anything and misses so many things. Terrible, should not teach OCHEM anymore

Chem7L was one of the hardest classes I've taken at UCSD because of the workload and specificity of the lab reports. Although his lab reports were tough (such inconsistent grading!), his exams were very straightforward and easy (multiple choice). Go to the chem help room/ TA office hours if you want a decent grade on lab reports for sure.

He seemed like a fair and cool guy through most of the course, but the grading was a mess. The TAs were very inconsistent in their grading (some were very strict and others were very lax), and he curved the class down two weeks after the final grades were posted. Its very disappointing to think you got an A- and have it turned into a B :/
Awful to change curve after grades final
Decent professor. He tells you exactly what is needed on his lab templates. I thought he was clear on what he wanted from the class, and his grading was fine for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He seemed like a fair teacher initially. But then, no proper communication or guidelines, and on top of that had no grade adjustments or curve factored into the class. Being a Chemistry course, you wouldn't except a professor to grade that strictly. Furthermore, he dropped all grades by 1/2 a week AFTER grades were finalized and posted to academics

By lowering all students' grades 2 weeks after grades were finalized, he jeopardized the futures of students who thought they passed 7L, took a class where 7L was a prereq, and now had to drop the class at the end of week 1 because they failed 7L. Now they can't enroll in 7L for this quarter, lost the class they took this quarter, and are set back.

Terrible professor. Absolutely would not recommend unless you want to feel completely undervalued as a student and go on an emotional roller coaster of not even having an idea of what grade to expect. He hints in lectures that he will end up curving the grades then decides to curve it so that we all do worse THREE WEEKS AFTER THE COURSE ENDED.
Arbitrary grading of labs, asked TAs to regrade multiple times because the average on the labs was too high, changed the grades 3 weeks after they were submitted.
First professor who curve down the entire class in my life, and that was after three weeks when the grade is posted. ��
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Cohen has no regard for his students and their grades. He changed our grades more than 10 days after uploading them and lowered them ! It hurt everybodys GPA and set back many by an entire quarter! His TAs are wildly inconsistent with grading and its always a guessing game. Ive never seen such a brash lack of concern for students. disgusting !!!

He never really specified what was required to actually get a good grade and on top of that he lowered everyone's grade by a 1/3 of a letter grade three weeks after the grades were submitted. This was a betrayal of the students' trust.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Seth Cohen is a terrible professor. He went against the University's policy and changed final grades three weeks after they were posted. There was no rubric posted for the course, or any of the labs. Every lab was graded meticulously, many TA's had discrepancies in their grading, we lost points over the smallest things, and he did not curve at all.

Awful teacher. Absolutely doesn't care about the students. Rude and disrespectful, when I asked him for a makeup on a quiz I missed because I had surgery, he said there was nothing I could do and that I would get a 0.

Extremely unclear about instruction throughout the quarter, expectations are vague, the lab reports are graded meticulously and you get docked points for the smallest things. TAs are inconsistent with their help and grading. No curve whatsoever, 93.9 is an A- thats FINAL. Oh wait, but 3 weeks after finals grades are posted, he drops all grades.

Seth Cohen is a nice guy. Seth Cohen is a decent lecturer. Seth Cohen is NOT A GOOD PROFESSOR. Professor's give students a detailed list of expectations and make demands transparent. This "professor" failed to post any sort of rubric for labs and then ravaged every report. Would not recommend if you're looking for a reasonable class.

I went to class, help hours, even rewatched podcasts many times. Unclear rubrics & clueless TAs. Lowering the grades of all students after they've been logged shows a fundamental disregard for the emotional state of his students. Reduced everyone's grade, harming their GPA. He hinted in lecture he might curve,but clearly didn't mean it. I'm so sad.

Professor Cohen begins his lecture's by stating how rudimentary this class is. He is rude over email, and has NO idea what's going on in his class. He hides the rubric for his labs, and doesn't guide us at all aside from giving us templates for lab which are vague. He told us there would a slight curve, then changed his mind. Super unprofessional.

My girlfriend took his class. And happily got an A after the final exam. As this quarter started, he changed the grading scale. And the score of every students are reduced half a letter grade. He need to pay my girlfriend mental damage compensation.

His lab report templates are vague misleading and do not match his own rubric, which he never disclosed to the students. Graders are inconsistent with their grading criteria throughout the quarter. AVOID HIM AT ALL COST

Completely vague on what he expects to see on a lab report. Insufficient guidelines that are set like traps for losing points. TAs were jokes, they "helped" me changed my own correct answers to wrong ones. And now, three weeks after the grade given, told us grades were all wrong, there's no curve, 94 is A, only 20 As in a 600 ppl class. Amazing.

Almost Three weeks after our grades were admitted, he decides to lower our grades claiming "the curve was too easy and there was an error". My grade dropped from an A- to a B. He really could care less about his students and was rude to me when I emailed him during the quarter. Seriously do not recommend! He is seriously absent from the course.

PROS -lecture is podcasted -has a cute dog -enthusiastic about teaching -lab report templates available -amazing TAs -class was out of 1000 points cons -unclear/vague about what will quizzes will cover -mysterious when it comes to what is expected out of lab report (besides general points) -very high ego

He does not put much tricky things as did by other profs. The class is based upon a pre-set scale of A>90PTS (which may be changed). He is a nice person. I filled out my scantron incorrectly and he helps me to figure it out. Recommend him to others!

I think the previous review is right to an extent when it comes to the professor answering questions, but the class and lab reports are pretty straightforward and not too difficult. His midterm was also really easy and the labs aren't incredibly complicated. This classes isn't that hard.

Such a disappointment after avoiding Judy Kim for the last year. His T.A's have no idea what they are doing and neither does he. He does not respond to emails, calls everything "extremely straight forward" and makes you feel inadequate. Do Not Recommend! :(

I was lucky to have him for 7L. Even through it was his first time teaching the class, he made the material well organized and as comprehensive as possible with powerpoints and podcasts. Lab reports were easy to complete because he provided a template easy to fill in. He also podcasts every lecture! My lab TA was also awesome and helpful.

Happy I was lucky enough to have him for 7L. Lectures are podcasted, quizzes are simple & based off of lecture slides/ lab manual (no tricks). His lecture slides are well organized and not confusing at all. Lab reports were easy to complete because he had a layout ready for you to use. I appreciate how non-stressful he tried to make the class :)

Very good, clear lecturer, explains the topic well. But not enjoyable in person and not helpful. Leaves no time to learn MO theory just throws you in then exam time. No curve. I would recommend to take the class due to clarity, but hopefully you will never have to engage with him personally or ever have any questions! Very arrogant department chair

I went into the class hoping to learn a little more than only how to do MO's but not too bad of a class. Cohen is a great guy although I'm not sure how much he really knows about the subject. He was unsure about a lot of the topics but the tests were fair and an overall decent class

Avoid this professor, at all costs. He makes you feel like an idiot in office hours, doesnt know how to communicate with students who actually need help with the material. Midterm material is unexpected. He doesnt use his own slides and makes mistakes, more frequently then normal. I looked forward to 120A but this professor ruined it. Avoid him...

This is a very easy class but the professor blatantly doesn't care for his students. There were 2 quizzes, 2 homework sets, and 2 midterms. there is a slight curve in the grade but not helpful enough to make real difference. lecture notes provided, section unhelpful

1)does not post answer keys online, you have to go to urey hall 2) lectures not clear AND rearranged the topics(diff. to study yourself) 3)exams are surprisingly ez, but b prepared to be panicky thruout because u feel as though u don't know anything. prof figuero guest lectured once, and i felt i learned more that one time, than other lects tgt
Very nice and helpful professor compared to other profs. in the honor series.

Amazing professor and one of the clearest lecturers I have ever had at UCSD.  Always willing to help and passionate about his subject.  The class is kind of a grab bag of chemistry, and may be a bit tough simply because of a lack of practice problems to do.  But Cohen is great and his tests are very fair.

very good professor. clear lecture, relatively easy test. however, the presentation at the end killed my grade - the guest graders were harsh and cohen did not take into consideration that we're not all PhDs. take him if you can, prepares you well for ochem.
He's hot, but the second midterm made me cry.  The forensics stuff was interesting but if I learned anything, it wasn't represented by the exams..

Cohen can actually teach. He knows the material VERY well. However, he sort of scares me (in an intimidating kind of way). The workload is light, and the midterms are only 20%. I highly recommend this class and Cohen!
Wonderful professor, he makes the class interesting and easy to understand.  I highly recommend him, but make sure not to miss a class since his class is mostly lecture based.

Prof. Cohen is REALLY smart and knows what he is talking about.  He seems to really love what he does, but he goes extremely fast.  I have never had a teacher that talks as fast as he does while teaching.  The material seems overwhelming but study it and you'll be fine.

Professor Cohen is an excellent! For chem 6CH, much of the material on the tests come from his lectures. If you need help go to his office hours (they can make a difference). He cares about his students, and he wants them to succeed. The grading is fair, but it won't be easy to get an A. Also, you can learn some interesting stuff about forensics.

Prof. Cohen is a marvelous professor, and I highly recommend him. He enjoys teaching and it really shows.  Unfortunately, he often tries to cover more material than is humanly possible, so be prepared to have lectures that end 3/4 of the way through.  Make sure you take CHEM120A and CHEM114A before you take CHEM124 or else you will regret it later.

i found his lectures to be clear, his understanding of the subject to be sufficient, and his tests to be fair - i didn't remember much of 120A i took a year ago but still did well in his class - be prepared to memorize your 1st row transition metals - he covers way more material in lecture than he admits to exams, don't stress over it all

He is a very good teacher and he made the class more interesting by focusing on forensics which was cool as well as having guest speakers.  You shouldnt skip class b/c you will end up missing alot.  Also on the tests make sure you know structures because we were tested on them everytime.
Interesting class especially for forensic people. Tests aren't very hard, time is the big issue.

Cohen is such an awesome professor.  His tests were very fair, though people didn't seem to do well on them.  We learned the most interesting and useful things in this class.  He turned it into a forensics chem class and brought in speakers from the DEA.  The TA was my favorite part of the class, though.  He was really knowlegeable and helpful, too

His readings are excessively long… His quizzes are so specific with it being based on long readings he expects you to master the material quickly. Not looking forward to his exams. I've heard negative things.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Boring lectures, grade is heavily dependent on your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lowkey a harsh grader without clear guidelines for grading. Lectures were all mandatory and tedious. Slides were vague, as lectures are primarily oral. The best way to get help was from the TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So much content and texts to cover but he explains it fairly well. Final and midterm were somewhat challenging, have to identify speaker and text out of so many readings we did. Overall an okay professor but lectures could drag on at times. Very strict on AI so all written assignments are in-person. Just do the readings and take good lecture notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly not as bad as everyone makes him out to be. His lectures can be boring at times but he is very thorough in his explanations and going over content.
