In-class writing response for each of the five Shakespeare plays, midterm, final, attendance/participation. Midterm was heavy and had too much to do for the 50 minute period but final was okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I struggled in this class due to limited communication and lectures that were hard to hear. The professor mostly read from the text, and slides weren't very clear. Office hours were short, so I relied on the TA for help. Overall, the course structure felt unsupported.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His slides can be very boring to follow. Made us sit in a seating chart and our TA was supposed to take daily attendance. If he catches you with your phone, airpods, or using your laptop for something other than notes he will call you out and make you an example in front of the entire class. Try to avoid for MMW 13, if not hope you get a chill TA.

Prof. Vitkus is disliked for one reason only: he's old school. People get upset with the fact that he wants you to put down your phone and pay attention for 50 minutes; he also doesn't tolerate being late. Lectures can be boring sometimes, but not horrible. Your grade is mostly dependent on your TA.

Take the bad reviews w a grain of salt, most of them are prob conservatives who don't like that Vitkus will comment on our political atmosphere. But he's tasteful about it, and brings up important points about how our politics became the way they are. Grade depends entirely on your TA tbh, but class is pretty easy if you're interested in history

No podcast and slides have very minimal words so you can only write notes based on what you hear. There's a seating chart based on TA and my TAs section is top left so I can barely hear. Midterms are all memory based. Way too much content for that type of midterm style. Wouldn't recommend. Also most readings long and irrelevant.
Dont join this
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: After finishing MMW 15 I can finally return to say yes, this is the absolute worst MMW professor I have ever taken. Lectures are not only extremely boring and vague, but he jumps from different time periods to confuse you. Not only this, multiple TAs had to call out some of the stuff in lecture he was saying was WRONG, going on irrelevant tangents.

Calls people out in lecture for being on their phones, having earbuds, or just making faces. You can get by by not paying attention in class if you read and have a good TA. Didn't let us text our families after an earthquake. world systems model inaccurate. ASSIGNED SEATING with TA. DO NOT TAKE AT ALL COSTS. Chang or Zhiri would have been better.

Super old fashioned and heavy final expectations; 2500-3500 word paper on top of an intense written exam. There's no TAs so any questions/concerns have to go straight to Vitkus, which is tough considering he doesn't create a welcoming class environment. Class is lecture heavy, so don't expect to have any meaningful discussions in class.

I would take him again simply because of how understanding he was. He was always willing to help with assignments over email or in office hours. He was even understanding and wanted to do anything to help when I missed my final. I also preferred that it was lecture heavy cause of my anxiety.

I was hoping to have great discussions instead I was forced to listen to him. I love Shakespeare, but I came out wishing I never did just to avoid this class. If you hate or love Shakespeare think twice before entering lest you wish to hate old Willy. The final is ridiculous with at least a 2500 word essay and crazy expectations for the final exam
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Vitkus is one of the most knowledgeable professors I've encountered at UCSD & has so much valuable insight to offer. Incredibly interesting instruction & looked forward to every class! His workload demand is high, but it's worth it. Despite what ppl say here, he's kind, & flexible with hw/grading if u just talk to him. Can't recommend enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You'll need an iClicker so lecture is mandatory. However, due to protesting and the strike he lowered the iClicker grade plus it's only worth 5%. He did reschedule the midterm 3 times due to the strike because some MMW TA's were injured. Everything that was on the midterm and final were on the study guides given to us. Review lecture slides!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Required to purchase an iclicker for lecture attendance. There are many readings assigned and they don't pertain to the assignments at all. Lectures are jumping all over the place and focus heavily on capitalism? Hard to pay attention to the lectures. Tests are in person, no notes allowed, include written responses only. Would not recommend

Vitkus cares little for his students and had horrible communication throughout the protests and strikes. It took me two weeks to reschedule a midterm that he had rescheduled three times - Ridiculous!! The tests take forever to study for and the TAs don't even agree with him most of the time. If he is your last resort you'll live, but if not avoid.

When people talk about the ways in which modern day university professors are indoctrinating students, they are inadvertently referring to Vitkus. His class is not THAT difficult, but listening to his anti-capitalist (pro-Marxist/Lennist) ideology is; I had to take his class for units, but would never recommend it to anyone else.

Expectations for exams and papers are ASTRONOMICAL and unclear. He's an extremely tough grader and tracks attendance religiously. The final exam consisted of defining 10 mystery terms, answering 6 mystery short answer questions, AND writing 2 whole essays AT ONCE. IN CLASS. whatever you do, AVOID. THIS. MAN. (he's also a pretentious boomer)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Disorganized lectures, disengaged lecturing style, so boring and awful to listen to but attendance is mandatory because of iClickers. Tests based on the readings but not allowed any notes.

Exams are the best part because they make you feel smart doing so many FRQs, very AP style. HE GIVES STUDY GUIDES but only a few days prior. He rambles about politics which won't tested. Interesting for aspiring socialists? I wouldn't mind but lectures are mandatory and exams are important yet lecture content is his personal TED talk stage.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you don't want a history class(memorizing all the dates for every event that happened), then don't choose this class. This professor asks us to do in-person exams with no notes when all the other mmw13 students are writing essays for their finals and midterms or having open-notes exams. 10 term identification, 6 short answer and an essay(3hrs).

AVOID PLZ. Worse MMW professor I've experienced. I got 2 A- for MMW 13 and 14 but I think I'm gonna fail this one. If there is no spot just take it next year. Don't torture yourself. His lecture makes me feel like I have ADHD(maybe I do). I can't focus in his class. Midterms and finals are unnecessary. If you can't memorize stuff, DONT CHOOSE HIM.

Vitkus is a tenured professor who loves to powertrip. He does not care about making the class helpful and accessible for his students. He requires a $65+ I-clicker just for attendance, does not provide a midterm or final study guide of any kind, and lectures in a disorganized and inconsistent way. Don't take this class if you can avoid it.

Does NOT promote academic equity, makes students who missed the midterm because of COVID, which is out of their control, take a 15 min oral exam & expects you to almost perfectly answer essay questions VERBALLY without any time to think or plan. And DOES NOT CURVE for the make-up. If you don't want your GPA to be destroyed, DO NOT take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Vitkus does not provide students with a study guide. Lectures are ultra snoozy and mandatory. There are no writing assignments other than the research paper itself, and the exams are not intellectually stimulating or significant for developing writing skills. He has an abhorrent hyperfixation on economics, which makes the course material repetitive

Mandatory iClicker ($65) lectures that hardly cover full content, so a regular textbook reading is necessary to understand the content he'll put on the exams. Only closed-note MMW professor for mmw13. I do appreciate his analysis of culture and economics and applying of readings in lecture. At least no weekly quizzes (or Chang reader lol).

Vitkus is an extremely boring lecturer. This class falls within what I typically learn about within my major, but Vitkus makes me understand why some people hate school. He just goes over everything we read for homework which feels pointless. He's also incredibly uppity and nitpicky about what he wants in terms of papers turned in.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Vitkus' teaching style is incredibly dull and uninteresting, much like the class he teaches. He goes all over the place and doesn't care to make things clear for his students, as he often makes a random, garbled mess on the blackboard instead of taking the time to make clear powerpoint presentations. Waste of time and effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: MMW online is already difficult but Vitkus makes it worse. The lectures are uninteresting and he posts 4-5 each week. As always, the TA you get will make or break your experience so just pray you get a good one.

Lackadaisical. Lectures, online at least, are a waste of time. Expects students to cite lectures, although skips out on referential details and instead only offers broad parallels to the contemporary that are opinionated.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Attendance not mandatory but lecture quizzes every week. Totally would suggest doing the reading early, discussions are based on that and the papers and final require you to know a lot about them. Tons of reading but the prof was amazing!
Lecture heavy for quizzes - just reading the plays won't get a good quiz grade! Vitkus works with the students for reading and lecture comprehension and both are necessary for the essays and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Vitkus seems very knowledgeable and makes things easy to understand in his lectures. Although his lecture videos were sometimes long, the information he provided was interesting and relevant to the topic.

A decent professor overall, but fond of making broad, unsubstantiated, statements. Three minute explanations about "Capitalism bad" do not reach the level of depth or nuance the topic deserves. He could be right, but frankly I'm not looking for his opinion. He might have more charm in person, I can only attest to his online lectures

I thought Professor Vitkus was very knowledgeable and insightful during lectures. I think he's a solid choice for an English professor and his TA, Stacie, helped me a lot with my writing. My only gripes are about the final. There were way too many essay topics given (13 topics, only writing on 2). Other than that, I really had no other problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I don't doubt he's a great teacher, but the structure of his class and the new Math 2 system isn't conducive to student success. The one-test system, which ignores grades and effort throughout the quarter, feels unfair and frustrating. I attended, did the homework, and still failed the PUP exam.
He is very intense but an amazing professor. Its not a supper easy class but he really wants students to learn and succeed and office hours and homework are super helpful

Math 181A is a tougher class but he does a great job with managing explaining the content. His lectures are interesting, he's hilarious. He won't wait for you or hold your hand which I think is a good thing!!
was pretty good, the homework helped prepare for the place up exam. He was kind of "tough" with the three homework assignments per week but it really helped when studying for the exam.

He focused a lot on heavy algebra. The class is test-heavy, and you shouldn't expect much of a curve. Also, there's no cheat sheet, you have to memorize everything! As he said before the final, "think of your life decisions”… I'd say do the same before deciding to take stats with Quarfoot. He's put effort into presenting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This course is to prepare students for the placement exam, and in my experience, if you understand the prerequisites it becomes clear how effective the professor is. He teaches by anticipating students' common weaknesses and explains material in a way that addresses them. If something doesn't click, there are additional capus resources available.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: With this professor he does really good on explaining the concept and shows his method of doing the math which is really good. The only thing I would say that is annoying is the 3 H'Ws a week and being able to do his challenges in class. But these do help you get ready for the PUP if you take the time to practice little day to day.
Easy class. Lots of homework around 3 ten problem sets (most a-f) weekly. Lectures are very boring tbh. Very tough graders for homework. Can get attendance even if you don't go through canvas.

I dont know what everyone else is saying, the final was a great representation of what we learned from the course, and rather easier than I expected (I bombed both midterms, this was much easier). Quarfoot is an inspirational and wonderful professor, if you actually do the work and attend classes, you'll be fine

DQ was overall a good professor for Math2, but I felt very unprepared for the PUP-Exam because there were no quizzes or exams. There's hw due 3x a week, but it's very manageable. However, hw is only graded on style and competition, not on accuracy. DQ will post the answers to the hw, but you have to go and look through it yourself to review.

That final was absurd. Why does every question on tests need to be a type of problem that we have never seen? I feel like I wasn't tested on my actual ability to apply what I learned and I wasted 10 weeks of effort. I learned a lot, looking forward to getting an A with another professor. No sense if over half the class fails tests then passes…

To be very objective since just finished my final, I don't know why he was giving out such a hard exam. I am a good student with extremely high GPA. I was trying to learn all the things because I put all my time on studying hw and practice test, really disappointed by the question he designed. There's no curve although the average was about 50.

The level of care and thought Quarfoot puts into this course is insane. Everything is thought out, except one thing - that we also have other classes to take... The problem is not even with the loads of homework, but rather with one hour exams in the morning that are graded super harshly, and the questions are very difficult. Learned a lot though

Nervous about the final bc I bombed one of the tests, but I want to leave a review before I know my final grade outcome. He has pretty amazing lectures and you can see how much effort he has put into designing the course. The material is challenging but he presents it optimally for a holistic understanding. Hard but personally rewarding class.
This guy is so freaking funny. He genuinely makes me laugh a lot. He made math really easy and simple to understand. There is homework 3 times a week but it shouldn't take you over an hour.

Difficult professor in every regard, proclaiming that his courses should 'mean something' and that he's 'disappointed' when the exam average is 50% because of his lectures. Complete disregard for students' circumstances and learning preferences while preaching how everyone should inherently know how everything comes together.

He has hilarious lectures. He was great at explaining topics and there was really nothing to complain about. A solid professor all around. If I did have a complaint, it would actually be to have some more homework because I found myself wanting more practice when it came to the place up exam.
I guess the lectures were good but exams' difficulty was insane compared to previous quarters. No cheat sheet either

Quarfoot is actually goated. He makes topics extremely understandable and completely changed my way of viewing stats (blew my mind over and over again). From my experience so far taking UD math classes, he's the only prof who I don't need to go back and review any material to understand the course at all. Absolutely amazing, 11/10.

This is a nice class, although the homeworks are due twice in a week and his tests are quite difficult. Lectures are very thorough and it is very straightforward to understand the content, but the questions themselves are difficult to solve. No cheat sheets, so it is a good idea to make flashcards from the beginning to memorize lots of formulas.

Nice professor who clearly wants you to learn, can be a bit dry in his remarks if you didn't listen to something he said during lecture. No formula sheet for exams so be ready to memorize many, many formulas. This class isn't just AP Stats, don't make that mistake, but a background foundation in stats should lead to easy success.

Interesting professor, with humor that's not everyone's cup of tea. Has a different teaching style than most, but I think it works for this class and gets students motivated to get better in math. Overall, HW can be time-consuming and sometimes feels like busy work, but studying HWs is the best way to pass the PUP-E at the end of the course.

Quarfoot has a subjective sense of humor (I found him funny personally). Class is based on attendance and homework. The final was taking the place up exam however I felt he insufficiently prepared the class to pass due to the lack of tests and quizzes within the course.

Very interesting man to say the least but his class was not difficult as long as you keep up with the 3 weekly homework's and attend lectures. I used the homework problems to study for the PUP-E bc he didn't really specify what would be on the exam. My advice is to just practice his hw sets over and over again for the PUP-E bc they helped me pass.

Took this class pass/no pass and passed it. Hw is 10 problems due MWF. Gives you 5 opportunities to miss class and hw and not judgmental at all cus you r in math 2. He's really smart and is incredibly helpful with everything. Only reason y i didn't give him a 5/5 was cus the class doesn't help on retaking the mpe. No midterm and no final.

Lectures are clear and well taught, but the homework assignments are long and tedious. Exams make up 70% of the grade and aren't conceptually difficult, but no cheat sheet or formula sheet is allowed, so you're expected to memorize countless formulas.

He's one of the only math profs where I felt like I didn't need to do tons of studying outside lecture just to understand what's going on, good lecturer. he does give homework 2x a week, roughly 4-6 problems, but on each homework he gives the full solution so u could technically copy if u want. no cheat sheet but u can use graphing calculators

Time management is gonna be your best friend for this class, considering the homework load he gave out for us (3 hw sets per week and takes 2-3 hours per set). His teaching style might be different from others, but I had no problems with it. Utilize ASC Math @ APM  because the tutors helped me with assignments and prepared me for the PUP-Exam.
Very hard to pass out with the content he teaches compared to the tests, makes others very uncomfortable in class with his word use.

Got placed in math 2 despite taking calculus in high school. Lectures all consisted of objectively simple subjects but we had about 2-3 hours of homework 3 times a week. Studied a lot for the place up exam and still failed. He makes it difficult to pass out of the class.

Sometimes the graders take points off homework for ridiculous reasons. The lectures consist of him rambling about random stuff like him calling numbers "sexy". Despite the math being objectively "easy", the time limit on the PUP-E was awful. Even after studying flashcards and spending hours on HW, I didn't pass. The only way out is passing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of homework. Pass/ No pass class.

If you sit on the end of the aisle he walks up and down and looks at your paper and will publicly shame you for doing anything wrong. The homework was unreasonably long and the word problems are really confusing. Also, the 2-3b exam is your only option to move up now, and you can't move up until you pass it. You basically have to self study tbh.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nice guy and fun personality. He assigns 3 homework assignments per week that are expected to take upwards of 3 hours per which can take a huge chunk of time. You can miss a couple of days for attendance and miss points on homework, and still get full points for the class. He doesn't extend assignments or allow you to miss, even for good reasons.
The class itself is easy but he makes a lot of students really uncomfortable. He says things like he finds numbers sexy and other stuff along those lines.
Oh no.. My GPA!!!! BYEBYE
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Still in the middle of this class (week 7). Bombed the first midterm. Regardless, I truly mean to say that Quarfoot is a genius. Every aspect of his teaching is catered towards the students. I might do bad, but this dudes integrity as a teacher and educator in a research based institution is remarkable. Its time to do hard stuff, dont back down now

No cheat sheets and imo more formulas to know than calc and linalg. 6 weeks in, theres around 8-9 different application RVs each w 4 equations on top of many others, also 2 hws a week each 3-4 hrs none dropped. His worldview is that you're smarter than most people and cheat sheets won't help you in the real world. I disagree..just take someone else

Had to drop with a W, the workload is insane. Homework is extremely difficult compared to what's covered in lecture, and the exams are brutal with no cheat sheet (while every other professor allows one). He's a good lecturer, but as a CS major, this class left me no time for anything else. HW is 2-3 hrs each, twice a week!! Take someone else
Funny guy. Very straightforward when it comes to what you need to know and do in order to be successful in the school's math department, especially if you're starting from this class.

Great professor, great lecturer, the exams were hard but they were most definitely fair. The grading is pretty harsh but at the same time, it's very clear. Besides the extremely hard grading, I feel like I finished this class learning a lot of things thanks to DQ, despite having a B- or B.

Dude, DQ is by far the best prof at ucsd. I think what helps is that he has a background of teaching at middle and highschools so i think thats where he gets that vibe from. But either way he makes a hard topic much easier to understand in the lecture slides. Great guy...great personality...easy to talk to. only thing is the homework is alot

Prof. Quarfoot is by far the best lecturer I've had at UCSD.  He captures every topic in complicated class with expertise and brings it to lecture in the most easy-to-understand and engaging way possible.  His command of the classroom is genuinely like no other.

Tough content, homework is hard as well, but the professor is super good. Very enthusiastic, obviously cares what we learn, and the man loves what he teaches - which makes his lecture bearable at 8:00 AM (dreadful hours). 

Creative homework problems, they're challenging, but they guide learning a lot. Impossible without watching lectures.

DQ was really chill prof, this was a P/NP for me and we have to go to tutoring at least four times a week in order to pass the class. However, the workload was not too much and he was pretty chill in class. We did have to go to tutoring four times a week but it was worth it bc I passed the class and skipped two math courses after re-taking the MPE.

Great professor! The homework is not bad at all. No midterms and your final is taking the MPE. I was at his office hours nearly every week, not necessarily for homework but to just talk. He genuinely cares and wants to make sure his students understand and do well in the class. Would take again!

i took math 2 with prof Quarfoot and I really liked his teaching style. he engages with students during class and actually makes lecture enjoyable, even at 8am. there was homework due once a week however I think the department is changing this.
For math 2 I think he is great if you want to move onto the next level. He gives you all the resources to be successful, you just have to put in the work tbh. Would recommend taking.
Was clear in math, genuinely cared about the students understanding and it wasn't boring he'd make jokes here and there and overall had my attention. lecture would go by fast
Very kind and funny. Lectures were very entertaining and helpful. A lot of homework but manageable. Overall a great professor who's passionate about math.

Quarfoot was really funny & it was entertaining to go to class. There is homework every week that takes ~4 hours to do, but it you plan well enough you should be fine! It is a good class to refresh your mind if you haven't done math in a while, but you will have to study for the MPE. Quarfoot is a fun professor who truly cares about his students.

Quarfoot is great! He lectures well, homework is manageable, and ALEKS is easy if you're consistent. However, his class won't help with the MPE. If you expect MATH 2 to prep you for it, you're wrong. You'll need to STUDY on your own. He's great though! His class is oversimplified, but he's nice. He's a sweet guy, the content just isn't the MPE.

Professor Quarfoot genuinely cares about your learning. Keep in mind you will have homework every week that takes approximately 4 hrs to complete so manage your time well and attend lectures. I'm bad at math and I don't believe it was that difficult and learned a lot in this course so it's very beneficial. Good luck!

Professor Quarfoot was my Math 2 instructor. Within all of his lectures he really addresses his dislike of calculators and how his students shouldn't be using them, which tended to be a bit frustrating at times. Also, you will come to see him mention his nephew multiple times, which shows he cares about him. Overall, means well and cares for us.

He gives a lot of hard questions in homework and tough exams but offers 4 OH a week and gives clear explanations on questions, which will help you establish a more solid understanding of math. So if you are interested in math, he is a great professor. If you take a course only because of the major requirement, avoid him.

Professor DQ runs a challenging but rewarding class. Expect a heavy workload, but the lectures and office hours are worthwhile. I found unstuck study and the free textbook very helpful for staying on top of the material.

Despite having experience with other fields of math, I feared statistics due to some past experiences. However, after taking this class, I really find statistics fascinating and wish I could have taken more classes with him. (It's my last quarter)

Professor Quarfoot is one of the best professors I've taken at UCSD. Really recommend that guy. :)

Homework due twice a week. 2 grading criteria at least. Really does belittle students by comparing "A+ students" to "C- students." Very discouraging. Did his best to teach the content, but oh my god was this class so draining. You will have to commit a lot of time to this course + go to office hours- trust it will help u succeed.

Calc 2 is hard in general despite the professor you take it with. He wants his students to succeed and tries to make class a little more interesting with his humor. No cheat sheets are allowed but he gives students previous years midterms and finals to give them a heads up of what to study. Around 35 people failed but the curve is really generous.
Oh my God this guy is pretentious. In lecture he makes remarks that belittle people with
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: David Quarfoot is an outstanding teacher that cares deeply about each and every student he comes across and it is very evident. He doesn't just lecture at you, he lectures with you, taking deeper approaches into the why it was wrong rather than just stating that it was wrong. Although hes a tough grader,he is funny/mannered and makes math exciting.

After just the first lecture in Math183, I felt compelled to write this because it's evident he's an exceptional professor. His caring nature, clear and structured teaching, along with a great sense of humor, make learning a pleasure. Truly an A+ professor from the start.

This class is genuinely one of the most interesting and information classes I have taken at UCSD. Professor DQ is a very engaging lecturer and very helpful during office hours.

However my depression worsened this quarter because I'm quite bad at math and almost failed the class. I would only recommend this class if you're a real math nerd.

one of the best professors and the best math professor I've ever had. His lectures are super entertaining and engaging, and he makes it very difficult to feel lost. Homeworks are hard and you should probably find people to do them with. Note - you do have to not hate math to enjoy his class, and his tests are hard (but fair)

I genuinely enjoyed Professor Quarfoot's class. If you study for the tests and go to office hours, you will definitely pass. The class is somewhat difficult because of how quickly the topics are taught, but the professor did a great job making lectures entertaining and informative.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He cares greatly about student success in the course. I liked how he had life tips in each lecture presentation because they proved to be insightful. He doesn't provide extra credit and there is a lot of homework in the course. Not too hard of a course to manage.

You either like this guy or hate him. The only teacher who made me understand the basics of math. He makes exams hard, but nothing that you haven't seen in class. A lot of HW, but just do it on time. Textbook provided online. Class can get boring but he tries
Amazing prof that clearly genuinely cares about students. Very entertaining lectures.

I'm typically a pretty good student and I've never received a grade like this before. He made the class unnecessarily difficult on a level I've never seen before. He gave excessive amounts of homework with very difficult problems and made the exams very difficult. There was also no curve, which seemed pretty harsh given the difficulty of the class.
Teacher is kind of quirky but nice. Lectures are not mandatory but discussions are (you can miss like 2). I took this class during the TA strike so the grade is probably inflated.
Horrible. Made the class unnecessarily difficult.
Very hard concepts and you will spend a lot of time just trying to complete the HW and understand the lectures. Funny guy tho
Blamed the class after everyone did poorly on the first midterm and then gave a very difficult final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lots of very difficult homework and tests are hard as well

One of the most difficult classes I've taken. If you want a good grade you have to know the homework (of which there is a lot) like the back of your hand and understand the lecture material inside and out, because the exams are SUPER difficult. That being said, he's a great teacher and you will learn a lot. Don't do this for an easy grade!

You can tell he's definitely passionate about math, which makes you more engaged in his lectures and also just more interested in concepts beyond the course syllabus. I loved taking this class even though I previously had already covered most of this material.

Dr. Quarfoot was a very knowledgeable professor and always made lecture easy to follow. Office Hours always had a pretty long wait, but he would always go over every question you had until completion. Exams were difficult but not unfair, and could be passed with good effort. There was a lot of homework but it helped prep for exams.
Office Hours helped a lot, and Professor Quarfoot would always go over any and all questions you had.

Probably the best math professor I've ever had. His lectures are incredibly organized and easy to follow, and he frequently uses them to teach random valuable lifelong habits. The course content was difficult, but he made it relatively simple.
amazing teacher, passionate about his subject, really tries to make sure you understand. I only got a C because i didnt study for the final LOL, but it was good

Excellent professor. Very organized, straightforward and dedicated toward helping students learn the material. His lectures are engaging and involve the perfect balance of learning material and problem solving. The slides are very helpful for homework and exams. The exams are not too difficult as they are constructed similar to the homework.

Best math professor I had in the Mathematics Department. Professor Quarfoot is good at teaching mathematics, as I had him for Math 20B, but I can tell he is good at any of the subjects. He has fantastic lectures that are very entertaining and engage me to learn. He is the best professor I have ever had and is a true inspiration for math.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER!!! However, the homework is time consuming and the material is challenging especially for those who have no foundation in calculus. It is clear to see that he wants us all to understand the concepts. The lecture slides are some of the most concise and clear slides I have seen, so you don't have to worry about bad handwriting.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Awful. He made this class unnecessarily hard.

He is very passionate about teaching and has wonderful lecture notes with good examples as well as in-class problems to go along with the material. Overall a very good and helpful teacher though the class was a bit difficult due to the pacing.
Professor is very passionate about math which makes him proficient and effective at teaching the subject. Has a great sense of humor and captures your attention.

Prof DQ is great. Please take this man if you have the opportunity. His lectures are amazing and he keeps them entertaining with jokes. He is so helpful and kind in office hours. He is by far the best teacher I've ever had in almost all categories. 20B is a hard class, and DQ does everything he can to make it easier.
Salute to DQ. Great Professor with heavy HW due biweekly. Midterms are hard but the final is easy to balance our performances.

He is an amazing teacher. He taught me so much statistics thanks to his fantastic lecture notes and S-tier homework sets. But I always watched the podcasts, since he always made me feel so tense during lectures.

Looks out for his students, and offers help. However, last midterm and final were too detached from coursework. Two full-problem set homeworks per week, this'll feel like two 4-unit classes alone. And homeworks must be done alone.

His teaching style is ok though, but he has lots of and lots of homework. Besides the large amount of hw, the difficulty of hw is also very hard. His 181A class needs you to spend tons of time and energy if you want to have a good grade. The exams also have the same difficulty with hw, so it's hard to make a good grade in his 181A class.

ONLY TAKE THIS PROFESSOR IF YOU WANT TO GO THE EXTRA MILE WITH STATS. Given that the course is on a tough subject, the teacher openly states how hard his class, and there are problems that aren't even covered in lecture you would expect for there to be additional help? Incorrect, the teacher SHUT DOWN our discord and only helps a handful through OH
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quarfoot is a great professor, you will only pass this class if you try and learn. His tests require a deep understanding of the concepts being taught. I studied about 4hrs/w, along with homework due twice a week. Office Hours WILL help, it's usually 1 on 1, and he goes over every question you have.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Quarfoot really does care about his students. His questions can get weird, and the homework takes FOREVER. However, I learned so much within his class. He helped me when I asked, and his advice was always very useful. He is an interesting guy, but his passion for teaching makes you feel motivated to succeed. If you work hard, take his class.

GOOD: -Reasonably good, prerecorded lectures. -Lenient 12 hour window for exams -Free textbook -You really do learn! NEUTRAL: -New homework problems every quarter BAD: -HW due twice a week. -Demand far outstrips OH supply. Expect long waits for OH. Prof. David genuinely cares about his work, but if you want/expect an easy class, avoid him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Just finished his final. I have to say I love his class. PERIOD.

I truly learned A LOT from him. He has the best math lectures I have ever had at UCSD. I have to say his class makes me understand AP Stats on another level. People bs about his hw/tests. I have to say those hws helped me learn and understand the materials. Remember, he gave everyone 12 hours to complete his exams. Who else at UCSD is doing this?
We can learn quite a bit from his class besides simple stats theory. I know the workload is real, but we can learn a LOT.

This professor is just extremely uncaring toward students, especially students in international time zone. He makes a 12 hour window and expects student to finish their take-home final(>3 hr workload for sure) from 1 am to 1 pm within their timezone. HIs hw are just over creative and requires cultural context, not reflecting stats understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He thinks he's one of the best professors to walk the earth.

The course reviews AP Statistics, but with more calculus involved. It is not, by any stretch, difficult content. It is, however, made artificially difficult by the degree to which ambiguities on homework are not disambiguated for tenuously educational reasons.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor had no lenicency for students during COVID. Each homework takes about 4-5 hours with 2 a week OH were incredibly difficult since he made it into 1-1 sessions and waittimes are hours if you don't get into the zoom link about 30 minutes early. Emails are replied quickly but only with a recommendation to go to OHs and denials for questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His homework takes a little bit of time but he just made stats easy.

I don't give a f about how people talking sh*t about his homework. Let's just be honest, his homework sets helped me and my friends learn. His lecture is clear and the way how he taught this subject makes this class so easy and understandable.

I expected him to be a good professor and he does seem like he will be when you hear him talk and explain stuff. It's just his damn tests. His lectures are so specific that it makes it very difficult to apply the concepts to other problems AKA the exams. It's also very weird to basically have no idea what your professor looks like unless you Google

Okay, I read the other reviews and I would just like to say, the lectures are fine. I took him for MATH 20B as well, and loved both classes (183 and 20B). While he does give a lot of homework, it helps you learn. This is coming from a CSE student who took 22 units at the time. I had no experience in stats before this and Quarfoot made it easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Quarfoot means well but is very hard, to succeed in this class you REALLY and I mean REALLY(!!!) need to know your stuff! Homework is not a good representation of what the exams will be like, they are 100 times harder. My HW avg was a 90.2 and I got a 68% Midterm1 and a 70% Midterm2. The final was so-so, first 1/2 was ez other 1/2 was difficult. GL
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Knows his stuff but not worth taking his class. Unrealistic amount of hw, no piazza, not accessible outside of class, no curve, and exams that you can't finish in the intended time even with lots of study. Sad to see a good guy so out of touch with why students feel the need to cheat to pass his class.

Couldn't find the class recording on the very first day... confusing canvas page... After 2 lectures, I ended up just reading the lecture pdf and not watching the class recording. Lots of hw, spending 7 to 8 hrs on hw at least every week. Very helpful during office hour, but still hope we could use piazza for discussion.

I was reported for violation of AI, but I won't disgrace a good professor just because he reported me. I recommend him because although the work load is a lot, I learned a lot from his class. However, I do recommend him to allow students to work more collaboratively.

This guy has a good heart but can't really teach. He just reads off his lecture slides but then the homework is ten times harder than what you've ever seen. Don't forget you have two homework sets due per week. The exams consist of 40% related material and 60% questions only he would be able to answer. These exams are for DQ, by DQ.

This professor teaches stats in the worst way possible. He does not use technical terms, preferring terms like PHANTOM so searching for help is impossible. Good luck trying to figure it out on your own since the professor does not host zoom lectures.
One of the worst professors. Slides are extremely unclear and he reads straight from them. Avoid at all cost
Very High-quality lectures and above-average workload, the exam difficulty is moderate. The best math prof I've met in the first year.

Honestly one of the worst professors. Doesn't host zoom lectures (lectures only via youtube) and does not make himself accessible outside class for zooms. Homework is poorly written and due twice a week. He does not allow students to post questions on Piazza for any clarification or help. There are a lot better professors for Math 183.

Homework is way much than a course should have and some problems are beyond the scope of what he has taught. He overemphasized calculation by hand than calculator. Also, there is nothing such as Piazza to discuss approach of solving problems. Every hw feels like exams. Though I have programming background, I don't know how to do his coding question
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Respected--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really enjoy stats, but I have to say this class has been pretty disappointing. HW is heavy. The textbook is good. The exams are unnecessarily difficult. Just expect the kind of difficult unrealistic problem solving that contributes less to learning and more to stereotypical academic ivory tower insularity and stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He really puts a lot of effort into teaching and designing all the problems. The lectures are inspirational. He can explain the concepts clearly. He is caring and accessible outside the class. He is actually my favorite professor at UCSD. Don't know why he is rated so low. The workload is real but you can really learn a lot from him.

Quarfoot is one of the best and hardest professors I've ever taken. He provides the material very clearly. He is happy to help any student that cares during office hours. His exams are incredibly difficult and challenge you to actually understand the material not just memorize similar example problems. Said he wouldnt curve but did by 6% in the end

Look, I get that homework is essential in building those math skills, but the fact that it focuses more on the computation rather than the concept is terrible. I rather spend an hour to really understand what I am doing rather than googling the formula or "the way" the problem should be solved. His teaching is bad when it can't be linked to the HW

If you're taking DQ with other engineering classes, be prepared. His homeworks take 3-4 hour each and are challenging. His midterms are fair but prepare for the final (complex questions and little time).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DQ knows his stuff and explains things very well with examples and interactive questions. My only complaint is that he can be a little bit too quiet, even if you are sitting up front.

He made HW question himself. Two HW due in one week. Messy HW grading criteria, you may get the minimum score even you do everything just correct(BUT LOOKS SLIGHTLY DIFFERENT TO HIS ANSWER). Got a good grade though.

He gives pretty good lectures and makes it pretty easy for students to engage, but his exam and tests are in a different level. (20B first midterm, average is around 50/100), he ended up curving the class by giving everyone 5+ points. Therefore be ready to learn well and prepare or his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DQ is very homework heavy, but he teaches well too. I attended his lectures quite often. I learned a lot in his class. He engages his student to his lecture, but his homework and tests are harder than his examples. Some problems are between graduate and college level. He also barely curves the grade, so keep that in mind too.

He cares about teaching but his approach isn't the best. He assigns two homework assignments a week, each of which take up to about 4 hours. I feel as though he made the course harder than it had to be. Lecture slides are solid, but can sometimes be cumbersome. Exams are fair/bit difficult. Unengaging voice. Take him only if you can commit the time

Amazing professor, but even tho i thought i knew the material rly well, the final kicked my grade down real fast. The gap of difficulty between the midterms and final is huge. I advise doing the extra practice problems he posts on tritoned too. Other than that he's a great lecturer and he obviously cares a lot abt advancing his teaching exp.

Professor Quarfoot is one of the best math teachers I have ever had. His lectures are truly intriguing and he genuinely cares about students. If you go to his office hours and try to get to know him, he is great st explaining and accessible to talk to. Highly recommend him for Math20B.
His lectures are not mandatory and he will give every class slide. Midterms are ok but finals will be more difficult, but he gives curves.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: (I took AP Stats before taking MATH11) QUarfoot's lectures are great for MATH11. The course is demanding for those who don't have any background in statistics. He has a lot of homework assignments (due twice a week) but they are helpful as they keep you on track. The labs have an unclear grading criteria. Exams are similar to homework problems.

Quarfoot seems like a cool guy, but he is easily the hardest Math20B professor at UCSD. His homework takes forever if you don't know what your doing. If you do know what you're doing there's still a good chance you'll bomb his tests. His tests are unnecessarily difficult and not reflective of the homework and practice problems he does in class.

So obviously Math 20B is a very hard course, but taking it with Quarfoot makes it 10x harder. He's good at teaching the material but his exams are INSANELY difficult. Also a lot of hw! (2 per week) I did average on both midterms (they felt more doable) and overall I was feeling good about the class but after taking his final... rip me :(

Quarfoot provides the materials to learn calculus but hes not very good at teaching them. He goes over very simple problems in a not so engaging lecture, but homework and tests get extremely difficult. Midterms were probably slightly easier than the homework but the final was extremely challenging. Usually doesnt curve. Wouldnt recommend.
He basically reads off the slides on his lecture. You'll do homework twice a week and it takes you 3 hours to complete one assignment. BTW, his final is super tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lots of homework, but honestly feel like it was kinda worth it. If this is your hardest class you'll be fine, if not you might be a bit overwhelmed. Midterms were hardish (avg of 70-75)
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Quarfoot is a great lecturer, he's very interesting and engaging and provides great examples. He doesn't curve tests but he will curve the class. His tests can be somewhat hard, the problems aren't straightforward and it can take awhile to figure it out. He assigns two homeworks a week which can be annoying but it's helpful.

Professor Quarfoot is one of the few who really puts an effort into his teachings to help you learn. In return he requires you to really work hard and earn your grade. What I noticed about a lot of the students in my class really don't work hard enough in the class since most of them are math/cs majors who couldn't care less about stats.

If you want to actually learn something take Quarfoot!! If you're just trying to get an "easy A" (or B lolol) look somewhere else... his tests are difficult and require a deep deep understanding of the material. He's a super interesting guy tho and somehow makes math bearable (:

Quarfoot is easily the best math teacher Ive ever had. He's an amazing lecturer and knows how to teach math really well. I always left class feeling like I learned alot. the only potential drawback is his tests are really hard. He tests you to see if you reallly know the material, theres no "practice midterm same as midterm" or anything like that.

Fantastic professor!! His homework assignments are very difficult but they are designed to make you really learn the material and make the actual exams seem much easier. His research is in math education, and you can tell - he knows how to teach. If you have the chance, take him!! He's super funny too and really cares about your success.

Overall, 1 of the better prof I ever had. Hes aninteresting guy, keeps lectures from being boring imo. 17 smaller HWs 6-12hrs depending on student. 2 Midterms somewhat more difficult than HW. Final nearly identical difficulty to practice finals and HW. All exam/hw material directly from lectures/text. His teaching makes course easier. Podcasted.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Quarfoot is a great lecturer. His slides are well structured and clear, he is always accessible and, yes, he assigns LOTS of hw. However, this is a very rare case when hw problems are actually interesting to work on: he uses real data sets from real researches. He also makes lots of sarcastic jokes which I find hilarious.
His lecture is very clear and well planned! And he can explain stuff down to the earth. Tests are fair. I've heard that 20B is somewhat difficult, but with him, I don't feel it.

Calculus was not hard because I had already taken Calc BC and I am good at math so this class was easier for me. His lectures are easy to follow and he is funny especially his analogies, they are not what you expect. He podcast so you don't have to attend but I did anyways. Homework is due Mon. Wed. and Friday.

Quarfoot is awesome and actually manages to make stats entertaining. He actually cares about teaching and is really trying to make the students succeed and work with the material. Take him if you can it is totally worth it.

By far the best math teacher I've had. He is quirky which make lectures interesting, but also very knowledgeable and skilled at explaining complex topics through metacognition. Online homework paired with the practice tests will prepare you well for exams. Exams are fair representation of class and he's lenient with partial credit.

I notice a lot of people who do well in his class have either taken Calculus in high school, retaken the class, or have a good background in math. If you have none of those things, good luck. Not only is he extremely difficult, he makes things more complicated than they should be. I went to Supplementary Instruction instead of his slides/lectures.

For math 10 series, as a student with a decent math background, his lectures are clear and the exams are easy that fairly represents the class material. Online homework are indeed a bit more challenging but definitely rewarding. Doing practice exams will prepare you well. Studying math with Quarfoot is easy and relaxing. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Quarfoot is extremely hard, if you do not show up to lectures or study on your own time, you will fail. His tests were fair, but his final was on a different level. His HW is also extremely hard. Overall he is a good lecturer, but it's not worth taking his class if he expects you to learn stuff that is usually for a tougher class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Would be difficult if you havent seen the material before. Hes entertaining during lecture, you wont fall asleep. His exams were unrelated to the HW and had a few things meant to throw you off. HW was ridiculously hard. Make sure you know the foundational material (trig, precalc, etc). His partial credit on exams made it worth it tho.

Slides and lectures were pointless - didn't explain anything well, and did not reflect exams. His homework problems even stumped the math tutors I went to see who I ran to in desperation because I learned NOTHING and his homework was difficult. Homework also didn't reflect exams.

I love the way he teaches. He clearly cares about the students and provides students with tons of material such as lecture slides, podcasts and lots of homework. He also is a genius of systematization and clarity. Take him and you will not be sorry!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you ever wanted to learn a math by having someone read what looks like something straight off of a Wikipedia page, then take this class. The lectures were useless, and the exams did not reflect any of the stuff in lecture. He reads off a PowerPoint and then uses Socrative to "quiz" us anonymously in order to mine data from students.

Quarfoot is the best math teacher I've ever had and I'm sad I wont be able to take him again for other classes. His teaching style ensures that you know the material and helps you build a solid foundation in calculus.

He is not bad at all, though I seeing the evaluations for most 10B instructors, all of them seem to be pretty difficulty (low averages). 2 HW's every week on WileyPlus, 3 exams, and one exam can be dropped. When I took him, his Midterm 1 was difficult (low average) but Midterm 2 and Final exam were not hard. Ask for help when needed. Take him.

He is an amazing lecturer. He covers most of the material during lecture (even the hard problems). He is really approachable when going to office hours. If you like math a lot and want somebody enthusiastic to teach you the subject, you should totally take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His class may feel very challenging and overwhelming at first, especially if you do not have a strong math background. It gets better tho, his midterms and final were honestly not bad at all due to partial credit. If you want the A, be ready to put in some work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic about the material and offers clear explanations. Funny guy. Clear lecture slides with a lot of visuals. Only complaint is that he can go too fast, but to compensate he releases slides 24h b/f class. Gives many resources to prep for exams including supplementary textbook problems and even past exams. Lenient w/ partial credit.

Quarfoot is an amazing lecturer, his slides are posted and it's organized very well. However, the homework is pretty tough, but it prepares you well for the midterm (which is easier in my opinion). Just go to lecture and you will be fine.

Lectures are very informative and helpful, he gives a lot of tips and hints to what he's going to put on the tests. The suggested homework is also helpful. Really funny professor, super enthusiastic about math which I think is nice c:

This man is more than just a capable professor. His slides are formatted in a way that they are easy to follow, and never fail to offer up math problems that allow for clarification of misconceptions and deeper understanding of the topic. He never fails to make the math more interesting, and is always aware of the learner's perspective.

Amazing, hilarious lectures, always learn something new. You can check his lectures at ucsd podcasts, he conveys concepts very clearly. Homework is tough, but prepares you very well for midterms (similar difficulty). Plus provides a list of suggested textbook problems, the midterm is again very similar to these. Just do these and you will be good.

I wish I could take Quarfoot for all my maths. I personally think he's funny and seems like a really nice person who wants his students to learn and understand what they're learning. 10/10 would recommend.

DQ is nice and friendly prof who really makes an effort to get to know his students. lectures are over simplified while the homework is very complex, so you often spend alot of time on the homework. His first midterm is hard to weed out people while the second is pretty fair. There'll be times he's very frustrating but overall he's not a bad prof

Professor Quarfoot's lectures are both fun and engaging. I look forward to his lectures everyday. More than what he teaches, the way he teaches makes him easy to understand and follow. Every day I come out having learned a lot more than I expect. He is a great professor and I am fortunate to have him.

Quarfoot is generally a nice professor but he doesn't give us enough review before midterms. The way he explains new chapters can be confusing. I'm about to take my second midterm and like the first, I still do not feel prepared. I don't think I'd take him again, but if you're up for a challenge (or if you're good at math), I think you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: As I sit here reviewing for my second midterm in Quarfoot's class, tears begin brimming in my eyes, threatening to fall, as I realize I am about to fail again. With nowhere else to turn, I drown my sorrows in Oreos. Nah but for real this class made me cry. Don't take Quarfoot unless you can think conceptually and have a good Calc background.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lectures, are funny and enjoyable, but can be lacking with some regard, leaving us sometimes struggling when it comes to the homework (twice a week but a usual max of 20 problems). But if you have a solid background with Calc AB (MATH20A), you should do reasonably well. There are MANY resources that we can use (e.g. podcasts, SI, office hrs...)

I think that coming in with a good calc background really makes a difference in his class. he can really enhance whatever youve learned before. If you have no experience with calc, then you may not be able to follow his lectures and rewatch his podcast. Homework is easy and midterm is fairly straightforward (if you understand the concepts)

Horrible professor. His lectures are not clear and he goes through them too fast. Midterm was nothing like the lectures and he always talks in a condescending tone. Avoid him at all costs. Homeworks are due 2 times a week and they are nothing like the lectures. NEVER TAKING HIM AGAIN
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher. skips steps that are needed. Extremely difficult problems for hw that is not properly taught during lecture. You are expected to know how to apply something that you are not taught how to apply. Do not take him as a teacher.

I ended up dropping this class, if you're a transfer student like me, I don't recommend you to take it unless you're good at math. Everything is tied to the previous course, which this school teaches it in its own way, so it was extremely hard for me to follow. The professor is awesome though, super kind, patient, and chill.

The reviews are true! Please avoid taking Quarfoot, he'll make your life miserable. All he does is present very difficult power point examples during lectures and doesn't really show you how to approach these math problems. Midterms are out there to trick you as well, please take it with another instructor if you really care about your grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: DON'T take his class if haven't take 10A with him. He expects you to know everything from 10A and he loves skipping steps while solving problems and using hard examples. It was pretty stressful

David Quarfoot is a very kind person who has a genuine passion for the material he teaches. Unfortunately, his teaching method leaves much to be desired, as he doesn't give students enough examples to work with before asking them unreasonably difficult questions on completely new topics the class is trying to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Quarfoot seems like a pretty nice guy, but not his 20B lectures. I feel as if he over complicates many topics and gets way too excited with throwing very difficult examples during lectures. Expect very difficult HW problems. I suggest finding a better professor if you're intimidated by math because he just makes it more difficult than it already is

I'm sorry but his 20b class is not what I expected. Topics overcomplicated. THE MAIN IDEA TO TAKE AWAY IS THIS: if you are not a math wiz, then there will be difficulties. Study all your 20A topics thoroughly to do well. You actually have to think about the concepts in this class and it is very difficult to keep up if you are not a math wiz
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Quarfoot is a very easygoing and enthusiastic presence in class. He loves to use relevant examples in class and is quite funny. Provides lots of practice tests which end up being similar to the actual tests. Lots of work for Math 11 but it is fairly easy.

Prof Quarfoot has the best lecture slides and really interesting and detailed lectures. He explains everything really clearly and all the examples he uses in lectures are relevant. He has two homework assignments due every week which force you to stay on track. He has free online textbook and all of his lectures are podcasted which is helpful 10/10

He's probably the most adorable professor I've ever had. You don't have to go to class since his lecture slides are enough, but I go anyway just to see him and hear his jokes. There's a lot of homework, but if you go to your TA's office hours, it's pretty manageable. His tests are reasonable as long as you study. He's really nice too.

Professor DQ was a great choice. He sets all his students up for success. Exams are straightforward even though they are more difficult than practice ones. If you put in any effort at all it's a sure pass.
DQ is one of the best professors I've had so far at UCSD! He's hilarious during lectures and actually makes learning math interesting. I would definitely take his course again!

sorry , his lecture is boring because of just clicking on the powerpoint slide , the hw need to scan out then have to turn in gradescoupe which made more work for student because the pic from scanning is just very blurry . it is just a boring class . have to code in rstudio to get good grade which it is suck since this is a math class not  cs class
Professor Quarfoot adds humor to his lectures and will keep your attention throughout the lecture. Will not bore you to sleep.

DQ is highly respected among the students and gives amazing lectures. He actually makes going to lecture something to look forward to. Discussions aren't mandatory. There are 2 hw assignments and 1 lab due every week. Get the recommended textbook that goes over the problems in the textbook, the problems in there will help you with the hw.
LOVE HIM!!!! It's never boring listening to his lecture even though it's math and I would definitely take his course again

One of the best professors I've taken! He is very clear in his lectures, providing many examples and explaining solutions step-by-step. Will often call upon students to answer questions in class. Labs and homework take a bit of time, but its great preparation for tests and the final.
He is a charismatic and funny professor. He will walk up and down the stairs and pick out students and make them talk in his mic sometimes. His lectures are clear and he posts his slides online.
Lectures are phenomenal! He makes lectures fun by actively trying to interact with the class. He shows sincere interest for the well being of his students.
y'all got me messed up this is one of the worst lecturers in the math department his lectures are over-complicated and he doesn't explain anything well in class beware and avoid at all costs
Fantaistic Professor. He gives very clear lecture and he's hilarious. I love his lectures.

We were all taking a gamble since it was his first time teaching at a university. He turned out to be an amazing professor, his points were all super clear even when the material starting getting a little difficult. Homework really reinforces what he teaches & for the first time, I actually enjoyed going to a math lecture. Definitely recommend!
An excellent professor specialized in teaching. He explains ideas very clearly and easy to understand.  Also, he helps students working on problems in class and explain how they should do this

One of the best professors I have ever had. Stats was always rough for me but DQ does an excellent job covering the material, he is very structured and passionate about what he teaches. Lectures are optional but definitely worth going to he is HILARIOUS. Often I would find myself watching his podcasts for fun! He is THAT good. Hope to have him agai
DQ is super fun and you can tell he loves what he does, you don't have to use the book but if you read it everything will be super easy
He's a funny guy and teaches really well. His lectures are also made available to the students for their access. Great help during Office hours.

His lectures are clear and he explained concepts well. Exams and homework not hard. Labs need quite much time to do. But given its a five-credit course the time spent for labs is acceptable. Good prof and educator!
Doable, just go to lecture, study, practice
FOR MATH 185!!! Professor Rava really cares about math and statistics. Not many homeworks, relevant topics on the tests, and lots of resources.

Lots of homework that doesn't translate well to exams, definitely not enough practice that is similar to exams. Lectures are clear but aren't good references for the exam either. Hard course, but there was a curve on the final grade.
This class will be HARD. The exams are not reflective of practice tests, lectures, and labs.
Difficulty of the class is overstated, just do the homework and a lot of practice tests and you'll be fine :)
There is a lot of work for this class, the exams are very lecture dense and at times can be challenging. I recommend going to office hours and studying early.

You might read this and think it can't be that bad. It is that bad. Do not take this class if you want to have peace of mind and keep your GPA. Exams were nothing like lectures, lectures were vague, so so so much homework that didn't help a ton for exams, and I would genuinely see material for the first time during an exam.
final average 50, effectively no curve. somehow an intro class. took AP stats prior to the class as well

Honestly, not amazing, but okay. A lot of students struggled probably because it's their second quarter, and this class was harder than what most expected. I felt that the lectures, homework, and past exams provided was enough to do good in the class. Slight curve of A -> A+. Should have a decent math background to succeed

I took AP Stats (+ coding) prior, so it was mostly repeat material. However, without this background, there definitely did not seem to be enough study material/review. Otherwise, I found the class commitment alright. Do note that she loves trick questions (looking at midterm #2)!! Additionally, I do not believe she curved the class (for fa25).

If your class average for both midterms is close to 48%, its time to stop being a professor and find a new job. Majority of the other math department staff average around 60-70% btw. Read the other reviews posted about her and just know that for an intro level class, there were people outside the lecture hall praying on their knees before the final
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For such a simple introductory subject, she makes content harder in everything we do outside of lecture. No easy to access reviews that reflect content, no notes posted after lecture, heavy amounts of coding that would be difficult for people with no experience in R. This professor is vague and questions during exams are tricky. Not recommended.

Not as bad as people describe her, but she makes relatively easy content much more difficult than it should be. Her lectures are decent except for her going fast and brushing over some important concepts, but her midterms and final are difficult and designed to trick you. She gave practice exams, but the real one was much harder imo. Didn't curve.

Her lectures may seem boring and repetitive, but it is very straightforward and clear. A lot of homework and the R coding require self-study, but they are very useful. The written homework and the practice exams align with the actual exams well. The heavy workload is because it is a 5-unit-course. Shouldn't blame her for that.

Most lecture content isn't reflective of what is on the exam. She teaches very basic processes and expects you to do a more complicated version of it on exams. There is a lot of homework (which is not that helpful) and labs are due once a week that aren't too bad if you've worked with R'Studio. Class is very hard and professor makes it harder.

Dont take this class please save me

Midterms are hard, questions are vague, homework and labs is tedious and unhelpful for exams, past exams arent that useful for exams, doesnt curve, and has no set letter grading policy until the very end. 

Just an unenjoyable experience for such a simple subject, UCSD please hire a new prof! :3

Class is pretty hard. You have to learn how to code by yourself and it isn't related to what's tested on the midterm and final. Podcasts everything and discussions are optional. Teaching wise she was ok but the content I just found pretty difficult. The only thing was that she doesn't curve anything and has hard cutoffs. Italian/Spanish accent too

She honestly just has a bad attitude and will disrespect you for asking simple questions. Gives coding labs that seemingly have no correlation with anything else in class and take forever because she doesn't teach how to do them. Exams are difficult and graded harshly. dtm for a class that ain't all that.
Very hard prof

RUN!!!!! Insane amount of homework. For the R code part don't teach anything in the class and don't test it on the exam. Can't understand the purpose of it. Every week have so many assignments need to do, for me who already learned about statistics, I still need 1.5hours for the statistical part and 1.5hours for the programming part.

I did not like her AT ALL. I loved her outfits because she always looked so chic, but beneath the good style, she is a tough professor. I really struggled with math, and it didn't help that we didn't have any review packets. We had to focus on the coding aspects of the class, which accounted for 40% of the class. I really struggled. Sorry

Very exam-driven lecture style: a lot of example questions during lectures. A LOT OF homework that require you to pay attention to details. Slightly unfair & strange grading criteria. Each midterm only worths 25-30 marks yet contributes ~15% of your total grade. Overall not recommended.

Order of topics was confusing, I would have done severely worse if not for doing stats in hs. Her questions are vague but rubric is strict, even for homework. Not much extra credit opportunity (only one point for midterm 2). Hw isnt put in as an assignment so does not show up on to do list on canvas, hw is in 3 different places which sucked.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Teacher does not have a set grading scale; do not know grade is until it is on your transcript. Her labs took forever and were not helpful for the tests. Discussions unhelpful. Required specific answers from general questions. Exams were harder than past exams. Didn't curve tests or final grade even with a ~50 avg midterm 2 and ~65 avg final.

Lectures are actually pretty clear, organized, and easy to follow. Labs don't really match what we do in lecture and there are a LOT of them. The workload is heavy w/ both written and online homework. For exams, she gives past exams, but the actual tests are harder. Syllabus says there's a curve, but i don't think we have this year (93 = A)

Good professor, tough class. Ask questions after lectures and sit in the front row for motivation. Study hard for midterms (especially the 2nd) and the final (do all online/written HW, lecture problems, practice materials/tests) and it's doable.

Decent lecturer, second midterm was mad difficult considering how lightly she covered the concepts tested on it. Labs have nothing to do w class, but they're easy if you've done coding before. Her late policy is buns and dropped my grade since she didn't let me make up missed work because I got off the waitlist later. An overall alright class

Ok lecturer, lectures somewhat helpful but very monotone. Labs have nothing to do with class and homeworks are long, but I think that's all MATH 11 since it's 5 units. Doesn't have a clear grading scale/cutoffs, even after the final is graded. Class was mostly just annoying. Would not take if you have other time consuming classes.

Do not take this professor if you care about your GPA; her/TAs are very strict graders. Lectures felt uninspiring and boring, and just felt like she was reading off a script. Her communication style is very cold, and be aware that your emails might just be sent to her trash can.
Nonsensical.

Homeworks were so long, despite being nothing like her tests. Labs are interesting but also nothing to do with tests. Practice exams are somehow also nothing like the actual exams. Exams ask questions about content in lecture that wasn't taught. Teacher is unfortunately also a little sassy. Overall hell and you should take it in community college.
Wrap it up 56% avg on mid2 and 67% avg on final. If u love ur gpa, don't take this class, esp bc it's a 5 unit course. No idea if there's a curve
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lab and homework sets due each week so just manage your time well. Attendance isn't mandatory but I highly recommend attending, prof is extremely nice and great at answering questions. Go to discussions!!

Written hw is reflective of exams, online hw is mainly for mastery of concepts. Nit-picky and trick MCQ on exams require specific conceptual knowledge. Weekly labs were largely unrelated to the exams but were part of the grade. Rewatch lectures and do the past exams that she provides to study for exams, as the format is similar.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class was decently hard. Midterm 1 was not bad, while Midterm 2 had an average of 56%. There is online hw, written hw, and coding labs, so the workload is extremely heavy. She does have a grade replacement plan where you can drop a midterm score and have the final weighted more. Overall, it was a decently hard class.

If you have more than 168 hours in your week, you might be fine. Coding assignments and homeworks take a ridiculous amount of time and don't actually cover the topics required to know for exams. I would recommend staying on top of studying, attending lectures, and praying you know the stuff she's gonna drop on you with no warning.
The test is not difficult as long as you review and do practice test. The instruction is clear, and all you need to do is to follow instruction, go to lecture, then you have a good grade.
pls take this at cc. midterm avg was 50%. Barely gives any practice problems and tests us on questions she barely goes over.

Honestly, Rava was a good teacher overall. She's very knowledgable in stats and does a good job of creating good lecture slides and lecture notes. The workload was pretty heavy, which can be expected for a 5 unit course, and your grade is heavily dependent on how well you do on the midterms and final. She does have a grade replacement plan, though.

Do not take her. Take this course at a cc, truly, you will thank me for the headache I saved you from doing SO MUCH damn homework and the pointless labs. Exams are difficult; the MCs are meant to trick you 99% of the time. I never felt ready for any exam; she put the hardest kinds of problems on them.
