Honest Review: Professor Denise is concise on her talking points; she emphasizes key distinctions in confusing concepts. She gets straight to the point when answering students' questions. Test questions, both mult. choice and open-ended, may be tricky. Labs are fine with help of TA. HW is at times tough b/c of its TA's nit-picky deductions.

Her class was ok, attendance isn't mandatory. Her homework is both online and written, more heavy on the online since some questions have multiple parts ranging from 2-10 parts. Also her handwriting is sometimes hard to read, u can easily confuse her 5 for (S) or 9 as a (g). she does have an accent so it might be hard to understand her sometimes.

She is ok at best. R-coding is completely unnecessary and time consuming (but I enjoyed learning it). Homework was helpful. Barely enough time for the midterms and you are expected to really know the concepts. Her lectures were great and informative. Attendance optional but HIGHLY RECOMMENDED. DONT SKIP or you're cooked. 🥀💔

The class has three main assignments: R-coding labs, Pearson online homework, and written homework. Workload was manageable with about two assignments a week, but the labs felt pointless since R isn't even tested on. The professor reads quickly, her 9s look like Gs, and the second midterm was brutal with no curve. Take this at community college!

Her lectures are organized, and she is patient when answering questions. So long as you are on pace or stay ahead, you will be fine.

There are three main homework assignments (a lab coding assignment, online homework through Pearson, and written homework) that take time, so prepare for that. Exams have tricky wording and trip many students up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Might be the first class I fail at UCSD since transferring. Prof reads and quickly guides through easy problems in class, but places difficult/tricky problems on exams. Exam 2 might as well had been written in a different language. PLEASE avoid this prof if you care about your GPA, I regret taking her sm

All she does i read the slides and then gives you a shit ton of homework every week, and her TA's are  a-holes and stingy with the grading. Take another teacher. Second midterm straight out of hell and does NOT curve anything. Lwk fire her ass. The coding part of the class is so unnecessary.

nice person & lectures easy to follow. but when i say take math 11 at cc, do it. its turkey break but she assigned work to do. its the same type of work we are assigned every week, but it's tedious and takes kinda long. i want to relax at home but cant. middies r alright. 2nd one was difficult, mean was 56%. i regret taking this course here

She is very organized in her lectures, BUT that's because she usually reads from her notes when lecturing, sometimes making her lectures not seem engaging. Plus, she might not seem very easy to approach. 
Her exams are tricky and focus a lot on the details; therefore, the average scores for the exams are often very low (midterm 2 avg 56%).
take stats at community college not here.

She was a pretty good professor. The class itself was pretty easy and she did cover all the content from exams. There is definitely a lot of work outside class with homework and labs every week, but that's just part of the class.

I remember the labs&homework were always a drag to do.There was so many things to do in that class,but if it helps I did them all the day they were due,so def manageable.I rarely went to lecture but put in loads of effort,curves significantly help I got a D on both the final&midterm but an A+ on the homework,labs&1st midterm, it all balances out.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Rava was the course coordinator for Math 11 this quarter, despite not having taught any sessions whatsoever. The entire course was taught by John Peca-Medlin, and she went out of her way to make sure the grade averages in our course were sub-par by prohibiting any significant grade-scale shift. It's clear she has no sympathy for students whatsoever

THE WORST professor at UCSD. If you decide to take a class and see rava as the professor, avoid her like the plague. Even if it means you need to take an extra quarter it's worth the money. Decided to go no cheat sheets for the class then made finals harder than previous finals. Rather sell my soul to the devil than take her again.

Huge majority of grade from tests. Recorded lectures with good explanation and intuition of topics. Good quality lecture notes and slides, although the updated slides were not posted after each class, but accessible through recordings. Class subject was hard, but she made things understandable. Proof heavy on tests, but all proofs were from lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class content is hard, but to me her lectures and logic were easy to follow. Homework problem sets were difficult, especially R questions, but tests were easier. The tests were also fair and tended to cover the main topics we covered in class, it's not like she asked questions on niche topics. Overall a solid professor

Honestly, one of the worst professors I've had at UCSD. I did well on the midterm and all homeworks, but Rava's lectures are useless; I educated myself on 99% of the material. Avoid at all costs, and if you're forced to take 181B with her, good luck.

Expected a lot out of this person.  Unfortunately, very underwhelming; lectures were unnecessarily dense and rushed over critical content while focusing on totally useless work (i.e. continually redefining what it means to reject a null hypothesis but glossing over how distribution proofs work).  Absolutely not her fault, but hard to understand :(

Her lectures are ok, hard to understand at times. I dont think shes a bad lecturer at all, but the exams were not really as reflective of the practice ones, though some questions were similar. Shes not a bad professor, but just take note that the average is a C+, and there's hardly a curve. Just make sure you prioritize this over any other class.

I honestly found Professor Rava to be great as the podcasts are now completely recorded and the tests were reflective of the material in class. If people did the previous years midterms and finals and studied the in class questions, the tests are really not that hard. Good lecturer

Solid professor, personally not a big fan. everything you need to know to pass this class is in the lectures and homeworks. Her class was so hard! it takes studying every single detail to pass this class, there is no question that she won't throw at you. So careful w tests which consist of 1midterm and 1final, makes up about 80% of final grade.

Lectures are helpful to attend however first part of course is very similar to AP Stats. Professor is super sweet and goes slowly during class, taking time to answer students' questions. Wording on tests can be VERY tricky and midterms/final often do not mimic practice tests (though they are helpful for studying). Workload is extremely manageable.

The workload isn't bad at all (anybody who says it is lacks time management skills). Lectures can be a bit confusing and sometimes she will contradict herself. She gives you practice exams to study and they are super helpful so use those to your advantage. If you have taken AP Stats before, this course should be a breeze--it is a lot of review.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Attendance is not mandatory, but lectures are very helpful, especially because she only has audio podcasts. Grading is not super strict, but pay attention to how she wants you to word your answers. Overall, not the worst teacher, and the class is relatively easy.
Attending classes is very helpful as she does not video podcast, only audio. Also, be mindful of exact wording in answers because she can be picky.

Lectures were very clear and correlated to what will be asked on homework/midterm/final. She said something in lectures regarding the material and that same comment showed up as a question on the midterm. So long as you show up to class, show up to discussions, and do the homework AND PRACTICE THE PROOFS, you will do fine

All around solid 9/10

She has a good command over the material. Mathematical statistics is hard, so do not underestimate the assignments and exams. This class is difficult, but I like her lectures. The assignments are representative of the lectures, but be very careful on exams because those are more challenging. I would recommend if you're looking for a challenge.

Her lectures are very organized and connected each topic really well. Will post annotated slides, lecture audio, and past exams on canvas for review. Will show how to solve sample problems during class. Super sweet and patient if you go ask her questions after class. The workload is a bit heavy, but it's manageable once you get used to it.

Rava's a great lecturer and made topics much easier to follow. She posts podcasts, annotated slides, and past exams which are all super useful to use when studying. The workload is insane (weekly lab, written/online hw) but kinda understandable since the class is 5 units. She lowk seems scary via her emails/Canvas but in-person she's super sweet!

Personally could not follow lectures (feels very slow to me), though annotated lecture slides were very helpful in studying. This class is easy enough to self-study and do well. Has a heavy workload (due to labs taking a lot of time), but is manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Rava's lecture slides are simple and easy to understand. She posts annotated slides but not recorded lectures. Her tests are mostly FRQ with only a few MCQ and follow examples from her lecture slides, making it easy to answer if you practice. Homework got really heavy at the end of the quarter and discussions were mandatory with 2 free absences.

Insane, but manageable workload. Rava is a great lecturer and is always open to questions. Learned a lot about stats. Lectures not recorded, but annotated slides uploaded. PLEASE, use her, and especially the lab TA's Office hours (both on Zoom) and you'll succeed in this class. drops lowest hw, lab, and 2 discussion. Very caring and sweet imo.
Worst professor in UCSD stats courses. Terrible lectures, no annotated slides, no grade round up and bad attitudes to students. Midterm and final are very proof-heavy and take up 60% of the grades.

Seriously, is she the only Math 11 professor at UCSD? Because if that's the case then we are all screwed. She is literally the worst professor ever. I understand it is a 5 unit course, but man the workload is insane.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Insane workload and the HWs have nothing to do with each other and the tests nothing like the HWs. It is nearly impossible to finish the exams in the time allotted as there's about 60 questions to answer in 50 mins. She said on the first lecture not to email her with any questions and she's not accessible outside of class

She does not podcast lectures but even if you dont go, she uploads her annotated slides to canvas. There are 2 midterms and a final with two final grade options to include one or both midterms with the final grade weighted differently for each option. Lectures were not to hard to digest. Lots of hw bc its a 5 unit class not hard its time consuming.

bruh she was BAD. I took her first quarter and my class failed both midterms (second scored a 58% avg.) and wouldn't curve! lectures are boring and there is SM hw. I scored a 5 on both calc ab and bc so im pretty good at math but struggled hard in this class. failed both midterms (below 50) and had to pull a 90% to get a B.

Professor Rava provides poor explanations of concepts and assigns an insane workload. The labs, written homework, and online homework have nothing to do with each other and do not correlate. Exams are filled with grammatical mistakes that make just reading questions difficult and are filled with trick questions. TAs made frequent grading mistakes.

Her lectures are very organized and concepts are easy to understand. I spent ~3 hrs for labs and 2-4 hrs for homework weekly, and both help you understand lecture materials. She also gives you a bunch of practice exams that prepare you well for the tests. It can be a lot of work if you start to procrastinate, but it's not that hard.

Stats is not real math.
Shoutout to her a**hole TAs who graded everything and took off points for the smallest reason.
Very good math professor; the class was a time sink, though. Make sure you're not taking too many credits when you're taking math 11 cause I spent like 10-15hr outside of class every week :(((
Genuinely hated this class. Lots of homework (double the amount on week 10), two midterms, mandatory discussion attendance, and a final.

Genuinely don't know why she is rated so low, I thought she was great. Her exams are very similar to the practice exams (she gives you the one from the previous quarter/year) and though the labs are a lot of work, it's not super difficult to get through. I definitely recommend her

"the f...  is that"
mandetory discussion

The material isn't bad and you'll be fine as long as you go through the lecture notes, but the grading isn't very merciful. There's only one midterm and no curve. I did poorly on the midterm, but got A's on the homeworks and the final, yet ended up with an 89 and she wouldn't bump it up. You're out of luck if you don't do well on the midterm.

Lectures are disorganized and incomprehensible, no Piazza, no professor office hours, and doesn't even post annotated lecture slides to Canvas. Homeworks are also poorly worded and graded entirely for accuracy. Grading scheme is also very unforgiving as there's only one midterm and a final that are each worth a huge part of your grade. Ridiculous

It's a 5-unit course so all the labs and homework are expected. Labs and homework grades raised my grade up a lot so they're important to complete. She is a really sweet person and the practice exams she posts from past quarters are practically the exam, which makes the exams really easy if you study using those. I would definitely take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Weekly homework & labs that take a lot of time and feel repetitive. She drops your lowest for each. 2 grading schemes (2 midterms + final or 1 midterm + final). Exams are extremely similar to practice exams, so if you do those you will be well-prepared. Lectures are digestible. The calculus involved is not hard, and is only used for 2 topics.

5-unit class, so it's a lot of assignments (homework and labs weekly), but the exams are representative of lectures and homework (she gives practice exams as well). Lectures are easy to digest. Graded on two midterms, final, homework, and labs. Two different grading schemes, the alternative one has dropped midterm and a higher-graded final.

I recommend Professor Rava--she gives informative lectures in her 40-minute timeframe while encouraging questions throughout. The Professor taught statistics straightforwardly and understandably. There are two midterms, making studying for the final much easier. There is an extensive formula sheet, so it is more application than memorization.

Very fair professor.  I found lectures to be very clear and the class was very organized.  Midterms and final make your grade and labs are very time consuming, but the class is 5 units and I found the tests to be fair (not easy, but fair). She was also very kind and seemed to care about our understanding.  I would definitely take her again!
easy to understand lectures. attendance is graded. homework assignments are time consuming (it's 5 units), but not particularly difficult. very similar to ap stats in terms of material

Do not skip the lectures! They are important to understanding the material and getting good grades. There is a lot of homework - do not procrastinate. I didn't attend discussion, but you should if you have questions. Don't take her quizzes lightly, they are not easy. Don't skip out anything and you can get a good grade. Not overly difficult.

Her midterms and finals are really fair and almost identical to lecture material and practice. She is understanding. Class is 5 units and hence there is a lot of work but she helps you out whenever needed and is always willing to listen. Lectures are worth going to. Amazing prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Math 11 consists of a lot of work, so choosing this class is a time investment. However, her midterms and exams are pretty fair because she gives practice exams that are almost identical to the ones you are going to take. No cheat sheet on her tests and all of them were in person.

The labs and homework are incredibly time-consuming, most frustrating thing about the course is that only certain parts of the assignments get graded rather than everything. She always asks for questions during lectures and the old exams are pretty much the same as the current ones. Not the greatest professor, but solid.
Many labs and assignments. Midterms and finals completely make or break your grade. Don't recommend it unless you're trying to lower your GPA.

Doing well on all exams and the course is impossible without being proactive on Homework deadlines, and the course becomes a joke otherwise since the material builds on itself. Time consuming labs require visual experimentation and conclusions (not tested on), while the Homeworks def require outside learning. AP Stats book and Khan helped a lot

It is a 5 unit class. The HW and the Labs are pretty time-consuming and graded on correctness, I would make sure you do well on those as they make up 15% and 20% of your grade. As for the midterms and finals, they were similar to the practice tests Professor provided. Just make sure you understand the concepts and you should be good.

I was fine w/ this class til it hit me that the final was worth 35% of our grade..Im about to graduate & have taken many classes where the final was worth A LOT but only b/c we didnt get hw. The hw/labs take so long to do so I dont get why it contributes so little. I had a solid A all quarter & a B- on the final dropped me a letter grade.

The homework and labs do take some time to complete, but they are not terribly difficult. TAs will help a lot with lab questions, so go to office hours to get your work checked. Lectures are clear and slides are informative. DO THE PRACTICE EXAMS! They are the same as the midterms and finals.

Thee professor makes the subject quite interesting and makes it easy to learn. HW, lectures and practice materials representative of lecture. This class is 5 units and a lot of work so be prepared! The only problem is that there is no extra credit or late submissions. Love the prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Unlike the previous comments, I felt that this professor made this class a lot more bearable than it is. Math 11 itself is a class that is very heavy as it involves a lot of work. However, she always responded to emails, was very approachable and a good lecturer. Midterms and finals were very similar to lecture material and the practice questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There is too much homework and they're all graded by correctness, you'll get burnt out very quickly from the sheer amount. Not including the labs in addition to lengthy homework problems both in the textbook and online. Trying to maintain a decent grade is so unbelievably hard that doing your best doesn't get you anywhere in this class.

The mean score of one of the midterms was 63%. If that doesn't say enough, I don't know what else will. The examples she provides in class are also so simplified in comparison to the homework and test questions. She is also insanely strict with her tests, as thinks everyone is trying to cheat.

Boring lectures, lots of work outside of class, homework and online labs combined are worth more than the 2 midterms. Provides practice exams with questions that are exactly like the real exam, just different numbers. However, final grade in the class is based off how you perform relative to the peers in your class rather than normal grading scale.

Stats itself is not hard to understand, but the way she teaches it is insanely confusing. Labs and homework are so time consuming and no proper feedback on why answers are wrong. None of our assignments are dropped and no late work is accepted. Absolutely no accommodations for students during the pandemic. Has no empathy for her students.

i do work for this class every single day and i'm not even a stem major. content is incomprehensible unless you're teaching yourself and even then, good luck. it's a class where you don't even know how to ask for help because you just don't know.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: other than that she has a little accent, all of her classes are organized designed. Super clear slides. I learned a lot and get interested in learning more about statistic analysis thanks to this professor. pretty with a caring heart. If you work hard you can get an A+. exam suppose to check only what you learned in class ,nothing she didn't cover

MATH 11 with Rava is a pretty easy A, but there is a lot of busy work (it is a 5 credit class). There is 1 textbook hw assignment and 1 lab due every week (both graded for correctness), which total to roughly 4-5 hours of work. The tests are free-response and pretty easy, especially if you attend the lectures to know what's important for studying.

This class has NO late policy, NO dropped exams. 1 or 2 missing assignments and you're struggling for a C. Heavy workload even for a 5 credit class, especially being online. Long weekly homework assignments and weekly labs. Inflexible and not accommodating of her students at all! The content isn't too difficult, but the class is awful. Frustrating!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 5 credit class that's as much effort and time as two 4 unit classes. Would not take again.

Tests are very fair and representative of the material, and she provides a lot of practice in the homework and with practice midterms that are basically the same as what you would see on the test. Grades pretty particularly, but that is just stats in general, once you memorize it, pretty easy. Also gives a formula sheet that is SO helpful for exams

Grades are based on labs, written hw, midterms, and final. (No assignments are dropped and no extra credit opportunities are given.) Final is 35 percent of your grade, with no curve. No accomodations were made considering the difficult transition students face from online to in person courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: SUPER HARD and SUPER not accommodating at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Kane is probably hands down the greatest professor at UCSD. He is definitely one of the smartest and there is a ton to learn from him. 101 is a very difficult class but you learn so much from him that will carry you later in your career.

It's one of those classes that covers a lot of material but at the same time requires that you can think/develop an algorithm that solves the problem. Prof. Kane walks you through how to develop these algorithms, and many test problems are essentially similar to the derivation taught in class with slight modifications. Very inspirational class.

Take CSE101 with Kane if you really want to learn and be pushed to your limit. It's one of the most important and transformative classes you can take as a CS major at UCSD. A class that you'll actually remember years later and be grateful that you took it. It also just helps with everything else once you've taken it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he's clearly a very smart guy, but not a great lecturer in my opinion: his explanations usually aren't too clear or organized and he often overcomplicates it. his grading is quite harsh too and the rubrics aren't always clear either, however there's a gigantic curve at the end which is nice

Daniel Kane is brilliant and down to earth. His lectures might require you to rewatch it again to understand but he's a thorough lecturer. Prepare to spend a lot of time on the HWs since they're proof based, but the exams are leagues easier than HW and he has a generous curve. I would take a class just because he's my prof
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kane is by far the most brilliant professor and just instructor in general I've had in my life (no joke). His homeworks and tests are very difficult especially the proof parts but there's always a significant curve at the end. He does tend to go fast and go deep into things during lectures which most cant follow but hes such a great guy overall.

The class has a harsh grading scheme, the grading criteria isnt very clear it is just "justifiable" for proofs. The prof himself is really good but his lectures arent super clear, he writes and moves on fast but he is also open to even fundamental questions so that is good. His grading criteria is tough but he also gives a heavy curve

tests were quite challenging and the homework was also incredibly difficult, but i do feel like his lectures were thorough and i liked how accessible he was over discord. i got a 28 on the first midterm and ended with a B+ in the class. it required a lot of effort but he is a great teacher. trust the curve + partial credit too

A late review. Professor Kane' lectures are great and his homework is inspirational(hard as well). I took his MATH184 and intentionally chose him again. He is very accessible and nice after class, in OH, and on discord despite being a math prodigy. His class is the best choice if you are ok with challenges and really want to learn something.
Incredibly difficult tests, but I feel like I learnt a lot. Get ready to spend a long time studying and doing homeworks, but you will really understand the content.

Kane is a great professor but MAN, is he a workload. Take his classes if you want to learn -- your grade might be in danger, but trust me, it'll make you think like few other classes have before. Fantastic lecturer who's very available through Piazza and Discord.
He designed the content to be hard, but I would definitely recommend students who like to challenge difficult work to take this class.

He definitely spends a lot of time coming up hw questions because they are just extremely hard to the point I spend three days and still get the wrong answer. I highly recommend this professor to those who want to struggle the whole quarter and learn a lot at the same time.

His class is amazing in terms of the difficulty and level of commitment you need to put into it. I feel I am so dumb by taking this class because I struggle with hw every week which is only worth 3%. However, once you figure out how to do a particular problem, you will feel everything is so rewarding in the class. Come if you want to learn!

extremely hard, I have taken his math 154 before and swore not to take it again, but I have to graduate with one last major course, cse 101 this quarter and only he taught this class. Really Really depressed

Professor Kane gives really amazing and engaging lectures. Although the homeworks are somewhat challenging, they really make you think deeply about the materials and help you have a solid understanding of combinatorics. Exams are much easier than homework and totally doable. I will definitely take his class again.

Professor Kane is a wonderful choice if you bear strong interest in mathematics and would like to embrace challenges. His homework is very hard and inspirational, and it usually takes me more than 3 hours to solve 3-4 problems. However, his lectures are amazing and his exams are doable. He is very accessible outside classes.

Professor Kane clearly has a strong grasp of the material that he is teaching and expects the students to gain a very rigrous understanding of the course material. However, he sometimes moves too fast during lectures and his homeworks and exams are both very difficult. Take his class if you're up for a challenge and want to learn a lot.

One of the hardest class I've taken in my 4 years here in this school. Even-though he curves his course by a huge margin, prepare to spend at least 10 hours for his homework because they are really heavy in the proofs. Tests are extremely hard. Requires every student to take the exam in-person during the pandemic. Very unforgiving

One of the hardest class I've taken in my 4 years here in this school. Even-though he curves his course by a huge margin, prepare to spend at least 10 hours for his homework because they are really heavy in the proofs. Tests are extremely hard. Requires every student to take the exam in-person during the pandemic.

Kane's class was not easy, but completely worth it. His homeworks and exams are extremely hard but he makes up for it with a generous curve. This class improved my understanding of algorithms a lot. It also helped me solve problems in coding interview questions. If you want to leave this class mastering algorithms, I would highly recommend Kane.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Does not structure his lectures at all. No notes given. Impatient with students' questions.

To me, Professor Kane's class was very challenging; both homework and exam material are difficult. However, his lectures are very clear and you can tell that he is very knowledgeable on the material himself. He is accessible through office hours and Piazza and is always willing to help students.
He makes the homework extremely difficult with very minimal preparation, and his solutions are extremely convoluted and difficult to follow. I do not think he should be teaching this course.

first, google him and read the wiki page about how he was a math prodigy by 3rd grade then consider if you can keep up w him trying to teach a bunch of ppl elementary statistics. His lectures are entertaining but easy to get lost considering his brain works so well it doesnt have to explain each step slowly or go over processes more than once.

He's very smart, but not the best at lecturing. His handwriting can get messy, but he acknowledges that and does his best. He can get a little hard to follow but does his best to clarify things. He also pretty cute imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is extremely smart and kind, he is energetic, young and passionate. However, he is too smart to be a great professor as he teaching pace is very fast, I sometimes can't follow his logic quite well(probably because I am dumb). He doesn't use or have a lot of online sources as well, so the only way to learn is to attend lectures.
I have never such professor. What ever I speak for him is even less. He is the best of best. I even watch his video mulitple times to gain more and more. He is best................

The professor always has a lot of accessibility during office hours and on Piazza. His lectures are a bit messy but they always have an elegant explanation and shows he's not just reading from a textbook. Questions are challenging, but rewarding since they go beyond just boring textbook questions and he writes them himself.

Daniel Kane is someone I really look up to. He actually cares a lot about his students. He tries to be really nice and always says "welcome!" whenever someone comes to his office hours. Daniel is so smart its kinda scary. When you talk to him, he just looks you in the eye and its absolutely terrifying. Also hes pretty attractive

Prof Kane is a mathematical prodigy. I love his class. I learned so much. Sometimes when I see his handwriting I think his brain thinks way too fast and his hand just cannot catch up with his thoughts so he scribbles. It is kind of intimidating to talk to him because he is so smart. His class is one my fav at UCSD. I wouldnt want it any other way!

Professor Kane is very intelligent, but he is a bad lecturer. He is very unorganized and messy in his explanation of concepts, making it very hard for anyone to understand. On top of that, he has exams where the average is around 60, and the homework is also very difficult, so much so that you end up understanding nothing. Don't take him.

Professor Kane is clearly a very intelligent person; however, the way he portrays information in his lectures was messy and unorganized. He never gave substantial examples during class, and his tests did not reflect any practice provided. The class doesn't have to be hard but he made it unnecessarily difficult.
Really bad professor, he doesn't care about students.

Kane's lectures consist of him scrawling on the chalkboard things that don't make sense. He's a nice guy, but not a great teacher. His explanations were confusing, answers to our questions on Piazza weren't helpful, homework was also time consuming. Unlike other stats classes that had online homework, we had pdfs sent out. Labs were fine though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you've taken AP Stats before, MATH 11 is just a regurgitation of it. Kane only writes on the blackboard, but he does post voice-only podcasts. The tests are doable and are similar to the homework packets. He's not a bad or good choice, but he can be boring while he's deriving formulas for 15-30 minutes.

Professor Kane's grading policy was in my opinion unfair to students. HW was due twice per week, where roughly 20 problems were assigned, but only 5 were graded. As a result, if one was wrong, then 20% of hw credit was lost. On one occasion, Professor even told me that I would not get credit even though my answer was right for "consistency."

His classes may sometimes feel fast paced and confusing.. He doesn't cover sums/examples much in class, but he does go over the concepts clearly which is definitely useful. Lecture isn't mandatory, but he teaches on the blackboard.. Very approachable and easy to interact with; definitely recommend!
Great but hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Sometimes confusing presentation (he needs to use less verbs and just get to the point), but made up for it by being really nice during office hours.  Also, I had a bit of a crush on him (Dr. Kane is pretty darn cute) so helped me focus :)

Professor Kane might be one of the smartest professors you would ever meet in UCSD. That being said, his homework is really challenging that you will need to go to his office hour. The midterms and finals are also hard and midterm is actually a lot harder because you will need to solve 3 questions in 45 minutes. Take him if you really want to learn

Took him for Math 184, and honestly one of the best lecturers I've had. It is difficult material and he is extremely smart, but he was able to present the material clear and make it easy to understand.  Listened to podcast like bible before the final, and was able to get a A+ without too much work. Really want to take CSE 101 with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a great lecturer - very enthusiastic, clearly knows what he's talking about, and explains concepts in a way that helps you understand WHY. He goes through a logical progression for how to approach and solve a problem, which is extremely important for figuring out homework/tests. His tests are difficult, but he curves the class VERY generously.

Professor Kane is brilliant - you have to give him that. However, he might be "so" brilliant that it's hard for students to follow/comprehend what he's teaching.  He goes through things very fast and it's easy to get lost in lecture. It also doesn't help that his handwriting is barely legible. Homework and exams, though curved, are very difficult.

Daniel Kane is a great professor. He is a very clear lecturer, which is good because the material is tough and requires a deep understanding to answer questions of any real substance. If you get distracted and look at your phone for a few minutes, though, you may find yourself very lost. His tests are very hard, but he curves the class heavily.

Has high expectations from his students but doesn't set them up with any realistic hopes of meeting them. Homework can be fairly difficult at times but doable given enough time. Tests on the other hand are very difficult. IMO his style of teaching unfairly rewards those who are more talented/clever vs those who might be more hardworking..

Very enthusiastic lecturer - does a good job of explaining the basic concepts of each chapter. However, his tests and homework assignments are very difficult and he doesn't help bridge the gap between the basics and the deep understanding required by them. I think he's better suited to teach grad students than undergrads.
Tests do not match homework, kinda assumes everyone knows what he's talking about. Should stick more to research and contributions to the mathematical world.

He was definitely passionate about teaching, but being his first quarter, we kinda jammed a lot of concepts lecture to lecture and sort of just sprinted through them. His homework was MUCH tougher than the exams; we had an average of around 60ish for each exam. Curve was very generous though, otherwise half the class would have failed.

He's not a bad guy, the curve helped alot. But frankly the average was in the low 60's and the questions weren't clear. Lectures weren't useful because he just rushed through algorithms and expected you to know them whether he was clear or not. Other students somehow knew exactly what would be on the test beforehand too, throwing the curve. :

Professor O'Keefe's course was well-structured and straightforward. Each week we watched a lecture video followed by a discussion post and quiz. The discussion topics encouraged deeper thinking, and the final project allowed for a lot of creativity. Clear expectations make the class manageable and rewarding.

Professor O'Keefe is great! He is easy going with his grading, responds quickly with his emails, and provides great lectures. His quizzes and exams are based on lecture videos. Overall, great professor!

Dr. O'Keefe is a great professor. He is very responsive and cares about his students. The course format allows students to explore topics of interest via the weekly discussions and optional extra credit reports. He grades fairly, and the lectures aligned well with the textbook. I would recommend this Genetics course.

Dr. O'keefe is amazing. He gives great feedback, plenty of opportunity to excel and cares about his students. His style of instruction encourages thoughtful discourse and maximum retention of course material. He is very accessible, grades fairly and in a timely manner. One of the most compassionate professors I've ever had.

Prof.O'Keefe is very knowledgable and patient. He replies to the questions with detailed information as soon as possible. Assignment grading is never late and always fair. The class is engagig specially the weekly discussions. Extra credit reports are a good chance to improve your grade. Really enjoyed the genetics class over summer.

I have taken over five courses with Professor Fisk. He is truly one of the best, if not the best professor in the Poli Sci department. Great for a GPA boost as well. Grade is based on attendance and two essays. Essays are very simple and based on class content. TA's do matter but I haven't had any bad experiences. Definitely recommend.

Class covered a lot of stuff in a small amount of time, total grade based only on attendance and two essays. Professor Fisk is very passionate about what he teaches, and makes sure to engage the students during every lecture. This is one of his more difficult classes due to the amount of content it contains however.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Straight forward class with 2 essays and participation (attendance) graded. Would definitely take it again. I would just reccommend doing the readings to prepare for the essay examinations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I Like him but the TA's are tough graders.
Great professor
Incompetent and unprofessional professor. My grade wasn't recorded properly on my transcript, and he doesn't respond to emails. The class wasn't difficult... but first time facing this

An amazing professor who I would definitely take again. Grade is based on attendance and two 6-8 page essays, and prompts are released weeks in advance. A decent amount of readings, but definitely manageable; ~30-50 pages a week. TAs can be unpredictable graders so maybe just go to their OH before the midterm. Otherwise, a perfect poli sci class!
Great Professor, both the midterm and final are essays that you are given 2 weeks to complete. Apart from that, you need a clicker remote and to be present at lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Professor Fisk's class! He's very passionate and informed on the subject + he does a great job  tying in current events to themes in the course. Attendance is measured witch iclickers but there's a lot of leniency imo. Two essays, clear criteria. TA feedback can be a little vague but they're very approachable in case of questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I couldn't keep up with this class. There's a lot of info to absorb and it depends on your TA's grading. Two essays for the midterm and final are 6-8 pages and attendance is mandatory. I hardly did the readings and managed to get a B+. I would not take him again, but I am giving him 4 stars because he was a nice person and wanted us to succeed.

Professor Fisk is a great professor-- very knowledgeable and easy to talk to, and a good lecturer. I also took him for POLI135 and loved the course, but I would recommend not taking 120H unless you're really passionate about it. I didn't think the lectures were as interesting in this course. Grading can feel arbitrary sometimes too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors on campus. Very passionate about what he teaches and wants his students to grasp the content. Love his suits. Grade was based on iclicker participation, 2 essays (1 midterm and a final). On that front, I would say Fisk is a great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof.Fisk was a good lecturer. He was very engaging during class, spoke very clearly, and was very knowledgeable in the coursework. He encouraged class discussion and class participation. Made the coursework very engaging. Fair grader and overall one of my favorite profs since being at UCSD.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: interesting class and graded fairly-- 20% attendance and 80% two essays. you get the essays early and the guidelines are clear. only thing is that there is no feedback and grading seems to be a bit arbitrary, so I would recommend going to office hours. still a great class overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: great prof. I have taken him 4 times now. his structure of grading is always the same. 40%midterm essay, 40%final, 20% clicker. its a nice class because you dont have to do any homework except write two 6 page essays the whole quarter. grading is pretty fair if you write a decent essay and use quotes/refferences from the books. i didnt read at all

Fisk is a solid POLI prof. His grading scheme is always the same with 40%midterm paper, 40%final paper, and 20%iClicker. As long as you go to class and pay attention you will be fine. There is reading but you can get away with skimming right before you write your papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Fisk is a good professor. His classes though only consist of lectures and they can drag sometimes so take the class if the topic interests you. He grades on participation through iclickers. Two essays.

Fisk is a great class to take. Personally, I don't enjoy POLI classes but I have to take them so if you are like me then take Fisk. 40% midterm paper and 40%final paper. no tests. just papers. 20% for Iclicker participation. super easy. I didn't pay much attention in class... Like at all and still got an A-. No homework just essays. go to class
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fisk is one of the best profs. at UCSD. His lectures are dense, but the grading is pretty straightforward. Grading based on clicker participation, a midterm essay, and a final essay. I had him for poli 126 and 120 and used the same criteria. A is very easy to obtain if you read the slides and know how to make an academic argument. GO FOR HIM!

Take as many of his classes as you can. I dreaded this class and thought it would be boring, but professor Fisk made the material interesting. He gives good lectures and creates an environment where it's easy to ask questions. Clicker is a decent chunk of the grade, so make sure you attend. The rest of the grade is 2 easy papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved taking Professor Fisk's course as he is a very personable and easygoing Professor. Make sure to attend at least 80% of the lectures as he uses iClicker as a form of participation and therefore is a major part of your grade. His midterm and finals are papers but as long as you read/paid attention, you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best professors in the political science department. Definitely cares about teaching and lectures are really interesting. He is always open to provide feedback and give career advice. He is one of the reasons I am pursuing grad school. I tried to take all the classes he taught.

Dr. Fisk is the best professor I have ever had. I often visit his office hours, and he is super inspirational. I really like his lecturing style, which he often pause and ask students for any questions. The class participation energy was super good because it helped to to understand the materials better. TA graded paper responsibly too.

Good prof. I took INTL 102. 1 midterm(35%) 1 final(35%). Both essays-not in-person exams. lecture clicker 15%. Section (15%). Pretty easy class if you go to lecture and discussion section. Kinda boring. lectures were a little boring but its easy. Prof is good. easy A if he put effort into the two essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I saw a lot of posts from Covid that said his lectures are out of date but he usually updates the lecture handouts with more accurate information. He always explains why he's using older lectures since much of the basic material is the same. He is very prompt with feedback and questions. Also, he will make time for you if you cant make office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The professor posted old lectures from over a year ago and it felt like he used covid as an excuse to barely do anything for the class. Due to the outdated information and lack of acknowledgment of how covid affected topics discussed in class I feel like the class was not helpful and the lack of effort by the professor was discouraging.

I've taken multiple classes with Dr. Fisk and can say that he is one of the most fair UCSD Political Science professors. You can tell that he cares about the material and is extremely helpful if you have questions and want to go to office hours.
Lectures were from previous quarters. Very lecture heavy with a lot of content that may seem disorganized if not familiar with EU concepts.
He's probably a fine professor but he took COVID as an excuse to be lazy. Posted outdated lectures that didn't accurately represent current EU Foreign Policy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fisk is the best professor at UCSD. I took him over summer and his class was great. We had weekly discussions, a midterm paper, and a final paper. He was always accessible, took the time to answer all my q's during office hours and sometimes just talk. It is clear he is passionate about what he teaches and really cares about his students.
One of the best in the department. Super nice, approachable, and knowledgeable. No nonsense classes that welcome discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took Professor Fisk and I have no complaints. He is exceptionally knowledgeable on a wide variety of topics. Fisk also encourages discussion both inside and outside the classroom. Class is pretty standard, two papers make up most of the grade. Grading is straight forward. Go to class and read and you wont have anything to complain about.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: My favorite Poli professor at UCSD. Engaging lectures even when the subject can be super dry, and he's very understanding of any issues. Two papers and clicker points are all you're graded by, but they aren't horribly tough on grading the papers, and getting the clicker points is as easy as showing up.

David Fisk is a great professor! I dealt with a difficult issue with my midterm but he was very accommodating and understanding. He is super kind and it is clear that he loves what he does. It is easy to interact with him in class too. There are a lot of readings which can be frustrating since we read them all at the same time, but they aren't hard
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: One of the best Poli Sci professor's I've had. Clear, concise, and entertaining lecturer even when the content is boring as paint drying. Seems like a super pleasant person too, and extremely helpful with questions and grade-related issues.

Fisk truly cares about his students and does not over complicate the material. If you go to class and read, you'll do well on the 2 assignments which consist of a midterm paper and a final paper. Lectures are super interesting and Professor Fisk is very knowledgable, approachable, and helpful.

Very good professor who does his best to provide as much information on a topic as possible. Addresses opinions from all sides, rarely puts in his own opinion, and encourages others to disagree and to voice their own opinions. Two papers, 6-8 pages long, that are easy enough if you follow the rubric and know the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: standard poli sci lectures and 2 semi-big papers
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Fisk is a great professor. This class is pretty good. 90% of the grade comes from two papers, with clear prompts and plenty of time to write. Nothing surprising from this class, lectures are based on the book, and Fisk is easy to listen to. Show up, read the books, put some effort into the papers, and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Fisk is an outstanding lecturer. He would explain things thoroughly and was very helpful. There's only a clicker and 2 papers in the class. I found that the papers were graded quite harshly. Overall, take his class if you want to learn a lot about the EU and like to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really great lecturer, easy to understand and enjoyable to attend hs classes, very willing to explain/clarify and answer questions.  Usually only 2 assignments, with lots of reading, but not particularly tough.

Mr. Fisk is a superlative professor. His United States foreign policy class is the most enjoyable course I have taken thus far in college by a wide margin. The subject matter is infinitely interesting, and each day the lectures were cogent, clear, and engaging. A must take for international relations students and those curious about the field.
Really good lectures that allowed for questions and engagement

This class started off great and ended well. He makes his lectures fun and interesting, he helps you as long as you ask for it, and will always be blunt. He answers questions, and ensure's that everyone understands the material. Easy and enjoyable class if you pay attention and try.
Dr. Fisk is an amazing professor. He is clearly passionate and knowledgable about foreign policy and international politics. I learned a lot in this class. I will definitely be taking him again.

Really awesome Prof. Super good lectures, he podcasts, comes in handy when flu season comes around. 2 papers graded by TAs. Type notes or re-listen to podcasts, talks fast. Power points useful for writing essays. At least skim all reading, interesting for the most part.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: FISK IS AWESOME! Grades depend on one midterm and one final, and of course how much your TA loves your paper. I've taken 3 of his classes so far and think he's probably one of the best profs at UCSD. You actually learn stuff (unlike Magagna, where you never show up lol) and are surrounded by students who are passionate about international relations
passionate but really dry and not super helpful when you don't understand something - super boring class
He talks really fast so its impossible to take notes by hand, but he does podcast. He is really knowledgeable. Papers really make you think.

Fisk is always interesting and really makes it worth going to class. Grade entirely based on midterm and final, both of which are take home papers and graded by TA. Reading is essential and lectures are really useful when writing the papers. He does a great job explaining everything. He can be very sassy and funny during class which is entertaining

Fisk is a very knowledgable professor, and he really wants his students to understand the material. The readings take a pretty long time; they can be helpful though. The subject itself (international relations) is actually kind of interesting if you put time into knowing the issues.

He podcasts but sections are mandatory. Great prof, but the TAs are HARSH. Class based on 2 essays but like I said, they can make or break you. Pray that you get a good TA, mine was picky and feedback was confusing/unhelpful. Take this class if you're into this stuff, but as far as an easy A goes its a hit or miss depending on your TA
This prof is awesome. Do the reading and go to lecture and you will learn a lot and do well. The TAs are usually very knowledgeable, although they are pretty hard graders for an undergrad class.
Approachable and respectable professor. Not a difficult course at all if you know how to write.
GREAT professor!! Truly respect this professor. He's entertaining in a witty way and is very knowledgeable.

If you want a super easy class, don't take Fisk. That being said, if you like professors who will actually take time to talk to you, this is a good class. I do have one piece of advice though: Go to the TAs office hours before turning in your midterm or final paper because the grading is brutal: An A isn't impossible, but its difficult.

Great Professor! Keeps lectures organized and midterms and finals don't depend on all lectures. Always answers your questions and allows for class discussion, but TAs are picky and little hard on the grading. So if you want to trust your writing skills, go ahead.
Professor Fisk even though he's a great lecturer and holds your attention, ALWAYS has strict TA's and hard graders...so if you want to get a good grade, try to avoid it.

His TAs are extremely picky and inconsistent with each other and hard graders. There were dozen or so students lined up for REGRADE. Professor claims that B- was an average for the class and thats a good result. Its not a hard class at all, in fact its a very fun class, its just seems like prof and TAs try to make it appear so with grading. AVOID

I had this class once a week and only went to 3 or 4 lectures in total. 3 papers total, one on an in-class game, then mid and final.  He is a really nice guy but political parties are just too boring for me. Lecture slides posted online. I rarely went to class but I spent a good amount of time writing the papers and got an A :) Take this class

Professor Fisk is very knowledgeable about European politics, and does a great job at conveying class material. The midterm and final were both papers, broken down into different aspects of the subject-grade dependent on the TA. Prof. Fisk is really nice and adorable too, so I'd recommend him!
Just go to lecture and write well in three papers and it is an easy A :D
I learned a lot of strategy in this class. there is a midterm paper and a final paper not too hard if you go to class and do the reading.
Professor Fisk is very helpful, knowledgeable, concerned about his students, and very attractive.

Prof. Fisk was extremely helpful and I found all of the readings to be interesting. lectures are to the point and and are helpful. class consisted of two essays and a participation grade so you really have to read and write well. in office hours he is extremely helpful as well.
Lecture was not so bad. More helpful than reading the materials. He knows what's he talking about.

Professor Fisk has very clear simple lectures that go to the point.  He always welcomes questions.   Discussion is where they grill you on whether or not you read so make sure you know what you're talking about! I got a B+ but could have gotten an A if i completed the reading to write a better final paper.
Fantastic professor! He made lectures really interesting. Class is definitely not an easy A but if you do the readings and go to lecture it's attainable. LOVE this prof.
He is such a great professor! I have taken 2 classes with him and plan to take more. He is very helpful if you need any help. He really knows alot about politics. I recommend him highly:0)

For undergrad class, he assigns a lot of work. There are three 5-7 pg essays and a lot of reading. The lectures are helpful because it summarizes lectures. I warn you to not rely or site lecture slides for papers!!! (Depends on TA)

Great professor! Take him if you want a fun and interesting class that wont require much work. Lectures are great and the powerpoints are really useful since they summarize the readings. You can also download them and use them on the essays, which is really helpful. Great professor. Take him
Interesting at times, but boring at others. You have to want to be there to get much out of the class. no test only two take home papers. you can get by not reading.
Lecture comes directly for  the book so its pointless to do both. I liked the professor but found the class a little dry

He's a great professor, although his TA was a tough grader and a little unreasonable about how she wanted the essays to be written. As for him: his lectures came directly from the 3 assigned books. So, you can either read the books or go to lecture. I even emailed the TA about what I was supposed to cite for my essays because they were identical!
interesting lectures!
Not an easy A, but professor and TA approachable. Liked the class.
YES YES! ;-)
not much fun to listen too. not excited about the material so makes the class boaring. 3 Papers, 2 are take home midterms and 1 is take home final

Midterms and finals were all essay prompts. If the prompts were unclear, the prof or TA's helped. Never been to his OH, but he seemed like an approachable prof who was genuinely interested in his students. Textbooks were, quite frankly dry and expensive, but his lectures broke em down into understandable tidbits. Ppt slides were online.
Interesting professor. Great lecturer. Papers are a bit tedious, but you go in-depth with political theories, which are fun to explore.

Loved this class! In part because of the professor and the TA who were both helpful, clear, and knowledgeable about their topic.  I would take another polisci class taught by this professor - he was an entertaining lecturer and always welcomed questions and comments. Also, the TA and Prof always made themselves available via office hours and email

His facial expressions are hilarious! The prompts are pretty clear, but if you still have trouble, then you can email him or the ta, and a reply will come. His downloadable powerpoints are very helpful since they summarize your reading assignments.
Seems like an easy course so far. he makes you but books that you don't really use at all.Go to section do good on the 2 papers you should be fine
there is a lot of work involved in this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She genuinely cares about the students and is always available outside of class via Piazza. Her lectures are clear and she always makes sure the students are not getting lost along the way. The lecture material is representative of the exam material, and there aren't any curveballs. 100% would recommend this professor, best in the math department!

Sincerely one of the best professors I've ever had. Her lectures are clear, direct, and extremely captivating. She always tries to make sure no one has any unanswered questions, and personally responds to every Piazza post within a few hours at most. Exams and homeworks are fair and instructive. I looked forward to every lecture. Highly recommend!
The class content is very interesting and she explains everything well. Leture notes are also posted so you can spend more time listening to the lectures rather than writing down notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dumitriu is a sweetheart, very caring and happy to answer any questions in office hours or during class. Also gives clear lectures that are easy to understand. The HW is reasonable, the lectures should give you all the info you need. The grading is heavily weighted on a midterm and final, but there are lots of practice problems to help you prepare.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
She is a very approachable and kind Professor, her lectures are also good. The only issue was the exams were a bit too hard. Especially in the finals, there were way too many questions in my opinion. The quizzes are also very rough. 

I am not 100% sure if the quizzes have any integrity, just because of how easy it is for some people to cheat.

The book is more straightforward and clearer than the lectures and slides in my opinion. midterm and final are not hard but very tricky. You have to pay attention to the examples talked about during lectures. The weekly quizes are not hard if you read the book carefully. No extra credit and curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this class if you don't have to. His exams are copy and paste of the clicker questions until the final. The final is totally different than all exams. He is blatantly trying to get as many students as possible to fail.

His lecture content is entirely hand written so you must have a good understanding and retention of spoken word but other than that he is great. His explanations are good and his midterms were based off practice questions. You may have heard that his final throws ppl off but it wasn't too bad. He applied a generous curve too.4midt-1drop+final=grade

Dude was generous with the curve. I hope he keeps the final exam format, as it was meticulously crafted and a good representation of student understanding. Had he exposed students to problem solving questions through HW and quizzes, I reckon his ratings would be higher. There is a gap between his teaching (great) and student preparation (lack of).

Mostly a memorization heavy class. His midterms are 75% word for word practice problems, and he holds a review session during lecture before every test His final, however, is much more difficult than any of the midterms, and he doesn't really warn you about this. Cram hard and study everything a few days before the final and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures and quizzes are chill but the final is not!! It will drop your grade to a great extent so be prepared. I like his lecture because he explains everything clearly but the final really scares me
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The quizzes were all super easy but then it came to that final. He twists words and tried to trick you, it is not worth taking this class me and my friends all regret it and are all very angry. Very unfair final questions and I knew every lecture word for word. No curve either!

I came in prepared knowing that the final questions were much different from the quizzes and boy did it still hit me like a truck. I didn't get enough sleep before the exam and the first question woke me right up! The questions were so creatively written I can't even get mad.

Do not be fooled by the quizzes. The final is 100x harder. I was talking a walk under a warm, sunny day and then a tornado swept me away at the end of the road.

You need to be good at making and applying connections—like case studies. Otherwise, the Prof is great at teaching and passionate about his work. Material is explained very clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You have a couple of quizzes then a final. A large part of the quiz will come from the review questions he gives out, but don't be a fool. For the final, he switched it up on us and put hard questions. The mean score for the final was 69% Def was an uncool move on his part. Had a B+ for most of his class, but will likely end with a C+ now

Not bad, but his slides are a bit disorganized. He does not split them up by lecture, and handwriting can be illegible at times. His explaining makes up for it well enough. I found the content very interesting and quizzes were fair, questions are usually word for word from the practice questions he does in class. Heard the final will be bad tho...
Lectures are pretty slow but the class is pretty easy
A little hard to understand because the microphone would keep on cutting off his speech, but everything is on the slides. Exams matched all of the like 10+ practice exams provided.

Uncaring, lectures extremely difficult to follow. Feels like he's out to get you, because he is. All I know is he took a break from teaching, and apparently used to be good. Something happened while he was away, and now I consider him one of the worst professors I've had in the ECON department. The only positive is his exams being nearly identical.

Now I can say I know a lot about CAPM model and expected utility theory. Professor Du is the perfect pofessor at UCSD. The Lecture is clear and recorded. The tests are fair and he is approachable and caring! My only regret is I took 100C with another professor a quater before he is the instructor.

He's an amazing professor and is available for appointments for those who couldn't make it to his regular office hours. If you practice all the problem sets and practice exams before midterms and finals, you will do well in this class.

A great man. Lectures cover relevant material for exams, practice/past exams he provides are almost identical to the upcoming exams. He extended my due date by three days on an assignment when I switched into his Econ 171 class during week 2. He's awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He made the final exam optional due to the strike, which was great because you are basically done with this course in week 8. Exams are easy if you be careful enough (almost got an A+ if I didn't make silly mistakes). 5/5 recommend taking him for your last econ course.

Professor Du teaches students in a fairly easy and understandable way. The course materials can be hard but he never confuses you with things you don't need to know. That being said, his exams were very fair based on what was taught in class. I would definitely recommend him.
Professor Du is the perfect professor at UCSD. He taught us a lot from this course, and the exam is very easy.

She is one of the most amazing professors at UCSD and in the WCWP program. She truly cares about her students and is understanding. The only reason I selected such a high level of difficulty in her class because if you truly want to grow you do need to put a lot of effort into analyzing your work and your writing. Anyone would be lucky to have her!
I would 100% take this prof again. She's the goat of warren writing. It's not like this class is SUPER easy or anything but if you have to pick a professor theres no reason not to pick Emma.
Best teacher of the WCWP series!
One of the best professors on campus, cares for students and their grades, as long as you put work in you can definitely get an A.

Really easy class and teacher. Contract graded and is really chill with late work and late attendance even if it violating contract. Genuinely a really nice person that assigns a reasonable amount of work that shouldnt take you more than 3 or 4 hours a week on average. Leaves meaningful feedback and puts effort into helping you improve.

Cares a lot about her students and gives great feedback on essays. Grading contract makes it nearly impossible to get a lower grade than you want. Would take this professor again for every WCWP course if I could.

Emma is a very nice instructor, she is caring, and just in general always comes to class with amazing energy. The class is fairly easy and simple, read/annotate, and write essays. Emma makes writing easy as her feedback is nice! So if you struggle with writing, Emma's feedback will help you become better at doing so.
Professor Emma is very understanding about every situation. Her feedback and Office hours helped immensely to create better essays. Insanely chill professor. I recommend taking her class for WCWP 10A

Course has a grading contract, reflecting how much work/effort you put into class. She is a great & kind professor and cares a lot about her students. The project essays challenged me to take risks, break old writing habits, and helped me develop my writing better. She gave good and encouraging feedback on your writing, and I overall enjoyed it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Entire final true or false and 50% of your grade... the canvas is so messy. would not recommend.

For a class with so little content, there is too much homework and most lectures involve group work so it's mandatory yet contributes nothing to understanding, just reiterating the homework we already completed. The exams are open notes so the MCQs are really specific and hard to predict or study for. The prof is nice but the class isn't worth it.
If you rlly care about critical thinking as a biomedical science researcher, this class may not be ideal because lots of memorizing and the answers to some test questions are qeustionable.

Many small homework that do not help students learn. Lectures don't go into core content in-depth; you either get it or you don't. If you don't, you'll have to figure it out by yourself. Tough tests, opted for P/NP after the midterm, and I'm usually a pretty good test taker. Tricky questions, multiple choices are a pain to look at. I wouldn't rec.
This class is an apprenticeship that lasts 5 weeks, and she teaches us a lot about teaching. She is also very kind in giving feedback and loves student input. I definitely learned a lot from her!
Prof Tour is rlly nice, but the lack of organization pisses me off. Lectures aren't rlly lectures, it's a lot of group activities, which are easy and sometimes fun.
Nice person, harsh grader. Very misleading. Partial credit is there, but not a lot. Would not recommend.

Dr. Tour is one of the sweetest professors I've ever had, I recommend getting to know her if you have the chance. Like most labs, this class is very time-intensive but you're not graded on accuracy so just complete everything and you'll be fine. Weekly quizzes and biweekly lab reports. Both the midterm and final were very straightforward.
not a very good professor overall

If you're not a fan of smaller assignments or groupwork, and you're just looking for a lecture and test-heavy course with heavy memorization, this may not be the best prof. HOWEVER if you want to actually learn how to read and interpret biological data, take Dr. Tour. She is also such a kind person and genuinely cares about who you are.

My biggest issue was haphazard (lack of) structure and homework schedule, so consider your learning style. Test content may be from from any readings, she does not need to cover it in class. Self study content is challenging yet quizzed for correctness. Exams are worth very few points, so the details you needed to learn are nebulous yet crucial.
she is a great professor! sometimes soft spoken but very easy professor. she is very fair and genuinely wants students to learn
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr Tour has a haphazard teaching style, frequent coverage (and homework!) of non-course material, a strange testing format, and extremely unclear and picky grading. The course material is a 2 in difficulty, but her teaching and grading make it a 4. Notes in the exams don't help since they're entirely free response and take full time. PLS DONT TAKE!

TERRIBLE lecturer for this course. The idea of having a scientific writing course was great, but the way she organizes it makes no sense. Shed rather spend half of the period getting participation points for unhelpful feedback on textbook readings than help people work on their thesis. The first 5 weeks was helpful, but the rest is a waste of time

Do not take her for BIMM 101. Ridiculous grading on lab reports, hard to understand during lecture, makes a sheet of paper with your lab bench faces on it and calls on you. When approached after class she really isn't helpful. Tests were open note but the everyone did bad at the lab reports
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She genuinely cared about student feedback and was very approachable. Her BIMM101 class focused a lot on troubleshooting, which is extremely applicable in an actual lab setting. She made an effort to get to know each one of us and if you get an A in the class, she's willing to write you a LOR! Take her for recombinant DNA!

She doesn't teach, basically she reads off of her slides, her tests are hard and ask to design experiments. With her new grading skills many of friends ended up dropping her class with W. No regrade. Extremely picky and all over the place. If you can don't take her
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Tour is an awesome person - encourages questions, makes extra time to talk to you, & does her best to make the class easy. The exams are open notes - YES, whatever notes you want - allowing focus on the learning.  Readings were always current & interesting. Her class equips you with scientific skills you'll need in the real world, unlike others

Initially, I did not like that Dr. Tour was teaching using active learning, but as the quarter passed I learned to enjoy it very much. She is honestly one of the best biology professors at UCSD and I promise I am not steering you wrong. Definitely take her if you want to learn and enjoy it at the same time. I have no regrets taking her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Don't take if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Tour was very caring and did her best to answer everyone's question in lecture, although her answers don't always provide much clarification. Group work was heavily emphasized; she had students sit with their groups in lecture. Quizzes and exams were pretty straightforward if you attended class and section

Tour is a good teacher. She makes the extra effort to encourage questions in class by allowing you to text in your questions, which is cool. Exams aren't hard. I started studying an hour before the final and did well on it.
Exams were all based on lecture notes. She is very helpful and explains concepts clearly!! She is great during office hours.

Definitely harder than BIBC103, but it's still an intro to bio lab. a lot of material, but if you attend her lectures, she goes over everything you need to know for quizzes and exams. lab reports are definitely the most difficult aspect of the class, but professor tour is very approachable and will always answer your question. great professor.

Very kind professor and passionate about teaching, but I found BIMM 110 EXTREMELY difficult. There was A LOT of material to cover (which I know isn't the professor's doing) but her exams asked you to design experiments and read papers, which allows for subjective grading. Also very picky about the details. Had a poor experience in her class.

Teaching was extremely clear and the professor had a great way to getting the information across. As long as you have some interest in this topics and go to class or at least listen to  the podcasts you should have no problem. It is not a piece of cake but with a little interest and work you will do well! recommended

One of the most helpful biology professors at UCSD. Sincerely cares for her students, unlike some lecturers who can appear condescending. Accent is really not a problem at all. We even had a few potlucks after lab! Explains well, exams are representative.
Just terrible. Questions asked on test don't relate to lectures, incomprehensible lectures and terribly worded test questions.
