She teaches pretty well. Midterm was relatively easy, however the final was significantly more difficult - expected a great deal more detail on the final. Clickers required, so attendance is mandatory. Discussion sections optional but recommended as she reuses a lot of questions.
nice professor, although a little tough. her questions really test whether you know the material. but she is available for help, doesn't require one set section, and does curve the class.

Either a good teacher, or a very easy one, but probably both! Accent's no problem. Checks attendance with clicker. You could go to any discussion you want, without enrolling in them. Podcasts, and posts lecture slides. Let her know if you think something's wrong with any question on the exam. She may compensate it with free points for all!
She is a very nice teacher.  Class isn't too hard.  Quizzes can be difficult.  I thought final was ok.  She curves her class.  One of the better UD bio classes I've taken.

Professor Tour is one of the nicest professors you'll have at UCSD, and so helpful. Class is interesting and you aren't graded by your data, so its pretty fun overall. 7 Quizzes and midterm were ok, final was a little tougher but nothing unexpected.

I took this class in the summer of '07 and it was pretty challenging! The material was super interesting and she really shows her interest and passion in the subject. Exams were fair, but grading was very strict! Great professor
Easy! SUper EASY. Just keep telling her the class is hard and she'll make it even easier HAHA.

Hands down best prof. If you're considering him, TAKE HIM. Attendance is mandatory. Hw due every other Sunday (lots of reading tbh but extremely manageable). Mandatory vignettes where you watch a movie and diagnose a character (you can choose a movie based on his list). Only had a final and didn't even study yet got a 90%. Topics were engaging.

I really like Chapman! He's chill, cracks some jokes in class, and the homework is easy. There is a decent amount of reading involved, but I personally found the topics interesting. Graded mainly on attendance, homework, one exam, and a vignette (u watch a movie and diagnose a character in groups and discuss, which was easy). Would take again :)

Too much busy work homework. Course is fine, boring if anything & annoying. Only goes into super general clinical stuff, I felt like I learned nothing. He is very intense & you have to do a clinical intake based on a movie & discuss it in a zoom later. He GRILLS you & it was super annoying & not very helpful either. Didn't learn anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Chapman is one of the worst professors I've had in my life. He is an extremely easy A if you go to class and read the material. He cares very little about his students and certain situations regarding group projects that he enforced. In some classes he also forces people to do "service learning". Failing to do so means -10% to your final grade

Super super strict about attendance. Only one super easy exam at the end of class, the rest of class is filled with online busy work. He's a great guy, but this class seems like it could be taught at a high school due to the format and rules. Material and work is not difficult.

A very easy A. His lectures we pretty summarized from the textbook, but he is a funny guy so it helped getting through lecture. Lots of busywork homeworks that are super easy, just tedious. Weekly journal reflections. Mandatory attendance and he likes participation from students in lecture. No midterm, just a final that was really easy.

I'm so shocked by ratings, well first of all lemme start off by saying that he's an amazing professor. And in the past year he's so much more strict, mandatory attendance, homeworks every week and everything but there's no exam it's just intakes and the TA's are very helpful. HE IS AN AMAZINGGG PROFESSOR TAKE HIM

A class all future clinicians should take. Focused on self discovery/career path, clinical intakes, and clinical psych as a career. Experienced as a therapist, not as teacher. Class is disorganized and information is given close to deadlines, not clearly. He has a big ego and is petty if you miss class or leave early. Only take if you want this job

I appreciate the real world assignments like case studies or learning to write an intake form, but it feels the assignments are stretched out too much. The class is very, very easy, which is why I think a lot of people like the class. Personally, what I was learning felt like filler and I wish I could have gotten more out of the class

Chapman is an alright professor. Lectures and attendance are mandatory, he's an easy A if you go to class. However, the content of lectures is dull at best. I had a particular case where things were out of my control, I brought legal proof. He said that we could talk about it, but his stance won't change. I felt dismissed and ignored.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: As a clinical psyc major, I was looking forward to this class . Wish I took it with Dickenson or Lacefield instead.. His ego was insane and most of lecture was useless discussion based. Used old slides and the whole class was busy work, v obvious that its simply an easy A class. If you actually care about clinical psyc i would take someone else.

Dr. Chapman DESTROYED my passion for Clinical Psychology. If you want an easy class then by all means take this for sure!! I mean, even I would take another class with him for an easy A. However, his class is ONLY busywork (which is all in Quizlet) but he is mundane in teaching and inspiring a new generation of psychologists. His ego is huge!

Lecture isn't really required for your grade but is great if you're interested in the subject. 70% of your grade is Achieve homework which is pretty useful in understanding the material. He uses the textbook-provided slides which are barebones, and Canvas is a little cluttered. Pretty easy A, wasn't always engaged but felt like I learned a lot!

I love Professor Chapman and the atmosphere he creates in his classroom. He facilitates discussions like no one else I've seen at UCSD. Class was all online, weekly quizzes and assignments. Very easy, but I still felt like I learned a fair amount, and was enjoyable.

Achieve system glitch,reset four of my already graded assignments to zero. Provided screenshot proof, but my valid concerns were dismissed, leading to an unfair grade. Attempts to discuss this with the professor were futile, negatively impacting my GPA. Note: grade appeals are not accepted unless is non academic based. Basically nothing you can do
Best professor at UCSD! He has great lectures that never get boring and the homework is pretty straightforward.

While Prof Chapman's class is super easy to get through grade-wise, I found it a bit boring. Lectures are dreary and structure of HW makes it tough to learn much of substance. HW depends on specific numbers found in textbook but answers are practically given to you, so pretty easy. Overall, Dr. Chapman is super chill but a little boring.

Great professor! Class is well structured, lectures are interesting and he is very inspirational. I recommend him for any psych class. The only thing I didn't like about the class was the TAs, Yilian Wang graded assignments unfairly.

I've really enjoyed his class! I'd recommend knowing what's in the syllabus because there are a few assignments that can sneak up on you. The iClicker was required but it was free online (just for his class tho) and thats how attendance was taken. The class is podcasted, but there were tech issues. Do the eBook assignments early in the week too!

Everybody really loves him because his class is pretty easy but in all honesty I was disappointed at the content of the class. We didn't talk much about treatment at all and the title was clinical assessment and treatment. Heavily project-based, which is definitely different from most classes. Not my favorite.

Incredible professor & teaching philosophy! Do the homework, you get an A. Attend class, you learn a ton. He is possibly the greatest professor at UCSD. Engage with him, he will literally help you understand yourself & what you want out of life. Heart of gold, dresses super snazzy, real master of psychology with so much experience. Take this class!

2nd time taking this prof (first time was PSYC100 online). He is a practicing clinical psychologist and has fascinating anecdotes and insights. Lectures don't get very far so most tested content is from interactive textbook, but we go through clinical diagnosis procedures in class. Encourages students to ask him for career advice after class.
I really liked this class. Not too hard but very interesting.

LOVE HIM! great professor without a doubt. Lots of readings and assignments but they are doable because they are all online. He can change due dates because he care for the success of his students. No extra credit however, assignments and doing the group discussion helps your grade so you should definitely get an A in his class and final is online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: the BEST Psych teacher at UCSD. His lectures are clear, his assignments are easy. You will get an A, and you WILL learn!

Professor Chapman was great! He's a clear, entertaining lecturer. I had this class in the morning and always looked forward to it. His assignments have simple criteria and you get a lot of practice. Most of them center around making sure YOU understand what you're learning and helping you get better. Amazing class.

This class is a total cake walk. Attendance isnt mandatory, homework due every Sunday takes 5 minutes to do, one exam which is the final and questions were verbatim from the homework. Only challenging part was the vignette (case example where you diagnose somebody). Barely studied for the course and got an A+.

Very easy A as long as you complete the work. Weekly online module homework (with as many attempts as you need), SONA study participation, and a two part final. As he tells you at the beginning, the course is set up for you to succeed - idk how anyone doesn't pass.

Professor Chapman is hands-down my favorite professor in my 4 years at college. Assignments have a thoughtful purpose, lectures allow for critical thinking and exploration, material is useful and relatable to other fields. Definitely take him if you get the chance.

Dr. Chapman was a wonderful lecturer. I had him for PSYC 168 and 124 and I enjoyed both classes. You can tell he truly cares about his students, and provided us with a lot of information beyond what was expected for the course, such as career advice. I would definitely take a class with him again!

100% RECOMMEND HIM!! By far one of the easiest and most understanding profs ever!! We are assigned module hwk which is easy all you need to do is keep yourself on track. The material is interesting and there is a 2 part final of a diagnosis + MC exam. Both are easy as long as you read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: LOL, it can't get easier than this idk why people trip. The cenage assignments literally save you on the Final cause the point of it is to get enough points where even if you bomb the Final, you still pass with an A. Also the book is really interesting!

Dont listen to the negative reviews!, Dr. Chapman is a great prof that really focuses on engaging the class during live lectures. All the homework and quizzes are on a virtual module textbook thing. I attended half of the lectures, read the textbooks, and earned an A+. Would totally take again for 100 or 168
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took his class online and we used this online program (I think it was cengage). The online program was what determined our whole grade for his class. It was full of readings and quizzes at the end of each chapter. In my opinion, I think it was an easy A since the quizzes were open notes. I never went to lecture and got a good grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He gives a ton of irrelevant busy work. Get ready to hate ur life. I just had to read an article about the POTENTIAL change of combining Aspergers + Autism into one term in the DSM5 & answer questions. That happened 9 years ago.. we're legit reading an article from 2012.. like are you kidding me? Has he even looked at what he's assigning? No.

Y'all. Do NOT take him. 21% of your grade is watching old videos that don't relate to lectures or the book & then answering irrelevant and HARD questions that aren't always covered in the videos. The class set-up as a whole is awful. Its one of those where the material isn't hard (its psych lol) but he's purposely made it hard to get an A..

Thought this class was just ok. Course outline was a bit confusing to me; didn't really know exactly why we were learning what we were, and the lectures were honestly boring to me/didn't feel well-organized. And grading criteria is NOT clear whatsoever.

Professor Eure is very passionate and knowledgeable about her subject, but we would often run out of lecture time b/c of poor time management. Not a lot of assignments, but she does not provide rubrics in advance, so you don't know how you're going to be graded and doesn't post grades to Canvas. I liked her awkward humor and energy though!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Eure has been great at teaching this somewhat unique subject offering within the literature department. She really tries to make class interesting and full of meaningful discussions. She is very much focused on students' thoughts during lecture which detracts from more developed explanations of the readings that could be confusing at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I've really enjoyed taking her class this quarter. There were in-class writings graded on completion once a week, a relatively easy midterm, and a final paper with an interview component. She is very caring and wants people to have open discussions about class themes and readings. She explains everything very well and adds complexity to topics.

3 quizzes are weighted pretty heavily along with a final.I did bad on the first quiz, 18/25 then got 23/25 & 24/25 on the next two. I got a 47/50 on the final so not bad & ended w a A-. Everything was curved by a few points. I recommend focusing on the details of the slides & making flash cards. Assignments every week, gives answers in class
A very caring professor. You know he loves what he teaches.
If you have the option to take this professor over the other intro to stats professor, please take him. he's a great prof and makes it very easy to know what's on each exam.

I know my grade might not reflect my rating very well but I enjoyed this professor a lot. I made a doc of questions I had for him and he responded the next day. Everything that's on the exams in on the lecture slides so ONLY pay attention to what's on the slides. Great professor and really wants you to succeed and pass his class.

Pure & insane amounts of memorizing, exams are SUPER specific & its difficult to memorize everything he asks us to. Exams every 2 weeks, with 200+ terms to memorize for each exam. It was incredibly specific exams & he does not grade very generously. Super animal heavy, it felt like a zoology course with all the random animal facts I had to memorize
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nothing overtly inappropriate, but some interactions may make students feel uncomfortable.

Exams reflect exactly what is in the slides, he is generous with curves and adding extra points for other assignments. Lectures can be very boring, and the content isn't very interesting. Two papers and 3 exams, unclear in areas surround the paper which could be frustrating. Talk to your IAs for paper help. Have to go to class.

rlly nice professor. just go to class and study enough for them midterms. for the research project, he basically holds your hand throughout the entire thing. also basically holds your hand during the labs. rlly easy just put in the work to study bc they're a huge chunk of ur grade. labs are worth 3 points each. have to go to lecture

Really easy, only needing to do 4 quizzes for the entire class (no cumulative exam). Will throw in free points for each quiz. Places easy assignments to add cushioning for your grade. All the answers are on the slides. Is a little fast-paced, having quizzes every week. Rounds grades to the nearest whole number. Great guy!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is going to be difficult. The topics are hard to understand and deep explanations will not be given. Grade is almost entirely exam reliant, with three exams and one final exam given and spread out along course. Lectures are also often non-engaging and hard to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great prof! Lectures were entertaining and he was very helpful at office hours. Explained things very clearly and tests reflected what we learned in class. Genuinely learned a lot about stats from his class.

Lecture attendance is mandatory as there are some parts of slides not revealed till class. He's very approachable and has very clear explanations. Class is more about concepts than calculations, so the tests are multiple choice. He also curves which is helpful!

Really cool guy! You can tell he cares about his students and makes lectures entertaining. Grades are based on SONA, 10 assignments which he gives the answers to in lecture, three 25 question quizzes, and a 50 question final. All exams were multiple choice and mostly memorization and he curved each based on how the class did. Would take him again!

Attendance is mandatory because some of the slides have information on them that he only gives in class, but homework is all done in class and he gives you the answers. Quizzes are all multiple choice and he curves them based on how everyone did. Def take him if you get the chance!

3 midterm questions and 1 final exam which are pretty easy if you study (they're all memorization). Attendance to lectures is mandatory as he does not podcast and he gives you the answers to the homework in class. As long as you go to class and study, you will do fine in this course. Steiner is also very funny and makes the class entertaining.

Homework is free points, quizzes make up the majority of your grade. If you go to every lecture and keep up with the material, you'll be fine. Good luck if you fall behind. No podcasts. Responsive to questions and has great energy in lecture, his goal is for all his students to understand what's going on. Office hours are helpful for clarification!

(Fall 2023) overall good guy! as simple as the class was, I just wish it wasn't so test heavy, he did give us extra points on some of the quizzes and a very generous curve on the final but I just wish there were other components to your grade rather than just the quizzes, SONA, the final, and 10 assignments. But overall would take him again :)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chill professor, you do your assignments in class with him.

(fall 2023) attendance isn't mandatory BUT lectures aren't recorded! his lectures are based off the slides but there are extra parts he only reveals during class time. quizzes and tests are super straight forward. as long as u pay attention in lecture and spend a decent amount of review time on the material, it's really easy to get an A.

Steiner is such a kind and caring professor. He genuinely wants his students to succeed. Cracks jokes in class and I loved his personal anecdotes. As someone who never took stats Steiner was very clear and detailed in his lectures. Took time to answer all questions. Quizzes/tests are mc and all based on slides. Hw is easy points. Take him!

Steiner was a very nice and funny prof (lowkey a goober but in a good way). His class is very straight forward which is nice when you have a stressful quarter. The quizzes and final exam is all on lecture material so the grade you get it 100% based on how much you studied ie you can't blame the prof in any way. Simple and easy class for a GE

Steiner is overall a really good professor, I took Psyc 60 twice, unfortunately didn't pass the first time with Lowe. Steiner is more conceptual, meaning having to learn definitions and what the concepts actually mean rather than the math. There are 3 quizzes, 10 assignments, Sona participation and the final.

One of the best math professors anyone with math anxiety would dream for. Exams and assignments are based on lecture slides and exam questions are direct. He is very caring (sometimes he'll give extra bonus points on quizzes) and is very funny. If you have to fulfil a math GE, I'd recommend taking Prof Steiner's class 100%.

Personally, I had a lot of experience with statistics so many concepts I already understood; however, he teaches by chapter each lecture, and the quizzes and final exam are heavily based on the slides and things he says during lectures, so attendance is recommended especially because he doesn't podcast. Multiple choice quizzes and exams, hw is ez.

Best professor that I have had at UCSD... if you ever see him as a professor, take his class!!!! Although his tests are a bit tricky as they are really conceptual, he gives out extra points. He's always in a great mood, which makes it so much easier to sit and listen in class.

The class has 9 discussion section assignments, three quizzes, a presentation, and a final paper. The class is easy if you attend lecture and put in some study hours. Lecture not mandatory, but it is helpful. Discussion is mandatory, and also very helpful. Would definitely take him again.

Professor Steiner is the embodiment of Ryan Reynolds in a professor. Super funny, lecture material is presented in an easy-to understand manner, and he adds a Spider-Man meme into all of his lecture slides. He makes statistics an accessible concept and his tests all draw clearly from the course content. You won't regret taking his class.

Prof Steiner's very organized which makes everything just so much easier. Only 5 non-cumulative quizzes, with one acting as the final. The material could be hard to understand, but he gives great feedback and so open to questions. He also threw in mini-lectures on philosophical subjects (optional and not tested) which just were fun to listen to.
No extra credits, straight forward. He is caring, professional, and a very kind professor.

This prof grew on me, I found his lectures boring in the beginning but he is extremely accessible & nice. 5 non-cumulative quizzes, no drops but there is 6 pts extra credit, 1 paper. Wish we went slower in the middle of class instead of slowing down at the end bc the concepts in the middle were hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great class for a GE, and awesome prof! Lectures were engaging, tests were fair. Some overlap with AP Stats so if you've taken that you'll have a good boost here. Prof spoke clearly and recorded his lectures well, with helpful slides. Assignments were very helpful with learning as well, and actually fun! I'd 100% recommend this class to anyone.

I am currently taking his PSYC70 and passed PSYC60 last quarter with an A+. Seriously he is probably going to be one of my favorite professors at UCSD. This man is so patient, caring, and actually sees things from the students' perspectives. He ONLY TEST YOU ON STUFF HE TEACHES and he makes it real specific. Love this guy so much, great personality

I took PSYC 60 with Steiner and had a great experienced. Just as a precursor, I did take AP Stats in high school so most of the concepts that were covered were overlapped. But Steiner still does a great job of clarifying things for people who are new to stats and he cares about his students. HW assignments took kind of long but were not difficult.

oh my gosh one of the best profs at ucsd! way to go hiring committee. such a kind, clear, and patient person who always gives examples for concepts for better understanding. I learned stats in hs but he actually made me UNDERSTAND stats. easy assignments, all mc quizzes, ec opportunity with cape evals, and he curves the final and overall grades!

Professor Steiner truly love his job and cares for his students. He is such a patient teacher and provides the resources needed to succeed in the class. Memorizing the slides and understanding the concepts are key to do well. It's an easy class if you put the time and effort into it.

Dr. Steiner was the best! I've had him for Psyc 70 before and loved him. He's funny and has clear, straightforward lectures. Grading for p132 was based on 5 quizzes (final was a quiz), all non-cumulative, plus 4 easy assignments and mandatory SONA. Quizzes are really fair if you study. One of my favorite profs and this class was super interesting
Nice lectures. Memorize the important stuff on the slides and you can get good score on quizzes.

I did not do the best because math is difficult for me, especially online, but professor Steiner gives very straight forward lectures and everything needed to pass the course. One of the best professors I've had and really cares for his students!

Prof. Steiner made complicated concepts easier. You don't need to read the textbook. His slides really help. Also the assignments are easy money. If you can memorize and UNDERSTAND everything from the slides, it's an easy A.
He is a great lecturer, very kind and funny. Also the class is super easy as long as you watch the lectures and take basic notes.

The class is based on 3 quizzes, 10 assignments (super easy dw) and the final and SONA credits. His lectures are easy to follow and he's honestly one of the best profs I've had. He's approachable and is knowledgeable about not just stats but psych as well! I didn't use the textbook cause his ppts are good by itself

Dr. Steiner keeps quizzes challenging but doable if you keep up with lectures. He is very direct of what you should know for the exams it's just a matter of memorizing. If you can memorize all the information you need you will do great on his exams. He is very enthusiastic and knowledgeable about all that he teaches. Really great guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: absolutely a gem of a teacher. you can't really say anything bad about the guy other than he's too patient sometimes like some ppl literally ask the dumbest questions and he's willing to answer them all. very clear and structured class. it won't be your hardest class if you just attend/watch lectures multiple times! take him you won't regret it
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: he is so patient. He goes through concepts slowly (almost spoon feeding you) and gives practice problems. Very small amount of homework. Many office hour available. You don't even need to read the textbook because the concepts on his slides stay consistent with the book.

Really nice and kind professor who clearly knows what he's talking about! Always willing to help students and gives light work. He emphasizes concepts more than solving problems! Also, he is decent looking but the other people on here have really boosted his looks like damn

I am sure Professor Steiner is one of the best professor at UCSD. He cares about every student's learning. His lecture is clear and straightforward, but you still have to spend certain amount of time studying and preparing for quizzes. His quizzes are mostly based on the conceptual theory, not calculation. Anyway, he is a very kind person!

Steiner is a great Stats Prof. His slides is what matters the most. No book is required for his class. As long as you review the slides and understand every concept then you should be set for it! Make sure to review slides more than once and assignments don't help as much. Attend OH if you have any concerns.

Professor Steiner is one of the best teachers I have had at UCSD. He is incredibly kind, understanding, and just an overall gem of a teacher. Not to mention this class was low stress and an easy A. Definitely recommend taking this class!

Great professor! This quarter has definitely been a weird one, but he's made the transition so much easier! I really enjoyed being in his class and I highly recommend him to anyone considering taking PSYC 70!

His lecture is well organized and interesting. He makes clear of whats gonna be on the test, and was attentive to the needs of students. I had emailed him multiple long emails asking questions and he would reply to those emails with very clear explanations that had helped me aaaaaaaaa lot. I wish he could teach an upper psych course.

I'm almost done wit my bachelors degree and this course was my favorite. The professor is professional his syllabus and course content match. His criteria is challenging. He is very well organized which allows you to excel in his course. In addition, his expectations are realistic and he gives you enough time to achieve them! Highly recommend

Really great teacher and makes the class easy enough to pass IF YOU PAY ATTENTION AND GO!!! Your grade truly depends on the midterm and final. Also... really handsome guy so it's kind of worth going to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I always loved going to this class because of the relaxed atmosphere and the material was presented in a concise way. He never made us learn things that weren't important regarding the subject, and the quizzes were fairly easy. There's only another quiz finals week, no big final, and buildup to writing an easy research paper throughout the quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Really explains every topic thoroughly. Is very laid back, and gives the answers for homework. However, you still need to study a decent amount for the midterms and finals, which were pretty tough, but were 100% related to the work we had in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: IF YOU CAN TAKE STEINER FOR PSYC 70, DO IT. SUPER EASY CLASS AND HE'S A NICE PERSON!! reviews.comment: The professor gives amazing examples and practice problems during class that actually help students understand the material unlike all professors in the physics department. The professor is always there to help and honestly can't ask for a better professor.

reviews.comment: Definitely one of my favorite professors I've ever taken. Took him for PSYC 1 and 60 (stats) and he did a phenomenal job of making sure we understood the material and keeping things interesting. He makes himself available for questions during and after lecture and cares a lot about his students. Keeps it simple with MC exams, take him if you can!

The first day of class he said he wanted this course to be a low stress course, and it was. I did not use the textbook in this class and I ended up good. Study his slides and you will be good on the quizzes. His slides are a little boring but he isn't. He is good looking so that helps.

Prof. Steiner teaches statistics in a very simple and clear manner. His lectures are very informative and he explains everything you need to know for the exam, just read his slides and hw which he gives step by step answers during class. His lectures usually ended early and lecture is not mandatory. Like someone else said... hes also good looking!

Awesome professor, lectures are straight from the textbook, but you don't even need to read it. He does assignments in class which helps you connect material and takes a load off having to worry about homework! He makes it really easy to learn and you can tell he cares about his students. Also lowkey hot.
Hes awesome. Tests are multiple choice and usually straight forward. Really nice professor.
great teacher, very straightforward and easy to pay attention to. you can tell he cares about his students too, which is why it's a shame he has no reviews. highly recommended
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Nice professor, but class feels disorganized, and your entire grade is based on how your final project demo runs to a TA.

Lectures poorly explained concepts due to extraneous info (too much background, specific HDL functions, outsourcing to YouTube/Wiki). The final exam unfairly tested unmentioned topics or footnotes rather than core material from lectures and assignments. Lectures were only worth attending when the TAs took over.

Honestly the worst professor in you can get in CSE/ECE. Have taken most of his courses and have never understand any of the lectures (CSE 30, 140, 141, 260). Prepared to learn all the contents by urself. Avoid him by all cost.

For the love of all is Holy, do NOT take his class if you're not prepared to self-study the material. 

As others have said, his lectures are unorganized, he tends to ramble about stuff not important to the content of the class.

His grading scheme is based on 2 midterms (25% each) and 1 final (50%) in which one of them was unnecessarily difficult.

Lectures are disorganized, and grades rely entirely on two midterms and a final. No practice exams are provided, and the optional homework problems differ significantly from the actual exams. The tests also stray from the listed topics, making it very difficult to prepare.

He doesn't really know whats hes doing, he kind just rambles and its hard to figure out what parts are important. His first midterm throw a lot of stuff he really didn't go over, 2nd midterm was more on track. Wait for Chin

reviews.comment: The class is designed horribly. Lectures are all over the place, it's clear he doesn't have any plan. 3 tests determine your whole grade, and this is by far the worst aspect. These exams are completely infeasible to be done in the time given.

Terrible Professor DO NOT TAKE HIM. No organization on his lectures and your left way more confused after. Discussions taught me everything and if you mess up on even part of his ridiculous tests it's over.

reviews.comment: Graded by 2 midterms and 1 final exam worth 25% and 50% for your grade. There is optional practice HW that isn't graded, so you are only graded based on your tests, no projects. Lectures are awful: most of the time it's random short rants or is just complex useless info that is not tested. Exams are hard. Rarely ever shows examples.

Avoid taking this class and wait, as the other reviews suggest. HW is not representative to exams. No structure so super hard to follow, and no practice exams provided, just general theoretical questions on the HWs so no idea what to expect on the exam. Final is 50% of grade, making it even more challenging. Slight curve helps. Very low averages.

good luck lol

Do NOT take CSE 30 with John Eldon. Wait to take it with Bryan Chin under any circumstance. Lectures are unstructured and hard to follow. reviews.comment: Lectures are confusing, and he skips through slides with barely any explanation. The grading system is all midterms and final, and the homework hardly reflects the tests at all.

reviews.comment: The professor is clearly knowledgeable and adds some humor to his lectures. Unfortunately, he's not a great lecturer. He often skips key concepts as if they're obvious, and frequently goes off on tangents about hardware that aren't relevant to the material. 25% each midterm and 50% final. Homework is optional, and doesn't reflect exam questions.

if anyone is scared of the reviews, don't be. you MUST read the textbook to understand his lectures and stuff that's gonna be on the exam. took 140 with him too, you absolutely won't understand anything unless you read the textbook (which helps ALOT). he grades off exams only and it's up to you to study up using textbook. don't b scared, just READ

reviews.comment: He can't teach and you won't learn anything from him. The whole class basically just cheats and use chatgpt during exam so dont expect a curve.

The course grade is entirely on lab assignments and he explains them pretty well in lectures, he is also very nice. However the starter code for the assignemnts are quite bad with some bugs in them that you have to fix yourself, the written instructions for them are also quite confusing.
Taken Eldon 3 times in undergraduate and this was my first graduate course with him. Would take him again if I had the chance

I have taken this professor many times and he is extremely helpful in and outside of class. Very friendly guy and you can tell he really enjoys teaching and cares about his students. Class itself was not too hard and mostly homework/lab based, with most labs having thorough instructions.
Very straight forward labs and an extremely helpful office hours to help with any issues regarding labs.
Love this guy. Very interesting lecturer giving much more industry experience than most professors.
Terrible lecture (I mean really really terrible, the slides aren't even in order). 100% grade based on exams. Avoid him

Easy A class. You don't need to even come to a single lecture, as most of them are useless as well. He is a very disorganized lecturer but he cares students. Weekly labs in groups, could be hard. Project is purely filling the blanks. Final is new in his ECE111, but it's extremely easy. Know the basics of SystemVerilog and you will be fine.
Nice person but not a good lecturer, grading based on only exams. No homework to test yourself, but it also means you don't have much workload in his class.

reviews.comment: Probably the most useless/misleading lectures out of any professor I've had. Every lecture involves him going over arbitrary parts of the material in a completely random order. No coherency/structure to any part of this class at all. It seems like he just shows up to class and talks about whatever he feels like. Gl following along in any capacity

It's really hard for summer session. I got C- for 71% grade and so upset. My teammates didn't do a lot after the 2nd lab. One of them gave up and joined another group without telling us. The other just knew nothing and was depressed about everything. The TAs didn't help too much neither. Final week I did 2 labs for 4 days all by myself...YUCK.

He's encouraging and enthusiastic. BUT, the grading is terrible! There are no rubrics on the grade scale. And the programming assignments are terribly made. They just give a pile of code and you have to chew it yourself. And they graded me down a LOT for the bug on their Autotrader which I don't have on my own machine or ieng6.

Lectures are pretty useless. He just skims over concepts that will appear on the lab. Lab writeups are vague and the labs are pretty tedious. Tutors especially were not helpful. This class definitely took more than 2 units of time because the labs were annoying.

He is a nice person but has no idea how to teach a class. His class is very chaotic and there is no structure or agenda as others have mentioned. He just shows up and goes over some concepts in random order and confuses you the whole time. Don't get fooled though. He says his exams are similar to HW problems but they are way harder.

I'm taking his class right now. He is pretty responsive on Piazza, but he often gives an incomplete answer because he doesn't always read questions. Also, he often forgets to do what he said he was gonna do (like updating a testbench) and even when a student asks about it, sometimes he still doesn't do it. It's kind of annoying.

I'm not entirely sure why Prof. Eldon has such low ratings. He is an awesome professor for 140L. He explains things very well in the lectures, and he is welcoming of student questions/interest. He is also considerate of students in regards to deadlines. If I had to critique anything, the project materials can be a little hard to find.

He's caring for students, hold extended office hours in holidays to help students get the labs done before the deadline, also the labs are not difficult and you can still learn a lot of stuff from them

It's very hard to follow in lecture as someone else has pointed out that he goes off on a lot of tangents. It's very hard to take notes, and it looks like he doesn't have an actual agenda as he just jumps around to different parts of the lecture slides. I learned mostly from reading. He does give a great curve and tells u exactly whats on the test.

reviews.comment: He treated 140L like it was a 6-unit class but it's actually 2. The amount of work you'll have to do is crazy. At least his lectures go over common mistakes and logic for the labs. No exams and no final is the only plus.

very quiet speaker, starts/ends class late, goes off on tangents while lecturing, bounces around from topic to topic without any logic, exams are harder than in class examples, very poor at explaining things, impossible to take notes, always forgets to upload slides to canvas, homework is optional and not graded, which doesn't help your learning.

Best CSE140L professor at UCSD, the others don't even come close. I took CSE140 before so this class was slightly easier. He goes over the labs in class, super helpfu

reviews.comment: I actually hated this class so much. So much unnecessary work and the finals/midterms are so hard for no reason... it is virtually impossible to study for them on top of work for other classes and I don't think he takes that into account. However, if you do put in the work, you will get a good grade. The class is also very TA based.

This info doesn't really matter bc it's his last quarter. But my biggest gripe w/ the class is the inconsistent grading. I got a C on both my midterm and final, and I truly believe I could have gotten a B or an A on both of them when I compared them to my friends in other sections. Do better, MMW department. Great prof though, sad to see him leave

This little bald man sparks a little joy into my life every time I hear his lectures. He is legendary and am so fortunate he is part of the MMW faculty. You will be reading for 6 hours every week and the studying for the midterm and the final will in fact turn you religious as you start praying at 5 am for it all to over. However, you will learn.

reviews.comment: Chang himself is a great guy although lectures are a little boring. This class depends entirely on your TA, I got a C on the midterm even though I had the exact same answers as my friend who got an A. Grading requirements on tests and essays are not clear. Good professor, Bad class.

Chang is a great lecturer and amazing to talk to outside of class, but there is a lot of reading assigned. I would definitely recommend taking this class with friends or working with people in your discussions, splitting up reading notes for exams makes it much more manageable.

He gets a lot of hate because he assigns a lot of readings, and there are a TON of readings, which are pretty much required in order to pass. However, he is a truly inspirational and fun lecturer, and he gives very clear study guides for his exams which make them easy to pass. I am currently taking him again for 12 and am enrolled in 13 for spring!
Extremely tough on the midterm and exams. Completely based on heavy readings. Quiz on every reading. Lectures are not mandatory, but if you don't go, you will not pass. Based on the TA's grading.
He wishes my downfall. He makes sure to use language that no one understands. He enjoys my pain. He diddys my GPA.

Chang's lectures are interesting and easy to follow. Workload is tedious and heavy, and too much for a college GE. Class is passable without doing all readings but amount of effort that goes into midterms and essays is insane. Unnecessary amount of work, annoying to deal with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Never felt such hatred towards a history class, the only reason I took this class was to complete my MMW requirement. The exam didn't evaluate your knowledge it was just memorization. The only good thing about the class was that Chang provided a clear outline of the lecture. So much reading for a GE requirement, not worth it.

reviews.comment: If you have medical problems, don't take this professor. Very rude in his emails and overall demeanor toward students needing accommodations. I'm honestly surprised there are good reviews at all.

Straightforward and organized but so much reading. Lectures are slow enough that you get bored and zone out super easily. However, exam study guides tell you exactly that you need to know so it easy to prepare. Vocabulary heavy. Not a bad class overall but lots of reading is needed for a good grade.

Chang is a lot of work, but I appreciate how his curriculum is structured by region+time period. Additionally, his study guide is extremely helpful and clear; as long as you memorize all the terms and prepare the frqs ahead of time you should be fine! Overall grade is somewhat TA dependent, so I highly recommend you to go to your TA's OH.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: DON'T underestimate the amount of reading, but also don't let that deter you from Chang's class as a whole. He is a very entertaining storyteller in lectures, and you can tell how much he genuinely looks up to the historical figures he talks about. Also the class felt more like a philosophy course than just a straight up history course.

Such a passionate and amazing lecturer, every day I came to class he made me want to learn. Definitely a lot of reading, but I feel that's just MMW in general. Midterm and Finals have super comprehensive study guides and make studying really organized and simple.

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable and underrated professor. A lot of reading, but he goes through the contents of the readings during the lecture, and it helps a lot with test prep. Attendance is not required, but lectures are not recorded, and I don't think you can afford to skip any. Nice guy; tries tries to get to know all his students during OHs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Barely read WTWA and got an A (you don't have to read it, just do course reader and lectures). Only need to do the readings, which are quite a bit. Gives the most clear midterm and final prep ever and if you don't get at least a B on them that's kind of on you, not him or the course. Is a good lecturer and gives extra credit on the midterm & final
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Chang is so inspirational and amazing lecturer. You will definitely LEARN and be immersed in the material but the homework is actually horrendous. Its like 6 hours+ of reading weekly and a quiz before every class. Despite this, its pretty easy to get an A, so i recommend him

Honestly I love Chang. It's A LOT of reading, but easy quizzes and assignments, & INSANELY DETAILED study guide before exams (time consuming but exactly what's on exam). 2 quizzes before LE each week, open note/book, lowest 5 drop. OH established. Really cares about students. Mandatory DI, no LE attendance but vids aren't posted. I suggest go to LE
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Evil, evil man. Like yeah "you'll get an A if you do the readings" if you're willing to read ~80 pages a week about phallic monuments in ancient India (on top of textbook chapters). If you don't get off the Herbst waitlist, try your luck next year

This class is a lot of reading - like often 30 pages or more. I love professor Chang as a person and his lectures are literally amazing. Even though it required a lot of work, it always felt like if you put in the time and prepared you would do well. His exam study guides have prompts for the essays on them so as long as you study you'll get those.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Great class, learned a lot (though very time consuming). Attend lectures since he explains the readings thoroughly and you can write those interpretations on the test.

I love the integrated humanities approach and I would probably have overwhelmingly positive feelings for MMW if it wasn't borderline torturous for an engineering major to complete.

Chang is amazing. His lectures are informative and funny and he's a sweet guy overall. There are a lot of readings though and if you struggle comprehending lots of text (like me) you'll struggle understanding the readings. Grades are very TA dependent. Discussions and exams are graded by your TA. So it's a lottery whether you'll get a A or not

He's very passionate about the material and his lectures are quite entertaining. It is a lot of reading but it's manageable - he also gives study guides so the tests are easy (just like AP world). Lecture isn't mandatory but I highly recommend going as it's super helpful since he goes over the reading's key points (so you don't have to read).

Professor Chang is an amazing lecturer and honestly made taking MMW a little more enjoyable. There is a lot of reading but it is manageable if you space out your time correctly. The midterm was extremely easy as he gives a comprehensive study guide which mirrors the test so you know what to expect. Show up to lectures and take notes on his stories!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Chang gets a lot of flack for the reading, but this class is truly what you make it. He's a very inspiring lecturer and very knowledgeable. Also genuinely care about students in my experience. Participate and ask questions! You can get a lot out of the reading if you really try.

MMW is just a real messed up thing ERC has to do. There isn't a "better" option between Chang and Herbst. One thing for certain tho, Chang gives A LOT!!!!! OF READING. like, an ungodly amount of reading. Like, 40 pages/week w size 5 font. It really depends on your TA.

i'm only taking this class bc i'm forced to but his tests don't even examine your actual knowledge of the cultures or anything they're just a buttload of studying for no reason like he genuinely just wants people to waste time in his class and he doesn't even know much about the topics he's teaching. he just makes you buy some 50 dollar reader

This highkenuinely is the worst class I've ever taken. I genuinely have never felt such hatred for history than I have now. The tests are the most braindead things ever created and require 100 hours of studying and for you to remember how kitto wiped his ass. The TAS expect you to know every aspect of the term even when it has no purpose. dont take

reviews.comment:
Really good lectures, but there is so much reading to do in the classes. It's super important to actually read EVERYTHING or you will fall behind.

Lectures aren't mandatory but please go and TAKE NOTES! Even if it's just copying down what he's written on the slides, it'll help you a ton when prepping for exams without re-reading everything.

read read read. reading the textbook/reader is 90% of this class. if you actually do it you'll be fine. Chang himself is very likable but his lectures are kinda boring. discussion are mandatory with participation points. its a fairly easy class but just a lot of work if you actually do it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The workload in his classes is a lot, especially with the amount of reading he assigns and there are two quizzes per week, in addition discussion is mandatory. Other than that he is a really good lecturer and he preps his students well by providing them a study guide a couple days before the exam. Exams are similar to APWH but memorize readings!

Pretty good dude that want's to see success in students undoubtedly, but do not expect to cut corners in class. Not reading and annotating is going to cost you a lot, but overall could be much much worse. It's a course that does not consider that you could be taking other rigorous classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment:
I have taken Chang for MMW 11, 12, 13, and 15. My biggest advice for incoming UCSD students, take his class because it will prepare you well ONLY if you are willing to put in the work with all the readings. Reading and taking notes on it is so long but doing this will GUARANTEE you an "A+" 
attend TA Hours because they do the grading for MMW.

reviews.comment:
Don't take MMW with Chang, unless you are ready to READ TONS OF MATERIAL, with low printing quality.

reviews.comment: Great prof, is a very caring man. Lectures are extremely entertaining but the amount of reading needed for that class is astounding. reviews.comment: Annoying class and teacher

His expectations for midterms/finals are very clear though and he makes great study guides. Overall fun lectures but ridiculous amounts of readings assigned.

Chang is an awesome lecturer and a really funny guy. However, he makes you buy the course reader he puts together full of primary sources and it's a lot of weekly reading with quizzes. The tests were okay, but mainly depend on how your TA grades.

I took him for 11 and 12 too. He's an amazing lecturer, very clear and entertaining and he posts lecture notes. There's an insane amount of reading and exams rely almost entirely on the readings, but if you do them and take good notes you're chilling. Lecture attendance not mandatory but helpful, he never mentions the research paper though
Favorite professor I've had at UCSD so far. Super caring and insightful. Very inspirational too. Would definitely recommend for MMW 13, 14, and 15 - open-note exams.
Chang is the goat!

Inspiring and engaging lectures. Literally just go to lecture and you'll be fine. He assigns so much reading but you can easily get away with skimming everything. Quizzes are easy and test expectations are very clear cut. Professor Chang is so knowledgeable and really interesting guy.

SO MANY READINGS! Do not take him if you're dyslexic, I had a hard time remembering 30-40 pages for the reading quizzes :( But don't let this discourage you! He is very nice and extremely passionate on the subject, and I'm glad I had him for my last MMW! He's also really funny, and the lectures always keep me entertained! Only TAs matter for grades

He's such a cool dude, you can build such a great rapport w him but BROOOOO THE READINGS ARE INSANE. imo there are too many that it's hard to get a fundamental understanding of any of the readings since there are so many

Lectures are very entertaining, engaging, and information-filled. The grade is comprised of weekly reading quizzes, course forums, a midterm exam, a final exam, a final paper, and section attendance/participation. He's a good lecturer, but sometimes gets weirdly distracted and won't finish his slides.

Tests: multiple choice, matching, passage ID, final adds an essay. Engaging lectures, but no slides/recording so attendance is key. Tough but informative, learned a lot.

Very difficult class with lots of readings and quizzes for each. You have to pay 50$ for his reader. Nice person with interesting stories, learned a lot from classes. Study hard for tests, but theres a study guide with most info. Mostly Ta graded assignments. Lecture not mandatory, but important for info for tests. No posted slides or vids.
honestly mmw 121 was one of my favorite classes because of chang. his lectures are interesting and if you get the right ta, you can totally get an a in the class.

didn't attend lecture once and still got an A in the class. highly recommend reading the textbook pages he assigns yourself and then using ai tools to help you trudge through the course reader to make the course load less overwhelming. he basically gives you the entire midterm/final on the study guides so you have no excuse to not do well
Stay on top of stuff and you will be fine. It is difficult but manageable.

Chang is such an amazing dude. He truly loves what he does and cares for all of his students. He will go out of his way to ask for your name in the middle of the lecture and remember it. I would 100% recommend taking Chang. You get used to the readings, and the overall experience is worth it even with the heavy readings.

MMW 11/12

Great teacher because he really cares about the subject and the content, which leads to informative lectures. Hes not a bad professor just a bad class the class just takes up so much time and there is so much work its ridiculous. and he expects us to read so much (40+ pages before each lecture) and a course forum with peer review weekly with quizzes every week. the quizzes aren't hard but the paper and reading is long and bad. will drain you mentally
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

Loved prof. chang, such a silly dude, but seriously reading heavy class. Like, 40+ pages twice per week. But he really, at the end of the day, cares more that you understand cause and affect. Tests are remarkably AP adjacent, and overall I enjoyed the learning!

reviews.comment: Expect a heavy workload, but Chang is an engaging lecturer who makes the dense material digestible. Go to class, use the study guide, and try Unstuck study AI for extra prep - you can get an A if you put in the effort.

I took Chang for 11 and I get his lecture-heavy style, but it just doesn't work in 13. Lots of reading from HIS book, no recordings, unusual test structure, but a very good lecturer.
my 13th reason
Do the reading, and prepare for the intellectual ride Chang will take you on.

Wonderful lecturer and clearly cares so much about his students. MMW (especially 12) kinda sucks by design but he works hard to make the content interesting and engaging. The reading is a lot and the test are intense, but if you stay on top of everything the class is doable. He means it when he says the test are about preparation, not memorization.

Chang gives amazing lectures and is very engaging. There are one or two weekly quizzes and LOTS of reading, but you'll probably learn lots. My TA was very strict and graded very harshly, but cared a lot about teaching. Overall, only take the class if you're willing to put work in.

reviews.comment: With all the reading and weekly quizzes, people aren't too fond of his classes, which I understand, but overall he's a nice guy and really does care about his students, I took him as well for MMW 15. He's really not that bad

He has a course reader for every class, its miserably long and the print is tiny. The midterm is multiple choice, matching terms and passage ID's and the final is the same but it has an essay. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great lecturer and does a great job finding modern significance in historical events. There are a lot of dense readings but lecture explains them really well. He's super approachable and kind, genuinely cares about the subject and wants students to succeed in his class. If you sit near the front, he will teach AT you (heads up lol).

Yes he does assign a lot of reading, but he is a spectacular lecturer and actually explains why the reading are significant. He is also very understanding and cares about engaging his students, highly recommend going to his office hours. The more you actually like your final essay topic the less painful it is to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There was a lot of hate on him but I loved this class and came out with an A. Go to his lectures, that's where all the important info is. The TAs are the ones who grade so understand their requirements. Only one essay during the final, and all other assignments are pretty quick

Professor Chang was an amazing lecturer. The key is to note down what he SAYS about each text. The midterm is a bit more difficult that the final and the exams were open note so take advantage. Only take if you actually want to read and don't just want an easy A. Readings assigned 2x week ~ 20-25 pages. Engaging and funny lectures, but would not take again due to workload and readings.

reviews.comment: I think Chang gets a bad rap, but he's probably one of the most interesting professors I'll encounter at UCSD. The class is perfectly completable assuming you actually do the work. Mandatory reader and lots of reading from it and the textbook, but it's manageable. Lectures aren't mandatory but worth attending, as he's so funny and really illuminates the course material. Chang's lectures were very well structured, he really tried to connect on a personal level with his students, and the passion he has is evident. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Was worried about the workload but it honestly wasn't that bad. He goes over the readings in class. The slides he shares in class aren't that important, it's what he says about them. Awesome professor and an inspiring class. Take him!

Great professor for MMW 13, don't listen to previous reviews. Yes there is a lot to read every week, and yes you do need to make sure to annotate. But the readings are very insightful,  and apart from that there is only one essay due. Would heavily recommend the class if you want to learn a lot but is willing to sacrifice more time into this class.

Cool and funny professor, but the readings assigned are hell. You will need to treat it like a full-time job because you will be spending more time reading and writing than doing your major classes combined.

reviews.comment: Although this class was challenging since there are a lot of readings (which was challenging to cram in 5 weeks), he truly cares for his students. I dont think Chang deserves the poor reputation he has. It was a lot of reading for a summer session but even with working I managed. He also is a pretty nice guy and is passionate about his students and course. It's a tough class but he makes the material interesting.

Great lectures, but SO MUCH READING! Readings are mandatory for reading quizzes. Up to 100 pages a week easily from his own reader! The money you spend on the reader lines his pockets. Downright greedy if you ask me. Lectures were always good though, but didn't offer much else besides regular MMW curriculum. DO NOT TAKE if you're a STEM major!!

This course is a GE course but it is treated like an upper division History course. There are a lot of readings a week and very few lectures so the majority of the content is through the readings. The readings average about 15 pages with about 6 readings per lecture.

went into this class expecting a train wreck based on other reviews, but to my shock I ended up enjoying all of the lectures and readings...sheesh it's a lot of work but his lectures are low key engaging. would recommend, but def do the readings, would NOT recommend slacking

A lot of reading from his $40+ reader, 2 midterms, and 1 final in addition to the writing project. You HAVE to do the readings for the exams and weekly quizzes. STUDY GUIDES HELP A TON DOTHEM

reviews.comment: BEST PROFESSOR EVER!

Such a fantastic professor to start MMW. He really tries to hype people up for the entire MMW sequence. Reading quizzes are randomly given, and they are worth a solid amount of your grade. Readings are extremely long. Prepare for 50 pages of reading regularly. If reading is not your forte, take Jordan. Gives extensive study guides for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Chang is really funny and nice. He engaged well with the class. The class definitely has a lot of reading and he has a reading quiz every week si you definitely have to show up to class. It's nice that he has these quizzes though because it takes pressure off of the midterm and final.

Professor Chang is a great lecturer. He lectures like story telling, and often would incorporate some humor into his lecture. Your grade depends entirely on the TA, and most of them are very tough graders. Chang also provides a very "extensive" study guide 1 week before the midterm and final. Lots of terms, concept, historical events to remember.

He's an outstanding lecturer.  The material he gives his students is phenomenal. Great sense of humor and just a good personality. He cares a lot about his students and really gives you a deeper understanding and perspective on what you are actually reading. Overall, AMAZING! I really do recommend Chang! He's the best of the best!

Prof Chang's lectures are very organized and coherent. Not only does he gives you an outline of his lecture but he also connects concepts to important themes. In addition, his study guides give you exactly what you need to know for exams. Grading wise, it really depends on your TA And how generous he or she is. Dont get behind on readings.
He is one of the best professors ever. I enjoyed going to his class.
Good lecturer. Just do the study guides and you can get As on the tests

Prof. Chang is awesome. His lectures are at times pretty inspirational! He def. knows his stuff, and he's great at putting things in perspective. He made me realize so much about the world! His lectures are engaging and he's pretty funny too. At times he digresses from the lecture, but that's OK, it makes the lecture more interesting.

This is a writing class. Be prepared to read and write. Attend class as the readings are super dense. Take good notes. Your TA is the only one who grades anything. He can be confusing. I think he means well, but I highly recommend the writing center and TA office hours to get a good grade. Hard exams but provides a study guide. Start papers early.

Chang is an excellent professor in the sense that he is clear, concise and entertaining during his lectures.  He also gives out study guides for the midterm and final that are almost identical due to the final and midterm. If you understand everything on the midterm, the midterm and final are EASY. Your writing  grade depends on your TA.

This IS a hard class, so if you find it struggling, it's not his fault. The class is actually very interesting, if you do all the readings (which is a lot though...). He is funny, passionate. Read ahead of time and you will do well in exams. Papers were given and graded by TA, so you need to attend dissucions. Overall I would say he is amazing.
Hand down !! Best MMW prof ever ! He give you the study guild that look exactly like what appear on mid-term and final :)

He is a great teacher, but I feel that the theme of the first quarter tied in together better, than the second one. Your grade depends on your TA, so you better learn their grading styles. I think he is clear on what he expects from you on the test. Lectures are not mandatory but it does see like it bothers him when people don't show up.
You won't fall asleep in his lectures and the material was alright. You have to buy a $100 reader though (didn't really read it).  Make sure to ace the research paper!

Lecture is a must as his tests are based off the information he talks about during lecture. He makes you buy a $100 course reader, but you really don't need it. He is an amazing lecturer and keeps you engaged with his style of discourse and funny jokes here and there. Would definitely take again if I had the luck to get in his.

The readings are ancient religious pieces, but the lectures (and essay assignments) were all based on his very subjective interpretations of what these mean in his personal life journey. Ugh. He mocked believers and nonbelievers, claiming  "I'll make agnostics of you all". Repeat his beliefs in your essays for As, if you can stomach his rants.

I love Chang. He's funny and tries to connect the context to current issues.  His lectures are heavily based off the readings, so you can possibly get away with not a reading once or twice, but the readings do help. His study guides are a lot of work but give you a fair chance of being well prepared for his test. Overall great professor!

Chang is a funny guy. I always wanted to skip class, but I never regretted going once I was there. He's a good lecturer, and taught me a lot. His office hours are all about him, which makes it hard to have a good conversation. He assigns hella reading, but you really only have to do the Bentley and some parts of the reader and you'll be fine.
Great professor

He is a very good professor and knows his stuff focus more on your essays then the actual reading material use your TA and your writing center to ensure an A. DONT GET BEHIND ON READING! Test are easy with his study guides.

I took 4 classes with Chang, and he is very helpful and wants to get to know his students. He encourages students to introduce themselves during office hours. His tests are given ahead of time  in the review outline. The extra credit come  from the tangents he talks about in class.

Professor Chang is the best! He's so passionate about history and he clearly loves to teach. Which is great because he's damn good at it! The best thing about him is that he's very approachable and easy to talk to. Don't be afraid to introduce yourself to him, he's like the nicest guy in the world and really cares about all his students!

Dr. Chang has been one of the best professors I've had at UCSD. His lecture style is one I favor. He is very passionate and it shows in his lectures. He truly cares for his students and provides them with all of the resources in order to succeed in his class. He is very approachable and a pleasure to chat with after class and during office hours.

Lectures are generally useless and full of several useless anecdotes from his personal life. The writing aspects of the class are rarely discussed, and readings and lectures are both useless if you just use wikipedia to complete study guides.

Chang is amazing! He is very passionate about teaching and is very helpful when it comes to exams. He is very supportive and really inspired me in his lectures. He is straightforward and he tells you what you need to know for the exams. I really loved his class!!! And my TA Sascha was so nice and helpful which made the class that much better!

Very passionate about his work. Teaches in a style where he just talks to the class. Teaches class off an outline he posts online. Midterm was very challenging. 3 papers that I wasn't interested in. You need to work hard. It's the TA's that matter.

He is a nice prof, but for me, an international student, taking notes at his class is really difficult. the review guide is always super super long. although i went to all his lecture and did all the readings, i still cannot rememeber everything for his exam.
his lecture was good, but he doesn't care about his students at all!!
Chang was the best MMW professor ever! Just go to lecture and listen and you'll get an A. Study guides are very helpful. He is really interesting and engages with the class. Loved him!

For some reason I felt MMW 21 was easier with him. There were a lot more terms to memorize this time so the class isn't exactly difficult. It's just a lot of memorization. I suggest u go to class and pay attention or take a tape recorder. Otherwise he gives an amazing lecture
Great guy. Gives the best lectures because he connects what he's teaching to a broader lesson. He has a way of teaching that speaks to each and every person in the room.

Great guy, and if you can stay awake, his lectures are actually pretty intriguing. However, TA's pretty much determine your grade since they grade your tests and essays. He gives you a study guide for each midterm/final that's 100% what the test will look like (of course you won't know the questions he'll choose). Not a bad class at all.

He is one of the best professors I have ever had. His lectures are so interesting that I actually liked coming to class. Originally I really hated the idea of taking this class but now after sitting through Chang's lectures I don't mind one bit.
Provides pretty thorough notes, can do well if listen in lecture without reading. Exams are A OK.

He's so nice and sweet. He tells lectures like a story and keeps you interested. He's pretty funny sometimes and he is super chill. It's the TA's you need to watch out for, they make or break your grade.

One of the best MMW professors! Lectures are very interesting. Chang tells it like a story and keeps you connecting things to the themes of the course. Very nice guy and genuinely is concerned about his students. Grading varies from TA to TA though. You must have Chang at least once in during your MMW sequence or else you will be missing out.
Great professor. But grades depend on the TA that you get....so rating the "easiness" really does not matter since the TAs do the grading.

Chang is a person that is rare to find anymore. He is passionate and humble, and just his character alone is enough to teach a student, let alone his class material. Go to class and take great notes and you will do well in his class. Absorb what he is teaching, because if we all did, we'd become better people in life.

Really fun guy to listen to during class. His tests are all based on what he says in lecture so I really recomend that u go. The best thing to do would be to buy a recoder and tape it. Really helps when u are going over the study guide. And grades are all based on what TA u get. Mine was really nice and graded easy, but some might not be that way..
Best lecturer ever. Must take class!

This guy is pretty cool. I absolutely hate MMW though. It's really annoying and time consuming, especially when you're a science/engineering major.Chang's exams are pretty fair. Study his review guides and you'll be fine. As for the papers though, it's all up to your TA. Luckily, I got a pretty easy going TA.
best professor at ucsd, enough said.
Professor Chang is so approachable and definitely cares about his students. Go to office hours!

AWESOME AWESOME. Out of all the professors for MMW, he's definitely the easiest IMO. His lectures are straightforward AND he puts a lecture outline online [but doesn't podcast]. He gives you study guides for the MTs and final, the terms are straight from lecture, AND he gives you the passage IDs and essay prompt ahead of time.

He is such a good professor! I love attending his lectures he is very good at explaining the subject matter. Tests are easy if you attend the lectures and take good notes. He gives review sessions before exams too! Would strongly recommend him. I'm taking him for MMW 5 too!

His lectures are great, like storytelling but the tests are HARD. SO much is on the study guides that it is impossible to know them all. Test structure for me was very difficult, matching obscure terms.

Pretty interesting Professor to have if you get a chance to take one of his courses. Besides the material you're supposed to learn he's full of interesting stories related to the class and it's great when he gets guest lecturers there. This man is funny to be around and his lectures are great to listen to! Fun, entertaining, and educational!!

This is by far one of the best Prof.'s at UCSD! Seriously! If you have to take the MMW sequence, do yourself a favor and take at least a class by him! He's on top of his lectures--everything's organized and clear. His study guides really help, too. He's really into wanting ppl to learn, and not as much into testing, so tests are extremely fair.

As a Poli-Sci Major, I've taken lots of politics classes. Of all the classes I have taken here, no professor has been more biased than him. He is extremely liberal and rants about how much he hates conservatives almost everyday. He referred to himself as "marxist leaning" in class after talking about how the IMF and World Bank are evil capitalists.

Professor Chang is the best professor I have had so far! He makes lectures interesting, and his outlines for the lectures make it easy to write down quality notes to study off of. His study guide is awesome!! He is very approachable and available for help about the course. Everyone should want Chang for MMW.

He is the BEST MMW teacher one could have. His lectures are VERY clear and easy to follow, unlike Jordan and Herbst who's lectures are all over the place. He is also extremely kind and ecstatic about what he is teaching. Chang is open and accessible outside of class. If you pay attention to lecture, you will do fine in the class.

He's an okay lecturer. He does his job and teaches. Not the most exciting, but one of the better prof. for mmw.  He gives study guide so is doable.  You can get a good grade in this class only if you get a good ta. But he is fair and is always helpful in & out of class.

Great professor!! He is very captivating.  I hate history, but he made that class one of my favorites.  He is unintentionally funny, which makes class always interesting.  You never know what he will say.

Great professor with a lot of passion in teaching the lessons that can be learned from history. I've had him ever since MMW2 and it's mostly been a smooth ride for the past 4 quarters with him. Just be sure to stay alert or otherwise you'll miss out on essential notes.

I really liked him as a professor overall. His lectures were interesting and they facilitated note-taking. However, his class requires a lot of reading (more than other MMW 4 classes) and two midterms. He isn't the most approachable at first, but get to know him because he's actually very friendly and helpful.

Your grade depends on your TA, that's how it is in MMW. He gave out study guide which was helpful. It was a little hard for me to take notes in his class, he used a lot of big words. The Bentley book is useless, so u could just save some money. Sometimes i think it is unfair to depend ur grades on TA, cuz every Ta had a different standard..

If you study for his exams, you will get an A since he provides a full study guide. Nice guy, good professor. Grade depends on TA as for all of MMW. Lecture style does not facilitate note taking until you have him more than once. Often goes on tangents.

Dr. Chang is a great lecturer; he organizes his lectures very well and links them together in a story format that is easy to follow. He also provides review guides before the tests which basically outline his tests. He is a very nice guy and very approachable. He does not surprise you in the tests, but he has a lot of reading to do.

I love Dr. Chang, he is the best teacher. His tests are difficult but he gives an amazing study guide. He is an awesome lecturer and he has interesting stories to help illustrate his points. Highly highly recommend him.

Easily one of the best teachers I've ever had. He makes MMW not only bearable but very enjoyable. I've had days full of crap but Prof. Chang always proves to be a bright spot in a rainy day. He will give you a more worldly perspective.
