My Favorite Professor so far at UCSD! He is so passionate about his subject, and genuinely cares about teaching things that are useful. Tests are easy to study for because he gives a very extensive study guide, and lectures are always interesting-His outline is very easy to follow/take notes on. Take him for MMW!!!!

Professor Chang is entertaining at times. However, I think he makes events connect to each other in ways that don't make any sense. The MMW TA makes or breaks your grade (Cat Gmuca is a difficult grader).

I've had Chang for four quarter of MMW. He is extremely passionate aobut everything he teaches and doesn't get caught up on history facts and dates. Rather, he lectures on big picture ideas. After these courses you are able to relate each one to the next and it's a continuous learning experience of how the world came to be what it is today.

Professor Chang is probably the best MMW professor on campus.  He really enjoys teaching and the material in class.  I had him for both section and lecture.  I would highly recommend all incoming MMW students to try to get him for MMW.

Chang is so passionate about MMW. I have Herbst now, an even though his lectures on history might be more interesting, Chang's lectures on philosophy and religion are just so passionate, he really wants you to understand the world and he's extremely helpful and nice in the process. The tests are easy and hes a really nice guy, like a little Buddha!

Chang is seriously my favorite professor at UCSD --he is a very genuine guy, and you can tell he is very passionate about what he is teaching. He is very helpful, easy to talk to, and funny. HIGHLY reccommend Chang for your MMW experience!!!

Great guy. After taking him for 4, it made me regret not picking him for 2 and 3 as well. Two midterms w/ MC, short answer, and IDs (given ahead of time so you can memorize them), useful study guide, and outlined lectures. Lectures were fairly interesting and he had open review sessions before every exam. He also reminds me of my dad.

I have taken Chang for 3 quarters of MMW (2,3,4). He is great MMW professor! He outlines all his lectures for you which makes it really easy to take lecture notes. I would highly recommend everyone who wants to enjoy there 6 quarters of MMW to take Chang.

His lectures can sometimes be boring, but go if you're not going to read, because he goes over the important readings during class.  ALso, he gives an overwhelming study guide for midterms & finals, listed with 100+ vocab words, 4-8 passage IDs, and essay questions.  If you review this, you'll be set for the exam.

Very approachable and makes the class interesting. Lectures don't have overwhelming amounts of info (sometimes I felt this way in Herbst/Chamberlain) and the material is not that difficult to learn and memorize. Since he gives you a great study guide with passages included you don't have to do the reading to do well. I

Chang is AWESOME! He is super friendly, approachable, and truly cares about his students. His lectures hold your attention pretty well, especially since he likes to crack some jokes here and there. I've had him for MMW2, MMW3, & MMW4. It would be a mistake if you didn't take this man.

I had Professor Chang for both MMW3 and MMW4. He is by far the best teacher I've ever had and is super friendly! I don't know anyone who doesn't like him and his classes always fill up the fastest. His study guides are extremely helpful so as long as you know everything on it, you're set for the test. He's always willing to help on essays + tests!
all i gots to say is study guides! a great prof, and he is very clear. needless to say, the study guides are helpful :)
he was extremely clear and to the point. made it extremly easy to get an A in the class
too cool for school. loves turtles!

Awesome professor. Definitely knows his subject matter and loves to teach it. His lectures are interesting, but also follow the reading closely. Tests are easy, but be sure to read everything since he likes to put questions on it that you could only know from doing reading all the source material. TAKE THIS PROFESSOR.
approachable and friendly. knowledgeable about his history. clear lectures, lecture outlines and study guides online. He is a newbie as a professor but he's quickly catching up. laidback and chill.

Chang is HILARIOUS. he is the nicest guy i have ever met.  he is very helpful, and always wants you to come talk to him in office hours if u need help. i had him as a TA too, and he was the BEST! Chang was one of my favorite professors this quarter. take him if you can. and hte study guides are short and to the point!
Chang was boring, often would go off topic during lecture and did not hold my attention the entire class. Study guides are way too elongated and convers way too much material. I do not recommend
No Comments
Don't take PSYC 70 unless you have to. Prof is good, just boring content and they randomly grade tough. The exams are all multiple choice traps too.

You can tell she really cares about her students' success! She takes “a flipped classroom” approach, so you watch the lectures before class and do group work during class time to test your knowledge. I learned a lot from this approach, but keep in mind there's lots of material to learn so additional study time is likely needed.

Her tests require a lot of memorization. She uses wording meant to trick you, she doesn't teach. All you do is come in and take a quiz then leave. Lectures are from 2020, some updates needed to her material as well.
Don't take this class. She uses trick wording on her exams.

Lectures were prerecorded from the COVID period and reused without updates, and class time involved minimal teaching. As a result, learning the material required a large amount of independent study. The exams relied on tricky wording, which made the course especially difficult for students who are not strong test-takers.

Prof Geller was trying a new layout for this course with a flipped classroom with three lectures due on Sundays and weekly group assignments & quizzes. Honestly didn't love this layout. It was meant to promote collaboration/discussion, but most of the time groups would divide and do work in silence. It seemed like the grading scale changed a lot.
Professor Geller is an amazing professor. Her courses are very straightforward and if you apply yourself you will do well. She cares so much about her students and it shows.

One of the more engagement-heavy classes but pretty fair. Group work on mondays, group quizzes on wednesdays and fridays mainly off. The material is also mainly self-paced and individual quizzes due on sundays.

Prof. Geller is one of the best teachers I've ever had. Feels like she wants you to succeed. She's very organized, and her teaching style is super efficient. 2 midterms and a final, all mcq. Best study method is rewatching lectures 1-2x and doing the practice quizzes. Content itself is dense and not super easy to understand without studying.

Okay, I just gotta be honest here as a student currently taking this course (and not having a bad score), currently an A, but this come at the cost of constant studying. You could cram everything in for the last two days before the exams, but just let me tell you that it's a lot of lectures and notes to cover. It's doable (I did it), just a lot.

I wait until the end of my time at UCSD to leave ratings for all my instructors as I don't like hiding behind anonymity. This professor is amazing I took her summer of 24. At the time Inez was the TA. They both did great. Dr. Geller changed the way I think about the field of psychology in a good way. She truly teaches well. 

-Aria.

She's cool and all but these quizzes and final are horrendous. Only extra credit is SONA and evaluations. She only drops 1 quiz  anything, curve, or round grades. Studied for hours but didn't pay off in the end because the quizzes weren't very similar to study guides or practice tests. A lot of dense material hard to stay on track.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lectures. She is amazing in answering any questions. Lots of practice in class and for HW. Quizzes are extremely similar to exams. As long as you do study for this class you'll do great.

I really liked PSYC70. There is a term paper but it's short and they hold your hand all quarter so it's not too bad. The midterm/final were pretty reflective of lectures and not bad. My favorite part of the class was her lectures as they were super engaging and interesting. She gives a lot of example problems too. Overall I really liked the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing!! Love Dr. Geller's teaching style and though this class seemed boring at first, I LOVED it. Feels like a lot of assignments, but every one is beneficial! Because of them + in lecture questions, I felt v prepared for the final & midterm. She's very welcoming and kind, always wants to help students do their best. 100% recommend

Even though attendance was mandatory, the lecture quizzes made it easy to learn and understand the topics. You work on the research paper in discussion which was also really helpful. Overall, I really enjoyed the structure of Geller's class and how she taught. Every assignment felt beneficial and prepared me for the midterm and final.

Professor Geller uses a "flipped classroom," which means that ALL "lectures" are online that you have watch, and the in-person lectures are "labs and review," in which you basically do homework. Personally, I was a big fan of this style because it allowed me to be able to go back to review. Her tests are pretty tough, but lots of extra credit.

Geller is a fantastic professor who is caring and knowledgeable. There are 3 recorded lectures outside regular lecture time per week, 2 labs per week, a quiz every week, 2 midterms and a cumulative final. I found the exams to be very tough and there was a lot of work, but the professor is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The midterms are VERYY VERYY HARD! I spent hours on this class and it did not pay off. She's very nice but genuinely VERY VERY difficult exams and assignment heavy, if you're looking for an easy class  do not take this.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Engaging lectures, but messy project structure lacking clear criteria. Very delayed feedback that's inconsistent between students. What specifically to address in FRQ on exams is ambiguous. Geller has an anxious presentation, insecure about her understanding of materials sometimes too. Seems friendly yet has little patience for incompetence.

I think shes awesome. It does feel like a lot of material though with the lectures being posted online and reviews on the first day of the class in the week. mini ''labs'' during class time to further understand the content of the weeks material in a more researcher mindset. Lectures allow you to study using active recal

Geller is great, organized and caring. Attendance is graded through assignments in lecture. Busywork, but really not that difficult and helps to stay engaged with course material. Most of the quizzes/exams are about understanding the (many) terms, slides give you everything you need. Final APA paper has nitpicky grading, follow the rubric exactly.

Attendance was kind of mandatory because of in class questions, but lectures were very clear and helpful; covered everything we needed to know. Had to write a whole APA paper but we were (kinda) walked through it. She's a very good educator, you can tell she cares about the subject and students

She is an amazing professor. Her lectures are very clear, very helpful, and though there is a lot of work every week, the lectures walk you through most of it and really help you understand them all! This is a very straightforward class. Attend lectures, pay attention, set aside time to study, and you'll pass easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is a busy-work class; none of the material is particularly hard, but it's a LOT. I took this class in the summer, though, which definitely made the work load feel worse. You have a bundle of weekly assignments plus two papers. The professor is really helpful, and her lectures are clear!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had! It was really clear that she cared about her students. Scarily good at coming up with questions that challenge students and highlight points of confusion. Definitely requires actual understanding of the content rather than memorization, but I think that's a good thing. Take this class!

Dr. Geller is one of the most kind professors I have ever met. She goes out of her way to make sure that students are following the material and that the workload is maintainable. She is also extremely personable and approachable for discussion about the class or about career and grad school questions (or just fun discussion!). Take her!!!

I'm STUNNED by all these negative reviews. They must not understand what a Research Methods class is about or just appropriate expectations for a college class? I took this class because of Dr. Geller's great reputation. She's an OVERLY caring and compassionate professor. Assignments give grade buffer and make it easier to do well. One of the best!

The professor gives way too many assignments in a single week and expects perfect performance on every single one of them, despite the fact that she spreads students thin. Grading was inconsistent and students had to regularly check in with TAs and the professor to get their work graded correctly.

This class was supposed to be in person but changed  to an online format. Very sad about that, but despite it being online, hands down one of my favorite classes that I have taken here at UCSD. The format was weekly quizzes (10, 2 lowest dropped), 3 modules per week, one mini lab, then 2 exams, and a final. Quizzes and exams weren't too bad!

Demoralizing structure of assignments and quizzes/exams.
It's as she expects this to be the only course during the quarter. The "mini-lectures" often go over 20 minutes and sometimes even 30 minutes and tedious. Very poor assistance and although she constantly reminds you of her being there to help, the so called "help" is ridiculous and so minute.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: So much busy work it’s crazy. A midterm exam, a final exam, a midterm paper, AND a final paper. On top of that a quiz every week on the same material the final and midterm already test us on?! honestly I find the amount of work ridiculous and unnecessary. Avoid her if you can.

You will be buried in so many unnecessary weekly readings and assignments. Grading is ridiculously harsh for APA paper with notsohelpful feedback. The quizzes and exams are beyond ludicrous with so many tricky and weird wordings. Too much work without effective help or system to accommodate the difficulty and workload. Do not take her for psyc70.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lots of assignments with weekly reading and quiz. Wording of questions on quizzes and exams are tricky. There’s also a big apa paper to write and graded harshly.

Honestly I did not enjoy this class. There's so many weekly assignments to do and some just seem a little unnecessary? Her weekly quizzes can be pretty tricky with the wording. There's a big APA paper due at the end, but she's looking for very specific detail and grades pretty harshly. She just throws info at you without actually teaching it.

Seems like a good person but definitely not a good 'teach'-er. Some concepts that she does not mention during lectures later often tend to be reason why certain problem should be interpreted in a certain way. Most importantly, the way test questions are formed/worded are simply ridiculous. It's not even the content difficulty but the tricks/wording

Professor Geller is great at what she teaches. Cognitive psyc is hard to explain in general and I felt that I grasped everything she taught. Her only downside is lots of work throughout the week, but to be fair, there was a lot of info to cover throughout the course. The tests are not easy but fair. They are timed at 1 hour or 3 hours for the final
Worst professor and teacher. Her lecture video does not help nor clearly teaching. Lazy teacher. She knows how to drag your grade down for sure.
Video lectures and exams don't match. Her course drags your GPA down for sure.
DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. Dr Geller is a great person but not for teaching. She has too much HW and heavy exams. Extra credit does not worth a lot of points lol

She is one of the best professor that I ever met. Honestly, there are many teachers that are very smart but suck at teaching. But this professor gives me a good impression. I love the way how she format the course. Take her class if you are a severe procrastinator that struggle with online learning mode. You will learn a lot with her.

Love her lectures: questions are embedded in them that everyone has to answer on their own form, but she encourages discussion especially of the wrong answers. If you say something wrong, you won't get shamed. There is a big 12-page APA style paper you write over 4 weeks, but instructions are precise; not bad if you don't cram. Solid class overall.

Dr. Geller is a great professor overall. She gives amazing lectures and is really good at making sure you understand the material. However, her quizzes and exams are actually ridiculous and a horrible representation of the material learned. Expect to feel like you are constantly being tricked!!!!

Prof. Geller is nice and has a very clear setup of the class. Her lectures are very interesting and full of info. However, her tests are incredibly hard. To do well on the tests, you need to actually understand the concept rather than memorizing it. They are such abstract and specific questions. Make sure to listen to EVERYTHING in her lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very kind professor, interesting lectures, the only problem I have are the exams, they were difficult. Even if you understand everything from lecture, the test questions seem to be a lot more difficult in a way where simply memorizing the concept isn't enough, you truly have to test your self to see if you can apply the question to a setting.

Her tests don't test you on your ability to learn new material. Instead, they test your cleverness in puzzling out abstract scenarios that only vaguely relate to the material. She also uses a lot of confirming communication but does so insincerely. She has all the empathy of Mark Zuckerberg. Do not recommend.

Professor Geller is a great professor. I was worried about transitioning to an online format but Professor Geller is incredibly organized and communicates her expectations very clearly. She is very fair, her quizzes/exams are based on lecture materials and modules (no surprises). You can tell she genuinely cares about her students success. TAKE HER

Have taken five classes with her and I can tell you she is the go-to professor if you wish to learn. She is super passionate about teaching, she can explain the concepts in a clear manner, and she takes pain to give students the best learning experience that she could offer. The classes surely aren't easy but you learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: You'll actually learn in her class because her lectures are constructed to facilitate understanding. Her tests are more conceptual than your typical (so obviously more difficult), but fun to do if you actually study for her class. She explains and clarifies concepts really well if you're confused, and is always willing to help! 10/10 :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You have a choice of reading the textbook for several hours or go to lecture for a little over an hour. It's pretty boring in her class, but she tells you everything you need to know and reviews everything you need to know several times a day. You probably won't fall asleep because it's pretty fast-paced. She's very caring and she's an anime fan.

Taking her for the second time and still enjoy her classes. Lecture attendance is mandatory but she knows the material well and keeps the class engaged. Tests are a little unusual if you aren't used to conceptual based questions and there is a fair bit of homework to keep up with but other than that, she's extremely helpful and easy to learn from
She is a great professor, very nice and well-spoken. She explains information clearly and gives many examples to help you understand.

Professor Geller is one of the best I have had at UCSD. She gives really clear and easy to understand lectures that are also very interesting. She does require participation in class but homework is pretty light. Exams aren't too bad, overall a great class

Dr. Geller is amazing! This doesn't mean her class is easy though. I struggled with the exams, but she's super attentive during office hours. Grades consist of two midterms and a final, weekly quizzes (not too difficult), daily in-class participation through topHat, and reading (also on topHat).

shes great! this is a hard class with lots of very dense concepts but she explains it very well and throughly! She is very knowledgable of the subject and takes the time to answer each question from students. she is pretty quick at responding her emails as well. Her exams are difficult and tricky but if you really apply yourself youll be fine!

The class itself is kinda dry but it's a psych requirement. Overall I think Prof Geller did a good job, her lectures were clear and interesting, and she cares about students a lot. Weekly quizzes + attendance points so have to attend class (she does podcast too tho). Exams kinda tricky but not horrible. APA paper was annoying but useful info.

Great class and professor. She is very accessible outside of class and very caring. Her lectures keep you interested and she is really funny and obviously very smart. You are graded by a lot of things so even if you don't perform extremely well on exams you have a good chance at still getting an A. 10/10. Abstract concepts but easy if you read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Geller is a phenomenal professor and her lectures were very insightful and easy to follow. She's open to any and all questions and really took pride in making sure all of her students understood the material. I felt that cognitive psychology was more of a dense course; but she teaches you a lot and she's actually pretty funny. highly recommend

Great prof. genuinely cares about students' performance. took it as a night class. very active learning environment. She's very patient. retrieval practice sections during lecture and repeats any unclear concepts. learned LOT of interesting concepts (ex memory, INTELLIGENCE) that can help me be a better student too! knows a lot! Best textbook ever

Very organized and weekly quizzes help you stay on top of material. Quizzes are easy if you read weekly research articles. Final was not too hard thanks to the weekly quizzes and peer instruction(clicker)questions. Need to attend class. APA paper was annoying but doable and useful for psych majors. Content isnt bad but some topics are harder
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Gives very clear lectures and is very helpful. Will answer any questions you have. Weekly quizzes that are very easy (and actually helpful for studying for the test). Participation in class & section counts for grade. Has you write an APA-style research paper which is great practice for those interested in research/grad school. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Geller is a wonderfully organized lecturer and professor. Every aspect of the class is thoughtful and organized making it incredibly easy to find resources and succeed. Weekly quizzes keep you on top of the material and readings are relevant and interesting. You'll want to work hard in her class and it will pay off!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There are weekly quizzes which forces you to keep up with the material. She is just GREAT when it comes to questions and clarifications about the material. E-mail her or post on discussion board and she's been willing to explain again. The final was super hard compared to anything else but if you do well throughout the class, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She's nice & specifies when you ask her to. But she gives you a quiz a week and they're DIFFICULT. Also, the midterm class average was around a C-. Its one of those tests where you think you didn't do too bad, then you did horrible. Also, she assigns a really hard final and a final paper (which is graded pretty harshly). Overall, i don't recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He is a really kind professor who clearly cares about his students and the subject. There are a lot of readings and some are combined so they can get long. The class had one final essay and a proctored final, both manageable if you keep up. Attendance is required.

He is amazing. His essay and final exams are not really tough and easy for A+. Although the reading assignments are pretty annoying. You can definitely be absent-minded on his lecture cuz they are not helpful for exams.

AMAZING PROF! He really cares for the students. There was no midterm and 2 "finals" which were really easy (easy A). Attendance is mandatory, but u could easily just write your name in the attendance sheet and leave class. There is a lot of reading, but all readings are interesting and are in Perrusall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Fusté is amazing, he cares so much about his students and tries to be as accessible as possible to ensure that every student feels prepared in class. The readings he assigns are interesting and his lecturers are great for anyone with ADHD/ADD because he speaks at a pace that is easy to follow. I love his classes!

ABSOLUTELY TAKE HIS CLASSES !! he's so caring and you can tell he enjoys his job and cares about the community, he's very sweet! everyone felt comfortable to share out in class. he made me realize I want to study more into ethnic studies :) readings are also great I was showing some of the articles to my whole fam bam, they've very interesting

AMAZING!! i love him I'm going to be taking his classes in the future for sure! he's very easy to talk to, he makes lectures fun, i rlly enjoyed his class. he gave everyone extra days to turn stuff in if needed which is very generous. theres a lot of readings assigned but they're super interesting. Best prof ive ever taken we need more like him :)

Professor Fuste is very charismatic! In his lectures, he likes to hear what the students have to say, and his grading style makes you feel less restricted on assignments. He does sometimes get distracted during lectures lol and there is a bit more amount of assignments throughout the course than in other classes.

The transition to this class being online was definitely difficult, yet Jose made it work. He is incredibly lenient and understanding. There were two group projects that didn't have a terrible workload, however groups were randomly assigned. Most of your grade was based on discussion posts.

A lot of readings, but I managed to get an A+ without reading. Pay attention to lectures and you'll understand the process of racism in our society. 2 group projects, very easy points but can be difficult if your group members suck. (random assignment) He's a great lecturer, cares about his students, and always addresses student concerns/issues!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Fuste was absolutely amazing. He is so passionate about what he teaches and he genuinely cares about what your opinions and beliefs. His class is NOT an easy A, as he does assign a lot of work however, he makes the class totally worth it. Take him if you genuinely want to learn new things and broaden your mind!
UCSD needs more professors like him!!! So sad he's leaving :(

I've taken him for multiple courses now and he's my favorite UCSD professor! Won't bore you like other ethnic professors will and connects every concept to modern day events and within the SD region. A LOT of reading but he thoroughly goes over it and constantly warns people to not fall behind on them. THE SCHOOL NEEDS MORE PROFESSORS LIKE HIM!!

Assigns a lot of reading, and has weekly reflection papers based on the readings but the material is interesting and they help for midterm and final paper. He's a great lecturer, passionate inspirational and funny! Also likes to having discussions which keep lectures interactive. One of my fave profs! Oh and readings are on Ted, no textbook!!
Professor Fusté is always willing to help students and as a lecturer he is amazing.
Fuste is a great lecturer. Hes clear and does assign a lot of reading so watch out but overall they are interesting. hes funny too

REALLY HARD, not because the topics covered but because he assigns TOO MUCH work. A lot of readings and papers to write... He is a nice guy but I think he believes that we only have one subject: his. Not enough time to do everything.

Fuste is a young dude and presents lecture materials in a very down-to-earth tone. He assigns a LOT of reading but the subject matter is pretty interesting.  Just going and listening to lecture is a trip  because you learn how racism is existent but kept under wraps. Sign-in sheet for attendance, a few reading responses and 2 take-home tests

GREAT PROFESSOR! He's very down to earth and makes classes fun and interesting. I had for summer session 2, each class was 3 hours and yet somehow he managed to hold my attention basically the whole time. Concepts are tricky but he is very clear in explaining and offering help. Definitely take him for whatever other class available!
He does not have notes, which means you need to go to the lecture. Hw is weekly and pretty hard. The midterm was alright, but the final was really tough. Discussions are not mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Homework was extremely difficult and not really representative of what was on exams. Midterms were fair, but final was bad. Took a while to respond on Piazza sometimes. Rubric for exams was unclear and unforgiving for small errors, but probably TA issue. Prof adjusted grading scale by about 2%. Overall, he was a caring guy but not the best prof.
He's bad at teaching. His classes are extremely disorganized and he jumps from one topic to another.

Chill guy. His biggest flaw is that he's very slow in lecture and only shows us basic concepts. He expects you to teach the complicated stuff yourself. He definitely knows what he's talking about and he's a good teacher. Not a very good orator however. Pretty funny at times. Take if you like independent study. Content itself is very challenging.

Grades by only 2 midterms and a final and doesn't let retake tests. He doesn't explain or teach the class, he only goes through practice problems in class. You will not learn anything from him, and he expects you to self study the stuff instead. Just pick a different prof, not worth the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: lectures are not worth going to. he goes over practice problems and does not teach material on the class. Homework has material that is harder than the midterms. organic chemistry tutor and other videos could explain the material better.
Be prepared to study!

Class graded by 2 midterms, discussion attendance, homework, and the final which can replace your lowest midterm score. Going to class did not help at all since his tests did not reflect lectures, the best way to study is using the textbook and talking with TA's. He curved a whole letter grade at the end since there was a 60 and 50% avg on midterms

Very solid professor in teaching complex analysis. Love how he look like a painter with his apron, gloves and toe shoes. Exams def got harder as qtr went on tho. however did seem grumpy at times. Very funny however. overall a solid professor in the way he gives practice exams and makes it somewhat like actual exams.

Eggers was a great professor, I didn't take calculus before this but if you read the textbook before class, the lecture should just clear things up and it's not too hard. Practice problems are honestly the way to go.

Homework makes a good chunk of the grade, but after taking his midterms, it doesn't even matter. Lectures aren't mando and arent really helpful; he does podcast. Discussions are also mando. If you take this class make sure to cover literally everything and spend alot of time on the problems so you dont fall behind.
Hard to follow along lectures, no lecture slides

He is very passionate about what he teaches, though I think he is sometimes unaware of the exact question people are asking, especially if it is a more basic one. His lectures can be pretty funny at times, and he does not call out on people, even if no one is answering, which I respect him for. He does rely on you reading the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: You will be able to pass this class ONLY if you self study every concept because the lectures aren't enough to help you. I found discussions with the TAs more helpful and the homeworks. The midterms were honestly hard, and it was frustrating because his lectures weren't helpful!! He isn't the best so make sure you put in the effort and study.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Eggers is a nice guy, but his lectures only cover basic-level knowledge of the content. Spam textbook and practice problems until you can do them effortlessly, and don't be afraid to talk to other students. There's a discord server for the 10A series, you might a the link through Piazza. Exam grading was forgiving, but prepare a lot.
He is nice! But his lectures confuse more than they help. I would recomend to take math 10A with other teacher.

If you don't have an incredibly strong basis in mathematics DO NOT take his classes. He goes into all lectures pretty much assuming you already have an understanding of the topic. I have previous experience in calc and struggled terribly in his class (I could not imagine going in with no prior knowledge). Teaches in proofs exclusively.

Eggers is a really nice professor and he really cares a lot. However, his lectures can be a bit slow and so he doesn't cover much in class. I had to study a lot outside of class, and you kind of have to be decent/good at math to do well in the class. Go to OH if you're struggling because they're really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I survived this class because of my TAs and going to the peer led learning sections. The lectures are good, but only for understanding basic applications of the concepts.

honestly just took him for 10a my first quarter and he was not that bad. main issue is that he spends most lecture time going over proofs. but if u study outside of class, actually do the hw, and ask for help when needed u should pass. everyone talking bad about him just didn't put the work in. he DOES curve at the end!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great prof, midterms were a bit difficult, but I found the final to be easy. Just do the HW and you'll be fine

I liked him. Not super exciting, but not a bad prof. Make sure you read the textbook -- he doesn't go over everything in class. Much better than other prof. Has established office hours, lets you work out the problem together. Explains things to the degree that you would need on exam (but not to the degree to fully understand, if that bothers you)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He did curve at the end, which was really kind of him. He is overall very nice and funny, but if you are not the best at math then get ready to do A LOT of studying because everything goes in the exams- even things he doesn't teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Eggers is a nice person but he is a mediocre teacher. He is knowledgeable except his lectures can be very slow (and only cover the basics), so you have to self-study to do well on exams. I did good in his class only becuase I took calculus in high school, but if it is your first time expect this class to be difficult (but it's still manageable).

Eggers made a lot of mistakes during lectures. His lectures were unhelpful in showing us what we needed to know for exams. Don't go to his office hours, he is unhelpful and honestly rude if you don't understand a problem. The exams were way harder than any practice problems we were given. There was a huge curve for our final grades though.

It's a Christmas miracle I passed this class. Went from around 63 cumulative to a C grade in the class. Curve saved me 🙏. Outside studying is a must in this class if you aren't good at math like me. Tests are way different than practice tests so don't just study those. Lectures aren't that useful but Eggers is a nice guy.
Nice professor, but just no!!!

Really difficult class especially for Calculus I. His lectures were not helpful at all, he goes through proofs and maybe 3-4 problems from the textbook. SI sessions and TA office hours helped, but that's it. You can be fully confident in the content, but get the most random conceptual questions on the exam.

While Professor Eggers is a cool in terms of his personality. His method of teaching is less than desired. For a majority of lectures, he goes off into completing mathematical proofs instead of actually teaching the material. Also, for a introductory class to calculus I, the tests were unreasonably harder compared to the practice midterms.

Unless you are a math major or you can read and comprehend math books, I highly discourage taking Eggers classes. His office hours are zero help, good luck getting a straight answer from him. Be prepared to do basically all self learning. There are just too many good math professors at UCSD to waste you time taking one of his classes.

the reviews ARE as bad as they seem. cant say dont take because theres only like 2 profs for 10a. unless youre a genius, this class is basically impossible because the f25 exams were 5x harder than the discussions/hw/past exams. only good thing was lectures were not mandatory, and they were NOT helpful. insane work
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: good luck!

Lectures are not helpful. Formulas and concepts will be written but will not be explained or given context. Homework has random problems/concepts that reflect nothing relevant in the course material, and same applies for discussion worksheets and practice exams. You will be given concepts to study but then tested on literal entire different ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are not so great. Amazing person and character. Cares about students. Tests for FA25 completely different than past exams. Learn concepts and practice (emphasis on concepts). If Eggers & He for Math10A, enroll Eggers for lectures and for grade cutoff & go to Professor He for review days. Professor He gives out concepts on exam, Eggers no.

If you've taken calculus before, the class is doable and not terrible as the reviews say. if not then good luck! he would often make mistakes during lectures and overall wasn't a accurate representation of what was going to be on the test, TAs and SI sessions did their best reviewing the basic skills needed. don't completely rely on past exams tho

His lectures don't cover the course material well so be prepared to do a lot of self studying. He goes over proofs (which we don't need to know for exams) and doesn't really explain a lot of concepts. Exam questions are very different from homework and textbook problems so they're difficult to study for.

worst math prof ever. seriously so incompetent, didn't know how to solve homework problems in class. lectures were a waste of time; would just write what was in the free textbook on the board. exams sucked major balls and where not fair, he would never give straight forward info. do not take.

If you're like me and you've sucked at math your whole life, Do NOT take this class. His midterms do not properly reflect lectures/homework. For the second midterm, we spent 2-3 weeks learning everything derivatives. There were barely any derivatives on the test. And guess what the stats were? 6/400 students got an A and the average was a D. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ineffective, makes errors frequently, and spends lecture time copying theorems from the textbook without explaining the actual steps to solve a given problem. Midterm content does not strongly align with the level of difficulty in course exercises. Horrible experience. Save yourself the trouble and seek another professor ASAP.

On my way to his 8am class, I wished dearly that anyone on an electric scooter would just ram into me and allow me to skip class. Formulas are glossed over with little to no explanation, self-study is a must for this class as explanations are not clear and provided materials are 10x easier than actual tests. As the final arrives I fear for my grade

I never hated a class so much in my entire life. If everyone is failing with the average grade of midterm being a D and every piazza post looks like a cry for help then it is clear it is not just the students' fault. I felt confident going into the second midterm and left like I just experienced war. If you want depression and anxiety take him

I wish I could go back in time to not take this class. Considering that this is a beginner calculus class, it is ridiculously difficult. I studied an embarrassing amount of hours to fail the midterm. Genuinely would rather have delayed taking this class than take it with this professor. I age 100 years every time I even think of this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He makes a lot of mistakes in lectures and mainly gave formulas and didn't teach how/when to use them. Exams were not like what we did in lectures or discussion. Gave no kind of hint as to what's on exams and practice midterms were useless. It was a guess as to what was on exams. If you're not good at math, avoid him.

Does not explain thoroughly or really at all. He assumes you already know things and tends to gloss over the finer details of concepts. Spends way too much time on proofs instead of practice. Midterms were unlike the practice ones we were given. The only reason I'm passing (for now) is self study; you will 100% have to review on your own.
The worst teacher I've ever had, does not teach what is on the exams or post the correct materials anywhere on canvas.

He didn't teach you anything that was tested on exams. The midterms were harder than the practice ones we got, which were just last year's midterms. The average on the second miterm was a F. He also doesn't do any review section or curves. I've heard that the final grade gets curved, but I'm not sure if that's gonna happen or not.

Eggers is a nice dude, don't get me wrong, but being a nice person doesn't really matter when you don't teach that well. I have no clue what happened, but I studied from the textbook for days and the exam wasn't anything like what we practiced (a good chunk of the class agreed to this on piazza). Choose a prof wisely ESPECIALLY FOR MATH.

Professor Eggers is a nice person, but his lectures are confusing and frustrating. He focuses on proving formulas instead of teaching how to solve problems, making even easy topics complicated. Exams are 25% midterm and 50% final. You have to self-study, read the textbook, and do tons of practice to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Eggers is a nice person, but his lectures are confusing and frustrating. He spends all the time proving formulas instead of teaching how to solve problems, making even easy topics complicated. Exams are 25% midterm and 50% final, so self-studying is a must.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grumpy    >:(

He is OK, he is not the best, he tends go fast but so does every math professor in this uni, I wouldnt say he was the best, because often times during class he was kind of anti questions, if someone asked a question because they missed something due he would just ignore or just say read the textbook. And the text book which he wrote sucks.

Horrible lectures that were very disorganized and incomplete. He would put practice problem up and only solve half of the problem and assume we know how to do the rest. If you took ap calc ab and bc in high school you'll be fine. His midterms and finals are just like the practice midterms and he does curve pretty heavy.

In my experience, taking Eggers for my first quarter at UCSD for Math10A was average. He writes on the chalkboard and talks at a pretty slow pace, but for me that was more difficult to work with. One thing I'll say is that personally, the only reason I was able to get through this class was because of self study. Without that, you might struggle.

Professor Eggers is a great professor. Lectures weren't mandatory, and honestly seemed very off topic to what we were tested on. The discussion worksheets are on par with what you need to know in the class. Eggers knows his stuff, he's such an awesome dude. Just make sure to study and try, there will be a lot of solo learning. The curve is insane:)

Eggers' style does not appeal to a lot of people here, however, you cannot expect professor will feed you with everything in class. Final hard? Indeed, yet it is not unsolvable. I did not know to approach about 1/3 of problems at beginning, yet, finish all at end and got 99 in Final. I did not rely on sheets, so that is also my suggestion.
Lectures are a lot of yapping but also optional, fun to just listen, as for the exams just practice them with the practice ones posted and you will get a good grade, HW is light.

Lectures not mandatory and not helpful, many tangents. If confused, ask TA or youtube. Straightforward exams, similar practice ones released. 1 cheatsheet per exam. Grade based off hw, discussions, 2 midterms, and final. If you read the book and do practice problems, you'll succeed. I skipped most lectures and ended with an A, but I studied well.

The exams are way too hard for what is taught and told to prepare. Preparation for exams with practice exams and textbook problems is not enough to guarantee you a good grade. I used to have an A with a good grade on my midterm, but the exams got extremely hard out of nowhere, and I got a C for a final grade.

Everything is alright until the exams. They are so much harder compared to the practice exams and it's even worse for the final. I have studied with a lot of practice problems and understood all the concepts with other class students.

He's a very friendly personality, and I do think he genuinely wants what's best for his students. My main issue with the course was the exams. The bulk of my missing points was my own doing from section attendance but the final exam average grade was less than a 50%, with no chance of a curve. Very nice guy, just study way harder than you'd think.

Lectures aren't mandatory and you are required to go to 6/10 of your discussion classes. Overall, very kind professor but classes are formatted a little weird. He basically just reviews textbook problems every lecture, so it wasn't much help for me. It felt like I should know the material (that I'm suppose to learn) before going to the lectures.

He's a nice professor but the lectures did not help me at all, I would leave class more confused even though I had seen the same topics before. He doesn't explain or go into depth about formulas, he just explains them.

He is a nice guy, but lectures are essentially useless. His lectures are generally just proving formulas instead of using the formulas, and he rarely goes over practice problems. I ended up going to a different 10A prof (Dr. Jor el) about halfway through and he was much better.

Prof Eggers only goes over textbook examples which makes it hard to understand the homework sometimes. You really have to self study this class A LOT. I encourage doing practice problems from the book and going on youtube.

Honestly, there isn't much to critique about him as a person as opposed to him as a teacher. I found myself more confused during the lectures rather than clearer, and basically had to teach myself the entire course. But to be fair, this might just be because of my learning style not matching with his teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The professor had his days of good and bad but I had to learn most of it on my own

This professor only gives examples out of the book. He generalizes when people who have taken calculus before answer his questions and proceeds to think everyone understands what is happening. The way he answers questions is very sarcastic and makes students feel scared to ask questions. The class structure is good.
I love when he blames the chalk for his mistakes. He's like “the chalk doesn't want to behave today” he's hilarious. Homework heavy, exams are insanely easy.
Does not teach, gives examples and expects class to already know and does not really explain if class does not know.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Eggers' class can be challenging, but engaging with the material and using resources like unstuckstudy AI makes it manageable. Exams are straightforward if you stay on top of the homework.

For the most part, the class was easy and the midterm exams were piece of cake. That was, until I took the final exam. He made his final exam unreasonably hard for no reason and added curveballs that we did not get to practice in the midterms or the practice final he gave us. The final exam dropped me 3 letter grades.

I like this professor he is the chilling guy, but I want to make some comments with the grading 
I do not know what happened this quarter the homework was graded WAY MORE HARSHLY than previous quarter, just format problem deduct 0.25 my score and no rubric 

Well except those two things, I think I will still take professor eggers again in future

Prof Eggers is one of the BEST for MATH 20E! His HW are challenging and requires deep thinking about materials, but you can always go to OH and TA are willing to help. Discussions are required but they are helpful so I would go anyway. Exam are straight and VERY EASY if you do HW carefully and try practice exam he gave.
This guy is literally the GOAT. John Eggers is my sunshine. Crystal clear lectures and straightforward exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nice guy! Awful professor. He is very very very unorganized with his lectures. His style of teaching is also very outdated. Overall, if you have no choice take him because he is a nice human being and helps you when you ask questions, but look elsewhere if you have options because he is not a good TEACHER!
One of the best Professor's I've taken, made the class enjoyable to attend.

He made the subject enjoyable during lectures, which got people to show up even though it wasn't mandatory. Even though he tends to focus on theory a lot, the examples he gives in lectures were pretty clear. The exams were really similar to the practice tests which was soo nice. Overall would recommend

His lectures are sort of disorganized and very theory/definition-heavy. He doesn't give enough examples, which makes the graded-for-accuracy hw difficult. Also, I rly don't like that the hw solutions are never posted. However, his exams aren't very hard and he makes it very clear what will be covered.

The professor is very nice and has a good sense of humor. His homework is very hard, but graded easily (the harder ones are graded on completion and the easier ones graded on accuracy). Exams are very easy compared to homework. If you understand the examples done in class, exams should be very easy.

His lectures, homework, quizzes, and exams are like four different courses.
The lectures are disorganized, so if you do not preview and read the textbook by yourself, you'll feel it hard when doing homework. The homework is very hard compared with his teaching though exams are easy though.
If you are not good at teaching yourself, don't choose him

His lectures are unclear. I have no idea if he is giving a proof for a formula or giving an example of using the formula. His lecture, homework and textbooks seems like separate three courses which has nothing to do with each other. His homework is extremely suffering since you cannot find examples from the textbook.
Easy!

This guy is an amazing professor and and amazing human. He is excellent. Would HIGHLY recommend. Makes lectures super entertaining. Teaches extremely difficult material in an easy to understand way. Cares about the students a great deal. Goes out of his way to make sure students are comfortable in class and asking questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Is ok at lecturing and gives fair midterms and tests but assigns very difficult homework that is mandatory. You will be teaching yourself 90% of the material required to complete the homework and you will be teaching yourself out of a difficult textbook. Nice guy but good luck.
He doesn't know how to teach. Prepare yourself if you are going to take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I have had Eggers for Math 10B and 10C, and I can fairly say that he is such a sweet, caring teacher. The quizzes are a bit weird, but the midterms and final are extremely fair and like the practice tests. He is so kind and approachable, and tells funny jokes in lecture. I would 100% take him again. Slight mistakes in lecture sometimes, but great

Eggers really cares about students' learning and his exams are really fair. This quizzes are very hard and all conceptual, but the lowest one gets dropped so usually it doesn't affect the overall grade too much. He was definitely much better when I took him for 10B than 10C, but I still love his style of teaching.
Would 100% recommend this professor, wears toe shoes and this guy is such a character. Didn't go to lecture that much, and didn't need to.

Overall Eggers knows exactly what he is doing and is a master of math. It is essential to show up to lectures and ask questions when you have them. The homework is not overwhelming at all, quizzes are straightforward, and the tests were weird. Every test would have a single question that we were not taught. Pay attention and work hard. Fairly easy.

My guy is a beast of a teacher. We have dubbed him 'jeggernaut' as a representation of his robust and effective teaching methods. He cares about every question asked and treats all questions - even the dumb ones - very seriously.

Homework is mainly about writing proofs and is really hard sometimes. But exams are generally not difficult. Just understand every example in the lecture notes and make sure to figure out the practice exam problems, and you can succeed in his course.

Sometimes there were errors in the lectures and students would have to point them out. The class was alright. I went to every single lecture and therefore ended up doing well in the class. First midterm was torture, second was great, and the final was pretty easy. The quizzes are weird. Eggers can be an alright professor, but sometimes has off days

Honestly, contrary to all the other ratings of 1.0/5, I took Mr. Eggers for this quarter and did pretty well. I think it genuinely just comes down to whether you are willing to put in the work to re-read the textbook and do a lot of practice questions. At the end of the day, this is college. The teacher isn't going to spoon-feed you everything.

This professor could not care less about his students. Lectures did little to help with test content. Be careful with all the good reviews, it isn't by mistake that hundreds of students petitioned to have an online final when the pandemic was at an all-time high. If you choose to take this professor I wish you good luck cause you're gonna need it.

I did really well in math 10A and then failed this class. The professor is very nice but the lectures are very difficult to learn from. The tests are extremely hard and like purposely try to trick you up. I know the professor didn't write the tests but there was no curve and no partial credit. very difficult course and very difficult professor :(

I came out of Math 10A with a B+. Math 10b is hectic due to the combined classes. Material on the exams was not reflective of Eggers' examples because of combined classes. The rubric is not lenient and is available after the exam. Lectures don't teach me anything. You're on your own. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was fine in my experience and did seem to care about your learning. Not very accommodating compared to other professors, but didn't do anything that was unfair. If an in-person final is planned since day 1 on the syllabus, it's completely fair game to not have an online option for the final (it's not that nice but it's not unfair or anything)

Great professor and lecturer. Attend lectures and ask questions; he's always open to questions during lectures. Study, and you'll do well. Exams can be challenging if you don't understand the concepts, but the grading is pretty lenient. I recommend this professor if you're willing to put in the work to attend every lecture; it's no easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer and has a firm command of the material. Exams were harsh, but they generally followed the homework.
VERY unaccommodating for genuine student needs. Practice material is not like the exams. Quizzes are designed to fail students with trick questions.
Homework has nothing to do with the exam. Don't know how to prepare for the exam!
Don't take this prof for a friendly warning
Do not take Eggers! The homework and exams are harder than the material taught in lectures. He does not care about his students in the slightest
I despise this man. No empathy for his students. He doesn’t teach the course material well.
This guy is terrible
This professor sucks. He is not good at teaching effectively and lacks human decency.
horrible professor.
The WORST professor ever. His teaching is terrible and his sympathy for his students is even worse. Avoid him at all costs

The good reviews are professor simps. Literally hundreds of students have petitioned for an online final and have stated they will do any proctoring necessary. It isn't a bunch of crybabies it is human compassion during a pandemic. Just because you did okay does not mean the literal hundreds of students aren't.

Everyone in this course seemed hellbent on getting an online final when they could have just filed for an incomplete and done the final later, which is why you will see many reviews attacking Eggers. Take Eggers and see for yourself. Good class and you'll get a good grade as long as you STUDY.

A lot of crybabies this quarter.

About the course: Homework and exams are much more difficult than that of the material taught in lecture and practice exams do not match the level of difficulty of the true exams. I often found myself unprepared and constantly feeling stressed out. 


About teacher: He lacks compassion and basic human decency. Doesn’t care about students at all.

Horrible professor. Will not allow for an alternative option for students despite being in a pandemic. His ego is more important to him than the health and well-being of his students. Wont allow calculators during the final? Homework is extremely hard. Screw this class overall. Do not take this professor!!!

Eggers would rather have all his students get covid then create an online option for the final exam. He changed his grading system in the middle of the year after the STUDENTS pointed it out to him. I have more empathy in my pinky toe, than Eggers has altogether.
Most arrogant man ever. Does not teach the material effectively and does not have any decency for his students.
Eggers is so rude and prideful. Does not care about his students AT ALL.
His teaching is ehh. His empathy towards students is horrible. Do not take eggers!

Some did great in his class, but that is because they never really watched the lectures and had already taken calculus before. If this is your first time taking Calculus, prepare yourself. You will be forced to learn the material on your own, the help you may receive from his lectures and practice exams will not get you through the actual exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
This quarter was very difficult due to COVID, changing grading criteria, online tests until the heavily weighted final, all the while, the math department was very unyielding... hence all of the cruel comments on Eggers. 

He does care for his students and teaches the practicality of what you are learning. Paired with reading, he teaches well!

It feels like he takes joy in tormenting his students. Ineffective lecturer in class and unwilling to help outside of class. He is rude to students asking questions on piazza, I cannot even imagine what his office hours must be like. Additionally, his TAs are just as bad as he is
rudest, meanest professor ever. So egotistical and he actually wants his students to fail. terrible lecturer, everyone has had to teach themselves the content. do not take under any circumstance
Cruel professor with a terribly overinflated ego. Cannot teach effectively and will not listen to students concerns regarding the class.

if u want to fail, take him. Would rather have all his students get covid then have an online option for final exam. Messed up on his grading system, changed mid year after students literally revolted against him. Unacceptable and unaccommodating to his students. Made out of state and international
students fly across the country to take 1 exam
Extremely unaccommodating professor, avoid at all costs. Does not care about his students' wellbeing. Would rather have students get COVID than challenge his ego.

Despite a high rating, he is the worst professor I have encountered. Not only do his lectures leave you unprepared for the homework, quizzes, and exams, he has a terrible attitude towards his students. In spite of major circumstances relating to the pandemic that hinder students' education, he refuses to let go of his ego and accommodate.

Quite possibly the meanest, most unaccommodating professor at UCSD. His comments when students have questions on the piazza are rude and inconsiderate. He barely even talks about math in his lectures and we are more behind than the other 10B classes, yet our tests are at the same time. He genuinely wants his students to fail. Do not take him!

I can't understand why he gets many good reviews. He is the worst professor in the Math department I met. Trust me, his lectures are totally useless and he just assumes we should know many things. The homework is tough and the TA can't explain materials well.

He encouraged students to learn on their own and you barely learn anything in lectures. The textbook is useless but it was required to purchase for the homework. Homework is way harder than anything you will ever do on the quizzes or tests. Had a lot of drops however so most kids were done by week 6 or 7.

I didnt particularly find his lectures helpful and stopped attending at some point. His explanations for topics are not clear enough for me to understand so it was just easier to try and learn the material on my own time through videos. They only took 1 out of 2 main exams for the grade though which was great.

Eggers was a great professor. He shows that he really cares about his job and will take the time to re-explain topics when a student asks. He is also really passionate about the subject and it rubs off on the whole class. You'll need to do some extra work independently, but that's just bc calc 2 is difficult, not his fault. Overall, love Eggers :)
Pretty decent lectures, and his grading policies were extremely, extremely lenient. In 20B, he dropped 1 out of 2 exams, dropped 2 of 6 quizzes, so pretty chill in grading.

His class is easy, and his policy is nice (only 5/7 hw, 4/6 quizzes, and 2/3 tests count toward your final grade). I'm basically chilling two weeks before the final week. However, his grader is awful and careless. There were students making piazza posts publically complaining about the grader but he himself never responded.

Eggers is a solid choice for this class because he doesnt make it extremely difficult. When I did the first homework assignment, I fully expected to fail this class by the end of the quarter. I made it out with a B+. His grading scale is pretty fair and midterms are pretty similar to practice exams. Homework is hard so go to discussion for help.

Prof. Eggers is a pretty nice guy. He gives 20% cushion for quizzes and allows you to drop one of the lowest. Lectures are a bit slow and confusing but if you do the hw you'll be fine. Exams and quizzes reflect course materials - pretty basic.

Lectures were pretty confusing and all over the place although he did go over lots of examples. Homework was hard to do based on just the lectures, definitely need the textbook to do well on the quizzes and exams. Also, not the most helpful professor, but he seems very nice and he does really care about the subject and learning.

reviews.comment: Great guy, super nice and knowledgeable of math. Lenient quiz drop policy. Would take again

This class is all about self-teaching. Your best bet to be successful in this class is the TEXTBOOK and PAUL's NOTES ONLINE!!! Professor Egger's lectures are not thorough enough to fully understand the content but he'll drop a few hints here and there what will be on the quizzes and exams. Quizzes and Exams are based on textbook homework questions

reviews.comment: Professor Eggers does not grade any of the work. However, become friends with the TAs they are really friendly and willing to help you with any of your questions about the course. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof Eggers is an amazing professor, but still, you must either read the book or learn online as he doesn't go too deep into how to solve the hw problems. Precalc was the highest math I took in high school, so I had a rough start, but I managed to get an A+ by attending lectures, doing both the required AND optional hw, and learning on Youtube.
He is a very kind professor. Even I know a lot of the material, I still attend the lectures.

Eggers is an extremely ineffective lecturer because what he teaches is only a fraction of what is asked on homework and tests. He goes extremely slowly and wastes so much time in class. reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His lectures are straightforward and he explains things well. Quizzes and exams reflect the material well.

Professor Eggers is amazing! He explains concepts very well in his lectures, and he's more than willing to help you out during office hours/respond on Piazza for extra help. I enjoyed his testing format of 6 quizzes and 3 exams, dropping your 2 worst quizzes and worst exam from your grade. If you improve in the class, your grade will reflect that!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: It is very clear how Prof Eggers is trying his best to deliver the lessons in an online format. He is also very active in Piazza if you have any questions or clarifications. reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Out of all my teachers I feel like Jeggers adapted to the online format the best. He does his lectures from an ipad and works through problems in real time. He likes students to point out mistakes when he makes them and is respectful about being corrected. My only gripe is he talks a bit slowly, I listened to all the recordings at 2x speed.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests were off-book at times. Lectures are a little slow, but Professor Eggers is available outside of class. If you are worried about a topic, there are plenty of opportunities to learn more during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Eggers is a good lecturer but since I haven't taken a lot of calculus the class was pretty difficult for me. reviews.comment: He looks pretty happy all the time and he talks really slowly in his lectures. Lectures are podcasted. Eggers really knows his material, but he does not take into consideration of those that take notes. He also responds to students questions on piazza, but it takes him at least a day to respond.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: lives in piazza answering questions, great and funny lectures, easy but helpful exams, and not so many homework. definitely will come back to his class if I have chance

He is my first professor for math at ucsd. He is passionate about what he teaches, although his lectures are pretty theoretical. He is good with responding on Piazza along with the TAs. Exams were very similar to his practice tests and are fair. I would definitely take him again for a future course!!
Great personality and lecture. Exams are easy if you do all the assignments.

He is wonderful and the homework helps a lot!!! The tests are not hard and very similar to the practice exams. If you study hard on the homework and the lectures, you own an "A"!!! Love him and definitly take him again if I have another chance. Look his podcast right now!

Ok guys, at first I hated going to this class because I didn't think he taught well, but after the first midterm the content either got much easier or he got more used to using Notability. Honestly, not a fan of John Eggers. He definitely thinks he's funnier than he is. reviews.comment: WebAssign, textbook, written hw each week, but its manageable. Tests are straightforward&easier than the hw. Good at answering questions (irl & Piazza). Lectures aren't mandatory but they're funeractive, & he's good at checking in with the audience to make sure they're following along. Gives definitions, pictures&examples. Highly recommend him.

reviews.comment: Homework has nothing to do with the exams.

Eggers is an amazing professor. Took him for 20A and 20B and can confirm he is amazing at explaining and an awesome professor overall. Would definitely recommend taking him for lower division math classes. He is a tough grader, but totally recommend his class. Gave a nice curve.

To be honest, weekly assignments were very helpful to me to deepen understanding in the chapter materials along with professor's lecture, and were not really a lot to me. reviews.comment: An absolute savior. Amazing lecturer and explains things in pretty good detail. For basic math like 20A and B definitely take him.

I had a really hard time with Professor Eggers. I feel like the first midterm brought a lot of people down and then the second one was okay and then the final was really hard. I feel like he teaches a lot of conceptual work and expects you to know the harder stuff. Try to do the textbook homework!

Eggers is a great professor since he was clear in his explanations and didn't rush through the material. He does give examples but doesn't go over everything in the book. Homework is the usual. When I attended the first few lectures, I was doing alright, nothing too difficult, mostly review. But when the midterms came around, we didn't do so well. The averages of both midterms were failing. one of the best professor ive ever had! Explain clearly and exams are fair. Definitely will take him again

If you want to teach yourself the whole class and be surprised by the questions he gives on the midterm that you've never seen before, take Eggers. Much harder than the other professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Hes alright

I do not like his teaching style. When solving question, he jumped some steps, which makes no sense. I have to study on my own. I guess he assume you know how it is done, but actually many of us don't.
He's pretty good.

John Eggers seems like a great guy outside of class, but as  a professor I found his lectures difficult to comprehend. I had to learn  everything outside of class to fully understand and I even attended a different professor's lectures.  If you're taking 20 C with Eggers, go to a different professor's lectures.

Don't get me wrong, Professor Eggers is an amazing person. He's funny and cares about his students. However, Math 20c is very hard and him taking entire lectures to explain theorems and main ideas feels like time wasted. You do a lot on your own. If you're like me, you prefer straightforward examples and little background info.

If you're like me, then you'll hate his teaching style. I learn well with lots of examples and brief references to the concepts. Eggers can take 15 minutes to explain concepts, which is WAY too long for me. He's conceptual and slow to the point that you don't get much application from it. One time we only did half a problem... in a 50 minute class.

maybe its because they just started a different curriculum but every  lecture is more confusing than the last. this class relies solely on finding outside help because lectures are unclear and he expects us to know it all before class starts. He even told us lectures arent for learning the material, we learn it by reading.

I had heard great things about Eggers but for some reason his Math 20C class was terrible for Spring 16. It was a coordinated course so he had to follow a strict schedule... maybe that's why it was terrible? I'm not sure. Nevertheless he was really unclear and unhelpful in lecture. I ended up going to Chris Deotte's lectures instead.
Eggers is a great lecturer.  Although I thought his class was challenging, he really does make the subject of calculus a little more bearable. He is very kind and always positive.
I didn't understand anything he was talking about and eventually resorted to self studying out of the book. His concepts are extremely confusing. He is not funny at all.
Professor Eggers has really nice lectures and is really helpful at office hours. Go to class and do the homework and you should be fine!

My expectations were set high when i signed up for Eggers, but not all of my expectations were met. Eggers is a great lecturer and hilarious during class, but he doesn't explain some concepts very clearly, so the textbook was a big resource to fill in the gaps. Exams are fair, not too hard but not easy. But if Eggers is an option, take him!

Legitimately one of the best math professors I have ever had over 2 states and 4 colleges. Clear explanations and expectations. Tests are challenging but fair. If you go to class, pay attention and put the effort into understanding the homework you'll be fine unless you're brain dead.
Great teacher who loves to teach.

He says he makes concepts more complicated than it really is so we would somehow understand it better but I'm completely lost. He takes an extremely roundabout way of explaining concepts that by the time he gets back to the point of the explanation, I'd forgotten everything.  His methods don't work for me. I'll probably fail this class.

I've had professor Eggers for both Math 20F & 20E. He teaches in a very clear manner with zero confusion. He does not simply teach students how to "get the answer,"rather, he takes time to drill into students' heads of how the math actually works. I attended the lectures, discussions, and several office hours and got A+s for both courses.

Professor eggers. Oh boy, where to start. So he's clear on what he teaches, not difficult to understand. His class is based 10% on hw and rest are 2 midterms 1 final. So far, those midterms were by far the hardest thing I've ever done, class average no higher than 60%. Nothing on midterm was like anything you practice. Let's see how the final goes
Tests are very short, with few questions, but are very specific. Allows cheat sheets on tests.

Eggers explains the concepts very, very well. His tests are really, really easy- as long as you go to class you should get at least a 85% on them.  He makes tons of practice midterms/finals available, and the actual exams will be very similar. Take advantage of this.
I LOVE THE PROFESSOR WITH WEIRD GREEN PANTS!

He helped me developed the abstract foundation to go to upper div math. He is inspirational, clear, and definitely approachable. Exams are ok. It's college, you have to work hard to get good grades. So I don't think people who said he's tough were actually working hard. Strongly recommend read the text before class and making flash cards from day 1

Ok lecturer but he failed so many people in my class by not curving any of the exams (which had VERY VERY low averages, around 40%). Do not recommend. Exams were hard and not a lot of partial credit was given.

Eggers is a very caring and humorous professor. Once in a while, it might not make sense when he does problems in class, but he is great at clearing up questions if you approach him after lecture. Homework is important for learning, but only 3 out of 5 assignments count. The midterms and final are fair and represent materials seen in class.

Eggers IS an excellent, clear, and helpful professor. I found both lecture & section helpful to my learning. However, he is a strict grader.
