Note taking was at least 2-3 pages front and back each day.  Very interesting and passionate.  She didn't grade anything though so your grade entirely depends on the TA.  Covers a lot of material and the quizes are easy if you do the reading.  You HAVE to do all the reading to pass the class.

I thought her class was extremely painful.  The pop essays, journals, etc. were unnecessary and didn't help me process or learn about the texts we were reading.  I felt like i was in high school again with all the busy work.  Lectures were not stimulating at all.

Prof. Forbes, is very down to earth. Going to class isn't a pain; however, there is a lot of material to cover. She is always willing to help, and it is obvious that she enjoys what she is teaching. I really enjoyed her class.
Eh, she can be very funny and cool, but needs to loosen up with regard to things like attendence.  Someone should remind her this isn't middle school.  She's also late a lot.

Professor was good but if you don't ask questions It can get hard. Homework was a lot about 20-30 problems a week that should be done in less than 2-3 hours. She cares about the class and wouldn't put you down if you asked questions. Exams were everything she taught and was on the homework. I recommend using outside resources(no practice tests).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Her midterms and finals are actually relatively easy and not tricky compared to other Winter 2026 Math20C professors. Her explanations in class is just ok and not the easiest to understand. However, she is very caring towards her students and is willing to answer questions asked by the students.

Although she is a new professor, she was very accommodating and responsive to student concerns, which you don't see in many professors. While she made a few minor mistakes, they did not detract from her lectures. After hearing concerns about the first midterm, she made the second exam much easier and the final manageable to help students recover.

She didn't know what she was lecturing half the time. She would act like her mistakes were secretly to test students paying attention. The exams were heavily based off her practice problems PDF. The exams would be very strictly graded, you could get the right answer but will get points off for silly things.

Makes frequent mistakes in lectures, gave extra credit to students who corrected her. Skipped some steps in examples and went over unnecessary proofs sometimes.However, midterms related to her review slides. Midterm 1 avg was 62, but midterm 2 avg was 85, final avg 85. Lower midterm gets dropped. Lacks confidence teaching but very sweet and caring!

A lot of times it feels like she doesn't know what she's doing and is just as confused as the students are and doesn't really explain concepts and how to do things well. It's like watching her do homework problems with little and unclear explanations to why she does something because she tends to skip steps a lot. No practice tests or cheat sheets.

She's an alright lecturer, she sometimes seems just as confused as the students. She goes through unnecessary things really slowly and then speeds through the more important stuff. Other than that, class is just doing practice problems, very boring but not bad for learning. First midterm was incredibly difficult, but second was easy.

She alright. It's very hard to keep up with her work and she does problems with little explanation. Homeworks do help but they also don't reflect the exam very well. But her syllabus is tuff, lowest midterm gets dropped out of the 2. She's good but don't expect to learn much from her.

Lectures were very hard to keep up with because she already had notes prepared and would not explain her work, it would be very crammed and hard to see or understand what's happening. Midterm did not directly reflect off of practice problems and homework she told us to do. The concepts were easy but she would make them harder than they were.
I even thought I was going to fail the course, but my final grade turned out to be quite good. The teacher was very gentle and didn't have any unreasonable demands.

Decent lectures, bit of an accent and trouble understanding questions. Huge curve in the class and easy exams, very sweet person. Made a good amount of mistakes in lecture and graded late, theory heavy lecture with application based exams and homework
Lectures were too theory heavy, and was more focused on proving theorems than solving problems. Attending them wasn't exactly useful because I'd have to learn on my own to get through the homework.

Decent and friendly professor. Was unsure often when asked questions. Often made mistakes in lecture, leading to many revisions in posted slides. Much easier exams than homework, but late grading. Would recommend looking into other sources rather than just her lecture

At the beginning, she used many helpful examples, but over time lectures became very theory heavy with few explanations of underlying concepts or examples. Questions were often deferred to after class and unanswered. Exams were easier than homework but very test heavy. No Homework was dropped, grading was late, and inconsistent exam grading.

Yi Fu's lectures were decent. Examples and walkthroughs helped a lot, but paraphrasings of topics were often non-simplifying. 
Though HW and lecture problems were difficult, exams had medium difficulty questions that required applicational understanding but avoided extreme momentary intuition.
The entire grade for the class is curved.

Lectures were pretty boring and attendance was extra credit but he was passionate about teaching. Lectures weren't recorded and the homework and tests were all online and super easy. There are quizzes in labs.

If you already know a coding language, this class is INCREDIBLY easy. Lectures are perfect for ppl who know nothing about coding, but a bit boring for others. But overall, a great explainer. Quizzes are easy 1 question, really just to see if you paid attention in lab. Final is take home for 1 week.
Compelling course with interdisciplinary multimodal, practical, projects. TA's were quite helpful, in assisting in the real-world implementation of engineering theory. Highly reccomended.

The professor gave amazing lectures and had a lot of other interesting ppl present too. The study approach was very research oriented and hence made you understand the topic pretty well 
. Homeworks were basically similar to what was done in class . Exams were very chill too
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His class is light work and doable. Weekly hw, 1 midterm, and 1 final. There are quizzes' polls on Zoom every lecture and lab and u have to participate to get the attendance credits. Overall, the TA and prof Kuester are nice and approachable. I recommend him to everyone

I am not sure why these reviews are so negative; Dr. Kuester did an excellent job of teaching a tough subject in a very short amount of time. Lectures were always very clear and helpful, and both homework and exams were challenging, but fair. Plus, if you can get through the material, you get to see some neat things in the world of engineering!

One of my favorite professors and classes at UCSD. A great opportunity to explore your engineering skills and put them to work. This is not a theory class but rather a hands on experience. Expect to go beyond your skill set, and learn a lot about other engineering fields and colleges. A team building class that prepares you for the real world.

Best professor in UCSD, really makes you think outside of the box and use your brain. You will learn the basics of code on a step by step approach. He does has an accent but he also has a lot of wisdom to share if you are willing to open your ears and mind. This class was fundamental to my success as a SE undergrad and grad student.

Professor Kuester neither records nor podcasts his lectures. He occasionally shows his screen on zoom, but he never unmutes and the zoom just has no audio, leaving the students entirely on their own. His final is on a COMPLETELY different scale from hw, both of which he fails to provide the bare minimum amt of info needed to complete them.

I don't know why so many these reviews are negative. He isn't my favorite professor, but he really isn't bad at all. His lectures basically just teach 1 new matlab technique a day, and then the hw goes over that technique in a problem. Not super difficult, and the midterm wasn't bad either. He's a pretty decent/average prof.

Probably one of the worst professor's I've ever had. It feels like he teaches random topics, and mention's important info late in the course that would have been useful in the beginning. Final was heavily based on previous SE classes even though this class DOES NOT have any prerequisites. Avoid this professor at all costs.

He definitely has his own style of free-form and collaborative teaching, but I really rather like the non-linear structure he has for covering information and encouraging in-depth research. He was helpful when asked to break things down further, had tons of field experts supplement his lectures and our presentations. Really opened my mind to SE.

The textbook is your teacher. He constantly gave homework assignments on concepts he never taught or are entirely beyond the scope of this course. Very, very disorganized. Also the TA's consistently recorded grades wrong.

Not a great professor. Takes the entire lecture to explain something that could probably be explained in 20 min. Didn't prepare us very well for his harder homeworks... especially the final. There were iclickers, but he gave everyone till the last week to register them...

Most useless professor I have ever had. No one paid attention. Bright side is that he gave a "practice midterm" the day before the exam and the midterm was an exact copy. The final was take home but it took 25+ hours. Find someone who understands matlab and cling to them, sure as hell arent learning anything from kuester.
Don't even bother reading the reviews here, he's your only option for this class. Just remember, google is your best friend when you take this course.
Lectures were somewhat useless. Homeworks did not represent material he taught in lecture. Unorganized. But even so, the material was still easy.

i cant understand a single thing he says! he mumbles like crazy and puts me to sleep. his lectures cover material that could be learned in 10 minutes but he takes 3 hours. homework is different from lectures and wayy harder. class is unorganized. we didnt have a class syllabus until week 6 and didnt know we had a midterm until the week right befor
Prepare for hell.  I am not kidding.

I can't believe they still let him teach this year. A number of us had complained to the SE dept.  The only time I went to his OH, he didn't show up for an hour. Only way you can pass is find a smart programming-savvy group member. I think people ended up dropping in Week 9. Good move, b/c there's essentially no curve. Couple in-class pop quizzes.
Possibly the worst professor you'll encounter at UCSD.  Nothing about him or his class is likeable.  good luck.

he is simply THE worst professor ever. he does not care about his students. he does not even show up to his own office hours. projects are way too hard, not to mention they are completely useless. DO NOT TAKE THIS GUY, YOU WILL GET A 'C' OR LOWER!

This guy is whacked.  His accent is beyond this planet.  He mumbles a lot and uses a lot of jargon.  Projects are stupid and have nothing to do with SE materials.  He knows graphics and OpenGL and GUI, he's obviously teaching the whole class.  Comes late everyday.  TA doesnt really help much and likes to do and answer his way... horrible class.

Lectures were completely useless.  Only a few students still attend them.  TA's a prick and gave a pop quiz during lab after attendance also fell.  Homeworks/projects are easy if you know how to use SAP/Solidworks.
chill and tests are similar to slides

Very sweet and kind professor, this was the first linguistics class ive taken and it was so interesting. Overall very easy, only a few easy homeworks (like 5-6?) assigned throughout the entire quarter. Attendance not required, lectures were recorded. Midterms and final were super easy, helpful study guides provided. def recommend!

These reviews played in my face. I saw these reviews and thought I was about to have an easy breezy quarter. I was MISTAKEN. I cried so many tears over this class I could've kept the entire state of California hydrated and eliminated the decade long drought we've been experiencing. Maybe it was just the TA but HOLY bro I've never suffered this much

This class was fun and I enjoyed it a lot, I took it as a random GE but I would take it again. It was interesting and easy to do well in if you put in just like a tiny bit of effort (not a lot is needed). Actually do the homework, they're quick and easy for points. Don't bother getting the book you don't need it. Lectures are recorded.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Funny story I didn't even know what class I signed up for so when he said we were making a language I was like ???. He's passionate and I enjoyed the lectures. One late homework is accepted and they're weighted a lot so make sure to keep up. Study guide for both midterms and final is provided and aligns almost exactly. Great prof! I learned a lot.

A very nice guy who makes linguistics very interesting and entertaining! The workload is okay but do submit assignments on time cuz late hw is automatically 60%. 2 fairly easy midterms and 1 final. There are also extra credits so I ended up with 101%

He is a very nice guy but do NOT take this class for a GE. Idk why he makes the class so demanding. There is truly no need to be assigning this many homeworks and surveys. 2 midterms, a cumulative final, and a final project is insane for a lower division GE class. Would not recommend at all

Nothing bad to say about the professor. You can tell hes a great guy but the course is so difficult and he doesnt make it easy to pass. I think if youre not a linguistics major maybe dont take the class with him lol

If you take this P/NP and just attend lectures, you'll be fine. If taken for a letter grade, an A is VERY attainable. 5 homeworks relating to the language you invent and all exams have an outline that is released well before the exam time.
Really fun and somewhat easy class. I really recommend.
pretty easy and fun class. do not slack on the homework because if you miss points it has long term effect on your grade, hence why I got a B. I overall recommend this prof and class.
No discussion is required. Study guides provided that outline what topics are being tested on for the two midterms and final. Material is easy to comprehend and lenient on the grading, I would say.

Very fun class! As long as you pay attention and take notes you are sure to succeed. Before tests make sure to go over the study guide thoroughly. The tests match up very well with the study guide and the course work.

Fall 2022. Coursework: short weekly homework, 2 midterms and 1 finals. The exams are very reflective of the lecture materials. I personally do not attend the lecture sessions are reading the lecture slides are more than enough. His lectures are actually very interesting and he knows a lot of things in regards to language in general.

No discussions. Lectures are interesting. Few short and easy homework. Two midterms and 1 final. All mc questions and short answer questions. PPT slides include all information. Have a final project. Grading is pretty loose. As long as you understand the key concept you would get full scores on project and hw. Gives out straightforward study guides
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome professor who clearly cares about linguistics (and his students)! Lectures were super interesting and engaging even though they do cover a fair bit of material. The class was also very cool as it centers around learning how invented languages are created by actually making up a language collectively as a class. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Goodall is a chill guy. His lectures are pretty interesting. He posts all of his material on TritonEd, so if you are to miss a class, you will still have access to the lecture slides (though I wouldn't recommend skipping his class). His midterms and final are multiple choice and short answer.
Do not take it unless it is mandatory. Do you think you are learning the new concept? No, please, learning by yourself.

Graded by midterms, homework, and final, and homework was only 5%. Horrible lecturer. Talks slow. Takes long breaths between words like he didn't plan what he would be talking about in lecture. What he teaches in class hardly relates to what's asked on homework. He posted a practice midterm and final which helped, allows a cheatsheet, and curves.

Garay is pretty unenthusiastic, barely scratching the surface of topics in lecture. Sometimes it seemed like he didn't care at all. The course definitely requires a solid amount of studying if you want to do well on the tests. If he gives practice test the actual test will be somewhat similar. But sometimes he wont. If that's the case, know it all.

Barely teaches during lecture. Assigns homework (10 hws, only worth 5% of grade) that covers some material that isn't even in the book. I asked a TA where a certain homework topic was in the book and he simply told me to "look it up". Even the book chapters to read on the syllabus are wrong. One of the most disorganized classes I've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 180A. Her final and midterms are fair, you can find similar questions for all the exam questions in lecture notes and textbook and HWs, so exams are not hard. she make computational mistakes but the methods to solve questions are still solid and understandable.Give late announcements, piazza relies, and sample exams(only 3 days before midterm)

It's actually Math 180A. Lectures are kinda boring and sometimes she don't explain things well, but she is accessible outside of class, replies to messages and hold office hours. Exams are comparatively easy, mainly repetition of homework problems.

If I had a minute left to live I would spent it in her class so it would feel like an eternity, her lectures are so boring and she is constantly making mistakes and students would correct her on them.That said just read the textbook and you'll be good.
Professor Ganesan answers questions during lectures with kindness and patience, so don't be afraid to ask if something is unclear.

The pace of the class is incredibly quick. The professor is not very friendly towards students and she is an OK explainer. She committed a lot of algebraic mistakes while doing examples and was unclear in some contexts. It gave me the vibe that she wanted to end lecture ASAP so she could go home or something.

I stopped going for lecture after week 3, course content is easy. Prof means well, and was a good lecturer, but went far too slow in class for me to pay attention. Homework does pile up, and late submissions is the reason I didnt get an A

She was trying to be helpful and indeed spent lots of extra time. However, I constantly went to her lectures and they were confusing. Frequent errors were made and they are always the most basic ones.

All notes and worksheets are posted decently. Past exams are posted for review. Lecture and notes are very clear. Homework is not heavy. Discussion is about doing worksheets, so I recommend you to attend. I went to all discussion and did all the worksheet and past exams, and the exams are pretty fair. Like her lectures and notes.
The exams weren't that tough so overall a decent proffessor, never really went for her lectures but the notes weren't bad

Dr. Ganesan isn't the most engaging lecturer but her expectations are clear and tests are fair/easy to prep for. Though I attended most of the lectures, I learned much more from the textbook and the Engineering Learning Community tutoring (shout out to Nathan!).

Once you figure out how to best approach the material, the course is a breeze.
Not the greatest lecturer (most people stopped coming after week 3). Tests seem to be fair so overall not a terrible class, though there are better alternatives.

Lectures are straightforward and the material is covered effectively. Ganesan talks like a textbook and discussions are surface level. However, the tests are cumulative and the homework is cements the knowledge in your head. That being said, the class textbook for Math 18 is AMAZING. So read the textbook and forget the class.

Professor Ganesan is not the greatest lecturer, so you have to do a lot of self-studying. Even then, her midterms so far have been like 5x harder than the practice exams she gives. Her lecture notes are just her writing down a lot of theories and definitions but only going in surface level without breaking it down, very difficult to follow her.
Professor Ganesan was not the best lecturer. Communication was not the best either. Exams were different from the preparation material.

Kinda confusing class. Got pressured by complaining students after midterm 1 to give an unreasonably massive curve and had to walk it back. Midterm practice exams were not representative but the final practice exam was almost word for word the same. Overall high grade distribution despite the negative reviews. DI not mandatory but go!!!
Her class was the hardest,   but I think it has made me smarter.

Professor Ganesan, while certainly not the most engaging lecturer with her characteristic monotone, does clearly convey the material. Homework is difficult and requires concerted effort to finish. Midterms were hard (mostly long) but highly reflective of homework. Final was easy and more like a 3rd midterm. She has long and frequent office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She may understand the content, but her teaching is completely ineffective. The exams are way harder than last quarter—easily 10x more difficult—and she reduced the curve she initially promised. The class average was 40%, and she did absolutely nothing about it. She purposely withholds curve info because everyone fails anyway. Avoid if possible.

She knows the material but doesn't know how to teach it properly. The class relies heavily on intuition rather than consistent practice. Practice tests are much easier than the real exams. She doesn't take student feedback and explains things as if we already understand them. Nearly impossible to get an A without strong intuition.
Her lectures and notes are very clear. The exams are difficult and lengthy,  but the practice exams are helpful.
Worst Prof ever had

Exams are almost impossible, she gives absolutely no time and her lectures and practice tests don't match the difficulty of the exams. She also grades every homework assignment very harshly. There are no easy points in this class to raise your grade. She promised extra credit, made us do the work for it, then took it away.

Nice, but does not explain things well. Does not allow cheat sheets, but gives one practice exam that is not very indicative of the actual exam. Grade heavily relies on exams, which is understandable since many upper-div math courses follow this. However, the problem lies in the lack of preparation.
Midterms were a lot harder than other sections. She also took back the extra credit she said she would give us. Avoid at all costs.
The midterms were so hard for no reason. When she gave us a curve she took it back and lowered it. The first midterm was too long but the second midterm was harsh in grading.

her tests are ridiculously hard, no cheat sheet, barely enough time to finish it usually. the homework is insanely difficult conceptual problems that take hours to work out and are graded extremely harshly for perfect accuracy, and none of the homework is dropped.
80% of the grade depends on exams. Her exam is impossibly hard. No cheatsheet allowed, tough long homework.
If you go to lecture the class is not too bad at all.

Her midterms are not doable, and little curve was applied to adjust the grades. Taking her class puts you disadvantaged since even if you know the material, she makes it exponentially harder than it should be (as shown through comparison with other sections) to bring your grades down.

gets confused on her own lecture material, refuses to accept feedback while other sections get half as much hw, cheat sheet, and shorter exams. it's better just to wait a quarter for a more lenient prof if she's your only option

Took Math 18 with her but it was a collaborative course with another professor who had better notes and similar exams. Exams that she made were hard compared to other sections, not a lot of people finished. Do not take her for a class if she is the only one teaching it.
super hard.
Homework cannot be completed just by knowledge from lectures. Midterms are hard and contains some grand new questions. Final weighs 40 to 50 percent.
The lectures, homeworks, and tests are three completely different things. Tests are impossible to finish.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The other section had cheatsheet, less questions, and easier exams. It's basically impossible to finish her exams on time.

She lectured pretty well in my opinion. A lot of people felt that she was just repeating the material instead of teaching it conceptually, but she is very patient and open to questions. I enjoyed having her as a professor
His lectures are clear but exams/homework are hard and kind of unpredictable
He rushes through a lot of the concepts, and just kind of expects you to understand whats going on.

It is much more useful to teach yourself than to go to his lectures.  Luckily, homework assignments and quizzes were easy. The final was a little harder, but doable. Also took a while to respond on Piazza or through email. He was also rude sometimes to students
He is kind of rude to students and lectures felt very disorganized. Would not take again, felt like I was teaching myself the class most of the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor over complicates things in class. Hand writting hard to read. Wouldnt recommend. Yells at you if you sit in a left handed seat

He actively ensured students had resources to excel but was a bit disorganized due to graduation. Quizzes were super easy I studied for around 10-20 minutes for each and completed them in ~10-20/50 minutes allotted. Final was also easy with no studying. Overall the material is easy and he taught in a digestible manner in the classes i did attend.
Trying to understand this guy gave me a headache, every lecture had a mistake and he never planned ahead, announcement's were always made last minute, I definitely do NOT recommend this 🧑‍🏫
Professor Ganapathy was new when I had him so he may have improved but he rushed through a lot of the material and wasn't very clear when explaining concepts.
He's new to teaching the course and there were difficulties translating the concepts but the tests were fair.

do not bother watching lectures or showing up to class,just read the textbook and do practice problems. his handwriting is borderline illegible at times which made his attempts at explaining his thought process even more convoluted. ive spoke to other students about this and its not just me who feels like this. try taking with other instructor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: didnt let us have notes for quizzes, made easy class hard, bad handwriting, made lot of mistakes during lecture solving example questions,didnt explain himself

He made this class unnecessarily hard and tedious. He often came to lecture unprepared and made a lot of mistakes. Self study is definitely recommended over watching lectures/going to class. Try to take this class with a different professor.
not super organized but very helpful in office hours
Fair exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Average professor, but is very accessible in office hours and willing to help. If you're new to proofs, maybe take this class in your sophomore year and prepare yourself beforehand as it can get super confusing later.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ganapathy is a caring and helpful teacher. He sometimes skips steps in lectures but clarifies in office hours, email, or Piazza. His exams are fair, and he gave a generous curve. I believe this is his first time teaching, and he's already pretty good. I only see him improving and would definitely recommend him as a professor.

Professor Ganapathy is kind and caring, but his teaching needs improvement. He doesn't seem to realize many students are new to this type of math. He skips steps to finish lectures quickly and speaks too fast, making it hard to follow. He has potential but isn't there yet. Midterms are fair, but the final is difficult. Unsure if class curved
There are two midterms and a final which were easy. Overall not that much work except the weekly homeworks for which you have to buy the textbook to get the access code. Karthik was nice and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Karthik was a good lecturer and happy to take questions in class. I didn't love the course material but Karthik made it  easy to follow along and is always available for office hours. Good prof, straightforward and doesn't make things overly complicated
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ganapathy goes through the lectures very fast and if you are not quick, you might not catch it. Attending office hours really helps and he actually cares about the students. He also shows plenty of example problems to strengthen understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures could improve but he was very helpful during office hours.

Not the head instructor (did not make exams, decide content, etc.). Not very good at teaching. Ended up watching lead instructor's lecture podcasts and going to lead instructor's office hours. I believe Karthik could become a good teacher with more time, but he's still pretty disorganized and not the best at explaining.

He's honestly kind of silly but he does engage in discussions with students during lectures. Lots of reading with it being HUM, but gives general background information about the text during lectures, so he expects you to already read it. But your grades are mainly determined by your TA who grades ur essays and other assignments so its a gamble

Honestly a solid professor. His lectures were always engaging. He says lecture isn't mandatory but he gives quick-writes once a week so watch out for that. Only difficult part are the 2 essays, but if your TA is good and you show up to office hours, you will be fine. Final was also easy.

Honestly a hilarious and knowledgeable guy, I just had a slightly sour experience because of the TA I got. Spent a full week crafting an essay and was given a 78 with rhetorical questions as comments. The TA felt very nitpicky and it is a TA that is often for this class. Other than that though lecture was fun, readings were manageable.

Lectures and the books we read were interesting. 
DO NOT BE FOOLED FIRST ESSAY WHEN THEY TELL YOU RUBRIC IS "OPTIONAL."
FOLLOW THE RUBRIC. FOLLOW THE RUBRIC. FOLLOW THE RUBRIC.
I had a bad TA that didn't teach essay structure, but as long as you follow canvas modules for writing you'll be fine. You've been warned. Other than that, great class.

reviews.comment: His lectures are entertaining and he gives EC to people who watch an extra movie. Once a week he will have a lecture reflection (attendance) which is part of your grade. reviews.comment: Entertaining lectures, they get you thinking about the course material without just being plain lectures about boring topics. Make sure you get a good TA, the TA is mainly the deciding factor on whether or not this class is enjoyable.

reviews.comment: West is an interesting prof. He enjoys in class discussion a lot and while he can be combative and opinionated he's a pretty chill guy in office hours. reviews.comment: Reddit tier professor who is combative to those who continuously ask him questions. No technology policy enforced to the degree of bullying. Very discussion and TA based final grade
he made fun of my no. 2 pencil

Prof. West's lectures aren't mandatory or podcasted but he covers the key themes/historical context of the readings. Discussion heavily impacts your grade. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: First, I would like to say that nobody in my class got an A+. reviews.comment: his lectures aren't mandatory or podcasted, but he basically just goes over the readings, analyzing their main themes and messages as well as sharing his own opinions on them. he's funny and friendly, happily conversing with students about random stuff. essays are graded by your TA, and discussion participation matters a lot.

He was such a great professor. Even though his lectures weren't mandatory I would still go because he would go over the readings that we needed to do and went deeper into them. Honestly if you read and ask for feedback from TAs the class is easy. Your grade does heavily depend on your TA though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I love his lectures. As with any Hum course, there's a lot of reading but the lectures give a good review of the text and help with understanding them better. He is certainly intimidating at first but it's really easy to get comfortable around him.

West is a great lecturer, he can seem a little intimidating and hard to approach but he's an overall nice guy. The readings and papers are consistent with the rest of the HUM series, with your final grade probably more dependent on your TA, but his finals are usually take-home and pretty chill and should boost your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment:
Child-like and hard to talk to. He threatened to take back extra credit assignment because someone completed it too fast. 
lectures are bullet points/quotations from book, and then he blabs from there or invites students to speak (he loves to challenge/ argue with the answers he receives). 
final: 2 essays and vocab definitions.

Fantastic lectures, marking important words in bold and underlined. Attendance is non-mandatory but makes the final much easier as he covers everything needed. Your TA makes or breaks your HUM experience, but Professor West assists by providing a quarter-long extra credit opportunity. Stay up-to-date with the readings, and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The prof is very laid back and pretty funny as well. His lectures are straight forward with important vocabs underlined for you in the slides that will be tested in the final exam. The actual essays gradings (majority of your class grade) depend heavily on you specific TA though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class is pretty straight-forward, but the special thing is that he offers extra credit that really helps your grade. He is not the easiest person to talk to, but that is okay because you mainly interact with your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof West is by far my favorite Hum professor. He cares about his students and the course. His lectures are very engaging and interesting. He gives extra credit, and honestly as long as you show up to lecture and do the majority of the readings you'll be good. Truly an amazing professor! Highly highly recommend!

Prof West actually makes his class structured for success. Getting a decent grade in the class isn't too tough (for a HUM class) if you put in the right amount of effort into the essays (you don't even have to read that much). Unfortunately, I felt a bit off in his lectures, and didn't find them nearly as engaging as HUM 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very close-minded guides conversation in a very specific direction and doesn't look into alternate perspectives. Class is not created to have open discussion. I don't even talk or participate in class or discussion but I get frustrated listening to this guy. At least the class is relatively easy

Prof West is one of the best in the department. His lectures are entertaining and he gives explicit answers to the final on days with light attendance. The workload is fair and he makes the texts interesting. Most of the final is given in advance. Offers generous extra credit opportunities.

There were two essays and a 3-part final exam. Most of your grade depends on your TA. He has an extra credit opportunity that gives you a 1/3 grade boost. His lectures were ok, he seemed knowledgeable and passionate about the content, but I rarely went because I didn't feel like I was learning anything useful from them.

I love this man. he's definitely not for everyone; he will kinda flex how much he knows and isn't afraid to get a little political, but he only uses that as a teaching tool. he is funny, engaging, and a little out of pocket sometimes. I had him over summer so cant attest to what he's like in a regular quarter but definitely take him over summer!

May not be the best lecturer, but he gives extra credit. As long as you do all your assignments, you will get a 1/3 letter grade bump. Highly recommend reading all the books, even if some of them aren't tied to an essay, and going to lecture for the key terms listed in the slides because both will be applicable to the final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His lectures are very engaging and informative, West is very knowledgable and passionate. Your grade largely depends on your TA and your ability to understand the essay prompts. West's grading criteria is very fair and he gives students opportunities to do well, you just have to take them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: West does not give the time, respect, or professionalism he demands of students. His analyses contradict the text, so I started using his class as a critical thinking exercise where I'd evaluate if evidence supported his lessons.

Dont listen to these trolls that degrade him, I absolutely adore him as he's willing to stay back after every lecture to provide extra help with works up until 2 hours later, easy system, TA-grade dependent.
I absolutely loved every lecture that I went to. I found myself looking forwards to lecture every morning I had it and felt as if I learned a lot, as long as I did the reading.

Obviously in Hum your grade is based on your TA. The prof set the course up well tho. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

Prof West is a knowledgeable and interesting lecturer. His take on points are sorta controversial when it comes, but extremely intriguing. reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love West for Hum. He really wants his students to succeed and gives assignments that will boost your final grade by 1/3 of a letter grade if you do it. West is a great prof. There are two formal essays, two revisions, and an informal final; he also gives a great extra credit opportunity. His lectures are more history based but still pretty interesting.

Professor West is an okay professor. Admittedly, he is a little disorganized with how he presents his lectures, making it hard to take notes, but his actual class structure is superb. Professor Gopal is a kind person who is passionate towards the material. This class is straight forward as it gets. Just study the lecture slide prior to taking exams and there's no reason to not get an A/B

Prof. Gopal was super nice!! Exams were based on the lecture slides. Make sure to review them before taking the exams. And he was super accessible and helpful outside of class. A is definitely approachable. If you don't mind that he has lil bit accent, go for him!!

i have no idea why her rating is so low. i went into this class super apprehensive but she was awesome. i also took poli113, 131, 214 with her. she was genuinely so nice and helpful for all the classes. i had issues w exam (wayyy lower score than expected, i lowk think my canvas was broken or smth) and she just let me retake the exam completely.

Heath expects you to figure out complex concepts in one go and says things like "It's basically saying 1 = 1" after doing complex series manipulations. Do not recommend. Take someone else.

The issue with this course is the lack of practice resources/info, but it's not as bad as most ppl say it is. 

Grading scheme is 25/25/50 tests mt/final

Do the HW problems but DONT bother doing supplemental problems, they're irrelevant to what's on the exam. 

Tests are ok, but the main difficulty was barely having any relevant material to study.

He doesn't teach, just summarizes topics. HW is given, but not graded. 2 midterms, 1 final. He can be condescending and appears to care more about his research. Tests are not overly difficult, so the class is doable if you teach yourself. Tests are kind of like homework. As long as you can teach yourself, you can pass. TLDR: he is bad at teaching.

Prof. Heath is a great lecturer with chill yet funny vibes. He knows what he's talking about and grounds the theoretical class to actual real-world applications. Homework are optional but please do it on your own for your own understanding. Class is graded solely on test, and he replaces 1 midterms with finals. It's always a good time on his class.

I am concerned about the quality of instruction in this course. The material lacks the clarity, precision, and scientific rigor expected for a university-level neuroscience course. The explanations are often overly simplistic and imprecise, which undermines the credibility of the content and makes it difficult to engage seriously with the material

Prof. knows her stuff but constantly updates her content alongside research- Slides were freq. unorganized or glitched- OH sessions are great for ?'s- Exams mostly fair but some ?s are tricky- EC clicker ?s in lecture- DI are mandatory w/req. readings. Busy work, but manageable- There's a NeuroTok  - Kind prof. who will reach out, but responds slow

Dr. Halpain is experienced and passionate about neuroscience
-Tries to keep class engaging
-Slides can be unclear; tech issues and Canvas mismatches were common
-Exams mostly fair but some tricky questions
-Discussions had occasional scheduling confusion & are mandatory for grade
-Includes 3 midterms, 1 final, NeuroTikTok assignment, & extra credit

Very nice person, just her slides are kinda messy,and the MTs are hard.Pick the best choice can be 3 of 4 answers sometimes and you really have to know your stuff-very detailed.3 MT and all are MC 30 Q with a Final MC too. Section is mandatory and you read articles before class and do Qs- kinda pointless not working with research like catalog says.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 3 mini MTs + final. tests were hard, mainly because the q's were extremely tricky and u rly need to know ur stuff to answer them correctly. there's a lot of select all that apply q's. Doesn't release the tests so you'll need to go to the review sessions / OHs to get the questions. She's obv a neuro expert but goes off on a tangent sometimes.
studying for this final is making me lose my will to live. too much info.

I would rather overdose on fentanyl than attend Shelley's Lecture.  They are super boring with some students began sleeping.  Tests are a little unfair as she tries to trick you.  Never knows the answer to student's questions.  No midterms are dropped and she is against curving.  I expected better from UCSD.

Class context is very interesting but this is an unprepared professor. Slides are unorganized. Class is a mess and she sometimes doesn't know how to answer questions. The podcast isn't guaranteed to have audio so don't miss the lecture. Would take professor again but expected better

She sucks and teaching and is super boring.  Shelley loves to go on long tangents about whatever topic we are learning about, then proceeds to rush through the content towards the end of class.  Midterms are quite unfair because she tries to trick you.  When students ask questions, her usual response is, "Idk".  Hard Pass!

Obv intelligent and cares about her field. In terms of lectures and communication, she is is honestly pretty mid, leaning bad... often goes off-topic and tends to be unclear on imperative concepts and mechanisms of disease and is quite rude to students and treated us like children. Clarify miscommunicated concepts in OH to get a good grade.

Great professor. Online exams were ridiculously easy (thanks COVID). She makes you read a scientific paper per week thou they are pretty easy to understand(and the material is relevant and interesting). She's actually available outside of the classroom and will help you if you ask.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This professor doesn't have the good skill to teach students. She is a verbal professor. She doesn't write anything on the board. She is always late to her class. She grades by word which if you don't mention a word she is looking for! too bad you will get 0 on the question. She required a lot of readings. I don't really recommend this professor:(
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Although the material can get really interesting, I would say that the professor is not that great. On top of pop quizzes, you have 2 group projects where for one you make a stupid video. On top of that, you have the constant stress of needless homework at the end of the week. Highly do not suggest taking this class. Go take something better.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class was super memorable; I loved learning about various developmental and psychiatric disorders. Her lectures are super interesting but long. Very knowledgeable prof. Only audiocasts which is frustrating. Pop quizzes. Go to lecture and section. Midterm is pretty easy if you go to class. Final was HARD tbh so don't underestimate it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She came late to about half the lectures. No lie. Even on the final she was late by 15+ minutes. Theres readings and homework every week, on top of 2 group projects. Letter of rec? Only if you get an A+ or if you donate to the school to fund her secretary. If you try and ask clarification questions on a test, too bad, it means you dont know it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I heard that this class was an easy A. That A might be attainable if you go to every lecture, pay attention, and take detailed notes. Not only does she not post all her lecture slides, the class is only audiocast with half of them starting off with sorry Im late again, traffic was so bad today or parking is so tough on campus (with my A pass).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: So many group projects that are more annoying than useful. Only audio podcast which is awful as she adds more content to the posted slides and never updates them. Midterm wasn't hard, but point distribution is ridiculous and had weird questions irrelevant to main topics. Wish she had a practice midterm. Pop quizzes forced me to attend lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She was late to the class many times, but one time she started the pop quiz in the beginning of the lecture and didn't allow students who were 10mins late to take the quiz. Should provide a practice midterm b/c her midterm has some irrelevant questions that are not important to the main concepts.

This is one of the most interesting classes I've taken at UCSD, and I find her lectures really cohesive and organized. She is really not that boring, students just give her a hard time. Her tests are extremely fair and straight forward. Really no complaints about this class!
horrible unorganized women, lectures are super boring and she always goes on tangents
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Her lectures are so boring. The only reason I showed up for class was because I'm paranoid about missing class and it was too painful to podcast her lectures; they're that boring! Overall the class is pretty easy tho. Lots of annoying assignments but they aren't hard, you just gotta do them.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: she is boring and a bad lecturer. Talks slow and seems to get lost in her own world. Lectures are disorganized and slides are just picture she found on google images lmao. Easy class though
Probably the worst, most disorganized and boring lecturer at UCSD but easy class

Phenomenal Professor! Excellent at explaining complicated topics in a clear fashion. Her class is exceptionally interesting. This class has lots of information, but is manageable if one understands the topics presented. Highly recommend for BIPN152! One of the most interesting classes here at UCSD! Feels like a COGS Neuro lecture with more biology.

Lots of paper homework (due every week)!!! You definitely need to read the book in order to pass the class. iClicker points are extra credit. Her tests are really really hard, but they are multiple choice. Her lectures are long and confusing, she skips over a ton of slides and expects you to know the material for the midtermfinal. She does curve.

There's a lot of HW in this class so it's pretty time-consuming. Get ready to pick up that textbook and READ READ READ. She offers extra credit by providing iclicker questions, which may raise your grade exponentially at the end. Her exams are fair and pretty straight-forward. TAs are very helpful so make sure to attend section and you will succeed

You may find the lectures to be a kind of knowledge review if you want to get a good grade, because you basically have to read the book and finish the relative assignments ahead the lectures. Her lectures are actually not that good for taking clear notes, so I don't think I'll take her again. clicker questions for extra credits& no podcast
She is a fair teacher. The class didn't have a curve, which could be good or bad.  There is a lots of material to learn per lecture but I would take again.

BILD is no joke and reading the book is a must do. Lectures are filled with info to the brim. This quarter, class was mandatory but next quarter Prof. Halpain might make iClickers as extra credit which will help a lot. She's a great teacher though and really cares for her students. Study, do practice problems, and get that A! :]

This class requires a lot of out of the classroom work. In order to succeed, you need to read the book until you understand every word and concept. Her lectures give a brief summary of what she thinks is important, but memorizing material int he book is your best bet. Midterms aren't too hard but the final was more challenging. She curves as well.

She lectures very fast, but is extremely clear and concise in what she has to tell her students.  She will always stop for questions and discussions and probably wont cover all the material required during the second half of the class. This class is hard overall, the first half was intense calculations and the second is all memorization. Not easy!

Excruciating. So scattered and unclear. Puts slides online for students to reference and then changes them before class, where they are STILL out of order and disorganized. All questions are worded unclear. Spends time on nuanced points and tests on random minute details. I do not recommend her. Even an A is not worth this.

She is a great teacher! At first I was nervous after seeing her previous reviews but don't let those scare you. She gives credit for iclickers and homework. You do have to study and read the book if you want to do well but as long as you know the material her tests are more than fair and you will receive and good grade as long as you put in effort!
Easy class. Bad lecturer. I-clicker needed. She wants you to know everything so she crams information in her unorganized slides. But above all, it's cell biology. If you memorize, how hard can it be?

In other BILD classes, all the test questions come from lecture. Not hers. You actually need to read the book. Her lectures are pointless, but she has clicker questions so it's mandatory. She goes through lecture too fast and it's hard to understand her. Do not take her.

This professor tries to help, but does too much and tries to cram in information instead of teach clearly. She's kinda snappy and wry in a bad way. Her class is difficult and has a lot of work. It wouldn't be so bad, it's just she piles on homework, with clicker points, plus 2 midterms. Don't take her if you have the option.
Knowing biochemistry will help you much more than knowing neuroscience. Exams required a pretty thorough knowledge of the material.

I give her credit for trying. But she just tries to cram way too much stuff into all the lectures. She falls behind easily and just lacks the conviction to burn the stuff into the mind of the student.

She is the sweetest person ever. I loved her lectures. She is very approachable and friendly. The class was really hard because the text book was hardly used but it was worth the studying. She is just wonderful.
this class was extremely easy. do the problem sets before the answer keys are posted and you will have no problem getting an A on the midterms and final.

Halpain isnt all that bad. She expects you to know every detail from the lectures but the slides are posted on the website and everything is podcasted. If you put in the work and study you will do well.

Her class is beyond hard. To the person below me, that explains why she had a 48% recommendation rate on the capes and this was before the final, it would have been much lower had capes been taken after the final. She doesn't get back to you if you e-mail her either. Shes the worst professor I've encountered at UCSD.

I am a freshman who rarely went to her lectures and still got an A in her class. Her tests were long (especially the first midterm), but really weren't that difficult. She puts questions that test students' understanding of the general concept covered in each chapters (not into detail). About two days of study before the final exam was enough to ac

There is a reason why her name is halPAIN. She is by far the WORST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER ENCOUNTERED HERE AT UCSD. Her unfair exams that test students' knowledge of minute details, not concepts that are requisite for the course are absolutely absurd. Her uptight demeanor and harsh tone have permanently been ingrained in my mind. Thank you, dr.pain.
Maybe if she stopped caring so much about her research and dedicated some more time to being a good teacher then she'd be worth taking. Thanks for failing me, I'm sure med school is going to love me!

WORST PROFESSOR. period. NEVER TAKE HER AS YOUR BILD 1 Professor EVER. I basically studied hardest for this class and still failed. Her class literally destroyed my gpa and now i'm not even sure if I can still get into med school. Thanks a lot prof halpain. Save yourself the trouble and stress and choose another professor!!!

TOTALLY AGRRE WITH OTHER "WORST PROFESSOR" COMMENTS! her exams are way too long and way too hard because of all the weird wording. questions on the final were EVEN HARDER than midterms since everything is multiple choice and all the choices sound almost the same!(cuz the wording)

Her class is absurd, I studied so much and still failed. Our midterm was ridiculous. Her exact words "Probably half of the class won't be able to finish this exam." I scored higher than most of the class on the midterm and still failed this class. Do NOT take her.

Studied so much for this class for not even a decent grade. She'll tell you that you'll need to know more than what's actually covered on the midterms. The midterms are also ridiculously long. Made the class more difficult than it actually is. Save your GPA and do not take her.

She is a horrible professor. Even the TA's said her tests were harder than any other BILD classes were. Please if you care about your GPA do not take her. I studied so hard for her final and passed both of the midterms and still could not manage a decent grade. I do not recommend her.

On her teaching performance, Halpain is a good professor and is crystal clear with her lectures. Her powerpoints are posted online, and are good for review. Nevertheless, her grading system is absolutely atrocious as she scales the class. I got an A on the first midterm because I read the book. The CLASS is difficult, but SHE helpful.

Professor Halpain is a really great professor. She posts her powerpoints online, and the midterms are not bad. You do need to study and read the textbook, but I am a freshman this year and I got an A on the first midterm. Making flashcards helped me a lot. She is very passionate about biology and her lectures are interesting. I recommend this class

I am also taking BILD 1,for Fall 10,& like the person below me,midterm #1 was ridiculously long.It was worth 141 points and she only gave us 30 mins. to do it. B/C 1/2 the class failed the 1st exam, the second midterm was worth 100 pts and gave us 45 mins to work on it.She takes the average of the top 10 scores and makes that the A. Don't take her!

her midterms are ridiculously LONNG only a couple people finished everything. The average was below 50%... most people dropped her class right after the first midterm but she seems to not care about it. her second midterm contains A LOT MORE details than the first one. Bild 1 should not be this hard. she doesnt even curve generously....

Dr. Halpain is a really good professor. she is always ready for lecture and she gives prizes for ppl who answer questions in lecture. her exams consist of everything, (short answer, mult. choice, matching, etc). she is extremely helpful in office hours. take her, you wont regret it.

New Professor and still learning what works, but is very nice. Overall a fair class and tests, but didn't give out practice exams so it was a shot in the dark when sitting down to take the test. Study the pictures and diagrams in the text and lecture as she likes you to recreate them. Would take another class with her again.
"Has interesting poilicies that are not helpful for the students"
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: "Interesting professor"

Her exams are easier than her homework, and focuses on concepts mostly. Her homework tends to be really long and time consuming. She's pretty helpful when you ask for it, and her lectures are pretty interesting, but also really closely tied to the textbook.

The classes were primarily conducted by TA, only saw professor 2-3 times during the quarter. Both the TA and the professor were amazing, gave detailed and personalized feedback, and showed immense care. Great class to learn public speaking, get to know people, and genuinely just enjoy.

Overall, the class was fun and a breather from separate classes. Class mainly taught by TA (Kennedy Tolson) who is overall great. Work load is more than do able, periodic reading (Free) + Q&As, 3 speeches that are graded lightly. Class involves speaking exercises/speech practices = step out of comfort zone = better public speaker.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Carla is an absolute joy. She is one of the most kind, caring, and intentional teachers I have ever experienced. She is a consummate professional and manages time perfectly. Her feedback is so unbelievably meaningful and genuine. Her patience is extraordinary and one of a saint. You can see and feel the passion and joy she has being here!

The class is mostly based on your TA, I had Kenneth and he was genuinely the greatest mentor I could've ever asked for, but Carla stopped by a couple of times. She was so sweet and caring and obviously so passionate about what we were doing. Such an amazing class would take and recommend a million times over.

Super easy class. However, the class is taught entirely by your TA. I saw Professor Harting twice during the quarter. Participation is important, and attendance is mandatory. Easy grading, just show that you put in effort and you'll do well. There is a textbook, but it's free and you only really need it for the biweekly quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best course ever taken in UCSD. Gets you out of your comfort. 90%of the class got an A. And unlike most easy A courses, you actually get to learn SO MUCH from this course in public speaking. Course is led by TA, and my TA was the best. So easy going, and chill, you can literally talk about anything you want in the class. 100% recommended.

Very fun class that will get you out of your comfort zone. You will learn a lot about tactics and objectives and receive great feedback from the professor. This class is great even if you're shy. Such a good beginners acting class and you WILL be proud of your work and acting by the end of it.

(Took class online) Class was run by TA, so all the grading was up to them. Didn't really see Prof. Harting at all throughout the quarter. But the class was very straightforward and my TA was great and super welcoming and understanding. Learned lots!

Carla is amazing. We spent the first few weeks building a community, which might have been a little much, but I made some really great friends in this class. Once we had that foundation it was so easy to get up and perform. The class is slow but well structured, and she is such a sweetheart.

Best Prof. ever. She cares so much about her students. Super nice and approachable. She makes the class so enjoyable. She definitely enjoys teaching, acting, and everything she does. I learned a lot from her class. Take her if you can!

She is a professional actress herself. She is responsible and planned. She almost never comes to any class even slightly less prepared. She is easy to satisfy, as kong as you do your work. She is fun and relaxed. She is also a great ice-breaker, which is important for an acting class. I feel like she really loves each student that she has.

I just dont believe real people are leaving these reviews. Myself and everyone ive asked all agree she is not a good teacher at all. She throws methods like active recall and knowledge organizations at you but barely has any actual technical knowledge of statics or does extensive problems in class. "Project" is a big waste of time.

Best professor at this school. Took time to teach us better learning techniques. Lectures are very helpful in understanding the content. Uses cool demos and passes out parts to better explain the concepts. Exams are similar to homework. The project is pretty big but it serves as a great way to practice and apply the concepts your learn. Start early

Unusual syllabus that isnt like other classes. Not a bad thing though. Group projects are hard and demanding. Lots of homework. But lots of Extra credit too. Tests are graded hard and her lectures consists of a lot of “talk to each other for a minute on this”.

She is a very sweet professor and cares about her students however her lectures are very quick and she moves onto another topic every lecture. She also assigns a group project and doesn't really elaborate on how to complete it. Be prepared to spend extra time prepping for her class unless you're used to a fast paced learning environment.
class is just time intensive but she's definitely the better professor in terms of extra credit and work. love her class and she's a great professor!

One of the best MAE professors I've had at UCSD by far. Does an excellent job adapting to different learning styles, making sure every student has a chance to succeed. Plenty of extra credit opportunities that genuinely help reinforce the material. Overall, she's supportive, organized, and truly cares about her students' success.

Completely loved the class. She had a "learning seminar" that was super helpful. No other professor has ever done something similar to support learning at that level.
She had a great way to teach, asking us questions and then giving us some time to think, see what we know and realize what we don't know, so we could learn that from her explanations.

As someone who learns by asking questions. She seemed very bothered by questions, especially from pereq topics. As in the "you should already know this" type of attitude. It was honestly weird because she wanted you to know she cares about students learning, but it did not seem like it. If you're a typical student who does well, then take her.

Very respectful when personal matters arose. She's not a bad teacher, but teaching style was not for me. Too much homework and tests (the at home quizzes killed me). I feel like she overcomplicated the material way too much. Had to do lots of self studying on top of the tons of hw that she gave. If you can keep up with her you will be fine.

Great professor, difficult, lots of EC. Def do HW honestly & supplement topics with textbook readings. The tests r very hard & in depth, but lectures r helpful and engaging. She has irl models & demonstrations, which also helps with understanding. Make sure to make friends bc take-home exams r rlly time consuming & hard, teamwork helps loads.

Very sweet, kind, and overall amazing professor with interactive lectures that helped solidify statics concepts in my head. She cares a lot about students, though her quizzes can be pretty hard compared to the homework she assigns and the lecture examples she goes over in class. Nonetheless, she prepares you pretty well and gives a lot of EC
She is the best person to teach MAE 30A. Look forward to take her MAE 131A next quarter
Best professor at UCSD so far.
I really like her teaching style with the demonstrations in class. It helps us understand how the deformations are taking place. Very kind and fair professor.
The class was really interesting and easy. A lot of the topics were eye opening and I felt like I learnt useful things and a new perspective. Take this class!
She is awesome! She is so sweet and teaches so well. She helps you push your boundaries further.

She overcomplicates the material when the material is on the easier side. She also has these insane quizzes that have alot of parts most of which take a long time to read and even longer time to write down.There is an overwhelming amount of assignments even when there are quizzes and exams. She expects you to spend your whole time on this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is the queen.

Qi can be a tough professor to learn from but is fair to her students. She would take the time to let her students study and review practice problems thoroughly. She is very coherent and clear in her teaching. Do not skip lecture! Ask her questions if you're confused in anything at all because she is very helpful.

She's the best - to the point where I get excited whenever a class is offered with her teaching it. Took 3 classes with her already, and she is a legend. Fun classes, you learn so much, and she cares so much about your learning, both how you learn and what you learn. Put in the effort and you'll be rewarded here, and you'll have a good time.

Professor Qi is amazing. She really cares about students learning and her lectures are very clear, organized, and easy to understand. She gives a very manageable amount of homework and nothing feels unnecessarily hard or unfair. Tests are fair as well and she gives great practice problems before each test. One of the best professors I've had.

Professor Qi is a passionate instructor who makes it her priority to have her students thoroughly understand the material. She is an awesome teacher, I enjoyed the class for both the awesome course material and Professor Qi's great teaching.

Professor Qi is by far my favorite so far. Obviously intro to aerospace engineering is going to be a difficult class, but Qi definitely makes it easier. Her lectures are clear and easy to follow and all exams and homework come straight from lecture. I learned so so much in this class I really hope you get a chance to learn from her too.
She teaches the concepts very clearly. The content is challenging, but she made it easy to understand.
Professor Qi is so sweet and caring for her students! She made the class very interesting! Work load is on the higher end but manageable. I had lots of fun and learned a lot!

So much unnecessary work especially for an introductory course. Maybe her other classes are better but mae3 had at least 2 long assignments on top of group project work per week. The instructions for everything were super complicated and unclear, yet were graded extremely harsh. Absolutely would not recommend for the amount of work she assigns.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Whoever is reading this, make sure you enroll in Prof. Qi's class in the FIRST pass, otherwise, you will not have a seat. Her class was filled so quickly. It was INSANE. I am frustrated now because I am on the waitlist for MAE 131A.
Professor HuiHui is the G.O.A.T. I took both 156A and B with her. Great professor
The worst instructor I ever had at UCSD. I wonder how come she has a 4.7 rating! definitely doesn't deserve it!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Qi is a phenomenal professor who clearly takes her time planning a class structure that will lead to the success of her students. She knows how to keep the class engaged and interested. The way she clearly explains everything is way better than any textbook. She is incredible and truly unique.

Professor Qi is a real gem of a teacher. She is caring and concerned about the learning and daily lives of her students. She accommodates everyones unique situations and always seeks to alleviate student stress. Besides this, her class is very engaging and digestible. You will learn a lot from her classes and have fun along the way!

Huihui is an amazing professor that very clearly keeps the best in mind for her students. Lectures are engaging, and she actively connects topics covered in class to the real world. Her grading is fair, and she is always accessible outside of the classroom for engineering and nonengineering related converstion.

Take any class Professor Qi teaches! Do not ask me why. If you really want to ask me. Because she is amazing! So caring, so good at teaching and explain ideas! She will often throw in funny and memorable analogies to make the lecture interesting. Yeah, she will have you to do quite some work though, it is worth it. I love this professor

Dr Qi is a super considerate & thoughtful & enthusiastic & engaged professor who genuinely cares about her students! Very important for young women studying in this field to have a professor to look up like her. I love the learning cycle she designed and it really helps my learning, and I try to do the same for my other class. My fav professor

Professor Qi has the biggest heart of anyone you'll ever meet. She's so kind, and incredibly accommodating for her students. She always asks for feedback, and is enthusiastic about teaching and improving her methods. Theres a good bit of homework, but it is worth it, and really helps you learn the material better. Hands down my favorite professor<3

Professor Qi demonstrates that she cares about student's learning every day. Even though there can be a lot of graded work, it is no more than what you probably should already be doing to study for the class (i.e. assigned readings before the lecture). Very passionate about her class and students, and an excellent lecturer. Very impactful professor

Professor Qi is one of those professors who clearly puts in a lot of effort to teach and explain concepts as well as she can. Her classes are fairly cohesive (different types of homework/participation), and she does assign a lot of homework, which can be a lot to deal with. However, she really makes classes interesting! Quickly became my fav prof.

Amazing professor! Dr Qi creates and safe learning environment for her students and genuinely cares about her students progress throughout the quarter. She always makes sure that her students understand the material before moving on to new topics. She is very welcome to questions. Taking MAE 131 A with her now!

Professor Qi is an amazing professor. She genuinely cares about her students and explains the material extremely thoroughly to ensure that the students understand the topics. She is my favorite professor at UCSD.

So many assignments during the first few weeks, it really stressed me out (especially trying to focus on my career-related courses). She's very nit-picky on how you approach homework, you have to do it a certain way or you lose points (units, axis, forces, etc...) No shortcutting the assignments. No grading curve.

One of the most amazing professors I have ever met, full stop. He puts an absolutely insane amount of care into his lectures, discussions, problem sessions and even office hours. He gets to know every student and gives so much attention to what they need and supporting their learning. I learned more in his class than any other, he's inspiring.

This continues the American Dream:his class welcomes every type of students. If you are competitive, you will FOR SURE ENJOY the discussion session. If you want to just leran more about physics, This is one of those physcis classes that includes a lot of fun demos of physcis phenomenons. If you are worried about your grade, his curve is generous.

"If you ever wonder what is American Dream, it is opportunity, success, and being Thomas' 2D student."
This is probably best structured class in UCSD that teaches you way more than just physics.  The teaching strucutre he used is very unqiue and creative, you will not regret going to his Office Hourse and Discussion sessions which helps a lot.

350 characters ISNT ENOUGH to describe how well designed and executed Wong's 2D is. This is simultaneously the hardest and most rewarding class I've taken at UCSD. Always go to office hours, there's never been a moment where I felt like my time was wasted. I have never been to more fun discussions. If I could, I'd take the class 10000000000x over.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Amazing professor, cares deeply about the subject and it shows. Difficult subject but the time and care he puts into the class is phenomenal, very accessible outside of class and will work with you to succeed. The effort you put in will be rewarded tenfold if you immerse yourself in the class and the community built in class. 
Top 3 professor oat

This man is one of the best professors on campus by a LONG shot. The amount of care and effort he puts into his students is simply inconceivable. He is super patient and kind. If you go to his office hours, it will be worth every second. He's able to break down difficult concepts into digestible things. My praise is only limited by the word count.

Super great professor can't recommend him enough. Stayed up late answering questions, stayed long after class answering, this man is available whenever you need him, and i cant recommend enough asking him questions. GO TO OFFICE HOURS it helps a TON and you will be grateful. Best professor I've had although it isn't even my major(which says a lot).

Nice and caring professor. Was never rude or unwilling to help. Sometimes homework can be a little heavy and I personally feel that the homework questions often strayed a bit from the scope of the lecture, forcing you to access outside sources to understand problems at times. The final really messed my grade up, so study up for that!

Homeworks weren't always relevant to what we were learning, and lectures sometimes felt like they were overcomplicating the course content. That being said, the exams were very similar to the practice exams, and discussion worksheets helped in preparing for exams.

When you think of the GOAT, who do you think of? Jordan? Lebron? Ronaldo? Messi? I think of prof. Ching Wei Ho. If Bam scored 83, he scored 84. Although lectures were a bit boring, he definitely was very knowledgeable and funny. Goated person and professor.

he's a good prof. he can teach, good vibes, and midterms are pretty easy if you studied. but prepare for the final. bro made the final more difficult compare to last quarter which is a bummer. not only that, HE DOESN'T CURVE. i repeat. HE DOESN'T CURVE. overall good prof but sadly could be better if he curved.

HW - 20%, Participation - 5%, 2 Midterms (22%), 1 Final (31%). The professor's lectures were clear, and going to lecture will 100% make the tests and studying easier. His attitude and attention to detail are above average. The midterms were easier than the homework and relatively straightforward, but the final is harder but fair. I would recommend!

Best professor I've had! Attendance isn't required & lectures are recorded, but going helps since test questions come from in-class examples. Exams allow a double-sided cheat sheet and are pretty easy if you review lecture examples & discussion worksheets. He's also extended hw deadlines and is very understanding and a great teacher. Love this guy
My goat! His lectures are super clear, highly recommended to attend it, and I got F on 20A from another professor, Ho just save my life!

Coming to class blessed my monday wednesday fridays. If you go to lecture and truly do the homework the class is a breeze. Dude explains everything like crystal clear water. Dont be afraid to ask questions or tell him if you think something is wrong - he will laugh it off and be as positive as a proton
