he's a solid lecturer and does a really good job at outlining things. his midterms are easy so really really study for those. his final will be much harder. like. much harder so lock in. you will see questions you have never seen before. TA's are rude and unhelpful but the professor is amazing.

His lectures actually helped me understand vectors so well. Attendance isn't mandatory, but since he uses a chalkboard, I recommend having someone to take notes for you if you miss class. This quarter, section attendance wasn't mandatory, though it could be in the future. All of his exams are very reasonable and have good practice exams.

Professor is caring and always available to help his students. Course is very easy to pass but in order to achieve a high grade I'd recommend studying. Practice exams reflect style of questions but not always the content. Lectures aren't the most engaging for me, but he is the best in the math dpt. Take him!

Very manageable, literally just pay attention in lecture, study a bit outside of class. Discussions are pretty boring since it's just doing practice problems but they aren't difficult themselves. He explains topics to the class like we are first learning them as if we have no background in math which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is THE GOAT. Chill and approachable professor who explains Calculus clearly and knows exactly what students does and doesn't know. He interacts with the class and makes math feel easy. Quizzes and finals match what he teaches, and discussions prepare you well. Lectures are podcasted, so you won't miss content if you can't attend.

He is honestly one of the best math professors at UCSD. He teaches the concept so clearly. The workload for homework isn't bad, however, his study guides aren't the most useful cus they end up not being that similar to the exam, but you do get a cheat sheet. If you show up to lecture, you should understand the concepts though.
He was awesome and explained things really well. Definitely take him and go to class, great math professor.

Absolutely loved this class. I went to Professor Ho's office hours every week and he is so sweet and helpful. Lectures are podcasted and optional, but definitely go to them so he doesn't have to talk to an empty hall :(. Midterms are fair and reflective of examples from lecture/homework. Worst part of the class was the mandatory discussions...

Midterms and homework were very easy, but be prepared for the final, which is worth 50% of the grade. Study guides won't prepare you for that and neither will the homework, so make sure you know every detail of everything gone over in the course, and stuff not even gone over.

Extremely easy class, you get a cheat sheet for exams. Just put the notes on there, and you'll struggle to do poorly. Exam questions are really similar to the lectures, so either attend them or watch the posted videos. The worst part of class is that you have to go to 6/9 discussion sections.
midterms and homework was easy, but the Final exam, which is a huge portion of your grade, is very difficult, even if you practice the homework, the lecture and the textbook.

The sweetest prof ever! Content isnt easy but he explains it in an easy way to understand. He lectures clearly + goes thru similar problems as HW and exams. Can have a cheat sheet for exams. HW + discussion worksheets are more difficult than exam problems, so if you understand those you're good for the exam. Records lectures + frequent office hours

He explains the material well and his lectures are very to the point and doesn't focus on proofs much. Everything is recorded, and with the exception of some angles of the blackboard not being captured, it's very easy to make up missed lectures. Cheat sheets and practice exams are generous, with basically everything on the exams similar to HW.

Very chilled professor. His class note is very clear. The exam is basically based on past exams. His lecture's attendance is not mandatory, but discussion is. Very chilled professor. His class note is very clear. The exam is basically based on past exams. His lecture's attendance is not mandatory, but discussion is.

very responsive prof, lectures not mandatory but go since podcast can be off sometimes. good lecturer and honestly one of the better math profs. midterms and final are very fair and like practice exams he posts. hw can be tricky sometimes but not bad, discussions are mandatory but not helpful. not a lot of curve though but would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
The best math class! 
Lectures are not mandatory, but discussion attendance is required (you can miss up to three sessions). All of the practice exams are the same difficulty as the actual exams. Personally, I did not need to study much. You are also allowed a cheat sheet. The professor is great and explains things well. An A is very achievable.
The king of Calculus! I am willing to switch to math major if he can teach all my math classes ;)

It is unfortunate for all econ major students that we have to take this class before we can take the major upper-division level courses. But the fortunate part is that if Ching Wei Ho is your professor, you can still manage to get the whole class through with an A! He cares for his students and is always responsive to email. He is a goat!
A true GOAT.
great class

Professor Ho is the best Calc professor. Goated! Very passionate about teaching, the lectures were easy to understand, and approachable after class. Btw, although lectures are not mandatory and there's recordings, the quality is quite poor. I recommend to just attend the lectures, and that Discussion session is mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are super helpful. Go to as many lectures as you can.
THE GOAT OF CALC PROFESSORS
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The best math prof I've had at UCSD, he legitimately teaches the material posts, study guides, the discussions are truly helpful. (I would've gotten an A if I had shown up to the threshold amount of discussions), really great lecturer and helps guide you on what is going to be on the test and how to answer those problems.
One of my favorite professors of all time, easy to follow grading criteria is clear, plus cheat sheats for all test - take him if you want to understand the fundamentals and excel

I could have tried harder but it was tough waking up for lecture. I ended up just studying the practice exam before tests. You get a front and back cheat sheet so there's no reason to fail this class. Not only should you write down all of the practice exam questions but also HW questions that were not on the practice exam as they will show up

Prepared us very well for the exams. If you study the practice exams and homework, the midterms and final should be light. Gives lots of examples in class and is very clear in his lectures. Very nice and definetely recommend!
Great math professor! His lectures are really clear and he uses examples that are very applicable to the midterms and finals, really cares about student needs would take him again!

He is by far my FAV math professor I've ever taken. I love that he writes all his notes on the chalk-board, and he is really easy to follow. He really takes the time to explain things and always demonstrates concepts (intersection of planes, vectors, etc.) with the markers he brings and you can tell he cares that you understand these things.

the practice exams are the same as the midterms and final. he lets you bring a cheat sheet to each test (front and back). he's super caring and just wants all his students to pass. attendance to lecture is not mandatory but discussions are (7/10), however lecture is recorded and posted. super chill teacher would so recommend
Very good calculus professor. The lectures are helpful for the exams. Homework was kinda hard, but not a lot of it (unlimited attempts). If you try hard throughout, you can easily get an A.

He is a great professor, even if you struggle with math. He was pretty clear in his lectures, and gave PLENTY of examples. Homework is online and is harder than the concepts in lecture/exams. The exams are very fair to what was taught. Overall, a nice guy as well!
Very enthusiastic lecturer, but sometimes wasn't very clear.
Very enthusiastic, but sometimes wasn't the most clear

He does not record lectures or release lecture notes!!! Other than that, he's my goat. Amazing in office hours and really seems to enjoy lecturing. I was actually a little interested in math which never happens.

Has a slight accent but besides that the Lectures were great. The Homework was 1000x harder to do than any test problems he gave. The tests were a good difficulty, if you studied a fair amount, you will do well. The homework is really hard, but you have unlimited tries so you can get it done.

My biggest regret is taking this class Pass/Fail—if I took it for a grade, I'd have gotten an A. Don't take it Pass/Fail—he's GOATED! I had never done calculus before, but he made it so simple. Lectures aren't recorded to encourage collaboration. Just read the book, go to lectures, and do the problems—you'll do great!
this professor is goated

Great 20A Prof—uses helpful examples that appear on tests. Writes fast on chalk board so hard to keep up at times. HW on Achieve (paid) is tough. Tests are hard with no curve, but the second grading scheme helped. Office hours are highly recommended; he explains well, helps with HW, and is great to talk to. Wish he taught more 20 series courses!

Professor does have an accent but he tries his best and honestly worked out for me. Lectures are good and gives a lot of examples in class. Discussions are mandatory and discussion worksheets and homework are a little difficult but the midterm and final questions are a lot easier than discussion and homework.

A really great professor! He explains things clearly and the examples he gives in class are pretty much the same as the exam questions. Attendance isn't required but id recommend going as much as possible as there isn't any podcasts. The homework is lowkey hard but the midterms are not nearly as difficult. I'd definitely recommend taking him

Great math professor. Yes he is heavily accented but is great at explaining things. Attendance is not mandatory but it is necessary to go to lectures because it is not podcasted and notes are not uploaded on canvas. I don't think there is a curve for grades but tests are easy and homework questions has unlimited attempts.

Good math20a professor
Pros: 
Shows very similar problems that the ones coming on the exam during review sessions
Gives 2 grading schemes and uses the one that benefits the student the most
Will likely curve the class's grade
Explains concepts clearly
Cons:
Homework is way too hard (harder than what you'll see on exams) 
Accent (not to strong tho)

Great math professor especially compared to other 20A professors. He has a bit of an accent but not too bad. Used a lot of examples for lectures that translate to tests. Not the greatest at answering questions. Homework was insanely difficult some weeks but still doable. Uses two grading schemes and takes the higher of the two to help your grade.

This was one of the easier math classes I've taken. I could've done better if I actually went to class, but I learned what I could online and from openstax. Set time apart to learn it, he's a good lecturer, few hws but 15% of the grade. Few quizzes that were actual problems instead of conceptual questions, usually only 4 Q's per quiz, but 13%.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She teaches well and drops your lowest test. Just study a lot and use the resources and it'll be fine (lots of content)

Dr. Maita is amazing! She bases her lectures on transparent learning outcomes that are used for exam questions. Provides tons of resources to practice material (discussion, prac exams). She tries her best to support her students and does a great job! Though tests were hard, she had a generous 1 dropped midterm out of three policy. Choose Dr. Maita!
Good professor, but difficult class.
So much material and exams are hard. 1/2 free response 1/2 MCQ. Avgs were about 71% Nice professor but save your GPA and take someone else.

The professor is nice and energetic. However, the cumulative final was overwhelming, worth 250 points, with a short amount of time to study all 17 lectures. Rushed topics ended up being heavily tested on the final. There was no FINAL clear study guide/prep resources, and extra credit was 3.5% MAX. Midterms are reasonable with larger gap to study ig
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is nice and very knowledgeable, but whether her class works for you depends a lot on your learning style. Her lectures are long and cover big amount of complex material. Just know that a lot of what's covered in lecture doesn't show up heavily on exams, focus on having a solid conceptual grasp of the topics rather than memorizing every detail.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought she was okay. She seemed nice and sometimes brought candy to lecture. But sometimes the lectures were a bit disorganized for me, and she would teach some things slowly, so she would skip things or teach really fast right before exams

She is VERY organized. The class is difficult, but just make sure you can answer the learning objectives. The 3 midterms were mostly short responses & some MCQs. challenging but were fair. The final was all MCQ. she gives lots of EC, MAKE SURE TO DO IT. Very clear lectures. Attendance wasn't mandatory. LOVED HER

You can tell she cares deeply for this topic. Her lecture style is very calm and easy to follow. Tests covered a lot of material, so study early! Final was tough bc the mc questions were cumulative so try to memorize pathways the most! Lots of extra credit opps.

The best prof I've had at UCSD!! She genuinely cares about her students and is accessible + approachable. Every learning outcome is clearly described in the syllabus and she always communicates her expectations. Also gives credit for unfair questions and is generally very fair when it comes to grading

Amazing professor.Lecture is very interactive and you actually learn-LOTS of material covered tho. Exams are not super close to lecture material and they are hard-MC and Free response.3 MTs and a MC final w/ weekly PS.Very kind and really cares.learned more from this professor than 2 other classes covering biological systems.Taking again for a Lab!

She was great! Lectures were super comprehensive, covering everything you need to know for the tests with examples, checkpoints, and diagrams. Look at the learning objectives on her syllabus, know her slides and you will do great. Plus, she offers tons of extra credit. Great prof, makes a hard class better

Professor Maita is the best!!! She genuinely cares about her students' success and constantly gives exam points back if she sees an unfair question. BIPN 100 is a dense class but her lectures are super organized.

Prof Maita is one of the best professors I have taken. She constantly updates her syllabus to reflect what learning outcomes would be covered in each midterm & final.

She offers up to 7% of extra credit, and the lowest grades of the weekly quiz, discussion activity & midterm would be dropped. Highly recommended, especially if you like self-study.

BIPN 100 is difficult material, but Professor Maita covers it very comprehensively and is highly accessible outside of class. Exams are hard but only cover material taught in lecture. Discussion assignments (graded for completion) are representative of the topics students are expected to know, and lectures are very interesting. Highly recommend!

Professor Maita is quite possibly the best professor I have had so far. Human Physio is already a very complex subject, but she knows this, so she helps her students understand the materials really well. No curve but she hands out extra credit. I appreciate her not cramming too much on her students and her super helpful office hours. Go to them!!

BIPN overall is a material heavy course however Prof. M was very accessible outside of class and as well she gives a generous amount of extra credit. there are 3 midterms, weakly quizzes, discussion assignments  with the lowest being dropped in each. lectures can be rushed though. however she gives many tips in how to study effectively.

I really love professor Maita. She is so kind and caring and really makes a huge effect to help her students and make class as clear and organized as possible. She is an amazing teacher and is super knowledgable. She is also really understanding and compassionate. LOVE HER!!!!

BIPN 145 is difficult and Professor Maita pushes her students thoroughly, but she's a very comprehensive, helpful, and inspiring instructor. Exams were tough but only tested lecture/lab material. Heavy focus on well-researched and well-written lab reports. Final project was pretty fun! My only gripe was small rubric ambiguities on some assignments.
Amazing professor! BIPN 100 is a difficult class so do not be discouraged.

Nice teacher but goes out of her way to take points away from assignments that she only gave vague instructions on. Midterms are fully based on lecture material and anything goes. Way bigger time commitment than it seems just to get a mediocre grade.

Took BIPN100 during her first quarter at UCSD, I was a nervous freshman & worried about her lack of teaching experience. Maita is a kind and funny person, and an upstanding professor. Her slides' immaculate organization helped everything connect logically in my mind. Go to lecture and study, and it's a clear path to success, even for a freshman :)

I am so impressed by her; she answers all questions quickly and succinctly. She's very organized and always on top of her game. The nature of this course is incredibly difficult so I do not blame her for anyone struggling in her class. She gives a lot of extra credit opportunities.

Lectures are not mandatory, DI sections aren't mandatory but you get to work on the assignments together. Online weekly quizzes (have a short time span, so difficult). Exams are application based and much harder than most profs offered. If possible, take it with another prof. She offers extra credit, and grades are curved but not as much as others.

GOAT professor. Her class is very well-structured and organized. I believe that she lays out what is needed to know very clearly, and her exams are not that bad as long as you put in the time and effort to study. She also offers tons of extra credit. This was my second time taking it, and she was so much better than a different professor I had.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The only homework you get are weekly quizzes that are pretty easy as long as you watched the lectures and read the questions carefully. The midterms and final are straightforward and all about what she talks about in class. Some people did struggle in the class though, but I think it mostly has to do with different foundations in biology.
I thought Maita was a decent professor, but definitely has room to grow. I struggled a lot in this class and feel as though I was never entirely sure how to approach the material.

Prof M is an amazing professor!! Definitely one of the best I've taken, she is very approachable and nice! I recommend going to office hours if you are ever struggling as they are super helpful and I probably would've done super bad if I hadn't gone since there is a lot of content to memorize

Physiology needs more drawing based diagrams for retention otherwise it becomes abstract and very difficult specially since there is so much. She is so wonderful, but her slides have room for improvement. It was her 2nd quarter. I am sure she will become a great professor specially because she cares so much. Exams are ok, but material is a lot.

A good lecturer and gave clear learning outcomes in lectures and assignments. Her exams: long but fair. Would've preferred normal homework instead of discussion assignments that were due same day. Quizzes were on canvas, given 10 minutes for 5 questions. Would have preferred 15 minutes. Overall engaging but some changes could be made to her course.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor M is very approachable. Go to OH. She understands physiology is a hard course, but she accurately tells you in the syllabus and in every lecture what the learning outcome goals. Lecture is not mandatory but if you fall behind, you're in for a long quarter. Every lecture is ~80 slides. Discussion is not mandatory. Gives 4% EC. No curve.

She is a nice professor but not good at teaching. She talks so fast during lectures that it is impossible to follow. I end up having to rewatch the podcast even then I still have trouble comprehending what is going on in her class.  This class is very lecture and test heavy. One bad test grade can heavily decrease your final grade. DO NOT TAKE!!

I took this class for a GE this quarter, and this class was specifically for non-bio majors. Class average for 3 midterms was a D with no curve, no study guide, and the tests are not open notes with 60 questions each. If you do poorly on the midterms, it'll be hard for you to pass. I would not recommend taking her unless you want to be stressed.

Discussion Assignment (DA) is annoying. Really long with many parts, basically impossible to do independently in an hour. Graded based on completion, eg there's 20 questions and you answer 19 and miss one, you still get zero for that assignment (each DA is 1% of your grade). 7 weekly quizzes (21%) , 2 midterms (20% each), 1 final (30%), 10 DA (9%).

She is very nice & approachable and her lectures are interesting. Exams were 1.5hrs, 70 questions & 20 are short answer responses, average was around a D w/ no curve. No study guide or practice exams. 1 hw assignment a week that is available same day its due, graded based on completion but didn't give out answer keys till later in the quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is extremely approachable and kind, so don't hesitate to reach out and ask for help. That being said, the class is difficult so you will need to put a bunch of time and effort into this class. Her tests, for the most part, are very straightforward, and as long as you understand what she is saying in the lectures, you will do good.

I honestly have nothing but the highest praises for Professor Budin. Lecture heavy, but it is podcasted and he in ultra clear and direct. He explained thing and made the whole course digestible. He should be teaching all of the 114 series I highly recommend him to anyone needing the class.
One of the best professors so far. Very organized and gives interesting lectures. There are 3 non-cumulative midterms, and he provides practice exams that are very similar to the actual ones.

Grade based on 2 midterms, a final (a 3rd midterm) non cumulative, and weekly problem sets (discussion went over most of the questions). No mandatory attendance. 2 office hour sessions, 1 where he goes through problems and helps with extra explanations (which he records), the other is more general. practice tests like exams. would recommend again!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Budin explains concepts in a way that is intuitive. This class has a lot of material, but his lectures made it seem manageable, memorable, and interesting. He is also a very kind professor, respectful and encouraging to his students. 

Take 114B with Budin!

Amazing professor. Focuses on the mechanistic view of biochemistry, and I personally love it. Explains everything in a very easy-to-digest manner, and exams are extremely fair. Final was third midterm. Would recommend and take again.

Easily one of the best profs at UCSD. The way he taught mechanisms makes them actually understandable compared to Ochem. Exams are super fair based on lectures and homework, and he's super willing to work with students. His lectures are informative but also super interesting, and easy to take notes with. He has 5 stars for a reason!!!

Budin is an all around great prof. Lectures are straightforward, he's really caring about his students, and clearly loves the subjects he teaches. I cannot find anything bad to say about him. 10/10 would learn about the citric acid cycle again

I was very hesitant to take this class as I previously had dropped it with a different processor due to the difficulty, however with Professor Budin he explains it in such simple terms and analogy it makes it easier to understand. I struggle a lot with Biochem since it is such a topic that requires a lot of memorization but was able to get an A!

Professor Budin is a nice guy. He's passionate about what he's teaching and explains it in an easy/straightforward manner. The class is heavy on mechanisms so you will have to study but the practice exams/lectures do reflect the midterms/finals. Always willing to answer your questions and is probably one of the best profs I've had in my 3 yrs here!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best chemistry professor in the world. Not only are lectures really clear and easy to understand, the lectures are really interesting as well. Super helpful and friendly in office hours twice a week and exams are very reflective of lecture material. I wish he would teach more classes, I would take every class with him if I could.

Literally a blessing to the chemistry department LOL. After taking 114B with him and seeing my 114C professor it makes me regret taking his class for granted. I genuinely don't think you can find a better biochemistry teacher better than him and you MUST take him. So straight foward and easy to understand. Appreciate it while you can lolol
11/10 prof. lectures were pure kino, conveyed information clearly and efficiently, tests were fair, hw was useful.

Professor Budin was a fantastic chemistry professor that I would absolutely have for another class again. His lectures are very straight forward and unlike other professors trying to teach me how to do mechanisms, I actually understood them! Anyone who has the opportunity to take biochemistry. I implore you to take it with Budin!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Budin is a new professor at UCSD & I was a bit reluctant going in blind taking his course, but I do not regret it one bit. He's one of the best STEM professors I have ever had. He's such a kind individual & my favorite part about his lectures is how much he lights up whenever he teaches! Exams are very reasonable & office hours are useful

Literally the best professor ever. He inspired me to continue studying biochemistry. Lectures are super clear and always really interesting. Homework is harder than exams, but exams are reflective of lecture material. Amazing professor.

Budin is an amazing biochem professor. His lectures are super good. As the class was metabolism, he made sure to draw out the mechanisms and explain the concepts really well. I would say the homework was actually harder than the exam. But otherwise, despite it being online, his exams were reasonable. Totally recommend him!

Professor Budin is easily one of the best professors at UCSD (took online). He draws the mechanisms for us during lectures, the problem sets aren't that hard sometimes they can be a little annoying but it wasn't bad. The practice exams were similar to actual exams and the difficulty level was pretty decent. Highly recommend his class

Professor Budin was such an awesome professor. His lectures are very easy to follow along with and made the material very clear. He had 2 midterms and a final but as long as you understand the problem sets, you should be pretty good for the class. He also curves the class generously!!!

Professor Budin is amazing. His lectures were very easy to follow and very easy to take notes on. He explained the material exceptionally well. I can tell he is passionate about teaching. I would highly recommend Professor Budin, he is certainly one of the best professors at UCSD. Professor Budin made Biochem very fun and rewarding.

(Took online) Very clear lectures, he explains the mechanisms very well. Class was graded 25% each for homework, 2 midterms and the final. His practice exams were very representative of the actual exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: By far the best math lectures I have ever attended, but due to the professor being new the class lacked a lot of basic structure and was generally disorganized. The tests are very conceptual so be ready to know everything about concepts not only just how to solve them. If you do take this class, I suggest having some preliminary knowledge.

I found his lectures understandable, he has good explanations but has no podcast so you have to go to class. But for the class that is graded on 60% test, he does not teach for the test! The rubric looks for certain points and key words but he wont mention it at all during lecture. and a bunch of people failed the final, he didn't curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 0 times he actually teaches. 0 times he answered my email. 7 times per lecture he explained the concept in the most confusing way possible.
Ummm this man did not teach whatsoever. We had to fend for ourselves the entire time. Do not recommend!

I thought this was the easy class, but the tests were heavily concept based. Additionally, there were no podcasts, no lecture notes, and he only wrote on the chalk board in lecture. While the other classes final was all multiple choice with a formula sheet, ours was 9 frq style pages with no formula sheet. He's super funny though
um the tests are somehow tough? lectures are unnecessary don't attend but he is extremely funny

ChatGPT practice exams with no answer key, doesn't have a set lesson plan, uses essentially invisible chalk on the already dirty chalkboard, basic level coverage of concepts during lecture, consistently behind homework topics, frequently late, goes on tangents, and seems overall unaware of what he's supposed to be teaching us. Take someone else!

Lectures were very disconnected and concept heavy. Lectures, homework, and tests were all very different from each other. We were provided a practice test before each midterm/final but answer keys were not provided and practice tests were never gone over in class. Lectures were not recorded and done on chalkboard so you're basically cooked.
Never take

He's a nice guy but a very disorganized lecturer. The tests are very conceptual and vague, not at all similar to the homework or what is covered in class. The average grade in the class was a C(2.08), don't take unless you absolutely have to.

He seems like a genuinely good dude but his lectures are kinda all over the place. Show up to class if you want notes. Homework problems nothing like the lectures. Tests are graded very vaguely with problems nothing like the homework. Practice tests were provided, but not solutions. Insane grading scale, below 70% is an F.

Exams are more conceptual and obscure compared to other professors. Practice tests are made using chatGPT and have no answer keys. No formulas or cheatsheet. Lectures, homeworks, and tests, are highly inconsistent between each other. Lectures are not recorded and quite unhelpful for comprehension.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He got no notes and no podcasts. He is just new and doesn't really have experience of teaching.

Exams focus on conceptual things rather than real calculation, so that there aren't exact answers. For example, he asks us to construct a matrix qualifying certain conditions. Practice tests are unhelpful at all since no solutions are given, and he doesn't discuss them in class either. No formula sheet or cheatsheet makes it even harder.

Oh boy where do I start, lectures are so unhelpful as nothing is ever planned, gives chatgpt generated practice exams without answer key, homeworks are nothing like exams and take forever to do, lectures don't help with homeworks so learning is up to you pretty much. Linear algebra is difficult. With Ian it is even more difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not the best class. Didn't learn anything.

Just an endless rant about the flaws of our society. Seriously made the claim that today's America is like Nazi Germany. Niall seems like a nice enough guy, but I couldn't get past his political ideology bias being pushed day after day. Stopped showing up after I couldn't take it anymore. Easy A gradewise, but I would never take this class again.

Class was WAY too political. I rarely showed up to class so that's why my grade wasn't so good. I got a headache every single time I did come to class because it felt like it was just an 80 minute rant about the evilness of conservatives.
Caring and respectful. He is the best teacher at writing department. Take his class, you won't regret.
he's awesome, def woke too. youll feel comfortable in his class. love the way he teached, def smth to look forward to in your day.
Absolutely amazing professor. Every student at UCSD should have to take a class like this.
It's very simple. Even I, a Chinese person who isn't good at English, could get an A. He also doesn't mind if you use translation software.

this class was honestly life-changing. you do need to buy a course reader from the bookstore (around 50 bucks). reading material is fairly easy and we'd discuss readings for the week during class. essays are creative in nature. you can tell that prof. twohig truly cares about the class and his students. one of the best professors at UCSD!

GOATed professor. You get pretty short yet insightful readings and videos, then you discuss them in class. Work otherwise is just a few essays and two weeks of journaling. In-class lectures are always interesting and engaging if you participate, he makes it easy. You do have to buy his course reader and a graphic novel from the bookstore.

Probably one of the most considerate and insightful professors at UCSD. Wasn't expecting much from this class rather than a requirement, but really changed my perspective in a lot of good conversations and 80 minute classes feel very short. You have to talk in class but all conversations are applicable so it's easy to converse! 10/10 recommend.

His class is an easy A and there's a bit of reading few writing assignments. Other than that, this was hands down one of the best and most inspirational classes I've ever taken. I'm glad I took it when I did, I needed this class. He made the class feel like a community and he is such a caring professor. This is a rare gem of a professor.
Professor Twohig has an incredibly immersive teaching style. He structures lectures in a really easy to follow way and the course is very fun. You get to know yourself really well during this course.

Such an easy A. You just have to turn the assignments in on time. You have to participate, and show up, if you don't it's going to bring your grade down. Makes you buy a 'textbook' for 80 bucks and another book that YOU SHOULD BUY ON AMAZON for 10 bucks. oh, also he doesn't give you your grade until the last day of school. And you have grade paths

Niall is one of the most genuine humans you will meet. Niall creates an environment for learning, reflection, and understanding of our place in this world. Niall confronts real problems in our society through academia, he is passionate and caring about these subjects. I adore Niall and his class. Don't think about a grade. It's bigger than that.
THE BEST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD.

Not your usual writing class, in a good way. No specific assignments are graded, final grade reflects your cumulative work and effort. Readings are genuinely interesting and relevant. Writing assignments are designed for students to reflect upon how their personal thoughts and life experiences relate to the themes taught in class + readings.

Niall's way of teaching is very eye opening and leads into more topics than sitting around in lecture and listening to boring things about a paper that's due, or things related to what you're "supposed" to write about. If you're seeking for a different experience other than just writing for an assignment, I would heavily recommend the course.

I have never care enough to rate any professor in my life but Niall Probably one of my favorite professor ever. .He really cares about the material he taught and he always to leave the students better when he found them. If you are hesitate to take his class, my advice is go for it. Come in class with an open mind and you're in for a treat.

Amazing professor period, I think he is one the best professor I have had until now at UCSD. I have always hated writing until I took this class, You will enjoy writing with him! Would definitely take more classes with him if I have the chance.
One of the best professors on campus
One of the best classes I've ever taken period.
You have lots of materials to read and watch like any other English course. He is very caring and helpful. His lecture is more than just a grading.

Easily one of my favorite professors I had taken so far! Most caring and inspiring professor as he provides interesting lectures that get you to thinking about the material. A lot of reading is involved, but its required in order to help you understand the things he teaches on a deeper level. I wish I can take him again if he offered other courses!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I'm in this class right now and believe me when I say Professor Twohig is one of the most caring professors. He is actively available to help his students, uses his own personal experiences to guide us along the way, and always has a smile on his face. I just wish I could take more classes with him because I'll greatly miss this class.

Best professor! Teaches you to open your eyes to the world rather than the narrow structure defined by society. There's a lot of reading, but they are enlightening to read. Niall is always there to support you and give you constructive criticism that allows you to truly thrive in the class. Definitely recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Niall is probably one of the best professors in UCSD. He is caring and respectful. He always gives lengthy feedbacks on papers to make sure that you understand where and how to improve your writing. I highly recommend him because he is not just another writing professor, he cares about hearing your voice as a writer, and he values your input.
best teacher

niall is a really nice instructor and will really help you write good essays. he posts his lecture slides (for reference but attendance is mandatory) and u can tell he puts time into the slides to make things clearer. the course was bleh but the niall was cool
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very good and caring professor. Mandatory attendance for lectures but they were canvas questions that she goes over in lecture. Your experience in lab is fully based on your TA but a very chill and enjoyable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, lots of extra credit opportunities. Lectures/labs are mandatory, and are worth quite a lot of your grade so you do have to stay on top of your work.

The professor was nice, but your grade depends more on the TA you get. There's one lecture and one lab a week. The lectures are boring and not that helpful. The lab notebook entries are due the night of the lab, which is pretty much busywork. Doable prelabs/quizzes. The class is easy and definitely doable, just heavy on the busywork.

Kinda a bit of work for 2 units, labs are a drag sometimes, but most things as long as you do it, you will get an A. Writing works are kinda sad, lecture is mandatory with points (I took virtual for lecture, in person for lab). The lectures are kinda an information dump, but you can lowk go into lab with 0 previous knowledge. Overall, better BILD4.

The professor is sweet and very understanding but the lectures weren't that helpful. Grades are mostly dependent on the content learned from what's done in lab. If you get a good TA and lab partners, like I did, the class is not hard at all. As long as you go to lab and keep up with the assignments, you will do fine. :)

Class was easy but professor didnt teach much. You have to sign up to go to her office hours which is a 15 minute slot on Calendy and filled up really fast and I had to wait months to see her even for a mandatory accommodations meeting because she didnt respond to my email. My TA was amazing though, shout out to Mikkey, definitely reccommend.

The TA will make or break your experience (and grade) for the class. The Professor herself is very nice and has office hours that you can schedule to talk with her. There is 3 quizzes and 4 writing assignments and the writing assignments definitely take at least 2-3 hours. Can miss up to 2 lectures. Final is a group research poster presentation.

Professor Gamboa is so sweet and cares a lot about her students. She makes sure to clearly go over all of the conceptual material necessary to understand the lab for the week. My IA was Mikkey Compuesto and she was AWESOME. She made the lab setting feel less scary than it seemed and was very patient with everyone learning lab ettiquette.

Professor Ivonne González-Gamboa is an excellent instructor who genuinely cares about her students and their success. Her lectures for BILD 4 are engaging, well-structured, and focus on helping students understand the material rather than just memorizing it.
Gamboa lays out instructions and purpose of the lab at the start of the week so it should be an easy class. Lab is very fun if you get the right people. Would recommend this class!

Easy class that taught me a lot of introductory laboratory skills. Professor is kind and empathetic. Pick a good lab bench partner on the first day of class since that is who you will be working with the entire quarter. The class grade is based on the TA since they are the ones running the labs.

Not much to say but that she's great! her class is super easy, the final is a simple presentation and her quizzes are nothing you aren't taught! lab grades are based off TA mostly but she picks good ones, the rubric is always clear

BILD 4 was pretty easy, most of the grade consists of lab practicals and quizzes but they arent too bad. The final was just a presentation on a bio project with your lab group. The lectures were nice but only a couple of them actually mattered to the lab content. My TA was very caring and understanding so it was easy. Definitely recommend

I had her online & she was so sweet and caring, even though she had a whole in-person lecture to manage! There's a few writing assignments but grading (which was by the TA) wasn't harsh at all and there's a rlly simple end of the year project that you'll be given time to work on during lab. If she has no fans I'm dead.

A lot of this is class is group work but it was very fun. Prof is rly nice and has great lectures. I took the lectures on zoom but she would be teaching students in person too. Lectures are mandatory and done through a Question she gives in lecture and you answer on canvas. You mainly interact with your TA more than the prof since they teach lab.
Professor was great and really cared about her students!

the professor was nice and funny. the lab experience depends on your lab group and TA (mine was great). the content wasn't hard and the grading was pretty lenient. the only thing I didn't like were the lab notebook questions because they were tedious and annoying to do.

Professor Ivonne was a very, very kind professor and cared for all her students. There were quite a few assignments to complete but they weren't bad at all and it was very easy to get an A+. Make sure to have a good lab group since you will be with them in labs and completing lab assignments all quarter. I would definitely take her again!

Dr. Ivonne was amazing and went out of her way to provide students with opportunities to further their bio knowledge outside the classroom. Class has a lot of assignments inside and outside of the lab, so make sure to have a good lab group. Attendance is required for everything which was a little inconvenient since my lecture was so late.

The Professor is very chill. Also, the class is very easy to pass with an A but you must have a good group since you will be working with them for the entire quarter. During the week you will have to complete a lab notebook which is in every lab, quiz or a writing lab assignment. This class does not have much homework so take it if you want an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super likeable professor, relatively easy class (i took during SS1). If you have a good group the class is pretty simple and straight forward.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: BILD4 lab was easy and Gonzalez was accessible outside of class.Very caring professor and wants her students to succeed. Highly recommend taking her. Weekly lab notebook, this course required a lot of group work, so pick a good lab bench

She was invested in our success outside of class as well as in. Even with a late lecture time, she was energetic and helped make sure everyone had clear expectations for the course/next lab assignments. She used her own research experience and guest lecturers to help us see how the topics were used outside the class. I would gladly take her again!

I recommend taking BIPN 108 if you have a genuine interest in exercise physiology. Exams are not hard, study the learning objectives you will be fine. Prof. Randy is very enthusiastic about the course, listen to his lectures again when preparing for the exams. OH are not that helpful, use the internet if you are confused on topics taught.

He incorporates his own experiences and interacts with students. Clicker questions will show up on exams sometimes and I think the way he teaches is straightforward, just lots of stuff to remember. He's funny but does go off topic. I still enjoyed the class. Not my best work, but he's understanding of life circumstances.

He is truly a great and welcoming person and delves into his own background as a marathon runner. However, his tests were very long and wording sometimes were difficult to understand to get the right answer. I wish he spent more time on the many bullet points he expects us to remember from each lecture!

truly favorite prof at ucsd, very welcoming. ur grade is based on attendance, weekly online quizzes (easy and 2 chances), 2 midterms, 1 final, so its easier to get a better grade. he makes his lectures really fun and he gives extra credit for SETs completion. hands down best prof

He's very much a "hello fellow kids" type of professor, which I'm sure many find refreshing, but personally I found it to be slightly too much. He's got great intentions, and when he's actually lecturing professionally, I am very intrigued. I wish he were more professional and lecture-focused instead of rambling on and on. And there's no syllabus.

Love him as a person, amazing personality and funny character. Would not recommend taking his class if you like structure. His slides are disorganized and he constantly drifts off topic during lecture making it hard to focus on the material. Ended up having to mainly learn everything on my own or from TA review videos for difficult exams.

Randy is a goofy guy, and though his lectures are funny, his slides are disorganized. It's not always easy to tell what we need to learn from class alone, so I strongly recommend going to discussion! I had a great IA luckily. Exams are tough, but the entire instructional team really does try to explain ideas. He truly cares to teach you though.

LOVE LOVE LOVE RANDY!!!!! The tests are hard butttt everything on the tests are on his study list and he will only test you on what is on this list! He has so many resources and is very easily accessible. Yes, lectures are mandatory but you get to miss about 6 and going to lectures help! You have weekly quizzes but they're basically free points.

Randy is very funny and a cool guy. His lectures are very entertaining, but not organized or clear. His tests are brutal and make up most of your grade. You need to know an insane level of detail to decipher his tricky wording, the grading is tough, and the tests are too long. Lectures mandatory with clickers, weekly readings he writes himself.

Randy is great. Very funny and down to earth. Tests are very representative of the lectures (but still rlly hard). He's very accommodating and understanding. We don't use the textbook, but rather he writes his own reading for us and they're pretty funny and very casual.

Professor Hampton makes biochem lectures engaging and enjoyable. Exams are challenging, but his study resources like homemade readings and extra credit opportunities are super helpful. unstuckstudy was a game-changer for my review prep - definitely give it a try!

Great guy, difficult class but biochem will always be. Exams however are very representative of lectures and the readings (he wrote them himself) are very helpful in understanding the material. Offered extra credit as well and very responsive outside of lecture

Randy is a really fun and energetic professor! He makes learning super enjoyable with his jokes and throwable mic. Quizzes are easy and he provides 20-40/1000 points EC for 85-95% SET rate. The only downside to the class is that it requires intense memorization and little partial credit given on exams.

There is absolutely nothing bad to say about Randy. His lectures are funny, and he is very engaging. Weekly two chance Canvas quizzes, two online midterms and an online final (all open note). Made learning about exercise super interesting and made me excited to come to class. 100/10 loved him!!!!!

The class material was super interesting and I put so much time in completing the recommended study lists  and taking detailed notes. I never found the material to be too challenging but when it came to the open-note exams I found them impossibly hard and unfair. Hampton words his questions really strange and the length of his exams are exhausting

He's so funny for one. He makes it seem like his exams are straightforward and there's no trickery, but the wording sometimes confuses the shit out of students, even on the concepts you know. 
That's the not so cool part.

BEST. PROFESSOR. EVER. 
AMAZING. 
On every level!!!

I felt it was impossible to succeed in this class even under the professors recommendation of completing the terms and study list. This did not prepare me for the midterm or final. To study break apart the pathways and categorize whats part of them. His questions are also based on differences and commonalities between pathways. Flash cards.

I won't lie, Hampton makes you work for your grade and this class is very lecture-heavy. But, he truly does care about his students. My piece of advice if you do choose to take this class is to focus on the little details and enjoy his lectures. He's a funny guy so that's a plus but the exams are pretty tough.

Taking this class with such an enthusiastic professor made the material so much more bearable. Hampton definitely did a great job in getting his students engaged in learning biochem, and offered a lot of study resources for exams as well. My only gripes were that his slides were pretty bare and he would sometimes go through concepts too quickly.

Randy is one of the most engaging lecturers I've had. Read all the assigned material. Take copious notes (that are searchable) as the exams are open note. Include notes on items that are not explicitly stated in the terms list. Be able to write the pathways and know the gist of what is happening in each one. Include pictures of pathways in notes.

Have never been more furious with a professor. I like him as a person & lecturer, but his slides are horrendous and the final we just took is prob the reason Im gonna have to graduate late I studied for 3 weeks straight and took an obscene amount of notes but apparently thats not enough? Oh and hell make it seem like hes going EASY on us too..

The way the material is presented is absolutely atrocious. He will show a metabolic pathway all zoomed out, comment on a few steps of that pathway, and move on like I'm not sitting here with my piehole gaped. He curves well, but what's the point in taking a tough professor even if he curves well? Tests were pretty difficult as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Engaging lectures, luckily he records them to rewatch - which really helps.

Professor Hampton cares about his students well being. The curve is generous. I loved taking BIPN 108 and felt inspired by Professor Hampton. 100% recommend. I honestly don't understand why anyone would give this professor a bad rating.

Whenever I asked a question, he was very condescending and rude about the questions and often would just ignore them to go off on tangents about bookstores/athletes he admired. His teaching style is bad, he only provides graphs and then talks about them while always going off on tangents about non-class info and wasting class time.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very surprised by some of the reviews on here. This guy is one of the best upper div bio professors at UCSD. I took him for BIBC 102 and am now taking BIPN 108 with him. If you have the opportunity, TAKE HIM. He makes coming to class actually fun, he's very sporadic which always makes you stay awake.

I def agree he can get a bit passive aggressive esp when too many students ask questions. But I thought his tests were fair (but hard) and had enough other work (DI sessions & quizzes/review) for class to be less stressful. Best thing about him is his lectures; interesting, incorporates material from outside the class, etc. Curves generously :)

Hes kinda a jerk tbh. VERY unapproachable. Whenever I would ask him questions he would be very passive aggressive and respond with an attitude which made me feel severely uncomfortable asking questions at all. His exam questions are worded very weirdly too which made it confusing at times, hes often pulling trickery in his questions with one word.

He is generally excited to be teaching, however I didn't enjoy his presentation of the material. Metabolic pathways were presented by powerpoint. We would often get an image of the pathway and he would spend merely seconds on the slide, though we were meant to memorize all aspects of the pathway. Most of the material was not covered by the reading
Hes kind of passive aggressive and it made me pretty uncomfortable. I tried talking to him during OH a few times and I just felt like he was constantly annoyed

Prof Hampton I a good professor. I took him for BIBC 102 and don't get me wrong it is not an easy class. The midterm and the final are all short answer and a small bit of T/F. They are not easy, however, he posts study topics you should know every week that will guide you fairly well. I really recommend staying caught up b/c things build up quick!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Prof Hampton is probably the best professor I've had at UCSD. Take him if you want a great lecturer! This class is very overwhelming but there's podcasts! His practice tests are very similar to the real ones. His tests are a lot simpler put than what he goes over in class so as long as you know the basics for all the processes you should be ok.

Prof. Hampton is great, but I found the way he taught Metabolic to be overwhelming. He would teach so much material, and you had to know all of it, and most of it would require memorizing full mechanisms that could be only partially referenced in his extremely difficult free-response tests where studying required heavy brute memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For teaching nutrition the first time, he did a decent job. Midterm was kinda hard side and too long with FRQs, but final is pretty straightforward with MC. Quizcussions are tedious and kinda useless, but fun to engage. His wording could be clearer, the terms list and study guide suffice to do well. Also curves quite generously. Pretty funny too.

Professor Hampton is a a good lecturer, his sense of humor keeps you engaged with the lecture. His only issue is that the test doesnt reflect what he teaches in class. Also, he asks very generic questions with confusing wording and he looks for a very specific answer.
Incredible professor. Slightly disorganized but always caters to student needs. Loves his job, is passionate and has a great attitude towards life.

He is a real gem! I didn't have much time to study for his midterm/final but still did well because his midterm was very fair yet his final was very hard (but he curved well). He is FUNNY and his caring/relaxing demeanor made me positive and less stressed. He is one of the most caring profs ever. Podcast and you'll do well.

I never have written a course review, but Randy Hampton deserves it! His passion and wit exude in his lectures, making them easy to pay attention to. His tests are clear and he explains exactly what is expected of you. Don't get me wrong Metabolic is not an easy course, but take it with him and you enjoy it, and will learn incredible things!
Really really hard for BIBC 102

Professor Hampton is a very talented lecturer who keeps engaged throughout his lectures. He provides clear slides, study plans and all available prior exams for better preparation for the exams. His questions are at times not straightforward and you really need to have a clear grasp of the concepts to get an A. He allows regrades of his exams.

He is obviously passionate about the topic and cares about his students. Maybe in a few years will have the class figured out. I do not recommend taking this class as an "easy A." His class is hard to follow and the exams were not a true reflection of the amount I studied or learned. The way that he words the questions is extremely confusing.

This class is my favorite class that I've taken at UCSD! The class itself is interesting and not too difficult (not an easy A tho, imo). Randy is hilarious. Overall, a decent lecturer, he can go off on tangents sometimes but it's entertaining. 2 midterms and the final (MC). He does curve. Take him if you can!

He's hands down one of the most entertaining professors I've had. Tests are pretty straightforward. The only down-side would be the organization of the slides. There aren't any good transitions between topics, which makes it hard to take notes that flow well.

The tests were very unclear. He ended up changing the answers for many questions each test because they were poorly worded. Just know that you could listening to lectures and study perfectly and still get questions wrong. There were so many questions that he said were wrong even though it was different in his slides. Overall very unprofessional!!!

Took Dr. Hampton's BIBC 102 class (which was great), so I decided to take BIPN 108 with him too. Was not disappointed! Every lecture is engaging and memorable, and covers interesting, applicable material. Even better, exams aren't difficult if you attend lecture and look at his study list. All in all, if you need an elective, take this class!

Professor Hampton is hands-down the funniest lecturer at UCSD. His lectures are super engaging and he integrates clinical applications into his metabolic lectures. He provides a LOT of practice/study material and is very clear about what you need to know for exams. I would HIGHLY recommend his class.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, very organized study materials,
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: Randy is hands down the BEST professor I've had at UCSD. He's so passionate about teaching and his lectures always kept me awake because he's so funny. The class, although requiring a lot of memorization, isn't too hard. He has a clear study list and if you know what's on that, you'll ace the exams.14/10 I am taking another class with him next qtr!

Had Randy for metabolic too and can say he is arguably the best professor on campus. Very clear grading criteria, provides a study list for exams that he takes questions right out of, and pretty funny during lecture/office hours. If you're lucky enough to have the opportunity to take a class with him, do it!

An amazing and funny professor who's really passionate about what he teaches and how he teaches. May go off on tangents every now and again but mostly in the interest of providing more material context or to make the lecture more interesting. Is more than willing to discuss and explain during Office Hours and is overall a great lecturer.

You need the read the lecture notes. Memorizing pathways and being able to regurgitate them is necessary as well, but the exams are very very fair. Each question is worth very little so it allows for more mistakes, BUT the exams are also very long. He also has a very generous curve.. I believe it was around 90% for a solid A. NO TEXTBOOK NEEDEDYAY

His lectures are not enough to know whats happening in the class. Go to multiple discussions to keep track of the material he wants you to know. His tests are super fair and similar to the practice tests.

Randy is an amazing professor! His lectures are very enjoyable due to his almost constant jokes (which can get a little distracting). I would say the only issue is that he can go through the material very quickly, so it can be hard to follow in lecture. Make sure to work outside of lecture to stay caught up!

Hampton is one of the best bio professors that you will ever have at UCSD. I learned so much and became genuinely interested in the subject, all thanks to Hampton. The course does involve a LOT of memorization. I personally feel like his exams (especially the final) were harder than the old exams. Get a TA who took the class with Hampton.

Ok, Randy is an amazing person but is overrated as a prof. First, he's absolutely hilarious! He also podcasts, has many old exams, and puts up slides - which are good. The down side is that he talks VERY FAST, hard to follow, and his slides are really unorganized. His exams are also long, and you must memorize lectures AND old exams.

Very funny prof! Don't just memorize his past finals/midterms (although 1 or 2 questions repeat), he will throw on new questions. i found myself falling asleep a lot but as long as you keep up with his study list and study guides, your good to go. Clickers were a part of the grade (not EC) but you get credit even if your wrong. Have fun :)

Dr. Hampton is such a sweet, understanding, and funny professor! His class is great! It is pretty tough (as any biochem class should be), but Dr. Hampton provides you with all of the materials you need to succeed. Take advantage of his study lists, terms, and old exams and you should do well!

PROS: posts a study list, clickers are extra credit, and recycles material from old exams CONS: he gets off topic a lot, his slides are not very helpful, and when he says "recognize" he really means memorize (you need to memorize something to recognize it since most of the molecules look similar) He was okay - straightforward A if you work hard

Fun fact: Dr. Hampton used to be a comedian. Thus, his lectures are HILARIOUS. Even listening to his podcasts I end up chuckling because he's so funny. I like how he's focused on the big picture rather than minute details on the test. You still need to memorize a ton of material though. Tons of resources and study material on his site. Class curved

Dr. Hampton is one of my favorite professors at UCSD! You can tell from his lectures that he's really passionate about the subject and loves to teach. Yes, he does go off topic sometimes but his stories and were entertaining and kept the class interesting. Make sure to study the problem sets and old exams to do well!

Randy is my favorite professor at UCSD. I took him based off of the reviews on RMP and I'm glad I did.  Like the other reviews said, he's not easy but he was fair, especially if you did the problem sets. This class is about Glycolysis, Gluconeogenesis, Krebs Cycle, Electron Transport Chain, Urea Cycle, Amino Acid and Lipid catabolism/anabolism.

Randy is a nice professor and he genuinely wants students to do well. He is one of the best professors and loves what he teaches.  HOW TO DO WELL: -Keep up with lectures. DON'T fall behind. -Print out his study list and use it as a checklist. -Do his problem sets. If you do these three, you WILL get an A. It takes work. Good luck!

Such a nice professor.  He's really smart but gets you to appreciate the Biochemistry in action rather than simply reading a text book.  His exams this year were pretty difficult but I'm sure he'll curve generously.  He even bought the class pizza after the final.  Not many professors do that.  Randy is the best so take him if you can.
I'm pretty disappointed in his teaching methods. Though Dr. Hampton is hilarious, he is pretty disorganized during lecture. He constantly goes off on tangents and doesn't explain things very well.

Dr. H is a really nice professor.  Even though I don't find the class "easy" like some reviewers made it seem, he's really friendly and generally wants you to learn.  The reason why some people say he doesn't teach testable stuff is because you can't learn a pathway during class, it takes time.  It helps to watch youtube before going to lecture.

This is an unpopular opinion but I did not enjoy his class at all. He himself often distracted from class material, and while his anecdotes on marathon running and the like are fun if pointless, his delivery of relevant, testable material is dry if I'm being generous.  To be fair, his tests are straight forward, and not tricky, so that's a plus.

One midterm and one final. If you fail your midterm on week 5, you have a chance to get an A with a 100% worth final. Tests: No application needed, all you need is storage space in your brain. Like all bibc102, invest lots of time, do all practice tests, no need to attend class--just extra clickers. No electron pushing and plants stuff-chloroplast

He is my favorite professor at UCSD!  He was very clear on what he wanted from you for the exam.  I went to lectures, and just did the problem sets.  His tests were very straightforward and very similar to the exams he posts on his website!
Got A! His exams are super straightforward. There are only TWO key points to succeed in his class -  1. find the excellent TA and 2. do the problem sets. If I could do it, you can do it.... Cheers!

This is my first post rating a professor that I absolutely loved! This class is a lot of memorization, but hampton gives you all the resources you need to do well. Tests straight forward. He really wants you to learn, and I retained a lot of what I learned bc of this. You'll find yourself in the vitamin/supplement aisle reading labels

Randy is BOSS! You'll understand what I mean when you take him. Always there to help, very enthusiastic about his material, and tests are very straight forward, NO TRICKS. Even posts study lists, practice problems (w/key) and previous exams (w/key)!! Gives you everything for success, as long as you put in the effort! Thanks Randy!!

Professor Hampton is one of the best professors I've ever had. He makes you want to come to class! He is so funny and tells you exactly what you need to know for exams. As long as you do and understand the problem sets you will do fine in the class!

I dreaded metabolics when I learned it in BILD 1, but Randy explains everything very clearly. Teaches the specific stuff on lecture, but tests on the overall picture. Very humorous and approachable. Very eccentric (in a good way) but very knowledgable. Option to have the final be 100% of your grade if you bombed the midterm.

Professor Hampton makes the class very manageable. For each lecture, he provides a study list and problem set that reflects the main concepts/pathways to know. Exams are straightforward as long as you memorize appropriately. There is extra credit for iClickers and a curve as well. I definitely recommend him.

One funny dude right here! His pace could be a bit hard to keep up with, but that's no problem as long as you keep up with his written study guides and problem sets on the website. The exams are straightforward, but, of course, demand some memorization of the material.  Also, you have the option to make the final 100% of your grade.

This man is a genuinely great professor! He tells you exactly what he wants and supplies you with everything you need for the basics. If you want to complain about "scatterbrained" lectures, feel free to take the dull, dry ones (plenty of them at UCSD) and leave the class openings to awesome future metabolites who want to earn an A the fun way!

One of the best professors at UCSD. Material is easy and doable if you take the time to keep up with the lectures and DO ALL THE PRACTICE PROBLEMS. The learning curve for this class is high, but "repetition is the mother of learning." He's very helpful in his office hours. I've learned a great deal from this class. Would highly recommend him!
Randy is totally boss.  As straightforward as Metabolic can be, wish he taught more classes.

Professor Hampton was such an entertaining lecturer. Before I attended the first class I was dreading biochemistry but he made it so fun. He gives you so many resources and his papers are particularly helpful on understanding certain topics. Also, he could have made this class so much harder than he did, which I am thankful for!

yes he lectures really fast and you do get quite lost but he has an incredible amount of resources (old exams, short questions, texted questions) for you to catch up. its not his responsibility to hold your hand and teach you every last detail. he is only there to guide you in the right direction and that how any class should be.

Professor Hampton is one cool cat. But he is one terrible lecturer. he is sooo all over the place! his lectures are incredibly hard to follow and in the midst of it all he blasts you with info and you have no idea whats important and whats not try ands study it all D: . If he's your best option take him. but I don't recommend him.

So far, this class has been my favorite because of the professor and the subject! He's hyper and animated when teaching which made the class very enjoyable! He actually took the time to get to know me. He's super straightforward on his exams. Study his study list and you will earn a good grade! No surprises!

Great professor! The material is difficult and rather tedious but hard work does pay off. He has many exams available from previous years for practice, which I found very helpful. Hampton is also very clear about what he expects and wants from the students. The material is not superbly exciting but his wit and humor is worth your time and effort.

I dreaded taking Metabolics, but with Randy Hampton I was so relieved. He is a great lecturer- very clear, funny. He even bought a prepaid phone so we could text him questions during lecture! It's extremely hard to fail this class because his exams are so straight forward! Go to class and read anything you don't understand. LOVE HIM!

Dr. Hampton is an amazing prof! Really puts metabolism in the perspective of human physiology, presents relevant information, smart, funny, truly cares about his students. Material is extremely difficult though, and his final this year was significantly more challenging/different than his practice finals from over 8 years. Definitely recommended!

I took Dr. Hampton for 102 last year and now that I'm graduating I wanted to point out that I retained the concepts he taught because he always emphasized the bigger picture.His class helped me so much in my other classes that rely on met. pathways like nutrition and endocrinology.His tricks to remember things really stick too.Don't take anyone els

Take this professor for metabolic! Dr. Hampton is enthusiastic and knowledgeable about the subject, helpful, and funny! Just stay on top of the material (get the molecules in pathways down >2 days before the exam) and go to office hours if you need help! Don't be fooled: THE SUBJECT IS DIFFICULT, but Dr. Hampton knows how to teach it.

If you're a Bio major at UCSD and have not taken a course with this brilliant man then you are seriously missing out! Lectures were so captivating and straightforward. definitely print out the powerpoint beforehand.

The best professor I have had at this school. He is very quirky and strange, like your typical awkward scientist but at the same time very friendly and spontaneous. Very funny especially when it comes to exam times when the mood is serious. Basically its 40% midterm 60% final but you can make the final 100% of your grade if it helps you. A = ~84%+

One of the best professors at UCSD. The class has a lot of memorize, but not as much as one would think. Dr. Hampton only wants you to know for the tests the surface level of the extremely complex metabio, and not get crowded in the details  as some other profs do. Much of what I learned I believe I will actually retain for a long time. Recommended

i strongly recommend Randy. He's funny, approachable and helpful. Even though it's podcasted, go to lecture. It's not video podcasted so it's difficult to follow which slide he's on. There is a lot of stuff to memorize but when studying for the midterm or final, go over previous ones he has posted on his website-he reuses a lot of questions.

best best best professor ever!!!! probably the funniest guy i have ever met..super helpful, super engaging.. makes sure to make biochem interesting and lectures were soo enjoyable.. he used to be a standup comedian and musician.. he's the only professor whose lectures i was able to podcast and not fall asleep.. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!!! seriously. :)
Prof. Hampton made my quarter! This class is really hard and requires lots of memorization, but your life will be lots easier with Hampton.

He is BOSS need i say more!Best professor ever at UCSD! so sad the class is over! This class with anyone else is pure hell and boring! TAKE RANDY IF YOU CAN!! EXAMS ARE SUPER STRAIGHT FORWARD AND NOT TRICKY!

This is the best teacher ever.  Hands down. As a senior at UCSD this is definitely the one teacher every bio person has got to take.  He used to be a comedian and so all of his classes are hilarious.  His tests are straight forward, so the curve is really high to get an A.
Who else will dress up for Halloween, turn off the classroom lights, and play scary music? I guarantee you no other professor at UCSD.

For BIBC103, I first took Price and dropped the class. Then I took Zhao and dropped the class again. 3rd times the charm wi/Randy! He's my fav prof as UCSD! He actually made the topic interesting w/his random spurts/gestures and his awesome raps songs. So funny! He's like your favorite elementary school teacher reincarnated as a college professor

Randy is the shizzle. Rekindled my love for biochem. Many test questions recycled for final. Midterm was a low average, like 67%, but I got like a 100%, so it's possible to do well, just study ALOT. Great lecturer even though I hate powerpoint, he knew metabolism inside and out. DEFINATELY recommend this man, the bomb bizzle king of metabolic bio.
Awesome professor, if you study you are sure to get an A.

Great prof. This prof has lots of ppl waiting to be added. I got added the third week, so I was a little behind. The midterm was fair. The final was multiple choice and questions were recycle from previous exam, which are posted on his website. Overall, good class. You can get an A+ if you study. Mostly memorization. Prof is funny & lecture is ok.

Hampton is pretty freaking awesome. His lectures are entertaining and he does a good job of lecturing. Everything is very straight forward. You can't help but to be excited about metabolics after seeing his enthusiasm and how he's willing to make a fool of himself in front of the entire class. Regardless of my grade, I really enjoyed this class.

The most entertaining class I have ever had in my LIFE. Seriously, I only attended all his lectures because it was better than stand-up comedy. He'll make you laugh till your guts hurt, and is always upto something goofy. Oh yeah, the exams: just like any bio class, cram the heck out of his study lists. He doesnt trick ppl on exams.

awesome person. funny lectures, but they're still kinda boring.  just follow his topic papers on what to know and you should ace the class.  it's not that hard.  lots of memorization but that's typical of any bio class.

As a lecturer he is okay...but as a person he is awesome. Definitely tries to keep you awake through the boring subject of metabolic. Finished the class with some awesome lectures on aging, cancer, diabetes and exercise. Has practice midterms and finals (final is multiple choice).

i know everyone has already said it, but Randy is my favortie professor! the first lecture was hilarious, and he wrote a rap about enzyme rates! He's very helpful in office hours and he loves to help students in any way he can. tests are straightforward. he tells you EXACTLY what  you need to know, so if you study what he tells you too, its easy.

He is definitely one of the more likeable bio profs.  He teaches w/ power point which you're encouraged to print out. Notes can be hard to take sometimes b/c he talks fast and barely writes stuff down.  Some lectures become boring but only b/c of the topic. He tries to keep things alive.  I loved his "yawn dance".  Tests weren't as hard as expected

R Hampton is a very entertaining instructor. The content of this class is no doubt a lot of memorization and challenging, but if you have to take it - take it with R Hampton. One midterm and one final, no homework, quizes, or papers due for this class.

Hampton was awesome, kept me laughing.  The material was easy to understand, just hard to memorize it all.  The class is no prob if you put in the time, otherwise you are screwed.  If you have to take BIBC102, take Hampton!  PS beware, he pretty much only gives straight As, Bs, Cs etc, barely any +s or -s.
