Hampton is great! I really enjoyed his class, though it was a challenging course. Just study and you should be fine, but don't forget to give yourself plenty of times to study.

Really good professor--he seems really interested in helping students and having his students do well.  The only thing is that this class is hard with a lot of memorizing.  Ouch.  But his tests are fair and he allows student imput to make them even more fair.

FAVORITE PROFESSOR EVER.  He made me love biochem.  He's actually interested in teaching, which is rare in the university scene.  Metabolic Biochem has been one of my favorite classes to date, and though you still have to make sure you know your info (LOTS of memorizing) his exams are 100% fair.  Study, and do well.  Enjoy. =)

Randy is insane.  He makes lecture really funny though.. honestly, it's like going to a comedy routine; except for the whole metabolism part.  Anyway, he at least makes it entertaining, and he's a good professor.
First bio professor I had, and boy, was he kooky!  He jumped on the table once during a midterm and said, "I'm a scorpion!"  Anyways, tests were straightforward and I enjoyed his lectures
funny as hell! The final is multiple choice,so it's not that bad. A lot of memorizations of structures and enzymes, so avoid cramming a night before.
Fan Freaking Tastic!  Biochem's kinda a ****, but he's hilarious (used to be a pro comic...)  Tests are fair and not too horrid...study and you'll do fine.  Prolly my fav. prof at UCSD so far!

If you dread taking this class, take it with Dr. H.  He's fun, cool, interesting, and his tests aren't that bad if you study, study, study.  There's no way to avoid the overload of memorization but make it more palatable with Hampton.

very funny guy but hard to learn anything from lectures cuz it's all memorization. this course is kind of pointless cuz the way we were required to cram stuff didn't help much of gaining understadning to biology. a bad course but if u have to do it, take it with randy hampton. at least u learn jokes
A very fun class to take since the prof. is a very cool guy. The class covers way too much materials but it'll open your eyes to the whole new world.

He's a good prof (likes to keep things interesting...don't yawn or he'll do the "yawn dance" to keep you awake). I had trouble actually learning anything from his lectures, so I pretty much taught myself from the book. Nice guy, extremely difficult class, but I would definitely recommend him. :)
He deffinetly makes class more intersting to sit through.  I don't understand how anyone could fall asleep in his class with all the electronic toilet movies and filmed demonstrations of concepts....
Very down to earth guy. Keeps lecture fun. His class is highly recommended.
No Comments
Very entertaining!
Do yourself a favor, take his class

Mid on all accounts. Actually took her for a Comm106 class not 100A, and it was easy enough. She tries to get people to engage with the material, which I respect, but its so boring and so unrelevant that no one really cared. I didnt really learn anything either, but if your looking for a sraightforward A, I think she would be a decent choice.

the TA's graded everything in this class so ignore her being a hard grader. her class was really easy and  she is very accommodating if any emergency or mental health issues arise. i've taken her 2 times and its been an easy A, she designs the classes to make sure everyone passes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Take her ! Attendance is not mandatory for lectures although if you go she tries her best to hear students comments and be interactive. The work isnt that hard if you put in at least some effort. The sections are always interesting and the TA's are good.

Professor Irani is pretty harsh grader on the assignments, the lectures are causing more confusion on the subject. She teaches a lot of classes in Communications department. I'd avoid her as any way possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took professor Irani's class in the fall online. It was pretty easy. Just show up to the lectures and read the articles assigned on modules, kinda lengthy. Weekly quizzes after every reading. Participation counts, but you can easily do it on canvas. 3 main papers are pretty simple and straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Irani's course. She is very flexible and if the class raises a concern to a due date, she is willing to compromise and change it. She cares about her students very much and her lectures are very interesting. There are a few readings each week followed up with a short reading quiz but they are not difficult if you did the reading.

Took COMM100A with Booker and Irani. Booker was excellent, but Irani always ended up making the lectures more confusing to the point where Booker would have to clarify. Irani is n extremely nice professor and is understanding, but her teaching style gives no value to the lectures and creates more confusion than necessary. Too scattered!

Good lectures, but bad class structure. Grades based on midterms and final only. He expects you to do all the algebras by hand while in lecture he says things like "do this in cadence blah blah". The tests focus heavily on circuit analysis instead of intuitions/mindset. No outside materials besides lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
我就要说他，他教的是个寄吧

100% graded by test,
Two midterm(one highest will be graded), but one is easier and the other is much harder. Good luck if you do bad in the easier one.
Huge amount of calculation, you may even have not enough time to finish the test. Im not here to take SAT or something.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's rude, arrogant, and disrespectful. He expects the world to bend to his will and way of doing things. Has no idea what life is like for non-white men and completely out of touch with humanity. Additionally, the work load is outrageously heavy. Don't take classes from this relic.

Learnt more analog design in ece164, this was just random math. Complicates simple concepts by introducing too many variables and overly formal mathy language. Lectures are online recordings- in person lectures are useless, no new content. Expects students to figure out everything by themselves. Half the course is "you'll prove this as homework".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Forced to take ECE 264 series courses due to major requirements. Absolutely doltish prof, who has absolutely no sense in including meaningful subject matter in his courses. Has just 2 tests, a final, and entire course conducted via online lectures. Conducts no office hrs himself, rarely approachable, never willing to really help students succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is way too heavy on theory, and confusing. I still don't know how to design even after taking this class. People also cheated on the final exam, don't know if the TA did anything about it.
Way too hard, he teaches this class with no intuition and just with math. I didn't learn much from his lectures, at least I still don't know how to design after taking this class.

Dr. Galton gives every student the tool to become independent thinkers, not mindless SPICE monkeys. He does provide intuition, but the foundation is mathematics. You don't want to be stuck doing low level and low quality designs at the mercy of SPICE.

I also made the mistake of falling in love with only intuition. Remember, easy come easy go...

Extremely bad for analog. Just writes a bunch of equations without any intuition - most important thing required for analog ic designer. Writing this review post 2 years after graduating and I work as an analog designer in well respected company. Please stay away from this guy. Analog is not like mindless algebra like he shows it to be.

Like if this course was listed as analog circuits and random algebra. He's lectures were recorded during the pandemic. I don't know how he's able to keep his lecture loosely structured while actually memorizing the bunch of equations he wrote down 10 minutes ago. Amazing test qualities btw, algebra brain stew.

I felt like my entire foundation in ECE circuits was wrecked because rather than supporting me, this INTRODUCTORY class did its very best to weed me out. During his lectures, Galton did more lecturing about how he was trying to weed out students  than actually trying to connect and support his students. Y teach if your primary objective is to fail?

This is rather just an advanced algebra class, solving ENDLESS KCL's for complex circuits. Professor is so theory heavy, theres NO industrial stuff. NOTHING on the design aspect, all about analytic skills. I pursue masters to become a IC designer but now I am very worried about my career cause I dont know how to design even after taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: useless content and most grade depends on exams.
Too much unnecessary algebra. Course content is not sufficient.

He is one of the best teachers I've had in my life.  I had 2midterms and hw quizzes every other week, and I don't understand why people were complaining about the tests, they were definitely not easy, but if you understand the lecture notes, then you are good to go!
Seriously don't take this guy. His Fall 2014 class had a 14% pass rate , and he still believes his methodology is correct.

DO NOT, I repeat, DO NOT take ANY class with this professor. You really have to be special to get a good grade in his class but he will try everything to make the midterms and finals the worst nightmare you've ever had. UCSD, its time to get another instructor and change the grading system that this guy  has applied.

The material covered in ECE 35 should have been easy, but, this instructor made it hard with his complicated problems. Some of the TAs aren't very clear, and cut huge points for a small mistake. No required textbook, but you should buy his lecture notes because it is really helpful to do self-practice. The quizzes are really based on the HWs.
Dropped immediately after the med-term.  Lectures were useless and  it was impossible to pass the  exams coz they were never mentioned in the lecture.

I have been studying at UCSD for a year.  I got my only B in ECE35 with Galton. I recommend not taking ECE35 with him if you are a beginner.  If you are already familiar with many concepts covered in this class, then take ECE35 with Galton and challenge yourself. Maybe you can be the next Nobel price winner.

Took the class in fall 2013 and dropped it week 9. He didn't explain the material well for a beginner because he only did theoretical examples/proofs. Now I am taking the class again with Xiang and he is great. He provides clear examples and definitions and its all FINALLY clicking! So avoid galton, he is only there to scare you out of the major.

Went to office hours (TA and Prof). Did all the homework. Went to every lecture. Still failed. Would not take again. I'm retaking the class right now and this other professor (Radic) is so much better and for the first time I understand what I am doing. Galton is too theoretical. I understood the proofs, but when it comes to the test.....

So first of all let me say that Prof. Galton is obviously incredibly smart. That being said, he's definitely lost touch with the new EE student. He insists on you copying his entirely proof based lectures down and expects you to pull the intuition out of the symbols on your own. Honestly avoid for lower div. Midterm was a bell curve centred at 0%
He and his TAs trying to scare you. He is not clear at all. The book explains much better than him, but if you follow the book, you'll get zeros
Big Class bagan with 350+ students and ended up with 190+ students took the final. see how hard his class? Exams are his weapons and killed his students. no fun at all.

He is very clear and I learned a lot.  His quizzes/exams were normally 1-2 question(s) and his TAs grade really strict (or there is a tough rubric in place) - almost a all or nothing system even for minor errors - Book is mostly used for homework, his lectures provide enough material to study on.  Copy what he writes on the board word for word.

Refuses to use actual numbers, only variables. Very challenging final. Hideous algebra and nothing simplified. The final expressions ended up taking up several lines. Because of this it was difficult to even finish. His tests don't test if you understand the concepts. They test your algebra skills and finesse. Avoid him if you can.

4 quizzes (sometimes on material we haven't even covered), one midterm (avg was a 37) and hw he concocts that didnt really help me learn the material. Every question was a proof, numbers were never used.
though he seems to be a nice professor. But I hate the way he test students. Can't we have some real numbers instead of letter??

His notes are a mini book which is nice. But his homework is useless, takes too much time, and doesn't help you learn the material. His attitude is very good if you're looking for a tutor who will train you to be the best.  In short: do not take this class if you want a guarenteed A or if you want less tedious homework.

Lecture was pretty much proofs 24/7, made it seem like a upper div ECE course. I learned how the things worked but practically no problem solving developed. Homework was PURELY PROOFS from his Lectures aka Lectures are Mandatory if you want to do the homework. Hated his style of teaching, also Uncurved 37/100 on Midterm + 4 quizes + Final.

This professor was just not very good. He didn't teach the material, he just basically presented it to you. All quizzes were very long proofs and the midterm was a 37 average. If you did anything the book way, he would take points off even though it was right. His methods were far more confusing than the book's. Just bad, avoid at all costs.

The midterm is fair but he is very strict at grading. There are more that 50 zeros in the first midterm and average is very low.  The quiz has nothing to do with the lecture and often tests on things you don't know. I feel I am quite stupid after taking this class.
Not quite the best EE professor. One midterm, 4 quizzes, and a final. The average on the midterm was 37 out of 100. All proofs, no numbers. Knocks you if you do it the "book" way.
He really wants that students learn in class well. He does his best. He is so nice. He tries to give students intuition related to  analog designing while it is more mathematics basis.
Very good class for people who want to do ic design for job. Tough class but clear sometimes funny
Good Teacher .. not helpful in OH
Extremely good prof, but it's a tough class.  This guy knows his stuff and knows how to teach. You work hard but learn a lot.  Great preparation for job interviews!
Great teacher.  Very useful class if you want to do this stuff for a job.

He cares for teaching.He is one of the few teachers who make conscious effort to deliver good lectures.But, he has some failings: He is sarcastic when he doesn't know right answers.He doesnt teach Analog Design intuitively .It seems all algebra.His exams are straightforward but lengthy.His homeworks are length too.But he is the best among the analo
Indifferent to students.
Best teacher in department
Way good teacher.

Very, very good prof.  Nice guy, but hard class.  Very helpful to students who try hard, but has low tolerance for students who try to skate by with little work.  Good students like him but bad students don't.

Galton can be a prick, but as long as you get to class on time and pay attention to his lectures, you'll be OK. The work and tests are exactly like what he goes over in class, and he's willing to at least give you hints if you go to his office hours. His attitude toward students could be better, but this is nothing new for most UCSD professors.
Best professor at UCSD.  Really cares about his students.  Extremely hard class, though.
He gives you no help whatsoever. Go to the TA's. They are your only hope.
the guy has no people skills, he is unpleasant to work with on a one to one basis doesnt care about students, sounds like a phd to me.
His homework takes too much time. When he is not being rude he is being arrogant.  He never goes out of his way to help you outside the classroom.

Arrogant, disrespectful, and rude, especially in office hours. Assignments do more harm than good since they leave no time to study for his test. Tries to make his exams simple, but remember, you have no time to study.

Lot of students are afraid of him. Actually he is the easiest professor I have ever seen in UCSD. His HWs are taking little time to do, but he asked Midterm from his HWs. If you don't know how to start the MIDTERM you will get F. If you get some piece of idea, you are definitely getting A. SURE A++

There are no tricks on his exam. Learn to think for yourself. His lectures are useful and applicable and entertaining to say the least. He's a friendly guy if you come into OH knowing something, rather than, "how do I do this?"

Can't speak for the undergrad course, but everyone in the class passed for CSE 202. As long as you submit all your assignments and half effort your exams ur good. But HWs were no joke, make sure to spend 20 hours per week on them. His lectures were hard to follow and as you got towards the end of the class he had about 5 students in his lectures.

No midterms, yet 60 pts from Final exam focused on last 2 wks of concepts and we didn't get back any quiz/hw grade pertaining to any of that material. There's a significant mismatch between Instructional support and exam difficulty. If ur taking him be prepared to self-study

Slides are incoherent text vomit, rambles throughout lecture like a buffering video. Got angry at the class for leaving early on Thanksgiving week while he himself didn't attend his own office hours on at least two occasions. Released two HWs on week 10 due to being 2 weeks behind schedule, and said we'll drop one anyway according to the syllabus.

Avoid taking him. Two HWs squished together in the last week, changed a quiz date last second on thanksgiving week and blamed us for wanting to change it, lectures incoherent, finals was only based on a couple of topics. Only take if you're familiar with 101, save yourself the headache.
My goat when he doesn't attend his own office hours

The class is disorganized. Homework was released later than scheduled, causing multiple to be due in the final week. Grading is extremely slow. Even after the final, only 5/8 HWs and 6/8 Quizzes are graded. The final exam is 48% of the grade, not representative of the class, and only covers a few very hard topics.

AVOID HIM PLS TRUST ME. He's a smart & nice guy but he is NOT good at lecturing. Lectures are slow and really hard to revisit. Super disorganized class and grading feedback on some assignments took 1/2 the quarter. Unresponsive on Piazza. Insanely hard HW that essentially requires you to go to OH. Fair midterms but hard final. Just a bad experience

Material throughout this course was unclear and poorly communicated. Professor Impagliazzo failed to do what he's paid to do in a timely manner. I had no idea of my midterm 2 grade until the night before the final. This entire course was unclear and un-cooperative throughout the entire quarter, avoid this class at all costs!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst professor I've had so far at UCSD. Caring professor, but extremely unable to lecture. Took way too long to grade all assignments and lectures. Advice to anyone taking him in the future for 101, just watch Miles Jones' lectures

Nice professor, but his class is an absolute joke. Losing midterms, missing and countless typos pages on exams, unorganized canvas, and on top of that the homework still isn't even graded and we just took the final. Very disappointed.

The professor is nice and it's clear that he wants to teach well, but he's just not cut out for it. The class feels super disorganized, and the slides are useless without any context - often they're just a bunch of keywords or code slapped onto a slide and that's about it. The lectures are a little better, but still pretty bad for learning.

I have no idea how he is allowed to teach a course as difficult as CSE 101. His lectures are very disorganized and messy, the Piazza board is full of unanswered questions, and grading takes forever (midterm 2 grades came out 2 weeks after it was taken and a few days before the final). The fact that he is teaching next quarter as well is shocking.

Super disorganized professor, did not grade some student's midterms until the day before the final. We never got back our homework and the answer key for the practice final is incomplete. Professor is unprepared for any exam (posted the midterm on accident before it happened) and TAs are not helpful. Lectures are slow, hard to pay attention.
I CANT STUDY THGE SLIDES ARE SO BAD I CANT UNDERSTAND ANYTHING HIS SLIDES ARE SO ABD

This guys handwriting is horrible! I legit cannot understand what the heck he is writing and I'm staring at the subtitles while he is talking. The hw is not related to what he talks about in class as well.

The professor is a really talented and experienced researcher, but his lectures and slides are rather confusing and unorganized. Also, the feedback given for our homework is slow and lagging. Upon final exam when we really needed our homework graded for final prep, only 3 out of 6 homework got feedback.

Please DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE WITH RUSSEL IMPAGLIAZZO. He is not a good professor if your goal is to learn the material or to succeed in the class. The HW was very difficult with some taking 10+ hrs per problem with no support from the professor on how to get a better grasp on concepts. This professor should not be teaching undergraduate students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Please don't take his classes. His homework's are extremely difficult and make up a large portion of your overall grade for the class. His lectures are almost entirely useless. The grading is messed up more often than not. He doesn't take feedback from students very well. It takes a 95 in this class to get an A, which is nearly impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not equate poor teaching to difficulty of material.
Lectures are very disorganized and confusing and office hours aren't much help either. I have no doubt that he's very brilliant and accomplished in his field, but he shouldn't be teaching undergrads.

Very likely the worst professor I have had at this school. Watching his lectures was like watching paint dry in slow motion. Seems like a very nice guy but not at all good at explaining concepts in a way that doesn't leave you even more confused than you started.

Russell is the worst professor I have ever had in my life. He is really good at interpreting an easy concept in a much more complex way. If you just watch his lectures and slides, you would definitely get lost. But when you read through the textbook for the same concept, you would realize how easy it is. So I really suggest he stop using slides.

Absolutely the worst professor I've had at UCSD. His lectures are completely useless because he cannot convey difficult concepts in an understandable way. Instead he just shows you his borderline unreadable slides. It feels like he does not care at all about teaching, as evidenced by him literally editing his slides as he's teaching. Avoid him.

Worst professor I've had out of the 30+ courses I've taken here. He has absolutely no clue how to teach and his slide decks (which he edits as he's presenting them) are terrible. You're better off literally doing nothing than going to his lectures because they are actually useless. And this is coming from someone who did great in 8AB, 12, and 20.

I'm sure he knows a lot about the field, but as a professor he does not know how to teach whatsoever. His writing is pure chicken scratch. His slides have little to no relation to the homework and I had to get/learn all of the material from online resources. Tests were also very dense with little time to actually think about your answer.

Seems like a very kind man, but a pretty average lecturer. He gets across what he needs to though. The homework has a lot to do with CSE 20 and he starts off without much review so make sure you know induction proofs and the other basic concepts from 20. You can do hw with friends though, so find a good group. Overall the class felt easier than 20.

As others have said, this guy has no idea how to teach. The hw assignments seem to be from some graduate classes. He doesn't care about students' learning and he is not helpful during office hours. He just mumbles things and if you are confused on something, he just reads the question back to you.
Sometimes hard to understand but great homework assignments--fun and challenging.

Although this class is a CSE course, it is of a mathematical flavor.  Mathematics is meant for the blackboard, not a powerpoint.   Secondly, this class is very disorganized, it has a very clear structure, but everything is handled in a very clumsy matter.  The final is graded very leniently, but the homework is very inconsistent in difficulty.

He is a great researcher but I learn absolutely nothing from his lectures or slides. I had to read the textbook and search online for hw. : ( Also 21 is a lot harder than 20, but if you do the practice exams and go to review sessions you will be fine on exams. HW is the hard part.
Overall great professor! Very helpful during OH. Lectures can be confusing though. Do homework, attend discussions, go to OH, go through practice exams and you will be fine!

Make use of prof's OH as he is most helpful at those. He is not good in holding his students' attention however it is easy enough to follow his lectures. Quizzes and final are very similar to practice ones. So make sure you can solve those. Overall Russell is a great instructor!

He lets me understand how easy could Analyzing Algorithms be. He is very tough and active in Piazza. There is no penalty for late HWs. Every Quiz is offered twice but equivalent. HWs are challenging but you can form at most 5 people as a team. Though I did my HWs alone, because I really can learn from doing them.

This guy is obviously very smart and is very intelligent in the work he does.  This does not mean he should be teaching.  I have no idea what on earth he is even talking about.  He is a researcher not a teacher.  Homework take forever, and are not straight to the point. Sometimes simple and direct is the best solution.  He does not take that route.

This class is H A R D.  Take advantage of Office Horus and the fact that there are two midterms.  The first one is MUCH easier and they take the best of the two midterms.  Russell's a nice guy but is crap at explaining things in an understandable way.  The HW takes forever so start early!  Actually, just take this class with a diff prof.
Take advantage of office hours and pick partners based on how much you all know rather than who you know.
This guy is worst CSE professor at UCSD. He should be fired!

Lectures were not very clear; they did a better job of putting me to sleep than actually explaining anything.  He mumbles a lot and speaks mostly to the board.  Homeworks were difficult, but the exams were easy in comparison.

Ok this professor is the most knowledgable professor i have ever seen at UCSD. the class is hard but you will do fine if you go to office hours. He is very smart and very polite and really cares for stuents

damn hard class! be prepared to work your ass off in this one. homeworks constitute the main work in the class. midterm was rather easy, but the final was hard. dont copy the homework from past quarters (same hws) because you will def get caught. No joke. Upside - professor is helpful.
Algorithms- If you like it you will do aight. Else you better study yo a$$ off.  Uses same hw sht but dont copy totally correct answer or you'll get caught. Boring class, just got to put up with it.

I took CSE 227 instead of 127, but they didn't have an option for 227. She made participation mandatory, which was annoying. She was uncomfortable with the material and used AI to generate pretty much everything from assignments to lectures. It is clear that she doesn't have experience teaching. This was a waste of time.

She is not qualified to teach this course. I have no idea why UCSD decided to hire her. She used ChatGPT to generate the entire course, and it is obvious during the lectures that she has no idea what she is talking about. Easily the worst instructor I've ever had, and she has the audacity to make people call her professor.

Took this course in Fall 2025 with Prof. Munyaka and learned a lot about interaction design. As a part of a course project, I did a research project that turned into a preprint. I would 100% recommend this course to PhD students looking to understand HCI research better.
Professor used a bunch of gpt to prepare classes. Very unclear grading rubric. Hard to communicate

No clue how the CSE department decided to hire her. Doesn't know anything. Seems like she is looking at the slides for the first time. Incompotent professor. Feel like some of the tutors coulda taught the class better than her. "not my research so idk how to teach it" was said multiple times.
shouldn't be allowed to teach
Literally the worst professor I've ever had, should be fired

She straight-up LIED to students about changing her syllabus midway into the quarter. The syllabus stated that the final could replace the midterm. A student asked on Piazza about it; she responded, "that was NEVER a thing". Another student posted screenshots of the syllabus from this quarter that proved otherwise. It had been deleted.

Very disorganized professor, they took slides/resources from a previous professor, and it doesn't seem like they even looked through them before re-use. States that certain topics aren't here "focus in research" and as such can't give much information, even though its fundamental to the topics at hand.
Very rude and no communication on piazza. Assignments are unclear without instructions and her lectures are extremely hard to follow without any organization

The entire class is completely a mess and is super confusing. The professor says something like "I'm not researching on this area so don't ask me about this" during lecture. Then why are you here? The tutors also seem to know nothing but teach confidently. I doubt if they have passed this course.
She does not the contents and how to teach..worst professor

Prof. Munyaka's course had unclear assignments and lacked timely updates. Responses on Piazza often felt indirect, affecting class inclusivity. Wikipedia tasks seemed purposeless. Better communication and clarity could improve the learning experience. There's room for improvement in her teaching approach. She really doesn't know what she is doing.

Possibly one of the worst professors I've ever had. Professor encourages asking questions, then when you ask she makes you feel bad for asking. No structure to the class and professor's attitude is just bad.

I regret taking this class with Munyaka. She honestly doesn't know how to teach. The assignments seemed to have been put together with little to no thought and seems like busy work. Even though it's not hard, I still regret taking this class every time I do work for it because it just feels like I'm wasting my time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is very poorly structured. A lot of the assignments that she has us do are just busy work with no end purpose. The assignment descriptions and deadlines are vague and confusing. The lectures are often taken up by her trying to fix logistical issues that she created. Overall a massive waste of time. I would never recommend her to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was a complete mess and a complete waste of time. She had us doing a bunch of different assignments with no clear focus. She also often spent large chunks of class time going over logistical issues. Overall, I very much regret taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I feel like CSE194 was supposed to be an interesting course but prof Munyaka did an awful job teaching it. Her lectures were lackluster, has this asserting dominance attitude, and the grading criteria for all assignments were confusing and unclear. Take this class with other profs if you can.

I love Nieh! He made this class truly enjoyable, and he is so sweet. He gave clear criteria for what he wants you to learn, and the exams reflect what you learn in lectures and readings. Exams are mainly MCQ with a few short answers. Memorize, but also get to learn the concepts, because they will easily come to you for exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof is very passionate but lectures felt a bit disorganized and sometimes it was hard to understand big picture concepts from his very specific examples. Exams are directly from lectures and lecture readings, so studying is mostly memorization but not too complicated.

Attendance is only 5% of the grade and you can miss many classes so don't worry too much about that. Nieh is a great and caring professor, and his class is super fun. You learn many practical yet fun facts about animals across the animal kingdom. Id highly recommend this class to any biology major looking for an interesting upper division elective.

Very nice and respectable professor. His lectures are very clear and he explicitly tells you what he expects. Grade is by attendance, weekly quiz (easy), 2 midterms and 1 final. Would def recommend taking him!

I love this Professor so much! His lectures are so so fun and interactive! He cares a lot for his students. He doesn't curve or give extra credit and is very clear of that since the beginning of the course. graded on 2 midterms and a final + weekly quizzes
The final was harder than the midterms for me so prepare well!

Prof. Nieh is fantastic!!! lectures are incredibly enriching with deliberately chosen video clips and readings that perfectly supplement the overall learning. Learned so much in this course and the concepts are so inspiring and intriguing! Really wish he can teach more classes! 
Manageable workload. Take good notes and you'll be fine!

sweetest professor ever. I wish I could take him for every class. Grading criteria is very clear, no curving or extra credit. He made mistakes on the exams but immediately corrected and awarded points back to students. Clear lectures, attendance not mandatory. It's a lot of information and takes some time to digest but I loved this class.

He is AMAZING! lectures are fun and he shows lots of videos. I felt like my last midterm was unfairly graded since some of the multiple choice questions he didn't cover in lecture, and I didnt even ask for a regrade request - but he acknowledged his mistake and gave everyone points back for questions he didn't cover. So sweet! recommend

One of the best professors in the Bio department. Always provides examples to pair with concepts we learn in class and explains them very well. I find that it is not that the material isn't hard, but rather that the content and Professor is so engaging that studying for his class becomes less of a chore.

Dr. Nieh is one of the best profs I have ever had at UCSD. His lectures are very interesting, he explains examples very well, and his quizzes/exams are straightforward. He is extremely knowledgeable & an expert in his field, super approachable, highly recommended.

This class is the most interesting one in the bio department. No HW, weekly minor quizzes, two midterms + final. How to pass: take good notes, read exam questions carefully, look over the past exams he posts, once you master how he asks questions (he can be a bit specific and tricky at times) you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take this class with this professor in your final year (preferably final quarter if you can). Im a fourth year and this class was not stressful at all and went by super smoothly. Weekly quizzes are easily doable (1 question per week). Listen to him lecture, take good notes, tests are very representative of class lectures. You'll have fun.

I absolutely loved this professor. He was well organized and inspiring when he taught. You can tell that he knows his stuff and will give examples for every concept! He understands how people learn. He was understanding when we didn’t do well on the 1st midterm and said that it wouldn’t affect our overall grade if we did badly. Overall, AMAZING

I am so happy that I got to take a class with this professor. He makes lectures so interesting and engaging and Ive learned so much in this course. You can tell he cares a lot for his students especially during these times. I highly recommend taking his class, you will learn so much!

He's a great professor but his tests are extremely difficult and tricky. You can study the material and know it A through Z but you can still do bad because of the tricky wording and concepts that you're being tested on. And if you mess up you really have no space for improvement.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Nieh was a great Professor! Hes definitely very interested in what hes teaching and wants the students to become more interested in it too. Hes open to questions and does all he can to clarify the material. Its a lot of info so i recommend reading the required readings and taking notes on the slides as well as what he says

One of the most helpful and most caring professors I have had, very willing to give advise and explains things clearly. Some of the hardest exams I have ever taken, you have to know the material down to the tiniest detail.

Nieh is amazing! His is so organized and knowledgeable. I highly recommend taking his class. The tests are very difficult, but he provides a lot of study material and only tests on what is said in lecture (which is podcasted).
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: THIS CLASS IS THE BEST. Dr. Nieh is also AMAZING. This class has a lot of information and details to know but they're easy to remember and follow because they're all so interesting. Lectures are not boring at all. He always show video examples and is also a funny guy. Read the required reading several times and you're good to go!

Dr. Nieh is amazing! He loves what he teaches. He is really great at lecturing and making his lectures easy to follow, especially for his exams. He is clear. He knows what he's talking about. I didn't expect to like this class, but it was amazing compared to what I expected. Study his power points and you'll do just fine. I highly recommend him!

AMAZING professor and an AMAZING person; very knowledgeable, very educated, and very helpful! His lectures go by easy; they're fun and very interesting! He does everything he can to make the material more understandable; Love this guy!!!! However, exams are fair but not easy, and final was tricky; ended up with A-. NO CURVE! WATCH OUT!

TONS of memorization, exams are all short answer with specific questions, T/F here and there. Regardless, material was interesting. It's not an easy A if you think bare minimum effort is enough, definitely need to put in fair amount of time for studying.

He made this quarter "harder" b/c the previous year was too easy, but it was still very fair. The class itself is interesting and different from other bio classes I've taken (first BIEB course). Exams are super straightforward and he reuses the same concepts from previous exams. There's a lot of material to memorize but it's not hard to get an A.

Made the class slightly more difficult and a more strict curve than previous quarters. and he probably will again since 68% of the class got at least a B-. materials not too difficult, but lots of memorization. he posts all his slides, past exams, and readings online while also video podcasts. final was really long and tested specific details

Crispy Clear Lecture. He know's his shiznet! MTs pretty ez. Final is so damn long.. i was shocked that we had 50 questions (multi/T.F/ and may be 80% all describing and written). Studied not even 24 hrs for his final. I prob got B. One of the easiest bio elective and INTERESTING! fun class

He made the exams a bit more difficult this quarter, I guess maybe because everyone said he was easy.. There's a lot of memorization needed. Examples/ concepts can become quite dense once you begin studying all of it but the class is nonetheless very interesting!

Dr. Nieh's class is very interesting. He shows a lot of cool animal examples. Feels like watching the animal planet. The class was easy because his tests were straightforward. Going in, you'll know what he is going to ask. Still have to study but ALL his past tests are posted, so no need to stress. Just enjoy the class.

The professor is really nice, and his class is also really interesting. He posts everything online, and the class is podcasted. Discussion section is optional, but it's helpful to go to one. The best thing is that you don't need to buy a book for the class!!! :D

Most amazing professor at UCSD. Dr. Nieh takes caring for his students success it to an entirely new level. He makes everything available to his students from the textbook being posted online, to video podcasting every lecture and review session, to releasing every exam ever given in the class. Take this class, best professor at UCSD
Great Professor. Has taught the course for several years and as result knows the best way to teach the material. Tests are straight from the lectures. No curve; just straight up earn your grade.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Gives you all the possible resources to succeed in the class. Don't have to buy a textbook, he posts everything online. Exams are mostly short answer format, with a couple multiple choice. Extremely straightforward.

Awesome Professor.  Great lectures and wants his students to like the material. Loves what he teaches and really shows. Cares very much about his students.  Tests are based ENTIRELY off lecture; NO BS. Extremely fair and helpful. Even provided textbook on WebCt.  Best Professor I have had at UCSD.

Really good and passionate professor. Lectures hold your attention. Grading is very generous. Tests are fair. 83% was an A. I think about half the class got As. Definitely recommended! Final is harder than midterms though. If you are good at memorizing, you will do well in this class! Take Nieh!

Awesome teacher, awesome class. Very clear lecturer, very interesting, understanding guy. Exams are very fair and there is NO curve in the sense that avg is NOT a B-.  Most of the class probably ended up with a B or better (A is 80 or above I believe and avgs were at like 76) Definetely take.

Dr. Nieh is very intelligent and nice - well at least for this quarter because the averages were freaking high and he gave a generous grading scale instead of a curve. Concepts are easy but there can be a lot of it - a lot as in if you don't really care about the subject then it is a lot. Final was harder than the midterms.

His class is very interesting, and the concepts are not hard. However, it is hard to get an A, since the class is curved to make the average a B-. Also, since the concepts are easy, lots of people do well, raising the curve. The class itself is not hard, but this is no easy A class. Write specific names of concepts to get full credit.

Good professor, really cares about students but expects certain specific words on exams, even if you show you clearly understand concepts, so forget about regrades. Do all practice exams and it's an easy A

Tests are a lot easier now that they are short answer and fill-in, as opposed to the tricky multiple choice questions he had before. Don't even bother reading anything in the sourcebook. Everything you need to know is in his lecture notes. Very manageable class if you are willing to put in 4-5 hours a week

very very caring professor. Answers email quick, podcasts extremely clear, so no need to go to lecture. All lecture slides/reading online or book. Tests are very straightforward from this quarter, but was tricky before when it was m.choice.Very fun and unboring class. EasyA if you study a lot and makingsure you understand everything. best bieb pro!

WI08 class was lucky enough to have fewer students, so we got free response test questions, which may have been easier.  Typical memorization of details and concepts bio class.  There is a TON of info though - might want to study directly off podcasts.  Some parts of the class were a drag, others interesting, but it was fairly enjoyable. Great prof

Dr. Nieh has superb presentations, and the material is clear and easy to understand...but there is a LOT of it. The class is very interesting & I really enjoyed it. His mid-terms were very tricky though...nothing was straight forward. Read the questions very carefully!! I highly recommend this course and this professor though.

This is one of those classes that comes back to bite you in the ass if you aren't careful. Taking this class for an easy "A" and going in thinking as such is a bad idea. Also, if you hate physics with a fiery passion, beware because many concepts covered in physics are revisited here.

He knows a lot about bees but a lot of the information he presents isn't completely accurate.  His tests ask a lot of tricky questions and are very knitpicky.  Lectures are pretty entertaining and you usually get out early.
A great professor! His lectures are interesting and fun. Tests are straightforward and representative of the material. I Highly suggest this professor and course!

He always ends class early while still going through all the information of the day.  Tests are very representative of lecture and readings.  This class, so far (and I've been here 4 years) is absolutely the easiest bio class I have EVER taken.
Excellent professor but his tests are quite hard.  Class are not only entertaining but i've also learn a lot.  He makes the class so much fun! wish he would have easier test.
Easier than hooking up with **** pi phis at the ranch house!

Professor Nieh is an exceptionally phenomenal professor. He definetely sets the standard of what a truly excellent teacher is. He is extremely clear, focused, organized and makes his class very interesting. Great for people who learn visually but his oratory itself is a piece of work!

It's fun and exciting. His lectures are always entertaining! You get to see cool clips on animals. Lots of memorizing like any other biology courses but this one is the coolest. Attend all of his lectures and you’ll do a fabulousooo jobieeee.

Professor Rabin's lectures were excellent and extremely engaging! There were SPARSE moments where I was 'lost' during lecture, as his intuitive explanations always got me back on track. I would be very excited to have him as a professor in an upper div math class later on. Graded on a curve, the exam difficulties were relatively balanced.
Great professor who makes lectures very engaging!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The professor is actually good. However, 31AH is an honors course(NOT meant to be easy). The course is heavy on proofs, so unless your major requires some background, don't take proof courses. He follows the textbook a lot, so I recommend previewing the sections before lecture. The grading can be harsh, sometimes graded incorrectly or w/o feedback
He is a nice professor, but compared to other honors professors, he doesn't teach as much.

I loved the way Rabin taught Linear Algebra. The tests and homework are proof heavy, and therefore quite difficult. Make sure to practice making logically consistent proofs since even a slight error will lose you points. However, the professor curves the class very generously - the average GPA for my section was 3.18.

Great Professor, he explained Linear Algebra with its motivations really clearly. Although his class is a bit hard, it's an Honors class - what do you expect. But, he's a really nice professor and teaches extremely clearly. Recommended class.

Great lecturer with easy to understand explanations of some pretty hard concepts. His tests reflect the coursework. The lectures will make you want to learn so much more and look things up outside of class. Homework is useful in terms of preparing you for exams and generally in giving you an understanding. Fantastic overall. Pick Rabin for 150.
Took in in 2019 in actual classroom settings. He gives good lectures and I ended up learning the materials just fine.

He doesn't give typical formal proofs in class. Proving as what he does in class will result in a loss of points. Exams are much harder than homework and lecture, and he doesn't offer practice exams or finals. While homework does not represent the exam well. He is very energetic in class but fails to explain things and proof strategies clearly.

Homework isn't bad, but it is the only test prep Professor Rabin provides. Tests were very similar to HW/lectures, but very long (compared to other math courses at ucsd) and your grade will suffer if you don't immediately recognize the proof strategy. Grading was the harshest I've ever seen, however that was mostly bc of the TA, I think.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Rabin is an excellent teacher and is very helpful. That being said, his tests (especially the final) were exceptionally confusing. Homework is textbook homework, which is relatively simple and straightforward, but does NOT prepare students for exams. I was shocked at the difference between lecture/HW material and exam questions.
Tests are hard, lectures are confusing, tough grader. Has no mercy on grading even considering that we're in a pandemic and this is his first time teaching this class. Take anybody else if possible
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am not a student of high GPA, but he never loses his patience when I came to talk with him. He is highly concerned about and interested in his students' future and very patient with his work, and also a genius in mathematics. His lecture is very useful and instructing so if you come to his lecture and listen carefully, you won't worry about exams
fair professor. The grading is so harsh. If you are average of the class, you should expect b- or c+. This class is not for credit. Even grading on HW is harsh. Be ready to experience real math.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I went to lectures but didnt get much out of it, instead I taught myself almost everything. However his assignments do prepare students for exams, which are pretty straightforward. Not sure about the other TA but my TAs sections were very helpful.
such a unreasonable ta, though prof is amazing, your grade is decided by your ta. be careful!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

In term of teaching and helping students. the Prof did good job about it. His lectures are prepared and easy to follow. Homework is a little tough for some of his "own homework". Exam is very challenge and tough. If you think you that formula is easy to use, yes definitely, then he will make it 4 times harder to compute. maybe that's his style

I can assert with the utmost certainty that Jeffrey Rabin was the best mathematics instructor I was enlightened by here in beautiful La Jolla, CA. He's one tough cookie, but he truly cares for his students, and is a paragon of what a mathematics professor SHOULD BE. Take Math 150A with Rabin and you won't regret it. It may murder your GPA though.

He gives really clear lectures and makes tough material seem easy, however his tests are extremely hard. The problem is that the homework he gives do not prepare students well for the difficulty of the questions presented on the exams. The TA I got for this class was also harsh at grading. I would not recommend him if you struggle with proofs.

He is hands down the best professor I have ever had. He is amazing at explaining concepts and I learned far more in his class than I have in any other math class. He is super nice and honestly cares about his students. His tests are really hard and require critical thinking so you really need to study to do well in his class.
He is an incredible professor and made writing proofs fun!
Lectures are pretty easy to follow along if you haven't opened the book. He as a monotone voice which makes it hard to stay awake. His tests were difficult, but fair.
he is really nice and enthusiastic. I like him so much. But the test is a little bit difficult though.

Lectures made me feel too confident. You don't learn enough from lectures, must study extra hard outside because there are not enough resources to learn. Doesn't post practice exams, doesn't give you study resources except the textbook. Homework is harshly graded, as are exams. Wouldn't mind this so much if the material was taught better.

Great lecturer - very well-spoken and easy to understand.  Most of the lectures just discuss the stuff in the book so it's not entirely necessary.  Tests are pretty fair and reflective of the homework (for the most part)

He's really cocky. Unless you're a math major you won't find this class interesting. He grades the homework really harshly and has very difficult exams. His lectures are pretty much him just doing the exact thing the book does. I would not recommend.

Im not a math major, so this class was a little painful to learn cause it's pretty much all theorem's and definitions.  He grades on a curve, which is helpful cause the avg for the second midterm was 63/100.  The lectures are usually straight out of the book, and some of the hw is really confusing. Make sure you get a good TA for this class
He's so cute!!! I really enjoyed learning about proofs with Jeff Rabin.  He teaches the material in way that's easy to understand, especially for a beginner.  Big thumbs up.

Out of all the lectures, I think I showed up to 4. Including mid-term days. I bombed the first mid-term, 2nd mid-term/final we got a full page of notes, and I wrote down all the solutions to the online homework, aced the tests. Did I really understand it? Nope. Glad lectures/discussions weren't mandatory :)
Great professor, challenging but interesting class. Rabin is extremely approachable, and very helpful.

Incredibly difficult class, I was not prepared at all to take it and only passed because the professor didn't want to fail anyone. He's fantastic though and I hope to get him when I'm readier to take one of his classes. Brilliant guy.
Great professor. He's well prepared and articulates clearly. very nice and approachable. The best math professor i've had so far

He's a great professor. He is very clear, and he really knows the material and enjoys the material, which comes across during lecture. Definitely go to class - that's the best way to learn. His exams are fair, although on the difficult side because the class is difficult.

Professor Rabin is a very polite professor. But his workload in homework and tests is ridiculous.The homework and midterm was super hard and time consuming. He has a PHD in Physics not Math. So I thought this was more of a physics class than a Math class as well. Prepare to work if you take him.
Simply the best lecturer I've had. His lectures are crystal clear and his exams very fair.
Really good lecturer. Even if you dont understand the concepts at the time, just keep going to lecture. I found that once I studied the material it came a lot easier because of his teaching.

He is a very clear lecturer. The hw is hard and he expects you to put in your best effort doing the hw. When you get stuck on a problem, he'll explain what you're doing wrong and he'll guide you the correct way to solve the hw problem. But he won't give you the full solution to a hw problem because he won't spoonfeed everything you need to know.
One of the best math professors ever. Truly teaches you how to THINK rather than just churn out answers by mindlessly applying formulas

He's an articulate speaker but I don't like how he teaches. He spends too much time talking about formulas, which won't be helpful for homework. All of his examples come from textbook exercise problems. Every example problem he uses from the textbook are the ones you can find in the student solutions manual. So going to lecture isn't very helpful.
Rabin is UCSD's gift to teaching

Two reasons why I feel so lost in this class: 1) The textbook does a HORRIBLE job at explaining the concepts and has minimal example problems. 2) I don't like Rabin's  teaching style; he only writes formulas on the board and rarely gives example problems. His office hrs aren't too  helpful either. I learn better when I'm exposed to example problems

Prof. Rabin is a great teacher. The class is pretty tough because you have to think about math in ways you probably haven't before (or at least that was the case for me). But yeah, Rabin takes his time to explain everything and put it into terms everyone can understand. Make sure to do the homework because the tests are pretty similar to it.

I hate calculus... but, I like this guy.  He was really nice, and explained things until we understood them.  Probably one of the easiest Calc teachers I've had or heard of.  If you're no good at math like myself, then definitely make use of the TAs and Rabin's office hours.  Very willing to help & friendly.

Outstanding professor! Prof. Rabin keeps the attention of the class by being energetic every single lecture. I described this professor to my friends as today's Santa Claus. The workload is on the low side and the midterms and final test what you really know about the subject and not just regular problems. Take this class if you want to learn!

One of the best math professors I've taken! He really explains things and cares for teaching/learning! He simplifies complex material. His tests are pretty straighfoward, but some can be "tricky". Curves each midterm, drops a homework grade, & curves the final. Then, curves your final grade. He also takes into account improvement in grades!

Professor Rabin is the one of the best Math teachers I have EVER had. He explains things really well, and his tests are based on the HW. He is a really nice teacher- GO TO LECTURE, because the book is really difficult to understand, but Rabin makes it really easy. If you do the HW and go to class, you can get an A. Just don't f up on the midterms!

Always bright and upbeat. Lectures are clear and cover the material well, but there's only so much you can get done in a 50m lect. If you invest the necessary time in hw and section you'll be okay. The two MTs aren't too hard, but the F is somewhat trickier. All three are curved. Material is easy at first but fairly complex by the last couple weeks

Great lecturer, will dumb down all the material for you and go very very slowly in class so that everyone understands the material.. which sometimes tempts you to fall asleep. He's willing to help during office hours. tests are relatively difficult..they require you to think .. so don't expect to go into the tests just memorizing the hw's and pass.
He is an excellent professor.  I was able to learn a lot from this class.  He is able to take something very complex and break it down into simple terms, even for non-math majors.
A WAS OK, BUT B WAS REALLY HARD. THE MATERIAL IS VERY DIFFICULT, SO GO TO OFFICE HOURS BECAUSE RABIN IS FREAK'IN AWSOME AT HELPING YOU TRY TO UNDERSTAND.

So look at the other 130A posts. does going  to OH and spending a lot of time working sound like you? WELL NOT LIKE ME AT ALL. This class is NOT for the lazy.  If you work hard, you're fine. If you don't, the prof will turn into a ban shou ren and pwnzor you!!1one!1eleven!

AWESOME professor.  Hands down the best lecturer at UCSD.  Explains the most difficult material in a manner that everyone understands.  Tests are very tough, but representative of the course.  Look forward to spending 2-3 hours a week in his ofice hours because its the best.
everything is better if u go to office hours

the book, an intro to diff eqs and chaos.. i forget the name exactly, IS FREAKING HORRIBLE. trust me, hmwk is impossible unless if you go to OH or devote an unaccceptable amount of time to it (10-14 hours).  not the class for the lazy. if u like ODEs, go ahead

One of the most clear-speaking lecturers I had, in a class that required the best explanations.  Very fair, even gave a take-home final.  Very enjoyable, enthusiastic prof.  I'd take his class again in a heartbeat.
Very clear and good teacher.  His midterms and exams are very difficult.

Probably one of the best lecturers you will ever have. Not only amazingly clear and helpful, but always happy and jolly. No matter how bad his jokes are you still laugh, and tests are representative of material, and grading fair.
Professor Rabin is a good professor who speaks clearly with a mic and writes neatly on the board. Seems to draw to perfectly too. Overall good guy but the course is too conceptual, but it's ok.
A very cheery and bubbly guy who was always smiling and patient when asked questions. Explained material well, didn't lecture straight from the book.
very good best match with the ta mark
Professor Rabin was the kindest, most hilarious professor I have had. His constant cheerfulness made class enjoyable and made the rather difficult class less painful.
very good teacher... i went to his lecture even though i wasnt in his class... very jolly and makes math interesting... i highly recommend

he's so jolly you can't help but laugh at his ridiculous jokes. Very nice and very clear on his lectures. He makes sure he gets to everyone's questions and does a lot of reviewing so that you're never lost...overall good professor
Very nice, funny, and open professor. I learned much from him and he definately kept me interested in calculus.
He is very clear in his explanations!
Funny guy who's always happy in class.  He is easy to understand and lectures very well.  Made calculus as interesting as it could be.
He is very clear and does everything step by step.. If you already know clac, you might be annoyed by this but I think it helps me a lot..
One of the most well-organized and clear-spoken lecturers I've had, and very helpful during office hours. But be warned -- he lectures at high speed, and homework assignments are hard!
best math professor i ever had!
Truely one of the best. Fair and balanced class. Made calc interesting.

MATH 194 is NOT an easy class, along with the relatively high workload which is consistent to his style(10 HW, no drops at all). HOWEVER, he is accessible, agrees to 1-to-1 office hours so that you can discuss your standing and learning in private settings. If you want easy A, avoid. If you want to learn well, you can consider him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Yes there was a lot of homework but the tests felt like an overall good representation of what we did in class. Tho he didnt show much emotion he was very caring in that he was easy to access outside of class and was always open to questions in class if something was ever confusing. 10/10 professor would reccomend to a friend

This is his first time teaching MATH 194, yet the first class is clear. The textbook is provided for free, and he provides extra course notes. Noted that he does not podcast, like reviews from other class said.
Great professor. Lectures weren't recorded but the notes, HW, and practice exams given were enough to study for tests. No cheatsheets but gave a formula sheet on exams that had everything you needed.

Lectures are structured and clear, with almost impeccable board writing. There are 10 Homework and no drops. Homework are related to lecture, and exams are similar to homework, though tend to be lighter work in terms of computation. Responds to email in an astonishing speed.

Took Professor Schweinsberg in the fall for 180C and the class structure was super reasonable. Tests weren't too bad as long as you did the homework. Lectures were very informative and the notes he provided on Canvas were really useful too. Lectures for the most part were easy to follow along with as well.

Took his MATH 180A, now are taking him again. VERY responsible. Wrote and used own course notes for whole MATH 180 series(which is just a little book). Beginning of the class is not easy, but perhaps that is usual among other professors too due to content of MATH 180C.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A great professor for this course. He teaches everything throughly and with very little error. He is one of the best math professors I've ever had. The course despite what some "pretentious" people say can be difficult for some people. Though he explains the content well that I feel I grew as a student and a problem solver after this course. 10/10
10HW with no drops, and also 1st midterm date is behind drop dates so you have to drop whenever you feel pressure, however other than that he is decent and caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Homework was long and tedious and was strictly graded. Midterms were fair however final was extremely hard and unlike the practice. He posts no podcasts and has long and confusing lectures that deal with very little in relation to the homework
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was one of my favorite professors in the Math department at UCSD so far. He clearly cares about the subject and is well-respected. Some of the lectures can be groggy due to the amount of note-taking required, but he makes a hard subject much easier to understand. The homeworks are tough so start them a few days in advance and get help!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lecture not mandatory, not podcasted. Notes posted, but reads like a textbook and difficult to understand w/o lecture as it lacks examples that match homework (graded on accuracy), so forced to go to class. Difficult exams. Expect to study lots. Professor's effort is there, but it doesn't impact grades which are based on where you stand in class.
Very responsible. Reply to email very quickly. Adds additional office hours in middle of quarter. 10HW overall, do them carefully.

Hard. Homework is difficult. Went to every discussion for class, my TA just flies through every concept. He basically sums up a concept in 5 minutes, then immediately leaves once his shift is up. Tests are just like homework, suggest studying alot

no drops in HW? you don't need it as it is very easy. He use notes that he wrote, which provides a lot of intuition/insight which helps a lot on understanding concepts. You can self-taught basic things of set theory by following book by eccles of MATH109 (which is recommended for this class too) if you found beginning hard to follow.

*Probably* the best professor I had in UCSD. Everything is clear, easy to comprehend, and in organized structure. You won't get a "review your notes, I just taught this" from him if you go to his office hours. Most prof won't help you with your homework, but he will ask for your thought process and lead you to the right track. Perfect professor!

His lectures were very clear, and any questions I ever had were answered perfectly. 

He's tough, yes, but never did I feel cheated. The homework and tests were fair, it just took a lot of studying.

Also held frequent office hours if anyone needed extra help. He's very respectful and you can tell he genuinely wanted you to understand the concepts.

He is clear, concise, and articulate, making complicated mathematical concepts easy to understand. As a lecturer, He is probably the best Math Professor at UCSD as he rarely makes mistakes in his speech. There is little to no confusion about any concepts and he makes a great effort to help students become better.

The best probability professor at UCSD. Professor Schweinsberg explains every concept crystal clear and provide lots of examples to help you understand the materials. He is much better than other professors who teach Math 180BC.
Well-organized class. Prof.Schweinsberg tends to make every concept crystal clear, supported by sample problems.

He does everything right on paper, precisely crosses his t's, and is quick to respond with hints on HW, but his exams target those with natural ability versus those who worked hard to learn the material. At least 2/5th of midterms are "clever" problems vs. direct questions. As a former straight A student, proceed with caution. No textbook, BTW.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: no collaboration on homework, no clear class grading criteria, straight forward lectures, difficult class (not the fault of prof), great at answering questions/guiding you to the correct process, lots of office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is an incredibly serious and austere man. He definitely cares about his students, so don't be intimidated to ask him for clarification. He is pretty boring though and in my many meetings with him he did not really show any interest in small talk or bonding. Super super serious

Professor Schweinsberg is very detailed in his lectures. His use of examples in his lectures are representative of the homework and labs, although you may need to read parts of the book to receive a better understanding of the material. I took AP statistics and this class was mostly review. The labs and homework are very time consuming.

TONS of reading and homework, id say at least 10hrs of hw a week outside of 4hrs of lectures. His online lectures were just recordings of him regurgitating powerpoint slides which were unmemorable and made concepts hard to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Pros: Professor Schweinsberg is a very good lecturer. His lectures are fantastic and his slides are very detailed. Cons: He lacks flexibility (even with online courses and the COVID-19 situation). He only accepts homework and labs up to one hour late for a 20% reduction.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: So much busy work in this class. Prof is a very tough grader and not understanding at all. RIP to your gpa if you take his class

Follow lectures and do the homework and youll be ok. Lots of work? yes given that its a five units class. Hard exams? no as long as you do the homework and labs. I dont understand why some people are complaining lol I mean dont blame the prof if your grade is not up to your expectation...

His lectures are clear and easy to understand. Course materials are well organized. Trading criteria is clear if you took sometime reading the syllabus. The midterms were fair if you put in the effort. It's a 5unit class so I expected a heavier workload. It's a rough quarter for all of us and to be fair, he didn't deserve the low ratings...
Awful class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The only hard thing about the class was the material, but the rest of the online course was easy. His lectures are good, and I read at first, but his lectures are enough to do the HW and lab. The midterms were easy; exactly like the HW and lab. Honestly didn't understand anything at all, and got A on MT I and B on MT II. He will curve.

A terrible professor. A terrible class. Very harsh grader on hws and exams. This class gives me high anxiety. So many hws and labs! Do not be mislead by the previous good reviews, I feel like he doesn't care about the students learning at all. AVOID HIM AT ALL COST! sb

WORST professor I ever had at UCSD. A very tough grader. He makes the class much harder than it needs to be. The homework and labs are very time consuming. He is not helpful and doesn't care about the students at all. The average in the class is around a C+. Would rather wait another year and take other professors instead.
I hate this class so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: I think all of these positive reviews come from having him in person.. Taking him online, he is terrible. He throws equations into the slides and doesn't explain what the variables mean or how they relate. He's one of the worst professors I've ever had and you're better off reading the textbook. It truly feels like he doesn't care if you understand
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I don't understand how there are so many good reviews. He is a very harsh grader, doesn't offer any extra credit, doesn't drop any hw or lab grade regardless whatever circumstances. The hw and labs takes extremely long time to finish, and he is very picky of wording on hw and labs. The grading scale is very unclear so you no idea what to expecct.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The lectures are pretty organized and clear. The contents of this course are quite challenging and it takes lots of time to do homework. Exams are fair. As long as you work hard your grade won't be bad.

The best math lecturer at UCSD. Lectures are super clear, and homework assignments are long and challenging, but are worth the effort. The only downside is that he can't deal with criticism. When asked about an unclear wording on an exam, he indirectly blamed the international students for their lack of English fluency (outside of class).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Jason is easy to access outside the class. He is very nice and patient to answer your questions even though u might not currently taking his class.

Took intro to probability with him. He was one of the best professors that I had taken a class with at UCSD. His lectures are very well structured, he writes very clearly on the board, he gives a lot of examples, and it's clear especially in his office hours that he cares about his students. Homeworks can be challenging but exams are fair.

Best math prof in UCSD. He knows exactly how to deliver the concept to you, his lectures are very structural and clear. He writes on the board so make sure you attend the lectures and follow his notes. The HW reflects what you have learned and what you will be having in the test. Study the HW, the notes, you will be OK.

Professor Schweinsberg is amazing! His lectures and clear and concise, and it really helps that he writes his notes on the chalkboard so that students may keep up with him. Although there is a lot of homework and reading, his lectures help clear up many concepts I had trouble with. Tests were very fair. Best professor I've ever had.
The best professor in UCSD! The lectures are well-organized and clear. Homework helps you learn and exams are fair. Highly recommend
Taking this class was an absolute joy and a pleasure. He makes even the most complicated concepts seem downright simple. The homework problems were fun.

THE best math professor at UCSD! He is patient and is always willing to help you with whatever questions you have with the lecture or the homework. Although his homework assignments are long and difficult at times, they are meaningful and really help you learn. His lectures are super clear and are well organized. Take him for any class he teaches.

Hat off to this professor! Such a caring and respected professor who will take time out of class to clarify any concerns or questions students may have. Coming from AP Stats, this course is literally a whole year condensed into ten weeks, but if you saved your notes it's a godsend. Tests are very fair BUT wow homework and labs are incredibly long.

He is one of very few professors at UCSD who genuinely care about their students. I had questions on pretty much every computer lab, and he would get back to me with very clear answer in a prompt manner. Homework can be difficult from time to time, but they are very reflective of exam questions.

His lectures broke down all the concepts perfectly. His tests were very representative of lectures and homework. He does everything on the chalkboard so go to lecture. Be careful on the homework since it is not graded so easily. Math labs take quite some time to finish but definitely help you more with understanding the conceptual information.

Don't take this class without having a clear schedule. You need to work hard to understand things, because they teach in terms of "this is how i'd explain it to someone who already knows it" instead of "this is what it means for those of you who are new to this subject".
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Low key in love with this guy. He gave us difficult homework at times, but the tests very much matched the homework. He emphasizes homework a lot (35%), but don't think you can just get 100% for completeness. It's graded on correctness. And don't try to cheat either. He's a stickler and will catch you. He caught someone every week. GO TO OFF. HOURS
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: VERY DIFFICULT HOMEWORK! EXAMS ARE EASIER THAN HOMEWOKR. THE HARDEST CLASS FOR ME EVER
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The homeworks are meaningful, but very challenging at times. I emphasize how difficult some of these assignments are, especially because of how many proofs would come out. Compared to the homeworks, the tests are nothing really, so he prepares you well. Go to lecture! It helps with the homework immensely. If not, you have to read the textbook.

Prof Schweinsberg is actually amazing! He's so patient in answering everyone's questions regardless of how irrelevant or redundant. His lectures are extremely clear because he writes everything down on the blackboard and gives more than sufficient examples that fully explain all the concepts. Everyone should take Math 11 with Schweinsberg!!!
