He is the BEST professor I've ever had in UCSD, lectures are so clear since he writes everything you need to know on the blackboard and also useful examples. He is SOOOO caring and nice, answering many questions in class and making sure students understand. Exams are fair enough!!! Recommend 100%!

I love this professor! Not only were his lectures crystal clear most of the time, he provided insights about the concepts that the textbook did not mention. To me it seems he acknowledges the fact that not everyone is smart and lectures in a way so that everyone can understand. He is frequently available and is able to answer many of your questions
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best professors! Lectures are very clear and interesting. All the topics are organized well. The final is a little bit hard compared to previous exams tho.

His lectures are very clear and coherent. He presents the material in a very intuitive and approachable manner. There are 10 homework assignments (35%), 2 midterm (15% each), and a final (35%). The homework assignments are fairly straight forward with a few challenging problems.

great professor, definitely would recommend. his lecture is very clear, engaging, and he writes everything you need to know on the chalkboard. homework is mandatory and so are the labs that accompany the class, but both are doable if you put some effort into them. midterms and final reflected the class well and there were no surprises.

This is the most difficult class I have had in a while.  Schweinsberg gives very difficult assignments but I have never gotten so much out of a class.  At the end of this course you will know the basics of probability.  His lectures are perfect, never missed a class.  I recommend him 100%.

He is an organized person.His lecture is easy to understand. The notation was set step by step, and there are very clear. His homework and exam are close related to his lecture. If we put attention to his homework, his exam is not hard at all. Btw,he is a cute professor.
He's fantastic! He's organized, clear, always on time, gives great example problems, and he's super nice in office hours. He's the best teacher I've ever had.

Brilliant professor! Schweinsberg's lectures are clear, he's very organized, writes everything out on the board, and is always willing to repeat concepts. His tests are straight from the homework and class notes, so no surprises. I'm really glad I got to have him as a teacher.

Awesome, awesome prof. Prof. Schweinsberg is a great teacher, albeit a little dry sometimes. Gives very concrete and clear examples relevent to HW, which can be hard since he writes it himself. The class is a challenge. BUT you will LEARN something, and that a lot. I don't usually go to lectures. But I went to all of 180A and ended up loving it.

His voice threw me off at first, but he's really an excellent professor. The material itself is easy enough, but he also explains everything clearly, has good examples, wants to help, gives very fair exams, and is very organized and on top of things. Don't get hung up on his voice because he's really a great professor.
Great professor! Explains concepts in a way that is easy to understand.  Exams are very fair.  I highly recommend him.

This is my first time ever commenting for a professor on this website.. just reading through the comments i could help myself but to say something. This professor is so ridiculously GOOD i cannot believe anyone said anything bad about him. Since when is being organized a bad thing? The man is extremely kind- he is the best prof ive had at UCSD.

Very clear professor, very precise.  You definitely should go to lecture, although his review lectures before the midterms are a bit pointless if you've done the required homework.  He is very detail oriented.  I feel bad for him cause some people make fun of him because of his appearance and voice, but he's really very nice and helpful.

Math 11 in general is an easy class. If you go to lecture, you definitely dont have to read the textbook. He is precise, and tells you exactly what is going to be on the tests. Tests are easy, homework may be challenging. Be careful with labs. Be picky with your wordings cuz one bad lab = decrease in 1/2 letter grade.

This prof really knows how to teach, he explains everything perfectly and is always willing to answer questions. The hw and labs take about 8 hours each week so be prepared for work. The midterms werent hard since he posts practice ones which are exactly like the one he gives you. Take him if you can, great teacher!!!
Take Psych 60 if you can. This class should be easier than it is, midterms were pretty hard.

he's the nerdiest person i've ever seen in my life...he looks like someone from the show "Beauty and the Geek." the class does sneak up on you because he tries to make each test harder and harder because he claims too many people were getting A's...his voice sounds like Tweety

Wow! Schweinsburger is quite the character. Probably one of the most awkward guys you will ever meet in your life, I kid you not! I saw him in the dining halls once, could hardly talk to me! He is super OCD too, his penmanship is perfect and he writes in perfect rows on the board. Weird yes, but did I love him, YES!!

Prof. Schweinsberg is quite the character (between the high, nasally voice and the baseball fanaticism), but he also happens to be an amazing teacher. Go to lecture and you will learn nearly everything you need to know. His lectures are crystal clear and you'd think he'd rehearsed them as he never (EVER) makes a mistake. Take this class!!

If you need to take a stats course, definitely take this prof. His lectures are extremely clear and helpful, and his tests are very fair and representative of the lecture and the homework he assigns.  One of the best profs I've had at UCSD.

His high-pitched voice is so annoying! He works out examples in class but his voice makes lectures unbearable. Lab takes a lot of time and is graded harshly even though it's only a 1 unit class... Study hard and do well on the tests. Barely a curve because EVERYONE does so well.

Probably the worst professor I have ever taken. Voice is high-pitched and annoying. Homework and labs are long and useless. Constantly looks at his watch to make sure he is on schedule. Class is TOO easy . ONLY TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU HAVE TO. This professor was ridiculous. Looked forward to the quarter being over, so i wouldnt see him anymore.

Teacher is very clear in class, but is also very boring.  Supposedly tried to change up his routine, and made the class harder. Homework and labs are graded pretty critically.  Midterms are homework problems. High pitched voice is sort of annoying.  Take the class only if you NEED to.

One of the best teachers; explains exactly what you need to know and only tests you on that.  Learned a lot, but an easy class, one of those classes that gives you the enthusiasm and confidence to keep going in the subject; not entertaining or funny but keeps your attention through clarity and really good explaning; I actually felt good at math

He reminds you of the little boy who was your neighbor growing up that was always building robots and probably dreams about esoteric math concepts. He is one of the best and brightest math teachers on campus despite looking not a day older than 12 years old.

This class was dull and boring (not because of the teacher). Schweinsberg was a good teacher. If you love stats, you'll love this class. If stats is boring to you, you won't like this class. It isn't hard to get a good grade, but it's hard to get an "A" (class is curved so that the average is a B-). You can get by just reading the book.

newer teacher at UCSD.  Really odd voice.  entire lecture is dictated to black board, with his back to the class.  Assigns extra HW problems that are later seen on midterms.  Class: good,  Teacher: not so much

Very good, clear, teacher.  Has a high pitched voice and explains everything very well.  Writes everything on the board and has very clear handwriting.  One of the best Math Professors on campus.  Has concern for students and makes sure students understand the material very well.  Recommend!! A+++

Basically a good teacher, he's new to UCSD. High-pitched voice gets annoying. Do the practice problems in the book as they're on midterms. TA for Fall quarter spoke poor English and had terrible communication skills. Class was very dry.

Kind prof. I hardly attended lectures but did decent. Exams are rough. They are extremely specific and despite lots of studying, I'd always get a 60%. There's a myth buster project you complete throughout the quarter and she has guidelines. Super specific, but it also helped raise my grade after I failed the exams. 3 exams total, 1 is dropped

So, so nice and clearly cares a lot about her students. I've taken her for PSYC 100 and PSYC 172, and both classes deal with some sensitive topics. She takes a lot of care in keeping everyone comfortable and engaged, which I really appreciated. I would take her again and again! Exams are fairly easy (cheat sheet is allowed!)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's a fine and caring teacher but her lectures are so unclear, she never gets to the main point and rambles on a lot about things that aren't in the exams. The questions are all application based and the answer choices are all technically "correct" but have to choose the best one. 3 in person exams, 1 dropped which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: personally, her lectures and slides were all over the place that i just stopped attending. her exams are application based, so pay close attention to wording. she prob wont implement the online quizzes/exams anymore because of FA25. attendance is extra credit and she drops lowest exam and quiz which are both open note. wouldnt take again ngl
i just dont like her teaching style, lots of trick questions, not clear.w us almost passive aggressive
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: im dumb as hell and passed the class with a B. 8 quizzes, one dropped and 3 exams, lowest dropped. online. except students are stupid and fumbled by using AI which is easily monitored through canvas when you take exams lol so final was in person. go to lecture tho, she can ramble sometimes but the class was rlly interesting and easy.
Super great professor. I don't understand the low ratings. Very clear and straightforward material with engaging lectures in my opinion. Am taking another class with her next quarter. def recommend.

Prof. Dickenson was an ok - a little boring to me but she was nice and loved to answer questions. Grade was made up of 2/3 exams and 8/9 quizzes. Everything was open book but exams were still confusing. Can get extra credit for attendance and requires SONA (about 4% of grade). She's not a bad prof but I knew too much of the material to be engaged.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof keeps you engaged during class and topics are interesting. With that said, 40% of your grade is based on exams that are extremely confusing. Went to office hours multiple times and even the TAs mentioned how the questions were tricky even when it EXPLICITLY SAYS no trick questions. For my fellow neurodivergent students I don't recommend her.

She's passionate for sure! But she's disorganized in her lecture style. She talks too fast and doesn't seem to have a plan for what she is going to say, so you hear a lot of umms. She hardly ever repeats or emphasizes the important point that she is trying to make, especially when asking the class questions, which can make lectures tough to follow.

I'm not into hiding behind anonymous reviews, so I waited for my time at ucsd to end. She is an amazing professor and teaches you in a way you WILL remember every single thing you learned forever. Dr. Dickenson is amazing. I truly respect her dedication to her field. Highly recommend taking 172, 127, etc with her. You won't regret it. 

- Aria

I don't understand the low ratings! If you're a student who has a life outside of school, seriously take this class. It's easy and she sets you up for success so that you don't procrastinate. We basically work on a project for the whole quarter which is easy because she breaks it down in steps. Also attendance is not mandatory and exams are online.

The IUG's were so bad for this quarter and often gave bad or just wrong advice. They were really nice though! Prof is very passionate and knowledgable and i learned a lot. The instructions for the mythbuster assignment are so much longer than they need to be.

Graded on the mythbuster and three exams, one is dropped. I wasn't a fan of the mythbuster and the TA/IAs were so particular and didn't explain feedback. However, the content was interesting and the exams are easy and they're open-note, literally just have the slides open and read the assigned readings before.
very fun course and lectures were very engaging. all exams were online and were given enough time for the amount of questions being asked.
Best professor at this school
Her class is pretty chill but the myth buster project is pretty time consuming and research heavy so get ready for that!

Professor Dickenson's class is structured with two midterms (the best is taken) and one final, along with a MASSIVE Mythbuster Project. Her grading is very fair, and office hours is a great resource to take advantage of if you need it. I made the mistake of thinking it was TOO easy, and ended with an A-, make sure to stay on top of things

Super caring and thoughtful professor. Graded by 2 things: weekly reading quiz and 3 exams. For reading quiz, skim the text - questions literally ask what the text says, so as long as ur active recall is good, ur good (open book). Exams are highly HIGHLY reflective of lectures. Don't just memorize the lecture... UNDERSTAND it. Lowest exam dropped.
I really enjoyed PSYC 100. Dr. Dickenson seems super knowledgable and I am looking forward to taking more of her classes.

Honestly I don't get why her ratings are so low. Her class was very fair and forgiving, and she cares DEEPLY about her students. She's not wasting your time, I've always found her lectures valuable with real life application. She challenges how you think about psychology by connecting abstract concepts rather than just plain memorization
Knows her stuff but lecture delivery is horrible. Throws in more information/comments than needed which really confuses people.

This prof really knows her stuff but I did not care for her teaching style. Attendance isn't mandatory but it actually is because the lecture slides don't include all of the information you need. Tests were very difficult and very specific to what she talks about in person and the extra readings she assigned. Very intense, don't recommend
I did not like her teaching style. Its personal preferance but she was very boring and monoton. I would not take a class with her again personally.

I thought that this class was interesting, but you have to be open minded. There is a really good timeline for your final project but I'd say to really pay attention during lectures because her midterm questions were very detailed and VERY specific to the readings.

I learned so much from this class, you will enjoy it if you have an open mind and are willing to work a little. The readings were long but really interesting, all exams had questions from readings. Mythbuster assignment was a little intimidating but you go through it step by step. It's podcasted but I recommend going so you can discuss with others!

Class is interesting but exams were extremely difficult. You don't know your actual grade until it's finalized. There is a curve at the end though. The only upside of the class was exams were online, but they were all application based and the most obscure topics barely went over.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Pros: group work was fun, material was digestable and easy, assignments were clear, open to all opinions, easy A

Cons: lectures fast, tests arent 100% reflective, group work would be better in an online setting or a bigger classroom to facilitate everyone hearing each other.

Overall, great class and great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment:
GET AWAY FROM THIS PROF
Unreasonable homework and replacement homework
A lot of work to do
Exams are online but hard

SUPER interesting class. Dr. Dickenson is a great lecturer. She is casual, but knowledgable and the lectures are  interesting. 
The downside about this class was that we (the students) never really got comfortable with each other, so some of our discussions lacked depth. I wish she would've facilitated a little more community amongst us.

Super engaging professor. She made the class super inclusive and interesting and always made sure students were comfortable. She was truly caring and willing to talk to students about anything. Sometimes the reading assignments were long, but exams were fair and lowest is dropped. One large project, but it's not difficult. I would recommend taking.

Least favorite class by FAR at UCSD. I dropped it once but it was the only option in my last quarter to finish my degree, would have rather walked on broken glass. Just painfully uninteresting, uninspired, common knowledge content. Horribly nitpickiy grading on the stupid busywork assignments, treats upper div students like they're freshmen. Awful.
Would not reccomend this class, so much busywork and the topics are a lot less interesting than you'd expect.

A good professor overall, but says "uhm" "ermm", A LOT during lecture and it was a little distracting. She was a good lecturer and exams were based on lecture, but her questions are definitely hard applied questions and not just memorization.

(+): Group discussions were fun, lecture material wasn't too difficult, drop the lowest group discussion and test score. 
(-): Exams don't represent material, lectures faster than you can write, group discussion rubric was ambiguous, OH was unhelpful for exam questions. Lecture recordings were a week late. 

Easy A- class, but harder to earn an A.
People who dont like Janna dont like being told 'no.' Do the readings, go to class, go to office hours and you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Disappointing quarter. Vague and ill prepared lectures. If you don't read you won't pass exams. Daily participation questions were never organized and too complex for a large class. Professor showed minimal care in students' concerns on any aspect of the class. Took weeks to receive some slides. 1 of 3 exams are dropped. Wouldn't take again.

Class structure is confusing. Reading quizzes based on book, exams based on lecture but exam questions are confusing and she doesn't go into enough detail during lecture for you to know the material. Says no trick questions but they feel like it. Lectures are awkward as well. You can get an A pretty easily but it's not an enjoyable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her class was straightforward  but she was incredibly ableist! She performed a monologue to teach us about disorganized symptoms of schizophrenia that was basically her mocking the disorder. Most bizarre and uncomfortable experience I've had in a classroom, and I can't imagine how much worse it must be for someone who has schizophrenia

Shes knowledgeable and the course is interesting. She is not too understanding or flexible. Test questions can be ambiguous and she wasnt very accommodating. Reading quizzes are very specific based on the textbook (which is very dense with material) and you really have to read it to do well on the quizzes. Attendance mandatory

I wanted to like this class. Since it was online maybe that had something to do with it, but there was a lot of negativity, it was unorganized and had ambiguous test questions. Never saw so many students upset with a professors testing before. I could have stayed and passed with an A, but I wouldn't have learned anything. Happy I dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A great professor who did an amazing job in explaining concepts and material that is discussed in the textbook. Your grade is based on reading quizzes, 2 midterms, and a final (all of which are non-cumulative). Two quizzes are dropped and your lowest exam is dropped. I would recommend doing the study glides before each exam!

The class is based on reading quizzes and the midterms/final exam. She is a really good professor who makes her lectures a fun learning environment that really grabs your attention. I would definitely take notes though because it will help with the quizzes and exams.

For this class, all you need to do was read the text book, and we were only graded on reading quizzes. She is a great teacher. My only complaint about her is that she goes through the slides really fast, so taking notes can be challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Janna genuinely cares about her students inside and outside of the classroom. Janna accommodates to each and every student and is flexible (i.e., removing unfair test questions from grading), and has a drop one midterm/drop 2 quizzes. Take her if you can, she is funny, kind, and a great teacher. Only knock is her slides can be clunky at times.

Loved this professor! Her exams were very representative of concepts we learned in class and were very engaging. She does make you read the textbook, however, I think it really is beneficial so you can come to class with a better understanding of the topics discussed in class. Also always answers everyone's questions to the best of her abilities!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a cool professor who wants to help her student succeed! She makes it abundantly clear what will be tested and is always open to answering open ended questions! (:

(+): Passionate, cares about students' learning, accommodates everyone (drop 2/8 lowest quizzes and 1/3 lowest exams), and has nerdy humor. If you have questions about being a psychologist, she is the person you want to ask. Lecture-based exams - noncumulative (-): 30-40 pages of reading a week for the reading quizzes (3 tries per quiz though!).
BEST PROF EVER!! so much extra credit you cannot do bad in this class. She is so dedicated and takes feedback seriously
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor is very kind, the class it self wasn't difficult at all. I could even go as far to say the class was quite enjoyable. 6 quizzes, lowest quiz dropped. The other assignment was just called a "myth buster" project where every week built upon your previous weeks work. Do the work and you'll get a great grade.

Worst professor I've ever had. Very boring and honestly a joke. Overall the class work was just tedious and was easy I feel like she could've done a better job at explaining things and being more specific about the material she was teaching.

Tough topics (basically a ton of physiology - felt like BIPN100 all over again) but she gives a lot of easy assignments to the point you don't even have to watch lecture. I did the weekly assignments in < 1 hour w/o watching lecture, & aced the midterm w/o watching lectures. Only midterm or final counted, so didn't have to take the final. Easy A

Topics are complex, the assignments helped a lot. Reading is graded, so if you're like me and benefit from it, but don't make time, it makes a world difference. I don't know my grade yet but (for your reference) I got a 100 on the hw and missed 1 on the midterm. I'm no genius so if you do the work it'll be great! She also gave tons of Extra credit!

It's obvious that Janna knows her stuff in her field. However, her class is very disorganized. It was hard to determine which points she lectured about would be useful to know for exams. Lots of reading. While there are some useful points in reading, most of it was unnecessary for exams. Exams felt unrepresentative of what was being taught.

Janna is a super cool and an amazing person to speak with on things not related to the class. That being said she kinda sucks as a professor. The lectures are her just reading off her bullet points and nothing really flows together well. She assigns textbook chapters but says she won't test on them. The exams are difficult but she drops one.

Very accommodating to students. Lectures were recorded and synchronous attendance was not mandatory. There is a weekly group activity. Tests are lecture based and reading is supplemental to lecture. Go to lecture, do the readings, and ask questions when you need help and youre good to go! Tons of extra credit.

The readings for this class are so long and meticulous and a majority of the information you don't need for exams. Lectures and boring and disorganized. The professor is not the greatest at explaining topics. Exams are hard and test specific material. For being a lower-division class, info goes very into detail and so much to memorize.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: So heres the tea. Its her first quarter teaching, and she is a lovely person to chat with, very accommodating w/ OSD stuff, but expectations & lectures were very confusingwhen students asked for clarification her extra notes were more confusing! I struggled to take notes & got a B+ only bc of prior knowledge. No study guide or practice tests ):
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She takes feedback after each of her exams and really takes it into consideration. Although the exams were tough, I studied minimally and did decently. By no means am I good at biological psych, but I received a good grade due to the amounts of extra credit that she offers. If you attend lecture and take good notes, you should be fine.

While the prof seems to know her stuff, she was incredibly unclear with what she expected of us and her exams were absurdly difficult and unrelated to the lectures to the point that I stopped going mid quarter. A ridiculous curve had to be used just so everyone didn't fail. Overall, a light 2/10 experience if I'm being generous.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The instructor is a passionate professor and is such a gem for anyone who is interested in clinical psychology. That being said, readings, activities, and lectures are super hard, but I would argue that level of difficulty of this course is necessary for a sensitive topic like clinical psychology where people's health are at stake.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: One of my least favorite professors I have had at UCSD. Pretty unreal that a lower division PSYC 2 class would be one of the hardest psychology classes at UCSD. So much memorization, and the small group activities are the biggest pain ever. Avoid this class if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: When she asked for feedback on the class, students complained about the amount of reading assigned. She retorted theyd have to read in grad school so why not start now in a bitter way. Also spends half of class time doing awkward group activities with contradictory, confusing instructions. Its not easy to ask her for clarification either.

Terrible experience, her lectures are disorganized and unrelated to exams, if you want to pass, read the textbook because her pdf notes won't help! Mandatory attendance for SLIC activities or no points! her class is 60% graded exams and the rest split between random assignments and the weekly group activity, would not recommend to anyone.
Lectures are boring, a bit inorganized. Exams are not very related to lecture.

Janna as a person is very nice and passionate but I wouldn't recommend her. She is not organized or clear and her exams are all over the place. She assigns about 120 pgs of reading per week all from different texts that are very dry and repetitive. We had weekly group activities where we spent most of our class time instead of lecturing. Good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took Math18 in Fall 2025, before his ratings dropped from a 4 to a 2. He is not a bad professor at all although his slides are just a copy paste of the textbook. He had a policy of mandatory homework quizzes where if failed will lead to a 5% deduction of the final grade. However, his lectures were decent and TA was amazing. Underrated for sure.

Not the best, not the worst. More tells you how to do something rather than teaching you and skips steps which threw me off. Exams were relatively difficult and weren't very reflective of homework content despite what you're told. Self teaching or going to TLC tutoring at ucsd will help you a lot more with understanding the content in his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You can tell that he is still upset about being reported to the math department and this caused him to be petty and unhelpful throughout the entire class. Whenever I went to lecture it just seemed like he was horribly miserable and it made the environment dull. He also rarely answered questions and would just tell us to ask the TA's instead.

all tests are based on the homework, the midterms were verrrrrry easy like 4 questions and all based on the homework, pretty generous curve at the end, the final wasn't hard it was just long but like if you just do the homework and study the homework you'll do fine theres no surprises and nothing to memorize, he changed everything from last quarter
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Briones had good lectures and always checked if students were following along. His tests (etc.) had to be approved by the math dept, but were modeled after HW. Grades were determined by the midterms and final. He's a good professor, it's the subject that's hard. There ended up being a curve but don't try to rely on that.

His lectures were unbearable to be in. Nothing he says in class is extra helpful, just repeating slides. I was disappointed by lack of whimsy, as I remember hearing about a pikachu suit and was hoping to make conversation about it. Overall, he can't be blamed for my performance (mental health is important), but generally not my favorite professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Your grade in his classes hinges on getting ALL your homework quizzes (unnanounced) 100% correct, every one you get wrong is a -5% to your full grade and even the slightest mistake can make you fail them. His slides aren't well-organized, and his explanation is hard to comprehend - using AI is recommended to self-teach the materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take his class. No curve, bad lectures, bad notes, exams not as described. No guidance as to what is important for tests. And, on the off chance there is guidance, it's either extremely vague or straight wrong.

Hated the class, but he was like fine. He had his whole curriculum scrubbed, so the class is very different now. Anything under 70% is an F (he doesn't do D's) and there is no curve. The grade is the best average of either 5% hw, 3% disc. attendance, 21% per midterm (there's 2), & 50% final OR 5% hw, 3% disc., 26% best midterm score, & 66% final.

I took Math 10A with Dr. Briones last quarter. He had some questionable policies surrounding homework and homework quizzes, but by the end of the quarter those didn't exist. His exams were quite easy and he gave EXTREMELY telling exam outlines. Class is very similar to AP Calc AB.

Examples are important to pay attention to in class. If you can teach yourself the homework questions and do lots of repetition with content until it's automatic, it is doable. Knowing how to self-study here really helps. Inconsistent in office hours, so make advantage of the knowledge of the TAs. Responds on Piazza and, surprisingly, Reddit.

Lectures were not helpful and he didn't do a good job of teaching material. I've heard he used to be a good professor but now he's not very good. He gave us the syllabus late, assigned homework after the final and tested us on that material. No bueno. He also is always canceling lectures.
Spiteful prof. He barely teaches and just mumbles the content to himself. If you can teach yourself the content you should be fine but if not, good luck finding ur will to live
Lack of professionalism. Often shows up late, cancels 2 mins before OH/lecture about to start.

You can tell he's very very sour at the administration for interfering with how he teaches the course. All of his whimsy has been drained out of him.

No textbook, weekly online hw with unlimited attempts, 2 midterms and a final.

Overall, its not that bad if you've taken a calc class before. However, I personally struggled a lot with the material.

Grade was entirely exams, but if you didn't do homework you would lose points. Same with quizzes, they didn't add to your grade, but would subtract 5% if you failed, and were just 1 question with varying difficulty. Exams were extremely tough. The department had to step in to change his exams and grading policy because even A+ students complained.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only complaint I can have about Mr. Pikachu is that he failed to clarify his rules on discussion quizzes in the original syllabus and left everyone worrying about their grade 24/7. But otherwise he was a fun and interesting teacher.

Worst professor ive ever had, the math department had to step in because of his grading policy, if nothing had changed before the final, half the class wouldve failed 10b. Extremely harsh grading, 80 page rubric that is so heavily relied on for things, did not even correct my grade on the final even though they blatantly made a mistake.

reviews.comment: Grading criteria was exceedingly harsh. A single failed quiz would deduct 5% from final grade, and final grade was almost solely based on two midterms and one final. reviews.comment: He was ok. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Always late for the class, and even for the midterm. He changed his grading policy less than a day before the final and made the course super stressful. I do NOT think he is here to help students to learn since I put too much time on being scared, instead of really being focused and learning something. Had to review everything by myself.

I used to think he was a bad professor because of his tough grading, but he later changed it and made multiple grading schemes. The one you got the best on was the one your grade would be. He is late, however. But you are in a tough class, so just ask for help.

Didnt know the location of my final until 10 minutes beforehand. Boring lectures where he just read off of the slides that were to be posted anyways. Midterms were slightly difficult but not unreasonable and final was really easy
Thought he was good. Showed up 20 minutes late to the final exam, though.

Can pass with hard word. Good lecturer giving time to ask questions and take notes. Tough grader but changed syllabus to be easier. Exams straightforward and based off homework. Homework can be difficult though because it's from the book, he doesn't make them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Do not take his classes

Pre-syllabus change, he's a 2. Post-syllabus change, he's a 3. You probably know the negatives so let me list the positives: LENIENT exam rubrics (the main reason I got an A+) and helpful exam outlines. I took AP Calc AB, barely scored a 3, and I consider myself a calculus hater. This class only solidified my hate, but you might prob do fine idk.

reviews.comment: never in class on time always spend more time end of class. HW is harder than anything

I do not recommend taking Math 10B with Professor Briones. Lectures & homework often did not align with midterms, and homework was extremely difficult with little guidance. Office hours and discussion were not helpful, as even the TA struggled with worksheets. This lack of support made the course very frustrating.

Lectures are funny, hard to understand, 10 mins late for every class. His ppt summarizes the key info from the textbook. Test questions are mostly theory-based, similar to "logically completes the text" in SAT. Need logic & long explanations otherwise you won't get full points. Math dept interferes to make sure we survive.
Pressure!

Be prepared! Originally HW was worth 0% , HW quizzes were brutal weekly occurrences that were pass or fail (a pass does not help your grade, just saves it), and he came to every lecture late dressed in a pikachu onesie. However, he is an excellent and forgiving grader, just study a lot and you will be fine. It won't be fun but it will be rewarding.

BEFORE the math department changed his syllabus it was hellish. Quizzes docked grade by 5% for each failed. Had to study incredibly hard to stay ahead of the curve. Lectures are solid, hes not really a bad professor just harsh policy to counter AI but imo went too far. NOW his grading policy is more fair, unsure which grading policy he keeps.

reviews.comment: always late, tests were conceptual instead of computational questions. He's very irresponsible and does not deliver lectures well (complicated sentences, which are hard to understand, and are accessible from textbooks). The instructions for making up quizzes were very strict, and he had lots of restrictions on grading and completing assignments.

Don't take this class if ur new-ish to calc. Took calc AB (got a 3) and BC (2), so this class was somewhat review, but he is not a good lecturer. This professor has a 37 page long syllabus to scare students. He does too much in general.

reviews.comment: Maybe if the professor stopped trying to debate people online via *THAT* website, he would have actually finished grading on time.

prof is always late and the tests material were not in lecture or in HW. Spent 2-3 hours on computational problems in the HW when 90% of the test was conceptual. Lectures were overly confusing  Fails at preparing students properly. the math dept had to step in and change his rubric and final test. Do not trust the 5 scores, it the prof own review.

Prof Pikachu is a really caring teacher. He's always there to help you if you genuinely want to learn the content. Just make sure you actually study the materials and do the hwk on your own, instead of relying on genAI for help. Exams and quizzes are exactly like what he's teaching. He doesn't deserve the hates!

please don't take him, he is very rude and started scaring students when the department chair started investigating his class, look on reddit for more detailed reviews, exams are extremely difficult and longer than they should be, always something wrong with exams printing or him being late, class should be worth 12 units at least
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Briones is nice, don't get me wrong. I just wouldn't take him again to save myself a lot of stress.

Man what can I say about this guy. He wears a pikachu onesie to class everyday and is late to every lecture. I have gotten a high B on both midterms, but this guys homework quiz policy might have me end up failing the class. -5% for each homework quiz you fail and if you fail a certain amount you fail the entire course!!!
Hes a chud

Switched out of 20B thinking 10B would be easier. im sure it is with a different professor. the whole quiz grading policy is just cruel. wish i dropped the class or switched back after reading that long, overly complicated syllabus. avoid at all cost. never felt worse taking a class.. and i thought i was strong in math.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: just dont.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Where do i start. I took him because he had good ratings. Ofc I had to be nerfed. This is hell. Homework i'm pretty sure is 0% of our grade. He was late to every lecture and complained when students would get up when class ended. The 5% quiz deduction is diabolical. I hope and pray the final is going to be curved.
I wont take his class again 100%.

Like most here I had his math 18 class and the best way I can explain his main issue (though far from the only one) here is that his syllabus is needlessly difficult and vague. Everything in it is designed to either punish you  for not understanding the material fast enough or vague enough to have you stressing out what material to prioritize.

This is my first math class here at UCSD and I swear I rather take the AP calc BC exam again for the rest of my life than go to his lectures which he late for every. Single. Day.
