Very very amazing math professor! I was able to understand all of his lectures and he explained new topics clearly & well, even doing short reviews of helpful prior knowledge so no one was left confused. Gives exam outline to study, and lots of office hours if you need extra help! Showed exam goals through lectures, so watch them! Take Dr. Jor-el!
Great professor! Made the lecture materials easy to understand and provided amazing exam outlines! Very accommodating and helpful outside of class
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had. Very sweet and easy to understand; the way the lectures are constructed are really easy to follow.
He wears a pikachu onesie to class. Enough said.

Without question the best professor I've had at UCSD. His lectures make me feel like my out-of-state tuition is worth it. Math 20B is supposed to be the hardest out of the series, but he makes it feel very fun and easy.
Professor came to every single lecture wearing a Pikachu onesie. He's a true G.

Such a great professor! Prof Briones communicates very clearly the expectations of class and exams. If you learn what he says to learn you are sure to get As! He does not try to trick students at all and is very transparent about what is tested and what isn't. There are so many ways to get help and he responds quickly to questions.

Handwriting isn't his forte but hes a really good professor. He is transparent on exams which is SUPER helpful and the lectures make sense if you follow along. His Pikachu costume and personality are a wholehearted break from the emotionally barren and demanding attitudes of other professors. I would recommend reading the textbook alongside lecture

Great professor!! His lectures could be a bit confusing sometimes (because of his handwriting), but slides are posted and lectures are recorded so it wasn't an issue. He is very funny and has a big personality, and does a really good job of explaining specifics for exams so I never felt too confused or surprised. Definitely cares about his students

Professor was funny (wore a Pikachu onesie to every lecture) and was very knowledgable on material. Lecture slides were messy and confusing at times, but if you follow along in class it is easy to understand. He sends out and outline of each test a week before that tells you exactly what will be on it, and tests reflect lecture material.

Lectures and annotated notes are posted for each lecture. Exam outlines were extremely helpful in preparing for both midterms and the final. One printer size cheat sheet and calculator allowed on each exam. Lecture material aligned with homework and exam content. Overall, manageable class with great prof!

This is the professor you want to take for 20B. He makes the concepts we learn extremely clear and his midterm/final reflect what we learn/cover on the homework. He also makes it clear what will be covered in the test and sometimes gives hints to what questions are similar to the exam question. Also he's the Pikachu Professor so you know he's good!

He was so so so amazing!!! His lectures were clear and engaging (and silly). The grading scale was awesome as hw was heavily weighted so there wasn't too much of a burden placed on tests. He also included a detailed outline of his tests that literally explained what each question would ask, so it made it easy to pinpoint what to study!
Professor Pikachu is the very best like no one ever was!

dr. jor-el or "pikachu guy" was awesome! I'm not the strongest at math but performed well because of the prof's clear midterm and final outlines. lecture and discussion is not mandatory and lectures are podcasted. highly recommend if you need to take this course bc it made calculus way less daunting and achievable :)

he gives very specific outlines for all exams and listens to constructive criticism (he used to rush through all the material making everything super confusing but at the end of the quarter he stopped doing that) he tries to relate to students and wants to make sure everyone does well in the class too

Great professor, though his handwriting can be tough to read and sometimes he is hard to hear, but overall I understood the material very well thanks to him. Attendance is not mandatory (inc. discussions), and all lectures are podcasted. The best part is the clear outlines he provides prior to exams, which lets you know what to study in particular.

Jor-El is the GOAT. Anyone would agree. Fun and engaging lectures, very heavily weighted HW category (which carries your grade), exam grading criteria that is in favor of student success, clearly defined outlines of exams prior to exam date (study guide on steroids), and allowance of a full page cheat sheet on exams. CHOOSE HIM AS YOUR PROFESSOR!
He is an amazing professor. His teaching style is impeccable. He makes the lectures really fun and enjoyable.

Amazing professor, wants to make sure that everyone in the class does well. I hated math but he made this class fun and learnable. Very caring, very helpful, very responsive. Would take his class for every math class if I could. Thank you Dr. Jorel!!!!!
PERFECT EXAM OUTLINES, LOVE HIM
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Made this my favorite class of the quarter. When I needed help on polar coordinates, I went to office hours and it was extremely helpful. He took time to re-explain the material, drew everything out, and checked to make sure I understood the content. Fun personality too, makes class very enjoyable.

DO NOT TAKE during summer. Much more relaxed teaching during the school year. Great guy, not so much teaching. Goes through important topics too fast, and doesn't focus on them enough. A lot of extra-credit opportunities as well.

Absolutely amazing professor, always accessible and very fair in the grading department. He constantly strived to make homework and lecture more interesting through comedy and working problems with the class. The only gripe you'll have with him is it takes a while to get grades back.

Professor Jor-El: The Guiding Light in CSE 21
I had the pleasure of taking CSE 21 with Professor Jor-El, and I must say, it was an unforgettable experience. While the class material was undeniably challenging, Professor Jor-El's teaching style and personality made the journey enjoyable and enlightening.

Jor-El, commonly known as Goat-El, is the man in the Pikachu onesie is honestly a phenomenal teacher. Aside from all the times he has rick-rolled us, he made sure to make every class session as entertaining as possible despite how long or late it was.

100% recommend taking him. CSE 20 is a difficult class however the way he teaches makes it a lot easier to understand. He gives a lot of extra credit opportunities in the homework and on the quizzes. He is very understanding and wishes the best for us all!  Also his Pikachu onesie is iconic and all the pop culture and meme references are amazing.
The best prof for cse 20 hands down

Best professor I have had! He literally dresses up as pikachu for every lecture and makes all the homework problems and lectures funny with memes. The conepts of CSE20 are very difficult and his lectures are really fast pace but he is a very good teacher. 1000% recommend

Stellar Professor! Made lectures, homework, and exams quite engaging and fun. Personally, I felt his grading policies were extremely fair and sometimes even generous as he does as much as he can to make sure students can have a good chance at excelling in class. He also makes it quite clear what will be on the exams in relation to the homework.

Professor Briones is a fantastic professor. His lecture is clear and understandable. He uses memes in lectures and homework to make the concepts fun to learn and solve. Additionally, the best thing about him is he is active on discord to answer students' questions, so don't be afraid if you can't attend his office hour.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Take different professor

While Wilbur has a strong resume, students shouldn't be fooled into thinking this means a helpful course. The learning environment was dampened by what felt like constant confrontation between the students and Professor. He refuses to listen to feedback and prefers condescension over advising. If you want an A, self study, don't bother with OH.

Super nice professor and cares about what he's teaching. Participation is not just showing up, but "verbal participation". HW is optional and he gives no answers to them or the practice tests. Tests were T/F, MC, and a few frq but if you left them blank he gives 2/4 on frq. Good luck guys!

One of the worst professors I've had at UCSD. Didn't show up to his office hours and didn't show up to the first midterm. Exams were disorganized, grading was unclear, and participation was nearly impossible. Refuses to adapt his teaching—no answer keys for homeworks or past exams despite testing directly on them. Also TA is rude and unhelpful.

Definitely take the other professor who teaches MGT 100. 

Grades favor student who want Bs. Impossible to get an A unless you basically ace his test. The curve is unfair cuz he caps the A to 8%. 

Just take the other professor. You can check sets and capes to see why.

The professor's lectures are not engaging and seemed to have issues with students throughout the course. Although class contribution is worth 10% of your grade, the average score was a 0.9/5 which significantly impacted grades. Attendance policies are strict which is frustrating as this is college, not high school. I don't recommend the professor.

Decent prof. Lectures are long and not the most engaging, but topics are wide ranging. Exams were a mix of lecture material and RStudio HW. Basic knowledge of R is expected. Can be challenging if you don't know, but help is available. HW not graded but STILL DO IT! Unlimited page cheat sheet allowed on exams. Grade distribution is done in z-score.
Boring Lectures and poorly explained concepts in class. The test is also confusing.
The lectures were boring. Most materials were poorly explained, leaving students uncertain about what to focus on.

Prof is clear and organized with material. Class requires RStudio which itself can be difficult for first time users. Ask questions and attend OH if you get stuck on it. He walks you through it and if you don't understand it than ask for help. He has resources to help you. Quizzes every week that can be done with others. Grades are done in Z-score.

I would not recommend him at all. He is kind of rude and unclear about what he wants. He has a weird attitude about him that makes it seem like no one is good enough or doing very well. He is a tough grader and his TA is as well. He 100% grades on how good he think your business is which is 100% subjective.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He doesn't have a clear rubric so everyone had really different work. He takes off a lot of points for a small reason. If you don't do a venture he is familiar with (Shopify) then you get feedback that doesn't make sense. He grades based on z scores, so you need to be at the top of the class to receive a good grade. Avoid this class. Tough grader!!

Prof Wilbur is nice but I wouldn't suggest it. The entire class is you building an online business. He tells you first class that you should expect to spend your own money. The two big grades are the midterm and final (both videos). They grade you if they like your venture, not weather or not you answer the prompts. His TA is kind of rude as well.
Radical politics don't belong in the classroom.

A quiz question marked correct shows up later with a different marked correct answer. He proceeds to blame students for picking the same answer as previously graded as a lesson to not... trust the professor? In his own words, "Did you really think what you thought was the correct answer did really sound correct?" Professor, you are the expert here.

Krysl does not teach the material he will test you on, and when you try to get help in the discussion forum he will usually respond with a sarcastic, rude, one sentence answer that does not actually answer the question. For SE131 he's okay, but do not take 130B with him because you will not learn anything. Also, he uses python instead of matlab??

When 80 people show up to a 9 pm office hours the day before the final, all confused about how to solve a practice exam, that's how you know you've failed as a professor. Somehow he will try to blame it on the students though.

worst professor i've ever had. exams were all about hand calcs, while homework was all about using the professor's provided python code. he was often rude on piazza and did not create a welcoming environment. sometimes he had valid takes every now and then tho.

This class was about 90% coding and 10% hand calculations, yet ALL exams are 100% by hand. Not a hard class but he makes it difficult, don't think about asking questions because he will respond like this," Wait, you are serious? You have not heard of clamped condition before?" ,"Good questions. I mean for you to answer. (Your homework, after all.)"

This class made me appreciate the sun more because of how depressed it makes me. But besides that, he's ok as a professor. His grading is generous (20% final) and he gave us a make up midterm when we bombed the first one. 
He answers questions when asked but his answers on Piazza are often veeerrryyy short. The topic is hard and he could be better
grumpy old man who thinks the world revolves around him

Genuinely evil professor. No matter how reasonable your request, he will likely not accommodate you either out of ego, laziness, or both. You are not seen as a students in this class. He will feed you work upon work and then blame it on you when the class average for the tests is 50%. No accountability. Terrible professor.

Incredibly unclear on grading and teaches the class via python although your tested on all handcalcs. Also why is solidworks needed in a matrix analysis class?! There is no reason why we need to use both python and solidworks for a class which tests you on hand calcs, which differs from the few we do. take this class over the summer to avoid him

Worst professor I've ever had. Doesn't teach the content that is on exams or give you any practice problems relevant to the exam. Out of control ego, you are either given a passive aggressive answer or ignored for asking questions. Refuses to take accountability for bad teaching and pins it entirely on students when they are struggling. AVOID!
his class is difficult. He uses python when every other prof has used matlab. He also assigns hw that doesnt reflect what you actually will get tested on for tests. avoid if possible
For context everyone is posting reviews right now because midterm grades just came out. And they're all negative which says a lot about the competence of this professor and his teaching.
Try to get a different professor. Hw is tough and exams are crazy hard
tests are nothing like homework. choose a diff prof.
wouldn't rec
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are nothing like homework or lectures. You will lose sanity taking this class so just be ready
do not take this class if you want to keep your hairline intact

Worst professor I've ever had.  Hasn't taught this course in a decade and it shows. He basically makes you go into tests blind. If you ask any questions, he will ridicule you. Don't expect to actually learn something in his lectures, he'll teach you unnecessary Python code that is not applicable to the midterms. AVOID FOR 130B

One of the worst professors in the department. He teaches a Python library he wrote, which will never be used in tests or your life. Extremely confusing lectures since he goes out of his way to teach irrelevant concepts. Passive-aggressive in and out of lecture. He spends more time protecting his ego than teaching.
Homework is irrelevant to tests

I took his 101C for S124 and it was not bad. 45% hw, 20% lab, 15% midterm, and 20% final. Hw and labs are free as long as u put in work and u only need 3/5 labs to get full 20%. I bombed the midterm but I have made it up with good scores on hw and final and it really paid me off with an A. You can also ask him exam questions on discord as well.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He uses his own textbook and does not stray a lot from the main material. There will be weekly Abaqus assignments. The midterm and final are both MCQ based. The exams are easy but have negative marking. They will mostly consist of simple hand calculations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I noticed no recent reviews so I figured I oughtta write something. He's good at teaching, but not great at answering questions. He'll ask you to ask questions, but then if he personally deems your question dumb he'll either ignore or respond with something unhelpful. Oh also he says class isn't mandatory but you'll definitely want to go to class
One Word, Everything... Disaster.

Professor Krysl is the best professor I've had at UCSD tied with Uang. Great guy. Tests are exact material of lectures. Homework is easy. Take the opportunity to learn from them instead of breezing through for a grade, and the class will be fantastic.

good txtbook (he wrote it himself). midterm was kind of a cheap shot just because it mainly focused on one or two subjects within the course but the final was definitely fair. the hw is alot easier than se102 just because krysl gives you functions that do the hard coding for you. not a fan of iclickers but he has a good system so it works out..
K cares about us. That is great. Sometimes he talks way over our heads and that is not so great. But I like what he's done with the clickers. The class is actually fun to go to.
Great teacher. Learned a lot.

This is a review for both SE 121 and SE 131. He's an arrogant D-bag, bad jokes, looks down upon you in office hours with contempt. Best strategy is to go to TA office hours for help, and form homework solving sessions with other students in computer labs. In all honesty, you will likely understand maybe 5-10% of each lecture. I got a B,thanks to TA

Krysl is the man, but class is hard as hell. You will NOT understand 70% of what you learn, and you're not supposed to. The basics can get you a passing grade, so pay attention to the little things. Some people think he's mean, pfffft, he's harmless. Just don't appear scared and you won't give him a window to dominate.
He's a genius. He cares about us.

Class is so hard. If you go to office hours he helps you out, but class still sucks. Man I got so frustrated with this work. You gotta be good with calculus to do well in this course. His curve is interesting.

Difficult class, and the reader seems like one big puzzle in the beginning. Once you learn the style of it though, and how he teaches, the class is not bad. You'll learn to appreciate Matlab. Always attend lecture, always do the homework. You can't survive without it. He's genius but comes off mean; you'll adapt though, if you're smart enough.
He is better than before, and I think he might be better if the material were different, but the stuff is so out there it is hard to understand.
No Comments

This class was a WASTE OF TIME!! Yes, we learned absolutely nothing. I don't like his way of grading but he palays favors, if you go to his OH and just pretend that you like what he talks about you get an 'A' you could score 50% and still get an A. However you learn NOTHING!! Going to class is a waste of beautiful life time!!

I liked him a lot.  The subject was usually difficult to grasp and his weekly quizzes were somewhat tricky, but he was lenient and seemed to mostly care for student attendance.  His explanations were hard to understand because one had to pay attention to details.  Good grading policy (read it carefully).  Do not cheat.  Show effort.

This professor is pretty generous on many of his grading schemes, especially the quizzes he gives during Friday lectures.  However, he will not tolerate cheating whatsoever on any of the homework assignments, and if you have similar answers to what other people have, you will get a zero.  Homework took so long to grade of the cheating policies!!!

Honestly one of the less interesting USP classes. Graded by three assignments makes it hard to balance a bad grade, TA graded one of my assignments purely with AI. Lectures are mandatory, but Professor Pezzoli often went off on tangents/tirades that while interesting/entertaining, did not necessarily help with or even correlate with class material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was a yap session. I'm a Bio major who know nothing abt USP. Lectures were lacking a key takeaway topic. TA was nice but harsh grader. Feedback on my essays was basically "needs more depth". My essay was 1,000 words I didn't know what else to say... Grade was made up of 3 essays + 1 group project. Give real effort on your essays i guess

Pezzoli seems like a great guy, but his teaching style is all over the place. Assignments will have 3 different docs all with differing instructions; it is very confusing. The lectures aren't that related to the assignments either. My TA was also a harsh grader marking us down for things that weren't even specified in the rubric or instructions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU HAVE ADHD!!!

I deeply respect Keith Pezzoli for everything he's done for the USP department and I admire his expertise and passion. HOWEVER -- this class was impossible to follow and frankly a pain to get through. He says so much yet so little. His instructions might as well be in a foreign language.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: I feel really terrible giving Keith anything but 5 stars because as a person he is incredible. His class however, was a mess. He somehow said SO MUCH and yet so little. Lectures were unorganized and just him rambling. It will probably be better next quarter because he was trying a new project and he worked out most of the kinks with our class.

LOVED Pezzoli! He is very passionate about his work and teaching. Assignments consist of one paper, a take-home midterm, and final project. For the lectures though, it's important to at least skim the readings otherwise you won't know what's going on and it will be impossible to write the paper. Overall, the material was interesting and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Nice guy. Rambles every 30 seconds. He loves his job and wants us to do well, but his lectures really lack structure of any sorts.

His class was kind of a mess organization-wise, so hopefully they change it up if he teaches USP 2 again. Great guy, and his passion was infectious, and liked that he let us do fieldwork. Lectures and reading frequently go off-tangent, though. Just make you write a decent paper and don't flunk the midterm and final, and it's a pretty easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Awesome professor, really loves what he does. I enjoyed his USP 2 class and would definitely take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: easy A tho. He really wants to to do well in the midterm and final while at most of the time he just keeps repeating himself but he is a nice guy and everything is straightforward. You have to spend some times on readying his articles or stuff like that to write a solid essay
This class is pretty easy, he gave us EVERYTHING that was going to be on the midterm so you just have to put in the effort. Really caring and focused on research. Required field trip, but very fun.
You will leArn alot about RESEARCH

I found Professor Pezzoli to be an enthusiastic practitioner. He lives what he teaches and offers the opportunity for his students to participate in community planning projects he is working on. Loves anecdotes for lecture, but don't be fooled, the assigned reading is going to be on exams whether discussed in detail or not. Not easy, educational.

Had him at SDSU. Pretty amazing instructor--dense material, but you will learn a ton. Check the website weekly, do a good bit of the readings, participate, have fun with it. Once you know the definitions, you can put the rest of the exams together. If you have a choice, take his class.

Pezzoli is a great guy, but his class is a waist of time. dont bother going to class, he puts the entire class on the website along with studied guide and final studied guide. he is a great guy that loves the subject, he makes up his own words such as BioGeo Chemical Earth lol. 50% Midterm 50% Final, here is the class web site urbanworldsystem.org

The SRP is the pivotal point of the USP major and Pezzoli is the only person next to Prof. Mirle Bussell that should be teaching and leading the students on doing their theses.  He is resourceful, direct and very welcoming.  His lecture material may be dense, but at least he's enthusiastic about teaching.  Definitely recommend.
This guy is freakin Awesome

Best format: 1 paper, 1 midterm & a final. Tells you EVERYTHING that will be on midterm/final. All you need to do is study for some hours and you'll get an A for sure. Even though i like USP, the readings are terrible. Don't bother with 80% of them. Lectures are interesting because they don't relate to readings (aka tangents)! Cool and funny guy.
Tests aren't too difficult, but what grade you get depends on your TA.  Pezzoli is a cool dude, but the format is sort of all over the place.

Very passionate about his work, his study guides let you know exactly what will be on the midterm/final. However, he tends to go off on tangents during lectures and rarely covers the assigned readings. Course material is VERY BORING, and there is a considerable amount of reading. Would only recommend taking this class if you are a USP major.
Really nice guy.  Passionate about his work.  Good class.
No Comments

he really knows and is into what he's talking about which makes things a lot easier for him and for us.  i enjoyed this class more because of him than because of the course material, so that's a plus.  lectures are sometimes pointless, though.  midterm and final review make testing super easy.
He is a nice guy but very unorganized and lost. Lectures are repetitive and boring so were readings. He is helpful with the exams though and the overall points are easy to understand.
Very funny and knowledgable. A really good guy too. Is relaxed and understanding. Very passionate about his topics.
Rambles a bit but is very knowledgable. Study guides make the midterm a breeze. Pretty cool guy overall
Very passionate....but it may be only he who is very interested.

I don't think you can get a better professor than him tbh for this class. Lectures covered relevant material for quizzes and hw (though mandatory attendance). He also has a very generous grading policy.

Lots of extra credit. Very clear & organised slides. Lecture mainly teaches concepts & how to approach different types of problems. Possible to self-study because all details are clearly shown in slides, which makes mandatory attendance a bit annoying. Overall still highly recommends him.

his class might be a little boring, but i think every physics class is just boring in its own way. His grading scale is very nice and the quizzes are very similar to the final. 4 quizzes, 1 final, lowerst can count lower if ur final is higher than it. overall pretty good

As someone who has never taken a physics course prior, his lectures, grading rubric, and opportunities for office hours/test corrections over summer session made it very easy to feel reassured that you can succeed with the right effort. Overall, he is also very understanding and easy to talk to when confused about new material. Highly recommend!

Run of the mill intro climate class, but the teacher had great lectures that leaned towards the informational side. Allowed cheat sheets, one per test and all previous cheat sheets on the final. Two midterms + one final, some lecture based assignments, as well as plenty of extra credit. Non-stressful GE
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance wasn't mandatory, but I attended whenever I could. The content in the midterms and final are on the slides and are tested mainly on recall of details. The TAs were always giving review sessions and homework help, so it seems like everyone involved in teaching the class were open to helping and giving feedback.

I took this class to fulfill the JTCCER requirement. It was lowkey kinda boring. Prof. Barbeau seems really sweet, but her lectures were so monotone and boring that I was doing crossword puzzles in her class. There was weekly HW based on class material. No discussions either. There were two midterms and a final, which could bring a cheat sheet.

although I took this for my climate change rqmt, I I lowkey had to work for a good grade. thought it would be an easier A class but overall still not hard I just actually had to study. HW every other week. 2 midterms and a final, cheat sheets for all. lowkey boring lectures but still attended all.

She seems very sweet but lectures can be boring. Attendance isn't mandatory but she gives a bonus extra credit question about once a week if you do show up to lecture. 2 midterms and a final which she allows cheat sheets for. Overall not too much of a workload just a homework assignment every 1-2 weeks.

Although this class is not the hardest class I've taken, I will say it is not a walk in the park. The study guides lists broad topics but the tests are mainly questions on micro-details. I wrote a microscopic cheat sheet and I recommend not following her study guides and just going off of the slides. She offers a lot of extra credit though.

She's really sweet, but she's just a really boring lecturer and just reads off of slides. The class itself is low commitment, you could easily miss lectures and get an A in the class as long as you go over her podcasts before the midterms and final and make a packed study guide. Overall its a chill GE to take for credit
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: very kind, if you're not interested in the subject this class might be a little boring as she just lectures at the class. cheat sheets are allowed for every midterm/final, class was very easy to study and prepare for

easy class, mostly based on midterms & final, which you get cheat sheets on. still exams were harder than i expected. a good amount of extra credit at the end but was graded very strictly, bonus questions for extra credit in class so try to attend

Easy class as long as you go to class or watch the lecture. Professor Barbeau gives extra credit for showing up to class and adds it to your midterm. You get 1 cheat sheet per midterm, 3 for the final, and tests are relatively easy. Professor Barbeau is very nice and passionate about the class, definitely take SIO 40 as a GE for non science majors.

Prof. Barbeau was super knowledgeable and passionate about the material which helped keep me engaged during lecture. She gives out bonus points that get added to midterm scores just for showing up in lecture. She also gives out an extra credit paper during finals. Grade based on HW, midterm, & final - you can have a cheat sheet for each exam.

Absolutely loved her and would take again easily. Lectures are recorded and tests are all multiple choice with cheat sheets. Gives out extra credit for showing up to class and can get a little boring but as a non stem major it was pretty light.

I took this class for a GE as a non-stem major and felt that it was pretty easy. The midterms and final are representative of the information in the lectures and you can use a cheat sheet which is nice. Attendance isn't required but sometimes she does extra credit questions for the people in class.

Strongly recommend SIO40! Professor Barbeau's lectures could be boring, but she was kind/ wanted her students to succeed. She gives bonus points, 5 homework assignments, podcasted lectures, many review sessions, and genuinely wants you to do well in the class. However, not many things contribute to your grade so do well on exams! Lecture heavy!

Barbeau was nice but a super dry/boring lecturer, often rambled off slide topics and bad at time management. Course not too difficult, weekly homework, 2 midterms 33 questions each all multiple choice T/F and a 50 question final. Gave out some extra credit too. Her grading scale is generously curved.

the grading scale is pretty generous but her tests are actually horrible, you could have a cheatsheet with everything you need to know and the test will ask you the most obscure questions about the smallest details of the lecture. some stuff on the test isnt even on the lecture and theres no textbook so no idea where it comes from. ehh avoid tbh

Probably one of the best classes to get a science GE out of the way. Barbeau sets this class up kinda like a transaction. You sit down and learn a little about climate and the Earth, she gives you all the opportunities to get an A. HW is quick and ez, lectures are podcasted, and tests aren't too bad as long as you make sure to study.

I genuinely don't know why her overall score isn't over a 4.5. Exams are MCQ, 20 something questions, and automatically gives a curve for your grade where 90%+ is an A. Very generous and accessible through online office hours, and although the material would be a little hard for non-STEM majors, you just need to memorize the information.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super sweet but awful lectures. She talks in circles. For every 5 minutes of content there's 15 minutes of filler. She's great if you're a slow learner but definitely avoid if you get bored quickly and need a prof that gets straight to the point.

i really like professor barbeau but wasn't a fan of the TAs as it didn't seem like they knew what they were talking about during reviews. extra credit is available but there are homework assignments that aren't hard but they're time-consuming. lectures were recorded and there were no discussion sections. great way to get a GE out of the way :)

I literally loved this class and the professor-- pretty easy and light especially if you're paying attention in class. Sometimes lectures can get a little dull but I'd encourage attending to them. Homework isn't hard and midterms are straight forward. Honestly, there's no reason to not take this class with Barbeau. Overall very positive.

One of the sweetest teachers I've ever had, genuinely cares about her students and knows the class is a science for non-STEM majors, but just teaches in the hopes that we learn something or gain a better perspective on climate change. I would definitely take again and highly recommend.

She is a good professor. She is able to explain topics well but she mainly reads from the slides and elaborates on it afterwards. After lecture, she heavily annotates her slides which are extremely helpful for homework and to prep for the exams. One of the easiest classes I've ever taken at UCSD so far.
SIO40 is an easy and also educational class. Prof Barbeau is easygoing and the exams were clearly based off of course materials. Take this class for your lower division credits!! Easy A

Professor Barbeau is a solid teacher. Her lectures connect with homework and especially exams which are also easy. The course revolves around lecture material - understand that and you're good to go. She is pretty accessible outside class, with podcasts posted for each lecture.

Professor Barbeau is good at explaining topics, but sometimes her lectures arent detailed enough to answer the midterm questions well. I appreciate that she held review sessions and offered a lot of extra credit opportunities. The midterms and final take a good amount of time to complete (3-8 hours) but she makes it up with the extra credit.

Easy class. 2 Midterms/1 final that take a couple of hours but it's open note and she gives you 36 hours to do it. A lot of extra credit opportunities and the TAs provide homework help/review sessions before exams. Lectures can be boring at times but she's passionate about the material. She also doesn't make you buy a textbook which is nice.

The final and midterm take forever to finish. FRQ questions can barely be found in slides and barely talked about in lecture so its hard to even answer them. She rlly out here freestyling all the questions. Easy concepts but free response format to reduce cheating online is so hard (she used to have MC in person) Going to class is useless n boring
her midterm and final is much more complicated than anything that she teaches in the class. Be ready to teach yourself because she certainly won't teach you anything.

her midterm questions literally don't correlate to the lecture. She just reads off her lecture slides with little to basic information and then asks for super detailed questions in the midterms. Sometimes I question why some people can be professors.
She likes to say climate change this, climate change that and how important it is, but doesn't really give any evidence or facts. She just rambles.
easy, but not worth the time. Written midterm takes way longer than it should.
it is easy, but so much unnecessary work that she makes us do. She is also not a good professor, she just reads slides and pretends like she knows what she is talking about.
easy, but she is not good at teaching at all. Just read the slides.
Just a bad class.

Very unorganized class. Easy concepts, but she doesn't do a great job at explaining them and makes the class soooo boring. Also midterm questions cant even be found in the lecture provided. The questions are so ambiguous that we have to spent 4 hours doing the midterm. Terrible teacher.

Extremely boring class. There is no point of going to lecture because she just reads off the slides. Also, she never assigns homework on time and some of the homework questions are horribly worded and the answer can't even be found. Big waste of time.

Very boring class and lecture is essentially useless. All you need to do is just read the slides however she words her question on the homework and midterms really weirdly, which creates a lot of confusion.

She's a great professor! The class was easy, and her tests are all multiple choice. The cheat sheets helped when taking the tests. Homework every week and it was easy. Lectures are interesting if you enjoy learning about climate.
She is a really good professor who understands we are not science majors and tries to do her best so we can succeed. Easy class, her lectures, and homework are all from powerpoint.
Don't take if you're a non science major. Incorporates too much chemistry into the class and is the most boring lecturer. Would not recommend taking this class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: EASY. 2 midterms and a final, cheatsheets allowed, lecture slides online and easy homework. Extra credit at the end, takes about an hour. If you feel like spending 2hours per test you can just copy everything onto your cheatsheet (yes, it fits).  Lectures aren't mandatory at all but she's a genuinely clear and interesting lecturer.

This class was excellent and interesting. Lectures are clear and helpful but can be skipped because she posts the lecture slide shows online. Tests are relatively easy, weekly homework is easy if you read the slide shows. No textbook.

Professor Barbeau is amazing! Her lectures are clear and interesting. The materials and weekly assignments are not hard as long as you pay attention on classes. There's no mandatory attendance but I've never skipped class, for they helped a lot. Midterms and final are easy, for cheat sheets are allowed. There're also extra credits. Love the class!

This was a super easy class! She doesn't require a textbook or attendance to lectures. There is weekly homework which is also easy and she let us use 3 cheat sheets on the final. Amazing class and professor!
Take this class if you wanna get an easy A. Don't ever have to go to lecture. Just look at lecture slides and fbgm.

Kathy is bae. Her class, homeworks, and midterms are super easy.  Class is optional and she puts everything online.  At times she can be dry but I love how passionate she can get (especially regarding coral reefs and polar bears) :)

Barbeau is an easy A if you listen in lecture (she doesn't podcast sadly). Really passionate about subject matter and a super nice and funny lady. Does NOT expect a scientific background at all and simplifies everything to a ninth grade level. Weekly homework assignments that are fairly easy, two midterms, and a final. Offers extra credit.

no required textbook. Cool TA's and a very funny professor. She puts lecture notes online and offers extra credit opportunities. Tests and homework are very easy. I highly recommend this class and professor if you want an easy A!

She is super nice. The TA's were very chill. She always puts her lecture notes online. The homework and tests are very straight forward , and you can bring cheat sheets. She even offered extra credit twice. The class is based off a curve. so a B is actually an A on a test.

Everything is listed below by the previous person. What you learn: the past of earth climate, saving earth, Green house gases, Earth's condition, etc. Pretty easy to memorize. If you have bad memory: small writing on cheat sheet, so pretty easy. Going to lectures help you memorize, but not going isnt going to punish you.

No textbook needed. ALL materials from slides are on midterms. One cheat sheet per midterm and 3 cheat sheets are final. With HW, The course material is easy enough to remember. All tests M/C. Midterm1/2: 82%+ is a A-; 64%+ is B-. Easy B+ to A+ course

Very nice lady! Lectures do get quite a bit dull at times but that's because of the topic. Great opportunities for extra credit and exams very straight forward. Beware that mostly everything that is covered in class will be on the exam, but she does allow one cheat sheet per exam, making it much easier. No excuse not to pass the class.

Great GE class to take. Her online lecture notes help with the weekly hw assignments. Midterms and final follow the study guide. This is a very low-maintenance class that helps you understand the environment. Highly recommended.

She's the nicest lady I have ever met in my life. She makes the class EXTREMELY easy to the point that it was kind of funny. All her tests are MC with cheat sheets and you even get to use all ur midterm cheatsheets on your final. And she offered a lot of extra credit as well. If you even slightly have some common sense in science, you can get an A+
Cares deeply about students and their grades. Highly recommended!

barbeau is such a great prof. she teaches through powerpoints which can be generally boring. but there is homework every week which is posted online. powerpoint lectures are online too! there is only one midterm and one final. no quizzes. she is really nice and CURVES ALOT!!! really recommend barbeau.
The nicest teacher ever. This is by far the least time consuming and most chill GE i've taken. All other classes are a pain in the ass but barbeau makes this class so easy and relaxed, it's great.
She is a very good teacher, and explains things very well. She is very concerned about her students, and always helps them if they don't understand the concepts.
Shes a real nice teacher, and fun too. Makes lectures interesting and throws in jokes.  She is very creative and uses sticks off the ground as a pointer hehe

Attendance is required, and exams are multiple choice based on homework and lectures, so if you study, you are set. Dr. Wilder is passionate and very admirable, I learned a lot from this course and would recommend her class.

she really loves what she teaches and you can learn a lot from her! participation counts towards your grade and there's no hw just study! both the midterm + final are worth 30% each. she makes it really clear what she puts on the test so there are no surprises. make sure to focus on the last few weeks of lecture!
Really great professor. Super passionate and caring. Make sure to do the extra credit and start studying earlier then you think you need to! would totally take again

She's a great professor she just goes a little too fast for me in lectures. And the nature of this class is memorizing things so it didn't go well for me but if you can memorize things you could easily get an A in this class.

She records and posts every lecture, discussion attendance is mandatory though. She goes pretty fast during lecture but the slides are available on canvas. She is very transparent regarding exam content and they are all easy to study for. There's a lot of information but she explains it clearly, and she's funny sometimes as well.
She's very passionate about the subject and really knows her stuff, but sometimes goes waaaay too fast.
I regret giving her a 3 this professor is awesome  I LOVE HERRRR

Dr. Wilder gives really great lectures which provide all of the information needed for the exams. She also gives hints as to what particular questions might be on the exam so make sure to pay attention to that. The midterms were super easy, so the final kind of caught me off guard but was still doable. Overall, an enjoyable GE class.

The class isn't hard, but it's lecture-heavy, and the tests require you to memorize so, so much. She provides a textbook, but readings aren't mandatory. I never read it and did well on tests. Only homework is weekly untimed quizzes. Wouldn't recommend taking this class unless you understand the insane amount of memorization you will have to do.

She is clearly very passionate about her work and loves her job. Her class wasn't difficult as long as you kept up with the lectures and labs. The discussions are mandatory and you can work on your labs with your peers. And her midterms were very memory based but she always had at least one extra credit question to answer.

She's really nice and approachable but the lectures get very boring and weren't about "human origins" IMO. Tests are HEAVILY based on memorization. There are 2 midterms that are mostly FRQ, and a final which was mostly MCQ. Discussions are mandatory but help for weekly labs which are super easy.  There's EC!!

The professor was a sweet young lady who loved to talk about her cute 2 year old daughter. She helped you out if you had questions. But the lectures were like 30-40 slides each & made it hard to understand the concept that shouldn't be hard to understand. But the TAs helped me understand it more. Theres 2 midterms she gives & a pretty intense final
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor who's very passionate and makes concepts easy to understand. She tells you basically all the questions on the exam, but you definitely need to be good at memorizing and attend the lecture, even though it's not mandatory. I would definitely take her again!

Free 3% extra credit if you watch an episode of an animal documentary and write a paper on it (1%, 3 times). Great gen ed class but heavy on the memorization. Basically gives away exam questions on the lecture before the exam which are super helpful for studying. Discussions are mandatory but very helpful for the labs giving a free 30% essentially.

A very sweet professor with a very clear passion for the subject (especially primates). It is a lot more like biology than study for socio-cultural things. Grades dependent on midterm/final, but so far is not too difficult. Just make sure to attend/watch lectures and study. Personally, would highly recommend Prof. Wilder for any class.

She is so so nice and very clearly extremely interested in the subject. I will say that it is more of a primate class than a human originas class and there was not a clear description of what would be on the midterms until day before, so I very much over studied.

LISTEN UP! If you don't really mess with monkeys bro...promise this ain't the class for you. These monkeys/primates have CRAZY names that are low hard to remember. THERE IS NO CHEAT SHEETS! But..I think if you pay attention the tests/midterms aren't that bad fr. She grades pretty easy especially for the free response. Grade also depends on TA!!!

Love love taking any of her courses. Specifically for this course, attendance was only mandatory on discussion days. One midterm and final which was open book/lecture and we were given plenty of days to see the questions online and submit our answers. She is very caring/nice, you can tell she loves what she does. She is very knowledgeable as well.

To get a good grade, simply show up to earn attendance and assignment points. The assignments are very easy. The study guides she provides are incredibly detailed and closely reflect the tests. The last three weeks are the hardest, but overall, it's a fairly easy class if you show up.

The class itself was fine but I struggling to understand why the professor would make attendance part of the grade if its not. So, you have to be presented but it won't count towards the final grade? The attendance grade only counts for penalty only? Make it make sense please. This is screwing over the Commuter students. So disappointing.

Her lectures were fun and educational. Every week you had to submit at least 2 discussion questions, and attendance was only taken on discussion days. Didnt record lectures, so its better to show up. Midterm and final were open note, encouraging us to use lectures and readings from the class. A good professor and class to take.

Professor Wilder is a great lecturer. She is very passionate about what she teaches. Beware there is a lot of memorization to do but she lets you know what will be needed to know on the midterms and final. She leaves weekly lab quizzes that can be answered if you go to discussions. Lectures are recorded and not mandatory.

She's very passionate about the subject which makes it super easy to engage with the content. It's fun how she gets so excited about monkeys, and it makes you more interested in them too. She can tend to go a little bit fast in lecture, but her study guides and expectations are super detailed and comprehensive. The course load is also very minimal.

I took Professor Wilder for a remote summer class and she was alright but her lectures were super long with so many slides. She made information very clear but I think she could've condensed lectures a little bit more. Grading was very easy but tests were mainly about lectures. Tests were open note.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 3 homework assignments per week; short summary of reading and provide a sample test question.  Midterms and final are based on peer generated questions posted to canvas.  All readings are on canvas.  Up to 2 absences allowed.  Very interesting topics covered, but it can be a bit dry at times.  Overall enjoyed this class and professor.

Her exams are easy because she gives students the questions and answers beforehand to study. Lecture is mandatory, but it is boring and feel unnecessary because the tests are mostly focused on the readings. Go to class, do the reading summaries, memorize the test questions and answers and you will be on your way to an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is both an easy and a frustrating class. Lectures were disengaging, even though attendance was mandatory with only 2 missed classes allowed. Reading summaries due before every class were just busy work and didn't help learning. Professor can't bother to write her own exam questions, only using ones written by students. Easy exams though.

Her class is very lecture heavy but she's passionate and wants to make sure you learn. There's 5 in class 5 point assignments, a midterm, a paper, and a final paper and final exam. The exams are worth the majority of your grade and are handwritten, so be prepared for your hand to hurt. But very engaging and interesting topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took her class online and her content was so tedious that it was hard to memorize all of the minuscule information that she wanted us to. Weekly "labs" which are just worksheets. I would not recommend, as the information that we had to memorize was so dense with information such as remembering dental patterns, making it unwarrantably difficult.

Taking this course online was rough. Prof. Wilder's lectures are super long and often don't get to the actual topics for the lecture until slide 45. Wilder herself is super sweet and passionate, but this course was really convoluted in terms of what we were learning, and how to succeed, and it wasn't very interesting - but it wasn't hard.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great prof, super super passionate about what she's teaching. Took it online which kinda killed it for me but was an interesting class. Weekly homework and midterms are really really easy but the final was entirely memorization based and threw everyone for a loop. If you pay attention in lecture you don't need to do any textbook reading.

I took the class on zoom, but she seemed really nice. Weekly homework assignments. Grades mainly based off midterms (2) and final. Lots of information and slides are posted. Not really a hard class as long as you pay attention
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Wilder is very caring and responsive to emails and questions. The material itself wasn't difficult, but the sheer amount covered in class makes it hard to go in-depth. She tends to read off slides and goes quickly through them, so reading beforehand makes the lectures easier to understand. Also, the material is not in chronological order.

The class is super boring. Professor Wilder is so meticulous with the grading that you're docked off points for the slightest of reasons. A+ is >100%. There's discussion of papers in class every Wednesdays. 40% in total for discussion and participation, midterm and final= 60%. She makes sure almost everyone will be at B at best, with a few As. Don'
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Its a class with a lot of information. 2 midterms and one final. I believe 20% for both midterms and final was 30%. Has key points for every lecture that are usually questions on tests. The first midterm was the most difficult exam, but she curves. Only one weekly short assignment.

All lecture slides are posted. As someone who has studied biology and evolution, some of the questions on the midterms I could answer because I already knew but often I would hear about how they were hard for others because it was questions about concepts not talked about. I would suggest the text that is provided with the class to solve that issue

STUDY & PAY ATTENTION TO LECTURES! Basically, a monkey class with evolution, kinda boring but the lectures are a little goofy. (Slides/lectures are posted after) Midterms you get to use a cheat sheet (no one checks the size of your sheet tbh), & she gives you an opportunity for extra credit to bump up your grade. Labs are graded by your TA.
Professor provided clear lectures, respected class time, and showed care for students. You don't have to worry much about any reading as long as you pay attention to class content.
Most information from lectures you can get from the readings assigned, but other than that her class is very interesting. She is very sweet and understanding if you reach out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was not worth taking since the content and lecture were super dry. Although anatomy is heavy memorization, the exams were too detailed, and the study guide was extremely vague on what particular materials were required to study. I did not attend a single lecture after the first lecture. Save your time and energy self-learning anatomy.

Nice professor, but extremely lecture heavy and mostly reads directly off the slides. When reading off the slides, she tends to skip through the material very quickly, so you feel like you haven't learned anything. Tests are difficult to study for, mostly because there is so much information that you don't remember hearing. Don't recommend.

Took this class for my GE because it was the lesser of the bio "evils." Lectures were monotone and unengaging so if you have an afternoon lecture time, you might have trouble staying awake. The midterms were super stressful to study for because there is SO much info you have to know. Final was cumulative which SUCKED.

Lectures are very thorough and everything she says out loud will always be on the slides. Provided study guides for the midterms and final and questions on the midterms/finals are straight from the study guide! Grade is composed of easy weekly quizzes, daily hw reading summaries, 2 midterms, and a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lecture quiz and 3 reading summaries per week. Assignments are easy, but it was very overwhelming keeping up with the amount to read and all assignments which made it easy to get behind on watching lectures. Material is interesting but would not recommend professor if you are taking other demanding classes or have a busy schedule overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Literally all multiple choice tests, really approachable. Went through the lectures kind of quick but all slides are available before class. The quizzes are pretty easy if you pay attention.

This class was okay. The lectures were a bit hard to sit through (mostly just reading from slides), and the midterms/final were challenging though there are easy weekly quizzes. I appreciated the extra credit (you can earn up to 3%), and the prof was nice, some of the material was interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Nice professor, but lectures were a bit hard to focus on since she would mostly read from the slides and not really ask questions to anyone. Weekly quizzes were alright, lab assignments were simple and to the point, also graded by TA. Two midterms and a final, however, I feel like the questions were difficult and answers choices would be similar.

The class was cool I actually learned a little, but the exams were hard she expected us to know a lot for the midterms, and the questions were also a bit difficult like one answer was more right than the other even though there is a one word difference, lectures recorded, slides posted, and weekly quizzes really easy and labs easy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Basically monkey class and could be more interesting but still a decent class.

Prof. Wilder was an overall good prof. Her class is daily reading assignments, 2 midterms, and final. The questions from the midterms and finals are questions she allows the class to come up with themselves, which I think is very helpful. Her lectures are straight forward and made learning very interesting.

This is my second class with Prof Wilder. She is so approachable, her lectures and slides are very organized. The class is set up so you learn in a fun and non-stressful way. She gives you a short easy quiz after each section, and her mid-term and final have clear expectations of what she wants from you. Highly recommend.

Professor Wilder is a very nice and down to earth person, but her lectures are VERY MONOTONE to say the least. She offers a lot of details that says "we shouldn't worry about" but then tests us about it. Her online discussions sections don't relate anything to the actual lab we need to turn in, so I don't see their purpose.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The quizzes she makes are TOO easy, but the midterms are a whole other story. She notoriously makes tests where "more than one answer is correct, but one is "more" correct :)". So if you enjoy enduring lame contraptions which test you more on the tiny details she doesn't mention during lecture rather than the actual material, definitely take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Wilder made the class super easy and enjoyable, she had only 3 midterms and no final which made the material distribution fairly easy. There is an 8-10 research paper due but she grades it very fairly. I totally recommend her class. Oh and she also gives study guides before the exams, study them and you are guaranteed an A
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Clear grading criteria. Willing to answer all of students' questions. Attendance is mandatory, but be ready to fall asleep. Her voice is very soft... Almost like asmr...
Awesome! Brilliant professor, very objective speaker on Anthropolgy.

Marina is a really good professor. 1 HW, Lab, skill test/discussion, and 2-3 reading quizzes weekly. It's very easily manageable, as I found only the HW to be the most time consuming. Also there are lots of EC opportunities by turning the HW and/or Lab in early. I found this class to be way easier than DSC 10
Best professor ever had. Strongly recommended.

her class was difficult but fair. as long as you put in the effort into paying attention in lecture and thoughtfully doing the homework, the class is very manageable. her lectures are very fun and she's very engaging
She is super passionate. The class is quite test- and homework-heavy. Her lecture slides are not really useful on their own.

Super kind and passionate, one of the best professors I've had so far! She is an amazing lecturer, and if you put in the work in this class and take advantages of the EC opportunities then you'll be set. All exams and materials were very fair and well reflective of course material. Strongly recommend!

Marina is awesome, genuinely one of the best teachers I've had so far. She explains things really well and her lectures are super informative. There is a lot of homework each week, but you have a lot of time to do it. The midterm and final were both not too bad. Definitely would take a class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Incredible professor and very enjoyable lectures. There are A LOT of homework and it takes a lot of time to complete, but I must admit it is necessary to understand the content. One of the best profs I ever had, made everything interesting. The exams and quizzes are tricky but is do-able if you took the time to actually understand lectures & hws

Marina is a super interesting lecturer who I genuinely l love going to class for. She's super fun and explains the class concepts super well, especially when it comes to specific exceptions and such in python. Attendance is mandatory, but slip days are allowed. Lots of EC opportunities on projects, HW and Labs. Weekly skill tests aren't too hard.

i love marina i've taken her for 20 and 40b and she's so sweet and passionate. if you talk to her and actually pay attention during lecture you will understand everything. will admit tests are a little tricky and they're a hit or miss. but she genuinely made me love certain topics that were otherwise boring!

Great lectures, lots of visuals on her slides. She's always very prepared and explains things well. Her labs, homeworks, and exams are well written and really make you think about how the algorithms work. I don't even like DSC that much but this class was interesting.

Took her for 40B but it wasn't listed as an option. 

Marina is the goat. Definitely one of the best dsc professors, passionate about teaching, willing to explain topics more outside of class, breaks down concepts to make them more understandable. I can't even be mad that the class is hard because she puts such a genuine effort into teaching.

Marina gives great lectures and use simple analogies to explain concepts. There's 1 Hw + 1 Lab every week and 3 reading quizzes on canvas so there's a lot of work. But don't worry too much about coding if u only have dsc10 coding experiences. She's super nice and willing to answer questions, truly caring your learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very nice and good at explaining concepts in fun and interactive ways. Advanced algorithms is an interesting class and Marina gave us lots of time to make sure we understood the material, even adjusting her lectures to match our feedback. Each week there is a lab and hw assignment. Final is optional if you are satisfied with your midterm grades.

Marina is the best lecturer and a wonderful person. I absolutely loved her lectures. She puts a LOT of effort into helping students understand the concepts. This is the only class I'm genuinely sad to see end. If you actually want to learn, take this class with Marina. I can't recommend it enough!

CSE8A was my first programming class. Marina is a good lecturer, charismatic and committed. She is approachable and warm outside of class and more than willing just to say hi and see how you are doing. I know some students struggle with her accent and that's understandable. It wasn't an issue for me.
Caring and passionate, was one of the best professors I have ever had.

You can tell she is passionate and tries to make concepts understandable, but her analogies don't work and confuse me even more. The midterm grades are released at the end of Week 7 so I don't have enough time to drop this class. Have a weird policy: have to get more than 50% points to pass this class REGARDLESS  OF OVERALL GRADE!!!

Though the class was a lot of work, her lectures were interesting enough to pay attention to. Lots of tutors available if needed and a LOT of extra credit opportunity for homework and labs (though they are capped at 100%). Was also really good at explaining hard concepts through analogies.

pros: passionate, interesting lectures, lots of resources available if u need extra help (office hrs, ed, etc.)
cons: a lot of time/energy needed for this class, difficult subject (esp. if no coding experience), but as long as you don't slack off and start assignments early u'll be fine :)

Great professor, even though attendance not mandatory still go to lectures and listen as she is really active and explains everything well. I didn't take notes but just went to lectures and still was able to feel comfortable on assignments, exams. Helps and supports outside of class too.
passionate teacher

Professor Langlois is passionate about the subject, but this DSC30 class has a heavy workload. Expect 8-12 hours per week on programming assignments. Attend office hours and use resources like Unstuck AI to stay on top of the material.

Amazing professor, she's really passionate about python. It makes lectures more interesting and easier to learn. She's very helpful and will always be open to helping students. Weekly homework and lab, the project is overwhelming at first but extremely doable. It's not an easy class, but I highly recommend Marina.

DSC20 is a very time consuming class. Many many different assignments, homeworks labs projects exams reading quizzes skill tests. It's a lot but Marina is very passionate and readily available. The class is something you can take to linkedin with the final project, and the skills you learn are very applicable to anyone interested in ds

Prof Langlois is passionate about data science.  Good teacher with extra credit opportunities on every assignment and test.  She always asks the class for feedback about the class and how the students are feeling.  If you know java, you shouldn't have difficulty in this class.  Would recommend.

Passionate and caring professor. She can be a little disorganized and things get confusing at times, but she gave a lot of extra credit opportunities for HWs and labs for dsc20. Attendance is required with 6 free skips. You'll be fine for as long as you go to office hours and understand what's going on.

- coding experience: dsc10, dsc20, apcsp(got a 3), 0 experience on JAVA
- 8-12hrs of work on weekly PA
- the course assumes you already knew JAVA, it focuses on data structure
- most of the time she teaches the content on the PAs after we already done
- PA write up very unclear, you must go OH for clarification
- take cse11&12 insead if you prefer
Great professor

Goat professor

Love her!  The assignments were super helpful and she really cares about the students.
