She gives study guides and does review sessions before each quiz/test (which you're allowed to take twice and it averages). The quizzes are short and taken remotely. Just watch the lectures and at least skim the readings and you'll be fine.

I honestly think this professor is the worst one I've had. She's super monotone and gives no mercy with grading and for a GE?? Choose another professor, this class isn't meant to be incredibly hard but she makes it so
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My experience with professor walkover was bad. She has an exceptionally tough grading policy that seems to lack flexibility and understanding of individual circumstances. Furthermore, as a white middle class professor she added a level of discomfort to me as a latin student with many intersectionality's as she over does her exchange of ideas.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very kind prof.  Taught GLBH with a very empathetic approach and made me love the material! Her lectures were also very interesting, clear, and concise.  Tests were fair and for the most part pretty easy. I'm premed but took the class for a GE and was very pleased with my experience. I highly recommend if you're looking for a GE!

Professor Walkover is a tough grader on tests and also assignments. Midterm and class assignments on average are around B-/B. Midterm and Final consist of multiple choice and fill in the blanks. Although exams are online, she makes them closed notes. Personally felt that we needed more time during exams. Not an easy class, if you want to relax.
I regret taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Walkover is by far, one of my favorite professors at UCSD. Although I am not a Global Health major, I decided to take ANSC 148 with Professor Walkover to get a break from my Political Science courses. Wow, what a great decision! She is truly amazing. Very passionate, incredibly intelligent, and overall an amazing and encouraging person.
Not much to say, just take her. She's honestly great and the class is very fair.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I liked this class better than I thought I would! Professor Walkover talks about a lot of interesting topics. You can tell she really enjoys what she teaches! Some of the readings were heavy but I think the workload is manageable! Only a few papers/writing assignments. I'd take her again :)
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She is very kind and cares about students' learning and she takes time to answer our questions. I would take her again! Your grade is based on 2 quizzes, the midterm, and final but there's ec opportunities. This class was insightful and you do need some case studies from the book. This class was insightful and manageable.
Its a hard course. I almost failed all tests but he still let me pass this course. HUGE curve glad He let me surrive on 1st quarter.
Very very mediocre. Cancelled the 2nd half of class and we had remote lectures.

Math 103B is supposed to be a more manageable version of its 100 counterpart. While most professors end up skipping over some 100 content, I think Lu did a pretty good job trying to get to all of the material. He's an effective instructor and is more than happy to address any conceptual gaps in the class. Exams are challenging, but grading is fair
Don't miss lecture, review his notes and attend office hours and you'll be fine. Always willing to answer any of my questions and was a generous grader
Don't miss lectures and make sure to go over his notes and you'll be fine. His office hours were super useful, he was always willing to go over concepts and any questions I had. Also curves

Tests were hard but gives generous curves. Really passionate in teaching and always ask us for any questions. Tests aligned with HW, but best to study with any resources (textbook sucks). His in-person notes and online notes are different so best to go to lecture to get better understanding. Highly recommend if you want to learn.
Great lectures, focuses a lot on explaining the intuition and high level ideas before delving into the details.

Lecture is not required. Weekly homework, 2 midterms, and a final. They are all difficult but he curves after the end of quarter. Class average is B- . I changed my grading option from Letter grade to P/NP for this class after I freaked out with the first midterm.

Lectures can be a little unclear with his slight accent and the way he writes, but he generally explains concepts well and makes himself available to help students. Also came in most the time with a T-shirt and shorts which I respect.

Solid prof with reasonable homework load and solid teaching.

Lectures were clear with some misunderstandings here and there. Posted supplemental lecture notes at the end of class. Wasn't too easy to contact, with some periods of time where the prof would go AWOL. However, was very lenient with grades and was explicit with what would/ wouldn't be on the test (overall grade was curved and dropped quizzes).

Mr. Lu is an extremely lenient professor. There is only 1 short homework assignment per week, 3 short quizzes throughout the quarter, and an easy final at the end. He even tries to curve grades so the top ~25% of the class gets an A. His lectures are easy to follow and he always posts notes online. For a Calc 2 class, this is as easy as they come.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A really good professor who will go over every detail if you ask. Pretty good at explaining, and gives partial credit on quizzes, but make sure you know the material and are careful, because one mistake can mess up your grade terribly.

I enjoyed this class. Only one short homework assignment per week, and you get points for attending discussion. He makes it very clear what will be on the quizzes and drops the lowest one. Made a challenging class very doable.

Professor Nichter is hands down the best professor I have ever had at UCSD. She single handedly sparked my interest in the legal field through her Intro to IP and Business Law classes, and she made every lecture genuinely fun and engaging. She is super uplifting and always wants her legal eagles to succeed. 10 out of 10 professor.

Professor Nichter gives a lot of pre-law opportunities, but if that's not your thing, there's nothing for you here. It's easy in that there's not much you could do to guarantee that you meet all the vague criteria that the course grades by, so it's pretty much up to luck. This course was not rigorous at all, and I felt like I gained nothing.

Have fun with a professor who teaches an introduction to business law class like you are at Harvard. She provides barely any information in lectures, then expects you to know everything she DIDN'T cover. Midterm is a sham. She fails to provide detailed instructions and then docks you for not following the instructions she never gave. DO NOT TAKE!

If you are interested in pursuing law, I HIGHLY recommend taking one of Professor Nichter's classes. I was lucky enough to take her legal reasoning course. She taught us how to thoroughly analyze cases via the IRAC method and write legal memos, client advice letters, and demand letters. TA's may strictly grade though and write minimal feedback.

104U was one of my favorite classes. The midterm paper is released the same day it is due, and if you pay attention, it's very doable and straightforward. The final is a seven-page max paper assigned the night before. Taker her class! It seems intimidating at first, but she makes it easily accessible, and her lectures are very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took her for both 104J and 104U this winter quarter.104J is writing-heavy with three papers, one being six pages, another being four, and the final being six pages (released the day before it's due). The papers were time-consuming and tedious, but if you pay attention, you will be fine. Take her class; she's an amazing professor and so helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great class with a great professor. Only thing to note is that final paper is 5-6 pages and is released the day before it's due, so you don't get very much time to work on it. Other assignments are usually done in class throughout the week they're due which is helpful+there's very clear instructions with rubrics for each assignment
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
One of the best professors in the department. Very engaging lectures and content materials. 
Encourages students to look into law school and inspires students to broaden their horizons in the legal field.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Nichter had an unparalleled positive impact on me and my educational career. She helped me navigate difficult life situations I experienced. She maintained high expectations for me so I could achieve what she knew I was capable of. She helped me become the best applicant I could be and believed in me when I did not believe in myself.  5/5

Professor Nichter is a compassionate and extermely knowledgeable professor who deeply cares for her students. She goes above and beyond to make sure her students have the support they need. She is a great resource for students who are interested in studying law in the future.
The best professor at UCSD!

She is a wonderful lady. Not only is she intelligent, she is also incredibly kind and helpful to her current and former students. Not long after I graduated she made herself available to me for the purposes of consultation regarding my personal statements. She was integral to improving them, and as a result I was accepted to several institutions.

Maysa is the kindest teacher I've ever taken and I highly recommend her classes for anyone considering law school. You can tell she really cares about her students and their success; you will know after taking this class whether or not law school is for you. For me, this is the most important class I've ever taken, and it might just be for you too.

I have not seen a person like Professor Nichter who not only cares but is truly passionate of what she teaches and how the students learn. She is amazingly accessible - she will definitely do her best to help you. Most importantly, her lectures are very concise and efficiently breaks down concepts that may be difficult.
One of the best professors in the department. Take the class any chance you get, whether you're interested in business law or not.
Nichter is compassionate and kind, she is a great professor teaching the ethics and complexities of Business Law. She does a great job making the larger pre-law class into smaller bite sized pieces
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Useful online lecture videos. Useful practice midterm and final that reflect the actual one. Unlimited attempts on quizzes and practice exams.

Great experience as usual. Lectures aren't mandatory but entertaining to attend. You can basically learn everything outside of lecture using the textbook or the Uflo course learner. Exams are around 75 percent of the grade but both the middie and final have multiple choice sections. Some profanity and politics during class if you are sensitive.

Everything in class could be learned from online textbooks and lectures covered a lot of extra things we didn't need to know. He gives practice midterms and finals but the practice midterm was a lot easier than the actual one. Final is worth half of the grade with short answer questions but wasn't too hard.
i don't recommend taking any econ with this guy if you think it'll be a "free A". do NOT underestimate this guy and his AI. he will ruin your experience in econ and your GPA.

Prof is pretty chill, very good at explaining concepts and teaching in general, but sometimes can be repetitive (maybe just the nature of microecon). Exams are not too bad with practice problems, considering the generous curve. Uploaded video podcasts. Only problem to me was relying on AI to grade exams (not officially confirmed tho).

This class was unnecessarily difficult for an intro course. I attended every lecture, studied, participated, and asked questions, yet the exams were nothing like the material covered. Lectures were confusing and did not help with quizzes and tests. Exams being graded by AI make it even worse. Would not recommend.

Sure, he's funny and cool, but for an Econ 1 class, he overcomplicates everything. He has hundreds of slides to explain a simple thing. Doesn't respond to emails. All tests were free-response; the final's average was 60%. He has good reviews because he's a cool guy, but for an actual econ class, take someone else. One midterm, one final.
Uses an AI platform for assignments that explains the logic from his lectures pretty well. Exams were pretty easy and the grading is pretty easy, too. Very clear lectures.

I could've done so much better if I didn't miss lectures so much. His exams are super similar to what he teaches. There's a curve to the final grades. He uses Uflo, an online platform which actually enjoyed beside the price. One midterm and one final. He's funny and entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The lectures can sometimes be interesting, but they don't reflect the difficulty of the actual exams even tho they get curved pretty well. you get a good amount of easy points but it's a difficult class to follow along.

avoid this prof at all cost. midterm is alright but finals is difficult. your exams are graded by an AI so it does make mistakes sometime. lecture is extremely boring and bro over complicates everything in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My final exam was graded by ChatGPT and made mistakes. Be ready to use regrade requests. Makes you pay for his buggy website that contains lecture slides & required quizzes. A test question was too ambiguous, heavily penalizing me. Uses too much profanity during lectures. The exams are difficult but worth studying for.  There is a generous curve.
Never replies to emails. The midterm is very easy, but be careful the final exam is difficult and will significantly lower your grade.
Class was difficult for me. Levkoff does provide good resources. I just found the lectures to be hard to follow and the exams difficult despite a long time spent studying.

He uses an Ai platform to run the course. It has a helpful Ai tutor that guides you through practice tests and quizzes. His practice tests are very similar to the tests. The content does get confusing, so make sure to stay on top of the work. Lectures are also podcasted. As long as you don't fall behind, it's manageable. Most people had to cram.

Practice tests are super close to exams. Final was decently hard, but not the worst to get an A if you attend or at least watch lectures. Gives lots of points from quizzes and practice exams, which are all unlimited attempts. Very passionate lecturer, can tell he enjoys teaching the course.

The midterm and final make up about 65% of the grade. Lectures and discussions are optional but difficult to find engaging and confusing at times. The practice exams he releases on Uflow are similar to the exams. He doesn't update grades until the end of the quarter. I personally found little interest in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Final was extremely difficult. Midterm/test are much harder than practice quizzes/practice tests assigned on uflo. Doesn't update grades AT ALL during the quarter. Only grade I had on canvas until AFTER finishing my final was my midterm grade.

Kind professor, content gets confusing after midterm. Midterm and final makes up 65 percent of your grade otherwise the other 25% is basically free. Over complicated things during lectures. Can be confusing at times. All lectures recorded. Attendance optional for lectures and discussion
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: W prof. wants to give you marks

Levkoff was a great professor and ECON 1 was overall very easy with the caveat that the final was pretty hard. Lectures are not mandatory but I'd highly recommend going as many people fell behind and failed the final. Lots of opportunities to bolster grade with infinite-attempt quizzes and surveys. I crammed for every test and was fine.

Not the worst, but personally didn't enjoy, disliked lecturing style- pretty dense, not very engaging, can be confusing. my advice: STAY ON TOP OF LECTURES/CONTENT, lectures recorded, but goes through slides for entire 80 min period (can go through 60+ slides in just 1 lecture)- easy to fall behind/get lost even by missing 1 or 2 classes/recordings
The midterm and finals are not that difficult. He gives practice midterm/finals which are very similar in format to the actual exams. He used Uflo for assignments and quizzes and it was very helpful.

I get mixed signals from Levkoff because he does not reply to emails unless you threaten to attend OH, so I don't think he wants to interact with his students. But he's chill when you talk to him. The final exam was graded by AI.

I would still take him again because the assignment deadlines are very straightforward and the exams are fairly easy.
Easy class Nothing more to say
Final difficult

His lectures were good but sometimes confusing. I would suggest going to the optional discussions if confused. Uses an online AI platform instead of a textbook for small homework assignments and quizzes. The midterm and final are all FRQ but he provides very similar practice exams. He also curves generously at the very end of the quarter.

Attendance wasn't mandatory in Lecture or discussion but I recommend going because lectures were sometimes confusing. Weekly quizzes help you practice and are free points. The midterm was easy, but the final was really hard and the AI platform is mostly annoying. He does seem like he wants the best for his students and curves the final grade.

Prof uses AI model for quizzes and course content, which is confusing to navigate and grades quizzes inconsistently. Very clear about course deliverables and exam content. Attend lectures and the review sessions and you'll be fine.
Good and fun lecturer but easy to get lost in lecture. Exams were hard but quizzes give you a small preview of the difficulty of said exams. Small paywall for class, but overall a fun experience.

Professor uses proprietary AI course system which is often confusing and unclear on its grading criteria. Lectures and slides are extremely unintuitive, and he bans calculus from being used to solve problems where it's useful, and instead forces students to use area functions that he has made up. AI platform grades inconsistently and often wrongly.

Homework are all multiple choice questions, but midterm and final are all frqs, which were unnecessarily hard. Have to pay for the AI website to do homework (the AI was most worst thing). Boring lectures and unclear ppts.

Got assigned a wrong grade for the class, and bro's gonna make me wait until week two of next quarter to fix this??? Enjoy your break all you want, but let me enjoy my break without the worry of my grade staying like this???

Fair midterm. Final had more computation but still very doable. Many questions were similar to ones on reviews/review sessions/discussions. You have to actually understand the material since tests are FRQ-based. His lecture slides are very thorough so I suggest reviewing them. Definitely recommend for Econ majors but you will have to study a bit.

Great lectures overall, but they can be a bit boring and it's easy to get lost during class. Lectures are podcasted and all materials are posted on Uflo, his AI website. The midterm was straightforward, but the final was extremely confusing and AI graded, no partial credit (I got a 49%). Thankfully, he gave a generous curve at the end.

Very very sweet guy and very understanding, the lectures and discussions are completely optional and the Uflo program he uses is super easy to use and is really helpful and benefitial. He is a good teacher and provides a lot of resources, from lots of review sessions to practice tests. He also gives plenty of ways to get a good grade in his class.

Professor Levkoff cares about his students and it shows. I got a 73% on the final and still ended up with an A- because he curves based on the class average. Attendance is not mandatory so I just skip and watch lectures on 2x speed.

Midterm + final make up 65% of your grade. The final is unnecessarily hard, I got a 95% on the midterm but the final was genuinely horrible. His final is also graded by an AI platform, which we have to pay for because it also grades all of our assignments. The AI was the most useless thing ever. Don't take him unless you absolutely have to!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor teaches well, but I never found his lectures really intriguing to me. I studied for the finals using the lecture slides & fully understanding those concepts instead of paying attention during his lectures. Class is pretty straightforward, tests are short response & pretty much you know it or don't. Crammed last week and got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't listen to the review bombing from people salty about not understanding econ or getting a good grade. He's a genuinely good and kind professor who explains concepts thoroughly, WHICH IS THE POINT OF ECON! He gives fudge points on take home work, and you can learn a lot from his lectures and just talking to him. One downside is the paywall.

Lectures were so boring and he over explains everything. Lectures are not informative or stimulating at all, they were a huge waste of time as he takes an entire hour to explain a concept that i could've learned in a 30 second youtube short. He uses AI to grade the final which was annoying. Exams were aight & he gives out useful practice tests.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROF! His exams are extremely difficult. His lectures are extremely boring and also he overexplains a lot. You have to buy this AI to access your assignments and quiz. Wouldn't recommend taking this class if you think it's a free A unless you have to. Many people that did well on the midterm ended up doing way worse on the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pros: He's very funny (dry humor) and connects his class to present day news and topics. No attendance is taken for either discussion or lecture. He podcasts all of his lectures. Cons: Overall grade is mostly dependent on midterm and final. Both the midterm and final is all free response. Doesn't use canvas and have to pay for his ai website.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: 2 tests make up 65% of ur grade which wouldn't be so bad if not for the fact that he offers ZERO partial credit on tests which is absurd considering all his questions are multipart (yes I lost TWELVE percent on a test because of one single mistake). Midterm was graded by TAs, I HOPE, because the final was literally AI GRADED. YES. AI GRADED.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor at UCSD. He doesn't use the canvas system to grade assignments and has his own website, UFLO where it's extremely difficult to know what grade you have in the class. His final reviews are not helpful at all and makes exams so much harder (no multiple choice only long answer). Save yourself and don't take his class.

Prof is very very generous and kind. Adds "fudge" points at the end and is super understanding in general. Attendance isn't mandatory but if you do go, he makes the lectures fun. Otherwise, every lecture is already prerecorded on canvas. Uses an ai system to help you learn which is pretty funny too. Gave us free test questions so we could all pass.

He's so kind. Attendance isn't mandatory unless its a test day, and he records and posts every lecture + slides and notes. I honestly never went to class and just watched all the lectures two days before the midterm and final and got an A. His lectures are so helpful and organized. He's easily one of the best professors I've had.

Incredible professor, enjoyable lectures, quizzes are online and super fair, engaging, and really cares for his students. offers so much material to help prepare and the practice questions are actually useful for midterms/finals. he loves what he does and you can tell, definitely recommend!!!

ive had the pleasure of taking econ 1 with levkoff, he is an amazing professor who clearly loves the subject he teaches. his class is genuinely for people to just learn and you can tell that he doesn't want anyone to fail. he provides plenty of resources that will guarantee your success in the grade and is an awesome prof.

Very chill professor. Attendance isn't mandatory for anything other than tests. Have to purchase AI assistant program $40 per quarter, all assignments are on there. Midterm is worth 20% of grade and final is worth 40%, all other assignments are super easy but grade matters on exams only pretty much but def recommend very easy class tbh.

Levkoff is literally my diva. He has an AI made by a past student that you can use on all assignments, quizzes, practice midterm, and practice final. It's extremely helpful. The midterm and final are extremely reasonable and go along with the assignments and practice tests. Highly recommend

He's honestly one of the best you can ask for. I understand where some people come from when saying that he "overcomplicates things," but I do feel it is necessary to understand the whole concept. Barely any homework and there are quizzes, but you do them online and you get unlimited attempts to get a 100%. Midterm is way easier than the quizzes.

Had a difficult time paying attention to class, Professor Levkoff is an energetic person but I wasn't able to absorb the material well. Had to pay for the AI website to gain access to his online lectures and practice study material which helped me significantly. Curve was pretty high at the end as well.
Pretty decent curve at end of class.

Prof. Levkoff is very straightforward when it comes to teaching, and is a bit funny. Lectures are recorded which is helpful as there is a lot of material covered. Exams are quite difficult but he does curve which did help me a bit. Would recommend watching any supplemental videos and working on the problem sets to be well prepared for the exams.

Curve will save you. Lecture and Disc are optional. Quizzes are open book unlimited attempts but time consuming. Exams are difficult, focus on the practice exam problems to apply lecture material to actual problems. Pay the $30 for the extra AI platform, Uflo, unfair but he posts extra exams there and the ai tutor helped me a lot.

Levkoff podcasts lectures which I definitely had to rely on because the syllabus is packed with so many topics and not enough time to digest them in class. Harsh grading criteria for his T/F questions – half of your points are slashed if you miss one key term. He curves but I honestly don't know if it's enough based on the test statistics he posts.

DO NOT TAKE UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCE. Goes over lecture slides way too quickly and focuses only on theory, completely neglecting applications. Not only that, but the quizzes and problem sets only show the most basic applications of the course content while the exams asked us applications of course content we've never seen. Hardest econ exams @ ucsd.

DON'T EVER TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!! I attended lecture and studied so much and the test was not at all reflective of any of the practice finals. Everyone I know bombed the final worth 40% of our grade. His curves are horrible as well. Unnecessarily tough exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests are harder than the practice exam, and no access is given to past exams. barely any space to write / work out problems on the exam. doesn't curve exams as well as he should - there are graduate students taking the course that pull the curve up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Didn't really feel like we got enough practice for the mid term and final. Most of the content is very theoretical for an accounting class I wish we would have had more examples on how to apply the theory, but unfortunately there just wasn't enough examples. Quizzes and hw are just multiple choice with really no applicable examples to prepare you.

Very interesting material but non-constructive grading structure. Curves aren't big enough from the distributions we see - most people get below the median score and he doesn't really curve the exams from what I can tell. Most people scored approximately 30-40% on the midterm that is 30% of their grade. Make of that what you will.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Levkoff is very kind, but his TA's /rubric are absolutely ruthless in terms of grading. Attending lectures is good to get you to stay on top of things. I would recommend rewatching them since they are fast paced & this class has material you need to chew on to grasp. Good professor, bad grading and evaluation. Standard combination I think.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His slides jump around a lot from concept to concept. Absolutely no flow in this class at all. He only explains the general concepts in lectures, doesn't actually teach you how to apply the concepts to a problem. Tbh kinda disappointed bc hella people said he was a goated prof

I am terrible at econ, but Professor Levkoff grades the final grades and exams A LOT so I passed. Neither lecture nor discussion attendance is required, but both are very beneficial to passing the exams. Take advantage of prof & TA office hours! Just don't fall behind on the weekly assignments and do the practice problems; you can at least get a C!

exams were too difficult
2 midterms and 1 final
both of the midterm averages are around 50 out of 100
final is 40% of your grade

Very charismatic when teaching, however, his test content is very difficult and not what I expected from lecture. I went to every lecture and spent time working on problem sets that are insanely difficult compared to what is taught. Unfortunate...
very solid class and nice professor, he is knowledgable about the material. not too much homework and tests are fair, just keep up with the class and lectures!

Lectures were pretty good, lots of examples and covered material very thoroughly. Quizzes and lrps were kinda difficult and took a lot of time but were harder than the questions on the midterm and finals.

No cheats sheets are allowed on exams which is a bit frustrating considering how most Econ 100 series allow one. Exams are harder than the provided sample exams and the grading is tough. Slide decks can also be hard to dissect and articulate without attending lectures (or watching recorded lectures) since there are too many slides.
Decent professor but lots of time needed for quizzes and lecture review problems graded outside class.
Good Lecturer. The homework can be tedious, but if you go to lecture, you should do well. The tests problems are very fair and not too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: quizzes and lrp's are hard but you have unlimited attempts (though you don't know what you get wrong). practice exams are somewhat useful for midterm/final. read the wording of exam questions really well so you don't lose major points on easy questions. watch lecture recordings in 2x since he overexplains. final is so much easier than the midterms.

Didn't attend a single lecture but watched all his podcasts on Canvas. Exams have tricky wording, but you just need to understand his grading style. There's a very specific way of answering that he looks for. To study make sure you do practice problems, all the LRPs and Quizzes and most importantly look at previous exams and the answer keys.

Great lecturer and will really help you feel passionate for microeconomics during class, which I normally find dull and enjoy macro much more. I will say compared to a lot of other economics courses, his always have the most online assignments (quizzes etc.). Would be fine if it wasn't graded but it can impact your chances at an A given the curve.
hrrible professor would never tae him again

Dr. Levkoff is one of the best professors I've encountered at UCSD!
Everything is podcasted, his lectures and slide decks are very clear. He gives bi-weekly online quizzes that can be repeated without penalty. They tend to be much harder than his exams and are great practice for them.
Midterms and final are very short, easy, and straightforward!

Dr. Levkoff was a great professor! I took the class for a GE, expecting it to be easy but severely underestimated the difficulty, especially math-wise. He overexplains a lot but I honestly didn't mind this. The curve is pretty solid, there are lots of opportunities to bring your grade up, and you can tell he really wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Biweekly quizzes you can retake. Good but dull lectures. Advertised some stupid AI thing he sits on the board of which was annoying. You could learn all the content from the quizzes and reviewing the practice exams in Canvas. Very chill in general.

Severely underestimated this class relative to my harder math/programming courses considering its reputation for being "easy". Professor is clear and is pretty engaging considering the subject. It's pretty easy to lose points on assessments if you're not focused during podcasts/lectures (2x speed not advised).

LRP and quizzes can be difficult, but unlimited attempts so they are ultimately a grade booster. Exams can significantly vary in difficulty. Grading rubric can be quite harsh, very possible to get 0/10 on some questions. He gives 5% extra credit as long as you do the LSQs. Slide decks are very useful for studying material outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't believe the good reviews, this is one of the worst lecturer in UCSD ECON. His tests are unnecessarily hard, and the are graded heavily. No partial credit, I almost ended up with an A-. His lectures are very confusing and he waste time going through easy concepts, and skim through the hard ones.

Ok, so I get it a lot of people like Levcoff—he's easy, has a few assignments, and throws a quiz here and there. But man, he drags out explanations just to make one small point. A two-hour lecture is equivalent to 13-minute YouTube video. If you want an A, be prepared to put in the work. 200+ lecture slides for one answer is crazy work my guy.

He over-explains EVERYTHING, but the TA discussion sections are really helpful. Not necessarily and easy A, but not like the worst class ever. Put some effort in and you'll be fine. The quizzes are unlimited attempts and honestly harder than the actual midterms and finals. Midterms and Final are 80% of your grade, but he curves a lot.

Don't expect it to be like AP Econ (except the beginning). Make sure to study every possible outcome because I didn't learn to calculate integrals because I thought the length and height would be provided for us but it wasn't so I got a bad score. He overexplains things but it helps sometimes just don't get confused.

Honestly this class wasn't too bad, funny guy, but he's one of the harder professors that teaches econ. His lectures are detailed, not too boring, discussions help a ton too. The tests are a lot like the practice exams that he posts, so it's always clear what to expect. Also quizzes have unlimited attempts so take advantage of that to boost grade.

I love his lectures; I am genuinely engaged and interested in the content during them. You will need to prepare quite a bit for the exams, but everything you need to know is said in lectures. Do the problem sets and past exams; they are extremely similar to the exams. Quizzes and LRPs are annoying; trial and error works, so team up with people.
Great Professor! He posts the old exams which are extremely helpful. Quizzes and LRPs do take a long time, but you have unlimited attempts. The midterms are pretty easy.

I love Steve, his teaching makes you feel included and is fun being part of his lecture as it doesn't feel boring or time passes very slowly. I would say he's amazing but the only thing I dislike would be the LRQ and quizzes because they are so annoying to deal with. Although they give you unlimited tries It takes me hours to get a decent score.
this is the type of class where if you get it, you get it, and if you don't, you have to struggle away at all your quizzes and spend hours on numerous attempts to get full points.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Levkoff made a class of 500 students feel engaging. His lectures were clear and he made concepts applicable to real life which made them easier to understand.

Levkoff's ECON1 is a challenging course, but worth the effort. Engaging lectures, fair tests, and helpful quizzes make it manageable. Unstuck study's AI-powered practice problems were a game-changer for exam prep. Overall, a rewarding learning experience.

The professor by himself is great but this class was very hard for me because the concepts sounded like a foreign language. I am grateful that the professor had his online lectures because they helped me. Also, he was very kind by allowing us to have several attempts at the assignments and quizzes. The final was the only thing that crushed me.

If you have to take econ 4 take it with him. Class is extremely hard and final was very very hard. But he has a very large curve. I got a 40% on the final still ended up with a B-. Also 5% extra credit for filling out a 2 second survey every week.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: hes pretty chill, but I personally didn't really understand his lectures that well. the final was really difficult.

No lecture notes for students to review, the recording is blurry, and almost all discussion session recordings have no sound and subtitles. The test is hard and confusing. Go for another teacher if you can.

Lecture heavy, needed to watch the lecture recording to do well on exams. 45% midterm 45% final. Midterm was simple and straightforward, final was difficult. I mostly self taught. Professor Levkoff is a great lecturer though! Enjoyed the class, tests are heavily curved.

Overall tough class and I pretty much taught myself all the content because most of the time his slides didn't make sense to me. The lectures are recorded which is nice. He does curve the grade because his midterm and final are difficult. I was initially scared of taking this because the midterm & final are 45% each, but the study guide helped.

pretty good professor and explains things good in class. has quizzes but they have unlimited attempts. also has homework. he provides problem sets and old exams which helps with studying for tests. the only thing was that some questions on the midterms and final were difficult, especially in the second midterm.
A big workload and lectures cover a lot of topics, but a great professor!

Levkoff is very knowledgable on the material. His lectures are clear and easy to follow. Tests are fair but beware of weekly quizzes. Unlimited attempts but questions are randomized every time and it doesn't tell you which ones you got wrong.

Levkoff is the man. Great lectures, clear grading criteria, and zero bullshit. I learned a ton just through his lectures, and the weekly quizzes genuinely helped prepare me for the exams, which often were just copied from the quizzes. As for the exams, they were reasonable, and nothing was unexpected. There wasn't much homework, either.

Extremely helpful in answering questions, good lectures, and providing exam preparation material. Class is definitely passable if you put the work in. Read the chapters before lecture to get context and keep up with practice problem sets to avoid the need to cram for exams. Overall grade curve is much appreciated (basically rose two letter grades).

Very Inspirational. Though I learned some AP micro(did not take test though) before attending his classes I still learned a lot. Problem Set and solutions, past exams offered so that you will have many opportunity to check your progress in learning. Prepare HEAVILY for exams.

Personally I passed the first midterm, flopping the other two exams, with my best effort in coursework, and quizzes, not attending lectures for the last half of the quarter and was still able to pass with a C. This course requires a good amount of effort, and studying, but you can still pass. As for Levkoff, he is a great straight foward professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor. Very solid lectures, lots of content so come with caffeine and pay attention. Everything in the lectures will be fair game on the midterms and final. Tests are graded very heavily, but make sure to do quizzes and other smaller assignments as you'll have the opportunity to redo them until you get 100% on them respectively.

Lectures were thorough and he did a great job of explaining concepts! He made sure to answer questions in class and emphasize important topics. Tests were weighted VERY heavily (90% of your grade) but they were pretty fair and were generously curved. There was also 5% extra credit for answering in class quiz questions on canvas which really helped

Really tough class. Detailed lectures, he's really willing to go over things, I'd feel like I understood--but then I'd struggle on the homework. I wish there was more mathematical examples in class, maybe going to discussion would help. Homework every other Sunday, quiz the Monday after, HARD final. 5% extra credit for simple before-class quizzes.

dr. levkoff is a great teacher but his midterms were tricky and a bit difficult. i performed way worse than I wanted in this course but got away with a B- due to a curve. our final's avg was 58/100 so you can go figure but the concepts are relatively simple but hard to grasp in such a short amount of time. honestly wish i could redo this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid him.

Honestly, he approaches the course logically, so missing a lecture or concept requires you catching up to speed. However, once you get the hang of it; his class difficulty isn't too hard. His tests seem fairly hard (looking from the class average). He does cover a lot of material on every lecture, so you need to make sure you're always attentive.

reviews.comment: This class was so difficult as much as I studied my efforts never showed that. I sent an email on week 5 regarding an emergency that I had  and never received an email back which to me was inconsiderate.
