reviews.comment: Funny guy but super hard class. But I ran the streets since I was young, (streets killed me)

AWFUL!!! While Levkoff does seem to be very intelligent, he'll only say things once, and there is so much content covered VERY quickly. None of the slide decks on Canvas match the lecture slides??? If you don't enjoy teaching yourself, choose a different course. And if it says anything, the mean grade on the midterm was 50/100.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Levkoff is a great guy and very knowledgeable. He does his best to get your attention during lectures and goes through a lot of example problems to understand concepts. While the class is very difficult and the exams are weighted heavily, he gives a VERY generous curve that allows for students to still pass the class and do well.

Few assignments, discussions not mandatory but could be helpful. Professor is clear in whats needed to have have a good grade in this class. Did good on one midterm, lowkey bombed the final but still mahaged to get a B- because of the curve. Really nice guy, would take this professor again but the material was hard.
This class was hard but really good professer he curves your grade ,you dont have homework ,you need to study for the midterm and test they were hard

45% midterm 45% final. Hw 5% Quizzes 5% Extra credit 5%. Midterms and final are fair. There are not many questions so make sure you know everything. The curve was very nice. Final only has 2 hours, only 10 questions, not cumulative. Overall it's not a difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For Econ4: pretty tough concepts in the class not gonna lie. Attendance not taken and lectures posted online. Tests on the tougher side. Great lecturer, funny at times, good dude. Also, he wants you to pass. He really does. The curves are HELPFUL. I got a C, but like honestly I didn't deserve it. Take this dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just study from his problem set and lecture slides. Make sure you understand everything and you will get an A.

Personally found his lectures interesting and the tangents he would go on were related to macro in the real world. The course is based off two midterms and the final, but the curve is quite generous. There is a textbook that is just supplemental, it is not necessary. He explained things well and would answer peoples questions clearly.

Fall 2022. Very chill professor. He wore flip-flops the first day of class. Very straightforward in explaining the lecture material. Exams are very reflective of the lecture material. I think the lecture itself is relatively challenging  and need time to understand. Make sure not to get left behind.

This class is ridiculously overcomplicated and overly difficult for an INTRO class. The midterm and final account for most of your grade (45%), but I will say the curves are pretty big. The midterm and especially the final did NOT reflect concepts on the assignments he told us to study the most like???? Skip this class if u can fr save yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a good professor when providing the knowledge for the class. If you are not a natural with financial accounting, you will need to rewatch the lecture, go through the textbook, and go through every practice problem heavily to understand. I wish the midterm and final had more questions similar to practice problems in the quizzes and LRPs.

Grading is insane with 45% midterm and 45% final, but everyone doesn't do great so the curve at the end of the course is good (80+ is an A). Lectures are often difficult to follow and not very coherently/logically paced. But, he gives you all the tools to succeed, its just that you need to review on your own to do well.

Clear, concise lectures. Always available to talk, is a pretty cool guy. Your grade is essentially your midterm (40%) and final (50%), so be prepared. Homework is (10%) and consists of biweekly quizzes. Discussion section attendance is not required. Textbook is available for purchase, but not required.

Best ECON professor, the class I took was actually 173B but wasn't an option. Make sure you go to his lectures and understand everything, so you won't even need to read any of the materials. His lectures are very dense, and you could learn a ton. 
Tests were easier than the practices he gave but can be tricky, make sure you go to his office hours.

Overall solid, cool dude. As a prof, he doesn't teach the concepts the best in my opinion. 40% midterm 50% final.  5% for five quizzes. 5% for hw probs w unlimited tries. Kinda dumb that he weights the midterm and final so heavily, bc if you flunk it like it did its bad, but there was a huge curve because everyone else flunked it. decent class.
Your grade is based on two main grades, a 40% midterm and a 50% final.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: overall a pretty cool & forgiving prof, always avail for office hours & questions after class. grades are dependent on biweekly quizzes, review problems, a midterm, and a final (midterm and final have heavy weight). discussions are not mandatory but were pretty helpful for learning class material. really good prof for an intro class.

I'd never taken an accounting class before but he broke down the basics and quickly built from there. The lecture notes and slides are imperative to following the class. Exams are based off slides. Interesting class and critical information to learn as business major.

Great lecturer, his hw and quizzes were manageable if you love math. Sometimes the wording is unclear or tricky on the quiz but it won't affect you getting an A in his class. The thing I dislike is the fact he would only award A+ to people with 100% cumulative average which is "impossible" with the unclear multiple-multiple choices on the quiz.

worse class I ever took at UCSD, it is no matter that this class is hard, what matter is the quiz and hw are crazy hard and not organized well as related to each other. definitely avoid it if possible.

The lack of clarity of the quizzes was so frustrating. I also disliked the trick questions he used: I don't want for my professors to trick me, I want for them to be on my side with my education.
I did very much like his lectures. I also feel like you could ask him any econ or finance question and he would know it.
He can explain lectures clearly, however, if you want to get a decent grade, you have be aware of the tricky questions on quizzes!
I like his style of teaching. He goes slow, very efficient and makes sure everyone understands everything. Quizzes can be a bit tricky, but if you show up and try you should be a good grade.
My favourite professor from UCSD, really miss his course after I graduated.
Very kind & good at explaining. The tests are based on his lectures, so make sure you go to those.

I've learned more in this class than I ever have in any other class. Levkoff is a great professor but my only gripe with the class is that the questions on the quiz are different from the material talked about in class. You'll end up practicing and working on questions you will never be tested on while seeing questions you've never seen on quizzes.

Prof. Levkoff is for sure a decent choice. 100 series can be hard. I took 100A in advance just to take his 100B. Glad that it paid off. Lecture slides are so informative and organized that make him sometimes like a slide-reader XD. Build on concepts clearly. Weekly quizzes can be hard and sometimes have little wording problem. Take him if you can.
NOT an easy A. Lectures are amazing and useful. Quizzes are open-book but they're very tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Ability to explain concepts are mediocre at best and the assignments/quizzes are not very representative of lecture contents. Very confusing flow of lecture and lots of trick questions are given out. You can try to respectfully make a case, but there's no chance it will get accepted. Although your explanation may be true, he'll insist his method.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of those professors where the examples gone over during lectures do not suffice for the quizzes/exams. Explanations are sometimes unnecessarily complicated and often confuses students more than the content should. Most importantly, does not spend enough time on important concepts while expecting you to develop more understanding during quizzes.
HARDEST CLASS I'VE EVER DONE. NOPE.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of my favorite econs professors. He has quizzes every week, but they are super fair and as long as you go to lecture they should be easy with minimal effort. His lectures are also super interesting and engaging, and he like to includes real-world examples to make it easier to understand. Overall, an amazing Professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Be ready to go to sleep when you enter one of his classes. He gives examples for one of the many things that he will cover - and never things that will actually be showing up on tests. Spend your time on working through problems on your own instead of letting him show you, and you will learn more! Honestly, don't bother attending his classes.
not for me. the course itself is already hard, but he makes it 10 times HARDER.

Professor Levkoff is great overall. He utilized a weekly 10-question quiz format, with difficulties varying by week but generally being pretty fair. The grade in the class mostly depends on the quizzes and weekly homework assignments, so it is not hard to keep a good grade. Lectures are important and very useful, especially with helpful examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He explains concepts very clearly and his lectures are attractive. His grading is not harsh. Recommended!

Professor Levkoff was my favorite Econ professor at UCSD. He made lectures so interesting and was amazing at teaching. His tests are definitely not for the faint of heart, but despite the difficulty of the exams he does have a pretty generous curve. He was also very helpful in office hours. 1 of my fav classes I took w/ him was econ 2, 100% recco
Amazing and explains concepts well. Also a nice sense of humor
Very clear and concise. His lectures were very understandable but he tend to move quite fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Levkoff was very organized in his teaching style and was a fair grader. His quizzes were pretty tricky sometimes, but he gives us enough resources in order to be successful on them. He always kept his lectures engaging and interesting and gave very clear explanations for concepts.

Graduated about a year back, but my last class I took for Econ was honestly the most horrifying one. Levkoff was unable to explain the theories proper, and none of the lectures guided you through the exams. I believe in teaching and allowing students to learn, not terrifying students by letting them know that 30% is a C grade.

Prof Levkoff is a very solid professor, and he was able to make a super boring class like financial accounting interesting! He knows the material from the bottom of his heart and makes very smart jokes. This class was super manageable; definitely will take courses from him again when he starts teaching upper division again!

I am so glad I chose Dr. Levkoff for my first (many more to come) Econ classes in UCSD. His lectures are clear and concise, you just have to put in a little effort than usual because the weekly assignments are somehow heavily conceptual but the weekly 10-item quizzes (in lieu of the midterms and finals) are much easier than the assignments.

Good professor and teaches well. His teaching style involves showing lots of graphs and calculations in order to prove concepts, which helps me understand what he is teaching. Some of the quizzes were difficult because of tricky questions. Like for some of the questions I didn't really understand what answer he was looking for. Overall solid choice

Levkoff is a gem bro. He's always prepared for class, and personally, I think he goes very very slowly to maximise comprehension. He's been teaching the class for a while, so he's very clear about what actions should be taken to guarantee your success in ECON 1. The quizzes are killer sometimes, but if you know the slides well you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He gives many real-life examples while explaining concepts. He can definitely help you better engage in class cuz It is never boring. But he always gives questions that are not mentioned in class and the lecture is fast! BE aware of his tricky and difficult tests(quizzes and review problems).

I took the online class so it was recorded if you missed class. You can't skip the classes or you won't pass. Weekly quizzes (you can drop lowest 2) plus weekend assignments due on Sundays at the last 3-4 weeks of class are all math and are 75% more difficult than prior classes. Lots of TA help if you need it. This teacher is solid and decent.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, he's a great lecturer and is able to explain complex microeconomics subjects as simple as possible. On your part, you HAVE to do the problem sets and lecture review problems to understand the algebra of the concepts. Also, make sure to understand the slides inside-out because the weekly quizzes are trickier than you think.

Very clear lecturer+organized class. Kinda overcomplicates micro but still understandable. Weekly quizzes instead of midterms/finals bc its online. The quizzes wording can be confusing so its easy to lose points so watch out for them. He drops your 2 lowest scores and curves the overall class. He takes class feedback well and adjusts accordingly

His lectures are amazing, especially since the material is dry. He provides screencasts, powerpoints, etc. He grades based on engagement of the material rather than on high-stake examinations due to the threat of the pandemic. Quizzes can have some tricks but nothing impossible and you can drop two quizzes. Overall, I would highly recommend him!
Esay A+. Go to the lectures and discussion sessions, then you can make it.

He is a great professor, but the homework's can be hard. If you have chegg you'll be fine. Tests are a little tricky but he puts a huge curve on them. This last semester on our midterm, a 32/40 was an A! Anyways, I highly recommend him for an easy A, while still learning a good amount of info about the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This dude is a frickin legend. His lectures are always really funny and engages the students. As a "true believer of freedom", this class is graded 100% off 3 exams, so there's not a single assignment you have to hand in. This saved me a lot of time to put into other classes. However, he always gives good resources to practice with online.
His test is extremely hard and it is quite different than what he posted on tritoned. His lectures are slides reading. Strongly do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Midterm 1 was super easy, Midterm 2 a lot more difficult as expected. Lecture slides are uploaded online, he reads off the slides during lecture and occasionally works out the problems on the board. Exams follow the format of the practice exams he uploads beforehand. Fair lecturer, class progressively gets harder.

Dr.L was a great professor. Exams are difficult, but if you show up to class and pay attention, and put in the effort, it is not bad. Attendance is not mandatory, but for every day you go to class, you get a bonus point added to your first midterm score, and an additional point if you get the mob lab question correct. Highly recommend Dr.L.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Took a dull and boring subject and made it bearable. His Econ 4/MGT 4 class consisted of pop quizzes and multiple choice exams. He explains content really well and tried to liven things up by making the occasional bad joke. Truly he is a caring professor and is really clear. I recommend him highly.

Levkoff is by far my favorite Econ professor. He's hilarious and great at introducing students Econ concepts. Tests look tricky but they are actually not if you put in the work on practicing his past exams. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fair Tests, not easy class, put efforts to get good grades.

He likes to assign hours long video for students to watch. Obviously, he couldn't finish teaching materials on time. So he let us watch hours long video and teach ourselves. He mentions that it's a fair game to test stuffs in the video in detail. He's taking students' time to fix his own fault of not able to go through those materials in class.

Great professor. He gives great lectures and really keeps the classroom greatly energized. He posts old midterms/finals, which is a great study tool. He posts lecture slides on ted which is also great. Understand the material on the lecture slides, study the practice tests, and you'll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not a hard class, but he made this class harder and being a nightmare, worst attitude to studs
the worst Econ Professor I never seen before, really bad attitude to students in office hour and during the class when asking him questions. Avoid him

I took levkoff for Financial Accounting, which is dry material at best but Prof. Levkoff made every lecture hilarious and engaging. His exams were representative of what had been covered in class and his grading criteria was straightfoward. I would highly recommend taking a class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Exams and the course is pretty straighforward, just keep in mind there are clicker-type questions during lecture
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Tests are similar to practice, but too many conceptual questions for which I lost all my points. Other parts are quite easy.
He is very smart, Is great at teaching but his attitude sks. Is arrogant, not helpful out of class room, I rather skip him next time.
Levkoff is a really good lecturer. He is really good at explaining the material and provides all the resources you need to succeed in the class.

Questions on tests were confusing. He intentionally tries to word test questions abstractly, so students have struggle with questions. A class with this much of material is hard enough, so there is no need to be more confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Since he spent a lot of time on materials relevant to 120B, he was behind the schedule for both midterms and final exam. On both 2nd midterm and final, he put questions which he definitely didnt teach them. I dont know how he does normally, but this quarter he was very inefficient, and I highly do not recommend him.

The combination of his condescending demeanor and his rudeness when answering questions made this class a bad experience. Furthermore, he fell way behind, had to cram most of 100c into 3 weeks, and assigned outside-class lectures to be tested on. He loves to test on info he failed to teach, so if you like surprises on exams be sure to take him.

I was wrong about Levkoff. I thought he wasn't clear, but if you truly listen through lectures, everything makes sense for the most part. He tries his best to make dry material more funny, and he is someone that you can tell is actually putting in effort. He used to be a CFO of a company, so he definitely knows his stuff. He's a great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Levkoff Is by far the best teacher I've had at UCSD in my four years. He lectures very clearly and is super receptive to student questions. Exams are pretty representative of problem sets and what he goes over in class, but he doesn't post slides or much content so you have to attend lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Steve is a very good instructor for ECON4/MGT4 course. He is so inspirational for his students. Attending his lectures does matter for two reason: 1)He provides better understanding of the class concepts. 2) Moblab activities in class that worth 10% of your overall grade. 2midterms: 1st weighs 25%, the 2nd weighs 30%, and a final weighs 35%, are MC
Very good professor!! I recommend to attend lectures because there is attendance check once a while! The time is annoying because it is from 6:30 to 7:50 but going to lecture is very helpful!
VERY GREAT AND HUMOROUS PROFESSOR... LOVE THIS CLASS....

Great lecturer. Always very organized. Interesting material, and just overall a very knowledgeable and funny guy. 3 exams, all MC. Way more theory heavy than I thought. Class is curved, top 25% gets an A. Median score for exams were around 75%. No quiz, no HW. Study the slides, disregard the problem sets. Also disregard the study sessions.
Great and knowledgeable prof. You need to attend every lecture and sit in the front rows because he makes material more sense than the power point. I would definitely take him again
The class was a harder course than those that I usually take. The last 3 weeks were dense with material that was tricky. The professor joked around but the exams were hard and were barely scaled.
He is an awosome professor, young, passionate and like chanllenges. Kind of person that will inspire you naturally.
Good lecturer but his hw for econ 4 is not very beneficial.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class material should be easy in a mathematical sense. However, the midterm start late and you are force to end early. TAs and grader does not respect the midterm rubric give you 0 if you get the answer wrong. No partial credit. If you regrade you get lower score because you will be regraded by all of your corrrect answer again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's one of the best lecturers I've had and easily the best Econ professor I've taken. That being said, his tests literally destroyed me. He's pretty straightforward and explains concepts really well during lecture but his final was insanely hard. He does curve generously, but not enough :( But if you get an A on the final you get an A in the class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I'm not actually in his class, but I sat in one night with one of my sorority sisters, and he is a pretty interesting professor. He is funny and engaged, if the class didn't have a waitlist I would have enrolled. Also, he's VERY HOT....10/10

Responds to e-mails with questions about the class almost instantly. Also I accidentally missed the final, but Levkoff was willing to allow me to make-up the final, even though his syllabus stated all missed exams would be a zero.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: The most clear and straightforward professor I've ever had. Lecturers are enjoyable and note-friendly. Tests are very challenging, but they are wholesome and have partial credit. Math is not based on your numbers as much as what you're attempting to do. Also has a wonderful curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Hard to understand what he says during the lecture. The test are hard. First part of question, no matter TRUE or False, you have to explain why. It doesn't make sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor! Clearly well-versed and helps students nail down any and all Econ concepts that he teaches. His class may be a bit tedious (especially in the summer) but he was awesome when approached by students (both in class and during office hours). He was an inspiring teacher, other teachers should take a page out of his book (in teaching)

Professor Levkoff was a joy of a professor to have. His lectures were interesting, and I really appreciated how he took particular care to teach us the intuitive reasoning behind everything. He's also a fun professor to take as he's very animated and personable in class. He was also very helpful during office hours!

he is definitely not the one who can teach econ110b well. he cannot explain definition clearly and always talking about something irrelevant. do not take his class for econ 110b!!!!!!exam so hard and tough graded. i need to find other professor's ppt to review his class.

I've literally never reviewed anyone on here but Prof Levkoff is great. Favorite professor at UCSD. His tests are hard but very reflective of the material he teaches and the curve is really generous. Never went to office hours or discussion but got an A in the class. You really learn a lot of cool things that you can tell your friends.
He's the man.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: good professor. this is not an easy class by any means but if you work hard and go to lectures, you should be fine. you have 2 chances to get a A. one by normal grading, and one for getting A on final exam. Definitely go to lectures or you will not pass with good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best professor
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His lectures are amazing. He shows sincere care for the learning of the students and explains things in a way that helps completely understand what it is youre learning and how to apply it. He also provides all of his past exams which gives you a great deal of practice towards the concepts he feels will be relevant to the test

Really good professor who is passionate about the material and really wants you to succeed. It is a challenge course but if you put in the work mastering the problem sets and old exams you'll do just fine.  If you take all of the midterms and score an A on the final he will give you an A in the class.

Probably the only professor whose lectures I attended for economics. He's Some people find his tests difficult, but he explains the concepts so well that you'll understand everything you need to know. Utilize his test banks.

Probably the only professor whose lectures I attended for economics. He's captivating and he explains the material better than anyone else I've taken thus far. Some people find his tests difficult, but he explains the concepts so well that you'll understand everything you need to know. Utilize his test banks.

I learned the most I've ever learned in any Econ course in his class. He explained things graphically, mathematically, and intuitively to ensure all students could understand no matter their preferred learning method. He hates cheating and got many students in trouble for it. My favorite professor and I would highly recommend him.

Class graded by two midterms and a final. Writes a lot on the board, so even though attendance isn't taken, you want to go to lecture. You COULD learn out of the book, but Levkoff explains things super clearly; take advantage of that. His lectures are engaging and he makes the concepts easy to understand.

Pros: Really good lecturer and explains things pretty clearly Cons: - Majority of his lecture is on the board so if you miss something (even if you're at the lecture), it'll be hard to review and go over it again - Grades are totally dependent on midterms and final... which are pretty tough Still would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Class wasn't as bad as the other ones in the 100 series - Levkoff made it pretty entertaining.  Several students were upset about another student that was cheating, but Levkoff PROMISED that he would catch the cheater.  In fact, he actually used game theory to catch the person cheating during the final exam - DON'T CHEAT!  HE WILL CATCH YOU!!!
Can not fail if you take the tests, he grades on a curve and the bottom 5% gets D's

What's really awesome about him is that he truly demonstrates the materials very well and clearly, makes everything easy to understand. Pay attention to the examples he gives during lecture because those are important applications of the concepts that may show up on the test. His slide and last-minute OHs are very helpful, too. TAKE HIM IF YOU CAN.

Gives really good lectures. Go through the homework and past exams to study. Has a big curve so don't worry too much if you do bad on the tests. Don't have to show up to lecture if you prepare off the homework and past exams.
Favorite ECON professor in UCSD so far. Interesting lecture. Exams are not easy but fair. Go to every lecture, you will passsssssss.

Steve is my all time favorite professor at UCSD. I took both 100C and 110A with him and got A's in both. He is super cool and makes lectures interesting and clear. He makes all his old exams available and if you do every question and understand the answers, you will get an easy A. Overall love this guy, thanks Steve!

I was so lucky that the problem set solutions are available and they are super clear and logical. I stuck to study those solutions right before each test so I got a decent grade. Prof Levkoff is just as clear in his lectures. Overall he is a super efficient professor, his delivery style is very enchanting too.

This professor is the best, his lecture is interesting, and his tests are easy, you will expect to get an easy A if you work hard like me. I recommend to take two of his classes together, and you will learn a lot of life.
Just take his class, and you will know the definitions of a good professor.
MY ECON GOD.

I'm really glad I took Steve's class. He's an awesome lecturer and really tries to make class interesting.  Be prepared to work because by no means was it an easy class. He definitely knows his stuff. Great guy too. Go to his office hours!!! I wish I went more often
I like the way Professor  Levkoff teaches and how he makes good use of mob lab in class!! He cares a lot about his students! Very nice ! Good professor !

I got a D on my 1st midterm because I slacked off and then got scared so I actually started listening to his lectures in class and studied the problem sets then the past exams (very helpful!), and got an A on the 2nd one. He's very clear and makes lectures interesting. I actually learned a lot from his class. Definitely my favorite professor!
He's a young and passionate professor. However, his exam is too hard. but it does have a large curve.

He's an amazing professor and you'll definitely learn a lot in his class. However, his tests are really tough and difficult. If you're looking for an easy A, I would avoid him. However, if you want to become enlightened and learn a lot, then he's a must.
lecture is clear, but his test the so harsh. 43 would have a A
One of the best professors at UCSD. Difficult exams but worth taking!
Really good teacher. Very clear with the content. Fair tests.
GREAT TEACHER AT UCSD.

Hands down the best professor I have ever had at UCSD. Explains things very clearly and can answer any question off the top of his head. If anything is confusing in class, then he would happily and even more clearly explain the problem. Always willing to help you out!
Great teacher! Very clear and organized. I like that he uses both the board and power point during lectures. Summer session wasn't too fast either.
His tests are really really hard

I took his class in summer session and it only have one midterm and one final. You can ace the class if you get a solid A on final. That's fairly good even though the final is usually harder than the midterm. He has great understanding about the material and can convey it to students in a clear and well-organized way. I like his lectures.

Inspirational lecturer! My thirst for Economics is temporarily fulfilled every quarter I took his class.  If you are eager to learn economics, take his class regardless of his TOUGH but DOABLE tests. my Econ GPA is 3.8 though
I love his lecture, but the exam is hard... There is not much homework!
I love his lecture, but the exam is hard...
TA's are very strict at grading!!!! Ask for re-grades. Has a very specific taste in correct answers look at practice problems and old exams. Good professor.
good lecturer, goes really in depth. Make sure you understand whats going on conceptually before you try to just memorize formulas.

As an econ major graduating I am glad that I was able to take his 100c class to end my time at UCSD. Simply put, the material is tough but he will keep your attention and focus on point with his dynamic and stimulating lectures. He  really makes the material as intuitive as possible. Very few profs. make the infamously dismal science less so.
Awesome professor! Fun class and great teaching style

Levkoff is super cool. Tough subject but his instruction is very good. The tests are very difficult. I mastered the problem sets and exam practice but the exam questions had slight variations making it difficult for the brain muscle memory frm repetition to kick in. He is super responsive, fair and I would totally take him again. Class mvs fast.
Quantitative approach
quantitative awesome approach
Attend all lectures, understand how to do the problem sets and you'll get above an A or B. Great professor and highly recommend taking his class

Fantastic lecturer. His exams are pretty difficult, but they're curved. If you're complaining about failing an exam, it's not because Levkoff did a bad job; it's probably because you didn't conceptually understand the material well enough to apply those principles to more difficult problems.
DONT TAKE!

Failed 1st midterm bc didn't know how he graded, he looks for specific steps you take and if you skip work, even if your answer is correct, you get marked off. After the first midterm, i studied the rubric and things he underlines in his practice problems, A+ on 2nd midterm and final.   Study what he looks for and its easy class

he wasn't that bad.  the final exam was really tough, but fair.  he makes you work for it, so if you don't want to work too hard on a lower div course, i'd avoid him.  otherwise, great lectures, very entertaining.

He is a good lecturer. However, his tests are much harder than what an Econ 2 class should be. Also, while the problem sets and homework sets are helpful, his tests are much harder and not reflective of the material of the covered in the problem sets. Avoid him if you can. He is not an easy A.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. His tests are confusing and he has so many last minute things he did not cover completely on his test. Moreover, his wording on the test is hard to understand. I regret taking his class. Do not ever take this guy.

His tests are super hard and not reflective of what we learned in class. Avoid him if you can. He's not worth taking for Econ 2. It was supposed to be an easy lower div class but he made much harder than what it was supposed to be.

Professor Steven Levkoff has made Economics 2, a section of the AP Micro  Macro which shouldn't have to be taken again, into an amazing course to take for a quarter. Although, there isn't that much course material to cover, he still managed to keep me interested for the entirety of the course. Tests are fair but graded strictly.

He's really nice, helpful and quite funny at times. He doesn't teach with powerpoints often but he will upload supplemental materials and problem sets. If you don't have prior knowledge and you skip class, content might be harder to grasp but the tests are still manageable. Sometimes he also offers extra points for attendance.

Perfect class. Entertaining and instructive. Professor Levkoff provides relevant examples and holds the interest of the class. The tests aren't extremely hard, but they are not ridiculously easy either. They reflect the course material well. Plus, the dude's pretty goodlooking. 1010 Would highly recommend this class and Professor Levkoff.
Amazing professor, tough tests, large curve. Best econ prof at UCSD hands down.
I would have never enrolled in this class if I know what I am feeling now.

He is a great guy who cares about his students but he's a terrible teacher. The exams are based on math that was never covered in class. His ppt slides are all about economic concepts, but then midterm day it's all math he NEVER went through. Review sessions would had been helpful is T.A.'s actually knew what they were doing. Go to his office hrs.
It is defintely not an easy class. But you will get the grade you earn :) The professor has very useful slides and problem sets that help to understsand the concepts.
Great professor. Great class. Easy to get a good grade.

A very good professor.  So good, that sometimes you feel all giddy after lectures because he explains everything so well.  And then your heart sinks because when you sit down for exams they are damned hard.  The math is easy, but the concepts aren't, and he really tests your understanding in the most straightforward way. Derive. Derive. Derive.

Prof Levkoff know the subject very very well and he is very smart. Just 2 small suggestions for him. First, he was not able to keep up with the syllabus (less thing to study for final  ). Second, he may wants to repeat or highlight some important concepts during lecture. Something show up in the ppt for 1 slide maybe 30% of your exam.

If you can do the problem set, you will be ready for the exam. Keep in mind that MT and problem set are meant to be hard, which motivated me to study very hard for the final. I got an A for the course; not an easy A, but learned a lot from the class. Understand the big picture of the course and do the problem, you should be fine. TY Prof. Levkoff.

Seems like the only bad evaluations were given by students that either didn't know what course they were taking (Levkoff doesn't teach Econometrics... this was the first part of the MACRO sequence) or don't understand how ranking students by grades works (ie: the variance issue).  Levkoff went out of his way to create supplemental materials for us.
NA

This professor had a lot of pointless slides. He went through the topics in the beginning too slow so he was really rushing to get through material at the end. One of the analysis questions on the final was on a concept he introduced during the last 30mins of his last lecture. Wish he was a better professor.

While he's a good professor he rushed through material routinely leaving students struggling with harder concepts. The curve is generous but shouldn't need to be if he took an extra day on harder concepts. I wouldn't take him again.
he is awesome, and he is really smart in class. his exams are aweful! be care if you are international student, this is a nice chance for you to improve youself.

Professor Levkoff's 100C class was a really interesting class. I was mostly interested in the game theory aspect of the course, which Levkoff taught very well. He was also super helpful in office hours!

I took this class during summer session, so the class being only 5 weeks long made it a bit difficult. However, Professor Levkoff instantly became one my my favorite professors at UCSD with his clear and concise lecture style. 3 hour lectures were not a burden with Levkoff!
Great professor. The test are almost related to the homework. Do it, and get it. Pass the class is easy. Answer one of the four test questions correctly you probably pass the class.

He's really not a very good professor. He was behind in teaching the material so he rushed through a lot of the material at the end and even failed to cover some of the topics. This course is the first of the Econometrics series, so I hope that he didn't skip anything incredibly important for the next class.

The tests for his class are really hard, but the curve is very generous. He tries to incorporate student interaction which is rare for most econ classes so lectures aren't too horrible to sit through. He's a great lecturer so try to go to class! Econtutor isn't that vital for this class.

I've taken almost every ECON professor at UCSD and Levkoff was in my top 2. He is a genuinely good lecturer, who's enthusiasm for the course shines through. He knows the material extremely well. I actually learned from going to lecture, how refreshing. IMO him and Lagakos are the 2 best professors in the department.
I took levkoff for 100C in the summer and he was great.  However for 110A his teaching seemed really choppy and it made understanding the curriculum harder.

Great professor. Lectures are very clear and interesting. Not an easy course but still do-able, just requires commitment. For midterms, study the lecture notes and review problems and you should be fine (Don't just do the practice problems, make sure you understand them). Highly suggest attending every lecture
He was really clear in lecture. Loved him, hottie too -c.l.

I took him for both 100C and 110A this quarter and he is an awesome professor for 100C but could be a little better at 110A. I think that since this was his first quarter teaching 110A it was hard to study since there wasn't really old exams to go off of. Overall, he is a really clear professor, no tricks. Come to class and you will do well.

Professor Levkoff is a really great lecturer. His way of teaching makes it very easy to absorb the materials. His tests aren't easy but it's not too difficult. If you pay attention and do the problem sets, then you can definitely get a good grade. Furthermore, he gives very generous curves. So he is definitely a professor you'd want to have.

I don't think he is a qualified professor at all. Mean 50 and standard deviation 22. That's why he curve generously. But personally speaking the ridiculously high variance indicates he didn't concern the student performance at all! It seemed like he successfully predicted what questions could make ppl get 95 and what could make ppl get 5 out of 100

He has a great sense of humor about the class. If you want the ball rolling in class just shout out answers. That being said it means you can slow down the class by not saying anything at all and waiting for some kindred spirit to take the plunge. Pretty straightforward class

tests reflective of problem sets and lectures fair tests. it definitely helps going to class. since it was summer the lecture was the full 3 hours and a lot of material but prof was very enthusiastic about material and explained concepts well. for some lectures he used slides which make material easier to understand. definitely recommend at ucsd
Knows his stuff. Enthusiastic and cares about your learning. Tests more intuitive than mathematical. Curve too generous if you ask me.

Levkoff's class is hard. There's no denying it. However, each class is like a beautifully crafted masterpiece of teaching. Even though the material is hard, he takes nothing for granted, and Levkoff will bring you to that level. He is an extremely gifted lecturer and is very helpful. Wish I could take more classes with him.

Had Levkoff for both 100C and 110B. Knows his stuff very thoroughly and I would always recommend him as a professor. He actually cares about his students to understand the material.His exams and grade distributions are fair and you'll fail if you do not put in effort. The courses he taught are not easy but I very much enjoyed his lectures. TY STEVE
Great lecturer. If you can solve the problem sets you pretty much guarantee yourself an A.

An EXCELLENT professor. I took him for both 100C and 110B, and I plan to take as many classes from him as possible. His lectures are both informative and entertaining, and he grounds abstract concepts using real-world examples. Tests are HARD but if you go to lecture you'll be fine. Make sure you know your stuff, watch out for the T/F questions!

Course is difficult. Levkoff has VERY high expectations, but it's worth the squeeze.  I had him for a micro course in the past and was pretty  shocked at how knowledgeable he is about macro / finance topics.  This guy CLEARLY explained the relationship between quantitative easing, the yield curve, and the stock market in a 15min class segment...

Best Professor at UCSD. Took him for 100c and 171. Most helpful professor you will find. I actually enjoyed going to class and these were 3 hour classes. His teaching style is very engaging and interactive. Tests were difficult but very fair. No real reason to read textbook if you go to lectures. If you want an A you must attend lecture and study!

Lectures are a mixture between chalkboard and Powerpoints. His powerpoint lectures tend to be harder to follow. His problem sets reflect his exams. Math wise, make sure to know concepts like random variables, expected values, var/covar, probability, Baye's Rule, integration by parts, limits, and basic multivariate calculus(partial derivatives).

One of the best/hottest professor I've ever had. Clear lectures, helpful problem sets. If you go to classes and do all the problem sets, you will do fine in his class. The most important thing is, hes HOT, like, yeah, HOT.

He's young (rare for the econ dept where most profs are like my grandpa's age) and I think younger profs are much better at engaging us than, say, profs like Machina who may be geniuses but haven't been students since the Carter era. Levkoff teaches like he was in the classroom himself a couple years ago, and it really helps. If you can, take him!

Wonderful teacher, super friendly and he really cares about students. I'd definitely recommend him for any Econ class. Tests reflect material and homework/pass exams, no complain. And did I mention he's HOT?

Very clear lecture, and Professor Levkoff makes it interesting and not painful to be in class. His lecture style helps note-taking a lot. Definitely guaranteed a B or above if you go to all lectures and do all problem sets. The Professor is pretty cute too ;)
I enjoyed going to Levkoff's class a lot! helpful professor and super generous curve

Levkoff is an awesome professor and the best Econ  professor I have had at UCSD! He explains topics clearly and is extremely interactive and cracks jokes which are actually funny. He's a really genuine guy and cares about his student's. If you do problem sets, look over all his old exams and attend his office hours then you're going to do well.

Hands down the best Economics teacher I have had at UCSD. He makes you think about topics at a higher level and truly cares about the welfare of his students. He is the cream of the crop of UCSD professors. Highly recommended.

His class was never boring. He's quite an entertaining professor and if you ever go to his office hours, he's a pretty cool guy to talk to. He's also really good at teaching but his tests are hard only if you do not study enough.

Levkoff is hands down my favorite prof at UCSD. Had him for Econ 1 and 100C and absolutely loved his teaching style, he is very clear and actually interacts with the class instead of speaking for the whole time.. as long as you go to class and do the problem sets you are solid. the book is def not necessary because he explains it well enough.

Great class and very engaging professor.  He speaks clearly and gives good examples to help understand the concepts.  Highly recommend taking Econ 1 with him.  Go to class and make sure you study the slides and problem sets before each exam and you'll get a good grade.
Great, solid professor.  One of the best at UCSD and I thoroughly enjoyed his class.  Make sure you go to all classes, pay attention and study the problem sets and you're good to go!

Best lecturer I've ever had. Lecture slides are all animated, color coded, and online. Homework + solutions are also posted on TED. Never used the book. Tests are pretty tricky though. I got a B- because I did poorly on the final (two finals that day). His test questions always ask for detailed answers that explains all scenarios to get full points

For a student with limited background in Corporate Finance, Levkoff helped make this subject more clear. Lectures were straight from the book, problem sets were difficult, but office hours were a great help. My only recommendation is to allow discussion on the homework assignments, but require individual submissions. Great professor!

This course is both enjoyable and useful. If you are econ major, I'm sure you can get a solid foundation from his class; if you are not, then you just take a course that can teach you how to rationally make choices. either way, even though the class  was 3 hrs long, most of us made it and we learned a lot from this.

Levkoff was awesome. he lectured both from slides and just him writing and explaining, both were great. his slides are extremely helpful and clear, as well as his lectures in class. i always enjoyed going to class even if it was 3 hours long. he's also easy on the eyes ;)

Forget reading the book - go to lecture and look through his slides and you'll be golden. Definite recommend for those who hate economics because your outlook on the subject will change after taking his class. Not only is he a great lecturer, he's also pretty good looking ;)

Very good at explaining things. He's a lot more clear than the textbook. I read like the first two chapters of the textbook and gave up and now I only use his lecture slides. His methods of solving problems are a lot simpler and clearer than the textbook's.

Professor Levkoff was awesome. I preferred when he lectured using boardwork rather than powerpoint, but either way he was extremely clear and helpful. Made econ fun and interesting :) Exams true to his problem sets and practice exams (obviously more difficult though). I recommend him especially if you haven't taken econ yet!

Damn, I've only had two lectures so far, and I can say this guy is really good at explaining concepts. He uses a lot of analogies that really help in understanding the material. He is very handsome, too.
Just about the greatest econ professor at UCSD. Incredibly helpful, legitimately  cares about his students learning and is about as clear as can possibly be. Highly recommend!

One of the best professors I've ever had! He is not easy though, so he'll make you work! But if you do, class is super interesting and an A is achievable. There is no textbook in class, so that's a bonus, everything you need is presented in lectures. Focus in class, do the problem sets and you'll do well.
Clear, commanding voice. One of the best professors Ive ever had. Extremely helpful clear and understandable

One of the best professors I have had during my 4 years at UCSD. Makes everything SUPER clear during lectures and relates well with students our age. Make sure to do the problem sets and the class is easy. Make sure to attend class too because he gives out tons of bonus points.

He is a great professor. He tries really hard to help the students learn and pass the course. Lectures are very clear and once you have a clear understanding of the problem sets and practice exams; the exams should be easy!

I don't know if he still does this, but when I took ECON 1, he had a policy where if you get an A on the final, you get an A in the class. The final was pretty easy compared to the second midterm. (MT 1: 95, MT 2: 68, FI: 94)
he is one of the nicest and coolest prof I have even met. Amazing lecture and he really teaches students a lot of stuffs. If you really want to learn economic, take him!!!!

Professor Levkoff truly cares about teaching students. Had him for two classes and I probably learned the most in those two classes than the rest of all  my other econ classes combined. As for difficulty, if you do the problem sets and actually spend some time studying. UCSD needs more econ professors like him!

Steve is one of the best econ professor in UCSD! Exams are tough, but really learn a great deal from him. His lecture is very clear and interesting. He's very responsible and concern about students' learning. No need of econ tutor if you just go to class and do your homework

One of the best econ professor in UCSD! His lecture is very clear and easy to understand. He's very responsible and concern about students' learning. Although the exams are really tough, but it's totally worth to take his class and overcome the challenge. I learned a great deal from Professor Levkoff, and highly recommend him to everyone!

Professor Levkoff is absolutely one of my favorite professors at UCSD. He is straight-forward and very eager to help his students. He commands attention so I never had any problem losing focus. The exams are fair and represent the problem sets given. He's truly a genuine guy and makes econ interesting.

Professor Levkoff is an awesome professor! He genuinely cares for his students and always makes sure that everyone is up to par. His exams are very fair and is very reflective of the problem sets that he provides. Definitely one of UCSD's finest professors.

Professor Levkoff was an excellent instructor in Microeconomics. The clarity and directness with which he taught the class is a testament to his expertise in the subject. Professor Levkoff was able to keep the entire class engaged for the duration of the course which made retaining the material an easier thing to do.

Best professor I've had, ever. While its an intangible, he makes you WANT to come to class, something no professor has done for me at UCSD thus far. He explains the material in a very easy to understand fashion, using fascinating examples that will make you "get it" immediately. His homework problems translate very closely to exam questions too.

Levkoff is one of the best professors I've ever had. He is always here to help his students. Classes are not hard as long as you go to classes, take notes, and do problem sets. I took his 100C last year as well. Always got an A in his class with little time in a library.

Professor Levkoff is super enthusiastic and tries to keep lecture entertaining. He's very straightforward and helpful. His exams are pretty fair and represent the material on the problem sets. Definitely one of the best professors in the econ department so far!

Super nice, easy going, helpful .. this class is not unreasonable.  I felt like I really learned something versus in 100A & B, and the information stuck.  There is also a very legitimate reason why the chili peppers are on fire!  Watch out for that smile.  I definitely recommend this professor.

I'm a third year in my spring quarter and have taken over 10 econ classes, and 32 in total, and professor Levkoff is hands down the absolute best professor I've had at UCSD. He is very clear, measurable, caring, and honest. If you ever get a chance to take a class with him, do NOT miss out on the opportunity!
Sets the standard for all UCSD professors

Very good professor (probably the best I've seen at UCSD), not overrated at all. Do the Problem Sets, go to lecture and even a little bit of study before the midterms and I assure you that you will get an A. He seems like a pretty chill guy as well.
Clear, helpful, chill dude. Keeps your attention during lecture and posts his slides online. Midterms are reflective of the HW problems. GO TO SECTION AND KEEP UP WITH PROBLEM SETS FOR BEST RESULTS.

Prof Levkoff is LITERALLY the BEST teacher I've EVER had! 500% better than any! I came in with very low interest & confidence in micro(from difficulties in 100AB). Prof Levkoff made it ALL make sense. I accepted I'd never understand micro.. but I was wrong! I'm literally a different guy now. I have confidence again! For that, I owe him everything.
Hands down, best professor at UCSD. Easy A if you pay attention in class and do all the hw (not mandatory). I wish he taught all the Econ classes.
He is an excellent lecturer with humor and creativity. I love his teaching style and I really appreciate his help this quarter!

Unbelievable, If it's your first time taking Econ, take this professor. He is extremely clear and very funny when it comes to lecturing and helps you understand in places you'd have trouble. Overall a good person all around, definitely recommend taking him.

Outstanding professor! I like how he dresses like a student, it makes him seem even that much more cool. His lectures are crystal clear and his tests are extremely fair. Cracks jokes here and there that are pretty hilarious, and no I am not one of those typical nerds that laugh at stupid jokes. This professor is ultra chill. Definitely recommend!

Dr. Levkoff's teaching is absolutely spectacular. He's clean-cut in his explanations and gets to the point. He's very math oriented and his PowerPoints are clear and easy to learn from. I didn't even touch the textbook. It's not difficult to do well in his class as long as you do the problem sets and study the ppts. HIGHLY recommend.

Great professor. Clear instruction and lecture slides and problem sets are very helpful in learning the material. Exams are not bad and the class is graded on a curve. This was my first time learning econ, it was a great class from a great prof !
A very nice instructor.

One of the chillest professors in UCSD. I'm not an Econ manager, but he makes this subject very interesting. You do not need the textbook. You can rely on his lecture slides and notes taken in class. The material towards the end is quite challenging (last two problem sets) but otherwise everything is straight forward and worth learning.
HE IS A REALLY GOOD, AND HIS TEACH IS VERY CLEAR. BUT FINALS R HARD
Great teacher who's clearly dedicated to his students to make sure they understand the material.  I really recommend you take him :)
Amazing professor! He makes everything super clear and his lectures interesting. I really enjoyed being in his class. I wish he taught all the Econ classes I need to take.
Great Professor! He is reasonable with his grading and explains each concept clearly. We did not have to use the textbook at all which was something i liked!
Very good professor - really good at teaching and extremely helpful in office hours.
GREAT ! Take Him!

Progessor Levkoff is one of the best professors I've had. He is super clear when lecturing in class an uses easy to follow examples that helped me learn concepts easier. He moves at a good pace, not too fast, but not too slow. I felt like we covered so much material within the hour lecture, but I never felt like we rushed through anything.

amiable and nice lecturer. wonderful lectures . quizzes are of reasonable difficulties.

She's nice, funny, and explains things very well. However, I never took physics before, so this class was hard. Because of that, I dropped it. One needs to put in the effort to do the ungraded homework problems in order to do well on her quizzes. I would've like to have her in other physics classes. I-clicker questions are good checkpoints and EC.

If you've either never taken or seen little of classical mechanics, Professor  Dudko's class is for you. She knows how to effectively explain concepts and is very open to questions from students. Reading the textbook and doing practice problems are very helpful. If you study the concepts and algorithms from the quizzes, the final should be fine.

Professor Dudko's class is really great! She goes through examples and explains everything pretty well. She has a sense of humor, but it's best not to mess with her. Do well on the quizzes and the final should be no issue. Extra credit is offered through clicker questions. Grading scale is fair.

Hard class but she's pretty nice. Can't say I learned alot because I already took physics in high school but she seemed like she was doing alright. Accent wasn't a big deal, but she could have explained things a little better. HW not mandatory. BUT,to get a B in this class you will have to put in more effort than usual because of the weekly quizzes

She gives really clear explanations. She gives extra credit clicker questions to test your understanding of the material. These are actually really helpful because she will re-explain the key concepts and these question also model some of the conceptual questions on the quizzes.
Easy lectures and homeworks, more challenging final project but graded nicely
Use iClickers. Weekly quiz not hard. Ukraine Accent but Pretty clear(not like my PHYS 2B professor this quarter, misery)

Homework was reasonable if you did the homework which was not mandatory. Homework was broken into easy, medium, and hard. Some of these questions were very similar to the ones on the exam. The lecture notes also had some examples that might be similar to exam questions.  Nice lady, boring class.

Like most physics classes, this class was not easy at all. However, the professor was a very great lecturer. She was very clear and precised on the theories and concepts. Her quizes and tests were very tricky and confusing. If you do most of the homework, you should be able to get a decent grade in this class since the class has a curved scale.
Great instructor! Weekly quizzes were reasonable enough. Not too hard, not too easy. Puts in a good effort explaining physics to her students. Lectures are not boring and easy to follow. Recommend!

Great professor! Shows care for her students and makes learning Physics fun. She has great powerpoints with animations. She gives 8 quizzes (2 are dropped) which make 60 percent of your grade. And final is 40 percent. Clicker questions can get you up to 5 percent extra credit. Take her if you can!

Dudko is AMAZING. Take her class if you can! You will never have such a great physics professor again. She explains concepts clearly and includes relevant examples during lectures. Homework is not mandatory. There are 8 quizzes and a final. Clicker questions are extra credit as well. Take her class! You won't regret it.

Amazing professor. I enjoyed coming to lecture every single time. She has a deep understanding of physics, along with much enthusiasm. She is also very funny as well. Makes physics understandable, clear, and interesting. Do your HW, go to lecture, and the quizzes will be fair. The final is based off of quiz questions and clicker questions.

Strictly follows ppt slides taken exactly from Phillips. Too much bio and minimal derivation. Lacks physical insight. Only knows one derivation per problem. Often asks "does anyone already know the derivation?" and when people offer ideas that differ from her lecture slides, she just says they're wrong and moves on. Mundane, easy, useless homework.
AWESOME

Prof Dudko is sweet, funny, and very knowledgeable. It's easy to tell that she cares that the class learns Physics really well. She gives all the resources to succeed in her class. The quizzes are based on concepts and homework; clicker is extra credit up to 5%; final is more than fair. Physics is a tough course, but not impossible to get an A.
Best professor ever met!

She is a wonderful professor, not only because she explains things well(even though we think it's too detailed) but also because her class will be rewarding if you put efforts in it. Although I am an engineering major student, it is worthwhile for me to wait for her class in spring as I didn't take physics 2A in the fall.
She's boring.She's hard. She has an accent. She absolutely did not change how I think of physics. I hated it. You have weekly quizzes, no curve.

I was dreading Phys for years before finally taking it. She changed my entire view. Very clear lectures, EC available, Read textbook and do problems! They help a lot. It is very possible to get an A in her class but you must work hard and be dedicated. She uses lots of life + in class examples to help you understand. Great teacher!!!

Professor Dudko probably saved my life. I was considering dropping out of college until I took this class. Her passion allowed me to learn so much and reminded me of my own passion for learning. Her powerpoints are humorous and she is extremely dedicated to making sure her students understand every step in her lecture. Best teacher ever.

Great professor who uses powerpoints in lecture, which helps with organization of notes. Unlike many other physics professors, she works out specific examples with numbers during lecture which is extremely helpful when doing homework and studying for tests. She has weekly quizzes and a final, which were pretty difficult but fair.

Physics is a laborious class. It requires alot of studying outside the class. Her lectures were very helpful and interesting. Her quizzes were challenging and her final was just the quiz questions and homework. Her grading scale isnt that generous but she offers 5% EC which let me get a B instead of C

Physics is hard, but it's really interesting.  I'm so glad I had Prof Dudko because she explains everything VERY well, unlike most professors.  Quizzes are not impossible and overall her class was a great experience.  Plus she is caring and funny and really does take teaching seriously.
She explains concepts REALLY well. Her quizzes are not easy, but they're fair if u took the time to do homework. Plus she is very attractive, and has an accent pleasing to the ears :)

It is a challenging course, but she's a GREAT prof. Has a slight accent, but it doesn't affect her clarity at all. Sometimes has demonstrations that keep lectures a little more interesting, and she sometimes shows her sense of humor, making her lectures much less monotonous. However, it's up to you to do the work to get a good grade.

Great professor with Iclicker as extra credit, she explains the materials very clearly and allow notes on the test and quizzes, although quizzes are fair, there are always one or two hard questions in it, i recommend this professor, u can skip the book, rely solely on the lecture and still be able to pass the class with at least a B-
she is AWESOME

she gives clicker attendance 5% bonus which will DEFINATELY help with grades. She's very clear in her lecture, therefore making physics a little easier than it naturally is. Physics is hard, so TAKE HER! she will help! office hours are HELPFUL!

She teaches off her ppt and most of the time, the quizzes will be based of the ppt and the hw, so go to the lecture, you get 5% extra credit for iclicker, but the thing doesn't work sometimes, which is a bit lame, overall physics is a very hard class, but she makes it a bit easier
Definitely take Dudko for Physics 2A.  She is one of the most sincere and helpful professors ever.  Highly recommended!
Professor Dudka really cares how her students do in the class. she explains the material very, very well but physics in inherently difficult so unfortunately hw is still important.  she's the bomb

Good and easy professor. Quizzes are very important, so do your homework and you will ace them. She basically teaches off her powerpoints, which are posted online so theres no real need to go to class. She does, however, offer 5% extra credit for clicker participation. Easy multiple choice final.

Physics is a hard class but quizzes which are worth 60% are reasonable. The final was comparable to the quizzes. Attendance is recommended because the extra 3% I got helped. Would recommend this professor for 2A.

Very manageable physics class...while not easy, Dudko makes the concepts easier to understand and tests them fairly on her quizzes.  Like the person below me said, class attendance is somewhat mandatory as she uses clicker questions for extra credit, and they often show up on the weekly quizzes.  Take her for PHYS 2A!

I suck at physics and even I passed her class. Just be really careful not to make mistakes on the quizes because they are worth 60% of your grade. When I went back to study for the final, I realized how well I could have done in the class :-/...Overall good prof though...way easier than Sharma.

Very clear and easy to follow. Her quizzes are relatively easy to fair. If you go to lectures and read the book, you should do well. Classes are kind of mandatory.. She has a clicker system except it's 5% extra credit if you answer all the clicker questions correctly. Excellent professor overall.
No Comments
so much homework and grunt work
Easy to get A+ if you have sophisticated Java programming skills. Also, Dr. Ochoa curved a lot. So, you can get almost 93-95 percent in the exams and be curved to 100 percent or more.
This professor gives you prelecture video and prelecture quizes and tremendous homework. You might be curved from B to A+, B-to A- or stay at B- not changed. So get ready for a gamble.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Not that hard to pass if you really put effort in, especially under the situation he gave a great curve. But the course system is already outdated. I can't agree on the strong emphasis on not using AI, and he's just being stubborn. Besides that, the professor has a good face card.

Live coding only helps if you still need to learn the basics. The amount of hours u need to put in for hw is long, just study for midterms and finals using the ones, along with knowing some basic strategies for problems. I did thoroughly learn the material though, so he did his job.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Homeworks were difficult, exams were difficult, but curves a lot!

Homework and prelecture quizzes are long and difficult, but his prelecture videos summarizes the topics of the class, while the lecture is when he applies the concepts to use. Exams are not a lot of the final grade and are simple compared to the prelecture quizzes
Homeworks were long and tedious. Exams aren't too difficult. Great curve.
A lot homework, but great curve.
Very clear lecture. Even though there are a lot of homework and the final is pretty hard, he offered a very generous curve.
A lot of homework especially the PA's. Prelecture quizzes were alright. Midterm wasn't that bad compared to the final which was pretty hard. The curve is very very generous though
the curve is so kind
Workload is kind of heavy but exams are easy and he curves a lot in the end.

low cortisol professor. high cholesterol course. The lectures do not cover enough to be useful for homework or exams. The homework's are extremely time consuming. Tricky pre-lecture quizzes. There is not enough time in the lectures and quarter to properly cover all the course material, be prepared to learn on your own. Python knowledge doesnt help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: very fast-paced, loads of homework, and every knowledge needs to learn by ourselves, and the lecture just shows a few examples.
boring syntax memorization
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you're already java fluent it will be easy. Otherwise the class will be the hardest you've taken and consume most of your life. It's just an insane amount of content and homework but at least the grading curricula is somewhat reasonable. Prof is a chill guy and decent teach but its just too much content for one quarter. U gotta grind
Insane amount and length of homework, lectures are unhelpful, prelectures are long and difficult. For an intro class the difficulty and lack of teaching is way too much

Super long lectures plus pre-lectures that can't keep students focused. Heavy pre-lecture quiz. Most of the PAs need to be types from blank or from creating the file. Need to follow strict guideline forms for PAs that takes almost 1 whole day to rerun and recheck the format. PAs are unreasonably heavy and repeated and they need forever to complete.
so much homework and teach nothing. go teach yourself.
Intro class with so much work, the professor doesn't teach well, just all over the place. Teaching methods are very bad

Be prepared for A LOT OF homework. Prelecture quizzes are tough, but you can do as many times as you want to get full credit. Exams are pretty easy and are related to the lecture, much easier than those prelecture quizzes. Overall, Benjamin Ochoa is a nice guy, and if you can withstand heavy workload from homework, getting a high score isn't hard.

The GPA of this class consists of homework, prelecture quiz, midterm and final exams. For prelecture quiz, although it largely based on the prelecture video and is very tricky and difficult, prof.Ochoa gives us infinite attempts so it won't be a problem. The homework is indeed quite long but it makes sense as we only got one per weeks.

i didn't go to class at all so idk how his teaching was but dunno why the reviews are complaining about the final, that test covered pretty basic/core stuff from lectures and the questions weren't very specific at all, plus the cheat sheet was double sided which should have let people cover everything
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The homework takes a very long time. Without prior coding experience, this class can be difficult. It is very fast-paced. Midterm and Final are fairly easy if you looked at all the slides. You learn the content before class and then he does live coding in class. Lots of opportunities to upgrade your grade. Great guy and decent teacher.

This class was just way too much. It tries to cover an insane amount of material to a very superficial level. I had to rewatch lectures 2 to 3 times just to have a semblance of what was going on at a high level. Unfortunately, the 40% final expected you to recollect dozens of arbitrary formulas rather than focus on understanding.

If you take his 252A, expect final exam to take 40% of total grade while it tests all the minor details showed up on corners of his twenty 100-page slides, the real final exam way harder than the sample exam which is simply there to confuse you on the actual difficulty, lots of classic CV instead of ML, long time spent on hw that does not help exam

After taking his class this quarter, I probably will have to agree with the others here. Lectures are so dense class could be split in two, yet expects to know every little detail for the final. Assignments were fun at least but lectures were not interactive, just him showing 30 different equations and not explaining well.

Ochoa basically does a flipped classroom where you come in knowing most of the material already. Assignments are worth a large portion of your grade and range from just a few hours to 10+ depending on your programming experience. Assignments are worth and really help you learn. Lectures are somewhat informative as well as recorded

This class will be difficult unless you already know java. 

The PAs are not enough practice to help you with the exams. He teaches a lot of theory but actual coding practice was insufficient. The pre lecture quizzes were all MCQs. He also had prelecture videos to watch and just repeated everything in lecture.

Alright I don't appreciate the slander here. Yes his homework is long. Yes his lectures aren't the MOST helpful. And yes, it's a lot for an intro course. But it's absolutely 100% doable. If you can do the homework, you can absolutely do his exams. I got a 100% on the last midterm. If you're taking other classes, beware. Good luck! He's nice :)

Worst class I've taken at UCSD. Homework and exams barely relate to the lectures. The instructor gets irritated easily, even when students ask normal questions, and often argues instead of explaining. Very disrespectful attitude overall. Avoid this class if possible — truly exhausting experience.
Lecture and prof is not bad but too much homework, and it is really not easy so get ready for it.

He may be bad at teaching, he may be giving a lot of homework, he may enjoy making easy things redundant, but he somehow still has a job at UCSD. This shows that the job market is not as bleak as it seems if someone like Ochoa has held a job at UCSD for years.

Ochoa isn't the best lecturer, but provides the info you need through pre-class vids. The material requires a lot of self-teaching, there's no way around it. It was my first coding class, but I was pretty dedicated to learning the material. With time and practice on PAs, you'll be fine. The exams were extremely easy compared to PA's.4% EC offered.

Definitely don't take this class if you have a lot on your plate already- it's a lot of time commitment and SO NOT worth it for the basic level of java I know now. He's a nice guy and whatever, but HOLYY his class destroyed me. I spent like 70% of my time this quarter doing the homework. You'll either hate or love cse11, and a lot of ppl hated it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Didn't finish my review- it has the same tags so it's a continuation from that rating. He's not as terrible as a professor as the other reviews make him out to be, but he 100% could have structured his course WAY better. It was A LOT of self learning for me, and I'm completely new to java. Only reason I didn't fail is because of his upgrade policy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Homework incredibly long and difficult for what he taught in class, it took me a minimum of 20 hours per assignment to complete after PA4. His prelecture videos were very conceptual. He does cover actual coding during his lectures, but they're very basic compared to what we have to do on the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Never ever take his course if u wanna get an A.
just dont save urself
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you know java or have a lot of prior coding experience you should be fine, otherwise you're most likely going to struggle. its very VERY fast paced and you have to be on top of it. exam and homework are time consuming and they feel like ur solving a puzzle, hes nice in office hours though and during lecture so + points for that

Coming into this class I was worried because of how low the rating, but honestly he was not that bad. He's a nice professor who will answer your questions during lecture or on Piazza. Homework/prelecture quizzes are long, but if you stay on top of it youll be fine. Exams were also pretty light, most common score was 100, average was a B on midterm.

Bro is just mad. Bro will be angry at every single tiny issue including the file header and your piazza post.
