Homework are just insane and you are just writing thousands lines of code for each PA like a bot. Quiz before each lecture which means that you have to learn the content before learn the content. Just take the course when its not him omfg
IF YOU VALUE YOUR SANITY, DO NOT TAKE IT WITH THIS PROFESSOR. PLEASE.

This was a truly awful class. There's really nothing to do about it since CSE 11 is a prerequisite for everything, but the department has clearly confused the terms "Accelerated Pace" with "Ridiculous, Tedious, & Guaranteed Burnout." The class a complete drawl for anyone with legit coding experience, and the homework is ridiculous. Don't take it.

I thought he was chill and the assignments weren't bad. That was until PA4...that is when things took a turn. The instructions were so VAGUE and I was like okay, thats on me. then again, the same ISSUE. I emailed him about it and he was so passive aggressive. like bro I shouldn't be spending hours trying to decipher the instructions like a riddle.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have considerable knowledge in Java going into this course and it was still extremely tough. I recommend taking it with another professor if you want to save your sanity.

I didn't have any problems with him whatsoever. People saying his lectures suck when I thought they were great. He was straight to the point and was completely clear and concise on what he was trying to convey. Tons of material to go through in lectures + pre-lectures so the quick pace isn't too tough. If you like comp sci you'll be just fine.

I think the lectures do not correlate to what is on the midterms and finals. the stuff we do in lecture is much easier in comparison to what is on the test. There are no practice problems done in class that are similar to what is on the test the few practice that we do is much easier and not that helpful.
Voice so monotone, hard to listen and pay attention in class

Egoistical. Everything is AI violation. Discuss assignments with classmates without showing code? AI violation, despite his collaboration policy stating otherwise. Wanted to discuss a paper his slides are based off? AI violation. Reading library documentation online? AI violation (Like how am I suppose to know what the function is doing otherwise).

Posted change in assignment on Piazza without announcing/pinning (bad communication). Monotonous tone when lecturing. Office hours at late night discouraging student to attend. Never listen to what his students suggest and assume that he's right all the time.
The worst professor at UCSD. His lectures are so boring and his voice is so monotonous. He reads off of slides and his exams are very tough. Avoid him at all costs!

Flipped classroom style where you would watch a pre-recorded lecture online, take a Quiz on said lecture with unlimited attempts, and watch the professor do live coding examples during class. Midterm and Final were fair and taken in the Triton Testing Center, some of the MCQs were tricky. Enjoyed talking with the professor during his office hours.
Do NOT take his class. Final is unreasonably hard, Final average is 68% with no curve. Go take math 102 or 170a and math 100 before you take his class. Otherwise it is math heavy.

Every time I went to lecture I felt like ending it all. This guy also refused to round my 89.85% to an A- despite the other CSE11 professor doing so. If you end up taking him, drop out and just take the class next term with Cao.
A quarter of the class failed so beware

Alright I don't like all this Ben Ochao slander. He is lowkey great, attendance ain't mandatory, and the class is very learn at your own pace. He posts the lectures early through the prelectures, and if you actually confused, just go ask for help. There is a prelecture quiz, and they ez and low risk.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: bad communications.
Do not take his class if you are not a self-learner. All he does is assign you pre-lecture videos and REPEAT what he said in the pre-lecture.
One of the worst professors at UCSD.

OK so I'm taking CSE12 right now, and CSE11 was so much better. Very well-structured, PAs ACTUALLY reflected what I learned in class, and professor knew all the material to a T. He taught in a very precise way. Going from that to CSE12 now, PAs are structured horribly and I spend hours figuring out how to start. Don't take this prof for granted.

The class has weekly homework and quizzes before each lecture but the first. Start early, they're hard but allow infinite tries.

The class was difficult, but it was curved generously. I gained a tremendous amount of programming skill and theoretical understanding. I recommend watching the lectures from home at 2X speed since he goes quite slowly.

After finishing the class, I'm bumping up my rating for Professor Ochoa from 1 to 3. Assignments and midterms were tough, but he is extremely generous with extra credit and curving. I also learned a ton from this class. The only thing keeping my rating down is impoliteness online. Great guy in person though.

The class was challenging, with tough programming assignments and difficult exams. The professor gave a generous curve (40%to77%)and extra credit opportunities. I didn't like his lecture style, so I had to self-teach a lot. He's great if you want to learn but tough if you want an easy grade. I didn't enjoy the class, but I definitely learned a lot.

Avoid this professor if you value your sanity. The programming assignments are insanely difficult and can easily eat up 20+ hours. The midterm was a nightmare, and the final wasn't much better. This class is way too hard to be an intro class. If you want to torture yourself and have no time for other classes, go ahead and take him.

Horrid lectures, ridiculous amount of work for PAs and lectures.
Exams were extremely tough, and the first midterm was so poor a 60 was increased to a 90.
DO NOT TAKE PROF. OCHOA for such a class as it builds core concepts for UD CS courses.
If you have no other choice, keep in mind the grading scheme allows for many increases and EC opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Don't take this class with Ochoa, even if it hurts your schedule. The exams are way too long for the time given and feel intentionally designed to trip you up. While I do feel like I have a decent understanding of the language now, my grades do not reflect that. The later assignments take ages too, which is hurting my grades in other classes.

This class is atrocious. Ochoa doesn't know how to structure a course for the appropriate skill level (this is intro to Java??) Homework started out easy and then progressively got more difficult-I spent 20+ hours on PA7. Looked at other professors' PA7 and they were dumb easy. Midterm was WAY too hard given the time constraint. Avoid at all costs.

Ochoa is a very good and respected person, you can tell from his personality. He's just a terrible lecturer. His lecture style is so incredibly mind numbing I just taught myself everything through youtube. PA's are incredibly time consuming, but not bad if you start early and they are very representative of the material.

Fair grading policy. Assignments are not hard if you start ahead of time. Prof Ochoa provides many opportunites to gain back lost points and there are always many TAs that can help outside of lecture. Midterm has quite difficult but there was a generous slant.

his tests and homework are catastrophic... worst course I've ever taken. the homework seems to be easy at first, and then becomes tougher and horribly longer. It took way more time than it should, if you ever wanna get a great score in this course or it is for your major, never ever consider taking class of this prof.

The lectures are bit boring (a lot of material is repeated and a lot of math/proof details), but besides fine. Homeworks are big and a bit scary, but with enough time (~5h a week) they are very doable.
No recordings, so if absent, we had to read the textbook and understand it on our own. Never saw him being impolite (in person or online) to anyone

Worst class of my life! I'm not new to coding with Java so I expected this class to be relatively fine. Unfortunately, I was wrong. Midterm was very, VERY difficult considering how little time we had to complete it. I sobbed for 2 hours after. Pretty sure no one finished and everyone did badly. I regret not dropping this when I had the chance.

I think he's really tried to improve his class, especially from reading previous reviews. The 2 biggest complaints I have right now are his exams and his impoliteness online. I won't go into the latter, but I've been coding on my own time this quarter and still felt like there was not nearly enough time to finish his exam. I think that says a lot.
Unreasonably hard midterm, he try to put contents that need a solid 3 hours to  complete into a 80 minutes midterm. No one in the lab finish it. Do not take him unless you are tired of a good GPA.
Terribly hard tests without sufficient instructions. Homework load takes up time equal to 2-3 regular classes. Take him if you want a C or below.
Please take his class if you are tired of boring school life.

1. Lectures require a lot of self reading.
2. Unnecessary strict. Deliberately stopped recording of classes to force students into coming.
3. Doesn't have strong grip on ML stuff, but conversely the classical CV is strong.
4. Grading is strict and plain wrong. TAs and prof. never admitted their mistakes.
5. 10 out of 100 didn't receive grade.
Agree with the other 1.0 evaluations. Avoid him if you want to have fun learning and get a good grade. Especially avoid interacting with him.

horrible class- professor doesn't take his job seriously, reads off slides, just because he has a job as a senior director full time elsewhere. unreasonable grading, it's not a computer vision class, its more of a comp graphics class. if you are international he will be the worst challenge of career (as compared to BITS pilani)
Simply reading slides during lectures and reusing old homeworks; very difficult final being unrelated to slides and lectures. Avoid him anyway!
Terrible professor. 252 is poorly organized. Practice questions for final exam is a joke. The worst and most hubris lecturer I came across at SD. Avoid.

Attendance is mandatory but doesn't actually explain things apart from what is on the slides, takes random and massive points off on homeworks for the smallest details like line length and , instructions are not very clear, test averages are horrible because the questions are on random things.
Removes points for no reason with no explanation. Mandatory attendance with no actual content covered.

Truly terrible professor. Lectures are difficult to follow, and no podcast. The slides are available, but they're confusing. The PAs were created by the TAs, and he barely knows them. The PAs are so bad, that so many people show up to office hours you'll have to fight to talk to the TAs. Additionally, he's condescending. Avoid him.

The PA's were impossible to do even at the very start even with the help of the TA. In fact, a lot of experienced programmers had no idea how to do some parts of the code. He doesn't care about whether or not students succeed. To me it seems like he lacks passion for this job and he is often rude to his students. Man got anger issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The quizzes in his class are short so every question weights a lot. Be prepared for a lot of learning on your own and to attend OH to get help with the PAs. He gave "secret" information about the final to the ~10 people who went to lecture in week 10 and cut off his mic for the podcast. I don't think this is professional but oh well!

Lectures mandatory but if you communicate he was good about letting me make up participation points. Creates code in class so you can follow along and see how everything is implemented. New structure of CSE 8B seems to be a lot better than previously.

Professors that relies far too much upon powerpoint presentations over programming examples and juts into concepts not covered until CSE 12.  Expected an introductory class to figure out BFS, DFS, and Binary Search algorithms before learning about basic data structures.  Awful professor, but more suited to upper-division classes

Very rude to students in the Piazza and when reached out to via email. For example, I sent him an email 15 minutes before a due date with photo proof of my finished project and my tech issue, and he was extremely dismissive and condescending, and didn't allow any leniency. His class had an abnormally high fail rate, which can't be a coincidence.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
PAs are useless and have no correlation between the files.

Quiz questions are unfair and cover small details in Java that is unnecessary for actual programming.

There is a reason why students who take him have low average GPAs. I refuse to believe everyone who takes him is dumber than the other students who take CS with other professors.
His lectures are very boring. Out of a class of 200, only 10 people attend. Please avoid taking his class.
Avoid him if you can. For real. He is terrible.
Prof. Ochoa is definitely an excellent professor if you take his course seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor cuts his microphone on purpose during class so only the people who are physically there get "secret" info on what is going to be on the final exam. He tells the those physically present to not tell any of the other students what he says during that time. This kind of behavior is so pathetic, unnecessary, and demotivating to otherstudents.

DO NOT TAKE OCHOA IF YOU CAN HELP IT. His lectures are filled with so much information you can't keep up, and he assumes you know Java even though it's an introductory course. The PAs are horrifying and the weekly quizzes are impossible to do well on. The final is in-person and one paper... be prepared.

This professor does have the competency for 8B, but truly doesn't have the ability to teach, listen to feedback, and grow. His lectures are him reading off his powerpoint (brimmed with text) of examples "he" created, but actually they are word for word identical to that of the class textbook, a textbook he tells his students that they dont need.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he doesn't really teach he just reads off the slides. He doesn't even write code during class, so if you're transitioning from 8A you'll have no idea how to approach problems differently compared to python. exams are very hard and they're usually about trivial things he says in class. he seems like a nice person but he's just not a good teacher.

He mostly reads off slides for lecture. The only feedback for programming assignments is from an autograder, but he hides testcases until grades come out, so it's hard to know what you're struggling with before the damage is already done. Exams are concept heavy, and are weighted heavily with no curve. He's nice though, if that counts for anything!

The coding portion of his exam is simply too small. Most of them are computer theory questions, which are basically carried through very quickly. I understand that as a college student, self-learning is a very important part. But as a basic programming course, what makes me speechless is that I can work out the homework well but not EXAMS.
Lectures barely help, PA's are doable if you go to tutoring, tests are horrible.

He's a good person, but generally not a good professor. Too harsh on exams (too much memorization to handle). PAs just sucked most of your time and are not related to your exams. The final grade depends on a very few things. No extra credit or what so ever that could boost your grade.

Take CSE11 if necessary. Guys avoid him :(

He's very hard to follow during lecture, and hands out PA's that are much more difficult than the content provided during the lecture, expecting us to just know how to code.The worst part about this professor is the exams. Each question is weighed so heavily in the exam, if you don't essentially ace it, you're not getting a good grade.
PAs do not make sense, are extremely time consuming, and lecture is no help.

The assignments are very difficult and don't correlate to the class material whatsoever. The grading system for them is also a joke and so are the instructions for the assignments. You will find yourself sitting in Warren for 3 days straight just to finish one PA. The instructions of the PA feel like they were written in Greek and translated.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: He expected you to just know things and was so hard. He didnt care about his students at all and was very unreasonable with his assignments. I had to neglect all my other classes for this class and barely passed

I would not recommend Ben to anyone. He cant explain materials clearly. Homework takes a lot of time and has basically nothing to do with exams. Take this class under him only if you absolutely have to do so. If you just want to study cv, free courses on YT are way better. BTW he closed Piazza and canvas immediately after the finals.

Honestly don't get why he has so many negative reviews. He is a pretty decent professor who seems like an actually good person. Although his lectures are pretty tough to follow along with, even as someone who took the class with some prior coding experience. If you have some prior coding experience, take him. If not, take CSE8A first.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This Professor can make simple things become very complicated. He was not able to explain lecture material well. For example, when he talked about PCA. He gave the derivation (SVD) and the results first. Then he defined what the data matrix is?? No idea for his logic. Also, his slides and exam are very confusing and misleading.

You think Ben is a nice person in the first class. However, if you have anything makes him feel not right? He will use everything he can do kill you. Like sending you to Academic Integrity Office, where they said my teammate did not violate any rule. He keeps being harsh on my teammate and changed our final project language from python to C++......

Lecture slides are sourced from the internet. Doesn't go in depth on everything. Shows essential equations but does not tell how to use it or how one should use it. Lectures are basically a series of vague descriptions taken from the first few paragraphs of the textbook Basically you're self learning from Youtube. Do not recommend at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: He speeds through the lectures and fails to explain a majority of the equations he introduces.

Hes a great person, which is why it pains me to write this review. You can tell he really cares about his students, but his assignments are very unclear and the quizzes are just "run this code in your head". If you already know Java, hes a fun prof. But if you dont, the PAs and tests can be immensely confusing. Id avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Tough grader

reviews.comment: See the rate, you will have a sense.
Tough homework and awful instructing.
He isnt a good instructor, maybe knowledgeable but no much help for students. Gotta self study a lot. I dropped his course in the middle.

If you take his class, your time would mostly be spent on taking his blackboard notes. Those notes are all in textbooks. It's hard to understand why he doesn't just make latex on slides. Maybe those writing notes would occupy most of the class time for teaching meaningful content. It's very boring and wasting time.
Avoid this instructor's classes.

Most of your grade is the PA's. The concepts are taught in class, and you are expected to learn the API (OpenGL, etc.) on your own or with help from TA's. No final exam, but a final project that counts as a PA and is done in groups. Midterm was fair. Does not podcast, so make sure you go to class. PA's are HARD so start early. Felt like grad class.

Pretty easy A; 80% of the grade is based on programming assignments which are a lot of work but doable. Only downside is that Ochoa is an awful lecturer. His slides are just copied from the LearnOpenGL website and he makes a big deal out of being a republican/trump supporter. Weird guy, unprofessional lecturer, easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: He seems nice but he is too smart for anyone. It doesn't feel like he enjoys teaching but is sadistic with a heavy workloads. When he says "easy" he means for him and not for students. The workload is a little unfair in terms of scope compared to other professors and he is very stiff even though he tries to come off as nice and humorous.

Seems knowledgeable but really obnoxious in lecture. I seldom attended because hes unpleasant to listen to. PAs are not terribly difficult but extremely time consuming. The LearnOpenGL website will be far more useful than lecture. Expect to waste several hours waiting for a tutor to come manually inspect your PAs on turn-in days.

Cannot actually tell how good or bad he is in explaining concepts because this course focuses on memorizing concepts and I don't think lecture matters. The course is hard though, definitely more than two units. As for him, no offense but his tone is tedious and the tone itself may get you sleepy.

Hes great - it seems that other reviewers were biased, especially considering his good CAPE reviews. While class may be tough, he makes it clear that it will be math intensive, and as long as you go to lecture + start assignments early, you should be fine. He grades fair, and is understanding of students. He is also very witty + great to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: There are around 200 students enrolled but only 20 attend his lecture. Contents are really boring. He didnt make the slides himself and he doesnt explain anything. We are own given the final exam score and Piazza is made inactive immediately after the final is finished. DONT TAKE HIM!

Only teaching matrix in the class, but require students to learn OpenGL on their own. No review session or any review material before the only exam, the past midterm was released by a tutor. Very hard homework that requires unusual workload.
Don't have podcast. Hard PAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Love Dr. Ochoa. You can tell she's passionate about research and teaching, lectures are tolerable since she isn't monotone. TAs do all the grading so just hope your isn't nitpicky with the writing assignments but lowkey BILD4 isn't meant to be super difficult. Would take her again.

Really good professor, knows her stuff. Participation is required through Learning Catalytics, and she also sets up "learning pods" so you'll be in a group with others to work through worksheets. She allows you to bring a one-sided cheat sheet, which is AMAZING, and she also provides study guides. You definitely need to study for this class.
attendance mandatory is a shame but she's an alright professor. barely studied on exams and passed, if there is an option i see why not taking her class

prof ochoa was great! 3 exams before the final but you can make up points after, there were also other extra credit opportunities. i didn't have a strong bio background, but she explained things good during lecture. one thing i would say is that the textbook didnt really help with exams. attendance is also mandatory (some dropped).

Quite a bit of work for a 2-unit class. Some materials are a bit unclear on the requirements for assignments, but grading isn't harsh, so it doesn't matter too much. The professor is very nice and understanding. You work with whoever you sit next to on the first day for most of the class, and with the 3 other people at your table for the final.

Very kind professor. Gives opportunity to get 5% of extra credit on each midterm, and lowest midterm is dropped. Content isn't difficult if you've taken any bio class before that talks about the cell. You're randomly assigned to groups at the start and work with them in lectures and discussions across the quarter, but it's all smaller work.

TAKE HER! She has engaging lectures and her exams are actually reflective of what she teaches in said lectures. Recommended textbook reading but exams are entirely based off the lectures. Required attendance for lectures and discussions but if you go, they boost your grade tremendously. Lowest 2 scores for everything dropped!

she drops lowest of everything and offers lots of ec. shes very knowledgeable of the material and she is very kind. One thing I always hate is how she doesn't specify the FRQ points on the test, you kinda just have to write out everything u know and pray u hit all their grading standards. but overall very interesting class!

Overall an easy class. To be honest the worst part of the class is the lectures professor Ochoa is very caring and a great instructor but the lectures were a little bit of a drag in some part and felt filler. The class overall is very group based which is good and as long as you choose a good partner that will take on equal work load you'll do well

Genuinely the one of the best teachers at SD. Super nice, class is easy to understand and completely mangable. She gives cheat sheets for midterms and final exams. Exams are accurate to what we cover in class. Take her for any class you can.

Great professor and has an amazing instructional team. 3 exams but the lowest score gets dropped, plus they aren't too difficult. Lots of extra credit opportunities. The workload isn't heavy. 10/10 would recommend taking BILD 1 with Ochoa.

I ended with nearly a 100 in the class, and she offers extra credit. The course itself is fairly easy, so I can't complain much. I found her lectures a bit uninteresting, but the material was very manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: So much extra credit. She was very nice
good lecturer, incredibly easy coursework, participation was mandatory. drops lowest grades on lecture participation and pre labs. loved my ia

Lectures are great, she is funny and very nice. She covers a lot in every lecture and is great at answering questions. She always breaks the topics down easily. Clear on grading instructions. Discussions are mandatory, but they are actually helpful.

Amazing professor. So nice and helpful. She genuinely wants to help you succeed and is very approachable. She is passionate about her work and wanting to help others get into research or internships. All BILD4 is lots of busywork, but she is a great professor. I also had a really great IA which was helpful too.

Super nice professor, definitely go to all of the lectures they are the most helpful to your understanding. She drops a ton of your lowest grades at the end and the discussion and homework were really helpful. Discussion is super easy, she really tries to make sure that everyone understands the content and the way the class is designed is helpful.

Prof Ochoa really wants her students to do well, I got an A- in the class after getting high 60's and 70's on the midterms. Information is tuff if you aren't a stem major. You can tell she wants everyone to do well in her class

Class is fairly straightforward even if you're not paying attention in lecture as long as you have some knowledge of biology. Professor is condescending and largely unhelpful, but the course is so easy that it doesn't really matter. Lecture is mandatory and lots of tedious busy work.

Sweet professor, but her lab manuals and work on canvas are extremely disorganized. The writing assignments are incredibly tedious, and the lab practicals, pre-labs, quizzes, etc., seem to be a lot of work for a 2-unit class. If you want a kind and caring professor, this is your girl, but be mindful of the amount of disorganized work!
If you're willing to put in the effort, an A is very attainable. She drops the lowest exam and the two lowest homework assignments. Also gives extra credit on tests.
The queen of extra credit. She gives extra credits for each exam. She is nice and caring. I didn't feel overwhelmed as a student who is not good at science at all. Also getting A is pretty easy.

caring and great teacher. attendance is mandatory. grading on frq of exams is a little annoying but overall exams are fair. cheat sheet allowed for every exam. not that hard just make sure you try to actually learn the concepts, memorization is not enough.

V lecture heavy class, lots of content taught in just one lecture, and tested on a lot of details about it on exams. Grading structure is lenient tho with EC after every exam and dropped scores at the end of the course. I hadn't taken bio in a while so that's probably why the content seemed difficult but definitely took some studying. Good lecturer

Hey class eases you into bio (as it is a non bio major class) and provides lots of material for you to study with. There were three midterms with a mandatory finals (all allowing one page cheat sheets and the final allowing a two page cheat sheet). The professor gives many opportunities to improve your grade so if you have a bad grade it's on you.

Professor Ochoa is soo nice however not the best lecturer. She goes through lectures quickly so it's hard to keep up. She provides 5 pts extra credit after each exam and many other extra credit opportunities. Drops lowest exam score (excluding final) & allows cheat sheets. Study guides are very helpful! Definitely recommend taking her class.

Before this course I had only taken biology my freshman year of high school. Course material is not too difficult, and Dr. Ochoa really cares about our learning it. She assigns groups, but assignments are easy. Worst two grades in almost every category on the syllabus are dropped, along with your worst midterm. Show up, and it's an easy A!

Prof Ochoa is very knowledgeable, expressive, and teaches well, my fav prof! While it is a lot of information to learn in one class, she makes the class enjoyable and easy to digest. The grading policy is very lenient and she gives extra credit! Attendance for lectures and discussions is mandatory but only a small price to pay. The 8am was worth :)

The class is hard as it goes through a lot of topics that you have to learn in depth, it isn't easy at all and you genuinely have to learn it, BUT, she offers a lot of extra credit and the way her grading works is probably the best. I have gotten one B and Two C's in both of my exams and still have an A in the class. If good in Bio take the class!

ike the other comments your grade could be partially dependent on your pod which SHE picks. A lot of the lecture isn't on the exam and it's REALLY comprehensive. if you miss one SAQ question it brings it from an A to a B basically cuz they're worth a lot of points each. The homework doesn't even help on the exam.

Love Dr. Ochoa! I think she's a great lecturer and her class was easy to understand. If you took AP Bio, this class will probably be very easy. Attendance is mandatory for the lecture and discussion. She puts you into learning pods, which are basically groups you work with on questions during lecture, which is helpful if you get a good one.
class is mandatory but your able to skip a certain amount of lectures/discussions so its all good. Shes really nice and drops 1/3 midterm scores and allows a one sided cheat sheet.

Overall, she's an OK professor, but she does entirely way too much for just a bio ge class. Other BILD 1 professors are completely online, way easier, just do that. The group pods thing she had us do were just too much work and effort. The exam material is not related to lecture, it's better to just go to TA office hours since they are better.

i LOVE ochoa. her lectures are so clear and she makes SURE you understand everything. she has learning activities at the end of each lecture where you practice the material and its so helpful. her grading is really flexible and she drops a lot of scores. PLEASE take her.

I've taken this prof for Bild 4 my first year and didn't think she was that terrible. I decided to take her again for Bild 1 and it was the worst decision ever. 3 midterms & 1 is dropped. Extremely tough grader and we get only one sided cheat sheet. Her hw was not in the exams (waste of time). Learning pods were okay if you get a good group.

She is so sweet and really nice. She provides lots of opportunities to practice your understanding of the content in class. She does “learning pods” which are a group of people you work with for activities in class and discussion which was honestly really helpful. Her exams are very fair and she is always willing to help.

very nice prof and good if you're bad at bio like i am. lots of textbook reading and uses it for learning catalytic questions (attendance) and weekly hw. lowest exam dropped, 2 lowest hw dropped, 2 lowest attendances dropped. crib sheet for each exam and shes super sweet 10/10 recommend

I am a first year, I saw these reviews and thought "a good start" wrong... this class lowkey ate me. Personally science aint my strongest subject however the test were just WACK and they heavily impact your grade... you work in groups which is alright if you GET a good group... she doesn't grade anything besides the damn Midterms (theirs 3 of em)
Requires Pearson for in class clicker questions (needs purchase), but she also drops the lowest test grade

Professor Ochoa very kind, caring, she definitely has a very engaging teaching style which is awesome since biology is hard to understand, her TAs are all super helpful for discussions and she is the best that a biology teacher can get, 1 guided homework per week and optional textbook reading, her lecture slides are enough to do well on tests.

I loved her personality and teaching! I do just suck at science so I found the material really hard to digest, but I think she had a very engaging teaching style. Curve is nice. Homework was a pain sometimes but they helped. This class itself is a lot of material but i think i was fine cause i took ap bio.
Very engaging teaching style

Make sure to fall on the good side of your TA and Prof Ochoa. It is explicitly stated that you can miss two labs maximum as long as it is not the first week and you will only lose credit for lab attendance. Participation and everything else is not jeopardized. They still gave me zeros on other assignments out of spite.

Super nice professor. 
Lecture attendance was mandatory and was taken through Pearson. 
Discussion attendance was also mandatory. 
The homework wasn't bad because you get multiple attempts and would get an A as long as you tried. 
There is also cheatsheet during midterms and finals so you don't have to memorize a lot of contents.

She goes through a lot of material, FAST. Besides that the class was very chill. She outlines what you need to study on each exam very clearly, and there are a lot of extra credit opportunities. Attendance was mandatory.

Absolutely LOVE this professor! She gives out an INSANE amount of extra credit. There is busy work but she is so accessible and caring it's usually not a big deal. Clicker questions aren't too crazy and she has a wonderful teaching style. Also during labs, she always checks in with students which is so nice. Wish she taught upper divs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: best bio prof you could take i miss her everyday
Very easy class. Basically reads off lecture slides and there are many extra credit opportunities. Attendance taken through pearson.

Her lectures are content heavy. She reads off the slides 90% of the time. Gives extra credit so getting a B won't be too hard, an A you'll have to WORK for it. Cumulative final. Mandatory attendance and discussions. Does too much for a lower division class tbh

Lectures are required, and 3 midterms + a final is just kind of unnecessary, but there are SO MANY opportunities for extra credit in this class. You don't have to do super well on any of the tests to get an A, bc there are so many ways to get points. Dr. Ochoa's slides could be more organized, but she is friendly and wants her students to succeed.

If you understand biology already, this course is a breeze, but if you don't it will be a lot of work. There is a lot of information and so little time to process before the next exam rolls around. Exams do have self-made study guides that you can use on them, however, they are only so useful.

Attendance in assigned discussion and lectures is mandatory. Uses Pearson for clicker questions, reading, and homework. She's really nice and really teaches the material well. The grade is three midterms, a final (one midterm is dropped) along with homework and participation. She gives opportunities to make up 5 points missed on exams which helps.
Shes really sweeet overall but 3 midterms and 1 final is a little toooo much for an intro to biology and her tests are wayy to difficult to understand love her tho

Overall she's a great professor, and really strives for her students to learn, but her lectures have a lot of information, and sometimes just reads off slides. Her tests are meant to really make you think, which made me stress a lot. Opportunities for EC, and drops low grades (homework, tests, session activities), so if you put in work, you'll pass

Overall she's sweet and cares. Her lectures will fry your brain because she tries to cram in a bunch on information at once. She loves doing questions that will trick you on the exam to “make you REALLY think”. There's easier BILD 1 professor don't go through the hassle of her unless you have to.

Lectures are fast-paced, reading the chapters beforehand is really helpful. Focus on the lecture examples and study guide, and truly understand the concepts. The exams require application of the material-study! There are extra credit opportunities, review sessions, and resources. The professor is supportive and genuinely wants students to succeed.
Prof. Ortony is amazing and you can tell she cares about her students and is knowledgeable in her subject! Very nice and overall the class is not too difficult as long as you pay attention!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Was very disrespectful to students and I heard a horror story from someone who had her before.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Attendance is mandatory for her lectures

There are bi-weekly quizzes (online, lowest dropped), lab practicals, and writing projects. This class does require more work than some of the other lectures, and the people you sit with will determine your grade in the course. Final project is a group project as well!

Dr Ochoa is nice however her grading and workload is a little harder compared to other profs from what I've heard. the lab group you choose and TA will make or break your grade. This is a very easy class to get an A in, just a lot of work for only 2 credits. Final is a group project with a presentation which isn't too difficult.

Funny and jolly, lowkey one of the best professors at UCSD. Starts from the beginning and goes into detail on subjects, and discussions are suited for test prep. Just study and you'll be fine really. Lowest test is dropped, so you have chances to improve yourself.

She assigns homework that's due at the end of the week (questions usually have multiple parts) and participation during class is required. Reading the book before lectures is also really helpful and make sure that you get questions during discussions correct. She's generous and gives opportunities for extra credit!

There is a MASSIVE (but welcome) amount of extra credit. 5 points after 2 midterms, one midterm dropped, like 15-30 ish miscellaneous, etc. That plus decent to good lectures and lots of resources. Highly recommend Dr. Ochoa Mikrut, she's really nice and her class structure is good. You need to study and HW is a pain but otherwise she's really good.

Easy A! Grade based on hw, lecture attendance, discussion, 3 midterms (lowest one dropped), and final. Lectures are fast and go over A LOT of content, but study and review and you'll be fine. There are so many extra credit opportunities so its hard to fail. GO TO DISCUSSION! Great for review and TA's are super helpful.

Great class! Shout out to Rae, awesome IA, she was very reassuring when I made mistakes in lab. Dr. Ochoa is cool too. The class isn't hard; attend lectures for iClicker points, and put effort into assignments. Be mindful of your seating in lab, sitting far from the projector can make it hard to see while working with Excel.

She reads off the slides as you could easily do yourself however you have to be in class to receive credit. Her tests are VERY hard and the material is hard to understand as you basically have to teach yourself. This course did not prepare me to move onto BILD 2. The positives are: cheat sheet on exams, drops lowest score of 1 test & 2 assignments.

Great class for intro to biology. Learning objectives make it super easy to know what you should be understanding. Lowest exam dropped along with many other assignments. Technically don't have to go to discussion since there are asynch assignments but you can also just checkin and leave. TA's were amazing, just need to study.

This class is conceptually really easy just takes a lot of work and studying. Professor is really nice and easy to talk to. Exams require a lot of application not just memorizing which can be really difficult as you really need to know the ins and outs of all the topics.

The experience with labs depends on the TA and your lab group. I had an amazing TA but some of the other sections had less knowledgeable TA's. Ochoa sometimes came into the lab and walked around to talk with us or answer questions. She was very approachable. Lots of grades and occasionally busy work. Final is a group presentation.

Learning objectives are given during lectures to tell you exactly what you need to know for exams. There are also plenty of extra credit opportunities, and your lowest exam will be dropped. Lectures are podcasted, but attendance is a portion of your grade. Overall, great professor: she makes the content digestible and easily applicable.

Gives all the resources u rlly need to pass the class. Do the hw. Cheat sheets allowed. 1 page for exams and 2 full pages for the final. Just do the hw and attend discussions/lectures. Also, lowest exam is dropped. Super easy lowkey, and I only took high school bio. Just study and keep up with the work since it's college now and ur an adult.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Good professor that cares about her students, she literally gives a study guide before tests with all the info you need to pass. Discussions vary though depending on which TA you get, since some TAs aren't that helpful. But the professor herself is nice and gives lots of materials to study with, and very good pacing in my opinion. Overall, 9/10.

Honestly, she's an amazing professor and you should take this professor if possible. Do the assignments on Pearson and actually read, and you will pass. This is college now so you need to keep pace of your own work. I didn't take AP bio in high school and she taught really well, and I am feeling confident for BILD 2 now. Also lots of extra creds.

Amazing professor that gives plenty of homework that relates to the exams. Do the assignments and you'll pass. Lectures were recorded and easy to follow. Lowest test is dropped and cheat sheets are allowed, and also extra credit is offered after each test up to like 5 points. Do this take professor if you can as she's cheerful and helpful!

Great person and engaging professor, however lectures can be tough to follow. Tests are very difficult and framing of questions can be very confusing. As an "intro" bio class this was very challenging to someone who is taking this class for general education purposes.

She's really thoughtful and accountable. She has a lot of really great methods that help you learn in her class. She does practice questions during lectures with the class and explains why the correct answers are correct or why the wrong is wrong. Homework is the same way, really great way to practice the material. One pagers allowed for tests too.

Sometimes she doesn't even know what she is talking about. One time her TA's had to answer a student's question during lecture. However, she is an excellent person, its just her exams are very difficult in that she could teach you one thing and expect you to be able to connect it with 100 different concepts in a short amount of time.

shes a fine professor just a lot of work with pre-labs, lab notebooks, practicals, quizzes, writing assignments, and a final project. Her grading is a bit stricter than other professors and her lectures are mandatory even though you don't need to attend to do well, there are definitely easier professors for Bild 4. grade depends on lab group and TA

First quarter teaching here, but she is really amazing at teaching the material. Goes through slides quickly, but effectively. Lowest test dropped and tests mostly multiple choice with analytical questions at the end. HW is confusing and doesn't always align with taught material. Besides that though I love Stacy and would recommend her to everyone!
Heavy lectures, but clear and informational. Engages well in lecture so it's not too boring. HW is weird and doesn't. Lm
Dr. Ochoa made it very fun to be in the lab. I definitely recommend her for BILD 4, she makes lab so much more inviting.

As someone who did biology in high school and didn't get credit, I found the course easy. However, some questions are really TERIBBLY framed and annoying to answer. If I were supposed to learn the course from scratch it would be really fast-paced.
Very easy, fun way to get into Lab. A little lecture heavy b

I love Ochoa style of teaching instead of the typical "just listen to me talk for 2 hour" she makes her class very engaging sometimes she puts up medical cases and as we learn the new topics we discover the answer to the case. class is mandatory(participation q's). discussion aren't but you get full credit if u go, otherwise its graded for accuracy

I think she is a good professor. There is a lot of material and I do agree that sometimes it feels like you need to know previous material. Just be ready to study and dedicate a lot of time to her class. Drops 1 (lowest) midterm, 2 (lowest) homeworks, 2 clicker assignments. Think this class just requires a lot of discipline and time to dedicate to.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Okay prof. LEs and DIs are all attendance mandatory

She's a kind professor who cares about her students but is rather inaccessible out of class. She didn't really follow her syllabus and changed her policy on the length of the final twice. She's hard to hear, but this is more of a building fault. Pretty easy class though, just pay attention, if you have a music background you will do very well.

Attendance is 10% of your grade (5% lecture and 5% lab). Her lectures is just going over the online "textbook" which we all already have access to (you have to pay ~$50 for Artusi which is the textbook I'm referring to). If you already have prior experience in music theory or playing music in general, you'll find this class to be easy.

Great prof. Sometimes her notifications are a bit unclear so ask her if there's anything incomprehensible. The course content is easy but that's because I had played the piano for several years. The pace might be a little fast if u r a complete beginner in music. Exams are all held online. Attendance is mandatory for both lecture and discussion.

(MUS 2AK/2BK/2CK) how easy the class is depends on your piano skills but the prof is pretty nice so the grading isn't too hard. just make sure to start practicing the pieces early if you need to. she is a little clumsy at times and really hard to reach by email, but she is very nice and supportive/encouraging.

She was a very good teacher and caring and respectful to everyone. She makes sure to explain everything to every student and gives hand outs and assignments weekly. Grades are based off in class "performances" that are low pressure, and she grades off improvement rather than skill immediately as well as allows retakes for these performances.

She gives me permission to enroll the class but when I start enrolling she said I am not able to enroll anymore without a specific reason. I finally enrolled in the course by talking to her and the department chair. Also she is so not accessible outside of the class. She will not check her emails and not available in person too.
Took 130 twice, great professor.

Excellent teacher, and the 2K series is a wonderful class (all taught by her except for 2JK). You do have to put in the work though, practice is necessary. Tests are performed in front of the class but she's very encouraging and helpful! A very great environment to learn piano :)

Professor Takae is extremely caring and really strives to make sure you understand how to play piano properly. You get graded based on improvement rather than in comparison with your other classmates, which was a huge bonus for someone like me who has never touched a piano before. I highly recommend taking her if you wish to learn piano.

Had a lot of tests; we had 4 midterms and a final so beware that. However, homework was easy and she is very understanding and caring to her students! Class overall not bad, just make sure to study ahead of time for the midterm because theres trick questions. Lectures pretty interesting.

Def take her, the readings she assigned were one the night before a lecture but they aren't that time consuming but do contain info for what the lecture is. The midterms are straight forwards and everything in it is what is learned. The lectures were good but they are recorded thankfully. She does muddiest point videos for the week and answers q's.

this class was unnecessarily filled with work. From readings due before each class and homework due sat & sunday, this class had me working round the clock. for a subject that i had passion for, this class truly drained me out. mind you, all the work in the class was only 30% of your grade, the other 70% was the 4 midterms and cumulative finals.

Not too hard just sooooo much work. 4 HW assignments a week, mandatory lectures and discussion, 4 midterms. Definitely just a poorly thought out class. Theres kind of an underlying malice with her as well. She constantly asks for feedback and then emails you to say shes not implementing your feedback because she doesn't like it. Weird.

there's lot of assignments to do for this class which help to balance out your grade. this can be a confusing subject but owens teaches it well and obviously cares for her students and wants them to succeed. exams were fair and attendance is mandatory. discussions are mandatory and on zoom. she made stickers about class topics for everyone so sweet
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures are easy to follow and are very informative in clarifying topics needed for the exam. She is always willing to answer any questions that students have. The exams do require a lot of conceptual thinking and is based of the content taught in the homework and the lectures. The discussion section doesn't really teach much and is general.

4 midterms, one final, no crib sheets. if u pay attention in class, ull do good on exams. provides study notes + what is expected on the exams. every exam is cumulative. discussion kinda optional (alternate section assignment if u dont go but its super easy). 4 assignments per week. i found exams very doable + fair. 5 EC pts per exam
super easy to learn the content. pre-lecture readings to understand material and clicker questions for attendance for examples of the content. shes really nice and cares about her students.

The material was definitely difficult and time consuming to understand, but I kinda preferred the flipped classroom for practice problems. You have to focus on understanding her learning objectives and take advantage of office hours, the TAs and PLAs often explain the material in a more digestible way. Requires a LOT of outside hours though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I agree with the other comments here about her tests (unnecessarily hard, discussion problem sets/in lecture problem sets are helpful for the formatting of the exam, BUT are not super representative of the content). You 100% teach yourself. She also has EC, but it's random surveys that are worth 1-2 pts. Writing assignments (3) are graded SO HARSH.

3 midterms and a final (can drop one of the midterms), but midterms are very difficult as there are many questions and are worded in a confused way, they take points off for basically anything they wish and the rubric seems arbitrary. homework at least every week with writing assignments, flipped classroom setting so you teach yourself, good ec tho

So much work, I went through long-term depression to the point she pruned my synapses, and I was hopeless. I'm in need of a calcium potion to revive my long-term potentiation at this point. I'm so burnt out, it is concluded there is no light at the end of the transducin.

Her exams will have full free rsp questions worth 30 pts based on 1 minuscule topic she briefly went over in lecture once that wasn't even specified in the slides. She expects too much for the lack of teaching she does

if you have a job, commute, or any semblance of a life outside of school, do not take. flipped classroom has you basically teaching yourself for the majority of the time. class is basically just iclickers you can study on your own but at least she offers lots of extra credit. exams are also unnecessarily hard, all frq, with no crib sheet.

Dont take her, it was awful. Exams are way too hard for the material covered in class, expects us to do 100 assignments some of which are unfairly graded, and 3 midterms (+practice midterms) all of which are cumulative and hard. It's doing too much for a course and definitely tanked my GPA. I had to spend so much time studying just to get a B-

Evil. This class is pure evil. The exams are not indicative of your material knowledge. Most questions are lengthy and wordy, which can confuse you entirely. No curve. If you have difficulty in other classes, prepare yourself for this one, it tanked my GPA. Avoid her if you can, if you can't, GOODLUCK.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Owens is super nice. But ngl this class traumatized me. She makes the tests way harder than necessary and then requires you to know exactly what she's expecting in an answer even though the question didn't ask for it. There's like 900 assignments due every week which is unnecessary. genuinely pls save yourself (pls)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Way too much work required for this class. Flipped lecture automatically makes the workload 50% worse on top of homework, papers, and studying for the exams. Grading is horrendous and ridiculously strict. Lectures felt like a waste of time doing clicker questions instead of actually teaching. Midterms are 100% short answer and hyperspecific. Avoid!

I've learned the most in this class than any other at UCSD. I feel like this is a good elective for premeds (ie challenges you to apply concepts and think critically),, but the content is so DENSE. For our 3rd midterm half of the content was material from earlier weeks... u need to be locked in the entire quarter and do well on the final(worth 30%)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Flipped classroom is a horrible experience. The graders grade with their eyes closed, had to submit regrade requests for each midterm and got around 40 points back each time, which says a lot. Had to spend hours learning material by myself as the professor does not teach in lecture and will instead answer questions that are unrelated to material.

I'd actually rather cut grass with a spoon than listen to her again. Even her explanations on exams are wordy and hard to understand. There's a reason why it's called an explanation, STOP MAKING IT HARDER TO UNDERSTAND THAN THE QUESTION ITSELF!! I would actually hope to see her retire soon because she needs to pack it up asap.

I often found myself memorizing what I think will show up on an exam rather than understanding. Even if I do understand, the exam rubrics still cost me tremendous point deductions for not mentioning something very specific. It's also difficult to catch up sometimes due to the expectations. This bipn140 flipped class is very bad. Not worth the money
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Most assignments (HW/etc) are completion-based, exams make up the majority of your grade, and the grading criteria are really strict. Exams are heavily conceptual and practice guides are not helpful. I study most of the time for this class, even sacrificing another class to focus on this one, and I'm barely passing.
studied all the time for this class, but her exams were unreasonable and extremely difficult. on the verge of not passing this class so highly would not recommend

LOTS of work required for this class, as she has a flipped lecture style of teaching. This means she doesn't actually teach anything during class, and it is instead spent doing mandatory clicker questions. Grading criteria on tests and writing assignments are extremely strict and somewhat arbitrary. Honestly, take this class with someone else.

3 Midterms & 1 Final are all free-response. Grading is harsh and follows a strict rubric, which is very unfair and results in frequent regrades. Flipped-style classroom on Codon, you must learn/watch the material before mandatory lecture. Spent hours studying/going to OH's, and still struggled. Professor has unrealistic expectations and inflexible.

Not a great teacher. I find it difficult to excel on her exams. I spent the majority of my time this quarter studying for this class, yet I still struggle a bit. Her grading system is tremendously horrific. She is definitely qualified to teach this course, but she doesn't grade you by what you know, but rather if you mention buzz words in exam
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class had 4 Midterms and a cumulative final. Very fast paced. However she has study guides that tells you EXACTLY what will be on the test with a cheat sheet so just study whats on the study guide and you'll be fine. DO NOT waste your time studying whats not on the sheet, trust me. Tests are graded a little harshly but can depend on your TA.

Pacing too fast, grading too harsh, req to watch lectures in your own time (4 hrs/week), mandatory lec that is not a lec but rather polls on problems that did'nt help at all for midterms (cumulative), midterm grading criteria are too harsh + unreasonable & midterm Qs are asked in a confusing way. VERY NICE PROF but unrealistic expectations.

Unfortunately, this class is way too paced. She doesn't give us time to really study and catch up -- especially for exams. It's continuous assignments that are ongoing that overwhelm you. Her exams are also all written-answers logic applications, which makes it even more difficult. This class is not worth 4 units honestly. It's worth like 5-6 units

I took Professor Owens for BILD 1 and thought the experience was wonderful. So I thought that BIPN 140 would be the same way right? Wrong. Professor Owens puts all material online that you have to learn BEFORE mandatory lecture. On top of that, writing assignments are graded harshly and there's three midterms which make the class strenuous.

Flipped classroom setting. Provides LOTS of practice exams and questions, so one can be well prepared. All midterms are 100% FRQ, and final is 90% FRQ. When someone asks a question during lectures, she would often stumble over her explanation and make me confused. Certain grading criteria are very strange and unfair. Overall not recommended.

I loved taking the class. I was so scared for neurobio, but her class was amazing. It takes work and participation, but the Codon system she uses gives so much practice, and with the collaboration in class you learn so easily and it stays fresh so studying is so easy as long as u keep up (which she ensures bc everything is mandatory). Loved it sm.

Though this is only my first year at UCSD, Prof Owens is by far one of the best professors I have had because she truly cares about helping her students learn and is extremely patient when explaining concepts. She is also very accessible outside of class. I personally really liked the flipped style of the class and would definitely take her again!

Very nice and kind person,teaching style is a little off and difficult to learn from tho.Not straightforward and very confusing.Didn't understand till another class on topics and even did OH and studied hard. Lots of HW,but it's all completion credit-based.There are 3 midterms,and they were moderately hard. Videos b/f class and worksheet in class.

Her rubrics aren't clear. Class is unnecessarily heavy. She doesn't actually care about students. Her mental health breaks are performative. BILD 2 topics are easy, but she just made them difficult. Always choose the other option.

I loved her teaching style and slides were clear and easy to follow. 4 midterms which were lowk hard and the final was long but if you know how the information is applied and not just facts this class will be easy. If you make good crib sheets, you'll be okay

There are four midterms that are mainly all free response so make sure you understand concepts fully. She also use iclicker so attendance is sort of mandatory, but either ways attend lecture so she can explain you answers. One thing I disliked was journals she gives before lectures as they are time consuming.

She's very passionate about her work, and a good lecturer. The learning objectives will help you on the test. She makes lectures mandatory (with i clickers), has weekly journals, quizzes, mandatory discussions, and four midterms (multiple choice & written response), which is a lot of work. She does provide extra credit and research opportunities.

Overall, it's an easy class. I didn't know this, but you can reschedule tests if you have multiple on the same day—my biggest regret was not doing that. The content is fairly easy, so don't make the mistake of taking three tests in one day. Just ask to reschedule. Also, she helped me get into a research lab—don't hesitate to ask for help!

She is SO COMMUNICATIVE (responded 5 min after I emailed her). She is such a caring person and her lectures are great, but her class is PACKED w/ lots of HW/reflections (multiple tasks every day). She's hard if you're typically busy but everything is clear and fair. Personally, I don't prefer her style but she is still a great prof overall.

She makes a class with EASY topics difficult for no reason. She gives out work like its the only class students are taking. It feels like I'm being gentle parented every lecture. The only exams I got A's on, I studied the least for which shows how strange her exams are. There isn't even regrade requests. Take another prof. I beg you.

After submitting my report she threw my laptop and spit on it while laughing... this is not behavior that should be tolerated in learning spaces. She made me switch my major from Biology to Education Sciences because she made me realize we need teachers who actually view their students as people and not an income source. DON'T RECOMMEND!

Professor Owens is great, she keeps you engaged in lectures, answers everyone's questions thoroughly, explains the concepts clearly, and grading in this class was done so efficiently and quickly it makes me jealous for bio majors. Only thing is participation to section and lecture is mandatory, and the weekly quiz+2 journals every week was a lot

Professor is INTERESTED in the material and it makes ME INTERESTED. Doing the homework and quiz every week helped and even having mandatory lectures because it really did make this class easy, as I was consistently interacting with the knowledge. It even allowed me to make friends I had always seen in my other classes but never talked to.

Overall, she's really good as long as you like to participate with your class peers. She incorporates several clicker questions to keep you engaged with the material and its not just material vomit. She does skims through slides sometimes, so just be sure to look back after. If you REALLY hate talking to others, then this probs aint for you.

I loved her teaching style! She always presented detailed lecture slides that were easy to digest. I personally liked her muddiest points videos at the end of each week, going through topics we learned. You can tell that this professor has a passion for her job, and I highly recommend taking her class! Also, there is lots of extra credit :)

Don't take her if you don't like talking to other people in class. She will make you talk to the people sitting next to you and if she sees that you're silent, she will go up to you to interrogate you. Her TA's are the same way. Very strange and intimidating classroom setting all around. Unfair midterms and will take random points off your HW's.

I didn't really prefer her lecture style because most of it involved clicker questions and having to discuss the questions with a partner. Grading on testing is crazy, got the answer right but still marked off points- she's picky on how you word things. Good amount of EC and resources though, you'll need those.

She taught well and the content was straightforward, but her test grading was insane. She would nitpick on answers despite the fact you got them 100% correct. There was always something for her to mark you down on even if the rubric did not state you had to mention a point in the question. Not fair at all.

Best bio professor ever. Ppl complain about how difficult her tests are but honestly they aren't that bad if you just stick to learning objectives and do practice problems. There are tons of resources for exam prep. Tests were personally rlly interesting too. Her lectures are interactive & well structured. She really tries to help you understand.

Professor Owens is engaging and makes the concepts accessible. While there's a lot of assessments, unstuck AI made studying more efficient. The class has a manageable difficulty if you stay on top of the work.

She mainly has you watch lectures outside of class and then in class you ask questions and do review problems with clickers. Her questions are more about application of the topic rather than just memorizing which I find super helpful. The content is also really interesting! Office hours right before class and midterms during class time

Dr. Owens' flipped classroom setup feels strange, but it does give students a lot of flexibility. Tests are somewhat difficult & entirely short-answer, but HW & pre-reading are graded for completion. Online lectures are comprehensive, but sometimes dull. Lowest midterm dropped. Prof is very active on Piazza. Overall, very interesting class.

Her class is a lot of work with a flipped classroom setup, requiring you to watch lectures beforehand. It kind of defeats the purpose of paying for in-person teaching. The material is dense and time-consuming, and her long, wordy questions on exams were tough to follow. On the plus side, she's very approachable, kind, and there's extra credit.

Prof. Owens is truly invested in taking the time to teach her students and goes above and beyond to make sure they understand a concept. If you post a question, she will often respond in less than 10 minutes. The class is content heavy, but if you put in the effort, it'll be a very rewarding experience.

Professor Owens explains concepts really well, and is very approachable and caring. However, there's a huge amount of homework. I think it was something like 4 assignments per week (all due on different days, too) apart from weekly homework. To get an A in this class, I think one would have to spend a lot of if not all of their time on this class.

There were 4 midterms and the final. The midterms are easy if you study off the slides but beware of free-response questions. She offers guaranteed extra credit at the end of the exams. A cheat sheet is also given. She is very easy-going and can tell she cares about her students.

I was so so disappointed with how the exam questions were laid out. Not only was there 4 midterms throughout the course, but certain exam questions would be a mere 3 points while others costed 16+ points. Be prepared to be clocked by these exams. Such a nice professor, but such a tough grader, coming from someone who took AP Bio in high school.

Attendance is largely mandatory as you can miss some days. Very flexible professor, as you can attend either lecture time and other discussion sections. How to succeed is very clear and is not difficult to understand how things work and is asked of you. SUPER HELPFUL Office Hours. Largest con is the 4 midterms.

She is a really good lecturer in which really helped me in understanding the concepts for this class! She is accessible outside of class and is a very caring professor. Throughout the weeks there are a lot of little assignments and there were 4 midterms, however they were somewhat manageable.

She's an amazing lecturer with clear slides and very kind. She has A TON of busy work, but it's not that hard just annoying. Three attempts on weekly quizzes, you need an iClicker remote for lecture (which is recorded), and there's a midterm every two weeks (she drops ur lowest). There are opportunities for extra credit and discussion is mandatory.

Owens is super accessible and accommodating for any issues. There are lots of tests and assignments, but the four midterms helps students stay on top of their work so the final exam isn't as stressful. Lots of assignments are dropped as well. The class started off more difficult but got easier. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Owens is great! Owens explains things well and really cares about her students. The only thing is her class had a lot of busy work; it wasn't too bad but annoying. She has like 4 midterms plus final so your grade is very dependent on those test. They aren't too hard though; I studied a little and would get A's; helps if you took ap bio tho.

Avoid taking her classes, any other prof is better than this one.. Lectures are boring and all over the place. Extremely harsh grader on every nitpicky detail on assignments that worth A TON of grade. Steer clear of her courses if you want to keep your 4.0. Do not recommend..

I love Owens! 2 hw assignments a week (on completion) and a weekly quiz (with 3 attempts and 5 questions). The Opps say otherwise. There are 4 midterms (she drops the lowest one). Clearly outlines the stuff on the test in her slides. Do the PRACTICE sets,(similar to the tests).Very passionate and loves answering questions.

I LOVE OWENS!!! She is honestly super caring and is always open to explain concepts to students. Not to mention, her TAs are really knowledgeable and patient too. She has easy homework assignments that take me less than 20 mins to do. All of her lectures and reviews are recorded, and she provides study guides and practice probs. 10/10 professor!

Owens gives a lot of homework, 2 journals a week for the entire the quarter, weekly quizzes, and she has 4 cumulative midterms. But, she cares about each of her students and is always willing to answer questions, she also has some pretty good IA/TA's, and they are really good at explaining content in section. Section is mandatory!

Ended up failing this class from the absurd amount of homework given, and my depression was not helping. The tests were overcomplicated and had no correlation between them and the HW's given. This ended up making all the HW given pretty useless and a waste of my time, eventually I gave up and just simply failed the class and protected my peace.

Easy to the point that I was bored. Offers lots of extra credit, drops lowest scores for assignments and midterms, & gives super generous cheat sheets. Emphasizes in class discussion among peers way too much. Attend lecture and do work on time and you'll do great

Professor Owens is an amazing professor that deeply cares about her students. Lectures are interactive, fun, and interesting! Be ready to think critically, apply yourself, and you'll be just fine in this course!

Do not take this professor if you like clear cut teaching. Her teaching is all over the place and messy, her homework is there to prepare for the class before but i found myself trying to just fill a word count. overall some of the things she does is useless and not of any value in learning, there are 4 midterms with cheatsheets which are ok.

Professor Owens is extremelyyy kind, supportive and accessible inside& outside class. really cares about that students learn. don't skip lectures, independently think through the materials, actively participate and do the practice problems. all helps prepare for the tests. A bit hw& assignments-heavy, great exercises for overall learning though.

Owens is very nice who definitely cares about her students.. However, we need to watch lectures before coming to class and these are SO confusing - she is literally speaking gibberish and reading off the slides. Midterms are cumulative and she focuses on other content rather than current and insanely tough. I literally want to change my major now
5 exams and she overcomplicates all of them. All HW is totally irrelevant to the exams. Too many trick questions. And mostly free response where you always have to justify your answers
Professor Owens is literally the best professor I've had so far. She is really caring and has a lot of supplemental help. Take her! if she has open spots.

My friend and I concluded that our class was the "control group" with bad teaching compared against a well-taught course. Confusing. e.g. she would teach us something entirely new, ask what our guess would be and would ALWAYS surprise us with the opposite, so when studying, I couldn't remember if it was the trick explanation or the real one.

SHE KNOWS WHAT SHE'S TALKING ABOUT, so best believe you're learning from a knowledgeable neuroscience expert. Exams and finals are HARD but there're a lot of assignments to recover from slightly low exam scores. 3 midterms, 1 will be dropped. You can look at notes and use the Internet but you have to really know your materials to answer them.

I enjoyed how Owens taught this course. She had good exams that represented what we learned in class. We were able to use a double sided cheat sheet for the tests and THREE for the final. It forced me to study and actually understand the material so they weren't even that necessary. I don't like the mandatory lectures, but it made me learn more.

4 midterms + 1 final, lowest midterm dropped, and you get a cheat sheet. A lot of it is explain your answer. Easy A if you just listen during lecture. Lectures involve talking to the people around you, and she does i-clickers (graded on participation, not correctness). Lots of extra credit opportunities. Owens is really understanding. Great class!!

If you know you suck at test don't take her or you automatically fail. Studying hard every day won't save you. She gave a midterm every 2 weeks and study session by TAs. Exams 57% of grade. Not multiple choice, on exams you always have to justify your answers. She always tries tricking you into the wrong answer on exam

Good at teaching and caring.

Professor Owens is genuinely the most caring, kind, and understanding professor I have ever had. She offers so much extra credit, goes out of her way to help students understand difficult content (posting supplemental videos to help reinforce difficult ideas), and is more than generous with the grading. Class is test heavy.

Dr. Owens is such a sweet and caring professor. You can tell she wants her students to succeed. Lectures are interactive with clicker questions. A downside is that there are lots of homework and 4 midterms but if you put in the work, you will succeed!

Super caring, clearly wants students to succeed. Offers lots of extra credit, drops lowest scores for assignments and midterms, & offers a lot of opportunities for office hours and supplementary instruction. Breaks down the material super clearly and emphasizes in class discussion among peers. Attend lecture and do work on time and you'll do great

professor is caring and she does provide feedback, but I just found the lectures boring and they are mainly pure discussion with the person next to you about the iclicker questions. very homework heavy, but I guess its alright since its like free points, but way too many midterms like what... midterms are hard since you have to justify your answer
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Going to lectures is mandatory, but they're rlly fun and interactive. Discussion section is also mandatory, but there's alternatives that you can do online and asynchronously. Overall, tests were a big hard, but the teacher is pretty helpful.

Professor Owens' lectures are amazing and teaches us a lot with a lot of detail yet not convoluting at all ! She is also very compassionate, understanding, and wise! Would definitely recommend her classes !
Super amazing, compassionate, and wise ! Patiently answers questions that people have and I really love her lectures. I would definitely take her class again.
She is literally the best teacher I have ever had. Her class in engaging, educational, and so so so easy.

Midterms every two weeks, but Professor Owens has clicker questions in ever class that help increase your understanding and practice exams help! It is a bit too clicker question heavy, but it helps. Assignments seem kind of pointless, but sometimes they really help you gain an understanding of material before the lecture.

her entire class is clicker questions and she makes us discuss before ever telling us answers(very confusing). exams are extremely difficult and seems like she does this on purpose-almost tricking us into the wrong answer. will not give extra credit even if class is 1% away from threshold. no curves at all despite students working hard to do well.
