Great prof: sends out assignment deadline reminders, plenty of extra credit, interesting lectures, caring, very fair bi-weekly midterms with a cheat sheet you probably won't need. Discussion sections are mandatory and a waste of time but it highly depends on the TA. Hope to take her again!

Easily one of the kindest professors at UCSD. Keeps lectures interesting sends out reminders for homework and other assignments, and plenty of extra credit. Bi-weekly midterms but you're allowed a 1-page cheat sheet and honestly, you probably won't need it. Discussion sections are a waste of time and are mandatory. Highly recommended!
BEST PROFESSOR EVER! If you have the opportunity to take one of her classes! take it! BY FAR the best professor at ucsd! shes very kind and truly cares abt her students!!

Professor Owens was pretty good! I found some of the exams a little challenging since they were heavily based on applied knowledge and given a situation you have to figure out. Her lectures are iClicker but she drops 9 lectures so if you are sick or don't feel like going 9 will be dropped!

Professor, Wife, Mother, Icon, and Queen. Dr. Owens is genuinely one of the most intelligent and caring professors I have ever had. She always makes herself available to help students and is so kind. I actually love Dr. Owens so much and feel so lucky to have gotten her for BILD 1 and 2.

She was very nice and caring. Lecture + discussion participation graded. Extra credit for going to office hours once + 90% CAPES completion (our class was one person away from getting that). Exams were difficult and  based on application (ex: research papers). 3 midterms (one dropped) that took at least 6-7 hours + an even longer final (20+ pages)

Had her for BILD 1, but she makes the material really digestible and even provides videos covering topics more in depth if the class generally is having trouble with them. Drops the lowest midterm and has good section times that are flexible for many schedules. Provides good feedback when you make errors, answer keys for practice are very thorough

wait until spring and take professor owens! there are 3 midterms (1 is dropped) that you have 1-2 days to complete, and a final that we had around 4 days to take. attendance & section is mandatory, but we can have 6 absences for lecture and can complete alternate assignments for section if we miss. everything is manageable and pretty stress free!

one of the best professors I've learned from at UCSD. she has designed the course in such a way that there are many avenues for learning the material, and literally always addresses student questions well. clearly extremely knowledgeable, cares for student learning, and patient. 100/10 would recommend

Melinda is the moment. She is the definition of a girl boss and great professor. Her grading and midterms are fair and she genuinely cares about helping her students learn. Three words to describe her? Queen icon slay

Great teacher. She teaches clearly and gets the information to students. Class is test heavy, 4 midterms and 1 final (lowest midterm is dropped). Tests are worth a lot of points and make up a large portion of your grade but they are fair and reflect what you learn. Lots of extra credit opportunities if you do them. Overall, I'd def recommend!
Great

Three midterms and a final, so lots of exams. She's an okay lecturer so you have to get a good understanding of the concepts discussed to do well in her class. Overall, fun instructor but lots of work.
Decent but managable amount of homework for this class and biweekly midterms but they truly reflect learning and lectures are easy to follow along, amazing prof

Prof Owens is amazing in my opinion. Really good at explaining the material. This quarter was hybrid so 4 midterms and the final were online and open-note, open-internet. A LOT of busy work in the course, about 4 assignments per week, but she has drops, but gives A TON of extra credit. Her tests reflect her lecture content, so it isn't tough.

Lectures: I took her hybrid courses. To be honest, the online course is compact and quite easy to follow (also make connections) between materials. DI is mandatory (It is super helpful, IAs are great) you can go any of the sessions. Even though there are four total midterms throughout the quarter, but there are extra credit and drop policies.

Professor Owens is an extremely caring and thorough educator. She studies learning strategies and therefore she is constantly improving her teaching methods and constantly checking in with her students to see how they are doing. The homework consists of fun snippets of reading about the amazing scientific research done by modern biologists!

Dr. Owens is a very solid professor, especially for lower divs. The structure of the class allows for very effective learning and the quizzes/exams actually facilitate learning. I would definitely take Dr. Owens again!

Dr. Owens is one of the best professors I've had at UCSD. I've hard that she may not be that great professor for in person classes, but online, her lectures were so clear and easy to understand. It made understanding cell biology so easy. In addition, her grading scale is ridiculously easy.

I loved taking Prof. Owen's class. It was a little bit difficult in the middle of the course and I did poorly on 2 exams yet I was still able to get an A because she drops 1/4 exams! Every time you wouldn't do so good, she'll send you a message asking if everything is okay and if you need extra help, she'll make time for you. She is so caring!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Owens is a great teacher who really explains concepts well. Super glad I took her and highly advise others to take as well!

Really good professor, class had 5 exams and you could drop the lowest. The exams were tricky so make sure you really understand the learning objectives. Responded to emails quickly and had extra credit. Busy work but manageable
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, Bild 1 with Professor Owens' class was a very fun and interesting class in which I felt like I learned a lot.

Professor Owens is by far my favorite professor I've ever had. She shows a genuine passion for biology, really cares about the students' learning, and is very receptive to student feedback. There are a lot of exams throughout the quarter, but they are always representative of the lecture material and problem sets.

Prof. Owens genuinely cares for her students. Her lectures were sometimes long and confusing, especially if you've never taken an upper level bio or chem class. Tests are tough and time consuming, and there is what seems to be"busy" work. But regardless if you're struggling she is accessible and always willing to provide extra help for her students

I don't understand why Prof. Owens has such a low rating! If you are able to have her as a professor I HIGHLY recommend. She is super caring and genuinely wants her students to succeed & you are given sooo many opportunities to be successful in the class. Seriously the best professor I have had so far at UCSD!

Dr. Owens is awesome! Really loved the way she taught and explained things. There are biweekly exams, but they are exactly what you'd expect from the practice problems and lectures and have extra credit. Homework is super quick and easy. Going to take her again next quarter for BILD 2!

I seriously don't understand how she is rated 3.2. She is the best professor I have ever had. I went from biology being my least favorite subject to actually enjoying it. She tries really hard to make her students understand the material. Tons of resources: Piazza, study guides, study sessions, muddiest point lectures, extra credit, etc..

Professor Owens is a great teacher who wants her students to succeed. She offers some extra credit and makes sure to clear up any confusion through her lectures. She has quizzes during the prerecorded lectures which are helpful in making sure you understand the material. The exams are mostly FRQ but if u understand how to apply the material ur good
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lots of assignments, but genuinely helpful in making the material more understandable & serve as plenty of opportunities to boost your grade. Lots of clicker questions, but mimick exam questions with full explanations & fit in pretty well within the lecture. Prof seems to genuinely care about students and actual learning vs just memorizing.

I love Dr. Owens!! Her pre-recorded lectures were simple to follow and she even adds video quizzes that help with understanding material! Lots of busy work but it helped me study in the long run. Exams are open notes, internet, everything but don't let that stop you from keeping up with class. Easy A if you put in the effort:)) 10/10 recommend

Professor Owens was a great professor. She was very caring and just wanted to know what she could do if you were struggling. Offered extra credit and there were weekly assignments that did help with the material that was going to be learned in the future lectures.
Really good professor who cares about students. Took for Bild 1 and 2. An A is very achievable as long as you do the homework and learn the learning objectives

I think Professor Owens is a really kind professor who really cares about her students and actively tries to better her teaching methods to accommodate to more students. She gives a lot of homework but it is easily done in 20 minutes and the weekly quizzes are really easy. Her tests are straightforward with some tricky questions here and there.

Dr. Owens is a really caring professor. She cares a lot that her students learn, which is sadly a rare thing. There is a lot of work, but it is all meant to facilitate learning. Neuroscience can be a challenging topic but I am glad I got to get my start with her! Also getting an A is very very doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nice teacher, she's funny even though she's not trying to be.

Lectures are pretty much useless but they're mandatory. Uses almost all of the time in class talking about clicker questions instead of covering material. Class is 80 minutes twice a week but I think it could easily be condensed to 50 minutes. she is very nice and you can tell she cares

Wastes half of class time on clicker questions. Lecture feels more like a discussion. She doesn't explain the concepts very well when she does talk. Lecture and discussion attendance count for a grade. Easy to get an A though because many things go into the grade. Most of the midterm q's are written response so know the learning objectives
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Owens struggles teaching well to the students, and tries to make up for this by giving a lot of extra credit. This doesn't help student's understandings and her tests had a gajillion mistakes on them which made test taking more stressful than needed. Only got an A+ because BILD 1 was review cuz of IB bio.

Gives you every chance to be successful. She gives 3 midterms (don't let that scare you) she drops the lowest one so you have a better chance at getting a good grade. She gives A LOT of homework but it cushions your grade. Going to office hours is helpful and extra credit. All you need to do to Ace the tests is to understand the learning Objective.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Do not take this class lightly. It is deceptively simple at first, but the difficulty ramps up sharply. No one will hold your hand and remind you to continue practicing the fundamentals, but the material makes sense if you continue to practice the fundamentals. Success in this class depends on self-motivation and finding the right study group.

Prof. Owens is a caring, but terrible professor. Her class material is relatively straightforward, but her exams have very confusing wording with insanely large amts. of points for "simple" questions. Lots of iclicker q's in her class, and writing assignm. must be answered with exact phrasing that she wants it. All the hw helps boost grade luckily.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: You can't not put in work and expect a good grade. Yes it is LOTS OF HW BUT she makes sure you know good foundations of biology. She is super sweet and if you do the homework, pay attention and follow the OBJECTIVES WHEN STUDYING! you will be more than prepared these are basically the test. if you do what is asked you should be fine

So I didn't do well on midterm 1, I got a D, but she drops your worst midterm. This last midterm, I got a 96%. Honestly just study and you should be fine. Yes, this class does require some dedication, (bio journals are due every Mon. & Wed. before class), but it's graded based on completion. Oh and go to office hours, she gives 10pts. extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She does not grade fairly and she's stubborn. Her lectures are SO long and boring and she makes you discuss all the clicker questions which most people don't so it's a waste of time. Her lectures are mandatory but they don't help at all. DON'T TAKE HER CLASS. She's not a good teacher and doesn't seem to care about any of her students

Professor Owens has an interesting teaching style that can definitely seem boring to some people. I love biology so it's not a problem for me. She wants people to make connections in what they're learning and to promote participation, hence the many iClicker questions. Honestly, the homework isn't that bad. It prepares you for the next lecture.

A lot of work and nothing can be turned in late. Some assignments can be dropped, but still, it's way too much work for a lower division course. I can't stress the ridiculous amount of work you're given. Homework 's due every day before lecture and tests or writing assignments every other week. She's your professor if you want a hard-to-get C.
Lecture is long, boring, and useless. Too many iClicker questions. A caring perfessor though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is A LOT of work for a lower div. There are 15 journals, 3 midterms (all free response), & 1 final. Attendance is mandatory because she uses clickers for participation. There are 4 writing assignments, 2 peer reviews per writing assignment, & a revision per writing assignment. I took 3 other classes besides her & struggled to keep up.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Owens cares a lot about her students and their learning and is always trying to find the best ways to teach students. The ones that get good grades in her class should have a solid biology knowledge if they continue on in the field. That being said this class is not an easy A and you should be prepared to work for your grade.

If you actually care about your GPA please dont take her class. Her instructions are never clear and at the same time her grading is incredibly tough. You have to write exactly what she wants to hear or else shell deduct a tremendous amount of points even if the answer is correct.

Her exam structure is not consistent and there are so many midterms that it seems that that's all the course is based around despite the intentions being that the course will be more about the learning process not exactly focused solely on midterm and final exams.

She is such a passionate teacher. Her homework was just reading about scientists from underrepresented backgrounds and writing your response (I found all articles inspiring). I don't know why there are so many negative reviews because this was my favorite bio class I've taken. If you want take the time to engage in the class, you'd love this prof.

Shes an amazing professor & she puts in so much effort to get us to FULLY understand the subject. YES, you have to put in the work to get an A but its seriously so doable as long as u go through the slides & do her study guide learning objectives (all answered on slides) for the exams. Shes super approachable & friendly. take her class!

She really makes an effort to be inclusive and make the lecture different from your typical lectures. For all the people from my class complaining about her, they're most likely upperclassmen who waited way too long to take an INTRODUCTORY class. She makes the effort, and if you put it in, you'll get the A. Study, go to class, and stop whining.

She teaches well because she takes time to read (from homework and index cards) what students think so that she can debunk myths about bio concepts. Expect to type a lot of written assignments before class though, and clickers. Recommend 5 hours total each week for hmwk and studying. Terrifically easy class if you've taken high school biology.

80-90% of her lectures she asks you to discuss questions with the people sitting next to you. Its feels like elementary school and is so annoying. THERE ARE FOUR midterms, and to do well you NEED to memorize the slides. I got a 100% on the last midterm cuz i literally memorized everything. Final was so long and asked the smallest details. AVOID

Horrible professor. Stubborn and doesn't take her students' wants into consideration bc she thinks her way of teaching is supreme. Wastes 60% of class time for students to talk to each other about a topic she hasn't taught yet. Made the final 21 free response questions with multiple parts to them. Yes, 21 FRQ's. Avoid her like the plague.

Horrible. She spends 70% of the lecture having students share answers with partners or asking students to share there response to clicker questions. She spends the other 30% speeding through valuable material. Class consistent of 4 midterms and an extremely long final with 21 free response A-D questions worth 3 midterms. Do not take her.

Class is set up like a discussion session, meaning you spend more time talking to other people who also have no clue what's going on than you do actually learning. Gives 4 midterms, all of which are HARD because she only looks for specific phrases. Homework is assigned every other day and is rarely useful. I went to every class and still struggled

Its obvious that those previous two people are the same person. Yes, she gives extra credit but its worth almost nothing since the 4 midterms are out of 160. On her test, she looks for certain words, and if you explain but don't have the keywords you will get it wrong. She doesn't curve and if you want to get an A, you have to get an A on the FINAl
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Applies lectures and test to real world biology. She likes group work but it facilitates discussion and learning. There's no curve but she gives ec and the hw is easy and ends up on the test. Her discussion sheets are the test so master the problems on there and you're guaranteed an A. Really nice and caring, I'm definitely taking her for BILD 2
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Offers numerous opportunities to succeed: you get 10 pts of extra credit for going to office hours and 5 pts of ec on each test. The tests are really easy to study for, just study her learning objectives and make sure you know how and why something happens or doesn't happen. She wants you to know the material and makes it so it's easy to learn
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: You will regret taking her. She DOSENT curve and her 4 midterms are unclear. She is a tough grader and does not give enough time on exams. Exams are every other week and the anount of material you need to know is unrealistic. Attendence is mandatory and hw is given every other day, and the hw is useless. If you like to struggle, take her:)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HER!!!Lectures are underdeveloped, not enough time to prepare for exams, she gives 4 midterms. Even if you know the material, her free response midterms are going to be challenging because she looks for specific phrases. Each question is worth 10 points and its about 5 questions with parts A-D in ONLY 30 MIN(expects us to go in depth).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Okay, so she was nice and really smart, but the way the class was set up was very very strange. She made you have name tents, mostly group work and barely lectured. This is a content heavy course and if you are looking to just come to class take notes and take your exams and thats it, this is not the class for you. If you like group work take her.
I acknowledge the creativity and care invested in the course materials. Yet the grade distribution is remarkably harsh.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures focus primarily on very basic concepts, similar to a high school–level overview, which may be helpful for beginners. However, the exams are significantly more challenging and require a deeper level of problem-solving than what is emphasized in lectures or homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had 255A with Alon, he does his best to make you learn and cares about you learning, he is not the best lecturer but does his best. The homeworks are copied from the book so it is not too difficult to complete. Be ready for very difficult exams. The grading is fair I would say. Best point about the great Lord Alon is that he is a very nice person

I took his class three years ago, and I'm just beginning to heal from that experience. His lectures were hard to follow, and without podcasts to revisit, missing one point felt like missing everything. The stress brought me to depression and caused acne breakouts that left permanent scars on my face. It was a nightmare I'd rather forget...

The lecture slides are nigh incomprehensible. The only way to effectively review lectures is to rewatch the entire lecture, which isn't always an option. More importantly, the professor *failed half the class*. In a graduate class. A class that's required for many people, including myself. He made so many of our lives so much harder by doing that.
The communication and presentation of material is very bad. The slides doesn't make sense unless you pay attention word  by-word. Exams are very hard.
I do not even know how I passed this class. I got saves by the curve.

The professor simply read through the slides. Homeworks on EdX are like free credits,  but the final is not easy. However, I could understand that he take over the class in a hustle. So overall I would give him a 3/5.

Homework problems (40%) on edX were simple (but you had a limited number of tries to get each answer correct). The final exam was an overwhelming 50% of the grade. The prof was going too slow at the beginning, so he crammed a lot of content in Week 10. The remaining 10% was a fun project/essay that was pretty leniently graded. Good overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Most boring and useless class I have taken so far. The professor just read through slides. The final is unrelated to class material.
Overall a good professor. Would definitely take any class offered by him. I enjoyed the course overall.

Alon Orlitsky might be one of the worst instructors I've ever had. He talks very fast, very softly, and spends most of class combing over derivations rather than explaining concepts clearly. Tons of homework, impossible exams, and a project due days after the final. Dude seems to have no heart or perception that not everyone is as smart as him.

This is the worst class I have ever taken. The communication, teaching, and class organization are all extremely bad. The class is also not recorded, which means miss it due to COVID or anything else and you have to learn from his overly simplified slides. Exams are also super difficult with a final project to boot, with little to no guidelines too
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Orlitsky is very kind and genuinely wants students to learn, but he is a poor lecturer. He talks too fast, his slides are usually too cluttered, and he spends lots of time going over algebraic derivations. He is very dry and doesnt have any enthusiasm while speaking. Exams and homework are absurdly hard, and theres a final project.

Be aware of the difficulty of the class. He is the nicest and the most knowledgeable professor and the best professor I ever had but if I go back I won't take his class again due to the very heavy homework and hard exams. Be prepared to spend a lot of time if you take this class.

Detailed lectures, and his dry humor is what keeps me awake in the 8 a.m. class when I took it. Class picks up pace around week 4. Midterm was brutal with a ton of coding questions on paper. Programming assignments are tested with corner cases, so make sure you test them well before you submit. Learned a lot overall.

Class started easy (I had programming experience), midterm was okay average was about 60-64%. Class picks up after the midterm ie: harder/longer homework assignments. Make sure you dedicate enough time to debugging and matching the executable files they provide. Piazza, office hours/discussion were a big help. Exam material is based on HW/Lectures.

I've never taken other coding classes before so I think he is fine. His lecture is clear but we can't review using the slides only because his explanation is key to understanding. As for homework, his "test program"is kind of crazy sometimes. At first everything was easy but after mid it's suddenly really hard, not only the material but also hw.

This class was definitely tough. Many people already had programming experience (Not me). I just suggest that you really DO the homework (30% of grade) and go to office hours. The TA's are really helpful. He posts his lecture slides online. Class gets really hard after first midterm so watch out, I was doing well until then. High avg for final.

Fairly challenging class, gets exponentially difficult after week 5 so don't be fooled by the initial ease of the class. Class was graded on a non-traditionally set grading scale: top 20% were awarded As, next 20% Bs, etc. This curve rounded down the grades-- for example an 85% was actually a C+ for this particular quarter.

His class was tough at times and his later homeworks took lots of time, but if you understand the homework and spend an hour reviewing the lecture weekly. You will do well in the class because the midterm and final are based off of concepts from the homework. Although he isnt the clearest lecturer, the TAs are very helpful.

With little experience in a class req. no prior experience, this class should've gone well. Material starts out easy and very quickly gets ridiculously difficult. I'm not a computer science major, nor intend on becoming a programmer when I graduate. Focused too much on the details of this outdated language rather than concepts I might actually use.
Way too hard for an intro class. Only take if you have prior coding experience. Class goes to 0-100 way too quick. Avoid if possible.

ECE 15 is VERY hard if you do not have programming experience even though it assumes no prior experience. If you read my comments, DO NOT take it in your first quarter!!! I am a sophomore and have prior programming experience, STILL I need to spend Friday night and the whole Saturday to do HW. Midterm is relatively easy cuz I got 98.  Good luck!!!

His lectures may be confusing at times, but if you are able to struggle your way through the homework WITHOUT getting help from anyone, you will learn a LOT in the process and be able to pass his class. His TA's are incredibly helpful. He teaches a tough class if you don't code, but he teaches you skills. If you can do the homework, you pass.

The first class, you'll find him very humorous. When you actually start learning, however, you'll be blown out of your shoes, especially if you've had no previous programming experience. He goes through slides too fast and doesn't explain things clearly. He adds a lot of extra stuff you don't need to know in the slides which is confusing.
Prepare to spend around 10 to 15 hours outside of class doing hw problems if you have no programming experience. Very interesting, but a lot of work.

For someone without any prior programming knowledge, this class was practically impossible. Rest assured knowing that there is a good curve in the class, but know that you will be spending hours upon hours doing homework.

Brilliant professor. Extremely knowledgeable. His Homework programs were hard but in the end you do end up solving them and in the process, strengthening your concepts inevitably. Midterm was perfectly reasonable while the final was more on the tough side. Take this class if you really want to learn something.

I understand this class is difficult and quick, but I think it could have been much better with a professor that knew what he was doing. He took time to explain the easy material and blew over the impossibly  difficult material, assuming you caught anything though his accent. His slides became confusing when he littered them with jokes.  AVOID

8 homework assignments, one midterm, and the final obviously. The homework is tough and takes up a lot of time but it's manageable and the midterm was surprisingly fair. In fact so was the final. His lectures slides are very clear and you can learn the material from them entirely.

To the recent reviewers who are "shocked by low ratings" -- keep in mind that professors change their styles over time. Just because the class was reasonable when you took it doesn't mean that it always was. This quarter, Orlitsky's class was especially reasonable. The homework was tough but doable. Same with the midterm and final.

ECE 15 was a great class to help a no programming experience student like me get a grasp on the info, but this professor is pretty terrible. I found the TAs to be the best I've had in any course, so look to them to gain a better understanding. Midterm was not bad, expect to spend about 10+ hours on hw and to go to about 2/3 discussions/wk

Wonderful professor, awesome class, and great TA's! Recommend class heartily, and am absolutely shocked by low ratings. Yes, homework is hard, but far from impossible, and always related to the lecture. Midterm was reasonable. Orlitsky is by far the best teacher I've ever had. Despite no programming experience, he's made me a competent programer.
Hard.Super hard. Extremely hard !!!!!! Ready for lowing down GPA.
His class is not easy.  If u wanna learn something , u should take his class.
Hard Class. Lots of Homework problems that will take a lot of time. Midterm and Final are very difficult.

Like everyone has said, the class is REALLY difficult, even with programming experience. But Alon is a nice guy, and he hints to correct answers for homework in class. Class requires many hours of work!

First 2 weeks are moderately challenging for HW. Then HW reqs. sky-rockets afterwards! HW uses up a lot of time if you have NO programming EXP. (i.e. 8+ hrs). Lectures are uploaded and are simple to understand. Book isn't needed, but used for reference reasons. More of a logical thinking class. Challenging to balance workload for EE majors.

Alon is horrible. For an intro class, he manages to make every little concept as difficult and confusing as possible. Doesn't answer questions, doesn't help, makes stupid jokes, and is absurdly blind to the fact that nobody understands what he says. Homework is impossible, midterm and final was extremely difficult, averaging 50%. TA's are okay.

The course supposed to be an "intro" to C programming, with "no prior programming exp. WRONG. Here's reality: in class you receive "intro" instruction, but you have to do grad-lvl hw, midterm and final. there is little correlation, if not at all, between lectures and HWs. AVOID AT ALL COST!

Had him for ECE 15, lectures are easy to understand if you already have some programming experience. He works out a lot of examples with the class during lectures, which is really helpful. The homework starts off decently easy, but gets hard and time-consuming pretty fast. If you don't give it 100% effort in this class you'll get a bad grade =P

The professor is easy to understand. However, his lectures depart entirely from what he tests the class on. The homework takes an insane amount of time and the tests are brutal. You definitely need some programming experience in order to pass this intro class.

The teacher first appeared great, but as the course progressed, most of what he taught was entirely unnecessary, and the last two classes were the most important to actually complete the final. You have to go to TAs for help, but the head TA, Tasha, was not only rude, but never really helpful, fairly condescending. Avoid this class if possible.

Probably one of the worst teachers you could ever come across. I've taken years of C++ so I expected this intro class to be a breeze. I will warn you now, YOU WILL NOT BE GRADED ON YOUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE MATERIAL. They will actually switch the requirements for HW (30% of your grade) over 7 days after it was assigned! !!AVOID THIS TEACHER!!

This class may seem easy because it's an intro class, but it is ridiculously hard. It doesn't even matter how well you understand what each function does, putting it all together is the greatest challenge. The TAs write insanely hard homework that is not even remotely related to what you just learned in class. Final was impossible. People cried.

This class was ridiculously hard for an intro class.  I had previous programming experience from 2 other classes in community college and I STILL struggled with this class.  I cannot imagine taking this class without any programming experience.  The TA Tasha is very helpful if you email her, but in section she can be rude sometimes.

Incredibly difficult teacher. Homework's(always more than 3) take an enormous amount of time if you have never programmed before. I took MAE 9 and then ECE 15 and thought it would an easy A. If you can, take this when you aren't taking other time demanding classes.

Hardest C programming class you can possibly find.  The course description says "no prior programming skills required". NOT TRUE. If you don't know anything about programming, do not take this class. YOU WILL FAIL. weekly homeworks take up a lot of time. tests are hard.
Worst ever class I've taken. Do not trust practice exam and final.. It does not help anything...( if u r really smart, u will get an A...)
Worst ever class I've taken.

Teacherwise, the most unfriendly on campus. He'd pay attention to students who are confused and single them out and give a sermon until that student understands. Sometimes makes you look like an intellectual joke in front of the class. Midterm and final were extremely hard. He even gave extra hour to finish exam, and people still didn't finish.

Completely disorganized, lectures are completely useless, and exams/hw are 1000x harder than what he reviews in class. First day of lecture he said the grade distribution will be 20% As, 20% Bs, 30% Cs and 30% FAILS. Plus, doing well seems completely luck dependent. AVOID HIM!

Intro to C class. Homework gets stupidly hard. Final is hard. No textbook required, but highly recommend "A Book on C", since a resource is needed to rely on. Teacher likes class participation, but hawks down on those who are incorrect, or imprecise which means everyone. Soft-voiced. Makes simple concepts confusing. If you have book, then skip lect

Stop speaking for me you asshat. Have you ever heard of skipping questions? Besides, he awarded full points for the question that didn't have an answer. Not only that, but he also changed the grading scale to ignore the midterm if you did better on the final EVEN THOUGH HE FIXED HIS MISTAKE BY AWARDING FULL POINTS. It's not his fault you're lazy.

The guy bellow couldn't have finished, considering 1/5 ?s was actually unanswerable. The highest grade for the midterm was 86% (taking into account 20% of that was automatic). I thought this class was extremely difficult. We cover basics in class then our homework and tests are the hardest problems possible. If you can don't take this prof.

I just wanted to note that what the guy below me said isn't true. While the midterm was difficult I can say that I, for one, finished on time. In any case,  I think this professor is under the impression that everyone knows the material as well as he does. His lectures consist of obvious things while he neglects to address the more important subjec

Professor is a total hardass. Nobody out of a class of 100+ finished the midterm on time. Homework and exams are fatally more difficult than what is covered in the textbook or in class. However, I didn't attend section or talk to him in office hours, so maybe that would make the class easier. Overall needlessly diffiicult for the material.
sux!! the midterm average is 30/100, the lecture is easy, but the homework and midterm are extremely hard. overall !! sux!
The tests are very difficult and unrelated to the course content taught in lectures. Lectures are also very confusing.

tough grading scale, you're only graded on a couple things with hard rubrics. Her TA's are harsh and will fail you for no reason. the lectures have nothing to do with exams and you're better off taking over the summer or with a different prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: boring; so boring. There was absolutely no need to attend lecture, we were never tested on lecture content. Your research paper could have nothing to do with it. I regret attending any of her lectures; I did not learn anything I already learned in fifth grade. I love history and this class hurt me.

She was a nice professor but boring, would just lecture and read off of slides. The class is based on a research paper that you write from week 1 due on week 10 on a chosen topic. Lectures had nothing to do with anything expect for the midterm and final which was a prompt with a 500 word limit. Didn't read sources much, skipped class, and passed.
Boring but so easy. Skipped all lectures and ended with an A. Depends who your TA is tho mine was stingy w the grading...

MMW 13 is a rough class overall, but she made it more accessible. Class is not mandatory, her lecture styles are flowing throughout the quarter and interesting to see how they all came together at the end. There is a CA 1000 word for the midterm and final that were take-home and easy prompts. the grade is mostly from the TA.

The class grading is entirely based on the different steps of writing the research paper, the take home midterm, and the take home final. Zhiri is a good professor besides the fact that her lectures are quite boring. You can skip her lectures and just do the readings, but it might be better to skip the readings and just go to lecture.

Course load was actually not bad for an MMW class.  The main assignments are a midterm paper, a 1500-2000 word paper that you'll work on for the whole quarter, and a final paper.  Your grade definitely depends on your TA, but it's not too hard to do well.  Readings are provided on Canvas.  Overall not a bad class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is a good professor in that her class isn't mandatory and her lectures have no effect on the class itself. You can skip all her lectures and still get an A in the class without extra effort. Pretty much everything depends on your TA. Her lectures are boring and talks super slow. Also has an accent that makes listening hard.

Attendance in lecture is not required and the final was a take home essay. As far as MMW13 goes this is your best bet, she was easier than the other teachers. A lot of it is up to your TA, but she had less required stuff. MMW13 sucks no matter what though.

Very easy class - recommend this professor for the sole reason that she didn't care about attendance and we had 3 assignments that were graded by the TA's (also very easily). The professor herself was not a good lecturer and that's why no one went to class and it didn't matter at all. Take this class!!

I asked for help because I was dropped from her class on day 1 and she did not respond to my questions in the email and simply informed me that she can't help me. I asked her to refer me to someone who could and she didn't. She doesn't take the time of day to actually help students in bad situations and did not care that she was screwing me over.

Zhiri's lectures were pretty boring but they were asynchronous and honestly not necessary to watch. Your TA will make or break your grade. The CA prompts and final were so easy and the readings were not necessary. She has a heavy accent is difficult to understand and her recordings were always her reading notes. I recommend her for an easy A.

She has easy CA and final prompts. However, this also means that you probably won't get good enough feedback. You could still pass her class if you never attend any of her lectures. The project is graded seriously.

She was an amazing professor. I wish I could take her for every mmw series.  Easy CA's and final prompts relative to the other professors. her grading system is split well and lectures are concise and easy to follow. as tough as mmw is, she made it bearable. loved her and appreciated her alot
Had good notes, very thick accent, exams were very hard. Very nice person, very strict grading. Good for people that just want notes. Attending lecture did not help me personally.
Talks so fast, would go over lecture time often, went to every lecture and was very confused by her teaching, the tests scores were bad and there were no curves. big fail rate for my class

If you're going to make a choice about this professor she stopped teaching at SD and has come to Berkeley. Check out her Berkeley Rate my professor to see how she horrendously ruined kids math experience.

Homework and discussion is worth much less than other 20 series classes. Exams graded heavy as 70-80% of everything. Thick accent, pretty fast. Admittedly didn't attend lecture but only because of the above reasons. Averages on midterms were D and F on the final. No curve on exams or total grade. Disagree with anything less than 5 difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Heavy accent, move pretty fast with insufficient explanation on how to handling different type of problem for each concept. Admittedly, she covered all the required topic, but the exam is super hard. the 2 midterm is some how fair, but the final is extremely hard (tested focus unexpected). The homework is a great practice, but heavy calculation.

class is a bit too fast paced towards the end when you get to double integrals, and the final is noticably more difficult than the midterm exams. limit questions do not get graded easier even though they are harder to get correct. try and do all the problems from optional hw and discussion if you can.
She was great! She is very organized and the exams reflect the lectures, homeworks, and discussions. Homework is very tedious though
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her classes were lecture and test heavy. Maybe its the math department requesting so much homework but it's so draining. She enters class and goes straight to giving the lecture and is extremely fast in which many students don't even bother taking any notes. She is often confused with what she is teaching herself.

I technically did not take this professor since I was enrolled in a different math class, but I attended her lectures. So much better. She posts the lecture notes and slides afterwards, and it is much easier to understand. The format of her lectures is really good, but may seem fast. Recommend taking.
Great professor! Provided many helpful practice exams for the final and solid lecture notes. Gave lots of HW but was good practice!!

Lectures are very clear, and she goes over concepts and derivations. 83% of the final grade was tests, but the midterms and final were very fair, and everything was basically in the practice tests. Homework was online on Achieve, but there were unlimited attempts for full credit.

Have accent, which you need try to translate first then understand the material. Indeed she give fair amount of homework, but the exam is slightly harder than all the works. Her organization of lecture is unconventional, she often use examples to teach before introducing a concept(never know where she skipped), which might be misleading.

Lectures make the content really straightforward, keep up w/ the class + don't skip too much lectures (they are recorded)! Doing the textbook homework and study guides helped me alot for the tests. Tests are exactly like lecture content questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall great professor, but she can teach a little fast sometimes. The practice exams she provides and optional paper pen problems are really helpful for exam prep.
Heavy, heavy accent and frequently goes way over time during lectures, but she still does a pretty good job with examples and helping everyone understand the material.

Goes fast in lecture, so I often needed to review/podcast lectures on my own time. Exams were fair for the most part but could be tricky algebraically. Lecture notes were helpful to review, and grading structure was fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ohm is great. She has a very heavy accent that could be hard to understand, and annoyingly mumbles after every sentence, which could be irritating. Other than that, everything was great. Lecture notes were the best, 10/10. HW is online with unlimited attempts. Exams were fair. You need to study though, just do the practice problems.

Amazing professor, amazing notes that are clear and helpful for exams. Exams are fair for the material covered. Do practice exams that are provided and you will do fine. Take this class with this professor as she explains complicated topics clearly and cares about her students. Best math professor thus far.
Very good prof. She has an accent but is still understandable.
Sweet woman who obviously cares a lot about her subject and making sure people understand it. Her demeanor makes the subject feel less boring and heavy. Accent but you'll get used to it.
Too complicated lecture slides

Goes pretty fast in lecture but has very good notes that she posts and also records them. Doesn't curve tests but does curve at the end (curved our class by 5%+). Difficult tests but overall was a good prof. Our TAs in the discussion sections were awful though. If you took AP Calc AB to pass 20A, you'll cruise for the first 1/3 of the class.

Goes a bit quickly, but posts note templates, completed notes, and recordings of all lectures. Answers questions and will slow down if you speak up in class. Stay up to date with notes and homework. TA's are helpful during discussion (mandatory), no lecture attendance. Use the textbook and google for extra help, as her explanations can be confusing

goes a bit fast but provides completed notes on canvas. Homework feedback helps on Achieve. ChatGPT is the #1 tutor. If you didn't do well in Calc. 1, it will be a challenge. Never get behind always be up to date with notes. Has a small accent but it's fine. Explains notes very well. Ochem tutor is a must for ch. 10. Allows cheat sheets.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very organized and caring professor. She has a bit accent and occasionally goes fast in lectures but she records every lecture with amazing lecture notes (I love her lecture notes!!). Exams weights 83% which stresses me out at first but she gives helpful practice exams so the exams ended up pretty fair.

In lectures, she sometimes teaches like it's stuff we already know or should grasp quickly. You are required to go to 6/9 discussions to get the full discussion grade. Good teacher with a slightly different and fast lecturing style. Also, she gives incredibly helpful practice exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's a little fast in lectures, but you can get used to it. Lectures are recorded; make sure you go or watch them. Go to the discussion, too, and do the extra homework questions she gives because they are different from the achievement questions, and she tests on them. She's straightforward with her grading, so do as she tells.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is very straightforward and well-taught. Cheat sheet allowed but no calculator. Prof Ohm is very nice and her teaching style is easy to follow. There are no surprises on tests and Prof Ohm is very transparent about what is to be expected. (DO THE PRACTICE TESTS!)

Has a heavy accent but you get used to it quickly, and she explains things well in class. My problem was that I didn't keep up with lectures and ended up super behind, which was my downfall during the final which is worth a pretty big portion of your grade. (just don't be like me and keep up with lectures)

Ko Ohm was an amazing professor! Beware that you might have to write a lot of notes if you do not have an IPAD, but she posts all the notes online and podcasts lectures. I 100% recommend her. She is very sweet and kind.

Very caring and well suited to teach 20C. She has a heavy accent but you'll get used to it. I felt that HW was sometimes too tedious, and several problems were never discussed in lecture/discussion. You get a cheat sheet front & back for each exam. Discussions can be worth 2% of grade and if you don't go your final will be worth 2% more
Overall, an amazing professor! I really enjoyed her lectures and she explained everything very thoroughly while still making the class a fun experience!

Prof Ohm is very caring of her students and wants you to succeed. Double-sided cheat sheets, plenty of examples in lecture *not mandatory (she has nice handwriting too!), DI attendance not mandatory but gives you 2% grade credit. Review the lecture notes, do practice problems provided, go to office hours to clarify and you will succeed. Take her.

She's the best! Super sweet and chill. she goes FAST; make sure you can write fast or else you'll be behind. tests were fair, 20c can be hard but not the prof. fault. She was good at teaching you what you needed to know. No fluff. Lectures not mandatory but discussions were; there is an option to skip them all and just have 2% added to final.

She uses guided notes so if you don't have an iPad you're gonna have to write a lot, and fast. Very sweet person and funny. She has kind of a thick accent but you'll get used to it. Overall probably one of the best math profs at ucsd.

Her homework is all extra credit, and she curves the class at the end making it very easy to get a good grade. Her lectures are posted, clear syllabus, probably the easiest CHEM 6A prof. Her content slides are similar to Stallings and his wife but the midterms and grading criteria are different. I believe her class is probably the easier one though

She really cares about her students' learning and her lectures reflect that. There is a lot of extra credit (10% for completing all hw) + curve at the end + grade replacement plan; she really wants you to get a good grade. The exams require a substantial amount of conceptual knowledge for tricky MCQ, hw is not reflective of exam questions.

Amazing lecturer. Very accessible outside of class and helpful during office hours. Super outgoing. Exams are hard but there's a good curve at the end of the quarter. Do the homework, go to class, and review lecture questions and you'll be fine!

She was a really good professor and helpful in office hours. I would say some of her exam questions wouldn't reflect what was taught in class;however she had the replacement plan from the final and a major curve.

She's hella chill. Mainly graded on the 2 midterms and final, but you can replace midterm grades with how you did on that section of the final. No cheat cheat but she gives you all the equations and values and tables you'll need. Podcasted lectures.

Nicest prof ever. Two midterms and a final, all multiple choice, and she provides all the notes you'll need as a handout provided with the exam. Super easy course, and she curves. Very open to questions/connecting with students. Could not recommend her enough!!

HUGE test curve!!! Need to invest a good amount of time outside of lecture. Pretty fast paced but possible to catch up if you fall behind. Lectures are a little unclear but available during office hours and very welcoming. Kindhearted but a little hard to follow.

Very kind and wonderful lecturer. I went into 6a without taking AP chem and pretty much no chem experience. Her lectures are amazing and I find them to be more helpful than watching outside resources. She is also incredibly generous with the 10% extra credit and getting an A is pretty much handed to you. I wish she taught the entire chem 6 sequence

If you have no previous chemistry experience, DONT TAKE HER!!!!! She would say "you guys can figure this out/you should remember this from high school". I struggled on exams because they were mainly concept based, nothing like what she went over in class. Lectures were eh, she gets confused with the concepts and dont know what she's talking about.

This course was definitely a struggle for me. I went into CHEM 6A with no prior knowledge of general chemsitry unlike most students. In lectures, I felt that this class was definitely tailored for students with prior knowledge in chemistry since large concepts would get brushed over and the exams looked nothing like practice, with heavy concept Q's

She is an amazing professor who truly cares about her students. She always responds to emails quickly and is always available to help. Her lectures are very clear and easy to understand. However, her exams are very difficult and require strong understanding and practice but she is very good grader and curved all the class. overall she is great.

Professor Ortony had great lectures where she gives us time to work out problems in class. She also gave us practice exam questions. She stayed after class to answer questions and she had lots of office hours, with extra before exams. HW was 10% EC! Exams are more difficult than those of other professors but she curves at the end of the course.

Took 6A with Professor Ortony. She has a grade replacement policy where you can use the corresponding grade from your final to replace the midterm grade. Her lectures can sometimes be hard to follow, but she does emphasize what concepts/drops hints in class about the midterm questions. Guaranteed A if you put in the work. Offers extra credit (HW).

Make sure to attend lecture and if not watch all the lectures they are recorded posted on canvas. Overall was a difficult class but there was 10% extra credit homework and a very generous curve. Grade replacement plan can drastically improve your grade. A lot of the class is conceptual so make sure you really understand the material before exams.

I don't like chemistry at all but Ortony is a great professor. Teaches the subjects very well, cares a lot for her students and wants you to succeed. The exams are kinda brutal but she has Grade Replacement plan for the final. All homework is an additional 10% extra credit. This class isn't easy and I'm so glad to be done. Beautiful Curve at end
.

she is so sweet! the class for me was a bit difficult bc i procrastinated a lot but if u show up to class and do work you should be fine. she offers 10% extra credit, and discussions are mandatory. if u struggle with chemistry already this class may be difficult but there is a curve at the end.
Posted lectures are very good. Homework is all EC for 10% boost. Good test grade-replacement plan. The first part of the course is a review of high school chemistry. Very kind prof
Thought the order of content was a little weird, but overall good prof. Class is pretty test heavy but there's a good curve system, just make sure you do all the non-test work.

Amazing professor, lectures were clear but maybe moved a little fast at times. All homework is extra credit and boosts your grade 10% and the entire class is curved at the end. This class made me not hate chem even though its hard. I did rewatch lectures outside of class a bit to really get the concepts. Definitely choose this professor for 6A!

I dont like chem so I was dreading this class but Ortony made it a lot better. Shes super nice, remembers who you are, and has a lot of office hours in person to help people. No cheat sheet but its honestly better bc she only focused on fundamentals and understanding rather than memory. Tests are all mcqs which is scary but they were heavily curved

Sweet professor who wants her students to do well. All homework was extra credit and she curves a lot. Only downside was her way of teaching; I didn't learn much from her lectures because it was fast, and sometimes she would be confused with her own work. I didn't have any chem experience so this class was hard, but I studied hard and got a B

Great prof overall. Tests are all multiple choice and mostly conceptual, which many students did not like, but personally, I think they are easier and actually the best way to learn (and test) chemistry knowledge. Might be a harder class for some w/o strong background in chem beforehand, but she makes clear what will be on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very straightforward grading; exams are all multiple choice, extra credit homework, mandatory discussions but not lectures. Class relies more on learning from textbook outside of lecture and then reviewing it with the professor during lecture. My TA wasn't very helpful during discussion, but professor was fine, just not my personal taste tbh

Great prof overall. LEs are not mandatory but attending in person is better than watching the podcasts, while DIs are mandatory but rather not helpful. HW is 11% extra credit which is super nice. Curved the grade. Exams (2 midterms + 1 final) contain many conceptual questions, even though they're all multiple-choice.
Really enjoys subject, also has really good grading plan for students and all HW is extra credit and can boost your grade by a letter.

Really good prof, explains topics, lecture heavy (& posts videos), had office hours established (& bonus OH near exams), she will accommodate conflicting schedules. Very willing to help students.
Don't get discouraged if you fail the first midterm!! Trust in the grade replacement plan.
Read textbook and take notes, but focus on LE more for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Chemistry is a difficult topic but Ortony makes it possible to pass the class even if you struggle with material. She makes you cheat sheets for tests with equations and the periodic table that's pretty helpful. One con of the class is that you do have to buy a book to do homework.

Clearly loves chemistry and wants to instill that love in her students. Just doing the HW earns 10% extra credit. Grade replacement ensures that final grades reflect overall knowledge @ end of the course, regardless of hiccups. A bit of a disorganized lecturer. Throws accidental curveballs on exams. Took a lot of textbook reading to stay caught up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: As some have iterated before, tests are majority of grade, doesn't go too deep into the subject. However, she's passionate about what she's teaching and is willing to answer any questions asked to her. Lectures are podcasted, discussions are mandatory, textbooks aren't mandatory to read but do help, homework is extra credit. Finals are cumulative
10% extra credit from doing homework, discussion attendance required but not lectures, exams are very straightforward if you understand the material at all.

Homework is worth up to 10% extra credit, I finished with an 88.5 and got an A-. Test average is around 65 but she has a grade replacement plan if you do better on the final. She makes lots of typos but is therefore more understanding with students. Grade is discussion attendance, 2 midterms, and a final + extra credit homework.

If you're taking CHEM 6A, pick Prof. Ortony. She is very passionate in teaching chemistry and takes everyone in class to understand the material. If you've taken high school chemistry or AP Chemistry, you'll do great in her class. However, keep in mind that her midterms and final are based on conceptual knowledge, so actually read the textbook!

Overall, a really good professor who gives a lot of extra credit. ALL the hw is optional for extra credit. Wants you to succeed and really prepares you for the tests and exams. You just have to be willing to put in the effort because it's chemistry.

Kind professor who cares about students. Much of the exams (all MC) were conceptual, and had many multiple-answer questions, which made it more difficult. However, she is very open to feedback, and will adjust to fit class needs. Homework is 10% EC, and there is an overall curve. Taking any chemistry in high school helps!

Real nice, but the sheer amount of mistakes on the final was laughable. I'd never taken a chemistry class before her, but math-wise, lectures and TA review sessions helped. I struggled heavily with the conceptual problems, which is why my grade is so low(not very beginner-friendly/no partial credit on MC). Tests 90% of grade. Generous curve/ec tho!

Lectures were engaging with practice. Exams had easy plug and chug math questions and other difficult conceptual heavy ones. Discussion attendance is mandatory, but worksheets not the most helpful since it didn't resemble anything on the exam. Gives 10% extra credit if you do all the homework by the end of the quarter. Super understanding though!

It was lowkey my fault for choking on the exams and not really studying, but Ortony is the GOAT. HW is extra credit & combined with the curve allows for a very generous grade. Lectures go by fast, but she covers key concepts. Focus on learning the actual concepts, as the math is easier, and she tests more on conceptual knowledge than just the math.

HW is extra credit and not too much to do. She does go a bit fast in lectures, however the exams reflect what she teaches well imo and they are fair if you study well. The curve + ec are lifesavers and she truly does care about you doing well in the class. Discussions are mandatory though.
She makes the material easier to understand and cares for her students' success, but her exams are a heavy 90% of the grade, and her question formatting can be ridiculous at times.

Overall good professor, but mainly graded on tests. However, she does provide 10% extra from homework, which helps a lot + curves.  Make sure to read the textbook because she tests on a lot of conceptual topics. I didn't do so well on the 1st midterm and did well on the 2nd, and studied 2 days before the final, and still got a good grade
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Ortony created practice exam questions that resembled content on the actual final. Overall lectures were great too, highly recommend! All questions on final exam were conceptual. They were fair, no surprises.

Great class but honestly just make sure you focus on understanding concepts rather than memorizing; her tests are very concept heavy and very minimal on math. Midterms are a bit of a time crunch but you can make up for it on the final. Overall though you'll be aight.

never take this professor she structors the class in a way where the midterms don't even matter and basically making the final worth 90% of your grade. In class the lecture covers basic information and the exams are much harder than any of the practice material you go over. She's so lazy she only does multiple choice exams no partial credit.

Professor Ortony is a great person and passionate about chemistry. Lectures aren't mandatory and you can be watched later. Content is pretty dense and is does require studying as are most STEM classes. Lots of extra credit is offered in the class which is very helpful. Discussions mandatory.

Fierce and confident professor. Watch online lectures to study. Midterms are very conceptual. Finals are similar to: midterms & ex. questions in lectures. TA's are nice but not as helpful. Extra Credit + Huge Curve. No cheat sheet, but don't worry; not needed for tests. Learn a lot of concepts. Lots of thinking. You learn to love her as a professor

Professor Ortony was a great professor; she cares about the students' grades. Very flexible gives homework, but it's all extra credit, so I suggest you do it as it does help with the exams. 2 exams and one final with three sections, but if you do well on the cumulative final, each section can replace your grade on the midterms.

Professor clearly cares about her students and implements many methods to raise your grade (grade replacement plan, extra credit, etc.). However, homework and discussion sheets aren't representative of the exam questions and it can be tricky to study for the exams. Amazing professor, just difficult tests and hard concepts to understand.

She seems nice but she's not a good professor. I personally found it really hard to learn from her. During lectures she would just take answers from students shouting it out but never go into depth of where the answers came from and how to really solve questions. her discussion worksheets and practice finals from TAs didn't reflect the exams.

Great professor, lots of opportunities for grade recovery, and exams reflected course content well. The only level of difficulty came from full MCQ exams that did not have room for partial credit. If you have a good conceptual understanding, you will excel.

Ortony's lectures were solid. Her class is graded entirely on tests, with 10% extra credit for completing homework, which was nice. Her tests are almost entirely conceptually based, nothing like the problems we went over in class, which made exams pretty hard. Discussion was mandatory but generally not too helpful.
She is a very nice professor and you can tell she genuinely cares about the topic and her students learning the material. If you have to take 6A I would highly recommend taking her class.

I think her lectures are organised but her exams are very conceptual on a level she doesn't teach, to be able to ace those conceptual questions you would have to read the textbook which is very long, she is very nice but if you don't like choose all that apply questions don't take this class, also questions are a little but confusing on the exam

incredibly easy class. Ortony is the goat and records all lectures (which also aren't mandatory). discussions are mandatory but kind of useless. barely studied for the midterms and still got good grades. all HW is extra credit which is nice. Ortony really wants you to succeed.

Ortony was awesome this quarter. Some of her lectures were kinda all over the place, but she was very aware of that and adjusted the midterms and finals accordingly. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory, but discussion attendance is. Her grade adjustment plan is also a life saver. 100% would take her classes again.

Amazing professor and the lectures were very informative. Book is required, but I never opened it. Homework is 10% extra credit (must buy access). Discussions were practically useless for me (and mandatory). If you bomb one of the midterms, you have a chance to get a grade replacement on the final which is really nice. 10/10 professor.

professor ortony is so chill she is sometimes funny i like her a lot but holy moly i hate chemistry and i hate the class. i did SO bad on the midterms and i will NEVER take this class EVER again. I HATE CHEMISTRY. the final replaces the midterms but IM COOKED. PLEASE STUDY TRUST ME DO NOT PROCRASTINATE.

Flexible, passionate, listens to feedback, and cares about student success. Mandatory discussions. The quality of lectures varies, but she moves at a moderate pace. Exams are multiple-choice; questions include both elementary plug-and-chug equations and more involved conceptual problems. She curves the class at the end. Homework is extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a kind and sweet person in general but her teaching style is very superficial. She teaches the basics but tests heavily conceptually on lessons that were quickly skimmed over. Be prepared to do a lot of your own studying outside of class if you aren't naturally a quick learner like me.
She is a really nice and kinda cool. Really flexible, and homework was extra credit.

A great instructor, her lectures are engaging, organized, and effective (I never felt a need to open the textbook) She's happy to answer questions and review topics. Discussion attendance is mandatory but the TAs are chill, just worked on practice problems. Midterms are multiple choice and there are trick conceptual questions thrown in.

She provides several outlets in the case that you are behind in classes. You can tell that she is genuinely passionate about the material which makes her lectures very interesting and engaging. Toward the end of the quarter, she had to lecture very fast because we were behind and it was harder to understand the material.
She really wants you to learn! Clear grading, accessible outside of class, and has good feedback. Seriously no complaints with this prof. Just put in the work and enjoy learning.

She's really nice and tried to make sure we got good grades. The exams were pretty fair imo and she curves the whole class at the end of the class. Her lectures are fine and the content isn't that hard

Good at lecturing, but made the exams harder than expected. Very conceptual. Also, there were many mistakes made which was frustrating. In lecture, she would make many corrections, made a mistake on a version of the midterm which was announced 3/4 into test time, made the first midterm too long... Could've gotten a better grd w/ diff Chem6A prof

Ortony is a solid professor, and though I had to watch lectures twice to get the material because she does go a bit fast, I had a very good experience. If you do homework, study, and go to lecture, you will do great. Exams are somewhat hard, but she curves a lot. Very cool lady.

Super nice lady, but expects you to already have a strong background in chemistry. I went in with 0 experience and was practically eaten alive- the other profs are much easier when it comes to testing.

genuinely if you want to succeed in chemistry please please please take this professor omg. holy mother of pearl ortony will save you even if you are not confident in chem. SO MUCH extra credit and a fantastic lecturer. the only thing is her midterms were short so like one problem is worth a lot of points but there's also a HUMONGOUS curve :D

A little difficult to understand sometimes because how fast she goes but overall lectures covered everything on midterms and finals. Homework is extra credit and she also curves hard with her "grade replacement" opportunity where final grade can replace midterm grades.

I loved her as a person & prof, but chemistry on itself is confusing & I think on her part she could've done better to help students, for the entire quarter I had a failing grade and not until the final I got a 60% which got me a B-, including extra cred, she drops the midterm with final, attend office hours, & look at the midterms to prepare.

Caring professor, and she is very accommodating to her students and ensures fair assessment in the class. Her explanation of the concepts during lecture were confusing so it is important to consult the textbook (it helps!!). Extra credit, class curve, and grade replacement plan helped me (barely) pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I loved Prof Ortony. Her lectures were amazing and she's super nice. Homework is EC and tests are curved, which helped a lot. The tests were hard and not always reflective of practice problems, so study as much as possible. Her lectures are podcasted and she posts slides. She gives you an equation sheet but no notes on tests. I learned a lot!

Best chem professor I have ever had! So good she deserves my rating, when she first came to UCSD she had no reviews of any sort so I went in blind. But boy did I hit the jackpot with this professor. She is the best teacher ever and her homework is ec and her exams are very fair. So happy she is receiving the love she deserves.

Really good professor. Her lectures were easy to understand and she didn't go too fast. She records her lectures and posts them on canvas. Attendance is mandatory for discussion, but you can miss like 2 times. She had two midterms and the averages were like 70s, but she curves everyones grade. Homework also counts as EC

Prof. Ortony was an AMAZING chem professor, she is so passionate about what she teaches and has a very fair grading policy/curve. The workload was quite reasonable and she gives you plenty of material to feel prepared for the exams.

Having prior AP chem knowledge helps, but is not needed as long as you understand the material. Prof Ortony is super understanding and lectures are recorded and posted on canvas. Entire class is curved at the end so as long as you hit the average for the midterms and finals you should be fine. HW is extra credit, but is helpful and not super long.

Great just the midterms were nothing that we worked on before hand just some small prior to knowledge for final make sure you look at midterms also make sure you are able to grab a equation and play with it a little bit but if you tank the first midterm this class is going to be a struggle for you

Amazing professor. She gives us a lot of extra credit for just doing homework. Her lectures are always very clear and engaging. She is also very caring, standing by students' perspectives and explaining everything we are concerned about. She is the best professor, and I 100% recommend her!

Professor Ortony was my favorite professor for my first quarter here. I did not take AP Chemistry and wasn't the best at Honors Chemistry in high school, but her class was accessible and she was a great teacher. I disagree with the ratings saying the midterms were too hard. They were fair. I ended with over 100% in the class from extra credit.

over all she is clear when she speaks, you can ask questions and she will make sure you understand, she is also accessible outside of school, during office hours, emails, or just after class, she is so kind 
She also gives 10% extra credit at the end of the quarter for doing the homework and curves the midterms + a grade replacement plan.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ortony is a really caring, however when I looked at the other chemistry professor midterms compared with hers, the other professors were MUCH easier. This class was, personally, really difficult for me. It felt like her practice questions weren't like the exam questions which is why I struggled, IMO! I also had no prior AP Chemistry knowledge.

Although she is a nice person, I just don't think she is fit to be a professor for such a large class. She doesn't let you bring cheat sheets to midterms or finals, and although her tests are all multiple-choice, they are pretty difficult—especially with midterms!  A hit or miss I would say.

HW is optional but adds 10% to your overall grade if completed. Even with that, I ended with 90%. Exam averages were ~65% and mcq, so getting even a few wrong can destroy your grade. Good lectures and genuinely wants students to do good, but exams were WAY harder than lecture or book examples and not accurate representation of student's knowledge.

She cares for your success and is very accessible. My problem was that a costly textbook gatekeeps 10% extra credit(qtr45$/yr85$). I couldn't afford it, but her lectures cover everything, so I still got excellent test results. The final can replace bad midterms, but 90% grade is tests. She lowers grade boundaries, you can succeed w/o extra credit.

Dr. Ortony is the best professor I've had. She's not only very passionate about chemistry and PHENOMENAL at teaching, but she genuinely cares so much for her students. If you get to know her, she's the sweetest person ever. It's very clear that she gives her all towards the course, despite that she's primarily a researcher with her own lab. 10/10.

Good professor for Chem 6A. No attendance mandatory and all homework on Achieve was E.C. (but helps a ton). I took AP Chem so I found it to be an easy class, but you still need to study for the more conceptual content. And there's also a curve which is nice.

I was worried bc she did not have that many reviews but she was super caring and extended deadlines often. All homework was extra credit and the grade replacement system was really nice bc the final was pretty decent. I would recommend taking her for 6A

She is probably one of the best professors out there. Homework is not mandatory, but rather extra credit. Because of this, the only things that truly make up your grade are the midterms and the final. There is a grade-replacement policy, which is generous. She does curve the scores at the end, and mostly in your favor. Made the course fun overall

If you give this professor anything less than a 5… then you were probably the issue buddy. Definitely the best professor I've had at UCSD. Super engaging lectures and gives a ton of extra credit. Her TA's were very helpful and she really wants you to LEARN the content not memorize 11/10 would highly recommend.

Dr. Ortony is simply the best. Most genuine, knowledgeable, and friendly person ever. Very passionate about Chem and is extremely caring for her students. She wants YOU to succeed in and out of the classroom. Even though she has lots on her plate to juggle, students never take the back seat. It's been a true privilege to have her this quarter.

Ortony is such a good professor, all the hw is extra credit, & she makes her tests easy. Her office hours are so helpful and classroom-style. She's passionate about teaching chem and explains the topics really well. She curves the whole class at the end so you don't know your grade until after the final. Office hours & SI were so helpful.
