Very test heavy (like 90%), but she gives a generous curve and hw is extra credit. She is super accessible and wants the best for her students. Very good lectures and always corrects any mistakes she makes. Overall she is very passionate and caring towards her students and I would absolutely take her again. Amazing professor!!

Hw is 10% extra credit and she curves test scores which is awesome. She goes fast during lectures so its recommended to brush up on whatever that days lecture is on before coming to lecture. She responds fairly quick to emails and is open to reopening hw questions that you missed. Overall a chill prof but her teaching style isnt for me

Ortony will let you have extra time on homework if you need it. Lectures were pretty good, and the tests were fair. I loved how she was passionate about chemistry and really wanted us to love it too. My 84% ended up being a B+ because of the curve at the end of the class.

She was super accommodating to her students (making midterm 2 optional) and she held lots of office hours, where she responded pretty well to our questions. She was also a very sweet professor. One complaint is that her lectures were fairly disorganized but she held herself accountable for that.
Favorite professor, amazing lecturer, really wants her students to succeed and makes all the homework extra credit.
just an amazing professor, she cares so much for her students

While I found the class really difficult, Ortony was very motivating and kind. She is very clearly passionate about chem and wants to help in any way she can. While attendance is optional, I went to almost every lecture because she was great. Get ready to spend a lot of time studying though.

she was amazing and made chem interesting! her blazers were so cute and def would take again!! u can tell shes passionate ab chem and wanted us to do well. also homework was 10% extra credit so grades are looking up rn!!!! but hw/textbook was $45 so... (but u get 10% ec so it was worth it). also grade replacement plan for midterms to final was nice
The perfect professor

I took chem6B with this prof. last quarter and it was a great experience and def one of my favorite profs at UCSD. It was clear that prof. Ortony  cared about student as she was supper accommodating. Lectures can feel fast passed at times with some of her writing being hard to read but overall prof. Ortony is an amazing prof, highly recommend.

True to her motto of making chemistry fun and not grade focused,  HW was Extra Cred (total course score out of 110%). Allowed me to focus on learning instead of stressing about the difference between a 92 and a 93. Hope she keeps this! Please improve organization and proofread lectures to reduce mistakes while walking through problems in class.

Awesome professor in the sense that she is all about improvement and giving her students second chances to improve their grades as well as the understanding of the content. 2 midterms and 1 final (portions of final can help change poor scores of midterms entirely). Also homework is extra credit. Great professor overall and pretty good lecturer too

CHEM 6B is going to be tough... however, Dr. Ortony tries to make the material as understanding as possible. Midterms were semi-difficult, but she gave a formula sheet. No outside notes are allowed, including the final. Overall, she was great.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chem 6B is difficult material, this professor makes it very understandable! Your grade is 90% exams (2 midterms and a final) and 10% EXTRA CREDIT. Exams are all mcq, questions are EXACTLY like lecture/homework questions. She is so sweet and genuinely wants what's best for her students, highly recommend taking this professor if u want a good grade!

Super caring and understanding professor, highly recommend. There were a few mistakes in the class but they were quickly resolved and exams were very fair. Although cheat sheets are not allowed she provides a thorough equation sheet that gives you everything you need for the exam. She gives lots of extra credit too!

I highly recommend Professor Ortony for Chem 6B. Lectures are structured and taught well, I never felt like I was missing any concepts. In class problems are very important and are often very similar to test questions, so take good notes. You can tell Professor Ortony cares a lot about the success of her students.

Prof Ortony does care about students and office hours are helpful. The office hours are once a week so if the time doesn't work for you it sucks. Lectures feel scattered and fast-paced but don't cover material quickly. I didn't finish a single test in this class because they were so fast. The textbook saved me as I understood it more than lecture.

Professor Ortony is very caring and has a great personality. She welcomes all question. However sometimes there are confusions or mistakes during lectures. Test heavy and midterms are harder than homework&discussion worksheets. Lectures are a little confusing and rushed. Not very clear grading scale. But gives extra credit (homework) overall ok

Professor Ortony is a great professor who cares for her students. Believe organizational mistakes were only made because it was her first quarter teaching at UCSD. Exams are fair and familiar from the class coursework. You also get a 10% EXTRA CREDIT grade boost from weekly Macmillan HW. And you can replace both midterms with the final. I recommend

Ortony genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed! Goes through problems in lectures and explains things in detail w/ examples. Sometimes went fast, but lectures were recorded so it's easy to refer back. MCQ Exams w/ equations sheets. Offers 10% Extra credit. Always accessible & open to questions after lecture & in Office hours!

This class challenging as is, this professor makes it 5x harder. She rushes through slides and has really messy hand writing. The tests are all multiple choice which I thought wasn't too bad at first but then I took them. Felt like the class was more about memorizing facts like IMF's or molecular structures. Formula sheets provided are not helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ortony is an amazing and one of my favorite professors by far. She is understanding in many ways and focuses on making sure everyone understands the topic. Go to her OH, she's very helpful. She has 2 midterms, no cheat sheets but gives a lot of free points her if needed. Homework (10% EC) optional. She tries her best since she is new.

This was Professor Ortona's first time teaching solo and at UCSD. She made mistakes on lectures and exams that sometimes cost students worse scores on exams. She has messy handwriting and goes too fast during lecture, I always had to go back and watch the recording. She is nice and understanding though, and tried her best to make up for mistakes.

I mean his class was very straightforward and easy. I don't think anyone failed in the class and the test were really easy (in respect to other exams). However, you could tell that he did not want to be there teaching, while I get that you signed up to do research and not teaching, atleast do not let it be visible. It felt awkward sometimes.
hes the goat
Prof Bandaru is one of my favorite professors. His classes are so traditional (blackboard notes) and he explains topics well. Also highly accessible outside of class. Highly recommend.
Average GPA is 2.44, almost 50% of the solution of homework and sample of exam is wrong. Difficult homework, difficult exam (midterm and final).
He's so tuff
The class was well taught...there were a lot of quizzes and midterms and I felt like I was studying the entire quarter for this class just to get by. The class was curved heavily.

Pretty fun course with relevant course content! Examinations has contents from class notes, books and homework assignments which makes everything easy to follow along. There were group presentations as well which are peer-graded exposing you to various applications of Thermal Processes!

Hands down one of the best professors at MAE UCSD. His courses aren't the easiest, but he is an amazing teacher and you will learn so much. MAE 20 & 105 had 4-5 quizzes, 2 midterms, & final. He ensures everyone understands the material and tells us exactly what'll be on exams. Curves generously, very accessible & kind-hearted, go to office hours!!

Very good professor, very nice guy too. Answers very deep philosophical questions as well, and teaches with a lot of enthusiasm. I genuinely enjoyed attending his lectures and also genuinely found interest in materials science thanks to the way he taught.

Great, kind, and understanding professor. Tough class though, heavily reliant on Math 20D. Be sure to understand the conceptual aspects of the Heat/Wave Equation for quizzes and get very comfortable with integration. Open Book/Note tests, closed note quizzes. Fantastic TA who helps with homework. Very hard final, but was curved generously.

Bandaru was a great professor, he explains everything to its smallest detail and cares that everyone understands, he also gives our review sheets and tells us what to expect on exams, and it ends up being almost identical. Homework or a quiz every week, but they are reasonable. I learned a lot with him and enjoyed material science.
amazing teacher but teaches in math language so get fluent

The professor is good and teaches all the topics well though all the topics seem strangely disconnected from each other, I would say his course structure isn't easy to follow. Grading based on midterm, endterm and project, exams are pretty difficult as they require thorough understanding of the subject matter.

Lectures weren't mandatory but I'd heavily recommend them. He explains the material very clearly and concisely and is very open to any questions throughout the lecture. Homework took a decent amount of time but doing the assignments prepared you for the midterms and final since they were similar in format and difficulty. Take him for MAE 20!

Fair class Grueling homework. Tricky quizzes, straightforward midterm, difficult final. Attend lecture because he explains very well and highly encourages that you ask questions, he won't move on until everyone understands.
Awesome professor!!!

His lectures and explanations are very clear, and he won't move on until everyone understands. The book is hard to understand and you don't need to know everything in it, so definitely attend lecture!! Quizzes are also heavily based on lecture material, while midterms/final are based on homework. Attending lecture is the key to getting an A!
Great professor. I had him for MAE 105 during a summer session. He explained the material really well. Tests and exams were very reasonable, even though the subject material is kinda complicated.

Good professor, explains material very well. Explains material very thoroughly, quizzes are easy. Midterm was a bit tough and final as harder, but not hard to get an A. Made me intrigued by the subject. Wish he taught more classes.

Professor very helpful in office hour. Quizzes are easy, so make sure you understand general concept in chapter before quiz. Midterm is similar to homework, so review homework problems prior to. Final is also similar to homework. Good professor.

Bandaru's lectures were like exactly the same for the first four weeks of class. I always looked forward to hearing him start off by saying, "OK, we were basically on the topic of the heat equation..." It turned out to be a good class. Bandaru is very helpful in office hours. I wish I had taken advantage of OH earlier-a lot of it was over my head..

I think he did a pretty good job with the material. Much of it is abstract and requires little derivation on your own, but its important to understand everything that he does. Homeworks are pretty much straight from lecture notes. Quizzes are cake if you have a good sheet. Exams are long but there is a generous curve at the end for everyone.
Awesome class, awesome professor.  Lectures were clear and easy to follow.
He is a pretty good teacher.  Pay attention to the review sheet.  Final follows almost precisely

One 3 hr class and let us leave an hr early. Rambles A LOT. It was hard to stay focused. Doesn't post his lecture slides before class and moves thru slides fast so it was hard to take notes. Had attendance Qs and  if you got a Q wrong, there's no way of gaining the point even if you attended class which sucked. No hw, just exam based.
All he does is crack jokes the entire lecture which is cool until we have to take the exam. Study guide is also poorly made.

Disorganized class, not podcasted and mandatory attendance. All lecture slides weren't posted until week of exam along with study guide. Study guide isn't that helpful since it's just a long bulleted list of every topic we talked about with no extra info. Overall not the most difficult but you definitely have to teach yourself most of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's super funny and adorable. His exams aren't hard either but his slides are not the best. I had to learn about the studies myself because the slides were confusing and his explanations weren't the best either. Mandatory attendance. Overall, this class was enjoyable, just wish it was more organized.

Really passionate about his work but causes him to digress during lecture a lot, it's not terrible. The content was super interesting and the work was manageable. Attendance mandatory for credit and if you want to pass the exam.

Funny, sweet professor! Coming to class was a delight. He has such expertise in the field, and many of the experiments he teaches are his own. Graded only by two exams (30% each), an "in the movies" essay (20%), and attendance (20%). Easy to ace the exams if you study and understand the experiments.

No recorded lecture; mandatory attendance; all you have are the slides (that aren't that good); textbook isn't helpful; lectures were not clear to follow. TAs carry that class with their study guides. He's a funny and good guy, cares about students, but I was lost all the time. Needs better organization and needs to prioritize material better.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were tough since he never released the slides before class. He expects you to take in a load of information while also noting down everything he says at the same time. The slides were unhelpful since it only had basic information and no explanation. And all the explanation he wants you to know for the exam are only shared in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Am I taking the psychology class or watching travel events of Professor & TA?

We are NOT paying high tuition fees for this type of both internally and externally biased & rude professor and so is TA. He never explains anything clear or specific to the subjects but he expects you to be super specific. He surely has no comprehension skill or inter personal skill. How did he pass to earn the PhD?

Professor offers many chances to keep your grade up; however, the lectures feel biased and most of the teaching seems to stem from large chunks of reading. He feels very unserious, and he promotes a lot of work/papers based on people he personally knows/has worked with. He can also be insensitive to serious/triggering topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Attendance is not a mandatory but he will give quiz at each lecture. His presentation slides are pointless while he views things under biased mind. Not recommend to take his classes.

He is a mess and his mind is all over the place. His TA doesn't even show up on the classes but he deducts points of attendance from the students who pay him. He doesn't prepare assignments ready for students to submit but still keep talking about submitting the assignments. Another UCSD ashamed representative.

(+): Relatable lectures, summarizes key studies for you, ONLY 25 pages of reading per week, exams are ALL lecture-based, TAs are TREMENDOUSLY helpful for studying and reviewing. He uses a MUCH smaller Textbook than before (220 total pages), HIS ACCENT (:; LOTS of EC! (-): Can be unclear at times, quizzes are harder than exams, a bit unorganized

Pio knows his stuff, but sometimes he can be a bit distracted or rushed. He also may take too much time on one topic and then not enough on the other. However, he's always willing to answer questions, and he has a great enthusiasm for the subject. His exams are all multiple choice, and he holds a reading quiz almost every week so make sure you read

Prof. is alright but he's a bit unorganized and sometimes hard to understand. Attendance is not required but lecture notes are not clear enough to understand without him explaining them. Hard to take notes in class. Takes forever to post lectures online. Review session are helpful. Amount of reading is ridiculous and not always related to the class

By far one of the best, most interesting professors at UCSD. Every Psych major has to take him, whatever course he teaches. His grading is reasonable fair. He offer a lot of extra credit opportunities. His exams can be hard but the review sessions are extremely helpful . Quizes are fair not hard not easy but they are funny!! TAKE HIM!! GREAT PROF.

Great professor! He is absolutely hilarious and pretty adorable too. The class is really easy and super fun. There is some overlap with social psyc but you might go over it in different ways and there is still plenty of new stuff too. I would highly recommend the professor.

I took social psych and cog psych so this was a breeze. I never cracked the book and rarely went to lecture but landed B's on both exams and aced the quizzes. Winkielman's hilarious but his lectures are a bit unfocused. Just memorize the slides and skim the book and you'll do fine.

Professor Winkielman is great! He seems to really care about his students and receptive to questions and concerns. I have enjoyed every lecture thus far this quarter and I hope that I can take a course again with him before I graduate. He loves for students to ask questions during class. Took him for SS2 and there was a LOT of reading.

He's a funny professor that is always making inappropriate jokes (it's the Polish in him). His quizes are extremely easy, his exams are a little tougher and his final is a paper. The material is interesting. He also let's out his 3 hour lectures an hour early.

Hilarious professor-we were almost let out early (3 hour lecture), but the lecture went by pretty quickly because the material is interesting and the professor keeps his lecture light and entertaining. Quizzes are ridiculously easy, but the exams are tougher-KEEP UP WITH THE READING. It isn't hard to get an A.
This guy is so hot, not in the cute way though.

I agree that class is kind of fluffy compared to the difficulty of the exams, but they were medium hard for Psych. The worst part was the appalling book we had to use that was 50% of the exam questions! He is entertaining, and lectures painless, but his TAs were REALLY slow about posting grades and things in any kind of timely manner.

Professor Winkielman's a cute, Polish Professor whose jokes references to Europe (culturally lost on American students) definitely keep class interesting. The quizzes are super easy if you skim the reading, but be careful, the midterms are a lot harder (using the TA's review sheet helped). Paper grading was lenient. All lecture slides online.

He is a nice guy and tries to be funny, but his joking and rambling makes lecture basically pointless. the 120 minute lecture could be compressed into 15 minutes if he just taught. posts the slides online, which you can read all of in 40 minutes. too much reading, tests are kinda hard, not enough teaching for all the learning he expects you to do.
What a fun and interesting class! Love him! He even quoted things from this website lol

I liked that his lectures SUPPLEMENT the readings. You learn a lot more that way... he doesn't just reiterate everything from the text. I thought the midterms were very manageable if you keep up with the readings (1/2 lecture, 1/2 textbook material). But it really helped me to take PSYC 105 concurrently since the material overlaps a lot.

The most adorable professor ever!! Lectures are entertaining because he is hilarious without even trying to be funny. Weekly quizzes are not hard at all. They're supposed to help you keep up with the readings, but as long as you have general knowledge of psyc principles you'll get 100%. Exams equally represent lecture and textbook material.
weekly quizzes, semi-hard midterm, 2 papers which aren't that bad.  The professor just makes you happy. He has the funniest accent and he's just so jolly its contagious.. =)

i found his lectures ridiculously boring. his lectures don't follow the readings. the readings were very long but easy to understand. the midterms were kinda difficult but all multiple choice. there were two essays which were easy, and you must be on top of the reading if you want to do well on the quizzes.  easy if willing to do all the work

The book we used was written in the 90s, which makes it way out of date.  The readings were long and painful. Pop quizzes weren't organized.  Professor was a great lecturer who holds attention well.  Plenty of opportunities for improving grade.
enthusiastic happy guy. material wasnt always the most interesting but he tried to make it entertaining by bringing pop culture references and cartoons in...hard tests

Quiz almost everyclass on reading.  Not so bad, makes you keep up.  and a lot of the quiz questions appear again on the test.  make sure you talk to the ta's about what he specifically wants on the first paper, it is much easier to write when you know and easier to get an A.  But there are a lot of questions on the tests for the time given.
Quizzes and papers were easy, but the midterms were extremely hard...there were too many long-winded questions that led to nowhere. 100 questions is too damn many for a hour and a half class.
Great class! Easy class quizzes, ok exams. Dr. Winkielman has a great sense of humor and carries an infectious enthusiasm with him.
He's nice, funny, relax, and helpful.  Interesting lectures.  Fair quiz, exam, and paper.  This guy is so cute, not in the hot way though.
No Comments

Really sweet professor. Make sure you pay attention in lecture or do the readings and you'll do fine. Easy-to-understand content, no homework, in-class assignments were pretty easy, and the final was take-home, fun, and creative.

The class was fairly interesting and very doable. Three in-person assignments+ a take-homefinal essay/assignment that you complete using AI. The assignments are fair b/c they are based on the information in the lecture slides. The lecture and discussions have attendance sheets, but you can get away with not going if you have a friend in the class.

her lectures aren't bad, nice, and caring. attendance is mandatory which is unfortunate but the bright side is the class is so easy. just do the hw (read) and you'll pass with flying colors. trust me, this is one of the easiest classes you'll ever take if you take it with her. majority of your grade is 4 in class writing assignments.

Prof. Marechal is an incredible lecturer and teaches this class very well. She makes the class extremely engaging and exciting. There are 4 short-assignments which are like free-response quizzes, and a final project at the end of the quarter. It is reading heavy but the lectures are based off of the reading, so that is a given. Great professor!!

Actually took Prof. Marechal for PHIL 31, but you can tell how passionate about what she teaches. She is so knowledgeable and extremely willing to help you understand class material. Grade was based on attendance, 4 in-class assignments, and our final was online. As long as you do the readings & go to the discussion, you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof.Marechal is very knowledge and passionate. She takes time to answer our questions and provide resources to explore further if we're interested. She encouraged students to discuss our thoughts beyond lecturing us. (her lecture is phenomenal by the way) Therefore, her class was fun, engaging, and full of great discovery.

Patricia Marechal is one of the smartest people I have had the pleasure of being a student for. If you just look her up you'll see her CV is 13 pages and she has been invited to speak all around the world. She has her PhD from Harvard. She is so intelligible in creating philosophical scenarios and blowing your mind. I would only take her if i could

Good lecturer, very knowledgeable. Attendance was not mandatory, but I say you should 100% go to understand the readings. Philosophy texts are not easy to understand but Professor Marechal explains it all in lecture which helps a lot to prepare for the midterm and final exam. The exams are mixture of multiple choice, matching, and writing.
Really kind and passionate professor. Class was pretty easy and required very little work outside of class, just a discussion post every week. Would recommend for an easy A and a fun time!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: The professor does a lot to prepare students for the midterm and final with practice questions completed in class. There's also weekly online discussions that are pretty straightforward, so those definitely help to balance out the grade. Otherwise, Professor Marechal is great at teaching her subject and cares about students.
Very engaging lectures, and is very invested in the topic. I highly enjoyed the class and recommend her as an amazing lecturer.

Excellent professor! Goes in depth about the readings and answers questions very well. Graded on one small assignment, a 750 word paper, and final test + extra credit. Accessible outside class. We had to buy 3 fairly cheap books. If you do poorly on one assignment it can be detrimental for your overall grade because so little is graded.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: provided outlines for every class, reasonable reading assignments, big on having discussions about the content, so it felt like conversations rather than teaching. very kind and understanding

The professor never responded to multiple emails. The midterm was not reflective of his lecture. His lecture is not engaging, and his slides are dense. Overall, I didn't learn anything new from MGT 45 Principles of Accounting. At the end, there was an investment report project. However, I did not feel equipped to complete the assignment.

Heavy lecture, lacks grabbing students attention. Grades base on completion. Midterm, no final just project/presentation. Responds really fast to emails and questions. Topics are heavy, open note exam but still a bit difficult. Many used AI while taking exam making it not fair. No TA which sucks cause no one helps unless it's prof, high %  curve.

Amazing professor. He talks about companies a lot and how to analyze them. 1 midterm, attendance taken, 1 group project, biweekly hw. He genuinely cares for his students, especially during office hours. Feel free to ask him questions. He seems rather distant at first, but once you talk with him, he is rlly willing go out of his way to help you out.

Caring and passionate about teaching and chemistry, I found watching lecture recordings easier to understand than attending lecture, makes a constant effort to engage with the class. Weekly-ish quizzes and achieve HW, 2 midterms + cumulative final (cheat sheet allowed for all). Overall, awesome teacher, difficult class

Course was intimidating at first but I grew to like this professor. Homework is way more complex compared to his exams, his weekly quizzes are much more telling of the midterms. Provided a practice exam for the 2nd midterm and final. Super understanding and tons of patience, he doesn't mind repeating himself if you don't understand a concept!

i used to love chem. not anymore after taking his class. took 2 years of chem in hs just for bro to ruin the experience. lectures are EXTREMELY boring and majority of it isn't even based off of AP CHEM. keep in mind, a 5 in AP CHEM clears the CHEM6 series yet half of the stuff taught in his class is not in ap chem. grading scale isn't bad tho.

This class is sorta difficult even if you have prior knowledge from AP Chem. His lectures are boring and his accent makes it harder to understand. He uploads slides but half the material on the slides is gatekept because he wants to make the lecture "more engaging". Homework can be frustrating sometimes. Generous grading scale. Overall, not bad.

One of the best and kindest profs I've had!! He does move a bit fast and goes more in-depth than other Chem 6A profs, probs cus its his first time teaching non-honors chem. theres 2 midterms (20q) and a final (40q) which can replace midterms. Discussions not mandatory and cheatsheets are allowed, also class is curved (61%+ is passing)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tests make up 80% of grade, 25% midterm 1, 25% midterm 2, 30% final. However, he does offer score replacement based on final exam. Discussions claim to be mandatory but you don't need the points to get full participation credit. Lectures are very boring. Practice exams are nothing like actual exams.

He's the chillest professor ever!! Gives extensions for everything midterms, quizzes, homework's of course with reasonable explanations but he is very caring and is passionate about what he teaches. Content could be challenging if you have no previous knowledge, but it shouldn't really be hard to catch up. Wish he taught the entire 6 series.

I LOVE PROF. PAESANI! He is so kind and understanding, grants so many extensions, and responds very fast outside the classroom. One of the best prof I've had so far. Attendance isn't mandatory but I recommend watching his lectures, they are very helpful. His accent is so cute and not hard to understand. Class isn't too difficult just pay attention.
He is chill and funny. Tests are really easy . Love everything about this class even if its difficult. would take it again .

Peasani is an easy professor,  his tests are all super easy(easier then CHEM 4) and are all multiple choice. The only problem are the lectures, it is easier to understand him when watching podcasts rather than going to his class. Gives a lot of extensions and is super understanding, even let some guy use his phone as a calculator during a test.

This professor is being very responsible for his students; he responds to messages quickly and with full patience and detail. He tries pretty hard to keep the class engaged, although attendance is not mandatory. Some accent is confusing, but overall, he is a very fun and cute professor:D

Professor Paesani is a really good teacher. I'm still in the process of taking his class but I genuinely enjoy it. I recommend watching his lectures outside of class to help with understanding so you can pause and rewind to take notes as many times as needed. He goes a little faster during lecture. He's just sweet and has a cute italian accent.

paesani is very nice and funny. he genuinely cares about your learning and makes sure to get to know you as his student as opposed to letting you just be another face in the lecture room. the lecture material definitely sometimes went into heavy detail that is unnecessary to focus on for exams, but his office hours were always super helpful and fun
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Paesani is goated! He's the type of professor that genuinely wants you to understand the material, not just learn it. Material is def challenging -- I'd highly recommend taking AP Chem bfr (still doable w/o). Tests are fair & accurate reflection of lectures, remember to also go over discussion problems & examples covered in class.

Prof Paesani was an amazing professor and genuinely cares about the success & wellbeing of his students. He is always ready to help and is truly passionate about chemistry and teaching. The material in the class is difficult (esp w/ quantum) but reading the textbook and doing practice problems you will do well. Start studying early and don't cram.

Nicest and most caring professor, he genuinely wants to see his students learn and succeed. Only thing I would say is I wish the lectures were less about deriving equations and more about doing practice examples together. Sometimes the lectures were very very difficult to understand. Great professor but the class itself caused me lots of stress

Paesani is goated. Good lecturer, super patient and knowledgeable. He genuinely cares about his students' success, and his grading policies emphasize learning and improvement. The course is challenging and will require a lot of study outside of class, but Paesani is happy to help if you seek it out.
Prof Paesani goes very deep into the theory
good lectures but tough class

Professor Paesani is one of the best at UCSD. The world starts to make sense after you take his class CHEM 6AH. Amazing professor, and exams are a bit tough, but its an honors class after all... Would def recommend him. 100%

Professor Paesani cares about his students a lot and is very funny. The course itself is hard but you learn a lot if you put in the time and his tests are difficult but straightfoward. Do the practice problems, as many as possible, and use application (practice) if you read.

Professor Paesani is a great teacher. He is infinitely patient with students' questions, and always goes over examples from his slides and explains any mathematical concepts that students may find unfamiliar. Furthermore, he regularly has office hours where he goes over confusing parts of the past week's lectures and/or practice midterms.

Professor Paesani is great at what he does and is very engaging in lectures. Attendance and homework are not mandatory but both I would highly recommend. If you take this course, please stay on top of assigned textbook readings to ensure understanding, and then use lectures to clarify further. I regret not doing so, as I could've gotten an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Paesani is an amazing professor and really cares about his students. The subject of the class is hard, but going to lecture and his office hours really helps. The homework wasn't for credit but I definitely recommend doing it to do well in the class.

Hands down the best professor I have ever had. He genuinely cares about his student's success and is available outside of class time. He explains very complex topics very understandably all while having a great sense of humor. Do all of the homework, go to discussion, office hours, and lectures and you will easily get an A. I slacked off and didn't
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 6AH is a challenging class and there is a learning curve with quantum. But if you put in the time you will find the most collaborative and encouraging learning environment. Fair exams similar to HW. Office hours are the best,  incredible and inspirational lectures, he rlly cares about our success. If you can take a class taught by Paesani, do it.

feeling: lost/helpless i went to office hours looking for help and it was basically a discussion led by us students  talking about one problem; I did not get help on the 5+ i needed help with. despite his wildly high ratings do not take his course. this is your sign. don't do it. take 6A. -someone who now has 4.0 bc i switched to 6A

I started out in this class because of the reviews. don't listen to them unless you have taken AP chem. I went into the class w honors chem knowledge and had no idea what was going on - there is no review at all. I moved to reg chem and got an A easy. sure hes cool, but unless u a chem nerd, its not worth the "H" on tran. protect your future self.

Dr. Paesani is an engaging lecturer, and though the class content was difficult, I loved his class overall, though I did need to put in extra work. He provides problem sets from the textbook, has office hours and problem solving sessions. He is extremely adaptive to students' scheduling needs. The class has 2 exams and a final.

An absolutely fantastic professor. Dr. Paesani challenges his students, but genuinely cares about their success. His lectures are entertaining, engaging, and efficient. 90% of the grade is split up equally between 3 tests. Problem sets and practice tests are optional, but helpful. The (online) textbook is also quite helpful if you're confused.

Chem 6AH is a difficult class, but Prof. Paesani is an outstanding teacher for it. He explains things very well and genuinely wants students to succeed. Very accessible outside of class. Homework/attendance are optional but super beneficial. Lectures are engaging and office hours are worth attending. If you can take his classes DO IT!

Excellent professor! Cares deeply for his students and challenges them to think about what they learn. Optional homework and attendance, but one felt excited to do homework and attend lecture because of Professor Paesani. 11/10 professor!
He was awesome! I wish I could take more classes with him

I took his class during the online COVID-19 situation. His lectures were asynchronous and going over concepts. And then he had synchronous to go over problems. His lectures weren't that bad, but not really similar to the homework. He is very caring and makes sure you understand the concept.

UCSD Chem Dept sucks in general but Paesani is their redeeming factor Truly cares and hold review sessions every 1-2 weeks Go to class, do the HW/practice MT, go to OH & you WILL get an A. Exams are VERY fair and representative of HW Book is helpful Final was much harder (due to covid19/online exam) but you get what you put in! Great prof!

He is a great person, always ready to help you no matter what your situation is. He would go over a concept so many times until you get it. he assigns a HW every week from the book, if you go to his office hours, he would help you with the HW. His midterm is very similar to the practice midterm and the HW and the problem session questions.

Dr. Paesani is one of those professors that you should try to take before you graduate. While his entire lecture is on the chalkboard, he does it so that he can explain things clearly. He encourages learning, and wants students to think and succeed. He is also very nice and helpful in office hours, and anyone who has gone would tell you to go.

The best professor I have ever had. He is super clear in explaining concepts in lecture and is accessible outside of class if you have any questions. He is very easy to talk to and you can really become friends with him. His tests are representative of what he teaches in class and pretty easy.

Everything you could ever want in a professor: good lecturer, available office hours, helpful problem sessions, approachable, fair grader, and someone who wants his students to do well. He will make you not regret taking the honors series.

One of the best professor in the general chemistry honor sequence. Even though the material he taught is kind of deep but useful and he just give basic stuffs in exams and will not be a problem for GPA. He's really a nice person whenever you talk to him and really interesting .

He's not only smart and clear, (he remembers his lectures and writes everything on the board) but also plays music sometimes in between his lectures(He played OMAM!) (And that's 3 straight hours of lecturing!). Even if you ask him awkward questions like "why are we doing this", he can still make it funny and take it back to science. Pretty amazing!

His review sessions had challenging problems that prepared me for the exams. He devoted much time to helping students understand the material both in and out of class. HW could be tough but it's an honors class and overall much better than regular chem series for those who actually want to learn and prepare themselves for upper divs.

You need to have studied this material before in high school to do well. The fundamentals are never discussed & higher level understanding is expected. That said, if you have no previous experience with the material & you're willing to put in A LOT of time & effort to be reading the textbook, you can do well. Paesani's also super nice and helpful!
Really good professor!Devote a lot to the class and students!!
Prof Paesani is the first professor who gives me the impulse to write something. He's awesome: he grades leniently and is available outside of class. Take him if you can: you won't regret it

Paesani has got to be one of the most caring professors at UCSD. He personally holds review sessions and has not only office hours but coffee hours to talk about life, profession, anything. His lectures are clear, but this was an honors class, so the tests were still extremely difficult, but that's how it is. If you have the chance, take his class!
Overall a great professor who truly cares about his students. He will do what he can to make sure you really understand the material. He is a pretty cool person who will definitely push you to think.

Great professor. Holds a ton of review sessions that he personally goes to! Encourages student participation and is really concerned with students' learning. He helped me get into undergraduate research. Highly recommend!!
One of the best professors I've ever had. He cares deeply about his students and their learning/retention of the material. Highly recommend taking this class, and any other class taught by him.

Probably one of the best professors I will ever have. He's super helpful, truly cares about his students and their learning, and is just overall an outstanding teacher. Highly recommend taking his class.

Definitely one of the most helpful professors I've ever had. He really cares about students! Always accessible and ready to help (even during exams, he sits down and works with you through the problems). My friends and I had dinner with him after the final and from talking to him, we can tell that he is really a chill and fun guy overall Recommend.

While his tests are hard and his lectures are fast paced, this was an honors class so what else should be expected? He did an excellent job guiding his students through the material, he held 6 review sessions (himself, not the TA),and if you go over your exam with him he will give you points where you should have gotten them. Highly recommend him.

Paesani truly cares for his students and gave fair tests and assignments. He genuinely enjoys the material he teaches and gives others the opportunity to do further research into the tics discussed. He was one of my favorite teachers thus far hands down!
good class, tough tests but reasonable with grading and a great teacher.  his accent can be tough to understand at points and his 9's look like g's
good professor. very reasonable. definitely recommend him

The course started manageable but became difficult to follow later. I don't want to act like the victim here and complain; however I want to voice that the class averages for the tests somehow increased with the content becoming much harder. Mind you less than a quarter of the class shows up for lecture and it was open notes and open electronics.

Fluid dynamics is a difficult concept to grasp, and Prof Zhu did a fair job at explaining it. His teaching could be improved by adding more examples in real life and less theoretical, but the content you'll find online is often worse. His quizzes and final are very similar to the review sheet and fair, and the homework is good practice.

The teaching style is unlike any other professor I've had. The lecture notes are not intuitive at all, so good luck studying on your own. He doesn't really go into detail on things, so you're left confused half the time on how we just skipped from one equation to the next with little explanation.
I have to work extremely hard just to keep up in this class. Be prepared for the quizzes and exams, because they make up a major part of the final grade.

Lectures are super boring and he just reads off the slides. Most of the time what he says makes no sense and his slides or solutions or examples have mistakes and it makes it impossible to learn. I've learned nothing this quarter, I've been relying on my knowledge from past classes. This prof doesn't care at all abt students

This professor taught me nothing regarding mechanics. I have nothing good to say about this professor. I emailed him to help me multiple times, and he would just send back a message with no actual help. His exam review sessions are composed of 90% him explaining his bullet points on the slides and ONE example.
His class is chill and materials are not too hard to absorb. Weekly hw and 2 midterms and a final which are doable. The grading is lenient also. Definitely take his class again if I have a chance.

Prof Zhu is pretty good. Although he does have an accent, he always speaks clearly and loudly. Grading is fair. Tests, including the final, were open note/book and they were not too difficult. However, always make sure to study beforehand to ensure you have mastered the material. Final is 40% of your grade, so be sure to study well.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As a first-year transfer student and being my first quarter (and also being online due to COVID), this class was great!! The quizzes and exams are very similar to the class notes, so make sure you read the notes and read textbook. Write down key things that he says during lecture!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible class. I can't believe I learned absolutely nothing in this course, I really know nothing about vibrations. Cannot speak proper English, hard to understand during lectures where he just reads off the slides that don't teach me anything except plug and chug. Grading is wack. Joke of a class and a sad excuse for a "respected" professor

I took Professor Zhu for Vibrations and Fluids. His lectures are very thorough and descriptive. He explains the conceptual parts of the material then introduces the necessary equations. Assignments are helpful. When I took him, his quizzes and exams were open note and I highly suggest you use your hw during exams. Overall, I really appreciated him!

Professor Zhu is hands down the best vibrations professor I have taken. Lectures were on point and exams were very representative of the homework, though not exactly the same problems. Does have an accent however lectures are very detailed. He does show a lot of helpful examples. I do recommend him.

A respectful professor who also respects his students and teaching assistants. Clear lectures in the best kind of format for engineering: theory, formulas, examples. Accent is not too heavy. He doesn't make lectures mandatory, but you should go because the notes he posts online aren't much.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nice audible voice with an accent. Lectures go over problems that are very similar to hw and exams (sometimes the same exact problem). HW usually doesn't take that long and are intermediate in difficulty. Gives very fair exams that are open book/notes even though the graders were harsh. TA will also help you check hw answers.
this class with zhu will help your gpa =D
Go to class take notes, All of this midterms are from the notes. For this midterms and Finals just study the homework. All of this homework problems are from his notes and homework.

Prof Zhu is a really nice guy. He allows make-up midterms and overall very friendly. However, he does have a strong accent which makes his lectures a bit hard to understand. His homework/exams reflect directly from his lectures.

Lectures were very engaging and interactive! Makes the information really stick and I didn't have to study that much for the midterm or final to do well. You get to have a cheat sheet on exams and there is a textbook but it's free and online.
Professor Pilegard was very passionate. I recommend takings this class.

I've had Pilegard a few times now and I love her. She's so sweet and makes even boring topics seem interesting! Statistics can be difficult for people, but she makes it very digestible and easy to understand. Cheat sheets allowed on every exam!

I loved Professor Pilegard! While her online lecture videos can be a little lengthy they're always interactive and engaging. The exam questions might seem a little difficult at first but as long as you are thoroughly prepared with the material and know how to apply it you should be fine. I would 100% take this class again if I could!

Very amazing lecturer, very clear and easy to understand. Monday lectures were optional but engaging and overall very fun to go to. We got a one page front and back cheat sheet on all exams so they were quite easy.If you took AP Psych, most if not all of the material is review and we had all week to submit labs and watch lectures.

psyc 3r has one lecture a week, and she always does a good job at keeping everyones attention and teaching the content in an invigorating way. There are only a few assignments a week and they can be done pretty quick, but the online lectures are usually an hour long so taking notes takes a while. There are a bunch of extra credit opportunities

Assignments are easy, just watch some vid lectures and you'll do fine. What is taught is interesting and is taught in an engaging manner. Only thing that made me get an A- rather than an A were the tests, which I feel were quite a bit of a step up from the video lectures and assignments (especially since there is quite a bit of info that is taught)

totally recommend! take it from someone who was somehow unable to come to any of the lectures (this quarter was on monday's) i still ended with a ~96-97. professor pilegard is nice and engaging, her exams are fair as long as you pay attention to the lecture videos, and actually do the self-explanation assignments/quizzes!

The lectures she gives are really funny and she's a really awesome professor. The material isn't hard and all you have to do is listen to her lectures do a couple of assignments, and she's very lenient on midterm grades. Totally recommend!!!! This was my favorite class this quarter!

Great professor who has really simple homework and lab assignments every week. Opens on canvas, was due every sunday. Exams were fair and representative of the material although you did have to think more on the exams than the homeworks or practice questions. But she does tell you this in advance and really makes you think about the material.

Even though I already had an interest in cognitive science, this class only amplified that and it was truly so enjoyable. The weekly assignments are not hard at all and can be pretty interesting, and lecture wasn't mandatory but I still found myself going just because. Definitely recommend, this was my favorite class of the quarter

Lectures are so engaging, it feels like all the info sticks with you bc her examples are just so specific and detailed when explaining concepts. Discussions are mandatory, but they are helpful with writing the research paper. Everything is explained in depth extremely well. Would take her for every psych class if I could.

Loved Professor Pileguard. Answered all my questions during office hours. Clear expectations about each aspect of the APA research paper. Discussion sections walk you through how to write the paper. Clear explanations during lecture. Genuinely learned a lot from this class.

1 APA style research paper, midterm, and final. Offers tons of extra credit and material is easy. Allows a cheat sheet on exams which can be printed. Lectures are very fun and she is very high energy.

Fun, engaging lectures and as long as you watch the lectures and do the bare minimum of making a cheat sheet, the tests are so easy. The content is also pretty interesting so it's not hard to sit through the one lecture that's given each week. 

In person lecture is not mandatory and it's better to just watch the online lecture tbh

Amazing Professor, though it was online class, I always went to her in-person lectures because they were actually fun and informative. Her recorded lectures weren't too boring on 2x speed either and the quizzes for them were also very easy.

LOVED Prof Pilegard!!! Her lectures make everything really easy to digest and they were super fun!! She also offers a ton of extra credit opportunities, and the tests are mostly based on concepts covered in the lecture. Reading is technically required, but the lectures basically cover all the content the book does.

She's alright, but her content on the test is way too complex according to how she teaches. There's too many uhs and buhs throughout the lecture and not enough leniency throughout the course like accepting late work. The test are what really are ridiculous and overall effect your grade. No study guide, just questions she answers.

She is very passionate about what she teaches and her lectures are very entertaining (some of my friends would ask to attend her lectures). I always struggled in the tests for some reason but everyone around me thought it was easy. I would recommend her class regardless as she does her best to engage you and make her course easy.

Professor Celeste Pilegard seems nice, the class is challenging in ways it feels frustrating. The lectures don't align well with the material on the exams.Teaching team is  undergrads who will be grading your papers, they have little experience in grading, teaching or giving feedback. At the end you discover the class was part of an experiment.

Professor Pilegard did an amazing job of making lectures engaging and fun (each one felt like a little magic show). She made concepts easily digestible by applying them to real-life examples, which helps to make them less boring. Her course overall is very accessible! There are many extra credit assignments and opportunities to improve your grade.

Great professor but wording on tests can be a little confusing. Nevertheless, a good amount of extra credit, very easy weekly assignments, and only one "project." 2 midterms with great grade replacement plan for the final ( 3 sections on the final but only the newest topic covers the final score, the other 2 are optional and correspond to midterms)
She was a fun lecturer despite the material being very boring lol. Exams are fair.

Overall, Professor Pilegard is a good instructor. Her lab assignments and reading/lecture quizzes were all easy A's. She offered a lot of extra credit opportunities. Many questions from midterms were based on either lecture or in class examples from Monday lectures. She's an okay professor, but you do have to study quite a lot.

Although I took the remote class, the weekly in-person lab demonstrations were very engaging. Her online lectures were also very organized and easy to understand. The assignments are manageable, but the tests were a bit difficult. You can tell she's one of those professors that are passionate about what they are teaching!

Professor Pilegard is an incredible instructor. I highly respect her and the lessons she has to teach. This class met only once a week in person for demonstrations, other assignments were posted online throughout the week. Very easy to pass as long as you turn in assignments on time and study for midterms and the final. She makes learning fun!

Pilegard was good! Psyc 70 is concepts, so it was interesting, especially in the beginning! Although, Pilegard's class is kinda a work overload: Quizzes every week, mandatory discussions/lectures, Sona, Midterm, Final exam & Final paper. So try your best to stay on top of things and you should be good!

Workload is intense every week. Participation for lectures and discussions matter a lot. The only reason why I'm writing this review is because she is deciding to have midterms the day after Halloween. Nobody can go out ON Halloween as Midterm is a 9am. How fun...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class although fairly direct and to the point, was super time consuming at times. As a non Psychology STEM major, I would find that some assignments would eat away at the time I allotted for my core stem classes. Nothing unbearable but can be hard to manage when all your classes are so content heavy.

Her content is honestly so hard to undestand and her tests are difficult for no reason. Her midterm was so difficult to complete in 50 minutes I was struggling and now her final short answer questions make no sense either. Why are there so many questions in such a short period of time like bffr.

AMAZING PROFESSOR!! Graded by online labs (google form questions), self-explanations (questions about lecture and graded on completion), 2 midterms, and a final. And there's extra credit. An incredibly fair class, and learned so many interesting things. 100/10 would recommend this class.

Her class wasn't difficult but it wasn't as easy as it could have been. Her syllabus isn't that clear so it is easy to get confused. Her exams were difficult and her textbook is not clear at all. She says that all the content for the exams are in her textbook or lecture but many times were in neither. Still an easy class but you do have to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Pilegard is a great professor, but this class was really difficult. The exams did not reflect the lectures and were incredibly tough. She explains things really well but the exams were not representative of what we learned.
She is the best teacher I've yet to have at UCSD. Very clear, engaging, and actually sparks genuine curiosity in her students. LOVE.

tests are mcqs, suoer conceptual and felt like the tests were a bit hard. 2 weekly assignments, 2 midterms, a short minute video to be done, offers a few extra credit opps. her lectures were engaing despite it being online, liked her format of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's super chill and VERY engaging. I actually enjoyed her lectures and they caught my attention. Midterms and finals weren't difficult at all.

LOVED her. I looked forward to her mon zoom lectures bc she always had a fun demo planned. She's always super cheerful, and u can definitely tell that she loves what she does. She also shows her cat! Two midterms and final that are open note but do affect your grade a lot. Hw was lecture vid, quick lab survey, and mini self lab, so super chill!

Definitely one of the best first classes to take when starting at UCSD. There's two midterms and a final, all of which are open note, but they do count for most of your grade. There are also two homework assignments each week that take less than an hour to finish. She's the GOAT.

Very caring professor that clearly loves what she does. Energetic and funny during lectures. 2 midterms and a final that take up the majority of your grade. Not a lot of homework, and only 1 zoom lecture per week. Would definitely take her again!

i had Celeste for MWF at 9am & i am NOT a morning person but she always made me want to go to class. so funny, so lovable, so relatable, and she makes the course material even more interesting. cheat sheets for both the midterm and final and one research paper that you write throughout the quarter. i'm honestly doing better than i expected

The weekly homework was not hard AT ALL, it probably took me anywhere from an hour to three hours per week which is super manageable. Two midterms and a final which is a pretty good chunk of your grade. Multiple extra credit opportunities. As long as you do the assignments and actually understand the content, you'll do fine!

Super easy class, well structured lectures, sometimes a bit repetitive. She's young and energetic, but her millennial shines through at times.
She's great at relating concepts to the real world and gives lots of examples and demonstrations that are really fun. If you are looking for depth and challenge this isn't the course though.
Great professor! Lectures were not mandatory but really helped with grasping the concepts better. If you are thinking abt taking this class, take it!
Prof Pilegard is such a great professor. Her lectures are fun and she includes the class in "labs" which makes the lecture very interactive. If you have the option, take Prof Pilegard!!

Good lecturer who made lectures interesting and made the somewhat abstract material understandable with good examples and explanations. Lecture participation and discussion attendance were both mandatory.

This was an easy course due mostly to it being online, so lectures weren't mandatory. The final was a bit difficult; however, there are so many opportunities for extra credit. She goes over things in depth, sometimes rambles a bit, but it's online so that doesn't really matter. Overall would recommend.

She is a really nice professor but I found that the tests were confusing and the questions could have been worded better. The weekly assignments for this class are easy and are online so you can speed up the lectures.

By far the best professor I've had here. She is funny and definitely keeps your attention in lectures. Her grading is very clear with routine assignments. HW is mostly completion and effort based. Her midterms are a bit hard if you don't watch her recordings so do so. I would recommend her to everyone. She's great and I'd definitely take her again!

Such a sweetheart, and the class is very well paced. The tests do require critical thinking, but are fair. Don't take PSYC70 with anyone else, she really makes the essay digestible and does her best to make the class engaging.

This professor was a really nice human being however her class is super hard. The concepts were very interesting honestly but exam heavy and the questions are really hard. There are assigned readings. Mondays are the only days you really need to attend Wednesday's are online and Fridays are questions (optional).

The lectures were entertaining and Professor Pilegard made it so everyone had a fun time in class. The homework was fairly graded all exams were open note, but the self-explanation and labs were enough review that you wouldn't need to rely on your notes. Some of the content required more attention to understand but it was interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Best professor I've ever had. Very engaging, caring, hilarious, and very dedicated to everyones learning.

Professor Celeste is so awesome! Gives many extra credit opportunities and has been very understanding with abrupt changes from COVID-19 pandemic (gave less questions on exams for those not used to taking exams in-person). Lectures are pretty engaging. Must attend lectures to get full participation credits, but still get half credit if you don't

Dr. P is an amazing prof/lecturer. There are learning participation questions throughout lecture, but you can submit them at a later time for half credit if you can't attend lecture. All throughout the quarter we're working on writing a research paper. Discussion is not mandatory, but can be of good help. Overall, highly recommend Dr. P!!!!
It is a pretty interesting courses and the materials are helpful in other courses at well! I would say she is the GOAT prof of PSYC at UCSD. (TBH, I think she's so good looking)
I think her classes are very inspirational and I actually learned study strategies that I know will benefit me for the rest of my life.
Her lectures are engaging. You only have to go to class once a week, the rest are videos. There's a lot of extra credit opportunities. Overall, it was an easy class.

Professor Pilegard is such a gem! We met 3x a week but you only really had to go to class on Mondays. Lectures were fun because she has this excitable energy she carries with her everywhere. Lesson roadmaps were very clear; she mostly teaches through video lectures. Make sure you understand how to apply the different psych concepts for tests.

Her lectures are very interactive and actually help you understand the material. The only day you have to go is Mondays, in order to do the assignment. But the other days are optional. Her tests are mediocre: not too hard or not too easy.. if you study 5-6 hours per midterm, you'll be fine. Also, DO ALL THE EXTRA CREDIT IT'LL GUARANTEE YOU AN A!!!

Dr. Pilegard is one of the most nicest professors. She makes the lectures very engaging and interesting. As for the textbook, for this class she wrote the textbook and gave it to us for free. Also, make sure to study hard for those midterms and final because they REALLY require you to have a good understanding of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Pilegard's lectures are fun and engaging. Plus, Monday lectures are the only ones you need to actually go to/watch for homework, the rest of the material is pre-recorded. The tests questions were kind of confusing imo.
Her class is easy but tests are not. You can totally understand everything and still got a b in test because the questions are confusing. No useful extra credit.

Very nice and funny professor. The workload isnt so bad. You have a week to turn in your homework and theres some extra credit points you can earn. Lectures arent mandatory and its recorded to go back to. Just make sure you understand the concepts of each chapter and you will be good for your exams

Pilegard is an amazing, hilarious, and engaging professor. Psyc 70 can be pretty dry at times but Pilegard always kept my attention with interesting examples and explanations. Her lectures are very easy to take notes with, and tests are based on in-class polls and lectures so as long as you take good notes you will do well.
Very kind and energetic lectures. Easy A imo.
She is awesome!!!!

The best prof I have had. She was very nice and engaging and really cared about every student understanding each concept. She was great at explaining abstract concepts and tying things together. This class really prepared me for my future psychology courses. Tests were very easy if you study at all. Highly recommend!
Thoughtful and caring, coursework was substantial as a good amount of info to intake; problem is that the exam questions are abstract therefore difficult within the given time frame.

(+): Caring and kind, exams based on lectures, lots of EC opportunities, you get to vote on what the second half of the quarter looks like in terms of topics learned, group discussion, OH! (-): nothing!!!

I absolutely love Prof. Pilegard. I wish I could take every class with her. The class content itself was pretty dry but she makes it so easy to understand and she's so down to earth, tells fun stories in class, and is just overall a joy. Always willing to help out if you're struggling and really cares about students. Take her classes!!

Prof Pilegard is AMAZING! She really breaks down the material into small pieces that are easy to digest and process. I completely bombed the midterm yet I was able to earn an A in the class. Make sure to not slack off on your research paper since it can get overwhelming

I took PSYC 70 and PSYC 105 with Pilegard. She is an amazing professor who shows clear concern for her students' learning! She teaches in a way that can make complex material seem more understandable and welcoming. She is definitely someone who is knowledgeable in psychology and clearly loves her field. Wish I could take more classes with her!

I love Dr. Pilegard! She is SO sweet and nice! There are weekly assignments which includes a discussion section with videos and quizzes, but they are easy. The assignments she provides helped me get a better understanding of the topics learned in class. I would definitely take her again!

I'm taking all online classes and Professor Pilegard was the only thing keeping me from ending it all. Her lectures are engaging and to the point. I always know what's important enough to write down and what is just to help me understand. For the first time I've been excited to go to class and learn. I can't recommend her enough.

I took Professor Pilegard's PSYC 3 class. Her lectures and assignments for each week at posted on Sunday and you can pace yourself. Exams are easy and open notes (during covid at least). Her lectures are fun and engaging and the audio/visual quality is good. She also wrote her own textbook for this class and gives it to students for free!

Dr. Pilegard is a gem. She is very clear in her lectures and is extremely personable. She breaks the concepts down very well and provides examples so that it would be easier to understand. There are 2 midterms (25 MC, 1FRQ) and a final exam (not sure what the format is yet) but the midterms aren't too hard if you watch her lectures.

Dr. Pilegard is by far my favorite prof. Since we're online, she uploads her lectures and assignments all at the beginning of the week so students can go at their own pace. Every lecture I watch I'm constantly laughing & the material is really interesting, plus she explains it really well. Weekly assignments are very easy, tests are not too bad.
I am taking pr. piligard's class this fall, she is just so nice, detail-oriented, and she is soooo cute!! definitely the best professor at UCSD.

Professor Pilegard is a very engaging and funny lecturer! The textbook reading, lectures, and overall workload was very manageable, even for a summer class. The exams were reflective of the course content, although some questions could be quite difficult, the grading was still fairly easy if you did the reading and watched all the lectures.

I took Professor Pilegard's online PSYC 3 course on Cognitive Foundations, and it was really fun and stress-free. She uploaded weekly lecture videos that are easy to follow. Her personality is very friendly and bubbly, which makes the learning environment facilitate participation and learning.

Professor Pilegard is a relatively new professor but she was great when lecturing for Cognitive Psychology. She makes her live weekly lectures and weekly Q&A fun and interactive. The way she explains concepts are very straight forward and definitely are helpful during lectures. I read some but only to clarify things. NOT REQUIRED READING.

(+): VERY caring, exams are 90% from the lecture, hilarious: even with remote instruction was able to put her flare on things, she actually wants you to LEARN the concepts, her OH!!!! (-): Exams make up 80% of the grade, exams can be rough if you underestimate them.

She is a hilarious lecturer so go to class! She has peer reviews which are group quizzes graded for participation and are VERY similar to exam questions! Dr. Pilegard is a fair grader, accessible outside of class (go to her OH for test-like examples for concepts), and REALLY cares about your success. Go to TA OH for research paper tips- helpful!

It was a pleasure to have Celeste for Psyc 3! Im a first year psychology major, and I really hope I get to take her for another class! She goes above and beyond as a lecturer and a human being. It was my first quarter, and even though I got a C, I can recognize that I could easily gotten a higher grade. (Like 70% of the class did.) Take her class!

Hilarious and charismatic, makes you actually interested in lectures! She podcasts so it helps a lot. Textbook chapters posted online, but I did not read at all and did fine. Exams were extremely doable if you watched all her podcasts! Exams were MC with one short answer, also gives extra credit. Random in class participation once a week.

Dr. Pilegard is really funny and engaging but still manages to teach you a lot during lecture. She's one of the best teachers I've had and hope to take her again in the future. Textbook isn't required and lectures are podcasted but there's random participation questions around once a week. The homework is also really doable and exams are very fair.

I love going to Dr. Pilegard's lectures. I wish I had her for more than just one class and for multiple quarters. She's very enthusiastic and her lectures are very organized. Sometimes there's in-class participation, but they're very doable. First midterm was great, attend lectures and you'll know your info. Hope to interact w her in the future! :)

She's by far one of the best teachers I've ever had. I feel so lucky to be in that class. Her enthusiasm for teaching, combined with her passion for psychology makes me smile all day in lecture. I wish I could have her for every class

It's only 1/3 way through the quarter but I just wanna say I love Dr. Pilegard. First midterm was really do-able. Her lectures are fun and she's super enthusiastic + she gives lots of great real life examples to help understand the topic. Not mandatory, but I highly recommend attending. I'm pretty sad that I only have her for one quarter :(.

Have to go to lectures for participation.  Class is test heavy, highly recommend going to class and following while he reads the slides. Take notes yourself or use his pdfs to take notes.  He curves like crazy for overall grades, so it won't turn out to bad.

lectures are him just reading off of the slides that are posted on canvas but has iclicker and makes class mandatory. tests seem super easy when taking them but then i did so bad every time, and each one is worth more than 20% of your final grade so if you aren't a good test taker, i don't recommend this prof.
unenthusiastic.

I took ECON 487 in the fall 2017 semester. I highly recommend getting the course reader that has plenty of examples. I used the textbook for its exercises which paid off. The quizzes and exams are definitly fair & are similiar to the examples that are discussed in class and in the textbook. He was easy to listen to, very collected and motivated!

Uses a "Course Reader" for all notes. Does really teach, more or less just fills in the blanks in said course reader for you. Most people failed his tests but he curves so as long as you're confident in your ability to self-teach better than others you might be ok. After the curve the average grade was a low C.

He posts terrible slides with fill-in-the-blanks that are only convenient for taking notes if you print out every slide before class.  I hated his style because it made me focus more on filling in blanks than digesting the lecture in real-time. There were also no solutions to practice midterms and finals posted online which makes it hard to prepare

Prof Nguyen was pretty nice but can be tough to follow in lectures. He lets you drop lowest test score which helps a lot but the class wasn't curved at all. I did better than I expected but it was def one of the hardest classes I've taken.
I think this guy has something going on internally.

I came in this course expecting it to be difficult because genetics is just a tricky subject in general. It was unorganized at the start, but became more organized further in the course. Attending discussions helps a ton even if it's not mandatory, please go. Tests are a bit difficult since its FRQ, highest I got was a B.

Professor Nguyen is a kind professor who notices patterns in the classes understanding of the content and adjusts in real time. He is also pretty receptive to advice. Lectures cover about 60% of what will be on exams, leaving the rest to homework. Lectures can be hard to follow at times. Discs. are not mandatory but will prolly help u.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Nguyen is a very nice guy and was quick to adapt when the class was struggling. The homework is a lot and is due at 5 pm, which was very annoying. Besides that, he is a pretty good lecturer and offers lots of extra credit opportunities. Discussion was not mandatory, but helpful especially for reviewing for midterms.

no clear grading criteria on problem sets, doing homework on mcgrawhill was extremely frustrating to deal with. course overall is disorganized and prof doesn't explain material clearly, lecture material has little to no correlation with homework problems. please wait another quarter for another genetics prof if possible

omg this guy is insane to understand and he really doesn't go in depth in topics at all unless someone asks him a question. go to ur discussions and ur ta's will be extremely helpful. nothing about the homework is explicitly covered in class and he really is all over the place. he says "um" and "uhh" like 10000 times during lecture. sweet guy tho.

I dropped right before the W deadline. The lectures were messy and unorganized, however, it was his first quarter of teaching. He seemed nice but I couldn't grasp his teaching style. I wouldn't recommend this professor. Also, iClickers were mandatory.

Not a good lecturer and most of the learning will be done by reading the textbook and analyzing the problem sets. Problem sets and assigned readings barely correlate with lecture material and exams. Covers more unnecessary content than other genetics professors. Exams are unpredictable with regard to content. Disorganized and confusing canvas.

Nice professor who is willing to listen to students' feedback and implement it into the course. Lectures are a little difficult to understand sometimes but he is willing to clarify things if you ask. I would recommend going to office hours and review sessions to make sure you understand the material for the exams. Discussion is optional but helpful

I think he's a nice professor, however as a professor he's pretty difficult. He teaches in a way that is hard to understand, and tests were difficult, especially the first midterm (class average was about 50%) 2nd midterm had a better average. Tests were only FRQ, you get cheat sheets, it's still difficult. He just made genetics 10x worse.

I had Professor Qin for the entire CHIN100M series and I learned a lot about an era of Chinese history that is not often talked about in other Chinese language courses I have taken in the past. She also provides students with the opportunity to speak with her about their homework, essays, and exams outside of class.

Qin Laoshi is a great teacher. She care about her student. She was super funny when I took her class. Highly rated teacher. I learned a lot with her class and honestly Mandarin is hard but I still remember some from her class.

I took Professor Qin for CHIN100AM and 100BM. She's an amazing caring professor, with very very straightforward grading and exams. If you try in the class with just some background level of Chinese, you'll do very well in the class.

Qin Laoshi's class is the first time I can genuinely say I enjoy learning Mandarin, and do not feel judged while trying to improve my speaking skills.
