She is very caring and accommodating, making project deadlines flexible. Her lectures are always engaging, and encourage you to truly improve in your Mandarin. One of the best profs I've ever had!

覃老师is the goat!! Her class has really developed both my listening and my tones. The class is small, so you get to know the professor and the other students, and the class is very manageable to take along with other time-consuming classes. 10/10 recommend :)))

覃老师 is a such a great professor, she is super passionate about the course and its content, and genuinely wants to see her students succeed. She is also extremely flexible and understanding, due dates aren't set in stone. I love how she contextualizes each work we read with the history behind it.

Compared to the 3 years of Chinese class that i took in my home country, I learned so much during this class. The professor is very nice, caring and really supports you to learn chinese. She encourages you to practice your speaking during class and office hours are available to read the texts. The course is quite dense in terms of vocabulary.

One of the best Chinese Language teachers, very clear grading criteria that is very forgiving to students who take this class P/NP out of interest for the language and culture. Lectures are 10/10, very well organized and highly tailored to effective language learning and retention.

Qin Laoshi is by far the most caring and dedicated teacher I've ever had at ucsd! If you have any interest in studying Chinese and are able to, give her class a shot. Further, the grade isn't too much of an issue; if you show up to class and put in the effort to learn characters then you'll see it's a super fun class and very worthwhile.

Qin laoshi is a very caring and enthusiastic teacher! She makes real world connections with the characters we learn to make it more memorable and understand the background of the Han zi. Every lesson, she brings lots of energy which creates a very fun learning environment.

Without a doubt, take her classes if you are considering learning Chinese!

Best teacher at UCSD. So kind and truly helps students learn. Teaches from a textbook, makes fun scenarios to learn vocab and grammar. Helped drastically improve pronunciation. Midterm/final is only 15% each for grade so lots of opportunities to showcase learning with no stress. Will be taking her all year long. All teachers should learn from her

If you have the opportunity to take a class with Professor Qin Hong Anderson, don't hesitate—you'll gain not only valuable skills but also a mentor who truly invests in your success. I'm forever grateful for her instruction and will always remember her impact on my academic and personal journey. Highly recommend taking her courses!

Her curriculum is thorough and engaging, focusing on practical skills that build a solid foundation in Mandarin. She has inspired me to continue my language studies beyond the classroom, and I now feel confident and optimistic about reaching advanced fluency. I owe much of this to her incredible teaching methods and encouragement.

Professor Qin Hong Anderson is truly an exceptional educator. Her passion for teaching and dedication to her students make her stand out as one of the best professors I've ever had. Her classes are challenging yet incredibly rewarding, offering a high-quality education that equips students with the tools needed for success in Mandarin.
This professor was very accommodating to students who struggled in the class even offering additional weekly tutoring with the TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Qin Laoshi is a great professor that is incredibly understanding and caring for her students; she really pushes us to learn and participate. Attendance is required, but there aren't too many assignments. Midterms and the final are also very fair! I was going to only take one quarter, but Qin Laoshi's teaching had me stay the whole year!

Qin Laoshi was one of the best professors I had in my time at UCSD. She is a kind a fair grader who cares about building fluency in her students. During covid online classes, she was very flexible in her teaching style and incorporated lots of feedback in her class. I would recommend her for anyone thinking about learning Mandarin Chinese!

Qin Laoshi is one of the best professors I had throughout my time at UCSD. Being a part of the 20 series in 2021, Qin Laoshi focuses on the progress of each and every student, especially in lecture when she encourages everyone to participate. I highly recommend the 20 series with Qin Laoshi, as my Chinese improved tremendously.

I was enrolled in CHIN20AM, and Qin lao shi was excellent. The class was very personal and she made sure everyone participated. This might be uncomfortable for those who aren't comfortable with Chinese, however, Professor Qin is incredibly kind, patient, and understanding. She works hard to make sure all the students understand the material.

Great person who cares deeply about her students. I'm awful at Mandarin but she makes it possible to get a good grade as long as you genuinely try. Was going to drop Chinese after this sem but she changed my mind.

An amazing professor and one of my favorites at UCSD. She genuinely cares about her students and is very understanding and respectful. She creates a collaborative and intimate class setting that encourages participation. Regardless of your proficiency, if you have any interest in learning Chinese, I would HIGHLY recommend taking one of her classes.

If you're continuing from CHIN10CN/are able to test into Qin Laoshi's class, I highly recommend doing so. Her main requirement is participation, and it's very manageable to keep up with the vocabulary/reading. Qin Laoshi is very accommodating, takes the effort to connect with students, and will give really great advice tailored to your own needs.

Qin Lao Shi is an amazing professor! Regardless if you have taken Chinese classes before or this is your first time, she makes sure that everyone participates and is actively learning/speaking the language. Your grade comes from daily vocab quizzes, homework assignments, group projects (film a skit in Chinese), midterms, and a final.

Qin laoshi's lectures are always full of energy.  She actually cares about each and every student.  She makes time after class for students who struggle with pronunciation.  She lets students use pinyin in quizzes and exams.  Not a lot of homework assignments.  Definitely recommend to people who are willing to learn Chinese!

Professor Qin was a very caring and effective professor! The assignments required reasonable work and trained comprehension, speaking, reading, and writing. She had clear grading criteria and the vocabulary quizzes we had at the beginning of every class were very straightforward and easy if you did a little bit of studying the night before.

Super vibrant, caring prof. Keeps spirits high and gives good feedback. She has you film videos for hw which I hate, but I understand why. Practice handwriting in your free time though, you need it for tests.
Professor Anderson was the most dedicated, most passionate for teaching, and most enthusiastic professor I ever had.

Qin-Hong is a fantastic Chinese instructor. In her class, I was able to quickly relearn the Chinese I had forgotten, as well as make a lot of new progress. She keeps you engaged with interesting topics. In my opinion, the pacing of the class is just right, and the textbook is excellent. I highly recommend her.

I had Professor Qin Hong Anderson in a few of my Chinese courses. She is challenging and you may have to put in work outside of class, however, my mandarin improved immensely because of her. She has a passion for teaching and you can tell that she wants you to succeed. Don't be afraid to ask for help! She is always happy to help!
Makes learning Chinese an amazing experience. Super passionate teacher whos accessible outside class to help you.

Qin Laoshi has a great gift for teaching Chinese to beginning and intermediate students, who naturally struggle to make the transition from English to Chinese expression! She made the process easy and enjoyable
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Qin Laoshi was one of the best professors I ever had at UCSD. She truly cares about all of her students and makes you feel so comfortable in her classroom. Obviously learning Chinese is not always so easy, but Qin Laoshi makes it fun and takes time to make sure that you understand. She is so easy to talk to and her video projects were so helpful!

Qin Lao Shi is a great professor that really cares about her students. She even knows when people have been improving their tones and she'll ask how they did it! Be one of those people ;) She also has a lot of energy (or caffeine) during lecture and that always makes the class fun. There's not much HW, just review before and after class.

One of the most genuine, caring professors I know. I enjoyed her pure lecture days the most. Qin laoshi does an amazing job of breaking down daunting passages and helping you learn the meaning and beauty of a piece. You will have to do presentations and write various essays, but it is all doable. Not an easy class, but you will learn a lot!

Qin Laoshi is a wonderful professor. She's very attentive to her students and wants to make sure that everyone does their best in class. She's very encouraging when things get difficult. Her classes are intuitive and understandable. Her classes are fun while at the same time educational. You not only learn the language but the culture as well.

Qin Laoshi made learning Chinese doable by teaching about the world and Chinese culture, so the language made more sense. Not only did I start gaining confidence during the 20 series with her, but I learned really interesting things about Chinese history and culture. She really cares about her students as well.

I love Qin laoshi's teaching style. Fast-paced to keep it interesting and everyone on their toes and heavy on student participation. She wants students to practice speaking as much/often as possible. Definitely be sure not to miss lecture or you will fall behind. I also appreciate how she lets us write in either pinyin or characters on exams.

One of my favorite professors from the university. The professor was very candid and respectful. She cared about students as much as them learning the material, and was accommodating to the students needs. As many students took CHIN20N with her for interest, she established a great learning environment with her passion for teaching her students.

I cannot say enough good things about this lady. Other Chinese teachers really need to take notes. She challenges students, but is completely fair. ONLY downside is that missing class can be quite costly. You lose points every time you miss a class. Other than that you are going to learn a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Qin Lao Shi is an awesome professor! She really cares for her students and is a great teacher. The course was at times hard because I had not been taking Chinese as long as my peers, but she always encouraged me and helped me keep up in class!

Qin laoshi is a wonderful professor. She has a very engaging teaching style and encourages everyone to participate in class. I highly recommend going to her office hours for additional feedback, practice, or just to chat. She really cares about her students. As long as you put in the effort, you'll do just fine!

Prof. Anderson's Chinese was really great. She adjusted her teaching style to accommodate students with varying degrees of fluency. I took this class P/NP and she requires a lighter work load for P/NP students. Compared to the first year of Chinese at UCSD the second year is less demanding (time wise) but you will be speaking a lot more.

Her courses were very interactive both in lectures and discussion sessions. Her explanations of Chinese grammar were always kept concise and easy to understand. Learnings from her class greatly helped me to survive in China when I studied abroad there.

She's a really amazing professor and she makes sure you learn and understand without getting too frustrated or feeling bad. I learned a lot in her class and had a lot of fun at the same time. You do have to do the work but it's well worth it.

I loved Professor Qin. She is very flexible, and is more worried about you learning than testing. As a result she is very flexible. If you are worried about your performance or anything, go talk to her! It's good that she knows you are really trying. I loved this class, felt like a second family.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you got by speaking English in your 20 series classes, be sure you practice speaking Chinese to prepare for class discussions (entirely in Chinese). Participation is really key so that you get the most out of the lessons. Schedule to meet with Qin laoshi if you need help. She's really passionate about her students.

Qin laoshi is an excellent professor.  A lot of 2nd year students are taking Chinese for fun, not because they have to, and Qin sees that and tries to keep everybody learning in an environment that is fun and engaging.  Don't doze off in class though; she will regularly call on everybody in the room!

Best Chinese teacher I have ever had in my life. I took Chinese out of interest and not for credit. She truly cares about her students' learning and she tries her best to support you if you are confused or are falling behind. Her lectures are funny and engaging; very detailed and easy to understand. She makes all her students love the language.
Great professor who really cares genuinely about both the subject and students taking it. Honestly made me realize that I wanted to continue the language past just taking it for college requirements.
Prof. Anderson is super sweet and funny! She's also very good at explaining grammar patterns and Chinese cultural tidbits. There are mandatory video projects, but you have the option to work alone.
Good teacher. Tries to keep everyone involved.

Qin Laoshi is an amazing professor. She is an expert on the subject, and makes learning Chinese fun and enjoyable. She is kind and respectful, but also expects her students to perform well. This combination makes for a really rewarding experience. Out of all of the Chinese professors I have ever had, Qin Laoshi is the best. I HIGHLY recommend her.

Best professor ever. She takes the time to identify each students'strengths and weaknesses and works with them one on one to strengthen their skills. Her positive feedback keeps you motivated throughout the course. She genuinely cares about her students' learning. I highly recommend this phenomenal professor.

Hands down the best chinese teacher in the department. Obviously class is going to be hard if you don't put work in but Qin Laoshi makes the class pretty fun and enjoyable imo. I highly recommend her!

Great Professor. I am taking her for two quarters and will take her again next quarter. Her class is very clear and enjoyable. Lots of participation goes on during the class. She is strict but fun and you will see your chinese improving.

She is a really great professor. Honestly the best Chinese prof in UCSD, definitely take her. Super clear as to what she's asking for on quizzes/final, and paper was decent, not too difficult. I actually learned quite a bit in this class. And since the class size is small, you get to know people in class pretty well =)

I love her. I've taken her classes for 4 quarters and she's very fair. She cares about her students and expects a lot but only because she puts a lot of effort into the class as well. She's funny and interesting. Definitely take her!

she's the very definition of "tough love"! She's strict, but only because she really does care about her students. I took two years with her- no regrets, only much better Chinese. I would definitely recommend her!

Really nice professor that cares about her students learning the Chinese language. Tests were okay if you studied. Only thing I did not like were the weekly journals. She really likes people to participate in class and makes it count as a big part in her grading scale. Overall highly recommended.

One of the best mandarin teachers at UCSD! Cares about students (tries to get to know them), clear lecturer, has funny stories!! Overall: GREAT!! The whole controversy about China/Taiwan is nonsense. Qin laoshi is very respectful. There's proper way to learn chinese and a colloqial way to learn chinese. Qin laoshi teaches the proper way.

I love Qin Lao Shi! I think she is so cool, caring and funny. She cares a lot about her students. Her tests are fair. She really holds my attention in class. Great teacher! Everyone loves her in my class. So TAKE HER!

Ask questions, take advantage of her helpfulness. She loves her students! She is strict, but encouraging. I'm very glad I had her for my first Chinese course. I will take her again next quarter. You are in for a treat!

Anderson's a pretty good teacher, but she picks favorites. That means she'll throw a lot of crap at your general direction if she doesn't like you, but she's generally really helpful to students. The journals will most likely destroy your grade, but the tests and other things are usually no problem. Take p/np if you are afraid of getting a b.

i had an okay experience. her teaching style can be a little disorganized, and sometimes her class felt a little boring. i wish she had more presentations and group work that had us actively reading instead of just straight lectures of her talking. i felt disengaged a lot of the time. also a semi tough grader. shes nice, but not my favorite.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Love her but her lectures are so boring and early its so hard to go to class and you are graded on attendance. She should really do some discussions, or student presenting of topics, SOMETHING. But she has a heart of pure gold, and I wish she was like my aunt or something. 2 essays, presentation and one final essay.

Several assignments, many readings (some were easier to understand, some were convoluted), and two midterms. She talks a lot and moves through lecture slides very slowly, but she is understanding and helpful. Midterms are not difficult, and she allows a cheat sheet for each one. The final was a very doable project. TA determines your grade though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Ribas is a clear communicator who evidently cares about her work and her students. If you're familiar with social research in any capacity, this course will be a breeze. If you're not, I imagine it could be confusing, but Ribas is very accessible and willing to answer questions!

Professor Ribas is so knowledgeable and passionate. Really enjoyed her lectures and hearing about her work. Definitely really cares about her students. Attendance mandatory and random spot checks. Reasonable grading. Only thing is grades on Canvas weren't weighted or accurate :( Overall great professor, super interesting and inspiring class!

The professor are nice and always return messages quickly, but your attendance is very much needed. As well as including two group work. TA gives you less help than you think and sometimes was disrespectful.

Class was easy. You definitely need to go to lectures to get ur participation points as they're important. One thing that messed me up was the final grade - it is NOT weighted on Canvas. Exams were easy and assignments were easy too. TA was not my favorite though - he would say very bizarre things and I didn't feel like i received noticeable help.

super easy class. 3 exercises that are p/np and 5 assignments that are graded either by completion or by rubric but i got a 100 on all of them. 2 exams that were 10 true or false and a short answer! 5 random attendance checks. the only thing is lecture slides dont have a lot of info but there is a quizlet that helped so much! Great TA as well!
Great prof, I just wish her slides were better organized. Her lectures were good, and the class overall was super simple. I loved the research project proposal, since that was our final.

Professor Ribas is understanding but does give a lot of work. 5 assignments, (one being a group project which was difficult and frustrating because I took it via zoom), 2 midterms (open note), and one final research paper, that wasn't too bad. The lectures are unorganized so I would recommend reading the textbook.

Shes pretty cool. Participation is 15% so make sure you go. (Sucks it was an 8am, WI20) You got 5 assignments, 2 midterms, and a final paper. You should honestly read the book. I got a B but didnt really try. I think if you put in the work and GO TO CLASS you can get an easy A :)

No need to read other readings, just the textbook is enough. A lot of homework. Must go to lecture. Lectures are sort of messy. Not very organized. But she is a very friendly professor overall. Grade really depends on TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Ribas is one of the best. The material covered is interesting: the videos, in-class activities, and lectures all relate and build on each other. This class is fun! 5 assignments, 2 midterms, 1 final (A research proposal which was really cool!) You learn how to apply research methods in the real world :) You'll also learn about yourself <3

Lecture is good. She goes over the essential topics that you would use for research. 5 assignments (theyre easy and very interactive), 2 midterms (both are easy if you pay attention during lecture), and one final research paper. Overall fun class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: SOCI111 was her idea & her passion showed. Cares about the students' learning. Attendance worth more than final (30% & 25%, respectively): 2 out-of-class field trips, roll taken each day, going to TA OH required. 3 short, straightforward papers on readings, a final paper w/ lots of freedom, easy grader. Take it if you can do the time commitment.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Readings had nothing to do with what was being taught in class and lectures were just straight from power points but weren't very clear. Grades aren't posted online at all and not accessible during office hours

I didn't read as much as I should have but I did attend every single class and lecture which helped me during the midterm. I did notice that attendance was more enforced during the beginning of quarter and then class was empty. Don't miss section! Attendance enforced. One final paper that you prepare for and wasn't too hard. 5 assignments.

Professor Ribas covered everything in the book well. She uses a lot of examples and shows videos in class often so that makes it easier to remember what she's teaching. The assignments are easy and the final was a paper that you spend the quarter working on. Attendance is part of the grade, but she only took it about four times the whole quarter.
Not bad professor. Not the easiest A tho.

I took a class with professor Ribas last quarter and I must say that she is one of the best professors that UCSD for Sociology. She is super cool and cares to hear about her students' opinions. She is a very nice and caring individual who truly cares about her students, this can be seen in her conduct. The topics covered in class were interesting.

Vanesa's lectures are not the most clear, and often seem like they were put together last minute or made up on the spot. The class itself was long, but she did seem to be knowledgeable about the subject. I was blessed with a super chill TA and that's what really matters

If you're not a soc sci major and want to take this for your dei, definitely do PNP! Way more work than I was expecting, especially crammed into summer. Lots of reading that is sometimes confusing so you have to come to class to get her take on it. The classgrade is based on the readings. Vanesa is cool though - laid back, helpful, super smart.

Professor Ribas is a very smart woman.  She genuinely cares for her students and wants them to understand the effects of racism, classism, sexism, inequality and gender.  That being said, her class requires a lot of reading and note taking.  Discussion and attendance is mandatory.  4 reflection papers 1 midterm 1 final 1 group presentation.

Vanesa relies too much on her ppt. I don't think she prepares adequately for every class because she always “eh...eh...eh..."in the class. Her thoughts seem disconnected and she could not hold the class's attention very well.
Vanesa is a very interesting professor. She is genuinely likeable but very disorganized with her thought processes and assignments. Not always the most clear.

She's a new professor. The content is interesting, however her lectures are kind of boring and it's hard for me to stay focused during class, which usually isn't a problem for me. But!, she is helpful when you need her and her TA's this quarter are awesome! Her tests aren't bad if you study a combination of her lectures and the book. Overall good!

Clearly very passionate but his lectures don't match up to test material. Most of the class was at a failing grade before curve. I studied 30 hours for midterm 2 towards his lecture material but it didn't pay off at all. You're better off reading the textbook 10 times and catching up on sleep during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bild 3 is not supposed to be a hard class. I got a C+ on the 1st midterm, a D on the 2nd and final. I studied for weeks for all the exams. Lectures have barely any correlation to do with the exams and the exams asked for us to regurgitate hundreds of textbook pages. Only positive was a generous curve at the end. Look for any other teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 60% of your grade, 2 midterms and the final. You can tell he loves teaching, but you'll end up skipping sleep trying to read the textbook. Also, you need an iClicker. I would have taken the 8am BILD 3 session, and that says a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the hardest class I have ever taken. The professor is nice and seems like he genuinely wants his students to succeed. There is so much reading and daily quizzes. Discussions and attendance are mandatory. The exams are unnecessarily difficult with the most annoying short answer questions. Take this class with anyone else but him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Rifkin is clearly very passionate, and it is fun hearing him talk. But majority of the info is in a dense online book, with so many pages you're expected to not only read, but remember all. The average grades for the midterms were around a 60 for both. I don't expect the final to be much better. He says he'll curve. Take a diff professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very nice professor and is passionate but his exam are really difficult and  lecture doesn't cover everything on the exams. He also doesn't curve the exam and if you fail, it drops your grade by like 20%. I studied for a week straight for a midterm and still failed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Rifkin is a nice guy and is clearly passionate about what he teaches, but his exams are unnecessarily difficult, the amount of content and reading he expects you to know and memorize is actually insane and the lectures barely cover what's actually on the exam. Way too difficult for a GE class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof is a very chill dude, but his exams are atrocious. Lecture is very surface level information, but you are also expected to know everything from the textbook. Each exam covers SO MUCH CONTENT. Only learning objectives are given, but don't really help and you'll probably have to self study. He says he'll curve the class tho. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: you can tell he loves what he teaches but he does not teach well whatsoever. Every class perhaps held 5% of the material that needs to be covered for exams and 95% of them were based on readings from the textbook and mind you for a single midterm you will have over a 100 pages of reading. 1 MCQ was worth 3 points and final's worth 200 points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Midterms are outrageously hard, assigns tons of readings, discussion isn't helpful to understanding. if you want to do well you have to study the learning objectives most of which were not taught in class and require you to self study. even with doing all of that the highest grad i have gotten on a midterm was 70%

BILD 3 is not supposed to be a diffcult course. This was his first quarter teaching and it shows. Exams are way more difficult then lecture content and are barely relevant. Readings are super long and often do no relate. Lectures are unorganized and is diffcult to know what he wants you to know. AVOID AT ALL COSTS, wait till another prof teaches
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I studied for weeks for both midterms. I got a 70 on the first and a 65 on the second. I am an A student. Assigns copious readings, doesn't hold review for exams, and requires physical iClickers. He cannot explain simple concepts and builds his exams to trick students into failing. He puts things youve never heard of on exams. Don't take this prof.

I loved Professor Rifkin's lecture and found myself really fascinated with the subject matter, though admittedly they have very little to do with how you're graded. The final research paper accounted for most of the grade, and I feel that the effort I put into that paper reflected the grade I received, i.e., it took a lot from me, but it worked out

Took this for a DEI and it was a pretty easy A. No exams, all you're graded on is annotated reading and one final research paper. The readings can get a bit long and boring but they're not hard to keep up with. Assignments are all basically graded by completion. You don't even really have to go to lectures to get an A in this class.

Prof. Rifkin does a good job for this course. I would have preferred not to have to take a DEI course, but, since it's mandated I chose BILD 60. This class has ALOT of reading that you have to do and annotate on perusal. There is also an essay due at the end, but as long as you stay caught up you should be fine. He is also very accomodating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So many readings that are poorly spaced, redundant, and largely irrelevant to the course. He tries so hard to make a lower division biology class into some pseudointellectual philosophy class. Assigned homework take 3-4 weeks to get graded and just pop up randomly with no mention in class. During the zoomdemic he has been lenient, but unorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof. Rifkin brings me lots of inspiration in coding structure. He has amazingly strong logic and good at solving problems via innovative way. However, because of his strong thinking ability, he sometimes may not be aware that students cannot catch up. The good thing is that he is very patient, so do not hesitate to ask.

He is very, *very*, passionate about stat. That being said, hes not a very good lecturer. He sometimes expect us to absorb a lot of information quickly. He covered first two chapters in three weeks, chapter 3 in one week while rushed through 4,5,6 in one week because he wanted to cover them in the midterm. Explanations are clear and interesting.

He's a really cool guy but if you want a good grade, you're not gonna get it. Too much work for a stats class. Had to teach myself b/c all he does in lecture is talk about the history of stats, which is not relevant to the homework OR exams. Also you need to know how to use an online app for the hw, which he doesn't teach you to use.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: So yes. it's true that you will  to spend 15 hours a week on homework, but the Hw system explains everything pretty well (actually better than most professors in this school) so you will pretty much know everything from it. You'll easily get 90 percent from all the hw and midterms but be prepared to get all screwed up on your final, seriously.

Tons of homework! Fortunately homework is very helpful. His lectures are not strongly related to his tests, but more like a deepening of understanding of the formulas and history behind it. Pretty cool if you want to dig into the logic side of statistics. Tests are not hard if you organize your own clues of the materials. The pace is pretty slow.

Probably one of the worst professors I have taken. He does online homework before even "teaching" the material. All he does is play around with his computer in class. Nothing really intellectually stimulating. He says his teaching style provides us a new way of thinking but in actuality, it's just his way of not wanting to teach. Tests are hard.

He gives extra credit & can appear to be a bit absent minded, but he seems to genuinely care that his students do well & emphasizes to get the help you need if you're not doing well. Its not an easy class because the way he organizes it can be confusing w/ regards to the statkey stuff he teaches, & it takes 9 weeks to get to a x2 table, work hard.

Professor Rifkin is a good professor! He assigns homework before EVERY lecture which is helpful in understanding concepts he explains in class. The weekly research assignments are helpful in understanding concepts. Exams can be tough! Tests are more concept based not just plugging numbers into formulas.

He does not explain the concepts very well and he asks you so many difficult questions. There are no partial credits for the homework. Take this class if you want to spend 15 hours every week doing the homework. If you still want to take it, reach the TA as many times as possible. They are much more helpful.

Class was fair and material was not ridiculously difficult, but Professor Rifkin can be confusing during lecture.  Does podcasts, but uses the boards a lot so they can be hard to follow.  The textbook was pretty bad and did not make it any easier to understand. Professor Rifkin really cares about his students' success. TAs are pretty helpful too.
I just came on here to give him a chili pepper. Also, you should take his class, great teacher.

I have heard nothing but bad reviews about Prof. Rikin. My experience with Scott (both in BIEB 100 and BIEB 143)nothing but good. He is extremely knowledgeable, patient, and helpful. He puts a lot of effort into helping his students. It is these qualities that make him an amazing teacher.

I'm honestly a fan of the class. His lectures were enjoyable and the test questions were very straight forward. There is a considerable amount of homework (and sometimes he doesn't explain the concepts clearly), but overall it's very doable. He's passionate about the subject and I actually enjoyed lecture.

Agree with the below comment. Overall liked the class, but it's more Research Methods than biostatistics. Graded homework is kind of a pain, but the quizzes/exams are more conceptual than memorization-based. His lectures were interesting and relevant.

I think Prof Rifkin restructured the entire class for this quarter, because it was not as difficult as I was told by past students. HW was problems from the textbook, with weekly problem sheets in discussion. Quizzes and tests are not that hard as long as you do the HW. Overall not as terrible as everyone says!

His grading scale is nice... his teaching style needs a LOT of work. Lot of random assignments everywhere, book isn't clear. Little Bio in this biostats. He seems new and trips over himself when trying to explain different answers which lost me. I considered taking another class with him then quickly talked myself out of it. Take at your own risk.
This is the kind of class where you have 3 hours of homework due by 7:00 a.m. Monday morning, EVEN THOUGH MONDAY IS A HOLIDAY! Freakin ridiculous!

His lecture is mandatory even though he just supplements the book. No discussion, just a lab that utilizes a statistics program that you will never use again (i.e. NOT excel), and there is over 10 hours of required homework a week. Worst of all, he rarely uses biology examples,which leads you to wonder why this class is called biostatis

It was a very difficult class that required a lot of work. However, I did learn a lot! But I did hate the class and work load, and it was impossible to finish the midterm on time. He is a cool professor and I'm sure the class will improve!

The worst class I have ever taken in my entire academic career.  Be prepared for 10+ hours of homework every week, and its graded on correctness, not effort. Tests were difficult and too long to even be finished in time. Lectures were disjointed--not organized at all, and he was easily flustered.

For his first time teaching 6B, it could have been worse. Coursework & the three exams were all weighed 25% each with the only the highest scores taken for Midterm 1 & 2 (a midterm or its corresponding section on the final taken). Sections are mandatory, and the exams were just like the practice ones he gave. Beware the technical errors.

A professor that cares about his students. Chem is my weak subject so I struggled with content and his lectures can get boring, but if you rewatch them and read the textbook, you'll manage like I did. His awkwardness makes him funny and tests were super fair. Allowed a notecard and you could replace midterm grades. Wish he taught 6C.

Very chill and hilarious guy, but his lecture style was very broad. Exams were exactly like the practice ones and had questions that were very reflective of the topics. Also lots of opportunities to get points for your grade (homework, online quizzes, etc)

First time teaching 6B, very unprepared! Once he said, “Do you guys ever have a dream about there being a test and you didn't study? That's me every time walking into this class.” He was funny, would go off on tangents, and is a slow lecturer. Practice midterms are essentially the same as the midterms, plus a notecard you could have with notes.
I really liked his lecture style, and found him to be entertaining. Textbook readings are extremely helpful for understanding concepts.

First time teaching 6B, and we were on the ride with him, so the grading scale was nice and forgiving. His midterm study guides were very nice and very similar to the tests, and he has multiple resources to help you learn the material outside of class. Rinehart is nice and funny; I would take him again in a heartbeat!

He's pretty nice and chill. First time teaching 6B, so he was a bit disorganized at times, but his practice exams were just like the real ones, so it isn't hard. The course has two midterms and a final that has three sections. He chooses the better score between midterm 1/2 and section 1/2 of the final when calculating grades.

Prof. Reinhart was pretty cool and was new to teaching CHEM 6B. He lectured at a slow pace. He also assumed that everyone used online notes. But he did offer practice exams that were like the actual exams, and allowed for a notecard. Please study the course content because he was constantly swamped with questions from confused students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The content itself wasn't hard, but 75% of the grade is tests and since it's all multiple choice and no partial credit, missing just a few questions can tank your grade. In office hours he was chill, just not the best at class organizing.

Nice, funny, but it was his first time teaching Chem 6B and you could tell. Not a good lecturer, gets through maybe 8 slides in an hour and 20 minutes, goes off on a lot of tangents and says a whole lot without teaching anything relevant. You kind of end up self-teaching a lot. Also, I'm somewhat certain his exams were ChatGPT generated.

I went into this class not knowing what to expect considering there were no reviews. Overall pretty chill professor, funny in class. The tests mimic the practice tests he provides. Also provides a reference sheet that has basically everything you need and even then you still get an index card for a cheat sheet.
professor rinehart taught at a slower pace than what I preferred but he did it with a lot of passion and humor.

Lots of slides, wish the completed ones were posted on canvas. Discussion material was difficult and didn't reflect what was taught in class. Overall kind of difficult to understand what we were learning in class and content was boring. I don't think that's his fault though, he seems like a good guy. Same midterm replacement as other chem classes.

Professor Rinehart was a funny professor and cares about his topic. Sometimes its confusing to understand the content due to lectures being off topic or just difficult content. Midterms offer grade replacement available on the final like other chem classes.
Unorganized and very bad at explaining the material. Midterms weren't too hard but you have to basically teach yourself.

Super funny. For his first time teaching the course and adapting to technology needs, things were a little messy. But no doubt he's knowledgeable and there to help. His practice tests were a goldmine for midterms. Perfecting the practice tests almost translated 1:1 to exams. Take him if you can.

Super sweet man but his lectures are disorganized. Doesn't know how to use tech and a lot of class time went into figuring out how to work it and usually ended up writing on the board which was confusing. His study guides are very similar to the exams so good on that but confusing lectures and quizzes before classes are what taught the course.

Very good teaching, but just stop teaching in the future. He gets more papers published, and we get better experience, which is better for everyone. But this is just for 120B. For other classes, maybe it's not this case.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great class and professor! The professor really broke down the material and made it really intuitive to understand. He provides diagrams and drawings during the lecture to help visualize symmetry. He had module knowledge checks after each chapter that amounted to 70% of your grade so staying caught up with the material was critical to your grade.

As the class was asynchronous, Rinhart provided lectures really late, so I felt like I was unintentionally procrastinating. He provided graded hw problems, but the difficulty was not in match with the quizzes. His lectures were good and has a quirky sense of humor. I feel like it would have been a great class in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Rinehart is one of the best professors I had!! He is super fun and makes the lectures very clear and easy to understand. The homeworks were only graded by completeness but they are helpful for preparing the exams so you should do them. Exams aren't too hard if you pay attention in class. HW were 20%, two midterms 20% each & 35% final.

I think the problem sets were harder than the actual exams themselves. Pay attention to the examples done in class, too. This was the first time he podcasted lecture, but you still need to pay attention. Class average is a B- with other grades set accordingly.
Great lectures and TA's were super helpful. Went in not knowing much about inorganic and came out loving it!

His powerpoint slides are colorful so its easier to read. He is willing to explain any confusion in class. The class material is hard so can't blame him if you get bad grade. Practice is the key for this class. TA can be very helpful. He gave alot of outside resource to visualize better. The test can be long so be very ready before taking it.
Super funny and made me love chemistry even more. Would definitely take him again :)

Great professor for 40A. Super nice, great lecturer, midterms and final are fair and match lectures and textbook. Has office hours twice a week, lectures recorded, and you get to keep all exams. She doesn't give practice midterms, but one practice final. Hard class, but she makes it manageable and easy to understand if you practice/study.

She lectures and explain concepts well and covers practice problems in class so that people can ask questions. However, random functional groups that she goes over once in lecture appear on exams despite her not mentioning that they would reappear. Plus her tests were harder than the exams given to the professors taking place at the same time.
Have her as a sub while my professor was traveling. Her lectures are hilarious. Would have taken her section if I know she is that funny.

The class was fascinating and she was one of the best lecturers I've ever had-engaging, funny, and clear. However, the grading for certain things like projects + HW was absurd and she took away too many points for the most minor details, or take points and not clarify why. She wasn't very approachable, and answered questions like they're obvious.

-Good lecturer and explains content very well. 
-Tests do not reflect the majority of the material covered and some questions are ambiguous or misleading in nature. 
-Her grading rubrics used are very subjective for some problems. 
-Would recommend auditing her class and not enrolling it if you can.
Valerie is an awesome lecturer! Her homework is tough, but I loved how she taught the course content.

At first glance she seems nice, but she was complaining about how entitled the students were, calling them "little f%ckers"

During a group project, she suspected some students of using chegg but because they were teams of 4 ended up reporting all of them. Like 10% of the class was accused of cheating. All the cases ended up being dismissed

She's good. She doesn't follow a curve but will raise grade bounds accordingly (which is not curving to her). Exams almost exactly 1:1 the same as her practice exams. I will say she's not very good at answering questions in office hours but that's why the TAs are there.
She was a great lecturer. Made sure we understood past topics and anything new that she taught. Very straight forward and fair exams. Made lots of jokes, funny professor. Would def take her again.

I was super scared to take her but I will say she is a WONDERFUL lecturer. She explains things well and in such depth. The class is definitely so hard though - 've never gotten under an A in a chem class until her. However, its ochem and its going to be hard regardless. I still had to watch ochem tutor vids but her lectures were helpful nonetheless
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I came here to defend Schmidt a bit. I was terrified to end up with her because of the low reviews, but was pleasantly surprised. You got to remember ochem is HARD, so yes, the class is hard and the tests are hard. Schmidt is an amazing professor though- seriously, so good at teaching/explaining concepts. No curve though so you have to work for it.
WOSRT PROFESSOR AT UCSD
A disgrace to UCSD

This class made me hate organic chemistry so much that I applied to law school instead of med school. Way to ruin other people's dreams, all for the sake of some esoteric belief in not curving. FORSHAME!!!!

Sometimes she seemed very approachable- she changed the way she did Sapling just because I asked. But when I came to her office hours she seemed annoyed and kept telling me that she already went over everything in lecture. She puts a lot of effort into simplifying notes but this also means I didn't understand the material as well as I could've.

Do not take her; she claims to be approachable during lecture, however, when you actually try to ask questions, she shuts you down. She was very deceiving and gave us stuff on the midterms that were BARELY covered. She baby fed us and expected us to eat steak during exams. So many people didn't pass her class, she was WAY TOO HARD for a quarter.

Took her expecting an easier quarter than the one with Hoeger but was completely pummeled by the midterms and final. I studied for over 12 hours the day before the final and felt what nonconsensual sex feels like basically. All with no curve. I feel so cheated because if I put in this much work with other profs I would have done fine.

Schmidt is one of the best professors I have had. Everyone is mad that she does not curve, but she establishes that fact on the first day of class and in her syllabus. She is very specific about what she expects and what is going to be on her exams. She really cares about her students and provides lots of opportunities to ask questions and practice

Professor claims to care about students, but as soon as the average grade in the class falls to a C, due to her own poor gauging of exam difficulty, she refuses to curve, resulting in a class that will tank any students GPA. Don't take her!

Minimal extra credit, you'll need a lot more than a couple points to get a good grade. Gives you lots of practice and weekly worksheets that trick you into thinking you understand the material. Mechanism heavy and the exams worsen throughout the quarter. Will not curve and undermine you for asking questions. Hard pass. CAPES did us dirty.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very good professor. Despite what many say the midterms and final were very simple. As long as you look at the slides (which she does for us) and the practice problems (which are many and have keys) it is not difficult at all to pass this class. She is a very interesting prof and is clearly very caring about her students.

Received a raw score of 92% and got an A! She is a very fair grader and is clear with her expectations. I thoroughly enjoyed her lectures and approach to the class! Very lucky to have such a sought out professor. Would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: take this class if you want to experience one of the hardest subjects in college (ochem) with NO curve! honestly was disappointed by the way prof schmidt made it seem as if an A in the class was attainable, when in reality it turned out to be nearly impossible. wouldnt recommend this class unfortunately, though I came into it with high expectations
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Class makes you work too hard for a grade you don't want
If you value your health and grade. DO NOT TAKE HER AND THIS CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I am at a loss for words, I feel so betrayed, so lost, and so alone And thank you professor for lying to us, for telling us that our hard work would pay off, that there was light at the end of that rainbow, For I have looked Hell in it's eyes, and seen a class without a curve, and an average grade of a C

Prof Schmidt is a great person and engaging lecturer - however, her exams were EXTREMELY DIFFICULT, and there is NO curve at the end. She offers a few points of extra credit, but this is likely not going to be enough to improve your grade significantly. Expect to put in lots and lots of effort into this class, but probably still end up with a C/B.
JUST NO
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst class ever! NO curve and exams were ridiculous hard for a no curve class. She talked a lot about believing in students but pulled a hard test with no curve. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH VALERIE
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I feel so cheated by this class. Like I learnt the concepts, I studied hard, I did all my homework, I did about as well as everyone else on the finals. And I got a C. Lesson learned, the CAPE is a lie.
Good prof, hard tests, no curves I repeat, no curves, no curves Seriously, I should have just taken Hoeger

I really never seen an ochem professor not curve at ALL. I worked my butt off (keep in mind I have like a 3.8) and even I couldnt get an a in this class. Whoever says she was easy and fair probably didnt take her this winter; because exams were FAR harder than any practice question ever seen. U need a high b/low a on exams to even consider an a

I wouldnt take this class again tbh. I worked so hard for it and everytime shed bring a question that wasnt expected, and you mess up your grade. The average was very low on the 2nd midterm, yet she brought a very hard final, and she doesnt even curve it!!

Shes really nice, but Chem 40B with her was extremely hard this quarter (Winter 19) & there are NO curves. You basically have to get very high uncurved scores on all the exams to even get an A-. Shes a great professor but I dont know whether I would take her again due to the grading scale. I have never put so much work into a class for a B+.

40B is hard. No way around it. There are so many mechanisms to memorize, but Schmidt makes lectures fun and entertaining. She gives plenty of clickers for credit. The exams are tough because of the nature of the class, but I think Schmidt does her part in teaching. The rest comes down to your own studying. Good luck to all.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Pretty good lectures, but class is uncurved. Tests this quarter were very difficult (particularly final and midterm 2). Some extra credit, clickers, mandatory discussion worksheets and sapling homework. Provides lots of practice problems, but test problems tend to be more difficult. Don't forget to study naming compounds.

Dr. Schmidt is a great professor and an excellent lecturer. Although o chem is extremely hard, she makes it as simple as it can be. She only tests on what's on her slides, so you don't even need the textbook. Very fair grading and extra credit to be earned. Lots of practice provided and resources for success. Very fun and caring professor! <3

Came into this class not doing so hot with 40A & honestly insecure. But, she makes her expectations and the required material VERY clear & straight forward. All material you need to know for the exams are on her slides, discus. worksheets, and prax exams. Prax exams are highly reflective of her exams. Study hard & consistently, & DO extra credit!!

Dr. Schmidt is hands-down the best professor I have taken so far. She's enthusiastic, articulate, organized, and most of all more than happy to answer your questions. There are no curves, but this only pushes you to work harder, really. She really nicely broke down 40B into sustainable chunks and never failed to make me chuckle in lecture.

She's really nice and she really cares about her students. 40B is said to be harder due to plethora of new mechanisms but explained every mechanism throughly. Everything that she assigns is doable and works to your benefit.

Probably the best Ochem prof ever. SUPER NICE, lots of ways to earn points in her classes, and she rewards those who work hard to learn the material. Lots of practice exams so you know exactly what to expect on her midterms and final. Her lectures are great and easy to understand, and she explains things very well. Don't hesitate to take her class!

Take her. She makes Organic Chemistry II extremely bearable compared to other 40B profs. She's knowledgeable and explains concepts very well. She emphasizes key points that will directly appear on the exams. Her practice exams are VERY representative of actual exams. Clickers, sapling, and discussion worksheets are easy points. 2 midterms 1 final.

Professor Schmidt truly cares about her students and I highly recommend her for organic chemistry. She rewards students for improvement over the quarter, provides extra credit opportunities, and gives out lots of practice exams.

Nice, very clear and fairly entertaining lecturer.  She made the hardest course in the ochem series accessible, and she was very clear about what she expected on the exams.  She covers an insane amount of material, but you need it all if you are taking the next class in the series, or need to learn it for MCAT anyway. TAKE HER OCHEM CLASS!!!

I highly recommend Professor Valerie's organic chemistry. CHEM 140B is said to be the toughest  in the whole series because of abunch of new reactions and long mechanisms to remember. However, her grading criteria is quite comprehensive consisting of  homework, attendance, discussion and exams, which makes it easier to get points than merely exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Schmidt excelled in her first quarter teaching organic chemistry. Lectures were clear and concise, and the exams were based entirely on what was covered in lecture. Homework and section worksheets weren't difficult, and the exams were challenging but fair. Doesn't grade on a curve, so be ready for that. Overall, a very solid professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I would highly recommend her. I don't understand the comment below me but she is a great teacher. Some people forget that this is college you won't get your grade handed down to you, you actually have to work for it and she makes you work for it. Her tests are exactly like the practice she's very straightforward with what you need to know.

She had informative lectures with periods of peer discussion, most of the work was 2 essays (min 1100 words), no tests. Policies are all the same as DOC 1. I didn't notice a difference in her teaching from DOC 1.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Idk why but Strom has a really bad rep, but lowkey is pretty chill if ur a good student. She can wander the room making sure phones are away and notebooks are out which is funny. TAs do all the grading so make sure yours is good (I've heard some horror stories about evil ones).

Just boring. Very hard to stay awake during the REQUIRED lectures. Take Solomon if possible, she's at least more fun to listen to. Lotta readings to do aswell. Grading for p8pers is determined by the TA, so you just gotta get lucky on that.

Honestly for DOC it doesn't matter which professor you take, how it fits into your schedule matters more. But I will say this teacher is probably the most strict of the three because you must be taking notes during her class.

Keep devices away until attendance question at end, don't talk while she is, and at least try to discuss content w/ partner when it's time - you won't have a problem in lecture. I found her lectures to be helpful in understanding readings, and readings are interesting if you're willing to engage w/ it. Midterm and final were writing on demand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super easy midterm and final. But she does tend to get very upset about minor things like side conversations during lecture and not taking notes. The DOC program also has a no tech policy, but lectures are podcasted.

Professor Strom is a great professor! However, DOC 1 is just so text heavy that it makes it difficult to fully enjoy the readings and the general course. She provides decent information on the texts and for midterm/final prep, but your grade mostly depends on your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very easy class, just the reading is annoying. Her lectures do cover enough of the information needed so you don't have to read closely; a light skim should be fine. Attendance for lectures and discussion sessions are mandatory. There is a no technology policy for the DOC program. She has gotten mad at people for being late or not taking notes.

Reading is not needed to get an A in this class; her lectures cover everything, and the exams are super easy. She can be stingy about students not having notebooks out to take notes, and electronic note-taking isn't allowed which is kinda dumb.

Dr. Strom is truly passionate about her topics. Some of reading materials are interesting for me. Because of the time limits, her lectures sometimes moved a bit quickly, but if you go to her office hour, she is definitely willing to help students to explain something more. I will take DOC 2 with her next quarter.

This course is required for all Marshall students. Very daunting before the midterm, but chills out after. Pay attention in lecture and have an idea of the readings and you'll generally know what to do for the assignments, midterm, and final. She is a bit blunt when speaking and often speeds through the end of lecture due to time.

One of the lecturers for the mandatory class series for all Marshall students at UCSD DoC. There's a no technology policy during class for the entire program no matter which DoC prof it is. Exams and work aren't that hard. Just do the readings and go to sections and lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great lecturer and is super passionate about the subject, but she is a bit cold and standoffish when speaking to her one-on-one. Your grade honestly depends on what TA you get, but the midterm and final are pretty straightforward, and they prep you the whole quarter for both. The bad part is that it's very anti-tech, and there is a LOT of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would say your entire grades depending on how strict your TA is. Strom is a great lecturer if you read the readings. Class is what you make of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is a great and strict lecturer, she would kick students out of the lecture hall if they are late for 5 minutes or take their phone out of their bag, however, she does this for people to focus on the course material. The grading is 100% based on your TA. Just join all the sections and go through all the readings, and you will get a fair score.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Fine lecturer. Not the most outwardly nice person, but good at teaching the course content. Hard on no technology/gen AI/cheating policies. Tended to rush the end of lecture due to lots of content and not enough time to go over it all. Will kick you out if you're later than 5 mins to class, sees you're not prepared for class, will call you out.

I enjoy DOC because of the professor. She is very passionate and doesn't tolerate any disrespect. Many of the complaints come from students who don't care enough to put in the effort in learning about the DOC series teachings. She isn't rude or condescending, she simply requires students to put in maximum effort and expects nothing less.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a very meh teacher- your grade relies heavily on TA's as they do all of the grading for the homework and the tests. I found Dr. Strom to be rude and not very approachable. I asked her a question one time and she cut me off and was very snappy. Overall, she's fine, but can be very rude if you have your phone out or come late to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: grade really depends on the ta. very anti-technology and will make people leave lecture for using phones or block them from entering after 10 mins. very repetitive and not very useful lectures. lots of research logs, research essay due week 8. research groups in discussion you have to sit with in lecture and do a final magazine with. get a good ta

probably the best doc lecturer outside of solomon, although pretty boring. lectures are mandatory, readings are not so don't bother. picture and music of the day is questionable. be ready to think pair share often. grades really depend on the ta so try to get a good one. four 1500 word essays to write and some journal reflections
She's chill. You'll be fine just put in some effort. Grade depends on TA
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took Strom for DOC 1,2,3, grade will depend on how lucky you get with the TA, some are chill, others will nitpick points for the smallest of reasons. Lectures are repetitive and boring and Strom reinforces the no technology policy strictly. She even gets mad if you are reading a book for another class. Annoying but you know what to expect

The class is really easy but you cant take notes with a laptop and she will actually eat your soul if you have your phone out. Repetitive lectures, she repeats no electronics rule every day for 10 weeks. She'll tell you to leave if you come 10 min past the start of class. She's very rude when you ask questions, and the lectures are a waste of time.

I really like her and how she lectures! found her to be super clear and informed in what she is teaching which makes lectures super helpful; provides amazing breakdowns and input about the readings, as well as guides you through assignments. lectures are mandatory. the ofc the class heavily depends on which TA you get

Overall a good professor. Very strict about in-class participation so make sure you keep up with all the readings. She was often pulling students outside to give them a talking-to (mainly because they were breaking a rule, etc.). Lots of essay writing. Grades are decided by your TA. Section meets twice a week which is why this class is 6 units.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Took this class during fall quarter and Dr. Strom was great! She was can be outspoken a times when interrupted but I never had an issue with that. Definitely read the texts, TAs grade assignments, discussion is mandatory and make su to be prepared bc you will get called on. Recommend Strom and would definitely take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Overall mid... there is a lot of reading and mini papers due every week, professor claims she is open to questions but then replies to them dismissively/curt. One good thing is so long as you meet the paper rubric you get full points
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
The lectures are the same for all of the DOC 1 professors. She is very passionate about the class, but your grade is 100% determined by your TA. Discussions are mandatory (both lecture and discussions), and weekly papers are due on Fridays (fairly straightforward). 

Be prepared to read a LOT.

Strom is a great professor, she's just kind of annoying when it comes to attendance but its understandable, this class is very skipabble. the class itself revolved mostly around your ta so if your ta is chill then you'll be fine. lots of reading but i never did it and still did well. no exams and assignments are extremely light just tedious.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She was strict about attendance requirements (showing up late and lecture engagement questions) and can be blunt but is a very good lecturer. Her lecture was the one I felt most engaged in this quarter. All assignments are graded based on TAs. Be sure to focus on formatting of assignments. Readings can be confusing but get discussed in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Only 100 points in the class so try on everything. Grade matters on TA. Attendance is mandatory. She explains the readings we have to which really helps understand the material better. All DOC professors have same homework so it doesn't matter which you get, it's all on the TA for your grade. Lecture is really boring sometimes though. But she alr.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Strom is very nice and shows deep care regarding the lecture content and students. She basically gives you all that you need to do the weekly writing assignment and everything is outlined clearly. I am taking her for DOC2 because I liked her as a professor this quarter. Just do the required readings, pay attention, and you're set.

I really enjoyed the DOC course! I didn't find her class boring. i thought she was good at lecturing and explaining the readings. The coursework is relatively easy. that being said, all doc lecturers are pretty much the same. your TA is what really determines whether you do well or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Strom was a nice professor, tried to make the material interesting and the class interactive. Plays music and shows nature pics submitted by the class before every lecture. Kinda treats students like kindergarteners though and really hates talking. She made the time to learn some of our names which was great. Overall a good choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Seriously I would say after finishing all 3 classes of DOC, the main takeaway from her DOC series was her PLAYLIST. The songs were pretty great, but her class was extremely boring.

lectures are not very insightful. felt like I was in elementary school or something by the way she talked to us students. still an easy A tho, so can't complain too much. id just take one of the other profs if I could so lecture is less painful as attendance turned mandatory.

DOC itself is a very easy class. Megan Strom, however, I was not a big fan of and I had her for all three DOCs (not by choice). Her lectures rarely add insight to the content, and lectures are mandatory (there are lecture cards that are randomly assigned in a few lectures).
Excessive writing, boring lectures, unnecessary work, you can get A+ without even reading a single text, its just mindless writing, and grades depends on the TAs

Graded based on completion, but on a scale of all or nothing. So missing slightly on your assignments leads to a zero. Due to the strike, everyone receives a blank automatically. The class did no have any plan to allow the class to continue during the strike, yet students are still required to finish the assigned work. 108 out of 128 for a D.

DOC overall is a really easy course and like others I don't think your lecturer determines much. Strom overall is pretty good but she does spend a lot of time talking about how to approach the course as opposed to the actual course material. Either way if you read you will be just fine. Lectures also aren't completely necessary, mostly readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had Strom for DOC 1/2/3. Personally, I think she is a good professor for DOC 1 and 2 but not 3. Her lectures were great for 1 & 2, they were straightforward and concise. However, her lectures for 3 were not helpful and a waste of time. Your grade also depends on the TA a lot and because my TA for 3 was bad, my grade suffered.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: The professor you get does not determine much in my opinion. My roommates and I had different lecturers and our experiences did not differ much. It really comes down to your TA and meeting all the criteria for the grade you want. My recommendation is take the course that works best for your schedule, not based of the lecturer, bc they're all good!

I had Strom for DOC 1 and DOC 2 and she was overall pretty good. There is daily reading which can be overwhelming to stay on top of but that is what you'll get with any DOC class. The grading for DOC is labor based so you definitely get out what you put in. Very helpful with providing resources for writing and solutions for any problems.

Dr. Strom goes out of her way to get to know her students in lectures and try to make personal connections. At times the lectures can get boring, but they are for the most part informative. A bit of a weird grading system but it seems to be favorable for students.

I only got a B because I turned in the wrong paper for one of the assignments. Because of the grading system, that pulls down my grade a whole letter. Otherwise, class is easy.... just don't be dumb like me

Strom as a professor is a great, and she is clearly knowledgeable and well versed in her studies. However, her lectures can at times be a bit boring, and I personally found it difficult to remain engaged. She likes incorporating interactive resources throughout lecture, where she'll submit a prompt, you answer it, and there'll be a discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Strom is a good professor. She's quite a boring lecturer, but is knowledgeable; if you actually listen to what she says during lecture (which is hard to do sometimes) you can actually learn something. I didn't like the DOC sequence in general but Dr. Strom gives good feedback and made the class manageable. It doesn't matter what DOC Prof you ch
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Good prof, knows her stuff, just not terribly engaging. Grade all depends on TAs in DOC anyway, so prof choice doesn't affect too much, but watch out for lecture cards!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very boring and ridiculously strict about technology. Not very interesting lectures but easy A.

She knows what she's doing and her lectures are very clear and to the point, they are also mandatory. DIscussion is also mandatory and participation is important as well as attendance. A lot of readings but paper prompts are relatively simple and easy to comprehend and write a decent paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Grade depends on TA, but as a lecturer Strom is clear and interesting. Reminds you of homework and reading every week and does a great job reinforcing the main ideas of the articles/chapters you were supposed to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Prof. was very nice, but the material/topic of this class was really hard & conceptual. Lectures moved way too fast to digest any info. So many proofs in lecture and on HW. Refresh your MATLAB skills for HW. Practice exams helped A LOT. Fair exams. Bonus optional project for 5% extra credit. If anything just avoid MATH175 in general

Homework are light to decent amount, but they prepare for tests well. Also give practice tests before both midterm and final which reflects format well. There are questions in midterm and final that are not easy, but only a very small portion. In addition, MATLAB code writing is not in tests.
Professor Tian is very caring and always kind when answering students' questions. Make sure you do the homework, discussion worksheets, and practice exams and you'll be fine.

She is open for questions during class and very chill. also she does extra credit if you do a presentation on a certain chapter in class which helps to keep the class more engaged especially since its a math class.

Very nice. Listens to student's advices (only put HW on gradescope in beginning, but put it on canvas either later) and also rearrange canvas to make to clearer for students. HW are light, yet thought provoking. However, it contains coding in MATLAB, so definitely work harder in beginning if have no experience of it before.

Good lecturer and a very nice person too. Allowed us to drop some exams and quizzes. Very straightforward and discusses concepts in great detail. Just make sure you attend her lectures and all is fine
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There is lots of homework but its relatively easy and she uses and good discussion forum so students and teachers can help each other. Quizzes and exams are difficult but she grades your work fir credit and drops a few grades from quizzes and exams t the end of the semester. Great class and great professor.

Really good professor ! Knowledgably, professional, and loves teaching for sure. He is accessible outside of class and really understanding. Makes participation really easy because even if you're wrong, he'll say "I understand why you said that because ...." Encourages participation. Would definitely recommend him !!
Lectures can be a bit slow at times but Professor Tronzo is very knowledgeable and approachable. Assigns 3 papers with fun and interesting prompts.

knowledgable professor....i feel like he knows so much that he gives off "secret society" vibes....excellent/interesting readings... tip: review the reading sizes prior to attending class bc he assigns readings by volunteer method, so be smart and pick the shortest reading, raise your hand first lol!

I really enjoy his class. I do have a lot of interest in Christian art but he just made the learning experience more enjoyable. I also really like the essay topic he assigned: the prompt he assigned is very broad and we can basically write about any perspective that we are interested. He is a wonderful professor.

I think it kinda depends on your TA how easy it is. There's only a few papers with a bunch of super short journals in between. He's a great guy and very likable, though his lectures can be a bit boring. He doesn't assign much reading and I didn't do much of what he did assign and still got an A. He doesn't podcast.

His CAT class was very easy. Only consisted of one essay and weekly journal entries that are extremely easy. I stopped going to lectures on week 2 and they are not mandatory. However, the discussion are mandatory. By far the easiest CAT 1 prof and a good choice if you don't want a lot of work.

Professor Tronzo is super nice and really smart but his lectures (not mandatory) were very boring. They were however, helpful for getting a few explanations of the weeks concepts for the journals. Grading depends on your TA for your discussion which is mandatory. This class isnt a lot of work but depending on your TA it can require more effort.
