Prof Tronzo's CAT class was very easygoing. Lectures (not mandatory) were useful for journal entries but also boring. If you want to pay attention to lecture, do not sit in the back, it's hard to hear him. Overall, your grade depends on your TA's grading standards because I've noticed that they seem to differ from each section(mandatory).

He is nice and patient. The workload for his CAT 1 is not heavy. There are only one final essay and journal entries, and he reduced 9 journal entries to 5. His lecture is okay and can really learn stuff, but his monotone voice makes me sleepy. Take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very caring and knowledgeable. He wants the best for his student. He cares more about students learning than "testing them". Taking his class, I have been surprised that I actually want to listen and learn because its a boring subject for me personally. However, he made the class fun. I recommend him 100 percent.

I had Tronzo for Culture, Art, and Technology 1. The focus of the class was the history of art. His lectures primarily consist of him talking in a monotone voice while showing slides of the art he is talking about. I would probably skip those, or you're going to fall asleep. Discussion sections are mandatory and the papers are easy.

I would recommend prof Tronzo 100%. Class is based upon three essays, all of which are pretty straightforward. The focus of this class is the bible which was a very boring subject, mainly because i'm not interested in it and I just took this class for an UD credit. Half the class doesn't show up because he doesn't take attendance. Take Prof Tronzo!

Tronzo is definitely a clear lecturer. Although the syllabus says that lecture is mandatory, about 90% of the class doesn't even go, probably because he podcasts (or mainly bc the subject is boring tbh). Grade is made up of 3, straightforward 4 paged essays; depends on mystery TAs bc no discussion. Perfect class to fulfill a GE, just very dull...

Professor Tronzo is very knowledgeable, approachable, and kind! He really knows this topic (medieval art) and understands that not everybody does so he explains things fully. 2 midterm essays 3-4 pages and 1 final essay 3-4 pages due anytime between the time he sends the prompt to the final day. I definitely recommend prof Tronzo!!

Professor Tronzo is great! His lectures are very clear and he reviews the material in a way that is easy to understand. The class is based on 3 essays, all of which are very straight forward and are based on your own interpretation of the prompt. Definitely take Tronzo, he is awesome.

Avoid at all costs. He is a very slow grader and it is hard to get a response outside of class. Extremely disorganized, disrespectful. I only took it because there were no other options, but if you have a choice, I would go with someone else. He says he cares about student success but clearly does not.
Really great professor and clear. Excellent materials. Only wish he taught more classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Genetics course- FYI - Dr. Wong is cordial but he does not grade assignments in a timely manner. It is Finals week and he hasn't even graded the midterm or any assignments from the past 7 weeks.Too late to know what you need to score on the final or improve,because there is nothing left to work on- no feedback.I have an A based off 3 weeks of work.

The structure of the class is interesting because Dr. Barbaro makes the lectures while Dr. Wong is the one who grades all work and handles all questions regarding the class. Dr. Wong was responsive and offered good feedback. He responded to emails promptly and was a very fair and reasonable grader. He offered good explanations to material questions
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took online Biochem w/ Professor Uranga, would highly recommend!
Responsive professor with straightforward syllabus and a willingness to accomodate personal situations that impact coursework.

Prof. Uranga was very helpful and was accessible during the day for office hours. Her feedback is very straightforward and she is very passionate about biochem. I do want to say, you have to put in the work for an A as exams are not just content based. The lectures are pre-recorded by someone else and the practice problems are nothing like the hw.

The one thing I really did not like were the discussions + 2 responses to your peers (14 pts), as she had a specific way to do them. You had to cite EVERYTHING, even the stuff you knew from before because the info had to come from somewhere. Homework is timed (8 q's, 25 mins) but is helpful for exams (35 q's, 90 mins). APPLICATION Q's NOT CONTENT.

I took biochemistry with Prof Uranga via UCSD Extended Studies. I loved how she was so enthusiastic about what she was teaching and related it to real life examples as to why it was important. Her expectations are clear, she gives extra credit. Would recommend!

She was one of the greatest professors I have had. I reached out to her regularly on things I struggled with and she was always very responsive and understanding. She helps you understand the content through connecting it to real life. Plus she has a great voice so you'll like listening to her. If you want another chance with Biochem, take her.
Dr Uranga responded quickly to messages. Gave feedback on discussions and why points were taken. This course weighs the three exams heavily. If you have test anxiety it is a difficult course.

Dr. Uranga was a phenomenal professor for Biochemistry! It is very obvious that she cares about her students in every aspect, whether that be their wellbeing, their progress in her class, or their general life success. She is always willing to help and is extremely reachable over Canvas. I would 100% take one of her classes again.

I had Dr. Uranga for BIOL 40145 course this Fall.  She was a great teacher, very kind and approachable.  Although class was online, she gave encouraging feedback on homework and helped me to cite research correctly.  The lectures taught by Dr. Barbaro are pretty dense since he really knows his science, but quizzes are fair and opportunity for EC.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She doesn't give any of the lectures herself and the quizzes are written for her, she is only a glorified "grader" and she is the worst and rudest person I've ever met. She regularly failed students on papers and gave no rational explanation as to why, except her big ego. If you value your GPA, you'll take a different person for Biochemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Luckily there are many other instructors for this class because Uranga's horrible attitude, ridiculous grading, and refusal to meet you halfway on assignments is a dumpster fire. Keep in mind, as someone mentioned, the lectures in the course are given by someone else, the only "power" Uranga has is to consistently fail ppl on written assignments.

I love the field of biochem and was a straight A student in all of my courses. Until I met this awful professor at UCSD. Mostly written assignments and she often gives 0 POINTS or grades VERY harshly, especially for an online class. She falsely accused several students of cheating simply because their citations were incorrect. Trust me STAY AWAY!
Really funny guy, also put labs and assignments up early for this offering.

All the assignments were online so we could complete the assignments early. He puts online quizzes with a code for our participation points. Very chill professor and understanding with deadlines. Would reccommend!

Great prof. Very caring, funny guy and not too many assignments. Class felt a bit unorganized, but his leniency and everything else made up for it. Assignments were easy and the grading was incredibly lenient (didn't think I'd get an A+). Take him if you can!!
Prof Mignozzetti was great! Don't buy the textbook. Lectures, assignments, lab, and final project were all straightforward and clear.
Overall a super nice guy, not a hard class if you pay attention and my TA was super helpful during lab times. Lab was just going over the weeks lab assignment, for sure recommend

This was the first time the professor taught this class in Julia so he wrote a lot of math on the whiteboards to explain what the coding was doing instead of having prepared slides so I got lost sometimes but he was very kind and patient and answered questions during and after class.  There were technical issues due to how new Julia is.

This professor cares about his students and will go out of his way to help you if you just ask.  He doesn't want to see anyone struggle.  The lectures and homework were very straightforward and easy to do.  I don't understand the negative reviews, he was wonderful.
Great professor, don't know what's with the bad reviews.

Don't trust low ratings. He may lack organization and might feel like he assumes you know things, but he'll explain things patiently if you let him know you need help. One of the smartest at the department. Every office hour session he generates at least 3 ideas for my research projects. would recommend for anyone serious in political science.

Prof. Umberto is honestly one of my favorites at UCSD. He makes an effort to cover tons of material but prioritizes understanding over getting through an entire lecture. He makes jokes but is also serious about the students succeeding in the class. If you go to class/lab/OH it's very easy to do well in the class. Don't be afraid of any bad reviews!

Professor M is a great teacher and is super caring about his students. If you went to office hours or contacted him outside of class, he was more than happy to help you through all the homework and make sure you understand. If you put in the effort and show up it will be a very easy class.
pretty sure this professor makes his own ratings lol

All the bad reviews were from people that didn't try in class. Prof M is amazing and cares about students. Grading was a bit confusing at first since he's new but students need to have patience. Prof M is great and I highly recommend him to beginners. Put in the effort and you will see results.

Prof Umberto is super laid back, taking his time to go through lectures; stopping to see if anyone had any questions. The classwork and final were all fairly easy. To be completely honest, I think most of the complaints are from people who never coded before in their life. They should have gone to office hours to learn how to code.
the grading for the coding assignments was very confusing. dont bother buying the textbook not necessary. attendance was mandatory.
The lectures had nothing to do with homework and other assignments. The final is extremely weird and changed multiple times. TAs are hard graders

Professor Mignozzetti is an AWESOME prof for CSS1. Understands that we are beginners in Python and rly takes his time explaining content. Super nice, funny & caring. Doesn't rush through anything and answers ALL questions. Grade is based off labs, practice problems and attendance. If you keep up w/ those & attend, you'll do great. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: CSS 1 is a class for beginners where we worked with python. He is new to UCSD and it took 2-3 for him to get used to the groove, but I have no complaints. He is very knowledgeable about different coding languages. He is very nice and kinda and funny. I would recommend him to others. Lecture attendance is required & he podcasts.

The lectures typically have nothing to do with our assignments, and the actual grading of our assignments is pretty confusing as well. I also ended up buying an I-clicker for no reason, as he told us they would be necessary, and then never ended up using them. Unsure why this is even a required poli sci class since it's just coding

The professor covers material in the lectures that are up to par with high school statistics plus it won't be what is covered in the homework/problem sets. This class is R (coding) heavy. The problem sets are all coding. TAs are the most confusing graders and grade based on what they think is right. The prof can also be very disorganized.
One of the best to do it in the game.

Was ridiculously hard to get in touch with outside of class. Would turn architecture into a political talk and ramble around random stuff. The class is graded off of 1 midterm and 1 final and there is no outline or rubric whatsoever. Avoid this class at all costs.
One of the best professors I've ever had. He talks a lot, but he's very sweet and understanding. Very inspirational and hardworking man.
Wish class was more focused. Very disorganized and disgruntled TA's. Final was a mess and had to report multiple times of group mates not participating yet nothing was done.

Extremely theory based class, more so poli sci w/sprinkling of vis arts ideas. Prof Cruz is VERY passionate and I respect him for this, though, this class was DISORGANIZED. TAs were awful and aggravating. Everyone I spoke to could not follow along w/lecture as prof would stop class every 30 min to complain about students not giving full attention.

i am currently taking his vis 100 for FA 25. Teddy himself is a nice guy and is extremely passionate about his field, but is not a great teacher. we are in week 8 now and every single person I have spoken to about this class has not learned a single thing. the class lacks proper structure and we aren't provided the tools we need to succeed :(

I took this class because I needed to fulfill an art requirement but Professor Cruz did such an amazing job at talking about the conflicts relating to the San Diego Tijuana border. You could really see how passionate he was about it and the lectures despite being during summer so 3 hours long were super interesting to listen to.

This was actually for VIS 102 but it wasn't an option to select. I don't get why he doesn't have better reviews, he is so passionate about what he teaches and about the success of his students. I'm not even an urban design major (im marine bio- took it for GE) but I was still able to succeed in this class.

Prof Cruz is passionate and kind, but this didn't always translate into a supportive learning experience. Having taken multiple classes with him, I've noticed that his TAs often focus more on enforcing structure than on supporting students. The grading was tough, and it often felt difficult to earn a strong grade despite putting in effort.

Professor Cruz is very passionate about Urban Ecology and made lectures very entertaining. I definitely learned a lot from the class and grew my interest in Urban Design/Architecture. Him and the TA were tough graders though, especially since the instructions for the final project were so vague/confusing.

Prof Cruz is remarkably inspirational. He has immense knowledge in architecture, and it shows in lectures. He tends to lack interaction with the students, but he is working on it! It is true that there is no indication of your grade throughout the quarter, but put in the work and he will see the effort and you will be okay:)
Teddy is so passionate! Love his lectures. Put in the work and you will get an A

He is very intelligent and passionate about architecture, but at week 8 we still have no indication of what our grades will be. Mandatory group projects and attendance. Difficult to take notes as he starts thoughts and never finishes them. He is an inspiring speaker and if this was only a seminar I would give a 5, but the class is very unstructured
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Has a genius-level mind with great compassion. An intellectual. Go to lectures, be engaged, ask questions and propose ideas. An extremely in demand academic in his field and so continue to try to get an appointment during office hours, those are conversations worth more than anything. Con: mandatory group projects

I think Teddy is a good instructor who works hard to engage students with course concepts. His time management could use improvement, but you can tell he is passionate about his work. Even if the specifics of his work aren't the most interesting to you, there are always valuable insights/ideas you can draw from his examples.

I'm sorry, but Professor Teddy Cruz is an Amazing ,  Deep ,  Passionate , Caring , professor and gentleman . I am discusted by the disrespect given here. I mean really???? There's something to learn from every thing in his lecture. Especially if it's about him. Look how far he has come in his life . Open your ears not mouths. And see the Empathy

This class is definitely one of the WORST classes I've taken at UCSD. DO NOT TAKE CLASS IF YOU HAVE TOMAS AS A TA. He was so pretentious, unwelcoming, and had a personal vendetta on bio majors. Teddy rambled a lot and I was hardly able to understand what projects were for. I lost total interest in class because of the staff's terrible behavior :(

Sometimes hard to make out what he is saying, but as others have said, your grade depends on your TA. 4 Assignments, almost counts as a production course, because it does take some outside time, along with some money, and show effort in your projects and go to office hours. Otherwise, he is an okay professor.

A really sweet guy. As days go by, you see more and more people facebooking because no one gets what he's talking about since he uses some extreme terminology to express his mind. Grading totally depends on TAs. Show effort and variety in your projects and attend all lectures and discussions, A guranteed!

He is a super sweet guy and I feel as though a lot of students are harsh on him because he is so passionate about topics pertaining to the border. It just happens to be his passion and he wishes to share it with all of us. Easy class, grading depends on TA, 4 assignments total.

He's super nice and very passionate about what he teaches which is why he is so respectable. Even though the material isn't the MOST interesting, I've found myself intrigued at some of the things he's showed us. You just have to be open minded about things, it's an art class. Overall, really nice guy, the class isn't that bad.
waste of time. pointless boring. all he talks about is tijuana and garbage. tas are on power trip and useless. worst class and porfessor in vis art dept.

OMG the worst class i have ever taken in my entire life.  pointless and boring to the point of extreme frustration.  apparently this class used to be different before Cruz took it but he made it an absolute joke.  the dept needs to change this requirement. it's a class on tijuana and maps, NOT artistically related at all.  TAs are pretentious.

the most articulate and inspiring professor on this campus. if you ever want to have your mind opened up and taken out of the classroom settings and into the world of architecture through san diego, this is your man.

Ok, so he is a nice guy, and I am sure he is a great urban planning professor. But this is visual arts, and he said nothing that had to do with art that couldn't be summed in half a lecture. He talks in circles (which being in vis arts, I am used to, but MAN this was tough). Don't have Susy as a TA. She is an attendance and notes Nazi.

is like vis 3. weekly projects decided by TA relating to a lecture topic then a portfolio.  cruz takes no part in what TA does. he just lectures about what artists did on global to site specific issues. he always talks about TJ. lecture is pointless but mandatory. depends on section. Dolissa is cool. do the work, try, make good portfolio, get A.

If you think you have waste your time in various classes in the past... you will be at a loss for words once you experience the immense pointlessness of this class.  Teddy seems to be a very nice person, but the general consensus amongst students that I spoke with was that nobody had a clue what he was saying.  IGUANA!

do not take him for VIS111 waste of your time since VIS111 is a req. class. Lecture is pointless and aimless!!!! he is speaking english but i cant understand what he's saying!!!! please do yourself a favor and dont take him!!!!!
His class could not be LESS related to Art. He is obsessed with the border issue and that is all he talks about. But the class is easy (no readings, no tests) because it is TOTALLY POINTLESS!

This is the most boring class I have ever had in my whole life.  He repeats himself over and over in lecture and trys to sound real intellectual and makes up words offten... his class is totally jumbled up and makes less and less sense every week... he may be good at architecture but for sure cant relate it to art well... don't take it!

He is lively extremely approachable and the best higher education has to offer. He is very interested in helping you to think about, work with and ultimately explore class topics instead of testing your ability to regurgitate facts or jump through the traditional academic hoops. As a facilitator he wants you to be inspired by whatever aspect of the class material interests you. 1 creative journal and 8-10pg paper.

Prof Manor is one of the best professors at UCSD. He's very passionate and clear about what he's teaching and his research is groundbreaking; he discusses it during lecture to apply the cellular theory we learn to real diseases. Tests are very fair if you study and grading scheme was very generous. He cares about students and wants you to do well

Good professor, lenient grading, no hw/assignments. Good grade achievable by studying study guides alone, and most exam questions are active recall and very surface level. Exams have buffer questions (5 for midterms and 10 for final). Participation points acquired by either answering questions or making ppt presentations on provided articles.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Manor is truly one of my favorite professors so far at UCSD. I enjoyed his lectures so much and his class has made me love Cell Bio. The material is very hard and dense but if you put a lot of effort into learning it, you will be able to succeed. He doesn't try to trick you, provides excellent practice problems, and takes time to review.

Despite what anyone else says, his lectures as extremely fascinating! I truly enjoyed them. Prof, is approachable and has a welcoming demeanor, always willing to stay if anyone has questions. The material is dense and comes with the territory of being a bio major, so for that you should be already warned, he offers so many ec and buffers! Take him!

Cell bio is hard in itself, so lectures will be dense and long. However, he makes it clear what needs to be known on exams. Super fast grading, and accommodated for commuter students by offering hybrid option over zoom. Offers buffer questions on midterms and final, so an 40/50 on the final still counts as 100%.

Cell bio is such a hard class but he makes it easier for you. There are two midterms and then final exam. Exams are pretty fair and based on his lectures. Attendance is not mandatory but it's better to have it to secure the grade. Overall. He is very nice and I enjoyed taking this class with him.

He is okay, not really the best at teaching would often have to rewatch lectures because he would talk way too fast to even take notes exams were fair but the amount of content in this course is insane you definitely need to study for hours. Participation was not explained well it sounded like it was optional but you def need it to get a good grade

his tests were easy, but very monotone during lecture, to me he seems like he'd rather be doing research full time than teaching. often ended lectures early but would have to send out emails re-explaining things he did not properly go over, i would rather have the full lecture time be used so students get correct lecture info

Cell Bio is info dense and it can be overwhelming, but the exams are representative of the material taught in class. Extremely lenient on the midterms and final. Option of in-class participation for points or video presentations. Disorganized at first yes, but I wouldn't give him a lower rating over it since it was resolved within reasonable time.

I can tell that he is very passionate about his research, but I can't say he is the best at teaching... Lectures were extremely dense, and the class was overall disorganized. Also can't really take notes in class because he speeds through the slides. Exams are fair as long as you study, but be prepared to teach yourself most of the material.

He wants his students to do well. exams r mcq & as long as you know some of the material u can get thru w process of elimination which i appreciate. His slides are dense, sometimes i get confused on the topic that certain details go under, but the study guides help so much. was disorganized w attendence at first but cares & listens to the students

This professor couldn't make up his mind on what should count for attendance, moved half the class to online zoom, his entire canvas page is run through just the "files" tab (no modules), and during the first midterm it took him like 25 minutes to pass out exams. His exams were probably written by AI but they were very easy.
great professor! awesome researcher! get ready to study study study but his lectures are amazing and organized, and contain all you need to get a great score

Cell bio itself is a difficult course because its mostly memorization but he explains everything in lecture to the extent that you need to know for exams and relates everything to real life scenarios. Is very kind to students and is always open and ready for questions. Great class overall!

genuinely cares about students success, always making time for questions! his enthusiasm for research and discovery is very radiant, and he encourage critical thinking rather than just memorization. lectures are very interesting and informative

I had an incredible experience in Dr. Manor's cell bio class. His passion for the subject is truly inspiring, and he has a unique ability to break down complex concepts into clear, understandable explanations. Lectures were always well-organized, engaging, and full of real-world applications that made the material feel relevant and exciting.

professor manor has really made me interested in cell bio! tests are multiple choice and very straight forward as long as you study content on the slides and pay attention to what he emphasizes during lecture. attendance is not mandatory for lecture and discussion, but i highly recommend going to them since you can earn participation points!

Dr. Manor is a friendly and amazing. There are two midterms and a final (both all multiple choice!). The exam questions were straight forward as long as you study! Attendance isn't mandatory but you can get participation points. His grading scale is very generous. Tough contents but he made it really easy to understand! take him if you can

Dr.Manor was very friendly and his exams were very reasonable. The class consisted of 2 midterms and a final, and 10% were for participation. The participation could be done via attending class/discussions and participating or submitting presentations about papers. He allows you to drop one midterm and make the other worth more if you did bad

I believe this is Dr. Manor's first time teaching this course and all I can say is that he is amazing. Great explanations of course material and clear expectations for his students. Every lecture was recorded and podcasted. He is truly understanding and loves teaching. Take him if you can!
Super easy class that takes about an hour a week. I felt that the professor did not have much of an impact on my learning in this course, but he made the course very easy.

This class is remote, so from the videos, he seems chill I guess. I know a lot of people complain about the journals. The strat that helped me get an A is just to write 150-200 words on summarizing the vids and the other 200 words on the lesson. Make sure to explicitly say "the lesson i take away is..." or something like that. Super easy class.

The class is run exclusively by TAs it would seem, Gneezy could not even be bothered to send a single announcement himself. The percentile grading sucks, you won't get a grade based on your effort, which is ridiculous given that Gneezy doesn't appear to put in much effort himself. Very few assignments, if you miss even one you're cooked.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly the whole class was decently easy, although I find it ridiculous that he uses AI in grading as part of his course. On top of having to pay for a reskinned canvas. I received lower grades on average when graded by AI and it pushed my grade down. The final touch was that grades are based on percentile, so I went from a 93 to a B+.

The reflections were graded very harshly. It was very difficult to get full credit even if you read the lecture and watched the peer videos. The grading scheme is by percentile ranking in the class, not actual grades. My final grade was lower than the actual grade I should have received based on assignment grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class as everything is done asynchronously. You meet with your randomly selected partner each week to conduct a negotiation and they are usually quickly completed. Journal assignments every week analyzing other's videos and lessons you learned. What I didn't like was how we had to pay $45 for what is essentially a reskin of canvas.

Definitely an easy class. there are recorded lectures that i watch some of the time. every week you are paired with a classmate and you record yourselves on zoom doing a negotiation which is very easy and takes very little time(25%). after that you do a write up on 3 other negotiations(75%). its very easy and takes little work. definitely take it.

This is for 20B; accent makes content difficult but still comprehensible. Sections mandatory. Nothing special to say about him, he's an alright prof. Better watching Organic Chemistry first then go to lecture second.

The lectures were really important in understanding the material. The reviews for tests were good as well, and everything about this class was fair. Posted lecture notes, which were a good source of review.
The lecture pace is a bit fast but other than that the midterms and final difficulty was as expected

Good lectures but can be rushed at times. Not an unreasonable amount of homework. Tests are fair and very similar to the practice tests. Discussion section attendance is mandatory, but lectures are not.

The midterms and final were pretty fair based on the lecture content and given practice exams. I honestly stopped showing up to the lectures after the first midterm because it felt like he went over the content too fast. Homework problems were okay and the lowest HW grade gets dropped.

Went to lecture like twice. His lectures are a bit all over the place, not very helpful. Used YouTube instead. Tests are honestly easy, I just barely studied. Homework is reflective of exams. Practice tests are very reflective of exams, just uses different numbers. Probably one of the easier 20D professors by far.

Pros: provides the material/formulas to succeed in the class and homework preps you for exams. 1-sided cheat cheat for midterms; 2-sided for final. Cons: no proofs or intuition for formulas. The class was effectively plug and chug because "the formula works." I would've waited a quarter for a different prof if I knew it would be this way.
Disorganized lectures which are hard to understand, but fair exams.

Very disorganized lectures that were not that relevant for the actual homeworks/exams - searching up the concepts online felt more beneficial than watching lectures. Also really bad handwriting so had to spend unnecessary time trying to figure out what he was writing. Practice exams were very similar to exams though so difficulty wasn't too bad.

He is a good professor. The homework prepares you well for the exam and the practice exams are the same as the midterms/final. It is unfortunate that the grading is so slow but its because of budget cuts, not its not rly his fault. overall solid.
Very good professor, really knows his stuff. Grading is similar to all other 20 series classes. Sometimes he goes on lengthy explanations, but sums it up pretty well at the end. Overall good prof.

This guy is hilarious. Midterm and final were VERY reflective of the actual exams which made it easy to score highly on. Homework is challenging once you get passed midterm 1. He will call you out if you're loud in class (pretty funny imo). Only con is the grading took forever on midterm 2 but stuff happens
Tests were hard, lectures were boring.
he speaks really quickly but everything is posted on canvas and tests are super similar to material covered in class I took him for 20B and 20D and got an A in both classes.
Tests are easy. Overcomplicates and can be confusing at times

He gives clearly structured lectures and proofs are easy to understand. Exam questions looks pretty much like hw and textbook questions so as long as u understand how to do those questions u can do good. He's very nice and he's feedbacks are mostly helpful but sometimes still a little confusing

Dr. Strasser is such a caring, kind professor. She genuinely cares about what you say during lecture and wants you to succeed in her class. I recommend answering her questions during lecture and listening to what she presents you with. I would take her class 1000 times over. She is passionate and funny, which makes her lectures enjoyable.
She is so passionate about teaching this topic, it's inspiring. I absolutely love her lectures, and you need to participate. The readings were interesting.

Asynchronous lectures were easy to follow and in person (zoom) discussion was focused on the readings. The "textbook" was monograph style (focused on women+gender but covering a few different time periods/societies/religions) and served as a foundation for the more specialized documents. Strasser is invested in the topic and it really shows!
really amazing lecture experience. He will lead you step by step to study the steel bible with full of details.
amazing lecturer. made topics really easy to understand and hw was a good reflection of the topics covered in class

My favorite professor this quarter. Fantastic at explaining things in an engaging way. The class is super difficult but I had more fun than my other classes just bc he made it a great classroom experience. He gives zoom as an option but in person lecture is way better (he won't let you zone out. "Look here!" lol)

Uses analogies to make sophisticated concepts easier. Often refers back to what we learned at the beginning to remind us of the foundation. He's always willing to go back and re-explain. He's blunt, funny, and practical.

HW was tedious but it exposed us to every nuance that we could encounter so if you can do the HW, you can do the exams.

One time I got 0/20 points on an exam question simply because I had misinterpreted the assumptions needed to perform the calculations. When I asked for a regrade Professor Uang had a personal 1 on 1 session with me and let me explain my design. He realized that I knew what I was doing and ended up giving me 19/20 on that question :) Great guy.

Prof. Uang is an amazing professor. Lectures are never boring and he constantly shows real world photos of topics we learn in class. I wish I had taken more classes with him, he is the best teacher I've had at UCSD.

Best professor I've had in all of my SE undergrad career. Every thing he talks about in lecture is essential to your learning so going to class is a must. He's super nice and down to earth and his assignments and exams are representative of what we learn in class. He actually cares for his students' understanding and does a great job as a lecture.

He's by far the best professor I have had at UCSD! He's very engaging with his lectures and the way he goes about explaining concepts. Gives you real life examples and analogies that will really help you understand stuff. Very funny and very knowledgeable. Highly recommend him. I wish he'd taught most of the classes I took if not all.
Great guy. Well respected professor in his field. He is a pretty funny guy. A little hard to understand at times but I wish he would teach 140B next quarter.
He is hands down the professor I have ever had
He is AMAZING!

He is the best professor any engineer can ever ask for!!!! He is hella smart, and knows his stuff....and on top of that, he is funny. If you really want to learn, make sure you get him, specially for steel design class.

Steel with Uang, can't go wrong. 2nd time with professor and it was just as good at the first. 8-10 hours a week for HW (except for weeks before exams), so helpful, funny, best professor I've ever had.
He's a great professor who really made me interested in the material. He's also really clear and makes funny comments throughout class.

Uang is the bomb, teaches so enthusiastically that the material isn't bad. You'll be a pro at shear/moment/deflection diagrams after this class. Lots of work, expect 8-10 hours a week of homework. Took it during summer so workload was really heavy. He is great though, and I don't know anyone that does not like him. Tests represent HW/lecture.

I will admit, this professor has lectures that definitely hold your attention in class.  Going to class IS VERY HELPFUL.  And he does give you A ZILLION AMOUNT OF HOMEWORK PROBLEMS but I guess its worth because it allows for you to gain practice in learning the material.  However, the exams are somewhat tough but if you do your homework, it helps!!

Uang teaches clearly and completely explains every topic he covers. He is one of if not the best professor I have had at UCSD. Be prepared to work hard and gain a great understanding of the material. In 152 he taught both his half and Restrepo's half in 5 weeks.

He's a nice guy, but he gives a lot of homework on stuff that he does not cover in class, so you have to learn half of the stuff yourself.  He basiclly just teaches out of the textbook (he is one of the authors) by copying examples in class.  Exams are very representative of the homework but usually have a lot of problems in a little amout of time.

Adorable accent "Soooooooooo", "Thennnnnnnn" &, "I continue, I continue" are his favorite words and he says them in such cute way =) He is a great teacher, LOVES his job and CARES a lot for his students’ learning. Dr. Uang deserves a golden medal for being a great Professor. All Profs should take him as a role model.

"You follow, you follow?" is an expression he often asks.  Which means he's always concerned about your understanding.  He gives plenty of examples, and provides clear definitions, and is willing to answer any of your questions.  The homework is relevant to real life and the tests.  overall, I really like this guy a lot.
gotta love that black hole analogy for the moment distribution method.  it stuck in my head.  tests are long.  understand the hw and u'll do fine
No Comments

great professor! even though there were much to learn all in one quarter, he simplified the material A LOT during lecture. don't skip lectures, put in good amount of effort, and you will realize how easy this class really is. also, take his word for it: KNOW YOUR STATICS!

I was not his student, I was a TA for CHEM 109. He was rude the whole quarter, even though I tried my best to be a good TA to the students and Prof. Ulrich. I had my weaknesses but I tried to overcome them by arriving early to learn from the lab manager. Yet he did not acknowledge my hardwork. Its just better to take this lab with a nicer professor

Ulrich Muller is the worst professor I have had at UC San Diego. He refuses to record lectures and provide PowerPoint slides/notes. He scheduled a lecture for a non-lecture day because of a holiday and refused to record it for those who have other responsibilities, such as work. This class is so stressful because of the administration.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Muller was one of my favorite professors. His exams are representative of the lectures and he provides homework questions after each lecture to make sure you understand the content covered during lectures. The class had 5 midterms and 1 final exam (lowest dropped) and the exams were 20-30 mins. Cool professor and has the best art skills!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Worst teacher that I have had at UCSD. Lectures are very disorganized, jumps from one idea to the next, does not introduce anything, just announces a question and starts solving it on the chalkboard. Tests are not representative of the material he teaches and does not assign any homework. Make mistakes during lecture which made things confusing.

Worst professor I have EVER had at UCSD. Got an easy A in 6a, and halfway through this class dropped. Guess what: I got an A in 6b with another professor the next quarter, so I clearly actually knew the material. Unorganized class, lots of mistakes, bad lectures, and no homework or recomended problems mean you will learn nothing.

Worst experience of college so far. Was very encouraged by reviews and by everyone saying he was easy, but the only thing easy about him was that he didn't assign any graded homework (he gave out a max of 4 optional problems after lecture) and discussion was optional. I literally did not learn anything in this class. You will cry after the final...

He's a genuinely nice and funny man. The problem was that his lecture style was often confusing. He would pull out problems during lecture with no background information and explanation, which often confused us. His 2nd midterm and final were also pretty hard and had random questions that a lot of people were not expecting.

Tests were hard. This wouldn't have been an issue if he taught us the concepts well though. He taught the stuff before the first midterm pretty well. But during the acid base chapters and thermodynamics, he would write one thing after another without introductions or explanations. Just copied down stuff from his ref. sheet to the chalk board.

He is super inconsistent. The first midterm was really easy, second one had a 50% CURVED average, and the final was seemingly easier but I guess not since I got a grade way lower than expected. Too many mistakes and when he tries to correct them over mass email, I become more confused. I heard this class was an easy A but this quarter, it wasn't!!!

took class because of the reviews and easy curve. had a relatively good background in chemistry and studied hard for both midterms and  received an A- and ended up with a solid B in the class. Numerous mistakes on all homework, test, notes. Self-studying is necessary for the class, yet the mistakes made it impossible to understand. Don't recommend!

He's a funny guy from time to time but not that great of a teacher. His lectures are scripted and filled with mistakes. Good news is that most test questions come from stuff he has done in class. But he failed to captivate students, which I believe is essential to being a professor. So overall he's OK, not the best.

People recommended him as easy and the best chem 6b prof offered during the quarter but... his exams are actually pretty hard (second midterm's avg was 50 percent). there's also not that many resources to prepare for the exams because he doesn't use the textbook. He's brilliant and he knows what he's talking about but I wouldn't takehim again

took this class because it had good reviews. worst teacher ive ever had. not clear about what going to be on the tests. terrible lecturer, only writes on the chalkboard and doesnt explain anything. he emails you homework and makes mistakes on the answers all the time.

He makes cute stupid chemistry jokes which keeps the class awake. The tests were basically like the homework questions. Overall relatively easy class if you know how to do the homework and attend section.

Pretty cool professor, made lecture pretty enjoyable. He doesn't really teach concepts though, and focuses on the problem solving aspect of the course which can make things a little difficult at times. However there are no surprises on the midterms or final, questions come right from lecture. Class and discussion not mandatory but extremely useful
The tests are exactly like the homework and example problems from lecture.  Discussions aren't mandatory.  It's easy to fall behind, but rote memorization can get you an A.

Chalkboard usage for a 400 lecture forces students to fight for front seats. No graded homework or textbook usage, most material comes from another source. No quizzes either, and midterms resemble the homework. Final is much more difficult. Generous curve though! Focuses much more on the concepts. Good Luck!

Explains things clearly and his test are pretty straight forward.  Like how he wrote on the board and the nice curve that he gave so the class was very do able so long as you go to lecture and put some effort into it.  Would totally recommend him

I've taken three quarters of chem here at UCSD and Dr. Muller has been my favorite chem professor. He writes clear notes on the chalkboard and he's an interesting guy. HUGE curve on exams, so it's almost impossible to get a grade lower than a B. His German accent is a plus.

Muller is a good professor but he can be confusing at times. For me, he got worst as the quarter went on. Overall though not that bad of a professor so long as you go to discussion or work with friends. Not that hard to get an A or B in the class do to the huge curve and frq style exams.
He lectures using the board, no powerpoints, which was very helpful. His tests are clear and easy because he has a huge curve. One of the best chem teachers I've taken by far, I highly recommend him.
He's a great professor and does his best to make the lectures interesting and give examples that are relatable. There's also a huge curve, which is really nice.

He curves every test with the highest score. His curve was 80+% is an A for sure and i think 60-79% was a B range. not too sure. He has very generous curves. He assigns HW but not too much. His sections are not mandatory which is a plus. His practice midterms are very accurate to the actual midterms. But his final is a lot harder.

I like his chalkboard style compare to boring power point slides. In order to get set yourself in A range, you need to do 90 or above on the first one or second one, then do decent on Final. My year's final was pretty difficult, but his final is fair as long as you do practice test. I highly recommend him.

Dr.Muller is a good professor and teaches by writing on the blackboard instead of using boring powerpoints. He focuses a lot of the math part of the class. He talks about the conceptual part a little bit. He prepares you well for the midterms by posting practice midterms online. I recommend him, he is willing to help you if you ask.

He's a funny teacher &his class was pretty easy. He assigned hw but most of his test problems came from lecture. I read the book along with lecture &you can tell his lectures somewhat follow the book. The person below is wrong, the highest grade on the first midterm was around 40/46 not 40/100. Anything above a 60% was a B. I would take him again.

He's a funny guy, but does not teach out of the book..he makes up his own problems which have no relevance to the hw we do or the stuff from the textbook. Really hard to get an A in this class. From the final exam histogram, over 60% people got "C" grade overall...

As said before, ridiculously easy to get a B in the class without even trying because of the curve. You have to study to get an A, but it's definitely not impossible. Do well on the first midterm (with 90% range), and you should be set through the class without trying too hard on the final. He even lets you try to get points back during OH.

his grading is ridiculously easy. curves midterms somewhat generously. they are also the only free response ones out of all the 6b professors, which means you get partial credit.however, he is bad at lecturing, and gives out no practice exams.
easy B , impossible A unless you are hella smart

Insanely hard tests. first miderm highest grade was 40/100. He gives you no formulas or constants and no cheat sheet. Tests are all open ~6-8 q's up to 25pts each. No podcast. No lecture slides. This class requires a massive dedication of time. And he constantly corrects his in class notes after the fact via mass email. Very hard class.

Easy teacher, especially compared to the other chem 6b teachers. lectures are decent, hes a funny guy in his own way, but hes somewhat unhelpful when it comes to trying to help you study. tells you to do problems by yourself. also doesnt use the book very much. you wont be as satisfied with the teaching/course, but your GPA will thank you for him.
He is so awesome and funny. One time he drew a elephant and a German woman on the board.

He is a horrible teacher. He goes slow and tends to be confusing during his lectures. For the ideal gas law, he uses pascals to calculate instead of the standard atmospheres which the book follows and it gets even more confusing. If you can avoid this teacher, do it.  While he is an interesting character, he is just not suited to teach a class.
He is a good teacher, likes to draw. His way of teaching is different but easy to understand. You don't really have to read the book, but reading the chapter before coming to class is a plus.

He isn't clear when he explains things, and you can't even use the book to study on your own because he doesn't teach from it. He makes up his own questions which aren't typical of most chemistry classes, so that takes getting used to. He also expects you to know things that aren't required in prior chem classes. Don't take him unless you have to.

Ridiculously nice guy, and will go out of his way to help you out. Tests are very fair, and one of the only GenChem professors that actually do fill-in tests and NOT scantron, which is a TOTAL +. Go to office hours, get to know him, he's a powerful ally.

He's a good professor - solid in  his understanding of the theoretical and practical. He explains stuff very clearly and apply them to situations in his own lab. He might not be the most "interesting" professor, but you'll have a good learning experience if you go to class & put in as much effort as any other chem class. Heplful/available, too.
If you're not willing to learn the material on your own and completely rely on the curve for your grade then do not take him.
He's very nice. Just read the book!

SYN 1 was pretty easy, in class discussions, focuses on improving upon learning goals. 3 projects: 2 "essays" and a creative 3rd/final project. Attendance definitely matters, there is a midterm conference where you discuss your progress and a final conference where you discuss what grade you think you deserve and why. Easy A if you just do the work

Very empathetic and sweet professor. Gives great feedback and really cares about students. His lectures are a little boring, but they are brief. As long as you complete assignments and show up, you will get an A.

Didn't have for SYN 150; Had for SYN 1. Vega is a caring guy who wants the students to succeed in his class and only does things to try and help them. You can tell he enjoys discussing the material that he covers and gives great insight on how students can develop and communicate their ideas. Flexible grader who emphasizes process and learning.
Confusing assignments, and says that grades are openly discussed but can be changed the last day of class. Will still be strict on attendance regardless of emergencies.

The class consists of random writing assignments that culminate to the final project which is creating a hypothetical proposal with a group in the form of an essay + presentation. The grading system can be confusing but essentially you're graded on effort put into your work rather than entirely the content. Not the worst class to take

Amazing lecturer. Professor Villegas really cares about her students and is super accessible through email or office hours. DOC content is really interesting and overall course is pretty easy with two essays and a midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lwk the prof doesn't really matter, the TA you get is what really matters. Overall lecture was chill and she is nice and has a cool dog.
Best lecturer of the three. Depends who your TA is. Cool dog though

Overall DOC 1 was a pretty interesting class and Dr. Villegas was a great professor. The class involved a lot of reading (anywhere from 5-50 pages of reading per lecture) but very few assignments and in-class exams were fairly easy. Each assignment and exam had very clear rubrics and class wasn't difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Probably the nicest DOC professor. The class is pretty much the same despite which professor you pick, but I believe her tone of voice is less monotonous/boring in lectures. She also brings her cute little dog sometimes.

She's so woke it's annoying. She is uneducated about anything having to do with real life and doesn't understand anything to do with politics yet that is what she teaches she preaches about being inclusive but hates white people and doesn't accept religion would never want to take this class again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I LOVE PROF VILLEGAS! You can tell she's passionate about what she teaches, which is so inspirational. Her dog is the cutest ever which she brought to lecture a few times. Other DOC teachers yell at their students, but she's patient with usnot strict at all. Pls take Villegas if you want an stress-free doc class. Can't wait for next quarter w her.
Pretty chill lectures. Has a cool dog so thats pretty cool.

AMAZING PROFESSOR! Genuinely one of my best professors so far! The lectures and reading can get kind of heavy, but she is an amazing lecturer, asking for participation and always engaging with students. In case you get a bad TA, just explain Villegas what did they you dirty, and she'll fix it. Such a good teacher and will 100% take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I'd say Professor Villegas is the nicest of the 3 doc instructors. All doc teachers follow the same curriculum so basically same workload for any and TAs do all the grading. She's very sweet and doesn't call on people but lectures can get boring but I'd definitely choose her again.

She's so nice and chill. Wanted to take her for DOC 2, but she was the first to be picked by everyone else, too. She encourages participation, but it's not mandatory or forced. Very understanding and easy to talk to! Definitely the best choice of the doc teachers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super fun lecture and professor, midterm and essays had note sheets, we do read a lot though. Easy grader fun topics, computers allowed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Not a very hard class, but a very unorganized prof. If you're actually interested in the material, take a different prof. He canceled class often, and his course schedule was constantly changed. It was hard to understand where we were in the course, and what we had to do. However, exams and final project weren't too hard and his lectures are okay.

He really doesn't assign a lot of reading, especially for a history teacher, so I'd suggest taking his class when you need the credits during a quarter you plan on being busy. He gave us the exam prompts beforehand, so there weren't any surprises. He yells during lectures (not at students, but just to be heard)

Vitz was nice and his lectures were engaging. There was 4 discussions, 2 short quizzes/exams, 1 short writing assignment and a final. I found that the assigned readings and lectures were relevant to what was being tested and gave a lot of info. Assignments and tests were very straightforward and he gave detailed expectations nothing was surprising.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Highly recommend taking his class during the summer. I didn't spend too much time on homework or our midterm and final papers. Consisted of mainly films in which some are boring and others are entertaining. Disclaimer: I don't know how different this class is during the school year but save your time and take it during summer!! I got a 93%

Professor Vitz was the worst teacher I've had here at UCSD. I took a film class with him,and he didn't make any of the films accessible. We had to pay to watch some. When we rose this concern to him, he did nothing. The class also had a really low average, and he wouldn't relook at people's assignments when asked. Be prepared to regurgitate info.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Doesn't let students form their own opinions and forces his upon everybody. This environment does not facilitate learning, rather, it tires to force a way of thinking upon you. I am dissapointed that the UC system would hire someone like this

So far I am really loving this class. With online learning I usually dread having to participate through zoom, but the professor seems super caring so far and I am loving the material we are learning about. Hope the rest of the quarter continues to be engaging!

Professor is very knowledgeable about the history of Mexico and his lectures are engaging and informative. Class films were very interesting and easy to write about. He is such a great professor, easy/fair grader and overall such a sweetheart that cares about all students.

Matthew Vitz made class pass in no time he's great lecturer. He has key terms as his lecture outline and the notes that follow are at the students' discretion to write. This is important as his exams are on such key terms that will need to be explained through readings. He gives a study guide and it is easy to manage the work. Overall pay attention
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Vitz genuinely cares and is passionate about what he teaches. However, the lectures are sometimes irrelevant to the material you are required to learn and his lecture slides are not of great help. You have midterm exam, 3 reading reflections (1-2 pages), a short essay (5-6 pages), and a final essay (originally 9-10, reduced due to COVID)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof is honestly so caring and considerate. He uses his platform to discuss the environmental crisis that we are facing. Although the class includes a low of work, he genuinely just wants us to learn. He was especially thoughtful and understanding during finals week amongst the school situation occurring. He's the better prof to take for INTL 101

A horrible professor that doesn't care whether he is speaking about opinion or facts, he simply combines the two during lectures. He is a boring lecturer that makes multiple gaffes every class and rarely answers a question straight. Avoid taking this class, you will learn nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Vitz is amazing. He cares about the students and respects all opinions. I learned a lot and more important he made me think about many important aspects of environmental issues. We need more professors like him!

As much as I'd love to find the good in professor Vitz at UCSD, I simply cannot. He does not "lecture" he simply reads out of the articles and adds unnecessary pauses in his voice to make it sound educating. Papers require lecture citations but all uploaded power points are useless (they are just pictures & words with no context). Avoid taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor. I really enjoyed the course material, and he is clearly very knowledgeable about the topics.

Professor Vitz is extremely passionate about environmental justice and politics. His lectures and assigned readings are lengthy, but essential to do well on the papers. 10/10. Would definitely take another class with him.
a joke of a class but such a boring professor. Slowest speaker I've ever listened to
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Vitz is up there with the best professors I have taken at my time at UCSD.  For those who have very little knowledge about Latin American history, he is without a doubt the most qualified Instructor for an introduction.  Those who are familiar will find he has a lot to say that is not included in the traditional narrative. Great guy.

Prof Vitz is a very detailed, forgiving professor. The tests were just two essays, and he provides a lot of help for these essays when he does his review. After the midterm essay he went through exactly what was wrong with essays and what we should do. Material was extensive but we didn't have to memorize it just understand it enough for an essay.

Vitz is a great lecturer. Although the class was 1.5 hours, he made it really interesting, so time just flies. He is relatively an easy grader and detailed professor. He tends to lecture fast but if you ask questions he won't mind. Although he is not hispanic, he has a love and passion for Latin American studies, which makes his lectures great.

negative comments are too dramatic. sure, sometimes it was hard to follow lecture because some concepts are over complicated and convention is changed. homeworks were long and sometimes difficult too. but exams were fair and thats the most important part since its a large chunk of grade. attendance technically not mandatory but we have pop quizzes.

Genuinely drop the class if you get this guy. If there's a convention for something in math, and it is something that COULD be misinterpreted, you bet this professor is going to use something that ISN'T the convention. Furthermore, you can't even argue to justify a convention because they NEVER review your regrade requests.

The most recent rating is misleading, unless the reviewer isn't taking Math183 in W26. The prof has not posted a 5 pg hw the day before it was due. The quizzes are 1 easy q, and barely affects our grades (2.5% each). It is valid to not like a teaching style. I do not prefer this prof either, but it's not ok to share things that are simply not true.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Math 189 is tough to teach since it requires students to follow along in Jupyter Notebook, but many don't pay attention. He seems unhappy when no one responds, which i fell bad for him. I felt he tries his best, but the class would work better if taught with both lecture and lab, like CSE 15L. It's not his problem, but how the class was designed.

He is approachable and supportive. He gives extra credit for answering in class, and per the Fall 2024 syllabus, the final can replace your midterm grade, which really helps. He explains concepts clearly and is fair with grading. Sometimes he arrives a little late, but it's rare and understandable. If you attend lectures and study, you'll succeed.

Overcomplicated material, strict grader, tests are difficult, and unlike practice exams. Expect yourself to rewatch many lectures to understand the material and struggle in this class. I would NOT recommend taking this professor's course.
Professor Sid is the GOAT. His notes are amazing and clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Sid gave great lectures and reasonable tests.

Although he improved on posting the slides early and being on time, there's a huge issue on how he explains the topic. He over-complicates not only the topic, but also some questions that I asked him. He even answered questions in a condescending manner. Anytime I tried to ask him about a material, something doesn't feel right. No thank you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: just not a good dude. would crash out on us and sounded very condescending sounding during his office hours. Also a horrible lecturer and makes lectures mandatory. honestly steer awayyyyyy from this guy.

Easy A, but prof isn't worth it. He's the kind to ask the class questions and wait until someone answers correctly, not only wasting our time, but making the room awkward. The class is easy—few HWs, mandatory lec's, weekly summaries, and a group project with a vague rubric—he'll tell you to figure it out if you have any q's about his expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Even though his UCSD Set grade average is high (3.3), it doesn't correlate to him being a good teacher. That is simply from the curving of the grades as you can see his average stays similar throughout all the times he has taught this class. I assume he is a smart man but he absolutely cannot teach. Exams aren't like the homework. Take someone else
Class work bad

This guy is the most disorganized professor I have ever had in my 4 years at UCSD. He insists on posting lecture slides a day after the lecture so you can't follow along, posts the homework late so that you only have 2-3 days to complete it (of course his office hours are not on those days), confusing typos on assignments...0/10 do not recommend

I agree with the comments about class being hard to follow, but I will say he is the only professor that gave me an extension when I got really sick, so he cares about his students. He does teach the class in a very proof heavy way and you are expected to use concepts from the proof to apply to questions.

The issue with this professor is that he is an intelligent man, but because he is intelligent, he doesn't understand what his students need to learn from him. It's better to go to his office hours because you can ask direct questions, lecture does go fast , and people who took some stats/probability are doing better than others.

Everything was fine up until week 7ish, where I felt like I actually understood what he taught in class, but I kid you not when I say I have never felt more lost in class before. He rushed through the last few weeks; the textbook's bad, and he's teaching us how to merely solve a singular type of problem, not the concept itself.

Course was unorganized. Had to write 10 page long weekly summaries of what we learned. Does not post his jupyter notebooks. In week 7 he suddenly decided to disable podcast (but eventually still kept it because all the students were unhappy about that). Learned 0 thing during his class. If you have taken 181A-B then you should be fine.

He knows what he's talking about, and there were many lectures where I learned a lot. I feel, however, that during some lectures he focused a lot on theoretical concepts, not tying them to practical problems, and I found myself confused a lot as a result. If you don't understand concepts at first, you should ask him for clarification or examples.

This class is supposed to be a fun and useful class, but I did not learn anything at all. Grading is not consistent, as sometimes they will take away a lot of points for certain things. He makes lectures mandatory (10% of your grade), but they are very boring and he has a monotone voice, so I was not engaged in his lectures. I do not recommend.
Professor is very messy and late with class material, super hard to follow in lectures and mandatory attendance for grade
i dont like the style of teaching. few visuals and vague definition. have the feeling that he obfuscates material so learning isnt 'easy'

Severely frustrating. Material isn't difficult, BUT: syllabus is very vague, with no details on assignments. Lectures hyperfocus on technicals while missing relevant info, and felt transactional versus educational. Material is shared a week after it's covered if we're lucky (2wks late rn). A rare case of a course burdened by the one leading it.

The most disorganized and stressful professor ever. Graded and related things late, taught the class COMPLETELY differently from previous professors, & would make some homework require info from lecture the day before. 

On a positive note, he did seem to care about our feedback and made an effort to improve. It just wasn't enough for many.

Course started out rough but improved as he accommodated our feedback. For me, there was a lot of self-studying to supplement lecture material. His lectures try to help you build intuition but sometimes they are a bit unclear. Overall not a bad class and pretty manageable, and exams are pretty straightforward.

He was a little standoffish during lectures but super approachable and helpful during office hours. He said it was his first quarter teaching and you can tell he really cares about the students understanding the material, he made interactive apps to illustrate concepts. Definitely challenging for students who struggle with math but grading is fair

I agree with the other comments here and the course was SO much harder than previous quarters. But I actually really liked the lectures and HW, he tries to make the examples relatable. Midterm and quiz 1 were rough but he changed the grading scheme after student feedback. SUPER generous with final grades, almost 90% of the class got B- or above.

A pretty rough start at the beginning of the quarter, but honestly it got much better by the end. He listened to our feedback and accommodated by allowing cheatsheets, and also making the quizzes and exams much more inline with the lectures and homework.
Rough start to the term, not gonna lie. But hey, massive improvement after midterm. Really listened to us and fixed stuff. Homework and exam was more doable after midterm and lectures were more chill

I understand and partially agree with other comments. Bad things were said already, I will leave something nice about this course here. HWs are very helpful. He began to allow cheatsheet for tests after hearing students' feedback, which helped me a ton during the final -- the questions on the final exams are similar to what we saw in HW.

Makes the class so much harder than it needs to be; also he begins example problems during lectures but never finishes them or gives the solutions later so you basically have to learn how to do everything on your own. Quizzes were a lot harder than the homework, and he goes through material way too fast to understand

The worst professor I've ever had, he overcomplicates everything. The quizzes/tests are extremely hard, 50% class averages, the TAs said he has made this class unnecessarily hard compared to past sections. He NEVER gives examples, so lectures are watching him throw complicated equations up on the board and reading them out to you. Proof heavy.
concise explanations in lecture, heavy excel use,  tough grader but generous curve at the end.

Dr. Xiong was a good professor to have mainly if you put in a lot of the hard work. Some of the grading is a little harsh but as long as you are able to get ahead on the lab reports, you'll be solid. I recommend getting in touch with your TAs often and the quizzes were very easy and straightforward.

Prof had a very unclear grading scheme, TAs copy and paste a few things from spreadsheets we spend hours doing & grade that. Prof only cares about his research, and it shows. Even if you do all the work, your grade will not reflect it. Final exam was unclear, had typos, no practice. It's average was a 45% & final grades were posted 3 days late!

If you care about your grade and expect fair, transparent grading, avoid this class. The expectations are extremely unclear, yet points are heavily deducted for things that are never stated. It feels more like guessing what the grader wants than actually being evaluated on understanding.

This was a very frustrating and poorly managed class. One of my lab experiments produced incorrect results due to an organism degrading the sample, something the instructors themselves acknowledged. Despite this, my work was not regraded, and the low score significantly damaged my overall grade. Lectures were difficult to follow and unclear.

Very unclear. Was very disconnected from the lab reports, spreadsheets, and TAs. Grading and rubrics were inconsistent. We were not given direction in our feedback for our calculations so we didn't know where we went wrong or how to improve. Lecture was messy. Didn't give a practice final or any clear examples of questions. AVOID IF U CAN!

Your grades only consist of the labs and the one final but he doesn't give a practice final or study guide so you have no idea what to expect. His reasoning for no practice final is that the previous prof didn't give one but the other profs give midterms so you know what to expect. Almost no instruction on lab reports or excel sheets
Very inconsistent grading not based on anything we are told.

If you are a student who studies a lot and puts in real effort, expecting it to be recognized, stay away from this class. Expectations are unclear and large point deductions happen for things that are never stated in the prompt. It often feels like guessing the grader's checklist rather than being evaluated on actual understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are sometimes clear, but the grading is inconsistent. The rubric isn't set up, so points are often deducted arbitrarily. Labs are worse—requirements aren't specified, and even complete work loses points. Could've been avoided with clear instructions.

This course is insanely hard and if you get an A- or above you are a mensa genius. A lot of the material is the same as in Harvards Math 55 which is the worlds hardest college course. The project is very fun and allows you to actually apply some of the scientific knowledge in class rather than just do math.

This is one of the chemistry departments smartest and best professors. He goes above and beyond to try and make concepts make sense for students. The topics for this class are conceptually easier than 130 and 131 but the exam questions are more abstract so its about the same difficulty.

Dr Xiong is very knowledgeable. His lectures are well structured and go into incredible depth and details. Most of the grade is based on homework which can be really challenging. Exams are relatively easy and at the end of the day he gives grades graciously.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: COGS 189: This professor is incredibly disorganized. She decides last minute that she wants to incorporate quizzes every week (not even giving us a weeks notice). The Canvas page is difficult to navigate. She expects students to know information beforehand and I'm lost. I'm sure she's great person outside of class but not as a professor. AVOID!

Choose her if you are self-motivated and really wanna LEARN SOMETHING (especially the math principles behind algorithms), and possess a solid foundation in math. If you're just looking for an easy credit, this course is not for you. Math never lie:)
Good lectures. Sometimes hard to follow but examples cleared up with homeworks and test study. High average on tests and just like practice ones. Good professor.
The class material is too challenging and she had a hard time explaining the concept. The test takes forever to grade and the entire class is lost.

Provides zero examples during lectures. Expects you to complete homework in MATLAB or Python and has never once pulled up either program during lecture to teach how to do so. Releases practice tests, but not the answers to it. During lecture provides complex equations, with different variables and never shows the implementation of those examples.

She is very knowledgeable. However, she is a terrible lecturer. She does not explain anything, just reads formulas out loud during lecture. She does not specify which formulas are most important. She makes any topic seem hard (you're better off with YouTube). Lecture are pointless for HW. HW took about 15 hours each.
slide reader
The lectures are very boring and do not help me to do the homeworks.

[COGS 189] I think she did a great job. However, her class was very unstructured. No clear lecture slides weekly. Best part of her class is the grading scale (55% is a C-, 85% is an A-) etc. It was pretty interesting material about BCIs. No exams. Just assignments, participation, and final project/paper/video! Highly suggest to work in groups.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Does good research but isn't a good Teacher or Lecturer. Soft-spoken and doesn't teach Math concepts from the Homework well. Expects you to know things without teaching them to you. Boring and dry lectures.

De Sa is knowledgeable but her lectures are not great. I'm usually good at math/stats but this class was hard to understand. The concepts are definitely graspable, but the professor doesn't take enough time to explain the math concepts and so you really have to think for yourself to learn. However, tests are very easy, especially being open book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: COGS189(not listed): This class requires you to just know things & doesn't have a clear structure. COGS 108 is a viable prereq option, but the professor doesn't think so (told us to reconsider if we didn't have an ML background--what??) PAs seem easy but its worded in such confusing ways, and they avoid answering clarification questions on Piazza.

It's machine learning so don't kid youself. Come with a strong coding and statistics background. noone is going to walk you through every conceptual step of the way. But she is highly respected in her field and gives incredibly in depth lectures which are podcasted so you should rewatch segments and read her slides to get the full picture.

She is a brilliant professor - knows her stuff, unfortunately this doesn't translate into good lectures. I honestly was lost for most of the material as she goes straight into complex mathematics with mediocre explanation. Luckily, her grading scheme is generous and getting a good grade is more than doable. However, I felt like I learned nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: 109 was super easy. She gives you the solutions! Got A despite taking in a rough quarter. What I really dislike about this prof is how she looks down on students.
