You cant not feel her attitude. Doesn't see her role as someone who needs to facilitate learning. It's students fault for not being CS majors, therefore not good enough. Problem never her

The material is different from most other required cogs classes, so many people hit a wall and have trouble with concepts.  However, she tries very hard to help you, with many office hours, review sessions, and an extremely generous grading scheme.  Basically, if you did well on the final, it would overwrite your grades in almost the entire class.

Its a difficult class, but she is more than helpful always. However you haev to take the tiem to seek out help if you need it, which you will. anyone who does poorly in this class does not belong there. She is great and will be there to help every step of the way, but if you are unmotivated you will do extremely poorly

Hard class. Extremely nice lady. The material was challenging, but interesting once you grasped it. Going to her office hours was exceptionally helpful. She ran lots of review sessions and was always available to answer any questions.

de Sa is awesome.  My secret favorite part of her class is when she tabs around on her computer and every gets to see like 50+ open windows.  Her teaching style tends to be a mixture of 60% slides and 40% board.  And her homeworks are sometimes cryptic and confusing, however I've never had a problem with the grading.  All and all shes worth it.

She is a nice lady though her teaching abilities are lacking.  Her grading style is awesome, but the tests are hard anyways.  The material sucks and she really doesn't explain it that well, making homework difficult.  Books don't help and half the stuff they just say "google it."  Frustrating material and could have been explained better!

Prof. DeSa is the WORST prof in the cog sci dept. She tried to teach matlab by telling us to use the 'help' section. She never once answered a question in a straight forward manner, nor, did she give a rat's behind about how her students were doing. The TA's didn't help at all either. I stopped going to section since they made it all worse...

One of the worst classes I've ever taken. Lectures are confusing, material seems like useless complicated BS (at least in the way it was presented), she's not a good lecturer at all and TAs occasionally make things worse. The majority of people fail the exams because this class is so awful, but since it's required what can you do.

Horrible teacher! When class didnt understand, she copied and pasted her notes to the next lecture and said the exact same thing again to explain. Class was made WAY harder than necessary for a beginning computing course. I had to get an engineer to help me and he didnt even know what was going on in the homework
I hate her. Useless. Everyone was failing and she didn't curve. Flashes slides at you and acts like that's teaching. NEVER AGAIN.

OOOh my goodness. She is a nice enough teacher but she just doesn't make sense. Hardly ever clarifies things in class (expects TA's to do it in section) HORRIBLE DON'T TAKE HER... if you must though her grading can be a little generous, dropping lowest HW and moving % around exams. YOU'LL NEED IT. Avg midterm score = 66%

She only lectured for us once, but hte class overall was great!  It was fun to have someone new everyday and to discuss a new topic.  She shows you most of the test questions ahead of time, so if you put in the effort you can easily get an A in the class.
This was a class with 16 different lecturers. Very fun class, really easy, De Sa let us write the exam questions. I would definitely recommend taking this class.
1st time teaching this class in FA2004 - her teaching style is alright. Very approachable in person but kind of a scatter brain when it comes to lecturing. Not terribly focused ...

she seems like a nice lady, but damn, she talks in circles and switches from back and forth all the time...follows the book so i dont know why i even went to lecture because she totally confused me!  she's smart though...but just didnt get through to me

The grading was completely unreasonable. The TA marked “unclear detail” and deducted points repeatedly without explanation, causing minor issues to add up unfairly. The final report guidelines were unclear and inconsistent, with key requirements are not stated on official announcements, which is really hard to follow.

This class is not useful. The hws are vague, no clear grading criteria. The professor and TA do not care about the class. Final project report was graded with AI generated feedback. Rubric was removed by the TAs. Nothing is clear in this class. You also learn absolutely nothing. To put it short, this professor doesn't respect his class at all.

Class is easy but did not learn anything new that I could learn myself. Waste of a class to be used for a requirement in a graduate program. Would suggest to take a different class if you wish to learn. Take it only for an easy grade but such a waste to be in this class.

Pengtao Xie is genuinely one of the greatest professors I have ever had. I am a Senior at UCSD in Electrical Engineering and I have attended 2 different universities. His lectures are so interesting and well structured. He is a fantastic lecturer and extremely knowledgeable. I would take any and every class he teaches. Highly recommend taking him!

Professor Xie cares about his students very much and is always open to discussions if you have difficulties. Professor Xie gives a reasonable amount of workload but the programming assignments (PAs) are a little challenging yet manageable. You can also choose to do a group project over PAs. For the exams, just do the practice exams and you're good.
Professor Xie is patient and willing to answer any questions. He is flexible and kind in adjusting deadlines. One  suggestion: try to cover more intuition behind theorems.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: professor is very nice and took many feedback from students. grace days are given to accommodate students' schedule. applications (dpp, gaussian processes) covered in lectures are very interesting.

A student-friendly instructor. He is very knowledgable in linear algebra. Can see that he puts a lot of efforts in preparing for lectures. I especially like the live derivation of proofs. Programming assignments helped me a lot in understanding the practical applications of linear algebra.

Pengtao gave good grades. But the lecture is poorly organized. The professor doesn't seem to care much about teaching. You can take it for credits, but you should not expect to learn anything useful from the course.
Lectures are clear and well-organized. Covers theory and applications. Very useful to my research.

I just could not ask for a worse instructor. 
HWs, exams and projects were easy or doable. Also they seemed to be pretty generous when grading them. The average on these were high they crazily graded last project. And even worse! they graded based on ranking in such unfair system he made. It was just unfair unfair and unfair. DO NOT TAKE WITH HIM!!
I learned a lot from this course. The instructor cares about students a lot.
Very considerate professor. Would love to take again any course offered by him.
Lot to learn.

Prof. Xie was very active in answering questions on piazza. He is very knowledgable about linear algebra and its applications in machine learning. He is willing to take suggestions on teaching the class from students.
Didn't learn much from the lecture. The assignments are poorly designed and slides are copied somewhere. Always no passion in class. Would never recommend others to take his course.
A very kind professor who cares students very much. You can ask anything, a very gentle prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pengtao is a good lecturer, and cares very much about his students. Decent prof.

CHEM 109: The professor did not offer clear instructions for assignments. Assignments and lab reports were rushed. Due dates often being within 3 days or less of the assignment opening. She referenced the lab manual in lecture, but students frequently pointed out conflicting statements with what was in the reading material versus what she taught.

Lectures can be non-engaging and quiet. There is a lot of information to digest at once, almost too much. Grades are reliant on online homework and exams. Exams were difficult, as information was so broad. The teacher is kind, but soft spoken and non-engaging. Also, be ready for a hefty cost, the website for the textbook/homework costs $200.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Huang was a good teacher and included many example problems relevant for the lectures and what'd be on the test. Though I'm not a STEM major and don't particularly enjoy chem,she gave us every possible resource to do well and whether you took advantage of them or not is up to you. Graded weekly HW, midterm, final, and attendance on discussions

Sweet Professor who genuinely cares if you understand and is always open to helping.Has bad rep because chemistry is just a difficult topic to learn but she does a good job w/ asking if people understand. Lecture not mandatory but not recorded. Required to buy the site in order to do homework. One chapter homework per week.

I really like this professor, she is very sweet. Lectures can be fun when you understand what is going on, but towards the continuing chapters the work starts to get a bit tough. Homework is honestly not too hard, she gives you almost a week to complete it.

My initial thought for taking Chem 11 is that it is for those in a non-science major, but it was just as difficult as taking the Chem 6 series. She seemed like a sweet person, however, her teaching style was just reading off slides. I have asked her if she can record the lectures but she specifically said this course is meant not to be recorded.

I had no prior knowledge on this topic, and CHEM 11 supposes to be for non-science major. This class was the most challenging one. Teaching style is basically reading the lecture slides. Don't rely on the lecture or lecture slide. Study textbook. Or, take other classes if you can. I didn't have an option so I just took it but the result is painful.

I still don't know what my grade will genuinely be because she takes so long to grade. It's been a full quarter, and I still don't know my grade. Grades are due, and I still don't know my actual grade. Save yourself the trouble, and don't take this, professor. She won't help you outside of class either, I tried that, and it didn't work.

This class was terrible. She waited till the end of the quarter to grade our entire class. She was not helpful when asking her questions outside of class. She only copies the notes from the online textbook and pastes them into the lecture slides. She taught us things for science majors (this course is for non-science majors). Don't take the class.

I only took this course to earn credit for a requirement.This professor won't grade anything until the end of the quarter when we need our grades to know if we passed. When I asked her if she could calculate it, she made it seem like I had to do it myself (and I'm the student, not the teacher, aka her job). AVOID THIS COURSE/TEACHER IF YOU CAN!

Worst professor I've ever had at UCSD. Her lectures are confusing and unclear for an introductory chemistry course. It is clear she has little understanding about the material. At one point in a lecture, the teacher had to be stopped by a TA mid-lecture so she could better explain a topic that the professor was struggling to teach.

I took Professor Huang for Chem 11 and was told it was a really easy class, I guess it depends on professor. She just reads off of her lecture slides. Many students requested for her to podcast lectures but she was not willing to :/ even though it would've been so helpful considering she explains examples on the chalkboard.
Lectures were very wordy and could be hard to focus on, but reading the textbook was enough to get through homework. The professor was super nice and knowledgeable.

Professor Huang was a nice prof. Although she isn't great at explaining things(basically just reads off lecture slides which she later posts), she gives relevant homework which helps you ace the exam. Would recommend her.
Pretty patient and nice professor! Exams are pretty close to homework, and she provided very clear and detailed study guide before every exams. Definitely recommend her!
Very approachable professor that showed interest in helping students in succeeding. Exams were straight forward and based off lecture slides. Would easily recommend this course she taught it again

Lectures focus on personal research rather than course material. Quizzes are difficult to prepare for, as questions cover niche in-class comments. The quizzes format on the classroom screen cause great pressure.
Most useful class I took, learned a ton and developed my own research interest through this course. and the prof is super nice, all his lectures are really interesting.

The final was easy if you have gone through lectures; it is open-book anyways. He introduces a wide array of topics related to HCI and invites PhD students to host interesting lectures that they are passionate about. Although he only started recording lectures after like week 4, he is an overall caring, passionate, and kind professor.

Very exciting materials. Most interesting course I have taken. If you are expecting spoon-feeding, this course is probably not the right for you. Quizzes can be challenging if you don't come to the lectures.

I don't think the instructor is even experienced or prepared in teaching... He covers lots of his own research materials for a class that should've covered a lot broader than that. His quiz questions can be extremely subjective to his own thoughts which the scoring distribution doesn't resemble any classes I took at UCSD. I feel so weird.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The instructor overemphasized his own research for a class that is supposed to survey the entire HCI. No lecture recordings, very few lectures notes, disorganized slides - which the instructor claimed (when asked) to be his teaching philosophy. Quizzes cannot be done without reading his research papers, which aren't part of the assigned readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Xia is a nice prof overall but unfortunately I don't think he did a great job teaching this class as I walked out feeling I've learned little to nothing. He just assigns a bunch of research papers for us to read and explain things at a highly theoretical surface. Hopefully in future editions of COGS 120 he can teach more practical stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lots of weekly readings and a few papers to write, but for me I did enjoy them because it wasn't like your typical English paper or essay. Professor Xia is really passionate about his work and really cares for his students, which is really nice given the circumstances of the pandemic. Very engaging, too!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: DSGN100 is by nature has a lot of workload. We delved a bit into font and layout before getting to the actual COVID design project. He was interactive in our Friday peer review and anything else was up to the TA. I think his presentations weren't too important but he cares for his students.
One of the best teachers at UCSD and always willing to help students.
Clear lectures, approachable, and genuinely cares about students. Fair and generous grading, although the material can be challenging for short summer session.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Last Econ course at UCSD. Good at explaining things and lectures are recorded for those who can't make it to class. Mentioned no extra credit but in the end provided opportunity for 5% bonus. Overall, tough class for summer session but good material. Be prepared to study and take advantage of the previous exams he provides for study material.
Great prof. Exams are reasonable as long as you do the practice one.
Prof Ma seems serious, but is nice if you talk to him. Lecture slides are clear, good examples. The practice exams are helpful. Tests are representative of the material. Not too much homework.
Clear lectures and well-organized. Grading is transparent and fair. No surprise questions in the exam.

Generally unaccommodating. No partial credit, no matter how trivial the mistake (i.e: calculation/input error). Slides are generally good enough to understand everything, high curve. He teaches so that you understand but the grading style falls short of reflecting that.
No lecture recordings, only provide his lecture notes. Even though you come to every class, you can never refer to previous lectures. Don't take his class if you can

I really like the cheatsheet he gives for exams. It covers everything taught in lectures. That being said, he is the first professor I ever took who really puts the words "understand not to memorize" into practice. Two exams are very easy and identical to practice ones so you should be good with preparation. He is also caring and nice to talk to.
One of the greatest prof in UCSD, nicely organized lecture, little HW, and generous grading, the test is good and related to HW, with no surprising tricky questions. Don't hesitate to take it.
As long as you practice the provided exams and read the problem sets carefully, the exams will be farely easy. Don't worry if you cannot understand all the proofs.
Very friendly professor, strongly recommended!

Professor Ma might seem like a serious guy, but he is super nice and always open to answer any questions! His exams are very similar to problem sets and examples gone over in class, so there are never any surprises. He grades more than fairly! I'm happy I took his class and didn't wait to take it with another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ma prerecorded lectures that were overall good for the material but could sometimes get a bit boring. Tests were very representative of the material gone over in class and problem sets, so there were never any big surprises. Overall very fair structure and good lecturer.

He's a nice person, but online he's super hard to learn from. His lectures are prerecorded and feel slow even on 2x speed. It's hard to motivate yourself in the class when it seems like the professor doesn't care. He holds lots of office hours, but most of the students can't attend them because they are behind on the material. Avoid him if online.

Professor Ma is amazing. His lectures are Prerecorded, but there is a plus size to that, he replaces his normal lecture time for Office hours, giving 6 hours of his time every single week, and answering any questions you may have. No other professor gives 6 hours of OH a week! Pro Ma is the best!!

He uses recorded videos from SP20, and his notations are super different from other Econometrics profs, which makes the class unnecessarily difficult. He doesn't have practice exams but had a sample midterm. I dropped his class because I deserve a better education for the tuition I am paying.

No live lectures, can not explain concepts clearly. His PPTs are just a bunch of concepts, full of messy and confusing notations. 20% Stata Assignment, 30% Midterm, 50% Final. If you know things very well, then go ahead and take his class. If you don't. then better avoid him.

Feels like professor does care, upload videos of the lectures and call it a day. If you are looking for a do it yourself education then this teacher is great. Otherwise, I think there is should be a limit on what classes you are allowed not to do a live lecture. Another problem is his notation, confusing and different from 120A class.

This class has been difficult and he made it even harder. Weekly quizzes are hard and not much curving. He sent almost 1/4 of the students to student conduct bc he thought they committed plagiarism, but indeed the students were just getting help from tutoring, esp when he wasn't being helpful when students are struggling to pass. DONT TAKE HIM.

Prof Ma is the GOAT. He explains econometric concepts very clearly and was very generous with grading/testing given the COVID-19 pandemic situation. I would definitely recommend him for anyone looking to understand econometrics well. An A isn't too hard to obtain as long as you take decent notes.
God bless this man at all costs

One of the best math profs I've had at UCSD!!! He cares so much about his students, and gives a ton of practice questions. Lectures are really clear and notes are top notch. Exams are not easy, but fair for an upper div math course, his practice material helps a ton. The only issue I can think of is his heavy accent, but he can be understood.

Ming is a great professor. Lectures are clear with plenty of examples that will help with exams. Homework isn't long or too difficult. He also provides many resources such as practice exams and extra hw problems that will help with the exam. Fair exams and overall a fair class, take him if he is teaching!

One of the best Math profs I've had at UCSD!! Really seems to care about student success, posts plenty of practice problems and resources for exams. Midterms were extremely fair and offers extra credit questions (haven't taken the final yet though), and you can tell he is passionate about the subject. Great guy, would take again

I personally didn't love his lecture style but lots of my friends did. His practice exams are similar to the real ones, but you don't get a cheat sheet for tests. Homework is fair and graded nicely, but exam grading is a little picky. He does give extra credit questions on exams. As long as you're comfortable in upper divs you'll be fine.

He's such a real one. Great at lecturing (though uses an iPad projected onto the screen instead of a chalkboard). Homework and tests are super straightforward, and he provided good practice midterms and final exams which helped with preparation. If you go to lectures and do the homework you will succeed in this class.

Professor gives good lecture and overall great course, practice exams are very reflective of actual exams - no cheat sheets are allowed, but the grading is ridiculously fussy and it's hard to predict exactly how the prof and grader want answers to be written, you could be right but not include all desired details easily.  Write answers carefully!!!
The best professor I ever had! Lectures were engaging and he gave plenty of hints for exams. Very friendly and always seemed interested in his students success.

One of the best math professors at UCSD! His lecture is clear. Make sure to follow the procedures he lists and do hws and practice exams, and then you will be fine during the exams. His final is a little more challenging than the midterms, but it is doable and learning-promoting. YYDS!

Wonderful Professor. Truly enjoyed taking this course and would be glad to take more courses with Xiao. The homeworks are designed to be slightly harder than the midterms so that you'll do good on the midterms. He's very understanding and tries his best to explain concepts you don't understand if you attend office hours.
Good lectures, below-average workload and average exam difficulties. Professor Ming gives clear lectures and detailed notes, one of the best professors of MATH 109.

I took this guy for both 142AB and 120. He is overall a really good professor. The only thing I could complain about is that he has a chinese accent but it pretty easy to understand. He offers extra credit but it isn't really required since he posts practice exams which are very similar to the actual exams. Finals are than harder than midterms.

Super nice and accessible professor. He gives extra credit on second midterms for feedback. He would also hint the questions that are on the tests during lecture. He gives good amount of practice problems but be aware that his final is typically harder than his midterms. Overall, you get to learn a lot in his class.
Professor Xiao's office hour is really helpful and the content of his lecture is clear. Most of the homework he assigned is manageable and you can really learn real analysis from his class!
Peferct Professor in UCSD Math Department! His exams are based on HW and trying to motivate your interest on Maths. Lectures are not mandatory but are very helpful to your understanding

Lecture notes are insightful (even better than the book at times). Sadly, HW is graded and due weekly (textbk problems). I learned a lot from this class, but the dense midterms/final admittedly added unnecessary stress. Otherwise, prof. is easily accessible, helpful, and quite understanding, I think. Great class for math majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I'm sure he tried his best considering Differential Equations are somewhat difficult. Will trail off sometimes and stare at the board when working through lecture problems. Midterms and the final felt tedious, but he was super generous with curving and grading scale for this class. Hopefully, he can improve himself for the future.

Not great at lecturing, just kinda lists out theory without much explanation so it's hard to follow along. Will get confused, stare at the board for a minute, then correct his mistakes often. First midterm was really easy, second was very hard. Homework is really short and easy. Doesn't podcast and his lecture notes are also hard to follow along.

Professor Wang is very kind and wants everyone to do well. The course material seems to be outdated and not super applicable to day to day life. Writing assignments were very hard and require a lot of work, especially if you don't already have a writing background. I highly recommend using a Chinese dictionary during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Wang was very encouraging/engaging-just an incredibly kind and sweet person overall. She makes sure everyone and understands the material and has made me feel supported in times I felt behind or had to miss class. Lectures were well organized/easy to follow. She uses positive reinforcement and never makes anyone feel bad for making a mistake.

I highly recommend Wang laoshi's course to prepare you for a clinical setting, regardless if you are the patient, family, or the provider! Her speech is clear and paced well, and she uses repetition and encourages participation, which I prefer when learning new language terms. The oral projects are great for practicing synthesizing everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Wang laoshi's class is beginner friendly if you already have a normal Chinese foundation but lack the vocabulary for a clinical setting. She teaches very clearly and encourages you to practice speaking in class. The class setting is small and everyone is very non-judgmental. I liked her class so much, I took her again for CHIN169B!

I took CHIN 169A and 169B (Medical Chinese), and what I learned was translatable to a clinical setting as a pre-med student. Wang laoshi was patient and understanding with clear grading guidelines. She had taught similar classes at Stanford before so I highly recommend her, especially if you want to learn Chinese that applies to your career path.

This class is honestly so chill and the prof is a very kind and caring person. Review Quizzes, homework, 1 midterm and 1 final exam and 1 midterm presentation are all super easy, took me only around 2-3 hours per week to do all the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: taken medical chinese if you have some knowledge in chinese. weekly quizzes that are hard even for native. fast paced quiz/testing sesion but htat the class itself is very boring. professor is nice.
Wonderful, caring professor. Very talented and good at engaging students and teaching them pronouniation and grammar. Very lenient and understanding. Love her!!!!!!!

One of the nicest teachers you'll meet. She genuinely wants you to do well, and it shows. She immediately recognized my strengths and weaknesses, and made sure I didn't get discouraged. Lots of quizzes, homework's long, but publishes a guide to the test in advance.

If you put in the effort, you're guaranteed an A, if not take it P/NP.

Love her. Really cares about her students, and is truly engaged with the process of learning. Definitely a lot easier than the 10 series. Her tests are too bad, she will usually tell you the problems for the essays ahead of time.

Good professor. I took her for B and C too. She really tries to get the students actively engaged. She's pretty lenient (will let you retake parts of tests if you do worse than usual). Lectures and tutorials are mandatory. Tutorials were usually boring. ?????????????????????????????????????????????? It's not hard to get an A ?????????(????????????)

She's really helpful and from personal experience, cares a lot about the success of her students. Assignments and exams are fair as long as you study and keep up with the material. Some class exercises, especially the readings that are insanely difficult, are useless since the content cannot be retained. However, I do recommend Wang Lao Shi :)
You can tell she cares a lot for her students' learning. One time we all failed a section of a test so she let us retake that exact section. Her class is only difficult if you don't study.

Professor Wang is hard to understand sometimes, has a very high pitched voice, and can have dry lectures, but she really cares about her students. She is really understanding and lenient. The class itself is not too difficult, but if you need help she is very understanding.

Great professor, very easy tests AS LONG AS YOU STUDY. It takes me 2hr to study and get an A. Students who do poorly on them probably never study anyway. The textbook is not as interesting as the 10 series' textbook. TA was very helpful. I thought this class was easier than the 10 series.

Wang Laoshi is a good teacher. She may be a little hard to understand, but she really does care about her students. I you let her know you are having trouble she tries really hard to help you. She is not weird. She is REALLY nice and kinda funny sometimes.

Horrible teacher. Doesn t help when you ask her. + shes really weird. I see her around talkign to herself constantly. & I know many in the class that have trouble understanding her english. Her teachering skills are low. Look at the scores and you tell its not the students.

Wang Laoshi was a fair teacher. Her tests are ok and homework is ok if you put in the work. However, she does not help with tones much at all and the way she teaches grammar does not help much either.

Wang Laoshi is a little hard to understand in English sometimes. She is pretty fair though. For our first test, we were tested on identifying tones, initials, and finals. The class did awful and she threw the test out and told us we would be retested at the end of the quarter to give more time for everyone to study it.
I thoroughly enjoyed this class. Wang laoshi can be a little weird and occasionally hard to understand, but she's funny and keeps the class interesting. My TA was also really nice and helpful.

She's a pretty good professor. She talks kinda fast but you get used to it after the first few lectures. Wang laoshi can be hilarious at times too. The TAs are nice, and you'll get to know them really well.
The class is easy if u pick the right TA.

she's really nice and helpful. put into a lot of effort. her tests r not that hard but she grades in great detail. one character wront = -.5. just be careful w/ ur usage of the three "de" if u know chinese
a good teacher, homework is not hard if you know some chinese

THIS COURSE IS NOT HARD. He just makes it hard since you can't understand him through his accent. The material is not bad, its just the midterms give you questions that you have not seen before or are much harder than the discussion problems. He curves a half-grade at the end.
reading the textbook def helps after lecture + doing practice problems, but generally working thru the hw helps a lot and exams r like the hw

Heavy, heavy accent. it's clear that it's this professor's first time teaching. Prepare to do a lot of self studying. Lectures is just him reading off the note. Don't really explain things clearly and just assuming you know it. Big mistake taking a course labelled "staff". Also MATH 20B is way too content heavy for a bad professor.

It is very clear that this is his first time teaching a college course.
He has a pretty thick accent and is tough to understand at times.
He is very unclear when it comes to explaining and is a pain, I ended up watching the podcasts of another instructor.
He is a nice guy though, but needs a lot more experience to teach a course like this.

He's a very nice professor, but his lectures are not easy to understand. He kind of rushes through some things and is not the clearest explainer. The discussions are attendance mandatory and help tons, and so does doing all the homework. The midterms were fine, the final exam was not!! But other than that I think its a manageable class

It was very difficult to understand the material because he doesn't know how to explain, he assumes we already know everything and goes very fast in every lecture. I was confused in every lecture and had to learn the material in my own.

Professor Yu is obviously a caring professor, and did a great job of providing lots of practice problems. However I had to spend a lot of time self studying/relearning material after class to feel prepared for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The homework and discussion questions are definitely harder than the exam questions but the homework is very flexible (can submit up to 3 days late, no deductions, unlimited attempts) and the discussion is only graded on attendance. The practice exams on the course website are the most similar in difficulty to the real exams
Extremely nice lecturer, highly recommended to take her class. Tests are easier than achieve homework so don't worry about that too much.

Math20B is hard. Zongxin makes it so much fun and explains things well for the little time you get in class. She has an accent, but not one that you can't understand. The homework and discussion are insanely hard compared to the actual coursework. The midterms are very fair. And the grading scale makes it very forgiving. Take her, she is so nice!

She is really great and helpful, happy to spend time to help any students that have questions. Lecture are tidy and helpful, really useful for midterm and finals. Homework and discussion is really hard, but it will be easier than midterm and finals. If you have the time, go to her office hours, it really helps, definitely choose her.

She is very kind and approachable. Her lecture notes are extremely helpful and well organized. If you study the problems in her notes and carefully go through the review notes before exams, you should be well prepared for all the tests. Definitely recommend taking her class!

Very kind but I found doing homework to be more helpful than going to lecture sometimes bc it's very fast paced and not everything is explained well + skips steps. Discussion/lecture not mandatory and discussion sheets are posted on Canvas. Questions asked on the midterm/final are pretty fair but still difficult class.
This is my queen.

She tends to skip steps when doing example problems and may brush through topics so doing practice problems is definitely needed and she may put them onto the exam! During reviews she'll emphasize on things that may be on the test so pay attention because she wont clearly say it. Tests are difficult compared to other professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I'd say definitely a VERY good professor! PASSIONATE! patient and supportive! HER notes cover all the things you need to know
She is really a nice person. Love her class.

She is the 2nd funniest most charismatic, sweet lady to ever grace the Earth. However, don't take the class if you don't have time to study due to various reasons your freshmen year of college causing some physical issues impairing your ability to test take.
Highly recommend her class!

Yu is a very nice professor. She really hopes that everyone can understand and achieve good grades. She is also very patient. Although the course itself is a bit difficult, her outlines and review materials are very useful!

Midterms and final match her lectures well. Bonus problems on both midterms. Seems to care for students a lot; actively sought student feedback mid-quarter and listened to advice to slow down her teaching and work through examples more.

She's one of the nicest professors I've had and genuinely cares about her students. Her lectures are good, though she moves a bit fast and her accent can be hard to understand at first. There are two midterms, but only the higher score counts. Tests are hard. 20C itself is a hard class but she tries her best to support you through it. Good prof.

Nice professor, but her accent and unclear handwriting can sometimes get in the way. Make sure to practice ALOT outside of class. She tries her best to give as many points as possible on exams. Also, there was a class curve. Notes outline is provided; use it! Overall, not a bad professor, but not the greatest. 20C is pretty hard in general.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very clear she wants everyone to succeed. Lecture notes are fast-paced and speaks with a heavy accent is still understandable. Syllabus tells you exactly how to do well in the class. MAKE SURE TO GO TO DISCUSSIONS. Very generous curve.

nice person clearly wants everybody to succeed ie learn the material and benefit from it in the future. Generous curve. It does require a lot of work outside of class however. Her lecture notes can be confusing at times but accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
The professor covers class materials for this class very well in class. Grading policies and assignments are not harsh, and exams are also not hard & reflects what we've learned in class well. Both lecture and discussion are not mandatory for us. Also she answers question in office hours clearly as well.

Will choose to take again if possible :)
queen GOAT 10/10 would recommend

She is really caring and wants her students to do well! She curved the final grade and is really understanding to how difficult the new math concepts can be. If you attend lecture and try outside class as well, you do well.

She's a great professor and genuinely wants the best for her students. Material is hard and midterms are difficult but she only keeps the highest score of the two. Very accessible outside of class and responds really quick. If you space your time out and do the practice problems in her notes you will do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tests are similar to her lecture example questions and provided practice problems, so what she teaches you is what you will be tested on. Helped me do the best I've done on a math final in UCSD so far than I ever have. She's accessible outside of class and a kind person.

Attendance/discussion is not mandatory & lecture is recorded. Professor is nice and seems like she really cares. 2 midterms (1 is dropped) and a final. Exams are decently similar to in class problems and partial credit is given on exam problems which is nice. Course is pretty challenging though so prepare to study a lot!

Yu is a great person and will showcase her wonderful splendid cat in many lectures. Besides this she also provides everything you need to pass her tests / class. Exams have been a fair representation of lecture notes for example and she tries to give hints on what we should focus on. Her lectures can be hard to understand but usually its fine

She's really nice and offers lot of extra credits for exams. Just that her notes can be a bit messy and her accent is hard to follow at first. It's her first time teaching this class so I'm sure she will get better next time.

Stopped attending lecture because they were not easy to follow, she goes really fast and while explaining some problems she just assumes you know how. Tests are hard, and will need to memorize everything, no formula sheet or anything. Homework is good, easy, but not really useful to study.

Lectures follow her guided notes and examples that are related to what she'll test. Discussion worksheets also related to exams. Very clear on what will/will not be on test. Homework is available 2-3 weeks before due date and due 1-2 weeks after topic is covered. Passionate on making sure you understand the material and always open to questions.
Very Good Professor!

Pretty good professor. Very sweet and kind individual. One should be aware this class is mostly coding on data analytics softwares. Personally I learned the weekly material through the textbook videos in the modules. Watching them all and doing the quizzes can take a while but its not too bad. Midterm was alright but final was definitely harder.

prof genuinely cares about students and wants them to succeed. our midterm 1 had a good avg so he made midterm 2 really difficult and there were printing issues so most didn't do well on midterm 2. however, he curves a lot, gives a lot of practice for exams and has a detailed study guide. ignore the bad reviews, study hard for the final (45% grade)

i like this prof, he's got good vibes and is very nice. only problem is, he isn't really good at teaching. also, the final is extremely difficult compared to the midterm. final is worth 50% of your grade but was brought down to 45%. did well on midterm just to do extremely bad in the final. good curve and some extra credit opportunities.

reviews.comment: Really great teacher, the course itself is very stats heavy so I think people get confused quick but he offers a lot of support and tests are super reflective of assignments and classwork
he curves well and his assignments are so manageable. most of his exams are very reflective of the study guides. the bad reviews are much too harsh. he is a great prof, very approachable.

Ignore these bad reviews. Professor Dai is super sweet and a great teacher. There was an issue with the printing center for an exam but he curved the exam tremendously and apologized for the incident. He records lectures and homework is very manageable.
super nice professor and obviously cares that his students do well!
never take it again

Was 20 min late to our exam and tried to pin it on the printing center not having the exam ready. You are getting paid hundreds of thousands of dollars a year to be a professor, it is your responsibility to ensure everything is in order for the exam. Any normal prof would have moved the exam, not taken off the question that takes 30 sec to answer.

If he feels like people are doing well he makes his next exam impossible. Very clearly does not want you to succeed, just wants to keep his averages. What is the point of making an exam so difficult (and long) that no one can solve it? What is being tested at that point, your ability to stress out students?
If your class's midterm 1 average is too high, you'll get a surprise during midterm 2.

Bad final experience. Had students stuck in the final room without enough copies. Students had to wait 2 hours without electronics. Then, at random, took off parts of the final, which now had to be completed in under an hour.

Econometrics is basically stats. You're learning economics applications and some of it is not intuitive. Professor Dai is super helpful. Curves are generous and he allows calculators on exams, which speed things up. He's great at taking questions and explaining some of the tougher concepts.
Soooo good prof

Extremely thorough with his teaching methods. He understands that students join the class with varying backgrounds in previous math experience, and accordingly tries his best to accommodate this by being super clear and understandable in his lectures. He genuinely wants you to succeed. If you put in the work, you will get an A.

Genuinely the most caring professor I had. He wants everyone to pass, and honestly wants everyone to get A's. If you go to class he literally will show you examples that are on the exams. The content is kind of boring but if you just go to class and do the homework and study guides you will do well.

My fav professor so far! Such a genuine guy who genuinely cares about his students and WANTS them to succeed. His class is generally easy to understand and grading criteria is made clear from the beginning. Take him if you get the chance!
Pretty good lecturer, midterm and final are really easy take-home essays.

The class can be hard if you've never coded before, but he moves at a slow pace and gives out lots of decent practice problems that are similar to those on the exams. He genuinely cares and can be really endearing if you go to office hours (I WENT TO OFFICE HOURS). He also makes the tests easier because he doesn't want people to fail.

Lectures are easy and if you actually goes to class, he tells you what questions will be on the exams. Posts practice problems that almost translate 1 to 1 to actual midterms / finals. Gives decent extra credit opportunities. My GOAT.
Very nice and caring Professor. Wants you to do well. Practice tests nearly identical to actual exams.
i love him. my king. he WANTS you to do well. he is so kind and he makes sure you will get what you want out of this class as long as you try. would take him again 100000%.

Took Dai for ECON 5 and 120A now, really like the way he structures his class. His lectures, homework and practice test reflect very well what will be on the midterm and final and he even tells you what exactly what to study. He gives lots of examples in lecture to build on concepts. Passionate about teaching and is really funny.

I took Dai for Econ 1 and Econ 120A. Honestly I find him quite endearing and invested in his students' success. He brings a positive energy to class. He moves at a relatively slow pace, which I enjoyed. And his practice tests are basically identical to his actual tests. He gives you all the resources you'd need to do well in this class.

All of his exams were multiple choice and the study guide and practice questions were VERY similar to the ones on the final exam. I had a friend who only memorized the study guides and got a B+ on the exams. Professor Dai is approachable and encourages questions. Just make sure that if you aren't gonna go to lecture then PLEASE WATCH THE LECTURES.

This class was extremely easy. It is basically introductory stats. and Dai tells you exactly what is going to be on the exam. He teaches well and records lectures and explains any concepts that are somewhat difficult.

Prof. Dai is a very good lecturer! Genuinely cares about student learning to ensure all students do well. Exams are extremely similar to practice exams, and Prof. just changes the numbers so there are no surprises. Sometimes, Prof tells students which questions on the practice exam to focus on to reduce stress. Would take again.

Has an accent and talks really slow, ended up just podcasting his lectures on 3x speed. Lectures are not bad and gives good examples of what might be seen on test. Do the practice exams as they are copy and paste of what the actual exams are going to be.
Nice person, his practice exams are highly related to real exams and he will curve all the exam during quarter or at the end of quarter.

Dai's lectures for this course is actually below average that I found the videos he gave us is more helpful. Final is way harder than the midterm and be ready to study yourself. He gotta change the data of the practice materials. One lab and one quiz each week but the due is loose so that you can arrange your time, which is good.
His lecture and podcast are terrible, you should be prepared to study by yourself.

reviews.comment: I don't think the test is heavy.Really great and patient Prof. HW's due time is long enough(almost2wk per HW)No attendence need.He did start giving us curve and practice questions that were 80% the same as the real exam.He do listens and care students' opinions.

Your midterm and finals make up your whole grade and they are extremely difficult. They are similar to practice exams given, however, midterm 2 is so much harder than the first one and he does not curve it. The final is extremely difficult and not enough practice is given to succeed.
Pretty easy class, midterms and final were basically what was covered in class. He can be a bit hard to understand but I still understood and he seemed super sweet

Professor Dai is a very good lecturer. His lectures are very clear and he provides slides. The content of exams is all covered in his lectures. As long as you understand all of his lectures and finish homework on time, it's easy to get an A.
his tests are way easier than levkoff. his lectures are easy to understand. he usually repeat his main points at least 5 times. sometimes his accent is hard to understand, but not too difficult
Second midterm was so much harder than the first midterm. Most things on exams were explained in lectures, some were not. Use your resources (especially practice exams).

Good professor. All the comments about his accent are true, it's very noticeable, but it doesn't really make him hard to understand. Just ask for clarification if you're truly confused. Definitely go to class to take notes. Try hard in the tests, they're worth 85% of your final grade. He's also very kind and willing to help if you don't understand.

reviews.comment: Great professor. Teaches concepts with great detail and is actively answering questions. However, exams have some questions that are worded odd which have answers that are not always clear cut or can be interpreted in different ways.
math major, taking his class for fun and to boost my gpa. two easy midterms just watch podcasts and study his practice exams. by far this one is the easiest course ever in my entire college life.

Professor Dai is passionate, and it shows, but he is a bit hard to understand. Attendance isn't required for the discussions or lectures, but he writes the notes himself during the lecture so it is helpful to go. reviews.comment: Prof. Dai's lecture is clear and extremely helpful when you go to his office hours. 100% recommend
Very passionate professor and it shows. Clear on material and fair exams if you actually watch the lectures and do the practice problems.

I don't understand why many previous comments about this professor are so negative. The negative comments were completely different from the classes and professors I attended. The professor is very responsible and cares about his students. He tries to make everything easy and make it possible for students to get good grade.  A nice professor.

The professor was a good man who cared deeply about his students. He is very conscientious about teaching. As long as you review the material he gives you and practice a lot. Super easy exam. The exam is exactly same like the past exam and practice problem what he gave. Most of questions not even change number. Just follow the class or do the practice. Easy A.

Yes he has an accent but not really an issue. He is just VERY wordy and give a TON of pre-lecture material. That is my main complaint. Videos + Textbook + Slides + in-class practice materials sums up the content. Allowed cheat sheets for exams, but still tricky and time consuming. I ended up just reading the book but going to class would be better.

Professor Dai made the midterms and final so easy and it's an easy A class. He just copy the practice exam and pastes on the final, he hopes his students can get A if they understand the lecture. Just go to his office hour and he will teach you how to do it. Don't try to threaten him just because he's the new professor.

Genuinely nice guy but his lectures aren't always reflective of the stuff you will see on his exams. However, problem sets contain literal problems from exams but with different numbers, so as long as you understand the problem sets well you should be fine. Also might be worth noting that exams are worth 90%+ of your grade.

I would say Dai is an excellent professor. I don't understand why his comment here is so negative. Admittedly, his accent is quite strong. For his 2 midterms, he basically just change the number of his HW question and provided Exam Practice. U can easily earn 100/100 if u review these two materials carefully.
DONT TAKE HIM

please don't take his class if you actually want to learn or get good grades. I took him last quarter and our first midterm was horrible for most people bc too many questions in 50 min. Dai's lectures were wordy and hard to understand. He spends more time deriving formulas than teaching students how to use them. Exams were tricky and were not a reflection of the study guides/general understanding of the content and the study guides were only provided 1-2 days ahead of the exams.
His accent is hard to understand and is holding our classes final study guide hostage with a 90% CAPES requirement, literally soooooo bad. Keep as far away as possible

Do yourself a favor and don't take this professor. He is a nice guy, but makes an easy class as difficult as he possibly could. Every other professor i've heard about that teaches this class makes it as easy for students to learn as possible, not Dai.

Very nice and caring guy, but dude cannot teach. Took this course in HS and learned way more then. Made an easy class really difficult. His teaching style and pace is terrible. I honestly liked the Professor. I didn't go to class, but I watched all the Lectures through the media gallery on Canvas. All of the midterms were reflective of what he talked in Lectures and what was in our Homework.

He makes alot of mistakes on his lectures and watching the lectures is already tough. I ended up having to do a lot of self teaching. Dai is a new professor and it definitely shows. GO TO LECTURE! She does demonstrations, uses the chalkboard, etc. that will not make it on the podcast. The tests are difficult, you need to know the concepts very well to understand the questions. I went into this class really interested in eyewitness memory, and she made it even more engaging. She's very funny and clearly knows a lot in this field. Great lecturer but when it came to studying, I felt scattered, the slides were repetitive but the exam content was very specific to something minute mentioned in lecture out of all the material from lectures and textbook assigned. Vague and test heavy, avoid the class.
test heavy, must read textbook.

Professor Yilmaz clearly knows the subject (she keeps reminding you of her expert status). reviews.comment:
a great lecturer (although sometimes goes off topic), and pretty engaging and easy course content
however the exams and overall grading are weirdly harsh if you aim for a A or A+, I messed up one homework and now need a 38/40 with all extra credits and perfect participation for an A+, and she was harsh and unforgiving when I tried talking to her

I do not recommend taking her class. She goes on personal tangents about her career and "expertise" in eye witness testimony. I love this prof she honestly is an amzing teacher and actually keeps you engaged. The class has a 2 point completion HW due each friday, 2 midterms and one final but honestly as long as you go to class I promise you will do great!

I waited for my time at UCSD to end since I don't like hiding behind anonymous reviews. Dr. Yilmaz is an amazing professor and she got a wrongfully convicted man out of prison. Take the class (especially if ur pre law) to see what I'm talking about. Some find the class hard, some don't, I personally did. But I loved the class. 

- Aria

This class is loaded with a lot of content, but it is doable and is super interesting. Extra credit also helped A LOT.   Overall a kind professor too!

If you're not a good test taker, I highly recommend to not take her class. If you study well however, it is possible to pass. There are weekly readings that are worth 2% and that's it. reviews.comment: Yilmaz is great, these reviews are way too harsh lol. You grade mainly relies on test scores but the tests are completely fair and not that difficult imo. the professor is very passionate and knowledgeable about what she teaches, since it's kind of her research area. Lots of memorization of experiments and terms, if you study well you'll do good on the midterms. She's very funny and makes the lectures entertaining!!

the professor is very passionate and knowledgeable about what she teaches, since it's kind of her research area. Lots of memorization of experiments and terms, if you study well you'll do good on the midterms. She's very funny and makes the lectures entertaining!!

reviews.comment: TRUST me, this course is NOT SUITABLE for beginners. 20 percent of our class has failed, and a question in the final exam is worth 30 percent. I only wrote half a line of code incorrectly and was not given a single point. The score dropped directly from 90 to 60. The professor will test about details he never mentioned

He's one of the best intro CS professors EVER. Has great prewritten notes he annotates, tons of past quizzes, midterms, and finals to practice off of, straightforward PAs that we learn before we work on them, and offers great feedback and advice during lectures and responses. Tests are really manageable and you learn alot

Don't listen to the bad reviews. This man doesn't deserve the hate he gets. This was my FIRST coding class and Prof Cao makes it simple to understand and learn. Midterm was easy/simple (coding was easy) and lab quizzes are simple. Discussion quizzes have redos. Just do the readings and pay attention in class and you'll do fine.

Do not listen to these lies. I skipped class sometimes and I studied with the textbook and it was identical to the teachers assignments. The quizzes get redos like two weeks later and they are the same thing basically. We have lab quizzes and more then half the questions are based on directions. I missed class and would take lab quizzes(100%)

Lectures are mandatory but he goes over the material very fast and it's difficult to keep up for beginners so it honestly feels pointless and podcasts work better. He adds trick questions in quizzes which I find annoying. Overall if you study enough then it shouldn't be too difficult, but it does take up a lot of time if you are a beginner.

two weekly quizzes with little to no time to study, the online textbook is some weird sketchy thing from russia that i think gave me a virus. mandatory 8am lectures, and don't fall for it the "monday discussion" is actually one of the weekly quizzes at 8am. way too hard for a beginner coding class, if i didn't need this class i would've dropped it.

Don't reallt enjoy his teaching style. Quizzes aren't based on understanding, but moreso, your ability to not get tricked by random things. I feel like they hardly measure how much you know in the class.

Even though I skipped alot of my lectures (despite being mandatory), when I went, he makes all the content clear and concise to us through prewritten notes with additional commentary and code that he handwrites during lectures. Projects aren't super difficult and redundant, you just need a good idea of Java logic to understand most of the content.

Great lecturer who knows the material well, but workload can be somewhat busy with PAs every week and zybook readings. He's very patient and answers questions clearly. Overall a great professor to introduce you to data structures. The notes template he provides is also helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I'm not going to lie, I skipped a lot of the lectures even though they were mandatory (you need an iClicker). But the ones I didn't skip he was a great help. Decent choice. Exams are just based on lectures and PA(he sends part exams too). Though reading is required through zybooks, they are not that needed for exam preparation.
The best cse prof for lower div
i very good instuctor, alway very patient. love him

reviews.comment: He explained every question in class clearly, no matter what it was, and his exams are all based on what he talks about in class. Moreover, Paul is a really nice person and you can communicate with him for all your worries and inconvenience.

Initially it was difficult to understand his lectures, but it got better overtime. My favorite part is how he constantly uses real life examples in relation to coding. I just wish he didn't emphasize writing code by hand so much, because you get docked hella even if the logic is right. It ends up being memorization. But tbh, I learned a lot.
getting under 55% in final automatically drops your entire grade, even if you have a A, B or C in the class. He does not care at all

He will get the point across - nothing more, nothing less. He has a very heavy accent that could be hard to understand at times, and has a very annoying passive aggressive tone every time he speaks. He loves 8 AM mandatory iClicker attendance, so get ready for that. Tests were fair, PAs took a lot of time but are great preparations for the tests.
He loves attendance, 8 am, and lots of homework. But the final is really easy, you should get a good grade if you have written the past year's exam.

Many of the negative reviews on Yingjun (Paul) Cao are nit picky and don't fully represent Cao's weaknesses as a lecture. Expect an "asian dad" level energy when coming to lecture, but also the fairness of a lecturer who wants everyone to pass. PA's are tough, but there are plenty resources. You will get what you make of this course. 4/5

Although Paul requires attendance and clickers (although I've heard he might allow the clicker app now), Paul is on the whole a very competent teacher that cares about his students (and his students getting jobs/internships). zyBooks textbook reading can feel annoyingly long (interactive textbook) but isn't difficult. Tests are completely fair.

Professor Cao's CSE12 class is a solid choice. While the lectures can be a bit dry, the content is well-structured and the homework is a great learning tool. Using unstuck AI and the textbook helped me grasp the material, despite the strict attendance policy. Overall, a rewarding class.

Great teacher! He definitely knows what he is talking about and it was so easy to just watch his lectures the day before the test and understand everything. Definitely learned a lot and was still easy to get the grade that I wanted.

content in lectures is way easier compared to homework. Interviews are hard because they want you to basically memorize the lectures and homework. Class is designed so that you will end up being confused and asking questions. Literally says so in syllabus. I don't know why they cant just teach clearly instead of having us guess and check.

good professor teaches well in lectures and is clear on topics for exams. some final and midterm MCQs came from quizzes we had during discussions or Iclicker questions, slight grade curve as well, The cons are $40 eBook for 10% of grade that u lose after quarter, no slip days for PAs, some of which were tedious, lot of content but he made it ez.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He seems dry at first, but you can tell he cares a lot about teaching. Mandatory attendance through iClicker questions, but they often show up on tests. $40 online textbook for mandatory weekly readings. Weekly coding assignments are very fair. MCQ quizzes during discussion. The class teaches you a lot while not being really hard at all.

Coming from a non-cs major who didn't take CSE 8A before this, it was definitely one of the hardest classes I've taken across the board. The weekly PAs were difficult and time-consuming, and he uses iclicker to check attendance. Spent a lot of time reading the textbook and attending multiple tutor sessions per week to get an A in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The PAs are much harder than the content he covered in lectures, really monotone lectures that came with strict attendance policies.

Monotone lecture that came with strict attendance requirements, heavy accent, and homework heavy. I think the lectures weren't beneficial for my learning and I'd rather just self-study through the assigned reading.

Like the previous comment, it's hard to understand him in lecture because of his monotone, heavy accent. He's also unresponsive to emails. Honestly, the lectures/lecture worksheets don't really help much and I feel very lost after them - you'll need to get help from TAs or tutors.
I cannot understand his lec, the monotone and thick accent make learning a hard topic 10x hard.

I am not sure if he is different for other CS classes, but the PAs were extremely difficult. Although it is an accelerated version of an intro class, he did not explain the material well. His lecture notes were useless and he did not really provide hands-on examples of concepts. I am thankful for the grade that I received, but wouldn't recommend.

Really good lectures and posts podcasts too, but clicker attendance is taken. Gives multiple chances for quizzes. Midterm and Final are not too hard. PAs are.. well PAs, get as much points as you can as they worth a lot. Very easy to understand and very patient. Overall a really solid professor and would definitely recommend!

Good professor, as long as you know basic cs stuff you should be fine even though its an accelerated class. Many concepts on the tests come from the PAs, so make sure to do the PAs and try and understand them. Overall, good class.

I had a medical emergency that took me out of school for a whole week, and Prof. Cao was more than understanding about my situation.  Fantastic professor that explains concepts thoroughly without digressing at all and keeps the class engaged with the perfect amount of participation questions.  His HW is a great learning tool.  Highly recommend
PAs and tests weren't too bad. He's a nice guy. Only downside is he requires lecture attendance with iclickers. I would say he's better than Miranda.

Probably one of the best CSE professors you can have. 

Exams and PAs correlate with what is taught. He also takes feedback from students since he actually listens to what the students have to say.
He teaches well and the structure of the class(workload) actually makes you learn a lot. However, it is tough for non-cs majors and he expects everyone taking this course to have cs major knowledge.
Great lecturer-made content very easy to understand. Programming assignments were easy and interesting. The midterm and final were also relatively easy. Only bad thing was the mandatory attendance.

He's teaching at a very fast pace and this class is not for beginners! There are four programming assignments in total and two exams. BUT he will randomly select 10% of the people at the end of the session for an interview of about 30 minutes!!! If you don't attend the interview, the grade will not be reported. Highly do not recommend this class!
One of my favorite professors in UCSD. His CSE 11, 12, and 100 are somewhat harder than other professors, but doable. You would learn a lot.

One of the best CSE profs I've had so far. His lectures consist of introducing the topic and providing a lot of examples/questions to help develop your understanding of the material. He definitely cares about his students. His PA's weren't too hard but his quizzes were pretty tricky which can be tough at times. Great prof, definitely take him.
My favorite CSE professor at UCSD.
Coding is awful. The prof is cool but why assign all these other assignments, readings, and homeworks, if we are just going to forget it or not be tested on it.

The professor taught content well, but a lot of times I felt it was completely unnecessary to go to lecture since he always assigned a huge amount of pre-lecture reading, that covered everything he was going to teach. After doing the reading, lecture just felt repetitive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Definitively one of the best CSE professors in UCSD.

This class is doable even if you have no experience in coding, like me. the PAs were kind of hard, but starting early and going to tutoring actually helped a lot. There are a lot of components to the final grade so even if you bomb a test it is possible to still do fine in the class. Overall, pretty good and simple class even if u dislike coding.
gives extra credits and curve!

One thing to say: DO YOUR PAs EARLY! Paul's PAs were quite fun, though it took some time to fully understand it. Otherwise, it's mostly using techniques we learnt in class. I enjoyed the way Paul taught CSE8A, it was very engaging with the constant questions to test your understanding of the material. I would take another class with Paul!
Solid professor for CSE 12. Tests and PAs were fair.

Really tough class for people without any previous coding experience. Prof. Cao is a strict person with indifferent attitude. His lectures are so confusing, and extremely hard to apply what we learned in class to the weekly programming assignments.

Paul is such a caring professor. I had no comp sci experience and went in completely blind, but he clearly puts in a lot of effort when it comes to teaching. He took to the time to create and pass out worksheets just so everyone could follow along. Complete all the assignments and you should be fine.

Professor Cao was the best professor I had in Fall 2021. I found the lectures to be clear, interesting, and engaging. Midterms and Final were fairly easy. PAs were great in further establishing coding concepts as well as your own skills

I took CSE 8A with professor Cao this quarter. I had no prior experience with python, and professor Cao was able to make learning this language clear and simple. He is very funny and uses good examples. The hardest part of the class is the PAs, make sure you start early and make use of tutor hours! The TA tutors are extremely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: we did python for 8A this quarter. Generally speaking, this class is easy A.

Do not take him!!!!!! He is been hyped!!!! His PAs are so hard and usually take one day to finish it and you will feel like you are tortured by the PAs mentally. The quizzes are tricky. His explanations and hints of the PAs are useless. Do not take him unless you like your mind suffering from torture once a week!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Cao is an amazing teacher. Just make sure to start early on the PAs so that you will be able to get help from autograder tutors. You will need it. Don't expect to do well in the course if you start the night of or the night before. Make sure you study for the midterms and finals (go over all quizzes, pas, and lectures). STAY CAUGHT UP ON LECTURES!

Paul is a really nice professor and he explains things well. He would use real life examples that are easy to understand to explain hard concepts. Took 8B and 12 with him and learned a great deal from his classes. PAs are time consuming but it's worth the time to do it.

Paul is very funny and explains the material clearly. Programming assignments can be overwhelming at times, but they are clearly explained and structured. They can be too structured at times though, sometimes there's little thought involved. Textbook work is mandatory, but I found it easy and also very useful.

Cao is really good at explaining concepts that could be really tough to understand otherwise. The PAs were time-consuming but they definitely helped solidify my knowledge. During our quarter, he co-taught the class with Greg Miranda, so they had the same lectures, assignments, and exams - which seems like it will be a theme going forward.

His lectures are very informative as his solid understanding allows him to effectively explain many concepts. The PAs get to be pretty time consuming, but there is always help available. Lectures were not mandatory but were very helpful. Readings are also pretty helpful. Prior experience in CS really helps reduce the workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Terrible Professor. Workloads are insane, and PAs are hard, confusing and tricky. Lots of hidden cases that are very hard to think about. Average of PAs grade are around 85-90%. Tests are very trick and test more on the concept rather than code. Test are open everything but the average is 80%. No extra credit. DONT TAKE HIM.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He was alright. He seemed to have a direct grasp of the knowledge and he answered most of the questions that students had but he did overlook some stuff that made the PAs harder than it needed to be and his final was hard compared to what he gave for the midterm. Overall, solid prof but do not be surprised by harder than usual exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Cao taught me data structures and it was wonderful. The PAs are directly related to the material of the lecture. Overall a wonderful experience.
Spent 3 quarters with Paul. Definitely a great prof! Always get wonderful grades by the end of the quarters! Lectures are amazing with insightful contents.

HE IS THE BEST. He cares about students and going to his office hours helps so much. And most importantly, he explains concepts with easy examples, which make so much more sense than just reading off the textbook.

I took his CSE8B and CSE100. One of the best professors in CSE Department. You really learn A LOT from his lectures. PAs are time consuming but worth doing them. Hope he can teach some upper division courses and I will definitely take them.

Highly recommend if you really wanna learn something. His assignment could be quite hellish if you have no previous experience in programming, but are pretty helpful. And most of all, he's lectures are always helpful with a lot of details, and he explains the material quite well.
Paul is one of the best CSE lecturers/professors at UCSD. He is really good at explaining materials. His PAs are hard but as long as you spend time on them, you will learn a looot from them.

Worst Professor I have taken so far . Workloads are insane, tests are meant to trick you with tiny descriptive language, during office hours hes very intimidating and will talk down to you not very helpful at all!. His podcasts lack details and he just talks in terrible monotone. Reading Quiz due every class meeting . Not lenient by any means.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Pros: podcast available, reasonable exams, explain concepts super well, take advice from students, iclicker discussion Cons: bursting workload of PAs, there are times when I spent tons of time and effort on one PA yet still get horrible grade (might bc i'm dumb af), he sound strict and mean at times but doesn't hurt

Hellish workload. Midterms and final were CSE-level, not too difficult. But the PA were difficult and lengthy, easily 20 hours a week. Fixed somewhat after multiple Piazza and TA requests. PA grading was strict (examining output) because expected in future upperCSE, but killed my grades. Professor was fine, but curved grades indicated difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Cao is one of my favorite professors at UCSD, and I definitely learned a lot in this course. He cares about preparing students for the industry, and he's very reasonable. If you're good at computer science or are willing to put in the work, this class should be very fun and fairly easy.

grading is unreasonable, prof do not take suggestions and doesnt care about student concerns. Need to spend long time to do the PA especially in the beginning of the quarter. Exams are not very hard but not as easy as the practice. Overall lecture is fine, you learn a lot. Worst cse prof in my entire college life

He gives out really simple past/sample exams, but then increase the difficulty by a lot during the actual exam. He also doesn't take suggestions from students very often. But aside from those, cool guy.

The worst professor I've ever seen. He doesn't take students' advices or concerns. I'm literally kicked off from his office when trying to tell him what's wrong with the course. He's not caring enough to be a professor. His PAs are not hard to finish, but hard to understand. 20+h to understand the requirements from piazza, and 10h actual coding.:)

CSE8A and CSE8B thought by him are really fun. You can finish many interesting programs even though you are just a beginner. However, his CSE100 is hard and he is trying to make harder. Even though exams are easy, PAs take over 24 hours and you may not make it correct. I suggest to take CSE8A/B with him but dont take CSE100 with him!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: One of the best professors Ive had at UCSD. He really knows his stuff. I highly recommend you take his classes if you have the choice. The only slight drawback is that his accent can be a little bit difficult to understand at times.

Cao was an inspiration teacher for CSE8. However the way he is managing CSE100 in intense. The workload is too much for PA1 and PA2 and students are spending countless hours on a waiting queue, but the tutors are changing to fix some difficulty. The PA write-ups are partially vague. His midterm and lectures are just like CSE8, but PA are hellish.

PAs are not extremely difficult, but they are time consuming Lecture is mandatory, Caring for students and listen to feedback Exams are not hard once you get the concept, I barely passed the first quiz and midterm, and got 100% on final after spent a lot of time studying the past exams

He does his best to keep their students on their toes but the teaching method was not very good. Attendance is mandatory because he will only hand out 'printed' class notes in class. Also don't even try to look for code snippets online, he will report you for Academic Integrity violation. Has heavy accent and difficult to understand.
