The final exam was 261 out of 236, and average was 236, literally 100 percent. I would highly recommend Paul if you want to learn CS well. The class is by no mean easy, but I definitely enjoy the material in cs30
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Paul is a horrible professor. "I want to conserve the integrity of UCSD " his words, not mine. He upped the difficulty of this class as if it wasn't already difficult enough. Never taking him again. Rather wait a whole quarter if he's the only choice.

If you go to the lectures and do the reading you will probably get the concept. He really explains things really well, the lecture is structural and clear. But the PAs are really time-consuming and tough, and you don't want to expect an extension. The quizzes and mid-term are tricky, I got a 50% on the midterm. The final is ok I got 100%.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He really cares your learning and will take in student feedback. He would modify the class if the majority of the opinion reflected that they want the change. Awesome prof!
One the best Professors at UCSD.

His final is so tricky, and no curve. You need to spend millions of time to do his psa, but you still cannot make sure you get a good grade. I did really hard work, but I still cannot get an A rather than A-.

The best way I can describe Paul is that he is a caring and very much a dad-figure to every one in the class. He makes it his goal to help you understand the rather confusing topics in Java and the in class examples (clicker questions) are incredibly helpful in demonstrating the nuances in the code. Do his quizzes on time and pay attention for an A
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Paul (Yingjun) knows what he is talking about and makes sure you understand. Reading quizzes three times per week and weekly programming assignments. The PA's can be time consuming and you will probably need help to complete them. 3 easy in-class quizzes.

Paul (Yingjun) clearly knows what he is talking about and makes sure you do too. Reading quizzes three times per week, review quizzes and programming assignments due once per week. Weekly lab sections are useful. He has plenty of office hours and there are always tutors in the lab if you need help.

If you want to learn Java, you should take this class. Paul (Yingjun) Cao goes into great depth explaining concepts, and will pause the lecture to expand on a concept if he feels that the class doesn't get a concept. Even though the PAs are time consuming, I found them relatively straightforward and educational. I did stuff last minute and got a B+

He explains things really well. You can understand him clearly even if you don't have any programming experience previously. The programming assignments are a little tough but you will really learn the concepts better after finishing them. Besides, most of the time the assignments are really fun. Good luck!
Knows his stuff. Reading quizzes every alternate day, review quizzes every week. Additional PSAs due every week. Lectures are informative and count for a small percentage of final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He's a great professor who really tries to make sure everyone understands and does well. Do your work and you're almost guaranteed an A. Easy midterms and final. Great class overall and great prof!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: A very good professor, can explain things very clear when you have a question.

A fast paced class with too many quizzes and very difficult weekly assignments. Paul Cao is a caring professor who values feedback, but his class is just much too fast-paced especially for beginning coders.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Paul Cao is a nice professor and tries really hard to make you understand the material, but the material itself is really difficult. There are too many quizzes that we have to take and you can never relax in the class because PSA's are due every week and they take forever to do. Midterm was hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof. Cao is a well-respected teacher among all my friends. He is kind, accessible outside of class, and sometimes with unexpected humor. His course is well designed and well prepared. Follow his reading assignments, handouts, practice exams, programming assignments and lecture. You will find his assignments doable because he gets you ready.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Cao is a great instructor. He truly cares about your learning and will help you without judgement, especially on your exams. His lectures are a little hard to follow but he will slow down if you ask him to. There are quizzes during class but as long as you do your PSAs and attend lectures, you should be set. Studying is strongly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: If you concentrate on lectures you won't need the book at all. You will get an easy A if you take him
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: has a clear grading standard to follow. easy to pick up all the point.

Professor Cao's class has been my favorite at ucsd so far. Attendance is mandatory, but I enjoyed his lectures. Exams were very fair. I appreciate that he asks for criticism and comments from his students to improve his own teaching.
Overall a good professor. Exam and quiz got harder this quarter but you should be fine if you study and pay attention during lecture.

Mr. Cao is a wonderful teacher. His lectures are very well structured, and deliver important information. There are reading quizzes due on the morning of each lecture, so reading is important. His class is not extremely difficult, but it isn't a catwalk. 10/10 would take again

One of the best professor. True. The class is time consuming. Reading quizzes, PSA, but all the cse classes are. It is not his fault.  The class is not that hard if you just follow his step. Professor Can is approachable and inspiring. Clear in explaining concepts. I think the university should let him teach more cse classes. He really cares about

Professor Cao is the best professor I've had at UCSD so far! His lectures are packed with valuable knowledge and material so going to lectures will definitely help your grade. All his PAs are explained very clearly and graded fairly as well. He's one of those professor where going to lecture is actually really worth it! Definitely recommend!

This is the second class that I took with Professor Cao. In general, he is responsible that he uses podcasts and posts the slides online timely. However, he assumes too much knowledge you should know before class, and usually he doesn't explain very clear. His lecture has a lot of discussion which he could have spent those time lecturing.
For those who claim Cao is not clear enough, I think  they won't find any  cs professor they like  in ucsd.  Take him, you will get an easy A and have solid cs fundation.

Very veerrrry nice person!!! It is really my pleasure to meet such a nice CSE professor. The final is very identical to all the previous works we had done so far. He gives all the materials such as podcast, past papers, lecture slides notes, study guide, etc. You can prepare all well and develop a strong base of CSE. Take this prof!!!

There's a lot of work in this class. (Labs, quizzes, homework, midterms) He posts everything online. He even posted the podcast of when we took our midterm, so it was a podcast of us staring at a watch for 80 minutes. But he is pretty good at explaining and he tries really hard. Getting a passing grade isn't hard, but you have to work for the A.
Fun class, great professor. Never leaves anyone behind.

Good prof.  Very clear and fair.  He challenges you to know material, but if you put in the effort and start hw early, you can definitely get an A. Just START EARLY and go to tutors for help and you are golden
CSE 8B is harder than 8A, but you have so many chances to get extra credits. Problem Solving Assignments are more fun but more time-consuming. Get ready to devote a couple weekends to PSAs!

Most would say accent is a problem, but it really is not. Attend lecture or watch podcast, and the tests would be chill. PAs will take time, especially pa2 (start wordcloud early). TA's are great. Tutors are great. In essence, he knows what he is doing.

Wouldn't have been the same without Cao! He's able to explain concepts well and in a way that's easy to understand. Granted, there are certain topics that are just harder to grasp, but he genuinely cares for his students and how they are performing. Coding assignment range from really hard to easy, and quizzes and exams are not hard but not easy

During my quarter, I believe that he gave an incredibly high number of quizzes. I think that 7 quizzes in 2 weeks is a bit too much. He was pretty unclear when he was explaining and I honestly learnt more from the internet than I did from him. Overall, I would not recommend this teacher based of this quarter's experiences.

I think Professor Cao is a very passionate teacher, however, I didn't gain much from his class. There were a few too many quizzes, tests, and assignments that set the expectations for the class to be a bit higher than I could realistically achieve. Many students like him but I became disenfranchised rather quickly and would not take his class again

I love Professor Cao! He explains everything very clearly and goes through each problem in detail even if no one asks (in case you're shy). There are lots of good examples&info in clicker questions that will help on projects! He's very kind with grading and extra help, and he takes time before class to just sit down and chat with students :)
He is a nice professor. He explains things clearly and his tests are fair
Professor Cao is super patient. However hard ur question is, he will answer u wiz a lot of details and make sure u understand it.
His classes are interesting and the exams are not too hard.

Awesome class. He was very clear and you knew exactly what he wanted you to know thanks to his good use of iclicker questions. My only problem with the class was the fact every assignment (once a week) was with a partner. All around, easy and well-educating class. And he podcasts. Find the book online.

Professor Cao teaches the material well and allows the students ample time to discuss questions amongst themselves. The course material was easy in itself so it's hard to say how much he really helped me. The one thing I really liked about him was how he made an effort to talk to students outside the class. Great professor!
Gives a lot of discussion time

Cao is an excellent, helpful, and reassuring professor.  1st midterm average was 92%, and the day the first project was due, he opened up tutor hours until midnight.  He has an accent, but is easy enough to understand.  Attendance is mandatory.  "It's normal to become frustrated when programming.  But don't get discouraged; you can do it!" -Cao
Awesome, one of the best professor that I have ever met. His lectures are so interesting and helpful!
Very good professor, very clear about what is needed for the students to get good grades. He always give good feedback and is very nice to students and very patient to students' questions.
The professor is very knowledgable and lectures are good. All the information for the tests are in the lectures, but the tests are hard

Really knowledgeable as a VLSI researcher, but not a good teacher at all. I had to self-study everything and the lectures were not useful. He also goes out of his way to make practice hard for students by not providing answer keys for practice problem sets and did not even provide any practice problems at all for the last chapter before the final.

Amazing prof. Approachable and explains every concept in a detailed and easy to understand manner. Exams can be challenging, but the class exercises and problem sets prepare you well. Very transparent about grading and expectations. Would highly recommend taking this class!

Worst class I've ever taken at ucsd. This dude will give out recordings delayed by a week. And he gave 0 practice exams, problem sets are unrelated to the exams themselves. All grades were based on exams and lab. No curve, TA bad as well. No examples in lectures, only bunch of theory and he explains them poorly. Take mingu kang instead of this guy.

Really good professor. Explains concepts in a clear and understandable way, and is clearly very passionate about the topics in VLSI. Answers questions with patience and want his students to learn everything that he has to offer. Take ECE 108 with him, highly recommend!

extremely clear explanations for anyone new to coding or stats. iclicker during lecture counts towards grade. overall grade is based on coding labs, concept checks and exams which are self explanatory if you understand the material well, but memorizing questions won't be enough; truly understand the coding syntax and concepts.
Incredibly passionate about research and the subjects. Cares a lot about his students. Provides really good feedback and is incredibly accessible. Literally no critiques.
Great guy, very helpful. If you ever ask a question, he will explain it in a way that makes sure you understand.

He is nice & respected, but the class is VERY time consuming. The study guides felt vague about what details matter, so I spent a lot of time learning material that did not end up on the exams. His practice questions are not enough to prepare you. Final class grade averages seem to range from C+ to B-. No curves. Only take him w/ lighter classes

Ming very clearly cares about his students both inside and outside of the classroom. He is such a passionate teacher and is great at explaining coding and statistics. He is extremely approachable and hosts several hours of office hours per week to provide additional support to students. His exam study materials prepare you immensely for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You can tell Professor Yang teaches because he loves teaching itself! Clear explanations and beautiful slide animations as well. Though the fixed grading scale and plethora of assignments seemed intimidating at first, I did find BILD 5 to be on the lighter side. Do note that I have taken (AP Stats +) Math 11 and coding (AP CSA) prior.

Professor Yang was probably the best professor I have had in my academic career so far. His class is very organized and know what to expect. Exams are hard and need to study alot but it is expected for the class. Exam heavy 2 mid terms and final in 2 parts 1 cumulative the other on the last bit of class. Provides study guide and problem sets for ex

Ming is an amazing and caring professor. Yes the class is hard, but I thought it was all completely fair. Exam averages were around 70%, but he padded everyone's grades with other things so the median grade was a B overall. I honestly don't understand why people find any of this unreasonable.

One of my favorite professors; cares about students, passionate, & makes the material easily digestible despite physio being a hard course, and he makes all the slides himself. I recommend going to office hours because he's so helpful, like if you have ANY questions about the material he immediately has the answer. Got a B+ tho, final was tricky..

Yang is a really nice person and encouraging. He can make class really engaging and easy to listen to. The only thing is his exams are worth most of your grade with there being two midterms and a final. Exams are hard to process. His class isn't curved and not much extra credit opportunities. His final average came out to a C- and felt very unfair
He is so kind, caring and dedicated. it is BIPN so you have to study a lotttt for a good grade but his exams are fair. He provides problems sets and practice questions.
He is such a nice professor who cares about students and is always present at every office hour, including those hosted by the TAs.

SO nice and fun lectures BUT grading was humbling since there was no curve/barely any EC. His lectures are very simple and straight to the point, but when it came to exam prep/study, study guides did not reflect test difficulty. Supa cool guy but favors strong test takers AND grade was 75% exams. Expects u to remember every single detail rip
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ming really cares about his students and this class. He really wants you to do well, and there is lots of opportunities to seek help outside of class. The class isn't curved, although the lectures are extremely clear and engaging. As long as you understand the lecture material you will do well in class. Cheat sheets allowed as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: take him for bild 5 if u can! genuinely the best prof here. his lectures are easy to follow & he does review at the beginning of each lecture to make sure everyone understands before moving onto new topics. plus, hes a cutie patootie :3 (idk why u guys hate him for bipn 100, but hes great for bild 5)
GOAT!!! Best professor at UCSD!

He's a decent professor and explains the material well, but the grading style for select-all-that-apply questions can be frustrating. Even if you choose multiple correct answers, selecting one wrong option can cancel out points. It feels a bit unfair when you mostly know the material but still lose credit.

Practice material didn't match exam style, making preparation hard. Class would be more engaging if we applied topics before exams. Lectures often felt rushed, which hurt clarity; some material might have been better covered via Zoom or recordings.

Ming is the best professor I've had at UCSD. He lectures very passionately and clearly and all of the content he teaches as well as the study guides are reflective of actual exam content. However, BIPN 100 is a tough course. Attendance is mandatory. Don't miss lectures. Grind all the practice problems for the exam. Grading criteria is clear.

Ming is a phenomenal professor and person. He shows up everyday with a smile on his face. His lectures are extremely clear and he repeats important concepts frequently to make sure we fully understand. He's very accessible in and out of the classroom. He's very supportive, often celebrating mid lecture to tell us he's proud of us for showing up.

Ming is actually the best professor ever.  He is so passionate about what he teaches and he truly cares about his students. His lectures are clear and his exams follow the practice questions almost exactly. He makes this course about as easy as it can get so I would recommend taking it with him! I would take a bullet for Ming tbh he's the goat

Ming is passionate and knowledgeable, but he is a tough grader and the course demands a lot of time. Many students advise not taking it alongside other heavy classes. There is also little accommodation for students who are busy or can't regularly attend office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While some students may have found the resources sufficient, that was not my experience. The course was extremely exam-heavy, and exam difficulty felt disproportionate to lectures and practice material. With no curve, a single poor exam had a major impact, making the course feel unforgiving despite effort and office hours.

Mingyu Yang was a great professor and you could really tell he cares for the course! The course was test heavy and a lot of work but similar to any other upper division course work. Everything was manageable with the amount of resources provided both in class and out of class (OH, emails etc.)

In my experience, this class was very challenging. The professor does not curve grades, so exam performance directly determines your final grade. The exams felt significantly harder than the practice material, so strong preparation is essential. Students who prefer structured guidance or a forgiving grading system may find this course difficult.
AVOID THIS PROFESSOR AT ALL COST. HE ALSO DOESNT CURVE THE CLASS SO THE GRADE YOU GET IS THE GRADE YOU GET.
Take BIPN 100 with him. Fantastic prof

Professor Ming tries to teach clearly, but the material is overwhelming and even his best isn't enough. Exams are harsh, minor errors cost points, and success favors only strong test takers. A small cheat sheet could have helped manage the heavy content.

This class mostly favors strong test takers. Ming teaches clearly but is a strict grader, deducting points for small mistakes. If you're not good at exams, it feels unfair. Success depends on adapting to how he frames questions and grades.

Ming may lecture clearly, but the exams are poorly aligned with what's taught and feel unnecessarily tricky. Effort doesn't reliably translate into grades. If this course isn't required for your major, taking it at a community college is a much better option since exams are more fair and actually reflect the material.

Ming explains concepts well, but the exams don't reflect what's emphasized in class and are unnecessarily tricky. If this course isn't required for your major, taking it at a community college is likely a better option, as the exams are usually more aligned with the material and easier to prepare for.

Physiology is already a hard class, and Ming does not do a strong job introducing new material. Lectures feel rushed and unclear, forcing a lot of self-teaching. That's frustrating when you're juggling other demanding classes or work. Expecting students to rely on in-person study sessions ignores commuters who can't stay on campus.

Best professor ever!! This class is hard whoever you take it with, but Professor Yang makes it doable and he cares SO MUCH. Don't be scared away by the review below. everyone else agrees his exams are hard but fair, and he gives you practice problems and a clear study guide.

The PCAs and practice problems don't prepare you for the exams at all. He tells students not to overstudy, but the exams expect tiny details straight from slides. Feels like mixed messages and leaves you blindsided. Be ready to self-teach most of the material.

He is the best. He genuinely makes you want to lear, his vibes and enthusiasm are out of this world. The content is difficult but he does a great job teaching it. Lots of practice, always helpful and you get extra credit. His exams are a fair representation of the homework, concept checks and other practice.

Class Structure: Uses Icliker (for class credit on completion!) and weekly concept checks. MANY practice problems, lots of structure! There is a lot of content and the expectation def isn't low, but he really believes that you can do it, and getting an A is 100% doable if you put in the work & attend office hours. 

Best prof I've ever had!!

This is by far my favorite professor of all time, literally the sweetest and most dedicated person I have ever met! He assigns pre-lecture assignments that are 5 minutes long. The class is fun and engaging, and we have weekly online quizzes. This is the only class I feel like has truly reflected the lectures and my time studying. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!

Professor Yang's lectures are very engaging with iClickers and concept checks (one try but collaborative). PCA pre-class assignments give a valuable preview of upcoming material. Attendance isn't required but helps your grade. Practice and extra problem sets are valuable for exam prep and mastering concepts. His clarity makes learning enjoyable.

He was alright. I wish I tried harder for my first midterm and final because I didn't do very well, but he was generous with points back, not gonna lie. However, he did replace my low midterm score with what I got on my final so that was clutch

AMAZING professor! His exams reflect a plethora of practice questions he provides (sometimes re-using some). This class is very tough but he does a wonderful job of condensing and explaining concepts in all his lectures. You can tell he is passionate about the subject and truly cares and wants his students to pass. Will take him again for BIPN 103
not sure why he thought it was a good idea to overwhelm us with the final. His midterms were chill, but he went rogue for two finals
Fantastic professor.
Extremely clear about grading expectations, very forgiving and fair grader (he gave back points on tests  if the class got low averages/agreed that a question is unfair), he's fun

He's literally the most caring and happy professor I've met at UCSD. Joined the course 2 weeks behind schedule, emailed him about my situation, and he offered so many ways for me to catch up with the class. Offers many extra credit and help opportunities. Super friendly and makes the lectures fun.

Professor Ming is such a respectful and fun professor. He really takes the time to explain something to you when you don't understand. I struggled a bit with coding but he was always very patient with me and let me fix my code. He is also really funny to talk to. I definitely recommend going to office hours when you need help, he never judges you!

The best professor I've ever had. Will absolutely be trying to take a class with him again in the future. He cares so much, is so easy to contact. He pours his heart into his lectures and attends ALL discussions so you can talk directly with him at any time. I truly loved him and this class so much (and I cannot code for the life of me).

He is always so passionate and excited. This was his first quarter teaching because he just graduated but he is very specific, organized, and has clear expectations. Decent extra credit and grade replacement for final. He puts so much effort into being available outside of class and wants everyone to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Mingyu is a very good professor. His class was full of passion. And he responds to emails really quick. But the coding in BILD 5 sometimes can be really harsh. And the data generator for the final project doesn't always provide good data. Be prepared for the coding!

Ming is by far the best professor I have had at UCSD. His course structure maximizes learning and sets students up for success. BIPN is a dense course, but Ming does a great job making it easier to digest. His tests are hard but fair, and he tells you everything you need to know on the study guide, so there are never any surprises.

Professor Yang is a a very good and passionate lecturer and wants to make sure you understand the material. If you are familiar with python and statistics, this class will be a breeze. Midterm and Final are very similar to practice material. I would definitely take him again if he taught another R-related course.

Ming is a kind and caring professor, and breaks down the content in a way that isn't difficult to understand. The examples provided in lecture were helpful in understanding the concepts, he was available outside of class and genuinely cared about students' success.

He's really good, the course for bipn100 is an upper-div so expect a lot of work and memorization. Study the material given each week to be prepared for the final since it's all cumulative by the end -- but the finals are divided into midterm 1 and 2 stuff, then the stuff after it. So humble he's scared to check his score on here. Would take again.

His class felt like UCSD premium. His organization of the course and content is so well put together. He has pre-recorded videos to introduce the lecture and provides tons of study material (study guides for ea. week/exam, weekly concept checks, study sessions). Super nice and funny. JHU + MIT-Harvard combo go crazy (inspirational).
Mingyu is my king

Great teacher he's so sweet. Sometimes the content gets complicated but all of the IAs and the teacher are welcoming. Assignments are also management. Be prepared to do a final project with about a week to do though. Also DO YOUR SETs/teacher evaluations

Ming was a great teacher. He's very organized so it's easy to learn the content. The course is hands on and manageable, with a concept check and coding lab each week. You can tell he genuinely cares about his students and he's extremely bubbly. Just work hard and keep up. For it being his first time teaching BILD 5, he hit it out of the ball park.

Ming has been one of my best professors in my college career. He genuinely cares about his students and their learning. His class consisted of weekly quizzes and a coding lab which were not difficult and if anyone had troubles he was easily accessible. He additionally had a midterm, final project, and final. I highly recommend for BILD 5!

Prof. Yang is amazing. He makes sure students understand the material and attends all discussion sections. He's very accessible and puts in full effort to help us succeed. I had no coding experience, but his office hours were super helpful. He's encouraging, sweet, and funny. Don't be afraid to ask for help. I highly recommend him!
Makes his curriculum and class tailored to the success of his students. Attendance is based on iClickers, best teacher I've had so far.

He was a good professor. I lwk hated that we had clickers but his lectures are needed to help understand  coding but it was nice that there was only one Midterm and it wasn't weighed that heavily. The assignments aren't long either so that helps grades a lot!!
He is a nice professor and his class is interesting.

I took BIPN100 with him during winter, and he was definitely one of my favorite professors. His lectures are engaging, and he explains complex concepts exceptionally well. His exams are fair, but you do need to spend time reviewing. He is super nice, and I would recommend everyone to take his classes.
He the best professor ever, i wish all my classes could be taught by him!!

TAKE HIM!! He is the BEST professor I have since coming to university! He has the best lecture style with super organized slides! Although participation was required, he truly made the lectures engaging. Fair grading and problem sets super similar to exams. I especially like that he provides study guide for exams so you know what to focus on.

mingyu is so king, i love his class so much because of the support he gives us, we have one multiple choice midterm, concept check and coding lab every week but theyre super easy once you get the hang of things!! He also gives us practice questions for our midterm which r super helpful for studying. Overall, he's great !

He is the best professor I have ever had in my entire life. He is INCREDIBLE at teaching, and does not expect you to have any prior experience or knowledge. Professor Yang is the sweetest and understanding professor! You can tell how much he prepares for each lecture. I seriously hope he teaches every biology class so I can take him in the future.

First upper div class I took and couldn't ask for a better professor. Physiology can be very content heavy and difficult to conceptually grasp but Prof. Ming broke everything down into beautiful slides and graphs. He deeply cares for students and his lectures were always engaging. His tests can be difficult but manageable with proper preparation.

Best professor I've ever had. He's so genuine and does everything he can to make difficult content as accessible and engaging as possible. Really clear, fun lectures and overall just a wonderful person!

Prof Ming is a relatively new professor in teaching BIPN, but he is goated. He's caring, the type of professor that really relates to students and does everything to ensure your learning. The thing I like the most is his Pre-Class Assignment, he makes videos himself that cover every chapter, making it easier for students to do preview.
Pretty easy class, and you'll definitely get something out of it.

A lot of reading which is kind of insane for a remote and DEI class but pretty much just skimmed through the text and passed. Participate in discussions as chunk of your grade comes from it. Only 3 assignments that were pretty straightforward. Did learn about history often not covered in education curriculum tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is pretty laidback. There's not a lot of homework rather a big group project assigned at the beginning of the quarter. The project was a bit disorganized. Some of the ideas taught in class are structured to change your mind. If you are neutral of class material there shouldnt be a problem. The final exam is also another project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There is a lot of reading for this class but I guarantee you will learn something new that will genuinely change or reform your opinions. The class is incredibly interesting and it is pretty easy to get an A as out of the three assignments, two are fun projects and only one is a short written piece.

Sections are required. There's only 3 assignments, along with section attendance on the grade. I went to 0 lectures, and read nothing and got 100%. But the professor is really passionate and knowledgeable about the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far best professor that I've taken at UCSD, she is so passionate about what she teaches about. Lecture consisted of teaching + class discussion, and participation does matter. I had a lot going on and communicated that w/ her & she was so nice and understanding about assignments. She also creates a welcoming space for POC & low income students.

The topic is pretty interesting, even for someone outside of the major. The readings are the strength of the class- they're insightful. The lectures are dry and hard to focus on. She's very kind and knows her stuff well, but terminology often gets you lost. Some terms are broad but have specific uses that feel difficult to memorize. Read and pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is amazing! Those that are saying otherwise have grown up in close-minded environments and have not been exposed to opinions from those in the peripheries and margins of society.

Be honest, I may not like the content of the class. I don't agree with some of the opinions. Other than this, if you are neutral of class material. Be aware that this class tends to brainwash you. It really ask you to answer those questions with their opinions, not yours. I don't care this class is easy A or not. It is extremely politically right
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: shes great alot of readings but if you go to lecture then youll be fine reading across text is key. Just study and you will suceed

Professor Espiritu is an exceptional professor. She is so passionate and bubbly and really makes you leave the lecture feeling enlightened. This class is really easy and if you attend lecture you are guaranteed an A. Professor Espiritu is easily my favorite professor at UCSD and I want to take every class she offers !

Professor Yen is great! She is knowledgeable in her field and makes many valid points in framing our culture. However, if you are not generally interested in the field of ethnic studies/interdisciplinary work, you should not take this class. Many professors in this field require an open mind and interest, not an easy A course.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS OR THIS TEACHER. I AM CURRENTLY TAKING THIS CLASS AND IT IS NOT CLEAR IT IS NOT STRAIT THE TEACHER TEACHES IN CIRCLES CLAIMING THAT WE MUST UNDERSTAND CONCEPTS FORMULATIONS AND EXAMPLES WHEN SHE ONLY GOES OVER VOCABULARY IN CLASS. Requires 100 PAGES OF "ETHNIC" papers. For non ethnic studies major dont take this class.
Extremely helpful. Easy to understand.
I learned something new and valuable in every lecture. One of the best professors I've ever had. Definitely take her if you can!

Excellent teacher. She is a respected scholar in the subject of race and ethnicity. I learned alot in this class and recommend it to everyone because we all need to be aware of the role that race plays in our society. Take her you fool!
class is really boring.  shes a good teacher.  lots of reading.  all depends on the ta.  which mine is not that great.
The material was difficult, however I learned so much in the class.  She is willing to clarify, but her papers are difficult. Go to office hours.. you'll be fine. She likes that.
Awesome!! Learned a great deal from her class. She's not easy but excellent in conveying her topics. Clear and concise. I still use her lectures for qoutes for my other classes.

Espiritu was awesome. Class was clear and very insightful. Sometimes hard to understand with her accent, but mostly clear. TA's are very helpful. The class teaches you soo much about Asian American studies. A really good undergrad class!! Totally recommend her.

Every class I took with her was hard because she really makes you think!  But they were the most valuable classes any undergraduate can take.  You can feel yourself gaining IQ points in her classes.  The most important things I ever learned in school I lea
awesome professor...extremely kind and caring, interested in what students had to say...one of the classes i looked forward to attending.
The professor is cute (personality and physically). The bulk of the class was focused on Filipinos, not Vietnamese. However the final project was enjoyable.

He's a ok lecturer. However, he goes through lecture very fast and it can get confusing especially if you didn't read the textbook ahead. He gives practice exams, but they only prepare you a bit as the real exams are way harder. The only thing I like about him is that he rewards improvement and exams are curved.

He would often use the chalkboard but in a class where drawing is a huge portion of the content, his drawings make things harder to understand. Both in person and on the lecture recordings, the drawings are not easy to see. The curve SAVED me.

OChem is hard, he does not make it easy. Practice exams aren't a great means of review for exam content, I'd more recommend reviewing lecture content or finding outside resources. Homework problems are also helpful. He clearly wants you to learn but OChem is just hard. While I'm sure there's better professors, his tests are fair enough.

the grade depended on 10 problem sets which would cover the content taught during class, 2 midterms and a final. the lectures were helpful and quite well explained, attending office hours was extremely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The exam material was not at all reflective of what was covered in lecture, and he stated that he expected the class averages on the exams to be between 50-60%, which is ridiculous because why is he making the test so hard that he expects people to fail? Overall, the professor was very discouraging, and honestly, it felt like I was set up to fail.

Had him for 41A, 25% both midterms and 50% final is all your grade is based on, and homework isn't mandatory, so hold yourself accountable. Fast lectures that are very messy because he uses chalk. No examples. Would not recommend taking him, you will have a breakdown over his tricky exams. Ochem is hard, and he makes it harder. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Orgo is already hard and he makes it harder. expect D's on his exams. His class average was in the high 50s and no one got 100s on the final. the only solace is that he's such a bad teacher that everyone else will also fail, so he curves intensely. Otherwise a nice guy, just not adept at lecturing; he moves super fast and doesn't explain problems.

Yang is most definitely hard. Fast lectures, difficult tests, not the best at explaining to students who don't understand. Attendance is not mandatory so you're better off just watching (and rewatching) the podcasts if you have to take him. Tests are designed to trick you. Curve was very generous though, which was appreciated.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a response to the TA strike, he decided to make the exams multiple choice. Picture a question with one right answer and you have 10-15 possible choices. A question like that could be 10% of the exam. His exams are unfair and try to trick you. Ochem is already hard and he makes the course far harder than needed.

Don't take him. Worst ochem professor. Hardest tests, the other professor's averages are letter grades higher and some even had online open note midterms. Expect a D on his midterms. He is also very ignorant and passive aggressive. Nice curve though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Yang is just a very fast paced professor. We were being told his final exam is easier than his practice final exam, but it was awful. His practice tests reflect on lecture material but his actual exams are TOUGH and he makes it very confusing. Just don't take it with him if you don't wanna hate ochem :)

Ochem can be a struggle for many and the way Yang lectures can be difficult. I found myself spending every class writing down the notes as fast as possible and rewatching each lecture to understand the material. However he's a pretty cool dude and after the little extra effort, his lectures make a lot of sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Organic chemistry is a hard class to begin with but Professor Yang's class is made so much better through office hours in terms of clarifying the content (TA's office hours are also very helpful). Tests are definitely fair + good practice exams. Expect to put effort in understanding material but that applies in any ochem class.

- Professor Jerry is a very nice person but I wouldn't recommend him for ochem. His tests are alright but idk why he does multiple choice with 15 points each sometimes. He is caring but the way he teaches makes you cry since it's so fast and sometimes out of order. Just don't take it with him if you have other options to take.
Just no in general
Made me wanna quit

Lectures are not required but go to them. He provides optional practice problems, but both reading the book and doing the problems are necessary to master the material. His teaching style is very logical and he does NOT believe memorizing  learning. He answers questions in class well. Graded solely on midterms and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Organic chem is going to be hard no matter who you have as a professor... but it was really difficult to listen to professor yang lecture for an hour and a half. But if you go to lecture and can actually pay attention then you should be able to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Jerry was a really good professor because his notes were, for the most part, comprehensive and detailed enough to study at home on your own. His tests are hard, but they're no more challenging than the next professor. Actually, he's arguably easier than most other o chem profs at UCSD. He does reward improvement and section is extremely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: O chem is hard no matter who you take. Yang is rough because its all midterms and final in terms of your grade. Also lecture are pretty monotone and hard to follow.... but you can do it. Just do the optional hw and go to discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His final was extremely hard cause his test questions could be really trick. If you expect to get a good grade,not to take him, or spend all your time with TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: 2 midterms, 1 final. Will bump you up 1/3 of a letter grade if he see's improvement on your test scores. Best resources that I had to use were the TAs, who provided handouts and summaries of the reactions you learn. Do the reading ahead of the lectures so you don't get lost and just spend a couple hours every week to do the problems.

He's a very fast writer and everything is on the board. Most of lecture is spent trying to write faster not listening to him. Reading the book and consulting the TA  is more helpful. However he understands the class is hard and grades generously,His tests are comparatively easy to others but still really hard -you really have to understand the rxns
Dr. Yang is tough, boring, and just writes reactions on the board without a whole lot of explanation. That being said, study his prior tests and you'll pass just fine. He grades generously.

Chem 140a is a pretty tough class. I got A since I have studied Ochem before entering ucsd. However, to grab an A is very difficult if you are a neophyte on Ochem since Prof Yang is expecting you to understand every subtle detail in his lecture and apply them in complicated cases. The final was disastrous, only 52% average and it will be curved.

Don't take this class. I got my first C in his class.  Made me think that I was bad at Ochem until I took 140B and aced it.  Lectures are confusing and doesn't podcast or give notes or anything.  Reuses exam questions from like 3-4 years ago.  Questions are random and don't reflect what he teaches.  Look at Cape, give have out 50% Cs in FA14.

Practice tests will be provided. The actual tests are harder than the practice tests, but the concepts remain the same. There's optional homework, but you should do it. Also go to discussions because your TA's will give you extra practice and maybe a summary of reactions. Know that everything's connected. Take lecture notes. They're very useful!!!!

Professor Yang is a pretty good lecturer, however he writes so fast that it is nearly impossible to keep up with him. He is very understanding of students and realizes how hard the concepts are, even though his tests are still extremely difficult. If you do all the hw problems and go to discussion, you should do relatively well in the class.

Prof. Yang covers a lot of material during lecture and it can be boring but he is overall pretty clearhelpful. The midterms for this class were pretty hard (average on 2nd midterm was 56100) and you only have a little over an hour to complete them. Fortunately he does curve the average to a B-, so there's that.

Dr. Yang is a nice professor but his exams are VERY difficult.  You get a little over 1 hour to take an exam but they are so detailed and tricky.   Compared to the practice exams, the real ones are much harder this year.

Moves too quick. Because if this he writes quick, small and messy. Once he says something once, you are expected to know it right then and there. He writes on the board with chalk for all his notes and provides no electronic sources to "catch up" or "make up" for a missed class. You will hear things from him in class but must TEACH it to yourself.

The class is hard enough, but especially when he is rushing through material in lecture. Writing is small and difficult to read. Mid terms are relatively okay, but its because you taught it to you on your own.

He is clear and presents the material in an organized fashion, but don't expect help outside of class. He is also super mean if you don't understand something and expects you to understand right away without allowing time and practice for the material to sink in. Easy to get a good grade but not a very approachable prof.

He writes everything you need to know on the board, and gives really good examples. Understand the examples, do the homework and practice tests and you'll be fine. His lectures aren't as interesting as Ternansky's, but he is really friendly. He doesn't like people studying off of the practice tests but his exams are very, very similar.

2 mid + final. All handwriting on board w/out slides. Slow paced at first but much faster when approaching final. Very clear on what he doesn't need you to know and doesn't trick you. I'd recommend him. Not hard.

Yang's tests are fair; I will admit that. While his knowledge of the information is fantastic, he does not wear a microphone during lecture and writes a myriad of information of the board while he is talking. It was hard trying to both decipher his handwriting and listen to what he was saying. Overall, he's okay, just be prepared beforehand.

He teaches what he wants to teach, not out of the book. Unfortunately his lectures are probably the most boring I've ever been to.I just ended up listening to another professor's podcast. Entire grade is based on two midterms and a final and he posts no information about anything at all online. But he's fine as long as you don't mind awful lectures

Okay, Organic Chemistry is a difficult subject already. Jerry is very nice. However, he spends the entire class writing on the board while you continue writing like a robot. Having said that, his exams are fair. If you understand the practice midterms and the homework problems, you will get an A. But you don't learn much inside the classroom.

Very easy to get a B, but must work super hard for the A. Got lazy, so ended up w/ a B. He writes everything you need to know on the board and it's actually a really great class. I definitely recommend him. Just be sure to study a lot and understand everything on practice exams.

He's alright. He tends to teach the easy concepts slowly and quickly lecture through difficult concepts. However, exam questions are essentially just like his practice exams. Class average is curved to a B-. Recommended.

Excellent Professor!  Goes over all of the material thoroughly and constantly reminds students about what are the really important concepts.  Attendance is a must.  Exams are very similar to the practice exams he provides.  Highly recommend!
Very conscientious-- Spends lots of time on WebCT discussion forum to answer student questions, and makes sure to teach us the full material. Test is fair. Curve the average as the lowest B-.
One of the easier ochem teachers.  Curve is very nice or else I wouldn't have done well.  The road-map on the final was a bit difficult.  Don't bother asking him for help though.
His tests are easy compared to the other O Chem profs, but don't expect help outside of class from anyone but your TA.
Good prof.  Good times.

Good professor.  The class was pretty hard, but you can do well if you work hard.  Attendance in lectures is a must...get there early because it is hard to find a seat. Generous curve so it is easy to pass.  Recommend

He lectures fast but his lecture notes are clear once you go over them again at home.  His exams come straight out of his notes and are pretty much like his past exams, so go to class and make sure you can do the practice tests!  The curve was OK in the end (he curves the average to a B-).  I would recommend him.

He's a great professor.  Exams were tough, but doable if you study hard.  He cares for the students and is really nice.  He has a very good idea of what is difficult for students and makes sure to point it out in class so that we pay extra attention.  I also wish he taught 140B.

Excellent professor. His lectures do go really fast and it is almost impossible to comprehend everything he says in lecture. My advice, read the book before lecture or just take notes in lecture, read the book after, then refer back to the notes. You will realize his notes are awesome. Exams are all fair, even his final! Wish he thought 140B.

Excellent Professor!  His lectures are clear and he lets you know exactly what to expect on the exams.  The exams were hard, but fair.  I would definitely recommend taking this professor again for Ochem.
In fact, I would go so far as to email this atrocious professor and really disclose his abominable teaching. i will.

truly a terrible professor, offers no fundamental understanding of the material,teaches it like a bio class, rather than what it is, a physics class. If you want to veritably comprehend what you are learning, DON'T go to lectures, they are a colossal waste of time, just read the book diligently, and  do the problems.The book is better at explaining

Class was pretty tough, but his test are fairly straightforward, similar to his practice midterms. T.A.'s will be incredibly useful in helping you understand what will be on the exams. Go to discussion sections!

Lectures WAY too fast. Study MT from previous quarter. Hope for TA's that wont jack you on points...I got no credit for having problems partially incorrect. He's okay, but not for everyone. I dropped and took it with a diff. professor.

Doesn't give you time to digest the notes you just took. he writes really fast and expects you to understand it almost immediately. MTs were free response and fair but the final was really really hard. To do well, study the MT from the quarter before, not the one he gives you for the current quarter, but still, work on it.

Professor Yang went through the lectures really fast, sometimes making it difficult. The nature of Chem 140A is tricky to understand and will require you to work out a lot of problems. The first MT wasn't too bad, but the final was mad hard.

He's a pretty good professor. The material is hard, but he goes over it pretty well. Midterms weren't bad (do the practice tests!) but the final was super hard. There was a good curve at the end. Just get above the avg and you'll get a B+ or better

His lectures are very representative of what is on the exam.  Do the practice exams and you will have a good idea of what to study for the test.  He is very nice and helpful.  Sometimes he lectures really quickly but he will always stop to take questions.
he's very nice in person, and a good lecturer.  Difficulty of exams is acceptable

His lectures are not that good. Basically, you just go crazy to keep up w/ his writing so u have no idea wat the subject is. But the bright side is that his tests come straight out from his notes, so Don't miss ANY class. And his tests are pretty fair. But he's kinda ignorant and impatient, so dont take it personal and ask the TAs instead

An average professor--not the best, but not the worst.  He writes everything on the chalkboard, and sometimes his handwriting is really hard to read.  Studying tests from previous years doesn't help much--he's constantly revising.  Just pay attention in class, and you should at least get a B.

Prof. Yang was fair in his grading, clear and organized in his lectures, and overall a pleasure to have as a professor. I attended all the lectures and reviewed my notes as well as completed the suggested problem sets. If you want to learn Ochem and be in a fair class, I would take the course with Prof. Yang.
great prof. it's true that he's always facing the board but if you have ever taken upper chem classes. it has to be like that way. don't complain about that. tests fair, not hard.
Very nice guy!  Lectures are clear and well organized.  Exams are straight from his notes.
great professor!  Very helpful.  Cares alot for students.  Exams are tough, but doable if you study hard.  Definitely recomend him.
Gawd, this professr is horrible. Don't take him at all; he goes too fast, doesn't explain things very well, and it ends up NOT MAKING ANY SENSE.

he covers teh book basically.  as in word for word and likes to put his back to the crowd and talk to the board.  he never put the finals out for the class last spring.  so he must have made up grades.
i like big molecules
Nice guy. Doesn't like stupid questions, like ones he just answered. Also, not good at explaining things. You should go somewhere else for help. Try OASIS workshops.
He's a great professor, very nice during office hours. I recommend this professor he's very clear and helpful. If you do the study and do the H.W you'll get an A.
No Comments

He's always facing the board...Writes what's on the book...tests are ok if you study...of course he doesn't explain the material very well - like someone below wrote, if you got a question he just says "you should know this...draw the mechanism" - how the hell...anyways, he's nice, but there are better profs out there - I Don't recommend him

Lectures were out of the book, but he emphasized what would appear on the tests. Tests are easy and fair if u study and know the material. Go over the problems he assigns for homework, and really know the ones he puts exclamation marks for, because they for sure appear on the test. good luck!

I would NOT recommend this teacher to anyone. He acts as if teaching is a burden to him and answers any questions that students have with the bare minimum. He goes through important lectures very quickly and expects students to already fully understand the material. The worst part is, he makes students feel stupid for asking questions!
This guy is really nice.  Good lectures.  Always appear ready to help.  Fair exams.

He's okay. Not great, but not bad. Although the lectures do seem kind of just straight out of the book, he is helpful with the discussion board online. But he seems to be easily annoyed by some questions. Tests are kind of tricky, but ok if you study.

I would not recommend this professor to anyone who is interesting in getting good grades and taking FAIR examinations. Lectures clear, but a pillow is a MUST if you dont want to bruise your head on the back of your seat exams are fairly difficult and i felt they were set up in a way that would promote weeding out/failure rather than actual learning

Gadddd, this guy was so bad.  He faces the board when he writes down mechanisms and talks striaght into the board.  The first 2.5 weeks were spent on the first chapter, lewis dots, hybridization, just gchem stuff and then the first midterm was during 4th week so he proceded to cover 3 more chapters in 4 lectures.. this guy is terrible, period.

Lectures consist of him writing the book on the board. Gives examples without telling you what it's for, and w/ no explanation. Answers based on circular logic-- Student says: "How should I figure out the mechanism for this reaction?" Response: "You should draw the mechanism to figure it out." Either that, or he says YOU SHOULD KNOW THIS BY NOW.

He speaks very clearly and regularly answers questions posted to a message board on his website.  He both writes and speaks very quickly, making it difficult to keep up, but I would recommend him to anyone.

Pretty much the book in person...he has notes on his spiral notebook that apparently are straight from the book, as soon as it's time for class, he just turns his back to the class and makes sure that you're familiar with the back of his head while he outlines the book for you...tests are ok but lectures will tell you what is really emphasized
His lectures are boring, and he reads off his notes the entire class.  His tests did represent the material in class well, but there isn't much partial credit on them.

Helpful and good-natured professor. Concerned for students' learning. Exams were straightforward. Gives credit for understanding even if you miss the details. No homework in this class. Just lectures, reading, paper (for grads).
No Comments
I really enjoyed my time in her class and thought the lectures were well planned and executed and the exams/homeworks were very fair.

She does have accent, and that can influence her quality of teaching as compared to other professors of this class. She also does not podcast. HOWEVER this does not contradicts the fact that she is very caring and approachable. One major caveat: Her HW due dates changed from Saturdays to Thursdays starting from Midterm week(week 5).

Zhang is super sweet and kind. Her lecture slides are clear, she doesn't podcast. Her overall teaching was OK, but her accent is heavy. The material is quite difficult, the exams are hard, she does curve generously. I didn't really enjoy this class, but I do think if you have to take this class, taking her is probably better than the other profs.

literally the greatest math professor of all time at ucsd, considering most other math profs get on average a 1.8 on rate my prof (and that's being generous), a rating above 4 should tell you everything you need to know about her. do not make the mistake of missing out on an easy A

Incredibly caring and makes sure that you will not fail the course, either through generous curving or additional support. Lectures were not podcasted but course notes and lecture slides were plenty enough to understand the content with supplementary book. Homework involved a combination of proprietary problems and book problems.

She is one of the most caring professors that I've had. Her lectures are outstanding and the material presented is always clear. Her assignments are tricky, but they help you prepare for the midterm and final. Her exams are also hard, but she curves a lot and does not want to fail any student. She is very nice during office hours too. Love her!

I had Professor Danna Zhang in Winter and Spring 2020. I LOVE this professor and I would consider her my number one professor for my major here at UCSD! Her lectures are both clear and understandable. Homework and exams can be tedious but she teaches great for both parts, especially for the exams. I got a B+ in 181A & an A- in 181B. LOVE YA DANNA!!

Danna is a super nice professor. She always cares about her students. Although the tests are a little tricky sometimes, they are fair. Do the homework and go over her slides carefully, you will get a good grade.

Pros: super nice person, very helpful office hour, hw solutions and lecture notes posted, no attendance Cons: lil bit accent but doesn't hurt, personally don't like her teaching style, no practice midterm/final

I love Prof Zhang! One of my favorite math professors at UCSD so far. She really cares about her students, and is one of the most helpful for test preparation. She grades students based on a "ranking" system, instead of a solid grade cutoff. Her homework is challenging, but not too hard and really helps prepare you for the exams.
She is amazing! She cares about students. Exam is a bit hard, but she did review class to help you prepare for it. Would recommend her.

The lecture notes she provides is very clear and helpful to understand the material and do the review. It is my first time to take her class. She is very caring, funny and nice. I do hope to have a chance to take her other classes.

She is a very good professor. I took her 180A and 181A. Never went to lectures because she posted lecture notes on TED everyday. Homeworks are not that hard, and exams are similar to problems in lecture notes. Just write some examples on the cheet sheet then it will be an easy A.

One of the best professor for Statistics classes in UCSD. Her lecture is fantastic, and the lecture notes would also provide later, that really helps for reviewing and save you plenty of time. Homework is easy, the final is a little bit harder than midterm but it's fair. Overall, I learned a lot in this course.

Lectures are straightforward, even though accent is a little bit hard to understand at times. New teacher so she's getting into her groove. Do the labs and homework relatively thoroughly. Go to office hours if you need help. She's more than willing to try and assist you. Study hard for midterms/finals since they're heavily weighted.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: awesome professor test and homework easy

Professor Zhang is an amazing person. If you dont understand something in lecture, 10/10 would recommend going to her Office Hours because thatll help a lot. Of course labs and homework is long and tedious, but she definitely wants her students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Would take again

reviews.comment: She is a very nice person but not a good lecturer/professor. She has trouble explaining herself through words and her accent doesn't help. Exams are fair but some not from lecture but rather hw. She doesn't assign her own hw problems to go with the class but rather take hw from another professor. Labs and homework are time consuming and hard.
Her lectures are extremely hard to understand due to her accent. Avoid if possible

She is a really nice professor. She is really patient when answer your questions, and she would like to listen to students concerns. The professor always prepared well for the class, and you can feel she want to help students in learning instead of giving hard exams or heavy homework. She uses PPT in classes, which is really helpful for reviewing.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Prof Zhang is a pretty good professor. You can tell she definitely wants everyone to learn the material. She is very hard to understand during the lecture due to her accent but its not impossible. Attendance is honestly no big deal. Do the homework and the exam is cake. The labs are pretty horrible and hw is long, but she prepares you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very nice and accessible. Exams and homework are a bit tricky.

Professor Zhang is amazing. There are no surprises on her tests. As long as you know how to do the homework and know everything she covers in her lecture notes, you should be on your way to an A. Your final score will consist of weekly homework (graded on accuracy), weekly labs, 2 midterms, and 1 final.

Danna has a pretty strong academic background. She is pretty good at explaining concepts and materials. She will tell you which part is essential and which part you just have to know. She also offered students with a lot of help during her office hour. So she is a pretty good professor.
Homework is easy and there are not many questions. Midterm is tricky, but not hard. She said there would be a curve on the overall grade so I think she is a great professor.

Does not strictly cover content in the same way as the book, so lecture attendance is important. Her accent is quite heavy, but it is improving noticably week by week. Her lecture slides are central to understanding content for exams and provides clear points and examples. Can also give short explanations in Mandarin in office hours or after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is essentially an audiobook for the textbook. And even if you teach yourself, the Labs and Tests will come back with less than ideal grades. The TA grades without partial credit. If they say you get partial credit, don't believe them.

Her lecture is confusing and exams are EXTREMLY HARD. Though she said the materials for exams are all from lecture notes and hws, going over these will NOT help the exam at all. She also have a terrible accent, so listening her lecture is a torture.

I took this class pass/no pass, hoping for an easy class, but it was very time-consuming. There is an insane amount of reading, so if you do not like that, do not take this class. Discussions are bad; you need to actively speak during class to get points. My TA was rude and a tough grader as well. Only take it if you actually care about phil.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I truly believe Brants is a solid professor. He never fails to be energetic and shows great passion for philosophy. His lectures were fun at the start though it got a little dull near the end. 5 P/NP assignments for the whole quarter. Study guide is provided, easy A for the midterm. Pop quizzes are P/NP and quite easy even w/o doing the reading.

His lectures were interesting and his analogies really helped me understand the material. 5 essays that are P/NP and a pop quiz every week that are P/NP. As long as you do the readings (that can range from 5-20 pages), you'll do fine in the class. Your TA grades everything, and I was lucky to have a really nice TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Not a hard class if you keep up with most readings. There are 10 pop quizzes for attendance, but grading is usually lenient. Lectures can be boring, though he's clearly passionate about philosophy. The midterm was moderately easy, but grading felt a bit harsher than expected for a GE. More of an easy A- than an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very passionate and an overall great lecturer. The midterm was very fair and matched the study guide. I wasn't the biggest fan of the pop quizzes but they were manageable. Not an easy GE by any means but he is a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Easy class but for a GE its way too much. If you don't mind the workload and the unnecessary unapllicable information he feeds you then you can take it.

Professor Brant's is an excellent lecturer who makes the content very interesting. The reviews who rate him poorly do not reflect his teaching style. If you do the readings (which are quite lengthy but interesting) you will be fine on pop quizzes. If you are looking for a throw away class and dont care to learn then dont take the course.

I thought this professor was excellent. He was very descriptive in his slides. Gave study guides for exams and easy pop quizzes on readings. If you participate in class discussions you will definitely learn more. Participating in class is a key part of your education so don't listen to the bad reviews it's people who don't do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Zack Brants is a good professor, don't listen to the bad reviews. Yes he does give a lot of readings but they are really easy and for the pop quizzes as long as you know a bit about the topic he will give you a passing grade. His midterm is very fair and his study guide really helps, the class overall is an easy A.

Zach Brants is genuinely one of the best professors I've had at UCSD whos clearly passionate about what he teaches. He engages with the class and allows for open dicussion with other students about ideas. Homework and tests are easy if you've read the reading. He does ask for written questions sometimes, so do attend class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The professor is a great, passionate lecturer, and does a good job engaging the class in discussion. There's no attendance, but there are pop quizzes, which are easy to pass if you did the reading, which is interesting and not long. The essays are pass/fail and you get much leeway on how to write them. Midterms and finals are easy.

Professor Brant's is awesome at his job, and very passionate about philosophy. I agree that I would not take this class as a GE, as it is very reading intensive, however if you are interested in philosophy definitely take him. Since it is my minor I like the course but you definitely have to keep up with readings and attend class
dont take this class its too hard for a ge

Not fond of pop quizzes at all. Mid term was pretty easy. He's interesting I like the way he explains things. Section is mandatory and fun. I really like my TA. 5 reading responses which are manageable. TA grades EVERYTHING.

reviews.comment: pop quizzes are an automatic one for me

reviews.comment: Too much work for a GE class. Legit majority of the things he teaches you can get on a motivational instagram page.

reviews.comment: This course feels overstructured for a lower-division philosophy class. Expect heavy reading, strict grading, and required revisions. Attendance is tracked through unannounced quizzes, laptops aren't allowed, and lectures often restate the readings. Not ideal if you want a lighter GE.

If you're taking philosophy as a GE, be cautious. The class is more time-consuming than expected for an intro course. There are frequent unannounced quizzes, long readings, strict grading with required revisions, a no-laptop policy, and lectures that mostly repeat the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
This class is way more demanding than it needs to be. You need consistent attendance and focus. There are several in class quizzes, and you have a lot of homework too. I would not recommend this class if you are taking it as a GE.

Lectures are also extremely boring, unless you are VERY interested in philosophy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: His passion for philosophy is admirable, but a little too much, as he often goes over time during lectures. Attendance is not considered mandatory, but he does do pop quizzes to ensure students are attending class. The lectures just go over the readings, and they're not engaging. Also, he has a no-technology policy, so come to class with a notebook
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is overall really essay and he doesn't give out too much hard work. He is very unorganized with too many pop quizzes, last-minute changes, and lectures are overall very unengaging and a repeat of the readings. If you like to structure your life, don't choose this teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very funny guy who kept roasting me. He also broke down proofs from Zimmer's functional analysis book in helpful ways.

His office hour are really helpful. As long as you make some progress, he can guide you neatly. Like a previous review said, his quiz is hard (median 30%), but midterm and final are better. Thinking and doing on and beyond HW problems is essential, as his tests are not in format similar to HW but still related in deep core. He also podcasts.

Zlatos is well known in the math department for having the most difficult 140 classes, and 140C was no exception. The class is difficult, but if you take advantage of the resources available (discussion, Zlatos' office hours, TA office hours), and put in the time to digest the material, you can do well. You will learn a lot in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Horrible teacher. Lecture material did not prepare you for the homework and exams. Not sure why there is a good review about Zlatos considering that student got a C (if you got a C, does that really mean your teacher taught you well?)

He's a solid prof for this class. It was no easier than it should have been, but his lectures were, for the most part, clear (and if not, he records and usually makes sense upon a second listen), and homework decent length. Strict at times (no dropping homeworks or exams), but his performance expectations are quite realistic given the difficulty
Fair, Exam similar to and easier than HW.

His first midterm, called quiz, allows you to drop without W in case you did not do well and received your scores before deadline. Also he actually worked with Rudin, the author of textbook, in his years in University of Wisconsin Madison!

The course is difficult by design; the homework problems are widely challenging and relatively nontrivial, which are designed by the professor if the book does not satisfy. The lectures are packed to the brim and are presented well. The exams are also exacting. But it is a very strong math course.
Really awful, instruction has nothing to do with homework or exams. Heavy workload.
Lectures are fine, homework are long and difficult. Rarely directly address you questions during office hours/email.

Compared with my peers taking the same class with other instructors, he is harder and more rigorous. Lectures are fantastic and he's hilarious. HWs for this class are long, as they take at least 10 hours a week. He definitely seems to care about us, and the small class size is great. Definitely recommend if you're up for the challenge.

Difficult and fair. He expects you to understand the material and doesn't wait for the class to understand. We had more than half the class drop before the first midterm. He explains things well, but be prepared to study his lecture notes thoroughly before class each day so you can keep up with his lectures.

Not even that bad of a lecturer, but the format of the class is so abysmal that it was likely the worst class I've ever taken. 100% final all multiple choice no partial credit. Does “flipped classroom” but his class lectures are the same as the videos which defeats the purpose. Says there will be 0 errors then has a multitude of errors on grading.

Has good lectures and effectively teaches material. However it is wild that the grade is 100% of the final which throws a lot of people off. Be very disciplined and teach yourself material throughout whole quarter.

Format of this class is abysmal. When I took it the grading scheme was 65% final exam+35% quizzes(9 quizzes), but now the exam is 100% of your grade. All MCQs (no marks for attempting). Class average is extremely bad so he curves it. No assignments which doesnt help because you dont get practice. Dont take ECE 45 with him unless you have to
You learn nothing. EVERYTHING IS JUST MCQ and you end up learning nothing because actually solving everything will get you no answer
The people that failed used chatgpt on the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is so funny

If you value your grades you'll wait to take it with a different professor. Class average this quarter was a C- after curving. Probably used to be good when he cared about teaching and curved properly.

I felt as if I at least studied hard enough to have a basic understanding of the course material yet the professor gave out a final with nothing on it that was taught. I truly believe I had enough knowledge to at the bare minimum pass the course, yet I didn't even make it out with a C. I think this professor is very unfair and should be avoided.

makes an already hard class 10 times harder than it needs to be. definitely the hardest and less helpful out of all the 45 professors, you can only do good if you do well under immense pressure. simple mistakes mean failing the class or getting a bad grade.

Avoid this professor at all costs. Black box (won't disclose any info) grading process with a self described “generous curve”, although class averages are usually in the C+ territory.
