Pawns all the real work off to his TA's, frequently cancels office hours, often spends 30 minutes in lecture on nonsensical integration problems, crazy weekly exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: worst professor ive ever had. No sympathy for students, doesnt record lectures. first time ive considered dropping my major was bec of him.
He is the GOAT.

If you want to learn the material deeply, 5/5. Zeger's lectures are lucid and crystal clear and he expects you to put in the work to learn the material. However, the quizzes are MC and the time pressure will get you. Generous curve at the end, so definitely passable. Getting an A is different though.

Very great professor, he teaches lecture very well, but students need to put some effort into reviewing and practice for doing well in quizzes and tests.  The TA is also nice for helping students to review the topics about quizzes and final.

Very hard and competitive. Zeger is also a very good lecturer and has great TA's. If you put the time in, you can do well. A lot of people complain because they aren't willing to put the work in and they don't do well.

His lectures are dense but informative. The weekly quizzes keep you on your feet. They are 3 "simple" MC questions, but due to the 15 min time constraint, any simple errors you make can mean failing it. Expect averages to be low and a generous curve at the end. Work hard until the very end and perform at around the class average you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Zeger's lectures are fantastic. He explains everything so clearly, and while he might seem a little blunt, he's very good to talk to in office hours. Over COVID, he changed from midterms to quizzes. This new format definitely emphasizes understanding over brute forcing equations -- remember that when taking them!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Zeger is a great teacher and is great at explaining concepts. However, the quizzes are very hard and stressful, the the grades are usually quite low, until at the very end there is a very generous curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Zeger's grading style for ECE 45 are weekly quizzes that are multiple choice, and a final exam at the end. The quizzes and exams are extremely difficult, with very low averages. At the very end of the course, Professor applies a massive curve. Not a helpful learning environment.

Zeger's lectures are crystal clear and his TA Spencer is just amazing. If you go sections of the class and UNDERSTAND every part in the lecture notes, you'll be fine. However, his exams are all multiple choice questions, and the avg tends to be around 50% (although he applies a fat curve at the end to make sure the class has a B- average)

I'm sorry, but most people have professor Zeger all wrong. I'm actually not sorry, he's one of the best professors I've ever had. The best advice I can give you is to attend at least 1-2 study time sessions weekly (with Spencer, he's awesome) and make sure to watch discussion videos. Hang in there and you will learn a lot, trust me.

Zeger needs to be reviewed by the education board. His teaching is 'lazy' and uninspired and he dumps all the real work on his TA Spencer and takes credit for it. Unless youve taken the class before, you wont pass. Tests are completely ambiguous, the whole class is canvas automated, NO PARTIAL CREDIT on problems. Avoid this professor at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Zeger creates a bad learning environment for students. If you already know the knowledge, you can probably do well. However, if you want to learn, AVOID HIM AT ALLLLL COST!!!!!!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Any professor that gives a midterms that have an average score of 39% and a final that's average is 51% (EVEN AFTER THE TEST IS TAKEN ONLINE AT HOME WITH THE INTERNET AS A RESOURCE AND SKEWED BY PEOPLE TAKING THE FINAL IN GROUPS) is a bad professor. Whether the test was too hard or he didn't prepare us well doesn't matter, one has to be true.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The level of difficulty of this professor, along with how the TAs grade the exams, is demonic. They are knowledgeable, but disrespectful to the students as they don't value work on the already super hard exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The Tests are INSANE. Such a huge leap from what we learn in class. Class midterm average's were 20% lol Avoid at all costs if possible. Wait Luganani doesn't teach anymore. Big oooof
Wonderful lectures but hard exams. It's not impossible to get an A because his lectures are so clear.

This class was hard. The concepts can be mathematically abstract and confusing. The class is graded to maximize pressure-- 40% midterm and 60% final, or, if midterm scores are bad, 100% final. The midterm resembled the practice midterms but the final is much longer, more math intensive, and requires deep thinking of the concepts holistically.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Do hard homework problems. Midterm is straightforward, but final is impossibly hard. Make sure you do much more to understand concepts than just doing homework problems or reviewing discussion notes.

Zeger knows his stuff and teaches the material in a way that makes it easy to understand conceptually. However, as many other here have stated, this doesn't help much on his tests which are extremely difficult compared to homework. Attending Discussion session is necessary cause that's where you learn to do harder problems like those on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Zeger is one of the best lecturers I've ever had. Unlike the other profs, Zeger actually takes the time to explain the intuition behind everything he does in a very straightforward manner. Exams are kinda insane for a UCSD class but are definitely doable if you learn the concepts rather than just memorize steps. And there's a very generous curve.

He is clearly a smart guy, but the leap in difficulty from what he teaches to what he tests on is gigantic. I mean, what purpose does it serve to make exams THAT difficult? ECE 109 was a hard subject, but I feel that the students should have been better prepared (by him) for what he expected out of us. I wish we could fill out CAPE's after finals.

Zeger knows his stuff really well, and he is very approachable if you have any questions. I found this class fairly straightforward; did all the homework, studied from the lecture notes, and did the practice exam to earn an A in the class. A lot of math, and final was pretty tough, but curved very generously.

Clear lectures, I strongly recommend attendance. Optional homework is a must-do if you want to succeed. Exams were fair, covering only lectured material. The final required a holistic understanding of the material, which takes time and deep thought. You must have strong math skills/reasoning to understand the material and do well in the class.

1 midterm, 1 final (40%, 60% or 100% final) Try to get an A on the midterm to buffer your final score. Final was extremely difficult. Midterm resembled the homework, final was MUCH more math intensive.

His lecture is straightforward and clear, but his tests are very hard. I am not saying his tests are impossible, but they are not closely related to the HW and practice exam. He never gives practice exam for the final exam. Everything he has mentioned in his class might be on the final.  If you want to get a good grade, try to avoid him.

Prof. Zeger is by far the best teacher I've ever had at UCSD. He is so clear down to the nitty gritty detail it's amazing. You can tell he wants you to really get what he's saying. The lectures are really math heavy so make sure you know your calc or you are doomed. You will get your tuition's worth with this guy!

Wow, people are not kidding when they say that Zeger is a professor who expects a lot out of you. His midterm was extremely difficult, and from someone who has never gotten a B before, I would be happy with a C. He's clear and I like his lecturing style, but in my opinion the tests are just a huge leap from the material in class.

Hard class if you're not very good at theorycalculustest-taking. He's a superb lecturer though; definitely a smart prof. Homework is optional but highly recommended. I didn't do any of it, but would have definitely gotten an A in this class if I put that work into it. Don't slack off, and get an A!

Professor Zeger is extremely knowledgeable and works through the proofs clearly, but aside from helping you understanding  the mathematics behind the concepts, it lectures won't help you much.  Go to discussion because that's where the TA will go over examples with you.  Tests are insanely hard and nothing like practice examsdisc noteshomework.

Zeger definitely isn't easy. However, I won't say his exams are totally ridiculous. They are hard for sure, but if you know the concepts you will do fine. Grading is just one midterm and the final, or you can choose it to be 100% your final score.
The final is so  hard. There was nothing similar to homework or anything talked in the lecture. You think you can handle it but you can't.

I thought he was a very good lecturer. Explained everything very clearly and kept me engaged and interested in the course material. I did none of the homework and didn't study for the midterm until the night before and I got an A, but if I didn't go to a few lectures I'm sure the test would've been a lot harder.
Very bad professor. The tests are impossible and lectures are unclear. Try to avoid this class.
Midterm was fair and based on lectures. Using his old midterms as practice helped a lot. Do as well as you can on the midterm, because his final was way too hard.

This is a very hard professor. If you are not willing to put in many additional hours a week, good luck! His tests are impossible and even though he knows that, he doesn't mind. Crazy guy. Curve doesn't really help much because 40? get C's anyways. His tests cover all the stuff you think he wouldn't ask and are complicated. If you have him, gd lk!

He is very clear and precise when it comes to explanations however besides that, to get an A/B you need to self study.  His suggested problems don't help at all and you have to be the top 30% in the class just to get a B- or higher.  Good news is that most people don't self study, but if you do, you will be far ahead of the game.

Hard class, great professor. He's crystal clear, knowledgeable, awesome lecturer, a lot of material. Straightforward class and guy. Don't be one of those students who doesn't go to class thn complains about how hard the inal was, go to class, study, do homework and you'll do fine. Hard course, great professor.

He is a really bad prof. in UCSD and his final was really hard for common student. If u miss the lecture, u will miss all knowledge, but if u do not miss the class, u also don't the question in final!

Zeger is a decent lecture but the course is challenging. Midterm resembled lectures and he gave hints as to what would be tested but exam was still hard. No homework, 1 midterm that is optional and a cumulative final. Be prepared to work for your grade.

He is a good lecturer. His final exam was beyond hard though, get ready for a GPA bump. If you must take 109 with him, I recommend you get a copy of Prob, Statistics and Random Processes (Alberto Leon-Garcia) for some supplementary reading. He's going to promise you that the final will be from the lecture notes... don't believe it.

Prof. Zeger is the most interesting and crystal clear teacher I've ever had in my life. He loves the topic and explains everything inside out. If you don't like math, forget about this course. If you like math, this is the best course you'll ever take!!

Prof. Zeger is the best teacher I've ever had at UCSD. His explanations are very very clear even when the material is difficult. His exams are hard but they are fair. He doesn't water down the material for the unprepared students.
This guy doesn't explain anything... he goes about a thousand miles an hour and just solves problems, doesn't explain why or how he is solving them.  I would not take him again for any class

Awesome professor. Presents the material clearly, slowly, carefully with examples. One of my favorite ECE professors. We didn't get through the most advanced material though. Material and test/final are very difficult.
Do not take him, his tests are wayyyyy harder than his lectures, his style of grading is awful(no partial credit)
he thought the final was "easy". ****!!

Professor Zeger is one the best lecturers I've had so far at UCSD.  He has extensive knowledge in his field.  The course in itself is very difficult.  He gives you the fundamentals in lecture and steps it up for homework, but the tests are very doable if you study.  Take him if you want to learn.  If you want an easy A you're in the wrong major.
terrible professor.. impossible to do homework based on lecture material, expects you to know what he hasn't taught you

His tests have nothing to do with his lectures. He gives out past tests, as practice, but beware they are not even remotely close to his tests. His tests are very unclear and leave you very frustrated. I recommend taking Acampora instead for 109.

One of the most considerate professors. I understand why her courses are always at max capacity. Her lectures are extremely informative and I love listening to the stories she has to share. If this class is one of your options, you should definitely choose this. You can apply a lot from this class to real life.
Great professor in public health! Interesting and personable lectures and is very caring towards students.
Extremely nice and easy going class, as long as you show up you should receive and A+.

Dr. Zoumas - best prof here! She is so knowledgable in her field and her story is so interesting. Her class was easy and low-commitment, but it was also engaging. The class consisted of a three part project analyzing your diet, weekly quizzes, occasional homework, and a group project w/ presentation. No exams. Would definitely recommend taking her!

Super kind professor who really loves connecting with the students. Lectures are a bit boring and repetitive information from PH 40 and 50. A final group paper, be careful of your groupmates, can really make or break your grade. Have weekly quizzes and assignments, a final, and a final paper.

She is the most amazing professor! She is very interesting when she speaks because you can see the amount of care she puts into her lectures and the material. But she is kinda off on her assignments and when they are due! so do all the assignments even if they don't have a due date.
Great professor tbh! She cares for her students and is very approachable. She gives extra credit and is very accessible outside of class for extra help.

Professor Zoumas is a gem!! Not only is the class very interesting/ relevant, but she makes me excited to come in at 8 am! She is so kind, patient, and an amazing professor. She is brilliant and is more than happy to answer any questions you have in class. I can't praise her enough!! Definitely take this class if you have the opportunity to do so!

She is the best professor I have ever had. It's amazing how much she cares about her students and nutrition. I would take her again in a heart beat. Just do the work and she is always there to support you. She is always. accessible to help students and genuinely wants everyone to learn and succeed. you'd be lucky to have her as your professor 10/10
Lectures were extremely convoluted and not very helpful for doing the homeworks. Had to watch YouTube tutorials and learn on my own. This class was a waste of time and money, don't recommend.

Professor Tu is one of the kindest professors I've had, and you can tell that he cares and is proud of what he teaches. He repeats himself sometimes and the logistics of the course can be a bit difficult, but he's very accessible and is very earnest. He tires to make everything as accessible as possible and this causes attendance to decrease IP.
The most chaotic course I have taken. Going to his lecture is wasting time. Office hours are the only helpful time for this course

Good guy, not a great lecturer. He repeats himself a lot and sometimes doesn't explain things very well BUT always asks if people are following along and makes time to answer everyone's questions. Easy to talk to outside of class and will help go over topics. Homework's aren't long but can be challenging.

Good professor overall. Explained many deep learning concepts clearly. Sometimes gives lots of homework but he's also generous about giving extra credits or extending deadlines. The overall workload is doable and the materials help you get a deeper understanding of the topic.
Can't understand where those hates come from. Prof. Tu is indeed a caring techear and very accessible outside classes. Those course materials and exams are also legitimate and informative.

Professor Tu is a nice person, as well as a good teacher. Sometimes he likes to explain some concept recursive, sounds redundant though, is not hard to extract the essence. The homework and exam are also reasonabl. Don't know where the hates come from, especially to such a professor cares about student. SHAME on those who put ugly words on him!
Tu is fine. An average professor in my opinion. Okay lectures, reasonable homework, easy exams. Don't know where all the hate comes from.
Minimize your loss function by avoiding Tu's ML class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Nice person, but awful at explaining concepts. Lecture slides all over the place, which makes it impossible to study efficiently because the notation is thrown all over the slides in all areas of the slide, with no cohesion as to how theorems are derived.

The assignments are relatively hard - you are expected to have a solid background in linear algebra and coding. However, the exams basically repeat the homework questions, so it's easy to get As. The lectures are elaborate in algorithm implementations and proofs, so you can learn a lot if you follow. The professor has a little accent but it's okay
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Effective teaching allows students an opportunity to learn and succeed. Mr. Tu's 118A course is the opposite of that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Zhuowen has to be one of my favorite lecturers that Ive had at UCSD. Lectures go through machine learning theory, and he does his best to make sure that everyone is at the same place. Hes also really willing to help explain concepts to you after class if you have trouble understanding
Zhuowen is hands down one of the worst lecturers I've encountered at UCSD. I can go on and on about how awful this class really is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: It makes me depressed to think that I suffered through 8 Math courses and 2 coding courses just to be confronted with the final boss of utter incompetence known as Zhuowen Tu all in the hopes of having a buzzword like Machine Learning on my degree. Avoid at all costs.. oh wait you cant.

There are courses that are difficult, yet rewarding. This course is difficult and unrewarding; it leaves you questioning if you even learned anything. At a prestigious institution like UCSD, that's unacceptable. This is the problem with the school requiring professors to teach when all the professor cares about is research, and it's more common now
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This is a message to other instructors - Tu does not seem qualified to teach at UCSD and that too so many important COGS classes. He confuses concepts and then zooms through them without proper explanation. Poor lecture slides, vague homework, and useless lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Tu is one of the worst lecturers I've had at UCSD. Any useful skill I learned in this class was acquired through researching the homework problems online, none from lecture. The tests are clearly made to be easy because if any of the real content (ML algorithms, any real math behind the content) was tested normally, most people would fail

Utilize the lectures/ notes from UC Irvine professor Alexander Ihler and the material makes so much more sense. There is flow with the material there; the way this class is structured is extremely poor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: You need to self-study Machine Learning topics online from other college professors' lectures because lectures/ slides in this class are inept & vague. Machine Learning is interesting stuff, but the way the class is currently taught & structured makes it extremely frustrating and not very intellectually rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Every morning I do ML, and every afternoon I finish my PA. At night, I lie awake in agony knowing I've just climbed out of the pit, only to be pushed back in by none other than Zhuowen. Taking this professor was the worst mistake I've ever made.
Cares if you are able to understand the course material. Homework is hard and tests are lengthy.
AWFUL AWFUL AVOID AT ANY COST!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Needs to take a look at how Steve Barrera organizes lectures, as every lecture has a specific purpose; with Zhuowen, all of the presented topics are meshed together and zoomed through, so then you're left dazed & confused when homework is presented. Don't even get me started on the vagueness of homework. Nice guy but not good at teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Class is disorganized from lecture to homework. Trying to figure out what homework questions are asking for is a challenge in itself. You basically need to go to OH & read a bunch of extra stuff online to understand what things are asking for. Needs better transition with material, as this is supposed to be an Intro Machine Learning class.
Only 2 weeks into the quarter, and already we can see Zhuowen is not fit to teach upper division COGS. Disorganized lectures, lecture slides, and vague homework questions.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His lectures are almost pointless. He doesn't speak clearly, he's tangential, he packs tons of notation into every slide and then blasts through them all at full speed, he doesn't realize most people are not paying attention, he makes simple concepts very confusing, and his homework is long and frustrating. His class is painful, find another prof.

Prof. Tu is an AMAZING researcher and a genuinely kind person, but unfortunately, his teaching skills leave much to be desired. Expect mass confusion, unclear assignments, vague instructions, and an overwhelming workload. Even with 10+ hours of self study each week, his class is very frustrating and intellectually and emotionally unrewarding.

Lots of extra credit, homework is difficult but fairly graded. Though the first few lectures were fairly slow, it sped up quite a bit. You should be fairly well versed in both a programming language of choice(Matlab Python or R for this course) and mathematics, or else the course will be significantly more difficult.

Final paper had 10% of raw extra credit available if you wrote a paper that met the requirements of a journal. The first exam was extremely easy, the second one was much harder. Doesn't have a final exam (just a paper)!! He really wants you to learn data modeling, so he'll teach what he tests you on for 1/3 the class then teaches data modeling.

The best professor I've ever had at UCSD (took him Spring 2025, only rating now).
Paused all of his research for his office hours to be open to us. An amazingly caring professor; I don't think anyone else as good.
He might seem scary, but he cares about his students and when asked, he will answer questions. NEVER made anyone feel bad.
Very straightforward lectures and exams compared to other professors. Hard work does pay off in his class. Very accessible in office hours as well.
Watch out he's tough
His course takes a lot of time from your schedule
Best professor ever! This guy is a GOAT!!!

Was ALWAYS willing to help students pass the class. Had so many extra discussions and office
hours to help students who missed class on the weekend!

The material was difficult to understand, but the professor's lectures made it clear. Quizzes were a good basis for your understanding of the material. The professor has his office hours open almost all the time, each week, making sure his students are able to understand the material.

Course content was difficult to understand and apply, but many practice questions were provided. Ndao was very helpful and reached out frequently, hosting many office hours and practice sessions before exams. Discussions, lectures, practice sessions, labs, and homework did, however, create a large time commitment.

Took LIPO 1AX w/ her. God bless this woman. Some technical difficulties with the homework website. She initially said 50% credit for late HW. Turned around at the end of the quarter and gave us full credit. Brought her cute ass dog to the final. Literally so kind and funny + genuinely explains so well! Way better than French class in high school.
She is super nice and lovely, definitely a firm grader but she is a wonderful professor and have taken many classes with her.

Amazing professor, teaches everything incredibly clearly and accessibly. She speaks only Portuguese in class but does so in a way that it completely understandable, and she'll clarify things in English if you're confused. Tests are fair and getting an A is certainly doable, but most people take pass-fail anyway. Take this class!
He's my dad and I don't go to college

He barely does anything on class. He never listens carefully to what a student says. He has been reported using suggestive language to a female student. What is more, he cancels them

He wastes one's time. One can barely learn anything with him even after almost a year. In conclusion, one shall avoid him against all odds and by any costs necessary.

I didn't even know which tags to use because he has canceled class so many times. Sometimes things are due then he'll cancel the whole class that day. Very textbook heavy, but the few lessons he taught were confusing. Also doesn't grade anything, it's week 7 and there is still no grade shown.

Abdelhak is the epitome of a grumpy Arab man. With a hilarious sense of humor, he can also be very difficult to approach with questions about due dates and homework assignments as he is not entirely sure of due dates and assignments himself. Quite passive teaching style, relies heavily on the textbook, and does not explain grammar concepts well.

Abdhelhak is the most mediocre professor I have had. Completely disorganized and unsympathetic towards his students. For instance, one night he sent an email assigning HW that was due the next morning for some god forsaken reason. He does not come up with lesson plans and simply relies on whatever the textbook provides. Don't bother taking him.

While a decent guy, he is a very very mediocre professor. His lectures are not enjoyable at all because all he does is say read from the book, do exercise ____. He never comes up with his own lessons. Also he can be quite unwelcoming in class, disorganized with due dates, and confusing with his grading process. His class is easy, but not fun.
A good teacher, he does his best to help his students succeed in attaining proficiency.

Professor Abdelehak is very very handsome. I like his class. In the first quarter, I did not enjoy much because I didn't participate enough but in the 1BX quarter I got to know him more and is more involved in his class. He gives a proper amount of assignment and the exams are not hard if you do the review sheet.

Nice and funny guy, but makes answering questions such an impossible process. When you're trying to ask a question, he plays games and most of the time he doesn't really understand what you're asking and answers a slightly different question. His attitude is a little unwelcoming at best and discouraging to introverted students at worst.
Professor Abdelhak is very professional, yet approachable and caring. He always plays it cool. He know's his stuff, so you'll be happy you took him.

In the beginning in 1A he was great and then he got progressively worse. Did not teach in class at all and just asked people about their day. Grammar is difficult especially because I had never seen arabic and he sometimes did not even go over it at all.
Abdelhak is great! Really cares about his students and makes class interesting. Quizzes/tests can be a little overwhelming, but overall, I had a great time learning Arabic from him!

I love Abdelhak! He's very funny and extremely helpful; class is usually very enjoyable. His exams are a bit difficult, but you learn arabic very well in his class and will greatly improve your abilities. It's a good class to take P/NP
Great teacher. Can move a little fast at times, but everything is clear and if you need to review any concepts he is very helpful.

Excellent professor- genuinely cares for students & actively promotes success in learning and practical use of Arabic. Brilliant, highly knowledgeable yet delivery is clear and quite clever; additionally, he is always available & friendly at OH & writes awesome letters of rec. It definitely is not a negative that he is RIDICULOUSLY GORGEOUS! YUM!
Great teacher and funny. Sometimes the class can get boring but he tries to make it better. And he's pretty hot. Take him!
Too tough of a teacher for a difficult language, can be intimidating. Don't recommend him.
He is a wonderful professor and also great to look at.  Loves grammar and always willing to help, no complaints.
Great professor. Wonderful sense of humor. Really, really nice to look at. Word.

He's got everything you need to succeed; clear hand writing, lecture notes, podcasts, a list of things you should understand for every week, and homework/activities that are relevant to the tests. I took the class for pass or fail and had no trouble getting a B.

If you have little/no background in chem (like me) and are scared to jump straight into the Chem 6 series, try taking Chem 6A with this professor! Incredibly kind, fair exams, and he holds a review session before every test emphasizing key topics. Use that info + the extra problems + the crib sheet he posts to make practice tests, it really helps!

after taking chem 4, chem 6a with prof zid was wayy better. exams are fair and he gives out practice problems, sometimes a practice exam, and also practice questions during lecture. he was good at explaining content and does what he can to set us up for success.
His exams were very fair and as long as you do practice problems you should be good!

Awesome chem prof. chem 6a does have a lot of content, can be hard but he is really helpful during office hours, lectures where useful but confusing at times on certain topics that took me a sec to learn, just do the practice reviews and GO TO DISCUSSION, its not required but no one goes and I treated it as a tutoring session which helped me a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Brian is, overall, a good professor, but sometimes he explains things in an overcomplicated way or out of order. His lectures are podcasted, and attendance isn't mandatory for the lecture or section (though you do have to do a discussion sheet graded on completion). He gives a practice midterm for the first midterm, but not the second one.

Goated professor. Make use of skeleton notes and the practice problems he has posted. Review days before midterms indicate exactly what will be on midterms. Answers questions clearly and is eager to help in office hours.

Zid is amazing. He tells you exactly what is going to be on each midterm and the final, and tells you exactly what to study. People who got a bad grade just didn't go to the lecture. Go to the lecture and follow along, and this will be a very good Chem 6A class. The discussion worksheets are also very good and actually helpful. Lecture podcasted.
The lectures can be a bit tedious but he was nice and the homework was helpful. He has a good policy for grading too if you do bad on one of the midterms.

Honestly decent lecturer, super friendly and outgoing but I was not prepared for the lecture heavy work, the homework didn't corelate much with the exams and was basic in comparison to the very in depth/ wordy exam questions. Grading was fair although there are many other better chem teachers I would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: No cheat sheet and extra credit threw me off a little bit. He's a chill guy, but you're going to be have to review the skeletal notes that are filled in class on your own. Lots of memorization and repetition needed. Tests aren't too hard but worth A LOT of points.

He's just the most meh teacher you'll ever have. He doesn't explain anything, and if you asks questions he'll dribble around them. He also overcomplicates his example problems when he shows them to the max.

Professor Zid was great!! Very clear slides that make the material pretty simple to understand. Sometimes he goes a bit fast. Two Midterms that are both fairly easy if you study a decent amount. There are no surprise questions, he tells you pretty much everything that will be on the exams. Discussion sections and lectures are not mandatory; podcast
Zid is my goat. Office hours were great, and lectures were very comprehensive.

Compared to other chem 6a professors his class and exams were a little more difficult (we don't have a cheat sheet, have frq's, etc). However, he is a great professor and teaches the content well in his lectures. He tells us what will be on his exams, and if you show up and take notes you will be fine.

Professor Zid was amazing! His lectures were well paced. I like to say they were slow enough to where you wouldn't fall behind, but fast enough to force you to remain engaged. If you attend lecture and do all the homework, you will be well prepared. Go to his office if you have a question! He is very helpful and willing.

Even though most of the grade consists of exams, Dr. Zid's lectures tell you exactly what you need to know to prepare. His office hours are helpful, and he truly cares about his students. The textbook is required for homework, but it covers more information than what is necessary.
easy if u did ap chem. great science teacher.

A great prof. the HW and the discussion work is a chore, but he cared if we did well on his tests i.e he let us stay over the time limit during midterms and finals to let us finish AND he went over basically everything that was going to be on the test the lecture before the exams. Legit the goat behavior.

Great dude. Didn't do AP Chem and this class was honestly really hard for me. Had to self-teach myself a lotta things as he just goes too fast for me. You'll be fine if you have a background in chem, are passionate in it, and can keep up with his pace. Most other 6A profs don't cover as much content as him, and no cheat sheet besides formula sheet.

Not taking AP Chem def makes the class a little harder, he's an okay lecturer. He moves through material really fast but talks really slow at the same time? He does podcast, which is helpful, and his midterms are pretty fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: didn't take ap chem... he goes really fast for me. the material is digestible, the formula sheet saved me on the midterms and he has a lenient homework policy. good basis for chem6a

Professor Zid is by far the best science teacher I've had. His lectures are very easy to understand, and his way of teaching is very effective. Lectures weren't mandatory, but you could easily catch up if you missed anything. Would definitely recommend for anyone who wants to take Chem.

amazing prof. lectures were alright, can go fast at times but if you took AP Chem, its just a review. If u didn't, good luck. Gave lots of points and explained the midterm rubric clearly. he was passionate about teaching the class and gave alot of helped in office hours. zid's the goat for a reason.

Good guy, okay professor. Struggled in this class because I had a bad chem background so if you took AP chem, you'll be fine. Goes fast in lectures that are also boring but after rewatching them I would get the concept(s). Homework assignments aren't bad. Tests are weighted 60% of grade!! No cheat sheet also.

Zid is goated, if you want a professor that teaches the material clearly, understands it well, and gives relatively easy tests he's great. I have friends taking 6A with other professors, and their tests are harder. Only gripe with this class is I feel that the discussion material didn't help me too much despite it being mandatory. Great prof tho
Best CHEM 6A prof to take during fall quarter. Would take any other chem classes with him if he taught besides 6A. Office hours were also very helpful.

Brian Zid was a great teacher. His lectures were easily comprehensible, and he would explain questions that students asked clearly. One iffy thing initially was that he doesn't allow you to create a crib sheet for midterms or finals, but he does give you a formula sheet that has everything you need to know. Just need a bit of studying!

Def my favorite professor at UCSD so far! His lectures are easy to follow and he also posts skeleton notes, making it easier to take notes in class. His tests are fair and the avg was relatively high compared to midterms for other classes. My hs teacher didn't rly teach us chem but I was able to understand most of the materials from his lectures.

I enjoyed the lectures because they were clear and understandable. The professor tells the students what to expect on the midterms and finals. I would recommend studying the lecture notes and doing the practice problems. The homework was fair and the TAs were friendly and approachable.

Midterms and final are very very hard but they are curved pretty heavily. His lectures are very fast with a lot of information all at once. I definitely would still go to lecture even though he doesn't take attendance.

Dr. Zid is a clear, effective lecturer! Optional discussion sections gave time to work on weekly worksheets graded on completion or weekly online homework with the opportunity to ask for help from TAs. Worksheets and HW help boost your grade which was mainly determined by 2 MTs and a Final. This course allows for a midterm to be dropped!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He goes extremely fast, so be prepared to have the lecture content written down before coming to class or have an iPad with the slides downloaded. He is a good professor who clearly knows what he is talking about, and his midterm and final were very fair. Make sure to study up on concepts well.

Never took chem so I struggled but he was so kind. He said it can be a hard class if you have 0 history of chem. I struggled but SI sessions helped me alot. His lectures are very reflective of his exams, no cheat sheet, no extra credit. HW was a frustrating software, my O-Chem friends struggled with it. Would rec taking chem 4 first if no chem hx.

Professor Zid was a great professor to have for chem 6a. I never took ap chem in high school so it was hard to understand some points he made but, he was understanding with every single one of his students. I had a medical emergency before the final and he allowed me to take a makeup exam on a later date. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good grading structure as grade is weighted 60% exams, and 40% HW and POGILs. Final can replace a midterm grade as well. Exams do not surprise you with new content. Lectures are good, occasionally he goes a little fast but overall quite good. HW is reasonable as well.

Great teacher with good lectures, but he speeds through quickly so it may be difficult to keep up. Tough class but he explains stuff well especially in office hours. Discussions are graded on completion not attendance so I stopped going after week 3 and just did the assignment. Tests are fair and reflective of lectures. Would definitely recommend.

For a gen chem class, this is pretty easy. If you have taken AP chem or CC chem it will be very easy for you. His exams are VERY reflective of what he lectures are on. 2 exams and a final make up 60% of your grade. Discussions aren't mandatory but are chill and a good time to get the section assignment done. I recommend this prof for chem 6A.

Dr. Zid was great. He tends to speed through slides, but if you rewatch the lectures at a slower pace, it is easier to understand material. His TAs were amazing. There is weekly HW that can take some time, and no cheat sheets for exams. Discussion is not mandatory though which was great considering mine was late. I would gladly take Dr. Zid again.

Awesome professor and you can tell he really likes what he does and cares for his students. Can go pretty fast during lecture but will answer your questions if you have any. Grade is based on homework due once week ranging from 15-20 question, two midterms, and a final. No cheat sheets allowed but he gives you a reference sheet.

Gave us notes to fill out as he gave lectures. The lectures were very clear, he would explain a topic and also allow students to work through it themselves with practice problems. Every week had 2-5 pages of additional questions to study for midterms (midterms were ~75% MC, 25% FRQ). Discussions allow for group work but are not mandatory at all.

I would definitely recommend taking Zid's class. He tells you everything you need to know for the exams. You don't get a cheat sheet, but you don't need one. He does practice problems that are due every week and the discussions aren't mandatory, but there is a worksheet due. He can be a little boring at times but otherwise is a good professor.

Zid reads from his slides, but is very knowledgeable when asked questions in lecture. Grade based upon 1 online hw per week, assignments in DI sections, and two midterms & a final. Very straightforward and a good lecturer.

Zid is a good teacher/lecturer. However I would not recommend him to students taking 6a, as he is the only teacher (from what I have heard) that 1. doesn't allow cheat sheets, 2. does multiple choice AND short answer, 3. and his tests are always a week before every other chem class. but if you took chem honors, or AP you should be good
He's a cool guy. Don't change Zid. You the goat.
loved his chem class- very clear lectures and he was very passionate ab the subject! barely studied but paid attention in lecture

Professor Zid's lecture can be a bit tedious at times. But I would take him over some Chemistry professors in UCSD. A shame he only teaches CHEM 6A. Super accessible outside, had meetings with him from time to time. Curved a lot during midterms/final. Doesn't do cheat sheets, but has a reference sheet (didn't help except for the periodic table).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Zid was a very straightforward and enthusiastic professor. He taught everything that would be on the exam and you should be good if you spend the time studying. Exams were mainly multiple choice. Just keep in mind that he doesn't do cheat sheets, I know some other 6A professors too and it can be a deal breaker for some people.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As someone who didn't take AP Chem this class was hard. I spent 1-2 hours outside of class each week studying and reviewing but ultimately did fine. Tests and lectures were very straightforward and to the point. He doesn't try to trick you and the class is padded with hw and di projects. Many lectures ended early. Good prof if you put in the work.

The other people mentioning that not having taken AP Chem make this class extremely difficult are correct. Zid is kind and clearly enjoys chemistry, but his lectures are hard to follow for those not already familiar with the topics presented. The hardest topics are glossed over with a max of one practice problem being shown and little explanation.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Zid was a bad lecturer. He is one of those teachers that say a lot but in reality, end up saying nothing. I basically ended up self-teaching the course to myself. The only good thing about the course was that his exams were straightforward, not tricky. Homework taught me more than the lectures did. Super sweet guy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Zid is a fast lecturer, but his slides were straight forward and easy to read. Exam were straight forward with majority of it being mc. Homework was a little difficult due to limited attempts + deduction for every wrong attempt. Coming from a person that never took ap chem, if you consistent review each week and put the work in then it'll go fine!

there are easier chem 6a professors. He is a good explainer but a fast. not bad professor. Doesn't give any type of cheat sheet which all the other classes get. If you have a long journey of chem ahead then take him because you ill learn a lot but if you only have to take one chemistry class then don't take him cause he makes his class extra hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Like plenty of others have said, if you haven't take AP chem prior to this course, it's incredibly difficult. Don't get me wrong, Professor Zid is incredibly nice. However, his explanations are really difficult to understand for an introductory class. Most of what I have learned I learned from either my friends or from online.
If you haven't taken AP chemistry before you will have a hard time. He is a very nice guy, but doest teach only reads off his slides and goes too fast. Not an intro course at all.
if you havent taken AP chem, good luck fam

Be warned, if you haven't taken AP Chem or IB Chem in high school, you will have hard time in his class. His lectures aren't helpful, and his lectures goes by very fast so if you miss a day, it will be hard to catch up. The discussions class aren't helpful at all either. But if you have taken AP Chem, this class should be okay.

Brian Zid was very generous but he could not explain things easily for students. I trusted all his great ratings but was so disappointed. Having only taken one chemistry course in h.s, it was so difficult to do well in his class. Lectures are basically useless, you will have to teach yourself. Big curve at the end saved my grade.

I enjoyed this professor. His powerpoints are straightforward, easy to follow, and facilitate note-taking. I wish he taught more courses in chemistry. He makes it important to go to discussion sections in order to finish worksheets but I didn't mind that at all. Exams were easy. Structure of class and lists of assignments sets you up for success.

Great professor, but sometimes the pace of the class was a little bit high in the most complex subjects. The PowerPoint slides went by fast, so you have to be focused on the whole lecture to take notes properly and understand the class. If you do that, you can get through the course.

I took Zid for an elective chem class. He's the best chem professor at UCSD. Explains things clearly and simply. He is very dedicated and encouraging. During TA strikes, he went to every discussion. If you get the opportunity to take him, definitely do it!

I had a really hard time in this class because I never took AP Chem and didnt know how to study in general. Super nice guy, gives dad of young girl vibes if that makes sense. He moves really quick and you NEED to  either go to lecture or watch it online. I did fail both midterm and final, but I passed with a B because heavily pads grade w homework.

Professor Zid is great! During the TA strike he would personally stand in for the TAs during discussion sections. The midterms and final were not too hard if you have taken chem before and are understanding/doing the homework. He does go fast during lectures, but there are podcasts you can look back on. Overall a chill and cool guy.

Professor Zid is a wonderful prof. He genuinely cares about his students and will put the work into helping you. This class is hard! If you havent taken a chem class in a while go take Chem4 then come back. Midterms and the final are worth 60% of your grade. They are all short response. I recommend him if youre ready! Go to office hours 100%!!

Zid knew what he was talking about and was easy to talk to. The class was very calculation heavy compared to other chem 6a classes. Tests were free response which had its pros and cons. Overall, I learned a lot but I wouldn't recommend him if you do not have a lot of chem knowledge already.

Pretty good professor who always answers questions during lectures and is willing to put in effort to ensure that his students succeed. If you take this class with no prior knowledge of chemistry, you might struggle a bit. Doesn't give a lot of homework and his exams are pretty much based on lecture material. Overall would recommend.

Professor Zid is a really good teacher for Chem 6A as he seems to always want the best for his students. This class is pretty difficult if you haven't taken chem in a while. If you do the homework and understand the practice problems, the exam is similar. The FRQ midterms were more difficult but partial credit helped.

Overall amazing professor, lectures aren't mandatory but I recommend going --podcasted if you can't make them. The first midterm is basically what the AP chem content was. He cares about his students a lot and taught discussion sections during the strike in place of TAs. 10/10 recommend, explains concepts well, and is open to questions & emails.

Took Professor Zid in FA21. Professor Zid is easily one of my favorite chemistry professors till date. Super helpful lecturer, answers questions very well. Tests were free response and VERY representative of homework and lecture content, not difficult if you study. If you have the opportunity to take him... do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Zid's teaching style is not very accessible for everyone, as in his lectures he uses fill-in-the-blank slides with around a couple vocab words added per slide. The first midterm was difficult, as it was a majority of mathematical questions and free-repsonse, though there are lots of opportunities for partial credit.

Solid Professor, makes himself easily available outside lectures, even came to teach the discussion sections after the TAs went on strike, his lectures, along with some other form of supplementary help make his homework and his exams manageable. Just make sure to study and ask questions, he is one of the nicest professors on campus.

Nicest professor I've ever met! Extremely caring and attentive. Professor Zid really cares about his students - spend a lot of time with students who are enthusiastic in science. He gives excellent lectures and provides students great opportunities to study. Don't hesitate to take his class!
Professor Zid is very excellent! He is patient, attentive, and caring. Definitely take his class! Everything in the course is perfectly arranged; the lectures are great, and he is so understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Reads slides and does not explain. Expects us to connect the dots (to an unreasonable extent) No reasons as to why one might not understand something, just blurs off with "it's difficult" or "it's beyond this course." No stream of consciousness, no guiding, just jumping from one thing to another with a "So." Nice dude but cannot teach.

Had an A- by the end of the quarter; decided to email him and he let me complete a homework assignment from weeks ago to reach an A. He's very caring about his students and is accessible outside of class. Tests are short answers with lots of partial credit. Lectures are very clear and as long as you watch them you should do fine on tests.

Probably the best 6A professor. Always made time to answer questions and was accessible after class. Was pretty clear about what topics were on the midterms and always had review lectures. Midterms were a bit complicated, and he gave everyone extra points on the second one after the class average was lower than the first one. Overall a solid choice

Prof Zid wants students to learn and is very accommodating if you have to miss an exam. There are 2 midterms and since the class average was lower on the second exam than the first so he blamed himself for not teaching well enough and gave everyone a couple extra points. Having taken AP Chem the class was a breeze, but if not it can seem fast paced

I did take AP Chem, however, I found the class a bit difficult. There were weekly online hw for points and weekly discussions graded for participation. The two midterms weren't anything more advanced than what Professor went over in class in his examples. The final is easier and he replaces a midterm if your final grade is higher. I recommend!

Amazing chem prof. I never took AP chem in high school and was still able to do well on midterms by making sure I understood all of the learning objectives and reviewing lecture problems. Very clear on what is on tests: if you didn't cover it in class, it's not on the test. Responds quickly to emails, office hours are very helpful.

Dr. Zid is easily the best chemistry teacher I have EVER had. I will admit that I have had AP Chem experience in high school before which made it easier, but he is extremely explicit that his test content will come straight from the lecture. If you didn't learn it in class, it's not on the test, which is super helpful. Take notes and you're golden.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Out of my 4 professors for my first quarter of college, Brian cared the most. He was always quick to answer emails and he was very flexible with homework and testing. His tests are very hard, but if you study and come to his lectures then you will be prepared. Overall, Zid is an amazing professor and I am glad I took his class.

Amazing! He answers your emails and actually cares about you. His lectures are very clear and his exams are straight forward as long as you understand everything on the lectures. He does go through the material very rapidly so if you have never taken chemistry before I do not recommend. The amount of homework is ok. Lectures are recorded

At the beginning of the quarter he mentioned that he "simultaneously goes too fast and too slow" through lectures, and he sure wasn't lying. Every Powerpoint took 1.5-2 lectures to get through what other professors normally cover in 20-30 minutes, and he glazed over the barebones summary of each slide while giving barely any time to take notes.

Perfect chemistry teacher. If you listen to lectures and actually put in some effort it is very easy to get close to a 100 on all the tests. Midterms and final were very straightforward. Study the learning objectives conceptually and know how to do problems similar to those on the lecture slides. Don't listen to the bad reviews; they're just wrong.

a really nice professor. his exams mostly cover his lectures and a bit of the homework. his office hours are extremely helpful. you need to fully understand the concepts to do well on the exam-dont just memorize bullet points. go to office hours if you questions about the content or your exam/how it was graded!

I will say you might struggle if you don't like calculations, as he's probably the most calculation based compared to the other professors. Besides this, he's honestly solid as long as you go over the learning objectives he provides. People say he goes too fast but he does it so we have more time to study the material before an exam.

Really nice guy. Class is well organized. Honestly I found the class too easy and too slow which was fine. His midterms are so doable and his lectures are slow but he explains things and is very patient with students. He will spend as much time needed to make sure all questions are answered.

WORST chemistry teacher. If you did not take AP chem you will not pass. All of the previous rating lied. Does not go into detail while teaching he expects you to know everything. Midterm grade average is a D. Don't recommend he doesn't care about his students at all. No curves, open ended exams, unnecessary hard when its gen. chem.

please trust me! If you didn't take AP Chem, it is going to be VERY difficult. it would've been nice to see the professor accommodate for everyone's type of learning. I just wish his pace was slower, I think we were on week 7 material during weeks 4-5, he doesn't elaborate. I felt played bc of his high ratings on RMP pls take my advice <3

Professor Zid's powerpoint slides are concise and easy to follow. The exam content comes straight from the lecture slides, so the test won't contain info not covered in lecture. Lots of opportunities for partial credit on exams. He takes the time to answer questions during class and moves through lessons relatively quickly but it is manageable.

He tries to keep his lectures simple and makes sure only to focus on the things we really need to know. Holds review lectures before midterms and goes over concepts that will be on the test and is open to any questions. Workload isn't too heavy. Records lectures and going back through lecture podcasts is a great way to study for tests.

Professor Zid is one of the nicest professors I've had. He takes the time to answer questions during lecture and go over practice problems so that we feel more equipped for the exams. Exams are fair with lots of partial credit- it's not black and white. Wish he was teaching the next level. All lectures are recorded and can be accessed online.
Zid goes through lectures really fast. His exams are written and very hard and often a step further than the homework. His grading is not forgiving either despite it being written. Don't take him.

Professor Zid would often be 2 to 3 weeks ahead in lecture material than what was originally scheduled. This being said he vaguely and quickly went over the material and didn't provide many example problems. Midterm was extremely difficult and he makes you memorize a bunch of unnecessary info. Doesn't curve even when majority of class does poorly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Zid is a young fellow who is very knowledgeable in the area of Chemistry. His lectures were easy to follow, as he allowed the use of skeleton notes that he provided. He makes all of his learning objectives very clear. His grading system is very generous as well. 10/10 highly recommend.

This class was A LOT of work. A 1-2 hour lecture took me 8-10 hours to get through because of the amount of content, plus the additional textbook reading (which I would recommend). However, the way the exams were structured (5 mini exams) allowed many chances to make up a bad grade. Exams kind of like AP Chem FRQs. Would recommend!
The lectures were all asynchronous which was nice. They were always very clear and made it so the homework and exams were easy. Overall a really great choice for 6A.

Professor Zid is amazing! He has pre-recorded lectures that makes hard material easily to understand. His office hours are very helpful and are a great opportunity to connect with him. If you go to them frequently, you're guaranteed to do well in the class. He really cares for the students and wants them to succeed. 100% would recommend!

Dr. Zid is super sweet! His lectures were amazing and really helpful for me, and I thought he did a good job breaking down complex concepts into understandable language. I was a little intimidated by him at first, but he was always welcoming during office hours. His tests are very conceptual and a bit difficult, but they're fair and helped me learn

Dr. Zid is a great professor. I only gave him a 5 in difficulty because his assessments (learning checks) are concept heavy and each learning check is so long (2hrs each for 5 learning check in total). I definitely do recommend him; he teaches chemistry well. I wish I could have met him in person.

Mr. Zid is an outstanding teacher. I found his lectures to be interesting and concise. While this class is material heavy, I think he does a great job of explaining the concepts and the way he grades is fair and equal throughout the course. Because of covid I did not get to meet him in person, but online he was great!

He is extremely understanding about the current circumstances and his grading reflects it. His lectures can be confusing at times, but if you ever need something cleared up there is always office hours, discussion sections and the textbook.

Dr. Zid is great. He teaches very well but be aware that his learning checks tend to lean more on the conceptual side. And so learning checks (which are like tests) arent too easy. However, the questions you see on the learning checks are all material that hes covered (even though you may feel stuck on the question, youll realize he taught it).

Chem 6A was a tough class after only taking reg chem in hs. His lectures were pretty slow so I watched them on 2x speed. (Fall 2020  COVID) Generally he explained things pretty well and was responsive to questions over email. The discussions are jsut group work on a POGIL led by a TA, mine was pretty chill. No specific complaints about Zid
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Zid is great! His lectures are recorded and asynchronous, but go over the material really well. There are five learning checks every other week, which can be a lot sometimes but are very straight-forward. All the other assignments make it easy to pad your grade a bit.

I am not too experience with chemistry, but Zid teaches it well and he definitely cares about his students. We had 5 learning checks which are like tests that you get up to 2 hours for, since there are 4 questions that are 30 minutes each. He drops the lowest one of them, but they are pretty tough (atleast for me). You should be fine, with lectures

Dr. Zid really cares about your well being and he also really wants you to succeed in his class. There are no midterm/final but instead there are 5 learning checks which are like 5 tests (each learning check covers 2 chapters; 2 hrs each). The learning check is not too difficult. Just do your required materials and you'll do just fine in his class.

I would 100% recommend! The lectures are pre-recorded and come with skeleton notes. Chemistry is hard, but Zid makes the information easy to understand and enjoyable. There are 5 learning checks (aka quizzes) every 2 weeks. The learning checks are fair, easy to understand, and cover everything from the lectures, group activities, and homework.

Zid felt like a really chill and clear professor (always communicated clearly about expectations). We did one lecture + HW a week which didn't feel too bad. Didn't give us final/midterm because of COVID, instead we had a learning check every two weeks which was fairly difficult (not too bad though). A very solid choice, would recommend!!

ZId is a solid Chem 6A choice. He explains well, but does go very fast. The material is not difficult and the tests and quizzes aren't too hard either. Go to class, because he does have "pop" class activities that you must write in hand and paper and turn in.
He was very passionate and always answered questions. His pace was a bit fast for me

Very clear and easy to understand lectures. The exams are extremely challenging, but Zid makes the expectation clear and if you study it is possible to do well. His class isnt hard but he pushes you to learn and fully grasp the information. Overall a rewarding class to do good in.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is really good at teaching and his exams are difficult but fair. Funny guy at times too. Homework every week with 20+ questions on each assignment
Zid is an overall good professor. Attendance isn't explicitly mandatory in lecture but he assigns group works in lecture which are turned in for points. One allowed discussion absence.

He's very knowledgeable about the subject but explains concepts in the most complicated way possible; his lectures are very easy to get lost in, and his tests, although usually fair and based off the homework and quizzes, are not curved. However, the discussions and his office hours are very helpful if you take the time to go to them.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Zid is a solid choice for Chem 6A. If you don't have a background in Chemistry, his lectures can be too fast-paced at times. However, if you complete his homework (once a week), you should be fine. He has 3 Quizzes, 2 Midterms and 1 Final which are all curved.

If you have somewhat of a background in Chem then this class should be an easy A. If you don't, Prof. Zid's lectures are moderately paced and goes into great depths in explaining concepts. He has 3 quizzes, 2 midterms, and 1 final with a generous grading policy. He has in class Group Work so attendance is mandatory. Class is both screencasted.

There's Group Work before class ends every now and then, it's easy. I was on my phone throughout the year, but the ample resources he provides on TritonEd is so darn helpful. HIs homework takes a good 1-2 hours to knockout and it's once a week. There's a quizzes in discussion that can be resubmitted for half the missed points and a group powerpoint

He isn't the best explainer in the world, but his lectures are fairly easy to understand, and he is very organized with the material. Thing is CHEM 6A is kind of annoying class in general, so much so that the band Switchfoot specifically wrote a song about it, but he makes it a little less annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Heavy assignments, hard exams, hard materials. But I do feel that I really learn something and that Brian cares a lot about us.

Professor Zid rocks!! He moves quickly through lecture & the material is difficult, but he does his best to teach it in a way that his students understand. If you want A, you need to go to lecture and also be prepared to read the textbook outside of class for additional help. Zid truly cares about his students & wants the best for them!
He really cares how he does lecturing and cares how all of his students do. Difficult material but he really tries to make it as easy to understand as possible.

Absolutely need to take Nicholas!! Course is based on his lectures, which are straight forward, so no textbooks. Exams are all based on his lectures so you will be ready! Participation matters, so just show up. He cares. Allows partners for exams sometimes. Very flexible! Take him, best class and professor! Accessible outside of class.

Hands down the best professor I have had the pleasure of taking at UCSD. He makes all of his lectures and uses information from his experience in the field so you do not need a text book. His quizzes are based on his lectures and lecture slides, offers enough time to do your quizzes and they are straight forward. Take him and you wont regret it.

Professor Abi-Samra is one of the best engineering professors in the university. His courses are like a breath of fresh air compared to the other engineering courses, as he has simple yet interesting things to teach that aren't difficult to understand. Very caring professor. Homeworks are just weekly take home quizzes and tests are straightforward.

One of the best professors I've met. Really knowledgeable and really responsible. Professor Nicholas always responded my email in time and answered my questions thoroughly. He tried to give us many opportunities for bonus points and made sure that each one of us keep up with the course during lectures. Truly a respected professor.

This class was an absolute breeze. Partly because the material is relatively easy, and partly because this professor has great experience in the field and explains things very well. This professor really cares about his students and is extremely nice.

Professor Abi-Samra is so caring and respected. He always thinks about students and wants us to learn more from him. He gave us a second chance to take midterm when he found out some of us are not satisfied. He replied emails really fast and made sure he solved your problem. He provided a lot of opportunities to help find job/intern, too.

Professor Samra was one of the best ECE professors at UCSD that I had. While it may seem like his classes are easy, you should pay attention to every single detail. He provides some real knowledge of what is the future in the power industry, and I firmly believe it will help you in the future finding jobs if you have hopes to work in the industry.

Incredibly caring professor. I felt like her quizzes were a little too easy at times lol but hey, I'm not complaining! Accessible outside of class and responds to questions really quickly. Take her class if you have the option, I cannot recommend her enough. You will feel valued as a student in her class. I hope she teaches more classes at UCSD.
She's an amazing teacher and also takes notes during the lecture while explaining the concepts. Final was no penalty and it could only improve your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: TAKE HER CLASS

Abby is the best professor Ive had during COVID-19. She adapted the class amazingly well to online format. Tests are very fair and homework has unlimited tries. She genuinely cares about students mental health and is very lenient on deadlines. Fun extra credit parts. Replies to questions real quick. Love her cats. A very sweet person in general.

This class had a LOT of required readings, with specific, lengthy weekly discussion posts. The readings are also very complex, so they take quite a bit of time to fully comprehend. Prof. Shragge is passionate about his teaching and is a somewhat tough, but fair, grader who gave great feedback. I learned much from this class but it was difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I took two of Professor Shragge's history classes: History of the American Suburb and War and American Society. He is one of the BEST professors I've ever had. His enthusiasm for the subject is contagious and every lecture was interesting. His classes made me wish I had majored in history.

Took Shragge for winter culture of war class, very interesting lectures, he was clearly interested in the material he was teaching which is always appreciated.  Happy to help students outside of class, approachable, grades a little too easily  but excellent teacher nonetheless. Knew people who easily got B's without trying, I got an A but tried.

An amazing professor!!! Intelligent,helpful,polite,and overall just a very nice and approachable person. Interested in striking a conversation,and values your opinions about the world.Prof.Shragge sees a potential in each and every one of his students. Also,he is always involved in his community.
Very good professor. He is very helpful, lets you know what will be on the tests. He also doesn't just lecture, he engages with students and cares what you think. Highly recommended
Very cool teacher who loves to chat.  His lectures are interesting and really loves students' participation.  Grades generously on essays.  A lot of reading!

Amazing Professor! Knows his stuff! So knowledgeable of history. Very helpful to students and really cares about his job. Wish I could take more of his classes! If you want to learn take his class! One midterm, paper and then final.

Good to great professor.  Lectures are rather engaging and help illuminate the texts we read.  The amount of reading for this class is immense (around 1200 pages).  That doesn't include the reading of outside sources for the final paper.  Grades pretty fairly.  Helpful to students, especially if you work with him in developing your term paper.

This prof is genuinely nice and really does care whether you understand or not. He uses podcast so you can listen to his lectures again if you need. I think it's so helpful! One paper, midterm and final. He's so passionate about what he teaches. Highly recommended!
Really great class, interesting material.  material with a message.  Got an A, barely did any work, just wrote good essays and wrote good paragraphs on my finals.  never went to class

Shragge is great professor that into teaching.The class that I took was about the relationship b/w US history & the American culture. Since I'm not from here nor into history,I had a hard time to understand some terms and evens from the course materials but he helped me a lot by giving clear lecture like telling a story. Not so organized but Easy A

If you aren't interested in urban studies, Shragge's lectures will probably bore you. If you're interested in the subject, the class is pretty straightforward and relatively easy. Just make an effort to do the readings and go to lectures and this class is a piece of cake.
Good professor. Easy midterm and final. Also, the course load was a bit too light (which was a good thing). Too bad i hated the subject because i hate history in general.
I loved this class! The readings were interesting and he was a great, enthusiastic lecturer. I also loved the "field trip." I HIGHLY recomend this class.

Excellent professor! I had no interest in the class prior to taking it, but Prof. Shragge's enthusiasm and excitement about the subject really made the class interesting. Some of the lectures were boring, but he usually had music or film or poetry in the beginning of class relating to the theme of the lecture. Very helpful during OH, terrific class

Prof.Shragge is great! I took his War in Society class, and he shined. He really wants students to do well. He will go out of his way to help them. He's really cute too. Love those smart guys with glasses.

Boring lecture, but it's DOC, what do you expect? However, he is very nice and his final was  a complete joke, easiest DOC final ever, and no midterm. I started studying the night before the final and got an A

Lectures are extremely hard to follow, especially compared to my previous DOC lecturers. Rarely refers to the readings. You will go into the final having NO CLUE what you need to know. So good luck with him. Take Ta instead.

Great teacher, teaches with a passion, he talks in a way using his hands and eyes as if he was there is WW1 or WW2 and witnessed it himself, he has good discussions with movies and if you go to his office hours, even for a billion times, he helps you a lot. great guy
He is an amazing teacher...gives students a lot of respect and cares about what he is teaching.  He is available for help and always gives good sugestions.

His lectures are incoherent and boring. He also said some extremely prejudiced stuff like "hopefully someday the immigrants will become like us" (when speaking about Mexican border patrol). He finds assimilation the "goal" of the immigrant, it seems. He also trivializes multiculturalism, thinking that it consitutes enjoying ethnic food.

He's alright, but nothing special. His lectures are interesting, but he tends to ramble and rant and sometimes notetaking is difficult. Class consists of 1 final, 1 project/paper, and attendance (which is mandatory). Test wasn't that difficult, but you certainly need to attend class/take good notes.
Good lecturer. Material was somewhat interesting, but based on clarity and test, very clear. Take SHRAGGE!

Great teacher!!! Definitely knows his stuff about this class, very clear and class consists of two papers and a final. read the books as much as you can and attend class to get more info for the paper. Highly Recommended!!!
Nice guy and always helpful. He used overheads and powerpoints so that was good and he went over some of the material. Class really depends on the TA though.

Took him during spring quarter and he was awesome! He picked interesting books and was very helpful at test time. He was very honest and his lectures were very concise and direct. I would take him again anytime. Take him and you won't regret it!

EXCELLENT TEACHER! Tells you his views from the start, you can embrace or reject them, but he tells you history the way it is, and he has facts to back it up. Very understanding and is willing to help any way he can! TAKE HIM!! you'll enjoy his class!

Actually he's a lil hard to follow. He has so much to say and his mouth can't move so fast, so he'll go off on interesting tangents but eventually he'll come back to what he was saying originally. That was the only annoying thing about taking notes in his lectures. He's very helpful outside of class
No Comments

He is a really good professor because he is passionate about what he teaches.  Lectures were very helpful for the tests and the project was really fun to do.  I would definitely take another class with him.

This guy is awesome! His lectures are insightful, interesting and his exams and papers required are not too bad. He requires you to do research and attend lectures but he is always willing to talk and has general interest in his students. I reccomend him for any class

Probably the most disorganized class I'll ever take at UCSD. She had no structure for what we needed to do and didn't really teach. One of the guest speakers we had probably taught us more in a day than what we learned in a quarter. Too bad the TAs were actually cool. I heard the last professor for this actually had a structure so idk what happened
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects
