reviews.comment: Highly do not recommend taking her. She has no structure and assigns homework that can take you upwards of 3 hours to do. It felt like the class was a complete waste of time and was filled with busy work, including the midterm. I feel like i learned absolutely nothing from this course. I am not paying tuition at UCSD to not learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: This is the worst professor I have ever taken at UCSD. The class is VERY pointless with busy work that can take you upwards of 3 hours to do. It is an absolute waste of time. For the Final, she wants us to write about all "musical parameters" learned in class for 32 group's video performances and their made up scores. DONT take her for MUS 5.

Classes are all lecture based.. She gives 2 unannounced in-class assignment, each 10% of your grade, and if you miss it, there's no make-ups. Lecture slides are unclear and sparse if you're counting on them. Exams are long essays + she gives study guides based on lecture material. She's monotonous and serious throughout so not a fun lecture either.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly this class wasn't hard but what screwed me and a lot of people was missing one of the days where she gave an unannounced participation assignment which was worth 10%. Also, if you don't include some specific words and definitions from her book will deduct A LOT of points. Both midterm and final are in class long essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class was a pretty straightforward, exciting, and accessible course. Professor Abrajano does give you a midterm and final study guide before class but, remember to fill out the study guide so she can look over it and provide you with feedback. If you do this, you will do well on the exams, but if you don't, then it is hard to do well on exams
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Grading for attendance/participation is a joke, but definitely not a very funny one if you're an unlucky student. Had 2 in-class assignments, each worth 10% of your overall grade, given on random unannounced days. What if you missed a day? Screwed. Lectures off of undetailed powerpoints, so hard to know what you missed if you missed lecture.

She was Awesome!! She really knows what she is talking about and really wants you to do well. She wants to educate you into action and to know that you can make a change. Class is very easy, just make sure you participate so she knows you and that you show up to class because she has a sign in sheet. 2essays and no final:) shes sweet

2 in-class assignments that weren't hard, however I didn't truly know what she expected as a good responses. A midterm and final which she gives a study guide. If you pay attention to lecture, you'll get an A. And she's very pretty!
She is very liberal, and it is her way or the highway. All she does is lecture with her powerpoint and her class is very boring.

The class includes an extensive amount of reading. She goes over some of the topics in class. The midterm and final aren't too bad. It depends more on your TA, because they grade everything. I saw the class as very boring and hard to pay attention to. She uses a power point so the notes are easy to take.
She is a great speaker. The class is very interesting if you do the work. Pay attention in class, take notes, and read the book and you're all set. Plus she is hot!

I once approached her and asked a clarification question regarding a chapter in the book we were supposed to read for the next class. She told me that I could find answers to my questions in the book.

I took her Race and Ethnicity class. Unless you're lazy or plain stupid, there is absolutely no way anyone could fail her class. She posts up her lecture slides on ted and gives you a clear cut final and midterm study guide that is very similar to the actual test. HOWEVER, i'm not going to lie...the class is boring.

Overall, class wasn't very difficult (thanks to my TA!). Abrajano goes over the material and points out everything you need to know, but as she was my first college professor, she made college seem a lot more intimidating than it really is. Not friendly or engaging. Also, not much enthusiasm on her part.
She is a very nice, caring lady. The material is very interesting too.

NOT HELPFUL AT ALL~~!!! shes more of a research person and cannot teach with enthusiasm. She reads every chart wrong on the powerpoint. She also adheres too closely to her outline and doesnt show any additional media that may help students understand the course better
Professor Abrajano is one of the best professors at UCSD! That's all I have to say about that.
She's not very interesting but she is pretty hot. Makes points along PowerPoint and not really jokingly or interestingly involved with students in the lecture

No attendance,lectures posted online,great study guides for midterm/final(blue book). One paper(5-7pg). She seems aloof and disinterested during lecture. Loves her TAs (the girl TA grades very harsh). Way too picky on blue book responses. Not helpful w/questions. I feel my exam and paper grades should have been at least B+  and I got B on everthing

I normally don't believe a lot of comments on ratemyprofessor, nor have I ever rated one before. But I felt it was necessary to advise students not to take this professor. She shows serious lack of concern for her students and is highly discourteous when u go to her for help. The grading is ridiculous and her graders aren't any nicer than she is
NOT recommended.
By far the meanest teacher I've ever had, grades EXTREMELY harshly.

The material the professor covered was all derived from the two text books almost word for word. She gave out study guides for both the midterm and final. Overall the class was extremely easy but the quality of professor was lacking. The TA's graded very harshly yet reasonable due to the fact that we received the tests beforehand via study guide.

Class seemed simple: lecture based on power points posted online, few readings per class and couple documentaries per week. Study guides also online. But, TAs graded HARSHLY (my ta told me they graded essay tests on specific words) and she was unfriendly and unhelpful during office hours. I would not recommend her.

She just doesn't seem like an intellectual individual. Her lectures are painful to hear since she's not very articulate nor does she seem like an expert on the subject. Her grading is also very harsh, and she wasn't very friendly when I went to office hours. I do not recommend her at all.

Not the best professor at UCSD. Her lectures are boring and unclear. She doesn't seem to care about the students much and seems to have a negative attitude. She will surprise you on tests/paper; go to class for this reason because she will tell you directions in class and then they wont be on the prompt. Not recommended. Lecture notes are online.

Class isn't super easy, but it's straight-forward, grading is weird but if you do all the reading and go to class, you will get an A. The professor is suuuuuper helpful outside of class and very amicable, and she is pretty too. Topic isn't super interesting, but it's cool.
Definitely not the best professor at UCSD. NOT an easy A like everyone says. Much harder than s he used to be apparently.
Best Professor ever!!! Very helpful! A must take!
AMAZING Professor!!! Cant stress it enough!

Good Prof. She is young and just started recently.  I think some of the bad comments are from her first classes took her Fall 07 class in Latino politics.  Good lecturer, fairly light course load and she is easy on the eyes too.  Take her class its worth it.

She's very nice, but her teaching style is kind of all oer the place. She cannot reference questions if she doesn't know the statisitics for them. It got kind of annoying after a while, but the class was very interesting as were the readings.
Super cool prof. lectures interesting most of the time. material tested is not difficult to understand, but TA graded very hard. 1 super short, easy paper. take her if you can!

EASY CLASS! it is extremely basic material. hopefully common knowledge for poli sci majors. Never went to class and never read and got an A+. Definately take it for poli sci requirement. lectures are completely useless. tests are multiple choice.

Abrajano is very helpful if you go to office hours. She gives a study guide for the midterm and final, so getting an A on those is pretty easy. Don't blow off the critical response paper, it is graded more toughly than the exams. It is refreshing to learn from a young woman.

Great professor.  TA was a fair grader also. I took her Latino politics class.  It is her passion and she taught it well.  Take home midterm. She also was cool enough to provide a study guide. She is easy on the eyes too! I recommend her.

lectures not super clear, does pwr point and posts them online but they arent very informative. gives study guide for midterm & final which are both ID & essay questions. on midterm her selections off the study guide seemed to be the least relevant ones to the course. would have been better if she had put defs on slides, but wikipedia works!
definitely as to be the easiest class i have ever taken. i really regret taking this class P/NP. I ended up getting an A in the class and barely even tried

easiest class i have ever taken. i regret taking it pass/no pass. if you go to lecture, u'll find out she basically summarizes the important parts of the book and her final "reviews" are basically a table of contents for her tests. if ur majoring in poli, avoid. but if ur doing it for as area of focus or just want an easy grade, highly recommended.

Professor was really easy. Attended lectures because I like this subject, but overall as a lecturer she is okay. First lectures sucked, then got a lot better towards the end of the year. Overall, I enjoyed this intro class.

Shes young, pretty,& articulate. Friendly and helpful during office hours. The course material is pretty easy. No need to take notes, everything is posted online. She might not know the answer to every question, but most were lame and stuff we didn't need to know.

Prof is reall nice. Class is extremely easy. She recites lectures from slides verbatim. No need to go to class. Scan the readings, and you'll do excellent on midter. Paper topic isn't too habby either. I'd take her again because she's so easy.

An overall good Professor. She is nice but her power point slides are redundant no need to go to class or take notes. The paper topic isn't that bad and The highest score was a 97 on the midterm. I should know it was me. Good teach overall

This professor is terrible. It's nearly impossible to take notes in her class. I even use a laptop and can type 80 wpm. Whenever someone asks her a question that the readings can't answer, she can't answer it either. She even lost the midterm I KNOW I took and told me and two other people that her TAs "don't think" they lost them.

Just had him this past summer session. He is a really nice professor and obviously cares for his students, but honestly..his tests were so unfair. there was only 5 questions on the midterm..50 point. And 6 questions on the final..60  points. I've never had an ECON professor that had tests like this! The questions are very specific (some). I got C-
he is a kind and active teacher. his classes are terrific.

This class is a joke!There's 1 MAIN exam at the 4th wk and that's 80% of the grade.final is a quiz(20%).The mid-term was one to one to the class grade.He's not helpful!Hard to understand him and he couldn't understand you as well...HORRIBLE class!!curve apply to over 60 only.he said exam is about what he taught in class or in bk,which is not true

Took Energy Economics w/ him SU08. Lectures were not thrilling but were very straightforward and simple and faciliate note-taking. There weren't any surprises on the exams if you just reviewed the lecture notes. He does have an accent, but it's not a big deal.

Good class -- take him in summer. 111 and 175 overlap. While he has an accent, he is a good teacher and lays out everything you need to know during lecture. To the guy complaining about him being hard, I am amazed you made it into UCSD. It's time for you to switch to a comm major. & about it being boring... PLEASE name an econ class thats thrilling

bad teacher; looks like freedy deeb. has an accent. says he doesnt want to repeat stuff again even though he said different things the first time. very disorganized. voice is very monotone.  class and teacher are both boring. very difficult to stay awake in class. stay away if possible.
Horrible Teacher!
his  exams are pull out 'directly' from his lecture notes! No trick questions at all!

I like him. He's REALLY straightforward and uncomplicated. The class material can be pretty boring, but Seifi does a good job explaining it. He's definitely a no-nonsense kind of guy, and his tests are straight from the lecture material. A good professor.
No Comments
His lectures are slow. He is a good guy, exams aren't hard and if you do everythign he says you'll do just fine.

Professor Seifi works very slowly, and his notes are straight from the book.  For this reason, class is pretty useless.  However, his tests involve application, all  20? multiple choice, so missing only a few can really hurt.  Do Practice Problems!
Goated professor, exams exactly like practice and HW, very clear expectations, so kind with grading, funny, lowkey beautiful looking

I thought he was a great professor that truly cares about his students. Offers so much help on midterms and final with practice exams almost identical, attendance either in person or zoom, helpful in OH. Material relevant for the future to familiarize you with it as a beginner. One of the best professors in this department. MidAvg:B and FinalAvg:A

You learn pretty much nothing in this class. General physics is more necessary and this course is mainly plug and chug. It is somewhat difficult because the questions for the homework have nothing to do with the lectures and you NEED to fully understand them. This is ironic since they are not taught in class. Also he denies his RMP rating... Cap

Chill with grades (+ lot of EC). Everyone has an A, yet you don't learn much. As long as you know how to use the formulas you're good. Guest speakers are interesting people, idk why people complain about them; its just an intro class. The bad: he doesn't care about the class much, is often late, skims through slides, and doesn't put effort.

Very unmotivated professor that puts his students second since he's always busy. Often gets to class late and speeds through the slides expecting you to know what he's talking about. Despite the extra credit for things like Halloween dress ups, HW are often hard to understand and does not give extensions. Lectures are Hybrid though so its flexible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ackerman is great! I sincerely enjoyed his lectures and he's also truly passionate about the course content. All the readings in this class are worth a read.
Great prof, but a lot of reading that overlaps with other classes (like MMW, Philosophy, and the sort).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ackerman is a very intelligent man. The topics he touches on are intriguing and always leave me wanting to know more. The grading criteria is straightforward; if you do the readings, complete the weekly homework assignments and attend class then you will pass. However, the hw does require a lot of careful contemplation. You will learn a LOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Ackerman barely lectured during this class (maybe 3 times the whole quarter), but when he did it was very heavy material. The class itself is pretty easy. Readings are optional and the homeworks (due once a week) are pretty straight forward. The content of HDS 1 is also very interesting, so guest lectures are engaging.

Professor Ackerman is at times funny and has a sense of humor. The class is mainly comprised of guests' lectures. He lectures, but it is rare. There are 7 homework assignments consist of questions mainly from the lectures. One midterm and an accumulative final. Go to the TAs' office hours  because they are mostly the ones that make the exam.

Most of the class is taught by guest lecturers, and I thought this made the class very interesting. Every lecture was something new. Exams were pretty reflective of the weekly HWs/discussions. Mandatory sections, HW graded for completion, 1 midterm, 1 final (both multiple choice). You are not tested on the readings.

Class is mainly taught by guest lecturers. The class was enjoyable; some guests were better than others. The times he did teach, he was a little humorous. The exams were fair; pay attention to the midterm material when studying for the final. Discussion sections are mandatory. Homework is based on completion. Readings are not necessary to pass.

HW is based on completion. one midterm which is all multiple choice. final is also all mc and the first half of it is literally questions pulled from the midterm. attendance isnt mandatory except for discussion. majority of course is taught by guest speakers. ackerman can get a bit boring and monotonous so sitting in the way front helped me focus.

He does not even teach the class. He has guest speakers mostly every class. His test are pretty straight forward. There is no textbook required. He has homework questions for you every week that you do need to spend some time on.

I had him for LIGN176 and LIGN120. He's a bit boring, I find it hard to follow his lectures but the material itself is very interesting. The assignments are super easy and in both classes homework was worth 70%. The midterms/finals are relatively easy too. In other words, if you want an A....take him! :)

Amazing class.. really opens your eyes to the world around you.. well, the worlds around you. He is not afraid to say what most people would refrain from saying; his goal is to engage our "system 2" across several contexts.. haha. I love this class, I wish it wasn't ending already. Take him. He cares about students' learning. Oh yeah, no exams...

Amazing prof. He talks in a bland manner but has a surprising sense of humor. He keeps things pretty interesting and use great examples to help cement understanding. Slides are up every week and there are weekly writing assignments to make sure we keep up with the readings and lectures. Very fair. Also, he looks a little like George Bluth Sr.

Great class. No textbook, readings all online, and you never have to read them. Lectures are all online too. Did well in the class and missed a majority of the lectures. Almost all guest lectures. Weekly homework assignments can be finished in an hour or less. Ackerman himself is not a good lecturer but I imagine would be fun to talk to 1 on 1.
Great professor, informative, friendly, helpful, and keeps material interesting. Favorite prof at UCSD so far.

Professor Ackerman's Ling 176 class was my favorite this quater. He gives you the tools to analyze and come to your own conclusions. I recommend his class to anyone. He is a warm, humble prof  that genuinely wants his students to walk away from his class with understanding of how our society works.  I will miss going to his lectures for sure.

Boring. Has guest lecturers almost every class so teaching style is very inconsistent. Homework (short paragraphs/question) were mostly on the slides which were all vague. Hard to stay awake. His specialty is on linguistics and it's apparent in his lectures, but I took the class to learn more about human development, not for lectures on verbs.
Great class. Great Professor. Not very difficult. Weekly mini-papers on the readings and a more substantive paper as the final. Fall Quarter well-spent.
Very interesting class. Makes you really think about how we are all manipulated by advertising.

I'm a ling major, however this was my favorite class all quarter. Not insanely hard but does require active engagement of the mind which is why I recommend attending lecture. Essential course for anyone seeking to understand human interaction and manipulation. Weekly course readings posted online were on target. Wonderful learning experience!
Prof Ackerman was great-- encouraged us to think about our world and how big of a role language plays in crafting messages. Interesting class, it has definitely made me more skeptical, not cynical.
I took Professor Ackerman's Morphology class. I had a hard time following lectures, but he seems like a nice person :)

need to go to class to understnad all the material..since it all guest lectures..just study all the slides very closely..and then go clarify the classes material with ta, since it will hlp you..got a B plus..and still tried quite a good effort..midterm hard..but final was esyy.
The class is pretty easy, all guest lectures. No text book and the required and suggested readings weren't tested
Ackerman is really interesting. He has a commanding voice. The subject is ok.. I wish he talked more about the role of linguistics in advertising, rather than the background
he is a very good professor...very interesting and encourages students to be skeptical, not cyinical....i truly enjoyed his class and learned a lot...
Intensely interesting lectures. Fun and provacative at the same time. Friendly and open to discussion on almost any topic. Definetly a professor to know around campus.

Lectures are done by different people so you must go to them. There is no textbook for this class but online readings which are long and sometimes unnecessary. Sections are mandatory with homework due every week. Midterm and final are MC questions only. This class focused on the acquisition of different human abilities.

itd be easier if there was a textbook to read from, but all u have are articles online, which i never read. gotta go to class b/c diff lecturers each time and take good notes for the midterms and tests. im pretty sure i passed the class with the minimal work i did. take it for pass/no pass if for GE, just in case. not about biological growth of ppl

The readings (HUGE reader) were really interesting but his lectures were not.  I didn't pay a whit of attention to his lectures and still did really well. He's a nice person and all (first professor to ever price check the readers for us) but not that great a lecturer.
The best New York liberal Jew you could hope for. Easy class, interesting, easy assignments.
Cool professor but BS class.
This class was so boring!
No Comments
He's the reason I became a ling major!
ackerman is cool and this class was especially fun and interesting. and i beg to differ with a previous post: neal peters is cool and nice and quite helpful. i like when neal is my TA.
No Comments
lectures are so hard to pay attention to, but he posts slides online.  both classes were boring as all hell
No Comments

Ackerman was a cool dude, I enjoyed his lecture style and passion for the subject.  Just looking at him is enough to make you laugh.  But if Neal Peters is the TA... watch out.  Lick my hairy nutsack Neal

He definitely goes through his slides too fast in 171, but I liked him enough to take 176 which was much better! There is a lot of reading (2 thick readers!), but reading is not necessary if you attend lecture or if an assignment is based on it. He's funny and he knows his stuff!

I don't know what these other people are talking about. He goes over his powerpt lectures too fast, but it doesn't matter bc they are useless anyways. His class is okay. it's not hard but it's not easy either. take this prof and his class ONLY if necessary

This class was an absolute blast. Even though it was a hard fight for an A, I enjoyed every second of it. Some of the readings were dreadfully boring, but Prof. Ackerman more than compensated for it! He wanted his students to take home a message rather than just memorize facts. Cool and funny guy!

VERY interesting and relevent class. I would recomend this class and professor Ackerman to students in any major. He is very passionate and makes a subject which is allready very intruiging to be totaly fascinating.

Took him for CENG 15 during summer session II. Homework can be tough, but he gives out amazing notes and guides us through problem sets. Final exam was a bit tough, but it was similar to the homework.
No homework, just in-class labs. He is a very good teacher and helps with advice about chemical engineering career choices.

Absolutely terrible. Took this class as a GE and it was the most difficult class I have ever taken. Was definitely not an intro class. Humbling experience to say the least. Do not recommend if you aren't familiar with coding.

Professor's handwriting on the board is amazing, especially with that fancy chalk! Lectures were very clear and helpful for doing the homework. The lectures are based off of his textbook so I would recommend reading through the discussed chapter either before or after lectures. The examples in the book are very helpful in doing the hw.
CENG4 is a very fun class as a new engineering major, professor is super nice on top of that. Great first quarter experience

This class isn't an easy A, but Prof. Drews. is very helpful and forthcoming with additional support. Grading was fair and Prof. Drews was very helpful working around the hohle COVID situation and very accommodating
Thank you Dr. Drews for being an awesome professor. Homeworks are really thoughtfully made, and he is always so encouraging to his students. Definitely one of the best prof in UCSD

Drews is just an outstanding professor in all aspects. His homeworks,projects, and quizzes really make you think as he expects a lot but if you work diligently and ask for help when you need it, he is super flexible. Take him any chance you get.

Very little guidance for lab assignments was provided, but reports were graded as if there had been. Often did not provide adequate answers to questions posed in lab. Be prepared to do almost everything on your own and be marked down for any mistakes you make. I understand the need for self-direction, but am glad that I am done with this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Lectures were very useful throughout the course. A little more guidance might have been offered with homework, but it was doable. Exams were fairly straightforward but felt somewhat time-constrained. Big group project due at the end of the quarter was a challenge--start early. Overall a solid choice in the ChemE department.

he has this obsession for minimalism, which is great, except   it makes his class page actually fairly confusing and links are covertly embedded here and there, and he is unwilling to bend rules, even though his rules are error and uncertainty-prone. it's obvious that grading is inconsistent between teams on the same report

Dr. Drews is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is probably my favorite. He is really brilliant and hilarious. His lectures are really clear as he writes on his ipad and record everything then posts it on his youtube page. Fluids is a tough course but he makes himself available outside of class to help students. Tests are very fair.
Great professor. Very helpful and makes time for all of his students. Extremely professional and fair.

Amazing, respectable, kind, funny, helpful, and caring professor. Puts a ton of effort into his classes. Appreciates feedback and actually changes his class based on it. Applies real world concepts to lab experiments, making them more interestingengaging. Can I please redo college and have him as my professor for all of my classes?!

Test heavy with 70% grade occupied. 2 midterms and 1 final with few curves. Lectures attendance with iClicker questions. Discussion not that helpful but mandatory. Treat your assignments well to save your final score.

Terrible command of the material, mind numbingly boring lectures, and shockingly disorganized. Her grading criteria for homework and exams was virtually impossible to figure out, and the actual number of points deducted for a single wrong answer was absurd to the point that you could lose 10% for missing one question on a 40 question assignment.

Dr. Aarons definitely cares about her students and is really sweet. She is okay at explaining things but her exams were fairly difficult. Definitely need to read the textbook and understand concepts pretty well in order to do well in her class.

The Homework assignments were short but very insightful, with optional extra problems. The exams reflected the Homework, Discussions, and Practice Exams very well. The optional Homework problems did not appear on the exams which was nice. Overall Professor Pollack was the best math professor I had at UCSD. Only needed around 85% for an A.

Smart guy but does not listen to the students. Get ready to spend 5 hrs+ per week on his weekly hw and one drop. 2 midterms and does not allow dropping. If you are sick and did poorly in one, you are done. He was teaching new material at the last lecture and expect us to prepare it on the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Does not explain anything during the lecture, he just writes stuff down and repeats it and expects you to understand.
Aaron is a solid professor
Overall, a great lecturer. Super nice and willing to help. Homeworks were super manageable, and he gives plenty of hints for tougher problems.
Homeworks were short and inspirational comparing to other professors. Exams usually contains some questions from the practice final and discussion sections.

His handwriting is definitely a problem but his lecture is not that bad. With that being said, if I have to review some concepts, I have to watch the videos again or read the textbook. I cannot just read the notes. However, homework is easy and inspirational. Overall an easy class. He could be a better instructor if he had better handwriting.

Worst professor I ever had. Couldn't read his handwriting, tests and quizzes are nothing of what we've learned and lectures are incredibly confusing. Despite reading 3 Abstract algebra textbooks, I still can't understand his lectures. Please stay away from this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Although the materials Prof. Aamari gave are really hard, his notes are helpful and his practice exams are also indicative. Overall, I like this professor, and I have learned a lot! By the way, the homework are tough.

He's a great professor! I really loved this class. He does give a lot of homework, but I found it manageable. He obviously cares about how his students do in his class. I would definitely take him again.

LECTURES ARE SUPER DENSE. but i really appreciated it being organized and easy to follow on PPT. He was very enjoyable and always had savage jokes and replies on piazza. Class is work intensive with labs and hw due every week but doable and prepares you well for exams. read the book for better explanations when u get confused. that really helped
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: i've never taken AP Stats, or any stats class at all so this was harder for me to learn. He talks super fast during the slides which makes it kinda hard to take notes in lecture, but he does post every powerpoint beforehand. He's not terrible but I wouldn't say he's 10/10 either.

Oh my goodness, I love this class. I'm not even done yet but I absolutely love him. If he taught all the math classes I'd need for a math minor, I'd do a math minor. He's super nice, I love his lectures, and he's really cute. Plus he has a nice accent. Very easy to pay attention in that class. I honestly wish we had more classes per week!!!

Prof. Aamari's lecture and slides are very clear and easy to follow. He also let students practice during lecture. Homework and exams are very fair, nothing tricky. His practice exams are not easy though.

Kind of nit-picky about grading, but as you go through the class grading criteria gets clearer. Exams are like the practice problems and the lab textbook is useful for the exams as well. As long as you put effort into the lab notebook and do as required its easy points. Definitely go see TA for the reports to get help if you need it. Overall easy!

Dr Coleman was good but his midterm/final was hard. Some quizzes weren't bad but some had very confusing wording. There were only two lab reports for this class and the experiments weren't too bad at all however the grading on the lab reports was a little harsh considering it's supposed to be a class where you are learning to write lab reports

Really depends on the TA. Lectures are recorded + online and are helpful to understanding why you do the lab stuff. Exams are on the harder side but not super unfair. Coleman is helpful and will look over your entire lab report before submission to give you tips.

The class was flipped so lectures were videos and designated lecture times were learning sessions where he went over the lecture content and did practice problems. I really liked this format, made it so that you were constantly reviewing the content and nothing was too new. Exams were fair, but metabolic is always hard and memorization based.

The class is very lecture-heavy, with a strong emphasis on memorizing chemical structures and pathways. Although challenging, the professor's clear explanations and use of unstuck ai for study prep helped me succeed. Overall, a rewarding experience if you're willing to put in the work.

Very nice man, but class is so dense and expects to know every detail about everything exams 375 points no curve for anything at all even with C averages. Smart and nice man but lectures are mediocre.

Surprisingly, I really enjoyed this class. teaching wise you watch podcasts on your own, and answer clicker questions during lecture time regarding the material. The exams I found them to be fairly easy and represent lecture material but memorization intensive and NOT impossible. He lets you know ahead of time whats required to know. PBS =study aid

took him for BIBC 102 and BIBC 103. 103 is definitely easier as that he podcasts and made the lab notebook digital. Towards the end of the class labs are easy since there are no big assignments based on them. First exam for 103 was reasonable unlike BIBC 102 being hard. 103 lectures are better structured than 102 for some reason too.

Doesn't curve and has no recorded podcasts. Everything is drawn out manically and there's no clear explanation of anything regarding the pathways. Even his TAs were confused during discussions because his lectures were so inconsistent. Pure, brute memorization of all chemical molecule structures, arrows, and names for every enzyme talked about.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture attendance was mandatory, so if you had an emergency, too bad! Lectures were random and not structured, so they were sometimes hard to follow, and HUGE emphasis on memorization of structures. I didn't do the readings, so I can't say if they were helpful or not, but make sure to know and be able to draw every single process by heart!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are based on lectures no lecture slides. AWFUL LECTURER. If he spent the time her runs back and forth drawing things on the board as he did putting information concisely and cohesively he would be great. Does not ask clear questions. Squirrel brained to say the least. Take someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved the way professor Coleman taught this class. He would take baby steps with the concepts learned in class, which was really helpful considering that most lab classes do not teach you why you do certain steps. Aside from his clear method of teaching, Coleman holds regular office hours where he explains practice problems. He really cares!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy, but this class is ridiculous for the amount of time it takes. There are two long research assignments, tests, and quizzes. On top of this, there is a lab notebook homework that one has to keep up with. The average grade for the first test was a D, so beware, this guy is extremely difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Took him for both BIBC 102/103 and his classes do require a lot of dedication to understanding the material. Highly recommend taking his class if you're willing to put in the effort! He's super nice and willing to help you through questions if you go to OH. His grading is super strict though with little room for partial credit ):
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tough grader

reviews.comment: For a professor that is involved in education research, he was pretty unaccommodating in terms of student learning style and teaching in the online format. He never posted the lecture slides or solutions to problem sets. In addition, he made no meaningful connection to the material to help remember and the class felt like a memorization/info dump.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor was really clear during lecture. I always get a high 90% just by doing the problem sets and listening to lecture. His lab reports may seem tricky, so its important to ask feedback from the TA and him. Hes pretty approachable and friendly! The class itself could be improved, sometimes my lab group feels lost by the instructions.

Doctor Coleman cares a lot about his students though many may miss this if they don't engage with him personally. Grading felt like shedding full letter grades for minor mistakes which crippled morale but in the end my grade was probably about right.

Professor Coleman is super caring! His lectures arent podcasted so you definitely have to attend and theyre a bit boring. The grade was mostly based off on one midterm and the final. Only about half of the discussions were mandatory. Do good on the first exam/final and youll get an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The only students who like him are the ones that think suffering through a class for an A is what makes it worth it. I dont recommend him for anyone who isnt trying to prove anything. Hes a very typical UCSD prof, doesnt care about the individuals. Do yourself a favor and take a more generous professor.

His tests are graded really harshly and to be honest as a person, I feel like he cares more about making his class difficult so only a few do well instead of actually caring that everyone learns. Hes just one of those professors that thinks the harder he makes his class, the more fair it is.

A great professor, even if it was a challenging class. You have to put the hours in to memorize and understand the different pathways and structures. His class format is very lecture heavy, where note taking is a must since he writes everything on the board. I liked that, because it forced me to take notes. All his exams are reflective of lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I personally found this class to be very interesting however the level of detail he says he expects us to know for the exams is a bit more simplistic than whats on the actual exam. The only thing I can say is that you need to work very hard to get good grades the first two midterms because the final exam is a pain, so dont wait . No podcast :(

The material is actually really cool, but having to memorize the details of metabolic charts was insanely boring and ultimately not useful. He's upfront about his strategy, but the class has no lasting impact as you forget most everything a couple weeks after the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class was personally very difficult for me to follow since he only wrote on the board and didn't post slides or anything. The beginning of the class started very basic and slow, and then a just few days before the midterm he would introduce very complex topics to remember. Overall a nice guy but the class style just didn't work for me that well

Coleman is one of the best biochem professors I have had. He is so knowledgable about the topic and can clearly explain everything. Biochem is a hard class, so be prepared to study a lot, but totally managable if you keep on top of studying. 2 midterms and a final. Hard but so worth, and he makes the class so interesting!

Dr. Coleman is one of the best professors I've had in my college experience (the other 2 being professors from my cc). He is really passionate about what he teaches and that makes the biggest difference. Lectures were never dull and it was easy to follow along since he writes everything you need to know on the board. I strongly recommend this prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Coleman gives great lectures. He's very clear about what will be on the tests and the practice problems are really representative. Tests are not hard. You do need to go to lecture as he writes everything on the chalkboard and doesn't podcast. He's a nice guy who you can tell is excited about the material, he's very bouncy.

Dr. Coleman is one of the best professors at UCSD. Caring, prepared, detailed... he is a great lecturer with an eye for how students learn, he is a great grader and provides clear expectations for his lab reports. His midterm and final can be challenging, but only if you haven't taken notes during lecture and have relied on your partner during lab.

Professor Coleman is an outstanding lecturer.  He makes it very easy to take notes and is very clear in his explanations of the course material.  He doesn't podcast, so you have to attend class to get the notes.  His exams are very representative of the course material and the problem sets he gives out.  Easy A if you put in the work.

Loved this class! Dr. Coleman frequently checks to make sure students don't have any unanswered questions, and obviously cares about his students learning the material and doing well in the course. DO THE PROBLEM SETS! A lot of test questions mirror the ones from problem sets.
this man deserves a hot pepper! makes it easy to understand and take notes. study all your notes hard and you will do well.

Was not a great lecture as everyone hyped him up to be. The midterm was unbelievably difficult that did not coordinate with his lectures at all. I've been to every lecture and even made use of his office hours. I'd personally stay away from him at all costs

Prof C is wonderful! His lectures are super clear, and the class material is straightforward. It is really easy to understand the concepts with his organized lectures, and it is easy to tell he loves to teach. He only has chalk lectures though, so attend class! Grading is ultimately up to the TAs - you have 3 reports, 4 quizzes, and 2 exams.

Coleman is a really chill guy and is in no way out to get his students or fail them. His midterm was very fair as was the final. Seriously, go to lecture each time, take notes and you will do well on the exams and quizzes. All his tests were very reasonable with some problems showing up directly from the problem sets. Really sweet, clear and chill

Really awesome professor. His lectures were very clear and the problem sets he made were very helpful bc they were very similiar to the tests. The class is hard in general bc their is a lot to memorize, but you can easily get a B or A if you study a lot.

Very nice professor but class is poorly structured. Vague lab report instructions with very specificpicky grading. Exams are easy and representative of class lecture, but his wordings are weird sometimes and lead you in the wrong direction. Overall, the professor is very friendly but the class is not worth the time or the money.

Dr. Coleman is a really great lecturer, and a nice guy in general. It's obvious that he really cares about students learning and isn't the type of professor who throws a ton of curveball questions. Pretty much everything on the exams is straight from lecture. My only complaint is that I wish he had more office hours.

I took Dr Coleman's biochem lab last quarter. As with previous reviews, he was an awesome lecturer and patient teacher. Very accessible in lab; he even personally helped us troubleshoot an experiment when it failed to run correctly! Fair exams that stress conceptual understanding (no useless memorizing). One of the best profs in the bio department.

Dr. Coleman is one of the best professors at UCSD. Very clear in lecture, makes biochemistry easy to understand. No podcasts or notes online so you have to go to lecture but exams are very straight forward. If you go to lecture, pay attention and take good notes you'll have no problem getting a good grade.

Lab is interesting, and you can certainly learn a lot. However, his exams are difficult. Mixture of poorly worded questions and super specific grading. Be prepared to word vomit every little thing you know, because you're not going to get the points otherwise. Everything you write down on the exam will be taken super literal with no room for error.

This is an amazing professor no doubt. You have to attend his lectures. Take good notes, but notes aren't good enough. You must also read the text to get a better understanding in order to get a good grade.

Best professor for metabolic. Super clear and goes over everything on the board. No textbook needed. All test material is based off the lectures. He is really nice and he is also really good to look at. Need to work to get an A, but not impossible. Would recommend!

Love Coleman! He's simply The Best. Lab was a bit boring though and hated writing the time consuming worthless reports and getting points taken off for stupid formatting as if that made a difference in learning anything. Labs are extremely LONG and annoying, but prof is AWESOME. He's really cool and intelligent, def recommend!

This course was not as easy as people made it out to be. The midterm was fairly straight forward but really long for class time given. The final on the other hand was really difficult and long even though it was said it would be shorter. Class was barely curved so my grade drastically fell! Def more Bs and Cs then A. Nice guy, but needs to be clear

I was dreading this class but Coleman made it enjoyable. His clear explanations made it actually interesting for me. He's helpful, there's a lot of material and no curve but definitely possible to get an A. I was 6 points away from an A made me regret not doing the extra credit presentation. He's awesome though!

Awesome professor! Very approachable and nice :) He's very clear in lecture about what you need to know. Exams were relatively easy if you go to all the classes. Never used the textbook. My favorite class ever!
Great professor! He's super friendly and a really good lecturer. I thought this class was going to be really hard and unpleasant but it wasn't that bad at all. I would definitely recommend him.

I love Dr. Coleman! He's AMAZING! I learned so much and was able to get an A (even w/ no curve). If you really work for it and pay attention, it's totally possible. He gives E.Credit opportunities and actually cares about teaching. Very humble, kind guy. He treats his students w/ respect, very approachable. The best class I've ever taken. A must!

Good professor. Lectures very useful. He tells you what you need to focus on for the exam. No practice exams, but homework problems are a good way to study. There is homework that is due, but very easy to finish on time. Fairly easy class, but will require study time.
kinda hard to understand his lectures, but fun to look at.

Great professor who cares about students' learning. Don't expect to simply memorize glycolysis, crebs and the ETC to get an A in the class. Know the big picture concepts (ask: why is this pathway important?) attend lecture, do the hw and you'll find biochem isn't that bad.

goes through everything thoroughly, and only tests on lecture material, so you dont need the book but you MUST go to lecture. 4 hw assignments, 1 midterm, 1 final. you really basically need to memorize everything from lecture. unfortunately, no curve, which makes getting an A nearly impossible. B is doable. still recommended

Biochem Lab was very enjoyable although that mostly depends on your TA. Professor's lectures are clear and if you pay attention to all the details of lecture, the lab manual and understand every procedure behind experiments, the midterms will be super easy. There isn't a ridiculous amount of material to cover and tests are not cumulative.

Seems like a decent class all the way up to the final. That's when you find out that you were supposed to intertwine all that straightforward stuff he was teaching somehow on your own. Thought I had a guaranteed A. Ended up with a C+. Any friend that recs this guy is not a friend.

He really cares about his students..is a very straightforward with lectures. lectures can be boring at times. his exams can be tricky at times, especially the final in which he makes half thinking-based and other half basic stuff. doesnt curve the class, may lower points depending on the cutoff situation. Overall, a GREAT professor! take him!

A good professor overall. Coleman is approachable in his OHs and going to them will help you a lot. He doesn't curve so  you need to keep up with everything. However, even if you do well in this class, don't expect that he will write you a LOR. He will say that he's busy. My older friends who asked him LORs got his "too busy".

He gives a decent curve.  Lectures are pretty straight forward.  A lot of stuff in class to remember but not bad compared to the other UD bio classes I've taken.  Do your problem sets!  They're free points.

No curve at all for either metabolic or biochem techniques... not sure what other ppl are talking about. His tests are fair, however and only tests on what was said in class. He is very likable and nice. For the lab: 2 lab reports and 2 MTs along with a couple quizzes and notebook checks. He is a really clear lecturer--definitely reccommended

Took him for BIBC 103 and now BIBC 102.  He's super clear and easier than other professors.  Plus, his tests are very straightforward and clear, and the curve is decent.  I would recommend him because you learn a LOT in his class.  One of my favourite biology professors.

Prof Coleman is so nice and always in a good mood! The curve seems alright but it's hard to tell since I don't know my grade on the final. Lectures are a must. Tests are doable because he realizes (unlike most profs) that testing on a bunch of memorization is useless and it's better that students learn concepts that they'll remember after the class

Professor Coleman is a solid lecturer who is very approachable in office hours. The good: easier midterms, clear lectures, homework points to boost your grade. The bad: no curve(he doesn't have tenure), he doesn't cover as much material as other professors, and you must attend lecture as the book is not very helpful. Overall, recommend.

Dr. Coleman is awesome! He's a super clear and organized lecturer. Also, he's always in lab helping you out. His exams aren't difficult but they are pretty thorough. Study and you'll do really well, no tricks. Most of the labs are pretty interesting. I really enjoyed this class and this professor.

Coleman is great!! This class was pretty interesting and laidback. You must go to lectures. The exams are lecture based. The exams are not bad at all, just study everything in lecture! All the graphs, charts, information he tells you about the experiments. Also every point counts in this class so do well on the quizzes and notebook checks.

Easily the best lecturer I've had in 4 years at UCSD. He could explain this stuff to a monkey. Tests are fair, easiest lab I've taken, experiments can be fun (a couple are a bit dull). you MUST take Coleman

One of the best professors at UCSD.  His lectures facilitates note-taking (a lot too) and really clears up what you're going to do in the lab.  He doesn't curve because the averages on the exams are usually C+/B-, but they're not so bad.  Just study a lot and memorize everything in lecture and in the lab manual.

Class is straightforward, he'll tell you what's on the test, kinda [just study the homeworks]. Grade cutoffs aren't great because he doesn't have tenure, but study what he tells you! He always responds to webCT, so that's pretty helpful. He is hot.

Mid-terms and Final are very easy if you study what he tells you to study.  The lectures are very reflective of the tests.  However, do not plan on getting an A in the class if you mess up on one test.  While the tests are easy, the grade cutoffs are ridiculous.  Have fun.
He's not terrible, but boy, when he puts up overheads get ready for some snooze time. The tests are reasonable and you'll be fine as long as you study the lectures. Don't bother with the book.

Took Dr. Coleman for both BIBC 102 and BIBC 103. He is perhaps the best professor I have taken at UCSD. Very clear and straight forward. The tests are easy if you study your lecture notes (don't bother with the textbook). Dr. Coleman is very helpful and extremely kind.
AWESOME PROFESSOR!!!! he is very nice and the test is extremly easy and straight forward  strongly recommended =)

Took him for metabolics and biochem techniques. Like everyone else has said, he's very fair. He's a very pleasant person to talk to. If he hasn't covered it in lecture, he won't test you on it. If he taught another class, I'd take it in a heartbeat.
Coleman was AWESOME!!! If you need to take this lab take it with coleman because he truly was amazing!!!!!
Made the subject clear, tests were very fair.

His Metabolic Biochem class was so easy! I took his class after failing Yaffe, and Coleman only covered like 40% of the material Yaffe did.  I feel sorry for he people who only took Coleman b/c they didn't learn a lot of material, but the exams were like high school level.
Good instructor, thorough exams.

He's a pretty good choice for this lab.  He claims he doesn't curve but he does at the end.  The midterms were not too hard, but the lectures were pretty boring.  The lab reports suck(3of them), but the class itself is pretty easy, not like chem labs at all.
Exams are very representative of lecture+ reader material.

Good professor, but doesn't know how to curve grades. Only 13% As????? When the norm for curving is 25% As, you know something has to be wrong. Take another professor who already has experience curving classes, i.e. Scheffler/Yaffe/Price.

The class is hard because the textbook doesn't do a good job of explaining the material so you have to spend lots of time trying to digest it but Coleman is a nice man and a decent lecturer. Try to study what he tells you and don't wait until the last minute then you'll be fine.

The class is hard because the textbook doesn't do a good job of explaining the material so you have to spend lots of time trying to digest it but Coleman is a nice man and a decent lecturer. Try to study what he tells you and don't wait until the last minute then you'll be fine.

Very nice man, always has a smile on his face. I disagree with previous comments: he told us exactly what to study for, and was an admirable lecturer. Grade scale is horrible, though, because it's not curved.

I took him for BIBC 120 and he it is a very managable class. just make sure that u understand everything that he says in class and for the things u don't understand go to office hrs, TAs, and refer to book.I like this class because it was a good introductory course that isn't too overwhelming.I ended up learning a lot.

Excellent lecturer on metabolic biochem.  He is fairly easier than other professors and his tests aren't that bad.  His homework is fairly easy.  His exams are more conceptual than I would like, but they're not difficult.  I highly recommend Coleman for this class.

Lectures were dull. He didn't seem to thoroughly know the material (i.e., he always had his clip board for reference), but he wanted us to know it all. Exams were tough & graded harsh. When someone asked a Q that wasn't directly related to the material, he wouldn't even try to answer; he'd just say he's not sure and we're not learning that anyway.

This class is very difficult. I believe it is more difficult than organic chemistry but this class is not even curved! Coleman moves very fast and is very vague in his lectures. He does not make it clear what you are supposed to study which makes studying a nightmare. The tests are graded very unfairly, no partial credit is given when it should be.

This class is very difficult. I believe it is more difficult than organic chemistry but this class is not even curved! Coleman moves very fast and is very vague in his lectures. He does not make it clear what you are supposed to study which makes studying a nightmare. The tests are graded very unfairly, no partial credit is given when it should be.

Helpful during office hours. But if I had a dispute with a test question or lab report he refused to help me (and this happened often with his many vague questions). Eventually had to dispute these problems with the dean.

Don't listen to the people below.  He was a perfectly competent teacher and grading is extremely fair if you just know everything on your notes and how to apply it in simple situations.  He was more than willing to help anyone with anything, the homework was easy, and the tests were extremely straightforward and short.  I would take him again.
coleman is an ok prof, but doesnt really know a lot, always seemed to struggle to answer questions in lectures. class is easy but hard to get an A with his grading scale.
Lets just say I was really interested and loved metabolic biochemistry until I met his face.  His tests are easy, but are graded very unfairly.  The grading system does not do you justice.
He is just and inconsiderate professor,who is definitely not willing to help his students and don't care at all.
he is a good professor and extremely helpful and clear.

This professor is one of the most boring professors I've ever had at UCSD. I could not even keep my eyes open during lecture.  But, he is very helpful at his office hours, adn he seems very nice, if that helps at all. Good Luck!
He is really nice and approachable if you have questions and overall a great professor.  The only thing is that his voice is a little quiet so that makes it hard to hear him sometimes.
He is the best professor i've had at ucsd.  He really cares about the students and explains everything clearly.  He will go over difficult subjects as many times as necessary.
Seems like an easy course but those lab reports really catch you off-guard in the beginning... Prof. Coleman's nice, has somewhat difficult exams but they're ok. I recommend this class overall.

Professor Coleman is a wonderful professor! I highly recommend him. Very kind and willing to help you learn basics of lab techniques. Doing well in the class is determined by how well you understand the concepts of experiments, not just brute memorization. Understand thoroughly what he is talking about!

Amazing professor. He IS intimidating looking, but do not let that deter you from ever going to office hours. I went every time available to get help for the course and it helps. He is friendly, but his monotone voice and demeanor can scare you off. But after getting used to his OH, he IS one of the best profs. I have ever had. GENEROUS curve!

he taught me 100a and 20c 3 years ago. I believe he can really teach abstract material very well (algebra analysis number theory etcetc) but taking calc with him was tough. The passing grade for 20c was a 33% when I had him. A very good professor but maybe not for those who takes math courses because they have to.

Had him in 140A and B. Would go off on 20 min tangents that really added nothing to the material. He was WAY TOO SLOW with how he went through Rudin and we skipped some of the most important proofs in that book. The tests were well written and he was helpful with individual Q's but the lectures lagged behind the homework.

Although in most cases I just couldn't follow anything he did in lectures, he's a very good professor who extremely cares about his students and will answer any questions you ask. Homework assignments and exams were very difficult (or not straightforward), but he had "overly generous" curve at the end.

I thought Dr. Evans was a fantastic professor. The class was very conceptual but I found that more useful than plugging in random numbers into random equations. The tests were completely fair and I thought they were relatively easy. He goes a little bit slow in lecture, but then you won't get left behind and he's totally hilarious too.

This rating is for all you who hate math or are not that great at math-don't take evans!! He has a monotone voice in lecture that just makes you soo bored, and then the worst part is his midterms and exams are a lot harder then he lets on. If I had taken Kong instead of Evans I would have gotten an A instead a C

VERY CONCEPTUAL! Compared to other 10 series profs, he is really tough! He somewhat expects us to know the material already but he gives an awesome curve at the end, I thought I was going to fail! (LOTS of students dropped his class though after first midterm and second FYI)

great professor. really tries to make sure everyone understands. answers all questions. quizzes are easy and are sometimes problems straight from the homework. midterms and finals very similar to the practice exams he puts online. would definitely recommend him
Professor Evans is very intelligent and will answer any question you ask, he goes at a rapid pace though and his tests are challenging. Overall a good professor.

Nice guy, very approachable, however I WOULD NOT recommend him for the 10 series. His tests were all what my friends in the 20 series said that they were studying. Not straightforward. If you do have to take him, make sure to go to class. You cannot do stuff just from the book.
awesome. gives out practice midterms and practice finals which are representative of the actual exams. do the practice tests, and you'll be fine on the real thing.

He's a fun professor, but he likes to go about things his own way, apart from the book, which results in a lot of unnecessary confusion. He's a very conceptual teacher, meaning the homework is more along the lines of proofs rather than problems.
great prof!  very clear.  the midterm and finals are hard but manageable and curved fairly

The midterms are very very hard! It can make taking one of his classes a bit stressful. Test quetions are often worded in such a complicated way, that it is hard to understand what exactly he is asking you to do. The only justification for taking his class is the nice curves. I struggled the entire quarter, yet managed to walk out with a C.
Hilarious and a genius. Tests are not hard at all if you do the practice exams and pay attention to what he says during lecture. Very nice when you ask questions...take him, he is totally awesome.
Awesome math professor.  By far my favorite so far at UCSD.  Is very humble and clear about his teaching and his dry humor makes him very likeable.  Good guy
Amazing prof.  Hard midterms, but curve is very generous (he curves teh average to a B-).  Very helpful lectures, and he uses some dry humor to make it entertaining.  Definitely recommended.
Great professor. Goes slow so good to take for difficult classes. Funny too. Good sense of humor. One of my fave professors at UCSD.
hilaroius!!!!
great professor. very smart and explains very well. very nice curve. materials not hard if you took math 20f. midterms and final okay. make sure u study the materials he gives before the exams.

Doesn't assign lots of hw; optional, but it helps because the weekly quizzes are exactly like the hw, only numbers change. Go to OH early in the course if you don't understand much. He's pretty good at clarifying. Midterms are HARD = nice curve..but for the final this qtr, he actually told us what kind of question #1 and #2 were going to be!

Doesn't assign lots of hw; optional, but it helps because the weekly quizzes are exactly like the hw, only numbers change. Go to OH early in the course if you don't understand much. He's pretty good at clarifying. Midterms are HARD = nice curve..but for the final this qtr, he actually told us what kind of question #1 and #2 were going to be!

Good professor, good sense of dry humor. Sections mandatory because of weekly quizzes, based off of homework but the values are changed. The level of homework is decent. I took the first midterm and I thought I understood the concepts but the midterm was unbelievably had, partly because of class, partly because of his question choices.
He's hilarious.  Cares about the subject, and you can tell.  The midterms are actually really hard, but the curb reflects that so you'll do fine as long as you do the optional homework.

he is funny! he makes me think of Mr. Bean! but his tests are much harder than the homework. There are really little homework, which is kind of bad because you don't get as much practice. Sections are mandatory because there is a quiz every week. but the quizzes are simple and my TA even goes over what we need to know for the quiz every week.
super nice guy and can make the class laugh with his jokes. approachable and you can tell he wants to help you learn although the tests are sometimes harder than the hw

Fantastic teacher. The gold standard in teaching -- extremely helpful, funny, and challenging. Also he's arguably the most brilliant prof in the math dept, and can discuss the most esoteric topics off the cuff, invent, and prove ideas just over a lecture discussion.
excellent teacher..worth taking if you are interested in learning...arguably one of the best at ucsd

Really nice guy who cares about the students.Lectures were always entertaining even when the topic wasn't.Tests were super hard,but the curve was always really good.Homework is really important,weekly quizzes on it and its all u have to study for the test.I hated this class, but I liked the teacher and I actually learned something.

Not a bad or a good teacher. However unlike most of our math teachers you can make sense of his lectures and actually learn something while you are there. Sometimes his tests are a lot harder then the homework and practice midterms he gives so get ready for it.

prof. evans is a very nice guy, very approachable, too. his lectures tended to be a little scattered, though, and sometimes unclear. i wouldn't recommend him, but i wouldnt' say avoid him, either. he's basically in the middle.

Tests are ridiculously hard but his curve defninitely helps.  It's weird when you can get a 47% B+ on a test.  Everyone passes, but damn the homework means too much, and with a TA who doesn't believe in partial credit that can really hurt you grade.

take him. i usually dont talk to professors at all but his guy is so easy to approach. he makes you want to learn. he cares about you ALOT. i would take him again anytime. i hope he teaches other classes that i need in the future.

Had Evans for 5 upper div. classes.  Dry humor which makes lectures very entertaining.  If you are interested in learning, you will do well in his classes.  Otherwise you will learn nothing, and you will give him a poor rating on this site. My favorite professor in college by far.

Pretty nice guy and entertaining to watch him in lectures.  If you think Evans sucks, then you probably suck at math.  Very approachable and his tests may be hard, but he does it intentionally to give a good challenge and of course the generous curve makes up for it too.

Prof. doesn't prepare, he is just a brainiac & teaches by ear. Therefore, b/c of his superior intelligence, he is often unclear, hard to follow, and does NOT know how to express concepts in a way that students can understand. HW=hard. Exams=impossible! The only good thing is that there is a HUGE curve.  I got a 50%, 27%, and who knows, but passed.
The tests are hard, but almost everyone passes the class.  Just have to work hard and always go to section.
Difficult to follow, but entertaining and likes to give higher grades than earned in upper division classes.

very smart guy, he does whatever he wants, so GO TO LECTURE. if you do that you'll be fine. VERY GENEROUS curve.  the guy who gave him a low rating is probably an idiot.  the prof is very approachable even tho he's sort of strange

He was the worst prof. I ever had. We didn't have a book for the class, so we had to rely on his unclear mumbo jumbo lectures that had no relevance to anything. I learned nothing and the test was incredibly unfair.
Good prof. Definitely knows what he's doing. He's really humble too. He tries his best with the large classes he's given, and IMO is a great teacher if you want to learn. He really cares.
He sincerely cares about his students.  Very approachable, and very helpful.  Tests are extremely straight foward, no tricks.  He has this innocent quality that makes him very amicable.
Very nice guy, also super easy to get to. The class is a P/NP class that should be very easy if you do all the assignments, which complements the tutoring work very well.

Professor Soosairaj can clearly communicate so many ideas in a way that is easy to follow; I highly suggest taking notes along with him.

*Took this class in Spring 25, where he was not running a min grading scheme.

Incredible professor, great, engaging teaching style! Very caring. TAs handle grading though, and grade harshly. Grading system is threshold based which is difficult and doesn't really reflect the grade you deserve, but I learned quite a bit from this class!
The professor was nice. The TAs, on the other hand, will grade your homework, and they are really tough on grading.
Just don't take this class with him

Class average GPA was 1.94. In short, his grading system is fvcked. If you care about getting an A, avoid him. If you're cool with an easy B+, he's your guy.There are 6 exam points total, and you need 6 to get an A. If you get 5/6 hw problems right, and the other partially correct, this results in 2/3 points on that assignment.Avoid him if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The way he grades leaves zero room for error. You have to pretty much ace every exam and ace every assignment as well as be on top of it with the attendance. There are meetings four times a week which are mandatory. This is a very time consuming BEGINNER course for no reason.

The professor grades in an out-of-3 standard for homework and exams. And students are expected to get 6/6 for two exams in total and 15/18 for six homework in total to get an A. Even it is converted based on a 40 max test or a five question homework, it still leaves no space for mistake.

Very nice and caring professor. Did well in the course without any prior coding knowledge and asking for help is very accessible. Homework is very strictly graded but feedback is helpful and the exams model the homework. Grading cutoff is also strict, but good professor overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: decent guy, tried his best to entertained student and make lecture interesting, but RUN! ... THIS CLASS IS NOT FOR BEGINNER!   the final is way too difficult for beginner. AND THE GRADER IS A B*(sorry for my language), grader is expecting you have the EXACTLY SAME steps as he/she has, they don't care if your answer is correct or not.

Not easy for beginning coding class, tutor for study groups even mentioned not understanding why we were expected to learn some topics in an intro to coding class. Had us sign up for 2 different classes after we were already enrolled for only a 4 unit class, weird grading systems for exams as you don't receive the actual points you get.

four meetings a week.midterm was pretty easy but theres very little room to make any mistakes or you lose your chance at an A. I had no prior knowledge of any coding but he made the material easy to pick up. Don't expect this to be an easy A it will require quite a bit of work and time to understand.

Class itself is not too bad if you have previous knowledge. Grading system is based on a system of points from Hw, tests, and social learning rather than the overall percentage you see on canvas. Final exam can replace midterm score. Pretty Charismatic guy but can get stuck explaining one part of the lecture for a while. Knows what he's teaching.

Its obvious he cares about his students. Great lecturer although sometimes if you miss the beginning of class the rest of the lecture is pretty hard to follow. Great lectures, don't fall behind and put in the work and you'll be fine. The practice exams are very close to the actual exam so take advantage of that! PA's are harder than CSE11,12

The professor himself was very motivational and tried to keep students entertained BUT THIS CLASS IS NOT FOR BEGINNERS, very hard tests. There is this policy where if you fail the testing portion of the class but have an A in homework and labs, you fail the class automatically. Super unfair in my opinion, good luck. made me want to rip my hair out.
Perfect professor. Great teaching. Highly recommended. Best course I've ever take.

Gerald is one of the professors you take where you just find motivation in actually internalizing the content. The way he teaches using paper is literally equivalent to Bob Ross painting. The labs were a great exposure to the industry tools that you might be exposed to. The entire staff felt wholesome.
Excellent Professor. Clear note and easy understand the concept, which is the best Prof I have ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great guy, he does try to motivate students and help them engage. Attendance if definitely mandatory, and there is a lot of assignments every single week. If you already have experience in compsci then you'll be fine however if you don't, I would not take this as it is a lot of information to memorize!

Loved this class! Made coding seem a lot easier than I thought it would be. His lectures are engaging, and discussions encourage working with others. Made a few friends! The way he grades is a little complicated, but overall encourages growth and even if you get a low grade on the midterm it can be made up with the final. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice professor, though the grading system is horrible. Do not take this course as an intro to computer science if you have no prior experience in coding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's knowledgeable, but it was frustrating how often he changed the syllabus and grading scales. The assignments felt pointless unless you did well on the final. The study guides didn't match the exams, and he didn't prepare us well for the tests. BTW- don't ask questions because if you hold the lecture back, he will keep bringing it up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Gerald was a very kind and knowledgeable teacher, but the grading made no sense. The skill demos were pretty much all or nothing, and the exams were very difficult. If you do not have any experience with cs this class will be very difficult!! Lots of homework and projects (6)

Gerald was a great professor. He had a bit of a heavy accent but 95% of what he says is understandable. He tries his best to make lectures fun.
Course was very easy but had too many HWs to do. Everything is podcasted. Attendance is mandatory and enforced with WebClicker, but the attendance credits get transferred to the final if you do not attend.

The best professor ever! Super motivating and keeps you engaged throughout the lecture. TAs and tutors are always available to help. The syllabus is very well organized, PAs and projects are interesting and review quizzes are fun too. Definitely use the Stepik textbook problems for extra practice. Might be a bit heavy for non-majors though.

Prof. Gerald is genuinely a nice person and has entertaining lectures. However, I had a really difficult time in his class because the grading system is outrageous (basically 100% of your grade is tests). Also, the tests were ridiculously hard and the lectures are somewhat disorganized. Overall, very difficult class and hard to get a good grade in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: : You Shall Not Pass!
He needs to improve his syllabus.

Ridiculous grading; remember he was saying to those people who failed on the skill demo in the lecture, “If you got 95% or 90% in the final and midterm exam, then you're still going to pass this course.” The sentence looks so easy to say out of mouth, but hard to achieve it.

Nice guy, but bad grade policy, complete the homework is totally useless to your final grade, cause your overall letter grade is only calculated by your Assessment grade(min(Assignment grade, Assessment Grade) there is also a worst part in Assessment called skill demo, if you not pass, then maximum of your final grade is 80%.
Horrid grading system

Constantly changing grade policy, attendance is mandatory but has no positive effect on your final grade (same for the assignment). The ONLY thing that matters in this course is your exam score, never take his class again!

First things first, he's a fantastic professor and a great guy. However, this course is a nightmare, format wise. Be ready to spend every single day of the week doing stuff for this class because lectures, lab, and discussions are all mandatory and occur every single day of the week. Exams are harshly graded as well.
Do not take his class as your first CS course! Unless you are enjoy his unique grade policy :)

A nice professor, but, for a beginner's course this was a horrible class. You're expected to know most of the things right off of the bat, the pacing in the lectures felt way off, and none of the lectures prepared me for the tests. The grading is also downright crazy min(Assignments Grade, Assessments Grade), and they constantly change the syllabus

He's the GOAT. I had absolutely no computer science experience before this class and I felt super comfortable with all the assignments and content.
