Not only is he fantastic at explaining things, he also genuinely cares for his students and their well being. He puts effort into making assignments interesting as well.

His grading system is evil. The grade is split into two categories-- "tests" and "everything else" Whichever category you have the worst grade in is your grade for the class. Bad at tests? Tests are now 100% of your grade-- homework won't help at all.

He constantly edited his syllabus to make things harder for students. He promised our skill demos would be hand-graded and, therefore, not pass-fail, yet after everyone had finished the skill demos, he announced that they were now pass/fail.very slow lecturer and spends entire lecture on one topic, yet expects us to know what he doesn't cover.

He is an amazing professor. Not only is he definitely caring of his students and their success, the lectures were a great way to learn the course information. Homework was somewhat lengthy but worth it to learn and pretty fun. Tests were very fair and in my opinion not extraordinarily difficult. Take him if you can.

This is the best professor I had! Gerald is a wonderful lecturer who does live coding and draws diagrams during class that help students understand concepts. The lecture is always energetic and engaging, while the content is structured well. His office hours are also a very welcoming place where you could clarify and discuss any questions you have.

I took his CSE 11 class in Fall 23 quarter. As a person with no programming experience, I found this class super difficult & challenging. I spent the most time for this class & not even passed. Take CSE 8A if you have no programming experience. I switched major after I received the midterm score. Weekly hw, 2 coding challenges, 1 midterm & final

Soosai Raj is an amazing professor. He breaks things down in a way people can understand easily. The only problem is he gives you the information you need for the PA up until the lecture before it is due. So if you don't know a lot about java you might have to go to tutor hours. Other than that he is a great professor who cares about his students.

He's great! The live coding parts of lecture really help me understand even if I zoned out for one second. The class isn't easy, however, so go to tutor hours when you get stuck on the PAs (you will at some point) or even have general Qs. The PAs take quite a while and is where most of your time will be spent on. The deadline policy is flexible.

Gerald is super nice and approachable and makes everyone feel that they belong. Him and all of the course staff really put in the work to help students and it shows.Take his class if you can; he's a real one.
By far the best CS professor ever.
Funny professor that explains all topics well. Even though there is a lot of homework, each assignment helps you gain a solid foundation in coding.
hes mad chill n shi.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Gerald is energetic and engaging, he strays away from the main topic sometimes but is very caring and helpful.

Great Professor! Coming from a background of zero cs knowledge, he taught in a way that made the class even fun knowing how difficult programming can be. The PA's were fair and even fun, especially the image analysis ones. The exams were fair, meaning as long as you study for them couple days prior, you'll be fine. Overall recommend him.
Great lectures. Easy to reach. He makes programming so much fun.
Amazing professor at UCSD! I'll take any class he teaches.

Best professor I have ever taken at UC San Diego! He cares so much about students. :) He makes sure that the class understands the concept. There are lots of assignments but I get it; it is a CS class. 100% recommend Gerald for any course he teaches.

As someone who isn't a cs major, this class was extremely difficult. The entire grade depended on a final exam and if you fail it, your hard work for the other assignments won't matter because you'll fail the course. However, the professor is understanding.There's no curve, the exam was in-person and on paper, closed-note.

He's very caring and heart-warming. Comforts you even when you think you don't need it but in reality, you do. Mandatory attendance which is actually a good thing-- definitely keeps you on top of things. A bit of HW but nothing too horrible. TAs are always available to help when you need it. Labs are FUN! Reading Quizzes on Stepik are not that fun.

Professor Gerald's class was one of the best classes I have ever taken, & fun! He is so unbelievably kind, and always willing to help you in whatever way he can. There is a lot of coursework, but it is an intro coding course so that is expected. It was absolutely amazing that he did live coding in class, and had so many opportunities to seek help.

I just started this class and I'm ready to drop. I'm not sure if the work load is more for in person because I saw previous reviews and it doesn't even compare. I've reached out to get help from TA's 4 different times and got none. I'm a psych major so it's frustrating taking this course as its not my main focus but takes most of my time

This class was SO hard, all gas and no breaks the entire quarter. There is literally always something to be done and my grades for other classes definitely took a hit due to how much I had to give to this class. Go to office hours!! The professor is super sweet and accessible, but yeah this class is brutal :/

The assignments are complex with vague instructions. The TAs are tough graders and have absolutely no mercy. 
If you are a Pych major or non-CSE major please take CSE3A or take this class in a community college. It is very easy to fail this class. Don't push your luck!

I really wanted to like this professor given all the great reviews however, I did not have a pleasant experience with him. He really does not teach much in lecture and you really are all on your own. He assigns WAYYYY TOOO much homework and does not give enough time to complete it. DO NOT RECOMMEND!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I don't think what he taught in lecture could actually apply to the PA and final exam. In most cases, you need to learn yourself or asking Tas. The professor is not that good but TAs are super helpful
Best professor I had in the CSE apartment. Really funny lectures and truly care about students.

Literally no other computer science professor at UCSD compares. One of the only professors that I've taken that live codes when he teaches. He is so attuned to the university student who is struggling with coding. If you can take him, 100% do it. Other CS professors have frustrated me with how terrible they are teaching coding.
It is a great professor for starting to learn programming. Makes things interesting and helps you te feel integrated
He is a funny professor. Plus He builds a good learning environment. I feel way less stressed attending his lectures. Remember to attend the lab though!

Best professor at UCSD. If you have the opportunity to take him please do. He is so caring and is really passionate about computer science. If I could take him for every subject I would. 100/10 recommend!!!!!
The best teacher in ucsd

He was ok in terms of explaining code. Everything was asynchronous/non-mandatory, even discussions/some labs. The assignments done weekly were lowkey difficult because the lectures were often generalized and non-specific to the exercises. You have a lot of access to TAs/prof. himself so everyone was helpful. If you already know python tho, ur good.

live coding really immerses you in the topic and explains concepts really well. pa's get tough and sometimes covers topics not necessarily covered in lecture but built off what you learned. there are a lot of resources for help tho. he's very caring and makes sure everyone feels comfortable. checked in with us in the beginning of every class
Gerald is the most approachable and nicest professor I've ever meet at UCSD. Take his class; you won't regret.

CSE 11 with Professor Gerald was honestly the best class I have ever taken! The lectures are so helpful in understanding the big picture of the topics, and live coding really helps us get into the details of what is going on behind the scenes. Gerald encourages students to discuss and ask questions, and his class was such a positive environment!!

I genuinely don't know how prof adrian has a 3.3. Her class was really easy in my opinion but I would only recommend to people that have taken neuroscience. Class wasn't mandatory (you get extra credit for attending) and her midterms are exactly what she teaches in her slides. Also her exams don't try to trick you and are all straight to the point.

love her!!! easy class only because its so straightforward and she even provides a study guide and quizlet for all three exams. also all the extra credit opportunities are awesome i would suggest doing them (going to class, sona, and a written summary after watching a tedtalk).

Prof. Adrian is such a slay. I have taken two of her classes now and she is clearly super into her subject matter. The lectures are entertaining cuz of her accent, and the material is explained very well. Tests are simple if you go to lecture. Def would recommend!
love this woman. class is easy. only tests on slides. so precious with her german ways.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took Psyc108 & 169 with Prof Adrian. Very straightforward exams with clear study guides. Extra credit lecture attendance & sona. Engages with the class very well & material is so interesting. Lots of topics so if you're unfamiliar w neurosci- it might be tough. overall great experience :)

Exams were very fair. She provided a study guide that guided us on the content she expects us to know. Her expectations were very straightforward. Some parts of the exam could be confusing, but it's not ridiculous and is extremely fair. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you do get extra credit for attending!

Professor Adrian was super chill, and you see she's very passionate about the subject. Extra credit for attendance, three exams total along with weekly quizzes. The TAs and PLAs where very involved and provided great resources alongside the prof's OH. Straight forward study guides and no tricky questions on exams.

Attendance is optional BUT is extra credit, very transparent for the study guides and what is gonna be on the exam. Pretty straightforward and a decent teacher. I personally recommend as the lectures help a lot and its free extra credit for the class ur paying for
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Though the content can be difficult, she has a great + clear way of explaining things. Never felt lost in her lectures. 2 midterms, 1 final (cumliv), quizzes that are basically hw/practice questions every week. Provides a study guide, if you can answer everything off of that you're set. Didn't expect to enjoy the class as much as I did!

Very passionate about the material that she teaches. Class has no prereqs, but will be extremely difficult if you haven't taken any psych or neuroscience courses before. If you have, the course material is easy. 

Course moves fast, and is graded 40% on open book weekly quizzes. The other 60% is graded on 2 midterms and 1 cumulative final.

Quizzes are weighted heavily. Make sure you don't forget to do them otherwise you wreck yourself. 

This class is actually extremely easy. The sobs who rated her a 1 and complained about how hard it is are just low IQ.

Prof Adrian, is however pretty mid as a lecturer and doesn't do a great job of explaining but she does seem to care!

I don't understand why Julia has such low ratings. She is a great lecturer and clearly cares about her students. She's very clear on what will be on the exam and prepares you! I would love to take her again. I'm a transfer student so having her as a prof was great. Honestly, compared to other professor's in PSYC, she's definitely one of my favs!

She made a spelling error by labeling an L3 quiz L2 on the slide shown in class so I mistakenly took the wrong one and when I asked what I could do she told me to accept the fact I didn't get the credit and immediately started talking to someone else and didn't bother to check her error. She just made me feel incredibly unwelcome. Not a fan.

Readings or studies assigned don't read since they didn't show up on any of the exams (more like extra help) & only focus on studying the lecture slides instead. Tough to score high on her exams in-person closed notes. Expect a B w/ a lot of study time since her exam wording can be tricky, but slides are straightforward even if you don't know much.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a really sweet person and clearly loves teaching. The only issue with the class is that the tests are so short (20 q, multiple choice & true/false, 2 short answer), and there's so much material covered between each midterm that it's difficult to gauge what will be on the test. Messed up on the first midterm and couldn't recover.

Prof Adrian is clearly passionate about the material, and she works well when few people show up to class. Two midterms and a final all in person, weekly assignments graded by completion. EC for attendance. She covers a lot of material, but gives plenty of help through TAs and study guides.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Adrian has an obvious passion for this material and is incredibly kind, but is a bit monotone in her lectures. The material is extremely difficult, but if you study you can definitely do well. You really get out of this class what you put into it. Recommend studying from the beginning--learning all material for the final will be impossible.

The content for the class is already very difficult but the professor makes it even more difficult than it needs to be. Also really hard to understand what she is saying so get ready to teach yourself. Tests are half MC half fill in the blank. Not much points to recover if you do bad

Nice professor, but it can be tough to score high on her exams. If you have to take this class make sure to study and memorize everything on her slides. Her exams include fill in the blank, multiple choice and T/F.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you want to get an A, its impossible unless you study 24/7. The good thing about this class is that the midterms are online, if you get A's on them and go to every class for participation points AND do all the extra cred she gives, then you can pass. You could pass if you get a 70 or 65 on the final too. Shes a bad prof tbh. exams are so hard

Only take Professor Adrian if you absolutely must. She does not care about supporting undergraduates. Her lectures are confusing: there's lots of random info that you don't need to know for exams and key points she glazes over or does not clearly explain. I had to study profusely for this class. Please, save yourself the struggle.

Professor is not the best at lecturing. She also can be a bit rude when going to her office hours if you have questions on the exam (even if you are right and are showing her own work as proof). Would not take her again; she is not for the students, and does not like to admit that low grades in her class stem from her own lack of teaching.

Content is dense and can be a lot to try and retain, but Professor Adrian does a good job of relaying what needs to be learned and goes over topics again when asked for clarity. It's not a fun class, the subject matter can only be made so enjoyable, but I liked her teaching style and the class format. Exams = 80% of your grade and she offers 4% EC.

This class is very heavy on terminology, definitions, and really just hardcore memorization. If you are good at cramming as well as remembering a lot of small details you will do well in the class. However, I understand that it would be hard to make course content like this captivating. Not the worst professor, but not the best either.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Adrian is the best! She's so sweet and funny and provides so many resources/different learning styles throughout her lectures. She also provides study guides and really helps students feel prepared for exams. The work is hard but doable.

I regret taking this class with this professor. She is very nice but her exams are nearly impossible, she expects us to have the memory of a computer. I studied for this class through memorization NOT understanding because of the amount she expects on her exams. She includes fill in the blanks, short answers, mcq, and t/f for her exams.

This is the most honest review you'll get, coming from a straight-A student. Never have I ever taken a class more uninteresting and uninspiring. Professor Adrian is a very sweet person but does not know how to lecture. Worst part is the textbook is of no use, expecting its readers to already be neuroscientists. I'm not sure if I learned anything
All I am going to say is avoid this professor unless you know about neuroscience and actually like it.

She is very nice and approachable but the lectures are just way too broad. Lots of memorizing. Not organized in a way where you feel like you can piece together whats happening in the brain (basically you just learn what areas are associated with what). It is nice that two of the tests are online but often included details that were not emphasized.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a person I admire her, however the lectures are hard to follow. It is hard to make connections to the big picture of the topic, thus making it difficult to understand ESPECIALLY if this is your first neuroscience course. The whole of your grade depends on how you perform on the midterms and finals (midterm 50%, final 40%)

She's a very sweet and nice professor for sure. I wouldn't say I liked this class because it has 2 midterms that's 50% and the final 40%, the rest are just weekly surveys 10%. She kinda failed to expand on the topics so everything was pretty vague and can be frustrating to study for, especially when the final covers all the materials.

2 midterms worth 50% altogether, surveys are 10% and final is 40%. If you miss a couple of points on 1 test it's very hard to get an A in the class unless you study hard. Tests also have vague questions that trick you, when I addressed this to the professor she said as long as the questions are in complete grammatical sentences they still count.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a very nice professor, but I do not think her lectures are helpful. If you are unfamiliar with neuroscience this class will be much more difficult for you. The grade is mainly only out of three tests so if you are not a great test taker would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although the material may be more difficult for those who have just been exposed to cognitive neuroscience, I enjoyed taking this course and Professor Adrian! You truly have to study for her tests as they are on the more difficult side, but it presents a challenge and I feel as if I have learned a lot after taking this course.

I like her as a person. She is funny and charismatic. I didn't like her lectures because she failed to narrow down the text to the crucial info. Her tests are hard and she tests on little details that aren't necessarily representative of the big picture. I did well ONLY because I already knew the course material from other classes.

Professor Adrian's class was not that bad, but it was only graded on 2 midterms and a final. However, there was extra credit , up to 3% doing sona or by summarizing psychology talks. It was a pretty challenging class, a lot of material to be learned, but it all depends on the effort you put in to study for the exams. If you study, you'll do fine

Professor Adrian is amazing!!! Take a class with her and you wont regret it; she's truly a sweetheart.  The way she sets up the exams makes doing well in this course very practicable. Just watch the lectures and create flashcards and you'll be set!

Random pop quizzes. A lot of readings. Lowest midterm dropped. Exam questions (MCQs) ask about very specific topics and graph interpretations. Averages were probably around 60-70% or so, but a 77 was an A. Felt difficult for what's supposed to be a GE. Does seem to genuinely care about the class/material.

reviews.comment: class structure was nice,seems like the professor genuinely cares about climate justice and how his students felt. but he had long readings (15+ pages) before every lecture. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid this profesor at all costs he will drop your gpa over small details don't waste your time and take another profesor there are thousands of better profesors to take other than him.

This profesor made my school life so much harder than it needed to be. He gives out tons of homework which is unclear and procedes to grade harshly. You could do all the reading and do everything right you still won't get the grade you deserve. Don't take this class
I will never be taking this class again, no matter how hard I studied and did the readings you get at best a b-. It seemed like everyone in the class agreed I do not recommend this guy.

Class is barely about psych, more about econ, policy, history, and climate justice. 20 page readings before every lecture. Weekly quizzes and exams ask abt very specific details from readings and labels on graphs in the slides, rather than capturing understanding of the content. Lecture is just repeat of the reading but with graphs and rants.

reviews.comment: he is so unorganized, doesn't know the instructions to his own assignments, added a final during week 8, claimed everyone was using chatgpt but had no evidence so punished everyone for it, encourages class participation, but then cut off everyone when speaking, had very biased opinions, overall dreaded going to the 3 hour class,would not take again
Would not recommend, the exams will be heavily graded on specifics even when you put in lot of time to study plus wanted us to buy his textbook 😂

reviews.comment: He was very passionate about collective action, but his class is so unclear. Directions of every assignment was unclear and when asking for clarification, it wasn't much help. The grading system is weird. There was a group presentation for 8 points and people who barely did anything received 6 of 8 points. Psychology was hardly even taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I actually had to put effort into this class, but the content was so cool. Weekly quizzes when I took it. Actually had to study for the midterm and final. He wrote his own book on climate change, and is super passionate about it. Strongly reccommend going to office hours especially if interested in climate change and activism outside of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed the class material and found lectures to be incredibly insightful. The group project was a bit out of my comfort zone (in terms of public speaking) but I enjoyed doing something new. The exams were a bit stressful but that's average so far for my experience at UCSD. Overall the class was super impactful to me because of the content

The class does cover a lot material, but when you get out of it you really feel like you gained so much knowledge on climate change. Preps you to analyze climate collapse from all sides (science, economics, politics...), have high level conversations about it, and gives you useful knowledge if you (want to) work on climate organizing. Cool class.

This lab was amazing. Learning more about activism - especially in the context of the current climate crisis and other issues - was super interesting and relevant. We conducted a study with opportunities to influence the design and to learn more about research. In-class discussions were great, I highly recommend!

Dr. Aron is one of my favorite teacher at UCSD. He is passionate about climate change and helps us engage with the crisis, both as students and as individuals. The class provides a great overview of different areas of the climate crisis from physics to political science to economy and to - of course - psychology. I highly recommend!

This is my favorite professor at UCSD. He has amazing insight to offer on very serious and important topics that I think everyone on campus should be involved in. His classes changed my perspective on life and my lifestyle going forward. It impacted my priorities and made me a better person beyond the knowledge I gained from the experience. 100/10.
Worst class I ever took, the exams are nothing like the study guide and expect to do HOURS of homework and readings. If I could go back in time and choose a different profesor I definitely would.

I had an extremely uncomfortable experience in this professor's class. He engages in behavior that made me and others feel uncomfortable, and when concerns were raised, UCSD did nothing to help. If you're considering taking this class, be aware that this professor is unprofessional unsupportive and difficult to deal with.

He is super passionate about teaching us about climate change. You can really feel his excitement, and it makes the class interesting. I learned a lot about climate change from him. He is always ready to help. If you miss some points on an assignment, he reaches out to you and shows you how to earn them back.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof is not very good at understanding student needs. Does not podcast, does not give extensions, and expects you to buy his own book for $30. Group project takes plenty of time outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He is incredibly knowledgeable and passionate. That being said, he tried to condensate all there is to know about the climate crisis,  one week you will cover physics and chemistry, the next, international politics and economy. Too much. Exam questions are of specific facts or graphs in lecture OR book. Class has potential, they're open to feedback

I would only recommend this class let alone Dr. Aron if you have dense knowledge of the climate crisis. A nice man, but personally this course contained complex material and busy work for something that is not my cup of tea. So, if you are passionate about climate change I recommend him! Personally, I did not gain much taking this class.

If you don't have a background in climate change and fossil fuels I would advise against taking this class. The professor is very passionate and funny, but the coursework is very dense and difficult for the average person to understand. The readings is extremely wordy and complex. 2 weekly quizzes on reading comprehension and 1 midterm and final.

The professor is nice but this class is very difficult if you don't have a background/passion in climate science. It essentially has nothing to do with psychology and is basically an environmental science class. The textbook and articles are incredibly wordy and very difficult for the average person to understand. Tests are hard. Textbook is dense.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The below review about this class being difficult to track and make progress in is plainly false. I did an unacceptably low amount of work and effort for this class and got an easy A, his lectures are some of the most engaging I have had in my three years here, and he brings in a multitude of distinguished guest speakers for lecture. Great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was one of my favorite classes at UCSD. The content of the class was super interesting and the topic is incredibly important. Prof Aron is also really great, he cares a lot of about the topic of this class and his students. The exams really aren't that hard either, just make sure you do the reading.

this class was an incredibly tedious course. Tons and tons of reading and the questions asked on exams often ask for you to remember the smallest details from his book. Offers a lil EC and has discussions twice a week for easy points, the exams are brutal, even with excessive studying the questions catch you off guard. he loves the topics though
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor, he wrote the textbook himself and knows what hes talking about. Very passionate about the topics. A lot of reading but its super interesting. Recommend him!

The hardest class I've taken at UCSD. The textbook was written by him and not yet published, so a little confusing. Tests were extremely difficult and wording was unnecessarily complicated. reviews.comment: I loved PSYC185. It was the most eye-opening college course I took, so it was easy to put in effort. Also, he really cares about the material which makes any class less dry. Highly recommend!

reviews.comment: This was my favorite class at UCSD. Beyond the incredibly important material covered regarding the climate crisis, Dr. Aarons passion for this subject is inspiring. This was a challenging class but in a very rewarding way. His constructive and clear feedback allowed me to tremendously improve my writing. I highly recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Aron is fantastic, and Psych of the Climate Crisis should be taken by every single student at UCSD. Aron is an inspiring climate activist and learning from him will have a lasting & positive impact on my life

I cannot stress this enough- do not take this professor. Save yourself from the pain. This class ruined my GPA. By far the worst professor I have ever had at any university. Definitely the hardest professor I've ever taken. I was not prepared to read such heavy material, and was not ready for such detail-oriented tests. Clicker questions based on accuracy, not participation. If you read and reread material and reference podcasts, you'll do better than I did.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Psychology of Climate Change was one of my favorite classes at UCSD. Workload was heavy, but readings were all fascinating. One of the most hardest professors I've ever had. His tests are known to be super difficult, they are super wordy and confusing. Doesn't care that he gets rated as a bad prof, only really cares about doing his research and about saving the planet.

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors. A little difficult to understand because he talked so fast and goes through slides so quickly, and a dry lecture. reviews.comment: He is pretty cool and obviously an expert. The class (cog. neuroscience) is very technical, not really difficult per se, just specific. He has a little bit of a British sense of humor, if you like that (which I do :))
he is great. he is an expert in his field without a doubt. strongly suggest this class for those with some initial interest in cognitive neuroscience...

Lecture is mandatory if you want a solid A. Great professor, very knowledgeable about cognitive neuroscience, if that's your thing. His midterms and final are fairly challenging, but it's nothing ridiculous. Overall, he's a very nice guy and does care about his students as well.
Very interesting class!  The exams were tough, but studying and paying attention in class really helps.
Aron isn't dumb, that's for sure.  But that doesn't mean he is a bit of an intellectual snob.
Adam is a very clear speaker and it is clear that he is an expert in his field.

Great Professor! He may come off boring in lecture, but he's a really nice guy who's there to help and talk. The class was frontal lobe studies, and he didn't even use a book, which saves you good money. I had to do a short paper, but when I went up to his OH he found actually found the articles FOR me to write the paper! He is really sociable too!

Tests are multiple choice and vaguely worded at best...for the midterms you have to rush through them, but take your time on the final and re-read them multiple times. Great professor though, he really helps you understand the subject...I was impressed.

I attended only half of the lectures, but he posts slides online. I think he curved a lot as I thought I'd fail but apparently I didn't. I felt the lecture was kinda boring, but he seems a nice professor. I think class was ok but definitely was a good intro to neuroscience; it definitely helped me when I took some other classes later.

Psyc 108: Cognitive Neuroscience.  Aron is a pretty decent professor.  His power point slides are informative, and he posts them on WebCT.  His tests are kind of hard, which he takes great pride in. Attendance is not mandatory, but you should go to his lectures to really understand.  Book reading is a must, but it's a decent book.  Overall, he is s
Very friendly and helpful in office hours. Stuck close to the book. Very clear lecture notes, which were posted soon before class started.
Professor Ioana explains very well and has clear and concise notes.

Exams are very difficult but fair for a course like this, and they match the practice ones pretty well. Both are also similar to the given homework problems. Sunk 10 hours a week into the class and probably 15-20 on exam weeks. No cheat sheets. For all three exams, one problem was guaranteed to be a proof covered in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great lectures, and workload was relatively light (though this might be mostly due to the course itself).
Super nice professor. His exam was not that bad, and neither was the qual.

Great lecturer, midterms were fair and final was decently hard, but doable if you studied. He writes his tests with a pattern that shows up in his notes, so look at old tests made by him to study effectively.
There is not extra credit in the class. Exams typically have 4 questions, partial credit can be received. Does not curve the exams nor the class, TA is very monotoned and has a heavy accent.

Good professor as a person, but I found the grading to be too harsh. You wouldn't really be rewarded for knowing the concepts, and there was a lot of emphasis on reaching the conclusion, which I don't feel is a fair way for math - especially math at this level - to be graded. Definitely attend lectures if you take with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: as someone coming from clac bc, this class was pretty good. material can get confusing during lecture but go back to read your notes and example problems given and you will be fine. homework can get tedious sometimes and not always representative of exams but lecture notes are your best friend

i love prof ioana!! his accent is kind of hard to adjust to at first but you end up getting used to it. i really like the way he structures the notes and it made it really easy when studying for the midterms/final. definitely prioritize in class examples because ioana is the one that writes the tests. i thought the final was pretty rough but 5/5!!

Don't take this class lightly!! While Prof Ioana is great (amazing lecture notes, genuine guy) this course really makes you work for the grade. Out of two midterms, worst score is dropped-- aim for a high score on the first as course material gets harder. Exams draw heavily from lecture examples, so give them priority when studying.

His lectures were ok, but his tests were kinda hard, and they don't give much partial credit which kinda made me fail, I did the right process but some computation errors and lost 80% of the points, the final was kinda bad, it had HW problems but on steroids, got s 54%, and ended with a C-.

BEST professor for 20C. EXCELLENT lecturer. My friends had another professor but their lectures sucked. Only mandatory attendence for most discussions. No E.C., but only the highest midterm counts towards your final grade which makes up for it. The exams are a lot like the review examples so its easy (with a cheat sheet). Online textbook HW weekly.
Was a very good lecturer, make topics easy to understand with good examples. Also seems like a genuinely nice and approachable guy. Midterms and finals were relatively easy.

His accent was confusing at first, but then you get used to it. He goes pretty quick in lectures and covers a lot of material each time efficiently. Hw is free, discussions and tests were difficult. When confused, just read the textbook and do a lot of practice. The grading is heavily weighted on tests. Not a bad class but need to put in the work.

Clear and interesting lectures, very helpful during office hours, genuinely enjoyed attending his lectures. Fair exams that are reflective of the content learned in class. Highly recommend taking his class.

LOVED IOANA! He was a great lecturer and a really nice, approachable guy. I attended every lecture and used his notes + practice exams to study for exams - never had to use the textbook except for homework assignments. Retained all the concepts from his course just because he taught them so well. Exams were very fair and there was a slight curve.

Lectures are easy to understand, but a light accent sometimes makes it hard to read the notes. Exams are as straightforward as practice problems/tests, making them easy to prep for. The downside is that tests are weighted very heavily, so even if with a 100% on HW and midterms you still need an 85% on the final to get an A.

Has a IMO silver medal when young, yet still willing to answer all questions in patience in office hours, whether  class materials or math topics outside of the class. Two midterms, only the best graded(which saved me). Final is not hard since he provided similar practice final and shows procedure in last lecture. Study that well.

I recommend using the textbook, especially if you take notes before lectures. The tests were usually easier than expected, but the final was harder. Lectures could be a bit boring, but following along with the example problems was especially helpful.

While I do believe he is a great professor, the coursework is challenging and the homework was not relevant to the tests. His lectures and study guides are what make him a great professor. He uploads lecture outlines you can use during lectures which are great. Math 20C is by far the hardest class I have had to take so prepare.

He is a great professor with organized structures of the class and the lectures are so amazing. 20% homework, 35% best midterm exam, 45% final. Homework is easy peasy and achieve is so good. Tests are a little bit of challenging, however, doing worksheets and practice exams will be fine ! 100 % recommended

Professor Ioana is a great professor in *most* regards.

Lectures: He explains topics well, with good detail, and does not waste lecture time. He uploads lecture note outlines before class.

Exams: Before Exams 1&2, he released review sheets, along with answers.

Final: More difficult than previous exams and review sheets imply, prepare HEAVILY.
Very lovable guy ngl. Math 20C was a bit difficult, but he was good at explaining each topic. His tests aren't too bad and the hw is manageable.

I took this class during winter 2022, when all classes unexpectedly went online. Ioana's lectures were terse at times but very true to the book. A very valuable skill I learned from this class was not only the subject material but learning how to teach myself mathematics, and his lectures were perfect for that. Overall very solid and a fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hes very clear in what he expects you to know and what will be on the test

Adrian was good, his accent is a bit heavy and his handwriting isn't the best, but is still a good professor. He was lenient with grades (drops one quiz score) and the homework site he used was pretty user-friendly. Definitely recommend watching his lectures since they are important to the class and he explains concepts well.

Overall if you watch his lectures ( asynchronous for me) and do the work he wants you to do, you will have a good time. The textbook HW isn't necessary, but the discussion work, achieve HW, and especially the practice tests are very important and helpful. Only occasionally will you have to use the text to but only solve a HW question.

The lectures are a bit difficult to understand. I would highly recommend reading ahead using the textbook, and solving the textbook problems as supplemental material. The midterm and final are a higher difficulty than the quizzes.

HOW I GOT MY A+: Quiz questions from the discussion; test questions from lectures. Professor Ioana's lecture is really explaining the test materials. Midterm average: 95%; Final quite challenging. Grading Scale: 15% HW+30% Quiz(best 2 out of 3)+20% Midterm + 35% Final.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures are recorded and very well structured. It's very no nonsense and provides a good number of examples. Quizzes are not too hard if you study the content well, and the proctoring is lenient. If I had to complain about anything, the instructor sometimes makes very small mistakes in lectures and the final is much harder than the quizzes.

Professor Ioana is amazing! He has pre-recorded lectures that are easy to understand. He is helpful in office hours and very friendly. He provides a lot of opportunities for students to prepare for quizzes and the final by posting practice problems. You know he wants his students to learn and exceed. 100% would recommend!

Lectures are the perfect balance of theory and practice, homework's nothing too crazy, and quizzes are easy to ace so long as you've been following along with lecture and doing HW. Final's way more difficult, though, so be ready for it. Understand the concepts and you'll do fine.

Professor Ioana is an amazing professor. His lectures have the perfect balance of theory and examples. His homework is very reasonable and manageable. His quizzes are straightforward and fair. The discussions are really great because they do much harder problems than we usually encounter. Also, he's very quick to answer on Piazza.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Ioana's quizzes are pretty easy and he gives you practice quizzes that are much harder than the actual quizzes. He lets you drop your lowest quiz. His lectures are almost all asynchronous, making it a bit harder to ask questions. Discussion has been really helpful for asking questions.

I had Ioana for MATH 142A and 142B. I appreciated his lectures and, personally, he helped me finally become better at doing math proofs after MATH 109 (Wish I had him for such a class). He is an amazing professor and even though I did not get in the A range he taught with fluidity and passion. I hope to see him again in the future. Take him 10/10

Professor Ioana is by far one of the nicest professors that Ive encountered at UCSD. He is very kind and helpful during office hours. However, his exams are extremely hard. The average was usually around 50%, but he curves generously. The average is usually assigned a C+ or B-. Thank goodness for the curve, it saved me.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures are clear, but the exams are sooooo hard!!! Always do homework and you will pass the exam.
The exams are really hard....
He is sooooo nice ! His tests are sooooo easy!

Class was super proof heavy. In retrospect, I would have done so much better if I had taken it after or concurrently with a basic proof class like CSE 20. Lectures were fast-paced and always a struggle. Material wasn't hard, but make sure you have a solid background of proof strategies before you do this class. Beware of the aloft students though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: highly recommend going to lecture (even though the proofs and examples are straight out of the book, he explains them so much better) homework (from book) is much harder (and different) than the exams (problems from him) so don't study the homework for exams, use his practice exams and his old exams and you'll do better (my grade is proof)

He lectures basically by the book with a few alternative proofs. MATH 31AH was extremely proof heavy, but the tests were always easier than the review problems he gave us before the test. The homework took only a few hours, so nothing extreme. Overall, the class is a lot of work, but prepares you well for higher level maths.
Professor Ioana's class is fast paced and commands the attention of students in the form of its difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class put Ioana under time pressure, so he likes to go through things quickly, leaving little opportunity for students to process the concepts in their minds. He welcomes questions during lectures, and he tries to answer all of them as patiently and clearly as possible. Office hours are helpful. Lecture material similar to what's in the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Lecture always covers what we need for homework. Not very accessible outside of class; neither he nor the TA can meet between our discussion section and when HW is due. Course is heavily proof-based, be ready for that. Midterms and homework usually graded clearly & fairly, and if not you can talk to your TA and get points back. Book needed for HW.

He's average. He's not great but he's not terrible either. His lectures are pretty straightforward although they are exactly the same as the textbook. He's practically reading the chapter to you. And I'm not sure why the other reviews here from math 31AH students say he's so great. Most students I know in the class didn't think he was that great.
Best professor ever. Very clear lectures and helpful practice exams. Exams are easier than homework.

Tests are easier than homeworks. I suggest prestudy for the proof of theorem, which in few cases are different than those he wrote on board. Eigenvalue and determinant are  more difficult, but it is not the main focus of final. Practice midterm and final are also  more difficult than the actual ones. Just go to OH and do the HW BY UR SELF.

Awesome Professor. He's always willing to help after class and in office hours; he really cares about his students. The material was hard, but that's to be expected with an honors class. His lectures are always interesting and animated. You can really tell that he enjoys teaching math. On top of all that, He's a fun guy. Take his class.

MATH 20F itself is not a difficult math class. It's the calculations that get me for the midterms. I can't do mental math and no calculator was allowed along with a time limit. This is coming from a person who got A's in MATH 20A-20D and I got a B- in this class. Ioana himself is a nice guy with an accent, but tests should be more concepts.

Harsh/inconsistent grading. His two midterms were the most straightforward, calculation-based tests I've ever taken for math. However, his final was totally proof/concept-based and was unexpected. Worst of all, NO CURVE whatsoever. If you decide to take his class, always be OVER prepared!
Has an accent but he's easy to understand. 2 midterms with cheat sheet front and back. final gets 2 cheat sheets front and back.

Ioana is a good professor. I recommend him for sure. He is very clear when speaking and writing. His lectures are very helpful and the midterms are exactly like the practice midterms. The class itself is pretty easy and boring. It is definitly possible to get an A in his class.
I don't think any professor can turn this class to an easy class. I mean who cares about Rolle's theorem anyways. Overall, he is a nice guy.

It's a difficult course, but Adrian is a friendly and helpful professor. Lectures are okay-I mean, I don't think no one can understand the course material at a first glance. Tests reflect lectures and homework. Overall, I recommend him.

He does what he can with the material, but iclickers are needed for every class even though he's lecturing on stuff that has almost(!!!) nothing to do with the actual work. I like that he's clearly passionate about what he's talking about but the entire course could be taught without him, as my TA went over everything we actually needed to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
(The class I took was MMW 121 & the grade format was complete/not complete)
Professor Adamiak is a good professor, BUT my TA was BAD, in this class you don't have a final exam, instead you write an essay that you built during all the quarter, the problem is that my TA graded very bias. You have a lot of non-sense guidelines that you need to follow.

they want this to be a community building class for new students yet they make it somehow more labor intensive than my organic chemistry class or any other stem class for that matter its enraging honestly because  all the other colleges get normal classes without a trillion guidelines and readings and here we with a billion things going on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
I took MMWR and it was an easy A. However, your grade depends on your TA. 
The lectures were helpful. There were no exams, only papers and discussion board questions which needed to be answered.
An amazing and entertaining lecturer who is passionate and knowledgeable on his field of study. I love attending his lectures, already sad to have the quarter end.

The main difficult parts of MMW12 were the essays which are graded dependent on your TA, but Adamiak made the tests relatively fair. His lectures are funny, but kind of hard to actually disseminate information from. A lot of the class depends on your TA and experience in section, but he's a solid professor overall.

Adamiak is very charming, funny, and clearly cares about this subject matter. While his lectures can feel a bit confusing, cluttered, or fast-paced at times, whether or not this is a negative is entirely dependent on your learning style. For me, it was manageable! His use of podcasts and cheat sheets definitely helps!

Probably the easiest MMW12 prof. Even though his lectures can be confusing/cluttered, he has much less reading and I liked essay based exams instead of MCQ. If you like that style, I'd recommend, but everything is graded by your TA. Honestly I mostly took him because I wanted to read less and it was easy for a 6 credit class. He's also nice.

Nice guy, I mean the professor doesn't really have much to do with your grade but rather the TA, he uses iClicker, which isn't too bad except sometimes he didn't know how to work the iClicker, he has a tendency to yap a bit but I like him because its easier to digest the material because of the flow of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty solid, just a couple of essays and he assigns these a couple days in advance, he did have weekly exams and discussion boards but in itself everything is really simple and nothing terrible
Really kind professor, makes MMW a slightly better experience because he condenses readings. Wish I could take him for all my MMW courses!
it was alright. im a bit salty about my ta though. but the class itself was fine, and adamiak is funny
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He jumped around different topics and cultures that made it hard to follow, goes very fast through slides, hard for slow typers/hand writers to take notes, joke/childish style/outdated memes, easier to get an A grade(Depends on TA), iclicker attendance, info blasted slides, didn't learn much. Short readings and cheat sheet for essay tests.

iClicker attendance 10%, take-home essays (10%, 20%), in-person midterm/final essays w/ cheatsheet (15%, 25%). TA preference matters for grading, not the Prof. Lectures were just for attendance—slides and time management were poor. Light reading load, good if balancing tough classes.

Iclicker attendance, lecture notes posted online and super accessible. I didn't really focus too much in the class and just studied the night before the midterm by creating a cheat sheet and I was fine. Grading is dependent on TAs so make sure you understand what they're thinking while they're grading. Short response mid terms. Writing heavy.

Taking MMW11 remote was really chill. I watched the lecture videos for the first few weeks but honestly just take notes on the slides and you'll be fine. Most of this course relied on TA grading, some are pickier than others. Take general notes on the readings too but that's it. The essays are simple with easy guidelines.

I took him online for 11R and it was very worth it. He's a nice professor and the lecture videos are pretty engaging, if a bit outdated. You are mostly graded by the TA but there is some in-class work that buffers it. He doesn't give too-long readings, and I didn't really pay attention to the videos but did fine.

Professor Adamiak was an incredible professor. He's a very engaged lecturer and he posts slides. Attendance is mandatory through Icklicker. Has a few essays and a take home final paper, no quizzes or any other exam. The best professor I have taken within the MMW series.
his jeans are to tight imo
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Pat is super chill and funny, he won't stress you out! I took MMW 121 with him and honestly your TA does most of the grading so it depends on who your TA is.
Online lectures were pretty easy to follow and his slides are well organised

His lectures can be long, but he's better than other MMW professors I've heard about. We have 3 Content Analyses, which are our midterms/final. He's not as accessible by email as he claimed. Thankfully, my TA was detail-oriented and easy to reach. Overall, though, take Adamiak. He's nice! Be prepared to read and listen to do well on the CA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Pat has very entertaining & fun lectures (though they can run on & go off topic a little lmao). Your grade basically just depends on your TA, but as long as you put effort in you will be fine. All readings are short pdf's, there's a DB each week + 3 content analysis papers (the 3rd being a longer final) & the video quizzes are super easy!

So I'll preface this with a couple of things. The professor is a great guy, you can tell he really does care about the students. However, I took this course (MMW) and it was hands down the most tedious and frustrating class I've taken at UCSD. The whole way it was taught felt like it was to be as tedious as possible instead of actually inform you.

Definitely take MMW11 remotely if you can. Weekly, you watch the lecture videos and take a quick quiz, and respond to a discussion post. He shows his dogs during lecture videos which is nice. I had no interaction with him besides watching his videos, which I didn't mind but if interaction is important to you, I'd go for in-person.

This class was terrible. I took this professor because everyone gave him 5's on this, but this is not an accurate rating. I hated coming to this class and listening to him talk about himself. Very disorganized, and I would not recommend this class/professor.

The entire MMW 121 Course was VERY UNCLEAR. TA does all the instruction/grading for assignments, the instructor did not post instructions for assignments until 1-3 nights before. Each week builds to a final paper, with no midterms/exams. So many requirements for assignments, very confusing. 

Lecture/Discussion MANDATORY.
Lectures were interesting and entertaining. He cares that students are engaged and wants us to learn. Graded on essays, midterm, and final exam as well as participation.

Great professor. His lectures are pretty interesting and he is a pretty funny guy. Class is entirely based off of your essays which are graded by your TAs. No surprises in his class and was very fair grading wise.

Not just an amazing professor, but an amazing person. This class made me look forward to lectures and made me interested in multiple different topics I'd never even known about. MMW is annoying, but this class would be worth taking even if it wasn't a requirement. If you have any possibility of taking Adamiak at any point... do it instantly.
literally the best professor ive had as uninteresting the content is adamiak makes it so funny and bearable and borderline enjoyable PICK HIM HES THE BEST

He was a great lecturer who often connected to his students beyond the slides! I really enjoyed that he posted slides ahead of time and podcasted all lectures. Adamiak cares deeply about his students and he even found a substitute for iClickers by using the free version for attendance. Would definitely recommend him!
horrible teacher who cusses so much!

Your grade in this class is mainly based on four essays. Lectures are only useful when you have to use them in your essays because many TAs want you to weave in lecture material. Professor Adamiak is a very nice person who tries to keep the class engaged, despite times where his lectures are boring. Awesome professor and I would take him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Adamiak gives awesome lectures. He's really good at responding to e-mails. There were no tests, just essays that are very manageable. Make sure to do the readings because you use them on the essays. The only thing is that sometimes he's late to posting things on Canvas, but he does have a newborn so it's understandable. Overall a great professor.
He is one of the most fun professors, he genuinely cares not only about teaching but about making sure that his students love history. He made me like the MMW series more than I thought I would.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Adamiak always podcasts lectures, which is great. Most of the grades come down to TA's over 4 papers and perusalls. His lectures are funny and he posts slides. He sometimes posts additional videos, but they aren't necessary.

super nice guy and relatively easy class. 4 shorter papers over the term, perusalls, and section make up most of your grade. lectures are heavy, but don't feel necessary - i just did the readings and i was fine. best case scenario for this class is to get this professor. he's silly and classes aren't too serious. participation in section matters!
Great professor that manages to always make lectures interesting, even when the content isn't the most interesting

Professor Adamiak was a great lecturer. He made MMW 11 more interesting than I had thought. Took him online asynchronously. Went to a few office hours, and was very kind. Loved his lectures. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Best lecturer I've ever had. He incorporates lots of jokes and modern examples that effectively engage students and help you further understand the material. He is very easy to talk to in office hours and the readings were very short compared to other MMW 11 professors.

Professor Adamiak uses effective contemporary analogies to convey his lecture material; our class was online and pre-recorded, but all of the information I needed was communicated effectively. He provided some awesome sources for us to use and analyze.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: i really disliked mmw coming in but he made it way more enjoyable

Very nice professor, teaches class in an interesting way. This is an online class, so we need to watch videos and participate in weekly discussions, which is graded. Great reading materials, not much! Professor chose the texts that best fit. CAs and final prompts are interesting and fair. Strongly recommend, makes me fear less about the MMW series.

Professor Adamiak provides a lot of information throughout his lecture videos all while making them entertaining and easy to watch. Everything he talks about relates back to the readings and overall does a good job at setting you up for success. Put in the time and effort, and I'm sure you'll do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very nice professor. Lots... and I mean lots of lecture material and reading

One of the best MMW professors I've ever had, way better than Chang and Balberg. Great lectures with memes and keeps you interested. Super fun professor, knows his stuff. Readings are a lot less compared to other MMW Course. However, I took this as a summer course so I don't know how different it is in person and in a regular quarter.

had a different professor but bowers explained it so much better i just went to his lectures. all profs follow him and he goes through everything so clearly. the homework is a copy paste of the quizzes.

Great professor. Lectures explained the material clearly and included examples. The course had a clear structure. The midterm could be retaken, and the practice tests are similar to the actual exams :)

Bowers is one of the best Math teachers, if you can take any class with him, you should do it! You don't need the textbook to learn with the homework and weekly Quizzes its fine. He has lots of office hours if you have question and he is a very charismatic and kind.

Lowkey, Prof. Bowers is probably the greatest math professor at UC San Diego. Engaging lectures and a free online "course" that replaces a paid textbook. Although there are weekly quizzes in the TTC, Prof. Bowers gives out online practice quizzes/midterms that mirror the actual in-person tests. Highly recommend!

Savior of the UCSD math department. Clear teaching during lectures and breaks down the basics for each question. The online homework actually does help teach and doesn't take that much time to do. His midterms and final are taken at the TTC, and he also provides unlimited practice tests that contain the same type of questions as the real exam.

Easiest A you will ever get in a 20 series math course. There are endless practice quizzes and exams that are identical to what is covered in the real thing. As long as you put the time in to study these topics, you'll pull through with an A. Chill grading policies but beware of how you format your answers on Prairie learn/test. That's all: W Prof!

Good prof, but the only thing that counts towards your grade is the weekly quizzes and midterms/final. All are proctored and with no cheat sheet with no do overs so you have to do well or it tanks your grade.  Homework is optional and doesnt affect your grade but if you do it, you will learn the material.

Good professor, very approachable and will answer emails and questions in lecture. does quizzes in the testing centre on the computers so you need to learn the syntax for prairie learn. has two midterms and a final. do the homework and you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: HE IS THE BEST MATH TEACHER EVER!!!! If you have the chance to take this class do it!! He is so good at explaining hard concepts in an understandable way and he makes math so fun! Lectures and discussions are not mandatory and the homework is SO HELPFUL and so manageable. The midterms are so straight forward and so are the weekly quizzes.

Good lecturer but sometimes gets carried away, midterms are standardized so some questions might come as a surprise if he didn't go over it too much in lecture. If he provides sample exams, do them, even though he says they're not gonna be similar to the real exams they will be. Textbook is optional. Easy biweekly quizzes.
Attendance not required for lecture or discussion. Passionate and funny guy. Homework is easy, quizes and tests are at the ttc and are easy.

BOWERS IS GOATED! LEs and DISs are suggested but not mandatory. The two midterms are fair. 4 Quizzes online, with 3 chances per question, given a practically identical practice quiz beforehand to prepare. Bowers is very knowledgeable, and his 8am was worth waking up for. He could prolly teach math to a sea slug he's that good at teaching. TAKE HIM
The class is super easy. The homework is optional but if you do it you're basically guaranteed an A. Lectures weren't super interesting, but clear and informative. Overall, would highly recommend.

Good lectures, provided examples and extra practices. Biweekly quizzes at AP&M, provided practices that were the same problems. Like any math exam, there were stuff that were never taught/discussed but weren't too bad. Just do the hw and quizzes. Final was also at AP&M, was told they were like the quizzes, but were pretty different.

He is an OK professor teaching an OK class. He is good in terms of teaching the content but isn't very friendly when you talk to him one on one which can be discouraging. Class isn't too difficult. I felt like he sometimes talked down to me.

None of the lectures and discussions are required for attendance, homework is optional, and your grade is only determined by the midterm, final, and 4 out of the 5 quizzes that you can take. If you took AP Calc and did good, this is an easy class for you and even then, his lectures are good. Probably the best professor at UCSD, he's a top class guy
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Quizzes are really easy if you do the practice ones, midterms were a bit hard, but the final was pretty easy. During the lectures, he goes over the easiest examples possible, but questions on exams are way harder. And he doesn't assign any homework to practice doing harder questions.

No lectures or homework are mandatory and all of your grades are from at the testing center quizzes and in class exams. You get three tries to get full credit  on the quizzes and questions are pulled from homework so they aren't difficult. His lectures are good, if not slightly boring, but it was a good way to learn and practice the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I appreciate how Professor Bowers cracks a few jokes in class sometimes. His slides are well-formatted and his handwriting is neat. Homework is optional, but completing it will help you. Quizzes are easy A's if you practice them with PrairieLearn. He's super generous and offers a makeup midterm that can't hurt your grade. No cheat sheets allowed.

I really enjoyed the class. I think there were enough chances to improve my grade. We had 2 out of 3 midterms counted, 4 out of 5 quizzes and one online final. If you are consistent, this class shouldn't be a problem.

Knowledgeable and prolific professor. Lectures were easy to digest and gave a good preview of future tests and quizzes. All quizzes and the final are taken online, practice materials for both are found on Canvas and PrairieLearn, respectively. Drops the lowest grade of three midterms/six quizzes, but only if you took the makeup.

Doc Bowers was a hilarious prof, attend discussions for practice (not mandatory though). Do student guide and all homework for your benefit... Can makeup one midterm (pretty easy) and one quiz to replace lowest score. Quizzes and final for me were at CBTF (be wary of parentheses and save before submitting..) Has free textbook, but I never read it.

Professor Bowers is not an unreasonable professor but his class is not as easy as many reviews lead you to believe. In my experience the homework and quizzes didn't connect well to the mid-terms and finals.

Skips through steps and calculations during lectures. Which I would understand in a higher level math but this is a prep course and those small bits hinders learning. Midterms were not too bad. Horrendous discussion sections. SKIP THOSE. NOT RECORDED LECTURES EITHER. HW is not at all representative of test material. Fall 2024 course

If you're bad at math, you NEED to actually put in the work. His office hours are very accessible and his explanations are pretty clear. Also, go to his lectures, they're very helpful. You do need to read the textbook for some homework problems though. I didn't pass this class (I'm horrible at exams) but he was a great professor. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The practice quizzes are literally made for you to ace the real ones (plus there's 3 attempts per question), and the HW & lessons on Learnvia are very easy. You're essentially guaranteed 100% on those categories, so lock in on midterms and the final!! He also offers a make-up midterm and a makeup quiz and drops the lowest score in those categories.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked his class! He's very goofy and made the content easy to understand. He makes his quizzes + midterms very easy and just wants everyone to do well. Lecture and discussion are not mandatory, but I would recommend going to the lecture.

MY ABSOLUTE KING!!!! I thought I was bad at math, but prof Bowers makes Calc II so straightforward. His lectures are very clear, and he shows the step-by-step process for each question in his slides. Class is based on two midterms, 4 homework quizzes, and a final. The exams are exactly like the lectures and homework. TAKE HIM!!! He's such a cutie!
Decent prof, just spend time on practice problems, review past midterms, AND GO TO LECTURES.

i love professor bowers. he is such a kind soul and if he was my age i would be best friends with him. you should go to lectures lowkey cs i regret skipping. he explains everything clearly in his lectures. the tests arent exactly like the lectures, but if you know the material from the lectures and you have critical thinking skills you'll be fine.
he is money minded

While lecture and discussion are not mandatory to attend, I heavily suggest attending lecture at minimum. He teaches in a way that is easy to digest and he goes through everything step-by-step if need be. Very approachable, kind, and has a very clear syllabus to follow. Highly recommend as someone who struggled in AP Calc AB and is now thriving.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: HW is optional & attendance isnt mandatory for the DI & LE so the whole class feels optional & easy to skip. Bc HW is optional, the only things graded are 2 Midterms, Final, & 4 Quizzes. The quizzes are very easy, you get 3 attempts per Q, 6 Q total, are everyother week & can be scheduled whenever. Prof is chill, v engaging, wears a bowtie everyday
Soild instructor, clear slides, and goes step by step through example problems so the concepts easy to understand.

i genuinely thought I was abt to bomb this class LOLL tests r reasonable in difficulty n have their fair share of easy/hard problems but sometimes throws a curveball. but it also math so u should master everything not js the basics?? but sups generous n gave a make-up quiz AND midterm bc of this funk as online testing that gave no partial credit.
The goat. applied a curve which saved me from failing. also gave quiz and midterm retake. Multiple grading methods available as well that pull from your best scores.

95% of your grade is made up of 6 exams, but the professor was kind enough to let us retake 2 for a higher score, and also gave us practice exams to offer more support. He's a great lecturer and very understanding. Seems like we also received a slight curve? because my B+ was rounded to an A-. Overall recommend, just beware of the TTC online exams.

95% percent of your grade is made up of exams, and quizzes lmao. and midterms and the final is being graded through autograder by a computer system, so no partial credit. gave a retake on a midterm and quiz because everybody was lowk failing, so much stress for a calc class. made things way too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I agree with the comment right below me because I took him for Math20A too. I was lowk failing hard af but he let us retake a quiz and a midterm just cos we were all failing and now im striving GGS
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Made understanding concepts way harder than they needed to be and midterms are very short and sometimes on concepts only covered in the textbook. He grades 95% testing and are online SO NO PARTIAL CREDIT. I don't believe that is fair for a calc math class of this type. He has decent slides but he is not helpful when talking to him in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor! For Fall 2022, lectures were in-person, with weekly online homework via Edfinity and weekly online quizzes. The lecture slides were useful for homework and exam prep. There were two midterms and a final exam, all online and open-note. Attendance at discussion and SI sections was mandatory.

He is good at explaining things I'm just not good at math. He's one of the best math teachers here, but he doesn't podcast which sucks. Gives plenty of resources outside of lectures to help prep for the two midterms and the final. He genuinely wanted his students to pass and you could tell by the way he kept checking in on everyone in the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I love how Professor Bowers would include a few jokes every once in a while. He always made sure to show plenty of examples of how to solve problems, which made understanding the course better. There were 2 homework assignments each week (online and paper), but doable. He also tried his best to set up convenient office hours.
Mr. Bowers is an amazing professor. He provides slides and genuinely cares. Weekly homework but they are fairly easy. His lectures are easy to follow and engaging

Prof. Bowers is a very funny man, but not the greatest lecturer. He posts annotated slides, but the lecture isn't recorded, so its not too clear how he got from one step to another. If you have taken pre-calc/trig before, the class materials should not be too difficult. 

Grade is 20% per midterm (2), 40% final. Lowest midterm replaced by final!

Speeds through important parts of lecture just to finish the section and I hated that. Does not podcast so you have to just gaslight yourself into thinking you understood the new material. Midterms and finals werent too bad but I found it so difficult to not have a cheat sheet considering how much your expected to know by memory. NO CURVE

Bowers is hilarious and teaches really clearly. I think math is difficult in a lecture setting(at least for me) so the TA in your discussion can make all the difference. I'd recommend Bowers to anyone though as I did enjoy all his jokes and lectures.

Dr. Bowers' lectures were always super helpful as he explained problems step-by-step. lectures are not recorded so make sure to attend otherwise posted slides can be confusing. discussions not mandatory. tests are very similar to practice exams and problem bank questions. he responds super quick to questions on piazza. office hours m, t, w, and f.

The professor is decent overall, with clear lectures and a fair grading system. There are a lot of assignments, but they serve as helpful practice. While the exams can be challenging, using resources like unstuckstudy ai alongside the textbook can really aid in preparation.

Best math professor. Lectures at a pace that welcomes questions and engages students new to the material. I went to almost all his office hours, and he was very helpful. Midterm was reflective of what was taught in class. View the homeworks as prep for exams. 10/10 would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: whatever you do, DO NOT take 10B with Bowers over the summer. He just pre recorded a bunch of lectures and they were super hard to follow. The exams were also difficult.

Bowers is a solid professor. Clear and informative lectures with lots of step by step examples. Lots of assignments. HW, quizzes, discussion worksheets are all graded, so plenty of safety nets if you don't do well on the midterms or final. Exams were relatively easy, just a lot of true or false questions pulled from lecture slides.

mandatory attendance in DI, overall really sweet professor who cares for his students. Lots of safety nets cause theres sm work, (weekly projects, quizzes and 3 hws), but that ensures that if u bomb the final youll do find if u got everything else done well. I did not do well on final, and i still passed w a B bc of all the work.

The final for WI24 was inperson. Most of the questions were from the quizzes and midterms, not rly the note examples. You get one, double sided cheat sheet. The midterms were online, so if u got good midterm scores, u can bomb the final and still pass with at least a B-.

His exams get difficult but his notes are very organized compared to the other profs. When I took it, the midterm and final were online, but after the fall quarter, the final became inperson for the next 10A class. The hw does help with understanding the basic concepts but IMO they didn't help that much for the exams. He has rare but funny jokes.

This class  has a lot of true or false questions that come out of absolute nowhere. You have 3 online midterm exams and an in person final. The midterms were a lot more difficult and not relevant to the type of examples seen in lecture. The final exam was more fair. You were given a cheat sheet but no calculator.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures would have been better if he didn't spend most of the time overexplaining proofs and theorems. Would only get through 1-2 examples in lecture which made the HW much harder to do. Test material was way more complicated than taught in lecture. Mostly ture/false questions that were super conceptual. Okay prof but very frustrating class
