He is a very nice professor. He post notes on TritonEd and has podcasts. The notes are very clear and easy to understand. They have definitions and examples that make you understand how to solve the problems. Homework every week has about 4 to 5 questions and exams are similar to the homework.

The exams are more difficult than lecture and homework. The lecture is boring and most of the time the professor reads off the powerpoint. Highly recommend taking a different professor. Lecture notes are useless and you can just read the book. Highly recommend reading the section before class if you want to get an A. Also there is no curve.

Aghajani is very passionate about statistics and that is seen in his lectures. Tests are straightforward and fair, and as long as you understand the homework the tests shouldn't be too bad. This class will increase in difficulty after the 1st midterm so get help early on. Office hours and SI are super helpful.

He is very hard to understand during lectures, especially because he gets sidetracked easily when explaining problems. Also, he sometimes forgets key points when explaining concepts. This class was easy for me because I've taken calc before, but for a first time calc student I feel his teaching style would make it a very difficult class to pass.
He cares about his students. However, his lectures are hard to understand. Attendance is optional. In preparation for the exams, I read the textbook re-did the homework.
He is a new professor, but compared to all other new professors I have had in the last year, he is easily the best out of all of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's awesome but you better be able to explain all the theories or you aren't gonna do too well. Tests are extra long, but the examples you give will stick cause he's effective.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Craig is an awesome teacher. Being a reletively involved student, he loved to laugh with us when we'd joke about course content and loves making funny examples to help us understand logic topics better. While being a serious teacher, Craig is always willing to help and really loves his subject, as well as knowing it like the back of his hand.

The class was difficult, yet entertaining. Since it was a small class he was able to give individual feedback to each student. His comments could have been more constructive, though. He places a great deal of emphasis on originality and being able to present. It is definitely not simple to get an A in his class; he will make you work for it.

First tests are the most difficult but it gets easier from there. READ the chapters before hand that way you have some background but it is not completely necessary. If you have questions he will be there for you and will accommodate. Would definitely take again!
makes class fun and interesting. not too much homework. well prepared for tests
Wonderful professor. Really cares for his student's understanding. Would definitely take him again. Opened my eyes to subjects that I would have otherwise ignored. Extremely intelligent man.
Professor Agule cares about his students. He is very encouraging and supporting. His tests are little tricky but in a reasonable range.

Dr. Al Ajrawi teaching at SDSU and I'm her student.
I asked her about this class and she wasn't the professor for this class, she was facilitating the class for once in 2021.
The last feedback is fake and a big lie.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: All the 5/5 ratings below are fake reviews, IGNORE them. I actually took the class and this prof completely slacked off the whole summer session. Reused the same syllabus and lecture slides from other ece 15 profs, and lecture recordings were posted weeks later than they should have been posted.
Dr. Al Ajrawi has been a great teacher, lecturer, and a Professor to me, and I fully enjoyed her lectures, she explained everything in detail and it made it easier for me to understand
I wish all the Professors are as articulated, intelligent and resourceful as Dr. Al Ajrawi. Her lectures are precise, concise and detailed.

Being an international student and also being one who left the school system many years after my first degree, I was too scared on how I was going to cope with the BS at UCSD, but your lecturing strategies and encouraging words to students have built that confidence in me. You are a source of inspiration to many.

Dr. Al Ajrawi's teaching method is the best because students are actively involved in the discussion and discussions are always lively and to the point.. Shenever distant herself from the students, even the shyest student participate in critical discussion. I consider myself very fortunate to have a full package to have a professor like you.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I just want to express my gratitude for her invaluable guidance, encouragement and most especially for devoting a substantial time for me during the time of my project. She has always been a listening lecturer, she is a rare gem! Please, keep up the good work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Al Ajrawi really a very good professor. You may think that I'm flattering her. No I'm not. Shall I tell you why I'm saying that she is a very good teacher? If you check my module results, you'll see I've got distinction mark only in her class, the module she taught us. I really miss her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is the best lecturer I have ever come across. I thank her very much and will always remember Dr. Al Ajrawi. Her motivational skill as a lecturer is one to reckon with and note worthy of.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is a message to say the biggest thank you for your recomendation and also for all your assistance during the duration of my programme. Saying you are the best lecturer that ever taught me might actually be an understatement. I so much believe that all Ive learnt from you will surely be beneficial as I continue to the next face of my career.

- Lectures are not on schedule and occasionally illegible (first week lectures were literally just static) - Professor doesnt follow syllabus and is unpredictable (almost changed the entire curve and grading system for summer course) - Unresponsive and doesnt answer emails - Used a final from 2018 but didnt provide required material

idk why the sdsu ratings are so high, professor went afk for the course. Slow response times, can only contact by text, lectures full of static, assignment due dates shifted without warning. Entire week of course content cut for no clear reason. Final exam recycled with obvious typos in the code. Most disorganized class I have taken in my life

He's the reason why I'm not doing linguistics anymore, hope this helps ❤️ Real review: he teaches the class as if you have had prior syntax knowledge. He also refuses to have video for his podcast when all the work he does is visual despite SO many students asking him to post a video recording.

This class was sooooo hard! I only passed with a C because I collaborated with 2 other people when doing homework and quizzes. He's a very nice professor BUT he moves on soooooo quickly bc you're expected to be an expert. You'll finally understand something and then bam, new topic already. FYI, this is nothing like what you learned in LIGN 101.

The class is very hard, the professor likes to move on very quick despite many of us still not understanding the material. Although office hours are available sometimes it doesn't help as he still expects you to have already understood the material. He's very kind but the material is very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Alex is super sweet but the class is very hard. There's a lot of content & the class would go pretty fast, sometimes he would stop to ask if we had questions but I hadn't even absorbed enough info to be able to ask one; I'd have to review the materials later. Going to his office hours helped a lot especially with the hw

Alex is great but this class is really really reaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaally difficult. Incredibly difficult. I would not take this class unless you're a ling major. My only critique of the prof is that the jump from 101 to 121 is huge and I feel like he thinks we know more about linguistics than we actually do. His lectures move fast so pay attention. gl.

This guy is the messiah for discrete mathematics. He taught me how to LaTeX as well as prove things through direct, contradiction, contraposition (he likes contraposition), counterexample, and all inductions. This course is basically all about proofs and he does a fair job explaining it.  Side note, this class is really similar to Math 109.
He's a young professor. The class was really confusing because he was not clear at all, mostly because he seemed nervous. On the other side he is really handsome.

The professor is so cute. The class material is tough though. But if you attend every class and do the homework I am sure you can get an A. The homework problem are easy and discussion session is really helpful. The professor really care about our study and answer every questions carefully. The textbook is helpful. Highly recommend him!
i luv micky my king becoz he made everything so easy and accessible and he knows his stuff.

Liked the professor, but the course was disorganized. Several classes were canceled and replaced with old videos that didn't always match. Dense material, tangents, and skipped topics appeared on exams. Final project was last minute and unclear; grades weren't shared.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I personally wouldn't take him again. The quizzes, midterms, and finals are harder than you think. Although they are open book and online, which is truly a lifesaver, it was still a headache to take. There's just so much memorization and information packed in that I barely even remember what was being taught.
He's an interesting lecturer. Explains things well though he does stutter at times - but it's usually because he's thinking and trying to make the points clearer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: amazing prof, amazing lectures. clearly cares about his students and made the class so interesting. the discussions were fun and insightful and there were lots of examples

Really boring class, and professor would not follow the slides, rather he would go off on tangents/get in discussions with students. Topic was uninteresting and quite hard to understand, especially at first, but ultimately it wasn't too difficult to score well if you did the reading, since the exams were open book.

Everything was so boring and he is also super duper boring but it's an easy A class but I was soooooooooo bored tbh, played fireboy and water girl during class but def take this class with him. Online exams. Be ready to get shushed. 
love u Micky

This professor will often go on rants outside the scope of the class and then rush through the slides with the important info. During discussion sections, TA's seem to not know as they can hardly reason with / understand the professor. Cogs 100 with this teacher is a philosophy class disguised as science.Boring lectures, and boring reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He definitely cares about his students and makes sure we get extra credit to pass the class. Only 1midterm, reading quizzes,perusall,and an assignment. He made the class so interesting and I really enjoyed learning about this different side of COGSCI. He gives so many examples during lecture to help us understand and actively communicates with us.

Agler's lectures are always fast- paced, and mostly repetitive with the textbook, but his explanations are helpful towards understanding the material. He is funny, has patience in explaining stuff, and gives generous curves. Homework based on correctness, hard quizzes; midterm and final are not as hard.
He is pretty laid back, but he is really messy with his use of the board. I liked his attitude but sometimes he seemed too informal.  In overall a good teacher.

I recommend him very much. Provided his own mini-"textbook" for the class which only cost $30 at the student reserves center. So even if you missed a concept in lecture, the textbook is all in his own writing. He's a pretty good lecturer too, and very helpful and approachable in office hours. Exams were very reflective of the material.

I thought his midterms were a bit hard since it was all concept based. Though the curve was crazy which I guessed helped everyone. I never attended his lectures cause as long as you did the hw and understood the material you're fine. Final was very similar to the midterms and practice final so that was an easy A.

His class was super hard and the midterms were hard. The averages were not great but he is not a bad professor. His teaching style is very different and he tries to make examples but ends up failing at it. His class is curved but if I were you, take another prof. Also use the book extensively!

Professor Agler understands the material, but does not always present it in the  clearest way. Midterms were REALLY hard because the level of difficulty was unexpected but the final was easy. Maybe the curve helps. If you're not interested in math or learning most everything on your own, I'd go with another professor.

He's not a good lecturer at all so I never went to class. Though his sample midterms and final are generally easier than his actual ones. This quarter, the average for his midterms were 40% and 56% ish which is pretty low even though the tests weren't hard but he ends up curving the grades at the end. His final looked exactly like the sample one.

Agler likes to describe the power behind the formulas, but does not always teach them well.  Usually late to class and wastes some time going off on tangents.  Practice midterms are not representative of actual midterms.  Midterms were hard.  40% was the average score on the first one.  No cheat sheets on the midterms.  Nice guy, though.

Had him in Winter 2009. His lectures were boring, couldn't stay awake in any of his lectures, probably because it was at 8am. He is very disorganized too and if you sit near the back of the lecture hall, you can barely hear him. However, his midterms and final were easy. I got an B on first midterm, A+ on the second one, and an A- on the final.
Great professor, take him if you get a chance.

TAKE HIM; your grade will thank you. His midterms and finals were completely straightforward; his final was almost exactly like his midterm problems. Yes, he mumbles, but his lectures/review sessions help narrow down what will be tested on. He also has a generous curve..
Math 20C. Always so hard to hear so sit in the front. Avoid taking if possible.

was hard to hear in center 101 so sit within the first couple rows... his final was hard and more complex than any of his midterms! also he ditched the last day of class and showed up an hour late to the final review session. overall ok teacher but would recommend a more thorough math professor if you suck at math

Professor Agler is the best math teacher I have ever had. He not only makes the mechanics behind concepts completely clear, he explains the power of the ideas being taught. Midterms and Final were completely straight forward and fair, but test concepts not just computations. Highly recommend.

Agler is really into his math business, but he mumbles and is disorganized. We didn't get a class syllabus until about week 4. The one time I asked him for help, he spoke to me in a condescending manner. I found his class difficult; Study, read the book, do all your homework, and you should be okay.
Do not take this class. Unorganized, hard to hear, does not do example problems in class, and assigns homework problems that do not show up on midterms nor the final. Take a different class!
He's awesome! He makes lame jokes that makes funny...(if that makes sense) He explains things well and gives reasonable exams. Check out his outfit ;)

Difficult to understand and take notes with. Disorganized and does not have a website. Could be a bit condescending. Not sure if he stayed for the entire final exam. Exams were fair. Does not drop a midterm (as most of the math dept does).
he's good

When I took this professor for the first time in 142A, I honestly didn't think much of him.  But after that quarter, I decided to take him again for 142B.  And then, 120B as well.Why?He's probably the best math professor I've ever had (this speaking from a math major).  Yes, he's extmly unorganized, but he teaches well, and gives you a C for effort

I found that Agler was not only very disorganized (in his thought process/lectures) but it seemed like he didn't care about his students or teaching.  I'm pretty into math, and this guy made it difficult to enjoy (but screw calculus anyway).  I thought his jokes were condescending.  I definitely think he's overrated.

His tests are really fair, similar to the homework. If you're really aware of the material or you read before his lecture then you'll understand what he is saying. If not, it'll probably go over your head but you can just read the book. He does review sessions before each midterm which really helps you narrow down the type of questions he'll ask.

He knows the subjects really well... however, really hard to have office hrs with him since he is never on campus for help. his midterm is extremely difficult. the final, he gives us what will be on the test and what to study. overall, he is a really good professor.
This class was so hard. And I took Calc for two years in high school! He doesn't explain the material so well, but the curve evens things out.
I actually liked math before I took Agler. He likes to talk off-topic and his explanations were lacking.

He's a good lecturer. Relatively easy midterms and final. Not too organized. Overall decent professor. Only problem with him is that it is impossible to know your grade until you recieve the final score. But his grading scale doesnt seem to hard.
He's pretty unorganized. Teaches all over the place.  Very hard to follow.  His midterms were alright...but the final was kinda crazy!  Wouldn't really suggest him.
he doesn't seem to care about the students at all

He's super laid-back.  Doesn't always have the greatest idea of what's going on in class, but he's totally cool!!!  I like that he talks about his family a lot because it shows he actually does something besides research...  like every other prof at the school!
He's interesting....wears the same shorts with chalk on them, tie-dye shirt and crocodile hunter hat every day. But he's super cool and mind opening.

Hard take-home midterm and less difficult in-class final. Lectures were clear and he was prepared. Likes to go over the time limit, though. Unfortunately, grades seemed to come down to how hard the TA's graded hw. Got a B first quarter with easy grader and C with Jiri, he was an ass. -_-

He doesn't give out a syllabus, he pops in a take home midterm 8th week of class which is extremely difficult, his speech is not very clear as he tends to mumble to the board at times, he has very little office hours, but he does not give out grades lower than a C-.

He is a little TOO knowledgeable in math. He likes it so much that he will go off on a tangent. But overall, sweet guy, he's patient and will explain many times. Really cares. Class is difficult but is do-able if you study homework, examples, and notes.

Seems to have ADHD and is unable to focus on the subject matter. Skips to a different problem while still in the process of explaining another. Didn't give out a syllabus on the first day; that's how disorganized and unprofessional he is. Grading policies on homework and curving on exams are unclear

This is one funny guy. He explains his notes very well and if you have any questions he would be more than happy to explain enough times until you understand him. In order to do well on his exams, you must study and know how to do every problem he has assigned for homework. I enjoyed his lectures.

He has a very "catch me if you can" sort of philosophy on office hours. Not helpful. If you pop in your math cd it does all the same examples he does in class, only you can rewind a cd. He also hates partial credit. You better be freakin awesome at memorizing all your trig. substitutions, etc.

Agler's a great teacher.  Not only is he down to earth and quirky in his own way, but he's a clear and understandable lecturer.  His tests are very reflective of what he goes over in class.  He doesn't really have OH's, so going to the TA's OH's helps a lot.  STUDY WHAT HE TELLS YOU TO STUDY!

Assigns homework and teaches solely on examples.  His midterms are a reflection of his examples in class, so take notes!!  Sometimes he assumes his students know too much so he will skip some parts in the book that the students have to be accountable for.  Overall though, highly recommended.
Tough

I thought he was a complete jerk.  He was not nearly as willing to help his students as any other professor.  Definitely would avoid him.  If you are a serious student, his office hours at the coffee shop are a turn-off.  Doesn't explain, and doesn't review.  Good luck.
i think hes very good. knows his stuff

Had him in 1998 for partial differential equations.  The most real, personable prof I had at UCSD.  Took our entire class out for coffee and discussion on what to do with a math degree.  Cares about teaching and people, and really knows his stuff.
Get ready for the monotone voice of Agler. He clarifies details too much and it is not important for test purposes.  Go to OASIS.

Don't let his appearance fool you, he's a good professor, who makes the concepts clear and easy to understand. I don't know why people don't want to go to lecture, because if you do, it's usually not necessary to read the book.
Really Good Professor!  Highly Intelligent and very helpful during office hours.  Tests are hard if you don't study do homework problems and you will do very well!!

teaches on theory, but provides enough examples.  goes over everything you need to know before the tests, which are very similar to homework problems, but you do have to go to lecture to get the homework assignments, which are collected and graded.

teaches soley by example... midterms and final do not reflect the problems assigned for hw.. so they are super hard.... he has a grudge against computers so if u dont go to class youre screwed.. he likes to say "ball of wax"  and "youre doo

He makes mistakes while lecturing and students have to correct him often. There is no course website or syllabus with the homework so you have to go to ALL classes. He seems to be an easy going guy but it's sometimes difficult to understand his class.

first of all you have to get hw in class...he doesn't believe in computers. he's so boring and tlks to students as if we are preschoolers. he makes the concepts more difficult than they have to be. do not choose this prof.
actually makes things understandable

Agler is a great math teacher, he really explains the material well! Material gets harder as quarter progresses, don't slack off. Exams were representative of homework, very fair teacher, only a couple total exam questions were tricky.

This Class can be difficult if you slack off, but i still think he is one of the best math teacher's i've ever had. He is always sure to point out the conceptual side of math, rather then make the class memorize formulas; which i find very important.

The best math professor at ucsd.  He had a strong command of the material and was so good at teaching it that an elementary school kid probably could've learned it.  Tests and homework were not outrageous and representative of the class and lecture.

This guy is a sage.  Although he has difficulty remembering who the students are, he is one of the brightest, most caring, and innovative teachers UCSD has ever had.  I learned more in this class than I did in all my other math classes combined.
Excellent professor.  Explains material the most clearly out of all math professors in my opinion
this guy is bull****.  well then again are all of the math professors at ucsd.  damn u guys are screwed if u take him. hahahhaha

Peole who liked this guy are all loser idiot nerds. stereotypical UCSD students.  Yeah he's smart, but he stands up there and mumble's and talks about math as if its sesame street.  Basically if you want a challenge, take him, otherwise, don't.
For good. He's lectures are very helpful and easy to follow most of the time. Midterms and final are challenging. Just need to study and you'll live
Lectures are interesting, clear and helpful with good examples. Challenging exams, but doable if you're prepared. Very good professor overall.
Overall very good, one of the more personable professors I've had.
Clear, organized, methodical teaching.  Soft spoken.  Funny.
She is condensending, easy class but she can be moody.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This professor really cares about the improvement of her students in this class. She gave personalized advice to each student and everyone seemed to become greate public speakers by the end of the quarter. She also offers career coaching to her students, such as internship interview advice, outside of the class during her office hours.

Don't listen to all the bad reviews. Yes, she discourages using devices in class, but if you are engaged, she won't care. Sometimes the rate my professor reviews are spot on, in this case, i dont think so, their is probably some credence to others' experience, but if you need this class for a credit, take it!

Take McKay. Her class is way easier and there is no group project to sabotage your grade. Meyer was nice to me, but I would like to think it was because I participated. She was a bit odd, but also nice and caring. She asked all of the students who stayed after the final to get coffee with her, she is better than the reviews make her seem.

MGT 119:super disorganized since she taught this class for the first time as an undergraduate rather than graduate course, can be rude and impatient with students, can be a pretty harsh grader when the assignments we're given aren't even fully clear in deadline, rubric, or point of them in terms of the class--  but the people in the class are great

She's emotionally volatile. Don't talk to her if she's in a bad mood (you'll be able to tell very easily). I haven't heard of a good office hours experience with her. Class holistically isn't hard, BUT she's very strict about very particular things (no devices, sentence count). Write the max amount the rubric asks, and over-explain every answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Don't take her! The content is easy but she makes it harder on purpose. Participation is graded but hardly to get a chance to speak in class, and still can not get full points even if answered questions multiple times. TA grades hw harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: No-device policy in her class which is a 3-hour lecture. Shows a pretty strong dislike towards Asians - I was singled out for having my phone under the desk (I sat in the back row), other people in the front were never called out. Yelled and embarrassed an Asian international student too, it was disgusting how she spoke to her in front of everyone

can be a little intimidating and unwelcoming despite preaching it in a leadership class. she was very demeaning towards a girl who was on her phone and yelled at her in front of the class. midterm is written, just go over important concepts and you'll be fine. final is take home. shes not as bad as the reviews make it seem, but still be wary

Has a no-device policy but people would still be on their computers. However, she would single out those she wanted to and would embarrass them. TA'S graded harder than the actual professor and deducted points for the dumbest reasons. Written midterm, even though for a class like this multiple choice would be better. Unnecessary group project!

3 hour lecture goes by quick - she gives two 10 min breaks. Get on her good side and participate or else she'll dislike you. High key micro aggresses on International students. Midterm was easy and final was online. Stickler for points, do everything exactly according to rubric. Teaches basic leadership material but overall I gained some valuable

Take this class if you're okay with getting a B. But if you're like me and aiming for an A, you'll find it very stressful. The professor and her TAs grade exams and even homework harshly. The material is just common sense, so she seems to find weird reasons to lower grades and works hard to keep the class average at a B.

Professor Meyer has some good advice and experiences, but she can sometimes be rude and condescending to students. The class content is easy to learn as a lot of it is just common sense. Though, participation in class is hard because she calls on the same 5 people every lecture.

The class is easy with 2 midterms, a final project, and a group project. The content of the class is easy to understand but you just need to be able to explain it well. The final was just a take home project which was somewhat easy. The group project is just a presentation. Only thing about this teacher is she is extremely rude. Take with caution.
Try and avoid if possible. Class is easy but pretty much one of my least favorite teachers I've had. If you want a nice teacher who cares about you, avoid this teacher.

Such a rude teacher. Content is easy, the way she grades though makes it very difficult. Group project was also super easy. She makes participation part of the grade but only calls on the same people over and over. Try and get on her good side otherwise she will be so condescending and rude.

Meyer is an alright teacher. Can come off as nice if she likes you, otherwise she can be very rude. Honestly her class is pretty useless as she doesn't really go over anything I can't just look up. Easy class as the assignments are easy and so are the presentation and midterms. Final was online for us.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Don't take this professor. It's not worth the headache of 3 hour classes and being graded so harshly for no reason. On the midterm I had questions marked wrong for not writing 3 "complete" sentences, even though my answer was confirmed correct by the TAs.

The content of this class is super easy but this professor made it unnecessarily difficult. Her class average for midterms is a low B due to "vague" descriptions even if you've answered the question correctly. She's rude and snaps at students. She does not seem to care for her students to succeed or learn. I wouldn't recommend.

I came into this class thinking I would love it... I didn't. Because the content of this class is common sense, Professor Meyer decided to make the grading unnecessarily difficult, and unexplainable when asked about it. She calls on the same students repeatedly, rarely giving other students an opportunity. Snaps at students and passive aggressive.
Cracks of her real personality show when she subtly puts down TAs, is condescending, and snaps at students but never to the point that its super obvious.

Participation in class was needed for credit but she picked the same students to answer questions and ignored others.  Said going to her office hours could be an alternative way to gain participation points but she was not present.  The class was made more difficult than needed by the professor and one of the TAs while others got the easier TA.

She was inaccessible after class.The requirement for class participation is to answer questions twice for full credit, but she called on the same students repeatedly, while others were rarely given the opportunity to participate despite raising our hands. The course was unnecessarily complicated and she made grading extremely unfair and messy.

Prof was rude to students throughout the quarter and would embarrass them in class. Class content is super simple and mostly common sense, however grading criteria was very unclear. This was especially clear in the final project where she graded based on criteria not even listed on the project rubric.

This woman drove me insane, she treats the lectures like they're life or death but the content itself is just common sense. Most Rady classes are super easy, and while this is no exception, 3 hours of Meyer made me consider dropping out altogether. In-class quiz every week, rude to TA's, condescending, unaccessible after class, mean jokes

Good professor. Nice but also strict. Not a hard class tho. Show up and listen and you'll be good. Definitely take it with her. midterm1=10% midterm2=15% both in person. final=10%online. homework journals=28%. team project/in class presentation(everyone in group had to present)=20%. discussion boards=10%. Attendance/tracked participation=5%.

I got a LOT out of this class, I found the readings and class discussions very interesting. But the class is very easy, assessments are easy too (I made a playlist for the final exam). You do have a big group project that's worth a bit of your grade, but it's a fun class overall and very low-stress.
Best Professor Ever! She's very supportive of her students and actually wants them to do well! Follow the study guide for the midterm.

Prof. Meyer is invested in your growth. If you go to her Office Hours and come with questions about how to grow professionally, then she will give you honest and genuine advice. The class has weekly journal entries, a group project, midterm, and a final project. The journals, group and final project are graded on effort!!

(+): Engaging and relevant readings and lectures, journal entry assignments are graded based on effort, can choose your group project members, exams are based on lecture slides, caring, will help you with interviews. (-): A bit disorganized at times during lectures!

She only gives examples using NH3 and water, then hw is harder. Exams were multiple choice, but results in no extra credit (which can really cost you). Homework is worth 1/3 of your grade, which is as much as the final exam. No room for error. Class avg GPA was a 2.65, she's not afraid to fail students. 30% of the class got an A minus or better.

Insanely organized lectures slides and discussions, every lecture seems to be planned down the minute. Inorganic chemistry as a subject is not easy but Dr. Schimpf does her best to simplify tough concepts. Her slides are the most organized I've seen and you can understand most concepts covered in class just by reviewing the slide. My goat.

I really enjoyed Prof Schimpf's class! She is very approachable and will happily answer any questions during lecture and in office hours. The exams feel fair, and she is very clear about what will be tested. The homework and practice exam problems are pretty good preparation for tests, and she goes through practice problems in lecture.

Professor Schimpf gives good lectures with helpful explanations and lots of examples. The older reviews aren't, in my opinion, a good representation of her teaching now because I found that she was very organized, knowledgeable, and answered questions in a helpful and encouraging way.

Worst teacher I've ever had. Uses another Prof's slides and I swear she reads them for the first time when she reads them out loud in her first lecture. Literally knows nothing about the material. Students ask basic questions during lectures that she can't answer. She does not know the material. Not enough space to rant abt more

Very fast when lecturing. The pace and questions she lectured assumed the topics were immediately understood after being taught. Knowledge checks asked questions not always covered in lecture and were worth a lot grading wise. 

There was no curve on the final or final grading scale. 
2.37 class GPA for my section

Schimpf is a really nice professor; her lectures are generally really clear and direct. Textbook not really necessary unless she fumbles a concept around for a bit. Tests were fairly long, but primarily multiple choice and easy. Discussions weren't too necessary, but it is kinda graded. Honestly easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: By taking her class, you can tell she truly cares about her students and their understanding of the material. Her lectures are clear and easy to understand and she gives examples to help students learn. Of all chem professors, I honestly think her exams are the easiest: Multiple Choice w/ one page short answer. Loved her!

Definitely take professor Schimpf! Lectures are clear, reasonable amount of hw, gives extra credit and tests are extremely fair (just like studyguide and clicker questions, have a small amount of extra credit, getting a 100% is definitely doable). I just showed up and paid attention in class, studied a bit before exams and got an A very easily.

A lot of work but I really liked the lectures and prof was really excited about chemistry. Clicker questions and discussion board and section count for the grade. Tests were fair. Gave good chances for extra credit.
Chem is hard but prof Schimpf if fair. clicker questions make sure you are following in lecture. they count for your grade but are not that hard. worst part is the class is too big
I didn't really think I would like chemistry but prof made it fun. One of the best profs I've had in any class at UCSD

Professor Schimpf is a great lecturer! I came into this class knowing nothing about chem but she's taught me a lot. Her lectures are very clear & easy to understand & she constantly asks if anyone has questions. Her exams are very easy. The only downside is that she asks a lot of clicker questions (easy) which made attendance mandatory.
chem is soo hard but Prof. Schimpf is very helpful and accessible and makes chem a little more enjoyable with her enthusiasm
explains the material in a way that is easy to understand. fair tests.

Really interactive lectures with clicker questions to make sure you are grasping the materials. Class moves fast but I think that happens in all chem classes. She is very easy to talk to and goes out of her way to answer everyone's questions.
tests were fair and we had lots of practice problems to prepare. more fun than some profs ive had
Her homework and example problems class are true to the test so pay attention in lecture!

Although she was very iClicker heavy, I believe it helped me understand the concepts she was teaching during class. She is not the best at grabbing your attention, but she is very nice and eager to help. She stresses that although chemistry is very math based, but she wants her students to know the chemistry behind all the math. Fair tests.

Very sweet and accessible. A lot of students would talk while she talks, had a hard time grasping students attention. iClicker heavy, took away from the lecture. First midterm and final were fair, second midterm was eh. Doesn't curve til the end. Discussions were a joke, often we didn't learn the material before. TAs incompetent except David.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: It was her first time teaching but she did a good job given her inexperience. Reading the textbook was recommended for homework. Her lectures weren't that engaging. Discussions were mandatory and not worth the time, if I'm honest. Her midterms were okay and the final was fair. She was always available outside of class and was eager to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Very inspirational man.
One of the best lecturers I have ever had. Amazing problem sets. Hard class!
good professor, and nice

If you go to lecture you will succeed in his class. I took this class in WI22 when the first portion of the class was online, but the final was in person. The content of 20C itself is not the easiest, the final was surprisingly calming compared to what I would have expected for the rigor. Very sweet and kind professor, and great at explaining math.

He is probably one of my favorite calculus professors who always explains things clearly. His lectures are inspirational and explain the concepts so well. Besides the lectures, I love how his class notes are clearly written and posted on canvas. Should be an easy A if not skipping lectures. And do go to office hours.

The prof is super good at teaching math! He always takes his time to answer everyone's questions and make the content really clear. His office hours are also super useful. Discussion sections require only 6/10 of the sections but were not as useful. Overall, really good for any math course.

Professor Golsefidy is a GOAT math professor. During lectures, professor Golsefidy explain everything very clearly. He definitely takes the time to make sure his students understand the course content. He's always happy to answer any questions. He also goes through everything step-by-step. Overall, a super nice and caring math professor.

Super refreshing after careless math Prof last quarter. Made things very clear. He always made it a priority that students are engaged and understanding.  Homework and quizzes were easy, class got slightly more difficult towards the end of the quarter but it was just a matter of the material. Great Prof, super nice!

Professor Golsefidy was an honor to have. He gives straightforward lectures and treats his students with extreme kindness.His quizzes and final are fair if you stay on top of the class, which isn’t hard to do with just his lectures and homework.His office hours is extremely helpful as well.This guy is a genius and it shows during lectures.

Thought he was nice since he had a 4.2/5 rating, then turned out to be the most difficult class I ever had. No examples in lecture at all and needs students to do incredibly hard homework and quiz. Quiz avg is 21/30(1st), 15/30(2nd), 15/30( 3rd). So tired of him

He is not accessible outside of the class. No reply to the email. Summer class is fast-paced and he mentioned our first exam will be heavily based on the week-1 HW which is due on Sunday. It is already Tuesday good sir, where are my HW1 solutions? We are having a test worthy of 20% of the grades tmr!!!

Highly recommend this professor. In fact, I took his 100A and I waited a full year just to take his 100B. Well, I did not know for sure that he will teach 100B ever but I guess I gambled and won. It seems like I am hitting a word limit so long story short, he is the perfect teacher you could ask for, who not only teaches why but also "why cares".
Love the man, awesome professor. Lectures are amazing. Tests are a little hard, but fair. go to lecture, he teaches in a really patient and well structured manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: He is such an amazing professor and highly recommended
Top notch professor in the field of mathematics. Rare gem.

All the ppl that gave this guy bad reviews are trippin. 103B is a hard class to understand in general, but he does his best to make everything as clear as possible. HW is avg 6 problems/wk and he gives you all the tools u need for tests and HW during lectures. Tests are no surprise, straight from lecture and HW, as it should be. I'd take him aagain

At the time of the final, we were literally 1.5 months ahead of the other class. Expect to walk out of every lecture with 5-6 new pages of notes, full of abstract dense proofs. Professor golsefidy is a nice guy, but the amount of workload for this class seems to be on par with graduate classes. Had to drop another class just to pass this one, tough
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He assigned too much homework and the lectures were confusing since they're long. The tests do not reflect the lectures nor the homework he assigned so expect the average is very low. I suggest finding another professor because this class requires too much work. This class is much more difficult than graduate level Math 100. Please CURVE THE CLASS!
Impossible to follow his lectures. The only way to learn the class is not to attend the lecture and learn by yourself with the given lecture notes and the textbook.

I'm willing to learn something from Prof. Salehi, I had to say for someone the course may not be easy, but for majority, fair Final, mid-terms and light homework requirements provide us a lot opportunity to work on other courses.
Good clear lectures and fair exams. Recommended

Prof. Alireza is by far the best professor i have ever had! He cares about students and is very approachable. His lecture and materials are AMAZINGLY easy to understand. His exams are reasonably easy/hard depends on the way you look at it, but they are all very straight forward and no tricks are involved.

Professor Golsefidy is a great teacher.  Lectures are easy to keep up with and to understand. Has weekly homework, easy points.  His exams are fair, and are based on in class examples and lecture notes as opposed to homework problems from the book.  Really enjoyed his class, and wish I could take him for every math class! He's great.

Professor Salehi-Golsefidy is a really good professor overall. His lectures are extremely clear and easy to understand, and he really cares about his students. His website is extremely helpful. He posts all lecture notes, homework assignments, and test and other helpful info on it. You'll have to study hard but it is possible to get an A.

His lecture is clear and his online notes help a lot. The first mid is normal and the second is really easy. I don't know about what the final will be but we got a lot of practice exams on his website so we can got enough exercises. Anyway he is a nice teacher and his office hour is helpful, too.
honestly i wasn't sure for being in hos class; but he is one of my best math professors in UCSD so far. grade teacher. he teaches very clearly, and care about the students.

His notes are wonderful. His lectures are good, but in my opinion they're overrated. He's EXTREMELY nice. One grader graded 400 people's homework, so hopefully he'll change that because getting homework back never really happened. His grading scheme is very flexible, which is nice.

Brilliant and caring professor. He is extremely well-prepared and clear in explaining as he goes through each example. His exams are fairly straightforward and reasonable, but you must study and understand the material thoroughly to do well in this class. He allows for a cheat sheet for every test, but no calculator. Take him! You won't regret it.

Such a good professor that I don't need to study extra hard and get an A+. He's funny. Well sometimes I feel sleepy in lectures because he tried to make everything very clear and solved examples really really slow to make sure everyone understand. But overall great professor! Good grader! Btw he draws 3D graphs so well which is really amazing...

He's so well prepared, knowledgable, has an adorable sense of humor, and really cares that his students learn. GO TO CLASS, copy down all his examples because he pulls exam questions straight from his lectures. His exams are not easy, but are straightforward. Be diligent about learning: do and UNDERSTAND the practice exams, go to office hours, etc.
Great lecturer, but went off on tangents on how to derive the formulas. His tests got ridiculously harder throughout the course.

Really good lecturer, sometimes will go off on tangents about how formulas are derived. The practice exams he posts are most helpful for his exams. Attendance isn't mandatory to do well in this class bc he posts all his lecture notes, but it certainly helps. If you fail a midterm, don't worry because you can drop one, but your final will be 60%.
Nice class, nice professor. He will show a lot of examples in class to make you easy to understand the theory. By the way, he is really cute.

He's a great lecturer and amazing at drawing 3D stuff. His tests got harder throughout the course but that's because probably too many people got A's in the first one. Overall good. I'd take him again.

Didn't like him at first, but by the end of the quarter I loved him. Writes notes on the board at a good pace with impeccable handwriting and stops to answer any questions. Has an accent that takes getting used to, but only serves to make him sound like even more of a math genius.

An awesome lecturer, he takes his time to make sure class understands before moving on. Rewrites all his course notes online for review, and provides at least 3 practice exams per test. His graphs are awesome! The class is tough at times, so his office hours are valuable for understanding the material.
Awesome professor in every aspects specially his summarized lecture note will help you gather all you have studied at last minutes before exam.

This professor was amazing. His handwriting is great, he explains everything that he says, he smiles and tells when we have questions, and more importantly, he only teaches the most important material and does it without any notes in front of him. This man is truly a genius. Highly recommend.

This professor is great! One of the best math teachers I've had in a subtle way. It wasn't until the end of the quarter where I found out all the practice test answers as well as the weekly lecture notes were all done by him. What professor does that? So. Good. Anyways, do the practice tests, they help TREMENDOUSLY. Average study time per week:3-5

Such a great professor and encourages questions in class. Has an accent but he is easy to understand and can draw 3D like no other. Voluntarily puts up summaries of his lecture notes each week, uploads prac. midterm/finals and gives step by step solutions. His TA Brian Longo is great.

This professor is awesome in every way!  He teaches very well, doesn't make the tests hard with no purpose and tests based on conceptual understanding to make sure we understand the topics. He is very friendly in office hours and once stayed an hour over to explain something to me. Also has weekly note summaries that are very useful!!

First midterm was very easy and second midterm made up for it. He teaches well and although he has an accent, he is easily understandable. 20C is a multivariable calculus class and many concepts are in 3D. He is able to draw 3D graphs like no one I've ever seen and it makes the concepts easier to grasp.

Good professor, his TA Brian Longo was also very good. I wish he was a little faster in teaching (we were behind the other classes up until the last two weeks). He has an accent but his voice is very clear so its not a problem. Also, his handwriting is very neat and his graphs are almost like they are printed.
Good professor. Makes you work hard, but you end up learning a lot of mathematics.

Lectures are hard to follow because he doesnt give many concrete examples of the abstractions laid out in class. Homework is near impossible without the help of the TAs. This class is WAY harder than it needs to be. Plan to spend about 20 hours a week on homework.

The homeowork (50% of grade) and midterm (take home) are IMPOSSIBLE without the TA pretty much showing us everything. Other 109 classes (look at old websites) are far easier. WARNING! Be prepared to know/memorize EVERYTHING he writes in class and homework he gives.

more often than not, the examples and proofs he does during lecture are straight out of the book. he also tends to get distracted during lecture and talk about random things... the grades are pretty lenient though-- 50% of your grade is based on hmwk!
Great professor, explained things very clearly and understandably. Transparent when it comes to test material and helps students succeed.
Straightforward in what she wants and expects. EC is very free. Gives a lot of practice. Be ready to memorize though, but she gives plenty of practice and review every test.

The professor is so sweet and a great lecturer. She made the class very interesting and easy to understand. There are biweekly homework assignments (for completion) and quizzes that were very fair. The final was cumulative, and she offers a lot of extra credit. I don't recommend buying the textbook because her tests are based on her lectures.

best biochem prof. Lectures are engaging, exams are memorization-based but she clearly outlines what you need to know, they are exactly like the practice material, and there are many extra credit opportunities. Homework is graded on completion, and discussion is not mandatory. she is very sweet and this was the easy A if u put in the effort

BEST PROFESSOR at UCSD! This class should be your number priority on that schedule of yours. Exam 2 averaged at 90%, she's pretty hip and teaches really well. I was intimidated by biochem but ended up being the most interesting and easiest class because of the way she teaches.

Hands down one of the best professors at UCSD. Quite frankly some of the best slides I've ever seen. In a class that is known for being dense and difficult to memorize. The way she lectures and utilizes her slides makes this class really accessible.
Protect this woman at all cost! She's the best we have at UCSD.

One of the best professors I've had at UCSD so far. Very caring about her students, passionate about what she teaches, and very clear about what material will get tested on the exam. Metabolic biochemistry is a hard topic to grasp, but Jazz makes the topic significantly easier and less stressful to understand.

SO AMAZING! Hated ochem but loved bibc bc of her(no memorizing mechanisms). She's so real and tells u what will/won't be on 3 exams + 1 final. Lectures can be boring but useful for exam prep. Problem set graded on effort, and it helps to go to discussion for clarity. Gave EC for SETs even tho we didnt reach threshold #goat (+20pt EC asgmt week6)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a really kind and straightforward professor. Her lectures match the exam questions and there is extra credit at the end of each exam. A lot of memorizing like Aminos and enzymes and such but she makes the class really interesting and enjoyable tbh. Also a 20pt ec assignment that was like week 6.
I don't know how this professor is this overrated. It was not bad but I rather take other professor if I were you.

very kind Prof! material is VERY reflective of lecture content. the class is straight memorization tbh (ex. 20 amino acids, glycolysis, CAC, etc, and all it's reverse reactions). must also memorize chem structures of ALL reagents in the mechanisms. lots of ec opportunities: ec questions at the end of each test + a whole ec assignment (20pts).

this is by far the goat teacher at ucsd. graded on 3 quizzes and a final that are all very representative of course material. she makes it very clear on what will be on exams and offers ample ec. if you are taking bibc 102, you can't not take this prof.

Fave professor at UCSD so far. She truly cares about her students; can't stress how nice it is to have a professor who treats you with empathy and compassion. Graded on 3 exams + final, as well as problem sets. Problem sets and lecture were v helpful in understanding the material. Gives lots of EC. I will miss her!!!!

Dickinson is by far the best biology professor on campus. She's clearly cares about her students and sets up class for you to succeed. Exams are straightforward and lectures don't beat around the bush. She highlights what is and isn't going to be on each exam.  There's a ton of opportunities for extra credit. I'd love to take her class again.

I came into this class expecting the worst from what everyone said about biochem. Dr. Jazz is clear about what you will see on exams, the lectures do not beat around the bush, and the class overall is designed to support your learning. She also offers 50 pts just from a review session to aid as a buffer. Flash cards helped a ton!

He's a bit too 'kind'. Says wanting to make things easy but intentionally makes this DEI and GENERAL EDUCATION course very troublesome and hostile. Mandatory attendance, but no points for homework. Does a progressive 'social experiment', but is rather conformity test. For such an 'amiable' professor, 'what's your meaning' is my only comment.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Fattal is very passionate about his subject. He definitely makes you work for an A, so you need to deeply engage with readings and films. He brought in several filmmakers throughout the quarter to speak to the class, and that was a really cool experience. Class was primarily graded on 3 essays (1 dropped), quizzes, and a presentation.

he gave us an excessive amount of work to do. Quizzes are very specific and timed. This year, the class had to attend 3 screenings (which were not on campus), help set up an event, work the event, and complete journal entries along with a 1000 journal reflection and a film review during FINALS WEEK. The lectures were not helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He was overall a good professor. His lectures weren't mandatory, but the discussions were. There was one group project at the end of the quarter, but it was fairly easy. There is a lot of reading and there are reading quizzes every week and film quizzes every other week. Overall, I didn't have to put that many hours a week into homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A lot of readings and films. Weekly reading quizzes, biweekly film quizzes, a group project, and final. Attendance is not mandatory for lectures but discussions. He also offers extra credits on quizzes but not too frequently. Take this class if you want an A but be careful because everyone's grade drops to A- or B+ after group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Assigns a lot of readings, but discusses them in his lectures. Imo, he is a bit unclear during his lectures. But, his slides cover essentially everything that comes up during the online final exam. His reading choices are stellar, I do like reading most of them (except the Debord reading) and this class provides a new lens to view social problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: lectures aren't mandatory but are definitely very helpful to understand weekly readings. can be very reading heavy but honestly not bad as long as you keep up with it and pay attention in discussion. no midterm, only a group project which is easy as long as you communicate with your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: its just the loads of readings and the group project will definitely be a hurdle. but besides that, Fattal is a very kind, funny, and enjoyable professor.

He's such a fun and charismatic prof. LE will be mandatory-ish because if I didn't go to it, it would be much harder to review the slides he would put out on canvas.  
I also like to mention that the quizzes and finals are on Canvas, and won't be taken in person unless you want to-
But again, he's a cool prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Your grade mostly depends on the final exam, which was pretty fair. You do not have to be good at science for this class because the prof breaks everything down pretty well. He uploads the lecture videos to Canvas, which really helps with studying. He provides 3 quizzes and will take your 2 best scores, which gave me room to do bad on one of them.
Super funny, understanding, amazing communication and teaching, very good at explaining concepts. Generous curve at the end of the course. Quizzes and final are all MCQs.

I've heard great things about Prof Albizati, but I personally didn't enjoy his teaching style. For 6B, I felt that he just reads off the slides super fast and doesn't go into enough conceptual detail (at least for me). I found the Achieve HW to be super inefficient/annoying and unrepresentative. Tests were completely fair though! Plus, he rounds!

There aren't any study guides provided and the TA's are responsible for making all of the quizzes which make up about a third of your grade. The quizzes don't reflect what you go over in lecture all that much, the average on two of the 3 quizzes have been failing grades this quarter, he doesn't provide any resources to help learn the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Albizati was a great lecturer and explained concepts well. His lectures were easy to follow, podcasted, and always posted on canvas as well. He is an all around funny and standup guy. He was accessible during online office hours every week. Practice exams were nearly identical to the real exams. Would definitely recommend for 40A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Albizati has been the best chem prof I've had at this school so far. His lectures were very clear and easy to follow, and practice exams were very indicative of what the real exams looked like. He had a great personality, and it was easy to see how much he cared for his students. Very straigthtforward class and professor if you dont fall behind
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall great professor, teaches content well, easy to understand. Homework on Achieve, which is required for the class; HW is due the night before exams, includes stuff not taught/on tests (be wary). The lowest HW grade is also dropped. Test grading was flexible; some questions were changed to partial credit depending on grades. Course curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Efficient, makes course easy to understand. Assigns homework on Achieve (which you do need to pay for), due the night before tests; sometimes HW includes material not taught/not on tests. Funny, lectures are enjoyable. Slightly flexible with test grading; may drop questions or give partial credit depending on grades; curves the course.

Love love LOVE this professor. I like his class because his tests are all free responses and that is what chem is about...showing work. That way I can get at least some credit for showing work. He truly cares about his students. Has online homework, 2 midterms and a final, lectures/discussions are not mando. TAKE HIM IF HE TEACHES.

Easy exams, exactly like practice exams given. Homework more bust work than helpful, much harder than the tests, however, does not count for credit just competition so it was whatever. Very chill dude, brought dog treats for dog. Lecture and section not mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: class was easier than i'd heard, nice professor who knew what he was talking about. midterms were easy but final was quite difficult if you didn't study hard for it

Professor Albizati really takes the time to try to get to know his students. He hosts Arteazen visits where he truly just wants to get to know the students better. During lecture, he is clear with his expectations and doesn't inundate you with too much information. Would definitely look to take a class with him in the future.

Albizati is absolutely amazing. This guy doesn't B.S. Bro gets straight to the point. If he covers all the material necessary, he's not gonna make you sit there for the remainder of lecture learning extra unnecessary stuff. He's also VERY clear about what to expect with his exams and the practice midterms are super helpful. Super chill guy overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I spent a LOT of time doing practice problems to prepare for exams. The actual graded homework had many questions beyond the scope of the course, so make sure to do the problems in the textbook (more reflective of exam content). I stopped going to lecture/discussion after Week 3 and basically self-studied the class and aced midterm 2/final.

Great prof, his lectures had practice problems and outlined everything you needed to know for midterms and the final. Definitely study the book problems, one of the midterms had a problem from the textbook word for word on it! He was really nice as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: None of the lecture and discussions are required for attendance. If you study and do the practice stuff, you'll be fine. As for the guy, he is chill but from my experience, he could care less about you or your grade. shoutout to the TAs though, awesome people.

Engaging lecturer, but he doesn't talk loud. He doesn't cover everything from textbook in lecture, but exams only based off lecture content. Does useful practice questions in lecture. HW, unlimited tries & no wrong answer penalty, is slightly harder if you don't read textbook. 80% of grade is based off 2 midterms + 1 final, all free response
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lectures with practice problems throughout to help solidify concepts. Discussion worksheets and practice exams for both midterms and final were given and were helpful, but of course, not identical. Overall, not too hard, especially if you have a good chem background going into it.
super easy, you don't have to study, no trick questions on exams, very generous curve; he gives practice problems throughout lecture, so you know what you're doing by the end of it

Albizati is great. Super funny and lectures were entertaining. Midterms were kind of brutal since there didn't feel like enough time but the exams were relatively similar to the practice. Drill practice problems and you will do well in the class. Also go to discussions as they go over the problem sets which can help a lot

Great prof. Your grade is basically 2 midterms and a final, but all the exams are very similar to the practice exams provided. TAs are super helpful for the weekly hw assignments. The final is pretty difficult compared to the midterms, so make sure to start studying early for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took his class during summer session 1, honestly was not bad. the final grade gets curved very heavily - focus studying from the textbook and do all the problems that relate to the final exam / archive questions. Overall, not a bad experience taking chem with albizati.
3 Quiz with one right before the final, 2 best ones matter. HW are easy but time consuming. Do use the discussion slides well to prepare the quiz cuz TA made them.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class as a non-STEM major for a GE--which is the same for everyone in the class, it isn't for stem majors--and it was bad. Kim doesn't cover content well, rushing through the slides and never fully explaining under the guise of being "easy to understand". Also, there are no study guides and the midterms/final are nothing like lecture.

Took this class for an easy GE, wish I hadn't. Kim doesn't communicate well and rushes through lectures without explaining. His TA writes the 3 quizzes, he has no clue what's on them, so only God knows how to prepare for them. The final that Kim wrote was easier than the quizzes, but overall, with no study guide you must resort to praying for hope.
hard exams, generous curve, straightforward, no nonsense lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is nice, but this class was a nightmare.I felt the lectures were all over the page.Goes at lightning speed, and most everyone just stepped out from Chem 40A, so GOOD LUCK.Also, he told us that we are his side gig, so kinda weird.Tests are HARD.Hw inconsistently graded for correctness, then not and just completion and syllabus is 1/2 a page...

Super chill professor, usually teaches at night since he works outside of teaching. Encourages students to reach out outside of class—loved Arteazen nights! His tests are super reasonable; just review the study guide early, and you'll be good.
Best chemistry professor for the gen chem series Ive had so far, makes chemistry understandable and you know what to expect for exams. As long as you put in the effort you should do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Clear lectures, fair exams, good curve. One of my favorite professors at UCSD. Lectures are clear and organized, and exams are VERY similar to the practice ones he provides. Very open about course policy and clearly wants students to do well. If you pay attention in lecture, do the hw, and read a bit, you will do well.

Professor Albizati is easily the best chemistry professor at UCSD. His lectures are all very easy to follow and include examples for every mechanism that is taught. His exams are a fair assessment of lecture material and the practice exams he provides are extremely similar to the actual exams. Couldn't have asked for a better professor.

I have Professor Albizati for my ochem series and HE IS THE GOAT!!!
So glad I decided to skip 6C last spring and began the 40 series with him.
The exams are fair and similar to practice exams.
He also curves the class A LOT (in 40A a 79 is around an A-) as he wants the class average to be around B-.
HIGHLY RECOMMEND TAKING HIS CLASS IF YOU CAN!!

Amazing professor. My favorite professor to teach chemistry and its for my worst feared course 40B. The most caring person, and makes everything very easy to understand. Humorous, and very unintimidating when it comes to questions. Everything is based off of lecture, not really textbook. Practice exams are very very similar to the exams. A+ teacher

Dr. Kim was an amazing professor. All of his exam material is based on the lectures. The book given in the modules is basically for prereading the material and practice. You do not have to read the book to do well in this class. Just pay attention during the lecture, do the take-home practice problems given, study well, and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Albizati was an amazing professor! His lectures make the material easy to understand and he provides a lot of helpful practice. He is also very funny and chill, so would highly recommend taking his classes.

Best professor for Ochem. Before the exams he would go through the questions for the class to know what to expect. Practice midterms exactly like exams. Just attend class and do practice problems at home. Ochem is tough but he makes it easier.

Professor Albizati is a fantastic professor. He lectures clearly and creates opportunities outside of class to connect with students. His grading is very test heavy but he does provide practice tests very similar in format to the real final, but I will say nowhere near the same difficulty. However, he does curve and I feel he prepared me for 40a.

Professor Albizati is good at explaining concepts well and providing lots of helpful practice both in lecture and to do on your own time. Midterm and Final is worth most of your grade but he provides practice exams with answer keys that are the same format as the actual tests. He also seems to care a lot about the students and is very chill.

Professor Albizati was great! Lecture isn't mandatory, but he goes over example problems in class, which is helpful. He also gives practice exams which are very similar to the actual tests, so I would highly recommend doing those.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took this introductory chem class with him for my GE. He is a chill professor, explains concepts pretty well, and curves the class by the end. Also I heard he's good for Ochem :) (CHEM 40A?)

Albizati was a great professor and really cared about teaching ochem. Test were super fair, since he also gave us a practice final and midterm, which had a similar format to real thing. The class though is just graded by 2 midterms, 1 final. He gives generous curves (average becomes a B-). Lectures also provided practice problems to help prepare.

He is very nice out of all Ochem professors, he acts aggressive but he's actually really understanding of the class's ability. So he has quite a nice grading system worked out. I would definitely recommend him for the chem41 series!

The class was test heavy and the exams were very difficult. However, the grades were curved heavily. You will also never catch him putting Acyl Halides in his body. Jokes aside, Albizati was very approachable during his office hours and explained organic chemistry mechanism with great clarity.

Exams were difficult, but were heavily curved. Entire grade was midterms and final, but practice exams were very indicative of the actual exam content. Great lecturer, never once caught him putting acyl halides in his body. 5/5

Test were very difficult but it is curved heavily. You will also never catch him putting a single molecule of Acyl Halides in his body. Jokes aside, He was very approachable during office hours and explained organic chemistry mechanisms with great clarity.

he is the best! so knowledgeable, taught me 40a so well as he is an extremely good lecturer. gives lots of examples and explains hard content very clearly. i took 40a during a summer session (5 weeks instead of 10) and i still learned all the content well because of him. cares deeply for his students, and is a great guy.

If only I took the ochem series here than at my C.C! Prof. Kim made the topics of ochem so easy to understand. He does practice problems in lecture and goes over it to make sure we understood how to get to the product. He is a chill professor and is so easy to talk too! Highly recommend taking him!

Prof. Albizati was overall a good professor for ochem. He had good lectures and went at a pretty reasonable pace which was nice. His practice exams were very helpful as were the grading feedback on homeworks. He also had helpful office hours online which made them more accessible.

His lectures are engaging and he has a knack for explaining complex concepts in a way that is easy to understand. He also has a great sense of humor and is always cracking good jokes, which helps to make the material more enjoyable. He is fair when it comes to exams.

Professor Albizati was great! His exams are all curved but he gives practice midterms that are like the real midterms and finals. DO THESE! Discussion is not required and attendance at lectures isn't either but I recommend you go because it helps a lot. Office hours are right after class. Only graded on 2 midterms,1 final, and homework.

A Lakers fan, which already makes him top-tier. But other than that, he's a great professor with a clear understanding of everything. Lectures are concise. Tests are fine as long as you study (start a week before the test). Tests are misgraded often but fixed with regrades. Ochem is obviously hard but study a lot and you're fine. Really good curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Explains ochem in a way that's easy to understand. His practice tests are very similar to actual exams, so you know what to expect. The class isn't easy, but he's there to answer any questions. Overall, cool guy - you can tell he cares about students and is willing to speak with you outside of class about research, etc.
Great professor and lecturer and made ochem fun and easy to understand. Cares about his students. Loves diet coke.
Stellar professor with an insane handle on chemistry. Truly cares for students, and the exams are exactly as clear as he says they will be, just make sure you keep up because you will drop behind.

Do your best. The material speeds by pretty fast, but we still ended up behind. HW due dates are close together, so don't slack off on that. Grading is determined by TAs' criteria, but they should be generally similar. 2 hard free-response midterms, so do the practice exams. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had him for 40A and 40B. 40B is much more difficult than 40A. But just like with 40A, if you keep up with the lectures, do the practice problems and questions, and be consistent with studying, you should be alright. He is a great professor who genuinely loves chemistry and tries to make it enjoyable and learnable for those who find it difficult.

Great professor! I hate organic chemistry, and it's still hard, but he actually makes it interesting. No homework, but he posts a question every day - make sure to do them. Do the practice exams! The actual exams are almost identical. I got by without the textbook, relied on my own notes and the lecture slides instead. Practice, practice, practice!

Prof. Albizati gives very clear and concise lectures. He also provides notes and slide so that we do not need to spend so much time on the textbook. The exams are very fair as they resemble the practice exams. However, his lectures are sometimes too simplified (some topics are skipped).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have so many regrets taking this class with this professor. Do you want a professor that teaches all the important stuff right before the exam? Well this ones for you then... Literally did not go over the major matertials needed on the midterm till the week of the exam. Absolute bull.

Though Professor's Albizati's class was perhaps the definition of one where you've really got to work hard, his practice exams mean that if you put in the work you at least know you're going to do decently. Class was entirely exam centric though practice exams were almost carbon copies of the tests. Solid choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good professor, I would recommend him. The practice tests he gives are identical in structure and question type to the actual tests. He was a good professor, however I felt like I had to watch his old recorded lectures a couple times to understand concepts. The only gripe I had was that he would not allow us to request regrades for the final.
