The only downside is she uses apps/products that require money and are MANDATORY for her class. Takes attendance through app before and after class and during class.

I have never taken stats before and after reading these comments I was really nervous about this class, but I can honestly say that Lowe is the reason I enjoy stats. Her lectures are clear, she gives thorough examples, there isn't an excessive amount of hw, and you get cheat sheets for your tests. If you put in the work, you will do well

She helped me get stats even tho Im awful at math. She gives awesome lectures, podcasts, and is really clear about everything she wants you to learn so studying is kinda easy. I studied a lot for this class and the only thing thats difficult is that she tests on concepts/the logic behind certain formulas but she gives you hella cheat sheets.

The professor is super caring and clear during lectures. She thoroughly explains what she wants you to learn, along with demonstrating several ex. CourseKey is used in this course. She does take attendance every lecture, but you can miss up to five and still be given full credit. Midterms are curved & very simple if you follow along her slides.

It takes a while to get adjusted to Lowe's teaching style, but I realized it's best to review class material both before and after class to grasp it best. The homework is graded and can be difficult, however Lowe is always willing to help if you have any questions and she is very clear in her explanations! She's very kind and lectures aren't boring
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Respectable Professor. Took Stats as a Freshmen. With curve managed to get an A+. I never took stats before but slowly did LEARN what she taught. Did I enjoy it? Eh. But if you take time to review her slides and prepare GOOD CHEATSHEETS while studying the test are not too bad. Homework once again takes under 2 hours. But make sure you are learning

She's very clear with instructions but if you have never taken stats then this class will be hard. There's a new lecture every day and the her tests are conceptual. But there's extra credit opportunities, get decent scores on the homework, go to class and you can get a B! The book is expensive and the app was $25.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Weekly homework assignments. I wouldn't say this is the easiest class since there are some concepts that you must learn in order to do well. At the same time, however, I didn't feel like it was the hardest class. The average grade is a BB- though. So put in the effort and you should be capable of getting an A/A-.

Professor Lowe uses CourseKey app and it is not easy to connect to network to do the assessment question and you have to pay 30 dollars. The textbook and homework you also need to purchase for 95 dollars required for only one quarter. I don't know other statistic classes also use this material but it is ridiculously expensive and unnecessary.

very awesome ge and very well explained, interesting material. only multiple choice and true or false quizzes and test and no hw at all, other than sona experiments. attendance is mandatory and she goes through the slides very quickly, but she posts the lecture beforehand. taking notes before class is recommended. easy A and interesting stuff.

She is a very nice professor and definitely willing to help her students. I had never taken stats before and I feel like that was the reason I found the class extremely hard. If you have a background in stats, psyc60 isn't too bad, but if not, prepare to study really hard since the class moves very fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: her lecture are very clear and organized, just review for the ppt she posted and you will be fine in exams.

Lowe is a caring professor and is accessible outside of class. She is also very eager to help whenever a student may need. Her tests are fair. I would take the class again. Lecture material can be interesting

I feel like I only did well because of AP stats. This class moves fast. Professor Lowe does a good job with the information and podcasts/posts her lectures and slides which is very helpful. Two midterms and a final where you can use cheat sheets. Offers a good amount of extra credit. Need to purchase app and textbook in total $125.
Caring professor. Please feel obliged to read her powerpoint carefully. It contains almost all possible points and knowledge that are going to show up in exams and quizzes.
Very comprehendible lectures. Provides adorable examples from her own kids. The only negative thing is you have to pay $25 for the CourseKey app for attendance and quizzes.

Makes you pay $25 for a buggy app that takes attendance every lecture, and makes you pay $100 for Aplia HW access. The HW isn't too difficult but get ready to read - at least one chapter a week, sometimes two. Unnecessarily difficult for a GE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Lots of lectures that aren't necessarily interesting but she does a good job of explaining all the content. Very generous with extra credit, class curves, and amount of cheat sheets you get for tests. Her tests took some time for me to get used to coming from AP Stats as her's are very conceptual.

The lecture materials can be difficult to understand, but Professor Lowe helps you to understand them very well. She's pretty good at lecturing and helping you get across the main points of the materials. Two midterms and an accumulative final. There are also lab hw which are really easy and are graded based on completion. No need for the textbook.

She's an excellent, very clear professor. I had never taken Stats before so I felt like I had to work a little harder to understand the homework than my peers, but she posts podcasts/slideshows of her lectures online, which was helpful. Midterms are  tricky at times, but it's ok if you bring a good cheat sheet and do the study guide she provides.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She takes attendance within the first five minutes of class and again in the last 10 minutes. You're allowed to miss 5 classes total without it taking a hit on your grade. Uses an app called CourseKey that costs $25 to take attendance and do graded assessments during lecture. homework can be a little hard but midterms are extremely conceptual &hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The homeworks can be very hard and time consuming. The first midterm was alright but the second midterm and final was very hard. 3% SONA EC is offered.

She was a real sweetheart! She really incorporates pictures of her kids in her lecture, so that was enjoyable. She podcasts her lectures, so if you don't attend class (which I stopped doing after the second midterm), you're fine. Her tests are very detailed-oriented, so really just study the lecture notes and you're solid. Easy A and interesting!

Lowe is very clear, with a structure to every lecture. The textbook was online with Aplia, the program you need to complete the weekly homework. She posts her PowerPoints online before class, although she has iClicker points which means you still need to go to lecture, but not section. She also offers extra credit if you do over 3 SONA study hours.

I felt like she explained concepts pretty well but not as well as she could have. I got an A without paying any attention in lecture since I'd taken AP Stats, but it sounded like other students were having trouble. She tried to answer questions to the best of her ability, but I think she ended up confusing some kids even more with her answers.

Her lectures make sense but she could stand to go over some of the missed concepts more . She's super nice and always answers questions the best she can. Clear lectures, but you don't have to go to every single one. Her tests are kinda weird though. Overall it was a pretty chill class.

She was great, I gotta be honest, very clear lecture and super helpful slide show. No homework or pop quizzes. However, attending lecture is critical for good grade in the class. I got an ez 92 on the first midterm and thought this class as an easy A thus stopped attending for roughly a month. Got a bloody 69 on the second midterm. SO ATTEND  A.

Professor Lowe is fantastic. She is definitely the best professor I've had at UCSD so far. The homework isn't bad, it usually takes from around 30 minutes to an hour, and there only one assignment each week. She is very clear in her lectures, and it's nice cause she puts up the podcasts after the lecture. She also gives up to 3% EC, which is a ton.

Lowe was definitely my best prof this quarter. Super clear lecturer, cares for student success, and digests harder parts of the course for your understanding. No homework, no readings, just lecture and two midterms along with a final. This class was completely straightforward. WOULD DEFINITELY RECOMMEND. Do not need textbook at all.

She is very organized and her lectures are crystal clear. You do get points for using the i-clicker in class, but class is not mandatory. I would still recommend going to class because a lot of the online homework problems are pretty similar to the examples presented in class. Discussion covers nothing new, but I definitely enjoyed her class.
WONDERFUL.

She's an amazing professor. Everything is clear and laid out. Most structured class iv'e had so far.  My only issue was that she would finish 10-15 minutes early and I'm still confused. Click in-s aren't a big deal,  free points for you. She's also very engaging and interactive, cares about her students.

Wasted $150 on textbook I never cracked open. Lectures are long, & while the content is interesting, she is very quite & docile so it's hard to stay focused. Just listen to the podcasts. 1 midterm, 1 cumulative final; neither are hard just make sure you review the lecture slides thoroughly. She DOES ask for specific examples of studies in her tests

This is one of the easier Psychology classes at UCSD. Tests are multiple choice with a short answer section and truefalse section. She also podcasts (visual and audio), so it's really easy to catch up for the tests. She also has a "lab" component of the class,  but these are online labs and they're painfully easy.

She's a good lecturer; she uses podcast and powerpoint. There are two midterms and one final, MC, TF, and short answers. The exams are very reasonable if you study. The material is pretty interesting. You'll do well if you study the notes. The textbook wasn't that helpful. I basically just used it for clarification.

Very clear when she gives lecture and always reiterates important points. If you go to lecture and listen to what she's saying then you can get an A. Paying attention and doing the assigned homework should definitely be enough to definitely get you a B or an A. She is very clear and great at explaining topics. Would definitely take her again!

Prof. Lowe is amazing. Her lectures are pretty clear and organized. You only need to study the PPT slides and listen to her lecture to pass the test. She uploads her lectures on Ted podcast, which is very useful to re-listen the lectures (recommended for exams).  5 online experiments (supper easy), 2 midterms, 1 finals,  and 2% extra credits.

professor lowe is a great professor. She is very clear in her lectures and gives specific examples of problems similar to what you may see on homeworkmidterms. Her midterms are somewhat difficult (I actually did pretty bad on both) but she gives a huge, generous curve at the end of the course. I would highly recommend taking her class.

Lectures are precise and a must! There are clicker questions and the professor usually goes over problems in class which are very helpful. Slides are posted online and much more useful than the book IMO. Great professor! Tests can be challenging and tricky  because demand solid knowledge of the material. Awesome professor though!
her tests are hard, but she gives a good curve!

There is nothing to complain about professor Lowe except the mandatory homework she assigns. Exams were somewhat challenging but you get a letter sized, two sided cheat sheet. Homework is time consuming but is easy points. Attendance is also free points since clicker responses are only for participation.

Lowe has a pretty organized teaching style and definitely  knows her stuff. Her podcasts make it easy to review the material and appears to genuinely care for her students. Aplia homework seems pointless at times as her exams are EXTREMELY conceptual. TAs are chill and mostly helpful. The material can pile up so seek help RIGHT AWAY if necessary.
Pretty straightforward class. The homework was all online. Midterm 1 was basic statistical concepts. The second midterm and the final were a little tough. Overall, good class, especially for a GE.

I would not recommend this teacher. I showed my HW to other friends who took psyc 60 before and 100% of them responded it to be tedious and a lot harder than their class. Mandatory iclickers. The midterms represent the lectures but an around 65% average of the class? We can see how tricky and harsh the questions can be.

At first, I was so scared of this class because I scored below average on my mid-term 2 and thought that I would end up with C. However, she curved so much that I ended up with B+. She is super generous and explains concepts by illustrating examples. I recommend her.
Do your homework and go to class. Don't be scared of your midterm grades, she gives out GENEROUS curve. You will get an A.

My friend recommended her. I do not know what happened but I think her teaching style changed (?). She utilizes iclicker participation. Her midterms so far were all multiple choice (around 15-20 questions).There is homework on Ted that is tedious. Overall, I wish I didn't take her:( Class average is 65-70% which is not great for a stats class.
She's pretty awesome. I would recommend showing up to every lecture because she gives random quizzes on the material from the previous class.

All you need to do is attend class and take notes and you'll get an A, fersure. Her exams are pretty much the practice exams. She makes everything simple which is just what I needed and is extremely kind and helpful. Homework is straight from her notes. Don't bother buying the textbook. If anything, borrow from the library.

definitely one of the easier upper division psyc classes. 6/8 easy pop quizzes for checking attendances. 2 midterms and 1 final. she posts study guides of what you need to know and her lectures cover basically everything. professor lowe is also very approachable and always answered any questions i had, even specific ones from study guides. SONA ec.

her lectures are really interesting and clear. and she is a really good lecturer. i did not open the textbook even once. just went to lecture and studied the notes and got an A. 8 pop quizzes and she counts the best 6. you get 9/10 points on the quiz just for writing something relevant even if its wrong.

She is a good lecturer. Exams are extremely fair everything in the exam is taught in class. The short answers would be considered harder, just study and you'll be fine. The quizzes were pop quizzes and they were fairly easy. DONT underestimate the days she gives pop quiz and watch out for the back to back quizzes; those are the surprisers!!

Sporadic in-class quizzes for attendance (which are very easy), 6/8 of which are graded. Two midterms and one final exam, plus SONA extra credit. Exams come straight from lecture, so know it VERY well. No tricks, but there are short-responses on all exams. All-in-all, very doable.
Lectures are boring and does not teach well.  Exams are hard and I didn't learn much from this class.

Tests are very straight forward which are composed of both multiple choice and short answers. Weekly quizzes are given but she only grades 6/8. She is a very good lecturer. I looked forward to going to her class everyday.

Prof. Lowe is the stats teachers for the non-math types out there. She makes concepts as easy as possible to understand. Some say that she teaches it like a kindergarten teacher but that is what I need when I'm trying to learn T-tests, Z-tests, Chi-square tests, etc. Awesome at teaching for sure

Professor Lowe is beyond amazing! Yes she does talk to you like you are in pre school, but it truly helps me understand the concepts she is talking about. I took a different stats class before this one and got a C. This one im guaranteed to get an A. T/F and multiple choice questions on a stats test?who woulda thought. if you take psyc 60, take her

Easiest professor in the entire world. If you read the book you don't even have to go to her lectures (but you will because you have 6/8 pop quizzes that count). Her questions are straightforward and the grading system is the same. She talks to you like you are a pre-school student... which is fine because you understand the material that way!

Nice professor. The tests are very fair and she doesn't try and trick you. However I found it very hard to pay attention to her since it was an 8am class and she wasn't using a microphone so I didn't really have the will power to pay attention, especially cause I found the lectures kind of boring. She's very nice but hard to focus on.

Pretty simple class - Prof. Lowe's lectures are super clear and come straight from the book - don't really need to read if you don't want to. She explains really well and gives great examples. Graded on best 6/8 random quizzes, so you should probably go. Midterms pretty straightforward if you review lectures (which she posts online). Take her!

This is the second time I'm taking Statistics! She is the BEST professor I had ever had at the University!! She is so clear on here lectures, so kind. Her homework is easy, (use the book) and her tests are very easy as well! If you do your homework and if you do her practice exams that she hands out you will get an A for sure!!

Much easier than cogs 14b. Participation is by Kahoot, and you're allowed to use AI on your homework quizzes (on the 4th attempt). Both midterms and finals are completely MCQs. The only issue is that only about 10% of her PPT notes are useful; the rest are filler.

professor hoffman is super nice and her lectures are very clear (she spends a lot of time explaining in different ways so that it sticks), the class structure and teaching style reminds me of 14a with professor creel. attendance in lectures and discussion arent mandatory and all lectures are recorded
Awesome professor

Much more of a philosophy course than a science course which can be misleading, and many figures mentioned in class hold prejudiced views when looked up. It makes the course feel tone deaf at best, eugenicist at worst. Assignments and final project were not well organized with little feedback, course size didn't suit a discussion-based structure.
super kind and thoroughly goes over the content. midterms are pretty tricky though.

Such a engaging lecturer. Content is delivered in super well-thought out and structured slides. She speaks in such academic terms - lovely to listen to. Exams very close to practice and lectures - completely fair. She also made highly missed questions on exam extra credit (so thoughtful). Attendance mandatory, but super chill and caring proff.

Professor Hoffman was pretty chill, lectures can feel boring but I think it's just the nature of the content. Allowed cheat sheets for each exam, weekly quiz on lecture content. Pretty easy class just a bit tedious.

She wasn't that accessible out of class. God knows how many times i emailed her or contacted her through piazza with no response. Shes very knowledgeable about what she teaches. Quiz every week about last weeks content+reading, readings through perusal, No mandatory discussion, group video project
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Hoffman (Walker) was so funny, but the lectures were really long and wordy. She values participation and there are weekly quizzes. The final is a group presentation. The content is great though and she makes the lectures fairly interesting
easy A, didn't do much in the exams. cheat sheets are very important.

Her class is great and she is a nice person. But, her exam is the most vague I have seen at all times; after receiving feedbacks her exams improved. But, after that correction exams start to contain all kinds of errors (i.e., testing on things that she never taught, two same options in MC). I like her and the class, but will never take her again.

Professor seems to not care at ALL about this class. She is not accessible outside of class, often cancels her office hours and holds them at an extremely unconventional time. Midterms + final are in person, which make no sense as lecture hall has 200+ students and desks are really small. Midterm average was extremely low, little to no curve.

Horrible experience with professor this quarter. Seems to be really unorganized, almost every homework has errors on them. She is not accessible AT ALL outside of class. Midterms are in person. Ive emailed her plenty of times throughout the quarter, have yet to receive a response back. She has yelled at us in lecture for being "loud".

Really friendly but this course has been very frustrating. Homeworks are a big part of our grade; often graded incorrectly. Students spend extra time making sure corrections are made. Test questions can be vague; it's hard to get feedback without sending reminders multiple times. Mostly seems like the Professor doesn't care about this course.
Easy course; though sometimes the lectures were pre-recorded, the exams were fair and they were mostly based on homework

Professor Hoffman is NOT accessible at all outside of class. The class itself is easy enough, but your questions about grading, assignments, or just topic info will not be answered through email or through piazza by the prof or the TAs. You can prob still get an A if you do all the work though!
She curves heavily. Take her!

Hoffman is a fine lecturer and speaks clearly, yet disorganized. But her exams are the worst. They are written in a way to trick students, often times with multiple answers so similar that only someone with her level of knowledge could differentiate them. Either she doesn't know how to write good exams or she wants people to fail rather than learn.

Prof Hoffman is my favorite teacher in the CogSci department. She's really caring and receptive to feedback, and she works extremely hard to accommodate everyone in a 250+ person class (especially with no TAs this quarter). This class overall is easy but you learn a lot, and it doesn't take that much effort to get a good grade.

I love professor Hoffman! I took her for two courses and I wish I could take more classes with her because she's the best. So understanding and she makes her class challenging but not hard. Seriously amazing

Probably the best Cognitive Science Professor I've had at UCSD. Fun lectures and straightforward class. Do well on the quizzes and exam and you're good to go. She even drops the lowest quiz score at the end of the quarter.

She is a good lecturer overall and is good at explaining many important concepts. However, sometimes she over-explained things. Sometimes the homework and labs are heavy. There is no midterm. As long as you understand the homework and labs, you will do pretty well in the final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Hoffman is a great instructor! Her lectures are clear and detailed, she is very helpful in OH, and super caring and accommodating to students.

All the lectures are pre-recorded. It's kinda boring to take this class with her. I don't think she addresses things very clearly and she often gives me confusions. I didn't learn much from this class.

My favorite professor in the Cog Sci department. Her class is a huge-discussion format. This isn't the class where you sit and listen, she makes sure you actively learn from relevant examples. We were assigned to read 2-3 articles per week but she uses a platform where you "actively" read and make comments, so the class isn't boring at all.

Prof Drew is incredible. She's funny, kind, and passionate, and although all of the course material is covered solely in her lectures, she does a really good job of making them interesting. When talking about a cognitive phenomenon, she always has some sort of demo set up like a game so that us students can fully understand what's going on. 1000/10

The course material is super interesting, she uses relevant examples in her lectures. I loved the class. The only thing I gotta say is the tests ... They are graded by the TAs, so your test grade depends heavily on the TA's perspective. I don't know who words the questions on the tests but they are so weird, especially the multiple choice ones :(
She tends to over-explain things in her lectures but overall very knowledgable and seems to care about her students. The final was take home and all the work was relatively easy.

It was my first stats class and she was very helpful. However, I didn't like how she would often over-explain things and how she would say 'uh' and other filler words so often. Her tests were fair, weekly homework was easy, weakly discussions were sometimes interesting, and attendance was not mandatory.

My first time taking stats & Professor Hoffman was an angel! She explains all key concepts well & provides a lot of examples. She and TAs are very responsive on Piazza/email, and theres a lot of extra credit! Homework reflects the tests very well, as long as you know the stats test to use and the reasoning behind it, you'll do well on exams!
The lectures are sometimes boring. But if you memorize and know about the key terms, you will nail the class. The tests are long, different from past quarters. But she is super caring and nice.

Lectures are not the greatest, but the tests are only on lecture material so it isn't too bad. Drew cares a lot about students and making sure they do well. The first midterm is really hard but if people don't do well she makes the other ones much easier. Pay attention to experiments in the lectures, you will be tested on those a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Drew is pretty chill. Although lectures were not that perfect if you care about logic a lot, overall the classes were good and resultful. The exams were straight forward and easy. Just know definition of every term mentioned and you will nail it. Very generous extra credit. Attendance takes up to 20%, but you have 7 freebies. Podcast is available.

Dr. Hoffman is such a good professor, and above that a great person! Material is very well explained and if you did not understand something, she is super accessible during office hours. Well informed on her topics and genuinely cares for students' learning.

She is very caring for students, talk to her if you have you difficulties. Focus on her lecture and don't blame on can't hearing her, that is because the class is too big, yeah I mean in GH! Her tests are fair, as long as you read the slide and understand all of it, the test should be easy.

She is awful. She doesnt know what is she talking about during lecture and her voice is so unclear. She can never finish an entire sentence. When she tries to explain something, she can never make it clear. Her answers are not complete sentences and just cant answer to the question. She just not know what is she teaching.
Not a very good professor. There's not really any material that should be challenging, but the tests are way too hard for no reason, with averages in the 60-71 range. Didn't learn anything useful.

Professor Drew is a very caring and considerate Professor, she is very accessible outside of class. Sometimes she talks a little fast, but she make things clear, and makes the class interesting! Her test is very fair and straightforward (our class average for midterm was 90). Just take notes and review her podcast and you will do well!

Writes vague test questions, each test feels like its trying to constantly trick you over minutia unrelated to the content. Classes like this are basically just memorizing the results of previous Psych research, it isn't important enough to be worth the amount of time invested in Hoffman's tests, where each question is worth 1% of your grade.

Almost guaranteed to get her for any COGS GE courses. She is very fair and interested in her content (the content overlaps with COGS101B quiet a bit). However she is mostly graded by her tests, which require a lot of inferring (which leads to a lot of disputes). Study the lecture notes carefully, possible to get a B or C but still hard.

She is a great professor and you can tell she really cares about her students and doesn't want anyone to fail. Her lectures are okay, hw is light. Her office hours are helpful and she offers a couple ways you can earn extra points to help your grade. She even offered to have students' final exam grades replace their overall grade if it is higher.

Professor Hoffman interacts with her students from time to time during lectures which are very enjoyable. There are clicker questions which are basically for attendance purposes. Weekly labs that you do on your computer take about 30 minutes. Personally, the wording of the test wasn't super clear so it made it harder that it should be.

She is an amazing professor at UCSD. While her teaching style can be a bit confusing, she really cares about students and wants to make sure that you will pass the class and understand the material. Study and go to office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took her Cogs 14B and I love her class! She cares about her students a lot, if you go to her office hour she will be really patient explaining materials. Homework is not much, but important for you to understand the materials. Exams are straight-forward. She did teach a bit slower than expected, but she adjusted the syllabus with it.

This class had some of the most poorly written tests I have ever seen. Other than the myriad of confusing typos (in spelling and syntax) the answers were frequently contradictory and used terms never mentioned in lecture. This is unfortunate because the 3 embarrassments of multiple choice tests are worth 80% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hoffman is one of the rare professors that actually really cares about her students. She really wants her students to succeed so she offers extra credit and is very accessible outside of class. I love her lectures as she is very knowledgeable about the material. Her exams are pretty challenging because it requires you to REALLY know the material.

She is a really nice person in general and helps students in whatever way she can. You can tell that she works hard to integrate the lectures and exam materials. Course material is fairly easy. Less topics covered compared to other professors. Participation worth 6% but can choose to opt-out. Exams are fair games, study guide provided.

I love Drew Hoffman. I've taken 3 classes with her and her class structure is always the same: clickers are worth 6 percent but you can opt out before Week 2. Her grading is always super clear and comprised 100% of stuff you can find from lecture slides. However, her tests are only 25-30 questions long (multiple choice) so you miss a few, ya know.

Prof. Hoffman is a great teacher. Her lectures are heavy and sometimes confusing, but you can tell her and she will try to modify her style. The class was difficult for me because I hand not had a a lot of background knowledge for that class. It is vital that you understand the material if you want to do good for that class.

She is a very nice professor, but overall she not that great as a lecturer. Her midterms are fairly straight forward however. During lectures, she almost always puts me to sleep as she never has any flow to them and often appears disorganized. But the material itself is very surface level and basic.
Teaches very well. Textbook is very useful. Easy calculation. Light homework.

His 3 tests are hard, all free response and harshly graded. He has a system that lets you redo one question on each test, which helps a lot. The lowest test score is dropped. A lot of the grading is iClicker attendance, so just go to the lecture and the discussion, and you will get a good grade. Just study, and you will do well on the tests.
iClicker attendance mandatory. Easy to follow lectures was good

His quizzes are graded very harshly, but he gives you chances to retake questions on the first three of four quizzes to earn points back. You also get points just for attending lecture and discussion, so as long as you attend them you will probably pass the class.

The criticism is not justified imo, just wait for upper div bio. Grading is generous, especially because extra credit and exam question redos are offered. Prof. Cooper explains concepts well and is a fair grader, my advice is to word things like he does in the lectures.

Content was a lot and he was pretty nit-picky with grading our answers. I will say though that he provides a lot of opportunities to fix our grades. He has a token system where we can fix a question on a midterm and earn the points back. Our lowest midterm also gets dropped.

Would never take again; he is an extremely tough grader. He likes to grade everything himself, even though he has TA's. Four exams, one final, allows for dropping one exam, 6 Hws, the lowest dropped. Never says why the answer is wrong, just takes a ridiculously large number of points. Final and last exam same day.

nice prof but all his tests are FRQ, with no cheat sheet so just be ready to memorize a lot. he's an okay lecturer but almost all his slides are images and he just draws on them, I had to buy an iPad so I can actually take notes. Wouldn't recommend to be honest, harsh grader. Legit got a 29.75/30 on a hw once. iClicker attendance physical/online
There are better BILD 1 professors whose classes are also easier. Covers less content than his peers too.

his lectures are very clear and concise. he does go a bit fast but he records so you can go back to his lectures whenever you want. everything is FRQ based and he is picky with the grading but as long as you regurgitate his explanations, you will be fine. i-clicker is used for attendance, u get 6 skips, and many chances to improve your grade too!

Knowledgeable and thorough explanations but fast-paced, watching podcasts of lectures to refine notes may be helpful. Picky grading but if you are concise + regurgitate/paraphrase his words from lecture, you'll be fine. Drops one of 4 exams, lowest hw, and offers 4 tokens to redo questions; many chances to improve your grade if needed

Cooper was a decent lecturer who sometimes skimmed topics & dove deep on others, but explained concepts clearly with simple examples. SUCH a picky grader even on hw. Little exam feedback unless you went to OH. Mandatory discussion, 6 hws (lowest dropped), 4 written exams & cumulative final, lowest exam dropped. Tokens for redos, iClicker attendance

The professor explains the material clearly, but the class moves at a very fast pace. While the lectures are helpful, keeping up can be challenging. Exams are graded by the professor rather than the TAs, and grading inflated. with similar answers sometimes receiving different outcomes. Regrade requests are also difficult to obtain.
I think he is a good professor and the discussion work is helpful. The homework is very managebale and you have a week to do it. The content can be heavy but he has a midterm drop policy.

Class is fairly easy and well-organized. His slides are clear and get straight to the point, and while you may occasionally need the textbook or outside resources, most of the material is easy to follow. The token system also allows you to correct work, making it easier to earn a high grade. Not to mention, he drops one of the midterms.

Great teacher, but did go through the slides fast. Certain topics that I would deem easy, he spent days reviewing, but the harder topics he sped through really fast. Remembering terms was great for the midterms and finals. I loved his grading; he dropped your lowest test and allowed you to redo 1 hw or test question 3 times a quarter.

The professor knows the material well, but the lectures moved very fast. Exams and homework were all free-response, and students had to show every step. Even small missing steps could lead to lost points.
The professor explains concepts, but the pace and expectations made the class feel difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clear, concise, amazing lecturer. Take this class if you want to really know the content, it was not an easy A for someone who hadn't taken bio since freshman year of high school. TAs were awesome and willing to help. If you just want to pass, you might want to take Ochoa's class instead. Everyone is willing to help, but grading standard is high.

Great teacher if you actually want to learn. if you want an easy A, there are other teachers that are easier and have open note quizzes and extra credit. However, if you need to know the material, his lectures are good and its easy to pass. He curves exams when necessary and the final exam was EXTREMELY easy. Study well for midterm 1 and use tokens
This class is super easy if you just do the work. A lot of the midterm/final questions ended up being recycled from section discussions and previous homework assignments.

Lectures are very content-heavy, but podcasted. He explains things pretty well. Exams are free response and they're very picky on points but in my opinion the material is not very difficult because Cooper tells you what to study. Curve is decent. The HW is similar to the midterms. Discussion is optional.
Very lecture heavy, but he records them so you can always go back if you miss something. Can be annoying with grading, very transparent with deadlines and test dates.
Better for BILD 1 than anything else. He talks fast but kept the class interesting. No surprises on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Cooper is amazing at teaching the fundamentals of biology at the microscopic level, and the class is easily understandable. But he is very scrutinizing with the free question exams and homework. Make sure you answer the questions concisely with the correct info to get full points.
I really liked him as a guy, and this is the easiest class ever, but my god, he's a picky grader.

Assignments and tests are difficult because they're all free response so you really need to understand the content to do well. There are specific points he'll want you to mention for the points. He has a token system that allows you to redo 4 exam questions or extensions on hw. Overall engaging lectures and VERY helpful TAs and discussions.

The lectures are pretty true to what's on the exams, and the discussion worksheets/hw are extremely helpful for the exams. Although the exams are open-response only, chances are you'll do fine if you try in discussion and listen to the lectures. Pretty even distribution of credit among attendance, exams, and homework; lowest unit exam + hw dropped.

Materials posted on canvas are clear and decent. Good lecturer, humorous guy. Lectures and discussions are mandatory. HW is about biology mechanicson class, and there are only 6 HWs. However, exams are toughly graded, so you have to use the same language that he uses on class. Recommend you to take all the captions from lectures and review

Professor Cooper has amazing lectures and has funny comments/thoughts, and doesn't assign reading. However unlike other BILD 1 professors, he does free response exams instead of multiple choice. Moreover, you must know the material and concisely write your answer to get full points. But if you pay attention and study, you'll do great with him.

The class material itself isn't hard but he expects very particular keywords but tbh the lectures themselves cover that so i dont think it should be an issue. He does goes fast but you can and should rewatch the lectures + he cancels classes if we're ahead that week. Attendance is mandatory but you get 7 absences. lowest hw + midterm is dropped.

He has a different setup on his syllabus than to what he expects you to do in class. His attendance is unfair. He is a good biology teacher but very restrictive about grading. If you don't answer it like he did he doesn't give you points.

Tests are very fair, and you can use "tokens" for a redo on a problem for a quiz/homework. His lectures are clear & interesting, and he was a funny & super nice prof! Make sure to take detailed notes as explanations for quizzes and homework need to be specific.

Prof Cooper is definitely one of the better professors I've had at UCSD. I'm not sure why his rating isn't higher because he genuinely made this class so easy to get an A in. Loved his grading policy. On unit exams, there are 6 questions but you choose 4 to answer. Pls don't listen to the negative reviews. Just put in the effort and you'll do well!

Professor goes through lecture so fast, but they're podcasted so rewatching is a must, especially because exams ask about very specific details. Grades are based on more than just exams which is nice (lecture participation, discussion, homework, exams, and the final).

Cooper's lectures are definitely important to go through because he doesn't have a lot of information on his slides, but the class itself was super easy to follow and lots of opportunities for points. (your grade isn't just exams) He also has a token system where you can get points back for homework and exams if you get a question wrong.

Great prof, very well organized and structured. Requires iClicker for class, for attendance. He gives homework, and 3 tests+final, and he gives grace on most of these assignments "tokens". Same thing with discussions just a worksheet that needs to be filled out in person w/ group (graded off attendance) or asynchronously (graded by accuracy).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: His exams were 8 FRQ questions, where you chose to answer 5, the 2 midterms were pretty easy if you memorized the mechanisms. I LOVED his teaching style and lectures. The token options for hw and exam q's were great, u get 4 tokens. The hw toward the end was a bit difficult, and the final was a little challenging. Make sure to take indepth notes.

I don't understand why Prof Cooper's rating is so low; he was a wonderful professor. His lectures were so clear and engaging despite the difficult material and I felt I learned a ton. Clickers were participation-based and exams were super fair/reflective of material and homework. He was also funny and clearly wants everyone to succeed in biology.

His lectures move fast, information isn't clear or written out (pictures mostly), his grading is tough, and he doesn't allow cheat sheets despite having THREE midterms (the other BILD1 teachers allow it). Even if we hit a rubric point, if anything was slightly off, he'd dock points. Discussions aren't mandatory, but the assignments are.

Personally, I LOVED Cooper. Felt like I got an in-depth on BILD 1 topics because of the grading criteria. Yes, he is nit-picky when it comes to grading (not to wordy responses, key words/phrases you have to put down), but otherwise it's not bad at all. He has "tokens" for you to use to recover point loses (from attendance, midterms, hw).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor, a great class. I really recommend taking bild 1 with Cooper. If you just go to lecture which is already mandatory you will do great in class.
I had this class at 8am but it wasn't too bad. Average difficulty, iClickers required and attendance is mandatory. Lectures podcasted, discussion part of grade so easier if you go in person.

Class and tests were not bad and you were able to correct your exam questions with tokens but good luck getting any assistance or guidance when something messes up. My roommates attendance was messed up on his part and he laughed at her and my test regrade portal closed early and he never responded to my 5 emails or walked away.

DO NOT take him for BIMM 101. He is the worst grader for homework, a big chunk of your grade. Assignments where I'm marked off for not being specific, and then I'm as specific as possible, and he marks off 40% because my answer was "too long." There is no pleasing this guy, he mentioned in lab that he wants us to suffer when it comes to homework.

His lectures are kinda bad because he would speed through the important stuff and only have like 1 photo on the slides. But, if you are a quick writer or already know the content, his exams are fair. There is also a decent amount of stuff graded that your exam scores don't have to be perfect.

Professor Cooper is amazing! Highly recommend. His lectures are fun and interesting. His tests focus on understanding rather than memorization, all short answer questions, no multiple choice. He does take attendance but his lectures are fun. He does not require a textbook. Discussions are also mandatory, but very helpful to prepare for tests.

Prof Cooper is reasonable. There is a small curve for exams although the course grade isnt curved. Very nitpicky when grading so you must hit the buzzwords. Everything is FRQ so you actually need to study. Put in more than minimal effort so you will be okay. I didnt take the class as seriously in the beginning and that came back to me, just study.

For everybody complaining, you clearly put zero effort into the class. Genuinely the easiest class i ever took. His grading is SO reasonable. Homeworks are once a week and take 30 mins max. The token system allows you to regrade midterm questions making it super easy to get A's. The prof is energetic and funny.

He deeply loves what he teaches and wants his students to know everything. The grading is harsh, all exams are written response. Section is mandatory unless you want to do it by yourself and be graded on correctness, not completion. Attendance is mandatory he uses iclickers.
This teacher is picky when grading assignments and doesn't respond to emails.

The tests are all free response with the grading criteria being all over the place. People would get knocked points while others got a full grade. He's very funny and very nice but it seems like he tanked peoples grade on the final on purpose since most had A's. He never returned the final after grading and never responding to emails asking for it
a funny teacher, midterms are fairly graded and curved. He did well on explaining the content of the course, making it pretty easy.

class was straight forward as a bio major that did not take ap bio in high school. class is structured very well, homework is graded fairly and on accuracy. both mid terms were slightly curved and you had chances to go back and redo one midterm problem using his "token" feature. gives out 4 tokens a quarter to redo a midterm or homework problem

I don't know why people are upset at Andrew Cooper for WI25. The course consists of 6 Homework assignments which take 30 minutes each, just make sure they are refined and it is easy. Discussion in person is based on completion, easy. Tokens make your midterm grades both 100% if you just study. The final is just a little harder. Super easy class.

Professor Cooper was a cool professor! Class was a breeze, but I wish I studied harder for exams. With the regrade tokens, you basically have 3 freebees for: turning in late assignments without deductions, redoing an exam question for full/partial credit, and free extension. Exams are all written but you only have to answer 5/8 questions!

Cooper was the best teacher I have had at college. He actually teaches properly and what he says in lecture is what is on the test. No surprises. Listening in lecture is all you need to do well. He can be a hard grader but if you focus on his lecture content you should be set up for success. He also records. Can be very forgiving.

Despite what the other reviews say he's a good prof. Is his grading strict? Yes it is. Course is info heavy but not impossible. What he says in lecture directly correlates to the exams, even the TA's say this. He's entertaining and funny, he is very open to questions. You need to put in actual effort in this class not for people who need an easy A.
Unreasonable
Wouldnt take again.
Most petty and unreasonable grader I've ever experienced.
Fine lecturer. Grading is nearly impossible to compete with.

Fast in lecture, with heavy lectures notes, and tough grader on all assignments, for quizzes he only give out very limited questions that's only from a couple topics when we were told to study all 5, didn't specifically tell us which part we should be more focused on, aware of vague instructions
he was actually pretty solid fr

He had great lectures and a genuine passion for teaching. I took BICD100 as a first year and ended with an A, but beware that he has very strict grading standards. You can't imply things on exams, you must say them explicitly. He taught very well and his exams were fair, definitely my most interesting class--I actually enjoyed going.

He always brought a vibrant energy to the lecture room every day. He was really nice, but his grading policy is strict. You accumulate points based on specific information you put into the hw, and your grade depends on your ability to answer FRQs well. Midterms were semi-difficult, and the final was not too bad. Take if you want to KNOW genetics.

Good lecturer- entertaining and passionate. Mandatory lectures but he does offer a fair # of absences. His hw grading criteria is specific, but helps with test prep. Test is very fair- he gives you the recipe to solve it during lecture, just make sure you know how to utilize it. He also offers tokens which is a great opportunity to re-try problems.

Do not take this professor. You will get knocked down so many points on the homework if you're not very specific. He was so sassy and rude. If he is your only option, don't bother taking his class. Just wait till next quarter for a better professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The lectures are very interesting. Attendance taken through clicker questions. The midterm exams were not bad as long as you practice the topics given in the homework questions. Discussions are mandatory, but usually do not take the entire 50 minutes.

He is an amazing professor. I took BILD 1 with him and i immidiately enrolled in BICD 100 when i saw he was teaching again. Very clear power point and good grading system. Its almost impossible to fail the class and there are many chances to get extra credits. You also get the grade back fast and have chance to get a regrade. HE IS AMAZING!!!!!

He is a funny professor but isn't clear on his grading criteria. He docks points on assignments without any clarification as to how you can correct your answer in the future for possible exam questions. Exams are fairly straightforward, and the format is lenient.

Best professor I have had at UCSD. Super passionate about bio and genetics and is very kind and funny, I always looked forward to going to class (even at 9am). The content is a lot but if you put time in you will do great. The exams are clear and reflect the material (discussion sections are great practice). 10/10 would take a class with him again.

The professor made the final exam unreasonably difficult to tank students' grades. Homework and midterms were manageable, but the final was a nightmare. Definitely use unstuckstudy and other study tools to ace this class.

Literally one of the worst professors at UCSD and the kind of person who takes pride in the fact. He will find any and every reason to take points away and completely does not care how well you grasp the concepts. For example, his questions are often super ambiguous or have outright errors in them and he gives you zero leeway for dealing with it.

He got mad that both his classes were doing well so he made the final way harder on purpose to drop people's grades. no +/- and will not respond to your emails. teaches courses once or once every few years so for those taking future classes with him good luck bc he will be out to get you if you are doing well throughout the quarter

Avoid!!! I took this class because he had great reviews from BILD1, but he was actually horrible for BIMM100. Lectures were fine but homework and midterms were graded EXTREMELY specifically. Thought I was going to finish with an A but the final was absolutely ridiculous. 89 is a B in this class, no +/- grades. Save your GPA and avoid at all costs!

Over 65% of the class was expecting an A grade up until the final where it dropped to an actual 35% of the class getting their A. He hated that most of the class was doing well bc he would never respond to emails and would never give you points back for your work. Midterms were fair but the final was criminal. good luck taking him to future classes

Goes through lectures thoroughly but not clear when it comes to grading criteria. First two midterms were fair and relatively simple, but final was much harder. Very harsh grader that will doc points if answers are not the same as the rubric. Would recommend taking another prof that is more caring of their students and fair at grading.

Cool guy, always very eager to help during office hours. 25% of your grade is just participation. Rest is homework, that can be answered easily as long as you paid attention in lecture, and exams. 4 tokens for redoing homework or exam questions.  Midterms were easy to get a high grade. Final was a bit harder but manageable

He grades very tough and doesn't answer emails. These are the only critics I have for him. I went to every single lecture, got a B on midterm 1, A on midterm 2, B on final, averaged A on HWs. All the questions are FRQ, which rlly isn't that bad bc partial credit. Yes the tests were hard, but some ppl def didn't put in the work...

A great person to befriend, but not a great professor. Lecturing was cool and all, assignments and exams were fair as he gives 4 'tokens' to redo any question. Midterms 1 & 2 were pretty fair, then he cranked the final difficulty up 10 notches. All your hardwork over 10 weeks and can get destroyed pretty fast.

STAY AWAY!!!! This class was horrible, he doesn't care about what you think, he cuts you off when you speak to him, he talks so fast, he never responds to emails, he's unfair with grading, and takes a bunch of points off even if you answer is correct. Don't get me started on the final, that was the hardest final I have ever taken.

horrible grader and will dock you off points even though u said exactly what the grading rubric says. his exams were fair but the final was not. absolutely brutal and did it on purpose bc he hates giving you points back and a good grade. no wonder hes only allowed to teach classes once or once every few years bc of his horrible format.
Midterms were fine but final was significantly harder. Extremely specific when it comes to grading and no curve.

Emails are not responsive in a timely manner or ignored completely. Specific grading will even deduct 0.5 just for a small difference from his wording. No curve. Late to class for 1 min will cause u to miss a clicker question and sometimes he only does 2 so you still dont meet 75% threshold to get credit for the day. Situations are excuses here
I would not recommend taking this class with him. He is so particular about grading but even i
STAY AWAY!!!

Please do yourself a favor and do not take BIMM with Cooper. His exams and homework are all free response and he is EXTREMELY picky with the grading. Like, you must write what he wants you to write or you are getting a very low grade. We are now in week 7 and I regret taking the class with him because I know for a fact he will not curve.
amazing professor. i came to class with a weaker biology background but that as long as you understand the corse you would be good to go. amazing lecgtures. would take again.

Prof Cooper is funny and keeps lectures (which can be very dense and content-heavy) interesting and interactive. If you pay attention, you will do well in the class. He sets you up for success with discussion and clicker problems that mirror the exam, and he's very approachable. You also get a good amount of free missed classes.

I enjoyed taking this professor very much, his lectures were entertaining but covered content very quickly. If you have taken AP Bio before this class shouldn't be too hard because it would be that and then more in depth. There wasn't too much homework and the tests were graded fairly. Overall a pretty good class, I would take again.
fast lecturer, fair grading policy. review the podcasts and do the practice questions. review discussion worksheets.
cool professor! do the homework and follow stuff word to word and that yo would be good. great professor and makes things very fun!

I had to retake BILD1 after failing it with another professor. Cooper was not easy at ALL but it was a lot better to manage his class having previously taken the class last quarter. I still ended up with a fat C, but I went to a lot of office hours to ask him why my tests were graded the way they were. The TA's were nice, and DI attendance was mand

Prof. Cooper provides us with 4 tokens, which we can use to correct our homework/ exam questions. This was extremely helpful in getting back the points you've lost. I got a 100 on all his midterms, even though I answered a few questions wrong, because he likes to lower his total exam score. Overall, his lectures were extremely entertaining.

I really enjoyed Professor Cooper's lectures and it was clear that he is passionate in what he is doing. He was also really funny in class. But the main problem that I had was how fast he talked. I almost always had to rewatch his lectures to study. He is a picky grader but you will be fine if you do the study guides that he provides.

I really liked his personality in lectures. He was funny and you could tell he is very passionate about what he teaches. My only problem is how fast his lectures were. Learning biology kind of felt like I was in an environment with another language. You could expect to see on exams material covered in homework and discussions.

Great professor and explains the content well, but getting 100% is nearly impossible because he will mark you down for literally anything. Uses iClickers for participation/attendance, but you can miss up to 8 lectures. He's honestly not that bad, just a harsh grader and he can be pretty funny at times.

Cooper is gives great lectures. If you do take him make sure to write down anything he says outside of the notes on the screen, those are usually the most important. The tests are basically what was on the homework. Also you only have 5 hw assignments, but they're worth 30 points each. He has a token system where you can redo hw and test questions.

The class was overall pretty easy. There are only 5 homework assignment for the entire quarter so not time consuming at all. You have to be specific on the tests and homework but if you study with the lectures and the explanations he uses, you'll be fine.

I dedicated a lot of time to studying for this class. He is nitpicky. I wouldn't recommend taking it unless you're a bio major. His lectures are packed with information, the tests require you to explain things exactly as he taught them. Grading for homework and tests is pretty tough. He offers extra credit opportunities that can boost your grade.

Copper doesn't use +/- for grading,which was helpful. He also gives students tokens.We spent them to redo a written exam problem.The exams were difficult to get full credit in the written section since it had to be word for word of what he said in the lecture.The discussion questions end up on those exams, so ask for help from a TA or office hours.

FRQ is the hardest thing in his class because he gave out no rubrics and grades harshly. You have to be as detailed as humanly possible for those questions and don't leave out any vocab or steps or explanations to get full points. The final felt easier than the midterms though. Use the tokens, they're grade-saving!

The professor is pretty good at teaching introductory biology to even non-bio majors who might be taking it for GE requirements. He dropped a few questions per midterm and a bunch from the final allowing me to score above a 100% on all of them. Most people I know who took this class were able to learn and score well.His lectures and slides are good

He gives good lectures, but talks very fast. The good thing is he has podcasts out so you can go back and watch them. Although he is a tough grader, he makes sure you know the material very well. You have to put the work in, as this is not as easy class. If you do not put in the effort, your grade will reflect that.

This professor is ok! Lecture heavy class, can be a tough grader and wants your explantation's on homework's and exam to be verbatim to how he explains it, so take good notes. There is ALOT of memorization, unlike some of the other BILD teachers, there is no cheat sheet. He cracks jokes during LE, but most times is focused on teaching & fast paced.

If u put in the work studying & going over lectures, u should be fine on exams! 5 hws total, iclickers for attendance. lecture isn't mandatory but i def rec going bc he can go fast thru the slides! he gives u 4 tokens for the quarter (to use for extension/redo on a hw/exam q). watch podcasts & go to discussion irl for full credit! super chill guy

Great professor over all but can be a harsh grader if you didn't use his language when it comes to homeworks and tests. Lectures are recorded. Nice teacher and great lectures but he goes extremely fast with no time for distractions. in person discussions are graded by participation. I enjoyed learning though because he explains concepts well.

Overall Prof. Cooper does a good job at explaining concepts in lectures. Attendance is taken by iclicker but there is a certain amount of unexcused absences that you can get. Can be picky about small details, but it will be discussed in lecture. As long as you put in good effort and go to lecture/watch lecture recordings you should be fine.

Professor Cooper is great and knows what he's talking about. I like how concise he is with his lectures but at the same time he can move too fast sometimes, which is okay since all the lectures are recorded. He also gives a lot of opportunities/flexibility with assignments, exams, and attendance. It's hard work but he provides the resources.

If you're not a Biology major, this class will be very hard regardless of who your professor is. He is such a hard grader on exams/assignments that if you do not basically write down what he said in lecture verbatim, you will get points deducted.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: BILD 1 itself is very content heavy so it can be hard to fall behind, but as long as you are consistently putting in the effort and paying attention during lecture, the class isn't too hard. He genuinely cares about his students and is very accessible at office hours. He also lets you rewrite the FRQs with his token system and has extra credit.

I was scared to take this class at first because of the mix reviews but he is amazing! His exams are not difficult and straightforward;he doesn't try to trick you with the questions. He is specific about wording but if you have the concepts down its an easy A. Just get prepared to stand in long lines in order to get into the discussion! Great prof!
Really kind professor and will answer all of your questions during office hours. Exams are exactly what we see during lectures. Nice guy!

He is a really good professor and is very witty, and can tell he loves his job. He does speak and move quite fast but gives podcasts to rewatch lecture if needed. Does grade very particularly and wants you to hit every single point about that one subject. Testing is a reflect of homework and practice problems. Is a hard class but would take again.

Goes pretty fast during lecture and uses iclickers for lecture attendance. grading is extremely sensitive to particular wording on tests and homework so even if you get everything right expect to not get full points. he curves fair but dont think its worth it. going to discussion is also a war zone so be cautious of that.

Is a good professor, and I believe that he prepared me for BILD 2 because he makes his test free response and BILD 2 is a free response. He is also a very passionate teacher. I believe that this is a good class to take if you are some sort of bio major because it teaches you how to be specific.

V polarizing. His lectures are simple and easy to follow, homework assignments directly relate to the content covered in class, and he is a bit witty at times. However, his exams are graded very harshly w/ solid 95% or above on all hw you can expect to get a ~70% on midterms, worse in finals, which overall lowers the grade significantly.

Cooper is an incredible professor! All content is covered in lecture at a perfect pace with questions incorporated in order to further understand content! He gives homework that is very representative of what is learned in lecture (4-5Q) and that homework prepares you extremely well for exams! He is AMAZING! Makes learning fun and easy!

Go to both the lectures and discussion it will help your grade in the end. Professor is very passionate about what he teaches and may go on rants so be ready. Take advantage of the study questions for each unit and study well before the test (questions are all in FRQ format).

Don't take this professor. 

Trust me.

Prof Cooper is evidently very knowledgeable and does provide you with all the information to succeed on his free response exams.  My biggest tip is to do the free response homework using the podcast of his lectures to get the wording as close to what he said in lecture.  To do well on exams, do all the study questions, write them down

Cooper grades based on free response. The key to doing this is to doing the study guides and word vomiting. If you're not a strong writer, I wouldn't take the class. He's a great lecturer and I was very interested. If you can write well, you should be fine as he explains the material well and I learned a great deal.

Cooper is a passionate professor but is a harsh grader. HW assignments, midterms, and final is all free response and his LE and DI are mandatory. HW assignments are worth more than the final and final is 20% of your grade. Drops one of the HW assignments and drops 3 absences from LE.

Professor is fair and can teach well! If you show up to class/discussion and spend some time on the homeworks there is no way you will fail. He makes the class challenging but not impossible. Would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is passionate about biology but you literally have to read his mind in order to get full credit on homework assignments and exams. Very heavy lecture-based material. All assignments and exams are free-response and have no grading rubric. Good luck to anyone who takes him.

Amazing Prof! Love his style of teaching, everything is clear and going to discussion is very helpful. You will do good on the tests if you attended lecture; lectures are very detailed and most of what's covered in class will be on the tests.

He's really understanding and easy to talk to. The tests allow leniency on what subjects you feel you know the best and they're open note and online! The feedback helps you a lot to answer future questions and the TAs are so helpful! Overall,I would take him again, no question! I also love how the lectures outline exactly what will be on the test.

I really like how Cooper structures his lectures, and assignments and tests. He is helpful during office hours and will explain things again if you're really confused. Exams are difficultly graded but honestly they're questions you can find right off the lecture so as long as you take detailed notes you'll be fine.

Extremely tough grader, docks pts for incomplete sentences/grammar on exams (didn't know this was an English course?), docks pts if you answer correct but uses one wrong word, 2% ExCr for CAPEs if 85%> of class submits, not accessible outside class, zero excuses for late submissions.

Professor Cooper is passionate about the subject matter at hand. He is a tough grader and rarely gives full points on an homework assignment. Homework and Exams are free response. Free response can seem fairly easy especially if you study your notes, but your answers need to be detailed EXACTLY how Professor Cooper states it in his video.

It's hard to get an A, simply because the class is graded very specifically. You have to write every little detail on the midterms in order to get full credit, but you have to remain between a 4-5 sentence guideline. It's hard to know exactly what it wants, but the class itself isn't very hard.

I regret taking this class 100%
The exams seem easy until they grade it, you may think you did well on them but turns out you forgot to mention small details that were not even part of the question. I disliked taking these exams, all these small details that seem insignificant end up being crucial for your final grade. Awful experience.

Way too picky on grading. I made study guides for every unit based on lecture outlines & homework q's and listened to podcasts to take notes word for word and still barely made a B. He acts like it should come naturally to everyone and despite critique on his methods, won't adjust. Do not recommend!

The class average for the first exam was a 74% and 69% for exam two. He said this is typical. Class averages that low are indicative of the high specificity with which he grades. It's hard to believe any professor that continually sees students performing poorly feels as though they are doing a good job at teaching and grading. It's demoralizing.

SHEESH, they were not exaggerating when they said that Professor Cooper is a tough grader. In order to perform well on his exams and homework assignments, you should write down what he says word for word during lectures because his questions are SOO specific. This class is all free-response & no grading rubric so take that info as you will.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Cooper was an amazing lecturer and teacher. I absolutely enjoyed his course. While tests were graded somewhat specifically, attendance of lectures covered everything you needed to know for the homework and tests. The course was well organized and clear what the expectations were.
tough grader but overall a great professor as he's understanding

Coming in to this class, I had taken Honors and AP Bio in high school, so I felt prepared for what was thrown at me. The grading on tests and homework was specific, but as long as you take notes and look back at the lecture videos, what is on the homework and tests is often right in the lectures word for word. Would 100% take Cooper again, so nice

YOU WILL NOT WANT TO TAKE HIS CLASS RUN his tests are all free response, and his grading rubric is so detailed It is very desperate for someone like me to take his class. I study very hard for the class and every time the result is lower than my expectation. EVERY TIME!!! Don't think as long as you study hard you will pass. That is not the case.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I love Prof Cooper, he's a very engaging lecturer and very nice to talk to outside of class. His lectures are clear and concise, but I will say his grading scale is pretty hard. It's a bit hard to get full points on work and exams (which are all free response).

Multiple grading scales for the testing aspect of this course, but everything is free response. Clicker questions during lectures and mandatory discussions for participation points with no way to make them up. Nice professor, just a tough grader on hw and tests
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Cooper is a really great lecturer. In fact, I would definitely take a course under him again if such an opportunity opens in the future. He always keeps everyone intrigued and hooked on the concepts. On the downside, the grading criteria is not stated on FRQ exams and you may lose crucial points if you fail to mention one word or phrase.

Yes, you have to be very specific on the exams, however I think this class isn't that difficult, you just have to be very fast when taking notes. If you can't keep up with the lecture, there is a recorded podcast that's posted, so it's not impossible. My section has both online and open note exams, so as long as you have good notes you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: It is also week 7 when I write this. Cooper is a friendly prof. but the exams require you to write very specific things to get a good grade. He record's his lectures so there's podcasts that you can look back at. The exams are VERY similar to what the lectures cover BUT they are graded hard. There are 4 midterms & class is mandatory .

At the time of writing, it's Week 7. As many other rating say, the HW and tests are graded very harshly. If you don't read his mind exactly, you will lose a lot of credit. He also talks very fast during lectures and sometimes once-overs extremely specific language that's worth 2 or 3 points on his 35 point exams. Exam 1: A+, Exam 2: C (BE WARNED).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really like Professor Cooper's lecture style. He speaks quickly but is very energetic and organized. He also occasionally includes ethical issues in lectures which is important for science! As everyone here said, very tough grader, but if you are extremely precise you will be fine. (It's open notes!) Note that exams are also free-response.

Professor Cooper is an amazing teacher. His lectures are really clear and make biology way more digestible. His tests are tough though and it can be difficult to answer free-response the way he is looking for. If you do all the learning objectives and take good notes you'll be set.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I liked Prof. Cooper's lectures and thought they were very straightforward which I liked. However, his tests were unreasonably harshly graded and you'll lose points for not being extremely specific so it's really hard to get an A on the exams. Wouldn't recommend.

Professor Coopers lectures are pretty straight forward, however when it comes to tests and assignments, you have to be extremely specific with your answers or you lose points. Honestly wouldnt recommend him unless youre really confident in biology.

You can tell he cares about the material, but his criteria is way too harsh. If you dont say something exactly how he wants it, you wont get credit. Also, between labs, lectures/participation quizzes, homework, and writing assignments, there is always something due for the class.

His tests were difficult because he was looking for very specific answers and they have to be around a paragraph long. But his lectures were mostly just him talking and explaining the pictures that he put up. For me at least, it was hard to just listen to him explain it and then try to write down what I heard because I am not an auditory learner.
The guy is so rude and condescending. He's unapproachable. His grading is unfair. This is the worst class and prof I've had here so far.

His exams are all free response meaning you need to know the material WELL. sometimes he doesnt even explain things well and then when you ask him questions in office hours he makes you feel dumb (like you should know it already). the IAs definitely help more than the professor himself so I would recommend going to discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I want to preface this by saying you will learn a lot from Professor Cooper. However, grading is ridiculous. 75% of your grade is 4 exams with 3 worth 15% each and final worth 30%. Rubrics for these tests are very strict and you will get no points if you don't mention exactly what he wants even if you understand the concept. TAKE VERY GOOD NOTES
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Andrew explains concepts really well in the class videos. We don't get +/- in our letter grades, so you can get an A with 90. As long as you listen carefully during the lectures, take good notes, and review before exams, it is possible to get an A although the free-response questions can be difficult to answer sometimes. He cares about students!

Solid professor! Yeah, his grading rubric is very nit-picky, however, I feel like as long as you studied what you needed to and watched all the lectures you'd be good for the exams. CREATE A STUDY GUIDE WITH HIS LEARNING OBJECTIVES AND THOUGHT QUESTIONS! TRY AND ANSWER THEM ALL WITH AS MUCH DETAIL AS POSSIBLE! YOU CAN ACE HIS EXAMS IF YOU DO SO!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Really good informative lectures. He knows his material well. Always was available during office hours. My only complaint would be that the grading rubric on the tests was a bit unpredictable.

Dr. Cooper had great lectures (all pre-recorded) with the only attendance a 4 question quiz (2 attempts allowed). His grading system does not includes +/-, so an A is 90%, but he makes you work for it. The grading is nit-picky, but getting low-As is achievable if you understand the material. Discussions mandatory.

Very solid professor. I took AP bio and didn't understand a thing, but he has clear explanations, easy to learn from. My only gripe is that the tough grading, you have to be very specific in the way you word things. However, he does allow for test corrections and is fair. STUDY HIS LEARNING OBJECTIVES! If you can answer those you'll do just fine.
His grading is all over the place and unreasonable

His lectures are pretty good, but the assignments and tests are extremely unreasonably strict and he expects every single detail to be mentioned. STAY AWAY AT ALL COSTS. Take any other prof. I enjoy biology and learning about it, but the grading criteria makes this class much harder than needed. Seems like he wants everyone to fail.
