reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I like his lectures a lot and he explains concepts well. However, tests are overly difficult and he has a strict grading rubric :/
bad grader, bad tests, stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Decent lectures but grading rubric for tests is heavily flawed. Test questions are very broad yet he still expects every single minuscule detail. I wish the test questions would just be more specific. It's always a guessing game what information to include and what not to include in an answer. Stay away from this prof if you don't want a headache.
bro is buns stay away i warn you. if youre not 100% right youre 100% wrong
His grading criteria is so flawed, his lectures and the rubric for tests dont match whatsoever avoid taking of you can

You can tell that Professor Cooper is really passionate about Biology. He honestly is a great professor and his asynchronous lectures are helpful. However, his exams and assignments are unnecessarily difficult. The topics are straightforward, but the grading criteria will be so specific that you are bound to miss a lot in your answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: (taken W21, remote) Lectures are prerecorded/asynchronous and there's a short quiz after each one . The lecture is divided into 2-3 shorter videos, which is nice and makes them easier to watch BUT the sum of the videos is almost always over the 50 minute lecture window. His grading is super strict, down to the 1/4 point.

This class is horrible with him. Almost every day of the week something needs to be done for the class. He has so much attitude. He looks for any petty reason to take points off your quiz scores. Sign up with another professor because BIMM101 is not supposed to be like this.

He's a nice guy - quite passionate about his research and caring towards his students, and generally makes for some interesting conversation. However, his grading for tests is SO NITPICKY and his exams were all time crunches too. Annoying because the concepts are not so hard, just that explaining in your own words simply isn't enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: seems like an ok guy but his grading on tests and homework assignments is extremely and I can't stress this enough, extremely nit-picky. Literally takes the fun out of the entire class. pity
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Tough Grader if you don't word things the exact way he likes, Dropped this course after receiving an F on first 2 assignments, he thought he was being reasonable.... this is not a course to take if you want an A, steer clear of this guy if you want a decent GPA. Gradescope exams make sure that right answers get marked down if worded wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He failed to take responsibility for the TA misleading his students. Our TA told us one way to solve a particular problem which was incorrect. He did not compensate for grade, and said that the lab manual has the right method, even after the TA confessed his mistake to him. He fails to take responsibility for his TA misleading us.

Don't take this professor. He is more concerned with ensuring not all of his students are doing well. He stated as such: I grade quizzes like this because you're all doing too well otherwise. Many of his questions are quite broad. Success comes with accurately predicting which direction it was he wanted you to take. Lengthy answers lose points.
I would not recommend taking this class with Professor Cooper as the Quizzes are very tough and he is a very tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Take this dude if you want to have engaging lectures and know the materials well. Don't take him if you would much prioritize having good grades over learning. There are other easier genetic profs out there for you. Save your time.

Prof Cooper is not that lenient and has high expectations for his students. The midterms were graded SO HARSHLY. If you were missing a keyword you would lose points. Exams make you think and apply your knowledge rather just fact recall. Must have super detailed answers so you have to really work for your grade. Avoid this prof if you're premed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Cooper is definitely not the professor for anyone. Although he's a knowledgeable prof, his 100% written response exams with a (VERY SPECIFIC) grading rubric wrecked me on the first midterm. You really need to adapt to his grading needs if you want an A, but it's not impossible. You would just need to way more work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a great guy but one of his IAs is rude and condescending. Just pray that you would get a caring IA. He is harder compare to other genetic professors so if you are one of the premed kids avoid him. But take him if you want to actually learn and know the materials. He made the class fun.

Andrew is a great teacher. He's knowledgable and explains things very well. Lectures are engaging even in an online environment. His tests can be very tricky though and the grading is harsh. Definitely not an easy A, but it depends how much you value learning vs getting a high grade. You will learn a lot, but he makes you work for your grade.

he is by far the worst professor i have taken at ucsd. he is way too strict & doesn't let us know what he really expects from us. he is very nitty gritty with what he wants and even marks us wrong sometimes... even when we have the right idea???? also has a very rude and insensitive demeanor. would not recommend EVER! horrible learning experience!

Hes a good lecturer & you learn really well by him. The only thing is your grades wont reflect how much you learned. His tests & assignments are horrible with no curve. He is picky on purpose to cut your grade down really low. You can answer the questions right but get them wrong?? It makes you feel so discouraged & its unnecessarily difficult.

I do think he is a good professor and he understands the material very well. However, his exams are actually tough. You get marked off points if you don't place answers in certain ways he wants them to be. If you miss small details on the exams, you get marked off. He says he doesn't curve, but there is the chance that he will scale the grades.

knows his material well, explains content properly. he has absolutely no regard for students. students scattered are across time zones and he doesnt seem to care (never gave any extensions). Marks are cut for the most specific things-we did math working for a q for the test and he said explaining is words, not math. dont take him. very rude.

I love biology, but his tests were hard! Doublethink before taking this professor, I'm sure there are better professors you can take. He wants specific terminology and if you don't have that, word for word thing down. Don't take him. He's a nice person as whole, his tests are just brutal!

Please do yourself a favor & not take Cooper. Hes extremely stingy with points & takes Chunks off on weekly quizzes. The quizzes are more than just lecture matieral and sometimes he throws in there Q's that we never discussed because we "should know how to approach it from other material." He also has a very sassy personality so OH does nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Cooper is a great lecturer who cares for students (esp. during global events), but his grading is very unclear. Grading criteria and comments on exams and assignments are nit-picky. His exams don't facilitate learning because his grading attacks the smallest details that you missed. Regrades are futile; they are rebuked.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's a good professor, but his grading criteria is way too hard. Our exams are all free-response questions, but if you do not mention all things in detail, you would lose score. There are 6 assignments that count for 10% of the total grade, but we cannot drop the lowest one and he still expects us to reach 93% to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Cooper teaches the material well and lectures are good and facilitate note taking. But, he's one of the hardest graders ever. On hw and midterms, if you don't answer the question in great detail and in the exact way he wants you to, he'll take points off. Feels like he's looking to take points off instead of reward students for knowing material.

The level of detail he expects students to answer his short/long answer questions are insane. Not because they are hard but because he expects you to only say it in a way he wants. He won't or his TAs won't accept anything other than that even if the answer is right. He doesn't give extra credit or do curves. Assignments are graded harshly.

Cooper is a well versed professor though his grading style feels catty in how specific he wants you to be. This combined with how many gaps there are in what is taught makes for a frustrating experience. His recombinant class took up way too much of our time at the end of the quarter where back to back papers abound.

His tests are not fair, while the questions seem simple, he has a very specific set of criteria that you must match to get the questions correct. His grading criteria is unreasonable, and he doesn't take feedback. You may know the subject well but unless you write the test in the specific way he wants you to you will not get points.

Doesnt overload it with the work. Exams are very fair. A couple hw assignments that are representative of exams that are graded and given back before the exams. Easy to take notes while he lectures, love his soap box moments. Very understanding, esp with covid. Take him if you can!

Andrew is a good person but a tough grader! Its a lot of work -spent so many hours on his class and ended up getting a B on metabolic Bio. Dont talk to classmates he takes points off. He made the class harder than it should be and many students were having a hard time trying to maintain the grade. Recommend taking a different professor if possible.
By far my favorite professor that I've taken at UCSD. Exams are based entirely off of lecture slides. Cooper makes class fun and engaging as well.

Andrew is a decent professor but I hate the way the class is designed. The FRQ is graded harshly, and some of the FRQ for the final was taken from past homework assignments or midterms. I wish the keys for the homework or midterms were given out so that students don't just have to "guess" the correct way to answer FRQ's.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Andrew is one of the best professors I've had at UCSD. He's really funny and engaging, and is great at explaining complicated concepts in simple, clear terms. As long as you go to class and study learning objectives you will succeed. His tests can be difficult due to the long answers, but they are always fair and representative of lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor. One thing to be noted: FOLLOW all his rules if you decide to take his class, like putting your last name on the test and upload assignments on time. He is less willing to bend his rules if you break them. His tests are a bit hard, but if you learn everything in his lecture, you will get a good grade. Hope this helps

I lost 16 points on my lab report for not adding color to one of my graphs when I went to go ask him about it he just said it doesn't involve him and sent me away. I came back for a different reason and he just said "NO" it was extremely disrespectful and I felt like he was speaking to a dog. lectures were meh not a very good or devoted teacher.

I personally found this class to be very interesting however the level of detail he says he expects us to know for the exams is a bit more than what's on the actual exam. His TA's give wrong information and if you write them on exam, professor takes points off. I would not recommend taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is a good person but a tough grader! Long essays were graded harshly. If you care about grades so much choose someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He lectures were really good and hardly ever got boring. The exams were really representative of the material covered in class and as long as you understood the material covered, you'd be fine. FYI: He does have clicker questions

Andrew's a solid prof. He cares about his students a lot and is usually present during labs, so he's accessible and always ready to answer questions. He's pretty funny and has good lectures, but he is not easy and you have to work for your grade: lab reports, iClickers, lecture participation, in class and pre-lab quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Andrew is a very good professor! His tests are extremely fair but are indeed a bit on the difficult side. They are also very representative of his lectures. This class does require quite a bit of studying but his engaging lectures do make it easier to learn the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Cooper is such an amazing professor! All of his tests relate back to his lectures!! STUDY PODCASTS!! He made lectures really fun and enjoyable and is super open to answering questions/reexplaining. Given I did have AP Bio as a background, put in some effort and the class is really manageable

Was super super super difficult. I never took AP Bio in HS, and most of the people in the class had at least some prior knowledge of bio, so be wary if you haven't taken bio before. He's a likable professor, but his class as a whole is difficult, with pretty harsh grading on the short and long answers for his tests.

Andrew is pretty funny during lecture and makes biology kind of fun. However, the grading on assignments and tests were not clear at times and I ended up losing points for details I didn't know were being asked for
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Never failed a class in life until I took his class. Lectures arent as clear. Things on the test arent emphasized as much. 2 Midterms and 1 Final. Midterms are really hard if you dont study the right things. IA wasnt much help either. Tries too hard to relate to students. Im not a STEM major, he assumes everyone must be one though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's super funny & a bit eccentric which threw me off at first. However, he's so good at keeping you engaged during lecture even if the material can get complicated. Always willing to answer questions. Not a lot of homework and reading is optional but I recommend it skimming over it. Tests are alright but the free response sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Andrew is a young professor. I think that helps him relate more and connect to his students. He was casual and engaging, largely because the class was small (a lab) which made it fun. The class has a report due most weeks and a quiz every week. He is transparent about the material. If you take BIMM 100 before this, it is easy, otherwise study!!

Cooper is honestly an amazing professor. He makes lectures entertaining while actually teaching you in a manner that is easy to understand. He doesn't complicate biology like many professors, he just goes straight to the point in a clear and precise way. His exams are extremely fair but very long. I definitely recommend Cooper.
Andrew has a great personality and is very funny. He tries to make lectures enjoyable as opposed to a chore! Would definitely take him again.

I can't say he's an unfair or hard professor, but none of anyone's learning was because of him. Like the people who gave him a 5 said, he just reads off of slides verbatim. People like him because 62.5% of our class got either an A or an A+. First midterm had a mistake, so 90% of us got 100%; this combined w/ his policies inflated the grade dist.

Love bro, would take his class again. Although he read straight from the slides, it helped me make sense of the concepts thru hearing him say it aloud. Perfect lecture speed. Requires mildly solid background in basic math. Bare minimum is taking notes and understanding clicker questions. Study hard and you'll definitely succeed :3

Makes physics actually understandable and his exam questions are lifted straight from iClicker and online homework. Just keep track of all the equations thrown at you and make sure you know how to do iClickers and you'll get an A. Super funny lecture slides also, he tries to make it fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Li is amazing. His grading system is super fair and actually gives you a bit of wiggle room. He does do iClicker, but you're allowed to miss 5 classes. I would still encourage you to attend as much as possible because a good chunk of midterm/final content is taken from the lecture slides (he posts them as well) and from the homework.

super easy exam, and a good lecture
if you got good score for two midterms, you can skip the final. 
he drops 5 class attendance
fast email response
perfect professor of ucsd

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have been lucky enough to have. Professor Kennemore is thoughtful and engaging. She seeks to drive meaningful dialect from her students in a way that makes you forget this is actually a class. I loved every minute of the material and her take on it. Truly a great person and an important topic everyone should learn.

super caring prof & is always accessible outside of class. attendance is graded by weekly portfolios (that you can make up when watching podcasted lectures). lectures can drag and readings are long but overall an easy course! graded by weekly discussion boards and a final group project. discussions aren't mandatory and are extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: everyone should take this course. not only is it interesting and insightful, but you're guaranteed to pass (probably with an A) if you put some effort into the weekly discussion boards. no exams, which both facilitates learning and reduces stress. Professor Kennemore is so genuine and approachable, there's a reason all her ratings are positive

This class is very eye-opening. She does a great job of connecting course concepts to real world events and explains things very well. The readings are genuinely very interesting even if they can be sometimes dense in terms of page count. No quizzes or tests. Just try to do the reading and put effort into discussion boards! Great class!

Awesome professor! Very caring and understanding, and genuinely likes her subject. A LOT of reading and writing to be done, so beware if you dislike that. Lectures were a tad boring, but it's still good to attend them. My least favorite part was the podcast, which is a group project, but other than that, I enjoyed the class and learnt a lot.

I loved having Kennemore so much! She is so accommodating and understands that we have a life outside of being students. There are NO quizzes or midterms, and the final is just a group project of a Podcast. Honestly, if you just do all of the assignments and put some effort in, you'll get an A. Also, she offers lots of extra credit. TAKE HER CLASS!

The best professor I've had so far. Gives thorough feedback on all work, explains everything in detail while making sense. You can tell she's passionate on the subjects she lectures on. Genuinely cares about her students, stays as long as necessary after class for questions. Readings can be long, but they can change perspectives. Take her classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Don't hesitate to take Prof. Just go for her! Amazing and understanding professor that cares about her students. Class is an Easy A and structured very nicely. One of the best professors I have had. Haven't had a professor as nice as her. Lots of Extra Credits and not too much work and very interesting topics that are covered. TRUST ME GO FOR HER!
Really really nice professor! Easy A. Reading is heavy but questions and discussions are easy to answer. Absolutely recommend if u want to satisfy GE requirement. I regret changing the grade to P/NP.

Learned a lot and she is passionate about the subject. Readings are long. Synchronous lectures do not have much structure, mainly just sharing how we felt about the issue. Would take this class again. Weekly discussion boards and portfolios, 2 essays, 1 annotated bibliography, 1 podcast group project. Assignments allowed me to reflect on content

Lots of reading, but every page felt meaningful as they serve as tools to think about racism and the fights for liberation. Took the class for GE, but instead fell in love with the material in the process. If you also want to satisfy the DEI and actually want to gain something from it, take LATI10 with Amy.

This class consisted only of turning in work. We had weekly assignments that were super easy and were graded on completion. We had few writing assignments which Dr. Kennemore provided a lot of help prior to due date. She is very understanding and is very lenient. I would definitely recommend this class to others.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I would suggest taking her only if you're heavily into research, specifically on biology and genetics. Most assignments consists of reading, writing, and critiquing research articles. Midterm was multiple choice. In my opinion I think her field is very niche but also very useful to know about, especially with the current political climate today.

Such a caring person and incredible professor. She does important work at UCSD and is passionate about it. She offers interesting courses with exciting content and is always willing to work with students. I highly recommend taking her courses, especially those who are interested in bio anthropology/ epigeneticsLove her!

She is very intelligent and considerate of her students. No quizzes, but there will be essays, student-led discussions (in groups) through presentations, and lots of dense readings (also some easy ones) weekly. She shows you how to read the dense articles so it's not really big deal. She also offers plenty of extra credit outside of class.

The material is very interesting and Non promoted open discussion within class. There were no exams but discussion boards and papers. Many extra credit opportunities were given. I would say there was not a clear prompt for the papers so you could have trouble with what to write and what not to write. However, overall easy DEI class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lectures are very passionate, you can tell she cares about the topics she's talking about. Grade depends on TA and if they like your writing.

Rated on her teaching style and attitudes overall against other professors because there's only 3 options for DOC. She goes over all relevant content very well, lectures are a little on the boring side, can be a little demeaning and passive aggressive. About as professional as a Karen can be. Overall good for getting an A in DOC.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Solomon was a great choice for DOC. She's passionate, thorough, and even gives nudges to what to possibly expect on the midterm and final exams. Despite DOC being a text-heavy and therefore overwhelming course in general, Solomon at least makes it interesting. I would take her again if I could. In general, attendance is key.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All the DOC professors follow the same syllabus so doesn't really matter who you choose. I thought Prof Solomon wasn't the best lecturer (spent a lot of time calling on students instead of explaining the material herself) and could be a bit overkill on certain policies. However, she definitely does care about what she teaches.

She is very passionate about what she teaches, and you can tell she cares. The course is very passable if you put the effort to try, tho there's a lot of reading. Attendance is mandatory for both lectures & discussions, but u get some free skips. She's great, just don't be late (you'll be locked out after 5 min.) & do not whip out any electronics.

You can definitely tell she's passionate about the subject, and her lectures will keep you engaged. Fair grading policies (i.e., 3 unexcused absences allowed, late windows for big assignments). Strict about no technology, but so are all DOC 1 profs. The midterm and final are very doable if you pay attention in class (a cheatsheet is allowed).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Solomon hints heavily at which texts are going to be featured on the midterm and final, so as long as you know those readings well, you can do well on the exams. It's definitely possible to get a 100% in this class without too much difficulty as long as you literally just do the assignments and show up.

Professor Solomon is probably the best DOC1 professor. Her lectures are very engaging despite being mandatory, and explains most of the author's projects that she wants students to understand. TA's are very response and gives good feedback. The writings are relatively easy, just need to hit key ideas and you will recieve full credit.

Although tedious at times, the readings were interesting and easy to understand to use in discussion and lecture.  Explicit grading rubrics are given for every assignment and exam, so it's easy to get full credit.  Solomon makes lecture engaging and follows a nice rhythm.  Show up to class and you'll do great, definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She takes the no-technology policy seriously and might embarrass you in front of the entire class, but her lectures are so engaging, it's honestly on you for not listening. Solomon is very passionate and educated, and presents material in a way that makes you feel bad you didn't do any of the reading. Unfortunately, I couldn't take her for DOC 3.

If you are taking DOC and care about social justice, take Solomon. The DOC sequence is pretty annoying when it comes to assignments and requirements, but Solomon makes it all worth it. She often will stop class entirely to engage in a discussion with students about the readings and topics, and really respects and hears everyone's opinions.

She leads the DOC program and makes everything overly complicated while claiming it's helpful. Her Canvas and syllabus pages are a mess. She could be a great professor if she didn't constantly push her political views. The professors she brings into the program, especially the DEI hire Professor Chapman, are even worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Solomon is very passionate about what she teaches which makes her a great professor. There's a lot of reading and you do 3 essays plus two reflections, although it's not that bad tbh. You're graded by your TA but they're usually chill. Overall easy and enjoyable class. No midterm no final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Outspoken and lectures are a refreshing take on over-saturated topics. She often lets the class be student and conversation driven. She only picks on students who are actively not paying attention or pick a fight with her. Provides extensive videos and help. Super passionate and caring.

Professor is ok despite coming across as arrogant and self-righteous at times. The material felt more than just a history-based writing course, rather more like political reeducation. TA's dismiss counter arguments to the status quo while talking down to you. This course is a clear example of liberal elitism and arrogance. Coming from a independent
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof. Solomon is very knowledgeable in her field and is very clear and concise in lectures. However, classes can easily get boring in my opinion. Homework isn't difficult and you should get an A if you follow the guidelines. No tests.

Dr. Solomon is an amazing lecturer. However, the assignments are entirely graded by your TA, and it does not necessarily require content from her lectures to write (although her lectures frequently offer helpful analyses that will make your writing process much easier). No electronic devices allowed (but this is the same for all DOC1 lectures).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Condescending. Extremely strict on attendance. She asks students to give her positive ('don't be harsh') reviews. Multiple people I know bring outside reading material because of boring lectures and her ban on all devices. Type to stare at you with a condescending smile and say 'are we ready to learn?' in a first-grade teacher voice.

Dr Solomon does not care about her students or the content that she teaches, she just rants on and on about nothing and her lectures don't teach us anything. Our assignments are useful and don't improve students in any way shape or form.

Took her during the TA stikes,that qtr I was working with counselors to email teachers/push back dates on assignments if possible due to family issues. I was asked to attend her office hours to discuss my situation BUT instead she complained the ENTIRE time & didnt offer any help. She pretends to care about students until someone needs actual help.
I feel like Dr. Solomon's lectures were helpful in writing the mini-portfolios and the final essay. Discussion sections weren't helpful but your grade in the class is decided by your TA.

I'm a strong writer so this class was easy to me, but you should be fine even if you're not good at writing. As long as you follow assignment directions, you'll get an A because grading is effort-based. You also have a week to redo an assignment if you get a grade you don't like. What prof you have doesn't matter, content is same for all classes.

dr. solomon was a joy to have! her lectures are very chill but engaging. i always felt comfortable joining in with discussions, and she made an effort to remember everyone's name. sections are mandatory, but just as engaging if you make an effort. barely read course material and still was able to manage incredibly well. wish i could take it again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: idk why the ratings amongst the professors are so equal. maybe just cause the class its self is generally easy? She is by far the best. if you can, take her. you wont be annoyed during lecture and she basically provides a step by step on how to do the writing assignments for an A. annoying that grades are blank tho, like just chilly i want my A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. ASA is a very caring professor. She will make sure to help all of her students and is accessible outside class. Her lectures are helpful for the writing assignments. I definitely want to take her for DOC 2 & DOC 3.

The person who wrote the review below me is tripping, Dr. Solomon was a great professor who is obviously very passionate about what she teaches, overall I enjoyed her class and the DOC 1 course, very welcoming space for first-years, listen to her lectures, this helped me out a lot when writing the DOC 1 Portfolio Project, she's amazing!

Pretentious, narcissistic, condescending.
Can't believe she gets paid for her quality of lecture. Frequent "I had daddy issues" vibe she needs to see a psychologist and sort out her insecurities before teaching a bunch of freshman.

Very caring and passionate. Makes concepts easy and digestible. Sometimes the reading is heavy (for a stem major) and there is a lot of work to do outside of lectures. But she is very forgiving of late work, missing assignments, and such. You will also have a close relationship with the TA. Your TA will make it or break it for your grades.

I think Dr. Solomon is an amazing prof for this course. Her lectures seem so genuine and passionate, you can really tell she cares about the topics she teaches and wants to educate you on them. Grading is based on completion and effort rather than quality or "correctness" so it really is not difficult at all to do well in this class.
The assignments in this class were graded on completion rather than quality. So, as long as you follow the directions for each assignment, you are guaranteed an A.

Had Dr. Solomon for freshman seminar on Filipina-American women of color. SO MUCH FUN!! Super closeknit and discussion based class, with fun guest speakers. We did have a group project of putting together a community event, but it wasn't too much work. Strongly recommend for Filipina students!

Dr. Solomon is a really caring professor and is very knowledgeable. I wish that she would grade our papers and not our TA's because I got a stuck with a really harsh grader as my TA and that is why I got an A-.

I really enjoyed having Dr. ASA as a professor for DOC3. I had Dr. Emily and Dr. Strom for DOC 1 and 2, and am glad to have been able to take Dr. ASA's course this quarter. She is intense but clearly passionate about the material and willing to work with individual students. Her lectures helped with the writing assignments.

She is by far the best DOC professor. Her lectures are engaging and make the students excited to learn. She helped me better understand what exactly DOC is about, and she is intimidating but comforting at the same time. I highly respect her and I'm now taking her for DOC 3.

Solomon is a very good lecturer who captures your attention. She is also like a hawk so dont even think about using your phone in class. Other than that she is great, kind of treats you like a high schooler but its whatever. Shes very respected and many students like her. Grading is really up to TAs so I cant say much about that.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Solomon is arguably the best professor that I have had for the DOC sequence so far. She keeps her students awake during lecture by taking a dry subject and making it applicable to our daily lives. I would absolutely urge any DOC students!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Solomon actually makes you think about the materials that DOC teaches and the impacts it has on society. I personally don't super like DOC, but I understand why it's important we learn these things. Reader is really expensive though, and you can't resell it. :(
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I literally LOVE HER. She is so inspirational and passionate about her lectures. She is so caring and she will help you in and outside of class. Participate and ask questions, you will not regret it. Make sure your TA knows your name and do not be scared to go to office hours!

Solomon is a great lecturer! She is very caring about her students success and offers some extra credit throughout the quarter. Lots of reading and a hard grader of papers but a very good course that actually inspired me.

I LOVE DR. SOLOMON! I took her for DOC 2 and 3 and do not regret it. She made lectures enjoyable and she was like a mom. Before lecture started, she would turn on some music and then would start the class. She is very knowledgeable and I'm grateful that I had the opportunity to take DOC with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Solomon is awesome! I decided to take her for DOC 2 after she lectured for my DOC 1 class and she is so clear in her lectures and the topics we discuss. I feel like I have a better understanding with her lectures than I did previously. We do have the assigned readings, but they aren't necessary to understand what we go over in lecture.
She is not a good professor. She never teaches things clearly enough for students to understand. You will need to guess what she means most of the time. However, she has good TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I really liked Solomon's style of lecturing as she genuinely is passionate about the material, which reflects in her teaching. She really tries to make the lectures engaging and connectable for the students.
She is nice, but she cannot explain things clearly enough for a normal student to understand. I guess I would never talk her class again.
Stupid prof. Won't take her class any more.
She is not clear on her policies but she still emphasize a lot on logics, which she never does. Its the worst prof Ive ever met.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Why can't we bring friends to class with us?
The lecture is sooooo boring. I cannot force myself not to sleep. While it is mandatory, non sense! I don't understand her logic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It is the worst class I've ever taken! This woman is not respected at all.

Really nice, caring professor who wants to make a change in her students' lives. She's well-spoken, energetic, and tries to keep the students engaged. The lectures can get a bit boring and there is a lot of reading. However, by going to class and at least skimming the reading you can do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She care so much about her students and is a super great lecturer. Lots of reading and writing but its manageable. If you take her class make sure you go to her office hours! She tried really hard to learn the names of the students who came to her office hours and she gave super helpful advice on her projects!

The professor is really nice nad very undertsanding, but the topic this year is a little boring and too many readings. Reading responses or drafts are turned in every week. Really need to put in time and effort in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Solomon is a very nice, young lady and very understanding of her students. However, she the head of the CAT department so she'll be busy. Her lectures are not too heavy and her readings were decent. Her class is based on migration narrative and a podcast is the final. She does notecards, although lecture attendance "not mandatory", go!

Totally recommend taking Dr. Solomon, she's awesome.  I really wasn't interested in the class, just took it for my diversity requirement but she made it interesting.  She's a really great speaker,as well as incredibly helpful and available. There's a lot of reading, but what else is new?   Not the easiest A in the world but not difficult!

Dr. Fox is a very kind professor who is very passionate about what she is teaching. However, she spends a lot of time during her lectures reviewing the course structure instead of actually going over content.

Professor is nice + topics were interesting but I didn't feel the prof conveyed ideas clearly. HW readings were long + confusing. Quizzes are take-home + graded on participation. Exams were difficult. No explicit grading rubric (esp for saqs). Grades are hidden the whole quarter. Tested on guest lectures that was confusing + outside scope of course

She cares about her students, and it is obvious. She is organized, takes feedback, and is an incredible teacher. The only con is that you can't see your grades which is quite stressful. If you go to lecture and do the readings, you will do well in this course.

Very sweet prof, seems like she truly cares and takes student feedback. Lectures and readings get a bit repetitive but ngl I did no readings, went to a few lectures and it was fine, discussions are only sometimes mandatory +many ways to make up points +extra credit. Group projects were a little annoying. If you read the syllabus you'll do fine!

Very sweet prof. 1 midterm, final, & 2 group projects. Tests were relatively easy as you're allowed a cheat sheet, which I rec making cus the questions get kinda specific. The weekly readings (needed for the quizzes) were tedious and lecs were kind of boring but not mandatory to go. Weekly quizzes were graded on completion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Lectures were not mandatory. Discussions were only mandatory Week 6 and beyond. Two simple projects. Weekly readings were long... but you can get away with not reading them if you attend lectures. Professor is very kind and considerate :) Class structure was definitely chaotic at times given Fox's freshness as an instructor. Easy midterm and final!

The professor is super sweet and nice, and not scary at all. Her readings, however, can get a bit heavy, but it corresponds with her lectures and they are quite interesting. Her midterm and final are based off of her readings and lecture slides, and contain multiple choice questions and SAQs. Two projects, and she also gies extra credit!

i honestly liked her lectures, and as long as you attended and read the (really long) weekly readings, then it wasn't hard to get a good grade. the exams are worded kinda specifically so the first one was hard to me but the final exam was reasonable. just go to lecture and pay attention. every quiz was designed to help u and was for completion only

Sometimes felt like she didn't know the content, especially when asked questions during lectures. Grades are not disclosed, so it's difficult to grasp how you're doing in the course. She overcomplicated content during lectures, and it was difficult to understand what was expected in projects and exams.

She was inconsistent with her lectures and what was applied on test. She lack a structure of her course, and was often more confusing then informative. Lacks attention and focus which causes unnecessary strain as student, she also lacks being able to decipher when a student is wrong or right, she cant fully answer a question furthering confusion.
She gets distracted easily and spends a lot of time focusing on the outline of the class.Was not clear and concise with lectures. Had students guessing and overcomplicated simple concepts.

Professor Fox is very nice, but as a cog sci student with no interest in design, this class was tough to get through lectures. There are two readings per week, which can be long, and there are two big projects. She doesn't disclose grades until end of quarter, and it is a bit confusing on how to get full participation (lectures aren't mandatory).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is online, and the lectures were straightforward! Grading criteria was also clearly outlined. Make sure you get a good team and submit assignments on time.

This was a fine class, but incredibly disappointing. The class is online and the TAs grade brutally and provide you with zero rubric. Class is simple, but you gain little learning and 50% of grade comes from a final project w/ minimal instruction. Incredibly frustrating and feels super slimy. Don't provide 0 educational value and then tank a grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Was a fairly chill class, You have 1 maybe 2 individual assignments, all the rest which is like 1-2  assignments per week, usually 1, are all group activities, that you really only need like 1-2 people for. If u need the credit take it.

It's a fully remote easy course but not well executed by the instructor. The lecture presentations lack a logical flow, coherence, and many concepts are out-dated.  Overall there's a feel of hastily done lectures with an apparent disengaged attitude toward the students. The professor does not respond to student's emails. Take it for an easy A.
Everything people say about him being lazy and vague is so true. He also spams your canvas inbox like crazy because his course isn't well structured. Easy A tho

Automated class with zero real teaching. Instructions are vague, confusing, and poorly written, forcing everyone to constantly email TAs for clarification. It's frustrating and lazy—feels like a glorified self-study course with no genuine instruction or accountability.
class is fully remote so pretty easy. there is a group project so as long as your group is solid, should be easy.

The class is completely online and is overall pretty easy conceptually. Lectures are by prerecorded videos. Most concepts are very easy, just with a few unclear topics regarding some of the software. Almost all work is group work. Overall a fun class but the TA can sometimes be hard to reach in office hours.

Professor uploads super short video clips that are meant to help you in your group assignments. No quizzes and barely any individual work besides a few assignments. Super interesting class where you learn the science behind surveys and consumers. Professor is hard to reach but TAs are pretty easy to reach and send out weekly reminders.

Very kind professor and you can tell she loves to teach, but here teacing style is a little hard to follow sometimes. The questions are VERY specific;you'd better know your stuff. It's 3 exams total,and all of the correct MC,not just one,and the questions are hard.Last test tanked my grade,so be aware that the tests matter ALOT.Not my fav subject.
She was a good professor, but the exams were pretty difficult. The exam questions were really specific so it was easy to lose points. She had a lot of extra credit which helped my grade a lot.

Amazing prof, has a super stacked background in molecular bio and lectures are great. Test format is tricky, but with the amount of extra credit in the class an A is obtainable (EC is thru HW and lecture attendance).

She literally worked as a postdoc in the lab that won the Nobel Prize this year. She is very much so qualified to teach, and she is really good at it imo. Her lectures are clear, and she explains concepts thoroughly. Offers a ton of extra credit, and you should do it. It literally saves your grade sm. Learned a lot from her!

Love the Prof, she's passionate ab what she teaches! Hard to keep up in class. Always had to rewatch lectures, takes like 3hrs for 1 video. HEAVY on reading experimental results, that's just the course itself tho. Exams are multi-select only. Lectures like she expects you to have prior knowledge in lab. Help idek how I got an A (EC clutched up fr).

Amazing lecturer, knows what she's talking about and is very clear, every class is podcast, but I recommend going in person. Lots of extra credit, and 90 - 96 is an A. Really just amazing lecturer!! Exams are mostly analyzing lab results and not 100% memorization, encourages critical thinking more than memorization. Really solid class love her!!

She is the most knowledgeable professor I've ever had. Amy is very passionate about her job, and she is very caring. The class is hard and she is very fast at lecturing, but the good thing is that she podcasts the class. there is so much extra credit opportunity, and her passion for her job just makes you more interested in the topic.

She teaches like you should already know all of the info. If you don't know the info, then you will feel behind in the class because she expects you to come to lecture with all of the info memorized.Exams are ridiculous, they are select all that apply but no partial credit, just all wrong if you make a mistake. GRADE IS ONLY EXAMS!! "ec" is offered
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor, difficult class

Her teaching style really suited me - clear lectures, a clear topic for each class, no random improv. The class is very material heavy, but she is able to split the topics quite well. However, the exams are difficult, and you only have a midterm and final. That's why - DO THE EXTRA CREDIT!!! So, so useful. Pretty sure that's the reason I got an A.

Great and caring professor! This class is difficult and time consuming, but you can learn a lot. It took me at least 2.5 hour to watch one lecture because I had to constantly pause and take notes. Tests are multiple-answer questions. Lots of ECs and you can get most of them by just participating in class and di. It bumped my grade from B to A+.

Grade was from a total of 125 points, 40 from the midterm, 80 from the final, and the last 5 from discussion section participation and integrity pledge. There was a total possible of 20 extra credit points which were easy to get. The professor was always on topic and cut and clear. Midterms and final were fair and based on lecture content. Take her

Amazing professor! Her lectures are super clear and organized. Professor Pasquinelli also offered practice exams and extra credits, which are super helpful! My advice is: Go to lectures and discussion sections, take some time to organize your notes after class, and you will receive a very good grade!

This class is no longer weekly quizzes and is mainly based on 1 midterm and a final. She offers lots of extra credit and even more to the people who participate a lot, but no matter how hard I studied and made a summary on every lecture including clicker questions, I scored Cs on her exams. The practices definitely help, but it's very experimental.

Her grading criteria is clear, lots of extra credit opportunities, weekly quizzes, and a final (no midterm). Took online, so it may be a bit different in-person. She's understanding and cares about her students. Overall, if you stay on top of the material and don't fall behind, you should be able to comfortably get a B+ or higher.

Great prof, CRAZY DIFFICULT CLASS. Do not take alongside other difficult classes. Be prepared to put a majority of your time into this course. Oh also: DO THE EXTRA CREDIT! Seriously. I failed nearly every quiz and the final exam but that ec saved my grade. She doesn't curve, so do yourself the favor. 8 quizzes (1 dropped), 1 final, and lots of ec.
Final was insane. Lot of EC tho. GOOD PROF. Hard exams.

The class is a lecture class but i felt like i was in a lab class. Also, the weekly quizzes are so difficult no matter how I thought I prepared, i ended up being surprised at my grade. The final exam was cumulative(lec 1-18) with a lot of information to cover. And shes tricky. In my opinion, the exams do not reflect material covered in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I'll tell you one thing, stay away from her class no matter what! Yes, you'll learn something, you'll also be subjected to brutality. She talks about experiments more than lectures as if it's a lab class. She twists the quizzes and exam wording to confuse you from answering the correct one. There are so many downside of taking Amy's class. Good luc
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fantastic Professor. The grading system is clear and there are lots of extra credit opportunities. The slides are very well-organized. Lectures are clear and precise. Exams reflect the lecture material. She only teaches this particular class and this class only. So she knows what to teach.

You have to thoroughly understand and apply what you learned. Attend more than 1 discussion! Talk to her early in the quarter if you are struggling! I did that, and I improved over time and she really does care for every student! I wish I was smarter to pass all of the quizzes, but molecular biology is just a really tough subject overall.

Weekly quizzes very tricky &challenging despite having studied hard & being well prepared. Final&quizzes are heavily experimental based. Lectures were well done & she explains concepts well but seems peeved if people don't understand concepts right away. I put in A LOT of time & effort &felt I had a good understanding,but still only ended with a C+
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures are clear. However, she does not pause to elaborate and seems like she is speed reading off a script. Exams feel like they test ability to decipher tricky wording or diagrams rather then bio content itself. Maybe molecular bio isnt her forte as she focuses more on the lab aspect. Quizzes are brutal, no midterm.... just a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Class is very experiment oriented and she talks REALLY FAST. 8 MC quizzes, 1 is dropped, but they are timed and super tricky. The class is on a 100 point scale and she offers 10-15 EC points which is nice. I feel like she expects students to have a lot of background knowledge so if you have no research experience you'll find it difficult to keep up
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed her class. Professor Pasquinelli is a good teacher and is focused on student learning. Students who say otherwise didn't talk to her to clarify concepts post lecture. She also rewards class participation heavily. Tests are difficult certainly, but they are representative of the course material. Review slides lots and you'll pass!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class is heavily experiment-oriented, so you need to have a good understanding of the experiments she introduces and how to differentiate one from the other. I recommend attending at least 1 or 2 discussions a week to check your homework answers. This class is not easy, but it's also not difficult if you put in the effort. Incredible lectures!

Good lecturer, but basically hides necessary info from students. No answers given to homework online, no answers given after midterm without having to meet directly with a TA or prof, so very difficult to work with if you prefer to work alone. Tests are very difficult and unforgiving. Wording is often difficult to understand and vague.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: 40% midterm. 60% final. 5% extra credit added to your grade for attendance. Up to 1% EC on top of that for CAPES if your whole class does them. Midterm was reflective of the practice midterm and assignments but the final was ridiculously difficult and didn't really match up with the assignments (post midterm)/practice final. Wouldn't recommend.

Class was 40% midterm and 60% final.  Midterm was reasonable and her lectures prepared me for it.  Final was incredibly conceptual and experiment-based, which I was not prepared for at all.  iCLICKER questions and assignments for the second half of the quarter did not match the type of questions she had asked in the final.  Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: No solutions provided for problem sets, threatened students w "video evidence" of students cheating with clickers, hinted that it's probably in our best interest NOT to ask for a regrade since she regrades entire exam and you'll probably LOSE points, impossible exams. Final destroyed me. Oh, and no curve. I've never taken a more unreasonable class.

When most of her class is failing and her excitement after her students studied for days straight is "There were more right answers than wrong answers" because she's overall happy with a C- average. Then comes the final, which was out of box, barely having anything to do with a majority of the lecture content. You sit there, destroyed and ask why

1 midterm and 1 final, practice midterm was similar to the actual midterm. final was completely different from the practice final. tests are experiment-based. know the experiments really well. answers to hw aren't posted on ted, must go to discussion for answers. cumulative final, no curve, good luck!

The test is experiment-oriented, which is really beneficial for learning experiments designing. Professor covered interesting materials and had a proper pace. It is not a easy course, but you can get an A if you work hard.

Decent prof, great at lecturing but she does talk pretty fast. There's no material to read (unless you count the optional textbook), so I wouldn't recommend if you're someone who learns better from reading rather than lectures. She doesn't curve, and the final this year was way harder than the midterm or practice final.

She needs to SLOW DOWN AND TAKE A BREATH. It can be frustrating how she zips through a ton of material without ever  pausing on a subject and elaborating. Just feels like shes throwing a ton of information at you at once, and you try to do your best to take all of it in.

Dr. Pasquinelli is one of my faves. She is very straight forward & reasonable, her tests are very fair (but not necessarily easy). She WANTS you to learn & succeed, & gives you everything you need to do so. Very clear, thorough, & coherent lectures. And very reasonable with grading on tests (unlike some other bio professors). GREAT PROFESSOR!

One of the most well organized, clear, straight forward lecturers at UCSD. Her expectations are very clear and exam material perfectly matches lecture material, although exams are challenging. She is funny, open to question, on top of it with grading and  getting back to you, engaging, and reasonable.

Dr. P is an amazing professor! I truly enjoyed her class and the way she presented the material. Her class was highly based on application of knowledge on experimental scenarios and not just pure regurgitation of the lecture slides. Truly caring. Clicker questions were extra credit and homework assignments were good guide to use while studying.

I've never enjoyed learning so much. She doesn't curve, which encourages students to actually communicate with each other, which is awesome. I wish every class @ UCSD was like this. The material was stimulating and the tests were very fair. Overall, I'd give everything about this class an A+. Oh and thanks Emily, you are a very patient TA. -J

Fantastic professor.  Young, clear voice, uses clickers.  Posts hw questions, practice exams, but no solutions.  She is very clear about what she wants you to study, does not bog you down with useless protein names, focuses on the overall concept which can be tough in mol bio.  Exams are fair, no curve in the class, avg usually falls in 70's.

Teachings & exams are straightforward. This class, like all bio classes, requires TREMENDOUS amount of time and THOROUGH MEMORIZATION. She makes things very clear and easy to understand, & tells you exactly what to know for exam. Dont study excessively. Spend >9 hours a week and should get an A. There was 10 pts extra credit in the final (Fall'06)

Lectures are packed with info, but she knows her stuff and can teach it well.  However, her tests are tricky. Go over her slides and makes sure you know the experiments.  Beware: she doesn't curve.  Overall, not the easiest course, but I learned a lot.  One of the better bio profs at UCSD.

I love biology, but I'm not a fan of molecular. This course was hard and it did not help that the prof posted hw and practice tests without solutions. The tests are relatively easy, but extremely tricky and without a curve! Hit or miss class that could have been worse with another professor, but at least Pasquinelli is nice, if not a bit too tough.
i thought it was a really easy class.  lots of memorization but sections help and office hours help.

She wants you to go to sections and review sessions, so she won't post answers, but it forces you to kinda stay on track so it's good. She is super nice and she REALLY wants to give you an A so make her happy and do the studying. Focus on memorizing experiments...the final was relatively difficult (to the midterm) but still very straightforward.
Great Professor!  She cares so genuinely and is a humble genius!  You will definitely get your money's worth!  I got an A!!!!

Her exams focus a lot on interpreting and setting up experments so make sure you really understand the molecular techniques and how to set them up. She provides problem sets and old exams and a lot of the questions come up again on the midterm/final. She doesn't provide the answers so you have to go to discussion/reviews in order to get answers.
fun teacher

She's extremely clear during lecture, but I don't like the fact that she only teaches using powerpoints.  Her voice can turn into a sleep-inducing drone, but hey, she's better looking than a lot of undergrads at this school so it's cool.
She is wonderful, extremely enthusiastic and wants to help everyone. She is very clear! Go see her in office hours. She is very interesting!

She's ok, considering it's a hard class if you don't keep up your reading, very young prof. compared to most doctors@ucsd. Her extra credit assignment:"WRITE about someone who's related to HER field of study-> C. elegans, if you want full credit! kiss-ass pts!" If she's not the only one teaching mole-bio 4 the quarter, consider taking someone else!
oh my god this was the worst experience that I could ever have in UCSD.................................like PLEASE DO NOT TAKE THIS PROF for real

his class is unbelievably unorganized. he's making up the structure as he goes, which in turn, leads to a mess.

homeworks were given extensions which was nice, but what was on the homework doesn't reflect on the exams. difficult relational algebra stuff covered in class was not on the exams.

everything is chaotic. don't take

In 4 years of (very difficult) Math and CS coursework at UCSD, this guy is the worst prof I've ever had. Constantly condescending to students in every lecture, exams are ridiculously unachievable within the time constraint and cover things NEVER mentioned in lecture or homework. Zero practice problems or guidelines for exam content. AVOID!

awful af. do not take. wants very specific things in his assigned project assignments but when you try to ask questions about what he wants, he says "you are asking for answers now" if the project is not as open-ended as you claim it to be, then give us specific directions like bffr
it's a miserable experience to take his class......

This teacher gave very poor marks. He tried hard to find mistakes in his classmates' homework, resulting in everyone getting low marks. The exam was very difficult, and there was a lot of content that he didn't clearly explain in class. The teacher's lectures were vague and he always asked a question but did not give an answer.

This is the worst professor I have ever met at UCSD. His class actually teaches nothing and he constantly changed his requirements to students. Very chaotic unstructured class content and homework. Sometimes he can't even remember what he said as homework requirement. This is my first time to give a bad thumb on a professor. DONT TAKE HIS CLASS!!!

This professor is not a good lecturer AT ALL. He is unclear, has no direction or context, and he puts people down in class. He uses Piazza for discussion but is wholly unresponsive to student questions. He makes assumptions about what the class knows. His homework assignments are not thought through, open-ended, and changed days before due. 0/10

With all honesty, don't take this professor. He never replies to the emails sent and he only cares about teaching and getting out of there. His exams are online but in honesty, they are quite unfair. He purposely curves by the smallest point even though averages are horrible so it does not impact the student's grade in any positive way.

His lectures are not reflective of exam material. Exams are not a good measure of how well you understand the information. Other BIMM profs are a lot more understanding and provide a lot more grade improvement opportunities and EC. Take anyone else.

Professor Akbari is amazing! The class was graded on 8 of 9 quizzes, each based on readings. Quizzes had 3-4 questions, were open-note, and easy if you understood the concepts. From Week 1, you join a group to present a paper. He's very caring, knowledgeable, and answers all questions. He even gave us a lab tour! Overall, an incredible class!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I think the class was okay. I liked that in lectures he would give real-life examples connecting to his research as well as doing a lab tour. This class is only exams so if you aren't a good test taker then this class may not be for you. Also, I felt like the wording on some questions was confusing. Dr Akbari is a nice person in lecture though.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. This whole 10-week class is based on 3 super difficult canvas exams. The questions are phrased in a way to intentionally confuse you. He seems like a nice, caring professor, but you can tell he does not care about teaching. Avoid at all costs!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Graded on 2 midterms and 1 final. Final is optional if you have the grade you want to receive in the course. Lectures were very surface level compared to the exams. Exams are all on Canvas but you aren't able to go back to a question once you've submit it. In the end, he curved the final very generously but I felt I didn't learn that much.

Exams were extremely difficult, probably because it was online, but still extremely difficult. Averages were consistently in the low to mid 70s. Doesn't let you go back on a question after you've answered it. He also kept asking us to fill out SETs but to "be nice please." Weird but wtv

3 exams (each 100 pts) with 1 drop. I scored over 1 standard deviation above the class on the 1st and 3rd exam with the 2nd exam dropped. Still received the AVERAGE grade of the class bc professor does not curve the final even though he said he would (source: Lecture about CAPES). He should've dropped 1 midterm since final is more comprehensive.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: tbh he's a decent prof and talks about interesting research in class. Lectures are straightforward and recorded. Exams are difficult. Pretty bummed tho that he did not curve the final. Me and a lot of other students included were thrown off by that. pity :/

ia's write exams so tests are way harder than lectures and he curves the first two exams but doesn't tell you until after that the final isn't curved. drops lowest exam score and final is optional but mostly everyone ends up taking it because their grade isnt good enough. problem set answers are only given during discussions too

Does not upload lecture slides before class, only talks for 1 hour in a 1 hour and 20 minute class, exam questions are really specific and difficult. Only 2 midterms and final but he drops one. I felt like it was difficult to understand the concepts through the way he explains them. Seems like a nice guy but challenging class :(

Prof Akbari probably changed his teaching style, i hesitated to take him because of his rating but im glad i gave him a chance. He has no hw, just the tests and the lowest exam gets dropped, including the final. The tests were fair based off of the lectures. He even gave us some extra points in the test if we did bad. Overall, he's a very cool!
Very great lecturer. Ties lecture content to current science. Approachable and inspirational. One of the best at UCSD.

Terrible professor. Inconsistent with syllabus and inconsistent with promises he makes to students. Exams unrepresentative of lecture content. I wish I took this with another professor because I would have liked to learn molecular biology. Save your money, dont enroll with Omar Akbari.

AH! This class was ROUGH! Exams were not very fair and out of 20ish points. 4 exams drop the lowest but even then I always went in feeling confident and ended up doing so poorly. He gave TWO extra credit points?! Doesn't make sense to me. His lectures were hard to get through and I wish I had taken this class with a different prof. Skip!

I would never recommend this professor to anyone. He was very unclear with everything he taught, I would literally rely on the most amazing Instructional Assitant to reteach things properly. There were always minor errors on his slides that the IAs/TAs would catch. The exams were unfair and not the type that actually cares for the students.

must do the readings because of midterm and pop quiz. There is one big paper due at the end of the quarter. Lectures are ranting and story telling. Beisdes that I love his class, it's really opened my eyes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Rona-Tas is well experienced in his field but the class is pretty confusing. 9 HW assignments worth 63% of your grade, final assignment 20%, 5% participation and midterm 12%. Had to buy expensive software programs (SPSS & NVIVO) and the work was hard, but if you go to his office hours he is really helpful and the one on one is worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Grade based on weekly/biweekly assignments (10 total), 1 midterm, 1 final. Very caring, allowed us the chance to try again for a couple assignments that a lot of the class was confused about. Lectures somewhat all over the place. Responds to emails very fast but short responses.

2 in class midterms and one final. There are three short writing assignments. Test material all relates to lectures and readings. I did not do all the readings but attended almost every lecture and got an A. Course offers a good selection of sociology related movies. Interesting lectures. I would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Akos is passionate about the films and our ideas - but ultimately he has joined the dots with the sociology and the films we are watching, and classes could get boring when not talking about the films. I thought he was kind, approachable and a generous marker. A good easy(ish) and enjoyable sociology option. I'll remember him more than the course.

Professor Rona Tas gets to know you personally if you go to his office hours for help! He was very caring and helped me a lot on the computer projects. If you need a research class for Sociology major req, def take this course!
worst professor ever

This class is definitely sociology, not film. The films are there to illustrate the concepts, not to be analyzed on their own. Pretty easy class, fun & interesting prof. Three exams, all short answer (not essay). The questions are grouped based on lectures, films, & readings. If you pay attention it's very easy.

Amazing Professor! I took the class over summer, meaning there were only roughly 10 people in it. His accent is super awesome, and although I agree that sometimes he makes things sound a bit more complicated than they actually are, he makes sure that everyone understands the concepts he is explaining. I definitely recommend him!

I would not recommend this Professor at all. Useless, grouchy, and unclear. I tried to make the most of this class but it was terrible. I have taken 3 of his class and I do not recommended him at all. Also, if you have a family emergency he requires actual paperwork and didn't believe my grandma had actually passed away with a certificate.

Useless class.  I guess that when you take a leisure topic, such as movies, and try to make it into an academic course you end up with a wreck of nonsense that only sociologists think is important.  The professor is good, but this class is time consuming cuz there is 1000's of long readings!

Book sucks; many sociologist have an intelligence complex, so they take simple concepts and explain them in difficult ways to sound smart, so the text won't help. The material is poorly explained b/c he has to move fast. Harder than calculus by far. Midterm crazy hard even with "crib sheet". I hate this class, and you will too.

very enterining and easy! as long as you show up, the material engrains itself in you. all texts are avable on line and the material is super familiar and easy. even though this clasasn't a huge challange, i ejoyed it the most!!

one in class midterm and in class final. watched a film everyday in class. reading topics coordinated with the film topic as well. he seems to know his stuff. okay teacher overall. not too bad of a class, ive had worse.

Professor Rona-Tas does the best he can at teaching this boring subject. Take it over summer. The midterm and final were kinda hard so attending every lecture will help. The information can be overwhelming, but if you have a good TA that should help. His tests are based on the book, lectures, and the CD that comes with the book.

Very good professor. Akos has a charming accent and is easy to understand. Very articulated and extremely intelligent. The subject is extremely boring though. Midterm was difficult and there are 3 assignments. make sure you do the CD exercices. Some of the midterm questions are straight from the CD exercices. I would take his classes again!

Difficult boring class. Professor does give good examples. Make sure you go to class and get a good TA. If unsure go to TA's office hours for clarification. Book was useful, but also boring. Important to learn material for future classes, since it will apply.
kinda boring class. get a good TA and you'll do fine. one midterm, final and five hws assignments. dont need the text, but there is a cd that comes with it that you need.

Lectures are very organized. The hungarian accent isnt that bad bc he speaks slowly and he uses examples to explain things. Midterm & Final are questions lifted from the cdrom quizzes & assignments are found online so you can plan ahead. I recommend taking this class in summer because the boring material is condensed into shorter weeks.

his hungarian accent is distracting, on top of the fact that his lectures are really boring. i suppose it has a lot to do with the boring subject matter, but he isn't very good at teaching either. his examples are not clear, assignments take up a lot of time, and his midterm and final are difficult. not an easy class. his face annoyed me.
Boring class. you have assignments and a midterm and final.  Assignments need to be very detailed.  Midterm and final were not easy. Get Tonya as your TA.  Lectures and discussions are a must.
Not the most exciting class and assignments SUCKED!!!!
class sucked. TA's werent too good. boring lectures
Midterm was hard, but Akos Rona-Tas does a great job making what could be a boring and tedious class into something fun and interesting.
The midterm was hard, allowed cheat sheet, dont write all the definitions on cheat sheet, instead give examples!!! i learned that the hard way : )
Great Professor. Really funny, helpful, nice.
Hot & charming professor. Funny, knowledgable, great sense of humor. I'll take more of his classes!
Long, boring, uninteresting lectures.  His hungarian accent helps only a little.
not very good at answering questions but he's nice and chill

Do not ever judge a chem prof by their 6 series reviews. Tezcan is easily one of the best profs at ucsd, and his course was amazing. He takes time and care to get to know his students, his lectures are interesting and engaging, and he is great at showing students recent research, which most other profs don't. If you can take a class with him, do it

Slow talker in person, recommend watching online lectures in 1.5-2x speed. Two midterms, one final; final percentage can replace the lowest midterm. No curve. HW online. Exams are definitely difficult, low class averages. Discussion attendance mandatory. Math and concept heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Did not adapt to online learning well. Placed lectures online to watch asynchronously and then held office hours during lecture time, which was not very understanding of rigid schedules.

This class is way harder than it should have been. Honestly, Tezcan is a nice person but lectures are incredibly long and nonengaging. He lectures fast and has no time for questions. Homework/workload was definitely good, but tests were extremely difficult and graded by the word. Even if the class average was low Tezcan wouldn't really be bothered.

I felt that Professor Tezcan made this class very difficult. The tests were not reflective of the material that the homework was on and were just extremely difficult. Even though it was open notes and book and I studied I still ended up doing very poorly.

Terrible professor. Was not passionate about teaching, which is clear in his lectures and his rude interactions with students. I have a background in chemistry yet he still made simple concepts difficult and complicated. Tests do not reflect homework or examples in class. Do not take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The work load is light but he's an awful lecturer. I had background in Chem already, so I turned out fine but he makes so many mistakes during his recorded lectures that he just never mentioned again or fixed. He's so terrible at explaining new concepts to students...I don't even know how ppl without chemistry background would even pass his class.
Nice professor but lectures are not really engaging and tests are very difficult as they do not match the homework... and there is no curve

Did not care about student's concerns or wellbeing. Doubled class content halfway through the quarter. Rude to students when they asked questions. Was snarky in response to students not having enough time on the midterm. Please. For the love of god. Take a different professor. If there are no other professors don't take chem this quarter.

Weekly homework and biweekly learning checks. I felt like I learned a lot in the class because he focuses on students mastering the concepts during lectures and is really helpful during office hours. Would definitely take the class again.
