The lectures are super long. He sometimes brushes over things and they appear on the tests. The homework helps out a lot on tests and he gives you practice questions which are also helpful. He was strict and kind of snarky but overall, he is very knowledgeable.
This class was easily one of the most assignment, test, and homework heavy class i've ever taken. He's a good professor just gives a TON of work and grades extremely hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Tezcan is honestly one of the BEST chemistry professors i have had in UCSD. Although sometimes the lectures may get a little bit tedious, he makes up for it with his enthusiasm and his care for students. He encouraged discussion and questions, and for those who say he was impatient, he really only got mad when people were straight up trashy

Professor Tezcan is intelligent and clearly loves chemistry, and wants his students to enjoy it as well. His lectures are organized but may sometimes brush over complex concepts. Midterms and final are extremely fair with extra credit q's. Although lowkey strict and sometimes sarky, he seems to care about his students as individuals.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tezcan knows what he's talking about, but he's kind of rude. He'll stop a 300 person lecture to call out or argue with a student. He's not very understanding either, so if you need an extension you might as well just not ask. Most students get by if they show up to every class/section because attendance is a big part of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you have the ability to take another professor please do yourself a favor and take the other professor. Professor Tezcan is definitely hilarious during lectures, however, his tests are hard and they are not curved. Personally, I attended all lectures and did all my homework but I found myself teaching myself everything by using book and videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Let me be clear. Chemistry is hard. Dr. Tezcan makes this subject as easy as it can be. His lectures are clear. DO NOT be afraid to ask questions, that is why most students fail chemistry. He makes the exams as easy as they possibly can be to demonstrate a basic understanding of the material nothing hard or tricky. will retake him for CHEM 120
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is by far one of the worst lecturers I have had and was mean to students. He would call specific students out in class, and made me feel like I could never ask questions. I am glad I had a background from AP Chem because otherwise, I don't think I would have done as well. Lectures were disorganized, confusing, and not enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Tezcan has been THE BEST professor Ive had so far at UCSD. He genuinely cares for his students by having extra office hours and responding to every single question on Piazza. He made chemistry interesting and taught everything in the simplest way so it could be easier to understand for all.

Prof. Tezcan was very passionate and efficient. Sometimes lectures can get a bit confusing, so make sure you read beforehand. Lectures are really important because he gets a lot of his test questions from things he writes on the board so definitely go to lecture and take notes. He's very caring and does a lot of cool experiments during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Tezcan is a solid choice. He definitely makes you work for a good grade. Two midterms, one final and all exams were fair. He goes at his own pace and teaches rather slow. Doing practice problems and challenge problems are extremely important for this class, but also make sure to really understand and STUDY definitions.

Solid choice. Doesn't go fast and tries to make sure everyone understands. His exams are more conceptual, so go over his slides before exams and do the challenge hw problems. Exams are very reflective of lecture and homework. Go to lecture & do the hw and you should be okay. Also, could curve depending on class average score on exams.

Prof. Tezcan is a pretty good lecturer imo. Mandatory attendance w/ iclicker, but it's for participation only. He's very accessible outside of class time and holds extra office hours, too! His exams are very much a fair reflection of the harder homework problems and topics covered in lecture and class. Textbook not necessary but will help a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I dreaded going to his lectures and found it hard to understand the concepts he was trying to teach on as he went into such detail that was not needed at this intro level of chemistry. Going to OASIS was the only thing that saved me and even then his quizzes were not reflective of the homework. Additionally, he expects you to learn from the book
Best chemistry professor I've had. Clear lectures, fair exams, and fair grading criteria. Extra credit given for challenge assignments. Gives plenty of examples of problems in class.

You'll do well in professor Tezcan class if you do two simple things: attend lecture and do the book problems. Most of his quizzes address concepts or certain types of problems  that are included in the lectures and/or book problems, and if you focus on that you'll be Gucci.
Gave me a zero on a quiz cuz  I was late now I might not pass the class. Do not recommend if you don't want to go to the lectures.

Absolutely love Professor Tezcan! His weekly quizzes are extremely fair with minimal surprises. He also curves generously and gives extra credit! It is evident that he is passionate about chemistry and does his best to make you interested too! I would definitely take his class again!

I would give negative grade to this instructor if I could.  Pretty much the worst one even see in my entire life.  quiz every week, and it not related to the lecture.  memorizing the periodic table. YES , entire periodic table.  having hard time arguing how unfair the grade is. please make your life easier,  avoid this terrible instructor.
Not clear .  Poor methodology. Unorganized. No clear example. Should not be allowed to teach.  Quizzes have nothing to do with lecture material.

I would greatly advise you to take avoid taking this professor, take it the next semester if you can. And to the guy below I'm sorry about your grade, especially since you were so close. But D+ aren't offered at UCSD.

Many questions you are tested on, you have never seen anything like it before. Unreliable at office hours. Terrible book. I wanted to learn but the class made it impossible. I got a D when I was 1% away from a C-, not even a D+? But he let 20% of the class to leave with their cell phones during the final. Avoid if you care about learning/grade.
Should not take this course with this Prof.
His lectures are mostly useless and the TA Was just as bad. His notes on how to do things are not comparable to his quizzes at all. In general try to avoid this teacher.

Professor Tezcan is great. He actually enjoys teaching and really cares about his students. Your grade is based on weekly quizzes, homework and a final. If you go to class and do the problem sets you will do fine. I came into this class with no prior knowledge about chem and ended up really loving the subject. Highly recommend Prof Tezcan.

Nice professor but difficult class. Weekly quizzes do not reflect material in lectures. Quizzes are basically a midterm and final is most of your grade. The only redeeming thing is that he is an EXTREMELY generous grader.

Good professor, relative to the rest of the 'teachers' at UCSD. He loves what he does and is very knowledgeable. The class is a bit frustrating though, there are weekly comprehensive quizzes that don't reflect the material that you have been studying. The questions are very tricky too, nothing is straight forward, and they are very short, time wise
Great professor! Clear explanations and interested in his subject.

Very interested in his subject. Does a good job of explaining basic chemistry especially since many have not taken a chem course for a few years since high school. good lecturer, breaks down material so a complement to the textbook rather than just reading slides. Sarcastic sense of humor. If you show interest great guy but don't piss him off.
i absolutely loved prof tezcan, and he has a wonderful turkish accent. he's really hard and kind of sassy, but as long as you study hard it will be fine. quizzes every week, no midterm. final is 1/3.
There are better teachers that will not confuse you and you will not have to suffer illogical explanations.

He lectures well considering the fact he has to teach such a hard subject. Weekly quizzes are fair as long as you pay attention to lectures and keep up with the reading (although not necessary).  He is approachable, funny, and an all around great professor who has a legitimate compassion for chemistry and the learning environment for his students.

Brutal marking on weekly tests, no marks for attempt no matter what ur methodology unless the answer is exactly right..may as well not ans the question at all-very disheartening. Most of material on tests is taught 2 days before exams. As if that isn't enough time to study, u need 2 know material inside out 2 b able answer trick questions presented

He was new. When I had him he used organic structures no one understood and wasn't very clear. His tests weren't that hard. However, the material is hard so it's all relative. I recommend Hoeger, but he is also a harder teacher. You won't learn as much in Tezcan's class.

His lectures are clear and easy to follow. His quizzes are not hard.. It only seems that way because he does not offer partial credit. BUT! He makes this up with extra credit questions on the quiz. His quizzes are representative of the lectures and the book so go to lecture and read the book. Overall excellent professor! I recommend!
Pretty hard teacher, but quizzes are mostly do-able. He doesn't give partial credit, but he does offer extra credit.
clear lectures..quiz every week but no midterms. pretty easy if you read the book and go to his lectures..lectures the day b4 the quiz is usually on the quizzes.
very clear and easy t follow.

Really interested in making sure his students learn through WebCT. Learned a lot for a new prof. Quizzes every Thurs so you HAD to come to lecture.  Kind of had to go Tues lectures since he explains some things not in the book that'll be on the quiz.  Usually gets mad over people talking during lecture.  But recommend :)
good teacher
hard teacher.
No Comments
No Comments

Class was really interesting. The textbook was GREAT. If you read you will get an A for sure. Professor has a lot of knowledge and her stories from the field are interesting. Lecture really isn't mandatory for a good grade. The only negative to the class is that she does not grade with +/-. My GPA went down when because I didn't get the + I earned.
Make sure to know lecture material and book material . Helpful professor but exams were pretty lengthy and have to know a lot of material.

The material was interesting; unfortunately, Professor Akshoomoff put us to sleep just about every day.  She tests based on information in the textbook and on the slides.  There isn't too much variation between the two.  The lecture notes are posted on WebCT, but are difficult to read, due to the small font.  Know EVERYTHING about the disorders!

Super easy imo. Final was online/not lockdown. Lectures were not mandatory. Mandatory discussions but super chill. There were only 4 HWs, a midterm that I felt was very fair, and a final. Lots of readings but the content is all pretty simple. Sutton is super nice, and gives extra credit just for going to lectures. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Honestly I thought I was cooked in this class. I got a C on the midterm, and was bogged down by the readings, but class was heavily curved and catered towards students success. The final was significantly easier, open note. 4 assignments to becompleted throughout quarter, that are practical and straightforward.

I think the class is very interesting and informative, Prof is very nice and wants students to succeed. I feel like I learned a lot of was engaged with the material. In this class, you work with a group for some assignments and she gives class time to do so. A fair amount of reading but nothing that isn't manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: 4 HW assignments, ea/very simple and she said herself she did not give out lower than (I think) a B on each one. Lots of extra credit in lecture and even on the midterm and final (which were a mix of MC, short answer). Her lectures were amazing and thorough, could easily replace the textbook. Section is mandatory, lecture isn't. I loved her class!

Professor Sutton is very nice and extremely knowledgeable. The class assignments are very interesting and helps facilitate learning. She gives extra credit that is presented as a surprise, so attendance is recommended because it could be up to 5 points which makes a difference. Tests are hard, no study guide ever.

Prof Sutton is so sweet and it's really easy to succeed in class. Four hw assignments, a midterm and final made up of multiple choice and short answer questions. Content isn't too difficult either  not much stats, mostly just memorization of terms that'll be useful in life if you plan on doing research. She also gives easy extra credit sometimes.

She is one of the nicest professors ever. She really cares about her students. Her lectures were interesting. We had a couple of assignment worksheets, which were pretty easy and straightforward. The midterm and final were multiple choice, which were questions from the slides. We read some articles and she Skyped the authors so we could ask Q's!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: The worst lecturer, easy tests.

Best physics class I've ever taken honestly. Granted that it was his first time teaching a regular quarter, he was a little disorganized.. However, he was very each to reach and took criticism really well.

he was really nice and chill but all comm was through discord and his lectures were just tangents and derivations. it got to the point that i gave up on going to lectures even tho they were mandatory and just relied on openstax to teach me. quiz avg was around 60-75% and only 60% iclicker points meant full points tho and final was easy

Yes tony is a new professor and you can definitely tell, but he's very easy to contact and clearly is making an effort. He just needs more expereince teaching, and there is only one way to do that. The final was very easy, and he clearly wants people to succeed. He will get better every quarter. Grading scheme is very forgiving

Very accessible outside of class (discord) but lectures unclear & disorganized. His lack of experience shows bc he wants an ideal world where curve isn't necessary but his teaching methods & poor explanations don't align with that ideology. He does clicker questions but doesn't know the answers.Only good thing is almost all MC exams but still hard.

He has the potential to improve for future physics courses, but this quarter was still disorganized. I found myself relying on textbooks, kudu, and YouTube videos to get me through this class. However, all tests heavily emphasize conceptual questions and some tough free-response questions.

Prof. Tony is nice, just needs to spend more time lecturing to get acquainted with lecturing effectively. I attended most lectures but reading the actual Kudu textbook was the only thing that adequately prepared me for the quizzes/final. Very few worked out examples, so prepare to spend time outside of class to practice. He is super accessible tho
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a good professor. He was fast to respond to messages and was very helpful with my situation. I was never able to go to lecture, but watching the podcasts, if you actually paid attention to the concepts he would teach in lecture, it is what was tested on the quizzes. It was conceptual heavy class, but I liked it.

lectures rarely included practice with actual values as opposed to conceptual questions or equation derivation, but practice was done in office hours. Prof included many interesting examples of applications in healthcare (pacemakers, defibrillators, etc). exams reflected problems in the textbook fairly well. fairly lenient grading.

If need the grade, absolutely take prof tony. Was going to be a hater but the quizzes/final are so ridiculously easy (I'm talking EC on literally everything). Yes, very conceptual but this means you can skip grinding problems and just actually understand the content. That being said don't expect to learn in lecture, just use YT vids/Kudu sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Probably the worst class I've taken ever, made me dislike the usually enjoyable physics. He would be mores suited to teach physics majors not bio physics, hates to give hw related to tests, long time to grade, trolls students hours before exams, says he takes criticism but makes no changes, no math questions in class bc he hates numbers, unhelpful.

While he wasn't great at lecturing because he is a newer teacher, he made the class very easy if you tried, and even made the final very similar to the old quizzes. I would never pay attention in lecture, but I could tell he was trying his best and really cared about the students.
He is a pretty average lecturer, not the greatest but not bad at all. The quizzes aren't terribly difficult and offers a lottttt of extra credit.

Professor Aportela does not deserve a bad rating. Lectures are mandatory and a bit disorganized, but quizzes are easier imo ~10 conceptual multiple choice questions and 2 free response lite, which are still multiple choice. If you can read the textbook and selfstudy you'll be fine, but if you need extra help maybe wait for Tsai. He's super nice tho

Do not take this man's course under any circumstances. He's genuinely one of the worst professors I've ever had. I would just wait to take physics another quarter unless you like confusing lectures, bad communication, and extra stress. Just dont do it.
nice guy, but very disorganized and not a good lecturer. You'll have to learn most material on your own

He is very open to criticism and makes it clear he is available to help outside the classroom, but he really is not fit for lecturing. Sitting in class, paying full attention, and taking handwritten notes has not been enough to understand what he teaches during lecture. It's very disorganized and much of what he explains does not make sense.

This professor is incredibly unorganized, unprofessional, and overall unprepared for PHYS 1B. Many students dropped the class (taking a W on their transcripts) rather than sit through his lectures. iClicker is mandatory, but Prof simply opens it in the last few minutes of class and tells students to select answers randomly. Don't take with him!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His lectures were probably the worst thing I've ever had to sit through. He makes so many mistakes and other students correct him all the time. He is also kinda disorganized, which makes the class harder to follow. Also, he refuses to use numbers in his examples and just does a bunch of proofs and derivations, which honestly made me more confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Tony is very caring, kind, taking notes on his lecture slides and examples that he does in class, along with reading the assigned Kudu textbook and understanding the Kudu homework and looking over the formula sheets that he posts before every quiz is enough to do well on his quizzes, but you definitely have to read a lot outside class.

Took during SS2 and dropped because the class was very disorganized. Quiz averages were ~35% and how he taught physics symbols instead of numbers just didn't make sense for me. Prof Tony is very caring, but he is soft spoken + goes on tangents, so it's easy to fall asleep in lectures (mandatory)... Prepare for a lot of self learning and good luck!

Prof. Tony doesn't use numbers in his lectures, examples, and exams, which I think was the steepest and hardest learning curve for everybody. Exams were a step up from hw problems which were a step up from lecture examples. But, Prof. Tony is incredibly nice and genuinely wants everyone to succeed and  provides the resources to help. But, fat curve

One day before grades are due and I literally have no idea what my grade is going to be due to all the confusing info about curves and different grading contigencies. I flunked two quizzes but the class avergaes were like below 50% so maybe I'm fine?? super stressful course even without considering the material

Prof Tony cares about his students and you can tell he wants to help where he can, but his lectures were very hard to follow. IMO, the first couple quizzes were not representative of what we learned in class, and HW did not prepare us. The class was hard because of the disorganized lectures, limited examples in class, but Prof is kind.

just to be super super clear, Tony is a nice guy and does everything on discord so it's easy to get in contact. However, the organization of the course is (or was?) really hard to follow, idk he did change a lot of stuff over the session and the grades seemed to improve, but you have to be major proactive to do well

This is for summer session 2, but you could really tell the professor read the constructive criticism given to him because he took his time to make sure the grading and exams were fair. Physics is hard, unless you really try to study and understand the concepts you will get it. I appreciate prof tony for his patience and help.

truly cares about his students and reading reviews from first session compared to summer session you can tell he took the time to create a system to help students succeed. He doesn't use numbers but I believe it's helped me truly understand how and why physics works the way it does, coming from someone who HATES physics. Sweetest and kindest prof

Prof Tony was amazing at telling us what he expects out of us.Everything you need to know is in the lectures. Many people complaining is because they're used to plug and chug formulas rather than actually solving.The content itself is hard, especially during a fast course like summer.Tony is open to student criticism and overall wants ppl to learn!

Pretty good teacher. Emphasizes problem solving skills rather than algebra which is cool, but takes a long time to derive laws in class where the derivation will never be seen again. Really cool guy with an obvious passion for physics, but trying to make bio majors be interested in the mathematical reasoning of E+M is not possible

This is based on Summer Session. Tony himself was great at presenting the material, and the notes I took in his lectures were primarily how I studied for quizzes and the final. Go to office hours and ask questions. He is being unfairly rated because of the difficulty of the class itself. I do not recommend taking class during summer.

New to teaching, so you will have to do more work. No practice quizzes, but a practice final & good curve. Treat office hours like another lecture. The class wasn't really organized, and the subject is difficult, but he is passionate & made me appreciate & like physics more. Take him if you can put in lots of work & manage a less organized course.
made me absolutely hate physics, most confusing class I've ever been in and we're not even done yet

Should have dropped it while I could. Idk he might be better when its not a summer session but I literally have no idea what is even going on and he changes everything about the class constantly, even tho you're literally not supposed to do that you're supposed to have a syllabus and stick to it
how does this guy have a job here. no practice exams so you will have to teach yourself everything that's on the quizzes!
yikes better off taking another class

Does not teach you anything about solving physics problems. Just heavily complicated quizzes questions without any numbers with a below 50% average on all quizzes. I get that he's hasn't been teaching for long, but if you actually want to understand and apply physics in the future like the MCAT, please pick someone else for your metal sake.

I took PHYS 1B with him during the first summer session but it isn't an option to add here! He doesn't use Canvas at all so everything is on discord, which is okay but very hard to catch when he said important stuff. There were no practice exams or anything and no KUDU, take someone else unless you're an incredible physics student.
literally prof in physics whic is saying something, took it SS1, he's not like mean he's just a really bad instructor

Merryman is a great professor who is enthusiastic, approachable, and cares about her class environment! The attendance policy is generous, the homework is easily manageable, and all homework can be redone for full credi, although that will likely be unnecessary because of how kind and lenient she is. She's amazing!

CCE 1 was easy and Professor Merryman was so kind and devoted to the course. Participation is semi mandatory (can miss 3 classes max). Lots of assignments and some projects, but they were not difficult, and often my group was able to finish early. We had lots of in class work time. Professor gave great feedback and very accessible outside class.

Prof Merryman is so sweet and understanding, and wants the best for you. She is very lenient (to any extensions) and provides great feedback. Most CCE classes teach the same thing, but she makes the content more enjoyable. They only thing is that I think she makes the students do more in-class discussions/activities compared to the other teachers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ash was so kind and caring. I would highly recommend them. Since CCE is regulated by 8th College most of the classes will be similar, but Ash approached CCE 1 with much care and willingness to help. Ash provides amazing feedback on everything and is lovely to work with, especially in this small class setting. Ash is so knowledgeable and it shows
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Unfortunately,  she no longer is at UC, San Diego. I still wanted to write her a review. She is sweet, beautiful and smart.
By far one of the greatest professors I have ever had. She is really interesting and very helpful. The work load is doable and isnt too difficult. Take her class! You won't regret it.

Amazing professor. In fact, best prof I have had at UCSD by far (took 3 classes). She is extremely clear and organized, and makes the topic even more interesting than it already is. The exams are very fair. In class midterm and final take home essay. Prof Linton is also very helpful outside of class. I highly recommend her and all of her classes.

Prof Linton is amazing. She engages the class, uses slides, gives a study guide for her tests, and shows films. My God, why can't my other professors be like her? I don't care what she's teaching - take it! Also, most readings are posted online, so textbook costs aren't a big issue.
Best professor at UCSD.  Very clear and organized; very helpful in terms of helping you with career goals.
Easy, lecture notes posted online, gives lots of extremely easy extra credit opportunities. Midterm straight from her lectures/notes. Final was easy paper. Recommended for sure.
Prof. Linton is amazing!  She's sweet as can be and is incredibly fair with grading.  She offers tons of extra credit and the material on exams are very straightforward.  Take!
She is a great professor. Speaks clearly, organized, and has done a lot of social research. Offered lots of extra credit and fair tests. Overall good experience and enjoyed the class.

I took SOCI87 as a freshman seminar class (worth 1 unit) just because it was the only one that fit into my schedule. I had no interest in consumerism whatsoever (didn't care about sweatshops) but her genuine concern for the society and environment rubs off and I ended up learning alot. She handmade a pumpkin cake for us at the last day of class =]
Great professor, great class!

Very nice professor, good class. Grading seemed to be a lot harder on the final (grade dropped from an A to a B). The lectures do not hold my attention at all. I felt real bad for falling asleep for most classes but I really couldn't help it. Lots of info to remember so keep up with the reading and you should be fine. 2 books.

Do readings, go to lecture and should get an A.  Readings were interesting- professor VERY nice and very welcoming during office hourse. Only thing is that she tends to read her notes. Can seem a little monotone.. But once you talk to her outside of lecture- passion comes out. It would be nice to see some during lecture.

Print out her slides before class and note-taking will be v. easy. Her notes/lectures really facilitate textbook readings. She's very approachable both after class and in office hours.  Take her class!
Great prof.  Very organized and work load is enough to keep you learning but not overly busy.  I highly recommend prof. Linton.
A very helpful and interesting class. But watch out for the neighborhood paper. I'm not sure of its usefulness and its quite a bit of trouble.
pretty good professor, class was pretty boring, but she was well organized and gave good study guides.
very very nice. interesting matter. she's very clear, i don't know what the other student referred to. very organized.

very nice professor. one midterm and final both in class. and a research paper. did not have to read the textbook, however there are other readings online. as long as you keep up with the class, it shouldnt be too hard.
very nice. organized. lectures are on slides so you can print them out before class. lots of readings. one in class midterm and take home final paper. interesting class overall.

She is very organized and all, but not as good as she is rated to be. There are times when she is very unclear, and keeps mumbling. Make sure u r along with the class, or else it will be hard to catch up. the subject matter is hella boring NOT RECOMMENDED
Excellent senior seminar on the ethical considerations of food consumption. We read 2 great books and discussed academic research of the issues in a roundtable format. Highly recommended.
This was a freshman seminar and I thought it was pretty interesting. The prof. is really really nice and it's worth taking.

Highly recommend! Lectures are very organized. Slides posted on Webct b4 class so attendance isn't crucial if you do the readings. Some of the texts are long but if you're serious about urban soc, the texts are a staple to any future sociologist. Midterm: short answers, MC, TF. Final is take home and Op ed piece on a community of yr choice.

LOVE HER! shes really nice and pretty easy. lectures are intersting and shes very organized. ocassional quizzes in class, but they are easy. the readings are mandatory, but are interesting and fairly easy. HIGHLY RECOMMEND HER! one midterm and take home final.
April Linton is really insightful. I NEVER read for my classes and I read for her class. That's saying a lot, you know? She's great.

An enjoyable class, albeit long at times. I took the summer school class so it had to be stretched out over 3 hours. The average grade for the mid-term was a 77 but the final is a take-home. Overall, a reccomended class.

Prof. Linton is a great professor, definitely recommended. This class was harder than I thought due to the amount of demographic data, but interesting. Midterm/Final are both M/C, TF, Short Answer. Some in class writes and either an 8 pg literature review paper or a 3 pg service learning paper/comm. service project. Overall, I enjoyed the class.

Great professor!  She is organized, very approachable and fair.  Her lectures are power points that you can get from web.  If you keep up with the reading you will ace the in-class midterm and final.  Loved this course!

Very pleasnat and approachable. Passionate about her class. Utilizes webct, so lectures are online along with study guides. Go to class do readings or at least comprehend the material covered on the study guide and you'll get an A. Plus she's cute, so there's some eyecandy.
Amazing professor, really helpful and fair!

Very helpful and sweet.  I realy enjoyed going to her class.  Her lectures are available on powerpoint, but it is more beneficial to go to class.  Her midterm and final are very easy if you keep up with the reading and attend lecture.  There is a lot of reading, so plan accordingly.  She is very fair though.  She is always available to help.

Linton is a great professor. She is very down-to-earth and has very structured lectures with printable web-ct notes. She does assign lots of reading, but most of it is very engaging, especially "Sidewalk" (great book). She is fair and very knowledgable about urban issues affecting out country. I highly recommend her courses.

Professor Linton is awesome.  She is well organized and lectures can be followed with her well articulated power points made available to all students.  She encourages class participation; exams and the required paper follow class content & are easily accomplished if you keep up.  She is a breath of fresh air to the Sociology Dept. at UCSD.
Professor Linton is the greatest. The workload is pretty fair because there is a lot of reading, but the final is easy.
Difficult organized class. You learn very little, but put in so much work and time. Very little benefit. Too much unnecessary work and very picky grading.
PLZ NO. DONT. JUST DONT.
OH MY GOD!!! NO!!! PLEASE STAY!!! DONT TAKE THIS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked Dr J. She's kind, did well at at simplifying coding and showing us practical uses in bio, and gave us a fun final group project where we really had creative reign. Weekly homeworks, a few quizzes (no midterms), and the TA's were very helpful. I didn't try nearly as much as I should've, think it wouldn't be hard to get an A in here!

Professor Juavinett is amazing! She handled the pandemic so well and is super understanding. The class is lab report heavy but they aren't terrible, try and you'll get at least a B. Labs are done in groups and we do a group grant proposal at the end. I recommend this class! Love the class but hate working in groups so much.
Great prof! Taken 145 (neurobiology lab) with her as well as the neural data science course (BIPN 162). Both courses are engaging and teach you a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Loved this class and this prof! BIPN 145 is my favorite class i've taken at ucsd so far and that's thanks to Dr.J.!! she makes lab interesting and lively, and she's always there if her students need help! Lab reports, midterms and final project were reasonable and fair imo, and Dr. J makes it very clear what she expects from you. 10/10 recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He should try to learn how to write neatly, his handwriting is bad and I could not decipher the words during lecture while sitting in front of the classroom + glasses. Another thing is that he is stingy and won't upload lecture notes or recordings while other 20C teachers do both. So I would recommend studying on your own and don't rely on him.

Hand writing isn't legible. Confuses himself during lectures often. He lectures way too fast to comprehend or make note of the material taught. Refuses to upload lectures on time whereas the other 20C professors do. Shakeel makes what should have been the easiest class in the Math 20 series into the hardest class in the series.

Do not take this professor unless you want to lower your gpa. It's not worth your time going to lecture because his notes/handwriting are incoherent, and he stopped recording and posting lecture notes halfway through the course. I ended up having to learn the material on my own and the resources don't really prepare you for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Same tests and finals as the other profs. I wish I could understand his lectures tho. And notes. Notes look like something id find inside the pyramids. Ancient hieroglyphics.
Cant understand him. Ended up going to another professor to learn the material. Midterms and finals were the same, so it did not matter.

The final was by far the worst final I have ever taken and he had the AUDACITY to not curve it or the class whatsoever. Study maybe two weeks ahead of time for this class if you want anything above a C. I tried hard on all the homeworks and labs. The homeworks are easy but the labs are graded harshly so I  go to office hours to get them checked.

tbh, he's not awful. it's just that his handwriting is BAD. i feel like i could've gotten a whole letter grade higher in this class if i could decipher his handwriting. lectures don't help much either since he's not explaining the material out loud in a particularly interesting way, just narrating as he solves problems in his gibberish handwriting.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If 0 was an option I would give him a 0. It feels like he is trying to teach himself as he is lecturing to us. Forgets what he is even talking about and pauses to think about what to even say. Just save your time and do not take him idek what ucsd is doing with these professors.

This professor has no idea what is going on. His responses to questions make no sense and going to lecture is a waste of time because you have to teach yourself everything anyways as lecture leaves you more confused than not going. I joined his office hours and he did not even show up. Handwriting is actually impossible to even interpret.

Kind & smart but disorganized.A thick accent,fast explanations, and no control over noisy freshmen (who talk like they are yelling and he just teaches over them) make lectures hard to follow.Unprepared—need to self-teach.Tests, labs, and heavy homework (2 parts) all graded harshly make it tougher. Chaotic class, minimal guidance.Learned more in DI.

By far the worst professor I have ever had. Thick accent, ungodly amount of work, mumbles for half the class, goes on tangents when students asks a question then never ends up answering it, speed reads through the slides, messes up setup of the equations, and will ask us to forget what he just said cause it was all wrong. Unacceptable UCSD!!!

OH my god this professor is so bad idk where to start. I can legit teach better than this guy; he explains concepts poorly and his annotations are useless. This QUARTER has been such a pain just because of this class. I feel scammed because this is not the quality of education I paid for. I miss my high school math teacher;

I don't think he has any idea as to what he is actually lecturing his students. His lectures are impossible to follow synchronously. His handwriting is not just reminiscent of Egyptian hieroglyphics; it is the hieroglyphics. The best thing from his class is you learn how to teach yourself the subject. Save yourself and take 20C with Ko Woon or Yin.

I don't know where to start. This professor seems to be reading the slides for the first time as he's trying to lecture. Notes are incoherent at best. Be prepared, if you ask a question he will likely forget it within 20 seconds of talking himself into a hole. Don't take unless you want to teach yourself everything.

It's inspirational how Shaq manages to make what should be the easiest of the 20 series classes difficult. His slides are pieces of paper that look more like notecards and his handwriting is quite reminiscent of ancient Egyptian hieroglyphics, he could probably teach a class on that and people would actually learn something.

One of the worst professors I've had. You literally can't understand what he's saying in lecture podcasts. He always messes up his podcasts and makes his handwriting illegible. The class itself should be easy but he somehow overcomplicates every topic, making it impossible to follow. I've resorted to self studying and its been 10x easier.

Really nice person but the worst professor--I feel bad leaving this review:(
Annotations are illegible
Concepts terribly explained on slides
Tests oddly tricky
Makes EVERYTHING sound unnecessarily complicated
Ended up self teaching everything ; concepts themselves turned out to be rlly simple lol;; Expecting A just bc I studied everything omo

really cool guy, but this is his first quarter teaching MATH 11 and man this guy is never prepared for lecture. He will sit there and think about what he is supposed to be teaching us DURING LECTURE. save yourself and take Rava.

He's clueless! We'll get finish an example and he'll say "oh nevermind that was all wrong." His handwriting is IMPOSSIBLE to read and he never clarifies what he is writing even if students ask. He mumbles to himself and sounds like he is trying to learn the material as he is teaching us. I had to teach myself everything... never take his class.
Easy class. Make a game, play other people's games, have fun, say nonsense with strong feelings, write one paper.
Pros: extra credits, interesting topic, enthusiastic, one paper only Cons: pop attendance
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is horrible and treats the students like little kids by the way she talks and gets their attention. Unreasonable as you are not allowed to use electronics or it will count as an absence and 3 absences equal an automatic fail in the class. She even tells people who missed missed 3+ classes to drop the class. Assignments are fine, depends on ta.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: BEST. CAT CLASS. EVER. Hands down. No essays in the traditional sense. Class is based on videos; main project is to make a short film (3-7 mins, though my group went over to 9min) with group which was very fun. Topic of vid was about design fiction of world 100yrs from now. Only essays are just reflection paper on the video. Highly recommend!
Really did not like her class. It was a lot of work for a writing class and made no sense to me. Her lectures were not engaging and were all over the place. Really glad to finally be done with her

Her lectures were all over the place and had no relevance to any assignments that we were doing  for that class. We basically just watch videos that she skips through so we cannot even understand what is going on at all. Also she acts like her class should be everyone's first priority when we all have other, more important classes.

She's nice but doesn't always explain things in a clear way.  She is an artist so maybe that is why she talks using words that are vague or dont really mean anything. But she was good at getting students to participate in conversations during lecture.  Her lectures don't always seem to really have a point though.
Terrible Professor. Lucky he is retiring soon

The devil himself. Often talks about evil demons. Makes everyone buy a book that he wont mention after the first class (He wrote it and will make you buy it from a sketchy website). Begins every lecture with a rant about how he is disappointed in attendance. Also does not believe in holidays or getting sick. Cool hat though. Nice sweater vests too.

I had said this before but Robert takes the cake for the worst Professor I've had. He's too old to be teaching anymore, and his lectures can hardly count as "teaching" anyway. His OH are just as bad. All the reviews about him are true. He is a sour mean old man who interrupts you and will not even let you speak if he has his mind made up about you.

Absolutely the worst prof in UCSD, expect everyone to attend his confusing lectures & OHs even tho its optional. Easily get mad over lil thing like attendance & being rude to students for no reason, also he used his lectures to talk about his life stories. Weekly hw, 1 midterm & final. The exams are similar to hw and the same every year. Avoid him

Easily get mad over lil thing like attendance or being rude to students for no reason & he used lectures to talk about his life stories. Weekly hw, 1 midterm & final. Avoid him at all costs!

reviews.comment: Worst profesor in the entire department even though he is entrusted with such an important course for your foundations as an engineer. His lectures and notes are incoherent and he never explains his methods. Often goes on tangents about obscure mathematical concepts unrelated to the course. Take 110A over the summer w another prof if possible

absolute worst professor I have ever come across in my 20 year existance. makes you buy a textbook that he just so happened to write himself from some sketchy website then proceeded to give two lectures about how he doesn't make any money from it. lectures are impossible to follow and anything you learn will be learned on your own time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Asaro is hands down the worst professor I have ever had at UCSD. In fact, he is the worst teacher/lecturer I've ever had in my educational career. While he is a smart man, he can not teach any material and just confuses the entire class. He also makes you buy a textbook which is as useless as he is when it comes to teaching. Avoid him at all costs

I hope I can have another course with Professor Asaro. His homework and test were extremely related to his lectures. He spent so much time re-covering material so it would stick. Went over countless ex . He is a character, so lectures were not boring, plus material not boring. Also, very approachable. He extended hw's and even rescheduled midterm.

No tests, but boy do his lectures confuse people!  If you don't have prior knowledge to continuum mechanics, learning can get tough. Wouldn't recommend his course if you aren't good at self learning .... but it is a mandatory one so ....

horrible. assumes se9 taught you well (which it didnt). LEARN HOW TO DO THE MATH because his quizzes and midterms and finals focus more on that than the programming. TA (anna) does not know how to program and is extremely unhelpful. I asked her to clarify one of the homework questions and her response was that the question wasn't unclear. Thanks.

Lectures go over the HW assignments indirectly. They are definitely boring to go through but he explains the code and what each line does so you should definitely attend. MT and Final look very similar to the practice sheet he gives you. Unreasonable expectations for writing code on tests though. HW will take you some hours, don't procrastinate.

He told us we would have pop quizzes, but he would usually announce them.  We ended up only having 2 or so in the last couple weeks of lecture.  Homeworks are confusing.  Midterm was really easy, it was exactly like the practice exam.  Open book/open note.  Final was a bit of a surprise, but I ended up with a good grade. Not sure how that happened.
Thanks god for his ta who helped me get through this beacuse it was very confusing.  He would be a good teacher maybe for a different class.

All SE majors are going to take this course, so listen and listen good. You need this course to get through your undergrad. DO NOT USE C++ ! Learn MATLAB and learn the problems (assignments) that are introduced because they're damn well going to show up again in later UG courswork. As for Asaro, good luck with that. See your TA as much as possible.
He gave homework and never collected it. He would set up appointmets to meet with students nand then just wouldn't show up to them. He's just a bad, bad man.

I'm surprised this guy isn't blind in his right eye from staring into the projector light all day long.  Also this guy is really hard to track down.  I'm 0/6 in showing up to his office and him actually being there.  his assignments are insane and i take forever to get to what he is looking for.
Didnt understand anything he taught in class.. but he can be helpful if you go to office hours and manage to find him there

Do the UCSD community a favor and REPORT this teacher on CAPE!!  If you have to take his class, contact CAPE and ask them to PLEASE come to this class so you can rate this guy.  If you look in CAPE, you'll see there is no rating for him due to a lack of responses.  This is b/c he avoids being rated!

This has to be one of THE WORST teachers I have had at UCSD. The money I spent on his lecture notes from the soft reserve was a waste; I think I used them once. He is disorganized; lectures make no sense; everything I learned came from the TAs. He cancelled class to avoid a review by CAPE!!!

Asaro is almost impossible to understand and so are his notes.  There is no text for the class other than his lecture notes soft reserve.  The TA grades your programs and I think he felt sorry for us, because the grading was fairly easy

The guy CAN'T TEACH!!!We always had to go to TA office hours to get help on homework. Lectures are CONFUSING! Advice: don't do homework the night before it's due... Oh, another thing, the class is BORING.

The guy is very into his lecture notes and loves to confuse the hell out of everyone.  If you seriously are in love with programming and like writing programs to execute math functions and commands, then this is the professor to have, otherwise, good luck trying to stay awake in his lectures.

This man is brilliant but feared.  If you ask him for help he will spend hours with you.  His classes are always extremely well organized but deal with very hard topics.  Every class I have taken with him has been hard but has taught me a huge amount.

Prof Asaro is amazing! She goes over everything as many times as you ask in order for the you to understand the material. Her tests and quizzes are very fair and overall was a very fun class that I looked forward to. It is a language class so you will need to memorize vocab and conjugations, but if you keep on top of it you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She really cares about students. You do a lot of reading in this class, but not an insane amount. 2 5pg essays, 2 quizzes, 2 projects and final make up your grade. Would def recommend.
very helpful, wants you to do well. Recommend taking
Appreciate taking her course. She genuinely works to help her students do well in the course. There's a lot of reading and class discussion is mandatory so I suggest reading.

Dr. Asaro is a very intellectual and caring professor. She is available outside of class and wants to help you learn. She has a lot of extra credit opportunities which is really nice! Homework, 2 quizzes, 2 tests, 2 papers and 2 presentations. Pretty clear and solid class. Loved it!
Great professor who has great lectures. The exams are very similar to the practice exams and as long as you stay caught up it isn't a difficult class
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: dry lecturer but very passionate and clear. teaches very well, exams are fair and he prepares you well based w/ practice material. study hard for exams and you'll do well in the class, prob the best econ prof  here. literally a saint compared to the other 100b profs. no curve for an a though, material after exam 2 is the most difficult so study up

He is such a W professor. He gives out practice exams that are very similar to the actual exams. He actually cares about you and wants you to succeed instead of trying to trick you on the exams. Very straight forward questions just like the practice or the examples he did in class. Everything is recorded no attendence for lecture or discussion.
Compared to the professor in other class, he's practically an angel. I hope he teaches 100B this fall.
Lecture notes are very clearly written. Aram tells you exactly what's on exams, and as long as you understand how to do the practice exams you will do well.
Prof is extremely clear and does not trick you. Wish I could have him for all my ECON classes. Grigoryan will not disappoint you, he is truly a G.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Aram is a king. Love him. Teaches well and tests fairly. Love you Aram!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The structure of his class is very clear: 4 homework assignments, 2 lowest are dropped, and the midterms and final study guides you are given are basically what is on the exams (same type of questions, different examples obviously). Make sure to attend lectures and discussions or watch them to understand the material.

He's a very slow and dry lecturer, so I stopped attending class after the second week. He's really passionate and knowledgable about the material but just boring to listen to - not his fault though, 100B is really easy after doing 100A. Tests and homework were very fair and graded leniently.
Great professor! 100% would take him again! Lectures were easy to understanding, make sure to do the hw there are 4 total and really study for the exxams.

Just take his course, you won't regret it. Amazing lectures and lecture notes provided, the review sessions are really helpful. Graded by two midterms, a final and homework (2 out of 4, he dropped two lowest grades!) If you lock in, EZ A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's still a new professor at UCSD from my knowledge, he's getting the hang of flowing from topic to topic, and keeping students engaged during lecture. He's explains the equations very well and is very straightforward with his problem sets and midterms! Definitely a professor I'd would love to take again and highly recommend.
Podcasting king !!! He explains concepts well and exams are very similar to the provided practice problems and former exams

Great prof! He explains concepts well and makes it easy to get a good grade. Notes are clearly organized, posted ahead of time, and tests are just like the practice. HW is light with easy grading. Great class overall.
If you follow this professor's lectures, complete his problem set and exercises, and understand his material. You will get good grades. His exams matched his practice perfectly
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: my fav class, and i learned a lot abt stats. yeah labs take ~10 hours, but theres 3 reports THE WHOLE QUARTER. if you cant manage your time, thats on YOU. i got a 95 having lost 25% on my late 1st lab because she halved the lowest grade's weight—she values improvement. TAs offer ~18 hours OH during lab report weeks; if you want an A, youll get one

Her lab report would take u 10 hour to complete and only receive 50% of the grade. She took half of the points off because my submission of gradescope was unclear.  However, when I ask TAs, they said all my words and graphs were nice and clear. and u would not know what u need to include in the lab report. the instruction is super obscure.

The class itself is flawed IMO, not much to do with the prof. Grades weigh heavily on prelab quizzes and reports. Quizzes are 5 Qs but they try to trick you. Reports are VERY repetitive and tedious, and feedback for me was minimal. However, the professors are accessible through piazza and quite accommodating. Still my least favorite class so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: if you are a masochist take this class, the work load is insane and she does not know how to teach, she quickly reads over the slides and doesn't explain anything

I wont lie, the class was hard, graded strictly, and there was more work than most of my other classes. However, I think the extra work definitely helped me master the material instead of just learn it for the test. Professor Arlett is super accessible outside of class, incredibly kind and helpful, and also offers a bunch of EC which is nice.

Professor Arlett really does care about students' success in her class. She gives opportunities for EC (up to 4.5% grade boost for my class). Some of the EC came from answering peers' questions on piazza which she's very active on as well so it's easy to get questions answered. The content is hard but the amount of work and its difficulty is fair.

Professor Arlett really does care about what she is teaching. Her exams were difficult because the content itself was difficult, but they were fair. The quizzes did not weigh as much because there were different kinds of HW and participation, which helped my grade. My biggest issue was the lecture slides because they were messy and hard to discern.

From this class, I learned that researching and choosing the right professor is important. Unfortunately, I learned this too late, and now I am going through this mess. Don't be tricked! She may be nice, but her class structure says otherwise. From an absolute point of view, she is the worst professor I have ever experienced at UCSD. BE WARNED!

Although she is a good person, she is NOT a good professor. This class gave me more anxiety than any other class I have taken in my life. So much unnecessary work that amounted nothing to my understanding of the concepts. Tests were poorly made and had many errors that confused me and led loss of points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lectures end up being useless for most students(because of clicker questions). Her quizzes are tenfold more difficult than the practice she covers. Her classes are designed for students to fail. There is so much more that I want to say, but can't because of the word limit. For your own mental health and wellbeing, avoid this professor at all costs!

She is genuinely the worst professor I've had in my three years at UCSD. She does care for the subject but does not care if the students succeed. Our quiz averages are around 60% yet she refuses to do anything about it. Our class averages are so bad but she refuses to acknowledge that is a result of her own teaching.

While her lectures are not terrible, she assigns an unnecessary amount of hw including prelecture assignments that can take over an hour at times. The quizzes are ridiculously difficult and do not match the difficulty of the discussion problems or hw problems. She makes an already challenging course even harder.
She does love the subject and care about physics. But her exams sometimes reflect the course. Most of all, most of her TAs are questionable, tutors are helpful and care about the students tho.

Physics 2B is a ton of work but I did genuinely enjoy this class. Office hours were super helpful and the assignments we had helped me learn. The lectures were somewhat engaging. My one complaint is that the averages on the quizzes were about 60% and they aren't curved. I wish she curved each quiz instead of curving at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Arlett has been one of the worst professors I've ever had here at UCSD. Her tests represent nothing of what you learn in class. She expects a lot from you. Weekly you have an FRQ, multiple sections of reading, and your hw. Although she is passionate she lacks the skill to teach the material well. Avoid her if you can. It's not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took Phys 2B with Arlett. The class was hard (lots of reading) but I learned a lot and I would definitely take it again. She cares a lot about the students and really tries to make sure the students understand the content. I went to her office hours a few times, and she was really good with answering my questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Arlett is definitely a better person that most of the reviews suggest. She answers questions passionately and is caring and approachable. One negative of this class was that the TAs were not adequately trained.
I learned a lot from this course.
She doesn't teach. You have to read... a lot.

Jessica has been the worst professor I've had in my educational career. She threatened to hit me with an Academic Integrity Violation early in the quarter for using the same data as my Lab Partner... Take a minute to process that. Instead she just gave us a 0 on the assignment. She was also late to meetings and an anal grader. Avoid at all costs.

Hardest class I have taken so far at ucsd. Her exams were so difficult. Quizzes, and a midterm, and pre lecture assignments that sometimes took forever. Her way of lecturing was not productive at all, I felt like I was learning how to do everything on my own. Hard grader. Would not recommend unless you have endless time on your hands.

This class was very exhausting and time heavy, especially if you are a commuter. I would say it is doable if it is the only responsibility you have in your life, but if you have anything else be prepared to make some sacrifices.

never thought i'd be defending her but a lot of these reviews are harsh. for a lab class, the work is about average but definitely feels like a 4 unit class (like most other lab classes). lots of points off for small details. holds lots of office hours though and is accessible outside of class. you definitely have to be proactive but she is nice.

Genuinely insufferable and infuriating to be in the presense of. Not to mention how unbelievably out of touch she is with how much she expects us to know considering the lack of clear instruction and grading criteria she gives. Lab instructions are very vague and grading is unforgiving. She gives no final practice or guide to studying for the final

Reviews on here seem needlessly harsh. Compared to other 2 unit lab classes at UCSD I've taken, this one is perfectly average in terms of course load. Grading wise points were taken off for small things, but points per question is clear. Lectures were not recorded but posted slides had examples. Prof was decently active on Piazza for lab questions.
