reviews.comment: Best professor ever
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Her 2 unit class did not feel like 2 units. Her lecture slides were messy and hard to follow. She's so nit-picky about homework and labs. She doesn't explain anything regarding the labs, and her final exam did not exactly reflect what we "learned". DO NOT recommend and avoid if you care about your mental health and your GPA.

If you want a reason to end it all, this is the professor to take. The professor does not teach effectively. There are no clear grading criteria, it's just based on what she feels the work deserves. I have only used thoughts and prayers to get through this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Please avoid this professor at all costs. The instructions for labs, homeworks, and finals were very unclear. She gives no practice questions or practice finals. She gave no regrade requests for labs.

Her TAs always grade the labs very precisely and take off a huge chunk of points for very small errors. She even gave a lot of ppl AI violations
Hardly any HW Help, No problem sets or material to excel in the class, No practice final to prepare, Indefinitely avoid taking this class with this professor.

This professor is incredibly awful. Despite being new to UCSD, she shows a lack of care for students. There is little to be said in the way she treats students because I feel as if she was disrespectful.

There was this one time where my lab partner and I were marked down for having similar reports despite her saying we should have similar reports.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. It felt like we were led blind into all the assignments, labs, and the final. The grading criteria is IMMENSELY unclear (even when you ask for clarifications, they give an excuse for not providing clearer instruction), yet all of the assignments are graded to the finest detail (points off for small rounding errors).

a four unit class w 5 mandatory hours of class a week w iclickers for lecture but doesnt teach very well. there are prelecture assignments that can take between 20 minutes to two hours each lecture. we have hw every week a quiz every two weeks AND a midterm. quiz the week after the midterm and the week after thanksgiving. avoid her if possible!
don't take her if you want a B or higher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: If you want learn something and enjoy your class he is great, definitely take him

Prof. Arroyo is a really inspiring professor. I am not even a USP student but his lectures still were interesting. He cares about teaching and is super knowledgeable. Just be prepared for the group projects since they are a huge part of your grade!
One of best professor , who will teach you but also don't pressurize , I would say easy class
He is very inspiring. would recommend.
I love John. Such a caring professor. If you are taking his class go to his office hour and talk to him. It is very therapeutic.

Homework and Labs were not required, but heavily recommended. Quizzes were challenging, with averages hovering like 40-50 percent. The ARM coding language and environment is specific to the class but straight up didn't work on my computer with no real alternatives found online, so tough luck if it doesn't work on yours. The curve was very generous.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: class is content heavy. Prof does a good job explaining the concepts and lectures are useful. grade is based solely on quizzes, final, project (all of which are hard) so if you are bad at test prep or takings tests in generally you will probably suffer. otherwise you'll appreciate not having hw, unless you actually do the labs, which are optional.

The workload isn't very crazy for me (6-8 hours), but the lecture and pre-lecture recording is boring and easy to get distracted. Some quizzes and the final are tough, and the study/example problem sets aren't very sufficient to test your knowledge thoroughly. No homework is graded so only quiz, final, and a project contribute to the final score.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor, explains concepts well. It is a flipped classroom, where we watch pre-lecture videos to learn the concepts, and then during the lectures, the professor shows examples. There is a lot of work for this class, at least 20 hours per week.

Get ready to spend a lot of time on this course. You have to watch around 40 min of pre-lecture before each lecture. Quiz are open notes while online, but not for final. Project is in pairs and if your partner disappeared, you may suffer. This course is hard and the online nature makes it harder. Be prepared to choose this course and spend time.
Great instructor! Very professional and passionate about dancing, and also have great personality and teaching method.

A great professor who genuinely likes ballet and cares about her students! She takes the time to learn about everyone, and gives feedback tailored to what you need. I've never done ballet before, but she is very easy on beginners. Enjoyable class!

Kristin is an amazing instructor. She makes sure that students have proper form and takes time to help those that are struggling. She is also very talented and has good music taste. An easy grader, but for good reason. I loved this class!

Ive taken her several times, so hopefully that tells shes a great teacher. I didnt grow up dancing, but she really devotes her time to help anyone. Shes so patient too! She really wants her students to achieve in her class. However, sometimes she does cater a lot more to the advanced students of the class. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Skip class? You won't pass.--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The class has a variety of tap styles to experiment with. Your experience doesn't matter because she caters to all levels. Her grading is generous too because it's based on attendance, 2 performances of a routine we learned in class and a paper. I would recommend this class to anyone who wants to raise their GPA by having fun dancing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Kristin is an amazing dance teacher. As a person with a lot of dance background, I can say she is one of the best teachers I have had. Her stretch routines, technique sequences, across the floor exercises, and dance choreography are perfect for growing as a dancer. She is helpful and encouraging.

Took Theatrical tap with Kristin-- she is awesome and incredibly helpful! Also an extremely clever and creative choreographer! My first time taking tap and I love it! Midterms/tests are strictly a formality; just go to class, try and have fun and it's an A in the bag! Kristin will tell you where to get tap shoes for a great deal too!

This class shortened my lifespan. I pulled so many all-nighters for lab reports I'd get 50/ to 60/100 on. Those lab reports took hours to complete and were absolutely brutal. The final was very challenging. Learned a lot. Somehow got away with a B.

This class will be the cause of many crashouts. A lot is going to be expected of you. Lab reports are treacherous and grading is unforgiving. Just pray you are ahead of the curve, it's your only hope. The final exam will destroy you. Good luck.

im js glad i passed this class tbh. lab reports are graded SO DIFFICULT. i advise everyone to consistently go to OHs. i went to OHs for the last individual report and i scored a 97% even tho i've been stuck in the 55-75% range for other reports. this class genuinely took 5yrs off my life tho... final exam cooked EVERYONE 💔

Professor Armour is no doubt knowledgeable and passionate about physiology. HOWEVER, this class takes 15-20 hours a week on top of the 10 hours of lectures. . TThis class is taught like a medical school class (probably because Dr. Armour is a medical school professor), Overall, a great professor, but the class kind of consumes your life.

We only did 2 dissections. He's a nice guy, but answers every question you ask with "idk, what do you think?". I think he means well, but it doesn't translate to good teaching. My TA gave me points off for having gridlines on a graph that the professor said was good. She said, "I just don't like it". Why am I getting graded on vibes? Ridiculous.
Human physiology is a tough class. Ther

Yes, he is very knowledgeable on the subject, but his pedagogy is severely lacking. His physiology, one course is at the level of medical school and expect students to master highly complicated concepts with very poor example choices and extremely confusing lecture formats. He seems like a good guy but you cannot pay me to retake this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Armour is nice, but the class is incredibly difficult. The lab reports are time consuming to say the least. In the end, I learned very little.

2 solo and 1 group lab report. 1 cumulative final exam. The TAs grade the lab reports, but Armour gives the instructions for each lab. Read lab manual before lab to get a head start. The practice problem sets are like the exam, so use them to study. Ask questions during lab.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: The best professor I have ever had throughout my undergraduate, medical school education. He is an inspiration to all undergraduate students and aspiring scientists.  His dedication, passion and teaching is truly amazing.  A master at his craft, and also has a caring and great personality.  Still remember his physiology lab as it was yesterday...

3 HW (super easy & 2/3 are group hw) + 1 final (hard, long, detailed, cumulative, rec: study from 1st day of class) = 40%, 4 individual lab reports (20% each, pretty easy, go over physio w/ ta or professor, did day b4 and got As and Bs), 1 group lab (15%, super easy), symposium (5%, group presentation, easy). TA and prof super accessible anytime.

Reading the other reviews - are we taking the same class? Perhaps because everything is virtual now it's different but definitely had a real rough time finding the information needed for the lab write ups. If you have the time and means to attend every office hour then you'll probably be ok. Seriously, the recorded labs are not enoughby themselves.

Took class during Fall 2020. Grade was based entirely on worksheet assignments. Lectures were pre-recorded, and had 2 parts: one part on conceptual material and the other on lab experiments. I HIGHLY recommend going to his office hours asap; during them he would help work us through understanding the mechanisms behind the data in the lab lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a very good professor, he actually teaches at the school of medicine so he knows what he's talking about. The class itself is quite difficult. His exams really test your understanding so make sure you understand everything rather than memorizing them. Very knowledgeable and respected, highly recommended!

Probably the hardest class i've taken at UCSD aside from ochem. The lab reports are super time consuming and hard and a lot of the answers to the questions cannot be found in the lecture notes or online. Doing the lab reports w/out going to discussion is nearly impossible so make sure to go to discussion sections because they will help a lot.

My favorite biology class taken at UCSD. He really knows what he's talking about and gets you interested in the topics. He takes more of a medicine spin on physiology and even if you're not interested in medicine it provides a wonderful angle on things. The class is a significant amount of work but I learned so much that's been useful in everything
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Amour is the best professor I ever had at UCSD in 4 years there. He is passionate about the material, insanely knowledgable, and really cares about forming relationships with his students and helping them understand physiology. I don't have enough good things to say about him. BIPN 105 is a lot of work, but it's also interesting and rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The effort and time you put into this class will not get you the grade you deserve. No podcasts. No lecture slides. Lectures may or may not help you on the lab reports. Lab reports are graded extremely harshly. Not everything's explained in lecture, so if the research you do yourself isn't the answer he was looking for you'll get marked down.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: HAVE to go to lecture and take notes, does not podcast but the lecture goes pretty fast so use your phone to record the lecture and go back to fill in the gaps. Starts and end the lecture on time-- fills the whole lecture, normally don't let out early.  Exams are pretty hard and often test on details not emphasized during lecture

Take hand written notes during class and record every single lecture on your phone. Following lecture, re-listen to your recording and add to your notes. All the physiology for lab reports comes from lectures, so use your notebook when writing discussions. Lab reports 60%, final 40% (KNOW ALL DETAILS FROM LECTURE, LABS, AND PROBLEM SET).

One of the hardest classes you'll take at UCSD.  John is a great TA. Probably 90% of the reason I got an A in BIPN 100, and probably just as big of a factor in my survival of this class. The failure who complained about John probably barely passed BIPN 100 since a lot of the concepts are from that class. Attend and record all the lectures.

This is the hardest class you will take in undergrad. Expect sequential all nighters, and tons of critical thinking! If you are a typical UCSD memorizing drone, avoid this class. You learn a ton, Chris is an outstanding professor, and John is an AMAZING TA. Whoever wrote that comment about him is obviously mad that laziness doesn't  reward A's.

Dr. Armour knows his stuff. Definitely take John's lab!!! He is a beast when it comes to physiology. He may be tough but that's what a curve is for! Just pay attention to detail. Like make sure if you say "too much," you don't accidentally spell it like "to."

Dr. Armour knows knows his stuff. Don't take John's Lab!!! Doesn't know much physiology. Average or below average TA and grades at his average knowledge, which can cost you a lot of points if you give to much detail.

This was by far my favorite class and professor. You absolutely need to attend lecture and sections but if you commit to studying the lecture notes, section notes, and problem sets, this class becomes 20x easier. I got an A and still managed to take another class. He is crystal clear and also gives real-life applications.

This class was honestly the hardest class I've ever taken... but SO WORTH IT! I learned so much and seriously developed my critical thinking skills.. almost wish I'd taken it before the MCAT. He works as hard as his students so they respect him! Only writes letters of rec for people who get an A+ though so work hard

Armour only teaches this during SSI; it's a lot of info to cram into only 5 weeks, but it's definitely doable. Attend every lecture, take meticulous notes by hand, constantly review them, attend discussions, and you're set. Textbook isn't needed, he tells you everything you need in lecture. Tests are extremely fair. He's a great professor!

Armour by far has been my favorite biology professor. I took his class during the summer session so it was lots of information crammed into such a small period of time but he went through it very gracefully. He is very clear on what he expects you to know. Take down ALL HIS NOTES and be sure to review constantly. Overall, his class was great!

Oh boy, where do we begin? This class is widely seen as a rite-of-passage for UCSD pre-meds with prospects of medical school. Your ability to cope with the prodigious amount of work being thrown at you will be put to the test incessantly. Don't even dream of skipping a single lecture, review session or section in this course.
Reading back from 2014, in 4th year of med school, on this course I took in 2007 and reading my lab reports for this course, I can't believe I learned so much stuff.

He definitely knows his stuff! TOP NOTCH BIO PROFESSOR! Since its summer sess, he goes through it really fast. He only lectures on what you will be tested on, and he lets you know if he's talking about something that you won't be tested on. The material is very intensive, YOU MUST PUT IN THE TIME TO EARN YOUR GRADE.

BIPN 105 is def time consuming. You need to go to all the lectures and labs if you wanna do well. That being said, Professor Armour is extremely helpful, funny, and makes taking this hard class very enjoyable. He's extremely friendly, knows his stuff, and is very willing to help his students in any way. The final is KILLER. so make sure you STUDY
Chris is one of the best professors at UCSD, hands down. He's friendly, caring, and a great instructor. The only thing is that his class is one of the hardest classes I have ever taken.

He's probably one of the coolest professor i'll encounter in UCSD bio dept. I practically went to all his office hours, I regularly attended 2 sections run by 2 different TAs and their office hours (I had no life that summer) but it was really fun and interesting! Dr. Armour definitely makes you earn your grade but it's totally worth the horror.

Also took him during the summer and so glad I did. He knows his stuff and he tries his best to help us too. Since the materials condensed, it takes a lot of stamina to stay focused during lecture. DO NOT take another rigorous class @ the same time. Do ALL the problem sets/tests beforehand and if you don't understand why you're wrong, ask armour.

Took the course in the summer. He is a GOD compared to Fortes. Lectures are focused and organized. He draws everything on the board. Emphasizes concepts, not structures. Exams were difficult but curved (you only need to do better than your peers). Nice guy. Very approachable during office hours.

Teaches in summer. blows through material. seems like a nice guy but his tests are incredibly difficult. they consist of matching, t/f, short answer, a-e (where any or none can be right)... etc. he tests on EVERY detail he lectures about. he lectures too quickly and its difficult to take notes (since you need to write every detail). dont take this.

Maybe his teaching style just wasn't compatible with my learning style, but I found his organization lacking and his explanations unclear. Also, he would test us on specifics not covered in class. Oftentimes, he would draw a vague semblance of a diagram on the board and expect us to know it perfectly. Btw, know EVERY WORD of your notes (literally).
very insightful and clear in his explanations

Great teacher! Notes are very organized and easy to follow. One of the best lecturers I have seen. Tests are somewhat tricky but study and you'll be fine. I wish he taught Mam Phys all year long! I waited to take it in the summer just so that he would be my professor.

Ok, I am a chemistry major and this was lab #8 for me. Saying that, I did not think this lab was that hard. You just have to know how to write lab reports. And if didn't know how to before, this class holds your hand and leads you through. Definitely learned a lot and had fun at the same time. Chris is a VERY good instructor.

Most rewarding but time consuming class. I definetely learned ALOT from him.  Very detailed lab reports, I put in probably 40hrs/wk for this class and got a B, but I'm sure an A is possible if you don't have a crazy schedule like i did. Definetely take easy classes w/ this lab, but it's really worth it. Chris is an amazing teacher, very nice guy.

Very good professor, Learned a lot about physiology. Works you hard, but if you put in the time you can get the results. Would not recommend this course if you have a busy schedule. But if you want to learn a lot take him!

Everyone says that this guy is a nice person, but beneath that kindness there is an intense egomaniac. The class is made hard just so he can say it is. Remember this and suck up to him because he may be more helpful then. Don't pile up extra units this quarter and don't expect any favors from him. It's all dog eat dog in this class.

Lab reports are easy if you don't put them off to the last minute. The final was easy but very, very long. You are so focused on the lab reports that you forget about the final. It is worth just as much as all the lab reports. STUDY FOR THE FINAL. DO THE PACKET HE GIVES YOU AT THE BEGINNING OF THE CLASS. IT IS ALMOST IDENTICAL TO THE FINAL.

He's a God,period. I've never met ANYONE SO smart before. He did undergrad at UCSD(Revelle, bioengineering). He has MD+PhD, which I believe he also got at UCSD. He has the record in UCSD history of graduating with the MOST units. He worked as a janitor and a firefighter before. He invented nearly EVERY MACHINE we used in lab. Therefore, he's a God.

COOLEST GUY EVER!! Insisted on being called by first name. Stayed with us in lab ALL 10+ hours every week. Always sat with each group to socialize and clear up any questions. Class is EXTREMELY hard, his final is ridiculously LONG! For a lab class of about ~100 people, he had to roll his finals in on a hand truck in multiple boxes.
Best prof I've ever had.  Learned more in this class than all others at UCSD combined.  Experience almost killed me.

Awesome professor! His class was VERY fast paced but he made the material very clear. His tests were fair, he made you work for your grade, but I learned a lot. I almost always read books for a class but I never had to use it for him. Just take thorough notes and you'll know all you need to for the tests.

An awesome class that will make you learn BIPN 100 all over again. Chris makes you earn your grade, so if you plan on slacking or just sliding through, expect a C. The labs are easy, but the write ups can take a good 20 hours to do. Long final but do able if you go to lecture. Chris is a great professor and I wish he taught every phys class.

All the information you need from BIPN 100 is given in lecture and in the course packet. His midterms were fair but his final was ten times more difficult than the practice final. I know several people who left that final in tears. The midterms were very similar to the practice tests but make sure you study even harder for the final.

People tell you not to take mam phys lab because it takes over your life. But with Chris, the labs are interesting, and his lectures are very clear too. super helpful and friendly. the subject itself is pretty difficult. Be ready for his final. Very long and in detail. but everyone loves chris! ps. he invented the preamp. how cool is that.

hella easy (if you arent a lazy tard).  He thinks his tests are hard but they are actually really simple with a few little "tricks" that are meant for weeding out idiots who cannot read the entire problem/follow directions.  It's really not that bad, although the lab is alot of tedious work.  Great teacher though, hes pretty badass.

Professor Armour also teaches at the med school, so he really knowledgeable about his material. The class requires you to know and understand the various processes so you can apply them to different scenarios. The textbook is also not very helpful, maybe except for the pictures and diagrams. Everything you need to know is in the lectures.

He's a very laidback and cool professor who can actually teach.  However, his lectures are very fast-paced, so it can be hard to take notes.  Labs are fun, but the lab reports take about a week to do.  Final is very intense.  Way too much work...
Amazing professor.  Very friendly, insists on being called by his first name, approachable and reasonable.  The best part is how well he lectures, going to them is necessary.
Interesting class. Lots of time spent doing homework and lab reports. Very long and difficult final.

Both the best professor you'll take at UCSD and the hardest. Summer classes are intense and he blasts through the abundant amount of info like speed racer.  Not an easy A class, you will have to work your ass off for it. Don't fall behind.

Awesome. The absolute best physiology professor at UCSD, and one of the best professors I've ever had. He's very concerned with students' learning and takes his job very seriously.  Everything you've heard about the difficulty of this class is true. You have to dedicate an extraordinary amount of time on the lab reports, and the final is difficult.
Pretty tough class, make sure to take an easy qtr if you're taking it! Labs take forever to write up, finals are pretty much impossible, but one of the best classes taught at UCSD.
Great professor.  Taught me physiology as an undergrad, and now that I'm in medical school, I wish that he were teaching my medical physiology class.  I recommend this professor above all others.

GREAT PROF! altho a lot of info are thrown at you in lectures and lab reports literally take DAYS to write up. TAs are very helpful and usually labs don't take up all 5 hours. ask your TA a lot of questions during lab b/c they're the ones grading your work and you can use what they say for the discussions part of the reports.

great prof, fast pace but very clear and organized.  writes on board, doesn't use powerpoint or overheads.  tests are hard but within reason.  book kind of sucks, way too longwinded.  just know the lecture notes and hwk problems very well and you'll get an A.
Phew... hard class because it is information intense. But, Armour really is a great teacher. One of the best lecturers I've ever had. Just be sure you're up for the challenge.

Amazing professor.  Fast pace, but clear.  able to hold my attention for 3 hours.  Tests are difficult but not impossible. Do the homework, know the lecture notes well, and do the reading if you have time.  Reading is the least important, he will never test you on anything he didnt talk about in lecture.  A.S. lecture notes are great, def. buy them

Both Mamm phys I and the lab will be two of the hardest classes you will take at UCSD, but Chris is by FAR one of the best teachers you will ever have in your educational career. He is SO intelligent but never condescending! You will never forget the material you learn in the class, even if it tortures you while you're there!

By far BEST professor at UCSD period. Clear, concise, and most importantly, organized. Nicest guy ever and more than willing to help or even just to talk about his MD/PhD experiences. Lab is fun and laid back, but beware of the final cuz it may kill you. Take his class if you wanna learn some worthwhile stuff!
No Comments

Chris is one of THE BEST BIO PROF @ UCSD!!  His classes were the hardest courses @ the school but the best taught there!!  He's helpful during office hours and always willing to explain things during lab!!  Take an easy load if taking the lab bc the reports will kill you!!  Start studying his material from the beginning of the quarter and throughout because he gives a lot of material and his exams resemble Med School level exams!!  An even greater person outside of class... writes great letters of recc...

He does go over everything required for reports and tests in his lectures.  Pay attention.  If you have questions, ask before the report is due or before the tests.  The TAs rock!  This is the hardest but best class I took at UCSD.  I spent a lot of time on reports so you may want to take a lighter than normal class schedule when you take this.
Though it's one of the hardest, most time-intensive courses, it was also my favorite, and Chris (Dr. Armour) was among my favorite profs.

Prof. is great, but moves way to fast, even for a summer class. 2 weeks scrammed into 1 summer session lecture. Midterms difficult but rep. of practice exams and problems. Final really rep. of midterms.
Straight up gangster!

he's cool and knows his stuff... will actually take the time out to sit next to you and talk, even if you don't want to.  VERY nice guy.  makes the class fun and enjoyable even though it's a lot of work.  probably the best class i've taken at ucsd

It is the best upper-div Bio class I ever took at UCSD. The material itself is very interesting...although it is a lot of work.. he is pretty reasonable with midterms and final. He doesn't pull out stuffs out of no where. overall, your grade depends on how much work you put into it...yes..and going over lecture notes is huge plus for the tests.

What is with this guy?  Apparently he hates doctors, b/c his problem sets diss doctors left and right and talk about how they're all about money.  My question is, why did he go to medical school if he hates medicine so much?  This class's material is from like 30 years ago, not updated at all.  Take someone else.  Somebody who's not so bitter.

Very difficult exams. I found him hard to talk to but that's more my deal than his. He did help me trach my rat when I asked him to. And he helped our group perfuse our frogs a lot. Overall, a nice guy who crams a lot into lecture.
Very hard class, but he is nice and knows his stuff
The best freaking class at UCSD!  He is awesome!  Lab reports are hard but the class is worth it.
His class is hard yet fair.  But maybe that's just me.  He's a cool guy.  Pay very close attention to his lectures because this guy is fast especially during his summer classes.
He's one of the coolest science professors I've ever had, he made learning fun but his tests were hard.

Fantastic. Complete and excellent lectures, very detailed. Exams are very critical thinking oriented, so rote memorization wont help. Humorous and gives everyday applications. Glad to see an enthusiastic professor!

I took mamm phys and endocrinology with Armour over the summer...total ball-buster but well worth it. Be prepared to write like a maniac because he zips through lecture. Take his class if at all possible, you won't find a better prof. anywhere!
First of all, really enjoyed his class. At times the material came fast, but its expected. Well worth it, great professor!
Very entertaining, GREAT teacher, but GPA buster. Well, if you're lazy...
No Comments
He rocks!
Summer School with him is worth it! Throw away your book!
CHANGE MAJORS to take Armour-- Hard, but BEST professor ever!

Fantastic prof and class. Amazing structure: 9 quizzes and 3 were dropped. Quiz corrections added extra points, clicker questions boosted almost 8%, homework on kudu and the final exam had 50% of repeated quiz questions! Great content and lots of opportunities to boost the grade. Definitely worth it!

Most uncaring professor at UCSD. Lab manuals have incorrect directions and the grading rubric doesn't clarify. A joke of a class. Homework, lab reports, mandatory lectures, lab sessions of 4 hours that will take you 8. No choice in picking your lab partner. He randomizes it for you. Wait another quarter if you see him for any of your classes.

Avoid the combination of him and PHYS120 if you can. The class (not designed by him) is already poorly designed and outdated and he made it even worse. Having an organized class material and clear instructions should be the basics of good teaching but unfortunately not in this class.

The worst professor I had at UCSD. He didn't accept my quiz corrections because I didn't include a screenshot of the original quiz question, despite having them all written down on the paper I submitted with all the work and correct solutions. He refused to let me send them afterward, too. I ended up failing his class by 0.9% as a result.

You definitely have to try a lot for this class in order to get an A, but definitely achievable. Does not do a good job at explaining the material, so you definitely have to teach yourself all the material.

Lectures were not very helpful for HW and weekly quizzes. Worked my tail off for this class and was doing well up until the final exam which counted for 40% of the final class grade. So be extra weary of the final exam. Class is very confusing & lectures only scratch the surface of the knowledge you need to know in order to succeed in HW & exams.

This class was hard; primarily due to the weekly quizzes and the fact that I had to teach myself all the material. His slides are taken directly from the textbook, so your best bet is the textbook or youtube video. Arnold is nice himself, but I would say use advantage of TA office hours rather than his. Prepare to study every single week.

He tried to make the quizzes harder so we would fail and the average would go down. There wasn't even a curve. Horrible guy, run away, get any other professor, or just don't take the class. Not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Now I found his course structure quite tedious for a 3 unit class. Weekly quizzes on fridays became quite repetitive and boring. He also liked asking tricky questions and was pretty rigid about his grading scheme. The only good part was that his lecture solving questions were fun to do but that was only for me as I mostly did it asynch.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Kam did not really teach the course so much as read off of the slides, so you really had to read to be able to learn. However, his exams definitely perfectly reflected the material, from the reading and the hw, so I would say you would do quite well assuming you are doing your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He actually doesn't care at all about his students. I get that he's one guy who has 800 students, but he never responded to my messages to the point where I thought he was deliberately ignoring me. He made our quizzes harder because we were doing well on them as if he wanted more of us to do badly on them. Worst prof I've ever had
Watching the lectures isnt going to help at all. The internet is a better teacher. I absolutely do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Meh is all I have to say after taking this condescending Professor. Out of the whole physics series, of course the last one offered would be mediocre at best. The slides he has are completely bombarded with texts and he skims over meticulous problems that may appear in the Kudu HW, as well as in the quizzes. Teach self on Kudu and try to avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: avoid if possible
Isn't as bad as everyone says. Might not be the best at explaining things but all the quizzes and final were very similar to practice problems and HW. Taking the practice final before really helped.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I dont know why the low rating, if the prof is different in person than online, but his class was the only physics class I ever took at UCSD where I actually learned stuff AND got an A in. His lectures are straightforward, he's very helpful. Quizzes every week but if you attend all lectures and do the homework I promise you an A in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: There is so much on his lecture slides that you wouldn't be able to follow along with his lectures. I do good on the weekly quizzes, but I honestly don't understand a thing this man teaches. I read the Kudu textbook and do 40 physics problems the night before his quizzes. Don't take this prof if you actually want to learn and have a good experience

Below-average professor for physics is a catch-all for him. He's a nice guy and all but he actively sought to increase the difficulty on weekly quizzes when the averages were "too high" - whatever that means. He should never be your first choice if you're taking physics, but if you end up with him prepare to go to Porkville.

Lectures got harder to keep up with as quarter progressed. So much text on the slides and just attending lecture won't be enough to fully understand the concepts to do all your hw. Weekly quizzes which I thought were a good way to reinforce material learned in a short period of time but not doing too well on those can really bring your grade down.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures were nice but imo the tests were just so difficult. I normally would make up quizzes with quiz corrections but II couldn't find my mistakes in the original way I did the problem and there was no answer key so I couldn't even do that. It was so defeating trying so hard and now i'm likely going to have to take the class again.

Though this class was not the best, Kam did an fine managing the class. The lectures + homework let you do decent in the quizzes and the curve seems to be really generous. There were a few hiccups here and there, but everything smoothed out by the end and the class really wasn't that bad.

He's not bad or good. If you go to lecture, you learn can sort of learn. Learning from kudu has the same effect though. Quizzes were sort of difficult but not bad either. Lowest quiz grade is dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class and material itself is quite easy. However, the actual professor makes the entire experience a lot more annoying than it needed to be. A majority of the time, it was way easier to learn from the online textbook than to learn from lecture. The quizzes weren't bad, but a lot of questions were made to trick you instead of test you.

Prof Arnold is def knowledgeable about physics however he is unsuccessful in passing on that knowledge... Lectures are unclear and not helpful for the homework and quizzes. If you actually want to learn from someone you are presumably paying, this is not your prof. If you're all for self-teaching, though, go for it. Averages were veryyy low.

Definitely a rough Phys course. While other professors have taken the time to build less punishing rubrics during this online period, this course struggled with quizzes on barely-practiced material, no homework drops, a mandatory 37% final, absence of formula sheets/study guides, and lack of communication with students. I would give our TA a 5/5!

Honestly, I'm leaving this review because so many others are hating on him because they didn't do as well as they liked on the weekly quizzes. But from my experience, all of the quizzes were reasonable in difficulty, and if you just read through the KUDU textbook and do all the homework, that is sufficient to pass and do well. The curve is generous

this was by far the hardest physics class & prof i have taken. lectures are not clear, not given enough time for WEEKLY quizzes (30min for 5-7 questions, other profs give 50 min for 8qs), hard questions. 18-45-37 hw-quiz-final, "7% of grade per week", low quiz avgs. no EC besides .33 back per lost point on quiz corrections. DO NOT RECOMMEND
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was honestly so hard for no reason. Compared to other UCSD physics professors, this professor made the class unreasonably difficult for no reason. He did not give good reason to why the average on a majority of the quizzes we had to take were 2/5 or 3/6 and he gives poor outlines to the subjects he teaches. D/N TAKE!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Arnold taught the subject well and gave decent resources for the course. Many people did not like him because they didn't do well on the tests. The tests were reasonable with decent results if you watch lectures, read the Kudu textbook, do the homework, and have in-depth understanding of the subject. I would take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class isn't that bad if you disregard the class and learn from the internet.

The worst professor I ever took. His lectures are very hard to understand and the class has quizzes every week. The quizzes are only 30 minutes, but it is not enough time considering the number of questions on the quiz. Also, the questions are unnecessarily difficult. Unless he is your only option, I repeat, do not take his class.
The class started out reasonable in difficulty, but all of a sudden, all of our exams became incredibly difficult for no good reason and no warning either, and the curve isn't reasonable either!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He did an excellent job of bringing in demos almost every week. He is very clear with his lectures and does a good job of using clicker questions to make sure we understand the lecture.
Too many assignments for an online course

Very disorganized. Leaves a lot of loose ends in her explanations, her video classes are extremely confusing. She covered some topics that I was already familiar with, and I was mesmerized on how complicated she made them. Questions are not worded well and are unclear. She has a lot of experience, but her teaching style does not work for me.

She is the first professor I have taken for the Accounting Certificate. I love her! She is such a caring professor who was very accessible. Asynchronous format so no lectures to attend at set times. She grades the course on points which I like. She allowed for late assignments and a few times she extended deadlines. You will learn in her class!

one of the best professors I have ever had at ucsd, he is so passionate about teaching and genuinly cares for all of his students success. Make sure to attend lectures because he provides so much more information than what is on the slides, midterms were very fair and reflective of course content. This course made me love my major and physiology.
This is the goat prof. Very digestible slides and straightforward concepts. The whole course is graded on 3 simple exams. He genuinely wants to see students succeed and have fun.

Amazing professor! Really cares about students and makes BIPN super digestible. Slides aren't the best so going to lecture is necessary. You are graded only by exams but he makes them extremely simple and tells you exactly what is on them. Also offers considerable extra credit and is very forgiving. Highly recommend for this infamously hard class!

This class was honestly really easy and extra credit was easy to get too. If you actually pay attention to the lectures the tests are very easy as well. Tests are made from the core concepts as long as you understand the list she provides you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is honestly one of the most unsupportive I've ever taken. Not only are her tests confusing and questions are made to throw you off with her wording, but she does not curve. You would imagine teaching this class for the first time there would be more leniency but she does not care how her class impacts students GPAs. Don't take!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lau is one of those professors that IS trying to trick you. Lectures are long and monotonous. Tests are unnecessarily difficult and overcomplicated, they account for most of your grade. She has no curve either despite low median scores. I wish I read these reviews before I enrolled.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is for PSYC 145 - very cool concepts but professor is incredibly demanding and creates arbitrarily difficult test, more focused on "gotcha" questions rather than application of material. Would recommend avoiding her at all costs

Exams test comprehension more than content knowledge. Study the lecture examples, since those are the focus of the exams! Dr. Lau's explanations were hard to follow, so I had to review the podcasts and outside sources (like using ChatGPT to explain things to me). Weekly homework takes 10 minutes tops. The grade is heavily exam-based.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor is quite knowledgeable and explains things in an easy-to-understand manner. However, the course itself is quite difficult as the majority of the grade is determined by the exams which are multiple-choice and require relatively deep understanding of the material.

Do not take this professor. Test questions are worded poorly and feel geared toward testing how awake you are rather than how well you know the material. The class average across all 3 exams, without the 7% total exam curve, was 66%. Exams cumulatively make up 70% of your grade, so little leniency in curving is ridiculous as a first-time professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: doesnt drop or curve exams. extremely confusing tests and lectures. ur grade is based off three exams basically. final was cumulative but no info on what would be on the exam or where to focus. dont take if you dont have to.

her lectures are super boring. she words her exams to be tricky and she does not curve. her extra credit will only boost you up to like .2% plus her final is cumulative which sucks because i had to go through all 10 lectures which consist of 2-3 hours and no study guide was given or what to expect on the test. do not recommend.

Professor Lau's class demands rigorous effort with challenging tests and no grade curve. Despite the difficulty, his passion for teaching shines through, but alternatives like PSY 101 or 105 offer a more enjoyable experience with achievable success. I don't like this class..... won't recommend to anyone........

her first year teaching and she's very sweet, but this is the most boring psyc class i've ever taken. lectures are long and content isn't explained well at all. I have to look up most of the topics separately. Average grades on the exams are barely passing but she doesn't curve.

Writes test questions to try to trick you, her first year teaching and has no leniency on her grading. Lectures are boring and it's hard to understand her expectations on the material. This class usually has an A average but so far, the average on the tests is barely passing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
He has an excellent grasp on the material & communicates in a concise manner

That being said, he is uninterested in teaching & he VERY obviously doesn't care about us as students

Highly recommend you take him if you want a unique perspective on Central American studies. He's also really awkward, especially when he laughs by himself, at himself. omg

He teaches at CSUN now & I would definitely suggest you take another professor. He's very rude & laughs at people who don't give him the answer he's looking for. Although his class was pretty easy, it can also get very boring. A LOT of readings. DON'T TAKE HIM!

Class was a bit boring. Tries to make it interesting. In class group work. May play favoritism with students so get on his good side. 3 essays. Manageable. Will help you if you show effort. Make sure to show up. Overall, nice guy with a funky clothing style, dry humor, but he truly wants you to learn the material through interesting lectures
Sometimes he speaks really quickly, but he's entertaining and I really wish I knew where he was from, I can't figure it out for the life of me

Axel was on of my favorite professors at UCSD! Although his class was challenging, it was also very interesting and I learned a lot about the Spanish language and South American / Spanish culture! If you want to actually learn Spanish, make sure Axel is your professor. His class is fulfilling and you will leave his class knowing Spanish!

Don't listen to other people. The only reason you would have to dislike him is if you don't try in class, but if you show some effort he is more than willing to help you out. It's not like it's an easy A but he's a really good teacher and just wants you to think critically, and thats your A. I would definitely recommend taking him.

This TA clearly plays favorites and is not afraid to give a large majority of the class Ds.  He asks questions that he knows the answers to and isn't very flexible when it comes to acknowledging other interpretations.  Luckily he liked me and gave me As across the board.  Unfortunately, the same cannot be said for my classmates.  Approach with caut
No Comments
CHANGE sections immediately. trust me, its not worth it. he made my life hell.

Ginoo Alicio is one of the best and most caring teachers I have had at UCSD. Though I must admit this class was a bit more challenging than your average high school Filipino course. It is very specific on grammar and tenses. It is important to go over vocab/pages before class so that you are able to ask questions and answer when called on.

Professor/Ginoo Alicio is the BEST teacher I have ever had in my life. I took LIHL132 a long time ago where I met Ginoo Alicio and I'm so glad I did. He is a very intellectual and intelligent man. He cares so much about his students and it shows. Literally the #1 teacher in the world! You will learn so much!

Taken as a remote learning class, both the professor and class went smooth. Class time is mainly made up of going over the previously assigned hw pages in the mandatory textbook. He popcorns people so make SURE you do the homework. One con is since he has some trouble navigating canvas, you won't know your grade until the end of the quarter really.

I did not know how to read or speak in Filipino so I was surprised I passed the placement exam. You do have to buy the textbook ($20) and if you are completely new the fact that it is completely in Tagalog can be scary (just use translators or ask the professor). He's super sweet and cares about his students. Great intro class!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Alicio is such an adorable little Lolo. He is a good lecturer and makes a lot of typical funny filipino dad jokes, which made it enjoyable to be in class. The grades when I took it were dependent on 3 quizzes, 4 homeworks, 1 oral/1 written final exam. Also class is mandatory but its only twice a week no discussion.
Great professor.

Professor Averitt is one of the best physics professors I've ever had. His office hours were very open. His lectures were fun and you can tell he is passionate about teaching well. Quizzes were fair and the extra credit was very useful, with there being opportunities on every test. Overall, he's a wonderful professor, I would 100% take him again.

He is one of the nicest professors you will encounter in your Physics journey. He offers a lot of extra credit on quizzes and the final exam. Going to office hours is very helpful as it helped me get a lot of conceptual gaps filled in. 

Also very flexible with unavoidable conflicts with quizzes

I think he is one of the most inspiring professors that I have had. His passion for physics is clear and makes me want to come to class to learn. The only reason my rating is not a 5 is that his lecture style is a little all of the the place, making some concepts a bit confusing. But if you want to feel excited about physics take this teacher.

Professor Averitt is really chill. Super engaging lectures, but very tedious homework. Quizzes are never that much different from lecture, hw, and practice problems, etc... He's very fair and offers extra credit on quizzes. The class isn't curved but the grading scheme makes is hard to fail. I would be happy to take one of his classes again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Could be better, but not too bad. Course was challenging overall, and there was weekly homework which required a lot of thinking, but was graded on effort. Lectures and discussions are mandatory, which is quite unsatisfying. Maybe not the best professor in the school, but surely not the worst and was generous with extra credit.

Four mandatory lectures, discussion, 2-5 ~25 min supplementary videos, every week. The class isn't difficult if you study things that are not assigned for the class, like other mechanics textbooks. At the very least he offered a lot of extra credit on the final.

Word of caution to those looking to take 4A, Math 20A is not an apt prerequisite.
Good person and sociable. He offered a lot of extra credit when the class grades were down. However, he is not a great lecturer and his class is test heavy.

Averitt is a nice person with a good sense of humor. However, you will need to read the textbook thoroughly and do a good number of practice problems to ace the quizzes and the final. Averitt noticed that the quiz averages were low and generously gave us extra credit opportunities to make up lost points.
Dont recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Richard Averitt is by far the nicest professor at UCSD. He is approachable and respects the students. But he cant teach well although he tries. Never answers emails. And difficult finals. If you think you can get away easily, then I would say this course isnt for you. You really have to study. Dont recommend overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He really isnt into teaching, more like research oriented. I heard his grad students work very hard. He went off-tangent too much while explanations and has a bad handwriting. Uploaded the materials in the last moment. The test was hard. That being said, he was very nice during office hours and was patient to answer the questions.

Hated his class so much. He posts docs and links to assignments at the last second right before due time, never answers emails. He is all over the place during lecture and has a very sloppy handwriting. He is very nice in a 1-1 set up, he just is not good at teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Passionate professor. Great lectures, and hard exams, but if you understand the knowledge you will know his exams are reasonable. Very helpful during experiments. Learned a lot from this man.

Most passionate professor I've had so far. Very down to Earth, which is saying something for Physics. There was always a quiz problem straight from lecture. This is for the 4 series tho (for phys majors) not 2 (for engineers) so we tend to love in depth. Actually wish he went more in depth. Final wrecked me tho since we were behind, so beware.

Clicker questions are the only form of examples you're ever going to get, so prepare to do your own reading and work.  Homework is worth 5% of the grade, but it's online, and you have to pay for it. I don't think 50 bucks is worth 5% of the grade.  Seriously, prepare to do your own notes and reading, because lecture will not reflect quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Richard Averitt has been by far my favorite Physics Professor here at UCSD,  I added this page just so I could review him. He's always excited for class and that enthusiasm really helps you stay invested in the material. He actually teaches the class instead of just lecturing, it's awesome. Can't wait to have him again next quarter!

Great professor and VERY accessible. He truly wants to help you succeed and aids you by providing a ton of extra credit opportunities. His class is honestly quite easy and it promotes a lot of learning.

This class is extremely hard, but he really cares that you understand the material. He listens to feedback, and tries to make sure the class is understanding the material. He stays back after class if anyone has any questions just to make sure people do good. As long as you complete all the work he assigns, you will be able to do well in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Narla really cares about his students, and he's very flexible. If you express your concerns he will listen to you and make changes about the course. He always makes time for questions and really wants the best for you! Doing all of the homework and extra credit may be time consuming but it works out!

Ok, so I wont lie this class is difficult. I came in with no previous physics knowledge and this class was hard. BUT, for all of you out there that have to take this class take Professor Narla! This guy really cares about you, which is hard to find in a prof at UCSD. And he makes it easier to get a good grade in a difficult class (extra credit)!

I never saw this dude the whole quarter but my TA Alessio was chill. Lab reports were kind of annoying but they drop 1 lab and 1 quiz so its alright. Anything above 90% is an A or A+, so generous cutoffs.
Physics labs suck here. Quizzes purposefully try to trick you, and you don't get feedback. You also barely get feedback on lab reports. The reports are mind-numbing and repetitive.

What even happened. Bro had good reviews and now it's really bad. Bro never shows up for the labs, and his TA's were pretty dog too. Like how do I a -1 deduction for including my raw lab data???? Make it make sense! Crib sheets are your only way of doing somewhat decent on the quizzes. And I think bro has a thing for uncertainties like holy cow.
Terrible professor and the worst three classes I took at this school were taught by him, yet he never shows up and relies on his unqualified, incompetent TA's to do the instructing.
Just wait for another quarter to take ANYONE else. You will regret it if you take this class with this professor.

This class gives very few tests and lab reports which means that if you do poorly on one of them then you're grade may be at jeopardy. This wouldn't usually be a problem unless if your professor and TA grade very harshly and don't give feedback to help you out. Not very professional when it comes to being at a top notch university.
Just forget about. It would be better learning from an illiterate 5-year-old then trying to takeaway anything from this class.

Yagil and Avi are genuinely the worst professors I've had to deal with in my college career. The TA you get also matters, for instance my TA Jiashu never helped out during labs and always made it more confusing and problematic. The professors are never present and create an uninviting experience. Just wait until next quarter if you need this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class only 6/10 weeks. Lab 5/6 weeks. Lab reports due 1 week after lab and grading policies were very unclear. He takes points off for minor mistakes and does not give half credit. 50% of the grade is four 5 question quizzes taken the first 15 minutes of the last four labs and they are so stupid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: (for the TA of my lab:) Worst lab ever taken. Got 5 on AP physics C and learned multivariable calculus in high school, but I still struggle in lab. Did not learn anything. Pick on the smallest mistakes. Zero useful feedback. Labs are super easy, but lab reports are hard and terrible. Quizzes are on every small detail in the syllabus.

This guy pulls in $348k/year (Transparent California) to not appear a single time throughout the quarter. Even the TA's have never seen him. Incredibly difficult pre-lab quizzes (time crunch/niche procedure stuff + physics problems not done in the 1A lecture class) with hard lab reports that have super inconsistent grading.

Never have seen Yagil in any of the PHYS1L labs. The TAs are not helpful in giving clear instruction for the lab, the lab conclusions are not graded fairly or consistently, and there is no support for this class. The quizzes never reflect the material we are supposed to know. Useless lab that doesn't help with understanding lecture topics

Spare yourself and take ANYONE else. Response expectations are nebulous, and that's being kind. If you give the correct answer but your wording didn't satisfy whatever the expectation is you can still get an f for it, and the expectation really is unclear. I've given thorough and correct responses and received almost no credit for them

Prof. Yagil and the other two profs "instructing" this course have never shown their faces to the class and have never held office hours. Extremely hard quizzes and the lab reports are graded ridiculously hard. No instruction on how to do things. Instead of trying to teach us, they lower the grading scale and we learn nothing. Incredibly lazy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a lab class so it really depends on your TA, but overall the TAs are gonna be just as confused as you are. Professor didn't even bother to introduce himself and just used videos from Professor Tsai to teach. Slow at responding to questions, and really just does not care at all about students and teaching in general.

Awful professor. Never bothers to introduce himself or even get involved with any of the students. Takes forever to respond to questions and is incredibly dismissive of any kind of gripe you might have about the assignments, grading, etc. We deserve a better teaching staff especially with the kind of money we're paying
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Yagil is never present in his class other than the occasional announcement. This class is horrible, I would never take this class again. TA's barely help, very harsh grading on labs, quizzes only 3 questions worth 7 points meaning it tanks your grade more than the actual lab. GPA dropper for no reason. It's better to take 2AL than 1AL.

He purposely makes the quizzes overly difficult and confusing, and will write specific instructions called "quiz prep" on what you should study for, then test you on none of that material. When students brought this up, he doubled down on dismissing their concerns and made the quizzes harder out of spite. Labs were ok. Watch out for the quizzes.

I can't rate the professor, as I do not know what he looks like whatsoever. He showed us old videos from another professor. The class itself, quizzes were okay but the labs were rough. Be ready to put in the work.

I was fine with the biweekly quizzes as I was mostly prepared for them. However, I felt the difficulty of the labs was quite variable. Either it would be too easy or too tedious (therefore hard). Hence, I feel that incongruity in lab difficulty kinda made it unpredictable as to how much time people would take to complete it in different weeks.

We were given biweekly quizzes about physics concepts even though we were already being quizzed on this material in 1c. When it was brought up to him, he purposely ignored anything we had to say and argued that we were just not studying hard enough. Avi Yagil, I don't hold any personal grudges towards you, but I hope u reconsider your career choice
DON'T TAKE ANY CLASSES WITH HIM!! he is not responsive to emails and we have never ever seen his face this quarter. it's finals week and we still don't know the grading scale for his garbage labs!
Simple: don't take his class.

Leave it to professor Yagil to make COVID learning more difficult than it needs to be. He introduced timed quizzes for your lab reports when the previous two quarters did it well with a pre-lab section on the actual lab write-up. He's so incredibly unempathetic to students during a pandemic; emailing us "just read more" when asked for help.

This class is unjustifiably more difficult and time-consuming than both of the prerequisite physics classes and labs (1AL and 1BL). This guy is the dirt on the bottom of my shoe compared to Philbert Tsai. No doubt. Garbage can of a class. Glad it's the last physics I ever have to deal with.

I really dont know how the grading criteria works in these labs, but I gotta say thank god for the curves. Also, I have never seen this man irl and have no idea who he is due to the nature of physics labs being that you only have contact and are graded by your lab TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: I have had Professor Yagil for two lab classes now. Obviously not by choice, he writes quizzes that are really difficulty considering the lecture is always behind the lab. I dont comprehend how UCSD decide curriculum for this class, but all I can say is I hope your TA is nice and can help you understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He looks like he'd be a grouch but he's actually a really nice guy. If you ask him for help, though, don't expect him to just give you the answer. He likes to make his students use their logic to come up with the answer. The final was really fast-paced (like his lectures). However, he puts all the lecture slides online, so it's not a huge deal.

45 quizzes (40%) and final (60%). He really cares for his students. He posts his lectures online, which are really clear and easy to follow. That's good since he goes kind of fast during class. The quizzes are representative of the easy and medium homework problems. Final was a little harder than quizzes but still doable.

Tests and quizzes are representative of the homework. Wants the student to ask questions about the lecture. Lecture goes fast but that's because there are a lot of material to cover. Lectures are not mandatory and slides are posted online. They are very clear and not confusing. He even arranges homework by difficulty. Overall, very solid teacher

Dr. Yagil is a good professor - he really wants to make sure you get down the fundamental concepts.  Quizzes are 10 questions each and about 1-3 questions are conceptual while the rest are calculation based.  I found the quizzes easier than the homework.  Final worth 60% of grade, quizzes are worth 10% each (top 4 out of 5 quizzes).  Get Chegg.
Didn't keep the class as involved as I would have liked. It was very difficult to pay attention to his lectures. But he knew what he was teaching very well and clearly enjoyed the topic.

He's fine, but I didn't get much out of the lab lecture. He's a good professor though and it seems like he cares. The lab isn't easy, and if you don't put in the work into the lab reports, you won't do well. You need to make sure you look at the grading rubrics (which are posted) and see that you do everything that's required of you.

He's a very caring professor. Go to lecture! It's not mandatory and he posts the slides online, you'll learn more by going to lecture and asking questions. Class depends on your TA, though. Start the lab reports BEFORE going to lab the day that they're due. Also, FOLLOW THE RUBRICS. The graders follow them. To ace the final, do the homework.

He is a very good professor! Go to class all the time and you won't be confused when taking the quizzes. He gives very good tips, good examples, good lectures, and he is VERY organized and prepared for every lecture.He is extremely nice and just a great professor overall. TAKE HIM!

There are only 4 lab reports in his class, along with 4 quizzes and a final exam. You get the quiz questions ahead of time, so make sure you get all the answers (20% of your grade). Lab reports take quite a bit of time to complete, so try to do the majority before  the 2nd lab. Don't bother going to class, lecture notes are online.

very kind hearted teacher.  Cares about his students, and wants everybody to learn.  Unfortunately the TA i got was horrible and very knitpicky so i got points off for every possible little thing.  I have a 54% in my class now, i'm just hoping i pass because of this dumb TA.  he supposedly checks for bias grades so lets hope!

Professor Yagil is probably one of the best science professors I have encountered at UCSD.  He will explain concepts in different ways to ensure comprehension, and will always take a question.  Very friendly.  His tests are almost identical to the homework he recommends you do, and you get a formula sheet.  I love him, and am sad he isn't doing 1B.
No Comments

Pretty helpful. Lectures clarify the what is expected on the labs. The rest of the lectures comes from the statistic part of the textbook, which relates to our finals. Do the homework problems! Labs are pretty interesting and easy.

Lecture slides are helpful in the labs, but impossible to follow during lectures. He is  a fast and soft speaker w/ an accent which makes things harder to follow. Homework is cake compared to final exam. Do many extra problems from book to prepare for final, lab material is not covered. TAs were usually confused about how to handle things in labs.

I took this course with Professor Ayden Maralani years ago. His approach to teaching transistor-level circuit design sparked a strong interest in the subject. Since graduating, I've been working in transistor-level design professionally, and I still love it.
The way professor Maralani taught analog circuit design I learned a great deal. His considerations for the final grade was very helpful too. Big like!
i must say that i was very happy with the professors teaching style and his pace. he made this subject very interesting to follow and i would certainly take him again.

Prof. Maralani has proven to be a very capable professor who cares about his students' learning. He really focuses on catering to students' needs and struggles and he is very helpful in his office hours. I would definitely take him again.
He did a fantastic job teaching us this quarter. Thank you, Sir! I am happy with my grade, too ...
Great professor, absolutely recommend
Professor Maralani has passion to deliver practical knowledge to his students. He genuinely cares about their learning.

Prof Maralani is a very humdrum lecturer. It's painful sitting through his lecture, also hard to understand what he's saying.  The quiz averages were incredibly low, the first one being around 36%. He did curve significantly though.  I got a grade higher than I felt I deserved, like in all the rest of my ECE classes. Caring and kind prof though.
Happy with my grade an important course and knowledgeable professor.
I had an interview for an internship. I can see why professor Maralani had a lot of emphasis on learning concepts. Some of the exam problems were challenging however they are rewarding for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Worst lecturer ever. Boring and dry. Constantly contradicts himself and glosses over stuff. Refuses to do any examples on the board.  He does not teach the material effectively at all. Class avg on one of the exams was less than 30%. At that point there is something wrong with the professor and not the class. Avoid if at all possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is one of the best ECE professor . He explains the materials clearly in class. You do no even need to read books outside of class. Reviewing material by looking lecture notes is enough. It is easy to get an A if taking his class.
He is the best prof I have met in UCSD. You can definitely get an A if you take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Maralani is a very good teacher and very helpful in office hours. He is very concerned about his students learning and succeeding and he gives an intuitive understanding of the course material and how to apply it. I did find ECE102 to be a harder-than-average class, but that intuition is essential if you continue with the circuits depth.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: You need to study everything by yourself if you are going to take his course.

He explains the material really well and create quizzes and exams that really tests your understanding of the concepts. He wants you to understand the concept rather than how to solve problems. He is a great professor.

I am happy with my grade. I appreciate a professor who deeply cares about his students success. He went out of his way and adjusted the syllabus based on the outcome of the class to help us. That is remarkable.

He is a great professor, fair and hardworking. I think it was his first time teaching this course. I can see that he is only going to get better. He genuinely cares about his students and gave everyone a chance to improve.
I got the grade that I want because I worked hard for it. Sorry, no free As here.
He really shows genuine concern for his students by offering incentives to boost their grades. I cant deny that helped me.

It is so true that you have to learn things on your own most of the time, but I heard it is the same for other professors too. There are so many details in the notes that you should fully understand; otherwise, exams are gonna be hard. Lectures are boring and tests are VERY challenging. However, he has a fairly generous curve. This class is hard.

Prof. Maralani is a great teacher. He really cares about the success of his students both inside and outside of the classroom. His class is challenging, but achieves its purpose in teaching the material and preparing the student for future circuit classes (ECE164).

Get ready to work hard in this course. It's got predefined lecture notes that every professor teaches off of them. What I like about this professor is that he explains them all on the blackboard and gives additional information to help understanding the material. As a professor, he really cares about students to learn and do well.

An extremely hard professor who isnt quite good at explaining material. Had him for ECE100 and all he did was read notes of the lecture slide that was already made by a previous professor. Barely wrote anything on the blackboard. I would highly recommend avoiding him. You will have to study everything on your own and his tests are pretty darn hard.

I do owe professor Maralani a good review! He was one of the best professors Ive had at UCSD. I had a successful job interview because of him. He truly tries to prepare his students for the real world problems. He is very passionate and knowledgeable in analog circuit design and I learned a great deal. He graded on a curve and was very generous.

I took this course with Professor Ayden Maralani years ago. His approach to teaching transistor-level circuit design sparked a strong interest in the subject. Since graduating, I've been working in transistor-level design professionally, and I still love it.
Professor Maralani was a genuine teacher, fair and hardworking. He really cared about his students learning and excelling. He was always available during his office hours and truly willing to help.
The way professor Maralani taught analog circuit design I learned a great deal. His considerations for the final grade was very helpful too. Big like!

He didn't offer a whole lot of material to prepare for testing, other than a single quarter of past exams. I would strongly recommend redoing homework to study. Lecture slides were pretty helpful with early course material but less so later on as the course gets more complex. Not the best experience in ECE but ultimately was a fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Honestly, the hardest professor i have ever taken in UCSD. Would strongly recommend avoiding him. Reads material off of the lecture slide that has already been posted before the class. Barely writes down anything to explain. Tests are extremely hard and he expects you to know everything.

He was always ready to answer questions, stressed the value of participation for all, regardless of confidence levels, which greatly enriched the learning atmosphere. I especially appreciated his encouragement that there are no dumb questions. His discussions were outstanding, Definitely looking forward to seeing him teach again.

At the start of Phil10, many friends warned me about how challenging and confusing Logic could be. However, with Ayoob's assistance, I've had an exceptional learning experience. He genuinely cares for students and ensures everyone feels comfortable seeking help when needed. Very grateful to have had him and only wish I had taken this class sooner.

Class was pretty easy considering, but the TA was a non-entity, so don't hold your breath for test grades. Reading was interesting but more focused on foundational philosophy of the mind than more advanced things. I really hope you like brains in vats.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Shahmoradi makes complicated stuff sound like a piece of cake. He is the most caring professor I have had at UCSD. Office hours turn into deep discussions about philosophy (and Godel whom he seems to know a lot about), not just homework. His passion for the subject is contagious. Made me decide to major in philosophy. Wish he taught more.

I completely agree with the comment below. I got extra credit points just by doing yoga. It is ridiculous. The class was super disorganized. She does not reply to emails and posts passive-aggressive announcements all the time. Even the TA was confused. The class was just super disappointing overall. Avoid at all costs.

You can literally get extra credit for playing among us with other classmates and its an UD class. For starters, she didnt post an exact syllabus until week 3 into the quarter. Shes always off topic, posts lectures late online late, dont expect to learn much, changes assignments, exams, and the grading constantly. Worst professor Ive ever had.
she likes to ignore students when they ask her for help and clarification. She is very not organized in everything. worst prof at UCSD

Most disorganized professor I have EVER had. Does not hold regular office hours, and forces the students to check the calendar constantly to see when they are. Her exams and assignments are poorly worded. Gets very defensive when feedback is given (or even questions about the course itself). Don't take if you want to stay sane (:

Never have I had a professor so unwilling to listen to their students' feedback. When I asked her a question about an assignment (that was graded on points, but was not provided with any description of what these points are for), her response was defensive and honestly very rude.

I was worried about all the writing esp term paper but she makes clear whats expected and you get feedback and help through the quarter. Exams are super fair. Based on lectures and she even gives out study guide. Wasnt disorganized or late when I took it. Really liked how lectures make you question and think. Felt a bit like a brain detective!
