Good class, learn a lot about MATLAB for research purposes.  The professor is very passionate about this, but the class is not well organized.  Prof. shows up late or not at all for lectures, leaving material to the TA (if he has it.... usually not).  Communication about calendar, assignments, etc. needs to improve

Professor Saygin taught a Matlab class that was hard but soooooooo useful! She developed this class. It was hard but wow we learned so much. I am using the knowledge in my research in the lab I am in. Professor cares about your learning, is engaging and fun. And the way she rolled her eyes at people walking into lab during quiz was awesome!

this was in COGNITIVE SCIENCE. anyway this class was interesting and fun. assignments made us think outside the box. she clealy knew her material and very enthustiastic. the videos were amazing and the "debate" session was really great. i learned so much amazing stuff in this class and remember it still several years later.
It was a few years ago but I remember Prof Saygin well. The class was great and I learned a lot! Shouldhave studied more but grades were fair.
No Comments
great teacher
No Comments

He is an angel! One of my favorite. It is stress free and pretty interesting. He is so knowledgable, helpful, clear, polite, and funny. I would definitely recommend for anybody who wants to take this class.
I really like his teaching method, he introduces the stuff as a problem and then asks class discuss the both sides of the argument. It really helps you remember the readings.

He explains complicated topics very clearly. Friendly and easy going. His lectures are always interesting. Class is a combination of lectures and discussions. Not so hard but you need to do the readings.

She is a clear and engaging lecturer who explains concepts in an easy-to-understand way. Her teaching style is organized and discussion-based, and she encourages participation. She is knowledgeable and makes the material feel accessible to students.
She's a good professor. Makes class fun and intriguing every time. This class can be an easy elective class for anyone to take fyi

(ohhhh don't take this profff, she's BADDDD) 
NAHHHH- just leave room for ME so I could take MOREE OF HER CLASSES BEFORE IT GETS WAITLISTED!!

Easy and interesting class that's definitely gonna be a GPA booster
Not a lot of stress for this class
No midterm or final
Lots of readings, but again, it's easy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: took this class as an elective; truly was a great decision i made
Made lectures engaging bc theres no quizzes, midterm or final. and bc there's no exams, this class was going at an easy pace
She's a nice prof who cares for her students. idk what else to say besides the fact that she's cool!!

it's literally week 2 and I'm writing this! I'm rating her this early, bc I KNOW she's going to continue to be an amazing prof this fall quarter!!
Work is manageable, and her lectures are entertaining. From what I know... no midterms or finals; just homework!
This is the best teacher in the Communications department. I have taken many classes with her and she is very caring and generous. She values student learning and is just awesome.

Amazing professor! We always had really great class discussions and she created such a great atmosphere in our class. She really cares about what students have to say and is super sweet. She also grades really easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor mumbles during lecture and it's not really clear what he is saying, especially if you are taking this course for the first time. Just writes down equations on a chalkboard without telling us where it came from and jumps from topic to topic without much guidance. Why does our math department have to be so bad
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's not good at teaching

His lectures and equivalent lecture notes were helpful and well-structured. While exams had no cheat sheet, he made exams so that every problem except one appeared in some form in the lecture notes, still excluding the most difficult & nonintuitive ones, with many points for definitions and basic properties (at least last quarter). Nice guy too.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chill and engaging,tells it like it is, great stories,fun to participate with. But don't let that fool you. Exams are brutal and make up most of your grade. Tests are unforgiving. The kind of guy you'd grab a beer with, just not someone you want writing your exams.

Course MGT 105. Chill dude. Lowk nonchalant. First test lowk took me by surprise, but I did good the other two. There's two individual small projects and one group project at the end. Three-hour lectures were longgg, but he gave a break in the middle. Didn't take attendance, but doesn't record the lecture. 3 exams are around 47-50 questions.

Very laid back class. Just studying the slides and taking some notes are enough to pass the class. If you like marketing than it may be the class for you, but otherwise its kinda boring. 3hr long lectures do make it a drag to get through but not a hard class at all. Chill guy as well.

engaging lecturer and interesting professor, but provided poor support and lack of guidance to students for exams and final project. three hour lecture format is difficult to focus and he does not record lectures. material was not difficult overall, just get ready for a LOT of memorization
Great teacher, the 3 hour class just made it hard for me to stay focused. I ended up doing textbook readings which helped a lot for the tests. The group project is also really straightforward!

One of the best lecturers at UCSD imo. Very engaging and just generally a cool dude. The class itself is a lot of term memorization, so quizlet will be your homie for the tests. The hw is super light, maybe an hour per assignment. There's also a group project, so make sure you take this class with some friends if you can. Overall a chill class.

If you want a class with structure, don't take this class. Gave no study guides for exams. Group project worth 20% of grade. He said the final would only be on the last two lectures as a treat for us but he surprised us by not even showing up and making the final cumulative. Gave interesting lectures. Just memorize slides to study.

Most engaging lectures at UCSD. HW is super easy, just do it and you'll get full credit + rady lab is 20% of your grade. Project is huge, get a good group, fair grader. Tests were super manageable (if you go to lecture, take notes and study a bit), and thats the whole class. Lectures really fly by and he left me wanting more

I personally loved this professor. He's a great lecturer and I thought his class was extremely interesting. The assignments throughout the class are simple but he'll take off points if you don't do it exactly as he wants. The projects easy but just get a good group. Study for the exams and you'll be fine, I didn't and still passed.

Caried a solid A+ the entire course until the final. No study guides provided, lectures are basically him just reading off the slide. He seems like a really cool dude but just not the best professor in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bates is a good, captivating lecturer. Even though the class was 3 hours, his lectures were interesting and consisted of a good balance between concepts, examples, videos and anecdotes related to the lecture content. For the exams, I would recommend reading the chapters corresponding to the lectures.

Asked him in class if final was cumulative and he gave a very vague answer: didn't want to leave us with a semester where we didn't learn anything, so I think it was cumulative, and only emailed the day before the exam to say that the final was taking the last three weeks :)
no clear rubric or answer for every question, exam or group project

Fall 21: It was 100% in person and we met once a week for 3 hours. His lectures were really engaging and easily digestible. This course is graded on a few homework assignments, group project, midterm, and final. Midterm is easier than final. Group project is a huge chunk of your grade so be sure to get a good group. Definitely read the textbook!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The project was heavy and the finals are optional. I managed to get an A without going to his lecture synchronously though it's still a must to watch the lectures. The project is the most important part and you need to attend office hours for a better understanding of what to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Caring

reviews.comment: The project takes 30% (did not give any specific instruction and expectation on the work, even does not explain how to do it) One midterm, one final exam. The midterm is more clear, but the final is the same as a project, no clear instruction, no study guide, no review. I even worried that he will give us the question out of the textbook.

Bates is a good lecturer, although the class can be boring since its 3 hours long. Midterm/Final are easy multiple choice exams. Little/no homework, but there is a group(4-7 ppl) final project worth 30%. Bates wasn't clear on his expectations for the project; grade is very dependent on the effort that you and your groupmates put in

Bewarned. Dont take him if you can. He does not give clear rubric from the project. His midterm is textbook heavy, which covers nothing he teaches in class. The homework is also irrelevant to his lectures. Stay away from him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst professor. Grades extremely hard on everything even though he doesn't give a clear rubric or any sort of guidelines. I asked him how to study for the midterm and he told me to just look at the lecture slides but a majority of questions on the actual exam could not be answered unless you read the textbook. Why did he give me misleading info?
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His group project thats 30% of your grade is a huge pain and does not have clear Instructions. His lectures are interesting but if you want to do well the class it all comes down to textbook details. I dont feel like I learned or gained anything in the class but he curved so thats pretty great - but wouldnt take him again.

Bates' class is not that hard as long as you have your time committed to reading the textbook and take notes in class. Even though it's a 3-hour long class, it's not that boring and there's a break halfway through. A couple of homework, 1 group project, 1 midterm, and 1 final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed prof Bates's class. He is funny and lectures were interesting even though they were 3 hours long. He doesn't include much in powerpoints, so going to class and taking notes is vital. The class involves a lot of memorization and the exams were somewhat challenging, but if go to class and study you should be fine! I recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Bates! Overall an excellent speaker. I actually found myself paying attention not because I had to but because I wanted to. His exams are very doable as long as you're studying. I liked how he structured the group assignment. He did so in a way to keep us on track also instructions are very clear. Take him for marketing!!!

Overall good prof. Funny, charismatic, good speaker. Likes to talk, but brings up funny and interesting things and plays some cool videos in class. Powerpoints are clear but the tests are 100% based on the textbook details, some of which weren't covered in class. Attendance is mandatory btw. He's a good teacher overall though and would take again.

Prof Bates is a great lecturer and is very knowledgeable in marketing. The class has a midterm and final, with small weekly homework assignments and a group project worth 30% of class grade. His tests are difficult but he curves it to a C average. He is very organized and clear on grading criteria.

Professor Bates' first quarter at UCSD so he is still feeling it out. Overall, absolutely knows material well and is experienced in the subject. He is a friendly, nice guy and is willing to help. 1 Group Project creating a product/service, Midterm, and Final. Tests were long and kinda tough (test bank questions). Not a hard to earn a B. Curved.

Prof Saba is wonderful. You can tell how intelligent he is by the way he explains concepts. There were 5 tests total (in class essays), and that's all. None were cumulative. He grades tough but fair, and is willing to discuss it with you and even change it. He is very funny so I enjoyed his lectures, but the content will stretch you. Pay attention.

The way Professor Saba lectures is so clear and organized, it's genuinely amazing. Readings were hard sometimes, but he helps you see the structure and the concepts when he lectures. Gives great and detailed feedback on tests.

His class is hard, I'm an A student and barely got an A-. There's so much reading and none of it makes sense unless you go to lecture (he doesn't podcast). Can't miss even one unless you're messed up. He grades hard (5 essay exams are the only grade) and is looking for specific answers that feel like you're being drowned in abstract phil thoughts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super organized class structure. Readings, lecture, weekly homework on readings -> repeat. He's a tough grader, but if you read before AND after class+pay attention to lecture (take good notes!), you will be prepared to get a good grade. You can't skirt by this class without doing anything tho, as he's looking for specific answers to the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His class is fun, and his explanation is clear though readings are hard. He sometimes throws out way too many jargons but he is willing to clarify. Not an intimidating class as long as you do the reading in a timely manner and go to the lectures.

He's an amazing lecturer. He holds your attention well and is pretty funny. Makes dense course readings palatable and easy to parse - he has outlines for each reading posted on Canvas which create a great compass to guide you through each one. He doesn't grade easily, but if you do the reading and pay attention in class, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's legit my favorite prof ever. Super caring, funny, and teaches really well. His exams are straightforward, and he doesn't try to make it difficult. Literally would take all my classes with him if i could.

I made an account just to Rate this Prof. Best lecturer I had at UCSD. Makes everything so nice and easy to understand and actually interesting. I looked forward to every lecture this class, it was a nice break from all my STEM classes. Love him please take this class!

He is one of the best professor. His lecture is amazing and he can explains things well. There are many things to read but if you listen to his lecture and take notes, it is not hard to have a good grade.

this professor has truly been one of my favorites during my undergrad experience. though he speaks quite quickly, he is more than happy to clarify when you ask. overall, as long as you are caught up on lecture, and go to OH before a test is due (and take his advice), then you should be ready to go for his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I found his comments and remarks to be pretty funny, but it's hard to vocalize that when it's over zoom and often dead silent. He doesn't exactly explain things the most clearly sometimes, but if you ask him to clarify, he is more than happy to help until you understand. Polite, caring, and humble are definitely right words to describe him.

If you just want to get this GE out of the way, Bazargan is the way to go. He is very clear about what is expected. His 3 "essay" assignments really just ask you to summarize a specific part of the author's arguments and to give your opinion. No final, discussion attendance is mandatory, should be easy to get a B with minimal effort.

Grade is dependent on 3 papers and going to discussions. Papers are very straightforward, as they ask to reiterate author's arguments. Prof provided outlines of readings which was SUPER useful for papers. Like other writing based courses, your grade on papers are dependent on the TA. Going to class is a great way to substitute the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Your grade in this class will HEAVILY depend on your TA. Like every other phil/writing class. As someone who consistently scored B+'s in all of my other writing classes, I managed to get an A in this class. Tests themselves are very straightforward and easy if you go to class and skim the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Class consists of a dozen or so readings. 3 short essay exams consisting of 3 questions each. First is worth 20%. Next two are worth 35%. The grading on the exams are pretty harsh, but the grading is skewed (kinda has like a curve).

If you're an auditory learner, you'll probably benefit a lot from going to lecture. If you're a visual learner, you might have a bit of trouble because his entire lecture is basically a 50 minute long speech on the readings with little to no visual texts or powerpoints.

Good professor, and is very fair with grading. The course material is interesting, but you must keep up with the readings (all online, no textbook) because they are very dense. Overall, I would recommend taking Phil 28 with Bazargan!

Pretty interesting class but things got more complex. His lectures are very clear, don't even need to read the readings or the book. I Just study his notes and got an A. He just writes the quizzes and the TA's grade them. He speaks slow so you can get everything down.

Good professor. He lectures by just speaking without writing anything down but it's easy to follow along and take notes because he's clear and well organized. His lectures are more or less summaries of the readings so it's easy to go back and look if you missed anything. I thought I would hate this class but it turned out to be really interesting!

Pretty good professor. He just talks and writes on the board occasionally so you will have to pay attention to what he is saying but he does his best to make sure the class gets the major points down. I would take him for another philosophy class if I had the chance
He's my young dude. This fool is a good guy and will make you laugh at least once a class. Is genuinely interested in students and their wellbeing. Go to office hours and talk about life to da homie.

Doesn't use powerpoint and doesn't write on board, so you need to pay attention to everything he says. He's pretty clear usually though, just take really good notes. He gives accurate study guides before each test so they aren't that hard. You don't really need to read as long as you pay attention in class. Sections are mandatory.

Nice professor, cracked some good jokes throughout the course. He was very adamant about helping his students understand the material. At first, the class seemed *too* difficult and convoluted (I wanted to drop it), but stick through the class and it gets much better. TA discussion sections were very, very helpful as well.

I had him for Phil 13 Ethics. Great guy very nice, go to his office hours the material can get very complex at times. Hes very nice, a bit awkward & not the most sociable guy, but at heart a good guy. His class isnt too hard study the study guides & you should be fine. His lectures are a bit heavy and hard to follow at times. but overall good prof
Yea.

Professor Doller never really had lectures prepared. Most of the classes were tedious "discussions" where he just waited in awkward silence for people to throw out ideas about the readings. He also interrupted presentations to add his thoughts. For one 10-minute presentation, I had to stand for over 30 minutes because he kept talking in between.

Professor Doller is very kind and nice. I felt like there was a lot of busy work in this class and they took a long time to grade assignments. It was a pretty easy class, but just a little boring for me.
Lectures can be kind of dry, but he is pretty chill otherwise and gives out easy assignments. Took him for 8B which I found very fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I really like Professor Ben Doller! I've had him for two classes and his upper division literature classes are small, close-knit, and very enjoyable. All the projects are very creative and doable, he is also very helpful if you have any question about literature in general; he helped me create a poetry portfolio. I highly recommend taking him!

He's so goated! Loved his lectures; he makes them interesting. He genuinely cares about the students. 2 mid-terms and a final. All the tests are MCQs, and there was a short-answer question on the first midterm.

Genuinely one of the best professors I have ever had. You can tell that he actually enjoys teaching and the content which is so rare to find now. I thought it would be a boring class but it ended up being my favorite of the entire quarter. Midterms and final are not bad at all as long you spend a couple days going over his study guides.
He just is my favorite professor in the entire world. He is so kind, so approachable, and SO GOOD at teaching. Midterms and Final in person, but he preps you well!
GOAT of cogsci department for a reason

He was a very good teacher. He was very kind and passionate about his work. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. 2 Midterms and Final online. There are extra credit options as well. Lot of info, but slides are clear and marked with what's important to know.

Not easy class, expect to memorize the entire eye & ear neuroanatomy! Class is dry & dense content but the prof is very passionate & he makes it digestible. Exams aren't easy & def requires studying + there is graded attendance. I averaged 83% on all my exams and got an A-

Taken fall 2025, this time tests were in person and not on canvas. Memorization heavy because tests aren't open-note, but can get difficult when taking other classes that require you to memorize. Fun professor and genuinely care about his class, I feel like I just have test anxiety no matter how much I study.
He's very enthusiastic and genuinely wants to help you succeed in his class.

This class was such a breeze, I honestly slacked off and that's why I got a B+ but I could've easily gotten an A if not. Weekly quizzes and take-home exams, all digital. Just copying his notes into a masterdoc and using that during exams is all you need. Also he's just super understanding and a great lecturer :)

Very kind and passionate professor, smiley and enthusiastic in lectures. The course content could tend to be boring but he tries his best to engage with the students and the slide questions reflect the lessons. The quizzes and exams are fair, accurately reflecting lecture concepts.

Very kind and funny professor. The course was very accommodating and relatively easy, especially if you go to lecture and take notes. Very passionate about what he teaches. Two midterms and a final online. Overall, very doable class and amazing Professor!

Very kind and caring professor. His course was pretty easy, especially if you go to lecture and take notes. Attendance not mandatory but will make final weigh less on your grade if you go. Assignments were pretty easy and there are weekly quizzes but they aren't that bad. Very passionate about what he teaches.

Attendance is mandatory, can miss 6 and is extra credit if not can opt out and the percentage moves to your exams. Discussions are mandatory only attend 5 for credit. 2 midterms online and final exam online and timed. 3 major discussion assignments. weekly quizzes online. Overall easy class. Very passionate about the topic, excellent professor.

This guy is awesome. Passionate, kind, considerate. Fantastic lecture materials, very engaging presence in class. You can tell he really cares. He seems like a very happy person and he really deserves to be.

Good professor, he was helpful in explaining the content at a reasonable pace and with enthusiasm. Lectures can cover lots of content so be prepared to take notes. Iclicker questions for attendance, 3 reasonable easy assignments, 2 midterms and weekly quizzes on lecture content. Final exam was cumulative and fairly straightforward.
He's very chill and personable - and his exams are online too

You can tell he is very passionate about what he teaches. His lectures are clear and pretty easy to follow along, plus he adds a bit of humor and tries making them as enjoyable as possible. Attendance for lectures is part of your grade, but you can opt out. Exams are online and study guides are provided. Amazing professor overall!

Professor Barrera is a gem - his lectures are engaging, and he breaks down complex concepts clearly. The quizzes and tests are challenging but fair. unstuckstudy and the free textbook are great study aids. Highly recommend this class!
Great professor - makes lecture interesting and clear, and grading is super fair. 10/10 would recommend him for any cog sci class
very kind dude with awesome energy. the content itself for the class was a bit boring but he tries to make it as interesting as possible, which i respect!

Online open-book exams that are very fair. He explained the material well and gave lots of flexibility in his attendance policy. Great lectures and manages to include lots of interesting real-world applications.

Has a consistent and comfortable format for lecture slides. Explains and breaks down concepts well! Quizzes get 3 tries with incorrect answers labeled. Quizzes and attendance quizzes are good prep for what the tests will be like. Tests slightly challenging. I really like Barrera, he is so smiley face coded :o)

His classes are very well organized and grades consist of attendance (which you can choose to opt-out of), weekly quizzes (3 tries), 2 midterms and a final (usually online, open notes). Lessons can be difficult but he teaches them very well. Probably one of my MOST favorite professors at UCSD.
Prof. Barrera has been one of the greatest instructors I've had so far! His grading criteria was really fair and his lectures were amazing. Great recommendation for COGS 14A.

Professor is amazing, and we are graded by a few things: 2 midterms, 1 final and weekly homework quizzes. The midterms were surprisingly difficult, he is lecture heavy and some of the topics were difficult. But overall he made it interesting and engaging. Cant recommend him enough.

I couldn't be more impressed. Research Methods is a heavy topic but this professor is passionate and super knowledgable about it and explains things very well. Adding in a bit of humor makes it even better. He goes at a great pace and makes sure students are comprehending. Very patient. Textbook and attendance not mandatory, 2 midterms and 1 final.

I've had Barrera for 3 classes (14b, 101a and b) and he's great. No homework outside of weekly take-home quizzes, exams have *typically* been online (and open note) -- not too difficult, given you are proficient with the material. Very caring for his students/your success in his classes. Barrera is my pookie bear fr.

There is a so called "required" textbook but in fact I don't think you'll need it. Lectures are clear, while quizzes are fully based on them. Tests are not hard at all and only requires a little bit of analysis. As all the other comments are 5 out of 5 for Prof. Barrera, I think I don't need to explain anymore.

Quizzes are 25% with 3 tries each, with an easy full credit here. P. Barrera's lectures are informative, and the class has multiple guest lecturers. Attendance not mandatory, but worth going to as quizzes/exams are directly based on them. Questions are simple, easy A class. Extra credit through section attendance or through SONA.

Last name ever, first name GREATEST! My favorite professor at UCSD. Very clear class structure and expectations and very receptive to student feedback. Weekly quizzes, but with 3 attempts so as to make the focus on your preparation rather than an additional test. Fun lectures w/questions embedded to keep learning on track. Very fair exams.

I LOVED professor Barrera. He was so passionate of what he is teaching, and explains concepts very clearly. This is my first upper div class and it wasn't difficult because of him. If you have a chance to take any class with him, DON'T THINK TWICE TAKE HIM YOU WONT REGRET IT.

Amazing professor. Lectures were easy to understand and detailed. Quizzes/exams were straightforward. He was easily accessible outside of class and has a good sense of humor. Hands down, would take again.

I took two classes with Professor Barrera. He was inspiring and caring in his class, and his classes were the best I have ever taken. His sole desire is for his students to gain knowledge and success in his class.
He is so organized and clear! He is not out there to trick you at all, he wants you to succeed!

Love this man, wish I could take every single COGS class with him. Barrera is so clearly passionate about the material he teaches and cares so much about his students. An absolute gem of a prof, protect him at all costs.

Definitely one of the best professors in the cognitive science department. Amazing lectures and clear grading. Quizzes and exams are easy and represent the class materials. Make sure to take notes and not skip any lectures, and should be an easy A.
He is an amazing professor, most lectures were guest lectures.

I resist the urge to tell this man I love him at the end of every lecture or office hour. He is so kind, patient, intelligent, and genuinely concerned about the well-being of the people in his classes. He loves the course material and makes every class engaging. I cannot recommend him enough! Truly the gem of the cognitive science department here.

He gives one of the most organized lectures at the COGS department @ UCSD. Exams are very fair and no tricky questions. Quizzes and sections are good sources to prepare for the exams. He is the exemplary instructor!

Weekly low stakes quizzes w/ 3 tries & feedback makes it a great source of studying for the 2 midterms & 1 final. I rarely feel lost, and if I do, it's nothing watching the zoom later on won't fix. Still in doubt? Email for clarification. I wish there was Piazza for 14b though so the whole class could benefit from questions.

Professor Barrera is excited to teach and cares more about his students that the average professor. I have taken him for COGS 1 and COGS 14B. You will do well if you work hard; it is an extremely fair grading system.

I've taken Barrera for COGS 1 and COGS 101B (and hopefully another class) and he is one of my favorite if not favorite professors I've had at UCSD? He's very engaging and all the material on his slides/lecture arev on the exam. NO trick questions and three attempts for quizzes.

A lot of guest lectures, but you could tell he was super passionate about cogsci and invested in student success. So many avenues to succeed (OHs, reviews of guest lectures, extra credit), on top of an easy class. I really enjoyed it and felt like I learned a lot. 10/10, would recommend
he is the most amazing prof and is super passionate! must take him if youre a cogs sci major :))
Professor Barrera is one of the most beloved professors in the cognitive science department. I have never heard any student say anything negative about him. absolute king.

Prof. Barrera is very chill and caring. His assignments/weekly quizzes are very straightforward and give you feedback on your wrong answers, to help you figure it out for attempts 2 and 3. Midterms are very reasonable content-wise, and he really takes student feedback into account when designing them. Easy A if you take notes and/or ask questions.

Professor Barrera is really kind and patient. He seems to genuinely care about the students' education and tries his best to help them. He makes sure to walk thru examples and provides extra study material on more difficult concepts. Would def recommend.

Only graded by 3 midterms and weekly quizzes. All of which are multiple choice. You get 3 chances on each quiz (remote learning). Super easy and fun class! Alot of opportunities for multiple choice. Barrera knows what hes talking about and is pretty good at explaining in simpler terms
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Barrera is one the greatest professor at UCSD. He cares about the topics that he teaches, but also takes to time to pause and make sure you are following along. If you are at Muir, I would recommend to take Cognitive Science classes for your social sciences GE, honestly just for this class and COGS 17 with Dr. Johnson, who's great too.

Prof. Barrera's class was genuinely enjoyable. He's a great lecturer, and his midterms were very fair. The class itself also wasn't too overbearing with work. I'm looking forward to taking his other classes!

Barrera is a kind, well-spoken, and knowledgeable lecturer. Watch 3 guest lectures per week, and he does his own live lecture to cover the topics. It's a great class to get a lot of exposure to different aspects of cogsci. The weekly quizzes are easy, and the exams are a usual difficulty as long as you watch all the lectures and study.

Professor Barrera is super kind and wonderful. Very enthusiastic. We have 2-3 recorded guest lectures / week followed up by his live lectures. Grading for this classes is based on 3 midterms and weekly mc quizzes. Sections are optional but they are EC if you go (2%). If you can't he has other EC options. Overall great professor and easy class

Amazing professor. Great lectures that fill in any gaps in student understanding, plus he always sets aside time to answer student questions. Super easy grading system too, a big chunk of your grade is made up of quizzes you get three attempts at. Overall, fantastic.

Literally the best professor I have had thus far. Prof. Barrera is extremely passionate about the material. Very understanding and kind person. Graded by three midterms and weekly quizzes + extra credit opportunities. Gives three attempts on quizzes w/ thorough explanation on why wrong answers are wrong. Highly, highly recommend.

My favorite prof of the year! He's super passionate about the course and is very good at explaining concepts. The quizzes were all multiple choice and open note and everything we needed to answer the questions was in guest lectures or his review lectures. We didn't have homework tho so quizzes mattered a lot.

Awesome at getting the material across in a digestible way, plus he's super enthusiastic about it. Free points via quizzes that you can take 3 times, and tests are easy A's as long as you show up to lecture.
Guest lectures for each class, very easy, quizzes every week but you get three chances for each one.

Professor Barrera is one of the best professor I've had at UCSD. He is super passionate about what he teaches and makes learning fun. Tests are very straightforward with a mix of mc, free response, and fill in the blank. As long as you study you should have no problem getting an A. TAKE HIM!!

Professor Barrera is easily one of my favorite professors at UCSD! Hilarious, charismatic, and explains the material perfectly. The readings were useful but you can do good by just studying the lectures. He's very understanding and accommodating especially when I took him during the coronavirus pandemic.
one of the best professors i've ever had!! he's also very understanding and his exams are fair and based off of lectures. i'd love to take him again

This class is made up of 3 guest lectures a week, meaning past podcasts in the online version of this course. There are interesting ones, and less interesting ones, but Professor Barrera is clearly caring and accommodating to every student's circumstances. The lecture he gave at the beginning was actually the most interesting one!

The class was okay. I am not a COGS major or a data science person so it wasn't my favorite thing but it was interesting. He is a good lecturer and it was interesting but you had to listen to a separate guest lecture on top of his own to take the exams and that sucked but there was not reading which was great

Professor Barrera is very enthusiastic about the material he teaches which is what I really liked about him! He knows his material but sometimes he doesn't explain the concepts in a way that someone with minimal background in stats would understand. Another thing is he is very specific with the type of responses he wants on midterms.

Perfect lectures, he goes through step-by-step examples on how to do everything he will test on. He's not always the best at explaining the concepts behind stats, but the concepts are already confusing so that's not really his fault. Tests are hard, but he lets you have a cheat sheet, and everything on the test is fair and taught in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: In my opinion should be one of the most respected professors at UCSD. Classes covered all of the most important topics important to the discipline. Clear lectures and challenging exams.

Barrera is truly one of the best professors I have had. He not only cares about his students, but does his best to make the material fun and interesting (even when its really not). His tests are very representative of the material and he provides many resources to help you study. TAKE HIM YOU WONT REGRET IT!!!!! <3 you barrera
My favorite professor in UCSD. He's lecture notes are super organized! Easy to follow along! He is super caring! Take his class!

Professor Barrera is the best!! He makes the material a lot more interesting and explains the concepts really well. I really enjoyed the class and would definitely recommend others to take his class!!
One of the most organized professors at UCSD, clear powerpoints and 2% of extra credit. Midterms are manageable if you know your stuff. TAKE WITH HIM IF POSSIBLE

Professor Barrera is one of the best professors I've had. His powerpoints are really well organized and easy to understand. He also podcasts his lectures which is always good. His tests are very straightforward and fair. He doesn't give much homework, only weekly quizzes which he gives 3 attempts for you to do.

Usually COGS1 is mostly composed of guest lecturers, but Professor Barrera is a funny guy and he keeps the class very well organized. His tests are very straight forward, just go through the lectures and memorize everything.

I would like to say that Barrera is an amazing Professor, he is very genuine and understandable. I took his stats class for SP17 quarter and also took his previous 14A course during W17 quarter and enjoyed every bit of his lecturing style. Tests weren't all too hard  but fairly reasonable. Gives out a great amount of Extra Credit as well. Take him!

Professor Barrera is amazing. He's an excellent lecturer; very clear, cracks jokes every now and then,  and makes sure you understand the material thoroughly. That being said, I hated the class. I'm CogSci major to learn more about neural networking of the brain, not about how to conduct experiments. Barrera made the class somewhat bearable though.

Hilarious, caring, understanding prof who is very fair. He made cogs14a, which most might consider to have "boring" material, very enjoyable and relevant. The class was also super easy, and there's even extra credit; imo impossible not to pass. My fav thing about this prof is he teaches with a huge smile on his face!

Learning about ethics in data science could not have been more enjoyable without him as a professor. Barrera is funny, loves what he teaches and cares about how we internalize the material. He also taught at a great pace, gave fair tests, and is accessible outside class. He's a gem. Made me happy to be a COGS major
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This is the kind of prof that anyone can come to and talk to.

BEST PROFESSOR AT UCSD. Literally, I've had Prof. Barrera for 3 classes, and he is such a great lecturer! He makes his lectures very clear and easy to understand. I never bought a textbook for his classes (COGS 1, 101A and 101B). and I easily got an A. He also offers EASY extra credit (SONA and section attendence). I would DEFINITELY recommend him!

Best Cognitive Science teacher! Hands down! Very thorough with his lecture and at times may be a lot to handle. This may be due to the nature of the course though. But just go over the study guide and you'll be golden! Has weekly quizzes but you get three attempts. Oh and don't need to buy the book for any of his classes!

Prof. Barrera is very passionate and interacts with students well. His lectures are straightforward and he uses detailed power points (but you still have to attend lectures to get participation credit). His online quizzes are SUPER easy (you get 3 tries and the entire weekend), as well as the exams. Don't need to read the book; lectures cover all.

Prof. Barrera is one of the best CogSci professors out there. His lectures are clear and efficient, and reading the book supplements his lectures perfectly. He provides study guides that make good exam grades easy and section labs (mandatory) are easy A's.

Barrera is one of the best lecturers that UCSD has to offer. I recommend taking him for any class you can. You will have a solid understanding of the material, and he's always available to students after class to go over material more in-depth, which is something UCSD is generally lacking.

Great lecturer, very clear, nice, relevant topics discussed. No textbook needed. Scantrons provided, review sessions are kind of extra and unecessary since theyre question based but he always offers them (IAs run it) labs are quick and simple and just apply material learned in class MANDATORY SECTIONS except when there is no lab

Best professor that I have ever taken. He is obviously passionate about the material, presents it in a clear manner, and tests in a way that is challenging but fair. Attending and reviewing lecture, reviewing weekly quizzes, and completing the labs is enough to succeed in this class. Really interesting material on top of that.

He's one of the nicest and most understanding professors I've met at UCSD - very friendly and obviously cares about his students. It's apparent that he's really excited about the material and his excitement is contagious. Very interesting lectures.

He is a very nice professor - COGS1 mainly has outside lecturers but Barrera was very thorough with review and his tests are easy if you just watch the podcasts and take notes. There are alot of lecturers so some miss, but the hits would be fascinating and I learned a great deal

Professor Barrera is my favorite professor at UCSD. Though Cogs 1 is primarily taught by guest lecturers, he organizes the course perfectly. He's extremely fair and creates a solid Cogs 1 course. No matter what your major, take a course with him before you graduate. He's friendly, genuine, and passionate about cogsci and his students.
He's great. This course has guest speakers who put me to sleep, but I love Barrera. Plus he looks like Jason Bateman, really he does.

Professor Barrera's exams are very straightforward. If you pay attention in lecture, you're good to go. You will never even want to miss lecture because of his great teaching style and his hilarious jokes.  He also provides students with an option to opt out of clicker Qs. He's by far one of the best professors I've had!
One of the best professors I've had. He makes the class interesting, and he really cares about the students. I will definitely be looking to take more classes taught by him.

Professor Barrera is amazing. He really cares about his students and he responds to emails fast. He offers sona extra credit and his lectures are very organized and clear. As long as you outline his lectures and look at the key points you will pass with a good grade. he gives option to opt out of clickers so you could miss class and just read notes

I never knew what Cognitive Science was just took this class for a GE. I was so happy I did, Barrera makes the subject interesting and mixes it up. Weekly online quizzes with 3 attempts, midterms and finals are not accumulative, so midterm 1 week 1-4, midterm 2 week 5-7, final week 7-end. Extremely fair class and material catches your attention.

Barrera is by far the best professor this university has ever had. Even if he left his job, he could become a comedian - he's one of the funniest people I've ever met. This course is pretty easy since it's mostly cognitive psychology (unlike 101A, which had a lot of neuroscience). I studied 2 hours tops for each exam and finished with a 98%.
Midterms and Final are based off the lectures. Do the study guide and you should be fine

Professor Barrera is amazing, period. All the things he teaches you are so engaging and are very practical to the real world. Hands down my favorite professor at UCSD so far. I never complain about attending his classes, and he really cares about his students :)   This guy should be a comedian.

So many more tags I could have used, and all positive. Clear grading criteria, hilarious, there for you, very helpful.  Sometimes it's hard to ask questions in class because of how fast-paced the lectures are, but he's available before and after and during office hours.

Professor Barrera is great! His lectures are very well organized and his tests are fair. Attendance is mandatory (clickers), but you can miss 5 classes without penalty (or just opt out of clickers). He is very friendly, always willing to help his students, and always open to feedbackimprovement.

The most incredible, charismatic professor I've ever had. Amazing lecturer (he's paid just to lecture!) and person, ridiculously funny and good-natured. Exams are pretty easy, I went 89%, 95%, and 104%, plenty of free points along the way as well. Makes you understand the material on the first run, and make you interested in it as well.

I've taken 2 classes in the last year and he is amazing. He's really passionate and tries hard to help his students. His lectures are well-organized with outlinesoverview and he has clicker questions. He is funny and keeps class interesting. Tests are straight forward and he throws out questions if everyone struggled with it and has extra credit
Very nice guy. Class is straightforward. Does everything to help you learn. His TAs were good.

Barrera is great- he's really into the material and I thinks that's contagious to a certain extent. He offers all sorts of reviews and tutorials and makes sure the material is as clear as possible. Always willing to answer questions and has a great sense of humor. LOVE this guy.
Uses iClickers for participation in lectures but the points u get for them aren't based on accuracy. He's a very chill professor and if I could take him for all my classes, I would :)
Lectures are clear and exams are fair. AND HE HAS SUCH A CUTE PERSONALITY! Take him if you can, you won't regret it!
AMAZING PROFESSOR!!! He is very interesting to listen to and the topic is fascinating. I will be seeking out classes that he teaches from now on.

Great teacher, all lectures are just an overview of the assigned chapters.  Quizzes are easy, taken online and multiple times offered.  Exams are based off of lecture slides and it's hard to get a bad grade in the class.  The labs in section are a bit lame but the class is interesting.

Professor is excellent, and very clear in his lectures. Not everything is engaging, but much is, and the class is worth it for that alone. Exams are fair, and representative of material. Prof is one of the best profs I've had at UCSD.
He is so nice!!!! He makes everything really easy and he is really easy to approach as well :) take him if you can!!

He is a great speaker, he knows how to make his slides easy to understand and does a great job at explaining the book. His exams are pretty straight-forward and he is so eager to answer questions or help you learn. Definitely recommend him. Some lectures are not as interesting, but some are very engaging. I want to take more of his classes!

He's a nice guy, but holy smokes is he boring. The lecture is clear and straightforward, but paying attention is very hard. He even acknowledges the fact that his lecture is dull. I reccomend the professor, but be prepared to spend many days watching the seconds pass by on the clock in something akin to agony.

I audited the class, so I can't say anything about the exams. As far as the class goes, Steve's an incredible lecturer -- without a doubt the best instructor I've had during my time at UCSD. More than highly recommended!

Don't read the book or the linked papers. Attend section, attend lecture occasionally. Tests are not especially tricky. Unlike some other classes, the amount of work you put in will actually determine the grade you receive.

Very good prof. Explains concepts well. Tests are directly based on lecture slides. Doesn't use textbook. It's just there for background reading. All exams are multiple choice, T/F, fill in the blank and not cumulative. Overall, highly recommend this prof.

A great professor! His lectures are crystal clear, and his tests reflect what he says in lecture. Book isn't exactly mandatory, but it helps to clear up some of the more complex stuff. I highly recommend taking him!

cThis was my first time taking an upper div cogs class. He is passionate in what he does. He know his stuff and can break it down for you. His lecture slides are awesome. Exams are VERY representative to the lecture slides :) I am shocked that he is a grad student and not a real prof! He is, so far, my fave COGS lecturer! HIGHLY RECOMMEND HIM!
a
Great professor and great guy. Easy teacher and very clear lectures/tests. Could not have been better.

Fair curves, midterms, and finals. You can retake the quizzes as many time as you want. Midterms and final are all based off of slideshow. Professor is approachable, nice, and fun. Attendance to discussion is mandatory though. No reason not to get an A in the class.
Amazing guy. Nothing is unclear or unfair, his expectations for you are clear, and it's evident he wants to help you succeed.

He is really funny and is a genuine good guy. The class was great, the books we read were great, the midterms and final were really easy. Only two 1 page essays due at the final and it was only 50 minutes, in class before the scheduled final
Nice, caring, and understanding. A little slow on grading the major assignments but gives good feedback. She makes grading criteria clear and goes over what you need to do thoroughly.

easy.. just follow the guidelines for each writing assignment then you will be fine.. she doesn't really care about the logic in the essay and more focus on the formatting so just passively follow her instruction.

Great professor! Super kind and caring, fairly grades, and gives good feedback. We have three papers: a proposal, AB, and a research paper with 1-2 drafts each week. Weekly work was around 10 hours and 15-20 during final papers. Overall, a hard course, but she does her best to help students and make the class more manageable.

I highly suggest strategizing & taking a light load if you want to advance this skill or if it's your weakness. If already a good writer, with great effort you can pass w/an A, if you strategize or B if you dont. Otherwise extremely smart prof. who knows their stuff. Insightful feedback and extremely informative in class suggestions. Awesome profe!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I actually enjoyed this professor so much. She is very kind and gives good feedback on your writing as well as very clearly stating expectations. If you pay attention to the rubric and to the advice she gives it is very possible to get an A in this class. However, a good amount of time will need to be dedicated to this course.

The rigor of MCWP 125 often translates to harsh critiques of the professors teaching the class, but Professor Miller was instrumental in my success. She is a fair grader who adheres to MCWP guidelines, provides constructive feedback, and is always happy to help. Stay in touch via email and attend her office hours for valuable writing support!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I just transferred to UCSD and needed this class for my writing requirement. I will say this isn't a class that you can just breeze through, you need to put in the work. However, one of the reasons I loved this class was because of Professor Miller. She was always so positive and she truly cares about her students. Overall, good course layout!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lizzy is an amazing professor! It's very obvious she loves doing what she does and always wants to see her students succeed. There are various opportunities throughout the quarter to receive feedback from her directly, which I thought was very helpful! Don't know where the negative reviews are coming from, would take MCWP again with her any day.

Miller is highly knowledgable in her field. She is very encouraging and helps you so much for brainstorming research topics. However, this class is very challenging and time consuming. Be prepared to read and write a 3800-4000 word research paper. The class helps you explore more topics and use resources you may not have taken advantage of.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is a great professor! There are a lot of assignments, but she gives you opportunities to submit the assignments late in case you missed one. She makes the class easy to pass and gives you feedback on your work. Also, if you submit all the assignments by the deadline, you will get an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Her canvas is extremely unorganized and so are her lectures. She repeats irrelevant information throughout lectures and is SUPER political. She talks about her opinions and political beliefs instead of teaching the class. Very unprofessional and horrible organization. I wish people like her didn't exist as professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Miller was super supportive despite the fast-paced and difficult environment of the summer session, which is to be expected of all summer classes. The MCWP classes are difficult as is and she knows that and tries to support her students in every way possible. Provides amazing feedback and support for your 3 papers, with forgiveness included.

The course itself is very hard, considering the time and the amount of writing that must be done, but the professor is extremely nice and genuinely cares for her students. She is accessible by email, at every office hour, and she offers to schedule appointments. If you explain your situation, she will happily give you an extension if necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: MCWP50 is a DIFFICULT class, but this professor is great! Very positive and professional professor who is encouraging. Graded on Proposal Paper, Annotated Bibliography, Research Paper (3500 words!), and Reflection Letter. Be ready to dedicate HOURS to this class and WORK AHEAD!!! Be like a draft ahead of the class or you will be drowning in work.

Definitely a heavy class but taking it with prof. Miller was a great choice. She is very understanding. Her grading criteria are clearly outlined in her rubrics but if you are confused about anything just ask, she is very willing to work with you outside of class without making you feel dumb for asking. Favorite prof. this quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I found her to be really tough in the beginning but now I think that she is very fair. I'm learning that a lot of the policies actually aren't her doing, but they are Muir's requirements and that she does the best with what she has. She is very caring, very open and quirky. She's a tough grader and it is very writing/reading intensive. Books req'd
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Please avoid this professor. I highly encourage you to avoid her at all costs and take some of the other professors in Muir writing. Her attendance policy is awful and is incredibly boring to listen to. She is also a tough grader. I have passed other writing college courses with easy A's but this course was life sucking.

Professor Miller is very caring and really wants to see everyone succeed. MCWP is not an easy class it is a writing class so obviously you should be prepared to write a whole lot. However, she is very patient and is always willing to extend deadlines for students and work with them to make sure they pass with a good grade. I would take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Miller is a very rigid insensitive person, and I believe that she could be a reason for degrading UCSD.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you do not agree with the professor point of view your paper will be graded very low. Unfair class.
Professor miller reminded me of my favorite high school English teacher. She was kind, lively, and fair. I would highly recommend this professor.
Professor Miller is great! Taking this class in the summer was difficult but professor Miller made it enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Miller was a great professor. MCWP is a tough class regardless of the professor but she grades fair and gives good feedback on papers. Overall Professor Miller really cares about her students and made a very difficult class bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It is a very hard course but she isn't really in control of a lot of the curriculum so it's not her fault. She does her best to make a difficult course manageable and as long as you reach out to her, she is willing to work with anyone. Don't procrastinate and go to her office hours/make an appointment often for guidance on the writing assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Worse professor!! As it is, it is difficult to get into the class and complete this unnecessary writing class but to be a harsh grader and stressing us more than our major classes is certainly unneeded. If you can avoid her, do so honestly you are going to stress yourself out more than you need to.

Anxiety, so much Hw, and grades harshly! I don't know what else to say. I just can't breath because of so much workload given. I didn't have the time to study for my other classes. I'm very sad with my grade. Overall writing has been a challenge for me but with her harsh grading it makes me feel sad to see my writing skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lots of homework and assignments due within couple days. You would barely breath in this class due to the intensive work that you have to do. One of the worst instructors ever
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: DISLIKE HER BIG TIME! she is a horrible professor due to her grading! she is a harsh grader and she expects us to be pro writers even when our English is not our fuerte. HER DEADLINES are exagerating. EX: we need 4-5 pages signal space essay and then we have to do another 4pgs in 2 day not to mention you still need to do the readings. HORRIBLE!

I'm very disappointed she isn't compassion to those who are bilingual, English not being your first language. she's a tough grader! she does check for plagiarism so careful otherwise. Her deadlines are strict, she doesn't give good feedback, she always states to refer back to the book. avoid her! she reiterates to take the class again if you fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class is very difficult, but I'm not sure how much of that is actually Dr. Miller's choice and how much of it is the class curriculum standard. There are quite a few deadlines, but as long as you stay on top of it, it's manageable. I would definitely suggest taking this course with other classes that are lighter on homework and deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Never take with her. The worst writing instructor ever

Miller is inconsiderate of the fact that students are simultaneously taking other courses as well. The amount of readings and assignments that she assigns is absurd. Class "lectures" and activities are barely relevant to the research question and annotated bibliography that are worth 90% the grade. Unhelpful and structures course to fail students
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Horrible instructor. Avoid at all costs. The course is already difficult, but Miller takes this to a different level. Just please do yourself a favor and take this course with a different instructor. Super inaccessible, gives poor feedback, all-around disaster.

Favorite prof so far! She was super accessible and gave the greatest advice on my assignments which made me do really well. The key is to set up an office hour with her WEEKLY to work on your paper. Lots of small assignments and busy work in the beginning of the quarter. You work on one big 13-15 page paper for the entire course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Course material is not relevant to any major and doesn't teach much aside from experiencing imposter syndrome due to intense critique. Honestly, did not help me learn how to write a research paper and it was stressful with the mandated absence regulation. The whole program believes writing is life, regardless of personal issues.
Ive had many writing professors through my educational experience, and she is by far the worst. I say this respectfully.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Bad. Good luck. Period.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller is really receptive. She makes the best out a hard course. I even got to write about underground rave culture. Def recoommend.

This is the most challenging writing class I've ever taken. There's A LOT of assignments and reading but I do feel like I'm leaving this course a MUCH better writer and peer reviewer. Miller gives great feedback and the topics were interesting. She grades and responds to emails quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overload work, ridiculous requirements for each assignment. Never enough and inflexible in office hours and limited in giving feedback. Difficult to understand the instructions to complete the paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class was very heavy with lots of writing (as expected) deadlines and discussion posts. She is a tough grader, but not unreasonably so. Gives great feedback if you communicate with her, so definitely take advantage of OHs and reach out to her if you need help. She'll steer you in the right direction if you're unsure about your writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Liz is a great professor! The class, Id argue, is more intense during the first couple of weeks. LOTS of boring reading at first but you spend the rest of the quarter working on your own research. This course is not the most difficult but DEFINITELY heavy. Do NOT procrastinate! That caused me a lot of stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: First off this class has a substantial workload, because on top of the graded papers, discussions/readings are required to get participation credit. The overall graded papers aren't that hard ( just require a lot of writing and research) stick to covering everything in the rubric and you are set.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: class frontloaded with tons of reading @ beginning of the quarter & was tedious at times, but liz was as accommodating as she could be during the pandemic while still adhering to program standards. communication w her is key, take advantage of her OH and conferences/email her, she'll help you a LOT. a requirement that felt hard but ended up beingok
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is very nice pro. If you put your efforts, you r fine. Make appointment with her, you will get very good feedback. You will learn a lot from her!

Elizabeth makes a dull class and subject interesting and doable. Writing is not my strong suit and her feedback and pointers were invaluable. I really enjoyed taking her. There is A LOT of reading during the beginning of the quarter but it slows down and then you only focus on your paper. No midterm but there is a final paper that you worked on.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: My writing improved a lot during this class!! :) I wasn't into it at first (lots of hard reading) but quickly got sucked in. Liz is a rad TA--gives great feedback and lots of it, and wants students to do well. Hard grader but so is everyone in MCWP. Dry sense of humor, pretty cool, empathetic to student problems (within reason)

Definitely the worst class I've taken at UCSD. If you thought this would be an easy GE, think again. Butler has the worst grading system I've ever seen and if you miss a single class you will drop a whole letter grade. She gets too deep about the subject and needs to realize she grades too hard. Do not take this class!!!!!

This is not an easy A class. You need to have your camera on and participate consistently or you'll get called out. Success in the class depends heavily on attendance and engagement. Grading is extremely strict, and lectures can feel very understimulating. Overall, it was one of the worst classes I've taken here.

The grading system is not good, and you have to attend every lecture, or your grade automatically drops. The exams are graded very harshly, where you have to give a detailed response while having a strict word limit. It is not an easy online class to take for gen ed, which you would think it is.

Took the class for a GE, would not recommend. You would think an online class would be easy but no. The weekly reflections do not have clear prompts and the TA does not give helpful feedback either. Seems like there is no communication made between the professor and the TA.When asked for more feedback, they refer you to the writing hub. So helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the worst professors Ive had here at UCSD. she grades on a scale of 4. readings due everyday before lecture, and a content quiz for every lecture. it is almost impossible to get a 4/4 on ANY assignment without going to the writing hub. if you miss even one lecture the highest grade you can get is a B.

My friend and I both dropped. Quizzes for readings every lecture, says an A is easy but took half the quarter to grade with no feedback to help improve. You had to be an expert on a researched topic, no instructions, made us teach the class and it was worth 10% of our grade. midterm and final were online but we didn't stay long enough to take it.

very strange way of teaching that doesn't sit right with many people but is supposed to be anti-racist and inclusive. I think your race, background, and personal preferences entirely shape your experience in this class and whether you like it or not. Easy A if you pay attention and attend lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She teaches the course in a weird way. It is an okay class if you do the work and show up to almost every lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class not too difficult if you show up everyday. (Kinda of have to because mandatory attendance) Lots of extra credit opportunities too like class quizzes and participation. Lectures are a little boring but as long as you do the weekly homework you should be good.

Highly recommend. You can almost skim through the readings and crank out a 250 word reflection and be done for the week. Professor Butler teaches African American studies in a way that can be a shock to people who haven't experienced very much of it. It's the easiest A ever, there's a take home midterm and final. Skim the readings and you'll live.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Quite a bit of reading, lots of splitting into groups based on race which is very weird. I also found it strange that we have an identity worksheet that we have to attach to every single project or assignment we do that isn't a discussion. Seems like the professor tries to bring the class together but ends up being racist and separates us instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I like Dr. Butler a lot! She's very understanding and passionate about the subject matter. Everything was very clear and she makes it very easy to do well in the course as long as you are able to put in the work to do it (which isn't difficult at all). The only slight difficulty is the heavy reading, but it's all very interesting.

fully agree with the person that said the prof would try to teach about inclusivity but made the class more separated. separated us based off race like twice which was a bit odd tbh. also insanely strict grader and absences are basically never excused unless you can prove you were hospitalized or something. otherwise ur grade drops. dont recommend

I did not like her lecturing at all. The TA was very harsh in grading and did not give helpful feedback. The professor was heavy on assignments. She had us prepare for a 60 minute presentation while also giving us a final reflection worth 35% of our grade, plus having other reflections due that where 50% of our grade.

reviews.comment: This professor tries to be inclusive for the class but ends up making the class feel separated by identity, which is very ironic. Grades are based on weekly reflections that the TA harshly grades, giving very vague, rarely helpful feedback. Thought this class would be similar to the DOC program, ended up being much harder. I wouldn't recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is so kind and caring

Class wasn't too hard but for the final, she has about four different rubrics all saying different things. Attendance counts towards your grade, she was constantly posting our assignments late and not postponing the due dates, she didn't always respond to emails and isn't available outside of class. I do not recommend, take something else.

Took as DEI requirement, pretty manageable workload, she often tries to experiment with how she runs class. Busywork can get tedious but helps you stay engaged. Class discussions can get a little awkward if you don't do the readings though. Very supportive, cares more about building character in each of her students than their final grade.
Worst Professor I ever had. The class itself is not hard, but she has the ability to make it harder and more stressful than my econ 100B. Poor ability to organize a class. Big nono.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I love Prof. Butler! She was super caring and always willing to help if I had a problem. The class is an easy A, and she lets you know that she wants the class to be easy. GO TO LECTURE, she makes it fun and gives out A LOT of extra credit.

I cant stress ENOUGH to stay away from Butler. She is apathetic and rude. She is very unclear about grading expectations and grades inconsistently. She does not care about what students are going through personally. Multiple students complained to the dean and threatened to drop out because of her. If you value your mental health, avoid her.

Not a particularly good professor. She didn't really teach much, got angry very easily from things as simple as her links not directing us to the right page, and was overall disrespectful in many ways but attributed it to her not holding back and speaking the truth. Would not recommend.

Prof. Butler was knowledgeable and passionate about teaching African American Studies. There is a reflection that is due each week and the grading can be strict. She assigns way too much reading and lectures rarely reflect the readings. She organizes the class based on student feedback which causes for the class to be extremely disorganized.

pretty easy class and she definitely cares about the material. she can be unorganized and her lectures are 50/50 on if they are engaging. I do feel as though sometimes she is unwilling to listen to students but it was never for serious issues, usually just for minor inconveniences that would just be annoying but tolerable
Great teacher, easy work load, engaging class activities, and very caring. 10/10.
Great professor and class is easy going. Nothing too difficult. I would say an easy A class overall.

This class doesn't require too much work but can get annoying at times, namely weeks 7-10. I didn't find the curriculum particularly engaging, but anyone can look past that. The issue is the grading of work is not consistent in the very least and can be subjective at times because you don't relate to anything, but otherwise easy enough A-.

I learned A LOT from this class, but let me tell you- I've never done SO MUCH WORK for 1 class here at UCSD. Libby really cares about her students and that we get the most we can out of this class, and I sure did. But while I was in the class I was suffering from the extreme work load.

She's a very approachable professor, though she does expect a lot of work and assigns a great deal of reading. It really isn't hard to get an A or B in the class, just put effort into the assignments and you'll be in good shape.
Lectures are not engaging and are sections unproductive; She's very biased and controlling. Refutes challenging opinions constantly.

Guidelines won't let me say what I want to say. For future 40 students, he does curve (quite big for our class F to C+), because EVERYONE failed. His lectures are incomprehensible, and he makes very strenuous exams that don't follow class material. My final exam score was 30%, that was the norm. If you must, be strong, you will pass. good luck.

reviews.comment: Truly...what was that?

reviews.comment: He thinks he's doing something novel with the class, but in reality he just reads out of his borderline incomprehensible textbook, refuses to assign homework since he believes it's detrimental to learning, and had us study his unfinished project “the hat for the Raspberry Pi”. I have never felt such immense vitriol for a class or professor before.

reviews.comment:
Truly abhorrent final, and the rest of the class was atrocious. Started the exam by saying "I got inspired, which is great for me but bad for you guys." 
I've never felt a purer, more distilled rage for anything tbh

reviews.comment: He uses his own textbook, which is very difficult to understand, and he references it for all assignments and tests. He spent a whole lecture talking about this super complicated board he designed and wanted us to memorize for the final. Avoid if possible.

I'm pretty sure this guy is teaching a different class because I have no idea what we are doing. The only homework assignment we were given was midterm corrections which we had to take twice because everyone failed the first time. Every lecture is just mumbo jumbo but at least we aren't pattern thinkers (kill me). No notes, no structure, avoid TB.

Worst teacher by far at UCSD. No structure for the class, teaches out of his own confusing textbook, goes on rambles and tangents, and doesn't know how to teach a linear circuits class. 90% of the material he teaches is controls and based off MAE 143A and 143B, so if you haven't taken those be ready to be lost. Even if you have you'll still be lost

Professor announced office hours on as the office hours occurred, did not write TA's information on syllabus, refused to assign homework for practice, had pop quizzes, did not update online lecture notes, had very sparse lecture notes since he preferred to use chapters from his pre-written textbooks that were written for other subjects, and more!

This class lacks so much structure. He tells you the only way to learn in his class is to "think different" and read his textbook that is impossible to read. To address the poor scores on the midterm he decided that announcing a second midterm a week before was appropriate. We received no homework other than test corrections. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He acts open to criticism but is not. He does not understand how he writes his own exam as it's mostly memorization.

If you need to take the class this quarter, if it's the last class you need to graduate, extend your graduation date just to not take it with this professor. I cannot stress how bad this class is. No homework, midterms are taken straight from the niche corners of his textbook and his grading scheme is whatever he feels like.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
AVOID AT ALL COSTS. you will learn nothing circuits-related from him.
