- pop quizzes have average of 45% 
- pop 2nd midterm with no cheat sheet after the class bombed the 1st

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy, but the work is hard. Has a very unorthodox teaching approach, however, his goal to inspire students and their ability to understand is nice. Can be flexible at times if given substantial reasons.
Everything below is most definitely true. I suggest picking any other professor as his teaching style makes things unnecessarily much more complicated.

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the worst classes I have ever taken. Halfway into the semester, we had one graded assignment!

Lectures are him reading out of his own textbook.

reviews.comment:
This is for MAE200.
I like the topic, but sadly I won't recommend anyone taking this course if Prof. Bewley is teaching. After our final exam, we got a HW and a project to complete in 4 days. IN FINALS WEEK.
His teaching style mainly consists of reading from the book, which leaves the class confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The exams are not relative to the assignments. He doesn't care about students. The lectures just are repeating the context of the textbook. You need to rely on your TA. However, I got a very cocky TA.

His lecture style of jumping around through the textbook is very dry, not conducive to note taking or learning. Homework assignments are extremely long. Exams are convoluted. reviews.comment: Horrible professor that lectures straight from the textbook that he wrote. He (and the book) overcomplicate simple ideas and his lectures are incredibly boring and hard to follow. Very unorganized class with extremely long homework assignments. (My current assignment is about 10 pages long)

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS The syllabus and grading scheme for this class DO NOT EXIST. The homeworks are arbitrary and unrelated to each other and have NOTHING to do with the final project. The final project was assigned during Tuesday of FINALS WEEK. The lectures are useless since he only uses buzzwords about controls and doesn't explain anything

unorganized (no class website, no feedback on homework or midterm, no communication on how the grades are determined), inappropriate lecture material (lectures are based on reading his book, or his research papers), good: available at office hours

This class is very difficult merely because of the huge amount of material covered (becoz he just reads the book). Need to work a lot for assignments. Luck plays a role in exams-it depends on whether an idea to solve a problem strikes u. Group work for assignments and reading text before class will help.

Lectures unorganized, not clear (he just reads the textbook he authored out loud). Explained/answered questions poorly. No homework returned or solutions posted. not good.... worst
bad prof

This professor made me to not like this course...
This professor does not teach at all. He simply reads the book. Nothing else.

Horrible! Simply pointed at screen of book he wrote. Returned 1 of my many emails. Worst teacher!!!
Too difficult to understand

I don't know if it was a bad semester or what, but the lectures seemed to lack focus and clarity. Do not expect to receive feedback on your performance in the course, graded homework was not returned.  Test are long and problems are very difficult and honestly would require use of MATLAB to accurately solve.  Be prepared to put in a lot of work.

He has a genuine desire for his students to understand the material and be able to use it in a practical, work/research focused way.  The textbook he wrote and lectures from is the best. Important to go to lecture, very helpful. Probably my favorite prof after 4 years at ucsd
This professor did an excellent job of teaching this class. He seemed to place more emphasis on control but it helped keep the class interesting. Make sure to take good notes and go to class.
Very good professor, Go to his Office Hours to get help, Ask TA's for help, use all the resources available
the greatest ever

His lectures were really interactive, and he is a funny guy altogether, which made it more enjoyable. He has daily readings assigned, but they're not too unreasonable. I had to rent out a lot of the books, but I'm sure you can find them online. Participation and attendance are mandatory but I missed a few days and ended up with an A anyway.

reviews.comment: Very engaging and funny lecturer, so the mandatory attendance rarely feels like a chore. Participation is 25% of the grade, but I only participated a handful of times and got an A. There are two essays, each 5 pages and pretty simple.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 2nd class with Cowan and he is so great! Lectures are mandatory and a part of your grade but he is so funny and knowledgeable so they always fly by. He draws a lot on the readings for class lectures and will call on you to give your opinion. Class grade is based on the midterm and final paper. As long as you start early you'll be good!

History of Brazil was one of my GE requirements, I loved his class, attendance was mandatory but lectures were always interesting and professor cowan was pretty funny. Grades were based off basically the midterm essay and the final essay. You have tons of time to prepare so I wouldn't worry at all. Definitely take this class if it satisfies credits
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cowan is HILARIOUS and an AMAZING lecturer and is super passionate about the subject. Participation is 30% of the grade and is based on the assigned reading, which there is ALOT of. There is a 7-10pg final paper which you have all quarter to work on. Put effort into the reading, talking in class, and research for the paper and you'll pass easily.

I took HILA 114 and professor Cowan is great. He makes already interesting lectures more enjoyable, but participation DOES matter. Both in class and with the short weekly assignment. Definitely take his class when you're not fully crammed already, or it'll be harder. Really cool prof and you learn a lot in his class.

I wasn't that interested in modern Brazilian history, but he made it interesting. 50% of the grade was weekly reading responses, so don't slack on these! The one complaint I had is that the prompt for the final research paper was kind of vague. Super chill prof though, as long as you stay on top of the assignments you'll get an A.

I loved taking Brazilian history from Cowan!The class is super interesting & the majority of your grade comes from reading the material & discussing in class. As long as you show that you're engaged & participate, you'll do well! Come to class, do the reading & put effort into the term paper. That's the best advice I can give if you want an A!

Professor Cowan is one of the nicest and amazing professors I have taken so far. I was never into Brazilian history, but his class was really interesting. The class itself is pretty easy to pass or get an A as long as you attend the lectures and put effort into the final paper. I would definitely take another class with Cowan.

I really enjoyed this class! Participation is 45% of your grade, so if you go to lecture, do the readings, and raise your hand in class you'll do very well. The midterm was take-home and the final was a research paper. Lectures were interesting and he's very funny. I would highly recommend him and this class, I loved it!

I love Prof Cowan!!! He cares mostly about everyone learning about Brazil, rather than testing you on it which is amazing. Participate in class and GO to it b/c its def worth it (and 40% of your grade). He's funny and caring!! You have a take-home midterm where you demonstrate you've paid attention in class and a 7-10 page paper due as the final.
Fantastic professor. The final paper was intensive and readings were essential for class, but lectures were entertaining and enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Cowan is one of the most sassiest prof I've ever had (in a good way). Lectures are very clear and straightforward that help introduce the film of the week. Attendance and participation are a must to get a good grade! Midterm is easy if you pay attention. Easy A.
I recommend you take a different professor.

She would explain things throughoughly which was appreciated as we went over topics of identity, that many may not have had prior knowledge to. Theres assigned readings for every lecture, and its best to read for quotes to use in the writings. Also watching episodes of reality TV was a nice breather between projects.

Caring but grading scheme was not for me. Feedback had me constantly feeling like I was not doing good enough. She was very adamant about how she was not asking for polished writing but to voice yourself in it.Yet I lost most of my points due to that. Readings, watch parties, free-writes, discussion boards/responses, essays, projects, peer reviews.

She has an amazing CAT 125 class. I love reality TV and we got to have a watch party based on the topic of the week such as "the self", "groups", "families" etc. She is very supportive of her class and makes writing and projects enjoyable. We got to watch shows like survivor, housewives and what not

Mid lectures, but luckily attendance isn't mandatory. Quizzes + final exam make up the majority of the grade in the class, with the projects / hw being mostly free points. The questions on the quizzes/exams are simple enough, and the professor provides ample resources before each one to study.

Very cool and passionate guy! The class structure was quite shaky at first, but he managed to pull it together as the weeks passed. Surprisingly caring and takes feedback very well. He wants you to understand the intuition behind the ML concepts. Lectures are not bad.

Very nice professor, cares about students. Open to discussion about anything ML or class related, and although his lecture style can be a bit unconventional, it does the job. Doesn't want you to suffer, instead wants to see you learn as much as you can. My only feedback is that quizzes can be chaotic and he talks during them when ur tryna focus

Taylor is a professor who cares about his students. He was very passionate about the concepts he covered in lecture. My only gripe is that the quizzes weren't exact reflections of the homework and lectures, but they're definitely doable if you do the practice quizzes and understand the concepts. The homework isn't too bad either.

Homework assignments and quizzes were pretty easy and fair. I felt that his lectures were engaging, but sometimes were not relevant to what we needed to know for the exams. He was very accessible over Piazza and very open to feedback from students

Super caring and engaging professor. He explains concepts clearly in lecture and is very open to feedback from students regarding the class format and quiz difficulty. Quizzes are every 2 weeks and are easy to do well on if you study the practice quizzes and past HWs. HWs graded on completion, with only 1 coding problem graded on correctness.

He really cares about his students. 
The quizzes and the final exam just followed the practice exams and homework.
Quizzes every other week that lectures and practice quizzes don't really prepare you for. Grades take a long time to come out and the class can be a bit disorganized at times.

The lectures do not help you whatsoever and he gives you a quiz every 2 weeks that has only the vaguest relevance to his lectures and practice quizzes, which are just a bunch of past exams that aren't even formatted the same.
Avoid at all costs

A lot of self studying is necessary. The lectures are based on simple 2D/3D visual diagrams with explanations (very little math) whereas the quizzes are entirely math and intuition heavy. Not very reflective of the content taught in class and there's no partial credit or grade replacement policy
pretty bad. all good ratings you see came from when the quizzes and exams were taken online.
This class is quite difficult, there is a quiz every two weeks, but it's fine if you study the concepts. Lectures aren't useful so self-study.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures on complex math concepts by just talking about them, rather than walking through concrete examples. Gives a quiz on a mid-term's worth of material every week. On top of this, there is a final and three 2-2.5 page projects. Starts every lecture 10 minutes late. Gives prep materials and makes quiz nothing like prep materials nor lecture.
Hard Quiz, lecture hard to follow

Well organized lectures delivered at an easy to follow pace. Professor really cares about students and is open to chat whenever possible. Though his material was introductory, he encouraged students to go beyond and explore through projects (which were graded generously). He makes sure that students are not under any stress due to the course.
Amazing professor. His lectures are really interesting and he explains everything very clearly. Would recommend 100%.

One of the best professors I have ever had, extremely great lecture and very engaging. Just take any class he teaches, you will not regret it. Assignments and quizzes are clear, some questions can be tricky but nothing unmanageable, and he prepares you pretty well for them. He genuinely wants you to learn from his class and live your best life.

I took him for NLP. His lectures are amazing. He's very good at explaining complex ideas in a simple way. Grading was very fair and you always felt like you had the knowledge you needed to complete assignments.

He's a super caring professor and doesn't overload students with any busy work. Each lecture is straight to the point and is intended to give you a deeper understanding of what you're doing on your assignments. 5 assignments plus corresponding quizzes and the lowest one of each is dropped. Great professor, great class!

Lecture content is pretty heavy, but he explains things in a way that's relatively easy to understand. Your whole grade consists of 5 homework assignments (each with a programming question) and 5 quizzes  no exams in his class! You also get to drop your lowest quiz and homework score! It really seems like he cares about his students. Recommended!
Very reasonable, caring professor & easy class. 5 quizzes & 5 homeworks are the entire grade & he drops 1 of each.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Taylor is an awesome professor, although he does lecture very quickly at times, but you can just slow down the podcast. Very caring, friendly, and fair prof. PAs can take a bit to understand but HW and quizzes (the whole grade) are not too difficult. Takes student feedback seriously. Always 5 minutes late to class. Would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: I took his AI class during Winter quarter of 2019. What a great experience!

The lectures were very hard to follow. The handwritten slides were messy and the explanations didn't make the material clearer. The course structure felt disorganized, so students were often confused about what was going on. At times it seemed like the issues were blamed on the TAs. The topics themselves were sometimes interesting.

The course is highly unstructured, he hops between topics Slides are impossible to read and understand. He assumes knowledge of concepts and skips explaining stuff attributing it to something that should already be known by all. Homeworks havent been changed in 7 yrs, doesn't evaluate the projects. No feedback on homeworks or why points were cut

Dinesh is a brilliant mind and a good lecturer. Yes, he is tough, but there are many resources. As a student pursuing DSP, I am happy that this is the person I was introduced to the field with. He makes what he expects clear, with a decent foundation in ECE 45, this course becomes fun. His exams are hard, study up, and you will manage a good grade.

Bharadia struggles to solve his own problems in class, and then expects students to solve yet more difficult ones under greater time pressure on exams. He is on the low end of intelligence for STEM professors and thus has skewed perspective on indicators of capability (grades). Unclear explanations in class; obfuscates with undefined terms/notation

He said, "We have been nice to everyone." The average term GPA is 2.94 and half the class got B-. The ECE department of ucsd is a place filled with excellent and amazing professors. Literally anyone else would be a better choice.

He said that the final should take one hour. no student finished in the three allotted the final was over two times the length of finals from other professors, problems were in bad English and required more assumptions. Its as if he relishes making students second guess themselves. He made numerous computational+conceptual errors in class

MATLAB projects are mostly busywork. Lectures are half-conceptual, half-problem solving: Prof. Bharadia is proficient with the material and is very interactive with students. Material is naturally hard (mostly ECE 45 review), but Prof. Bharadia does his best to accommodate and ask feedback from student. Great TA/tutors. Very solid choice!

He is very smart, like forbes 30under30 smart. And the typical with these professors are they sometimes give extremely hard exam unintentionally. I like him and his passion to help students understand the material, but it is really hard sometimes to keep up and understand him completely. Matlab is interesting and fun, exams are hard.
worst prof i've ever head, give extremely hard exams

The professor seems to assume that the students have 30+ hours for this course every week. He teaches as if everyone has taken the course before, leaving many things unexplained. The workload is very heavy and the progress of lectures is way too fast. The grading is extremely tough and you'd better avoid this course if you want a good grade.
He teaches like he is talking to himself. Didn't learn jack from this class. Extremely tough grader and don't know how to teach. One of the worst professor I've taken

Professor Rao is very knowledgeable. The problem with that is he overlooks that sometimes students dont understand what hes saying because its trivial to him. Furthermore, he does not like to discuss anything that inconveniences him. If you want to know more about an upcoming test, you have to wait until a few days before it! Unprofessional.

reviews.comment: Professor Rao is an amazing lecturer who is very interested in student success! He does a great job giving feedback and really likes to answer questions. Take advantage of his office hours - he is very patient with even trivial questions. His class is a bit time-intensive, but it was a fantastic learning experience and he is a great professor.
The worst ever!
Bhaskar is a tough grader but he is very smart. His lecture is very fast but contains a lot of information. Generally, a good class but you have to devote significant time on it.
Knowledgable professor

Ran into him this past weekend and man is he still one of the most interesting people to talk to. He can always make me smile. Wish he was still teaching at UCSD but he is on to bigger and better things. He owns his own company and is going to Law School at Stanford. Best of luck! Mwah!
thought he was a student the first day of class since he was totally younger than any professor I have ever had. super intelligent, super funny, super interesting.

awsome professor. he is probably one of the smartest person and professor i have ever met in my life. This school is honestly lucky to have such a person teaching its classses. He will be one hell of a lawyer and an equally amazing professor. He is always available to his students and willing to help out with assignments. Great feedback on papers
miss this guy since he doesn't teach anymore. it was shortlived and i can definitely say that it was an honor taking his class. hope he comes back to teach my grad seminar!

Great grt teacher! He made class interestingg and he would actually teach us something worth listenin too. Umm he sometimes went off book which was a pain for notes. Just read the assigned readings and yu will do fine in the classs! But still a great class! :)

I definitely had a great time with this teacher. Interesting approach. I don't know what happened to him, but if anyone knows if he is still teaching please post his classes on here. I have recommended him to everyone.
A little difficult to keep up with. You need to know alot about political science in order to succeed in this class. I kinda felt left behind.

This teacher is amazing! Not only does he know his stuff, but he is able to break it down to each students level so they can understand and grasp the material. Whats so weird is that he is younger than most of his students. I am trying to get in all of his classes right now since he just started teaching! A++++++ Loved the class!

chill guy but way too many readings a week, this course is heavy and the grading is hard. i'd say this course is equivalent to 6 units with how much time you have to invest. i've never had the urge to write a ratemyprofessor until now. I hate to be that guy but avoid this class if you can.
I just was not motivated to invest that much time into this class
Just run if you're not a go-to-lecture person.

Took Winter 2024. We were his experiment class, and the midterm grades were an all-time low. Ended up P/NP the class because the midterm was week 6. Final was much more manageable. Lectures were very interesting, but there is a lot of reading for homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He gives awesome lecture. Attending class is a necessity to achieve a good grade. Takes good care of his students to make sure everything is fairly graded. Lots of research papers to read but super interesting and on the tests. Asking questions helps.

took this class in order to fulfill my upper div election and DEI requirement, I could've chosen so many classes but im glad I chose this one. If you attend lecture the class is easy, I never did the readings only reviewed my notes and lecture slides before exams and did above the class average. The professor is great, easily one of my favs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class itself is a fascinating topic because it challenges one to consider economics from a different perspective. However, the TAs and the professor leave a lot to be desired. The TAs take forever to respond or leave no feedback on assignments. Also, there are a lot of readings around 6 or 7 per week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took class in WI24 & forgot to rate him. Definitely one of my top 3 professors. Lots of readings but breaks them down in class so don't worry. He gives ample study materials & the class is not hard if you pay attention. Also is easy to talk to & very engaging during lecture. I wish he taught more undergraduate classes to I could take them.
Was very engaging during lecture, I enjoyed this class a lot but the content was kind of hard. If you go to lectures and engage you should have a good time though

The best professor and best class I've taken at UCSD. Class is so engaging that usually when the prof asks a question, multiple students raise their hands and we have great conversations. He clearly cares about his students and their success a lot. Super interesting, intellectualy stimulating, and he's funny. I highly recommend. Learned a lot.

The class is very interesting, and he explains the materials very well. The lectures are also very engaging, but he did not record the lectures, at least for the quarter when I took it. However there are many papers that you have to read before class in order to understand what's going on. The final and the essays are also very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is a class is not an easy A if you don't attend lectures (they aren't recorded). But attending lectures were fun for me because Prof Bharadwaj explains the concepts in a way that invites you to think critically. Grading is 60% Writing assignments and 40% Final. I didn't read all of the readings, just listen attentively in class to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Salute my guy
Salute.

I was getting a B+ (curved grade) before final. However, after the final, the curve was canceled!!!! The reason from the Prof is the average is an 80 so there's no need for a curve. Excuse me??? That only make our grade even worse!! only few students can get A mostly get a B/B- and now you cancel the curve since the average on the final was 80???

There are quizs and three papers. Make sure that you meet everything for the paper to have an A. There are so many materials to read each week and you have to read these to take quiz. He give curve at the end. Amazing class!

The quizzes weren't bad, but challenge your reading comprehension and understanding of the points he highlights in lecture more than formulas or mathematical skills. Quite different from other upper div econ courses I've taken at UCSD. Nonetheless he explains everything carefully and, as a DEI, challenges your perspective on race, gender, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: A genuine teacher who wants to see his students succeed. I personally enjoyed his lectures and how interactive they made them feel while being remote. The quizzes are taken through Canvas weekly and will be deceptively hard. The quiz questions almost feel artificially difficult sometimes. 3 short essays in total; most students receive high A's.

A genuine teacher who wants to see his students succeed. I personally enjoyed his lectures and how interactive they made them feel while being remote. The quizzes are taken through Canvas weekly and will be deceptively hard. The quiz questions almost feel artificially difficult someitmes. 3 short essays in total; most students receive high A's.

The writing assignments are open-ended, but you could get points deducted... He said he would curve the class, but he didn't. Although you are more than one standard deviation above the average, you will still end up with B+.

His PPT is not very helpful and his lectures are not clear either. The grading policy is strict. There is no textbook, but very heavy reading. All the mutiple choice questions on exams are about readings. If you do not read and unferstand readings well, you will not pass both exams and quizes. If you are not good at reading, don't take this class.

Dont trust the evaluation on UCSD capes. Nobody understood what he teaches on class, he speaks too fast and always explains a simple point by a harder way. If you really want to know what he is talking about, go for a Econ tutor, otherwise you will doubt your learning ability. Worst class experience I have ever had.

He is the worst professor I have ever had. Sooo much of readings and heavy lectures. He teaches us by just talking his PPT and he hardly writes on the board. His TA's review class is much much useful than his lectures! The grading and reagrading polies are tough. If you do not read the readings well, you will fail the class. Do not take his class.

Hands down one of the best professors I've had at UCSD. Prashant presents really interesting material and basically changed my life and research interests. The class relies on you both doing the readings and having critical thinking skills. If you take the time to actually think about and analyze the material, assignments and exams are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: This class is lecture and reading heavy. If you dont keep up with your readings or come to lecture, you will fail. His style of teaching is all over the place and does not explain concepts well enough. His study guides do not help whatsoever. Overall, if you want to have a bad time and read a lot, then he is your guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cool guy. Helpful during office hours. Quizzes on readings every class (clicker). Its heavy reading, but many of the articles are interesting. Recommend. Definitely not easy but worth your while.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: His powerpoints are no that helpful and is too strict as you lose points on your exam if your regrade is not approved or when you have to ask what your seat assignment is on the midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Way too much material for time allotted - very little room for students' self interpretation. His tests go either you know it or you don't and questions were often too non-specific. I found it very difficult to agree with his perspective sometimes, as open-ended questions on tests are only correct with his interpretation (no partial credit).

Great professor. The course material is really fascinating to begin with, but he does a great job with keeping his lectures interesting and to the point. The readings can be a bit tedious, but they reinforce concepts from the lectures. Tests are not too bad as long as you pay attention in lecture. I learned a great deal from this class!

Had him a few years ago.  Best prof. I had at UCSD (besides Magagna).  Very easy to relate to and pretty good soccer knowledge.  The man made economics with an African focus interesting and relevant, especially for someone who had no interest in either.

The material is very interesting and lectures are long but not boring. The bad part was that the readings were very long, so you have to sift through useless information to get to the point. The midterm was harder than the final. Overall he likes to tests you on applications of the concepts he taught in lecture, which is both good and bad.

Very young, but a very good professor! I've noticed that old professors tend to get lazy. He makes his own slides and cares a lot about his students' learning. I loved every second of his class, I never missed one lecture! Which you shouldn't because his tests are alll about his lectures.

One of my favorite Prof. at UCSD. Lectures are interesting and easy to follow, his focus is more on Economics but still easy enough for those non-econ people. Very helpful during office hours and an overall great professor.
Great teacher. clear in class and helpful in office hours. concise powerpoints. attendance is mandatory and discussion is fairly limited but lectures are interesting.

This prof was such a genuinely cool dude and I could tell he really cared about his students. He was really easy to get a hold of over email and always made sure to address any questions. Attendance is mandatory and you can only miss two lectures. There is A LOT of reading but as long as you skim it before class you should be good.

Mr. B is a reasonable & charismatic guy, but bro needs to realize HDS 175 isn't the only one we are taking. Reading review basically the midterm, 4x (biweekly) papers, x2 summaries of all readings, 10 page final, and a few more manageable HWs. 6-9 readings a week but I would only read a few to get the idea. Not a hard class, but lots of busy work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Lord Jesus Christ this man wants so many long and detailed assignments each and every day. Several readings, reflections on each, discussions on each, reviews on each, it's consuming. I just need this class to pass the totally unnecessary dei requirement. Wish I knew that the amount of homework he assigns is so heavy please be forewarned.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. B is a good prof. I liked being in his class. There is a lot of work, but he was willing to push back assignments if we needed more time. He is good, just not the best professor I've had. You'll do okay in the class if you do the labs and homework assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. B is an absolutely amazing prof!!! HDS 181 is a lot of work (3 papers+weekly hw & readings), but he makes it manageable and easy to handle. He encourages participation and asking questions, which if you do, you will succeed in his class. The most caring, inspirational, and thoughtful prof I've ever had. Cannot say enough good things about him

Prof Bjorklund makes HDS181 super manageable. He presents the material in a way that is easy to understand and all lectures/classwork/homework are designed to go hand in hand so you're never left confused. He also goes out of his way to get to know all of the students in the class and wants everyone to succeed. 3 labs/research papers + homework
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bjorklund made it so easy for us to go to him for any concerns/questions. You can tell hes very passionate about teaching and is the epitome of what a teacher should be. Hes even adjusted his syllabus for us many times to ensure we all learn and succeed. I have learned a lot from in terms of writing research papers. Definitely recommend

Very nice and fun prof. Class is basically P/NP. If you meet the minimum requirements on assignments, you will get an A. Super easy class that felt connected and tight-knit. Attendance is mandatory. She also gives lots of feedback to help your writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very good teacher. Just give a least a little bit of effort and pay attention in class and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, won't make you fall asleep in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Super sweet and funny prof, grade is based on completion of assignments, and as long as you put in a good amount of effort, you get full credit. If she doesn't think it's finished, you have lots of time to revise and get it turned back in. This class is what you make it

Had her for 3 quarter of CCE (CCE1-CCE3). She's very considerate when it comes to attendance and due dates. She gives a lot of feedback which may seem overwhelming, but it really helps you become a better writer. Definitely recommend her for anyone taking CCE and looking to better their writing! Also, easy class overall. Just do your work.

Super chill professor, easy class with light requirements. You choose what grade you want and complete whats asked of you. Just make sure you follow assignment requirements for the three projects exactly how she wants them. Allowed to miss up to a few classes but shes superrr flexible with people leaving early (I always left 20 mins early).

Awful class with awful requirements. this class requires absolutely no academic skills, you are graded solely based on your own opinions yet you won't receive credit unless you write an insane amount of BS to kiss up to the teacher. This class should be eliminated as a graduating requirement.

least favorite class of all time. professor is very nice but such a tough grader. class is impossible. You're graded based on completion - which sounds amazing, but trust me its NOT. Basically you wont receive a complete until she thinks its worth an A+ even if you dont want an A in the class. hope they change everything about this class over break

Professor Bigley is one of the most hands on and supportive teacher I have ever met so far at ucsd. She cares for her students and has always displayed admiration for her students and their opinions. Unfortunately, she is teaching a class that is not a favorable one among some students, but she tries her best and I see that everyday.
Isn't very clear on what she wants and the assignments. Cool as a person but not as a teacher. Is flexible when turning in work and deadlines. Groupwork for the main core projects.

I love, love, LOVE Michele. Dynamic lecturer, involves every student in the class. Really understands what it means to create and build community. Very accessible, very kind, very understanding. Gives clear, concise feedback, and clearly loves her students very dearly. She is truly a gem, and I adore her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bigley is very sweet. She really cares about her students' academics and their personal lives. She gives timely feedback and is always available outside of class if you need help. I would recommend taking her if you can.

Inside the class, she is pleasant and very laid back, which makes it a good experience. Outside of class tho, she is a very tough grader and constantly contradicts things she says in class. When comparing my work to others with different professors, I would receive a C for a paper that resembled the work of my peers yet they would receive an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: was fine nothing note worthy but for CAT was good
You are graded on how well you can show that you understand the reading material.    Attendance matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Super fun lectures where you get to listen to music almost everyday. 2 essays and 4 short assignments on pretty interesting, everyday-life related, topics, one of which was the Super Bowl. Grades mainly depend on TA but prof himself also does the grading sometimes. Not that much reading for a writing class. Genuinely cares and listens to students.
The homework instructions were kind of vague sometimes. However, Professor Bigham is enthusiastic and his lectures are intriguing!
Best teacher I had this quarter and the only class I would actually be happy going to. Very easy class and he wants you to get the best possible grade.
Just make sure you care about the topic because I found his lectures extremely boring.

In my opinion, lectures are useless and boring, but he takes attendance, and they count for grades. Your grade depends on your TA; all the work in this class is done in discussion: easy class, easy articles, easy assignments. A good chunk of our assignments were graded as complete/incomplete.
This professor was super flamboyant and creative, always showing up to class with amazing outfits! He is extremely cheerful and funny, with entertaining lectures and engaging classes.

I'm not really interested in music, so the topics were a bit boring to me. But he has very few assignments and makes the class pretty easy so I'd recommend taking him. TA matters more though, as they are the ones grading everything. No exams, only papers, making soundscapes, and a group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures were pretty boring in my opinion, and generally lost my attention. I could tell he was really trying to make his lectures entertaining, but the topic just didn't interest me. As for grading, essay grades are heavily dependent on the TA (TA's could be strict or lenient on essay grades). The workload was pretty light.
He's very passionate about what he's teaching which makes lectures not too bad. His assignments are reasonable, usually an assignment a week. All attendance is mandatory so plan for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: It's hard to rate the professor when 95% of your grade is based on the TA you receive. After having him for CAT 2 and 3 though, I can say that he was an enthusiastic professor who gave good guidance on assignments and pushed back deadlines due to student stress. I found most lectures useless and irrelevant to assignments though unfortunately.

Bigham is an enthusiastic lecturer, but he doesn't seem very organized: he missed the deadline for making his class remote, so people ended up having to come back to campus for a single weekly in-person discussion. During the remote half of the quarter, he only had recorded lecture videos, which made it hard to interact with him and other students.

Really fun and chill teacher- wish we didn't start off online. Lots of reading but the minor assignments were really fun and made me appreciate music more. Prof was definitely rushed due to a last minute course switch but put a lot of effort. Weird how a 100% on an essay was rare but earning an A is still possible

I get the impression that he really cares about his students. Lots of lectures but at least they were fun. Assignments were fun, actually useful, and had clear grading criteria. Required reading wasn't that useful, but at least it's free. Overall, I highly recommend him he's the best CAT professor I've had at UCSD!

The best professor so far. It is hard to write the assignments until I start going to his office hours. His office hours are super helpful. I literally scheduled a meeting with him almost every week and that I started to feel bad about it lol. But he's super nice and unbothered. My IA is bad but he's good.

Prof Bigham is a super sweet dude, I don't understand the negative reviews. I didn't have an in person class w him due to covid, but his online format is amazing and low stress while still being useful. I am usually only interested in STEM but his passion for music and futurism makes the class interesting. Definitely recommend him for online CAT 3.

He's a great lecturer and puts a lot of passion into what he does because he's a musician at heart. He also understands that you have other classes besides his, so the workload is quite reasonable. If you have the chance, take him.
Prof Bigham's lectures radiate positive energy. Very chill and nice guy and sympathetic towards students. The last essay is due the week before finals. Your grade depends on your TA.

Hey Sixth Freshman how's it going. If somebody's talking poorly about Bigham you got some real issues. Had him for CAT 1 and 3, top Professor you can get outside of maybe Bronstein because of how easy she grades. Vibrates joy in everything he does, cares about the students and doesn't overwhelm them during finals week, take him for the love of God

Really cool prof. Connects his experiences in music world to concepts we are learning and try's to get us to see new perspectives and links between music and culture. Papers can be tricky, but the TA's are helpful and the prompts are unusual but fun. Good at giving lectures and taking adjusting teaching style to student response.
Boring class
Really Tough Grader!!!
Sign-in sheets in lectures. Lectures were fun. Grades depend on TAs.

The worst class I've taken at UCSD. The whole concept, to learn a musical instrument in 10 weeks and then write a paper on the process of music-learning, is flat out stupid. Grading depends solely on the TAs so count your blessings: some of the TAs take pleasure in speaking down to their students and grading harshly for a dumb and pointless class.

He's a solid, interesting professor who's very passionate about music. His CAT2 class only had 3 papers with max 5 pages (other CAT2 profs had 8 pages for some) which was nice. Grade depends on your TA, so the difficulty varies. Lots of (pretty dull) reading but I only did them right before essay was due, no need to do all of them.

His lectures are great! Everything is based on your TA (typical of CAT). SO much reading but I didn't do it all and I was fine so don't worry about it. Lectures didn't really connect to the essays, which was fine. Open ended topics, but I like that but I know some hate it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Bigham's attitude towards the lecture is passionate, which makes his lecture interesting. However, he seems like he doesn't know what he is teaching... 75%of your grade depends on the papers. Your grade depends on TA. It's really hard to understand the prompt and my TA thinks my 3 papers vague every time. But it's a great "music appreciation" class

Great teacher! Tons of reading material if you try to read it all. For the papers you can take quotes from lecture or from skimming the readings. Professor Bigham is very enthusiastic about music and his passion shows! Would highly recommend him again! Go to your TA and the CAT writing studio for help! Otherwise the grades may not be as good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easy class. The papers are more creative than other CATs and it's while you do have to work for it, an A isn't extremely hard. Reading isn't that important. It's needed for papers but you can just skim when the paper is due. Lectures are also interesting. He is very enthusiastic about music.

In the beginning of each lecture, he'll play a music video, and usually 2 or 3 more throughout. He is very enthusiastic and knowledgeable about the subject, although not everything lectured was useful for our essays. Your grade depends on your TA. We had to learn an instrument, but were not judged on how well we played, just how we analyzed it.

Professor Bigham is extremely enthusiastic. It's quite hard to fall asleep in his class. He knows what he's talking about and loves it. Grade depends on TA. We had to learn an instrument for this class and were given an opportunity to perform at the end of the quarter. If you're not that into music, then his class won't be for you.
A well-thought of class with poor organization and execution. All that potential down the drain.

very enthusiastic about the subject even when most students aren't. a great lecturer which made the 2 hours bearable (lecture is optional but he did random attendance twice). He's SUPER helpful during office hours so if you're struggling with projects he'll give you great feedback & suggestions. 1 personal statement,1 ignite presentation, 1website
10/10 would not take again. :)

Very enthusiastic about what he's teaching. One of the few professors I could stay awake for (lectures were once a week but 2 hours long). Also very encouraging to students. Wants you to "do great work". If you take CAT125, take it with him.
bravo! good stuff.

Best class so far. Difficult material but office hours extremely useful. Blatant cheating in Matlab & assignments by some. Real worry these guys will become 'engineers' in a couple of years, and tarnish rest of us. Major ethics violations. Employers & internships: avoid B or lower at all costs. Previous reviewer claims A, seriously doubt it.
Avoid at all costs.

Excellent class sabotaged by a few bad students. Prof  taught really well.  UCSD should not admit students who cannot understand elementary math and english. Employers beware of students that failed/barely passed MAE 143A this quarter. My classmates know  several cheated - including the guy who wrote the previous 5 reviews.
He wrote on the blackboard in illegible handwriting. He seemed to be completely unaware that his students were dozing off, doodling in their notebooks, or staring blankly into space.

As the semester wore on, the students became increasingly desperate. They formed study groups, consulted textbooks, and even hired tutors, but nothing could prepare them for the professor's final exam. It was a mishmash of random questions, typos, and grammatical errors. Some of the questions were so unclear that no one knew what they were asking.

When the results were posted, the students were horrified. Almost everyone had failed. Some had even received negative scores, thanks to the professor's deductive skills. But the professor remained unrepentant. "I don't believe in coddling my students," he said. "If you can't handle a little challenge, you don't belong in my class."
bro just reads off the slides... worst professor I've ever had at this university

Rating scared me at first, but I loved his class. Casual lecture style, and its clear that he wants everyone to do well. Some of the later homeworks are more challenge problems than standard exercises, but that just makes the exams super easy comparatively, and he basically gives away what will be on them in lectures. I actually learned.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Doesn't teach at the level that he gives hw, would not recommend taking him at all. Worst prof I have ever had in the MAE department. He only reads off the lecture slides and does not actually teach or explain very well.

Does not teach what is needed to know to successfully understand the hw. Reads off the lecture slides and doesn't really teach, then gives homework that is way more advanced than any class example. Wish I had never chosen this prof tbh.
good bloke. class is tough, but it's clear he has genuine interest in making you better. welcomes students to visit if they don't understand.

Homeworks are dreadful to do, especially the matlab sections. Lectures are useless and the professor berates the class for not answering questions he asks during lecture. Just study from the slides/homework/previous exams and you'll be fine. The exams are open book/open notes so bring as much as you can with you to the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the BEST professors at UCSD. Bob doesn't teach for the sake of teaching; he actually introduces you to stuff that has been done in industry. Yes, we weren't tested on the MATLAB stuff he did in lecture, but by god data analysis is an important skill and I appreciated the he took the time to teach it to us. He is a genius!

Pros: Gives you access to previous class resources. Grading system is super clear-cut. Extremely knowledgeable on signals/systems. Cons: Teaches an introductory class like its a grad class. Tedious homework. Beware - he 100% gives out Fs to students who dont make the cutoff (no curving). Make use of ALL the resources he offers.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He makes students feel horrible about their education. The class is one of the hardest in Engineering. He does not explain anything during lecture. He spends hours on Matlab and he does not even test you on it. Horrible professor.
Great guy
Good prof and good class. Used singals and systems, good book. Decent amount of hw assigned. Grades were curved at end.

Bitmead is one of the few professors I've taken classes from who actually cares about providing insight on the subject he's teaching.   Yes it's a hard class, but it's because Bitmead holds his students to a higher standard; do the same for yourself!
Definitely one of the best prof here in UCSD. Intellectual effort will be rewarded in this class.
Good professor, the only problem is he teaches in his level, not at student's level

I really enjoyed this class/professor. Bitmead's a really cool guy full of stories. His lecture slides were very good summaries of major concepts, the homework is imperative to complete for a good grade. Tests are VERY difficult because he tests method and actual knowledge versus memorization skills.
The worse professor at UCSD by far! I wish I could go back and drop his class when I had the chance.  He's a GPA killer!

I agree(Difficulty = inf) and he is not good at teaching the subject at an undergrad level but his homework was challenging enough to not be impossible and it actually taught you a lot of what he was trying to teach you in class. GO TO OFFICE HR AND LEARN FROM HW!!! You should treat office hrs as if they were class hrs. I can't stress that enough!

This is not an easy course and Pro Rob's approch to the matieral can make it hard(er) to understand.  I had hard time understanding the material when I took it, but things became much more clear after I took the related Math courses.  Good understanding of transfer function (and related math material) can make this course easier.

Pro Rob is cool.  Very willing to help as I had visited him with questions outside of course work in and out of his office hours and he rarely turned me down.  His lecture can be hard to understand at times but as long as students do and understand the HW material, the exams are manageable.  Work hard and it will reflect on your grade.
I wish I could kill myself for taking this course with this creature!

By far, he is the second worst MAE teacher at UCSD following Goddard. Lectures are useless and students ask the TAs "what's this course for?" even on the ninth week. Anyone who says "you're gonna get it by the end of the quarter", can not be a good teacher.
Really bad professor and overall bad experience. Waste of time...
I honestly think I could wake up with swine flu and my left nut alone could still be a better professor.
By far one of the worst classes and professors at this university!
Difficulty = inf.
Awful teacher!!

This professor really knows control. If you want to learn control avoid him because he will just confuse you. He is confusing and unable to teach effectively. Constantly berating students and TA's. Work around this professor if possible.
Awful teacehr!

He's weird but he's a good teacher. This class requires that you spend time on your own studying the material. Homeworks aren't that important because you can double the final (normally 50%) to represent your whole grade. His exams are generally pretty easy if you know what to look for in the shortest way to solve the problem. Pretty good overall.

Bitmead really knows what he's talking about since he's an EE. Good teacher, he makes sure you know the basics. Really wants class participation. He posts his past exams, which are really helpful. Going to his office hours is a big plus, it's more like a section than office hours. Tends to go off on random tangents but keeps the class interesting.

Really intimidating class. He says things only once and expects you to get it quickly, then he moves on... The book he chose didn't help at all, you have to rely on the TA or other students to catch all the small details. He's entertaining enough, though.
At first, the class was very intimidating, but Prof. Bitmead did a good job at explaining the subject matter, while interjecting various past experiences
GOOD professor! passionate! care about students, detailed and useful readings! you can learn a lot from his seminars! definitely take it again!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great teacher, very passionate and understanding. Definitely a good teacher, I took him for ANSC 124 which is a very straightforward class. 2 midterms and 1 final, all are take home essays that you have 10 days to complete. Great guy, would 100% take his class again and will miss him after I am done with my final.
Great prof, recorded lectures, interesting topics, not too much work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a very caring and kind professor who is passionate in what he teaches. My fav professor at UCSD. His classes are easy if you put in the effort. Graded by discussion posts, a midterm paper, and a final paper. The discussion posts are graded on if you tried hard enough, he'll give you a 10/10. The midterm and finals you need readings. Love him!

He's a passionate teacher who clearly loves to teach the material. This was an experimental class so the class was new, but there were weekly discussion posts and two papers, which count as the midterm and final. You just have to show you made the effort and tried, and he will be generous with the points. Do the readings for the midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class is pretty similar to any other anthropology class where you just have to read and provide analysis to the readings. Grade determined by 3 papers. If you attend class, he will offer you the "answer" to the rubrics or at least provide you with different approaches you can take to analyze the readings and formulate your argument.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The kindest, most considerate professor I've ever had the privilege of learning from. Obviously an expert in what he does and cares about teaching. Take every single class he has to offer! Super fair to his students and will do anything to make sure you succeed.

I have taken 3 classes from Dr. Bialecki. He is by far the kindest, most approachable, responsive professor I have had at UCSD. I'm a SC Anthro major & Bialecki's lectures are always fun(ny) & informative, as he takes a very philosophical approach to the discipline... something I very much admire. He's made distance learning a breeze. TAKE HIM.

Prof Bialecki showed so much kindness and consideration during our online classes. He understood that everyone had things going on bc of the coronavirus pandemic and offered a lot of leniency and consideration for students. He had very funny lectures, and all midterms and finals were reasonable. Kindest professor I've ever had.

One of the most inspirational, entertaining, and mentally stimulating professors I've ever had! A genius SC anthropologist who really gets your brain moving. I would recommend Bialecki to anyone in any field for any class

Easy A, but he says nothing of substance. Class was neither valuable nor useful (and I don't mean in a practical sense, as this is anthropology, but rather it was useless for intellectual development). Furthermore, makes simple topics/readings sound more complex than they are. He's a nice guy, but he needs to learn how to teach effectively.

Stay away. Lectures are a waste of time. He talks, and talks but says nothing. NOT concise at all. Very verbose. I am sure he is a nice guy and you can get an easy A, however, as a professor he does not really teach you anything.

Best Professor I've ever encountered. The way he teaches is amazing and even though he doesn't have in class midterms or finals it's still well worth the effort to take thorough notes. I've reread mine many times just for fun. Wonderful professor.
Incredible professor, well worth the time and effort!

Taken several of Bialecki's classes and each one of them has been incredible. By far my favorite professor on this campus, and in anthropology at that. I have learned tons, his classes are extremely informative and amazing. By far the best professor I have ever had.
Great Professor. Very entertaining. Although the material can be difficult, he is more than happy to help. Class consisted of two mid-terms and a final.

Interesting class, also a bit complicated subject material. I am not an ANSC major, so it was very philosophical and kind of difficult for me to follow. Jon was really entertaining though, he definitely knew a lot aobut the subject too. I became more interested and understood more as the class went on.

Scott is THE BEST professor I had so far. He really cares about student and worked so hard to make everyone understand the material. Super generous on the exams, so many extra credits, and his lectures are clear in explaining concepts. Also really want his students to become a virologist haha

One of the greats. Only 4 exams in the class, one of which is dropped. Practice exams are incredibly similar to the actual exams, almost down to the word. Very very clear on what will be on the exams. Weekly homework is just free points. I don't think he's teaching bicd100 again but if he is take him.

He was one of the best professors I ever had at UCSD. He gives so many extra credits and opportunities to boost your grade. There are 4 midterms and lowest one will be dropped. Midterms are similar to practice exams. He is so nice and caring.

one of the nicest and most caring professors i've ever had at ucsd, his practice exams are very representative of the real thing, offers so much extra credit and drops the 2 lowest hws, definitely take him!!

Such an iconic professor! He always listened to students' feedback to improve his teaching. Sometimes rushed topics, but overall did amazing at lecturing! Very forgiving course grading systems. Created such a warm class environment and even his TA's were amazing. Exams were pretty representative. Great upper div introduction. Take him if you can!

Probably the best genetics professor at UCSD. He's new and this was his first quarter and compared to the stories my friends have told me about genetics as a subject and overall taking it at UCSD I was expecting torture, but with him he made it fun and understandable and fair! All his exams are extremely fair with cheat sheets and extra credit(15+)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Three words to describe him: king, icon, slay.

BEST PROF EVER!!!! He may genuinely be the only professor I really liked at UCSD. He has a quirky personality and is genuinely empathetic and caring for students. He allows a cheat sheet front and back,  180 out of 200 points for an A-, lots of extra credit, lowest midterm dropped, gives practice exams, wants everyone to succeed and get an A!

Professor Bering is one of the best professor I've ever met. He understands the student's obstacle and full of empathy, and his class is interesting with flexible grading policy. It is really worth to take his class if there is ever a chance.

Dr. Scott is kind, silly, inspiring & passionate abt his field. He cares abt his students and does his best to ensure everybody understands the material and he wants everybody to get an A or a B+. He teaches the difficult subject well and grades on a point system. Attendance not mandatory but worth extra credit and lecture heavy. He's cool/chill af

I was so nervous to take him bc he had no reviews but honestly he is one of my favorite profs. i have ever had. you can tell he is really interested in genetics and wants you to succeed. he gives four exams and it's all on a point based grade and not weighted. exams are 40 pts homework and reading are 80. and EC was 15. all out of 200 pts. TAKE HIM

He is amazing, clear on what is expected on the exams, 4 midterms, lowest is dropped. attendance is extra credit. He makes sure you understand the material and he goes over everything that will be on the final. Cheat sheet front and back. I was a little behind on my lectures for the first midterm so I didn't do as well. take him if you can.

The only way to pass the class is to teach yourself the content outside of class hours. I spent 10-15+ hours a week outside of class learning the content and still averaged 65% on the midterms+final (which make up 80% of your grade). Lectures are confusing, scattered, and poorly organized. You also only get 2 units for 4C if taken after 3C.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He seemingly expects you to have a good understanding of everything going into the class. The lectures are way too fast to actually learn anything, and there is an absurd amount of homework. I was working for around 10 hours a week for this class doing everything I could to pass it (anything below a C is failing).

Passionate about the subject but not good at teaching at all. Provides no feedback and 75% of the students were failing before the final. Lectures, homework, and tests were all covering different things and you have to self teach yourself the content. Never updates canvas. Take this course at community if he's the only professor available here.

Lectures are fast, hard to follow and exams are extremely hard. Homework and exams include techniques not mentioned during lectures. Don't take unless you already know the content and expect to work very hard and find outside resources for a passing grade. Passionate about math but doesn't care about the class and laughs about 30% averages for exam

Just don't even choose this man. Run far away. He makes the test way more difficult than what he teaches us and expects us to know it. You can spend HOURS studying for his exams and still manage to fail because of how difficult the problems are on the exams (exactly what happened to me)!

Run. This prof makes simple concepts so much harder than they have to be and doesn't care about his students succeeding. No extra credit, no curves, 80% of your grade is midterms and the final, and a 70% is an F.

Lectures/notes unorganized and difficult to follow. Midterms and final worth a combined 80% of your grade. Genuinely the worst class and prof I've ever taken. I spent ~8 hours every week on hw for this class that didn't help me on quizzes or tests at all. If you have to take this prof you're better off changing your major.
Everything we learned was not reflective of exams, which were worth so much of our grade. I lost my will to live over this class.

Within this class, you are expected to know all topics and have no other way of learning. Other classes give out cheat sheets and give better explanations as to what to do for problems. He'll put the blame on you when he doesn't give enough help as to what to expect. In a class where the average for the midterm was 50%, you'd think he would help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 80% of your grade is based on exams that are nothing sinilar to what the math department offers as sample exams. He avidly makes his own exams and makes them so much more difficult in comparison the the math department samples. Hes borderline sadistic.

The only thank you I have to give him is for making me a more active member of my church and devoted to my religion because he left me praying every day to get through this class. Join the waitlist (doesn't matter how long) before you register for him. Expects you to already know the lecture, wants people to drop out, and have more people fail.

Lectures are extremely unorganized and fast paced without any thorough explanation of anything. The worst part is that the exams he writes (worth total 80% of your grade) are not a true reflection of the material in the copious amount of homework/quizzes assigned weekly. Math department is the true evil, no curve in a class with a D/F average.
Tests are 75% of his class, the homework take hours and don't reflect whats on the midterm and exams. Wouldn't recommend to anymore.

He seems passionate about the course, but his teaching style is hard to follow. Does notes on blackboard with unclear format. The examples he does in lectures are extremely easy compared to those in the homework or exams + context heavy. Barely passed the class by being near the average (usually around 40s / 100 for midterms, 90s / 200 for final)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Interesting personality, but a good professor. Lectures move fast—review the textbook before class. He is extremely intelligent, but sometimes makes errors during lecture. His office hours are really helpful—I wish I had gone sooner! He doesn't have control over exams so no curve. Not a prof for everyone, but if you want to learn concepts, take him

I wish I could go back and tell myself to stray away from this evil man. He assigns SO MUCH busy work. And it's not even hard it's just extremely time consuming. He also has extremely tough graders. He was put on this earth to make my life terrible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: oh my god. writing this right now is making me relive it all. never ever take this class. I took it for credits and because of my major but taking this class made me want to change my major as a whole. BLOOD, SWEAT, AND TEARS WITH LITTLE TO NO REWARD. oh god please.

Had him for MATH 20A as well, great professor. I felt that the lectures combined with the homework taught the material to me at a good level. The exams are definitely more difficult than the homework, but if you gain a deep understanding of the concepts rather than replicating HW answers / lecture examples you should be fine.

reviews.comment: Professor cheng has a unique way of how he runs his class, Cheng will lecture the basic math problems in class and assign homework that is more difficult than what he taught. His homework is not online at all, and graded harshly. His exams are 90% of your overall grade and his exams include content that he does not go over, I wouldnt recommend.

He gives a lot of homework problems that include questions that were not taught during class. He expects you to learn most of the content through the homework. The exams were tough evidently from the roughly 40% averages on exams. He is very exam heavy with 90% of the course grade coming from exams.

reviews.comment: I would not recommend Prof Cheng for 20C.  Heavy homework with lots of problems.  Homework is not done on Achieve and it is graded on correctness.  Class mid-term average was roughly 40%.

reviews.comment: Do not take this professor. The grading is 90% exams 10% written graded homework, and he expects you to learn basically everything through the homework. The averages for his midterms were around 40%, which should tell you everything you need to know. No cheat sheet, no study guides.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just come to his office hours and he walks you through the solution steps. Then the exams are nearly the same as the practice. Cheng is the best prof at ucsd.

Cheng is the second-best professor for math classes (#1Briones). Yes, his tests are hard but the class is incredibly passable. He gives huge curves based on the mean, it is more likely for u to get an A with him than most other profs. Yes, there are low averages; this is a reflection of the too fast quarter system rather than him as a teacher.

His way of teaching is different in the way it analyzes and goes to the roots of how we come to understand the rules of the problem. A lot of homework so that I end up only grading three questions to which you have to put all the details of the answers. And the exams are too difficult compared to what he explains to us.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take this class at all costs. Exams were unreasonably difficult. His class average for midterm 2 was 36%. We were only given homework problems to prepare for exams but they didn't have full solutions guides. During class time he over-explained concepts and only would get through 2 practice problems each day during a 50 min lecture.

I cannot emphasize enough just how test-heavy this course is. Ninety percent of your grade depends on the two midterms and the one final. Decently lenient on giving pity points if you request regrades. The avg on tests is about 65% ish, but the final's is a lot lower. However, he is very open to questions during lectures and office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hes chill, im being 100% honest he was good until he did optimization. This brings me up to my next point he give a lot of homework and only grades 3 questions from each section. For exams, the average for both of his midterms was around 40-50, the final rn is being grated, but I'm assuming its going to be in the 60's.

His class is so straightforward but his exams are HARD. There is so much homework, but if you do it without looking at the answers, you will understand the material well. This class took up sm of my time, but I feel prepared for math 10b now. I know ppl in math 10b who are struggling due to an "easier" prof for 10a. Hes also funny asf

reviews.comment: I'm gonna be honest, he is a nice professor, but he does not fulfill the requirements of being a great, let alone, a decent professor. Even attending lectures were not helpful. Watching the podcasts and taking notes helped me learn more. EXCEPT you do not learn anything in this class. You have to find other resources to get a decent grade.
Although I think Professor Cheng's personality is fun and caring, pretty much everything else sucks. The midterms are brutal and pretty much expect to rely on the curve

reviews.comment: imo cheng is a great professor. doesn't have outlines available to students for his lecture notes, but still explains it pretty well. homework is harder than what he goes over in lecture, but i find that exam questions are typically easier than the homework questions. no paying for hw, it comes from openstax. pretty funny guy, fits are [fire emoji]

reviews.comment: Your grade for the class relies solely on your exams, plus like 10% for homework. The average on the past midterm for were below 50%, and he doesn't seem to care at all that people are doing horrible in his class. Sucks to be stuck with him when this class is needed for my major and to graduate on time. Please avoid him at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: be prepared to pray on your classmates downfall because the only saving grace for this class is the curve. Tests are 90% of grade yet the average test grade is 40%? Hw is SO much harder than what is "taught" in class and only 4/10-30 problems are graded. I relied heavily on TAs, mathway, chatgpt, and praying to god everyone else does as bad as me.

Sent straight from heII... The examples he shows in class do not reflect on what is on the homework. The questions on the homework also do not reflect on what is on the test. Intro to Calc? Intro to HeII maybe!!

Unless you are good at math or want to attend office hours every week, I don't suggest taking him. He's a good and nice guy but he teaches like you are already familiar with the concepts. 2 Midterms 25% homework 10% and final 45%, homework each week ranges from 10-30 problems. Good curve but you have to lock in to pass the class.

Just don't take him, please. I think unless you are just naturally good at understanding math, then this class is going to be hard for you. The tests are only 4 problems in 50 min but don't reflect what is taught in lecture or with the 30 questions of homework (due weekly). There is apparently a curve but I just would not recommend him to anyone.

reviews.comment: he has little structure in his lectures with no time awareness so he extends over meaningless topics and rushes the important things. GO TO OFFICE HOURS he doesn't explain almost anything of the homework so you'll have to rely on your TAs or his own office hours. The tests are horribly short, we aren't able to use a lot of formulas and it ain't it

reviews.comment: Please save yourself by not taking him. He assumes everyone has taken calculus before so he will do so much mental math that you won't understand if you have not ever taken calculus. He constantly yaps about many things that are unrelated and takes forever to solve problems (and most times he doesn't even fully solve them).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a funny and pretty outgoing professor. However, I disliked the way he teached the class. Concepts were skimmed over and the professor did not prepare us well for the midterms. Luckily, the curve was pretty strong. However I feel as if the way lectures were orientated and ran were very unorganized and substandard.

Lecture wise he's not great but hes way better in office hours but honestly this class isn't worth taking because I took AP Calc AB before and I thought this class was going to be a breeze but he just made it harder than it needed to be, he's a funny guy though.

The professor was disorganized during lectures. Lectures did not adequately cover homework material. Apparently, the curve is good, but the class is homework and test-heavy. He claims to hate the textbook we use, but all the homework is from there. The textbook is genuinely awful. He's nice and helpful in OH, but I'd never take his class again
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Midterms were difficult and were not similar to the examples in the lectures. Homework is difficult as well. Thank god the curve was okay.

Horrible lecturer. Would constantly go on unrelated tangents for the entire class period and not cover anything on the test. He also hates technology, so get ready for no calculators on your exams, plus hand-writing your 5+ hours of weekly homework. I got an A, and it nearly killed me. Take another professor.

This professor is very disorganized during lectures, he uses the chalkboard which makes it hard to see if you happen to get a seat toward the back. He only goes over 1-2 problems during the 50 minute lecture, which is very unhelpful when doing the homework. Grades depend on the 2 midterms (25% each) and final exam (40%), no cheat sheets/calculator.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very test heavy, as grading is 10% and the rest midterms and finals. There is a pretty nice curve though. Professor is very engaging during lectures, albeit the lectures are not very helpful, as they cover material at a surface level. Recommend doing additional textbook problems on top of the homework for better understanding, and you'll get an A.

Professor Cheng was very difficult, but he grades on a curve, and he's definitely still passionate about math and teaching. Tbh most of the questions on the exams are very similar to homework and example problems he covers in class, he just makes them wayy harder. I think he's a good teacher but I definitely would've preferred an easier prof.

He is fast during lectures, but if you meet him during office hours, he slows down a lot more. His midterms are similar to the homework. The homework is, on average, more difficult than the lecture examples; that's where office hours come in. His final is harder than anything we covered in class and he doesn't allow any calculators on anything.

reviews.comment: He's a super nice person but that's about it. His class and homework have very little to do with what will be on exams. No cheat sheets. He shows up to class, yaps, does like 3 examples, eventually gets corrected by a student that his large blob of random equations is actually incorrect. Does not teach. Super confusing. Don't take.

reviews.comment: Wonderful person, funny. Teaching is not his forte, the only person this man teaches is himself bc he talks so fast and makes a lot of mistakes because of the speed he carries his lectures at. He forces you to use his ways of approaching/solving problems, if not, no credit. you gotta teach everything to urself. Never take him for 20A, ur welcome.
