reviews.comment: Almost 3 stars.Passionate about math and fun person. He teaches very quickly with minimal to no examples (not always quality examples). He provides practice exams but never posts any solutions so it is hard to know how you are doing. He is good one-on-one though. Grades based on the midterms and final. The class is curved at the end of quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Cheng is passionate about math but homework does not truly reflect the test, a lot of self teaching is required, and his tests are really tough. Tests are raw score only and grades are curved at the end of the year, which I am not a really big fan of... Don't recommend, though he is a really nice person.

Professor is a very enjoyable and caring professor, but regarding course lectures, they are very disorganized and do not help most times for course material. Tests are very difficult even though they are curved nicely. Homework and lectures do not reflect what is on the test. Would recommend other professor if possible for 20A.

Not a very difficult class, he's very accessible outside of class, but also is a very disorganized teacher.  It's blatantly obvious that he doesn't prepare lecture materials/notes in advance; he'll chat for a while, then rush through the important material at the end.  Uses gradescope instead of achieve, get ready to photograph all your homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Might as well list the class as taught by Prof Google cause Prof Bing Cheng teaches nothing. One example per section (takes 50 min). The homework doesn't correlate to the tests, there are no cheat sheets allowed, and no study guide. Also, the TAs are given no instruction so discussions are useless and very few attend (like 10 of 400). Curve is nice
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No cheat sheet and gives one example per section. Whatever is on the exams has barely been covered. The curve is nice, but a professor is supposed to TEACH, not make their students have to learn everything themselves.

Really fascinating to watch lecture. Passionate about math. Cares that students don't just memorize, but actually understand content. Answers questions without hesitation. Pretty funny. Overall a really great person.
You will NOT learn from his classes you will have to self-teach. Everybody in this class is self-taught.

I took this man for math 20A, and he is the worst professor I've ever had. The midterms are extremely difficult, and the amount of homework is horrible, but he is a decent lecturer. Just be prepared for a very not fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great teacher, Very knowledgeable and fair on tests. Overall a great teacher and I would take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a pretty good lecturer, but he doesnt let you drop anything or have a cheat sheet like most other 20 series profs do. Grading is 25% for each midterm, 10% hw, and 40% final, so you cant drop a midterm or any homeworks. The averages on both midterms and the final was around a 60% so he curved the class pretty nicely. I got an A with an 87%

Prof. Cheng is awesome. hw amount is fairly large (expect 6+ hours of work/week). Lecture is very clear, helpful and interesting (don't miss it!). Midterms are fair (just understand all hw/lecture). The final was hard, but as you understand everything, getting a 90% is doable. He curves! Prof is very respectful and nice. No cheatsheet. Good class.

Great professor with a great attitude that gets you excited about learning. He doesn't allow cheat sheets for tests which means you have to memorize everything. Hand written homework that takes FOREVER and is actually graded for correct answers. Fair midterms, difficult final. Good professor, but difficult subject. But he curves!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Everyone can easily understand his lecture as long as he takes notes. He is super nice and always allows students to ask questions when he finishes a topic. He is the best professor you can get for linear algebra class. He knows his stuff and also teaches you interesting and useful knowledge beyond the realm of linear algebra. Highly recommend.

Really nice prof who actually cares about his students. However, he did not allow us to have cheat sheets like every other linear class and his exams are harder than thoe of other classes. He does have a decent curve though 25% As and 30% Bs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Cheng has lots of extra office hours for problems, and he's definitely caring and approachable after class. However, the tests are hard and require a deep understanding of the materials. Be prepared.
I skip other math lectures while choose to show up in this one. He explains material really well and is really enthusiastic in teaching. Bad thing is that no cheat sheet allowed in exam

Although there's a lot of homework just like any other math classes, Professor Cheng does his best to explain the course material. He's very energetic and will sometimes gets carried away in his explanations but he slows down if you ask kindly. His office hours are super helpful and he holds a lot of them, so take advantage of that!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Bing Cheng was nice and helpful when I told him I wanted to switch into his class from Wang Xu's after week 3, so that worked out right away. He was a much better lecturer and actually worked out problems on the board. He's a little harder than some other profs (i.e. no cheat sheets and focuses on specific topics) but I learned a lot.

Cheng's awesome! He's a really good professor in that he helps you understand the material deeply. He held a lot of office hours (more than the required), and stayed a long time after class for questions. He's really energetic during lecture, really kind, and shows you how cool math is . Take him if you can! I definitely miss his classes.

He is the super friendly. He is always there for his students. You can learn a lot from his office hour, if you go. Do not fear ask him questions!  He is a fantastic lecture for math compare to other profs, and he care about the application about the material.  But for sure, his test is super hard. Be prepared!!! But he give "hints" in lecture.

Lecture is definitely very fast paced and not boring. But the exams were a bit unfair IMO, and normally a cheat sheet is allowed in a 20F course as its highly theoretical, but he doesn't allow a cheat sheet which makes the tests ridiculously hard.
Best Math Prof Ever. Though his lectures and exams may not be easy, they are really inspiring and help you understand why those materials matter. Lectures are very fun as well.

All professors teaching 20D agreed a sheet of note paper would be allowed on test, or provided their own,  Cheng did not allow any. When asked how we should memorize all the derivations, he said don't, just derive them yourself... During tests? If taking 20d, expect to memorize it all. Was usually not prepared for lecture as well.

Cheng's lectures are pretty clear. He can explain concepts clearly. Homework is about 10 or 20 questions from textbook every week, must be hand-written, no code or other online hw. Tests are relatively easy if u understand the homework.

He is very clear about the materials and he gets no accent. There are only two midterms and one final, so no pop quiz or any other quizzes in any kind. He does not use slides, only the blackboard. attendance is not mandatory but I do recommend to attend the class; it is helpful! he is really nice and reachable after class through office hours.

He talks really fast and sometimes it seems as if he hasn't planned his whole lecture out but it works out ok in the end. Really nice guy and can be funny at times but his lectures are boring and I found it hard to stay awake. You can avoid lecture and learn out of the book like I did
Tests can be difficult, but you have to study and practice (as with any math class). Would recommend going to lecture. I personally didn't, so I had to spend a bit more time to get an A in the class.

His courses are really funny. He explains everything pretty clear.  Though his homework's really basic and easy(even the extra HW he provides), tests are really really tough. You may need extra exercise to pass the tests.  But the tests are curved. So if you think you can beat the curve, definitely take his course!

Good lecturer, material isn't too hard. Only annoying part is that the problems he does in lecture are much easier compared to the homework and the tests. Tests are hard. 4 FRQs on the midterms so they're each worth a lot. Either really easy to do or impossible. Study the homework but thats all you can do. 30 percent get As, 30 Bs, and 30 Cs, etc
tests are hard but all you have to do is beat the curve. a very helpfulgenuine prof

He knows the material, gives homework that'll help you understand the material, but when it comes to the midterms and final it is 10X harder than what he is teaching you. Would never want him as a teacher.

You must attend lecture and take notes. His exams are pretty difficult, but if you do your homework and go over it with him in office hours then they are completely doable. No cheat sheet and homework was graded a bit harsher than necessary but overall a great professor who made sure you understood the concepts and was very available

Cheng is a terrible lecturer. He messes up on almost all in class examples, and his in class examples are always conceptual and have virtually nothing to do with the homework or tests. His midterms are ridiculously hard, averages were in the 50s on both. They are nothing like the homework, which is graded harshly as well. Don't take this professor!

I believe that he is the same professor that used to teach at UCI. He now teaches lower div math at UCSD. He is harder than other professors as he doesn't allow the usage of cheatsheets. As a result though, I actually learned all the materials. Attend class. It will help you a lot.

The tests are exactly the homework questions; this class will require intense and rote memorization just because of that.  Answers to the homework questions are given during discussion, so make sure to attend those. Lectures can be a bit dry, but he will bring guest lecturers towards the end of the semester and I found those to be more fun lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He def knows his stuff, but lecture's a bit monotonous and not very stimulating. Your grade is hw, 2 midterms, and 1 final. Exams only have questions off of the hw, so it's an easy A if you're good at memorizing. He never had OH, and some students got an F on the final for no reason and he was MIA when they emailed him. Apathetic but knowledgeable

If you try to ask the professor any questions, he gets annoyed and turns you away. The entire class is focused on a specific set of findings in fly genetics from his own lab, which is irrelevant and useless for anything in your life (unless you work in his lab). the material is a complete waste of time, you wont learn any developmental neuro.

Awful class , awful professor, awful TA's.  It is all mundane memorization, and unless you have psychic abilities, even if you are correct but do not word it exactly how it is on their answer key you lose a lot of points. Worst of all, the prof doesnt care about you, the class, or the TA's.  His lectures are scattered everywhere and hard to follow.

no podcasts, and no office hours. good luck trying to ask him a question beforeafter class. If you enjoy memorizing thousands of names of genes and proteins, and not learning a single concept, take this class. To be blunt, the material you memorize in this class is  completely useless, unless your becoming a fly biologist.

One of the best professors I've had. Explains everything extremely well and the class was the easiest I've taken. Short answer questions pulled directly from lectures (no book reqd.) and TAs grade very leniently. TOTALLY RECOMMEND HIM!

LOVE LOVE LOVE this professor. His enthusiasm for the course material makes everything interesting.Granted, this class would be a lot easier with some background in neurobiology, but I was still able to understand everything and do well.The professor's jokes and sense of humor are like my dads'...

He is funny and gives you all the details you need to ace the midterms. Lecture-based until the final. Very easy midterms. The final is based on the book and was very hard, based on concepts in the book not on lecture. I recommend him

he is a great professor, idk why he doesnt have better reviews, hes really funny. His exams are all lecture based so we dont need a book which was nice and if you go to lecture and take notes  youll be fine, i had minimal time to study for this class since i was taking mam phys and molecular and i still pulled off an A. take him!! hes great!!

I have to say he tries way to hard. At first he was somewhat funny with the jokes, then it got old after 1 week of the same crap over and over again. He tries WAYYY to hard to be funny and interesting which makes it ridiculous. Midterms were quite easy but final consist of a lot of random information that didn't connect. He's hard to listen to

He is clearly interested in teaching, but his lectures aren't presented in a logical manner and you often have no idea what will be on the tests.  Go to the review sessions - they will teach you way more than lectures.

Professor Bier's lectures are ridiculously hard to pay attention to, even when he threatens to dance on his tables if nobody answers his questions--which is often, seeing as answering questions is difficult when the material isn't well-explained. The work here is the hardest I've ever done for a lower-div class.

The TAs graded our tests absolutely RIDICULOUSLY!! I clearly wrote the correct answers, yet they put 0 points out of 10 & sheisty stuff like that... Then, I go & ask him to review my midterm & he tells me to only pick 3 questions for review that the TAs effed-up on. Hardest work I've ever done for a class which doesn't even count towards bio major.

Really cool class.  Tests are fair but can be trricky.  Go to section and try to get Keith or Sue as your TA.  Their the best TAs at UCSD.  Have them for section and atend lecture and you're 100% sure to get an A in the class.

This class is purely lecture based...Don't buy the book. As long as you take good notes and attend discussion sections, this class will be a breeze. The tests are short answer/essay but they are really easy and the TAs grade leniently. The prof is really cool and the subject matter is interesting. Recommended!
Pretty easy class. He is really nice and funny. Attendence not that important, just study the study guides.

First, this prof is not hot. Second, test are not multiple choice and hard. However, they do reflect the material cover in lectures. You will need to know the material well for the test. The subject/course is extremely hard and challenging. Study flies and frogs embryo & neurology development, which doesn't spark my interest. AS note are helpful.
he is really hot
god he's hot. and teaches a lot of useful things. should take him when possible. nobody has enlightened me so much about evolution/development and various model organisms ever before.

My friend told me this is supposed to be an easy A biology class. Maybe it was back then, but it is not anymore. TA's are very anal about giving out points on tests, they will mark you down for stupid reasons. The mean is high compared to other classes. It is not because it is easy, but probably because people have old exams.
pretty good prof. clear and concise. take him if you can
hes not a good lecturer. says he cares about students, but he actually doesnt. ask if students have qtns, then snaps back at them. hes horrible. if you want to learn bout nothing, then take his class
Don't take it if you can't take good lecture notes since there's no book to back up his words. He was only available immediately after class, sucks for people with tight schedule.

(RATING FOR CAT124) - Great professor, however the grading scale for this class specfically is based on a cumulative grade from other people in sixth college that help him teach the class, and they are immensely unqualified and the feedback on projects is very vague and changes day to day. Hope that he picks better support staff in the future.

CAT90 is an Experiential Learning seminar for Sixth GEs. The class was way more helpful than I thought would be and totally set me on a good path for finding internships/careers using the experiences I've had in college. Professor was super nice and friendly, we started every class talking about personal wins we had each week! I def recommend!

Professor Geibel is one of the best CAT125 professors out there! He cares deeply for his students and is always engaging during the class. Keep up with the weekly readings before class to get ready for discussion. Would highly recommend him for this class.

Professor Geibel is a solid choice as a professor and gives a well-outlined agenda on what is required from us. The lecture was laid back and he was more than happy to answer questions about the material. The only downside was it was a communication class so a lot of the meetings felt unnecessary and skippable. Mandatory SI participation for 10%.

She is the best professor I have ever had. Very nice and sweet. There are weekly journals that takes time to do every week. Gradings are very fair and you can get an easy A if you follow the instructions . I loved this class and gained very good experience at my site.

My favorite professor. The content of lectures is interesting, assignments are relatively easy, clear grading criteria, and she is very understanding. She provides extra credit opportunities and is easy to access outside of class. Passionate about what she teaches & an incredible person. I have taken 3 of her classes and I highly recommend her.
So sincerely sweet and wants you to come to her for help. Easy grader and passionate about topic.

She is my FAVORITE professor at UCSD. I had no idea professor's could be so nice until I entered here class. She truly cares for students and wants all of us to suceed. I looked foward to going to class everyday and she presented the material in such an engaging way. I will never forget her kindness and encouragment that she gave all quarter.

Dr. Bintliff is amazing and I highly, highly recommend her! Her class is set up for you to succeed and if anything happens to come up for you, she is incredibly accommodating. She brings a lot of interesting experiences to the table, her lectures are engaging, the assignments aren't too difficult, and she makes an effort to get to know her students

Dr. Bintliff taught an interesting and informative class on adolescent development through Zoom. I learned so much and had fun doing so. Her lectures are recorded but she prefers students to join live. The midterm and the weekly short quizzes were not difficult and very straightforward. Assignments were easy to complete. Great professor!

Dr. Bintliff is extremely caring, helpful, and an overall gem. The course is usually co-enrolled with EDS 139, which is the practicum portion. The practicum is the only tough part as you must complete 40 hours; however, she gives plenty of opportunities and ways you can fulfill these hours. There will only be 2 projects, and your practicum hours.

Dr. Bintliff is super accommodating and tries to build genuine relationships with her student. Due to Covid-19, we were not able to participate in person mentoring and tutoring. She tried to make sure that we had alternative options to fulfill our practicum requirement and be involved with our sites. She invited professionals to talk in class.
If you do the assignments, you'll pass this class with an A. Classroom attendance is basically mandatory but there are no exams. All in all, an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took this as a GE completely uninterested in music hoping this would be one of those classes where you're like "wow, that was pretty cool." But, unfortunately it wasn't. He does his lectures by reading off a Word document and playing some music when relevant. Super easy class, but just dull to me. If you're interested in music, you might like it.

Kyle Adam Blaire is an angel on earth. He genuinely loves music and is so entertaining and engaging. There are no midterms, just 2 performance attendances and write ups on how they make you feel. Lecture attendance is required but you get 2 free passes (same for dis).  Final is online, open all week, open note, take home. TAKE HIM IF YOU CAN!!!

Hes a very kind and nice professor. If you did something wrong or missed assignments, he will be very patient and give you another chance let you get full credits. His lectures are very amazing and easy to understand even for 0 basic students. You might take some time for hw but it's unlimited trials. Exams and final project are not hard. Pick him!

Blair's class was amazingly simple and complex at the same time. Teaching introductory music theory in a way that although myself am a musician, still found learning opportunity, which was refreshing. Great lectures and engaging material, highly recommend.

I've been playing an instrument for almost 5 years now but professor Blair explained music theory better than I've ever understood. The class was fun, and attendance was only mandatory to encourage participation. Easy HW on an interactive platform called Artusi, very comprehensive. Online, open book midterm and final, would recommend as a GE

Bliss is a good and fun professor and her class is very helpful for basic fundamental understand of finance concepts. Classes are long and filled with most just concepts and examples through excel but I thought it was very helpful as the examples and homework were exactly what was reflected on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Bliss is a great professor. The class itself is really hard but she breaks it down for you and she is really good at teaching. I am not done with this quarter yet, but you can tell she wants you to pass the class. She has curved both midterms and dropped the lowest HW score. Definitely take her class!!!

Professor Bliss is clearly brilliant and dedicated to her craft. However, I had her for a three-hour lecture weekly, and never in my life has a class been so boring. It was literally only excel examples again and again and again. It almost seems more difficult to be this boring instead of trying to make it interesting.

Chill and straightforward professor. Homeworks can be long, but as long as you do them, it's an easy 25% of your grade. Midterm and final are open note/book. They can still be kinda hard tho, so make sure u understand the hw problems. There's also a group case, but it's graded more on completion rather than accuracy. Ez class if u put the time in.

For MGT 180! Nice professor, just lectures extremely fast as its one class a week for 2 hours and 50 minutes. TAs are very accessible. HW is Pearson and you can for sure get 100% on it every time because it lets you redo questions. One midterm, One final, and they are open note so if you understand the material and have good notes you will be good.

Prof.Bliss is a great teacher who you can tell knows the material well. She's very friendly and easy to talk to if you need help. Test heavy class. Study hard for the tests+the curve and you should be fine.

Really interesting class. The Professor teaches the material very well. Two midterms and one final, worth 30% each and non cumulative. The material in the tests are all covered during class. Highly suggest taking this class

The course content itself is not hard, BUT!!! The final was unexpected and its difficulty was not reflective of the homework and practices. If you want to get an A in this class, be sure to prepare thoroughly...

She piled up the knowledge which made me feel overwhelmed. This class is fast-paced so you need to get ready to be 100% focused on her lecture, never get distracted, or you will find it hard to follow. Midterm 2 did not reflect 100% of what you learned. She will make slight changes to the problems which makes it more tricky and difficult.
Amazing professor, really engaging lectures, and great personality. She wants you to succeed and will work with you to get there.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Bliss is very caring towards students and helping everybody understand the material. Although it was online, she would always answer any questions on the material and go over it as many times as needed if you didn't understand. Review sessions before exams were EXTREMELY helpful. Dont be afraid to ask for help if you dont understand the topics
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bliss is really caring about her students and will if needed. Given the course material, I feel like it is relatively difficult but she does do her best to explain concepts and offer extra help when needed. I highly recommend taking advantage of review sessions for exams. Lectures are really important to understand the material!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I feel that the tests were not representative of the material learned in class. Also, she would go through the material really fast and often focus on things that did not actually matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Bliss is super considerate and caring. I took the class asynchronously outside of the U.S. due to COVID-19, and I missed the midterm because I incorrectly calculate the time lag. Prof. Bliss sent me an email asking whether I had problems with taking the midterm and reopened the midterm assignment window for me. She is really nice, go for her!
i did not enjoy
not good!

Very inexperienced professor who is trying his best in the first couple of terms teaching. Pays very close attention to research and advice from other professors to become better which is very encouraging. Sets very ambiguous questions on exams, and in class he can't really gauge what the class doesn't understand and how to explain. Fairly nervous.

Professor Blanco is a nice man, but something that didn't sit right w/ me was that he brought his wife in to speak, disguised as a guest, and she went on to make anti-semitic and racist comments in general about a variety of cultures in defense of her cause. She set a bad example and he was quiet. He's also disorganized & that made it hard to plan.

(LTEN 28) The section was mandatory but the lecture was encouraged. Had quizzes during the lecture only open for 5-10 minutes tops. Lots of reading. The lecture was just he talking most of the time (post slides on canvas but don't think he recorded lectures). The grading is split into 4 main things (quiz, section, midterm, and final paper).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Nice but unorganized. His lectures and essay prompts are long-winded and unclear. Being open-ended and being vague are two different things; he was the latter. What the syllabus says is arbitrary. We were assigned a "group writing assignment" a few days before it was due; don't think he knows that coordinating writing for EIGHT people is difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Blanco is one of the most caring professors I've ever had at UCSD and he truly cares about his students. He opens up dialogues in class and even asked the class what we would like to do with the percentage points from our canceled final. Attendance for lectures wasn't mandatory but there were clickers so best to attend! Not a hard grader.
Good class. Great professor. Helpful during office hours. Read the texts, pay attention during class, and you will learn useful information you won't find from other professors.

Professor Blanco is always smiling. He's a very approachable guy and he's really nice. he cares about the students and he's very generous in his grading. Try to participate and pay attention in the class discussions and lecture and you'll get the most out of it. Reading wasn't that necessary to read, if it's too much just skim it or read a summary

Reviews are spot on. The syllabus doesn't matter. I entered the course thinking I would learn about Filipino literature when actuality the majority of the time he spent talking about the history. Reading is also too excessive for a four unit course. Would not recommend if you expect a light course load.

Nice guy. Great ideas. Not that great of a teacher. Most of the criticisms on this page are spot on. This is more like a Hist class than a Lit class. Syllabus means nothing as he adds (without subtracting) on a whim. In my estimation, too much work for a 4 unit class.

He's very passionate about his work, and displays a real willingness to help students learn.  He encouraged us to participate in campus protests during an important time in UCSD's history, and put aside time to discuss current events  and facilitate discussions.   Although he doesn't always stay on topic, he is a good teacher.

Highly invested in his students' education and wellbeing.  Tough but helpful grader - CONTACT him and show him drafts of paragraphs/essays; he will respond with constructive advice.  In lectures, often uses students' questions as a launch point for his read of the text.  Teaches on themes more so than on the readings themselves.

Wonderful professor! Very nice and intelligent. Helpful in office hours. Hard grader but learned a LOT about writing a good paper. His class is a moderate workload but it definitely challenged me to push myself to work hard. Listen to class discussion and presentations--it will help with the papers. I recommend bringing a laptop to take notes on.

He has all the information, he just doesn't present it very well. Lectures, class structure and syllabus were very unorganized. The class was suppose to be on literature, but most of the class was spent on talking about history. He needs to work on his organization and public speaking skills.
No Comments
Professor knows what he is talking about but is super boring and he stutters! He tends to ramble on random tangents that make you wonder why you came to class that day but he is really nice.
Very very unclear and scatterbrained.  His lectures are the worst I've had at UCSD.  Also, you will read a lot!!  Not recommended.
No Comments

Really friendly and approachable prof.  He's a bit scatter-brained with the structure of the class (revised the syllabus like 3 times).  Sometimes it was hard to keep up with the class because there were a lot of readings or he doesn't keep class on time.
The readings and post colonial theory are hot now a days, but not as hot as the prof.  grrrrr.

Professor Bloodgood is the kindest professor I've had at UCSD. You can tell just by listening to her lectures that she is very passionate about the subject. While physiology is relatively dense she gives out a lot of extra credit points in the form of clicker questions. If you put in the effort and go to class you should be able to do well.

she is awesome, caring and supoportive, weekly quizzes with tricky questions, for the final make sure to really understand the material bc is hard but she did an amazing job making this difficult class as better as possible. She gave us like 10% of final grade in extra credits

I really loved Dr. Bloodgood for BIPN 100! There was definitely a ton of content, but she made it super relevant and interesting in her lectures, and gave a ton of opportunities during lecture to ask (lots!) of questions. Dr. Bloodvood gave a ton of extra credit, something like ~10%. Overall an amazing professor and super super kind.

weekly post-lecture quizzes were a bummer in the beginning but helped so much when it came to the final. amazing lectures that are so easy to get immersed in + almost every lecture has clicker questions that count as extra credit. i absolutely adore dr. bloodgood as professor and a person!

Dr. Bloodgood is very caring and generous towards her students. Her lecture content is heavy, but she explains it well and makes it understandable. She has SO much extra credit through clicker points per lecture, extra credit assignment, and CAPES. She has weekly quizzes that are async, open book and you get to drop one. Definitely recommend her!

I truly dont' understand as to why Doctor Bloodgood got bad reviews, students get pressed when they have a professor that actually wants you to learn and doesn't make it easy to cheat. Were the weekly quizzes tricky? yes. But she gave every opportunity to really apply what you learned in class to the assignments. Best professor ever and so caring!

I was doing really well until some1 cheated in our class using Chegg and ever since then the quizzes were much harder that averages were a D. She is a really nice prof but I still think it was unfair for her to punish the whole class. Also it was near impossible to get an A with her grading scale + quizzes. EC barely saved me from not failing.

Even though she is a nice Professor but this class sucks the soul out of me. I was so depressed this quarter, literally cry after taking the quizzes. When you study hard and are confident with your answers, the results are the opposite. Take another Professor if possible to protect your GPA. 92 % is A meanwhile average for the final is ~72 %.

If you're looking at other ratings, know that the the people that gave her bad reviews are rightfully mad, and the people that gave her good ratings got their A/grade they wanted. This class is hard, lectures are long/boring, tests are application questions that aren't taught, and the professor made some unnecessary changes. Be careful taking her.

This professor is the GOAT with a capital G. People had problems with the harsh measures she took as a result of someone cheating but she really cares for her students as the class is relatively stress-free with the sheer amount of extra credit and she is very VERY knowledgeable about the subject and makes an OMEGA DENSE subject somewhat fun.

This class is great for those who wish to enter the medical field and great for those who plan on entering fields with research where memorization is not key. She gives very detailed lectures which can easily be managed with proper study habits. Her quizzes are based upon the lectures as well as application of material rather than memorization.

Everyone who is complaining about these quizzes is expecting to get handed all the answers.  The whole point is to LEARN the material she is giving you.  All of her quizzes have been representative of the material and are asked in a way that forces you to really understand and not just memorize - the whole point of school.
JUST BAD LUCK! GOOD LUCK Y'ALL! LECTURE IS HEAVY AND BORING! quizzes will kill your mind.. very disappointing!

SHE is a good professor, however, grading criteria sucks! Her lectures are long and is so dense that will bored you easily. Hate her quizzes they need to be worked on better. Many of her students have been struggling and have suffered mentally because of her quizzes. To get an A is 95, like seriously?! just don't even bother to look at her name!

Her lectures are so dense they go in one ear and out the other. Each recorded lecture probably takes a few days to get thru. Most of your grade is based on tests and quizzes, so you have to learn to problem solve, not memorize the material. The worst part is that she does not really teach how to problem solve or apply the material in lecture. avoid

Its been an interesting quarter to say the least. People are really upset with her because she changed the level of difficulty of exams after a student cheated, and now our averages are extremely low. But shes not a bad professor. She teaches well. its jus inadequate to prepare us for her application based exam questions. I both love & hate her.

92A ,how the "food"do you expect us to get an A in this class when quizzes hurt your grade not to mention they aren't related to what she lectures and what we study. She is AMAZING but she should think of her students like what changes should she make to make her students successful. PERIOD! just avoid her y'all not even a joke. I'M Just tired!!

You a premed? Then welcome to this comment because I can tell you AVIOD HER! a quiz is dropped since there's weekly quizzes, but why do questions that harm your grade? makes no sense! why study if they aren't related to what you study. don't even bother. TA's really?! they do advocate for you but do they try their best to make changes possible?

Very DISAPPOINTING without a doubt! She a great professor, however, her grading is not helpful! more than half of the class grades are suffering due to weekly quizzes because they aren't related to what you study. WHY can she do MC and Open-ended question to have partial credit! " it takes too long to grade!" AVIOD HER! use P/NP instead.. Good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She doesnt cover the material she exams you on. She has weekly quizzes and a cumulative final exam. No homework, but section is mandatory. Offers some EC, but not enough to make up for her unreasonable qs on exams. No curve in the class whatsoever. Her exam questions are worth so much that losing even a few would bring ur grade down significantly

She teaches one thing and then exams you on a different thing. Her exam questions are impossible to answer bc theyre super specific and all application based, even though she doesnt teach any of them sufficiently and does not practice application based questions with us. Avg grades in a class with 300 students are usually 50-60%. Do P/NP if u can.

Her exams are simply ridiculous. Her own TAs admit that and a lot of times they cannot even answer her exam questions correctly. She designs her exams in a way that students fail them and she admits it. She is knowledgable like everyone else has said, but she expects you to know unnecessary details and her lectures are so dense and long its awful

KEEP IN MIND: bad reviews written in February 2022 are due to a drastic changes Prof. Bloodgood made to her quiz parameters after someone openly submitted quiz questions to Chegg DURING the quiz. These people are reasonably frustrated BUT she is a gem of a professor through and through. CLEARLY knows her content and is concise. STUDY. ENJOY LECTURE

Pros: nice &knowledgable, explains things well, her class is not based on just big exams, offers extra credit, takes time to answer questions. cons: the exams she has do not reflect class material at all, does not curve no matter how poorly students perform, tough grader, dense lectures. You will learn, but also your grade will suffer & no curve.

In no way she prepares us for her tests. They are all insanely difficult application based questions she never teaches. Class avg is barely a D- at best. All the good reviews are from before she changes the structure of her class. She openly gets upset when people do well on her exams. Your exam scores will never reflect your hard work in her class

Unfortunately both positive and negative reviews are true here. Shes a solid prof, but she changed her exam method mid quarter, went against her syllabus, and caused students to perform poorly on their exams because one student cheated in the class. It was uncool to mess with an entire class bc of 1 person, so I would take someone else if you can

She has extremely unreasonable rules for her exams as of recently. She doesnt care what students think and openly disregards their comments and concerns. She teaches well, but if you are hoping to get an A or a decent score, shes designed her exams in a way that will ruin your GPA, though you can still learn the material fine from her lectures.

One of the best professors at UCSD. Dr. Bloodgood is super nice and kind, and you will find out on the first day of class. She is super patient and would offer intermission (question time) in each lecture. She also explains everything super well and loves discussing other topics during her office hour. All the low-rate comments are not true.

She seems nice, but shes incredibly unfair. She decided to punish an entire class of 300 people just because one student cheated on their exam. Sounds beyond unreasonable. Its crazy to think that she sets up an overwhelming amount of students for failure because one person made a mistake. Id never take her again.

Dr. Bloodgood is one of the best professors I had so far in the UCSD. She is very accessible outside the classroom and runs two office hours per week. I took her class online and she runs her lectures live in zoom and record them for students who can't attend. Instead of midterms, she gave us 8 quizzes and a final exam which I found very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I just wanna say Dr. Bloodgood is absolutely amazing! Took her BIPN 100 online and she made the experience so much fun and I actually look forward to her lectures each week. A lot of work, but definitely doable if you put in the work. Tons of extra credits and the EKG video bonus was hilarious XD

She is a great lecturer - she carefully considers her words as she speaks, is interesting and is quite intelligent. The lowest exam score is dropped. The wording of the final was confusing, but the EC made up for it. She can at times be rather unapproachable and is hard to get to know. Though she is good at it, she doesn't seem to enjoy teaching.

Exams have both multiple choice and written portions. VERY application based; make sure to know pathways and how they are affected. Attendance for lectures is extra credit. Discussion attendance for points. She really wants to prepare you for a future in bio/health! I very much recommend her, but make sure you work hard and keep up w/ the material!

Prof Bloodgood is probably one of the best professors I've had at UCSD. Her lectures are extremely helpful and interesting especially if you plan on going to a health related field. Her exams are not easy and her multiple choices are a bit tricky but she offers almost 5% increase to your grade with extra credit, she also drops one midterm.

Dr.B was hands down the greatest professor I have had as a bio major at UCSD. She exudes so much passion for physiology and neurobiology, which is really reflected in her lectures. The course is dense, but she chooses her words wisely and concisely to convey all the details necessary for understanding the material. Highly recommend her for BIPN100!

lectures can be boring but she podcasts. she is very helpful in office hours. the best thing is that she drops a midterm. extra credit adds up to 5% of the grade, so you can literally get an A with 87%(and 5% EC). just review every single slide. reading the book is a waste of time. probably the best physio prof at UCSD.

Difficult class, but def manageable. Lecture covers tons of info, and prof tries her best to fit it all. Do clicker points. They'll total up to about a letter grade boost overall. Drops a midterm (out of 3) and takes final with all the ec clicker points as an overall grade. Application based questions on tests, NOT MEMORIZATION. Remember that.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Studying/doing the work for MTs is up to the students, so totally understandable if this isn't the style for everyone. Some students want more hw to facilitate understanding/learning, and get problem solving experience. If u take her, attend her lectures for tons of EC (your grade is 2 MT+final) & carefully rewatch all her podcasts to do well on MT
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Brenda Bloodgood is one of the most passionate professors I've ever had! She really cares for her students and she makes her clickers extra credit. This class is not easy for most, but if you put the work in - obtaining an A is definitely not that bad! She gives 3 midterms but you can drop 1!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's really nice and clearly knows physiology, but she makes the class impossible with the so much cramming of info in her slides. Even then her slides are all over the place. If one wants to do well on her exams, one must memorize her slides front and back. She provides a lot of extra credit, but this class felt like a medical school class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She gives you everything you need to succeed in her class, but you have to work for it. Aka you have to study for her exams! Discussions aren't mandatory and she gives extra credit for attending lecture. Her lectures are podcasted and she releases non-graded problem sets so that you can see examples of the way she asks questions. 3 MTs, 2 count

She tries to cram a lot of content into each lecture, leaving a lot of uncertainty in what you actually want to know. Multiple choice was fairly straightforward, but the free response was often vague to the point where you don't really know the answer she is looking for. Exam "curving" and extra credit clickers saved my grade.

The information she gives in lecture isn't enough to do well in the class, and it was hard to tell what topics she wanted us to learn more about on our own. Textbook isn't required, but helps elaborate on things she can't cover completely in lecture. She was an ok professor, but there was too much uncertainty about what and how to study.

She is very nice and seems caring, but her tests are very hard. Yes, you do have to memorize everything she says (podcast the lectures and write/know EVERYTHING down), but you have to apply this knowledge on tests. Her final was the hardest final I've had. All clickers are EC, 3 midterms (1 dropped), and a final. Tests are 1/2 MC and 1/2 written.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: lectures had a lot of info and tests cover a lot of info but lots of opportunities for extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This is the hardest biology class I've taken at UCSD. Professor is really nice and helpful, but her exams are intense. Clicker points are EC, but only for correct answers. Exam scores are normalized according to top 5 scores. I felt like I was too stupid to understand the material, and I regret not dropping. Pretty sure I failed the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Amazing human being, and she really makes you learn whether u like it or not through her critical thinking class! u really have to know and apply what you learned on the midterms and final. Also an amazing lecturer but her class is really hard. Finally she is hot!!

This professor was literally my favorite at UCSD. She knows her class is hard and tries to take the stress off. Her exams are very detailed, be prepared to memorize a lot, but don't think you won't have to think on the exam. In all if you work hard she is the best, totally possible to get an A+. She is also really friendly and helpful.

Very kind and caring professor. All the info you need is in her ppts. Awkward jokes here and there lol. MC weights too high for me though (5 points per and is 70% of the test). But either way, she offers so much extra credit + a curve to the individual test! Even drops lowest one. Your loss if you don't take! If only she taugt bipn 102 too :(

What a lovely lady. Honestly the best professor I've had in college. She offers so many extra credit opportunities. Her lecture style is clear and concise. Very approachable person. Does her best in every single way to help students succeed. She leads and guides students through every little step of physiology to make sure everyone gets it.

I loved learning from her, as she really cares about the class and wants students to learn. However, I found that she goes way too fast for me to pick up the material. Tests are really in-depth and usually include a question about disease/medicine. Clicker points really do help your grade, but if you don't study you'll find it hard to pass.

Dr. Bloodgood is a REALLY good professor and you will not be disappointed if you take her. Makes you think, but she drops subtle hints in lecture and guides you on what to study for the exam. "I encourage you to think about how __ " is her way of saying "it is going to be on the exam." Her office hours are valuable, she offers like 60 EC clickers.

BEST professor I've taken - cares more about you than making you work for a grade. 4 midterms (final counts as a midterm & is NOT cumulative) and you can drop one, meaning you don't have to go to the final if you do well enough. Lectures are packed with info but podcastable; however GO TO CLASS - clicker questions are EC (5 correct CQ  1 WHOLE %)

The exams make you think critically and never test you on simple facts. You have to use your knowledge to answer topics that weren't discussed in class. The extra credit clicker points boost you about half a grade. Lectures go very fast so listening to podcasts is a must.  There are 4 exams (1 dropped) and NO cumulative final. Never used book.

Nice person but she does not know how to teach! Lot of info, in depth tests, she goes super fast. I listened to podcasts, pausing and writing word for word what she says during lecture. When I went back to read the sentences, they wouldn't make sense because her sentences are incomplete and vague. Be prepared to self teach yourself using the book.
Lots of extra credit through clickers, never even needed to read the book. Study and show up to class and you should get an easy A. Her office hours are really helpful too.

I loved this class! Dr. Bloodgood is a great professor. Her lectures go by really quick but she podcasts. She is very clear and organized. Her slides are very helpful. I didn't have to read the textbook at all. There were 3 midterms (1 dropped) and a final. The exams are tough but the curves are generous and the extra credit clickers really help.

If you didn't know anything about physiology in the first place, this class is for you. If you are a "hard facts" kind of person, run the other direction. This class was interesting, but she teaches it off of her own understanding, which unfortunately is not very well-rounded when it comes to some of the topics.

Professor Bloodgood was fantastic! Her lectures were organized and sprinkled with interesting facts. She's very passionate about physiology and helping her students. Showing up for class helps because she gives extra credit points with iClickers (it's accuracy based). She's one of the best professors I have had at UCSD.

Loved Dr. Bloodgood, she's extremely organized and clear and is obviously very passionate about her work in both teaching and research, her office hours are very helpful though not plentiful so try not to miss any, the class is tough unless you put work in so be prepared to study, if you do its an easy A with all the clicker EC points

Her tests make you think. Get ready for lots of information thrown at your face. I definitely put a lot of time and effort into this class. I also learned a great deal from this class because her exams really forces you to think critically about the subject rather than memorization. Wonderful class and professor. The extra credit and curve saved me
she's very organized and clear, her tests are difficult but fair and she gives A LOT of extra credit if you can get her clicker questions right

She expects you to know everything before you even come into class. Her lectures aren't helpful, you learn more from the book. You can't even take notes because she goes so fast. Some of her test questions are ridiculous and not on topic. This class made me less interested in the topic than I was before.

Clicker questions were extra credit and came straight out of the book. Tests are very in depth, and she looks for key words. For those who take it with her as an elective, like I did, unless you are super enthralled by human systems, anatomy and molecular bio I would not recommend this course.

Tends to drone on and repeat things a lot in lectures. She knows her stuff and is published in the subject but just isn't the best at clearly explaining concepts and expectations to students. Graded on reading-heavy (closed note) quizzes and a group project. Not very tech savvy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 6 quizzes overall, 2 were dropped and a lot of readings to do before each lecture. Did not really like her as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: When asked questions about lecture she was not able to provide answers. Rubric on tests in unclear. When asked about test answers and explanations about them she said that its in the reading. Essays were not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Show up to class, pay attention, take notes, and review the readings the day before the quizzes if you want to do well. Professor Blair-Loy is kind and well-respected in her field. She encourages questions and discussion from the class but it seems like my section was a bit on the quiet side. The workload isn't bad and I felt comfortable in class.

Took this class for an easy A. Graded on 2 papers, responses to a group member's paper, 2 discussions in class, 4 weekly quizzes, and a final test. Drop your lowest quiz grade + extra credit. Papers were easy and could be written in 20 minutes, 750 words. Lecture was not important.The quizzes were verbatim of the text book and readings.

She is very sweet, but the work look is awful! Definitely be prepared to READ A LOT no joke.she has weekly memos and in order to finish them you need to read what she give and they are extremely long, I hate those memos! we do group quizzes drops 2 and drops 2 memos. midterm/final are based on readings.I wouldn't take her again Hate those readings
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She grades the papers very harshly. I personally did not like the lectures either.

Prof Blair-Loy is kind and definitely not hard at all. If you pay attention during the lectures and take notes on the slides you will get an easy A. I would most likely not take her again bc she is VERY soft spoken and it can be hard to hear her. Sometimes people ask Q's and her response is just straight up "I dont know" and then moves on.

The course schedule was very manageable. The weekly reading included textbook chapters and articles. There was a lot of writing involved - weekly discussion memos (analyses) and a final essay but nothing extreme. I enjoyed lectures and found the course easy to follow along with remotely.

She really cares for all her students and is always finding ways to improve her lectures (she asks us for our feedback!!) Her assignments are straightforward and pretty easy to get A's on as long as you do the readings. I highly recommend this professor!! You won't regret taking her SOC 118 class :-)

Her material is really interesting and the textbook is a great resource and it can be found for free online. For her online course, there's a short lecture every week and usually a quiz or discussion forum. No midterm but there's a final. Just watch the lectures (which go over the readings) and her quiz is usually based off of it. She's great!

Professional Blair-Loy is unqualified and unprofessional when it comes to teaching gender related topics. She does not fully respond to students' questions and often her answers are inadequate and contradictory. Overall I would not recommend her to anyone!

Second class with Blair-Loy and it was just as chaotic as the first time. Frequently late to class, technical difficulties, and lengthy lectures. Class material is really straightforward & easy, lecturing pretty much from the book. One in class midterm, one final, and participation points for random attendance at 5 points in the quarter.

Professor Blair-Loy is well-established in her field and lectures beautifully but class content can get mixed up very quickly. Asks for participation from students but the class environment isn't quite welcoming for it. Straightforward material, but readings are lengthy. Make sure you know the readings she discusses in class and she refers back.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Blair-Loy is so sweet and so knowledagble in her field. She has done a good amount of research and is well known in her field. The lectures are not very entertaining but you can tell she tries. The lectures are her reading off of slides and elaborating on them. Lots of reading. Make sure to keep up with them because they are on the exams.

Her 1st time teaching in shorter blocks and it shows. She was late or ended class late, and fell behind on lectures. She had to change the midterm to fit the shorter class but most of us still struggled to finish. The reading is interesting and she cares about the subject, but because you're graded on 2 papers I wish she'd give us her rubric first.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: she is very intelligent and has published quite a few papers on the topic. no textbooks just articles, and midterm and final is open book. no papers but there is one group project. very easy class but show up for lectures for future clarity and enlightenment. she is a bit awkward and boring at times but can be very caring and knowledgeable.

Took her class last quarter for sociology of gender and I was one of very few males in class. Her class was an eye opener and has influenced me in many ways. Professor Blair-Loy is very passionate about what she teaches and that makes a great difference. I would take a take a class with her again and would suggest others to do so as well.

Mary Blair-Loy is a great teacher, she is an expert in her field so you will learn a lot. She gives the students the opportunity to talk and express themselves and she always listens and makes participation a part of the class. You will not regret taking this course

Sociology is an interesting topic but the class can be dull at times. The grade can greatly depend on your TA because the midterm and final is an essay that is graded by your TA. Unfortunately for me, I'm not the best at writing essays so I'm getting an average grade. Pick a good TA and you will have a great time.

She was a little confusing but if you keep up with readings and pay attention to sections which are mandatory ( lecture is not) then you'll be fine. Open book and open notes tests. other than the midterm and final all other work depends on your TA. I had Olsen she gave homework every other week

Lectures are most helpful if reading is done prior to class, but they are still easy to follow if you don't read (I didn't until the midterm) Midterm and Final were both open note and open book. Very interesting course and teacher for those interested in Sociology

Section mandatory. Reading important; however I love the topic and went without the book for 7 weeks & I did well. Subject is honest, Blair-Loy wants students to question material and seeks input. Easy to talk to. I thought lecture was awesome, but i love soci. Many students fall asleep in her class, find her boring. 1 midterm, 1 final

She maybe a boring lecturer, but this class was easy and the subject is interesting. The midterm and final was open book and open notes, so it was really easy and the TAs prepare you well for it. Easily got an A. As long as you read you're good, and lecture is not mandatory.

I think Soc is really interesting, but this professor IS SO DULL. How you do on the midterm just depends on the TA you get. It's not a difficult class at all, but I dont understand how this professor inspires anyone to be interested in sociology.
really great professor... sweet, down to earth. you will like her.

Her class is the reason I changed my major to Sociology.  She is a boring during lecture, but section is really helpful.  Go to her office hours and talk to her one on one.  Amazing women and she is extremely helpful.  The reader has really interesting articles.  you will learn ALOT

boring lecture...no need to go to lectures, cuz she puts notes online. Just go to sections and read the book, thats all you need. TA was helpful, mid-terms are openbooked, and my TA was a easy grader. Easy class but you won't learn much.

boring lecture, posts all her powerpoints online, SUPER easy class and a nice GPA boost if you need one.  just do the reading and you're fine.  you dont have to attend lecture but you definitely have to attend discussion section b/c its part of your grade.

VERY VERY VERY BORING CLASS. It's impossible to stay awake in her lecture. Her voice is so calm that it puts everyone into sleep. Also, she's late very often. Lectures are not necessary to go but sections are DEFINITELY MANDATORY!! your section grades count A LOT and DON'T EVER GET BEHIND IN READING!
had a TA who was really into it. graded easily in my opinion. professor was really interesting and pretty funny! one midterm one final

Lectures were pretty boring, you don't really need to go. Keep up with the readings, go to section..you'll get an A. It's not a hard class but definitely not for the lazy. All tests are essay based, most homeworks for me were outlines/papers. Leah was the best TA EVER!

VERY BORING CLASS. We don't even learn about sociology. We learn about sociological theory or research people had conducted. Textbook is non-refundable since the textbook changes every year. And also the class depends on the TA. I don't even think my TA (April Huff) gives ANY student an A on hw assignments. Avoid her at all costs!
lectures were a bit dry but the content was very interesting. Good professor.
Lectures are very dry. Book is hard to read and long. Lots of reading. You better be smart and on top of it or you're screwed.

Bulging eyes that scare me, and brings out the boringness in sociology. I thought sociology was going to be fun, but in this class, it is not about the study of society, but rather the history of society, and other boring studies such as racial discrimination etc.

Prof. Blair-Loy talks in monotone when she lectures, so she's too boring to keep me awake. Midterms and finals are full-length in class essays, and you can bring your notes and textbook. In addition, attendance & participation count toward your grade in section (25%). For those who don't like participating, I won't suggest this class.

readings and lectures were fairly easy and interesting. lectures are podcast as well so attendance can be optional. just make sure you know the terms and keep up with the material going on in class and you'll be good

She is a really fascinating lecturer. My class was at 8am and I never missed it. She has very clear slides and goes into great depth on each reading. She also encourages discussion, which made class really interesting. One of the best professors I've had.

don't even go to her lectures. you will fall asleep. instead, buy as lecture notes and attend sections. dont need to do any reading. bring your a.s lecture notes to exams and use them. you will get an a

class material is interesting, but she is not that enthusiastic about teaching. she comes off as the strict, feminist type. posts all her lectures and podcasts. the lecture slides are basically all you need. section is mandatory and helpful.

The class is great... but Mary fails at teaching. A sociology lecture is supposed to be taught by someone with a strong demeanor-to keep people interested and actively participating. Instead she uses lame examples: "Imagine if Southern Californians were treated differently from Northern Californians" what the hell lady just say black and white
Really easy. Didn't really have to read any of the material, she spoon feeds you EVERYTHING. Instead of a final we had a paper. I wrote the entire thing in one sitting and got an A.

The class itself sucks, I was so interested when I came in, but throughout the whole class I was writing papers and midterms arguing against my own beliefs, and chances are, you will be too, DONT TAKE THIS CLASS, unless your a sociology major.

Good professor. Her lectures can be a bit boring sometimes but she has a sort of dry humor that makes it interesting. I just skimmed through the readings she asked us to do. and i'm ending with a decent grade. Sections are important though, always go to both section and lecture as she will tell you exactly what she wants on papers.

She doesn't make her points clear enough to understand. She will circle the point but will never directly get to it which gets kinda annoying..for me at least. Her class is really boring compared to other sociology classes I've taken because she's not energetic at all. Monotoned and simply no spark in her lectures.

Very clear on what she wants in papers. Its easy to do well as long as you agree with her. I didn't read any of the course readings all the way through and got an A on midterms/final. Don't bother asking a question in class of her if you disagree with something she said.

Came into this class not too excited. Turned out extremely interesting. Blair-Loy is a great professor. Up-to-date data. Guest speakers. Relevant material to current events. Stresses key vocab in essays. Good amount of reading. Discussion section could make/break the class. Katie Kenny is a great TA.
Didn't think she is that good until i take DOC2 and DOC3. Gave good note. Don't fall asleep in class cuz she keep u busy copy down the note.
the way she talks and how much she moves her hands is pretty annoying.  she clarifies the readings though and gave us the midterm question beforehand.

I'd say best of the DOC1 profs. Only read parts of readings to get general ideas for papers, still got an A. Easy lecturing style, a bit boring though. Has everything on transparencies. Midterm and final were very clear. Always write really strong, opinionated, bold papers and you will get an A. Travis is a good/easy TA if you can get his section.
if you keep on top of the readings, class is easy.  blair-loy is boring, and so is the material.   become friends with your TA and you will do well.    late
Boring class (not her fault, the curriculum is just boring).  At least she tells you what's on the midterms/finals.  TA was a hardass.  Hope you get someone easier.

Blair-Loy is a great professor; obviously intelligent and funny.  She moves pretty slowly through lecture, so even if you miss one, you'll be all right.  Lectures do rely on the reading, and she has about 5 random days she chose to do in-class assignments or homework which counts as attendance.
she definitely has a theme to the class, and if you get a good grasp of that, you'll do fine in her class.
She is really interesting, she knows the material well and the class is really well-rounded. There were also several guest speakers which was a nice change of pace. I definitely recommend her.

Nice Prof. You must attend lectures and know how to apply the vocabulary from lectures & readings to your essays. Midterm & Final are short essays and she lets you know which of readings are needed to write your essays. Also has a study guide. Attend lectures & keep up with reading = A+. Highly recommend if you need a low stress class.
Blair-Loy knows her stuff but can be a little boring.  Just know the readings that she talks about the most during lectures and you'll be okay for the midterm.
I could barely stay awake in lectures. She follows her outline really well so it's easy to take notes. Her midterm and final require less effort than the other DOC professors so that was nice.

She looks like she's going to cry.  The lecture is not very interesting, but her notes are pretty helpful. DOC depends on your TA, so buddy up to your TA.  I'm glad that she's not teaching DOC 2 because I would've jumped off OVT the instant I found that out.
Professor was very informed on the material.  Encouraged intelligent discussion and gave well organized and thought out lectures.  Tests were representative of the reading and the lectures.

straight forward lecturer and is organized, follows an outline throughout the lecture. makes things interesting by providing relevant examples. not a good public speaker, says "um" a lot, but if you look past all that, she has solid stuff to say. but again, DOC depends a lot on the TA
umm... any questions? extremely annoying mannerisms and hand gestures. did not answer questions well at all even though she asks us if we have any all the time
very repetitive, but lots of the stuff she repeats ends up on the exams. your grade mainly depends on your TA, though. she's a so-so lecturer. not too boring, but not really interesting either
lectures are useless.  grade depends entirely on ta.  swings arms about as she talks.  doesn't know answers to students questions.

Shes a organized but boring lecturer. You will learn much more from your TAs. In the end, it is your TA, not the professor that will make or break your grade and time in DOC. I would only recommend her because her tests are easy.
Okay Class, But TA's are most important. Sometimes they take roll so you have to go to class. Straight forward, tests rather easy. Easiest of all the doc professors
useless class
she looks like one of the raptors from jurrasic park and swings alot to the left. if you have to take doc im sorry
No Comments

the class wasn't too difficult (the midterm and final were VERY similar!) I guess the difficulty of this class really depends on your TAs expectations! blair-loy always seemed unprepared for class and if you ask her a question she didn't ask you, she will likely never go back to it! otherwise, she explains all material well enough for the course.
Very easy and fun class.  Although sometimes repeatative, she still has a good idea of what she is talking about.
pretty cool class. your grade depends on ur TA so just form a good relationship with your TA
never actually read the required readings, she went over all of the ones in class that would be on the test. YAY
she explained the readings in class most of the time so we never really had to read the stuff. And she's pretty hot...

She's a very flaky teacher if you ask me.  Overall, the class is just really interesting.  Sometimes she seems a little nervous up at front.  It also seems like she isn't really prepared for the class.  But the midterms are pretty straightforward and easy.  It's an interesting class.

This was her 1st time teaching DOC so she seemed a little nervous and completely different than the other DOC teachers. The midterm was more complicated than the other classes, but the subject material is definitely her specialty. Accompanies lectures with overheads, everything self explanatory.

Professor Blakely has a wealth of experience as an auditor. As such, he has many good stories that give you an inside look at what a career in the field might look like. However, as class goes, the (multiple choice) tests are heavily based on textbook material. In order to do well you must have a thorough understanding of the textbook content.

Professor Blakley is a good professor and lecturer and it is obvious that he is extremely knowledgeable about the auditing field. His lectures can get a bit slow at times and not all the slides are important. The exams were actually structured pretty nicely with T/F and MC but they were still very difficult and grades were barely curved at all.

I read the textbook, did before you go on questions, practiced the MC questions and watched Youtube videos before each exam and still did bad. The professor doesn't prepare you for exams and just reads the ppt provided by the textbook. He doesn't go over the hw and you need to learn yourself. I recommend reading the textbook at least twice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Midterm 1 didn't go so well since this was my first accounting class without numerical calculations and I didn't know what to expect. Midterm 2 and the final were a breeze since I knew exactly what to expect and how to study for it. PRO TIP: READ THE TEXTBOOK!! He also gives a lot of extra credit for the CAPE review and the group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: INCREDIBLE PROFESSOR!!! As long as you read the textbook, you will be set for the midterms and final! He gives so much extra credit too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The Exams are nothing like what is learned in class. The exam questions seems like they are from question banks. The really disappointing thing is that he starts his lecture, talks about his experiences for quite a bit, rushes through the lecture slides and says "ok you guys are ready for the exam, good luck". Auditing should be divided into 2 part

Decent professor. You'll have weekly homework but they aren't too hard. Interesting life stories IMO, but he likes to ramble. His lectures are inconsistent and not what is reflected on the test. If you do poorly on the final (like me) he will curve.

idk why people complain that he reads off slides, because he does not at all.. He gives examples of audits. Auditing is not an easy topic to teach and he tries to help us understand with real life stuff.. His exams are based on the textbook so just read the end of chapter summary and do the MC questions. homework isnt hard and also gives paper 10EC

The comments below are completely false. He is the most caring professor I have ever encountered at UCSD. He truly cares about his students, and if you take the time to get to know him you will not regret it. Ya, the class is difficult and the material is kind of dry but that is not his fault. He is an awesome resource! Take his class!

this class is really tough.BUT you still need to pass this gate for the acct minor regardless.my best advice would be to:DO THE MULTIPLE CHOICE Q'S on the end of the txtbook chapters.Cut him some slack auditing is just a hard topic in itself regardless of who's teaching.If possible,try to befriend the ta to get extra tips and help.curved grades too
Read off from the book provided powerpoint. Worst professor. Exams are so hard.
Do not take his class..worst professor
Wow, if there was an award for the worst teacher of the year, he should be nominated. You have to basically study 4000 thousand slides of boredom and the test was way too hard.

I took him for both 131b and 132. His classes are really boring. He basically spends his time reading off of slides that come from the book. Prepare for disaster. He once scheduled an exam and canceled it on the same exam day at exam time. Then gave the makeup exam a week before finals. There are no answer keys given out for midterms.

Midterm and final reasonable, but homework is kinda difficult. However he was always available during office hours and is very patient with you when you ask questions. Class grade determined only by tests and homework though, so that kinda sucked. Overall though great professor, didn't overcomplicate topics!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Probably one of if not the best math professors on campus. He is very caring and makes the material as accessible as possible to everyone. This class felt like a huge break compared to many of my other math courses.
Really good teacher, posts all lecture notes and explains what concepts will or wont be tested. 100% take him if you can
Bo is a very caring and nice guy. Definitely take his class.
Really kind but is not very engaging in lectures. Attendance is not mandatory. Class is fairly easy.
Easy professor. Clear lectures and pretty good lecture notes.

He is the best math prof I ever meet in UCSD. His lecture is very clear and his notes on the blackboard are really helpful. I always go to his office hour, and Bo is very nice and friendly. He likes to answer your questions and give you objective feedback. I would like to take his other classes for sure. BEST PROF IN MATH DEPARTMENT!

I like this professor. His class is not very hard and his lectures explain things well. The only difficulty is that he does not allow any cheatsheet or notecards during the tests. But in terms of MATH 18, I believe it's not difficult to get a good grade even without a notecard since the materials are way easier than other math classes.
He knows his content, but he fails to deliver. His lectures appear unstructured and confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The first midterm is way too easy.
Has an accent, jumps around a lot when explaining problems
A good professor but he was a bit slower than he was suppposed to be. Very nice in office hour. accent is minor.

Although he does not let us use cheet sheet, but his exam is extremely easy, not tricky problems and no hard problems. I don't think he is good at teaching, but he is a very nice person and his exam is easy! He lets you add class

Li Bo is a very nice professor. Many people might find this class tough. But go to the lecture and do all the homework you would be fine since it all about formula and calculation. Don't too worry about your exam score because if you are doing bad so does everyone else. Just be above the average score you would be OK.
I like this BO LI, a Chinese prof with some accent. But it is not hard to get him. And you could feel his caring for students and love for his job. I love him making some strange jokes on the class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: very clear and logical teaching style. Tough tests, but always give great curves.

WARNING: no cheat sheet, no practice test, no mid-term dropped!I realized what he said in lecture was basically what is in the text book so I just stopped going.
