Easiest DEI class. No final group project because of strike. Mandatory discussions. Few easy hw. Midterm is oral and it is pretty straightforward and easy. Definitely an easy A as long as you prepare well for midterm and turn in all hw on time. Lots of people even get A+.

Professor Kang is a gem. He's such a sweet person. He gets emotional easily and even shared some personal stories with us during lectures. You can tell he really cares about the topic. There's a few short writing assignments, weekly assigned readings, and the exams are easy. Discussions are mandatory (you can miss 2 tho) but lecture's aren't.
TAKE TAKE TAKE his class was SO interesting and important for the world rn class set up is so nice just pls don't cheat

Easiest class ever. Professor is so chill. Clicker quizzes on readings that you can easily use intuition on. Oral midterm that did take a decent amount of studying but still very simple. Final is a group video; people turned in garbage and still got perfect scores. Discussion mandatory but all you gotta do is show up. A lot of extra credit too.

Had daily reading quizzes, not hard but had to at least skim for the main ideas Interesting assignments like iimplicit bias test Midterm is oral, wacky but in the end i think it helps you remember the main points Final is group project teaching other students key concepts Not hard as long as you keep up and turn everything in had 2 hr coffee convo!

Awesome professor, took ANSC 148 with him. This was his first time teaching the course and was incredibly open to student feedback. Lectures are interesting and he really cares that you learn the material.

Professor Lim is very transparent about the difficulty level of his class. This course has helped me grow as a researcher more than any course at UCSD. If you attend class, read the papers, and go to OH you can succeed. The first exam was definitely a shock, but if you learn how to take them it'll be ok. It's worth it to grow and be challenged.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Your grades are determined by two midterms and a cumulative final; he advertises the fact that a lot of people fail his class and constantly encourage students to drop the class. For the record here are the stats for his class
Midterm 1: Average (17.1/30)
Midterm 2: Average (20.7/30)
Final: (22.97/40)

He is the type of professor that blames his students rather than take accountability for his own actions.  He showed us how poorly the previous year's class did in trying to scare us to drop.  You really think if the averages for midterms are in the D-F range, it is the student's fault? He does statistics in Neurobiology but can't comprehend this
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Lim spent the 1st lecture saying how everyone fails his class, even showing horrifying statistics. When entire classes are consistently failing, the professor should reconsider their teaching ability, not blame the students for being dumb. Teachers are supposed to inspire, not flaunt how impossible it is for someone to succeed in their course.

Do not take this professor or course. He just wants to do his research and is required to teach. Exams are difficult and the rubric is very strict. Like if you don't put one part the entire question is wrong. No problem sets or guides for exams. Just 40% each midterm and 30% final. No support, lectures are awful, and exams are insane.

Dr. Lim is honestly one of the best professors at UCSD.  He is actually a genius!  BIPN 154 is 90% going over papers from researchers and his lab and telling the class what they found.  The class is super interesting as you learn so much about how the brain is wired.  Tests are actually fairly difficult but if you study, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was the first time BIPN154 has been taught. He is very passionate about it + its his area of research. Large emphasis on experimental design and analysis. Would highly recommend taking BICD110 beforehand to know bio mechanisms better! Generous curve, graded only by midterms + final. You'll learn a lot from him, but you HAVE to study hard!!

Professor Lim is research faculty and only teaches this one class every Spring quarter. His class size is small by choice. He goes through lecture material very fast and it is very dense, but he tries to be specific. He cares about the lecture material and although teaching isn't his focus, he does a good job trying to get feedback from students.
Take her class as letter grade, fat curve in the beginning, fat curve in the end. More than half the class got A's

Okay, so her lectures are about 100 slides per class and she tends to drone on for the entire duration until there is a confusing clicker question, but I found getting an A pretty attainable. Go to lecture(mandatory), discussion(mandatory), take your online quizzes, and READ THE SLIDES ON YOUR OWN. Byrne is not very reliable, but there is hope.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is probably the worst professor at UCSD. She is not clear on what will be on tests. Literally reads off her slides does not elaborate. You literally could do the same in your dorm but she makes attendance mandatory by using iclickers. There were multiple times where all answers on questions were right but A was just a little more right to her
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you have taken Biology in highschool, then this class will be a GPA booster. However, I don't recommend this professor since she only reads her powerpoint slides that essentially sums up the textbook. Attending lectures are unnecessary, but she has iclicker. Her exams are mainly factual recall.

Pretty fair when it comes to grading lab reports, however I wish that her quizzes were easier considering the typos and errors in her keys. Thankfully, her slides are well-detailed enough to understand the labs as the lab manual was not edited very well. Final was a bit tricky as she does like to give some trick questions. Not bad, but not good.

Her slides are clear and organized so be true you know or memorize the stuff on them. Also, listen to your TA's suggestions carefully. They may tell you what would be focused on the tests.

Ruined Bio for me ... This class was supposed to be an easy lower div but this prof made it the worst class I've ever taken in college. Only thing she does in lecture is reading off her ppt (in extremely slow pace). Specifically told us not to read the book and tested us on materials in the book and barely included anything on her lecture slide.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: You'd be better off reading the textbook (which isn't mandatory) or the slides yourself than going to lecture but clicker questions are a part of your grade. Her weekly quizzes are TOO easy compared to her exams. She's very hard to reach outside of class, she'll either respond to your emails too late or not at all. Be prepared to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The worst professor I've had in college. Talks incredibly slowly and only reads off her powerpoint. When she doesn't know what she's talking about she will mumble and trail off. It would be faster to stay home and look at the slides yourself but clicker participation is necessary and based off of questions that she doesn't teach in class.

Dr. Byrne showed no enthusiasm towards the course and was only present to read her PowerPoint. She struggled to give clear answers to her own Iclicker questions, and lacked a clear grading scale. Her exams tested on content she did not instruct/ expand on and would test content she instructed not to study. She did have weekly quizzes that were rela
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Sarah is simply wonderful. Not only is she fun and sweet, she is an exceptional writer and teacher, and taking a class from her will undoubtedly make you a better writer.

It's a treat to learn writing from Sarah Bynum, a passionate and profound writer. Her teaching style nurtures both structured and subversive writing styles, which helped me discover my "voice" in a natural way.

best teacher in the ucsd writing dept hands down!! she is so adorable and really cares about her students. class is easy and fun. she makes you want to be a better writer. you're lucky if you get the chance to take her

Bynum was fun, in every sense of the word.  The assignments were good, the reading fun, the writing fun ,and the lectures fun.  You can tell she's honestly passionate about her field, and it rubs off on her students.  Loved her mannerisms, too!

She's one of the best professors i've had. She's really interested and involved with her students, and yes, while she does have work, it's fairly easy, and as long as you do it (it's just papers, 2-3 pages each of fiction! come on you writers!) you'll get an A.
Bynum really cares about her students and it is obvious.  I think she required more work than the other writing teachers I have had, but it definately expands your writing ability.

She is the first writing professor I have had at UCSD that makes a genuine attempt to teach writing! Really cares about students, gets to know the entire lecture on first name basis, and delivers an awesome class.

She is a great professor, really cares about her students and has an honest and invigorating love for writing. She is so supportive of everyone's work, is welcoming to new ideas, and just has just a passion for the written word. Definitely recommend her.
Flipped Classroom teaching style. I loved the class, I learned a lot. Participating helped me be engaged in class. She curves heavy. My fav MGT professor.
Not as bad as people make her out to be. She does play favorites a bit, but I genuinely learnt a lot from her class and enjoyed her course format.

class isn't necessarily difficult and the quizzes/essays aren't hard either., just pay attention to the terms that are on the slides

only complaint is that participation is weighted heavily but your chances of being called on in class are near 0 if you're not one of 3 people that raises their hand for every question

Amazing lectures and interesting topic, participation is graded, but fun due to the small size class. I do say there are 6 quizzes and 5 in class essays on lockdown and some in class assignments. There is a debate but super chill you just need to speak for like 2 minutes. midterm and final. Overall grading scale is based on class average at the end

This class was unnecessarily difficult for what it's about. The concepts themselves aren't that hard, and she is a knowledgeable professor, but between the weekly quizzes, the in-class essays, the debate, and the exams... It's a lot. The essays suck and are harshly graded. You'd better memorize EVERY definition, or else you'll get screwed over.

One time, after a quiz, I had to leave right after. She stopped me and said, "Thanks for dropping by," very passively aggressive. Like, wow, I'm sorry I have other things going on in my life other than your class. Tough grader. She makes her midterm difficult for no reason, and her essays? Very difficult to please her with my answers.

When I read the negative reviews I thought it would be your avg mgt prof that was pretty cool all things considered. Her flipped classroom approach makes her lectures extremely boring, you do not learn anything new but she forces you to be there cause of in class work. TOUGH GRADER, essays are 30 min in class and you have to be very precise hate it

She gives out a fairly heavy workload before each class that you have to do if you wanna understand the context of what she lectures. She makes you do one debate in front of the class and has weekly quizzes. She's a good lecturer but for such an easy class, she gives out too much of a workload. Honestly, don't take if you don't have to.

Honestly the reviews are too scary for no reason, she's tough and participation is required toward grade but she is mostly reasonable. A lot of busy work but helps cushion your grade, got a B but with curve got an A. Definitely has class favorites but just show up and listen, you will do well.

Honestly, I don't understand the bad reviews. Sure, she does not allow devices in class, but it's really not that big of a deal since the material/ lecture slides do not require you to write a lot of information down. It is just important that you understand the main concepts. The professor is very nice and if you go to class, you will do well.

This professor isn't particularly engaging and is clearly biased to one point of view. The topics she teaches in this class is genuinely benign as it feels that she ignores a significant amount of information that contradicts many of her points. This class is very much a lot of busy work with little substance, just like her lectures. Don't take.

The professor is actually very nice and the TA does not grade hard. The ratings scared be but they were overreacting. Just follow the lecture, read the powerpoint ahead from class and you should do good. The rubrics was clear and quizzes are weekly but all from the lecture. I got 99% before the curve, and the only hard thing is the many homeworks!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I know the other ratings are scary, but this class is so easy. Very easy concepts, just a lot of outside work since she has a flipped classroom approach. But the class is curved its really hard to get a bad grade, plus she has changed essays to in person so they're super easy and take 20 minutes. the only annoying part are the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: A lot of easy work, but if you do it, you'll get an A. Quizzes, essays, and exams are all easy if you have done the work. Lectures are interesting and the class is engaging. The most we had to read was about 10 pages. Honestly, the low reviews are from students who didn't want to put in the effort.

This class could literally be summed up in a week or two, its pretty useless. Prof. is cold and treats students like children. She messed up my test multiple times and tries to trick you on her test questions. She also treats the TA poorly.

One of those teachers who loves to make a simple and straightforward class way more complicated than it should be. She assigns a ton of busy work, there's a quiz and assignment every week. She also treats the students like we are in elementary school. As long as you raise your hand and say some bs and do the pre class materials you'll get an A.

Was told the final would be like the quiz and midterm, but shocker it was not. For the midterm and final she introduces new words to trick you. The final was long question scenarios you had to match the term to, it was confusing. Back-to-back quizzes in class, in-class essay, you have to participate or your grade will drop if not.
Ridiculously outdated teaching style in 2025. Plus, I every class had an hour of lecture, we were expected to have watched videos and read almost double that by the time we got to class.

Good luck being able to focus on any other classes than this one if you have any less than spectacular stamina. This class has a quiz or an essay due every single time it meets (twice a week.) For every quiz, you must bring your own scantrons, and the quizzes are primarily on the readings and "Pre-class lectures," not anything gone over in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is the most unnecessarily challenging management class I've taken. Two quizzes a week requiring scantons, pre-recorded lectures to watch before class, in-person essays, mandatory debates, a no-technology policy (everything handwritten), and lectures that always run late. If it's not a major requirement, avoid this class at all costs.

I understand why she gets low ratings. Quizzes are not easy. But, I honestly learned a lot from this class and don't regret putting in the effort. The grades are curved and most students got a B or higher. She also offers extra credits.

READ THIS:I was terrified of her because of these reviews than realized that most of the people who write these probably dropped the class half way through. 60 out of 64 students passed the class. Class has a ton of work and quiz but she makes up for it by offering a huge curve. A 57% in her class is a C-. Im not joking. Put in effort you'll pass.

This class is unnecessarily hard and has continuous quizzes. And the class comes with a pre-lecture for a class twice a week? It's a CSR class. the grading of writing assignments is also absurd. Very strict grading from TA and receiving a good grade is impossible. And 15% of your grade is participation? In a business class? Try ur best to avoid.

Good class content, passionate professor, but the workload is too much. With quizzes, debates, and in-class writing assignments, we don't have any time to breathe because every class is full of these activities and we have to speak up to get participation credit. Kind of stressful, but I hope this knowledge can stay longer.

I pay a lot of money to go to UCSD. I don't want an easy A where I forget all the material after a quarter. MGT 166 inspired me and taught me critical information about modern/future CSR. Moran is a highly knowledgeable professor, but you must seek her out and take your academic career into your own hands. Anything worthwhile is never easy.

Worst professor I've taken in UCSD by far. Don't take this class if you don't need to or wait till she stops teaching. For a class on social corporate responsibility, she makes the class way more complicated than it should be. Everyone I've spoken to in the class hates it and hates her teaching style. Never seen a mgt class that needs a curve btw!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Made an account just for this. I went into this class thinking "how bad could it be". It was worse than i could ever imagine. Previous reviews are all accurate. Moran is essentially the type of power tripping, stick up her professor that thinks her job is more serious that it actually is. I learned nothing of importance in this class.

The flipped learning approach means 6+ hours of useless busy work per week that could easily just be gone over in class quizzes test on memorization of random facts rather than actual content, participation is mandatory and if you don't speak your grade will suffer, vague rubric and grading policies, NOT worth your time and effort!!

Super hard professor, baseline MGT class but yet her class needs a curve because of how tough her grading is. Participation is mandatory twice a week or you will get a 0, quizzes were super specific on the readings and the only thing graded not extremely harsh was the group assignments. No devices in class policy, overall just a bad professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Do not take this class I was aiming for an A, but ended up with a C. Hard quizzes, exams, and a majority of the class does terrible on the final group presentation. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IT IS NOT AN EASY A, B, OR C.

One of the worst professors at UCSD. She changed her syllabus in week 6, has too many things she grades you on, while being ambiguous with her grading criteria. The lectures are also extremely boring. HER ENTIRE CLASS CAN BE SUMMARIZED IN A TIKTOK.

The worst professor and class I have ever seen in my entire four years of undergrads here at UCSD. Unfair and unclear grading, worst ever class policy, heavy load of work but meaningless.

This is by far the worst class I have ever taken, not at UCSD, but in my entire life. There is no way she believes a college student can handle all that homework on top of weekly quizzes, short papers, participation, and debates WHILE the TA is also a harsh grader? Help me and stay as far away from this class. I'm so sorry to all business majors.

Probably one of the worst classes I have ever taken at UCSD! A business class...

Pre-Lecture videos for upcoming lectures
Quizzes on pre-lecture + readings
Participation required or 0s
Debates
TAs are tough graders on papers
Locked grade

She's old-fashioned. What's the device policy? We're in 21 century!

There are so many remaining seats every quarter for only this professor. other mgt 166 classes taught by other professors are full which means her teaching style has problems or something.
This class lack of transparency. AVERAGE grades for papers are 5 and quizzes are 6. Too tough grader.

Quiz every week, sometimes quiz twice per week, debate, discussion post every week, class active participation, in-class assignments (no device allowed). No device policy. Lots of readings. Pre-class videos. Too much things to do per week!! We have other classes to handle too! OMG

avoid this professor. I would give her a big fat zero if I could. Tons of readings and long pre-class videos for this meaningless class. This professor does not know what she was doing in the lecture. Extremely tough grader, make the quiz very hard and essays as well. DO NOT TAKE HER !

grading is clear and fair, material is just a bit dense sometimes. ENROLL IN AN EARLIER SECTION (11 am or 2 pm) AND YOU WILL HAVE MORE TIME FOR YOUR FINAL EXAM/PAPER!!!!!

Please enroll in her MGT166 to gain the following exciting experience: Attending irresponsibly arranged lectures teaching social responsibility Taking meaningless quiz focusing on memorizing details & numbers Receiving 3/8 by "not reading prompts" on subjective, open-ended essays Confronting indifferent TA that despises appropriate dissents
I can't even believe that she has taught MGT166 for over ten years. THE WORST remote class in UCSD

Failed to empathize with the struggles college students and nation are going through right now. Continued to give difficult assignments and final throughout the quarter and ignored persistent voices of students. Very disorganized course.

It is obvious Professor Moran does not support her students to succeed, even during this difficult time. reviews.comment: Quickly became clear that she does not want her students to succeed whatsoever by sneaking in in-class assignments when attendance was prohibited this quarter. reviews.comment: A class in which I learned absolutely nothing. To say that this class was disappointing would be an understatement. I put in a minimal amount of effort while also noting how often she relied on sources that lack credibility.

Papers, quizzes, participation, attendance, debate, easy midterm and final. Class is not hard at all if you actually try and do the readings which are interesting and not too long. Go to her OH and the TAs OH if you need help. Both were very willing to help. Class is on a solid curve.

reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class is really interesting and I think you learn a lot about topics that people are generally unaware of. Prof Moran is very well prepared and cares about your learning but lectures can get kind of boring and it can be hard to pay attention. Papers are graded pretty harshly and you have to do the readings to do well on the quizzes.

Lectures are mandatory, but if you pay attention it will really help when studying. There are 5 quizzes and 5 papers, but they're relatively straightforward. If you study and are actively engaged in class you will do well. She is always very prepared and really cares about the class and I enjoyed it! The topic was interesting and diverse.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Interesting class that taught me a lot about corporate social responsibility. There was also a lot of reading and writing involved. TA's are harsh graders when it comes to the papers so going to their office hours would be helpful. Attendance and participation are mandatory since it's 10% of your grade. Also no electronic devices allowed.

10% MT, 20% Final, 25% Paper, 19% Quizzes, 25% Class Participation, 10% Debate, 1% Rady Lab. She's nice and passionate about the topic. Her study guides are super generous, its pretty much identical to the exams. She can be a bit boring for people's taste. Some days it wasn't as boring though imo. No laptops in class.
A very tough grader who is unclear about what she wants from you. Tests are representative but lectures will out you to sleep.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She sounds boring, but participation is part of your grade. Has multiple papers that will be graded by your TAs, so pray you get a nice one. She gives study guides for your midterm and final. Exam is representative of stuff she mentions in lectures and in the study guide.

She's a great professor and the course material , but there's so much busy work in this class like readings, papers, and assignments. Also you have to go to class since they count attendance. The exams aren't too bad and the course is curved, so it's more hard to get an A or B.

She has an unconventional way of teaching which keeps the audience interested and on task. I was fascinated by everything she presented because she used her lecture, videos, movies, and various ways of class participation to keep everyone interested. She is very knowledgeable about the subject and truly cares about her students. Great class!

Good professor. I found the class topics very interesting. Lots of reading but skimming it is usually enough. Grades based on about over 5 categories. Attendance and participation matters. She usually gives the median score in the class a BB+ but the median scores in the class are fairly high.  Easy class but requires some time and effort.

Professor Moran is a great prof. I had to crash her class on late notice but I was able to catch up quickly. I found all of the readings and discussions quite interesting; it wasn't difficult having to write about them in a journal or be quizzed and tested on them. Tests are 12 short answer and 12 multiple choice.

She is a a wonderful instructor with a passion in what she is doing. Grading might be tough, but there is a ton you can learn in the class. There is no textbook needed, but there is a collection of online sources and a course reader. Most of them are very exciting to read. You should definitely take this class if you have some interest in business.

Super genuine guy, you can tell he really cares about his students. I don't like chem, but his lectures were actually engaging and he usually explained things well. I will say the homework is NOT fun or easy and there are a lot of exams (every other week), but they test what we learn in lecture and you get a full sized cheat sheet.
Chem 4 had a lot of homework but he gave great feedback to students and made sure we were prepared for tests.

Difficult for an introductory class. Lots of hw that don't align with lectures so you need to figure it out on your own. Tests bi-weekly but you are allowed a cheat sheet that doesn't need to be handwritten. Nice professor and points out some topics that will be on the test during lecture.
AMAZING!!!! My favorite professor yet! Makes content engaging and interesting, the class is laid out very clearly and gave lots of partial credit on exams. 100% recommend!

Sometimes his lecture helps and sometimes it doesn't, but it's not mandatory. I spent the most time in this class for this quarter cuz his tests are pretty hard if you don't prepare a lot. The reading quiz is a lot and really confusing cuz it's mostly materials that he will not cover in the test and things we don't need to know. Overall not bad

Prof. Bussey is a very good professor, it's just the course content itself that's difficult. It can get tricky to keep up so it's important to communicate w/ your TA and ask for help. I didn't go to lectures but I was fine due to taking the class P/NP. Grading is quite fair considering the fact some things are dropped at the end of the course.

reviews.comment: Professor Bussey is good lecturer and engages with students. Reading reviews and problem sets due every week (multiple attempts). Bi-weekly exams that are typically based on 3 lectures (written response) and your allowed a front & back cheat sheet. Hints at topics that are going to be on exams during lectures.

Bussey is very helpful outside of class. However, during lectures he tends to go fast to cover all the content. I would not recommend him for a beginning level course like chem4a because it is hard to keep up if you don't already have a strong foundation. TAs grade all work, but test qs are free response, so grading is on a strict rubric.

Doing well on tests required literally regurgitating super specific pieces of information. The rubrics were ridiculous. He overcomplicates the content. None of the assignments prepared you for the exams, but there were SO much homework and so many tests. I took this class as a science GE and honestly should've taken 6A.

Difficult class but good professor. Very caring during his lectures and made sure to answer any questions. Readings and quizzes that need to be done before class are pretty frustrating (but low % of grade). Learned a lot but was tough. Be ready to work in a group weekly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Nearly thought I was going to die while taking this class. This class is harder than CHEM6A which makes absolutely no sense. Save yourself from doom and despair by not taking this class. Also we had a test every two weeks that made up majority of our grade but the homework had nothing to do with our tests.

Only way to pass is to have a good discussion group since part of the exams is a team test. A lot of hw and much of the material did not match the tests and we had tests biweekly. The lectures helped a little bit but u have to study a lot if u want to pass. I feel like the class was too hard just for it to be an intro class. He does not curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: all the good reviews are for other classes. please ignore them and do not take this class.
i hate this class just don't take it

This is the worst class you could ever take for a science GE. The tests are nothing like any of the material, the lectures make every concept so impossible to understand and the quick pacing of a test every other week means you basically start studying for the next the second you finish the 1st. If you need a science GE do NOT take this class.

The lectures are helpful and informative. There's required readings each week, which I find boring and that it overcomplicates things. There are 4 tests every other week, which can get overwhelming but are helpful to help prepare for the final. Make sure to get a good discussion group, as there are group portions for each test and the final.

reviews.comment: Literally horrible, his lectures are so boring that most of the class passes out before you do.He podcasts everything, so you realistically just take notes from that. Learning checks rarely match readings, reviews, or lectures. Discussions are in groups of 3–5; pick a helpful group, or you'll get 0/3 since solo submissions don't count.Take CHEM6A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: as a person he's funny, he's just a cool guy. but lord, readings that dont make sense, exams that make or break your grade, if you dont get a good group you're actually beyond cooked, besides that DO NOT TAKE AS GE. Do Chem6A!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: To be real Bussey isn't that bad, he does OVERCOMPLICATE a lot of his material, like there is bunch of simple stuff that can be told easier, but he js makes it much more complex. His tests are made up in a way where you have to add as much information as you can, and if the information is correct he will give you points. TAs also matter, good luck!

The class was ok, it really depends on your group, that will make or break your grade during tests. Has weekly assignments that you are supposed to do before he explains the topic, which makes the class difficult. His lectures are good but tests can be super niche at times, does allow a cheat sheet, it's a lot of free response and wasn't helpful.

I think Bussey is a very good lecturer and his lectures are by far the mot useful piece of learning for the class. However, his course layout is horrendous. The reading reviews, problem sets, discussions, lectures, and even exams are completely disjointed and don't feel like the same class at all. Also LOTS of homework. Very hard for entry level.

As a professor, Bussey is good. His lectures are the best thing about the class because he explains the content very well, so I'd recommend attending even though attendance isn't mandatory. However, the class is unnecessarily complicated with the weekly problem sets, readings, and 4 midterms. Good professor, frustrating class structure.
save yourself and your mental health and don't take this class

This class is very difficult for gen ed. Superrr heavy on homework and lectures. Each unit has problem sets with only 5 attempts. Exams are the worst—4 tests plus a cumulative final. The first test average was 15.75/30, and he doesn't curve. Super nice guy, but I'd recommend going straight into CHEM 6A to save yourself stress :')

Lots of reading. He doesn't explain the concepts well that are needed for the 5 exams that are given. Going into this class, you should expect to self-study the material, but I recommend going to office hours with TAs. He says himself that he changes the grading scale depending on factors, and also he drops the lowest test score at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I have beef with all of you who rated him highly last quarter. guys please do yourselves a favor and take a different professor.

There are midterm style exams every other week, you have barely any time to think out your answers, and all of them are entirely FRQ. There is also a group section, so if you get unlucky with a bad group, sucks for you! He made this course so in depth for no reason, my friend in Chem 6A didn't learn half of the stuff we did. Avoid Dr. Bussey.

Professor Bussey is a very sweet guy but I DO NOT recommend him as a professor, specially if you're just taking GE chem. He speaks too fast, and just repeats himself when answering questions. There are new assignments and content everyday. Mind you this is finals week and he is still GIVING CONTENT. Test heavy and unnecessary stress. CHOOSE CHEM6

Dr. Bussey tends to overcomplicate subjects at times. He has a grading scale that is awful, instead of any curves for exams, with a usual avg of 50%, exams might I add that are biweekly and 40% of your grade, he offers one exam at the end of the quarter that replaces your lowest score. Work heavy. Course is definitely passable but not recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although attendance wasn't mandatory for lectures it's mandatory for discussions. Class grade was curved by a lot 60% and above was a passing grade (60-79% was a C) 50% of grade was based on 5 tests (no midterm), which were very difficult not relating to the material in class sometimes, on average the mean score for these tests was 17/30.
Get ready  to write everything and anything ever mentioned about that subject for the answers in the test questions. Quite ridiculous rubrics.

DO NOT TAKE HIM IF YOU WANT TO DO WELL!!! I love chemistry and this is nothing against the professor but rather the class. we have to do readings, discussion activities, reading quizzes, and problem sets but the kicker is that NONE of these even prepare you for the material on the exams which are every other week. be prepared to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
He overcomplicates what he teaches. You need to do readings before the lectures which go over the same things. There are discussion activities and also practice problems but the content on them and also the readings and lectures are nothing like the tests. 
There are five tests throughout the quarter which takes a lot of time to study for.

He is an alright guy. However, his teaching style is horrendous. All of the "reading comprehension" assignments and problem sets are from a textbook and guess what? The test is nothing like the problem sets :))) Lectures aren't really helpful when studying

Be prepared to teach yourself. This man talks in the most convoluting way possible. He also is really bad at emailing you back. His tests are not multiple choice and biweekly. He also overcomplicates the questions and most of the time you're wondering what is going on instead of actually doing the exam. It's also not within the 80 minutes. BEWARE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: guys i'm writing this before enrollment so you know not to take him. he's very entertaining and lively but unfortunately the lectures, readings, and discussions don't match with the exams at all. he overcomplicates chemistry and then under delivers the information necessary to succeed. exams are free response and many people do not finish on time

I took this during the summer and it was all asych. I loved his teaching style & his notes/lectures were always clear. The midterms weren't too difficult. He gives you a chance to grade replace them during the final (do pt 3 of final if u want grade replace, if not, then skip).
Took his class last year! His lectures were super informative, he was super clear, and he podcasted :) Definitely take his class if he's teaching the intro chem courses.

Overall a nice guy and gave clear directions on what to do. There were 3 tests in total and they are like 60% of your grade, so don't mess that up. Homework isn't hard, just read and you will be fine. He records his lectures but sometimes it's not very clear, as his lectures are directly to the reading and the reading isn't fully clear sometimes.
One of the best professors at UCSD. Great lecturer, always made learning engaging.

Great guy, was never not entertained in lecture and he genuinely seemed to care about his student's success. This translated to the way he would vocalize topics during lectures. Didn't mind going over a topic more than once and recorded his lectures!

I honestly should've just taken chem 6a because the content that I learned in that class was taught in a significantly easier way. He overcomplicates the content. Your grade and learning relies heavily on discussion (mandatory). If you take him make sure you get a good group because you do literally everything with them including tests.

He's a nice person, but I now hate chem. He overcomplicates a lot too. Very dependent on your TA, I had a bad one who wouldn't go over concepts and left us behind on material. I BEG OF YOU TO GET A GOOD GROUP IN DISCUSSIONS OR ELSE THE DI WORK AND EXAMS WILL BE TERRIBLE. I had a good group and got lucky, I probably wouldn't have passed otherwise.

Lighthearted vibe during lectures and covered content well. As someone who is currently taking CHEM 6A, he made certain problems easier to understand the thought process of.

DI's are definitely mandatory though since part of quizzes (no midterms) were taken with your DI group. If you didn't have a DI group you'd be placed with a random group.
Awesome lecturer. Caring, and respectful to students.

The class has a lot of tests (one test every two weeks plus the final, so five total), and required a lot of studying.  The discussion groups are important because you take part of the tests with your group and all your discussion assignments are group-based. He's a good lecturer and mostly explains things well, but moves quickly.
This class made me lose interest in chem :(

Bussey wasn't the best at explaining topics, instead he overcomplicated them. He was quite unapproachable during office hours. I couldn't ask much. There was a midterm every 2 weeks(4 midterms & 1 final), which was very stressful. The group work was heavily based, the group you pick depends on your grade. You work together on part 2 of the exams.
Grade largely based on 5 tests (4 every other week and 1 cumulative final). there are individual and group parts of the quizzes. make sure you get a good group!

Best professor I've had at UCSD. Such organized and clear lectures, makes tough concepts simple and explains them thoroughly, and always leaves room for questions and answers questions thoughtfully. Funny and cares about his students, and all the assigned material is easy to get through but still super helpful and worthwhile.

This prof was amazing! He is very kind and will take the time to go over topics already covered if you need it. The bookwork HW assignments are due before he actually teaches it in lecture which is the only downside but when he explains it it all it makes sense. Very fair grader and will replace your lowest exam score.

Prof Bussey is very fair. There is a bit of work, but it all is very helpful for studying for the test and can be redone to get full credit. There are a lot of tests (5 total). The lowest score is replaced by the final. All tests have a group portion and have generous partial credit. A cheat sheet is allowed on all tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very easy class, in my opinion. Though discussions were mandatory if you wanted full credit on the discussion activities. Online textbook you have to buy but hw was all MCQ w/ unlimited attempts for full credit. Lowest score of everything was dropped (even tests) Tests were FRQ with 80% individual and 20% in you discussion groups so pick a good one

Very thorough lectures and interactive homework, which helps with the difficult subject. 5 tests throughout the year, each one having an individual and group portion. The group is from your discussion groups so choose wisely. Each test also allows a calculator and cheat sheet and the last test is cumulative and replaces lowest score. Super easy.

Best chemistry professor at UCSD, explains the topics better than anyone on campus. Exams are reflective of lecture content, time is just sufficient. If you get the chance to take him, definitely do it!

I took this class first quarter of my first year; however, I enjoyed this professor. Discussions are mandatory and there were 4 midterms and 1 final; however, you get a cheat sheet and are relatively easy. You work in groups your whole discussion and have group portions for the tests. If you have a good group and TA, you should do fine.

The BEST chemistry professor I've taken at UCSD. Exams are more than fair. Final will replace the lowest midterm grade. No practice exam, but learning objectives are laid out for each chapter. Exams are made to correspond with the learning objectives. Class GPA is 2.5, but people also don't come to class. The class is hard, and podcasts are not it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great lecturer but terrible examer and grader. There's NO practice exams and the homeworks don't represent exam questions. Exams are lengthy and handwritten and you will lose points for your wording. Grading is hilarious that he curved the class based on the top student, which changed nothing. The average is at C just cuz someone did great lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I recommend him to everyone. He gives so many hints as to what will be on the exams and is super helpful. Homework was a bit time-consuming and discussions were the most helpful. "Learning checks" were split in two parts. Individual portion and group portion and group depended on the group you chose in the discussion so be wary of who you choose.

great class!
grades come from 4 tests + a final (none of the questions are structured to be tricky or too bad), discussion activities, and an interactive textbook. you'll be good on the tests as long as you actually understand the material, which is easy since the professor explains everything really well and sets you up for future Chem classes

Professor Bussey gave a great explanations of the topics and was very helpful in class when it came to questions. Bi-weekly learning checks were given that were all free response. He also provides summary videos aside from lecture that were helpful. Discussions were all group based as you just did a worksheet the whole time.

Prof. Bussey oversimplifies chem concepts and complicates them at the same time. The class average on the tests was quite low and he was happy with them. As a non stem major, I had to take this class for my GE and ended up p/np the class because it was not aceable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing professor. Take him if you are able to. He gives hints of what will be on tests, and the tests are pretty straightforward. Discussions are in groups and graded on the completion of assignments. Grading is fair and pretty easy to get an A. His lectures are very clear and if I could retake him if, I would definitely do so.

Overall great professor. I would recommend paying attention in lecture, as he drops a lot of hints as to what will be covered on the tests. The tests are fair, though they do require you to know all of the concepts in order to properly apply that knowledge to your answers (as there are no multiple choice tests, all are FRQs).
Very caring teacher who excels at his job. His tests were difficult, but his teaching method was excellent. Very informative and ensured you understood the concepts.

He is a great teacher and does care about his students, he gives hints to what will be on the quizzes and drops/replaces your lowest test score if you do better on the last learning check. If you're not great at chemistry or science this class will probably be difficult at first, but I recommend going to his office hours and joining a study group!

Professor Bussey is very interactive, and makes the content easy to understand. You can tell he is really passionate in what he does, and cares for students' success and understanding. The TopHat extension is especially useful to prepare for lectures and exams. I would highly recommend his class. He's also funny.

The lectures aren't mandatory as they are recorded usually, but the discussion sections ARE mandatory. You are graded on attendance and participation of the assignments. He also does give hints about what will be on the quizzes and lets you bring a cheat sheet for the quizzes! I would very very strongly recommend him!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lots of homework, but it is good preparation for the exams. You can bring a cheat sheet to exams, so as long as you pay attention to the material they aren't super difficult. Choose your discussion groups carefully, because you're expected to stick to the same group all quarter and part of every exam is completed as a group.
This Professor was great, super respected. There is a lot of homework in the course, and exams every two weeks, but its good if you watch the videos
Goes over topics very quickly. Expect discussion section to be mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took Bussey remote class and his videos were super easy to follow and gave a great understanding of the content. If you understand all the information the tests were super straightforward and easy.

There are 4 learning checks besides final and they can be hard. The good thing is you can take cheat sheets. Drop lowest homework, reading assignment, and discussion activity. There are two discussions each week and they are mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took a remote version of the class with professor Bussey and he made it extremely easy to follow and his lectures were prompt and to the point with good examples. He was rather easy to reach when I needed help and would check up on us throughout the quarter.

Took online FA21. Accessible, caring & approachable. OH helpful - sometimes gives hints about exams. 4 midterms: non-cumulative, short answer, yes partial credit, open-note. No final. Best way to study: fully answer/understand all learning targets, redo lecture & prob set problems. All lectures async - explains concepts clearly. Fair drop policies.
The outcome of your grade will heavily be counted on learning checks. As long you take good notes and pay attention during the lectures, the class won't be as hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: don't.

Dr. Bussey is an amazing professor, highly recommended. His tests are hard but if you put time in to study and understand the concept of each module you are tested on, then you should be okay. Tests are all free response. Homework is almost-all multiple choice and unlimited attempts.

I really liked Bussey for chem4, the lectures were super in depth and he made it very clear what he was planning to put on learning checks. He made the intro to chem super easy and understandable and most of the tests had average grades above an 85%. I would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You have a textbook reading due for each lecture, but I usually did the readings first and then watched all of the lectures at the end of the week. He really cares about students and how they approach his class, it makes the class a lot less stressful. Take good notes! They will benefit you more than you know.

dr. bussey is one of my fav profs this year. he is extremely nice and you can tell that he truly cares about his students as well as chemistry in general. his lectures are full of useful information and he teaches in a very engaging manner. homework is pretty easy but beware of biweekly learning checks (but you do get to bring a cheat sheet)

He's a great professor who is clear with what he needs from you. The math on the exams can get a little difficult, but that's the case with all chemistry and from what I've heard from peers, the way he teaches it is the best comparatively. If you keep up, you'll do well for the most part, but he's available for aid and I'd seriously take advantage.

His tests are difficult to study for and when I did I still scored well below what I would in any other class, stay away if you're looking for a Chem class that is easy to understand, not to mention the assignments are due on the same week he hold tests, his grading scale would be easy except his exams are UPLOADED PDFS, which takes time.

The homework isn't hard, it barley gives you any credit (multiple choice and online) PLEASE go to lecture, you have bi-weekly learning checks that are rather difficult if you DON'T master the content in lectures. I liked the class because it pushed me to do well for my grade. He's a super good professor, but office hours is still necessary lol.
Tests are worth 60% of your grade and the scale is skewed to exams, the professor is nice but the tests are ones you need to read for
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just an overall amazing professor! He makes me feel like that he was MADE FOR TEACHING. He explains much better than the textbook. He will also answer any questions you have in class. Pretty funny guy as well.

I loved this class. He made the concepts easy and the lectures further explained the textbook concepts. Its hard to fail, just pay attention and do the work. He drops some assignments (1 per section) but you have to stay organized with due dates.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: very kind and helpful throughout the quarter. his tests were hard sometimes but he always helped during office hours and gave an extra credit opportunity during finals week. would definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His lectures are amazing but super long. You have to pause them every five seconds to write stuff down. Tests are completely free-response and the grading criteria is very harsh. He's not the most friendly but he does care and will help you at office hours. Better than most profs but you really have to work for an A.

I took Dr. Bussey during the pandemic and I really think he did a great job. He would have asynchronous lectures and use the actual "class time" to answer questions. To do well on the Learning Checks, you need to really listen to the lectures and use what you learned in the lecture to answer the learning objectives. I don't think you need the TB.

One of the best chemistry classes I've ever had, and I highly recommend taking Bussey. He made it easy to understand the content, so if you watch the lectures and do the work then you will do well in the class. Practice problems were very reflective of what is on the exams, and he gives a lot of resources to help you prepare.

He is a good professor, he cares for his students and is always helpful. However, I think his lectures are hard to understand and you need to put a lot of effort to pass this course which is a thing I didn't do.

The material covered has a new and interesting twist even if you have taken chemistry before. But this also means that you need to be really attentive to the lectures and not fool yourself by thinking you already know the material. Ex. Ionic bond can be explained by wikipedia in one sentence but the entire theory required his 80 min lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Bussey's class, and feel like I learned a lot from taking the course. I did take the class online, so lectures were pre-recorded, but they were very clear. If you watch the lectures and take notes you will have a clear idea of what is going on. I regret not going to office hours more often, they were helpful when I did go
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Because this was an online class, all the lectures were prerecorded. They weren't the most exciting but very easy to understand and follow. Overall the assignments were easy and office hours helped greatly with getting questions answered. I'm not the greatest at chem but if you do the reading and watch the videos you will do well

Dr. Bussey is very knowledgeable and his class is straightforward in terms of what you need to do to get an A. Because I took this class online, he had 5 Learning Check Tests over the course of the quarter which were time consuming and at times mentally taxing. This is not an easy class, but an A is certainly attainable. Make sure to attend lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: While my course was taken online, Professor Bussey provided a clear outline with what is expected from you to earn your grade. There's alot of conceptual understanding mixed in with a bit of math in his learning checks which were essentially quizzes and the main grade determining thing during the course, but just watch the lecture at 2x
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Bussey was an okay-ish teacher for me. His structure for the class is very clear and easy to follow. All of his lectures are prerecorded and after every 2 chapters, there are learning checks to assess your knowledge of the 2 chapters. So its your responsibility to watch the lectures and take notes. You also get homework every week.

Professor Bussey is a good professor, but I feel like that more true if we were still in an in-person environment. His lecture pre-recordings are relatively long and it can be hard to focus especially during this pandemic. He also gives biweekly learning checks and they can be challenging if you don't watch/understand the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bussey explains things very conceptually and my grade relied mostly on the learning checks he gave every two weeks. The lectures are upwards of an hour each and sometimes don't cover everything in the homework. The homework isn't too bad, 30 questions every week plus notes/discussion posts. I used the textbook for most of my learning and did fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bussey is such a good professor. His open office hours are really helpful and he explains concepts very well. His lectures are very clear and I never had to read the textbook. I highly recommend him

HIGHLY RECOMMEND! Professor Bussey and his TAs know what they're doing. You'll have bi-weekly exams & most answers come straight from the lecture. He's very thorough so make sure to take notes on every little thing he mentions. At OH, he'll usually tell you key topics to know for the exam. Workload is completely manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I didn't have a good chem background from high school, but Prof. Bussey gives a great overview of Gen Chem and is able to do so at a manageable pace. Always open to questions, and always gives thorough answers, even to the dumb questions. His tests are fair and I think if I studied a little more I would've have gotten an A.

If you have a chance to take the TMC Honors Seminar, I highly recommend. I learned a lot, about the world and about myself, and Professor Bussey was an amazing facilitator. I'd take any class he teaches, he's that good.

Bussey is an amazing lecturer. His tests cover whats on the lectures, so no surprise curveballs. However, his tests are comparatively harder than other 6 series profs (free response, concept-heavy, nitpicky grading, no cheatsheet) and an A- begins at 92. I did not take AP Chem, so I had to study hard. Thanks to him, I feel more confident in chem.

he's really good at explaining things, even though they can be boring--if that makes sense. test questions are fair, but harshly graded, especially the short answers. Discussions are mandatory, which was actually kind of good for me I think! I'm not used to STEM classes requiring discussion and I think it helped. I should go to more discussions lol
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: No curves, no cheat-sheet, no love. Take at your own risk. He is very concept based so little to no use of equations. Based on who you are this is either good or bad. But if you're expecting easy tests, take someone else. There is always room for error when it comes to free response questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Was super excited to get Bussey for Chem 6C. BIG Regret. He is a good teacher but he grades exams so harshly you go to class and he says Congrats. You guys did really good. The average was a 63. Like are you kidding me? How is that good?! I took AP Chem in high school so a lot of it was review but I still struggled. You have to teach yourself.

Dr. Bussey is an absolutely brilliant lecturer. His slides have lots of information, but he explains all of the topics very well, and always makes sure he answers all questions before moving on. His tests are all free-response and HEAVILY concept-based, so they require a deep understanding of the material and WHY things happen. Take him if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This proffesor is amongst the best chem proffesor the campus has to offer. He is very concept-based so you need to understand the why of the content to pass his class. That also means he is not heavy on math but you still need to be careful with your algebra. No clicker questions.

I don't know why everyone gives Professor Bussey such good reviews. He lectures way too fast to understand and he comes off as condescending. His philosophy is "more is more", so he puts lots of practice problems and learning objectives on his website, however no extent of preparation can prepare you for his extremely hard tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Greatest prof in chem dept. Attendance is somehow mandatory since there will have group work done on the class. Easy A if you go through the lectures (podcast as well) and homework and follow the learning objective to review.

Bussey's an amazing professor. He lectures well and seems very likable as a person. His tests are hard, but fair. Study the learning objectives, do lots of practice, and really understand the concepts and how everything can connect. Don't just memorize terms and ideas. Understand them. As hard as this class was, I'd say I learned a lot at least.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Probably the best professor I've taken this quarter. He really knows his material and does a great job lecturing and explaining all of the material. He also posts lecture slides with fill-in-the-blank type notes, and the class is podcasted. Exams are difficult but fair, and they are all free response. There usually isn't a curve.

An amazing professor, very interesting and entertaining. His lectures are engaging and easy to follow. He posts his lecture outlines on canvas, making note-taking easy. There are podcasts although attendance is mandatory. What's taught in class is very reflective of his tests. A little hard, but learning is guaranteed. My favorite professor so far!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Bussey is honestly an amazing teacher. I wish I would've had him for the whole gen chem series, if I did I might have actually learned something in chem 6A/B. The only downsides to him are the fact that his grading scale is harsh (a 92 is an A) and his test are very long, hard, and conceptual. But overall I would definitely recommend him.

Taking his class currently and it is impossible. The average was a D- on the midterm and he doesn't curve so.....? Also just because you understand the material does not mean you will do well if you don't say exactly word for word what he wants you get points off. Also he has errors on the midterms so that's great.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Bussey is truly amazing. I take his Chem 6A and his lecture is well organized and he is really knowledgable and clear in explaining Chem ideas. But here are some tips for u in order to get an A! Read the textbook prior to his lecture or after his lecture. In-class group work is really important which might be on the test.

He is a great teacher; very clear and concise in his lectures, and is willing to offer extra explanation if needed. If you don't pay attention or show up to class, it is VERY easy to get lost, even if you review the online powerpoint from lecture. If you did not take honors/AP chemistry in high school- this class will be extremely difficult!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Bussey is an amazing professor who does a great job explaining chemistry concepts. In CHEM 6C I had to skip class once a week due to conflicting schedules but I was able to catch up via podcast and review sessions in order to make sure I still knew the material. He teaches exactly what is needed to be known for his exams too.

A brilliant lecturer, he even explains what is important to takeaway in lecture, what he expects of you to do on an exam, and offers abundant resources. But beware, his grading scale makes it slightly harder to get an A (92 is B+) so there is a minor setback to guaranteed learning. Exams are all free-response, get ready to grind out chem knowledge.

Took him for B and C, and it was great! He's really clear on what he wants you to know! His material is very conceptual, so be prepare to write and explain things. For exams, all I used was his lecture. The final is mostly the midterms but with different numbers or reworded.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Not worth it tbh, he say you won't need the textbook when you will you won't pass with his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: At the end of each chapter, there is an in-lecture group assignment submitted for credit. Bussey allows you to drop the lowest grade in every category at the end of the quarter, and your final replaces the lowest midterm if you score better on it. He also offers five points of extra credit before the final which is more helpful than it sounds.

Agree with some reviews that grading sometimes doesnt match your learning achievements. Tip: write as much as you can even though the knowledge is obvious because you will mark down if you dont, including units in every calculation and shows work even the simpliest things. There is pros and cons in free reaponding style. An A is doable though.

He is a very kind and respected professor but he oversimplifies the lectures. Then on exams, he combines all of the information. There is no practice exams and no practice problems so the only thing I had to rely on were Sapling and book problems that I got from my other friends. The in class group assignments takes time away from the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is he best chem teacher ever. His tests may be slightly more difficult compared to others (all free response). However, he really cares about his students and is willing to help. I thought I knew chem before. But now I actually jow chem because of this guy. He's got a good sense of humor which is a plus. Take him if you get the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great teacher but tests are ridiculously unreasonable in both expectation and grading. They're long and entirely free response. He expects answers to include every redundant obvious detail and if it isn't written in the exact words and direction he wants, it's wrong. Then you have to argue for points. Grades don't match actual learning achievement.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: 6C was my favorite class out of the chem 6 series and I think taking it with Bussey made it even more enjoyable! He's a great lecturer, gives fair exams and even gives extra credit opportunities. Attendance is mandatory just bc he gives random group work assignments but other than that 10/10 would recommend. Wish I got an A in the class though
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I think that bussey is a great lecturer and really helps you understand the concepts. His lectures were very clear and precise and he podcasts. His test are extremely long usually taking the whole time but are fair. His grading scale on the other hand isnt, he curves of the top score even tho my 91% in the class turned out to be a B+.

His lectures are SUPER good. He focuses more on making sure everyone undsrstands the content. I would highly recommend. The class isnt an easy A though, you have to make sure you know your stuff. All the content is on his lectures tho so if you get that, youll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor, in lectures he hints at content that will be on tests. Book reading and practice problems are suggested and helpful but not mandatory. He is really great at breaking down ideas and making chemistry fun. Grading is fair and based on a set scale then adjusted to the highest earned points. You should take his class.
Very caring professor, felt like he enjoyed teaching and made it more bearable to attend lectures. Very reasonable tests and grading scale.

Prof Bussey makes Chem as interesting as possible during lectures. You must attend lecture as there are graded groupwork assignments and skipping those will affect your grade. Discussion is also mandatory and each week there is a group assignment too. Homework is due once weekly online and never took up too much time. Overall a good Chem class!
Doesnt really help learn anything. Pretty much have to know stuff on your own.
BEST CHEM PROFESSOR EVER!!!

I hated chemistry but after taking his class, I love it! His lectures are very conceptual, but easy to understand due to his explanations. One of the best lecturers I have ever had. His tests are all free response but they are very fair and doable.

Clear voice and made sure the concepts were clear. Lectures are mandatory because he assigns random "group work" activities (5 min long). 2 midterms per quarter that are 10ish pages all free response, but all based on lecture material so it wasn't too bad. Discussions are mandatory. Curve based on top scoring students. Highly recommend.

He is a great lecturer who wants to make sure you really understand the material. Exams are usually free response. If you pay attention in class, go over lecture material, go to discussion... you'll be fine. Discussions are also mandatory! I loved taking his class over summer. He also ended up curving a little bit! Great professor!
Awesome professor! Definitely will take again!

Best prof ever! I don't like Chemistry but he made it so enjoyable. All his exams are based solely off of his lectures so if you watch his podcasts a couple times you will be set for the exam! Totally recommend
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Bussey is a great lecturer but I guess his teaching style just didn't click with me. I felt like a lot of times he went over difficult material way too quickly. Tests were all free response so you need to know all of the material in depth. Harsh grading scale but he gives an extra credit opportunity and test score replacement.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Gives extra credit based on online practice. Good Professor, knows his stuff.

Bussey is an amazing professor! His slides are clear and his online homework is very useful for learning and reviewing. His exams are a little bit hard b/c there are no multiple choices, so you need to understand every concept very well. I love him so much that I recommend every one to take his class!!!
In my opinion he was one of the professors that i enjoyed the most because his lectures were very enjoyable but his test were mediocre and another thing is his random group session during lectures.

He speaks very clearly and is a little punny during his lectures. The only "downside" is that he will do random "group work" in lectures, just to make sure that you are attending them. He was very enjoyable and I would definitely take him again as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: His lectures are well thought out with powerpoint live drawings and diagrams and he podcasts as well. After almost every topic he's done introducing, he'll stop the class and ask if there's any questions and he's patient enough to answer every question the class has. His learning objectives (and picky wording) are his tests so study his lectures.

Bussey is a great chem prof, he'll deconstruct complex topics and make sure you really understand everything. His tests are very specific and often more concept based than math, however the hw is math intensive. He's a great lecturer and very helpful during office hours. If you're stuck between Bussey and Johnson I'd say go for Bussey, less work.

He is a literal god sent from the heavens to UCSD, a godless place in need of enlightenment. Never have I heard ideas expressed so clearly and with such grace. If you value your education or your life, take Dr. Bussey.
Excellent lectures, no weekly quizzes. 10/10

Don't know about other chem professors but his tests are HARD and he expects you to know every single detail from his lecture slides. His grading scale is hard too (94% for a solid A and not much curve). Great lecturer though so take him if you really want to learn and work hard.

Great lecturer but his exams are hard (all free response and 10 pages too long) and his grading is hard AND on top of that the cut off for an A- is 92-93 and B+ is 91-90 (what happened to the old school days when a 90 was an A-?) so any adjustments to the class point total does nothing for you. You will put in the work for an A and still get a B!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Bussey is a great professor in all aspects. He speaks clearly, he answers questions thoroughly, and he structures the class in a way so that if you pay attention during lectures, you will do well on the exams (which by the way are quite difficult). However, if you do tend to nod off, he podcasts his lectures online as well! Overall great prof!

I loved Bussey because if you attended his lectures and rewatched the podcasts, you would get a good grade. Compared to Johnson, Bussey is a lot easier and he is so much more thorough in the way he teaches. Bussey will go over a concept many times in order for you to understand and he really cares about his students. Take him!

Test hevy b/c his tests weren't hevy on the grade percentage (beside the usual) but his tests were very long. All free response with about 8 pages but subsections of a, b, and c. GREAT lectures, GREAT teacher, and also wrote work on tablet so you could easily make up lecture on podcast; however, didn't have clicker pts but had group wk. worth 2 pts
Tests are all free response, 9 pages each midterm and 14 pages final and he sometimes grades unfairly. If you don't mind that then go ahead and take him, his lectures are good.

Professor Bussey is the best professor so far. I entered UCSD and had a terrible 6A professor and made me dislike chem very badly. Taking 6B with Bussey made me like chemistry A LOT. His skeleton-style notes are worthy of printing out and going along during class. THAT WON'T BE ENOUGH. I rewrote my notes very carefully to make sure I learn them.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He is a good professor tho, but his tests were so hard. And also his curve is not that big, so dont take him if you expect a big curve at the end. Also, the attendance for discussion is mandatory, for the lecture, it's not, but he has those unannounced groupworks, which I missed 2 because I overslept.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is an amazing lecturer, so if you pay attention and take good notes you will learn the material.  Basically every topic he covers will be on the exam, especially the "conceptual" ideas.  The exams are completely free response and he looks for specific terminology.  You'll do great if you KNOW the material, since he doesn't try to trick you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Bussey is the best. He explains chemistry concepts with such clarity and makes it relevant by providing in class demos and real life examples. He has a lot of learning checks in his powerpoints which I personally like, and the way he structures his notes is conducive to note taking. But his grading scale is cancer, so work hard for the A!

Prof. Bussey was an AMAZING Chem 6B professor. He makes everything extremely easy to understand and what he teaches in lecture truly does reflect his learning objectives and the tests. However, his grading scale is harsh, making a 91% a B+, so you have to work really hard if you want an A in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took both Chem 6A and 6B with professor Bussey, by far the best professor I've had at ucsd so far. His lectures are clear and organized and easy to take notes for. Attendance is checked through mini-group works throughout the quarter that are more like concept checks and are really helpful.

By far the best professor I have had yet. His lectures make chemistry really understandable and he often relates what we're learning to a real life situation (which makes everything seem more relevant). His tests are all free response which is brutal but with him you can still get a decent score.  Definitely recommend

I took 6C with Bussey and all in all, he's probably the best professor I've had till yet. His lectures are brilliant and the notes(which I recommend you take cuz it's not too hard) are self explanatory. The class was enjoyable and the Chemistry I learnt from him ACTUALLY stayed in my head. Definitely recommend.

He gives 2 midterms and a final with a lot of sapling online homework, in class group work and discussion section group work so it is easy to bring up your grade if you do not do well on one of the exams. All of his exams are free response but he gives partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Extremely fair exams, honestly isn't trying to trick you. Never touched the textbook as he made very clear what he expected us to learn through lecture and homework. He's also very clear at explaining things, so overall definitely recommend him!

This guy really is an outstanding educator. He is explicit in both his grading criteria and exams. Homework is fair. He honestly turned what was basically my least favorite subject into my favorite. Re-watch the podcasts, exams are almost entirely based off of what was discussed in lecture. Thank you Dr. Bussey for making chem accessible to me.
Professor Bussey is literally the best professor I've ever had. If you aren't taking him at least once here at UCSD, you're messin up
Chill guy, helpful in office hours and approachable.

AMAZING Bussey is a great prof! The exams are straightforward. The practice problems are a great way to prep. He explains everything so well in lecture and does a ton of examples.
