There is only one group project in the end of the year, one midterm and a final, both open book and online. Does have homework and reflection every other week.

Readings before lecture was a lot but it genuinely helped me understand the material better. Two lab reports wasn't that bad but they will grade you harshly on those! Don't know your grade until the end but she curves. Exams are fair but be prepared to remember small things. I'd love to take her class again if I could, def one of the better profs.

Dr. Gus cares about the subject, but in an extreme level. She assigns workload as if this was our only class. Too much reading, clicker/math quizzes etc. She assigns points to everything. Tricky exams from tiny details. Low averages. Also she does not stop talking. Experiments were not finished due to her surprise lectures. Never ending stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Gus is a passionate lecturer, but her class is challenging, especially for non-bio majors. Exams are tough, covering specific details. Utilize Unstuck AI and other study tools to manage the workload.

Dr. Gus has a tendency to ramble during lectures. The exams are quite challenging as a lot of the test questions test on very specific information that I struggle to understand and recall. This course was particularly challenging for me as a non-biology major class, and I had to put in a lot of effort to study and get an A.

Need to attend lectures since recordings dont capture entire lectures shes always off-topic. 2 midterms worth 21 and 22% with hw being 25% (just reading articles and answering questions). Final worth 33%. PURE MEMORIZATION, memorize slides and videos she tells you to watch, do that and you can get at least an A-. u wont know your grade until end!!

Cindy is very caring and nice, but was often late to lecture which messed up the recordings for those who didn't show up and made those who came stay later. Her tests are also so annoying. She places information in the smallest text possible and tests you on it.

idc how many reviews you read. not only is this class graded difficulty and particularly but Professor Brown RANTSSSS and tests you on her rants. not to mention her lectures are boring. the curve is really nice but if you know what's good for you don't take this class. its DEFINITELY not graded or tested like a non science major course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Gus is really passionate about what she teaches. However, she adds a lot of assignments that were NOT listed in the syllabus. You are expected to write two 8+ page papers about your lab results while is really confusing and time consuming. The structure of the class is also a mess. She teaches content weeks after doing them in lab. Good luck...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr Gus is passionate and caring. She's an entertaining lecturer and knows her stuff. However, this class was a mess. We were doing labs and having the corresponding lecture weeks after. Doing labs with no prior context makes understanding everything very difficult. Exams are hard and she expects a lot out of you. Expect to put in a LOT of work.

By far one of the best classes I've taken at UC San Diego, very informative and interesting. Everything is fair game so be very thorough when studying for quizzes or exams as figures or even small details mentioned in the textbook or lecture can and have been asked about. Very content heavy but don't fall behind especially on reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She really cares about her students and is very passionate about biology. For a non-bio class, this one is more difficult than it needs to be but Dr. Gus's passion makes up for it! Homework is easy, but the tests are difficult and involve a lot of short answer/essay responses. Study hard, or take the class pass/no pass!

Wouldn't recommend. The material isn't super difficult but I didn't like the prof's teaching style. Homework is easy and you get 3 tries for it, but tests are very difficult and sometimes she added stuff that she told us wouldn't be on the exams. Course is curved, but I would recommend taking P/NP if you can. You have to pay 90 dollars for the HW

It's not difficult to get a good grade in Dr. Gus's class if you stay on top of your work. She assigns textbook readings and homework assignments, and the class has 2 midterms and a final. The class is curved as well. You also have to watch 2-3 films depending on the quarter. As a non-bio major, this class was great for my bio credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Gus is a great teacher and preps you to the best of her ability. She focuses on critical thinking rather than memorizing and her test reflect it. Lots of reading before and after class though so be ready. Also her exams are rough but in the end she standardized them to the average. Challenging class but great teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Pro Gustafson is a lovely lady. She is excellent for people who love bio; however if you want to pass this class for GE. IMPOSSIBLE. I am an art student and international student, and the level of this class is just not for people who are non-bio majors or don't have strong fundamentals of bio. She tests super complicated things on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great person but exams are graded super harshly. Could be disorganized but is knowledgeable on the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She knows what she's talking about. You have to read an entire textbook and take quizzes every week on 60-80 pages of the reading. If you can stay on top of this then you'll do fine in the course. She's extremely understanding so reach out to her for any questions or concerns.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She explained the material well but gave an unnecessary amount of work. Insane amounts of reading required despite the course material being very easy. Also made made us watch three films and read two scientific articles to significantly add to the already large workload. I recommend the course but not the professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Gus was very passionate about her material. Reccommended taking for pass no pass. She went above and beyond to clarify her lecture material and was eager to answer many of the students questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I took BILD 10 with Gus-Brown over the summer, and she has responded to the online format amazingly! I enjoy Gus-Brown's philosophy that emphasizes short, consistent studying each day instead of cramming. Each week, in addition to lectures, we were given bite-sized readings and mini-modules, and it made the material that much more approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: The reader is mandatory. Exams are on both material from lecture and reader; watch out for material from lecture that is not in the reader. Class material covers both SOCIAL and BIOLOGICAL aspects of HIV, prepare to memorize a lot. Outside of lecture she's fun to talk to and truly wants to get to know you.

Lectures are 1 hr and 20 minutes and she spends the entire hour doing clickers and does not highlight the correct answer when she posts them on Canvas. Going to class is a waste of time, if you just read the book you'll pass. Everything is based of the textbook and all she does is repeating textbook materials.

Dr. Gus as a person is wonderful person, but I take a lot of issues with her approach to academics. Much of her grading relies on whether or not you had "key phrases" in your answer instead of demonstrating subject material comprehension. No regrades, even if you were 100% incorrectly penalized, and NEVER covers all the lecture material in class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class itself is SUPER interesting, but the exams are SO HARD. There is a lot of information presented in the class to begin with and you really are expected to know every single bit of it, down to statistics, acronym names, disease, and pathogen names, etc. Definitely make sure to keep up with the class or you might get overwhelmed towards end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There is a lack of clarification in exams question especially section paper questions so beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: 5% are quiz clicker questions (need 72% to get all 5%) 5% are class clicker question (just need to answer 75% of this) Optional 10% are section paper (3 of them) 5% section participation (Show up to section) 20% final section paper optional 15% midterm exam 40%, 50%, or, 65% Final exam depending on the "optionals"
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This professor is AMAZING. I'm not good at biology, and when I enrolled in her class I was a little nervous because of her ratings. I took her summer session II course, and still managed to get a B in her class dedicating the recommended hours of studying each week. If you need help, just go to office hours. Cindy is MORE than happy to help!

This class is pretty hard, but if you commit the time to it, it's doable, and you will become terrified by the horrible ways microbes will find to kill you. I was dreading taking the class because I'm not interested in medicine, but it was still really cool to learn about all of the different things in the class.

Im 30 now, about 10 years out of school, and I STILL cite this class in discussions. Its one of my top 5 recommended classes at UCSD. Take microbiology lab with her too. Tough, frank, and interesting! I took her summer class so maybe it was a bit more intensive.
Great teacher. Interesting class. I would take her again.

One of the best and valuable teachers from the UCSD faculty that I've ver had. This HIV/AIDS class is not hard if you follow her advice and study for a little each week. If you wait, the readings and the material will be overwhelming because this course is very content-heavy. Other than keeping up, I found this class very fascinating and enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Wow. Absolutely one of the best teachers I've ever had. Yes the class was hard and yes I had to work a ton, but I learned so much. She made me so interested in the topics that I enjoyed the research and reading and lectures. I loved this class so so much and I would absolutely take another class with her as my prof.

Dr. Gus is an amazing lecturer and always held my attention despite it being a 6pm course. She cares a lot about the topic and posts A LOT of resources on her page for students who need extra help or would like additional outside reading. I will try to take more of her other courses, as she is an amazing professor and role model that I look up to.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She posts podcasts of her lectures, and class is only mandatory when guest speakers come, which is awesome because it allows flexibility when studying for other classes. She baked brownies for the class for finals, which is pretty cool I guess. I would definitely recommend her.

Too much workload! She makes us read 2 book chapters and 1 research paper every week, making it very hard to catch up. It is actually doable if you dont take any other classes that has workload, but considering that most students do, this class is So TIRING. Dr Gus is, despite all that, a nice lady. However, too much information jammed to class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Gus is a nice lady but her exams are tough.  They're mostly short answer/short essay and you're expected to memorize a lot of detail.  The weekly reading quizzes are ridiculously hard.  The material for the class is social/history, statistics/demographics, and the biology of AIDS.  IT'S A LOT OF READING, DON'T TAKE WITH OTHER HARD CLASSES!!

Dr. Gus is an amazing lecturer. She holds your attention and makes the material interesting, but only covers--at times--30% of it. The rest you have to read/learn on your own. A LOT of material/reading/work for a 4 unit class. Exams are long and very detailed. Would be no problem if this was the only class I was taking...

Professor Gustafson-Brown is great as a person. She is very like-able and tries to make lectures fun. BUT, when it comes to material she over complicates things and her exams are very long and she expects you to remember every single detail. I do not recommend taking this class with her.

Dr. Gus is the MOST interesting professor I've ever had; Only professor that kept me paying attention in lecture. She's the opposite of boring! So alive and energetic; has so much passion! She's a joker; lots of funny stories! Yet, the class is difficult. Lots of readings and YOU NEED TO KEEP UP. If you have the time, you'll absolutely love her!

Wonderful professor! I very nearly dropped the class before it started because I was scared of the grading distribution. But if you stay on top of everything, you're going to be fine. She's a very sweet person and really cares about her students. Would especially recommend class to publicglobal health majors. Best class I ever took at UCSD.

This class isn't hard. It's her ridiculous grading. The real reason people score badly in her classes is that she has so many ways to penalize you for every little thing. She does it to make you artificially lower her average and make you feel stupid. Avoid! Avoid! Avoid!

Wow this class is hard. You will read 2-3 research articles per week along with book readings as well as lecture slide material. You will write papers and be quizzed left and right. A VERY involved class but still by far one of the best at Ucsd: engaging and fun. Thanks dr g!

Great professor & lecturer, and you'll have a great time in her class if you get involved and go to OH's. But yes, BIMM 121 was a lot more work than it should have been for 4 units, as she acknowledged. And her questions/grading can be extremely detail oriented. But overall, you'll learn a lot and you can get an A if you put in the work.

Dr Gus is a FANTASTIC lecturer. This class has no peer in the BioSci dept, but it is every bit one of the most interesting upper div bio classes UCSD has to offer. She is crystal clear, her reader is interesting, her exams are fair... just keep up with the reading and film material, and you will do well.

Had Dr.Gus for BIMM 121 and 124. She is an AMAZING lecturer! Very clear and helpful and loves to tell you nerdy jokes/stories. These 2 classes are my favorite at UCSD. Both classes are definitely challenging but totally worth all the studying. It was really fun studying and reading for these classes too! Dr.Gus needs to teach more classes!!

Dr. Gus taught medical microbiology together with Dr. Aroian. Dr. Gus really knows her stuff and genuinely cares about the well-being of her students. Very accessible outside of class. The course was based in primary literature and very challenging. Thoroughly recommend it thought, since it teaches you to how think.

I've taken BICD 136 and BIMM121 with Dr. Gustafson. First thing first, shes is a very dynamic and engaging lecturer, probably one of the best I've seen. She makes you want to learn what she presents because she really loves what she's teaching. You will work harder then you have ever worked, but probably won't get above a B-. She's a GPA murderer.

Everyone on here keeps saying she's a really nice. Well how about this? She's not nice if she's assigning wholly unrealistic tasks for her class. The amount of hours required to get an "A" far exceed her allotted unit credits. We take classes with the understanding that the load will be fair & reasonable  compared to our other classes. Not cool.

Honestly, people give Dr. Gus a bad rap. To get an A in the class you have to get a solid 90% or higher. There is no curve. That being said, however, she DOES provide clear and thorough explanations. People are caught off-guard b/c she's nice. Just b/c she's nice doesn't mean she should dole out A's. Great professor. Tough grade

BEST PROFESSOR IVE HAD AT UCSD! Engaging, passionate, and genuinely interesteed in educating her students about AIDS and Global health. Grading/exams were VERY challenging but fair.DO NOT take for an easy A, take to learn the material!
On first impression, she was nice, but on final impression, she was not.
Avoid if possible.

Loved this class. Dr. Gus is a very clear and tells you all you need to know in class for the midterms. Don't buy the book because she doesn't refer to it. If you pay attention in class, you shoulD have no problem getting an A.

My bio class so far. Really interesting lectures. Exams are long and very specific so make sure you know your stuff. Love the guest speakers. Dr. Gus is so cute, it will feel like she's your mom not your professor that's how much she cares! Got an A+ in this class pretty easily. Make sure you do the reading!
Dr. Gus is the best!

Wow, this was seriously the best class I've taken at UCSD. She does make you memorize a LOT of detail for the tests, and it's NOT an easy A class, but def. manageable. The subject material is incredibly interesting and her lectures went by so fast. She did the funniest impressions of the HIV life cycle, it was hysterical! Take her without a doubt!

Heard that UCSD is not offering this class next year due to budget class which is a shame because I learned so much from the class. She holds you accntable for EVERYTHING found in lecture, movies, readings. If you don't go to class, at least listen to the podcasts. She really is like a mom.  Take her!!
I really like Dr. G's teaching style. Her tests are pretty straight forward if u focus on her lectures, and she's always happy to help out. I'm taking virology with Her :)

Wow! way too much material to memorize for a basic bio class. Test were extremely difficult, I recommend you do not take this class if you just want to get a GE requirement done! Take another class or professor.
Pretty tough class. You definitely need to study. But she is really passionate about what she teaches, and she really knows what she's talking about. Good Prof overall

The amount and detail and information expected of students is WAY beyond intro level. Tests are hard and information tested is mainly details barely gone over. This class was a headache and not at all enjoyable. Unless you are planning to major in bio or have a strong bio base to work off of then do not take this class
Dont take her for BILD 10. Shes an upper div. teacher and makes this class impossible if your just trying to get a GE done

This class is really interesting and Prof. Gus can hold your attention. You must do ALL the reading but her tests are really straight forward DO HER STUDY GUIDES. I liked her teaching style so much I plan on taking her Virology class which I had no interest in previously.

Dr. Gus is a great teacher. She is competent and articulate. There is a lot of material to know in BICD136 but it's really not that bad. The upper div AIDS class is so interesting, it was a great experience taking this class with Dr. Gus.

Compared to other Upper Division Biology courses, this class isn't as tough.  However, it's EASILY the most interesting Bio class I've taken (Human Bio major).  She's really sweet and helpful, and is crystal clear when lecturing.  Tests are detailed and include some minute details, but very doable if you don't procrastinate.

Dr. Gus is one of the best profs at UCSD. She's nice and very helpful if asked questions. There's a lot of material covered, but she's very knowledgeable and makes it interesting. The articles assigned enable you to connect what's being learned in lectures to the real world. Tests are detailed, but straightforward and doable if you put in the work.

Hard class, but not because of a good reason. Tests are nitpicky, and if you're like me, the questions that ask you information that can be looked up in five seconds on wiki will drive you crazy. Very little of the information learned is relevant for non-virology grad students. If you're a microbio major, tough luck - if not, pick another course.
I love Dr. Gus! lectures easy to follow, writes it out on the board, helpful in OH, cares about teaching, not intimidating, exams are very comprehensive but straightforward answers/no trick questions

She keeps the class very interesting. She is rude in emails. Be prepared for ~5 vids to watch before test, tons supplemental readings, text book info besides what she goes over in class. This class has TONS of stuff you have to do outside of class....seriously-TONS! There is a reason everyone else is saying this. Be prepared.

Love/Hate relationship w this class. I loved learning about everything taught in the class, but I hated how MUCH we had to know for the exams! This class is very interesting, and despite having to study a TON, I'm so glad I took this class. If you're not willing to dedicate time to this class, don't take it. It's a lot of work.

Her class was relatively difficult simply due to the enormous amount you had to not only write in lectures, but info memorized down to the minute details. Very informative and knowledgeable but I felt her standards for her tests were set exorbitantly high. Her study-aids were not exceedingly helpful and you really did not have to read the book.

Interesting class on AIDS. Be prepared to spend extra time on supplemental readings and videos. The material is easy to comprehend, and test questions are straight forward, but there is a lot of material to memorize.

Dr. Gus is NOT approachable. She appears to be nice but it's all fake. She writes rude emails back. She gives too much information that it is impossible to memorize all of it and her exams are too long. She doesn't give enough time to finish and she's super anal about cheating. She wastes so much paper by using them to cover the exam!

Dr Gus knew she was teaching a class that didn't really care about bio, so she taught us exactly what we needed to know. Really good teacher, I learned a lot, but her tests are tricky. Pay attention to the supplemental reading not the book reading. It seems stupid but she asks way more from it. Anything in the book she goes over in lecture.
This teacher is bent on details, and her TA's seemed to grade essay questions according to her specific words. Beware, this class requires hours of reading on top of studying

I actually was a TA for this class. Don't worry about the low averages. That just means that it's easier to beat if you study your lecture notes *regularly*. I liked her lecture style: Write main points on the board, elaborate on them, and provide visual aid through power point. Very passionate and helpful teacher. Take for P/NP if it's your GE.

THIS IS NOT AN EASY BIO FOR HUMANITIES KIDS BIO... TAKE BILD 1 IF YOU CAN. She expects you to know EVERYTHING. She's a nice lady and teaches this class like it's an elementary school class. Shoves a TON of information into last three lectures and expects you to know it all. HARD TESTS- ALL SHORT ANSWER- BUYER BEWARE OF HER...

The class average before the curve was a 62% which I think is a strong indication of what sort of professor she is. She asks for a lot of detail on exams that you were more likely to learn from the reading because lectures were all over the place at times. She was very intimidating and condescending toward students which made her unapproachable.
this is a non-major class and she makes it look like major class by asking so much details on the test. lectures are boring. would never take any class with her.
expects a lot of detail on exams. Midterm 1 had a class average of an F... Midterm 2 was a C... We'll see about the final.
Its a difficult class but it's very interesting and as long as you pay attention, an A is obtainable. She's very nice and helpful

I absolutely loved this professor/class. It is relatively difficult though, you have to go to lecture and take good notes to do well on the test but it is well worth it as the material is very interesting.

She always makes herself available to meet with students, but when I talked to her once she was kind of rude. I dropped this course after taking the midterm because that is 30% of your grade and the final is 60%. The midterm was impossible and was not at all reflective of study guides or class lectures. The subject matter is fascinating though.

Dr.Gus is awesome! Not only is she passionate about what she teaches but she's passionate that her students will actually learn what she's actually teaching. I took both her lower and upper division classes and they were my world. She's hard but i mean that's really what's college is about. Challenging yourself. and Dr. Gus is awesome.

virology is a difficult class. if you are taking this because you like AIDS class, then you're taking this class for the wrong reasons.  its nothing like that class.  its harder and more in depth.  if you're not required to take this class, you shouldn't.  its probably the most difficult bio class at ucsd.

Dr. Gus is sooo awesome. She's like a mom in lecture and she actually is a mom. She helps you, walks you through everything when you go to office hours. Her lectures are engaging and makes you wonder about the world. Material is interesting in of itself and she adds on to that. Dr. Gus is AWESOME!

You are expected to know every single minuscule point. What's more, most of her lectures are just exorbitantly lengthy lists of facts. For being a lower-div, non-major's class, you're expected to do a lot of work. The exams go into asinine detail. Very boring and she makes the class a lot harder than it needs to be.

Overall, an interesting class to take and Dr. Gus is a pretty good professor. However, it's definitely not an easy A class because you actually have to do legitimate studying. You have to go to class and do the readings because she tests on the most randomly specific questions. The midterm was so long and they graded very strictly. Tests are hard.

thot this was a class for non-majors.material is really interesting but it's all stuff i learned in ap bio in high school..i think that's what saved me.i don't want to say the exam was difficult/tricky but she definitely requires u to know everything down to the smallest detail. her ta(emily) was helpful & nice but is instructed to be a hard grader

this is a hard class.  personally, i would not take it if i wasn't a microbiology major.  if you want a challenging class, this is it.  otherwise, stick to nutrition or molecular basis.  micro majors are forced to take this so good luck.

Horrible professor.  1) she requires too much, exams on top of videos and papers  2) her grading is very strict, I felt I knew the topics well but if you didnt use the exact words she used its wrong, some of the TAs were kind graders so that was nice  3) She rushed the last 8 virus families in two lectures, something she allocated 1 lecture p
She wasn't helpful at all, I asked her a question and she wasn't willing to clarify. The material is very easy, but she wants specific words and examples on her exams which makes her exams difficult.

Professor Gus is absolutely wonderful. Every bio student should take her AIDS class. I learned SO MUCH from this class. She's very clear and knowledgable.. I think it's her first time teaching upper div but I think she did an awesome job. I recommend taking her classes! :)
On the annoying scale, her voice is the female equivalent to Gilbert Gottfried.

such an interesting class.  she really cares about what she teaches and the information is really interesting.  it's not an easy A class, but if you study well for the tests you can definetely get an A
I got an A+ w/out doing the last half of the bio book reading. I paid attention in the first half, the other book, and in class and got AS lecture notes instead. Just in case that helps anyone.

She's a good lecturer, however if you don't go to every lecture and write down everything she's saying, it won't help you on the midterm or final. She made an extremely comprehensive outline for the final (~22 pages typed out) and about 20% of it was on the exam. Hard and not very helpful.

Dr. Gus is to the max! She is very knowlegable and the class is very interesting. Much of the reading is the kind that goes by fast (like a novel-like memoir). I was extremely behind on bio knowelege compared to the rest of the class but the lectures/reading were so clear that it was no problem. Get AS lecture notes, there's a lot of info. Take it!

Good professor. Clear and interesting class but a lot of information to memorize in order to pass the midterm and final. going to lecture is important & actually readying the text is important. memorize everything or you are doomed. very specific tests.
The class is kind of hard, but the lectures are interesting and I always look forward to going to class.

Hard teacher, I had to struggle to even get a C+, which was bad because this was for my major.  She makes you memorize everything, especially little details, and even if you submit a regrade, she doesn't really give you many chances to let you appeal for questions (only 3!).  read the book and memorize her notes to try to get above the curve

She will make you memorize everything about viruses. I took this class for interest, I'm not pre-med, nor a bio major, so why the **** should i care what some the symptoms are called if you get sick with Hanta virus? I got the general picture, that your lungs get filled with fluid. But because i forgot the exact name, i can't get any points for it.
evil teacher, avoid her at all cost unless you want bad grades on your transcript.

Too much notes taking. Midterms are easy, but the final was very hard. Too much memorization. The point is if you memorize everthing on the notes you'll A's the test. But I don't think that's possible!!!

I took this lab class one quarter, all my labs were being graded as D's, so i dropped. Took it next quarter had the same labs submitted and got an A in the class, if you have a choice Do not take this professor, take M.Butler or Chilukuri.L

OK, considering this class is for NON bio majors, she makes this wayyyyyyyyyyyy too hard. the averages on the midterms were F and D and the final, the average was an F. and the final was REALLY hard... tests you on EVERYTHING she says in lecture, and the curve isn't that great either, take a diff teacher!
really knows her stuff but sometimes hard to follow in lecture, pay attn to all the little details bc the tests are evil and ask for information that she may have mentioned once offhand
Don't take her unless you want a C

Should be avoided at all cost, unless you feel that your GPA is too high! I still have nightmares about her and its been 6 months!  She seems really sweet but her tests are not only hard but poorly written.  Her grading scale is also horrible.  Our class avg. was under 50%
i really liked her for this class.  I heard she's tough for cell bio, but i think she's really sweet.. like a kindergarten teacher!  she's very approachable and a good prof with fair tests.

She's not mean like ppl say, Cellbio is a hard subject. Her MT was written quite rudimentarily, her final was a different story, I almost blackedout! anyhoo, i think her exams were OK! just her grading scale(avg) is WACKED! i wish i was a psych major, where the avgs are in the 50's and everyone gets A for stroking each other's ego, pre-meds my-azz!

She's very nice but don't let that fool u, her grading scale is wacked! I had her both for BIBC103 & BICD110: in lab, the avg. was 75% and that's a "C-" to get an A, you must get above 90%! mofo pos that's BS!the lab reports were easy to write b/c of her guideline, which tells you exactly what to write, don't be STUPID and stray from it! take Gould
nice

She is truly awful. I never knew material until about 2 days before the exams and that was learned from reading and review sessions. I went to every lecture and they were worthless. I had nightmares about failing this class that haunted me for 2 weeks. I ended up with an A- somehow, but the awful things she put me through scarred me for life.

what can I say about this lecturer, except that she's ****y and freaking hard. Her exams were poor written since she ran out all of good questions for her previous cell bio course. Do not take her if you want your GPA to remain the same or improve. Also, did I mention that she's mean and ****y? Trust me, I received my first B from this bio class.

I hated this prof-way too much detail, horribly confusing lecture style,too much reading, condescending witch, thinks the class is composed of grad students apparently, gets mad if averages are around 60 (normal!!)...just avoid at all costs.

The good: she speaks clearly and writes a fair amount of notes on the board.  The bad: tests are hard. reviews.comment: She uses something called skills based grading where instead of getting grades on individual assignments you demonstrate mastery of concepts. If you do well on quizzes and homework you don't have to take the final. She also does flipped classroom style so all the learning is from videos. Personally hated both of these systems but it's a fun class.

Syntax is a hard class -- HW takes a long time and is not intuitive. But her grading system reduced stress and made it much more manageable; midterm and final were like 'catchup points' not 'if you get a B, you'll never recover'. I didn't think her lectures were boring at all; I think she's one of the best professors I've had.

Shes not bad or anything, but I couldnt focus on any of her lectures. This was an issue because syntax almost killed me. I recommend going to office hours or section. The homework is once a week but very hard so PLEASE join a student homework group because if you try to do everything alone there is a chance you might fail. Trust me.

reviews.comment: This was her first quarter at UCSD and I applaud how smooth the course was. I'm not a linguistics major and this class was manageable if you take the time to review the lectures. Weekly homework but most of the answers can be found through the lectures. Final was long/hard but she generously curved the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Class was simple in the beginning and catches you off guard in an instant. Homework was pretty challenging at times (once spent over 10 hours working on one). Her examples are simple compared to the homework and exams. You will most likely try everything on google with no luck and a bunch PDFs to read through. Lectures are boring and Podcast-ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a great professor, only graded by a few things  that are the same every week: Discussion post, Weekly quiz (with three attempts), small writing opinion in class, and reply to discussion post. The class has only one midterm and one final. The final and midterm are only worth 15%, while the weekly quizzes are worth like 21%. Easy class for an A
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Phil 35: He is not a good lecturer (goes on rants and isn't concise), lecture participation is mandatory and there's extra credit for additional discussion posts. There are 2-4 readings (25+ pages) each week, the midterm guidelines are similar to the final (1 midterm/final), and there are multiple choice quizzes each week.

Took phil 181 with him. Lectures were really nice in the beginning but as the course went on I only went once a week. I think it was more the material i didn't care much for. in class assignment once a week, discussion post every week and quiz. But he gave a pdf of quiz on canvas and that helped me get through the readings. Lectures not recorded.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is my 2nd time taking Professor Tolley  He's very nice and talks about a lot of interesting topics in class and plays cool songs Everything is very doable if you pay attention in lecture and do the readings :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Weekly tests that are take home and due by friday and one final paper.  Lectures are extremely interesting and engaging.  Tolley is really open to what students have to say and, in a way, he allows the students to lead the discussion.
!) HE IS SO CUTE! 2) He is super helpful. 3) The topic is so interesting. Overall amazing teacher. Best teacher I have had so far.

This class can be very confusing, especially since professor tolley has such HORRIBLE handwriting. Overall though this class isn't too difficult if you get the gist of what he is saying on the material. Understand about 50% of what he's talking about and you'll do fine.

When you see him writing notes on the board, don't worry, you don't have glaucoma, literally it is unreadable and there are NO lecture slides, 1 midterm, 1 final, both take home papers, i dont know how good of a grader he is because I havent finished the course yet, im only doing this because im procrastinating on one of his papers as we speak
One of the best professors I've ever had and probably will ever have. I never want to miss class. He's smart AND hot!

Very laid back, patient, and friendly.  He does not give very definitive answers though and his notes on the board are disorganized.  He is a very fair grader though and willing to help students as best he can.  Very nice guy.

Great guy, brilliant, very highly recommended. 1 midterm and 1 final-both papers. If you take good notes (and make way through his penmanship) you'll get an A. I thought this class would be terrible but Dr. Tolley is a great chill guy and made it interesting. Take him for any class!

A pretty clear lecturer who's passionate about his subject matter. Presents material in a straightforward, historical manner that doesn't betray much of his own beliefs, actually. I did need to read the book pretty carefully and his class has been moderately difficult.

I thought it would be at least a semi-interesting class, and it was, until I realized he believes everything Descartes says. May want to check out what's going to be covered (such as Meditations) before you decide to take his class.

Seems like he really enjoys teaching and the grade rubric is not harsh at all. Attending lectures is helpful and he tries hard to explain the materials for you to understand. He does leave you with more questions than answers but that's probably the whole point. It's a philosophy class--he doesn't demand one absolute answer to everything
No Comments

Not the greatest professor I've ever had.  He tends to over-complicate simple concepts quite a bit.  I'm a philosophy major who took this same subject matter in upper-division depth and detail, and it is not as weird or hard as he makes it out to be.  He's kind of like an episode of "LOST": he leaves more questions than he give answers.
extremely engaging and actually excited to talk about his interests with students.   he is very capable of explaining difficult material in a straight forward manner.
Truly the most engaging math lecturer I've ever taken. 10/10 would recommend. Great at giving advice: straightforward and honest but caring and kind. truly a model professor
This is one of the most densely packed course I've ever taken. The content he goes over in class doesn't nearly prepare you for the homeworks or the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good lecturer, energetic and clear.

Professor Cloninger makes complicated concepts accessible, and he is responsive to feedbacks. HWs involve a lot of coding (not just playing around with parameters but writing from scratch), which is surprising since the prerequisite doesn't require any coding background.

no midterm and weekly hw assignments every week. Wish more respect was given to the science of teaching. For hearing these things for the first time flow of information feels ironically unoptimized. There were not many visuals time is spent writing on the chalkboard every lecture

Personally felt like the flow of information in lectures, as an audience member hearing these ideas for the first time, wasn't super coherent, and felt like lecture material did not prepare us nearly enough for the difficulty of weekly homeworks. Besides that he's a swell guy

Well, the grades are out, he ended up adding 10 points to everyone's exam which is only worth 30% of your grade. Grading was one of the least strict I have ever seen in the math department so far (probably because the exam was hard). But anyways, he made our Christmas merry. Thanks Prof!
Just took his final exam and I can only say one word: RUN!

Great guy, very friendly and approachable, will answer your questions & clear up any confusion. Book isn't necessary but helps (personally I didn't use it that much). All math teachers work together (so all math10A prof. work together). The grading,hw,quizzes,& midterms assigned is the same for all professors. Lecture style is only difference rly.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Quizzes and tests really didn't reflect the homework or lecture, so make sure you practice really difficult examples ahead of time, or you'll drown. Other than that, super nice guy and answers everyone's questions. I'd take him again but with these things in mind.

If I could take every math class with Professor Cloninger I would. His lectures were so helpful for exams so please make sure to watch and take notes. A few curveball questions but he drops low grades in the end so its fine. Super chill guy; he was understanding, welcoming, and accommodating. One of the best professors at UCSD.
Didnt attend lectures. Course material probably wasnt that helpful in preparing for actual Calculus work, but a free A is a free A. Quizzes and tests manageable even without prep.

I thought Professor Cloninger was a good guy. The quizzes were bit or miss in terms of difficulty, and the tests were pretty difficult. But, I felt pretty well prepared heading into the tests, and the workload is definitely manageable.

Prof Cloninger is probably my favorite math prof ever! He always stays behind after class for almost half an hour answering questions, and is constantly listening to feedback. He let us drop one test + two quizzes, and added 20% to each of our quiz grades when we complained about them being too hard. Also has a cute cat.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Cloninger listens to his students and is open to recommendations/advice. Struggled in the beginning but going strong. His handwriting isn't that good tho. Attend lectures/discussions to get a good grade. Easygoing guy and is understanding. Class itself is hard. Accessible by email, always willing to help students. HW weekly, 6 quizzes, 3 midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dont get afraid of Ave GPA posted on Evaluation, take him if you could. He gives good lectures and let you know clearly what he is expected from you. His midterms are piece of cake, but you do have to work hard for Final. The Final was intense and calculation heavy but if you know materials well, you should be fine, because he gives good partials.

I had difficulty surviving this class due to many personal factors but Cloninger was very helpful and cared for his students. I thought I was going to fail this course but his curve helped out in getting me to pass. Although the class, homework, and exams were all tough, I respect Cloninger for his humanity. I do also love some of the work he does.

I dont think Ive learned a lot. Possibly since Im just not so interested in the topics. However his exams were pretty easy and I didnt spend much time studying but still ended up with an A-. Some HW assignments took me hours but the TAs were very helpful.

Overall a great professor. Exams were 75% HW / 25% Past exam problems. Very good and informative lectures. Podcasted lectures, which he mentioned he might not do again. Homework load was a little heavy at times, lots of material covered. Skipped around the textbook too much, sometimes I had to go read previous chapter to know what was going on

Cloninger is passionate about his profession and keeps his lectures very focused on the class itself. Ht goes through the material pretty quickly, but is open to questions and he writes his notes in a way that makes it very easy to take notes. Although I didn't like the class every much he is a great professor that I would recommend to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: such a great math professor! he made everything understandable and i wouldn't doubt that it transfers to all of the other math classes he teaches beside from the one i took. he's really fair and supportive and the tests reflect his teachings and review!! :)
great professor ever
Honestly enjoyed a math class for the first time. He introduces practical applications for the material and it makes lecture intriguing.
He is amazing! His lectures are so clear and easily understandable. Exams are based on lectures and he also provides a lot of practice exams.
Professor Cloninger is amazing! The curve of is super generous and he's supper nice and helpful in office hour!

Professor Cloninger really really cares about his students. There were so many times I couldn't make his office hours and he would constantly set up different times just to help me out. He curved the class so everyone should pass. If you didn't, you're probably lazy. The material is tough and he is aware. He uses surveys to see how well he is doing
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Cloninger was an EXCELLENT professor. He explains all of the concepts clearly and concisely, and he's willing to go over topics multiple times the class doesn't understand. He's extremely friendly and approachable, and his tests are extremely straight-forward. If you pay attention and ask for help when you need it, the class is easy
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Amazing. I dont know whats going on on the blackboard. Math is hard enough, and professor cloninger is trying his best to make it harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Cloninger is a very smart and passionate professor and its obvious that he likes to teach what he teaches. This in itself makes it easy to understand and comprehend his lectures. He makes it a point to remind students about homework due and cares a lot about how his students are doing in the class. While he may talk very fast, hes pretty good!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Cloninger is an exceptional instructor, and I would recommend him to everyone interested taking any of his future classes. He not only explains every concept clearly, but he also makes sure that everyone understands these same concept by constantly answering questions for anyone confused. If you want to learn, he'll guide you along the way.

Took her for the "Tropical Disease" class. Love her, she's such a great lecturer. She also has supplemental lectures that she records, which are great when going for a walk to go over the readings. It's a lot of reading, but you don't need to read all of them to do well. I got an A+ due to the extra credit she gave at the end. Certified mother.

Literally just take the class if you guys are wondering if you should. She is the easiest history teacher you will find and she is so nice. It's clear that she cares about her students and literally she barely gives out any homework. There are group discussions but they're so easy. Take it, its such easy credit!!

"woke"? lmao that comment makes me mad oml. bro doesnt know the meaning of the word. This class is so eye opening, the prof is very passionate and amazing at lecturing, this class talks a lot about decolonization and provides a lot of different perspectives through different mediums to really communicate how decolonization has shaped society. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: interesting and super well rounded class, not very woke, no tests but there are some well paced projects. You can tell Prof Edington puts a lot of effort into this class, lovely course, lovely professor

I loved this class so much! If you're thinking of taking her class, just do it. She is very engaging when lecturing and sooo easygoing. There isn't a lot of homework AT ALL, the main thing she has students do is read the material before she presents it in class. Even if you don't read it, it's still clear to understand when she's teaching it later.

It was personally difficult to obtain all lecture material as she does not provide recordings. However, she is extremely understanding and caring, as well as willing to help if you put in the effort to reach out. She truly cares about the material she teaches as well.

One of my favorite professors at UCSD! The class is well structured and Professor Edington sets up the course with core themes that are weaved throughout the lectures + brought up again during written exams. Had a very flexible late policy (could be up to 2 days late for all assignments). Highly recommend any of Professor Edington's classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Edington has been the most caring and supportive teacher I have had here at UCSD. She is so sweet and does not make the class more difficult than it has to be. She is available outside of class and has offered resources and opportunities to students who ask. She grades fairly and offers tons of support and feedback.

She is nice and cares for students. The class was interesting and you learn about colonized populations and their struggles under imperialism. Lots of reading!!! We have to read every week + take a quiz before class. This is a smaller class, set up more like a discussion where we talk about the readings. Midterm essay and final essay! Easy class!
I really liked her, but she is very inaccessible outside of class; she never responded to any of my emails.

She is the most amazing lady I ever met during my first quarter of college. Speaks French. Very flexible and kind. And her TA is awesome too. You will have to read and write a discussion prompt every two weeks, but it is easy if you listen to the lecture.

Honestly, she and her TA Matt were the most accommodating during COVID. I wish I could stay in her classes forever. I learned a lot about history and untold stories. She shifts the narrative from European ideas to other stories that need to be told.
Prof. Edington made history a fun, interesting topic. Easy A if you go to lectures/discussion. Not the best lecturer but will seriously make you consider changing your major to history.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT--Would take again

reviews.comment: Claus' class was wonderful. The class became much more difficult at the midterm, which is good to be ready for. It's clear that he truly cares about students and their learning. I hope he teaches more undergraduate courses in the future. Definitely take him if you can.
Excellent lecture quality.

Dr. Sorensen is great. He gives very organized, well-paced and detailed lectures. It is important to closely follow everything he writes because of how precisely he structures it. He does not always present conceptual interpretations though. He typed his own notes for the course which are as good as any textbook. He's also a really nice dude.

Excellent professor for algebra. Lectures are well-organized and useful. HW is tough, but TAs/prof office hours give lots of hints/details. Exams are fair if you study lectures and HW problems (recommended ones too).

Although he is a nice professor, I would not recommend his class. He is a really smart guy and he has a very high expectation of his students so he doesn't explain his examples because they are "obvious" to him. Definitely go to discussions if you want to pass. I did not learn anything from the professor, or from the textbook that he wrote.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clearly intelligent, but addled by expert syndrome. His lectures lack effective pedagogy and he rarely understands the point of view the students are coming from. Simple questions about material are answered with vagueness and arrogance. "You need sample problems? This is easy. Just study." I don't blame Sorensen, this is a pattern in UCSD Math dep
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: he's awesome, always walk out of his lectures with a smile. super lucid lecturer, and more than happy to answer every question.

Sorensen covers way too many topics and I easily get lost in class and don't know what to focus on. A LOT OF hard homework and I can only finish 80% myself. Exams feel OK but I got low scores, but everyone did badly so that's fine, and he did curve very generously. I was completely lost taking 103AB with him, and I'm so glad I'm done with it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof Sorensen's lectures are tough. He writes everything on the blackboard and you should be ready to keep taking notes, however, it's hard to follow him when I am coping. Alternative is you focus on listening and take photos of his notes. It's helpful to preview the materials before lectures, otherwise I cannot catch up. A lot of hard homework.

Prof Sorensen is definitely a good lecturer. His lecture is very well organized and gives many examples to explain concepts. His exams are very fair. Easy A if you attend the lecture and do the homework.

Lectures were somehow lack of logic so easy to get lost. As one comment here says, you have to keep taking notes and have no time to think. A LOT OF homework, some make take more than 15 hours to do. Midterm and finals are fair though (for my quarter, some of the previous finals were pretty tough).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Definitely don't recommend Professor Claus' class because he is not a good lecturer; especially, in his class, students are forced to keep taking note and don't have time to actually learn; other than that, he does't focus on concept and often only talks about examples. I honestly don't like him, and I regret it so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's not a bad lecturer. And his proof in class is clear and rigorous. But I feel like he regards us freshmen as graduate students. To be specific, his lecture is mostly proof based but one must practice a lot to do well in his two midterms. He should have informed us of this on the first day.

Professor Sorensen is a super smart guy so be prepared before his lecture. 103A is not hard at all. TAKE NOTES and do some practice problems you would be fine. Also he is handsome. So don't skip class.
Modern algebra is a hard class. He is trying to make everything simple. Exams are easier than the homework.

Class has changed the way I view math. Extremely tough class. Hard tests. Long homework assignments. Do not skip a single class and attend every discussion session if possible. Lectures are mostly proof-based, but they give you a good understanding of the material. Overall though, this class has taught me a lot this quarter; do take it!

His proof were not always clear but were fair enough. I believe he could have address the class in better ways. His test are a mixture of fair questions that reflect the material and a few questions that are almost impossible to solve. I went to his office hours and he seemed to always be busy, it would be great if he was more available to students

I feel sorry for Sorensen.  He cares a lot about his students, but is a TERRIBLE lecturer.    The concept matter in 20F isn't very hard, but he makes it much more complicated than it should be.  Midterms are nothing like the homework.  Learn EVERY section out of the book before going to class.

Need to pay attention and actually do the homework. Go to discussion that saved my life. The tests were somewhat fair but nonetheless pretty difficult. You have to study and know what is going on in order to pass.

Avoid like the plague. He is really confusing, lectures are spent proving theorems rather than explaining their uses making homework a massive struggle. Abstract jargon language, he literally talks like a poorly written textbook making it impossible to follow. Exams alway need more time then allotted. I wish i took 20F with anyone else.

104A isn't a very easy class but Prof. Sorenson is a very helpful and easy professor. He doesn't want you to have to memorize everything so all exams are open notes, book, HW, and basically anything other than electronics. He is also very concerned about students learning the material and pauses for questions. I highly recommend taking him.

Besides being the best looking prof I've ever had, he's also a great teacher! He has perfect handwriting, and he always stops to ask for questions. He doesn't have any accent worth mentioning. He's also really helpful in office hours. I definitely recommend him!

Professor Sorensen will take time to help you if you go to his office hours. But like the rest of the reviews, he is a pretty bad lecturer. He mumbles, and has an accent.Homework is difficult (I spent a lot of time in the APM room) But if this is your last option I would still take it rather than being behind in my math sequence

Absolutely terrible. Just listen to all the comments below, they sum it up pretty well. Except for the two fake reviews probably written by Sorensen himself. The only good part was that everyone failed so drastically that he made an insane curve. I got somewhere around 40% in the class and it curved up to an 88%. Yes, he's that bad.

First of all, he has this accent (I think Danish)and he mumbles A LOT! You can barely hear him and if you do hear him, you can't understand him. He doesn't teach. He talks like a textbook. I eventually saved myself from failing by teaching myself straight from reading the book (so much better). TA's have much more clarity and are alot more helpful.
Confusing, boring, difficult.  Nice guy but its obvious he's here to research, not teach.

First half of the course is pretty much review of AP Calc AB. Second half of the course was dreadful. Sorensen isn't really great at explaining and mumbles a lot. Reading the text and looking at the examples in the book is much more helpful. On the plus side, he has really neat handwriting and all the exams are curved ^^.
Terrible, hard to understand and recites the book. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Like others have said, he just recites from the textbook while somehow making it more difficult to understand. Just read the book, don't bother going to class. His mid-term reviews have been good so far, but the mid-terms have always had 1 problem that wasn't on the homework, but was covered in class.
Claus is amazing. Easy class, hilarious lectures. Take him.

Claus is literally amazing. He usually does a great job of explaining general lessons, and if you have a basic understanding of the lessons and the book, you should do fine on the exams. Note: he drops one of the exams if you do better on the final, so its's really not too hard. Analogously, other math classes are not as good in my opinion.
Seriously the worst teacher I have ever had. Horrible at teaching, only does proofs and cannot explain anything.

I am not a fan of Professor Sorensen.  He is a nice guy, but not a great professor. His lectures are just direct copies from the book that he writes on the board.  When asked questions, he doesn't directly answer them. Basically, he doesn't teach, he just reiterates what the textbook says (badly), gives us difficult homework and mumbles.
Claus is not so good.

This is a very bad professor. He is very hard to understand and does no real examples, only proofs. He leaves out many steps for solving problems because he can do them in his head and it is up to you to puzzle everything together and try to figure out what is even going on. You must self teach heavily in this class or you will fail.
His class is easy. Lectures are easy to understand and he is very clear and precise.
Very hard to understand, rushes through all his lectures and leaves everyone confused. DON'T TAKE HIS CLASS
Math is hard

Very knowledgeable and passionate to help students understand. Tests reflect PS and practice exams pretty well + she gives a lot of extra credit thru case studies/disc attend. Clickers used in class, but helpful for engaging with/practicing material. BIMM100 is a tough class, but if you use her resources + put in work, it is worth it.
it is clear she is a very smart woman but she cannot teach
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Know mechanisms REALLY well, tested on malfunction. Focus on PS and practice exams ONLY, some pre-lecture videos of experiments make it into the exam. DO ALL THE EC (5%) - allowed to miss 2 classes. If you do all EC and attend class you'd need to avg 82's on both exams. Only 2 exams, no final. She's nice but doesn't teach how to apply lecture to PS

Her lectures are really hard to follow because she speaks very quietly. The exams don't match what she teaches or the practice problems, which makes them confusing and unfair. Most of your grade comes from just two exams, so it's very stressful. I wouldn't recommend taking her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst experience, I've had as a student. Lectures are reading off slides, problems sets are hard, and 80 percent of your grade is two incredibly difficult exams that the coursework doesn't prepare you for. I'm also not convinced she cares if students do well. FYI, her class MEDIAN on the first midterm was a 66, and she only bumped it to a C-
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DON'T TAKE HER. She doesn't understand the material herself, bluffing/stuttering throughout the lectures. Imagine lecture is 1 + 1, which you have to rewatch multiple times, then HW is calculus. Discussion tells you to ChatGPT. Exam is finding the velocity of the sun. Can't explain, only facts,but expect student to UNDERSTAND & apply bs questions.

if you put in the work the class is not too bad. While the lectures themselves might not teach you how to answer the questions, she spends a third of the class time going over problems and how to solve them. She's very sweet, and if you take the time to ask her what you don't understand it will make your life much easier.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She teaches as if she doesn't know the material herself, can't get a clear sentence out, and lectures at a whisper. Tests and homework don't reflect the material she teaches in lecture. Even if you are a good student, good luck.
SLOW lectures. Can not understand anything in class. Discussions not helpful at all. Exams- super hard. Avoid her at all cost.

Lectures are extremely boring and slow, found myself going back and watching them at 2x speed. Exams are very difficult, discussions and office hours aren't helpful. Does not offer helpful advice on how to do well. She's just not it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ratings are real, guys. Don't take her if you care about your grade and lecture quality. She can't explain well of the mechanisms and details, I feel confused at most of time in class. The midterm doesn't reflect the course materials, including the slides, the PS, and the practice exams, that makes feel like learning a completely new thing.

Dr. Cook-Andersen is the sweetest and most admiral professor I've had at UCSD. I would take her over any other BIMM professor. The classes content is super interesting but not the easiest. Focus on the problem sets and practice exams, they are the most representative of exam material.

This course is HARD. The concepts are hard, and studying is essential. I did all assignments, went to all discussions, and rewatched all the lectures and still failed every test. She allowed us to retake the exam for 1/2 credit to improve our scores. Extra credit is also available. I still ended up with a B thanks to the curve/E.C.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Cook-Andersen is super knowledgeable and does her best to make lectures interesting even though the material can get a little dense. go to class!! go to your discussion section!!! grading is clear and fair with wiggle room for low test averages. definitely would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: i dont even need to say anything besides that if u take this class you will spend 10 weeks hating biology imagine testing on a concept and then combining it with 4 other concepts but not giving clear/concise information on where these concepts are applied and not teaching it in class either class so good bro makes me wanna commit apoptosis
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take her class if you care about your GPA. She is nice and she does give extra credit, but her tests and homeworks do not reflect the material she teaches in class.

The homework assignments were optional which I was grateful for at the beginning of the quarter but I definitely would have been able to get a higher grade if I actually did the assignments. But even without them I was able to get a decent grade just from watching her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: While a good professor in the sense that she's very nice and good at teaching, she does not cover what she tests on the exams for the most part. Her exams are somewhat difficult and without a curve it is nearly impossible to achieve an A grade in this class. Avoid if you plan on going to medical school/grad school!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Even though she is super nice as a person, her lectures do not match the exams. The material she covers in lecture is a lot easier than the exams which are multiple part free response questions. She does not cover how to apply the concepts she teaches which makes her problem sets and exams difficult. She does offer some extra credit.

Professor Cook-Anderson gives lectures that are perfectly understandable but her exams and her problem sets are much much harder than what she teaches. I read the textbook and have gone over her lectures numerous times but when it comes to the exams they are almost completely different from what she teaches. Oh ya your grade is based on only exams.

YOU MUST TAKE THIS CLASS! This class was really chill and attendance is not required, lectures are not recorded but the slides are clear to review and learn. He really passionate in his own study field. Exams are all MCQs really easy less time consuming.

TAKE THIS CLASS. Professor Cook is the best professor I have had at UCSD. He is so kind and genuinely cares about his students. He is actually passionate about what he teaches and who he is teaching it to. Take this class if you want to have a fun time, learn some pretty cool things about volcanoes, and leave with some friends.

Prime example why you should not trust RMP. Worst professor I have ever had. The only positive I could say is that his class is not that difficult, however he makes the course difficult for students out of spite.

Genuinely the best professor ive ever had the joy of taken. Extremely passionate in his work, made every single lecture interesting and engaging, wonderful funny and kind guy, labs were kind of tedious with the work but was feasible every time. I miss this guy. Take him if possible.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Cares about what students are interested in learning about and what students struggle with. His lectures are amazing; very informative and descriptive. Nothing about this course was difficult to me in any way.

I took his GS(global seminar) class when studying abroad this summer. He 100% meets the expectations that r written everywhere in any ratings students give him. He made Switzerland fun; I recommend it for students to go there! iI happy I'll still have close ties with him/his wife- they r AMAZING PPL!!

Very passionate about his subject. I took his seminar on rocks and had a lot of fun. The assignments are just writing a bit about what you learnt every class and thats it. Doesnt take any time, just attend the seminars and you'll learn a lot
Just had to show up to class to get a P!

Took a seminar about minerals with very little prior knowledge and Professor Cook made it extremely engaging and enjoyable! Attendance is mandatory, if you miss 1 seminar you can't pass the class. VERY small weekly writing assignments that could be done in less than 5 minutes. 10/10! (Grade is P/NP)

Professor Cook is very passionate and enthusiastic about this course's material, so lectures were always enjoyable! Lectures are not mandatory, but they are also NOT recorded! Weekly assignments were easy and engaging, work overall is very light and manageable, 10/10!

Professor Cook is an amazing professor. You can tell that he truly is passionate about what he teaches. He truly cares about his students and even sends emails to us reminding us of assignment that are due. Would 100% take again.
Took his Volcano first year seminar, very fun and engaging, attendance mandatory, pretty easy reflection questions every week, but very interesting and fun intro to a fun topic

Prof Cook is very caring to all his students. He made sure to check in with us multiple times. Its a smaller class so he really tries to get to know just about everybody. As a geoscience major myself, he is so helpful because he is the advisor for the major. The mandatory field trip for the class is such a cool experience. Lectures are engaging.
Take him! Literally the best professor

I took Professor Cook's minerals seminar and he made the class really fun by showcasing various specimens from both the school's and his own collection while explaining their characteristics along the way. You will have to write a short essay every week to get a pass, but don't worry about it. It was like a weekly museum trip.
He is very passionate about material, which keeps me engaged and excited to go to class. Weekly assignments and quizzes were very manageable.

Course content is clear and manageable. Lectures aren't mandatory but they also aren't recorded. It was honestly a really fun and engaging and easy class with a light course load. Professor Cook is awesome and you can tell he really loves what he does. Be prepared for volcano noises and videos.
Caring and entertaining professor, weekly readings, discussion, and quiz which are all easy. Grade mostly relies on midterm and final and homework but all very easy, loved this class
The BEST Professor Ever.

Amazing prof, definitely take him if you can! Very passionate and cares a lot about us students. Super flexible and understands/enjoys concepts he teaches! Tests/quizzes were on material taught in lecture or in the textbook :)

Cook is very passionate about geology and you can tell he enjoys teaching. Lectures are pretty straight forward. One midterm week 5 and weekly open book online reading quizzes. Would highly recommend this class.

Prof Cook is the nicest professor I've had yet. He really cares about the wellbeing and success of his students. Weekly quizzes are super easy, you just have to do the reading (like one/two chapters) and pay attention in lecture. Since this was a weird COVID online class everything was open note/book which definitely helped.

one of the best professors ever. super accessible outside class, just send him an email and he'll find time to talk whatever. really wish to know him more in person so i'll absolutely take his other classes. so passionate about teaching.
The professor is passionate about the subject and is really nice. Took this in summer and the reading is a lot. But if you do the reading+work you will pass.

Professor Cook is such an animated guy, he truly cares about volcanoes and it shows in how he presents lectures. We focused mainly on ways to avoid volcanic hazards; he made it fascinating with volcanic footage that he would play during lectures. Even in an online format, Professor Cook made me absolutely fall in love with volcanology!

Would absolutely recommend taking a class with Prof. Cook!! His lectures are great, and you can tell he's genuinely passionate about his subject and about teaching it to other people. Super sweet and knowledgeable, too. 10/10 would take again :-)
huge dork, in the best way possible. he gets so excited showing us his rock and mineral collection. he mentions his wife and daughter a lot which i think is also adorable. amazing guy. take!

Took the Freshman Seminar "Treasures of the Earth: Minerals, Crystals and Gems" 10/10 class and professor. Really loves the material, and is brings up interesting topics all the time. Even brought a bunch of stuff to show the class from his personal collection!

By far one of the best professors I have ever had. He is incredibly passionate about the subject as well as very knowledgeable. He is super helpful and understanding and will make time to meet with you outside of class if you need help. I'm not a science major, but I still loved this class and highly recommend taking one of his courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: It was a super fun class! You could see his passion for volcanoes. Do come to class because there will be pop quizzes (but he will warn you a few days in advance and tell you what to study). Part of the final you present about a volcano you find interesting which I thought was pretty cool. Overall, really great guy and cares about his students!

Super sweet guy who is passionate about what he is teaching! The class is primarily based on your labs which are graded pretty leniently since they understand that we are just learning. We were required to bring the textbook just for identification for lab. Always straight forward, do the tritoned quizzes if he has any

Absolutely the best professor at UCSD. Very passionate and enthusiastic. Must take his class before you graduated from UCSD. Show his respect and care for students. HIGHLY RECOMMEND. You won't regret your choice. I would definitely take more his classes even though I am not an SIO major, but Cook worth.

Super nice guy and very helpful! I was scared I wasn't doing too well on the labs but a lot of people struggle with that and TAs are really accessible. You don't really need to go to class but it helps out a lot because there are some things he goes over in class that is not on the slides. We also get to go camping which is really fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Absolutely one of the best professors I have had so far. He knows his material well and is very passionate about his subject. He is nice and always helpful. Lectures are interesting and informative. The lab portion of the class has a lot of worksheet like excersises that can add up and take time, but are not a big deal. BEST CLASS!

My favorite professor and class of all time. He is super nice and funny and knows how to make a supposedly boring topic super interesting. He gives easy in class assignments and online ones, but it's mostly graded on participation and attendance. Tests were easy, however, he passes back a lot of papers so that's annoying. I would highly recommend.

Geoffrey Cook is one of the best professors at UCSD. He loves teaching and truly cares about his students. Even if you are not required to take any of his courses you should at least try out one of his freshman seminars to see what a great professor is like. I intend to take as many of his classes as I can and I wish he would adopt me.

Always show up to lecture as he randomly gives out extra credit for attendance, especially on lectures that are close to holidays like Halloween and Thanksgiving. Strong professor who is passionate about the subject, especially volcanoes!! Lab for the class was the harder part.

Although I'm a engineering student,  I love this professor and his seminar! He's sooooo passionate about his topic and can always tell students a lot of story about his collection of stones. If you are a freshman, please try his seminar! I've decided to take his SIO 50 after taking his seminar in two quarters.

Professor Cook is precious! The amount of energy he brings into the room is comforting, and the passion he has for the material definitely shows. I left this quarter knowing more about volcanoes than I expected, and I wish we had more time to learn more. He is approachable and wants the best for his students. I would recommend taking this class!
Enthusiastic and passionate about material. Really wants everyone to pass. Go to class, don't break his heart, easy A.
He inspired me to change from Literature to Earth Sciences. Awesome professor. I would always recommend his classes. He is always trying to help students and helped me get a research internship,
HE IS SO AWESOME! He is truly passionate about what he teaches and is the most understanding professor I have ever taken. AMAZING PROFESSOR!

Geoff Cook is by far the best professor I have ever had. He is so incredibly passionate about geology (especially volcanoes) which makes his lectures really engaging. He is super approachable and friendly, and always willing to work with you if you are having difficulty. He's the best!
