He starts out with many volcano videos (wish he had more throughout the quarter), but most of the quarter he uses powerpoints with many cool pictures of volcanoes and supplements that with making volcano explosion noises to give the class an idea of what the picture of the volcano sounds like.  Overall it was a super cool and interesting class.

He is sooooo passionate. He knows about the material very well. You won't get boring during the class. He also have a field which was very interesting and I we learned a lot. Take the class and enjoy your life
He was an all around swell guy, not one of the professors that you regret meeting with. His lectures were entertaining and he was very enthusiastic and knowledgeable of the subject.

He keeps lectures short, is very enthusiastic about the topic, and makes the class interesting. The content is easy (including homeworks and exams) and he takes the time out of class to do volcano experiments. I would definitely take him again.

One of the best professors, if not the best, I've had all of my years at UCSD! He is so passionate about what he teaches. Super funny, but doesn't even try, which makes him so cute :) Midterm and final were really easy. 6 unit class but feels like a 4 or 3 unit. Plus theres a cool weekend fieldtrip. TAKE HIM!!

Very good teacher. Pretty easy and extremely helpful. Made me interested in Volcanoes and want to pursue the subject. Tests are the same as what he teaches, and the homework is easy. He's super nice and a great teacher!
Geoff and Heather were an amazing teaching duo. The class was interesting and fun. Couldn't have taken it with a better professor.

Amazing professor. My favorite professor by far at UC San Diego. Taking his class has inspired me to pursue further into the earth sciences field. I can't stress how important his enthusiasm for his study kept students alert and attentive in class. I look forward to taking another course with him in the future.

Wonderful professor. Very enthusiastic about topic. Readily answers any questions students have. Very approachable. Keeps lecture fresh with humor and witty remarks. Homeworks are simple, he refers you to internet sources to find answers. Exam was easy. Wish more professors were like this guy. Two thumbs up!!

Dr. Root is a really kind person. The class is flipped and the material is so dense that people tend to cram their entire cheat sheet. Unfortunately, it feels like the class is more of a "how detailed can you make your cheat sheet and retrieve the information" class rather than a class built on memorization and memorization.

Flipped classroom style. He doesn't really care about teaching. Lots of typos and mistakes in his pre-recorded lectures. In-person lectures are mundane, and he lets everyone talk over him. Allows cheat sheet (1-sided for midterm & 2-sided for final) which is very helpful. Exam questions are very similar to his practice tests. Easy but boring class.

flipped lecture classroom, cheat sheets for midterms and finals, and good feedback is given. he gives a lot of practice material to prepare you for the exams so you know what to expect. the discussion style lectures were lackluster, he lets everyone talk over him and he isn't very engaging. interesting material though.

Really great professor with the reverse classroom thing. He is very kind and willing to help when you ask or attend OH. In his exams, you are allowed 1 sided 8x11sheet and the final both sides. The exams are heavy on the short-answer parts, so you do need to know the material pretty well but he is a great teacher. Iclicker is used for attendance.

Professor Root was so great! The lecturers were recorded, the class time was for practice and these questions were similar to ones on the test. Tons of review periods that made it easier to fully grasp the material. The tests are only worth about 58% of your grade so you have a lot of other ways to get credit. He is also so funny without trying.

One of my favorite professors at UCSD. Flipped classroom, with recorded lectures being a little long, but pretty engaging still. Exams and problem sets all come from the lectures, no tricks or unexpected questions. Really fun class, especially if you're into neurobiology.

Overall dense and not very engaging but makes it easy to get an A compared to other bio (extra credit, practice problems, note sheet on exams). Uses flipped classroom; lectures are prerecorded, in class is mandatory review with some absences allowed. Recordings were long but helpful, but he gave very unclear answers during live lecture reviews

This was honestly the best course ever! Cory Root is an amazing professor! Everything you need to know for the exams is based on past exam questions or the problem sets. He also gives roughly 5 points of extra credit or more.

Cory is a nice professor and the exams are very fair but he is careless in teaching. So many errors/typos in the recorded lectures.  It is come to a point were I don't even know what he is saying is factual.  The test averages are around 85% which is quire high.  Allows 1 sided note sheets for exams which helps a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are very dense and he goes pretty fast. He mumbles a lot and makes a good amount of errors on his slides/questions. Exams are still very fair and lecture/problem set based and he offers a decent amount of extra credit.

Had a great time in Prof Root's class. He gives out a lot of extra credit and there are problems sets that will help you boost your grade. The exams are based on the lecture so very fair and half the questions are multiple choice. Would recommend.

Pretty chill prof take him if you want an A+learn something (super caring and is very clear on what he needs you to know on exams, 20+ extra credit too). Lecture content on his research and neuroscience experiments made the class a lot more interesting. He was enthusiastic to teach this quarter and always asked for feedback. Overall, Great prof

He is a great professor who really wants his students to do well. He also gives a lot of extra credit and is always asking for students' feedback. He is one of the best professors I have taken at UCSD.

Even though considering the fact that this is his first time to teach, he fails so badly. He is not prepared for the lecture material at all and does not interested in the material he teaches, which is ridiculous. He lost himself in those slides made before the lecture day and then skipped all important information. He ruined my last bio class.

Amazing professor, this was by far the best class I have taken as a MSCS student. Amazing TA (Jacob) as well. I can't state enough how much I have learned and the group project element was a great way to finish off the course. There are quite a lot of readings and assignments, but both midterms were very chill. Most of the class probably got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you have other courses, do not take this one. The workload is way too heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Zero clarity/accountability. He only taught Konva - had to self-learn coding for project w/ AI (and be tested on it via oral exam). No project sprints got graded til AFTER EOQ on a rubric he literally NEVER showed before. My project TA (Devanshi) was unhelpful and at one point had bizarrely insisted on joining my team's group chat, which was weird.

Faux-structured class: too many assignments & unclear directions. Randomly assigned group + TA is an absolute pain since it affects grade. Refused to let me switch and I lost points due to bad teammates.
Final exam grading was the worst I've ever seen: inaccurate grading and didn't approve regrade solely because I wasn't "close to a grade boundary"

The professor is very supportive and attentive to students. The class project is well-structured and closely reflects real-world SWE internship experiences. Since teams are assigned randomly, the project experience can vary depending on group dynamics. There is an oral exam, where students must explain  their own code. I liked this class a lot.

Class is not structured very well. Some TAs are good, while others don't provide prompt and constructive feedback. We didn't spend time with React as the previous class did, but instead made games for K-12 students using Konva.js. Lectures are mandatory and not very useful, while labs are busy work.

Lectures are good an the professor cares about the class, however the class is horribly organized with assignments that can only be found scattered on the class website and no other way to know they exist, an experimental feedback system that counts for grade, and discussion sections that my whole group missed becuase we didn't know they exist.

Mr. Coblenz is the most amazing professor I have ever had at UCSD. He is extremely, kind, caring and I can tell he wants us to succeed. He is very understanding and always encourages us to do our best. I wish more people (or professors) were like him, he is a rare gem. Shoutout Coblenz-- the best CSE professor at UCSD!!!

One of my favorite CSE classes that I have taken, lectures were interesting and the technologies taught (REACT, Typescript, SQL) I found to be extremely relevant for internships/jobs. The group project can be hit or miss depending on who your with, I lucked out with mine and had a relatively solid experience. Lots of freedom given for the project.

Took SE125 back in Fall 2024. Not too bad for a statistics class, just make sure you go to office hours so you can learn how to do the homework, because the office hours is almost more important than lecture for this class. Love Big Man Conte!

Geniunely top-tier professor. Might even be the greatest of all time. This guy cares for his student & loves what he is teaching. Super fair grading and heavy curve. 

But the course itself is something else. Content-heavy, hard and time-consuming, you gotta put a lot of effort in. Office hours are a must, and the content is a lot to digest.

Anyone who thinks Conte isn't a good professor cannot be trusted. Prof Conte is the greatest and most caring professor I have had. This class was not easy but he has many office hours that are very helpful. He also explains problems really well. He wants every student taking this class to succeed, truly. CONTE ROCKS!

I took SE 125 with him in Fall 2024. Weekly hw, 1 close-book quiz, open-book midterm and final. Go to office hours to get the hw done otherwise u will fail this class. He curves generously. He's very knowledgable and even gave me his textbook for free
Fantastic professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I love the big conte
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Conte is one of the nicest profs I have ever met. Lectures are clear, not too fast, with good logic, combining theory and examples. He gives clear explanation on your questions. He focus on usage of theories in real life and tests and hwks all require thorough understanding of the material. Tests are hard though, the average is around 70/100.

SE125 really depends on how well you ingest information because there is a lot of it. If you go to lecture every time though the class is rather simple. The final was pretty straight forward and the two TAs, Angshuman and Giovanni, were excellent and if you have them as TAs, take every opportunity to get their help because the class isn't a gimme.

Honestly I consider myself a good student having gotten A's in a majority of my upper division classes. However this class was very hard. He NEVER does a single example that relates to the homework/tests. He focuses too much on relating the course to structural engineering instead of teaching the core concepts. Avoid if possible.

Professor Conte is one of the best teacher I've ever met. His class is definitely not easy but he is really kind and helpful. He is really passionate about his work and also shows apparent concern for students. :)
He's good

The most helpful and caring professor I've had at UCSD. HW was dreadful sometimes and you always had to go to office hours to do the problems correctly. However, in Conte's OH he practically does the problem for you, so go to as many OH as you can. The subject material is cumulative so don't be scared if you don't do well on the midterm/quiz.
Made the material very clear and spent time in assuring that the students understanding the concepts. He's the best professor I've had at UCSD.

This guy is a very smart, however, because of this he will make you feel like crap sometimes.  He expects you to know the materials that he covered and will get offended if you ask a "dumb" question.  Go to his OH only if you know the materials well enough but can't get the question right or else he will embarrass the heck out of you.
Great professor.  Reader is hard to understand unless you go to class.  Tests are fair (open book/notes). Homework is very long, but it forces you to understand the material very well.
His notes are very helpful, even though his tests are open book and notes they are still really hard.  He gives you a ton of work and it is very long.  He is pretty good though, just a ton of work.
very dedicated to students. class is hard, but he tries his best to communicate the material. always willing to answer question. i would strongly recommend taking this prof.
He is a great professor and you will learn a lot. Expect to work very hard for the hw and the tests

Amazing professor.  I graduated from UCSD two years ago.  He is there reason I love structural engineering and I owe great portion of my success to him.  No doubt he was really hard, but he was fair and responsible.
Conte is the man, gotta love the diagrams.
Conte's the man.  Don't be frightened, his class won't be a walk in the park but he's passionate about his subjects and he's there to help you!
No Comments
tests are ridiculously long and will effect your grade if you don't at least write something down for each problem.

Being in Conte's class is like no other.  connecting the reader to what he is talking about is the key to both of his classes.  Trying to learn out anything else will confuse the heck out of you, because conte's classes are that unique to the material.  Brilliant Guy...scary

This professor is great :) He is one of the most brilliant professors that you will ever meet. Teaches very well and cares sooooo much about learning, never tries to screw up his students. Happy person :) I love you Professor Conte. Thanks for being so great!

The material is very hard for the first 8 weeks then you'll start understanding whats going on so basically u'll be prepared for the final. He is a very nice prof. Prepare to spend about 22hrs/week between lecture, hw, and OH. He Cares about learning the material. Prepare to work hard, Good luck.

Good instructor; he really shows that he cares about his students' understanding of the material.  Do NOT underestimate this class; plan on putting in many hours per week on the homework assignments to do well.  Good homework understanding = high test scores.
Lectures real fast and the homework looks nothing like his lecture notes.
Great teacher!
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Easiest class I've ever taken, put absolutely no effort into this class, but I was taking this class to learn about jazz culture and instead was forced to listen to a bunch of experimental music only VERY tangentially related to jazz. I would have much preferred a more difficult class that taught me what I wanted to learn.
good class good professor
Super interesting lectures, tests were easy, he's super sweet and wants it to be an easy, fun class.

10/10 Professor. Class is graded on attendance for lecture and discussion, midterm, and final. He does attendance the first 15 minutes of class and never got mad students left early. He wants the class to be stress free as possible. Midterm and Final are super easy and online. We did not have class week 10  or midterm day. Easy A fr

Crum is my favorite prof I've ever had. His makes it extremely clear what is expected of you in essays and reading responses. Attendance is not mandatory, but a big section of the final is from stuff he says in class that's not on the slides/in the readings. Lots and lots of reading, but I actually enjoyed a lot of it. So caring and kind!

Crum is a great professor. very approachable and kind, he cares about his students and makes an effort to get to know them. Assignments are not marked by him and it's up to the TA. He doesn't teach much related to the actual assignments in lecture. He does weekly reading reflections and has EC assignments in lecture and outside. 2 essays 1 revision
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As usual, your hum grade really depends on your TA. Crum's course style was really helpful and had a lot of buffer with reflections and extra credits, so one essay doesn't define your grade. The final was also pretty easy and the essay prompts were released before.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Crum is genuinely the best professor I've had, and I don't usually like writing/history so this is surprising. He turns what could be a boring class into an exciting one as he finds themes we can relate to. Your grade entirely depends on the TA, so you just have to hope for the best. If you go to lecture and discussions regularly you will succeed.
easy class but a LOT of reading, only discussions are mandatory
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Super nice professor, interacts with students in lecture and makes the class feel really personal. Didn't have any trouble engaging in this class. There are two essays and they are graded sort of harshly but its really easy to find resources to help and the modules in canvas basically outline the essay format. Best HUM prof ever

Matthew S. Crum is amongst one of the greatest professors of all time. Not only is he an exceptional professor, but he is an outstanding human being. Humanities is boring and hard, but he makes it cool. I've taken two of his courses (HUM100 and HUM4), and both of which changed my life.

Prof Crum was awesome. He had really good lectures, essay prompts were fairly easy to understand, and readings for the most part were fun and engaging. He had a lot of chances for extra credit throughout the quarter and was very sociable and funny. I would definitely try to get him for any HUM if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super nice professor, allowed me to have my essay regraded and was extremely polite when conversing.
pretty hard class, wouldn't reccomend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
Matt Crum my GOAT. I took both HUM 2 and 3 with him and his lecture style is super fun and thought provoking.

Lectures aren't strictly mandatory, no in class quick writes or quizzes but he will talk about the definitions of key terms that will appear on finals. I had to miss classes due to other midterms but he's super understanding about it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I love Crum. The nicest person you will ever meet. Most humble down to Earth and caring prof out there.  interesting lectures & gives good interpretations of the texts. essay prompts aren't too hard. HUM=lots of reading and TA grading, but where Crum can be helpful he is. Wrote him an email a qtr later and he still remembered me. Absolute class.

Professor Crum is super helpful and his lecture content is interesting. The final is short ID (he went over all possible terms in lectures), and 2 short essays (gave prompts before hand). The texts he chose were also super fun to read through! But like all humanities, your grade really just depends on your TA.

it may just be me but crum is so fine. on a serious note I had crum for hum 2-3 and he made the class so easy. if you attend all lectures, you barely need to study for the final, and you're basically given all of the ideas you need to write essays and reflections. assignments were super easy as well (except the essays, but that's all of hum)

The only hum professor I have had that keeps me engaged in what we are learning. His lectures are incredibly helpful and he gives such good insight into the texts that are assigned. I also love the material he chose and that he made sure to include female authors in a typically male dominated field for the time period.
AMAZING. LIFE CHANGING!
He has two dogs that he will bring to class. While lecture attendance isn't mandatory, discussion attendance is. He is very understanding of circumstances that relate to late submissions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: yes he makes jokes but he also clearly states what's going to be on the exams. personally i think those that say he's bad didn't pay attention in class. i felt like the exams were fair especially for an upper div., it's obvious that the exams and class in general won't be easy. i recommend attending discussion they go over past exam questions.

He is unique. Some love him; some hate him, and I belong to the latter. He tries to be funny to an extent that is distracting. Exams cover very niche topics. The lecture slides are messy and sometimes contradict the answers in his end-of-week practices. However, his grading scale is very lenient (>85% is an A) and accommodating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Other ratings for this professor are pretty harsh. He does tend to joke around in class, but he really cares about his student's success. He's very helpful in OH. I would suggest studying thoroughly for all of his tests, because even though he says they're to "test your understanding," they're still worth a big portion of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor cares more about being a comedian than making sure his students understand the concepts. He goes way too fast. Asks niche questions that are impossible to answer, even if you understand concepts. I would not take this professor again. The other professors for this  class have a way higher pass rate. Nice guy, bad teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've had. Ironic that professors who center research on "education" are the worst at teaching. Spent too much time joking around than actually clarifying concepts. Would pause during explanations to say a joke, leaving us to self-teach. Prerequisite was only BIPN 100 but I felt I needed an entire genetics background to understand.

Really good professor. I got an A but because I attended PLA's OH. Class is very content heavy and you will need to look for help outside class but he's a good professor, my class was only once a week for 3 hours and still my fav class that quarter. Make sure to do your work and you'll get a good grade.

Professor jokes too much instead of teaching material. Does not teach the mechanics of physiological systems as much, does more application. Make sure to go to discussion as worksheets are very similar to midterm in terms of content and format. Try to attend SI and review sessions because they will tell you what topics are on the exam.
please do not take! time rushed exams, poor and boring lecture, extremely unhelpful slides, extreme poor podcast quality

He was a bit "quirky" in class, but it help make the 3 hour lecture more tolerable. He very picky about what is consider a correct answer for quizzes/tests and Discussions are not mandatory, but highly recommended since they provide you with review stuff and test format (might be dependent on TAs but if provided SAVE THE LINKS to each weeks slides)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jim is a great person, but his course is extremely tough. Lectures feel like stand‑up comedy, yet tests are strict and rushed—midterms are 20 minutes, and the final felt arbitrary. Exams are 95% of the grade, averages were low, and many students failed. Attend discussions and TA office hours to survive. Section GPA was 2.06, 41% failed.

Got an A+ but it was ture suffering taking BIPN100 with Jim. He is a funny and nice professor for sure but his tests are badly worded and he enjoys to trick his fellow students. If you study hard, A+ is not impossible but overall I don't recommend taking BIPN100 with him. Once again, nice guy, tones of funny jokes in class

Please don't pick him for bipn100. He doesn't know how to teach. Slides super messy, a lot of time no texts and he explains the mechanisms badly. Himself is super nice and approachable, just not good at teaching

Exams will for sure cook you so make sure you know your stuff, other than that they are short but practically entirely free response. 

The resources he provides are amazing like codon and the openstax textbook (which is free). 

Emailed him once but he never responded.

Lectures feel more like a social event than learning but not mandatory.

One of the best lecturers I've taken; he made three hours go by quick. Clear learning objectives and if you study/ memorize his slides, you'll do well. Exams are ALL free response and can be very specific regarding grading rubric. Make sure you understand the concepts well as his exams require application, not just rote memorization.
Man spends too much time tryna be funny than actually teach.

Probably the worst professor I've had. Can't believe I had the displeasure of having to sit through this man's course. His lecturing is terrible. His tests are awful. His jokes are even worse. I hope he learns to ‘joke' less and TEACH more. Avoid tbh, not worth the effort when there are way better profs you can get a higher grade with.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Engaging lectures, but the exams are no joke. Definitely take advantage of all study resources like Unstuck ai to prepare. The class is tough, but rewarding if you stay on top of it.

Lectures were straightforward, but that's because I had already learned a lot of the material in other classes. I didn't appreciate how he made discussion section optional but then refused to post the discussion materials. Tests are okay, just lots of writing. Get ready to watch on 2x speed cause half the lecture is just him making jokes.

How about instead of trying to be so hehe haha funny you just TEACH the class? Idk just an idea. Disgustingly hard tests accommodated by impressively poor lecturing. If you want to tank your gpa but potentially get in a chuckle at a mediocre joke, he's your guy. Seriously tho, I'd avoid him if you can.

Doesn't curve for a ridiculously hard class with C averages or lower on exams. Doesn't explain concepts thoroughly enough for how he wants it in the exams. Exams were probably the toughest exams I've taken even harder than metabolic biochem, ochem, etc. Do not take

Hands down one of the best professors at UCSD. Hilarious lectures that are very straightforward at communicating content. If you do not enjoy the subject matter the tests will be long and difficult but if you have genuine interest then he is the best professor to take and tests will be like fun discussion activities. Makes you excited to learn.
easy content and chilling lecture style, but his tests are the worst ever
Hilarious professor, I like how he lectures but his tests and finals really Cooked me....

He's a super funny prof, but his teaching style is hard to follow along with at times and he grades VERY heavily on midterms and the final. I wouldn't take him again, but I'm sure he's a great person, just a very difficult professor.

Very engaging during class but tests are extremely hard, final is cumulative. Mispronounces words on purpose which is confusing for someone who's first language is not english. His final ended with a 57% average but he does not curve. Tests are 95% of your grade.
Very engaging professor. Does an amazing job explaining tough concepts. Tests are fair. Graded 95% 2 midterms and final.

You have to sort through all the things he doesn't understand in order to pass/get an A as the two are synonymous when it comes to this course that he teaches. He's not very good at biology at all and obviously never passed out of his own bachelor's you'll pass as you basically taught his entire class for him.

cooke is so straight forward during lectures, his lecture practice q's are nearly identical to the ones on the test, i got an a- by watching all the podcasts the day before the test, he tells u what the question topics are b4 the test so u study the right thing, literally everything is in his slides, such an easy A if u watch podcasts on 2x speed

BIPN is a challenging course regardless of which professor you take. Although Cooke is a friendly and fun professor who tries his best to explain the material, his exams are difficult and require a deep understanding of the concepts you learned in lectures. On top of all this, your whole quarter grade depends on those exams, which is unfair.
most of his focus on the first 10 sildes of each lecture then he runs through the 50 remainng slides.
Professor's exams are really tough and the grading is usually unfair. Answers given on practice exams are short and simple yet you get marked off tons of points if you do something similar

i think all BIPN courses will be difficult, so for what its worth Cooke made it significantly easier than I expected. He really tries to give you as many points as he can on the tests, and everything is exactly as expected. Its a super interesting course and Cooke is super funny and explains everything really well. one of my fav profs ever

I love Professor Cooke! I have taken him 3 times at UCSD and have enjoyed each class. Not only is he hilarious, he is a fantastic lecturer and ensures that he talks about everything that you will need to know on the exam. His exams are fair and consistent. Thanks Dr. Cooke!

Why is his rate so high? WITHOUT a doubt a tough grader! The exams are your grade. You do bad well too bad! NO curves, no grade shown on canvas, practice problems are not like exams, and no EC. Basically, You do better when you learn on your own. exams are NOT multiple choice rather you write and not everything you right is correct so it harms you!

Cooke was funny and entertaining during his lectures but he was unresponsive to emails. The class has a really weird grading format and the exams are worth the entirety of your grade and he had grades disabled on canvas for the entire quarter so you won't know your actual grade until the very end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not accessible outside of class at all. Final exam average was a D and he doesnt curve. The lectures are fast paced and not detailed at all while the exams are very difficult. Avoid at all costs. As a person he can be funny but this class and the way he teaches is a GPA killer

Entertaining lectures, he gave practice exams with basically the same questions that would be on the exams. Discussions weren't required for attendance but they also gave a lot of help with what to expect on the tests.
Very hard exams
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't bother submitting regrades for his class because he's only interested in dropping your grade. Literally didn't give points back for answers that matched the answer keys exactly. Extremely unresponsive to emails for no reason. Lectures were straightforward and understandable, he explains the content well. But the test questions were tricky.

study all the practice test, question, or what ever practice material you are given. If you master the study questions you'll do fine. Finally, do not be discourage if you don't know a concept, just youtube it until you grasp concept. The professor response quickly if you e mail him. good luck

This is the third time I have taken a course with Dr. Cooke. Although his exams are challenging, his practice exams, weekly and discussion worksheets are true representations of his exams and are a great source of study. I love how Cooke makes the content applicable in a clinical setting. Encourages you to learn beyond memorization.

Prof Cooke's lectures were quite heavy and midterms were tedious but he provided lots of opportunities to practice concepts, either in the form of practice q's during lectures, or end-of-week practice problems. He also provided practice exams which were great study tools for the midterms. Overall, class was enjoyable and the lectures were fun:)

Dr. Cooke is a great lecturer but the exams are so intense. The grading was super tough and overall super test-heavy with 2 midterms + the final counting for over 90% of your total grade. Although I learned SO much in this class and genuinely enjoyed the material, I would never take another class with Dr. Cooke.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests are exactly what you'd expect if you take the time to look at discussion worksheets. He got his PhD in pharm so expect a lot of drug-related questions. TBF, I found this class to be 80% memorization and 20% application. There's no padding so make sure you do well on exams; the rest of ur grade comes down to how fast of a test-taker you are.

Exams are long for the amount of time given, but Professor Cooke is one of my favourite lecturers. Very passionate about the topic and answers questions clearly. Weekly pre-lecture quizzes graded for effort. Discussion worksheets & exam reviews are super helpful, too.

Professor Cooke is clear on what he wants you to know.  Create life-like scenarios with the topics because that’s what the exams will reflect. Create a self test and be able to describe processes. Not a difficult class if you put in the time. What he says in his lectures are on the exams. Good luck!!

I liked professor Cooke.  He was funny and I enjoyed watching his lectures.  The one gripe I had was with the difficulty of his tests and his refusal to curve besides the initial cutoffs (85 was an A, 80 was an A- and so on) The average score on the final was a 59.1(A D according to his cutoffs) and he refused to curve or change cutoffs.

Professor Cooke is the best professor I’ve had at UCSD. His lectures are super interesting and hilarious, to the point where an 80 min lecture is never boring. His tests are tough though; all free response and very long. As long as you pay attention in class and rewatch the lectures you should be fine.

This is my second time taking Dr. Cooke, and he is hands down the best bio professor here. Lectures and the overall class were well-structured. He provides a LOT of worksheets and practice problems that are extremely helpful for the exams. The exams are no joke (lengthy and difficult). They are all free-response and clinical applications.

He is a great professor with very engaging lectures. BIPN 134 is honestly such a fun class only because he is teaching it. His exams are understanding based, but if you watch the lectures and go to OH you will honestly be fine. One of the best lecturers in the biology department.

I've come to have a love/hate relationship with Cooke. Pros: Dr. Cooke definitely knows how to make his lectures engaging. It seems he's very into active learning! Cons: His lectures are very dense and he would at times skim over class material he would later test you on. His exams are hard and he's a very harsh grader. Class averages were low.

Funny, organized, concise lecturer. Discussion worksheets reinforce the knowledge that you will need to tackle his conceptual exam questions. They are much easier than his exams which are difficult and tiring, but if you understand how everything connects you will do well. Midterm reviews were not helpful as there was no practice. Rewatch lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The exams were absolutely NOTHING like the lectures. During lecture, everything was super easy and simplistic, but the exams were all application-based, free response questions that he did not adequately prepare the class for. Grading was way too harsh and points were marked off if the wording wasn't exactly to their liking, even if correct.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Seems more interested in being perceived as funny and charismatic than actual education. Office hours are a disaster. Many TAs get critical details wrong and are oddly attracted to the prof. Exams are ridiculously convoluted.

honestly really liked cooke. hes a great lecturer. he made physio. interesting and easily digestible for me. his tests are tricky and dense, but i managed to get good grades on the first 2 midterms. the final was terribly difficult but i still ended with a B. the canvas grade thing sucked, and he should def. fix that, but hes still a great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Amazing lectures--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the first class I failed in college. He was a nice dude but the exams were nothing like what was covered in lecture. They were extremely application-based free response exams, which would be fine if the grading wasn't so ridiculously & unnecessarily tough. I've had tough graders before, but no one like this. Left every midterm crying lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I know many people who did not pass this class last quarter and 100% understand the negative reviews people are giving out. My best advice for those who take this class in future quarters is to talk to the IAs and rewatch the living sh*t out of lectures. Pay attention when he gives hints about certain material being on future exams, it will!!!!!!

Professor Cooke has disappointed me. Because of his lack of communication on canvas, the % shown was ENTIRELY off of my grade and was expecting to receive a B+, but ended up with D. His lectures seems to be chill, but his (2) midterms and the final were long, very detailed and required a LOT of memorization. Just expect to learn by yourself.

LISTEN... Hes a good person yes outgoing whtver, but DAMN .. his class is based on 2 Midterms and your final (no hw). The midterms and final are all free response and graded very harshly like EXTREMELY. The class was interesting but honestly it was impossible to pass the tests no matter how hard I studied and did practice problems.

Worst human ever. He should of at least told the whole class the canvas grades werent scaled correctly by 15% I hope the class gets together and petitions for their grades from canvas . From a Straight A student to this.. smh Cooke do better ayyy

I was a straight A student before taking this class and never in my life did I fail every test given in a class. In class hes a super funny and he over simplifies the material but when you get to the tests no amount of memorization or practice problems prepares you. Super harsh grader where the class averages were below failing and no curves given

I have never gotten a bad grade till now. I am not sure how because I studied 20+ hours/week for this class... then bam the midterms messed up my grade with the final... he messed up everyone's grade on canvas by giving the wrong grades the whole quarter. idk how he's a professor at UCSD.

I am truly heart broken... I retained the material so well by putting in work MYSELF not from his lectures which he makes look so easy... the two midterms took the whole 2 and half hours. final was 3 hours. I failed the class for the first time even though I did everything in this class... Wish I took somebody else...
Not sure what goes through this mans head to oversimplify everything and give tests that are nothing like the practice. Do not waste your time with this clown

I wouldn't take him again due to the tests given. They were extremely different and difficult for no reason. He's nice but his tests aren't. I got lucky yo pass the class I know many students who did not. Average class GPA was a 2.2

I did the end of the week, DI questions, practice midterm exams, and the final practice. I also technically memorized the whole damn book, and his lectures. Always went to OH of IA and his OH. I failed the class because he failed to inform students about the grades on canvas. Tests were nothing like he teaches. 15 page final and no multiple choice.

This guy teaches you 2+2 then gets to the exam and gives you integrals. The whole quarter I thought I had a decent grade B and above and then apparently he just messed up on canvas and ended up getting a D. So unprofessional of him. I am a straight A student and if I knew I was going to get a D I would have dropped the class. FALSE info...

Hes a good teacher, but his exams are so hard to get an average grade. Despite studying for 10 hours a week, it still didnt matter there were always random questions and grading was always super strict on wording, wouldnt recommend solely based on his exams. No one in the class got higher than a 93 on the final so its clearly impossible.

honestly the greatest professor I have ever taken. you would never expect physio to be a class you look forward to but he really makes you enjoy being in the lecture and is extremely knowledgeable. he is a very fun professor and knows how to teach in a manner that is both fun and engaging for the class. I highly recommend taking any class with him.

Professor cook explains the material well so it is easy to understand. However, be warned of his exams. They are extremely difficult and tricky. He looks for specific wording in the written responses. So be a master in the material. Memorize everything (ie., mechanisms, definitions) and be able to apply or manipulate TONS of info. I Don't recommend

This is my fourth year of college and he's one of the best professors I have ever had. He explains things very well and incorporates a lot of humor which makes the material easier to understand. His exams are very conceptual so you have to really understand the material to do well. He's also very cute so that's another reason to attend class lol
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Wish he would ask what he wants during exams. The questions are to confuse students which is unfair. Memorized and conceptually understood everything until I got to his midterms. He makes it so difficult to get at least a C on exams. Averages on midterms are 60-65%. He teaches well, but exams are very difficult for no reason. Do better cooke.

Alright listen, He is funny, charming, and nice. HOWEVER, he oversimplifies everything, and gives 5 year old names to scientific terms THEN he tests you on what has to be a specific name of scientific terms. He seems like a chill, laid back dude until your first midterm gets graded. 2 midterms, and one final, midterms are 8-10pg, final 15pg. :')

Professor Cooke is so nice. Always greets us hello and says goodbye. I basically handed myself a B- by missing half of a midterm, but I think that his lectures really do prepare for the midterms and final. I won't lie, the final was thick. However, somehow, I still really enjoyed the class and I learned a lot.

For some reason his method for delivering the material was really confusing. He looked for specific wording on exams, but never specified what he was looking for. On lectures he asked questions, but didn't bother to go over concepts because reading the assigned reading and doing the prelecture quizzes should have been enfough.

Everyone likes Cooke because lectures are engaging. However, a 19 page final & FOUR midterms? And tests go beyond lectures, so study hard. He made this my worst quarter yet. Don't recommend taking with more than 1 other STEM class. Curve's nice, but he doesn't even respond to emails and his OH are always packed with struggling students.

His lectures are really engaging and he would crack some jokes at the end. 90% of the grade is weighted on exams but his grading scale is very generous. His exams are fair but can be challenging. Attend discussions, do the practice problems, and thoroughly understand the learning objectives.

Good and interesting lectures. Explains the information very clearly and concisely. Take clear notes because concepts often flow together. BEWARE of the FINAL. the tests during the quarter were 3-4 pages of multipart questions. the FINAL was 15 pages long of 10 multipart questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: LOVED this class! super inspiring content, has opened my eyes to so many aspects of endocrine physio and pathology! Dr. Cooke trains us to think critically rather than purely memorize content. Tests are challenging but if you work concepts and details will do great! go to office hours, lots of useful questions are asked. engaging lectures!

The online format doesn't suit this professor. Lectures were ok but rarely approached the depth seen on exams. Attend section for crucial practice problems and use the textbook for clarity. The goal of education is to educe, to bring out one's potential, unfortunately this course focused on minutiae instead of concepts, a missed opportunity.

I have taken a couple of classes with Professor Cooke. Overall, great professor! One of my favorite professors at UCSD. His exams are based on applying what you have learned in lecture in like clinical type problems. Before COVID, the exams were individual and also group-based. Either way with the group exam, it helped your grade.

Cooke comes from a teaching background. Gives clear and simple lectures. His enthusiasm and occasional jokes make the more dry and boring parts of the class curriculum much bearable. Has given group exams in the past and it is possible he will continue to. He is nonetheless a generous grader.

All-around wonderful professor and person. I took this class just because I had him for bipn 100 and knew he was great.. I ended up really enjoying the class - human reproduction is so cool! His lectures are fun and hold my attention, while also conveying the material clearly. Definitely recommend taking this class with Cooke!
Take him, you wont regret it!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very engaging & a clear lecturer! Does a lot of group work during class which can be super helpful with a good group. Tests are pretty difficult but the TAs are very fair about grading and Cooke is super accessible outside of class. Lectures aren't technically mandatory & he podcasts but they're too helpful to be skippable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Cooke is my favorite professor at UCSD thus far. His lectures are informative and he keeps things interesting and tries to make a lot of jokes. His exams can be challenging but most of them align exactly with the lectures so make sure to watch all of the lectures and attend discussion where you will do practice worksheets that will help you.
Hands down the BEST professor Ive had at UCSD

Sure, he is funny, charismatic, and presents the material in a clear and efficient way. HOWEVER, his tests are vague in what they want. Ask more direct questions, Cooke. The nature of human reproductive biology makes tests difficult because there are a lot of "grey"-area questions. Cooke does NOT go out of his way to make it black or white.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Jim is a hilarious professor and really keeps the class engaged throughout the entire lecture. His tests are hard and can be somewhat long for the amount of time given, but as long as you read through and answer the questions you know first, you will be fine. Relisten to the podcasts and take notes.

I took this class an upper division elective but now I may want to continue taking physiology. He is SO ENTERTAINING during lectures that it is a breath of fresh air compared to many other professors in the stem departments. His tests are HARD never the less just take good notes you will be fine! He's easy on the eyes too ;) Will def take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures are pretty entertaining and informative but are very fast pace so I always re-watched them via podcast and took very detailed notes. Exams are quite hard and require not only lots of memorization but also a good understanding of the material. I would definitely recommend taking prof Cooke; he's good at teaching and is super attractive.

One of my fav profs at UCSD, he's hilarious, super chill and is def very knowledgable with what he's teaching. I learned a great deal and really enjoyed everything. He just spoke a little fast for me, ended up having to review the podcasts a lot. tests were moderately hard.

I took him for summer and had a 3 hour lecture he's such a great professor he's funny which kept a 3 hour class interesting. He podcast, post test practice & discussions are optional but he gives out practice sheets that are VERY similar to the exams. I got an A didn't really use the podcast because i feel like he covers material fairly well pace.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took him for BIPN 100 and now BIPN 134 and he is hands down my favorite professor at UCSD. Funny, engaging, and caring are only some of his best qualities. He's really focused on teaching students and not just lecturing at them. Go to class, attend sections, and understand the concepts. That's all it takes to get an A.
There's a lot to remember but if you go to section and lecture you'll do fine. He has a nice curve and he's pretty funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great Prof. He is really funny, which will help to keep some people awake through lecture. 2 midterm and 1 final. midterms are okay, you get to redo one question with a group. Final is a killer and worth 45%. Very long and tough. Sections are not mandatory, but they supply worksheets that are really helpful. Class is podcast. Isn't an easy A.

Amazing prof who will teach you EVERYTHING there is to know about the repro system, but you will have to work for it! Class is very detail-oriented and covers a lot of material, so expect to study at least 5 hours a week (outside class). That being said, he truly cares about his students and provides lots of office hours/problem sets/practice exams

Great professor. Extremely strong command of the material, and also is an entertaining guy. His format can be annoying at times (online pre-reading quizzes) but it definitely helps you learn the material better. Optional discussion section but if you go it will absolutely help a ton. His final is an absolute monster compared to the midterms.

Cooke has a sense of humor and shows it in his lectures. He's a fun guy that shows actual interest in the material. Other reviews say the free response exams are vague, which is kind of true. There's a lot of detail in class material and the exams involve applying/working off concepts from it, so podcasting lectures and doing problems is a must!

This professor is an amazing guy. Super energetic and knowledgable about the material. Approachable and cares about his students success. That being said this is the hardest class I have ever taken. There are SO many details that you have to know. Don't take him unless you have to

Within the span of one quarter, Professor Cooke taught me more about biology than any other teacher. He genuinely cares about his students and goes out of his way to host many office hours. His class is challenging (definitely study lecture notes and go to office hours) but you will gain a lot from it.

I liked him, hated the class. No matter how much I thought I understood everything, could never get an A on the exams even though 80% gets you an A, ended up with a B+, guess I am just stupid. He is hilarious, very clear, easy to understand and follow. 2 small quizzes, 2 exams, 1 final. 80% gets you an A, 70% is B, etc. Tests are hard and LONG!!

This professor tries too hard to be funny during the lectures rather than focusing on actually teaching his students. He would say not to worry about a topic and would put it on the exam. Doesn't really teach about what he's actually putting on the exams. Do yourself a favor and take someone else.

Exams are definitely pretty difficult. He is a funny and engaging professor though and very understanding and fair! I didn't do well on the first midterm but neither did other students so he changed the syllabus so that if you do better on the final, it would count for more of your grade. Studied my butt off for the final and pulled up my grade

He is one of the first professors in my 3 years here that has made me want to write a rating. He is one of the funniest professors ever & I have really enjoyed my time in his class. He is very funny and his lectures are engaging. Tests are fair and representative of the class material. Pretty sad he only teaches two courses at UCSD :(

Jim is a great professor! He is really smart but also not afraid to admit when he doesn't know the answer to something. The practice problems are almost exactly like the midterms so definitely do them. Engaging lecturer, plus podcasts If you're not ready to laugh don't take this class, its 50% stand up comedy

Don't take this professor under any circumstances. He tests you on material that he has never gone over or goes over for only a few seconds and he does this because he makes the mistake of thinking he taught it. Whatever you do, please avoid this professor. I took 140B the same quarter and got an A in it, but did a lot worse in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Jim is a breath of fresh air after years of STEM classes taught by boring researchers. He's hilarious, and genuinely interested in students actually learning. His tests are HARD but fair. Not much memorization, all application. Not only is he physically attractive, his humor makes him really hot! Got an A in the class & I want to TA next quarter!

His exams are fair if you are willing to put in the work. He provides you with more than enough material that you could study from and learn his exam style. Some ppl here are giving him bad ratings bc they thought this would be a memorization class like most ucsd bio classes. It's not. Always be ready to explain yourself.  Def a must take prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Tests are all free response, is very vague on what he wants when it comes to the questions and then expects very specific terms to be present in terms of answer for you to even get partial points. there is no curve. avoid at all costs!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I loved coming to lecture! Dr. Cooke is hilarious and keeps the class engaged. 1 midterm, 1 final, 2 article-based assignments. None were too bad. Exams require critical thinking, but your grade on the assignment really depended on which TA you had.
HUB HUB sexy professor that makes me want to go to class, he is  fantastic professor, has a reverse classroom model loves joking and making classroom light

Dr. Cooke is a hilarious professor with a great personality. It was his first time teaching this course so things were a little hectic but it was definitely enjoyable. Highly recommend him for any class you are preparing to take although his "reverse classroom" strategy is something you'll either hate or love.
Don't take him if you really want to learn something. Too much joking during the lectures. And there is no assigned reading before the lectures but he wants you to have class discussions.

Jim is an extraordinary professor. If you really buckle down and try and understand the concepts that he emphasizes in class, you will have no problem getting an A or even an A+ in his class. Make sure to attend office hours and really get into his head in terms of how he will test you.

WHAT A PROFESSOR! I'm telling you, I loved James because I ACTUALLY learned, not just memorized and forgot. His method of open class discussions are very useful. The weekly quizzes helped me keep up with the readings, which I recommend if you want to keep up with class discussion. I also loved his humor. This guy sets the bar for college teaching.

Avoid if possible. Sure Cooke is charming and funny but do not be fooled by the false sense of security. The worksheets, practice exams, discussion section problems are not at all reflective of what is to come on the tests. The only slightly helpful material were the end of the week problems. Also, hardest final I have ever taken in my life.

You will either love or hate the reverse class room method, but no matter how you feel about it he gets you to actually learn and struggle through the material before he just give it to you to word vomit on an exam. His tests are challenging, but I did not come to UCSD to float through my classes. Definitely worth taking him.

Pretty good guy and good personality. However, he is vague on what to learn for the course. Test are graded harshly. If you don't specify certain things you wont get the points for it even for effort.  Questions a vague and hard to know what he exactly wants. Could be better if practices were more like the test and given before the end of the week

Jim is an interesting professor. He is extremely helpful in that he keeps everyone awake even with early classes. He is fairly clear in his lectures and what he wants you to learn, but in the end of the day his exams are difficult like any other BIPN I suspect.

He's a nice guy and all, but I don't think he is a good professor. His lectures are so brief and only touch on the general idea instead of the detailed mechanisms, yet his tests were complete free response and he requires so much details. Tests are vague and I never know what he wants. Worksheets in class are useless. Please don't take him.
He is a very hard grader, he expects so much out of his students on his exams when the questions are extremely ambiguous and vague. Do NOT recommend him, take another professor if you can.

For his first quarter teaching here, Dr. Cooke was funny and a great lecturer . He takes a flipped classroom approach where you are expected to learn before lesson and do probs in class. But tbh, I enjoyed it more during the parts when he just lectured. Tests were based on prob sets and midterms were part individual and group test.

His lectures are very interactive. Jim expects everyone to pre-read and has a pre-reading quiz per week which are very helpful during lecture. His teachings methods might be confusing at first but they worked really with my study habits and also kept me from procrastinating. Jim is an excellent professor if you are willing to be a good student.
LISTEN TO THE PODCASTS AND MAKE SURE YOU KNOW/UNDERSTAND EVERYTHING HE MENTIONS IN LECTURES. an A is definitely doable but you'll have to earn it.

Cooke is awesome! He's one of the best lecturers I've encountered. His classes were always interesting and engaging. His test are REALLY hard because they require a thorough understanding of the material and an ability to think about it and not only just know it. I worked hard but getting an A wasn't impossible, even after failing the first midterm

Great lecturer! I had him for an 8 am but falling asleep was never a problem because he's really funny and energetic. He's great to go to during office hours but usually crowded. The only issue is that it was hard to understand what he's looking for when grading and he doesn't curve. Tests are really long and difficult so don't fall behind studying

Amazing and funny lecturer! NOT AN EASY GRADER! He has high expectations for his exams, but if you attend his office hours or really listen to his lectures (PODCASTS!) you can get a good grasp of what he wants. He gives online weekly quizzes, gives group and individual exams! He is always willing to help and I would definitely recommend his class
Does not curve. Tests are difficult and long. Ruined my GPA. Take another professor.

I love Professor Cooke! He's very helpful and his main goal is really to make sure students learn. There will be a lot of in-class group activities, but honestly they weren't bad at all! There were also pre-reading quizzes and homework which really helped me understand lectures better. He also reminds me of Freddie Prinze Jr. for some reason

Dr. Cooke is an amazing professor, he makes an 8am worth going to.  He is very helpful in OH and is clear in his explanations of the course material.  I recommend him for BIPN 100 and any other class he teaches.
She was the best! I adored going to her class and she was a great lecturer. She drops one of the 3 exams which was clutch after not doing great on midterm 2.
As a STEM major I always hated and never understood econ before this class. Crane is one of my favorite teachers. Take her.

She's a great professor. Since it's her first time teaching this class, you can tell she's putting in a lot of effort to make it engaging and enjoyable. The homework isn't difficult and is exactly what appears on the exams, which makes it very fair. She also offers a generous test drop policy.

Really good professor and overall really easy class. Lectures are really easy to follow and understand. The homework follows what was taught in the lectures and the test is very similar to questions on the homework. She drops one of your 3 test which is very clutch.
Goated Professor. She gives all the content needed to study right at the start and learning how to do the practice material should consolidate a 70-80+ on every exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: MY QUEEN, she literally drops one of your exams (whichever one's your lowest) and this includes the midterms and the final. I skipped the final lol. Homework is lightwork you get like 4 attempts. Genuinely the nicest the professor I have ever had. REALLY CLEAR LECTURER. I love her sm.

Absolutely goated econ prof. Easiest class I've ever taken in my life, high school included. Three exams is most your grade, bombed the second exam bc I forgot it was happening and came in late and threw the third bc I had another final and still got an A-. Didn't go to many lectures or study for any exams but if you do, you can easily get an A+

CRANE IS THE BEST. The lectures are so easy to follow. Solutions to HWs are literally given in the discussions (which are recorded!). 3 exams, all non-cumulative, with lowest score dropped. I did well in exam 1 and 2 and did nothing in the course (0 in final) and got an A+. She is also very attractive. 10/10 professor, no complaints.

Crane is the best Econ professor ever. She's really kind and super caring. Her lecture slides are amazing and she makes the concept easy to understand. You can drop one of the exams (including final) as only 2 out of 3 is taken into account. Her exams are relatively easy compared to the other econ professors

Professor Crane is extremely fair with her tests and will even drop the lowest one, including the final. Meaning, if you did great on the first two midterms, you don't even have to take the final. One of the best econ professor at UCSD. Take her if you get the chance.

Material is difficult, but she is just an amazing professor. Trust me you wont fail this class. The only bad thing about this class is the exams. Material on exams is exactly like study guide and homework, but there are too many questions for a 50 minute class period. Keep that in mind and you will pass! One exam and hw is dropped at the end.

42.5% on top 2 tests. Cheat sheet is allowed and if you study the material and watch lectures then they are very manageable. Absolutely great professor, with engaging lectures, homework that was helpful and useful for tests, and good review sessions. Also very clear on grading and has very fast turn around on grading tests, about a few days.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best Economics professor I have ever taken. Especially for an upper-division class like 100B. She provides good feedback, super nice personality andis very patient to deal with your questions. Her exams are easy, just understand lectures and does homework. Lectures and recorded, gives opportunity for extra credit as well.
She is literally the best econ professor I ever met in UCSD!!! She is a very caring and super sweet professor, and she is always trying to help her student even outside of the class.

Professor Crane is very informative and clear with her coursework and lectures. She is very understanding and takes her time to make sure all her students understand the subject matter. Thank you so much Professor Crane!

She is such a great teacher! I think she is very fair with her policies and offers many opportunities to get help. However, her lectures can be a bit boring since she does make sure to slowly go through every single topic and idea. I think her class is a good balance of work and ease, and she seems to actually want her students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very kind and engaging professor. Weekly homeworks and three tests but only 2/3 of your best tests are graded and one homework gets dropped. All test material comes from the homework practice problems and were pretty easy. As long as you study the practice problems and complete the homework you should get an A.

Prof Crane is a very sweet professor. I just think that lectures were just boring especially since I took it in the middle of the day. Often there were questions on the midterms that didn't really reflect study guide material or even questions we had been exposed to. I think if you understand lectures and how HW is structured you can get a B.
Her class is pretty simple and straightforward.

The professor is fine but for my class this quarter, the homework was $110, and she didn't bother to tell us until week 2 (where it's too late to opt-out of the textbook required for homework), making us all pay the $110, even though she initially quoted that it was $45. Overall good teacher, but unreliable person.
Best econ professor at UCSD! Strongly recommend taking any of her classes.
She is very nice and cares about her students, even asked if anyone has schedule conflicts for midterms so she could offer alternative times. Also very accessible if you have any questions.
I wish I could take Crane for every one of my economics courses. She's so nice and her practice tests were similar to the actual tests so that I was never once surprised by a test question.

(Econ 2) Although a little slow in speaking and lectures, she's very caring and nice, always trying to help out her students inside and outside of the class. She also tries to keep the class entertained with different activities and trying to be relatable.

Great econ prof!
If you have any chance take with Dr Crane for any of your econ classes. She is the best professor I have ever had at UCSD and she is really caring to her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Econ 2 (couldn't find button), only midterm and final were your grade. It was difficult to gauge how test would be, but she gives a generous curve. Not to mention she is very funny and relatable in lecture. Attendance is not mandatory and she records them do the study guide and go to the review sessions.

Really nice professor. She cares about students. She frequently talks about contents from Econ 1, 3, and 100A to help students review previous knowledge to lay a more solid foundation of current content. Exams are not so hard but you need to be careful.
Ive taken many econ profs at UCSD and she is by far the best. So caring about her students and really knows what she is teaching.
THE BEST ECON PROFESSOR AT UCSD!!

Professor Crane very clearly cares about the success of her students. She was one of the nicest and honestly best professors I have had at UCSD. Her exams actually tested you on content you were taught, and if you do the reviews and watch the lectures you'll do well, which is how it should always be in my opinion.

I had Crane for Econ 1, 2, and 3, and she is one of the nicest and most caring profs I have ever had. She records everything, even discussions and review sessions. One minor complaint is that her lectures did not make me feel entirely prepped for the tests and hw. But she is there for you for help if needed.
She is so nice and caring. The best econ prof I've met in ucsd.

I had done Econ before in high school hence I barely went to any Econ lecture and got an easy A+. She is a nice person in general who quickly responds to her students queries. However, I think the slides she provides from her lectures could be better. They are confusing.she sometimes jumbles up concepts she wants to teach aswell
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Crane cares a lot about her students. Homework and quizzes were relatively simple and her lectures are simple to understand.

Best professor I had in my life. Very caring, easily accessible during office hours, and supportive. She will explain things to you and will not treat you like an idiot. Her midterms/final were also very easy as they were a copy and paste of the review problems assigned in class. I went to class 4 times during the quarter and came out with an A.

The lectures are very fast, sometimes not posted, only make sense with the actual lecture, not by themselves. They repeat the readings with less full content. The readings are per class and kind of long. Sometimes he has easy class quizzes based on the readings, never pop tho. Midterms are kinda hard, but final not so much, not curved. Mostly Bs.

Funny guy and passionate about his material and brings his dog to class! Assignments are randomly assigned and not too hard. Tests are fair but super weighted and will affect your grade heavily. Lectures are mandatory and a little hard to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a pretty chill dude, but his lectures were all over the place most of the time, and his Canvas was even more disorganized than his lectures. Lectures are mandatory, and he'll call you out if you go on your phone and do other things on your laptop. Grade is based mostly on midterm, final, and a big project, so it's easy to lose your A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Funniest professor ever, but his grading and class as a whole were very disorganized. Didn't know what was being expected for the writing assignments besides some broad outlines (no rubrics given). Classes sometimes deviated off track. Finding things in canvas was like finding a needle in a haystack. Still found the course enjoyable though.

he's a really nice guy but he assigns a lot of hw (20+ page readings sometimes). if you're not willing to put that work in and attend all the lectures (doesn't podcast and attendance is worth a good amount of ur grade) then i wouldn't recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very funny and kind professor. Free zoo field trip was a blast! There is a lot of reading but if you just attend and read, class should be fairly easy as P/NP.

There would be 1-3 weekly discussion posts about a reading or article. There were randomly assigned groups for a project about debunking which was worth a good chunk of grade. Two 600 word papers and some other random writing projects. No midterm but a final with short and long answer q's that no one knew about until week 8, and only gave 2 hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Easy and fun class, TAs grade discussions hard though

Super nice and funny guy, can def tell that he's passionate about the subject. Lectures can get boring, but attendance is mandatory and all his material is based on articles he sends out for reading. Most of things were graded by the TA, who seemed very opinionated on what was right/wrong (even though it was a philosophy class?)

He's a nice guy and he creates fun events for the class to enjoy. Although his lectures were kind of messy and all over the place, his class isn't difficult as long as you read the required readings and understand their grading criteria. This was my first philosophy class and it was within the difficulty I expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great professor!  Definitely recommend taking him, if you are or are not interested in philosophy.  He knows his stuff!  So interesting.
Very nice, laid back, and willing to help students.  As with most UD Phil classes, the material will not be easy though.
he's a cool guy he would be a cool guy to hang with...but he assigns homework and everybody has to wiki the answer. then when you turn it in, he then helps/lectures the answer to the class.

Great sense of humor. He makes the class pretty fun if you're in to the subject (this was Philosophy of Physics). I wish I had taken the class P/NP, though, as grades were not curved, which he did not make explicit.

One of the most boring teachers I have ever taken. He is a philosophy teacher teaching environmental studies. Seems like he is learning the material with us. When you ask him a question, half the time he does not know the answer and asks the class if they know the answer. Does not present lecture material well. Don't take this class unless you Must

Why UCSD would elect a philosophy prof to teach an soc. based environmental class I cannot begin to understand. I like Callender, but his grasp and clarity of environmental issues is not sufficient to be of any use for this class, it's as if he's learning along with us. If you do not have to take ENVR 130 with him don't, stick to phil.

Best professor at UCSD, at least out of those I've taken.  I loved that class.  Callender made the class fun and still managed to touch on all the issues that needed to be addressed.  I enjoyed going to class.  Definitely take this class!
Great professor with interesting lectures. He loves the topic, and he's very clear and coherent in explaining many confusing topics. Tricky multiple choice questions on tests though.
While Prof. Callender is a nice guy and willing to help, he's a bit boring in lecture. His TAs also grade very harshly, so watch out. His exam are rough, but go to lecture and you'll be fine.
craig callender is a bad ass and i loved this class.
When teaching a worldview that is contrary to his own, he has been known to depict them with straw man arguments.

Lectures had a comfortable feel to them, though I got the impression that the professor was nervous around us.  His enthusiasm for the subject is obvious, and the assignments were easy-going, essay-based.  Watch out for grading--I got a nasty surprise.

100% would and will take Professor Crofts again. It is obvious that she cares a lot about her course content, and she encourages students to share their thoughts. She takes students' opinions seriously, and answers questions so clearly and concisely. Assignments are not difficult. Not too much reading. VERY easy to talk to outside of class.

Amazing and sweet professor! Lectures are engaging and she encourages participation in class but doesn't force it. You can choose to have graded attendance or not, she accepts late work with no penalty, assignments and tests are easy and don't require too much. She's an easy grader just as long as you meet all the requirements. Highly recommend!!

WOW! I loved Prof. Crofts' class! Very engaging, invites discussion but is also understanding of every students' circumstances. Fun assignments and discussions; since I took her Food class it was often applicable to daily life. Attendance is mandatory if you want to to be! (you can choose which is cool). Take her classes, you won't regret it.

SHE IS AMAZING! I actually took her for soci 137: sociology of food! She is very caring, flexible and understanding. For the class itself, class is mandatory if you choose it to be (she gives you the choice). There is one group paper and the rest are papers instead of a midterm and final! Very chill easy A class. Take this class with her!

Lectures are actually fun never minded attending. optional occasional group work or solo. grade is mostly homework and a take home final and yeah that's it. the actual content was really good too honestly so it made it even easier to actually learn something without it hurting.

Professor Crofts is one of my favorite professors at UCSD. Her class is structured so students can succeed. You have the option of getting graded for attendance or opting out if you plan to miss more than the number allowed. There's numerous assignments and papers due throughout the course so get ready for busy work, but she does grant extensions.
Professor Crofts is amazing! I'm so glad that I took her Sociology of Food course and look forward to taking more classes with her. Highy recommend any of the courses she's teaching!

Professor Crofts is truly the sweetest person. She's an amazing professor, and it's been a wonderful experience taking her course. She's been incredibly supportive and cares deeply for her students' wellbeing and success.

Professor Crofts is an amazing professor, her lectures and assignments were incredibly engaging. She is very caring and takes the time to leave thoughtful feedback which is greatly appreciated. I 100% would recommend and would take another class with her again.

Amazing prof!!! Lectures were interesting and she really takes the time to give feedback to each and every assignment, she is super thoughtful and caring. Take her if you want to take an enjoyable class and get an A!

Professor Crofts is truly amazing, caring, and very sweet. Her contents for this specific class were genuinely really interesting and all her assignments were fair to complete. She gives amazing feedback to all of them and makes you feel appreciated for putting in time and effort in her class. I could not recommend her more!

Professor Madigan and her TAs are so thorough with their explanations I really appreciated all the work they put into the presentation slides and the mandatory discussions.
