The only thing that stopped me from getting an A+ was I missed a discussion class, but they give you 2 free excused absences so thats on me. 10/10 would take again

Dr. Madigan's class has been one of my favorites by far. As a non-biology major, the class content was fairly easy to understand and really interesting, especially the historical aspects. She is also very passionate about what she teaches. Discussion is online and there are 5 short quizzes (not cumulative) every 3-5 lectures along with a final.

Loved this class. Not a stem major so was scared to take bio but it couldn't have been more manageable. She used iClicker multiple-choice questions for attendance and discussion was optional. 4 midterms all online open note multiple choice, and same for the final. Loved it overall.

She goes fast during lectures, you can tell she is only reading off the slides. I felt like she didn't care if there was a mistake in her syllabus or study guides, outdated. Attendance is required now, I did bad with attendance but still managed to get A. Exams are poorly worded and can get confusing but should be ok w videos and extra studying.

Mandatory attendance via iclicker attendance polls that are worth a good chunk of your grade - lots of opportunity for extra credit - short exams but can be worded difficult at times - good lecturer and TA's who were always accessible outside of class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the easiest professors IMO. Class attendance is mandatory through iClicker, and lectures were easy to grasp. There are weekly journals; it's a bit tedious but helpful for me in understanding what we're going to learn in lectures. Bless her soul for making all the exams online b/c it's such a life saver. Would strongly recommend!

She is not a good lecturer and goes fast, making everyone confused. I mostly self-taught the material, but this wasn't too difficult. 4 midterms & final are all online, open note, and taken remotely. Exams tested on learning objectives and were fairly easy. 1-3 biologist journals per week are kinda a waste of time but easy.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Midterms are online and open note. There are 2-3 weekly assignments that don't take too much time. Attendance is mandatory but she reads straight off the slides and doesn't really add anything to them while talking. Doesn't really interact with students, not super inviting.

Very easy class. Key to passing the exams is reading the slides as well as any other resouces given the fact that the exams are open everything and can be taken remotely. Biologist journals are basically just a paragraph of you yapping lol very easy but you need to stay consistent with participation and attendance.
First midterm was the worst but they got better after that. Contrary to prior reviews, attendance now requires iclicker use so you have to go everyday as it is a good chunk of your grade.

This was the easiest class I have ever taken. The first midterm was very problematic due to the wording on many of the questions. But after many students complained through muddiest points, she changed improved the rest of the midterms which was great!!! All exams are open note, open internet, and could also be done remotely or in class. Would rec!

The lectures are fine and I like how discussing with peers is encouraged. Despite this, I would never take this class again. The grading is extremely unfair. The tests have few questions, no partial credit, and the are worded poorly. I felt at times that I was guessing what the prof Madigan wanted rather than finding what was correct.

Her slides are very straightforward and her tests are all online and really short. They are open everything, so it was a great class to take. Some questions were too basic that they could have multiple answers but she gives extra credit anyways. Had over a 100 the whole quarter! DEF RECOMMEND HER!!!!!!

Although her classes are fast-paced and can get kind of confusing, in general, she is an amazing professor. Gives a TON of extra credit. All of the midterms and even final are online. Replies to emails super fast as well! The only homework are Biological Journals, which are just sort of reflections and research. I would take her again.

I ACTALLY TOOK BILD30 with her!! idky rmp doesnt have the tag but she was very easy! lots of quizzes but all quizzes and exams were online! discussions mandatory but super helpful, not super duper biology based but rather historical and simple.

Professor Madigan is very generous: lots of extra credit, awarded extra points to underperforming exam questions, easy homework. Though lectures were boring and her way of explaining was often difficult to understand, all of the other perks mentioned made up for it. If you needed clarification she was always willing to explain. Recommend for BILD 1
Bad lectures. The professor only reads the slides nonstop, in an extremely non-engaging way, and fast. Do not recommend it.

The best professor I have had at UCSD so far. Her lectures and PowerPoint slides are amazing and they clearly communicate the material. Her tests are also amazing, they are multiple choice and open internet and notes. If I had the option to choose her for every bio class, I would. Overall 10/10 professor HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!!

Attendance is not mandatory, there are menti polls. Tests are on gradescope and open-note, provides supplementary material and study guides as well as practice problems. Adjusts tests since if everyone got it wrong she reasons that the question's formatting was confusing, super equitable and smart. offers "muddiest point" fourm feedback !

The tests are kind of misleading in some senses. Wish the professor can make the tests more specified and increase number of questions. Lectures did not use iClickers, wish the lectures in the future to switch to iclickers for better class participation.
The tests are on the platform Gradescope. The questions are sometimes confusing due to lack of clarity.

I felt like Prof. Madigan's lectures were very straightforward and informative. It really felt like you learned something when leaving the class. Her lectures hold a lot of information, so it may seem overwhelming for some people. They are not boring, and she tries her best to make the information applicable to real-world situations.

Very nice professor, knowledgeable in her field. However super test heavy, and tests were a bit too hard to study for (review session didn't even cover half of what was on test). Midterm1 super curved to accommodate, M2 easier. Lecture doesn't really help but still counted towards grade unfortunately.

You don't need to go to lecture because its just her reading off the slides with more words added. The tests are just like the TA review sessions/practice tests she give. Pretty common sense class and easy A if you study for a few hours.
Honestly it's an easy class. Reading textbook helps tremendously with understanding the material.
she does go off topic very commonly. The lecture slides are quite unclear. She cares way too much about attendance. Take her only if you have to.

You should definitely take Dr. Creel's class. She has an extremely fair and truly excellent grading system, and she uses scientific methods to help you genuinely master what she teaches. Before every exam, the TAs hold a review session—both the review slides and the problems are helpful! Everything she tests you on can be found in the lectures.

The best grading system among all the lectures I've taken. Only need to participate in half of the lectures and sections to get full score in attendance. However there's about 30 questions in each midterm and all are multiple choices so 1 wrong answer will make you lose many points.
The fact that her grading system is fair and well-designed already puts her above many others. I also love her teaching style.

Professor is very knowledgable in her field (language). Class structure is well organized/ easy to follow. Overall grade is mostly reliant on exams, exams are heavy, not multiple choice, they require more studying than other courses. Final is cumulative but she does round. Slides were at times overly complicated, reading the book was more helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Profesor is very knowledge in her field (language). Class structure is well organized easy to follow. Overall grade mostly based on exams, exams are not multiple choice so they require more studying than other courses, Final is cumulative. Slides can be confusing, overly complicated, reading the book was more helpful.

She is a very quirky professor that puts a lot of her personality into lectures. I find it very entertaining, and you can tell she is very interested and inspired by her field of study. I highly recommend this course for 14a.

Easy class and all content is in her lectures. She rambles a little bit but that's just because there's not much material to go over. She had us buy a textbook but it was never used, so I would suggest opting out of the online textbook if you want to save $30. Midterms and finals were easy and all multiple choice. Pretty boring but very easy class.

The professor structures the class very straight forward and rarely leaves stuff out that is in the book. The midterms are quiet difficult but if you dedicate a good amount of study time to this class, it's not impossible to do well. Creel gives out no homework just weekly quizzes that are on Canvas. She's super sweet!!

She is an amazing lecturer. She doesn't make the course material boring. She is witty, and has a clear layout on Canvas of what is expected from the students. She is responsive, and has a very comprehensible layout of her course both in lecture and on Canvas. The material is of average difficulty, and with some studying, tests are a breeze.

An ok class with an ok professor... The bulk of the course was just lecture, and that was pretty much just Dr. Creel repeating what was on the slides. There were two midterms (each worth 20%) and a final exam worth 30% of the course grade.

Quizzed on material presented a week after. I feel like she tries to come off chill but you're left confused with her way of explaining. Exam averages in the low-mid 70-65% range. Curved each to B- average. Make sure to write VERY GOOD notes & actually read the textbook to try to understand because her ridiculous slides won't get you far at all
All of her tests are tricky. Examples given in class are hard to understand for beginner. Speak too fast

Professor isn't terrible, but the course itself is confusing and takes a lot more effort than just taking notes during lecture. Her examples can be helpful, but I would highly recommend reading the textbook and creating your own examples.

Lectures are awfully boring and attending lectures becomes a burden because of them being mandatory. Also her slides lectures are a thousand percent useless when it comes to studying and it's pretty much the only thing we can study. Write lots of notes.

The subject is kind of hard to understand even if you have a music and linguistic background, but if you ask for help Dr. Creel is available outside of class and enthusiastic to answer questions. I would say it's overwhelming to keep up with the article summaries, but overall I liked this class and am glad to have taken this professor.

The quizes are based on the book; quiz topics are barely covered in lecture; they are taken on Canvas, and the correct answers aren't shown. There was no practice tests given, so you have to go over EVERYTHING yourself and you might not know what to practice or where your weaknesses are. Lectures feel useless, and sometimes slides are unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Creel is clearly an enthusiastic person in the field she is studying and shows care towards her students. She tries to be make the class as interesting as possible. Still, the materials are just quite boring sometimes. I guess it will be better if you take classes of the areas she is researching in.

Concerned about confirmation bias in these comments. I just reported blatant lies about another prof (claims she late or didn't show up;  can easily be shown false).  For Creel it's more subtle.  She's not at all bad! ppl see prev neg comments & capes.  When they don't like class or prof, parrot the same. Creel is fine, some of these comments not!

Music and the mind: Her lectures and slides give you hints to the only exam in the course. She also provides a study guide, do it, you will get an A on the midterm. Simple, Concise, and thought provoking. If you have a background in instrumental music performance, this course is for you. if you don't. Put in the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I think if you go to lecture & study this class is  difficult. Prof Creel is actually funny and she is not bad as some of the reviewers here. The expectations were clear and grading was fair. She was not the best of the best but I would not avoid her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She isn't an interesting lecturer. The material had the potential to be very interesting but she didn't do a good job of presenting it.

Her tests are ridiculous. You can't learn from your mistakes since she doesn't tell us what we got wrong on our weekly quizzes. Her midterm is fill in the blank with the most specific words that you most likely forgot about. The book is more informative than her lectures. She makes this intro to stats way harder than it needs to be. Don't take her.

Hilarious. She doesn't even cover the material that will be on the weekly quiz until the week after. She posts up hilarious lecture slides which are full of blanks so you need to sit through her boring lecture which teaches nothing at all. For her weekly online quizzes, she does not give ANY feedback so you don't even know what you got wrong. RAGEE

She's a nice lady (a little small minded from some of the comments she makes),  but is a very unorganized and scattered lecturer. I don't find her lectures or notes very helpful. She tends to over complicate the material.

She is officially my worst experience in UCSD. Her lectures are basically the repetition of what's written in the book. She cuts her own explanations with random, irrelevant stuff, which makes it even harder to focus on her lectures. She deliberately tries to make the easy material harder than it is, young idealistic lecturer  complex probably.

Creel is a bit pretentious and can say some semi-offensive things sometimes for a joke. Although she is a nice woman, she is a poor professor. She is unclear and is bad at explaining concepts. She gets caught up in the nitty-gritty of experiments and by passes the important ideas altogether. Her notes are useless and not helpful. Tests are hard too
So easy. Never went to class except for once. She's clear and easy to follow but her speaking voice irritated me.

Ok professor. Pretty clear on what she presents. Material is not too hard to understand.  Grading can be a bit tough. Also exams can very from very hard (1st midterm I got a 65%) to pretty easy (2nd midterm I got a 95%). Language is her specialty so she's very knowledgeable on the topic.

This class is incredibly boring, but it is easy to get a good grade if you go to each lecture and take good notes. She's not great at explaining sometimes and I did use the older edition of the book on a few occasions to clear up certain concepts. Overall not the worst, not the best. I think she needs to ripen a bit as a professor.

She's a dull lecturer and she makes her midterms way harder than they need to be. Her class is kind of a joke. The only plus side to taking her class is there's no book to read. However, her lecture notes are practically non-existent because they are so poorly done. Avoid her if you can.

Class format is every lecture is taught by a different UCSD professor discussing their work. Topics are all over the place so there is no real continuity between lectures, making it memorization for the most part. Most of the lecturers were pretty bad and very boring. Class isn't too hard, studying will get you an A- easily.

She didnt doing anything. This class revolves around guest lecturers, which really sucks because there isnt a very good flow of information since all the lectures were on different topics. No textbook was nice. Easy grading scale, and tests werent too difficult. Extremely boring though.

Her tests were not reflective of the material, which is probably because her lectures were always unclear. She gives you the basics of a concept, but then does not elaborate on it but expects you to know it on the tests. Bad TAs too- can't tally points up, wrong grading, etc. I did well in her class, so don't think it's because I'm bitter!

She made sense, yes, but her tests didn't seem to represent what she taught... Or at least the wording was weird. And, I'm sorry, but the TAs weren't very helpful... I went to 5 sections hoping it would help, but it didn't... AND SHE PODCASTS!!!!!! :)   (also, COGS 14 with her was easy.)

i feel like she didnt really clarify alot of her material enough.  some of her TAs didnt even understand the material fully cuz there would be times in review session that they didnt know some of the material as well.  to me thats a little unacceptable.  as for her exams, they're easy for hte mos part.  but for some reasonthe final was worded badly

Prof. Creel is fun and entertaining and I'm certain that she is a good professor for other classes. However, her cogs 14 class is useless. She does not provide examples or explain the material in such a way that is comprehensible. The assignments and tests are either ludicrously cover material that was not explained in class or are pointless.
Awesome class! Easy A ! Just study lecture notes and you will be fine ! Great professor !

This was one of the most straightforward classes I've taken at UCSD. Were the tests harder than others? Yes, but it's an upper division course--you have to THINK while taking the test. The questions weren't ambiguous at all--straight from lecture slides and the study guide. You didn't even have to read the book. Also the TA's were awesome.

Class/material is not hard, after taking PSYC105, but her exams are ambiguous, her lecture slides are not very helpful in understanding material, and it's HARD to pay attention in her class. You drift off and stop going because it's PODCASTED, but then you get lazy with the class. Podcasts = great for an 8AM class. She's a nice prof though!

It sucks that there are limited professors from Cog Sci to teach because I don't think Creel could teach at all.  Even though the materials were not hard, it was difficult to see what she was asking for. I wouldn't recommend her, but not much choice.  Her exams were ambiguously questioned and the answer she looks for is something very specific!!

She is nice and has a good sense of humor, but her tests are ambiguously written. Even if you know the material well, it is difficult to know what she is looking for on an exam. I would still recommend her overall, but only if you're a good test-taker.
Creel needs to rethink her tests. I know the material very well but her exams make it difficult to show that. I don't even understand some of her questions. I really dislike her style.

I am glad to see that other students also had a hard time deciphering the test questions for 101B. The material, while not incredibly difficult, when presented on the tests transforms into something vague. Not being an excellent test taker myself, but feeling that I know the material, has been a challenge in this class.

I don't know why some people gave her such a bad rating. Her exams were fair and straight forward. As long as you go to the lectures, you will get an A. You don't even need to read the book since practically everything on the test is based on her lectures.

Terrrrible professor. Doing well on the exams requires deciphering her wordy questions to figure out what she really means. Very unprofessional, she yawns during her own lectures!!! Please spare yourself the pain and avoid Dr. Creel.
Just took her midterm. JOKE. I hate when professors try to make such easy material into complicated shenanigans. DISLIKE.
the final was pretty easy and straight forward.

I thought the class was pretty boring overall but most of the class consisted of guest speakers who presented different topics. Therefore, it didn't build on one topic like I would have liked. However, the final was pretty easy and straight forward.

The poster who said that she tests you on your testing abilities: 100% agreement here. The test questions were by and large phrased ambiguously. A correct answer was based more on your ability to figure out what the question meant than any understanding of the material. Do not recommend this professor (she is nice tho) unless you have to take her.

I went into this class with a positive attitude, but her lectures were soooo boring! The class itself was fairly easy, but the material was not intellectually stimulating, and I spent most lectures on facebook. Also, she did a terrible job of explaining relatively simple concepts. When I study for her tests, I ignore the lectures and just read.

One of the best, most delightful profs I've had! Lectures were interesting (she used funny youtubes to illustrate points), stimulating, & engaging. Her dry sense of humor had chuckling every class and the exams were very fair. You can get an A by paying attention to lectures alone. She's also adorable and I loved her outfits!

The professor is helpful, but the class itself is stupid and useless. I got an A- in the class, but still i think there are more beneficial classes than Cogs 1. I was really interested by the subject, but class is boring. I rarely attended lectures and still managed to get an A- in the class. I wouldn't recommend spending your tuition money on this

The materials in this class are fairly easy if you study, BUT she tests you on your testing abilities, not the information you retained. Therefore, no matter how much you study, it's hard to get an A if you don't have good testing skills. She especially likes to trick you with questions that can go both ways. Take this class with another prof :)
She's really cool and helpful. Her class is really interesting!!
Great class; it's as simple as that. She's obviously brilliant, but Dr. Creel's sense of humor is what keeps class interesting. On an academically unrelated note, she's hot.

Fantastic. One of the best profs I had at UCSD. Took this class for a Computer Science elective. I thought it was so fun, it made me wish I was a COGS major! Dr Creel has this awesome dry sense of humor that had me cracking up almost every class period, and showed xkcd comics on her slides. I only fell asleep once all quarter... a record for me!

She explained things well, and she also podcasted and posted her slides. She throws in funny things here and there too, which helps to keep the mood light. She used LOTS of examples of experiments done to prove or disprove a theory, which I enjoyed. I never did any reading aside from skimming it for the homework, just pay attention in lecture.
Inspiring. Gives great feedback and lots of individual attention.
Super nice, helpful, smart.
Great professor

I think he is most suitable to teach scripting classes. The methods and frameworks he taught in writing script really influence me a lot. Especially the long emails he sends every week can really teach you things. Someone said that he pretends to be nice and smart but only cares himself, but all in all he is really GENEROUS IN GRADING.

Excellent individuated resource suggestions - really smart in this way. Blunt/tough in email but get over it because he's really caring in person. I said VIS183 but I had an independent study and writing course and none of the above listed.
Great

Jordan Crandall is one of my favorite VIS professors. His VIS149 (Contemporary Computer Subjects) class was really inspiring and it actually changed the way I think about popular culture.  He is nice, helpful, and willing to work with students.  This class was also an easy A.
excellent professor

no no no no. this professor is really full of himself and likes to try to talk really intelligently. so much so that it hinders most of us from understanding what he's talking about. im sure he's a nice person(sometimes), but as a teacher... only take him if you really need to. he grades strangely.

u discuss readings in class. u have one project. midterm is presenting idea. final is finished project. u can do whatever u want on a chosen topic (video/flash/website)with ur skills(if u learned any from vis program at ucsd). u learn nothing from this class, it's boring, and his remarks at times can make him seem like an ass, but it's an easy A.
awesome
I actually learned a lot in this class. His lectures can be complicated but it is worth it if you stay with him.

He showed up 60% of the time. He even missed the first lecture. When he was actually there, he would lecture on the same single point for over an hour (the apparatus). Doesn't explain things well at all. He trys to make himself sound intelligent by using unnecessary jargon and he even made up vocabulary which hinders the flow of information.
the most interesting professor i've ever had

Didn't really do much except stand around talking about apparatus. Also, he bailed for a couple of classes, durng which the TAs taught the class. During the times he wasn't there, the quality of the lecture was basically the same, which shows how necessary he is to the class.

Was quite good at first. Becomes very disorganized at the end of the quarter. I like the topics we go through in class, but his notes on screen prove to be a big distraction. I'd rather have him talk instead. Trying to listen to him and copy down the notes that he would never post at the same time is too much to handle.
Hate this guy... He was gone the last half of the quarter and we had practically no lectures during that time period.  I also had a power-hungry TA which doesn't help either.
Awesome
No Comments
No Comments
Fun class.  Watched lots of movies during lectures.  Yudi is great TA.  Made movies.  Crandall fair on exams.  TA's grade them.  Fast lecturer.  Type your notes you'll never get them down.
Topics are interesting.  Very good at administering and providing a enviroment that promotes discussion.
No Comments
He seems very interested in us. Very smart and he's really buff.
Decent class, but 3 hours is a long time to sit and discuss readings. He has very little humor, but the topics of the class are pretty interesting overall.
He's serious about his work, and it shows.  The only thing he needs is a new outfit.  The white collared shirt and tight wornout jeans are just a tad fruity.

Brian Cross was very insightful and had some really interesting films that I would have otherwise would never watch. He is also very chill and just overall pretty easy to talk to, and is pretty much very understanding if there is any problems with assignments and stuff like that

I've had Brian for two quarters now and I genuinely love his class. He is an inspiring artist and truly cares about what he teaches. He is super laid back and only asks that you try your best and show up. He is understanding and actually cares about his students beyond the classroom.Having him as a professor reminded me why I want to be an artist.

Cares about his students and is really funny. Gives good feedback and conducts crit in a way that leaves none feeling awful about themselves. Classes are 3 hours, but his jokes and humor make time pass fast.

His lecture is inspirational, and he always wants us to think very deeply as a filmmaker by displaying certain documentary during the class. However, in terms of his assignments, I am sick of that. His topic description is usually very unclear, and his critique is very self-centered.

I didn't understand his lectures. The gist was social justice issues. He grades tough yet doesn't even do the grading. I felt that he explained the standards of his "tough" grading to the TAs pretty vaguely. One group got an A that didn't even follow directions yet we got a B & followed directions like what. The readings are difficult & don't help.
Probably the best thing that has happened to UCSD media. He has really shaped the department and is very down to earth yet knowledgable and inspiring.

His lectures had nothing to do with homework and most of what he did was go off on political tangents and promoting Kahlil Joseph, who is a great filmmaker but come on. Obvious communication gap between him and TA's because they would show material in section that he would show in lecture so I saw Citizen Kane and a 15 hour documentary 2x in a day
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Easily the best Professor UCSD has in regards to media. Great teacher with tons of real world experience.

Brian Cross teaches media however after lecture 2 it was clear that politics and racism are the only thing he ever considers. In no way am I doubting his passion or integrity, this criticism is of his complete lack of awareness. He goes off on long tangents about racism, patriarchy & politics. Sadly, I have very little to take away from this course
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: While the films he shows in lecture are useful to watch, his lectures themselves go too off topic too often. The class is supposed to be an introduction to media but he goes into tangents about historical backgrounds and his political views.

Excellent professor. Honestly, I slept through the lectures, but that's because they were 3 hours (6pm-9pm). He's really passionate about the course and the TAs are amazing. Only four assignments the entire quarter (two papers and two videos), which weren't too bad. There were a lot of readings, but you can get by without them. Highly recommend.

Lectures are somewhat boring, and can put you to sleep easily.  The projects during the quarter were interesting and somewhat fun.  The midterm and final papers are not too difficult either.  Overall, just meh. TBH I just slept in his class and did the homework.  Oh yeah, mandatory attendance sucks.

Good professor. Tons of reading, but what he assigns is actually interesting. Attendance is mandatory, but classes are mostly spent discussing the readings, so make sure you get them done. Grade is based only on 2 tests, but he also gave 1 extra-credit assignment and curved a LOT. His TA Ben Merrill is really sweet and understand, loved him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Csordas is one of the most unique professors, I've been fortunate enough to meet. I was impressed by his research and past educational career. During class, I was frequently engaged and the readings were super interesting. You won't find another class like this at UCSD. Make sure to show up even if you don't finish the reading.

He is a facilitator for the small seminar-style capstone for Global Health. He's kind of quirky and follows the mold of an absent-minded professor sometimes (b/c he's so busy!) He's still very knowledgeable but is not super approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Csordas is one of the brightest anthropologists out there today and this class is one of the most interesting you will ever find. It's not for everyone, and you must read the material, but if you do, the payoff is great. We were graded on two take-home essays of 8-10 pages. If you come to class and do the reading, you will do fine.

Loved this professor this course is very chill. He has lots of anecdotal experience and most have some value. Lectures are easy midterm and final are online. He rambles a bit but explicitly says whats on tests

Just make sure to pay attention in class and take notes. The people giving this lecturer a 1/5 clearly didn't pay attention/go to class lol

his slides are terrible for studying (they're just pictures) of topic unrelated to the finals and midterm, he doesn't follow the textbook, and  the exam is based off things he said in class (not podcasted), his teaching style is just awful.

I actually don't know why the professor has such low ratings, he wasn't as bad as I thought. He does lectures but I would say the only hard thing about the class was the exam, just study for the math problems and you'll do fine. The concepts he taught was easy to understand too so I would say go for it if you're thinking about it.
After finishing undergraduate and experiencing multiple professors, by far the most unreasonable professor I've experienced
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: entire grade is basically based on exams so if you do badly, oh well. questions on exams were multi-step, so if you get one wrong, you get the whole question wrong basically (there's 4 multi-part questions).

Like the other comment, I was really worried about this class and the prof but he does care about his students and he does want us to succeed. If you did well on the midterm, he let us use that score for the final so most of the class didn't have to take a final. Attend class, pay attention, take good notes, and study and you'll succeed.

To be honest, going into the quarter I was super nervous after reading all of the comments but I ended with a 98% in the class. As long as you go to a lecture, pay attention, and study, you will be fine. His tests are pretty detailed but it is not information that is too advanced. The class is structured well and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: worst Professor ever don't take this class. Classes where mandatory in order to pass and you had to memorize EVERYTHING he said during class

The midterm and final were very difficult because he expected you have known everything already, and there is never a curve. Please rethink of yourself why you have to go through this situation if you do not want to waste time and money.Finally, you struggle with it.Not a chance at success.

reviews.comment: Grade based on the Midterm and the Final only. He offers no study guides, just says "review the slides," with half the slides being pics of Warren Buffet with inspirational quotes. The class average for both the midterm and final was an F at less than 55%, and there is never a curve. Required textbook material not covered. Not a chance at success.

Do yourself a favor, stay away from this worst professor at UCSD. He graded the Midterm 1, 2 and the Final are extremely difficult. The lectures were interesting but He talked mostly of stories about his asset and personal life which were not important to the exams. Stay away if u don't want to have the bad grades from him.Tough grader on exams.

reviews.comment:
Tested on material that is not slide based so showing up to lecture is important because he tests you on THINGS HE SAYS, aka: fill in the blank of sentences I told you from Week 1. 
This class is crazily weighted and you are only graded on your exams. Go to office hours. Befriend the TA. There is ec though which do every. single. one.
Worst Rady professor I have experienced
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Attend lecture & pay attention, & you will do fine. Plenty of extra credit! He shares life stories/goes on tangents, but they're all interesting & useful. If you are looking for a class to slack off in, this is not for you. But there is no homework, no readings, & he wants to set you up for success as an adult in the workforce! 10/10 recommended!

Such a horrible experience. I've never had such an uninspiring and non supportive professor. He expects you to know things even if and he goes off on so may tangents about his life. The things that were important were only talked about for a few minutes out of the whole lecture. Be prepared to be confused for majority of the class. Dont recommend.

Horrible experience, class was graded almost completely on exams which were very difficult. The lectures were interesting but consisted mostly of stories about his life which were not important to the exams. Lecture slides were not helpful at all, as most do not include the information talked about in class. Good guy, but worst professor at UCSD.

reviews.comment: Please im warning you now do not take this class. The grade is purely based off the exams. His lectures are so confusing you have to remember every little thing he says or you will fail. Will literally blab about random stuff. I hated this class please don't take
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid. I was forced to switch from another professor to this class and the there was a stark contrast in the teachers and courses. I genuinely want to retake this class just so that I can actually learn the content, not for the grade. I look back with regret. Do not make the same mistake I have made.

reviews.comment: If you want to keep your high GPA, don't take his class!!
the slides are not very helpful for study

While attendance isn't mandatory, the slides from class that he would upload would be missing information. He can be condescending and rude towards students at times. He would also grade things unfairly at times. Overall, he was not a great professor, most of the class material, I had to self-teach myself or go to my friends and the TA.

reviews.comment: His in person lectures may seem enjoyable however he makes the tests seem easy and simple. However to score well the tests require you write down everything in every lecture verbatim and memorize every detail. His tests are awful without enough time and do not reflect the course. Average for midterm for both classes was D- with no curve DO NOT TAKE
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As others said, class is easy overall, and there gives you more than enough time to work on your other courses but exam questions are slightly made a bit confusing or harder than they should be. I liked attending lecture, typically ended early after 1.5 hours.

Do not take him. If you don't remember every little thing in lecture you will not pass his exams. If you skip lecture once you will miss 2-3 questions on the next midterm or final. Uses practically nothing from the textbook, midterm and final were extremely difficult. If u don't remember everything from lecture you wont pass either. MGT181
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's a marketing class, not a mathematics class. Eberhard's 103 had more math involved than a marketing class should have. Also, he likes to trick-up the exams, and put things in there that aren't covered in his lectures. He literally sets up his students for failure. Please, for the sake of your grade, take another professor.

The class content was interesting, but the focus of the lectures leaned heavily towards the instructor's life stories and opinions. Communication proved challenging; he occasionally came off as rude and displayed a lack of concern for his students.

Eberhard's teaching is confusing. Lectures and exams are tough, and he's not easy to reach. He says don't use the book, but his slides are a mess. I studied a lot but got a D on the midterm. Asked for help, but it's hard to get. Things need to be clearer and more helpful.

BEWARE: his teaching methods need improvement. Class content lacks organization. Despite extensive study efforts, exam time constraints pose significant challenges. Limited communication avenues and infrequent office hours create obstacles for seeking assistance. He makes it clear that student success isnt a priority and. The job is for extra cash.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Without a doubt the worst professor I've had at Rady. Difficult tests, pointless lectures talking about his life and experiences, while not clearly reviewing the material that ends up being on tests. While he's a nice guy and has interesting stories/perspectives, going to class was (mostly) useless for my grade.

Professor Eberhard is a captivating lecturer and pretty accessible outside of normal class hours. All the exam questions are derived from the lecture slides, verbally gone over, or done through whiteboard work. He is a fair grader and passionate about the subject. Honestly one of the best professors I've had.

His exams are unnecessarily difficult and his lectures don't accurately reflect the exams. He is rude and makes it difficult to ask for help. It makes me wonder if he even enjoys teaching or is passionate about marketing. I do not recommend at all.

What other people say is true. I like him as a person, I enjoy his harsh personality and I loved the content of the course. However, the exams were so, so much harder than they need to be. It's for that reason alone that I give him such a low score, if was even slightly more generous with the grading he'd be a 4. NOT an easy A, avoid if possible

For those who dislike Eberhard, its because they either dont show up/listen. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF IT DOESN'T INTEREST YOU! This class requires that you be present and if you aren't ready for that then this class isn't for you. Eberhard is a professor that doesn't take any bs and if you care about your college career you will get his respect.

RUN! I never leave a review but for this class I will. I have read every reading assignment, done all the extra credit & even received full credit on an extra credit assignment that apparently not everyone gets fully credit on and none of this helped. His exams are unnecessarily difficult & some questions are random. He is also rude.

This class does not measure your knowledge. It measures your ability to memorize and take verbatim notes of what the professor states, regardless of relevancy to the material. This class with Craig Eberhard is lecture-based and not learning by doing or project-based. If you want to learn anything, avoid taking this class with Craig Eberhard.
RUN, do not take his class if you want a good GPA! You don't even learn anything in this class anyway.

If you want a bad grade take his class. His lectures are all over the place and you are expected to get all the information down. The classes aren't recorded, try not to miss class even if you are sick. Tests are graded very toughly, and your grade is determined by midterm and final. He is not very respectful and a bit rude. Not even that good.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All the reviews who say his harsh and rude is just that they are so spoiled. If you are a try hard student, this course will be easy A. He is so generous with questions, if you ask good and proper questions. He only gets tough on students when they do not read announcements or emails and ask him what he has told them already. I recommend him 100%.

I like his personality. He's like New York type of person & is not California type who sugarcoating everything. That's why comments say he's mean/rude. But,I think he is straightforward. He was understandable&humanly when I explained my personal consultants. He's more understandable than inhumanity STEM professors who is restricted to their rules.

The professor treats students in a very mean way. Every time he replies to emails, he is always disrespectful and impatient. The exam is very difficult, and there is no time to finish all of the questions.
1000 total points, 450 mid, 550 final, only 90 points ec. Just took his midterm,30 Multiple choices + 6 essay questions in 1.5 hour, which is ridiculous. Bye my 4.0 GPA. RUN. DO NOT TAKE HIM.

Students asked questions during his lectures. But he ignored questions most of the time!! He only responded to students's answers that he wants. No consideration for students.

reviews.comment: Professor Eberhard was one of my favorite professors this quarter. He's a nice guy and tries to keep lecture interesting. Lecture is mandatory but worth it because he gives random extra credit and direct test questions. There's one big project which is a launch plan but it's super straightforward and he's a lenient grader. Overall, great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Listen, I had no problems with this class or professor the entire quarter. In fact I thought he was a funny, charismatic guy who really did know what he was talking about. But the final... I had my legs kicked out from under me. The questions are irrationally nitpicky. If you take him, write down EVERYTHING YOU SEE DURING LECTURE. horrible grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Its an easy subject, but the professor makes it very confusing your grade can go from A to C in seconds. 400pts midterm, 130pts project, and 450pts for a tough final. No feedback on exams you cant even see which answers you got wrong. Be careful and make sure to take notes of everything he says even if its a corny joke. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class itself consists of 20 lectures where he goes over a PowerPoint each class and basically in his own words tells you what he wants and whats important to him. There is 1 assignment throughout the whole class which means that your grade will be determined by 2 things a 400 point midterm and a 400+ point final and 80% of your final grade.

reviews.comment: Not the best lecturer but is open abt how things will b graded. reviews.comment: The class was just hard, tests were based on his words, so you really need to focus.

reviews.comment: Although Craig's lectures can sometimes be boring, he adds his own personal experiences which makes the lectures interesting. His exams are not difficult as long as you pay attention and take notes in his class. Often times he even tells you what will be on the exams.
Interesting lectures but his tests were unnecessarily difficult and heavily favored asinine details casually mentioned in class. A couple of the final questions had nothing to do with concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: rude, arrogant, pretentious. the class is hard but you can do well if you study. I just really hated him as a person

Don't be fooled, his exams are HARD. Never miss class, since he'll surprise you by drawing a diagram on the board that you have to copy exactly on the exam. Half of the final wasn't even about marketing, just his random tangents. Rude to students, condescending if you ask for help, and he doesn't really have office hours.

reviews.comment: He's a good lecturer, but it's hard to distinguish when you need to take notes, and when you can just listen. Most of the time he sounds super easy-going, so you just assume you don't need to take notes, but his exams are HARD. I studied extremely hard for the Midterm and the questions were so nitpicky. Definitely pay attention to every detail
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's OK as a professor. It's sometimes hard to tell what will be on the tests. Sometimes even if you attend all the lectures, you will miss a few questions on the tests because it seemed like it didn't matter. Midterm was easy and final was too hard. I got an A- on midterm and B- on the final, and I studied way more for the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof Eberhard is very likable and fun but he makes you work for it. He's a great professor but can be a little all over the place in his lectures, bouncing around from his slides to problems on the whiteboard but he's fair and rewards you for showing up to class. Exams are specific and challenging but the cumulative grade was curved
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He means well as a person but as a professor he is just not my favorite. Very tough class because he's a tough teacher. highly regretted taking him. midterm and final were very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: You would think a marketing would at least be not too daunting. Not the case with Eberhard. His exams are based entirely on lecture so you better be focused in/attend class. Forget the textbook. Rushes through problems that can't be found in slides or textbook. I was so lost in this class I didn't even know what I didn't know. Exams were HARD.

I hated Eberhard. His lectures made no sense, he does problems in class that he did a bad job of explaining & that show up on the exams, and his exams were long and difficult. He doesn't provide a grading template for group project and you're left lost. Only three groups out of whole class got an A.

Eberhard's a very nice guy and his lectures are quite engaging but I had a hard time understanding what he was talking about - he goes on a lot of tangents. When it came to the midterm I had no idea what to study for and failed. :( Maybe his lecture style just isn't my cup of tea idk. I personally will not be taking him again...
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I really liked his lecture style because he was engaging and he actually got to know you throughout the course of the quarter. A big portion of his tests involve stuff that he wrote on the board so actually going to class is important. You don't need the book to get an A in the class. Overall cool dude.

I really liked eberhard and feel like hes been getting chewed up by these reviews, hes funny sweet and engaging. Lecture feels like a discussion, eberhard will talk and the slides are secondary. If youre mentally present in class you will do well. This is not a class where you cram the lecture notes and expect to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: I really didn't like how Craig taught the class. As a person, he is nice and would banter with the students and has a clear and audible voice, but his style of lecture was laid out in such a weird way. He would constantly go on tangents and talk about random stuff. When it came to the tests I had no idea what to study or focus on.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Don't fall for his niceness. He claims that majority of his tests are based on the lecture, so you don't need a book. WRONG. The mid-term is a joke (scored a high A), while his final is absolutely irrelevant to the material covered in lecture. My grade dropped from a high A to a mid B so goodbye 4.0 GPA. Don't set yourself up for failure. regretful
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed his class. He is respectable and fair. He does not take participation but there are whiteboard works that will be on exams. There is one group project and about 3 case studies where he takes attendance. I would definitely take his class again.

His lecture style sometimes seems like some casual conversation, but he will sometimes emphasize that he is going to test you on this and that. The fun part about this course is the group project. Other than that, the course is less practical and more theoretical which I don't really think that's what marketing should look like.

He's only bee teaching a few years, but has tons of experience and he brings that to class. He mostly worked in medical sales, so he talks about that, but he tries to add other examples too. His lectures are casual and he's good at relating to students. The class seems to be base on broad concepts, but beware, he tests on specifics!

Professor Eberhard has a lot of experience in business, and he always shares his tips and tricks to help us succeed. He genuinely cares for his students and his work. His lectures are entertaining, and he asks for feedback so he can also learn and grow. His midterm was straight forward and fair, although his final was difficult.

I was happy to be in Mr. Eberhard's class. He speaks very cordially and his lectures make you feel like you're having a laid-back conversation. It seemed to me the tests were a little too 'specific' and didn't quite match up with his more broad style of teaching, but they were quite easy nonetheless if you paid attention.

His class was easy. This course is based on mechanical physics, which is a prereq for this class. Sometimes, his lecture seems too simple and you end up not paying attention. It is okay. I did the same. However, when it is time for you to do your homework, you might be a bit irritated by the difference in difficulty. However, watch some youtube vid
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nemat is a very engaging professor. He is one of the few engineering professors I have had who truly cares to spend time making sure the students understand the material, absolutely. He will tend to spend times on material that seems simple, however, it is with good reason. FUNNY which is great for eng. class. Exams very close to HW & pract. ones.

A very knowledgeable and genuine professor. He is a little goofy during lectures but this makes the class much more palatable and even funny. Almost too easy at times (could be difficult if you have a different prof for a later class in the series) but great at reinforcing full comprehension of a topic.

He's (more than) a little crazy, but definitely knows what he is talking about. If you put in any effort, the class is pretty straightforward. Midterms pulled straight from the homeworks with different numbers.

He knows the materials and he knows them well. I don't know if he's helpful in his office or not, but the lecture comes right of his head. Makes small mistakes at times. READ the book at least once before or after the lecture. DO the homework and sample quizzes and tests and you should be fine.
Yea, what the guy below said. Stay away from professor nemat. he's ignorant, and he doesn't care about students learning. Everybody literally cheated, and he doesn't even know it. Dumb old dude.

PROFESSOR IS AWESOME! The class is hard, but he provides every resource to help you. I didn't attend office hours so I don't know how good he is at helping 1 on 1, but the TA's are helpful. Old test and quizzes are posted w/solutions which are useful. Class is clear and straightforward. UNderstand your HW and you'll get an A. Also be fast.

Very to the point with his lectures. Class didn't make sense until right before the first midterm. After that, tests were exactly what he said they'd be on, which was also very similar to the hw/quizes.

frequently gave pointless/unhelpful explanations of ideas. preparation of presentations extremely time-consuming and ultimately pointless. spent large amounts of time on things that seemed straightforward/obvious/unimportant. didn't cover much material. very liberal late policy.
Nice guy who tries his best, can explain some things well, but other topics you are totally lost. Needs to do examples.
Very engaging.
No Comments
This is the worst professor I ever had.  Does not answer questions.
This professor is one of the best.

Awesome professor. CGS 101 felt like a breeze yet I learned many interesting things and was opened up to new perspectives. For CGS 101, it was MWF, but we only met MW. There's a required reading before each lecture, but if you forget to read it, don't sweat it, there's just a short period of about 10 minutes where you talk to classmates about it.

Great great great caring professor. You can tell that her students' well being matters to her. Attendance is absolutely mandatory, but worth it. 2/3 lectures are in person and friday's lecture is asynchronous, which basically means you read on your own. Very progressive and gives her final before the finals week. Love her

Easy class but a LOT reading. Professor goes over the material but she is kind of difficult to follow along with bc she goes on tangents and I got the vibe she expected us to know more than what was discussed, which is why she didn't elaborate much. so maybe don't take this class if youre new to CGS content. Shes very knowledgeable and nice-ish
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was a lot more work than I expected, especially for an English major. The essay assignments were time-consuming, requiring around 5+ hours of work each. Despite putting in the effort, I've been struggling to get decent grades, mostly C's. Might not be the best fit for those looking for an easy elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took this class to be more informed and aware of sexual violence and I feel like Professor Cuong did an amazing job at lecturing giving the class material to spread awareness. Everyone in the class was very respectful and understanding, which was very heartwarming to see and helped the atmosphere of the class. Highly recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Cuong was one of the best I've ever had. She gives very passionate lectures and tries to make them as relevant as possible so that the students can understand. Participation is very important in class, not just attendance. Lots of seminar/discussion work and reading. Weekly journals are due on Friday. Everything is fairly graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The best professor in UCSD , like you can learn a lot and free A if you always show on class.

Amazing professor. This is my second class from her and she is incredibly engaging and makes an effort to make students feel comfortable participating. Readings are sometimes a little long/difficult but class discussions help you to understand the material. She is very passionate about what she teaches. Highly recommend taking her.

Professor Cuong is very kind and caring about her students. Engaging in class and reading the material is all that is necessary to getting a good grade. Genuinely feel more educated on Gender Studies after taking her class!

She is very knowledgable about the subjects in class and runs very open-discussion based lectures that involves everyone's ideas. The assignments are really fairly graded and it is not hard to get an A.
Professor was fun and easygoing, loved having the Socratic circle and talking about the readings it was very intellectually stimulating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: CGS 109. Prof. Cuong is amazing and understanding, she cares a lot about her students and their feelings and takes a lot of value towards her teaching and learning. She wants students to truthfully grasp ideas, rather than take tests all the time. She integrates readings extremely well into lectures and applies them well towards short writings.

She was a breath of fresh air compared to other profs I've had. She's super relatable and very chill, I actually looked forward to coming to class, and the students also helped guide discussion with class material so it was very intellectually engaging. Hw was easy and the midterm/final were straightforward. I'll miss this class :(

I love her! She was very kind and knew it was a summer course, so she did not assign a lot of work. We only had 3 journals, a midterm paper, and a final paper. There were also readings and films to complete before class, but it was very fair for a summer class. Marisol is a good professor who truly cares about students' learning and feelings!

Amazing and truly nice professor! would do tuesday lecture online and thurs in person, attendance taken thurs sometimes for credit (10%) and the other percentages are 3 papers which are super easy. luckily made the final optional so only had to do 2 super easy papers. love this man, take him! so nice
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super easy class. Two easy papers, Pinterest posts, and discussion posts. Graded super easily, movies are good, lectures are short and you don't really need to watch them at all. That said, Marez gives interesting lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class and professor. Just watch the movies, two essays, pinterest posts, and weekly mandatory discussion. No attendance to lecture really needed. Mandatory discussion though unless you do asynchronous option which requires longer discussion post

Super easy class and professor. Lectures are interesting and relevant to the assignments, which are a weekly discussion post based on the movie or reading for that week, all graded on participation. Midterm and final were also very easy and participation based. Great professor for an easy, interesting class!

Super easy humanities course! Lectures were a bit drawn out (lots of him just reading paragraphs off of the slides) but the grading was generous. Discussion participation counts (with an asynchronous option), easy midterm (5 page paper OR creative project), and easy final (2 pages on what you hope to remember from the class). TAs were all great

Easiest humanities class I've ever taken. For Spring 2021, grades were consisted of weekly discussion posts for completion, an easy midterm essay, and a final class reflection paper. Lectures weren't needed to get an A either. Definitely recommend!

This is based on his class during the first quarter we started remote learning: He only had weekly Pinterest posts one midterm paper and the final paper. I didn't show up to class much but it is easy as long as you watch the films and put some effort into the work he gives.
Great class and prof!

He is horrible teacher, says um or uh between every word, reads off of slides verbatim, brings nothing useful to class. He won't post lectures, until midterm, otherwise no one would come to class. Never answers question, and gives inaccurate facts about history.

I definitely like this class a lot more walking out of it than when I walked in to it. I learned a lot of interesting things. Professor Marez is a pretty cool guy. He's passionate. Some said he stuttered a little but it didn't seem to bother me. Five two page papers to make sure you did the readings. Three pop quizzes to ensure you go to class.
I must say that he is a very interesting professor, he is funny and passionate. Haven't finish this class yet but I really like him.
Top Academician!
Great professor!
Professor was unprepared for most classes. He turned me off to ethnic studies. Very arrogant. Lacks knowledge of ethnic groups beyond his own. Most students took class for easy grade.
Great professor, very caring--interested in technology and uses it in class, just asks you to sit in the first few rows if you are using a computer

Assigns way too much reading, some that he never discusses. Gives reading quizzes that ask about ambiguous and insignificant terms that were from reading. Hates all things technological and doesn't let you take notes on your laptop unless you sit in the front two rows.

Terrible professor. Says "um" about five times in between each word. lectures have very little to do with readings, and reading is unnecessarily heavy. All he did was spout off against neoliberalism. Doesn't answer emails, and goes through powerpoints way too fast for notetaking. Also, he is against everything electronic. No laptops. DO NOT TAKE.

PLEASE RUN!
RUN FAST! PLEASE
I don't understand his behavior

Great professor, easy to get a good grade like most humanities classes. Class was actually decently interesting though not super exciting or anything, but I mean what do you expect going into a music class. Overall, I liked it and most of all it was easy.
If you make an effort, you can definitely get an a good grade in this class. The class material is also pretty interesting . Would definitely recommend.
ohh.... what can I say, it's Charles Curtis. I wonder where he shops for his clothes. :)
This guy is amazing! Dresses sharply, always makes things interesting. Love him.

most boring class i've ever taken.  midterm/final have nothing to do with any material.  you listen to stuff and analyze it.  don't go to class.  only like 13 kids did.  he's a total hippie. "i like to define music not by what music is, but by what it isn't."  yeah.
Eccentric guy. Lectures can be terribly boring. It's an easy A though.

This is a cool dude.  The music you listen to throws a lot of people off since it is pretty obscure, but if you try to get into it, the class can be pretty fun.  It's different than any other music class and it really opens up your mind to things you would have never known.
Dropped the class after 2 weeks. Too boring.

he's a bit off his rocker, but he sometimes tells some interesting stories. don't say anything bad about a composer on hw or tests though, he doesn't like that very much. So just ramble on and on in every assignment, and you'll be fine

it's my First class where I really had to know how to BS on everything-hw and tests-to get a good grade.He seems pretty intelligent and knows what he's talking about.  Although he may seem strange/unique, he's nice, approachable & wiling to help/clarify.
This guy is a really good dresser. I wish I knew where he got his clothing. This class is like pie, sweet and crumbly. Its also easy.

I agree with the 5/16/04 review. His voice sounds very educated. He rambles a lot and goes off topic. Still not really sure what this class is about but BS-ing is easy and his grading system is super lenient (he gives two makeup midterms).
He reminds me of a hippie-- he's a little weird and boring. Contemporary music is painful to listen to, but the class is pretty easy if you're a good BS-er.

Paul is the homie. Pretty straightforward class. Show up, skim the readings and you'll be fine. Paul genuinely cares about his students too, so it's pretty easy to talk to him. The weekly quizzes suck but are manageable.
quizzes out of two points suck.

Paul is such a gem. He is extremely knowledgable about all aspects of urban studies and planning and has connections in the industry like no one else. Expect guest speakers and group assignments. His teaching style is dependent on you caring about the material. If you aren't passionate about USP don't take the course, but if you are, he's the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I absolutely LOVED this class! I was a bio major (now a cog sci/psych major) and I found the public transportation class to be my favorite class I've taken. The small class size gives you lots of opportunity to interact with Paul directly. He's just the sweetest guy and you'll learn *so* much you never even considered about transportation. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures are pretty structured and you can expect what to come. Learned a lot about public transportation which I would never have known if I didn't take the class. He is approachable and makes lectures casual, like a conversation. He has a lot of practical knowledge many academics don't. Would definitely take another class from him.
No idea about what he talks about and he makes this class incredibly different from previous years. Strongly not recommended and most students skip classes or don't listen!

Professor is very knowledgeable in the subject, and topics are applicable to current events in the field of transportation. The class structure allows for real discussion alongside guest speakers in the profession every week. To gain the most out of lectures every week, be sure to keep up with readings before class.

class was set up to have guest lecturers every week. was an interesting class, but it was hard to tell what was course work and what was not. no midterm or final- just a book review and metrics assignment. curious to see if he will be teaching this course again in the winter

Absolute goat of a prof. It's a flipped classroom so you watch short lecture videos before class followed by practice problems in class that are super helpful. SO many tutoring hours. Definitely go to his office hours, even just to do the homework. I know the fail rate's high, but if you put in the effort, 35 is a very achievable class.

Has a whole discussion section dedicated to improving our studying strategies. Lectures feel like brain teasers sometimes, but useful for learning. Alongside the course, I highly recommend just going through a circuits textbook to fill in the gaps before the quizzes, and just to solidify your mental model of the material, in general. Curt is goated
Highly recommend.

Coming in with previous coding experience certainly helps, however, I think if you work hard you can learn it quick enough. Importantly, he emphasizes how different concepts work together. He provides the textbook which there are online quizzes for but they're easy if you do the reading. Exams are fair and open book/notes. Highly recommend.

I had taken a circuits class before, but many concepts were still unclear to me. He explained them so well that I finally understand them now. If you start the practice exams early and well before the quizzes, you will do fine on the exams. His lectures are engaging because you actively solve problems and get direct feedback from him.

Conceptually difficult and the tests are hard, but Curt does a great job of giving students all the resources they need to succeed. Whether that be constant tutoring hours, tons of previous exams to study with, or his bootcamps. If you can manage your time well and study effectively, you can do well. If you only try to memorize, expect to fail.

His lectures and practice exams are really helpful. He is also willing to help you with any questions during office hours. However, the work is really fast paced and challenging even though I had some programming experience.
Amazing professor. PAs can get a bit difficult. Definitely helps of you have a background in programming.

This is a challenging class but Professor Curt makes it a lot easier to get through.

He follows a flipped classroom style. The quizzes, exams and homework assignments are challenging but doable if you put in the work. This class will take alot of your time so manage your classes properly. However, I learnt a lot from this class.

Average ECE 35 fail rate w/Schurgers is 47%. Half the class! Consider taking with another professor, as SP25 (not curt) fail rate was ~30%. Much better than with Curt. Also, this is a flipped lecture, so do with that info what you will. Not much actual "teaching" in class, just on videos. Works for some, but doesn't for me :/ Exams extremely hard!
Love Curt he is actually the bomb. He was really helpful and a great lecturer. If he is teaching a class you need to take, def take the opprotunity.

Took Eng30 with Curt and it was really fun made friends and the final wasn't as hard as they had us do it one step at a time starting from week 6 instead of having it due week 10/finals week. The group projects also were very hands on.
He is good! But try to focus on class, and prep review before lectures. You will fall behind if you dont keep up the speed of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The concepts may be difficult at first, but Curt makes it easy to learn. Everything gets replaced by the final afterwards, so don't worry too much if the quizzes don't go well. There are a lot of office hours, so there are a lot of opportunities to get help, but the concepts take time and practice to learn, so don't slack off.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: horrible class

Great professor for a very difficult course. ECE 35 is a weeder class for 1/2nd year Electrical Engineers and naturally has difficult to grasp content, especially squeezed in 10 weeks. Exams are tough, but require students to master content to succeed. Schurgers puts content in layman terms so even students with no electronics background can pass.

Professor Schurgers is one of the best instructors at UCSD. He encourages participation in class through clicker questions that reasonably challenge students' understanding of the key concepts.
I appreciated his "inverted classroom" method where students are expected to read before the lecture and later attempt to digest the materials in class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Curt is amazing!  There are so many lectures and resources and he genuinely cares about 35.  Its not easy per say but its definitely doable with all the materials they offer you.

Final can be used to replace quiz/hw/lab if you score higher on final. Quizzes and homework are not that hard but required some thinking. This class is not that computation heavy instead he focused more on concepts and how to apply those concepts. Final is kinda hard tho. Also his lectures are good.

If you have basic knowledge in programming (arrays, functions, loops, pointers), this class will be a breeze. Even if you don't, don't worry. PAs are enjoyable but take a good amount of time. If you understand how the concepts interact (use gpt), the exams will be easy. Study past exams. Study in class problems. Grading is supremely generous.
He knows the material well and how to teach. If you follow his lectures and complete hw on time, you will get an easy A.

Professor Schurgers is truly an exceptional professor. He's great at explaining and breaking down concepts. His lectures are always engaging and he is often very attentive and caring towards his students. I'd definitely take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Honestly wasn't expecting to like this class but ended up really liking it because of how good of a professor Curt is. He has a reputation for being a good professor with hard tests but if you use the study materials he provides the quizzes weren't too hard and were very similar to the homework.

I personally really love Curt and I think he's an amazing professor who teaches really really well in lectures and utilizes time in lectures pretty efficiently compared to my other professors. The only drawback would be if you don't any coding background like me you might struggle doing the PA's but if you have experience this might be an easy A.

Curt is very good at teaching C. He explains the memory structures like the stack, pointers, etc. very well and gives tricky problems in class to make people think. The programming assignments require a good bit of problem solving and logic, especially the extra credit problems. I think this class is slightly harder than CSE 11, but not that bad.

He is alright at teaching C, but he puts trick questions on the tests that are worth almost half the test. I got a 50% on one of the midterms because I missed a small detail on a problem that was written in extremely small font.
geezer. He do not allow small talking during the class.

ECE 35 is time-consuming but manageable. I had severe test anxiety and struggled, but Curt and Sahar (down the road) are great professors who help you succeed, and both have wonderful TA teams. If you still fail, consider another major. ECE 65 builds on 35, 45 can be depressing, 109 challenges your sanity, and 100 will break you.
Yes, this is the man you need. If you want a real authentic engineering experience as you enter the ECE department. This is the man from Belgium you want.

He will give a lecture video before the lecture to let you know the concepts. During the lecture, he will explain a lot of examples. An excellent professor, his explanation is very clear and good. Also, he has a lot of office hours, from morning to afternoon. Easy A if you go to his lecture and watch lecture videos.
Honestly some of the stuff he said in class went over my head, but the homework and practice tests/quizzes are enough to do well.

This is definitely the worst professor ever. Do not take unless you are willing to teach yourself. He is not good at explaining and can barely speak English properly. Very bad experience for a UC professor. Spends more time trying to trick you then actually teaching the class. Horrible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor who expects you to put in the work and genuinely cares for his students. He provides plenty of resources to help you succeed. As long as you put in the time studying and listening, then passing is a cinch. Getting an A is different though.

This class is as hard as you have heard. However, Curt give a lot of work and past resources to allow you to succeed. !00% of your grade is replaceable by the final, meaning if you struggle in the beginning but begin to master it later you can still do very well (pretty much what happened to me).

You can learn a lot about C in the course. But the homework is so heavy! pace is so quick, questions are extremely tricky. Even though You do everything well in hw, reading quiz, participation, and midterm, you also have to spare no effort on preparing final which is solid 45% of the final course grades. I'm so tired..
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures are mandatory for a participation grade, the professor wasn't too bad, but the class was very hard, with too much homework and not too much time to do it. He is interested in what he teaches, but I don't think he helped much in what we have to do for the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Curt is a legendary professor. Ece 35 is a super intimidating class but it honestly felt easy with him. He's strict with how he runs class, but it's for a reason. He genuinely wants his students to succeed and he gives them everything they need in order to do so. Definitely take this professor its a no-brainer.

ECE 15 with Curt is very hard if you have no background coding or C code. I mistakenly picked the class thinking it would be chill but its not. The class is curved so 50% is a C but the final exam is worth 45% of the grade while the midterm is worth 15%. Plus Curt doesn't teach you anything useful to use in code. Try to take CSE if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things
