reviews.comment: There is a lot of homework and programming required for this class, and the autograding is very specific and it is easy to lose many points. However, the revised grading scale is very helpful. Overall, Curt is a great professor and one of the best in the ECE department.

This is one of those notorious classes at UCSD where you need to attend/watch every lecture & discussion, do every homework assignment (even those that are "nonmandatory") & lab, review old exams, and you might do alright. However, Curt is one of the best professors I've ever had and by the end of the class, I got really good at solving circuits.

ECE 35 is a hard class, but Curt wants us to succeed, and his grading scale is generous. He teaches us things to watch out for. He does a flipped classroom, so the lectures are for practice, but the lecture videos become HW. The class is not competitive because he doesn't curve, and we get access to all his past quizzes and finals for practice.

I took him for fall and he was an awesome prof. Straight to the point lectures and clear explanations for solving problems. This class requires a lot of effort. If you take the time to practice do all the HW's and review quizzes you should pass. The content is hard to grasp but there are many TA office hours at all times of the day that will help.

Took Curt for ECE 15 and 35. You would always be tricked in his lecture, which is fun and intellectual-simulating. Really a brilliant guy. You could learn how to deal with those tricky problems from him. Tests were heavy but as long as you do past quiz and bootcamp questions, you will be fine!

Professor Curt teaches very well and addresses some questions in class with participation of webclicker. Read and do questions before class. PAs are heavy but very interesting which include games that makes me love C. No Midterms, Final is a doable paper exam. TAs and tutors are extremely helpful. This class inspires my interests in programming.

Curt is a really good professor. He genuinely cares for students and he explains things clearly and well. He offers a lot of extra practice (homework, bootcamp, office hours) and I recommend that you use them so that you can do well on tests. Another tip to do well is to DO THE PRACTICE QUIZZES. I did not a few times and got whooped.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Just be aware that he has made ece 35 EXTREMELY difficult. Not by giving hard exams, but by implementing policies that are intended to make you fail the class no matter how hard you study. For instance, Hes made the final into five mini exams, meaning you have a time limit for each question so that you cant go back at all. UNBELIEVABLE!!!!!!!!!

The course is tough and theres no doubt in that. You have to work really hard no matter who teaches it but with this prof, ece 35 is all about being stressed all the time as opposed to actually learning. For instance, his oral exam(if u dont pass it u fail the class) is so stressful and unnecessary for an engineering course.
He is one of the few very caring professors you can find at the Univesity level course. He really cares about teaching his students.

Had professor Curt for both ECE 15 and 35. He's a great lecturer and is responsive on Piazza. He provides you all the extra resources and help you need to succeed on the quizzes. He cares about teaching and grading will be focused on the method rather than the answer. He teaches notoriously hard classes but makes them straightforward and manageable
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: The professor is super clear in class and assign reasonable amount of homework for us to practice. Super organized with course materials. Quizzes and tests are pretty relevant to materials covered in class. Expected to be harder but professor Curt did his best to make a hard class easier. Really learned a lot as the first ECE course I've taken here
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Curt is a great professor, I also took his ECE 15. His courses (ECE 15 and 35) are difficult for ECE beginers, but essential for future courses. My suggestion is invest time on in homework and review frequently. Ask him for help if you have questions, he is really accessible. I built a solid foundation by doing these and get A in final.
Difficult class and was made more difficult during virtual classes :/
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor was pretty unaccommodating and made the course harder and stressful this quarter by adding additional examination

Curt is the best lower div prof at UCSD. He was by far the MOST prepared for virtual classes of any of my profs; there were ZERO issues this quarter with the tech, and it all went very smoothly. He really cares about student success; many resources for keeping up with the material. Flipped classroom model is great. Class is hard, don't fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Class was difficult throughout the quarter because it was online. I felt unwelcomed in the discussion boards as sometimes the answers he would give would be passive aggressive.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor seemed to be not accommodating during times like these, especially with the switch to virtual classes on top of events happening outside in our society. The Academic Senate has given the option to have professors give out no-fault finals. Curt had the option to make his class accommodating but chose to make his class harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The course was harder than I expected. The way they grade homework is inefficient and it is difficult to tell why you got your points deducted. The worst part was that this professor is sarcastic af . His attitude in the discussion board sounds so rude and not helpful. I would rather have a difficult but caring professor than this guy

Although he was extremely hard, he was a great lecturer and showed that he really cared about your grade. To get a good grade, you just need to keep practicing, going to office hours, and MAKE SURE YOU DON'T FALL BEHIND. This class goes by so fast.
He is a really good professor. He has a good command on C. He will make you work for the course but eventually you'll feel really good!

Curt is a great professor, but his class is quite difficult. If you want a good grade, go to office hours, do lots of practice problems, and make sure not to fall behind because concepts will build on top of each other.
Hes the most amzing prof Ive had for ECE class by now. Passionate and caring. Definitely recommend him.

Curt is a solid lecturer, and I think he ran the "reverse classroom" style very well with the pre-lecture videos, weekly bootcamp problems, helpful clicker discussions. Even though I was doing poorly throughout the whole quarter, I was definitely learning and that all paid off in my final, which replaced my entire grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: He is a great professor and cares deeply about students. The class is difficult, you will need to spend some time before things begin to come easily.

I barely passed the class and even I can say this professor will go the extra mile for his students, the format for this class was new this quarter and yet I think if I put more effort into the class I would have done better. Disregard negative reviews below, nowhere close to reality highly recommended professor.

Curt really cares about teaching his students. He goes the extra mile by providing extra review sessions to really help his students. His video lectures are for the most part clear and his lectures are helpful. His quizzes were fair but the final was a little hard. Know your linear algebra and do a lot of practice problems and you should do well.
He is a good professor, he explains material very well, but he is extremely difficult, the key to get a good grade in his class is to go to his office hour and ask him questions.

Very Good teacher. Explains concepts very well. Extremely helpful in office hours. To do well in this class just do every problem from the old exams and understand them, because he asks all the same questions again, just in a different way. Great Teacher.

Expect to work your butt off for this class. I didn't get too much out of lecture but his notes are extremely useful, and he's great in office hours. Not the prof to take if you want an easy A, but ECE102 isn't a class to take if you want an easy A anyway.

ECE 102 with schurgers is a really informative course...the material can be hard to grasp, but schurgers's notes really help with labs and quizzes...don't expect an easy A though, because a lot of time is required to truly understand the concepts in this course...and since quizzes test you on concepts...be well prepared
Very hard class, but if you put in some effort youll learn a lot

This prof genuinely likes teaching and will always help you learn the material if you want it.  Many students thought he was intimidating but actually he is really cool.  He does have a serious hang up with cheaters and lazy students, which I think accounts for many of the other comments on this page.

One of the best teachers at UCSD. People who dont like him are just lazy students who like to be spoonfed rather than think about the material. He is dedicated to teaching concepts rather than drowning us in calculations. You will learn alot from this guy if you give it some effort.

He is one of the more "down to earth" professors at UCSD. He would literally put jokes on the labs or write amusing test questions. His lectures were clear, but his tests seemed to kill the class (The average midterm score was 35%). There's ABSOLUTELY no reason you will do poorly if you STUDY for the tests, something the average student didn't do.

it was the worst class that I have throughout my ece life.Reading the notes and the book is better than his lecture.His tests were terrible.If you have to add 2% for everyone,that means you suck at making up the test and lack of communicating with your students.That just frustarted ppl.He sucks
horrible professor. he is too young to teach. no experience and sometimes try to screw students in purpose. avoid him at all costs.

It is hard to understand his accent and his attitude toward students is rude and unrespectful. Taking too many questions in the lecture makes people want to fall asleep in the class. Grading on the exam is not always the same. It seems he has double standards for different groups of students.

A brilliant guy who teaches you very useful and practical material. He is very helpful during office hours. He has a good sense of humor that even show up on his exams. His exams were relatively hard, but very doable. EASY FINAL!!

I never hated a professor like Curry Sean so much. I took his Math142B on Spring 2018. The course material was so difficult, and his explanation was so bad. I had to read the textbook by myself. Because of him, I did not graduate successfully, and I lost my summer holiday. Never ever took his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He cares his students and wants everyone to succeed.
Super nice professor. Clear notes, decent homeworks, fair exams.

Good lecturer, but ran out of time going too in-depth into examples or answering questions. Math 20B is a HARD CLASS, and requires LOTS of work. It matters the work you put in more than who you have. The practice exams really helped with the midterms and final, and SI helped with understanding the homework and lecture examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The final exam is super hard. And the professor combined his office hours for two classes which makes it hard to ask questions for final exam
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Impeccable
Almost every week there is homework, and it is very difficult. The professor did not explain things clearly, and I have to search online by myself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Curry did not organize his office hours properly, and the midterm is so hard. Avoid him at all cost
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: As long as you do all the homework problems including the ones that you do not have to turn in and read along in the book, you are guaranteed to get a good grade. This class was pretty easy because Professor curry explains the concepts in an effective manner. Great teacher I highly recommend him
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Not too much homework, mostly easy problems with a challenge or two thrown in. Exams are very fair, nothing surprising. Lectures are really enjoyable, they go by fast and you learn a lot . Overall really great professor
The professor did not have any passion to teach the class. For him, it seems like teaching is just producing goods in a production line. His lecture basicly repeats what is in the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The lecture is very boring, and it is very hard to get access to the professor after class. Exams are super hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The professor did not give the answers for his practice midterm and finals, which make students feel hard to review. I asked him about answers but he said no. Also, he did not give enough office hours during final week. He combined his MATH142B office hour with another class so I do not have enough time to ask questions.
The professor talks too fast in the class, so it is hard to follow up. Also, he covers too many chapters for this course, so it is very difficult for me to review.
Curry's 142B is easy compared to his 142A. He posts all notes which is helpful. Not a lot of homework and he makes sure you can learn things from your homework. Great professor.

His logic is very clear and he is reachable out of lecture. For me, any MATH Professor who meets these two things is good enough. For the general, I think his class in the winter was better than other Professors', as other courses either had lots of students dropped or had lower average. So, take his if you are not decided, because he can save you!

He's enthusiatic about his job, but his lecture are heavily based on theorems and words instead of examples. His lectures are fast paced and vague and didn't help at all with homework or tests. I feel like I've learned nothing over this quarter with him. I wouldn't recommend unless you're a fast math learner.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Curry is one of my favorite professors at UCSD. He cares about his students succeeding but he wants you to work for it. If you need help, he is very willing if you go to his office hours or a meeting with him. Helped me go from getting a 61% on the first midterm to 100% on the second. He's lectures are funny too, always a plus.

Professor Curry is new to UCSD but he is doing great. He is humorous, and his lectures are super clear. He sends out lecture notes and handouts often. Calculus II is hard, but Curry helped me make through this.
Professor Curry is humorous, caring, and professional. His lectures are clear, and his exams are fair. I would definitely take him again.
Lecture is repeating what is on the notebook, and the first midterm is so hard. AVOID.

Prof. Curry is one of the best professors I've encountered here in UCSD Mathematics. He's rather young and thus very approachable and amiable. He also gives handouts sometimes which are very helpful. His lectures are clear and well organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Curry was always so helpful and available to anyone. His method of teaching math and explaining complex terms was a breath of fresh air. He was a wonderful instructor and I would recommend him to anyone!

I do not recommend this professor. I learned everything from YouTube tutors and nothing from his lectures. Once I understood the concepts I went back to my notes to see what he was trying to teach and still didn't understand his lectures. He knows what he's teaching but he doesn't explain enough to understand. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Quirky new prof. Timing for lectures isn't efficient- ends classes rushed and often carries information over to next lecture. TOO OFTEN adds confusing extra history/info of the why's.  Weekly mandatory HW graded on correctness (use the answer book). 2 midterms and a final. Easy if you study past tests he gives or you can get more from other profs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Curry is a relatively new prof at UCSD, he's a pretty funny guy and is still trying to solidify his teaching style. I had him Mon, Wed, and Fri so lectures were 50 min long and he tried to squeeze in as much material as he could in this time. He does a lot of example problems and I felt like he was a decent professor.

Professor Curry is a new professor, so he doesn't really know how to teach that well compared to other lecturers. His lectures consist of him just putting problems on the board, but he doesn't really explain them. If you go to his office hours, he'll explain more in depth about concepts. He is caring, but I relied on AP Calc/TA way more than him.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Curry is a new professor here so he's not the best lecturer. But he does care about his students and always answers questions on Piazza that people bring up. Also, if you don't go to class, you might have a hard time catching up on exactly what we learned since he expands heavily on the given materials in the textbook. But overall, a decent prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Curry is a good professor overall, IF you are good at math. He has limited time in his lectures, so he might not clearly state the "whys" that I think are needed to fully understand concepts, BUT he will explain all of those answers if you go to office hours. His homework is straight from the book, and the grading is fair--based off work shown too.

He's a newer prof, but does a decent job explaining concepts. Not the most enthralling lecturer, but at this point in your math education, are you really expecting that? He does speak intelligibly, and his lectures have a good pace.   He is also very responsive on Piazza for questions, and his homework and exams are not unnecessarily difficult.

You can tell that professor Curry is new to teaching here at UCSD. He does not care about his students and gives full discretion to the TAs and graders on how they grade your tests and homework. Homework is based on correctness and grading system is unfair. Curry is boring and confused me in lecture. I went in thinking I knew calc, but I was wrong
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Cullen is my all time favorite professor. Especially at a public school, you won't find many people who are as dedicated to teaching the material and ensuring the success of her students like Professor Cullen. The content is straight-forward, but the tests are designed to assess your understanding of the material rather than memorization.
Lectures were pretty straightforward, still beneficial to go, but the slides are online. Exams were a bit difficult but the curve was generous.

Professor Cullen is awesome! super nice, flexible, and truly cares about her students. lectures are interesting. She lectures off of her slides that are posted on ted. On top of her shtuff! First week of class she already had most of the stuff for the quarter uploaded on ted. responds to questions and emails super fast!

Very easy class..go to lecture and do the problem sets and practice midterms, Material is very stratightforward and with a little time and practice, getting an A is very doable! She curves nicely and there arent any curve balls on her exams! DEFINITELY TAKE HER!! :)

Really great professor. Compared to 100B, 100C is a lot more hands on than conceptual. Her tests are all clear and concise, and extremely fair! They aren't hard nor are they easy but very fair. Pay attention in class, and print out her notes!

She looks like Sarah Palin. Her lecture is so fast and boring. Lecture doesn't help unless you have read her slides before lecture. Just study her lecture and slides before midterm and finals. She put examples on the midterm which extracted from slides. And study final review slides because you can find answers to final exam questions from it.

Really great professor.  It's hard only because it's economics but she makes it as easy as she can.  Always available during office hours;  I was scared of econ but now I'm not anymore.  I'm really bad at math but she showed me how I can do the problems with algebra instead of integrals--now that's a teacher instead of just making me feel dumb!
Great!

After taking Machina, I was scared to take 100b. But Cullen is SOOO sweet. She's really enthusiastic so she speaks really fast. Her lectures are clear and concise. Absolutely NO tricks on the midterm or final. Some questions are tricky but these are meant to separate the A and B students. Easy Midterm, Hard final. (at least I thought it was) No HW!
She is a "fast talker." Very fast. If you pay attention to the power points and do the readings you will get an A. If you don't, thanks for keeping the curve down :)
Prof Cullen makes for an excellent Faculty Research Advisor. Very few professors are ever willing to advise undergraduate students, but Prof Cullen was more than willing to assume this capacity.

Professor Cullen is a very nice, smart woman who is extremely enthusuastic about economics. Her tests are very difficult compared to the Aplia homework and are sometimes hard to get through. Office hours and inclass experiments were helpful. I recommend Cullen, but Econ100B itself is very difficult.
She's the nicest person you'll ever meet and she definitely knows what she's talking about.  However, she makes you do hwk online and talks really quickly.  If you're okay with that, I recommend her!
Very friendly teacher.  The homework was difficult at times, but the tests were representative of the matarial covered.
Horrible Teacher. Makes up stuff as she goes along in class. Her test are not related to her readings. She's doesn't even know how to do her homework that she assigns.
Amazing Professor! It was my favorite class of the quarter and I was so happy to finally get an A in a bio class. Definitely take this professor!

A really conscientious, caring professor. Also volunteers at the school free clinic for homeless people. Used humor and clinical stories in lectures. Though BICD100 is a huge class, Dr. John made the extra effort to learn your name if you came to office hours or asked him questions. Taking a class from a real doctor rocks!

The lectures were exciting and the professor had a lot of clinical examples. The exams (mixture of multiple choice and free response) were pretty straightforward if you studied. Mastering Genetics helps to keep you up to speed. The professor is very sweet and animated; he makes genetics interesting. Best upper div bio experience so far!

Very good professor. A little stern about not letting you turn in late assignments, but generally very reasonable. Seemed to really care about teaching and making sure you understand the materials. If you get a chance, go to his office hours. Great teaching there!

As a non bio major, he made the class incredibly understandable. really, all you need is the BILD 1-3 series to fully grasp these concepts. homework and quiz section are so helpful. He has a stutter but its not distracting at all

Best professor I ever had. He made dull information interesting and engaging. He's funny and positive. His tests are not too bad and actually test you on concepts you should know. Definitely take his class!

This class is my favorite class! Curington is so funny! I just love attending lecture because he stutters and the things he say can be very funny. He has a great sense of humor. Sometimes he may be a bit boring when he just repeats himself like 3 times or even 4 times and when he just reads the slides. But still I love him and his class! :D
Awesome professor, really did a good job of taking over for another professor the second week of school. Was very generous and funny, great class!

One of my favorite lecturers at UCSD and it was his first time teaching BICD 100. His midterm was easy (his first test written) while his final was fair. People eased off thinking that his final was going to be easy as well but he explicitly said that it was going to be harder than the "easy" midterm. These people shouldn't cry about their grades.

Decent guy. Took over the course from another professor. Very clear lectures. Seemed enthusiastic. Brought in lots of clinical examples. Had very interesting and useful office hours. Grading was a little on the easy side, but that's OK by me.

Replaced Ghiara for Genetics in the fall. Gave an easy midterm, but screwed us over on the final exam. My A went down to a B really not happy about it and his supposed curve ended up hurting me because I got the questions he didnt count correct. Lectures were straight from slides word for word, really boring. Nice guy, but beware of easiness.
Nice lectures, but we had to read the book before class so it felt a bit repetitive at times. Overall a great professor, only complaint is that the TA's took far too long to grade assignments.

She is a good professor but sometimes struggled to finish lecture material. That being said, easy A class, pretty interesting (unless you have prior programming experience). Cynthia Lee is one of my favorites at UCSD.

The mandatory lectures were tedious and she gets caught up answering questions instead of finishing what she planned to cover. She reinforced key points, but it was repetitive. Exam material covered concepts covered in the programming assignments and reading. The discussions are only helpful if you're struggling with the assignments. Easy A.

Tends to get off track and usually sees her lecture presentations for the first time during the lecture. Overall, it takes extra self motivation to really learn in that class because she isn't a very good teacher. She is however always willing to help, and the class as a whole is very easy.

She's an enthusiastic professor, and tried to help the students as much as possible. But she doesn't lecture well, and sometimes answer too much question and slowed down the lectures. An OK professor.
She's not bad. But it's hard to judge the professors in this course very comprehensively because of the really bad lecture format. But professor Lee was very clear, fun and a good teacher overall.

She doesn't really teach you anything, it's all on you to read the book and teach yourself. Tests you on how well you write code under pressure. I don't see how that's helpful to beginners but whatever. It's a manageable A. She's super condescending in office hours. Ask the TAs for help!

This professor is a glorified stereotypical geek and a joke. She doesn't teach because she thinks we'll learn from our peers. But-big news- my peers are idoits that have never done CSE, they're not qualified teachers. Her methods are reserved for art history classes that can be abstact and silly, not a straightforward science class like CSE.

Great professor!! Lectures were clear and she took the time to explain everything which was really helpful for me as a first-time programmer. Go to class for the clicker points. Both midterms and the final exam were straight from lectures and labs. 1-page cheat sheet for each exam. TAs and tutors were extremely helpful during labs and tutor hours.
Great professor, but the attendance is mandatory.

Great prof! Very flexible and willing to help anyone who puts in the time to succeed. The class is a bit time consuming between the labs and assignments. She also gives participation points using clicker questions so you pretty much have to go to class. The midterms and final are pretty much from the lectures. If you put in the time it is an enjoyable class!  The TAs were also awesome! Very helpful and very accessible!

Great prof. I don't know if it was just because it was an introductory type class, but she explained everything thoroughly and in an easy-to-understand manner. She seemed to spend a lot of [her own] time on this class as well. The TAs were also great and helpful. Exams were straight from LE/Labs.

Quite a reasonable class. Didn't find the peer assessment useful though. Lectures were a bit boring but the subject's not my thing. Homeworks were reasonable as were the exams. Probably would have been much harder with another professor, but still learned the material.
Boring lecture, but lectures slides very helpful for homework, midterm, and final. Participation counts as 5% of the grade. Midterm and final are hard especially the proof questions.

One of the best professors in the CSE department. I can see how this material would be difficult with another professor but Professor Lee gives so many examples and her homeworks/exams are very much based on the examples. Even the clicker questions really help you learn and when you go back to study those can be very useful. Overall, excellent prof

Very enthusiastic. Programming assignments are well-tuned in terms of difficulty and time required. Exams are somewhat difficult, but the is a very generous curve, especially if you do well on the PA's. Some students didn't like her lecture pacing and explanations (I had no problems), but she's probably loads better than Burkhard! I recommend her.

Overall, a very understanding and helpful professor. Dedicated towards helping students, and shows it though answering several questions on webboard. The programming assignments will take time, but you will become very familiar with Java, and generics; since every assignment will have generics. Good Professor.

Very good professor. Is willing to help anyone succeed in the class. Quizzes, midterm, and final reflect the homework problems. She even makes CSE 20 fun, and offers "extra credit" as well. Highly recommend.

Very upbeat professor, who enjoys teaching. Sometimes can be a bit goofy, but she is sweet. Be prepared for quizzes by staying on top of your homework. Midterm and Final are well-related to homework, and lecture notes. A very fair professor. Sometimes she gave out post-cards, and/or candy for participation.

SHE IS SO NICE! The class itself can be a bit dry and there is a lot of reading, but she is extremely helpful in OH and email. There's a lot of reading and the midterm is a bit difficult, but she gives you study guides.
A bit flitty but do the reading, if you have questions go to office hours. I didn't expect an A at all and there it was!
A nice and knowledgeable professor, but her class was about as exciting as watching paint dry. Lots of reading. Be prepared to study hard for the exams.

One of the most accessible and caring professors at UCSD. I would go to her office hours to ask about the material and just to chat about whatever else. She is very clear about what she wants from her students, and she provides helpful study guides. If you're interested in European women history, you must take her.
She is soooo nice and helpful.

She is such a nice professor and genuinely cares about her students. The study guide she gave us for the final was very helpful. I would really recommend going to lectures, she discusses the readings in detail.

All I can say is I have never met a professor who is more available and cares more about the interest of her students that Professor Truant. For those who don't understand this about her it is simply because you did not take the time or invest the energy in her course.

very good professor, cares about the students. Although her lectures are dry, i found them necessary because she goes over the reading, and there is A LOT of reading for this class, luckily most of it was interesting.

Loved the class, and most of all the professor! Wish all teachers at UCSD were more like her. Responds to emails very promptly. Shows concern for her students, and is very helpful when you have questions. The class had one midterm, a paper, and a final. But she provides pretty clear guidelines in all cases. Highly recommended!

Lovely professor. She is so sweet and extremely helpful. You can tell that she really cares about her students. There is lots of reading to be done, but if you put in the work, you should get the according grade.
Took her French Revolution class; she assigns a lot of reading but I didn't do most of it and still got a good grade. Mostly need to go to lectures and study and you will do well.

Even though her lectures are incredibly dry, she is interesting. She assigns a TON of reading, but reviews it all in class, so just focus on the main themes of the class and you can get out of the superfluous reading. Lots of assignments, but overall an easy class. Also, visiting her in OH will almost guarantee you a better grade.

Requirements are straight forward, does give a study guide, but because of that is a bit tougher on grading.Midterm+essay+take-home final.Recommend if you are interested in the subject. If you'll take it for some requirement,you'll be bored. Professor is a real sweetheart and now and than would throw out some really funny jokes

One of the most enjoyable classes I took for my regional specialization requirement at ERC. Taking a section option instead of the midterm is the best thing you can do. Susanne Hillman was the kindest, sweetest TA. The prof herself is very sweet but her lectures can be boring seeing that she talks so slowly. Regardless take the class!

Took several classes with her and by far she is the chillest teacher ever, you can wing it if you know what your doing and still end up with an A in the class. Her lectures are BORING though so you should bring something that'll keep you awake for 1hr20mins

His lectures are not always interesting and she has a horrible lecturing style. She repeats some same points over and over, but all in all she is a good teacher in that she cares that you under her points and what will be on the test.

This class is easy, especially if you choose the section option.  The readings are interesting, if a bit repetitive towards the end. Truant seems to really care about her students, to the point of wanting to get to know everyone in her lecture by name. Her lectures can be slow, but if you attend you don't always have to do the readings.

Senior Seminar is great for seniors.  Only have to read two of the reading and eventually write a 15-20pg paper. Classes are so boring you want to jump out the window, but overall nest chocie for the Senior who doesn't really want to be there.
Very helpful and interesting lectures

Great readings. She lets u know what will be on test w/study sheet, a lot of studying to do but at least u know what to study for. MUST STAY UP WITH READINGS! Her lecture voice sucks, but overall she is a great professor

Very fashionably forward......rocked a red fleece vest (North Face) with red flats! Must have been quite a looker in her younger years. Aesthetics aside, her lectures are cogently laid out and engaging, the class work is moderate, and the material is extremely interesting. Highly recommend!
the course material was decent enough, but she is seriously sexy while lecturing
Lots of reading.  Make sure you have an easy TA.  The TA this quarter is really hot.
SOOOOOOOOOOOO Easy, I went to a couple classes and only read what out essay was on and easilly passed. TAKE HER!

She was a little wacky at times, this was a few years back when I took her class.  Class was very interesting, Paris-Past & Present, and she had a lot of great information, she proofed and actually corrected the graders work if she felt it deserved higher! Sometimes she was just a little spacey, but always very pleasant.

LOTS of reading, but she's a great professor. If you actually talk to her, you'd see how great of a person she is too. Classes can be a little boring, but she's so smart and really knows her stuff. But just be ready for lots and lots of reading.

Great teacher, her lectures are extremely clear so it is really easy to take notes.  Her grading is extremely fair, two take-home essays, and you get to pick those essays and then a study guide of the exact test.  I strongly recommend this professor for any class.

Simply wonderful. She's passionate & dedicated towards her subject and genuninely cares about her students. HIEU 129 had 2 take home midterms + study guide w/ all the possible questions for the finals. HIEU 131 had 1 essay, and study guides for final & midterm. Lots of reading and books to get, but are very interesting. I highly recommend her!!

Way too much reading. Make sure u don't get on her bad side. She'll hold it against you. She made a mistake on my test. When I pointed it out to her she said she was glad I said something cause now she didn't have a bad opinion of me. She told my friend to drop her class if he wasn't taking it p/np
Enjoyable as a lecturer, very knowledgeable and makes the subject matter interesting. Tests and writing assignments very straightforward. (And yes, she's pretty hot, too)

She knows her material very well and wows you with the amount of knowledge she has of European history. A bit vague at times throughtout lecture, and reading is definitely required to pass.I would recommend Truant, great teacher.1 midterm, 2 papers, and a final (not too bad)
Really really nice and helpful teacher, very knowledgeable as well.  TONS of reading assigned, but you dont need to do all of it to get an A.  Midterm, take home paper, and final.
Great prof. a lot of reading, the exams are pretty self-explanitory seeing how she gives you a study guide telling you exactly what's being covered on the exam.
She is very very nice and sweet. There is a lot of reading, sometimes unnecessarily. The tests are mostly essay and pretty easy, once you figure out what she wants.
Not the best lecturer, but very knowledgeable.  A lot of reading assigned, sometimes too much, but not a bad teacher.
Her lectures are a little vague and she can be hard to understand... she jumps from topic to topic which can be hard to follow.
very passionate about teaching; cares about her students; great lecturer
No Comments
Fun class! She makes the material interesting.
No Comments
Great course content and even better instructor!
Very good lecturer, knows his material, welcomes all questions. He creates a healthy learning environment.

If you have a chance to take ML class with him, do it, by all means, do it. His lectures are easy to follow and also so so inspirational. He is a great professor, to say the least. Maybe, just maybe, it will be one of the few classes that remind you of your time at UCSD when you graduated.

Clear and well organized lectures (prepare all lecture handouts and HWs on his own). There are 3 quizzes with lowest dropped and 1 final. Though the content is not in depth, one needs to prepare very throughly for them, for example pay attention to lecture details is crucial. HW can take up a lot of time.
Awesome lecturer
just watched his first lecture, his explanations are amazing

Professor Dasgupta is a phenomenal lecturer. Coming into CSE 151A, I had little knowledge of Machine Learning concepts, but Prof. Dasgupta made learning these concepts incredibly easy. The homework assignments are incredibly helpful in passing the course. Whether attending in-person or watching through podcast, Dasgupta is a 10/10 recommendation.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Take him for any ML class, he explains the concepts so well in lecture. Homeworks are very tedious and a little challenging, but going to OH helps. Quizzes are very straightforward if you did HW. Only complaint is his grade breakdown: 40% quizzes (3 w/ lowest dropped), 20% HW (9 total), and 40% final. Hard to get A if you mess up one of these 3.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There's nothing wrong with the professor or the course material, but the grade cutoff for an A is a 95 which is insane
Pretty cool prof and pretty chill class. We knew exactly what to expect on quizzes and homework feedback was timely and efficient!
He's the god of algorithm in ucsd
The content is pretty simple, with exams involving many homework questions. A good intro to a multitude of machine learning topics.

mostly docking stars over small things like not knowing how to use canvas, uploading the syllabus two weeks late, switching all exam dates days before the first exam (remote students wasted $100s-$1000s on flights), and TAs docking whole letter grades for percentage answers instead of decimal. cognitive decline or just in unprofessionalism?

Dasgupta is very wholesome and very willing to help you out. Answers every question and is super knowledgeable in the topic. His lectures were top-notch and his explanations were amazing at understanding the material. While the class was hard, he allowed me to look forward to each new topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Absolutely fantastic professor and person. Incredibly accomplished yet humble and inspiring. I would recommend Professor Dasgupta 1000 times over.
Sanjoy is one of the rare profs who are amazing in all ways. I learnt so much from him by simply just attending his lecture. If you are at UCSD, you HAVE to take his course!
You have to take 250B under Dasgupta. He is simply awesome!
Great lectures, amazing depth of knowledge.
His professor is awesome. You can't say you are a student in Computer Science at UC San Diego if you never take his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Inspirational
One of my favorite lecturers at UCSD. He wrote the textbook too!
One of UCSD's best lecturers. Go to class and you'll learn so much.

Algorithms are fundamentally important for any CS/CE student, and Dasgupta the best at it. Having co-written the textbook used by students at other universities including Berkeley, the material in his lectures are clear and identical to the that of his textbook. The homework was tough, but the quizzes were extremely easy by comparison.

Sanjoy Dasgupta is one of those rare professors that you'll get once every blue moon. He is extremely good at teaching and will make sure that you walk out of every lecture with a good understanding of what he just taught. Outside of lecture, he is also very helpful as he shows great care for his students performances. Take dasgupta for cse 101.
Sanjoy is fantastic. Best I have ever had
Seriously he is the best professor I had in UCSD!!!!! His  notes are clear and organized. His lecture is easy to understand. I love this professor!!!!

Ive heard a ton of good things from this professor so I waited for him. Lectures are simple and clear. Professor seems to care a lot and he employees a great TA named Quentin. But the weekly quizzes/2 midterms does get annoying and the class is not easy. Prepare to spend a lot of time doing the homeworks. he is also lenient on failing people
One awesome professor, and exams were really fair, but you should definitely perfect doing your homework before calling yourself a master otherwise you will make stupid mistakes.

He really knows how to teach. If you put the time in to this class you will learn fundamental algorithm techniques that actually stick.This could've been theory intensive, but he made understandable and applicable.
One of the best at UCSD.  Download the podcasts and keep the book for posterity, he's that good.
Awesome professor. One of my favorite professors at UCSD. Everyone should make an effort to take algorithms with him. Pay special attention to the hw's and read the book.
Sanjoy is a boss. This topic is difficult (especially the topics prior to the first midterm). Keep up with the reading and do the homework with a group.

He's the best math professor at UCSD. His lectures are clear and helpful, which make reading the book optional. He's also extremely helpful during office hours if you need help with homeworks. Exams and quizzes are fair as long as you put your time on practicing how to write algorithms and other materials he covered in class.
GOOD prof but quiz and exam is hard
He's cool. He takes things slowly.
I guess, his lecture is excellent and he has good sense of humor. However, it does not really guarantee good grade.( I guess, more than 30% class dropped the cse 103.)
One of the greatest professors Iǘe had

Dasgupta is an excellent lecturer with a good sense of humor. His slides are concise and clear, and follow the textbook (since he co-wrote it). The material and homeworks are somewhat difficult, but if you keep at it and practice and study, the exams are not too bad. One of the best CS profs I've encountered.
Amazing professor. Clarity and total awareness of how his material is affecting students as he presents it.

Fantastic professor, one of the few on campus that are extremely  talented and can actually teach. Homeworks were challenging at times, but overall very fair. Midterms usually consisted of a few homework problems. Dasgupta was one of the best lecturers I've ever had (in any department) and the class was very rewarding.

The beginning of the class is easy, but it gets progressively harder so watch out. Awesome professor, his lectures are actually worth while. Watch out for other students, for some reason everyone was HIGHLY competitive.
Nice guy and a good lecturer. Homeworks were really hard and harshly graded. Another awful theory class but good prof.

I thought Algorithms would be absolutely dreadful, but Prof Dasgupta actually made it interesting. He is one of the clearest, most systematic and thorough lecturers I've ever encountered. He freaking wrote the textbook so it fits perfectly with the class. Great inclass examples. Homeworks are tough but promote learning, tests are easy. GREAT PROF.
Excellent teacher.  Take him for algorithms if you can.  Homework is pretty harsh, but tests are pretty easy for the most part.

Excellent lecturer. Has an accent but it doesn't affect anything. Made algorithms interesting! I felt like I learned a lot from class, but I was manhandled by the homeworks. The TA's give away the answers though, so go to OH if you need help on hwk. Tests are easier than hwk but still tough..

Extremely interesting lectures. (The only boring ones in CSE91 were when he had guest speakers.) His accent is NOT thick, and he's perfectly easy to understand once you hear him for 5 minutes and get acclimated to it. Homework and quizzes are extremely easy. Easy -- but FUN -- pass. Go to lecture.

Class is extremely easy to pass, although you remain in the dark about your grade since you never get your assignments back. Hard to understand and the material covered is extremely boring / meaningless. ATTEND CLASS! There are in-class assignments.

The class is insanely easy, maybe two homework assignments and a single quiz all quarter. His accent is really thick though, hard to understand. A lot of the material covered is meaningless and a waste of your time.

Extremely well taught class. Lectures were very clear and made a potentially dull subject interesting. Very well organized, makeing note taking easy. Also provided complete lecture notes, so note taking wasn't necessary. One of the best classes I've ever taken.
Has absolutely the best lectures! Is very clear, precise, and most of all interesting! Makes great analogies to difficult topics.
This class was asynchronous and her lecture format was very accessible and kept it interesting. The readings were interesting but not required to do well in the class.

Soci 2 was asynchronous with an in-person discussion, so she would post 3 lecture videos weekly for you to keep up with. It is important to watch because you should be able to cite lectures and discussions for exams. Everything was clear and easily accessible. Great lectures that were easy to engage, even though it was online.

Easiest class ever. The readings are in Canvas, and the lectures are not long if you simply put them in 2x speed. There are two midterms, a final exam, a response to weekly discussion posts, and a mandatory attendance discussion. The exams were open note, and as long as you write down what each lecture topic was, citing will be very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: There's absolutely no clarity. The midterms are online, but you have to be extremely precise with your answers. If you looking for take it for requirements take some other class
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was both one of the easiest and most interesting courses I've taken. I enrolled in it to fulfill my DEI requirement, and it exceeded my expectations. The midterms were straightforward, and the course requirements were manageable, with weekly participation and discussion attendance.

Professor does not reply to emails. I sent several and did not receive email back. She does not give enough insight into what the midterm is going to look like. Online lectures are quite lengthy + she speaks in a very monotonous tone. She requires us to cite which lecture she discussed something in the midterm answers= this takes a lot of time!!

Prof Raudenbush and SOCI40 is one of the best out of all the classes I've taken. She never cuts any corners, is always prepared and engaging with students, and truly cares for her students and what she teaches. Attendance for lectures and discussions are mandatory. Would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took her for both Soci 2 and 40 and was amazing both times. Im a Bio major but her teaching style has even gotten me interested in sociology. Provides readings to us, but lectures cover most of what you need to know. 2 midterms & final w/ very digestible prompts if you studied! Highly suggest studying central Q's and remebering examples for exams.

Raudenbush was amazing. I took this class because I needed one more lower div for my minor, and I highly recommend it. She is one of the best professors I've had at UCSD. She is a great lecturer, and the exams were straightforward. (three written and one essay). Study the concept questions in her lectures and you will be fine.

Professor Raudenbush is a great and engaging professor. She really made it clear what was meant to be studied, and what her lectures were about. Her midterms are structured through 'central questions', where you have to remember information (based on lectures) for each one. But, she did a good job explaining answers, and cared for her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took Professor Raudenbush for SOCI2 + SOCI40 and loved it. She's an amazing lecturer and just a super cool person in general. Doesn't record lectures and grades based on section participation so attendance is mandatory but splits classes into half remote and half in-person. Tests are fair as long as you pay attention and review the slides.

She does a great job at talking about what she talks about, this class is interesting. Try to read as much as possible it really does help to know them especially for tests which are written, 2 short answer and 1 essay question. If you put the work in and take some time to read you will be fine and it's fairly easy. Discussion is mandatory.

Prof. Raudenbush is amazing! I absolutely loved this course. I was initially nervous to take it as it requires you to conduct qualitative interviews, but the professor was so reassuring and incredibly helpful. You can tell that she enjoys teaching and wants her students to succeed. Overall a great professor and great person!

Soci 2 is really straightforward, easy, and important. SOCI2 was graded by 2 midterms, a final, and section participation. As long as you're used to hand-writing essays and can write a thorough paper, you'll coast by. Concepts are easy as is, and can be learned in depth through lecture/readings. I ended with 100%.Raudenbush is intelligent & solid.

She really cares about the topics she teaches which is always a plus. Course is graded from two midterms, the final, and discussion attendance/participation. Although you're grade on a few things, it's a very easy class, and as long as you show up to lecture + discussion, don't really need to do the readings

I absolutely loved taking this class! All the readings were interesting, and sections were very helpful. Despite the class basically being graded on just midterms and the final, her lectures teach you everything you need to know on them. So it was very straightforward, take this class!!

I went to 3 lectures all quarter and still passed with an A, the terms are on her slides if you need them. Two midterms and a final, not cumulative. Section attendance is mandatory, its helpful depending on your TA. Content is a lot of common sense, so if you don't know a term on the exam, chances are that context clues will be your saving grace.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor with clear criteria for grading. Awesome lectures.

Currently her class is asynchronous (in person on Tuesday and Thursday online.) Her slides are very beneficial when studying as she covers several central points that appear on the midterms. There are two midterms and one final. There is no homework given besides the readings she assigns per week and one discussion posts every Friday.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof's teaching style is great. Her lecture's are intentional and well-thought out. When I was in her class, one day of the week was synchronous and discussions were mandatory. I learned a good amount and enjoyed her lectures! Best professor I've had so far during my time here

great class + professor! asynchronous half the time. workload is never a ton, and TA discussion sections are really helpful, especially when reviewing for exams. exams are fair and do not trick you. i do recommend putting the online lectures on 2x speed. she's really knowledgable and cares about her students.

Proffesor Raudenbush was amazing and easily accessible! Lectures are explained clearly and always willing to clear up the topic if your confused! Her lectures reflect what will be on midterms, although I didnt read the papers she assigned because she mostly reviews them over in class, I took good notes during lecture and was able to pass with an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is great! Will take her again. You work in groups and conduct basic qualitative research. Sometimes it can be a little unclear what she wants, but just be proactive and sign up for her office hours. There is also plenty of time to talk in class and its often ended early.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought this class would be hard since it's a soci methods requirement, but it's basically one drawn out, chill group project where you interview people and then present/write about it. Prof Raudenbush is so nice and really does care about her students. The quarter isn't demanding either – we had 3 hour long classes that were often cut short.

Professor Raudenbush is by far my favorite professor that I have taken a class with at UCSD yet. She is super nice, very accommodating, and listens to/cares about her students. I was originally hesitant about taking this course when I saw how heavily grades depended on exams, however, the exams were fairly easy as long as you did the readings.
Just very nice and understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: If you keep up with lectures and readings this class should be fine for you. We had 2 midterms and a final and they were essay style questions. The only "homework" we had was completing a discussion post every other week. I really recommend taking this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She makes her class really interesting and shes a good lecturer. Exams are very reflective of the class materials. You dont HAVE to do the readings but it might be the thing that determines whether you get an A vs B.

Raudenbush is a great lecturer and the class is split up into 4 categories all accounting for 25% of the grade. Because of this you must get good grades on the first 2 midterms to get a good grade. Sometimes obviously biased in lectures but not too common and doesn't get in the way of learning. Grading can be a little harsh so put in good effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Raudenbush is a great lecturer. She is very knowledgable and passionate about the material that she teaches. There is 2 midterms and a final. The written exams are straightforward and based on the lectures & readings. The grading depends on your TA. Overall she is an excellent professor.

Professor Raudenbush was a great professor overall. Her lecture videos were always straight to the point and easy to follow. I also appreciate that they were all pretty short too. She did a great job highlighting the main points of our readings. The exams were reasonable as well.

Attendance is not mandatory but every now and then you'll have iClicker questions that count towards your participation grade. Tests are all about applying what you learned in lecture/readings. She posts all the content online. Encourages discussion and participation during class. Your grade is all based on your tests, section, and participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Raudenbush is very caring. She makes the effort to learn names during class and her lectures are pretty interesting. Attendance is taken through iClickers. 2 midterms, lecture attendance via iClicker, discussion section attendance, and final exam. She goes over reading during class so not really necessary to do ahead of time.

She does icliskers, gives readings, and is straightforward in her test. The discussion class are mandatory and they give out homework for the class. It is usually a memo about your thought and incorporation of what you learned. For this class I just had to do 3 short ones but for SOCI 2 I had to do one page single space every week or so, not hard.

She does not podcast but her lectures are easy to follow, I would recommend typing but LISTEN to watch she says do not zone out. She has clicker points for participation and gives out readings to further understand the content but you do not have to fully analyze the text because she goes over it in class. Her test are straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Raudenbush is a sweetheart. The readings she assigns are interesting and the conversations that follow are engaging. She is knowledgeable in her subject and cares about her students. She does everything she can to help with the field research assigned for the class. Would definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Raudenbush really cares about the students and she wants you to do well. She did't grade our essays or tests, but they were relatively straightforward. You get more points if you know the names of the authors when you write your midterm and final tests. The class was pretty basic but enjoyable.

Have i-clicker questions for participation credits. You have to attend the discussion and do the readings. There're 2 2-page papers that in total worth 20% of your grade. Come to class and skim the readings, you'll be fine with your grade.

This was her first year teaching so she's more than likely to change things up. She has pop clicker questions to get students to attend her 8AM lectures. Sections are mandatory. Midterm and final are both blue book free-response so do the readings. Overall, the class was interesting although her lectures weren't because she just reiterates readings

Not as funny as he thinks he is tbh... Class is mandatory, and lectures are boring. TAs are the most helpful part of the class, but if you fall behind, good luck trying to do well on the final, which is half your grade.

While the topic of this class wasn't hard to learn, I found his lectures to be very boring and not helpful to understanding the material. The homework assignments were really long, and difficult if you didn't quite understand how to use the software for the course.
NEVER TAKING HIM AGAIN!! I will not be taking him ever again. He talks extremely low and the lectures are very boring
Quite strict with essays, especially for the midterms and final. You need to learn beyond the lecture/reading materials to find examples. Readings matter a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class as long as you review lecture slides. Lectures are a bit monotone but are pretty interesting! Tests rely on readings, but you only really need to know main points which are discussed in lecture. Study guides are lowkey disorganized. Your best test score is weighed heaviest and raises grades a lot. TAs are harsh graders but very helpful!

His lectures are interesting and informative, but he often goes over them too quickly and has a bit of a monotone voice. The homework assignments are part based on lecture material, and part based on data analysis using Stata, which he does not go over in class. No midterm but the final exam is lengthy and covers a lot of content.

He was very interested in the course, which was appreciated. He can get quite disorganized in terms of lecture slides. I didn't study the last topic of the course before my final because 2 lectures' worth of information wasn't uploaded. The majority of examples mentioned in class came from Latin America (Brazil), and could have been more varied.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Graded mainly on midterms and the final. Attendance is mandatory and checked through iClicker participation, as well as section attendance forms. Goes in depth during lectures (recorded), but study guides and slides are oftentimes incomplete. A lot of reading to really understand the material. Got through it due to good TA.

He goes through the slides way too quickly, making it difficult to take notes. Additionally, a significant portion of what he says is not included on his slides. He does curve the class, but his study guides for tests are not helpful. If you get a good TA, you are set for the class because that's where you actually learn the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are easy to follow and are representative of the exams. Two midterms and one final, all exams with a writing portion. Just understand the basics of every reading so you can reference them on exams, and study his slides well before midterms/finals. It's an easy class if you put the work in/review a little everyday
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good prof. Bit confusing when lecturing but slides are reflective of what he puts on the final/hw. Class is graded by 4 very tedious HWs + final worth 50% of the grade. Be prepared to teach yourself everything, because I did. Final is representative of lectures + two readings never discussed. Use hw/lectures to study! I'm bad at math, but did well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was easy content wise (very subjective), but be fully prepared to teach yourself everything. No communication between TAs and Prof, section is unhelpful but required. Grading is very inconsistent and TAs are often wrong. Final was relatively easy and curved. He is a solid lecturer, but lectures do not reflect coursework. Take it with Anderson

chill guy who seems kind; never went to OHs because I felt like I didn't need to; had EC opportunities; what I did not like was using STATA and how he we would mention confusing topics and then never talk about them again; I was really confused on what to study for the final; I survived even though I hate math; class made me cry; has deep voice

Love this guy's sense of humor. POLI 30D depends a lot on your TA, but overall this class was a breeze. Lectures move pretty quickly and cover a lot of content. Professor Desposato uses many real and relevant examples to illustrate concepts.

Class overall wasn't too bad. The exams require you to actually know the material well though. TAs were either helpful or really unhelpful, and were generally tough graders on exam essays. Go to lecture and review the slides/podcasts for the final. He adjusted grade weight really weirdly at the end of the quarter but it brought grades up a LOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Professor was entertaining
- the final study guide was vague
-the finals are NOT like the homework
- TAs are tough graders 
- the material covered in the TA finals study session could not help me with the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lectures were rushed and content-heavy, making them hard to follow. Grades were based on attendance, 4 homeworks, and a 50% final, making the final extremely high-stakes. TA grading was inconsistent. We used Stata a lot but it wasn't on the final, while “optional” readings were. Overall, the course felt disorganized and misaligned.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a transfer, I didn't love taking an intro course, and this guy made sure of it. I would say I generally have a strong interest in politics, but Desposato is so boring. If this was my first POLI class at UCSD I would probably change my major. He also never stops talking about his time in Israel. Worst POLI class I've taken at UCSD.

If you have the chance, do not take this class with him. On top of complex materials being skimmed through in a very short amount of time during the day, there was no consistency or cordination between the prof and TA's. Final was 50% of your grade, it was closed note, and he didn't allow for a calculator either. Made us use Stata

Lecture slides and podcasts are posted - content not too hard. The final exam is worth 50% of the grade and the study guide is minimal at best - anything mentioned in lecture is 'fair game'. Readings barely mentioned in section/lecture but are still on final. No prior requirement to take coding/math but lots of homework is heavy on coding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grade is determined by 2 midterms and the final. He is funny during lecture and easily approachable in person or through office hours. TA's and section are helpful but they do grade hard on essays and want you to show that you deeply understand the readings. For the most part though you can skim the readings and do well.

Homework is awful if you have no experience with Strata. TAs are unclear about the homework. Grade is 50% final, which is a closed note, no calculator, and no curve. I attend office hours every week, complete the readings, and spend hours on homework, and I am still concerned about passing the class. I would try to take with a different professor.

Lecture attendance is tracked via iClicker (that you must pay for). Attend section and office hours, it truly makes a difference! The grade is based on participation quizzes, homework "exams," and the final (closed note, closed book, no calculator). A sprinkle of stats in poli sci is the best way to describe this class.

He's one of the best professors I've ever taken. He is very clear on what you should know, and the TAs are absolutely wonderful. I've gone to many office hours for help on the HW, and they are incredibly helpful in ensuring you feel supported and receive an A. Final was representative of lectures, and was fairly easy. Study early & you'll be fine!

He was honestly my fav professor of my quarter and I'm a human bio major lol. I took his class for a GE so I would recommend if you are interested in politics. He's funny and adjusts the weighting so it benefits the students. I literally studied the day before each exam so if you actually put in the effort you'll do great!

He seems really kind & has a good sense of humor, but can be minorly disorganized at times. I also had no idea what was going on in terms of grading, because he constantly adjusts weighting as we go (which was kinda nice).

Prof. was alright but I got more out of attending section than his lectures. If you attend both lecture/section, and stay on top of the homework assignments, you'll be fine. Start the hw assignments as soon as they are released because they can be quite long and tedious; there was extra credit for submitting one of the hw assignments on time.

Honestly, this class was hard for me. I am not good at math, but you don't have to be if you go to lecture and study hard for the final. I was dreading this class, but lecture was actually very enjoyable.

Chill af & cares. Held his own section for waitlisted students. Makes himself accessible. Class is just stats, poli sci, and minimal coding. HW is easy to get through, stay on top of it. Final is 50%, with stats experience it's an easy A. Lectures are v condensed for time but TAs elaborate super well. Put effort in, ATTEND SECTIONS and you're fine.

I may hate math, but Desposato made it fun. He's fun to talk to, lectures were enjoyable and engaging, and made the content easy to digest. The class itself is super easy IF you put genuine, honest effort into it and not cheat. My main gripe is that the study guide and readings were functionally useless. 10/10 would get a beer with him later on.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: one of the least work-heavy ps classes imo. no midterm/essays, just 4 easy (&boring) hws+a very easy final. if u have any stats background the class will be super easy (just brushes on the basic intro topics), but if not just study up the lecture slides. prof is pretty monotone but funny and clearly cares abt his students. 0 surprises on the final.

I wish there were more options for 30D professors. He is clearly knowledgable about the topic but with how the class was structured, there is simply no way to cram that much info into 10 weeks reasonably. He locked notes before final. I strongly suggest planning around this class. Easily the hardest class in political science at UCSD HANDS DOWN.

Honestly, he's nice and funny and all, but 14 pages of closed notes closed books by hand calculator-banned final is ridiculous to me. Also lectures are way too fast-paced (common recognition) and content-heavy for a 10-weeks class. I scored 6/7 on IB stat and still find it intense cuz he tries to explain stats, polisci, and math together.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: THIS IS A STATS CLASS. Professor states at the beginning of the quarter that this class has the highest fail rate. With enduring this long 10 week course, I can understand why the students performed so poorly(and its not the curriculum). Prepare to learn how to code in a political science class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is Podcasted. Two midterms, one final all have short definition questions and an essay (final has 2 essays). Don't really need to do the readings, just take good notes. His lectures are monotone but the class wasn't hard if you study before exams. He provides study guides and sometimes extra credit if you attend class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He asks a lot of opinion based questions, and he'll learn your name if you talk to him enough. AMAZING professor, I loved his class and his teaching style. Exams consist of open ended questions, which have a few term identification questions, and one essay on a topic that he'll inform you of beforehand. It's an easy class if you study just a bit!

His lectures were confusing to me. it was difficult to follow what he was saying because he'd go through slides really quickly. iclicker was always a problem in class. study at the start of the quarter because if not you will get really lost.

I was very intimidated by this summer class but he did a GREAT job at walking through the subjects and applying them to real-world scenarios like his previous work. He listens to the students' worries & has clear lectures posted both synchronously and asynchronously. In synchronous classes, he talks WITH you & not AT you.

 - 4 HW's & 1 Final -
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Really great professor. His class is super straight forward and easy to follow. His lectures are well organizes and his exams are very simple. Just study his lecture slides and you'll be able to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't be fooled, this is essentially a stats class. Homework makes up a large portion of your grade. 4 Homework projects, about 20-30 questions each. Final is just based on the Homework and lecture slides. He also gives a (kind of useless) study guide for the final. Had to use iclickers for participation points. He's a genius, but class is rough.

Overall the course is fine. Prof Desposato goes through lectures quickly and doesn't explain things thoroughly. He does go over some interesting information and personal stories. He says this isn't a stats class but it totally is. Participation and attendance is mandatory. Homework could be ambiguous so use your TA's for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Desposato was very interesting. He made the material super easy to understand. Him and his TA's were very helpful. This class ended up being a lot easier than I thought, with just 2 midterms and a final. Definitely recommend.

I was really worried about taking POLI30 because the school made it seem super difficult, but Professor Desposato made it my favorite class so far. His lectures were super helpful and he explained super difficult concepts really well. I've taken other statistics classes and none of them outlined the material as clear as he did. Take his class!

Prof. Desposato is a nice person and clearly cares about his students, but his teaching style is very laid back and carefree, not the greatest for learning about statistical data and Stata. The homeworks can be tedious and unclear, so I cannot stress enough to go to your TA's section as well as office hours. The TAs are extremely helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Cool guy. Wish he taught us Stata instead of expecting us to learn through a book.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Class component is what tests (midterm as I recall, and a final) are about, TA component is what the assignments are about (5 of them). Going to class is sooo helpful. He's a cool guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Desposato was a real gem to learn with. His lectures were a perfect reflection of the homework and exams, overall class was super clear to follow. He truly cares about his students and wants them all to succeed. Taking POLI 30 with him even pushed me to switch my concentration to data analytics. Absolutely 10/10 recommend, he is truly inspiring.

His class is interesting and the assignments are easy AS LONG AS YOU SHOW UP TO CLASS. This is basically a math class, and unless you're a math major, you probably can't afford to snooze through every class. He's definitely caring, no question about it. I once didn't submit my homework on time, and he emailed me asking about it.

He's pretty mediocre and sounds really bored/tired during all of his lectures. For some reason he assumes we all hate him so that didn't help and it made it a little awkward. He obviously knows his stuff but you rely way more on the TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grading is largely based on the TA's, but prof did not make it easy to understand what is going to be expected from each homework or how it is graded. Class material is almost entirely unrelated to the homework, but the exams are reasonable if you understand the basic content of the class. Also, get familiar with STATA before this class if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: What a mess. Prof. Desposato describes his approach as "intuitive", and what that means is that he doesn't actually teach; you have you use your "intuition" to figure it all out. The whole class was super confused and frustrated the entire quarter. He isn't available, doesn't answer your questions, and I think he puts a lot of the work on his T.A.s

Professor Desposato is a great professor who cares about the success of his students. He wants to see everyone succeed and goes out of his way to help with that. Being a stats class, I was nervous at first as I'm not great at math but Desposato simplified a lot of it and offered endless amounts of help through himself, TAs and online. Recommended.

He's super nice but is one of those profs who explains what something means in a sentence in lecture, spends of the rest of the lecture on one example, then gives a harder question on the homework. Lectures were pretty unhelpful imo. The class is super basic/easy though so it wasn't a super big deal.
