Thought the class would be more difficult, but he made it somewhat easy because he cares about his students grades. Also has a sense of humor that makes the lectures better.

I was terrified of this class because I have a phobia of numbers but Professor Desposato made the material less intimidating, helped greatly by his sense of humor. Never thought I would be laughing so much in a math(?)/statistics class. Also the course itself is not very difficult if you ask for help and attend lecture/discussion. Overall great guy

Desposato's a pretty good professor. Attendance matters somewhat because he might give an in class check in randomly. Homework projects aren't too difficult and are given plenty of time to complete. Extra credit has been offered for each homework project so far. Pay attention during lecture because it's more important than just reading his slides.

Desposato is a fine choice for clearing your POLI30 requirement. The class has very little math. Basically you just interpret statistics. If you have trouble with the math or data analysis, ask the prof or the TAs, or just google it. Thats what I did, and I got an A+. Its really not that hard of a class.

His POLI 30 class is easy only if you have taken a statistics class before. His lecture is vague and explains nothing. He loves to make jokes, but barely clarifies any concept. His homework is ok, but the questions are unclear and confusing.

His voice is kinda dry but he really tries to hold your attention in lecture. He works hard to get everyone to do well and he really cares. Accessible outside class. I definitely want to take another class with him. He gave a bunch of extra credit through the class and moved due dates back. Do not wait to do homework, start early-ish.

You must work for an A. 4 HW assingments and a final exam. Section participation is a must. The HW are lengthy and expect a minimum of 10-15 hours of dedication per HW. Lots of questions must be addressed during TA office hours. Clark was my TA and she is a gem. Tough class, but I learned a lot. Desposato is an asset to students and UCSD.

Very dedicated to the success of all students. Doesn't allow time to take notes from the slides which is frustrating. Explains ideas and processes in vague terms that necessitate further investigation for comprehension. While the Professor always made time for questions from students, answers were often given with a sarcastic comment.

He's one of the rare teachers who really goes out of his way to help his students succeed, and if you need to take this class, that's enough reason to take it with him. If you don't need to take this class, SAVE YOURSELF. Grading is fair, and he gives you loads of time for homework. No midterm, grade based on section attendance, homework & final.

I really liked this class. It was more about self-learning and discussion that "learning". It's really helpful to come in with some poli and/or econ knowledge but not necessary. His voice may be a bit bland but he's really funny and interesting and so I never found myself sleeping in the class. We also watched a lot of films and discussed them.

His lectures were unclear and unhelpful. He is a sweet and entertaining person, but I wish I'd taken the course with a different prof. I learned very little, and the whole course was completely (and unnecessarily) confusing. Luckily, the final was fair (if you go to lecture) and he was a very generous grader.

It's a college class, and he's a college professor. It's time to work. He knows his stuff, so just keep up with the homework, and ask him for help whenever. If you pay attention to his lectures (as well as the subtle humor) it will be a rewarding experience. /raises eyebrow

He lectures faster than Lorelei Gilmore could ever speak. His slide shows are vague and, even though they're posted online, completely unhelpful. Goes off syllabus. The grading completely depends on the TAs, who often contradicted the professor, each other, and were often completely clueless about the homework assignments.

The professor is really witty, funny and informative. I thought I would hate the class, especially after reading some comments from here, but I ended up loving it. He's really down to help his students and wants the best for them as long as they're willing to try their best.

You do not learn from this professor at all, you learn more from the TAs (whom there was only one good one) than the professor. You have homework that all of the TAs have different guidelines of grading. Wait to take this class with Galderisi.

While I didn't have a huge interest in this topic originally, Desposato made it my favorite class ever. His lectures are interesting and certainly not monotonous, I laughed in lecture on a daily basis. He really wants you to succeed, but you have to be willing to push yourself. Welcome to college, boys and girls.

I hate this class. I hate the lectures, I hate the hw, and I strongly dislike professor Desposato's monotone voice when teaching! The book sucks, and if it weren't for my TA I would have failed miserably. Let's just say I learned more from my TA than I did from my professor. I highly recommend you take this class with a different professor.

Very nice and down to earth guy. If you go to him with interest he will be glad to assist you in whatever you need. The class is complicated, but can be interesting. Easy grader if you analyze thoroughly and show you understand. I recommend this professor and class.

The class was very interesting and informative. His class is definitely not as hard as people make him sound. In fact, it was very easy as long as you don't procrastinate. There are various HW assignments and a Final. Complete the HW and you get an A. Lectures were somewhat boring but provided skills every student studying polisci should have!

Great class and great prof. I took the class over the summer in 09' but even taking that into account the class is great and Desposato is very accessible. His slides sometimes need explaining and sometimes he goes through material too fast but he is always open to questions and stops to clarify when needed.

The course itself is very interesting, especially if you are a Poli Sci major. Desposato can be hard to understand at time and often rushes through material. However, he always leaves room for students to ask questions. If you have never taken a stats class definitely use the book.

The material is relatively simple, however the professor is extremely monotone and boring.  Lectures did not help with the homework.  If it wasn't for discussions, I would have failed.  I would advise not to take this professor.

The class in itself is not difficult. The homework is fairly simple, but VERY time consuming. It is harshly graded & if you turn in your homework late, you get docked MORE than 50% of your hw score, so beware. In order to make grading "fair" the TA's each have their own section for grading. Cantu is a really helpful TA & the final wasn't too bad...

Scott is an okay professor, who I think is hot. His lectures and section are similar, but the section is where you get all the needed info for your homework. The homework was not that difficult, but I had an AWESOME TA that aided me. The class really depends on your TA, MAKE SURE TO double CHECK your homework scores and talk to TAs IMMEDIATELY.

Desposato is nice and funny but his lectures and the sections feel like two different classes. The homework is hard and harshly graded. The TAs are reluctant to help and are unorganized. The professor is good but I would NOT recommend this class.

This class was badly organized - the TA's were unhelpful and difficult to reach, and if you wanted to figure out what you did wrong on homework you had to track down all of them. Desposato is pretty good, but don't take him if you're not a math major - I really struggled. Definitely difficult, hard grading. Go to lecture.

Desposato is an interesting, really proud alum from Cal who automatically assumes that the entire class is disinterested in political stats. Honestly HW grading is really disorganized and homework is very time consuming so talk to your TAs about it and make sure you start early.

Great Prof! Desposato is very clear with his points in lecture and as to what he is expecting you to know for tests. Papers are to the point and his TAs dont grade harshly. Always accessible outside of class, and a great UCSD PoliSci resource generally.

I will agree to some extent with the comments about his clarity.  But for what he is teaching (stats to a bunch of people not interested in stats), I believe he does a decent job.  As has been previously said though, also talk with your TA (good advice for any course)

Desposato is an extremely helpful professor. He tries his best to engage the class in lecture, and he's quite entertaining. He's very willing to set up appointments if you can't make office hours. READING IS CRUCIAL!!!
By far one of the worst prof at ucsd. Very unclear; I got a good grade but dont understand any of the material. I suggest taking another if you have the option.

The material isn't terribly hard, and the time-consuming assignments (three of them) help to ensure that you learn everything. He's actually a great professor -- though lecture slides may not always be completely straightforward if you're looking at them while not in lecture, if you pay attention in class it helps a lot.

This is a pretty easy class if you keep up with the readings. The lectures aren't really clear... but discussions help a lot! Reading BEFORE class will make a difference because the professor goes over everything really fast. Basically, if you just read and do the homework, it's an easy A! (reading the random articles on the syllabus is a MUST!)
Go to lecture, read books. I took 20 units with this class, didn't have a lot of time. pay attention in class and do work and you be fine. Very cool professor if you get a chance to talk to him.

He is a nice guy and knows his stuff but he struggles teaching this subject to such a big class. The homework assignments are extremely time consuming and difficult. If you want to do well in this class you really have to keep up on reading and go to office hours. Not an easy class.

was only for honors class so he wasnt really in a normal teaching role but he is a nice guy, accessible, and knows what hes talking about. good guy to go to to bounce ideas off of & to help you think thru things. rating of "hard" only pertains to class (Poli Honors) & has nothing to do with him

Desposato is a really nice guy and he definitely knows his material, but he is a really really HORRIBLE professor. He doesn't explain thoroughly and jumps from topic to topic. If you want to take PS30 and actually learn something from that class, TAKE KOUSSER. I dropped Desposato for Kousser... best decision ever.

i feel sorry for desposato.  he is really nice, he is a good teacher and his jokes arent all that bad.  he just happens to be interested in a subject that everyone else hates but has to take.  he explains everything really well.  if you go to all of the lectures, you will do well.

This class is mandatory for PS majors and tends to not be the most interesting. Desposato knows his stuff, however does talk fast and sometimes mumbles.  Ask your TA for help, they are really the teachers of this course.

He kind of looks like Quentin Tarantino to me...Anyway, this professor is really hard to follow because he moves fast and expects students to understand everything. However, overall he's an easy grader and really cares about his students. Not the best professor if you want to learn something though. Hope you get a good TA :]

Best professor ever. She was extremely accessible outside of class through discord, and also had office hours three days a week (not counting TAs). Course materials were always posted in a timely fashion. Her lectures were very clear and engaging. Homeworks were interesting but not too hard. Exams were fairly easy with nice curves. Just wonderful.

Took this Winter 2025. Made topics that seemed incredibly difficult in the textbook a lot more manageable. Moves very quickly so read the textbook before class. Material is very difficult, notably at the beginning and at the end.
I like this professor she was good. A little slow. Hope she'd go faster sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Makes my brain much smarter and smoother

I'm taking her for 100A, but the BEST professor in the math department. God bless this lovely woman! She's so nice and caring and always accessible for help. The most down to earth prof here. I can't stress this enough.... TAKE HER IF YOU CAN!
Great professor. no notes! You have to work hard for this class but she makes the material very easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Kristin is great. Her lectures are clear, and she posts notes online. Her homeworks are manageable, and she prepares you for exams with practice exams that closely resemble real exams. She is super caring and accessible by email or Discord, and she's always willing to give hints on homework. She does require attendance once a week. Take if you can.

Dr. De Vleming is a professor who truly cares about her students. She's easily accessible outside of class through OHs/Piazza/her class Discord, and the grading policy is very fair. Instead of a midterm/final, we have ten weekly quizzes (the 2 lowest are dropped), and a final project that is much more applicable in the real world than a final exam.

Professor De Vleming is super good; the best math teacher I've ever met in UCSD. Her lecture notes are clear, and she often stops to see if someone has any questions. Her responses on Piazza are helpful! Really Five Stars!

Professor DeVleming is very clear and concise with her teaching. She cares for the students and always holds extra office hours for those who need more practice. Her tests were relatively easy, and the only homework was WebAssign. Overall 10/10!

Dr. DeVleming was by far my favorite profs. She really helped in students' success by tailoring the course to the world events around us. She was always available for office hours, so if you take the help offered, you should have no problem getting and A in this class.

I was so grateful to take Professor Devleming for Math 10B this quarter. She made calculus so enjoyable and she genuinely cared about her students. Going to her office hours really helps and make sure to pay attention during lectures to prepare for quizzes.

Made examples easy to understand. Non cumulative test each week with a study guide to help us. Office hours and Discussion did a great job to explain the homework. Overall, great class, the only hard part about it was the supplemental homework, but you have 2 weeks to finish it.
The best math professor I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor DeVleming is the goat! One of the best math teachers I have ever had

Oh how I LOVE Professor DeVleming. The material in the lectures is so easy to understand, office hours are SO so helpful, quizzes are reflective of class, decent amount of homework but prepares you for quizzes. Textbook not required, but good resource. As long as you watch the lectures and do your work, you should be solid. Super caring and kind.

Professor De Vleming is an excellent lecturer, as she teaches the concepts in a clear way that allows us to easily take notes. There is quite a bit of homework and it is on the more challenging side, but they are great for preparing for the quizzes. I was so grateful that we had no actual exams, midterms, or finals. Highly recommend.

Dr. DeVleming is such a great professor! Although attendance is not mandatory because you can watch the recordings, you need to understand the lectures, but they are very easy to understand. Take this with a grain of salt, but her explanations made calc lowkey simple (this is coming from someone who only has 10A as prior knowledge of Calc)

The other ratings speak for themselves. If you have the chance to take her, DO IT. She explains everything beautifully and she gives practice quizzes that are pretty much the same thing as the quizzes. The class isnt stressful at all. I highly recommend taking her.

Prof. Devleming is hands down one of the best math professors I've ever taken. I found her exams to be quite challenging; however, as long as you do her helpful worksheets, homework and ask for her help, you should do well in the class. Also, she is super sweet!

Professor Devleming is the best professor I've had during my time at UCSD so far. Although classes were online this quarter, I've learned more from her than any other in-person lectures. She makes accommodations for students under these stressful times and is always accessible outside of class. I have nothing negative to say about her! Amazing
She is an amazing professor. She is super helpful and gives fair assignments. The quizes were not hard to do especially since she gives practice worksheets that are very similar to the quizes.

DeVleming clearly teaches the materials in her lectures and gives reasonably challenging homework. She helps makes harder concepts digestible. She is also highly receptive to student feedback. She is one of UCSD finest professors overall. She is a must-take prof.!

Hands down a must take professor! Her lectures are clear and concise , she compliments them with helpful worksheets and activities .Wants to make sure everyone understands. Shes very caring and is always available to help outside of class to helps with homework or overall understanding of the materials. Exams and homework are reasonable and fair

A+, gold star and two thumbs up, Dr. DeVleming is an excellent instructor. From the little things like taking 2 seconds to remind the class of the notation we're using (which makes a big difference for those embarrassed to ask) to providing clear notes/worksheets/practice exams and lots of help on Piazza. Looking forward to any class taught by her!

I took her for 10B in fall 2018. It was her first quarter teaching at UCSD i believe, but HANDS DOWN my favorite math professor. The averages for midterm 1 and 2 were really low, but as long as you do above the average, you'll be fine. Not sure if lecture is podcasted cause she relies entirely on chalkboard, but I think she posts her notes online?

The Good: - Drops one out of two midterms - Curves fairly - Friendly & Approachable - Homework & Matlab isn't worth too much The Bad: - Tests are very confusing - Assigns a ton of MyMathLab HW - No Recordings The Ugly: - Lectures and rushed and notes are useless She's not bad and tries really hard, but is super unorganized in the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. Took Advertising & Society and loved it. Great banter, keeps class engaging.Come ready to hold real discussions and actually participate. If you can do that, you'll have a great time. Highly recommend..
Easy-going professor and interesting class topics. I didn't get a whole lot out of this course as it was mainly watching group presentations each week, but it's an easy A.

Lectures were kind of everywhere. He rambled on a lot and was also a little passive-aggressive when students were asking for clarification. He has his cool moments, though. I felt like I didn't take away much from his class.
Goes super off topic. hard to follow. lectures and class is overall lacking in organization and clarity.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Save your time and pick a different professor :/ He's cool and all but his class isn't that organized, theres lose guidelines and he monologues during lectures about random stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dewey's cool. I think I can agree with some of these reviews but also, were in college. Your attention is needed, and believe it or not you actually have to put in effort and do the work. Cool class, cool prof, and he would let us out like 2 minutes late. Cmon people

Dewey weirdly called out students who weren't paying attention, which felt unnecessary as almost the entire class was never paying attention. Dewey's class is annoyingly tedious but not hard. Respectfully, Matt, if students aren't paying attention, it's your problem. Have fun writing a case study and an essay about topics he SKIMMED over.

Dewey needs to get organized. Entire class was very loosely guided; instructions at times were unclear, he would drone on in his lectures (unrelated content) and would often run out of time. The work he expects of us goes against the work he puts into both teaching and helping us. Final assignments are exhausting, and will grade them tediously.

Hes honestly a decent person and is nice, but he doesnt teach what hes preaching. The tests and what we retain in his lectures are always completing different, if youre going to take him get ready to learn chemistry basically on your own. And he grades so religious on the exams to the dot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Czworkowski is one of the best professors I've ever taken for chemistry. I did only take one class this semester, but he gives thorough lectures. He is very open to asking questions and even calling out the right answer. 88% is an A! Tests go by homework, review problems, and what he emphasizes in class. Would take again for Chem 142 :)

People are making a big fuss over nothing. He's a really good guy and the material is so easy that theres no need for him to really teach. Midterms multiple choice, quizzes, and no clicker. Honestly, his lecture slides were all i ever really used to study. I messed up on one midterm which is the only reason i didn't get an A. Would recommend.

Came to lecture everyday, when it got tough (ch 4, ch 9) I fell behind in the lectures, but if you stick to the book, do all the homework and make sure you understand each one (sapling gives you explanations - use em!) the midterms and the final are pieces of cake. Exactly what I wanted out of a class - I learned the material and gained an interest

Czworkowski had a great attitude and seemed glad to teach, however, the way he taught was not very useful for the way we were graded (i.e. quizzes developed by TA's). There was plenty of opportunity for help with office hours, discussion, and the chem lab. Final and midterms were fair game.

He's such a nice guy but he isn't the best teacher. His tests aren't curved but they are pretty easy and fair. I hadn't taken ap chem in high school but I still managed to do pretty well in his class thanks to the book. His lectures were pretty useless plus he posts all his slides anyway. Overall the class wasn't bad. His teaching skills however….

Doesn't curve, MC choice tests that make you second guess, useless lectures. I pre-read the text, took notes, and did tutoring to understand what was going on. As a Prof, he's useless. Do not recommend.
Dr. C doesn't curve his midterms or exams but he really doesn't need to. So long as you don't fall behind on the assigned (but optional) readings and homeworks you should be fine in this class.

Dr. C is a horrible teacher and on top of that doesn't have a curve. His tests are relatively easy, but there are under 20 questions so if you miss one it's like 6%. Sapling is easy and quick. His class has no extra credit or any curve. NOT RECOMMENDED.

Class is relatively easy, however it is heavily reliant on you to read the book to learn. Lectures are good for just introducing you to the basic concepts of things, but it's up to you to do all of the readings and learn it more in depth. Could probably pass the class without ever going to lecture.
Lectures are all but useless. Very nice guy but his explanations of concepts just aren't that great. Tests are relatively easy and always multiple choice
Lectures are all but useless. Very nice guy but his explanations of concepts just aren't that great. Tests are relatively easy and always multiple choice.

Dont let the negative comments scare you. Professor C's class is the easiest out of the all chem 6A classes. He has two midterms which are a lot easier than the other chem6A classes and they are all multiple choice. No clickers required. DO the optional txtbook problems since the weekly quizzes and midterms/final are  based off those.

Reading is required and he assigns practice problems that don't need to be turned in. The problems he assigns help the most when studying for the exams. Exams tend to be conceptual but there are, in general, no surprises. He gives a curve at the end of the course overall, and he doesn't require an iClicker or Aris.

He's a nice guy, but a horrible lecturer. It's extremely hard to understand what he's explaining and you're better off reading the book yourself and getting help from friends. Practice tests are nothing like the actual exam which are harder. I only recommend him if you took some form of chemistry class in high school in the past 1 or 2  years.

I got an A+ for the course because I pre-read, practiced, went to weekly quizzes and post-read. Period. Not hard to ace it but his lectures didn't help much. He's more clear and helpful during office hours. Nice guy. Love multiple choice haha. You want an easy A? Take him.

His teaching is meh. You can pretty much skip the lecture if you understand the homework/material. But the real kicker is the TA. TA's grade and make your quizzes so if you get a hard one you're screwed. If you have a good background for chem, might as well take him. If you don't like chem or a little rusty, it's doable but annoying.

.... Attendance not mandatory! Nice guy, but lectures are super boring! Uses Aleks for EC, which can bring up a letter grade if you are doing well on midterms and quizzes..

The guys a really nice guy, I really like him, just his lectures aren't very helpful. And the tests are easy, but if you make one stupid mistake you are done for, only 11 questions, multiple choice. 4 tests, drops lowest, and the final is only worth 2 tests. the textbook will help. a lot.

you have to do the practice problems. if you've never taken chem before, not the best teacher for you. A lot of people are really rude and leave in the middle of class and talk. it's hard to hear, i recommend sitting in the front and getting an oasis workshop.

Reads off powerpoint. very few examples. went to lectures just for clicker points, other than that no need to go, just read the book and powerpoints he posts online. tests are all multiple choice, pretty easy if you do the assigned problems and the self tests. i liked that he didnt have a midterm, just tests. ta sergio was bad.

He's pretty much a good professor. What you get from the course is what you make of it ( if you come to class with a negative attidude towards it you're not going to enjoy or learn much). Notice the correlation between easiness of the course with the perceived clarity/interest/helpfulness of the four previous posters.

Though the lectures may be a bit boring, they definitely help toward your understanding of the subject.  The tests are very reasonable and the TA I have is great (I have Shannon). Most of all, I've talked to the professor  before and he's really nice.
This professor is so boring. Lots of the people in the class leave right after the clicker question(extra credit point).

He does not know how to lecture. Do not even bother to go to the lectures because everything is online.  He just reads off the powerpoint.  The book is your best friend, and the TA's don't help either.  I think you'll be better off with Sawrey (who is a bit harder) than this guy.  The tests are easy tho.
speaks in monotone all the time, lectures with powerpoints using pictures that don't contribute to your understanding of the material at all. basically you learn more by reading the textbook.

You are graded by your worst performance in review quizzes, medium-size projects, and exams. It's very easy to let a review quiz slip past you and there are no drops. Projects are tedious and TAs aren't allowed to help you on them. Textbook and videos are helpful but I felt like I didn't need to go to class since they explained it better.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grading is rigid, with full exam score, missing 2/26 quizzes gives an A-, 3 gives a B. Teaching quality is very poor. Course relies on YouTube videos. He never replies my email. This course should be redesigned. The grade doesn't reflect real learning. He uses rigid policies to lower grades because the exams are too easy.

Incredibly harsh grading scheme which takes the minimum of your reading quiz average, exam average and programming assignments average and makes that your final grade. That too, there are no drops. So if you mess up on one thing, you're cooked for the class. Also assigned a very long, tedious project the week before finals.

Incredibly harsh grading scheme which takes the minimum of your reading quiz average, exam average and programming assignments average and makes that your final grade. That too, there are no drops. So if you mess up on one thing, you're cooked for the class. Also assigned a long, tedious project the week before finals.

Low-effort teaching." or "Not very engaged as an instructor.. Makes his class artificially hard by using the minimum grading schema. Doesn't even give a full 3 hour final window like every other professor in the school, so good luck trying to finish the final on time. This guy also just copies Niema's material (take it with Niema if you can).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really reasonable grading system. A lot of people here do complain on the reading quizes but there really isn't any excuse. At the start of the quarter, you are allowed to take all of the reading quizzes in advance in case you miss anything. PAs are straightforward, and the tests are literally rehashed practice problems from reading quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The grading is based on the lowest grade of tests, before lecture quizzes, and PA. Which is an bad way to grade as you can get 100 on quizzes and PA but do badly on one test and tank you grade. The tests aren't hard but it's easy to make a mistake. His lectures are boring and not of use and he tends to just drone on.

Most atrocious grading system ever. He does not care about students and expects everyone to live perfectly managed lives without ever missing one of his irrelevant, extremely frequent hw quizzes. Miss 3 hw quizzes because life happens sometimes, and you're capped to a B. He gives 0 exceptions no matter the situation. Most inconsiderate professor.

The most straightforward UD CS class. Lectures are extra practice, and everything you need to know comes from Niema's videos. Straightforward PAs, but 2 tedious projects. Grading scheme is rough if you mess up one area (your grade is the minimum score of reading quizzes, PAs/projects, exams). Understand reading quiz content and you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very easy class. The lecture was kinda boring also it was an 8am class. Homeworks are easy, just be consistent.

Relatively easy class; however, the grading scheme, as others pointed out, added unneeded, extra stress, and the course itself was relatively dry and boring imho (the professor was nice, but their teaching style did not get me excited to learn the content)
Easy class. Grading scheme is bad but there is a generous curve at the end. Honestly way better and more interesting than CSE12.

Honestly a very easy class! Every assignment was done online, through prairielearn, and the only gripe I have with this class is the quite unfair grading system. You get the lowest grade out of 3 categories, projects, assignments, and quizzes. You could do great and ace all homework, projects but bomb one test and it's over.

This course was coordinated by Niema and personally, I did not like this professor's lectures. Most of my learning came from Niema's videos. The PAs are not difficult, but the difficulty ramps up when it comes to the two projects. It is a very doable course, but I personally did not like this professor because his lectures are not engaging at all.

Really nice professor with clear lectures. Everything was recorded, even discussions, which made it easy to look back for reference. There were weekly programming assignments until about week 6, to which there were 2 projects and 2 weeks to do each project. All assignments were doable, and the exams were very much like the practice exams.

Sahoo does talk slow and is very long winded. He's responsive on Edstem and offers some extra credit on the final exam. First 6 weeks are chill, the projects in the last 4 weeks of the course are tricky but doable; you have 2 weeks each to complete them. You can get a good grade in this class if you put in the work. Learned a lot from this course.

First 6 weeks are pretty chill as the weekly PAs are really easy. The class does get tough in the last 4 weeks due to the projects, but they're totally managable. Sahoo is very caring and answers all questions asked by student. Exams only makes ~25% of grade and are pretty simple if you understand the concepts.
Although he talks slowly, he explains things well. He discusses minute details such as time complexity and whatnots. He also encourages students to ask questions and have discussions during lectures.

I think Sahoo is a very underrated professor, relative to his scores on CAPES. His lectures may be slow (perfect for 2x speed podcast imo), but he himself is a fair, helpful and accommodating professor who does his best to help students. Exams and PAs are what you'd expect out of CSE100, pretty challenging but doable

His lectures sometimes put me to sleep because he talks really slowly. However this also means I did not have to study a lot in my free time. He is very nice during office hours. PAs are time consuming but this is the same for all coding classes.

Although Professor Sahoo's class feel boring, he care students a lot. He is willing to answer every questions after class even standing outside in a raining day. Don't be afraid of him. Just ask! There are no hard coding question in his exam. You just need to pay attention in class and be prepared to understand every word he speak in the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He's a below average lecturer. Talks slowly and makes (huge) mistakes. Boring. It's the same class as with Alvarado (like, identical and we could go to her lecture). Lots of work on like 5 different websites. No real criteria for +/-, kind of arbitrary (gave me a c- w/ 73%, so 1.7 not 2.0, below SAP). I just don't like the guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The professor is developing the course and makes it very strict for not having her own stuff in order. Grading is unclear, + 5000-word peer project review that's due at the end, which had no gainful purpose. She was pretty condescending and chose to flex her background. I was left feeling frustrated, uneducated, and annoyed.

Pulls out grades out her ah! You have to participate a lot and of course attend the class every time. The group project will mess you with grading, since she provided no rubric or feedback and pulled grades out her ah crack. Also encourages us to use AI, but changes her mind 50 times about when can you use it or not.

professor genuinely cares for students and loves what she teaches. very short MCQ quiz in the beginning of class and 1 midterm + final that are mostly short answer questions. there's a group project throughout the quarter so make sure to contribute because ur members rate you based on that. + a short 5 minute presentation on week 10

She's an amazing person but the class can be a little work heavy especially if your group for the project is not very involved. However, the final and mt had reasonable Qs (MC+short ans) so if you study the lectures/book you should be good. There's a reading quiz every class 4 Qs, pretty easy but you need to buy the book or go to geisel reserves.

Dr. Deal is a phenomenal teacher and inspirer  she takes every opportunity she gets to help students improve their conceptual understanding of the material and she makes it fun along the way! Do the reading, pay attention in lectures, be a helpful group member in the group project, and you will be successful.

Professor Deal is one of the sweetest people I have met. She cares about her students and it honestly made me sad when people wouldn't participate. I had personal issues while taking her class and she was more than accommodating and considerate. A little unorganized with the assignments but overall funny and caring.

Prof. Dhir is one of my favorite professors that I've ever taken. She is soo kind and you can tell she really wants you to succeed and really does listen to you and your thoughts. I really enjoyed her class. Although there was a lot of reading and having to discuss with others, she made class enjoyable! I recommended her to all my friends!!

I usually never rate my professor but for her I needed to she is amazing. Best writing Professor at UCSD. She doesn't give out as much work and really cares for her students. I am also taking her for WCWP 10B. That's how good she is. Would suggest picking her out of all the other writing professors.

Professor Dhir is so caring. She really wants you to learn and never judges you for not knowing the answer to something. I definitely recommend taking her class, I look forward to enrolling in her WCWP 10B.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's a caring professor and very interested in students as individuals. Although she does repeat herself often taking up majority of class time, she is interested in what you have to say even it's similar to your peers. Very thorough with her critiques in writing that helps you create work you'll be satisfied with. Would recommend!
Best teacher I have taken at UCSD. Professor Dhir is kind and clearly wants her students to do well. I would 100% recommend.

Enjoyable and relaxing class. Dr Dhir is very kind. She is knowledgeable and passionate about teaching. Class readings, videos and discussions were fun. She gives prompt and detailed feedback on drafts. I was able to develop both projects very well. She makes every student feel special. I definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Writing is one of my favorite subjects however this teacher made me hate this class. She would repeat herself constantly and treat the class like we were kindergarteners. I have never hated a class so much and it wasn't even the material that was the issue. Sitting in that class was pure torture and there is no other way to put it.

Professor Dhir is really kind. She gives lot of contextualization when it comes to whatever she is talking about for the class and it really helped me a lot when writing my essays. The prompts were also really easy and I was almost instantly able to have ideas. Totally recommend!

super kind and caring. workload wasn't bad, I spent around 1-3 hrs/week. as long as you go to every class, engage in class discussions, put effort in writing assignments, you'll be fine. overall, I def recommend!!!

She's kind, and her lectures are what you expect from a Writing class, super easy. The essays for this class are fairly easy. In order to get an A, you need to go to every lecture, do all your homework on time, and do your essays. She's super nice and gives good feedback to improve your writing. Notebook for readings is cheap too.

Passionate teacher, great lecturer, interesting course. Class consists of 3 quizzes (each worth 30 points) and a cumulative final worth 40 points. One quiz dropped at the end. All quizzes and final taken via canvas (you have a 24 hour window). Extra credit via SONA.

Professor Mukku comes off as intimidating at first but he is really passionate about his studies and research. Attending his lectures and reviewing content after class is a must. Once you see how his first quiz is, you'll get a hang of the rest. This course requires a lot of studying, so if you procrastinate or don't like studying. Drop the course.

You know when people are really intelligent but arent the greatest teachers? Dr. Mukku speaks so fast and expects students to understand what hes talking about. His lectures are SUPER dense. Theres 3 open note tests and a final so its not terrible. Most students stopped showing up synchronously b/c hes not interactive and speaks too quickly.

Very good lecturer and explains things pretty well. The homework was often very long and was usually harder than the midterms and final. The tests were a good representation of the class but the equation sheet he gives usually is not enough you need to memorize a lot more.

He explained the concepts decently, and his usage of the chalkboard eraser as a beam helped with visualizing the concepts. Sometimes he'd go on tangents though for a while or explain a topic in a non linear manner, confusing the class. Though after lecture you'd look up the topic on YouTube and become even more confused... so it's not really him.
The lack of access to resources made this class kinda horrible. Lectures always made the content more confusing for me which added hours of relearning the material outside of class.

The overall grade is graded based on 2 midterms and a final only. Study his notes & hw solutions and you'llbe fine. However, his lectures can be confusing sometimes & his written notes & explanations are unclear so definitely come to office hours for helps. Attendance is required and contributed to 10% of overall grade and lectures are not recorded

Professor Francesco Lanza Di Scalea is by the best solid mechanics professor I ever had. He's an inspirational and hilarious guy. Tests are straight forward. Do the homework and you will do just fine on the midterm. I highly recommend him.
Good class to get to know about SE!
Good Professor. OH are really important.

This guy was horrible! He sometimes goes over the same stuff over and over again and rarely ever does examples. He loves to express mechanical forces using the chalk eraser. You get the feeling sometimes that he's either a new prof, he doesn't know how to teach, or not sure what he's talking about. Try to avoid if you can.

Wasn't the best lecturer but his office hours were extremely useful. Worst was when he was gone and let the TAs teach the class. Had to memorize the equations for midterm and final, but similar to hwk questions.
No Comments

A good professor overall. Explains things not in the best possible manner, but he is aware of this and compensates by longer explanations. Class material needs practice; it cannot be mastered in short periods of time. Has attendance checks.

Lanza is one of the best at UCSD. His accent takes some getting used to, but once you do it's not a problem at all. Likes his students, and does a good job getting to know them. Attendence is mandatory and he takes roll from time to time. He will often put examples that he does in class on midterms and finals, so study what he does in class!

Had for both BIEB 150 and 156 and was amazing both times. Does a great job at explaining what she wants you to understand from lecture. Exams were representative. Both classes had some type of project where you had to work with a classmate (but both weren't bad). Podcasts. Usually gives some form of extra credit. Grading scheme isn't exam-heavy :)

The content of the lectures were easy but on the actual quizzes, the questions were worded to confuse you intentionally. I feel like the exams were made to make it seem like the material is hard, when it really isn't and shouldn't be difficult. Felt like I was being tested on my English more than the actual content.

Had an A leading up in the class and then her final hit like a truck. completely different from midterms in terms of question style that tanked my grade. Ended at 89.56 but due to her policy she only rounded up at 89.70 so I kinda got screwed over at the end. Low stress leading up though. Take if you're desperate.

Her lectures are decent, but her grading is interesting to say the least. All quarter gave easy assignments, then harshly graded the final and podcast assignment. Strange how her grading took a turn after the evaluations were due, I anticipate students would have much different evaluations. The quizzes are not reflective of material taught. AVOID!
Relatively easy exams straight from the lecture slides. Homework and discussion assignments are graded nicely, but the final project is graded harshly.
She is super sweet and breaks down very dense evolution material very well. Her class is pretty interesting overall.

Grading is unfair, do not take her if you care about your GPA. Out of nowhere gives bad grades for the last two major assignments, and is completely unreasonable about giving any kind of help to the class, even though so many people did poorly on the final and quizzes. Lacks compassion for hardworking students, your grade is subjective.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rennison is really nice but her quizzes were not a great assessment of what she taught and were not exactly easy. Also only rounded grades by 0.02 and was a pretty harsh grader. Cool content but not definitely not worth the difficulty if you're looking for an easy A
Professor Rennison is really nice, but I do believe her quizzes/exams are not fair assessments of what is taught during class.

Very accessible and caring, provides a lot of EC opportunities, and adjusts grades for quizzes frequently (so wont be marked down for tricky questions). But sometimes explanation is unclear, and terminology not used in class can pop out in quizzes. More extra research has to be done to fully understand the content. Overall recommended.

Dr. Rennison was a great professor to have for my first quarter at UCSD. Although lectures were asynchronous she was still incredibly accessible. She gave plenty of opportunity for gimme points, but her quizzes were killer and were what really separated your A from your B students. Passing this class is easy but getting an A takes effort.
DEI, don't take this course
Hardest lectures I've ever had to sit through. Take the other teachers, they are way easier to listen to.
Don't take

She's fine. Kind of quiet and easy to tune out if you're sitting in the back, but she can be funny sometimes. DOC 3 is easy and doesn't require too much effort so it's bearable enough compared to other classes.

Some of these reviews are rooted in implicit bias. Prof. Chapman is a diva who doesn't tolerate disrespect in her lectures. She also provides in-lecture summaries of the readings, and models the expectations of the projects/assignments.

She was alright. DOC 3 isnt hard, but she can be rude and make the class feel awkward. The topics discussed in class are interesting. You don't need to read everything, but you do need to read some for ur research project.

I didn't think she was bad but I do think her lectures were boring just cause of her teaching style and the way she spoke. Not very engaging with the material or with students, but I found the class itself to be really easy! Many of the mandatory lecture responses were difficult if you did not do the readings.

Take Strom. Hardest lectures I've ever had to sit through because they were so boring and we couldn't use electronics. Never did any of the readings though and still got an A. Grade determined by TA and anti racist grading policy means you can write whatever as long as it follows the prompt.

The class itself is not difficult so I'm assuming she has low ratings because of her attitude. She can be passive aggressive at times but it's not horrible. She will give examples of assignments and your grade is essentially determined by your TA. There is a good amount of reading but I've heard you can get away with summaries of the text.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Your actual grade in the class is more reliant on which TA you get than the lecturer herself. The lecture material can be presented in interesting ways that you can choose to engage in by answering any open floor questions or talking to a neighbor during a think, pair, share.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lots of weekly reading, it helps to read but a skim and summary is enough. Weekly writing assignments and a final essay. Grade determined entirely by TA (pray yours is lax). She cares about the subject, but drones on and makes lectures boring. Easy to get an A if you put in just enough effort.

Grade really depends on the TA. Frequent discussion time during class so I received more feedback/insights from peers than the professor herself. She started using worksheets in class at the end of the quarter and expected you to finish them by the end of class, which I personally think caused a mess. She can be insightful sometimes though.
Your grade is super dependent on your TA but the class is super easy. Professor can be hard to talk to but is definitely passionate about what she teaches which goes a long way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Attendance is worth a lot in this class, not optional.  Personally, I found Professor Chapman not easy to talk to, so I relied a lot on my TAs for assistance throughout the course. Other than that she is okay.

This review is for all three-quarters of DOC! Overall Professor Chapman is a great lecturer and she has a soothing tone when speaking! She is great at reminding students to do the assignments before the due date and she provides great personal examples of the essays and journals needed to be completed! Definitely would recommend it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I found lectures to be super interesting and she gives thoughtful synthesis of the texts but Chapman definitely relies on participation and doesn't appreciate the fact that you can do virtually no work and still pass, so at least skim over the readings before hand. Other than that, your grade really depends on your TA.

Lectures can feel redundant if you have read material before class. Time is set aside for peer discussion during lectures. She does occasionally threaten cold calls if there are no volunteers. Lots of reading, but it is gone over in lecture and sections. All assignments are writing assignments, but they are short.

Relies heavily on class engagement when teaching lecture. Sometimes cold called students during lectures. Made us wait until someone raised their hand, sometimes the class sat in silence for up to 5 minutes until we moved on.
She is really caring to all her students, makes sure directions for assignments are crystal clear, and does a lot of those "think pair share" activities in class. Be open to participating!!

Professor Chapman is a very nice professor and keeps class engagement by doing a lot of those "think pair share" discussions during class. She's big on class engagement and participation so be prepared!!

Messy handwriting and very conceptual lectures. This class is 20D on hard mode. You definitely have to put in work and practice to get an A. Hardest part of this class imo were the amount of homework problems given. Discussions were extra practice. Attend lecture for the best results. Doable, but hard

The course is very challenging, but the instructional support does not match the difficulty level. There is a significant mismatch between homework difficulty and exam expectations. No practice material is provided before exams. Students considering this course should be prepared for a steep learning curve and limited guidance.
He was a good lecturer, explains things very well. Kind of awkward. I like him. I learnt a lot. I took his MATH180A class in UCSD, idk what's going on with the course code

First midterm average was 38/60. Lectures in general are confusing, written in cursive, barely even legible, and take a lot of time to take in. Lectures are not podcasted, notes uploaded inconsistent with what's taught. YouTube videos teach this 100x better, but there's only so many you can find for this class. At least practice similar to tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: No recorded lectures. Tests didn't reflect lecture material or homework. Class averaged LOW on midterms and final. Unclear lecture notes. Numerical analysis is a tough subject with lots of studying required outside of class, but I don't think this teacher helped me as much as possible.

Lectures are not recorded, lecture notes are only posted until after the "topic" is finished (not posted after each lecture), very hard to read handwriting, and very low midterm averages. Goodluck to you if you don't go to lecture and actually pay attention. Avoid taking this prof unless you really have to. If not, wait for another quarter.

This is an amazing class. If you go to the discussions, you're guaranteed a good grade because the midterm problems are very similar to the ones covered there. Lectures focus on proofs and are interactive. The professor actively engages students to participate.

When to almost all Office Hours, the average for midterm was low, 33/60 but I guess attending lectures was very important. 2/5 questions were mentioned from lectures. This lectures are theory heavy, so stick to the concepts. He has multiple ways of grading 50% or more got B or higher

Horrible lecturer. Him + the TAs didn't explain the material well at all. I stopped attending lecture after the first few weeks bc there was no point. Exams are way more difficult than the practice he gave us, and I felt like I received little guidance. He gets irritated w questions. If you can't get a different prof just wait til next quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Class felt like Math 20D on hard mode (2.3 GPA in class compared to 2.8 & 3.1 from other classes). Lectures were hard to follow so look up videos. He's new but shows signs of improving. A good reminder to practice self-study. You're not screwed if you take him. Grading scheme is very forgiving but midterms had lots of computation in little time.

Profs lectures felt too convoluted and his hand writing was very hard to read. You are better off just reading the textbook. Midterm problems were unnecessarily hard for the time we had to complete them and not representative of the homework. He at least sort of improved this on the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: None of the midterms or finals had a passing grade. If he doesn't change grading curves half the class might end with a C. Horrible professor and you won't learn anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst professor I have ever seen.

Exams were not reflective of the material learned in lecture. Homework and practice tests were not helpful at all in preparing for tests and bad handwriting made it extremely difficult to take notes in lecture.
Lectures aren't helpful at all. Exams are harder than necessary. Feel like practice tests/hw are WAY different than exams.
Lectures only made the content more confusing, made tests significantly harder than necessary
Knowledgable professor. I thoroughly enjoyed taking his class, What use is a Math class if it ain't fun?
Bad handwriting, lectures are not comprehendible. Tests are in no way reflective of the practice tests.

Professor Dinco is one of my favorites I've taken at UCSD. Every time we show up to class it just feels like hanging out with friends and laughing the whole time. He's very knowledgeable when working through projects and creating media. Highly recommend.

Do not take this professor. It's as simple as that. Don't let the low volume of reviews confuse you. He is not qualified and proved it with his unprofessionalism and lack of effort. This is a production course- and if you were, let's say, hoping to learn about production, then find another professor. Will fail if you miss class.

If you miss three (3) classes- you will fail the class. not a point reduction, not a letter drop, a fail, no matter what. claims it is to prepare you for the industry. does not teach in order to prepare you industry. outlandish standards with no credibility to back it up. do not take.
Worst vis professor Iv'e taken do not take this teacher by any means.

Great professor to talk to but he gets distracted easily and is a tough grader. By missing one deadline, it messed up my grade. The grading is clear however there is a lot of work and he does not accept any late work for any reason so try to turn in work early if you can and be there all the time for participation. He is also picky on grammar too.

I wished I chose a different class or at least taken the class with another professor because of the many scripts we had to write nearly every week which took a toll on my other classes. The professor excepts no late work and marks you down hard for any grammar mistakes. Lastly I didn’t learn anything as it was just us writing our own scripts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: He seems like a chill dude however his lectures become very dull. what should have been a fun class turned out to be quite the opposite. I didn't really learn anything new that I already knew. You will be writing down scripts almost every week and make sure you turn them in on time because he won't accept late work no matter what the excuse.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Hands down one of the best professors in visual art. His teaching method is unique and inspiring. His class really makes you think about who you are and who you want to be. And he really cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Ever heard of STEM classes designed to weed out students from the program? This is the film equivalent class. You're expected to hand in a project each week. It is designed to prepare you for the absolute demanding environment of film production. Giving constructive feedback is necessary, and phoning it in will only get you chewed out by the class.

Outstanding professor who is truly caring and thoughtful about his students, as well as fair, kind-hearted, and humorous. Class was always interesting and 3 hours seemed to go by in a flash (he always let us take a break in the middle). He gives extremely great feedback about everyone's work and I loved participating (and I'm usually not the type!)

Critique sessions are objective but grades are very subjective. No matter what level class you take with him you will always have a project due every week. Subject is alterity and he could not definitively explain the term. Makes no room to consider alternative points of view that isn't his lived experience. Not very academic either.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Diagne seems to love teaching students. He often engaged with his students during lectures and actively solicits student feedback and questions. He doesn't record lectures and strongly encourages attendance, though it is not required. His homework is fair and allows students to correct their own work. He picks accessible textbooks.

Professor Diagne is an outstanding instructor who genuinely supports student learning. Coursework is fair, exams are reasonable with study, and he is always available for help, including review sessions before exams. His clear and engaging teaching style creates a challenging yet rewarding learning experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The professor truly cares about student learning. Homework is fair, and exams are manageable with proper study. He's approachable, offers Saturday review sessions before exams, and is always willing to help. Friendly and supportive, he makes the course both engaging and highly recommended.

I feel like the material could've been taught better. Half the time lectures seemed very unhelpful. But he does explain well if he understands the question. Exams were curved which was life-saving. Homework is not bad at all. If you want to truly understand and learn material, might not be best class.

Professor Zurita is so passionate about his job, he is so caring and the material he teaches in class is different from all the film classes I have been taking. a lot of time I fee like I can just learn the stuff professors saying from YouTube video but professor Zurita invite you to have critical view into art and grow as both a person and artist
Best professor I've ever had. Always pushes students to care deeply about their work. Would definitely take his class again.

Professor Zurita is an astounding teacher who inspires students and creates a safe space in the classroom for all types of art to be shared. He provides good critique and grades at the end of the quarter to give students enough time to do the best they can on assignments. He's just a chill guy, grades easily, and brings out the best in students.

Easily one of the best professors at UCSD. His teaching is unorthodox but the results speak for themselves. He made the class feel safe and was always encouraging us to follow our own paths. In his class I found my voice as an artist and made more friends than I have in years here because of the community he creates in class.

The best professor I've had at UCSD. You do have to make a film every week but how can you be a better filmmaker without making more films bro. He cares about each of his students so much. You get a lot of valuable feedback on filmmaking in this class. You will grow a lot as an artist and a person. Take him if you can!! Go HAM

A very inspiring artist and professor that pushes us to actually achieve what we're here for. He
tries to connect with every student in the class, he is actually concerned for our learning.

WARNING
for the girls or guys who are willing to take this class to learn film - 
he will push you to do naked pictures/films. if you didn't do anything HAM
which is like being naked or actually hurting yourself(I'm serious), he will question you for not taking the class seriously.
doesn't grade till the end of the quarter, but the grades are easy.
Greatest professor ever!
THE MOST AMAZING PROFESSOR EVER PLEASE TAKE HIM BY ALL MEANS!! Encourages students to GO HAM and follow their creative aspirations.
Literally one of the best professors at UCSD, very caring and inspiring. I would take this class again.
Easily my favorite class/professor I've had at UCSD.
Amazing lecture and great assignments. Doesn't care much about grades but cares a lot about his students.

If you're not planning on showing up to class, take someone else. The last email she sent was letting us know she wouldn't curve or bump up grades even if you're at a 89.99. Let that sink in. Great lectures and she's very interactive. But there are 3 exams and they are worth 85% of your grade..
Great teacher. Meditates with the class which I found initially unnecessary, but ended up very grateful with. A very good woman and a wonderful teacher. Thanks Karen Dobkins! I wish you all the best.
Tests were worth 85% of our grade (no cheat sheet). Despite the mindful moments every morning, they didn't work the morning she said she should curve down because the average was a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams are worth 85% of ur grade. There are 3 exams and they were all 60-65 questions long. Unlucky for me, it was an 8am class. Lectures are super dense. Try not to take other lecture heavy classes along with this one. I wouldn't take her again. Exams were super hard and class average is low!!!

Boring. Attendance checked by code &question prompt. lectures recorded. 3 exams Tests are actually very difficult she made a lot of mistakes & corrected grade accordingly and even with that the average score was a C in the class. not much homework so that helps study for the test its just end of the week prompt 2 paragraphs what was your fav topic

Professor Dobkins is a great lecturer, class content is a little dense but her teaching style is awesome. Only real criticism is that 3 exams account for 85% of your grade and there's not much else you're graded on, so small mistakes can be worth a lot. There's only 1% extra credit but exams aren't cumulative, it's decently fair.

Overall, great professor!! She is very caring, calm and knowledgable. Subject is very information heavy, there's a lot of materials and small details that we must memorize. Grade consist of 3 test and weekly reflections. Test can be a bit tough but all multiple choice. Always accessible outside of class and lectures are interesting and fun.
Dobkins is a great lecturer! Her grading criteria is a little weird, but the class is generally straightforward. The material is VERY dense but if you pace yourself it's an ez dub.

Prof. Dobkins is almost neglectfully easy on her students. This class was so easy that I frequently forgot I was taking it. I liked her as a person and I actually enjoyed her holistic approach. She does "mindful moments" at the beginning of class, and they're pretty based.

This professor is my favorite ever. I love her so much. Her lecture did not feel like they were an hour long because the material was super interesting. Her exams are SUPER straightforward. Just take notes and use the slides and you will Ace it. I love her so so much. Super caring and inspirational. I 100% recommend her

Okay listen up, Professor Dobkins is the most caring professor at UCSD, her classes are filled with wisdom and I can promise you'll be a better person after taking any of her classes. And you get to learn about neuroscience along the way :)

Professor Dobkins is hands down my favorite professor at UCSD so far. I loved her mindful moments before the lecture begins and the breaks every 30 mins or so. She gives clear and conceptual-based lectures, her slides are straightforward, there are 3 non-cumulative tests, which were all pretty easy, and weekly reflections. Take her!

Professor Dobkins was an amazing and kind professor. With everything going on, she still tried her best to have engaging lectures and genuinely wanted everyone to pass. Averages on exams were 88-92%. Easy weekly discussions and 3 exams including the final. All exams were extremely fair and did not have any tricks to them. One of the best professors

Karen is a great professor! She is willing to answer any questions and is humble. She likes to have mindful moments before lecture starts and gives breaks throughout lecture, so that students do not feel overwhelmed. She really cares about teaching and goes over material thoroughly. All 3 exams are multiple choice. Live lecture is the best!

Prof Dobkins is amazing! Her class had really high averages for each of the midterms (around 89-90's) and the questions are straightforward. I recommend taking detailed notes and writing down everything from the lecture because the exam questions can get specific. Totally recommend this class since we're only graded on 3 midterms and reflections.

Overdue Post: She gets too defensive when you want an open dialogue about test questions that you get wrong. Why am I paying your salary then, Karen? For you to talk about ABBA too much in lecture and get upset when I ask to you explain why my written test question was wrong?
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Your grade is based on 2 midterms, a final, and weekly reflective writing that are a couple paragraphs. She tends to go on random tangents, but they are always interesting. She is very passionate about the subject and is overall a great person and professor.
She is an angel.

Dobkins is a great lecturer with amazing insight. She is passionate about what she teaches which makes lecture easier. 3 tests total (2 midterms, 1 final) worht same percentage of grade, 1% EC. Need to go to lecture, she goes in depth about what is on the ppt and examples are on test. Book not used at all, know EVERYTHING on slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Phenomenal professor. She makes her lectures fun and helps students to understand the content. Lecture is not mandatory but there are things that she discusses that is not on the lecture slides and will potentially be on the exams, so might be convenient to attend. Not much goes in to your grade. 3 exams and EC. Her exam are super fair. Take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She talks to us with a sense of superiority, and when we don't answer something exactly the way she wants, she would keep asking the same question. Additionally, she seems to be very arrogant and a bad listener. If a student challenges her in class, she will quickly dismiss the idea before the student even finishes his/her thoughts.

Professor Dobkins is hands down my favorite professor from UCSD. Yes, it's true that not that much goes into your grade (2 midterms and a final, all of which are non-cumulative) but her slides are organized and she gives great examples/demonstrations. Put in the time and you will get the grade you want, the tests are extremely clear if you study
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class is lowkey cringe with the meditation and "mindful moments" which sheds a time off lecture. I believe more material on her slides would be covered and wouldn't have to be learnt on their own if she didn't do those things. She goes off topic sometimes but they do relate to the material. I wish she podcasted her lectures.

Prof is good and passionate about her job but this isnt a class you can bs. All of the important information is articulated in lecture so make sure you either take good notes or record her lectures bc no podcast. Make sure you study and hit up office hours bc she is really friendly and will help. The material isnt too bad & she explains clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is all over the place which she informs on the 1st day. The 1st midterm is the hardest. She says that most students will usually drop after that. The others were not that hard. She always makes sure to correct herself about what she wants you to know. Don't get discourage after 1st midterm. Long tests (50+ ?s). Loved her mindful moments.

Bio + CBN double major taking Dobkins. If you are familiar with COGS 17 + neuro basics from bio (BIPN100), you should be solid for this class. Still look over her slides bc some details like depolarization values for APs are more specific. She's a lousy lecturer, + some felt its unfair that she skips over concepts for students to teach themselves

I have her for PSYC 106 this quarter. I failed her midterm. I went to class every day even though lecture is not mandatory and took detailed notes. She is not using the textbook this quarter, but her slides are not detailed enough to go off of and she lectures way too quickly. The exam has stuff that she only mentioned briefly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had. Exams are all multiple choice and are based ONLY on lectures so don't bother with the book. Take detailed notes and you'll be fine. Every single question on the exam was covered in lecture... no surprises. Loved her meditation sessions which really help you calm down. TAKE HER! you learn a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The problem with her class is that there's no consistency. She would often ask questions about things she only briefly mentioned and were ignored by the book and her own powerpoints, her TAs would discuss topics that she would go on later to say should be ignored. Questions are also terribly worded. (She removed 20% of the first exam's questions)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the coolest professors I've ever had! She starts the lecture off with a grounding mindful moment. You can tell she is very smart and passionate about neuroscience. Although some topics maybe complex, she makes it easy to comprehend. The exams are very reflective of the material learned. Pay attention, take good notes, and you'll be fine.

The course materials can be challenging at times, but once you get them, they're pretty interesting. She's kind and always start the class with a "mindful moment" about her perspectives on life. There are 2 midterms and a final that's noncumulative. Recording her lectures would definitely help pass her class since the exams are lecture based.

She teaches in a clear way, and she explicitly tells you which information you need to know for the midterm. Also, apparently, the midterm grades are curved, so A+ is definitely doable. In general, I think her class is relatively easy compared to some other upper division psychology courses. I don't think people should whine about her "hard" exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's an extremely intelligent professor and has cool things to say, but the test are so hard. The most received grade on mister one was an F and her reply was simply that those students will just drop. I don't think that very fair at all. If you don't have a good neuroscience background get ready to study extremely hard and expect to struggle.
Very interesting, funny lectures for otherwise difficult subjects. By far the best professor I've had.

Great class, great prof! Definitely recommend. She is super enthusiastic and explains the material very well. 2 midterms, 1 final all non-cumulative (multiple choice + short answer). No papers. No clickers. You should go to class if you want an A, only seeing the slides isn't good enough because a lot of what she says ends up on the exams.

This class is super easy!  Her exams are multiple choice and her questions are basic recall from lecture. Half of the class scores higher than 95% on her midterms, and there is no cumulative final. She also likes to spend a lot of time talking about mindfulness and how to be happy during lecture.  She is also super nice, I would recommend.
Would take again

The best professor I've had at UCSD!!! I learned so much from this class, and the way she presents the material makes it difficult not to understand it. She's an excellent lecture, inspiring and cares for her students. She's very clear and if you follow her lectures, and study, you'll learn a ton and receive a good grade. TAKE HER CLASS!

Awesome teacher! She makes everything very clear and she clearly has a passion for teaching. Only used the book a little bit, but I would recommend reading if you want to get a solid A. And the class is interesting so you will LIKE reading the book. Going to class is mandatory since she doesn't do podcasting

Professor Dobkins is by far my favorite professor to date. Her lecturing style is crystal clear and her tests are very straight-forward. Having a bio background definitely helps with this class. If you don't have a bio background though you're going to have to put a bit more effort into studying but it's definitely not impossible to get an A.
She is one of the best professors. Made everything taught in class easy. Two exams and a final. Very very easy. Take this class and enjoy the free time that you don't have to spend studying.

She really is a great professor. The book was of little to no use, barely even glanced at it and got an A+. You only have to learn the slides she gives out and she is very clear. I recommend her, very easy A.
alright nothing great, didnt make the material interesting at all
No Comments
Class was not fun at all.
explains things to death. offers extra credit. overall not bad.
caring, approachable teacher.  class isn't easy thou, and the extra credit points/experiment ratio is unfair
No Comments
tests aren't THAT easy.  Experiment hours for extra credit ratio sucks
No Comments
nice lady but she does kinda beat the horse
Easy material; great personality, but overexplains (treats us like kids)

Easy A class. Lots of course content was hard to watch. There should be a warning for the content. The lectures were sometimes boring, but the movie clips were interesting. Half way into the year no devises were allowed during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: easiest class ever all you have to do is show up and one weekly assignment.

As an engineering major who needed VIS 31 for a GE, this was one of the best classes I have ever taken at UCSD. Prof. Dominguez tells the history of zombies and how they first appeared on screens. HW is only watching a movie and writing a paragraph. Don't goof off or fall asleep in class, or else Prof. Dominguez is gonna feed you to the zombies.

This man is probably the single coolest professor at UCSD. Not only does he make classes interesting, but the breadth of his field work is astounding and he cares about every aspect of the topics that he teaches on. The class itself was really fun, just watching a different zombie movie every week and writing about it. Prof. Dominguez is my GOAT.

Very Fun Class, he stays in character as if there is a ongoing zombie outbreak. Dont fall asleep or doze off in class because he'll make sure that the zombies will get you. Never had such a fun easy class where I actually wanted to go to a class for almost entertainment.
prof. dominguez is a great + caring professor give this man all of the money

I did not know what to expect going into this class but I am so glad I took it. I never knew someone could speak so passionately about zombies, all while being hilarious at it too! 50% grades based on weekly zombie move reflections (300 words min). 50% based on attendance (based on online i-clicker). 100% recommend him!

I have never rated a Professor but Professor Dominguez has been one of my favorite at UCSD.
