The lectures are mandatory and you use online I-clicker but his lectures are interesting and he's extremely passionate and nice. No final or midterm just one movie to watch and write about each week. Definitely take this class if you are wanting to! 10/10

Professor Dominguez is amazing! You can tell he is passionate about his work and never fails to make the class laugh. Not only is he extremely understanding but also very interactive with his feedback on weekly assignments. It's crazy how much time and effort he puts into his responses. I hope to take a class with him again!

This has been the most entertaining and interesting class ever! The professor is extremely understanding, and there's an obvious emphasis on learning over stressing for grades. Grading is based on lecture attendance and weekly movie reflection. The move reflection had fun prompts, and lecture attendance can be made up! I highly recommend!

He's honestly a very entertaining lecturer and the class homework is just to watch a zombie movie and write a paragraph once a week. He does require attendance to his lectures but they're fun so I didn't mind.
fun and easy

If you care about social justice, Prof Dominguez is the person to go to. He is so inspirational and also extremely funny like he will drop the funniest jokes and just continue on with his lecture. VIS 10 was honestly one of the easiest classes I've taken. It was for major lower divs but would work great for arts GE too.

VIS10 with Dominguez is the easiest A I have ever gotten. Basically, you go to class once a week, let bro cook for an hour about computer arts, and then he brings on a guest to talk about their career. There are reflections due at the end of every week and one big one at the end. Take this class for an easy GE credit.

Professor Dominguez is a caring and great professor! Helped me get a scholarship through letters of reccomendations. He is open and very accessible. I love him. I try to take any classes I can with him!

Now the the quarter is over and I have time to think about what Speculative Design is and or could be, I feel I learned so much, even if I did not understand what it was at the start. Our projects really helped me get a strong sense of what it is and how I could use it in my future work. Professor Dominguez was willing to meet with me and help.

Professor Ricardo is so caring and supportive professor that I can easily ask any questions. He really encourages students to expand their hidden creative and artistic energy in any form. In this class, you can build and explore your own virtual spaces freely without any restrictions. This class is amazing. I strongly recommend this class.
Nice VR class, so fun and helpful!

Professor Dominguezs class is fun and inspiring. He cares not only how you develop your conceptual gesture as an artist individually but also how you and your group contribute to a complete art project through Unity. He is knowledgeable and available for students. He also updates you many helpful VR info that is happening on the campus.

Just finished VIS 30 Speculative Design and it was strange to start with in terms of understanding what each term meant. But I found that by the end of the class my finals team and I were speaking Spec Design or Professor Dominguez's framing of how to develop the final project. All the projects were great and professor Dominguez was amazing.

Brilliant, but violent and out-of-control. Has a bizarre obsession with bathrooms, verbally abuses (mostly women) for interuppting his amazing masculine lecture to go to the bathroom. Also has the most childish temper tantrums about phones (instead of asking people to turn them off) and undermines the TAs (they undermine him back, hilariously).

Every 2 hour lecture is mandatory. Professor is incredibly boring and pretentious. The videos shown in class are sometimes interesting but most of the time just too weird to be interesting anymore. If you're taking this for a ge you're better off taking Vis 1 or 3 instead.

I don't doubt the guy is a talented artist and knows a lot, but I've seen him lecture in different classes, and I swear the man he becomes for VIS2 is just an annoying character he does to shock the first-years. I stopped going to lecture because the things he showed didn't help with projects and the only people grading your gestures were the TAs.

The class was super productive for me, since I had wanted to  get sense of what it was like to do performance art and to use myself in the my installation work. The class pushed me, created a really unique and safe space for making work. The gesture were specific and open. They gave me a lot of room to create in. Yes the media was crazy-just do it!
Actually cares about his students

Ricardo is great.  I took this class to finish up my minor and just hoped I might gain some new perspective on my art practice through embodying my practice rather than just creating objects and video, and I got a lot of it.  Ricardo's method of approaching the "self" as a "canvas" for different modes of provided a wonderful context to explore.
This class is awesome and amazing; why Visual Art Department of  UCSD want to cancel it? I don't understand.

My only complaint about this class is that I had the joy of experiencing it for only one brief quarter. The assignments will push you out of your comfort zone (in a good way!) - be prepared to do performances live and participate in short critiques every class session.  Ricardo is a wonderful professor and this class is a hidden gem in VisArts!

This class was one of the most intense and joyful that I have ever had at UCSD. Professor Dominguez kept us focused on our work as the media was making it difficult. I have gained a very clear and strong sense of how I can work with my body in relation to my art-if I chose to use it.  I was pushed beyond my self, my art, in a safe space. Take it!

We had one crazy quarter with all the media buzzing around this course. We all banded together and had a beautiful, wonderful time. This class is such a confidence builder, and Ricardo is an amazing professor who made this space a safe and comfortable one to bare one's soul.
Really hard to describe him and his class, you kind of just have to be there.

At UCSD the much criticized and overlooked medium of performance is cultivated and passed on by Prof. Ricardo Dominguez.  The art department's best kept secret, performance scares most away due to the emphasis on the body, there's good probability to encounter others willing to take risks.  Performance IS the media of the future and UCSD is lucky.

A really interesting and enlightening class, with one of the best professors in the visarts dept. Plenty of exposure to key performance art movements, ton of experimentation and risk. As a painting and drawing-focused studio major, I REALLY recommend this class - you don't know how horizon-broadening these classes are until you try them!!

Ricardo is inspiring in performing the self.  I was very apprehensive, but hopeful that this would be a good class...and my expectations were blown away.  This course truly teaches you about yourself and skills learn are actually applicable to daily life.  I HIGHLY recommend this unit to anyone willing to push themselves a little.

He's a great professor. Real genuine,very knowledgable, and tells great stories. I've had 3 classes with him and they NEVER got boring.  The risks you have to take in his class are well worth it in my opinion. Because of that man, I've gained a lot of self confidence and I am very honored to have had him as a professor.

I couldn't make heads or tails of this class when I got there, but in the end I'm so glad I took it. Definitely covers some shocking material, but this class changed the way I think about art. The environment is really open and gives you a chance to really explore yourself. Conceptually challenging. I recommend it!

I'm not sure what to think of this guy. I don't care for his lecturing personality, very confrontational. His lectures were very terse; more of a philosophy class than art. I have to say though, the assignments he gives can be very fun if you're willing to just let loose and go with it!

Performing the Self was absolutely fantastic. Dominguez is a living legend; he is incredibly erudite and creates a safe and comfortable environment in which to work. I would recommend this professor to anyone interested in challenging themselves to explore new realms of the self. Excellent teacher.

Kinda mean when he's in a big class, but really nice when he's in a smaller setting. Really encouraging and knowledgeable in the area... it's easy to talk to him about assignments and difficulties. His classes are extraordinarily weird for normal people, but worth a try to break your mentality about alot of things...

I actually had professor Dominguez for both Vis 2 and ICAM 130.  Upon first entering his class, I thought that he was very engaging and I was actually almost afraid of his booming voice, complex topics and etc.  At the end of the quarter, I appreciated his care at educating his students, and how he wanted to remind us all that we do have a voice!
Extremely compelling guy, his lecutres contain more wild conceptualizing than anyone you'll ever meet.

Well, you can't please everyone in this world. Some people are too close minded that they can't see things as more than what they are.(Vis2) We are all diff. and act, talk, & TEACH differently, just in case some people didn't know this. We all have diff. ways of trying to make sense of this world, and Ricardo only shows us the way he does. (cont.)

I highly recommend Ricardo Dominguez for any of his classes.  With his intelligence, passion for his work, and his upbeat personality all combined, we get the best of both him and the topics discussed in class. The material discussed will keep you focused at all times.

Professor Dominguez is very passionate about the topic which makes lectures interesting.  I was scared at first as the subject of Electronic Civil Disobedience went over my head but by the second lecture it became clear. I recommend this class.

Professor Ricardo Dominguez ultimately has been a key inspiration in my life. Because of Dominguez, my main focus became performance art and I am continuing to grad school with endeavors that started in the class, Vis 2.  He challenged our class with projects and gave grounded, well structured explanations during lecture. He is one of the best! -TM

Dominguez is extremely smart, cares about his students, and is the reason I decided to change my major to Visual Arts. I don't know where all these negative comments are coming from. Someone said he****female students? Are you kidding me? That is so insulting and ridiculous, and...so far from the truth. He is really professional, and definitel

ATTENTION all students at UCSD: take this course!It will change your life.Never again will you get the chance to explore art this radical! Don't be afraid.Take a risk, explore something new, get out of your comfort zone.  Perform your body, perform your self, perform your life. Live your art work! S-O-M-A, the body, art as life.Dare you to try it!

Vis 2 is a course for those interested in using the body as their primary medium.It is rather abstract compared to most art classes.If one wants an intro to body art/ performance art, this is the course.Dominguez is quite a character, but has a great amount of knowledge about performance art and cares for students interested in this type of art.

This is my favorite professor on campus. Richardo is always there for you pushing you to do better. He honestly cares about his students he works one on one with your personal talents and interests, continuously pushing you to grow. His lectures are refreshing, preformative and full of useful information. You will not regret knowing him.

Love the class. Def. require critical thinking, and active engagement in participation. Topics are interesting and crucial, and make you more aware of social, political, and economical issues. Assignments are not very difficult if you are willing to put research efforts. Prof. is very responsible in giving feedbacks.

This is my favorite professor on campus. Richardo is always there for you pushing you to do better. He honestly cares about his students he works one on one with your personal talents and interests, continuously pushing you to grow. His lectures are refreshing, preformative and full of useful information. You will not regret knowing this man!

other comments r immature! ricardo is a genius in public intervention &  is well known 4 the virtual sit-ins he initiated. He emphasizes theory and concept a lot to back actions so that could be boring to some (hey we'r at ucsd) He doesnt give a s*it about grades (that's y he grades so easy), he actually cares that you learn SOMETHING in his class.

This professor does not know how to teach. Talks in some sort of fake tone which he thinks make him sound more professorial. Assignments are vague and expectations seem to vary by the student. Way too much sexual material shown in lectures, no concern for students who might find material offensive. Avoid this class if you can.

Talks in a clear tone, very easy to comprehend his words. However, the majority of the time in the MANDATORY lecture is dedicated to watching films and documentations of performance artists which often are naked or doing sexually inappropriate things. In the class you have to do 5 public performance gestures and write a paper so it's not that bad.

I found him to be extremely good at framing art work that would be difficult to think about and even more try to create. I never really thought about any other art form beyond painting - but I now thinking about doing something like pefromance as part of my work. I you want to think beyond what you think you know about art...go for this prof!

Dominguez was a lot of fun! He speaks intelligently and quickly, and is completely crazy. It's awesome, especially when the class creates its own inside jokes. You definitely can't be afraid of your own body or human sexuality, though, or it will totally scare you off.

This was by far the most offensive and disturbing professor I've come across in my life, and his class content is frequently****ographic and completely inappropriate no matter what age or education level. He makes up words and thinks he's all smart, but I see him as a long-winded, burnt out failure of an "artist" who should never be teaching. Ever

He is very interested, very helpful, very intelligent and has recent experience with film in conjunction with the internet. As long as you are truly interested in film and willing to work, you will like this professor.

He is a really cool and interesting guy except for his tendency to talk and talk which isnt always interesting. fun guy, though. he lets you run the classes which is nice. make him talk less. he is out of his mind and i love it.
He is very long-winded an boring, but easy. He's actually an well-known political hacker.

One of the most frustrating classes I've taken. The professor was disorganized, lectures were unclear, and it was difficult to learn the material. I would strongly recommend avoiding this course if possible.

You could have blessings all the way from Jesus Christ himself to Anu the Mesopotamian god of the heavens, and you'd still get a C. World class neurobiologists can't explain the synapse patterns in his mind. Agitated by lack of participation, telepathic connection is expected. Failure to do so results in fighting with students in 200 person lecture

He is incredibly knowledgeable about communications and speaks of it in an extremely sociological context. Overall, lectures are so interesting and informative; however, the grading criteria are incredibly unclear. Even if you understand the course concepts well, you are likely to receive a C on your in-class essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Don't take his class. Not clear with grading, and very harsh. Has this kind of stuck up attitude, where he requires you to particpate in class, but embarrasses you if(when) you saying something wrong. Just save yourself the stress and dont take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Everyone on here is trippinnnn, or maybe he just changed as a teacher, but I took him for COMM164, he's a genius. Class feels like having a conversation with a smart person. He is very interactive with the class and gets you thinking. He likes to ask questions to get students involved and he doesn't believe in testing (no final or midterm).
He is a great professor. Don't have much to say, just an awesome, kind, and fun person!

There were only a few people got an A in my class. He went through the lecture very quickly and do not allowed us to get his PowerPoint, also do not provide the recording. Two essays in total, but grades depends on the TA, you will not know your grade until the very end. Heavy readings every week. Never responded email back.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Rubio was a great professor! I took his class in the fall of 2021, his lectures were always interesting and provided a good foundation for the rest of my COMM classes at UCSD. Most of the readings I've seen again in other classes, which is great for learning the fundamentals. The only major grades were two in class essays, which weren't bad!

Do not take if you want to spend your whole week reading. Professor takes a philosophical approach to communication which is confusing and does not share slides nor recordings. You will never know your true grade until the very end of the quarter.

Honestly, AVOID THIS CLASS. He never specified his grading criteria and you never know the grades of past assignments. HE NEVER REPLIED EMAILS. I ended up getting a C without having any idea why I lost those points. Taking this class is really a terrible experience.

Just took his Comm 10 last quarter. Short conclusion? Do not take his course. Throughout the quarter there are two projects, you will be forced to work with other 9 students to get the project done. He will grade you only base on the grade of projects instead of your effort. Also you will have no clue what ur grades will be all time, NO CLUE

Took this class during the fall of 2020. All you had to do was make two group projects, but the kicker is this class had no clear cut grading criteria. I literally went the entire 10 weeks not knowing what my final grade was going to be. Is it based on participation, how good the proposal is? You would never know. Avoid this class or P/NP it.

He speaks fast is the main complaint but if you can get past that his lectures are incredibly engaging some of the best I have attended at UCSD so far. They are very content dense and there is quite a bit of reading but he summarized each reading well and holds my attention through out the class (rare). Glad I took this class. more secure in comm
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's not a bad teacher, but not a particularly good one either. He made COMM 10 way harder than it needed to be (although it depends on your TA). He assigns a lot of reading and is a tough grader. But his lectures are pretty interesting if you decide to go.

Not a good prof. Very pretentious and unfriendly, especially to those with different opinions than him. When it comes to the op-ed, he says any subject is on the table and that students are free to express whatever opinions they have. Trust me when I say, that is not true at all. If you don't spit back his opinions your grade will be affected.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Whole class is based upon section attendance/participation, and two essays. One is an op-ed and one is the final exam. The entire grade is determined by the TA. Breakdown of grade - 25% section, 35% op-ed, 40% final essay. Be prepared to read about 100 or so pages per week if you're looking to get an A

Prof Rubio was intimidating at first but he explains the readings very well in lecture, tbh I never read the readings assigned until the final essay. You are epected to participate in discussion but fortunately I got a really laid back TA. You can miss lectures if you want but make sure to get all of the notes. There are only 2 assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Dominguez Rubio explains concepts from readings clearly and simplistically. Instead of a midterm, students have to write an Op-Ed. The final exam is a take-home final essay. You should attend lectures, as they aren't on podcasts. The readings, unfortunately, are very long and tedious.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Great lectures. Interesting material. Lots of reading but readings extensively covered in lectures. Attend all Sections, don't miss more than 1 section or you will be marked down a full letter grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: By far one of the best professors on campus. Phenomenal teaching style with wonderful lectures and synthesis of course material. He is passionate and will transfer that same passion to you, even after the course is completed.  There are only 2 essays for the grade but they are fairly easy if you follow guidelines. Easy A if you just go to lectures.

DO NOT TAKE UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES. If you're looking for a well-rounded, discussion-stimulating class, this is not it. He argues with students who don't agree with his viewpoints, or even just try to present an alternative argument. He does not give clear instruction on assignments and makes students feel dumb for asking questions.

He is rude to students and made my classmates and I feel stupid for answering his questions in classs. He does not give clear direction, and in most cases does not give any direction, on assignments. All he does in lecture is show maps and bar graphs, which are not helpful. Would not recommend him to anyone under any circumstance. DO NOT TAKE.

He had an insane curve at the end of the class, making sure that around 40-50% of the students would get an A. On top of that, his tests were standardized to fit the set up of the homework and practice problems. He also has a really fun candence of speaking that kept me engaged.

Prof Smith is great. He does not try to screw you over or confuse you. Only SI units used and his lectures, HW, and practice questions prepare you perfectly for the exams. You put in full effort and you will do more than okay, half effort and you still pass. His explanations are good and there is lots of help. He applied a generous curve too.
Chill and funny lectures. Tests reflect the homework and slides pretty well. T/F questions killed me but everything else was pretty straightforward. Gives good practice.

Prof Smith did a great job explaining the concepts clearly and only testing us on stuff he went over in lecture. Quizzes are reflective of homework questions, lots of true/false questions, drops 1 out of 3 quizzes. Huge curve at the end too. Would definitely recommend taking the class with him if you get the chance.

He was very caring and funny during lectures, but can't say the lectures directly correlated to a lot of the conceptual problems on the quizzes so you definitely have to stare at practice problems and think about what they mean. The quizzes/exams were fair and were similar to the HWs, and the curve was generous as well!

The lectures for this class were not very content dense but all of a sudden you get to the exams and nothing makes sense. His t/f questions do get you on exams and they are so randomly specific but there was a giant curve at the end of the course.

The majority of the class grade was made up by two of your three quiz scores with the lowest being dropped as well as your final which is 40 percent of the grade. The exams were overall pretty understandable but make sure to watch lectures to understand even though it's all multiple choice it's a lot of material. Curved generously and recommend!

My fav physics prof hands down. His lectures were amazingly taught. The class was bot well aligned with the lab. Quizzes followed the HW but the final did not. Mix of T/F and MCQ.  He ended up grading the class on a curve to give 50% an A and 40% a B
The amount of t/f questions on both quizzes and the final were unnecessary. Other than that, it was ok; I would not personally recommend taking him in the future.

He is so funny and his lectures have so many random jokes and dry humor. Content not that difficult if you pay attention in class and do the homeworks. Quizzes and final exactly like homework questions and all multiple choice so easy to study for.

Curve pretty good. Got a 95 overall. I never even went to lecture and still did fine. You really have to understand the concepts to do well on the quizzes and exams, because even if you know the definition, they can twist the question in a way that tests whether you actually understand it. I personally didn't really like him as much due to the t/f.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Biweekly homework, 3 quizzes with 1 drop, 40% final. Attendance not mandatory, ok lecturer but reading off the posted slides was fine too. Quizzes/final multiple choice, really checks for understanding with a lot of T/F. Very similar to HW and extra practice problems. Formula sheet provided, no cheat sheet.

i used to hate physics before this professor. he should have a higher rating. he doesn't try and trick students by giving overly complicated problems. his exam questions are super similar to the homework and practice problems. lectures are great too. definitely try taking him if you can. i loved this professor.

Tests not that similar to exams - qs formed similar but not given certain things you were given before. Very tight on time. TF qs were very hard. Tests had a lot of qs and we didn't have a lot of time. Overall probably wouldn't take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really engaging lectures and has a really clear system of homework. Quizzes are similar to homework. Doesn't try and trick students, keeps things simple, genuinely interested in making sure students learn physics and not unnecessary information. Also funny

Professor Smith is awesome. Lecture slides are clear and he teaches the content very well. His rating should be way higher. Homework is all made by him and his quizzes are exactly as his homework problems. He doesn't have homework whenever there are quizzes which is great since he wants you to focus on studying for the quiz. Overall, he's great!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a funny good person, but he don't know how to teach....

I hated physics before and came in really intimidated by the content, but he explains things great, has clear and organized slides, and the class is extremely fair. HW questions are very similar to quizzes since he writes the questions, so you won't need the bad kudu textbook. I've never done so well in a physics class.. Take it with him!!
Prof is an amazing lecturer! I absolutely hated physics before this, but he makes it interesting with lots of connections to biology/medicine and he's a rly funny dude. Highly recommend taking him!

Loved this professor! Good lecturer, clear about what was on exams, clear and fair grading. I'm not very skilled or interested in physics but this professor made it very manageable. He tried to connect what we were learning with biology as often as possible which is awesome for a physics for bio students class! Take him if you can!!

The best physics professor I have ever had. He structures the class so the homework is exactly like the quizzes. Therefore, it is super easy to do well in the class as long as you do the homework. The final exam was just like the previous quizzes and homework. Super easy, definitely recommend!!

I don't understand how he doesn't have a higher average rating. I didn't really attend lecture in person but whenever I watched his podcasts to catch up on the material, I found myself learning fairly easily. He does a really good job explaining the concepts and his slides are pretty organized.

unlimited attempts in HW, 3 quizzes with lowest being dropped. Curves overall grade and curved my class's final due to avg being a little lower than his other class. Highly recommend, quizzes are literally based off of his lectures and similar to HW and practice problems.
He's a great professor; he writes his own hw questions which very well reflects the questions that appear on quizzes and the final. There are t/f questions though that a

He's really funny, and a good lecturer. He has unlimited attempts for his weekly homework, three multiple choice quizzes (20 questions, with t/f questions), and a multiple choice final. His quizzes were similar to the homework and were fair, and he had extra practice questions. He would also post the homework and solutions after they were due.
No mandatory attendance, he is a super nice guy and a bit funny but he does not normally reply to the emails. Quizzes are fair! & he curves. I recommend his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed his class! Unlimited attempts on homework, and quizzes represented the content of the class. Physics can be a hard subject to keep people entertained, so he always tried to put in jokes into his lectures. Final was also a good representation of what we had learned.

Prof is so sweet and explains things very extensively. Lectures can get boring, but watching them on 2x or even looking at the very detailed slides will ensure success. The quizzes were exactly like the homework and extra problems, so studying that will set up an A. There are a lot of true/false questions with some math. Recommend him a lot!

As soon as he said "students don't really learn by textbooks anymore," I knew this was going to be an amazing class. 3 quizzez, very reflective of homework sets (7 sets total). Lectures had everything you needed to know in a concise and understandable manner. Gave extra practice and posted quiz/homework answers after due date. 10/10 Recommend!

Homework is weekly canvas quizzes with unlimited attempts. Quizzes and class material are conceptually slightly challenging but mathematically easy. Professor does everything he can to buff your grade. It would take more effort to fail the class than to pass it.
Chill dude. Tests are exactly like the HW, also gives extra practice problems. Unlimited attempts on HW. Pretty easy course.

This professor knows what he is talking about. He is such a sweet soul. His tests are exact as his homework and extra problems. Class isn't mandatory, he podcasts and in his grading scale 85% is A. He's really funny with his pick up lines too, overall a great class. Isn't hard to study for his class. I would take his class again.

He's literally the GOAT, his quiz are exactly like the HW and he frames the lecture slides so that they are easy to look back on and understand what's going on. he also makes funny jokes and is just goofy. probs one of my fav professors at ucsd. side note I thought 1B was much easier than 1A, and I think he played a major part in that.

Protect this man at all costs. Canvas HW due every other week (except on quiz weeks). Quizzes on weeks 3,6,9. No Kudu [derogatory] HW. No attendance taken. Hilarious, goofy personality, and makes content digestible. Pretty sure class quiz averages were in the mid C to mid B range. 

His lecture class was far less stressful than Tsai's 1A.

Professor made a tough subject easy. Exams were straightforward, with helpful formula sheets. Lectures clear, slides useful. Unstuck AI great for practice problems. Generous curve too - this class is a must-take!

Professor Smith made a difficult subject very easy to understand. His exams were very straightforward and almost identical to the homework and practice exams. He even gave us a very helpful formula sheet to use. His lecture slides are very useful and he sums everything you need to know during lecture. He's pretty funny too without even trying.

GOATed professor. Optional attendance, very clear lectures, has a good grading structure. As long as you study for the exams, do his extra practice problems, you will do well. If I really have to complain is that he isn't very accessible via email, though he is active on piazza a lot

As someone who was terrible at physics, Professor Smith made it extremely easy to pass the class even if you do poorly on quizzes. I thought I would fail the class but a generous curve was used! Formula sheets for quizzes but make sure you know how to use it.

Everything you need to know is in his lecture slides. I wish I tried harder because professor Smith gives you all the resources to do well in his class. Some of the contents of the lectures are just difficult.

Best teacher ever. Would take him for every single class if I could. I only went to class for exams and ended with an A even without the curve. Homework and extra practice problems were identical to the quizzes and finals. If you can't take 1B with Smith, wait until you can. He is that good.

Doug was a phenomenal professor, gave students every opportunity to succeed. Homework had unlimited attempts and looked just like the quizzes and the final. Lectures and lecture slides explained everything extremely clearly. Gives formula sheet on all tests. If you fail this class, you deserve it, because Doug could not have made it any better

Genuinely believe he a 10/10 professor. His guides to how to get an engineering major to go out with you had won me over. He gives a bunch of extra problems to help you study for the final and quizzes. If you do them then with enough practice you will get an A.

Absolute goated prof. Hated 1a so much, so I went into 1b with little expectations. Smith is incredibly kind and caring. His quizzes are very fair and nearly identical to the HW and extra practice problems he gives. He speaks a little slow but he records all lectures so it's easy to get past. Would 1000% take again

His lectures are usually dull (sorry!) but everything he expects of students is completely clear and reasonable from the get-go. grade weighting is 30%/35%/35% homework/quizzes/final; students get unlimited tries on homework and can drop 2 HW and 1 quiz out of 3. Quizzes are just like the HW. Very generous curve, top 40-50% of class gets an A.

He explains things very clearly in lectures and provides examples. If you understand the slides, the homework and tests are very easy and straight forward. Just have an understanding and the formula sheet is helpful.
His lectures are very good and straight forward but his tests are pretty difficult. I just regret not putting in more work but the lessons have definitely been useful for me to use again.

Top 40-50% got whole A's (4.0!). Quizzes and final were easy if you kept up with lectures, and the professor really cared about his students' concerns. I would take all of my classes with him if I could. 10/10.

Used a flipped classroom...not super helpful tbh. Quizzes and final were annoyingly tough with difficult conceptual questions. The good thing about his class is the curve is MASSIVE, and any quizzes below the final grade get replaced. Top 40-50% get an A, and the score for each assignment is dependent on the average, so favors a decent performance.

His class was a flipped classroom format, which wasn't very helpful because the in-person lectures basically became useless. His tests are hard, filled with confusing conceptual questions, and I felt like he does very little in helping students learn. I also didn't appreciate how your grade relies entirely upon how well others do.

This professor used pre-recorded lectures to teach the majority of the course. His quizzes and tests were fairly difficult but he had a forgiving grading policy where all quizzes lower than the final would be dropped. I didn't do the best on all the quizzes but did good on the final and ended with an A. He curves 40-50% get a grade in A range.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Not bad. The class was tough but I blame myself for not putting in the work. I actually thought the jokes were funny and appreciated the jokes.

The class wasn't too bad, it was just that the quizzes and final were probably the hardest tests ever. His answer choices for math questions were always in ranges ie. 0-10 and 10-20 and so on... As for the conceptual questions there would be an all of the above or none of the above. However his lectures were kinda funny.

His lectures were not engaging whatsoever. I tried to make an attempt to give his flipped lessons a chance, but given that his classes required students to watch an extra lecture prior to the in-person lecture, it was not helpful. There was no use attending his in-person lectures and he would go on tangents.

He is a nice guy and makes good jokes. However the flipped classroom format was not the best for me. I think I would've learned more if he lectured in person. I also did not enjoy the answer ranges. Other than that he is pretty straightforward.

So lazy! Didn't even lecture, but instead used poorly done, confusing old recordings from COVID lectures. Quizzes averaged around 5s, and were awful MCs, with answer choices given in ranges like "between 3.0-6.0" or "All of the above" or "None of the above". Disorganized and disappointing, given the difficulty of the material. :(

Quiz averages are around a 6.5-5.5/10 and linearly went down as the quarter progressed. I would do all the lecture problems before the quiz, go over the lecture slides and homework, and still end up with a 7/10 at best on his quizzes. Only good thing about this class is his curving system because no one really ends up failing and most ppl get Bs.

Idk what professor these wackos took but DO NOT TAKE THIS FOOL! Homie spent more of his class teaching me how to rizz up a pretend "electrical engineering student" with circuits rather than teaching me physics. Quiz averages are a 50% and he gives ranges for answer choices. He tries to do a flipped classroom style but fails at making it effective

The most poorly organized and frustrating class (and professor) I've ever taken in my life. Lecture slides are cluttered, poorly worded, and have tons of grammatical errors. Smith's ability to convey concepts are subpar at best. Quiz averages are around 5-6/10. No idea why he has so many good reviews, maybe I missed something. Avoid if possible.

Professor Smith is a lovely man who genuinely cares about what he teaches. Attend his lectures and I guarantee the class will be a breeze. He is a little dorky and very friendly and funny. Lecture slides sometimes get cluttered but I have enjoyed this class thoroughly, as far as physics classes go.

Overall Professor can teach and quizzes were fair. His curving system on the other hand is horrible. Class is graded on a curve and you have no idea what your grade is until final grades is released. Some sections had higher averages than others making it difficult to get an A if you were in a smarter section. Overall didn't like the way he curved.
Great professor! Definitely gives off Dad vibes and is very caring of his students. Explains concepts fairly well, but you really need to have a clear grasp on the concept to do well on his exams.

AMAZING professor. very reasonable quizzes (he never tries to deliberately trick you). Very accessible outside of class and homework is a reasonable amount of work every week. He also replaces your quiz grades if your final is higher. Overall such a great professor, I highly recommend him!!! UCSD pls hire him for phys1c!!

His slides and lectures are very well organized and easy to understand. Gave lots of optional extra practice before quizzes. Quite funny and very understanding, it really seemed he was trying his best to help us learn and get a good grades. If you're lowkey bad at physics like me, don't worry, Prof Smith is great!

Just a great professor and funny guy. Wish he was my dad. Lectures were super clear and straight to the point. Lots of practice problems in lecture and biweekly quizzes that were just like the homework/lecture problems.

Honestly one of the best professors I've had. I was kind of scared because I struggled in PHYS 1A, but his quizzes and homework are representative of the content viewed during lecture and he always tries to do things easier for you. He does practice problems during lectures that are very helpful. I love his sense of humor, 10/10 would recommend

The best professor ever! Especially for physics ;-; I didn't do the best in Physics 1A so I was scared for this class. But, Physics 1B was the exact opposite. His explanations were extremely clear and his tests are super easy as long as you took notes. He doesn't dwell on extra calculus explanations, and he gets straight to the point!

For the ones thinking about grades, he really focuses on making sure everyone is on board with getting a B+ as he curves based to that based on the class average (quizzes ranged from 50%-60% so that's a huge bump). Another plus to professor Smith is his humor and willingness to help as much as he can with this new online platform. Really recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Beware of dad jokes! Fun, caring physics prof and always willing to explain things further if you are ever confused. Handled online teaching very well, very organized, though the quizzes were kinda tricky sometimes and would really test if you knew your formulas and concepts. Overall, really great choice and happy to have taken him.

Lectures are pre-recorded. He answers questions very fast on Piazza. He explains concepts pretty well. 3 quizzes, weekly hw, and 2 hour final. Grading was fair. Quizzes represent hw. Conceptual questions as well as math. Nice guy, cares about students. I've never taken physics and I learned a lot.

Weekly online HW, 3 quizzes, final. Make sure to do HW because it goes toward your grade. The quizzes are only counted towards your grade if they can help it. Lectures relatively reflected in quizzes & exam. Conceptual questions were very hard for me. Prof Smith is precious and great at walking you through the problems & presenting the concepts.

He's a pretty funny dude so I never dreaded going to class. There's an endless amount of positive things to say about the guy. The only thing is that sometimes I felt as if there wasn't enough practice problems since the extra hw problems weren't that similar to the quiz but this is easily alleviated with "The Organic Chemistry Tutor" on YouTube.

Professor Smith was really helpful in the transition to online learning. I can definitely approve that he really kept me entertained by using real-world examples in his lectures which added more understanding of a concept. I hope he continues to teach this way and in regards to grading, it's one of the fairest systems I've witnessed in physics.

Smith is such a chill teacher that really has all the dad jokes in the book. He's sarcastically fantastic, and I loved his lectures. Because of how quirky they were, it helped me be less bored throughout his online class. His quizzes are extremely fair and as long as you understand the math you'll do well in his class.

I loved Smith's class format with three quizzes with short lectures loaded with example problems. He gives hand-written solutions to quizzes which I VERY MUCH appreciate and it really helped me learn the past-tested concepts to prep for the final. Its the small details and work he puts in that really helps students like me learn efficiently :)

Professor Smith is one of the best professors ever in terms of making himself available and attentive to student needs. He makes funny jokes during lecture and gives clear due dates as well as grading criteria. Physics in general is not a very straightforward subject to teach so given that, I think Professor Smith did a fine job!

Professor Smith is such a kind & pure man. Physics was the scourge of my existence up until now but with Smith it was actually kind of enjoyable. Most of his exams are plug and chug with some multiple choice concept questions (which are usually past clicker ?s) so it's super straight forward. Hmwk is short & easily managed without any outside help
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I was hesitant about Prof Smith due to his bad reviews from the past, but he really surprised me. His lectures were helpful and representative of the quizzes/exam. He lets you drop all quizzes that won't help your grade if you do better on the final. His nerdy dad jokes during lecture make him even more lovable. One of my favorite profs at UCSD!

Amazing guy. He's very nerdy which makes him really fun and chill. He has a unique sense of humor He doesn't give extra stress. He gives you everything you need to do well. His tests are representative of the material. His hw is short. Quizzes only help your grade. Def recommend him

Professor Smith is a total dork. His lectures are a little bland but he does throw in some fun humor. He simplifies the material. Lectures are somewhat mandatory because he does clicker questions. There is assigned online homework and 3 quizzes which are designed to boost your grade. He always grades on a curve towards B+. Definitely recommend.

Loved him so much took him again for 1B, and now his grading scale is EVEN better, homework is worth more, exams less . It's very evident he really cares about our success, he takes advice from students and changes things so we do better, like more kudu attempts, a formula sheet, etc. I'm taking paddock now and now I REALLY know how great smith is

This man is great, he may not be the best lecturer but he def tries very hard to ensure his students' success. His grading scale is really geared toward making sure we do well. quizzes are chill, he doesn't pull anything crazy out and he gives very little HW compared to paddock. On top of this, he's also very funny, I always looked forward to class

Professor Smith is a literal dad. Hes precious and actually cares about his students. Even changed the grading scale to help his students out. Quizzes are not hard and actually representative of material he teaches

I love Douglas! He really cares about his students & wants all of us to succeed, which can be seen in his grading scale. Literally asked all of us if we wanted him to change the scale, add a formula sheet, and to cancel the last quiz (bc our final was the following Monday). Such a dad & makes you look forward to lecture, one of my fav profs at UCSD

Clickers are used. You only have to click once for full attendance and there's video of the board and slides. Slides and examples are reflective of quiz problems, so that's mostly all you need to do well. If you do poorly on any of the quizzes or miss class often, your final can replace the scores. The prof does a decent job explaining the material

I love Douglas. He has a quirky sense of humor and is really funny, often unintentionally so. There are clicker questions, but you can make them up during the final so attendance isn't necessary. Very generous in terms of grades. I hope I can take him in the future.

Not the best explainer but if you go over his slides the quizzes are an easy A to B range. He has a great grading system. He'll drop all quizzes and make the final worth more. you can make up iclicker points on the final. Only need one click in for the day's attendance. Quizzes are very representative of the final.

He is not an amazing lecturer bc he's not too great on explaining things. but he is very clear and funny, I always look forward to his class. he has a great grading scale (can drop all your quizzes but final worth more, can drop 3 hrs, curves to B+,etc) his quizzes can be difficult but his final is about the same difficulty. super fun

He explains very clear on his lectures. He has quizzes every 2 weeks, roughly 12 questions/quiz and he curved the average grade to B and quizzes are not that hard if you actually understand the overall concept. Quizzes and Final score are adjusted so that only grade that help your overall grade will be counted. Taking him again this quarter for 1B.

His quizzes are honestly really really easy. I usually need to study for one to two days for other profs' Physics 1 series classes and do some practice problems; but for his, I just needed to spend 2 hours reviewing the slides and that's it (and I got full points basically for each quiz). Very straightforward and very generous curve.

Prof smith is such a dad character!! Hes a genuinely kind professor and has pretty dry humor that makes lectures entertaining at times. he does his best to make a rather dull subject relatable and I always appreciated that he connected the material to real life applications. Very generous curve, quizzes easier than hw that are directly from slides!

Dougie is such an awesome guy! He is very monotoned but has a sense of humor if you get to know him. The guy is also a genius! Class is difficult and he doesnt lecture well, but is slides are super helpful and he quizzes from his slides. Also curves the class to a B+, so as long as you do better than the average youll get an A. Final is brutal tho

I took him for physics IB and he is great. He curves to a B+ which is rare at UCSD and he tests only from his slides. However he does not know how to drive nor can he park but he does have a nice BMW :)

I don't know why Smith has such a low score. I took the risk of taking his class over Paddock, and he's a great professor in my book! I get how he can sound monotone in some lecture, but really funny in most of them. He makes physics concepts simple. Quizzes are representative of his slides and are quite easy if you review just those slides alone.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you pay close attention in his class, his example is actually worth taking note of. He's pretty clear in explaining

I really enjoyed Doug's class. The material isn't too difficult, but you'll definitely need to study for several hours before his quizzes. His lectures are clear and he gives many example problems that are useful for the quizzes. Doug is a good lecturer with  a touch of sass. He's also retro, using an IBM laptop from the 1990s.

He speaks very clearly. He explains things in a very simple way, and it makes you feel like you are learning the ABCs. He's thorough in lecture, funny, and organized. You won't be confused in lecture. He gives tons of example problems in power points and works them out slowly in class. Tests are fair, you know exactly what will be on the test.
if you do the homework and understand his in-class examples, you'll ace the quizzes and final

Just graduated. Took him for Physics 1A. Got an A+ by realizing that I only needed to study from the packet he wrote - which was much more comprehensible than the lectures were. Never attended class. Did the extra credit and used other resources to study for the quizzes.

Seeing Smith's ratings, I'm led to believe people didn't give him a chance because he comes across as super nerdy. However, I really enjoyed Smith's class! He focuses on big picture ideas over minute details, which is what matters in the long run. Also, he's absolutely hilarious! His saucy humor made made me look forward to class.

I really liked smith! Although he comes intitally off as a boring and monotonous, he's actually pretty funny and sassy. Stick around for his lectures (he hints at possible quiz q's all the time), read the text, and stay on top of things. He curved the class av. to a B+ so it was no prob getting an A.

The major pro to his class is his 17-18 problems quizzes vs. the usual 10 problems quizzes! This allows for more room to make mistakes and still earn a pretty good grade!!! He really made physics clear to me and was concise. Although he can be slow sometimes, he reminds me of your typical nerdy professor. Haha! I definitely recommend him! :)

He's an alright professor. He posts lecture slides, but not until a couple days after the lecture, and it takes a while to get quiz grades back. He's also funny as hell. He did not make us learn computer code like other reviewers have complained about. Final curve to a B+
I enjoyed having Smith, he gave the class a great curve and I found his style of teaching clear and concise. I really understood everything he explained to us, and he is very approachable.

Announced in the first lecture that he doesn't remember much of the subject, and to compensate, he  (massively) inflates the grades. He said he did the exact same for the 1 series. Anyone who received a bad grade truly deserved it. If you treated this class as independent study, you can actually get a lot out of it because of all the freedom.

He is not as bad as everyone says for physics 1c.  He doesn't say everything that is on the quizzes, but the final is a sum of the quizzes, and the textbook explains all of the topics.  Easy grader and teaches from multiple angles. The lectures aren't enough on their own.

People who take PHYS1C and claim "other people who rate him badly are dumb", are dumb. Take a real physics class. This teacher is very helpful and tries hard. Unfortunately, his teaching barely scrapes the surface and doesn't cover the depth that the quizes are at. Self study is the way to go with him.
funny, nice, helpful, easy.

These people who rated Prof Smith so horribly, are dumb. Just go to class, listen, ask for help when you need it, and study for the quizzes. It's UCSD, you have to try a little. I just went to class and listened intently and got an A+, very easy if you are a student willing to learn.
He understands the class is for non science majors and tries to make it as easy as possible. He was also pretty funny with this class. Final was 50% and quizes were 50% but pretty easy.
Dear Prof. Smith, tt's been over a year since taking your class and I can still smell the stench of your horrible teaching. FYL.

Graduated from Stanford. Extremely intelligent man, perfect for RESEARCH! Go back to research and never teach Physics again! Don't ever take this professor, he is the worse professor out of all the physics course, I'd rather jump off the Brooklyn Bridge than take him again
Probably the worst professor ever.  Reads straight out of the reader he wrote himself.  Spent most of the lectures trying to find the mistake he did while copying out of his reader.

Lectures were dry, boring and read straight off of his reader (one that I did not buy). Prof. Smith is a very generous grader

He's not a great teacher but if you didn't pass... wow. He's a great professor. No idea what these peeps are saying. I enjoyed his class and you seriously learn a lot and he gives like 80% As so definitely worth taking. 100% RECOMMEND.

HORRIBLE PROFESSOR! He is honestly the worst teacher I have ever had in my life. His quizzes were ridiculously impossible. You know he needs to fix things when the average is a 2/9. He curves the average to a B, which is very lenient for a physics prof. Some lectures feel like a waste of time.

Prof. Smith is really smart. However, this quality alone is NOT enough to be a good professor. No textbook, only a course reader that in no way resembles the first few chapters of the regular text. BAD IDEA!
take his class he is brilliant
Don't take his class.  This was worst class I have taken my entire life.  I can not emphasize enough, avoid this man.
yeah yeah he can't teach, quizzes are hard, yada yada.  But really:  class average = B+.  That's pretty flippin nice.

this guy was horrible. i took oasis, went to the problem sessions, lecture, and did the extra credit and i still got a C. the test formats are unreasonable, there is no textbook, few practice problems, he's goring, and just a plain awful teacher. you could know how to do every problem and still fail. stay clear!

Don't recommend if this is your first physics class. Although his lectures show the actual derivation of equations through calculus, most of them are completely irrelevant to the quizzes. Easy extra credits to substitute poor quiz grades. Occasional attempts at jokes, most of which fail miserably

This class was a waste of time. Attending lectures was painful as he never taught what we needed to know to pass the quizzes he gave- which were impossibly hard. Scantron but not multiple choice...if you round off just a little you get no credit. :( don't take him unless you're looking for your GPA to drop.

The absolute worst professor I have ever had the displeasure of enduring. DO NOT TAKE HIM AT ANY COST! DO NOT TAKE HIM NO MATTER WHAT! HIS TEACHING IS HORRIBLE! USELESS! HE DOES NOT FULFILL HIS ROLE AS A PROFESSOR! HOPE HE GETS FIRED ASAP!! FFS!

horrible prof. the few times i went to lecture, there were only about 30 students present, really spare for a class of about 300 students. there is no text for this class, its near impossible to learn the concepts from the course reader that he compiled. i should've listened to the reviews i read here DON'T TAKE THIS PROF EVEN IF HE IS THE ONLY ONE

TO Professor: For the future generations of scientists/doctors please do not teach. TO students: stay away from Doug Smith like the swine flu. no lies. I wouldn't want this guy to build my bridges. People will d-i-e.

you'd learn better physics from watching a monkey jumping up and down. he even spent a whole mothereffing lecture about how he's not a physics nerd.  once he even lectured about something and at the very end of class..he said "but u dont need to know this" even the TAs and Lab instructors call doug smith a tard who cant teach for shiit

The worst teacher I have ever had.  I was so excited to write this review so I could vent my anger.  He is not qualified to teach and I didn't learn sh**. what everyone else is saying... its all true... In lecture he even gets stuck on problems he made himself... seriously... and quiz scores take like two weeks to get posted after taking it. The TA was waaaay more helpful than this guy... so don't EVER take him!

This guy is so terrible that he makes me want to shoot myself in the head and has made me lose all hope in humanity. He has shattered the myth that professors are all-knowing(this guy is the complete opposite)/intelligent(dumber than amoeba).

He's simply the worst professor on the planet. His lectures often don't have a direction, and he is constantly compensating for his numerous mistakes and delays IN CLASS by trying to make us feel compassionate for him. Maybe we will once someone competent comes along and kicks him off the job.
Seriously everybody needs to relax. Like him or not he is a human being and the ratings below are making us as students look ridiculous.Finish out the quarter and move on.

Everyone is right, but u just gotta know how he works to pass. Just do HIS (and only his) practice examples that he gives cuz the quizzes are similar. okay. all jokes aside, this professor is horrible. he wrote a USELESS course reader for us instead of giving us a text book.  he doesn't give as practice problems that are relevant to his near impossible quizzes.  he spends ALL of lecture deriving equations instead of actually teaching us HOW TO DO PROBLEMS. WARNING!! DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!! That is, if you can even call this guy a professor...he's a joke that will be hunted down by all the students that were forced to drop his class! If not taking this class means not graduating on time, it's still worth it not to take it!!
Do NOT take this professor. I suggest you wait a quarter for another physics professor. Anyone BUT HIM!

Without a doubt, the worst possible professor in the entire universe. He reads straight from his terrible reader and then quizzes on things that are totally irrelevant. Not to mention his awkward mustache and ridiculously annoying voice. Don't take, or prepare for an F.

Worst Professor I've ever had at UCSD. He should be banned from ever "attempting" to teach students, if you could even call it that. Horrible Professor. who knew you could take a Physics 1A class and have no textbook...Epic Fail doug smith, Epic fail. It is almost like sitting in a lecture hall with NPH as doogie mixed with professor frink, but not awesome at all.

This teacher is such a lair!! He told my friend that he will give a good curve! the avg should be B+/A-!!! but I don't think that is the case! this guy sucked. the worst physics prof. highly recommend taking anderson instead of smith.

worst professor of the PHYS 1 series. you don't learn physics. instead, you cover the material that he thinks is important, all the while skipping randomly in the textbook and screwing you over for the lab. do not take! quizzes are all conceptual. programming is useless. the reviewer below must've been one of the few in the front rows...

Teach whatever he wants, and ending up teaching nothing. No idea how to study for his quizzes because most of it is on conceptual things that he talked about in class that has nothing to do with physics.

He's not that bad. many people who actually know the physics concepts do bad in the lecture and good in lab.  what a total waste

Worst professor I have ever taken at UCSD. I have never before been so disorientated with this professor's method of teaching...if it can even be called that. week 9 and still way behind on grades :(

This teacher is slow in teaching, which is bad for the physics labs because you end up spending much more time teaching yourself the material that the teacher should have already at least touched upon. DO NOT TAKE! sophomores who have to take 1A next year when this guy is teaching... good luck. i'd wait to take it. this guy doesn't teach you physics. he makes us do useless MATLAB computer programming stuff that is completely irrelevant. worst class i've ever taken at UCSD! he'd rather show off about himself than teach you anything.. Wait out physics until next quarter when a worthier professor comes around.even the people running the physics lab don't like how he's teaching.5 weeks into the course,  still on the second chapter.This makes lab harder because we have to learn the material on our own.How is making physics into a computer programming class useful to bio students?

In trying to make physics more relevant for bio majors, he turned the class into a MATLAB/Octave programming class. Horribly boring, unless you are into that stuff. Quizzes are fairly easy, but would not recommend since he has definitely changed the course from previous quarters.

quizzes are tricky and he expects you to know things intuitively.  he is also so boring and goes over the same program for almost a week.  he is completely useless. don't take him if you are good at physics because that will mean nothing in his programming class.  all he does is trick you with calc/computer program questions.

class time is spent 90% on computer programming and the class hardly resembles an actual physics course.  he doesn't even teach the concepts in the books but talks about tumors and ultrasound.  The physics part of the class has turned into just a few side comments.  This is a complete and utter waste of time.  At least Basov stuck to the material.

The guy hates teaching. That's why he gives a quiz every Friday...so he can reduce the number of lectures. LOVED THIS CLASS!  Ok, I hated it at first, but once I actually started STUDYING, I started enjoying it. Great professor to take if you want an easy physics class ,but don't count on learning anything, cause you won't. But he gives extra credit up to 20%...yup you read it right, 20%! So this is basically an easy class to take, but if you need to learn something...take the other professor.

He was an awesome teacher. he made physics 1c a very interesting class and he explains things quite well. he doesn't trick you like other professors on the tests/quizzes. Best physics teacher ive had in the whole 1 series

This guy is just something else.  He has a really nerdy and annoying voice that can drone on, but he is the best physics professor ive ever had. Prof. Smith is a very nice guy who cares about his students and makes physics fun and easy. Of the entire physics series, I enjoyed this class the most. Take him if you can!

I love this man. Haha. All kidding aside; I HATE physics (just like all the ppl who commented already), but-- with Prof. Smith, I actually WANT to be at lecture, and he manages to make it interesting!!! O__O
Hes funny and his lecutures were clear and helpful.

He is the best Physics professor ever!  I hate physics on got a B+ and C+ the last two quarters, but with him, I got my only UCSD A+!  He's funny, makes physics entertaining, and pokes fun of student learning...plus gives out extra credit, the best thing about the class.  Take him if you have to take any physics!

I HATE HATE HATE physics! But Prof. Smith was the best physics professor I had at UCSD. He's funny and knows his stuff. His powerpoint presentation goes way too fast to take notes, but he posts them on his site.
Just go to class... so much extra credit is awarded through class attendance. Also extra credit questions on the quizes
He actually made the class fun. His sense of humor goes a long way witht the predictably boring topic. great way to end the series
He's a great professor. He tries hard to make class interesting and cracks jokes a lot. He also gives tons of extra credit for the transmitter and extra questions on the quizes.

Best physics prof you'll ever have. Tries his best to entertain us during lecture and get us to care about physics, easy to get good grade w/ simple tests and extra credit...you really cant ask for more

Prof. Smith is by far my favorite physics teacher yet. Lecture is pretty interesting and the transmitters are fun. This is the first physics class that I've actually found that going to lecture actually helps. He travels a decent pace and stuff he goes over in lecture has relevance to his quizes.

He's great, makes everything clear and concise. Definitely the best physics teacher I've had at UCSD. He's also got quite the sense of humor and he kinda reminds me of Napolean's brother from Napolean dynamite.

reviews.comment: Nitz is a great professor. I learned more about Learning and Memory in 1 Nitz lecture than I did from literally all of 101b. reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very knowledgable teacher, although the class feels like a combination of the 101 and 107 series (familiar repetition). Entire grade is on three tests. reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Nitz is a rather solid professor. Lectures on material like neuroanatomy and physiology can tend to be really boring but somehow he makes it still bearable to hear with his odd jokes sprinkled in between. The whole grade is based on three exams, which makes each one rather important but he provides a lot of resources to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: good prof, cares about student understanding. If he writes it on the board its not on the slides and it is on the test, so pay close attention to those and copy his board work down! lots of EC in tests, grade is based on 3 tests (including final) all weighted equally and a mix of multiple choice and fill in the blank, no free response. Solid prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Nitz is a very down to earth, hilarious and brilliant teacher.  This class is purely driven by research papers on a very complex subject but he explains them very well in class and has helpful slides.  The entire grade is on 2 tests (about 10 questions total), but he gives the questions out a week before. There's no excuse not to do well!

You will be graded by your test performance in his class and his tests are heavy on memorization of brain systems. Dont be surprised in his class since his class is specifically teaching those intricate systems. Yes, his tests are hard but if you are diligent and do your reading, go to class, engage with your note taking you will pass with a B-A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This is an 8am class, and he won't record video postcast (just audio), which is a HUGE minus. Average for 1st midterm is a C- , and he won't curve, his slide look really sloppy, some of the slide is just a picture like really?. He did not emphasize enough what he's going to be testing on exams. Would NOT take again!

Nitz is a fantastic person and professor. Extremely complex subject matter but not a particularly difficult class if you know how to study properly. Exams have tons of bonus points - just take detailed notes on podcasts for every lecture. I finished with over 100% in the class and never actually attended.

Class is somewhat an overview of some info from COGS 107A and 101A.  Two midterms, one final with a few bonus points (which he points out will be bonus questions in lecture).  You don't have to attend class, but it's beneficial to do so.  Take good notes and review slides and you will do well.  Sections help too so go to them!!

very nice and funny prof, wants his students to do well. 2 MTs and final, all non-cumulative and have lots of bonus questions. great TAs. I did well by going to lecture and re-watching the podcasts. you can almost guess what will be tested on based on how its presented in lecture. easy to do well if you write down everything he says!

Nitz is AMAZING! Take this class if you can. You will have NO regrets. If you go to class, listen, and study a decent amount-- you're guaranteed an A. Nitz cares about his students, and is passionate about what he teaches. Plus he has an amazing personality, and is a very attractive grntleman.

Nitz is great! One of my favorite profs in the cogsci department. Really enjoyed this class. There's a lot of material but he kept it interesting and overall the class wasn't too difficult. Plus he's pretty foxy imo :)

he is a great professor. He's pretty clear, funny, and really cares about his students learning the material. His research also is super interesting. Overall, he's a great professor, teaches interesting material, and he's very easy on the eyes.

Class material was interesting, he can be  dull at times, comes off as a complete introvert. He was sort of adorable when he would joke around or share stories; overall not bad. 3 exams, can be a bit tricky; hoping for a curve; asks you random bonus questions.

Nitzy is a great professor. He's straight forward with the material and is clear and concise in explaining. His exams are kinda hard, but he offers bonus points and usually curves. He's a pretty nice person, too. Don't mess with him or interrupt his class though, he doesn't take any BS.

I LOVE Prof. Nitz. He's a chill dude. One easy way to get As on all of his tests are to go to class, write (or type like I did) down everything he says! I relistened to podcasts and typed down more things he said. Honestly, if you do that, and just memorize it all, you will def get an A. If you aren't good at memorizing then this class will be hard

Great professor. His exams are all based off what he says so don't think you can get away with just reading the slides. I got an A by listening in class and reviewing the podcasts. Very clear professor. He's pretty funny too
Need to listen closely to his lectures to understand the material. Material can be difficult but tests are very fair and offer many bonus questions. Don't expect a curve.

Two midterms and a final, each 33.3%. The tests are MC, T/F and a fair amount of fill-in-the-blank. There were screen casts most of the time and podcasts all the time. He's a good lecturer, one of the more organized professors I've had. I found his class pretty hard but the material is interesting enough.

Nitz is a godsend to the CogSci Department. More of them should take notes from his style. His classes were all very interesting and I learned quite a lot. He kept me interested and wanting to go home and learn more. Finally a professor that teaches from papers and shows you the real data then explains it. Its how science is done.

Super clear, open to questions and discussion, tests were reflective of the material, did not try to trick you, no quizzes. Two midterms and one final. Only con: He likes to teach early classes ): But he podcasts and all his slides are online so you're free to sleep in on most days!
LOVED this professor. He's awesome, very clear lecturer. Test are fair but a bit tough. Learned a lot from him. His mannerisms are adorable. He should teach more courses.

Offers plenty of extra credit, and tests are fair: they cover just the material that he puts on his slides. Read the book if you want background, otherwise just listen to the podcasts while going over the posted notes.

Lecture slides always contain all you need to know for the exams. No quizzes or required reading (REALLY you don't have to read, I learned the hard way that the "suggested" reading is just a waste of time). It's hard to attend 8am lecture, people just podcast. Overall the concepts are interesting, especially if you like neuroscience :)
prof nitz was really good, he's new but has quite a bit of experience. he's really interesting and so is the subject so lectures aren't boring at all. he has a cute dog too.

I really like his class. It's much better than my COGS 101B class...AHEM, Creel=hell. The material is interesting, Prof. Nitz explains all of his slides, all of the TAs are extremely helpful and his tests are VERY fair. I wish he taught more courses. :(

He's really fair. His test is extremely easy if you go to lectures (which are podcasted...highly recommended) and review your notes. Two mt and a final...not cummulative. I took this class before and failed. Second time around, I love it! I'm actually learning and not just memorizing to try and pass the class. His teaching has truly improved!

Pretty cool professor, the class itself is based on guest lecturers, so he didn't do a lot, but when he did lecture it was reasonably straightforward and easy to understand. Since there is no unified theme to the class, he was limited what he could ask on tests, meaning they were the easiest tests ever. Great way to see if you like cog sci.
Try to get Kaya as your TA

I love this prof!! His lectures at time where a little hard to follow but I think it's because he is really passionate about his field and wanted us to know as much as we could. Also it was his first quarter teaching and so I think gradually the kinks will work themselves out! DEFINITELY RECOMMEND HIM...HE'S A HOTTY TOO!!

Nice guy, but just not that experienced. Can be extremely dry and difficult to understand... His slides were mostly just graphs and pictures of experiments, making it difficult to take notes on. The quizzes were pretty hard, there aren't any sort of study guides or anything. He'll probably get better though, this was his first class taught at UCSD.

He does not know how to make the class fair!  He gives quizzes according to section days so if you have an early section you get to take the quiz early and everyone then passes on the information to the later sections.  But yet believes there is NO problem with this because has "taken appropriate measures".  He also has selective feedback hearing!

Loved her class; she seemed to really care for her students as she created a rapport. Attendance is mandatory yet flexible. Assignments were well thought out, complex and not stressful. I really recommend taking Profe Dominguez's classes

Professor Dominguez genuinely cares about her students. Her class was really easy but still worthwhile. Enjoyed talking to her, definitely get the sense that she is fun and kind, it truly matters to her that we do well.

If you have to take this spanish course, take this professor ! One of the best i've had at UCSD she is super caring and funny. She won't judge if you can't say certain words in spanish she allows you to say them in english. Assignments are super easy and quick.

I loveeeeee professor Dominguez. She's so kind, so understanding. She does have weekly writing assignments and some projects, but they're easy. She doesn't judge you regardless if your Spanish is bad. (lol) She's also very inclusive. 
Easy class, love the professor.

Prof Dominguez really cares about her students and gives plenty opportunities to practice Spanish. Participation and attendance are mandatory, but she cancels Friday classes. Half of the classes are w the TA (covers grammar), the other half with the Prof (goes over textbook). The weekly movie assignments were fun! No tests, just a final project.

This class was interesting, but I didn't love how it was split between two profs. The lectures were really interesting, but the tests blindsided me. We don't get any practice tests so I honestly went into it not knowing what to expect, and it focused way too much on species. Other than that, i enjoyed the discussion sections and Dovi is very kind

Great professor! Graded on discussion participation, weekly quizzes, a term paper, & a final exam. Lectures were podcasted. Discussion required a pre-posted question and speaking during the section for credit. The term paper on marine mammals included multiple assignments with feedback. Final exam was in-person, closed-note (mainly short answer)

Great lectures, cool shirts, reasonable grading, a little inaccessible for contact outside of class but he seems to have a lot going on back and forth between SIO campus and main campus classes? Overall would absolutely recommend bc the class was still great and well instructed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: amazing, chill prof. one of the best I have had so far, really cares about students. doesn't give too many assignments and the ones he does give is just to make sure you are getting and understanding material. tests were on material learned in class it was more just applying the info. 1000% would recommend and take again.

Unfortunately Dovi is completed inaccessible. He will not respond to emails, an issue that I discussed with many many other students who experienced the same. Setting up a meeting (since he has no designated office hours) was impossible-he did not respond for weeks. Students reach out for help and he isnt there, it makes it difficult to praise him.

Amazing professor! Explains things very well and is extremely accommodating to students. Lectures are not mandatory but are extremely helpful. Tests are all FR, so he focuses more on applications over just definitions.
