Lectures were confusing and hard to follow. Some concepts weren't explained well, included unnecessary info, and overall disorganized. But grading is very lenient. Gave HUGE curves for tests, and extra credit for attendance. Tests were also similar to discussion questions. Okay if you already know some genetics, don't recommend if new to it.

Grade based on two midterms (one can be dropped) and a final. Not too hard if you study, and has a generous curve. Discussion and lecture attendance isn't mandatory, and neither are weekly practice problems. Gives good idea of concepts on exams, and practice problems are helpful. Overall nice professor, and willing to help.

This might've been the hardest class I've taken. The lectures were a bit hard to understand and sometimes gives unnecessary information that doesn't help us prep for the midterm and tests. Grade is test-based, but gives us a generous curve. The hw assignments are optional but the exams are much more harder than the hw.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: final grade is only on 2 midterms and 1 final (u can drop a midterm). very generous curve (220/300 is an A on the midterms), but with that you dont rlly know ur grade until he puts it into acad. history. lectures were boring but got the content across; he says some random things but they become EC on the final. hw and disc optional.

Lectures are interesting and straightforward. Practice sets provided but they vaguely represent the midterms. The midterms are about 2x harder then the provided practices. On both midterms I got 200/300 which turned out to be an A. Difficult tests, generous curve. Grading solely based off two midterms and a final.

I just took him this Winter quarter, and I barely learned a single thing, lectures are random and all over the place. Exams are not representative of what we learn in class didn't know my grade because he applies a "curve" at the end. The final was on very specific details mentioned in class. Better to read outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is difficult, but Prof Pun provides you with all the resources you need to succeed. He only uses the chalkboard during lecture, which really helps with learning why each step of a mechanism happens. Exams are reflective of problem sets and lecture examples. I was nervous going into this class, but genuinely found it to be kinda fun.

difficult class but you can succeed if you really put the work in. i got a 70% on the first exam but got 100% on the second and clutched up the final and got an A in the class. good lectures, he chalks and explains each step, often giving us time to do the problems ourself before tackling it on the board. good at explaining concepts.

Exams were multiple choice which is kinda strange for an ochem class. Because of this i've tanked points for small errors, but averages were 70 on both midterms. No curve since averages were high. He does a good job explaining things, but building intuition for mechanisms is challenging regardless. Spam practice problems and ur probably fine

The lectures for this class were super interesting and really relevant to the problem sets and exams. My only complaint is that the multiple choice made averages higher than they should've been which probably ruined the curve.

I mighta just had a bad experience with him. Whenever he answered my questions, I feel like he answered very condescendingly. Office hours was way too cramped to get anything helpful outta it. Having only MCQ exams and homework answers spoonfed to us by TAs didn't make for the best teaching strat imo.

It's definitely a difficult class, but his notes and teaching styles do make it somewhat easier to comprehend. CHEM40B is a difficult class for anyone, but he is a good professor and does teach very passionately. Way easier than 40A for me.

I don't know why professor Pun's rating was low but he's lowkey sleeper chalkboard professor build. Tests are multiple choice and tells you no memorization needed, you just have to be able to figure out what to do next. Grading is like the usual for all ochem classes. I don't think he curved this quarter, averages too high.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Actually goated. I loved the way he taught the class. He made ochem enjoyable and I loved learning it! I did avg (70%s) on the midterms but lowkey popped off on the final and got an A-. Idk if he curved but I'm assuming he did, although the curve wouldn't be much because all his tests were mc. His tests were a fair representation of the content.

Prof Pun is AMAZING! He uses the chalkboard exclusively, but for a class like 40B where all the content is basically mechanisms, it's super helpful to see his reasoning and follow along with him. His pace during lecture is perfect, he explains questions really well, and exams and problem sets are super fair. Can't recommend enough!
boring class and ineffective.

(Taken Winter 2025) Dr. Pun is kind and knowledgeable about the subject. Organic chemistry is DIFFICULT no matter the professor, so can't blame him for the tough material. He writes on the whiteboard which helps with speed. Only thing is sometimes he assumes students know more than they do. Fair curve for exams. Homework helps. MEMORIZATION BASED.

I think the people complaining about Andrew are people who just struggled because ochem is difficult in its nature. Andrew uses the chalkboard and draws out each mechanism so you know what is happening in each step. I hated ochem until his class. I learned so much, and I finally feel like chem, in general, makes sense to me. Also, fat curve in end.

He only chalks so the class may seem intimidating at first but eventually the content builds on itself and it all starts making sense. The first midterm scores were very low but improved by the time we got to the final. Classes aren't mandatory but go, and midterms/final do matter. I still got an A though despite failing Midterm 1. You learn a ton!

Professor Pun was very funny, nice, and wants to see his students succeed. However, this class was very hard. He gave practice exams and problem sets which were pretty similar to the exams, its just challenging in general. I personally did well in Ochem 1 and still really struggled in his class. not sure who to blame, professor or material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The prof is not a bad lecturer, but he doesn't show his work on the practice tests, and sometimes skips over the mechanisms for problems. The tests did represent his lectures/homework, and you're only graded on the weekly homework (get answers through discussions), the two midterms, and final. He does curve, and he writes on the chalkboard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I like how he uses the whiteboard since it shows everyone a slower process step by step and I appreciated that. Overall a good teacher, he wants to see his students improve. Tests were representative of what he lectured, as well as discussion section hw, and the lecture slides he provides.

horrible professor. Every midterm has been super hard and he cant teach. 
Fails to explain concepts while lecturing, just blows right through a question and leaves everyone in lecture confused. 
Stopped attending lectures and started studying on my own. No homework. Graded on the weekly discussion worksheets + 2 Midterms + Final. 
AVOID AT ALL COST

Prof.Pun explained everything very clearly. And his teaching style with chalk really helped with controling the pace of the class so you can have enough time to take notes. His exams were pretty resonable (one or two questions can be tricky) and he curved the final grade. Man! What can I say? Take him!

Amazing professor. Ochem is a hard subject but Prof Pun made it much more bearable. The way he taught content was much more digestible than other professors and the textbook as he focused on the fundamental concepts. Midterms and finals are heavily based on problems done in lectures and problem sets. He genuinely cares about his students as well.

Really nice and caring professor, I appreciated his teaching style and pace of lecture. Does not provide practice exams, but exams are heavily based on problem set and lecture material (so make sure to study those). He is also very accessible after class and is super helpful if you ask him questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures felt way too simple in the way that he didn't explain things enough and kind of assumed we would fit together the pieces. Tests had little to no partial credit and the grading scale is very unforgiving. Would recommend other profs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ochem is hard regardless, even attending lectures I was so confused I feel as though he is too smart to be able to dumb it down more. I personally did good in ochem I and was not expecting to feel so lost and behind in ochem II. The format of exams does not allow for partial credit since only the answer is graded, which makes it very difficult too!

By far one of my favorite professors at UCSD. He cares about his student's success. I always went to his office hour for help. Ochem is hard but Professor Pun makes it way easier compared to the other Professors. All you need is to practice as much as possible and you should be good.

His tests match his lectures, ppl who say otherwise don't go to lecture and/or don't pay attention. Some worksheets aren't helpful bc they're made by other profs, but if you go to discussion, you can get it done quickly. Ochem is always gonna be hard, but if you genuinely try in his class, you will succeed. This is man made me enjoy ochem.
Very entertaining lectures, makes chemistry understandable and easy, dependent on test grades although, chemistry hard subject overall but Stallings certainly made it slightly easier.

I took Chem 11 with Prof Stallings for a GE requirement, and he was great! I went to his office hours often because chemistry is really hard for me. He has a great sense of humor and wants his students to succeed.

He's a great lecturer for sure, and I learned a lot. However I was met with a passive aggressive and almost belittling attitude when I actually interacted with him personally, which you would never expect. Class is decent and straightforward for such a difficult topic though.

Good lecturer and tests are easy if you study for them. All multiple choice w/ cheat sheet. 8 am sucks but he has recording so u can sleep in if u don't feel like 8am. Just go to lecture during reviews before midterms/finals since he doesn't upload those recordings. overall great class
All of the tests are multiple choice and lectures are option but well taught and organized.

He is not the best lecturer but definitely thinks he is. His grading is pretty generous, and the class is curved. I got a D on both midterms and failed the final and still got a B-. I only had to take one chem class so I didn't try. If you but any effort at all you'll be fine. It's an intro class so he really isn't trying to fail anyone.
Great professor honestly. Very hard to get into his or Schurmeier's class though unless good enrollment times and first passing it. Lots of chances for extra credit that basically carry your grade.

Great in the sense that he's easy to talk to but lectures and hw didn't really reflect the difficulty of the exams. Sometimes he will go off topic during to keep students engaged. I liked the way he graded as exams did not make up most of one's grade. He allows cheat sheets and had a grade improvement plan. Hated how Achieve was required and $$.

Great energy and funny stories but sometimes too many stories for my learning style. With longer lectures, he would try to implement stories to keep us from burning out mid-class, but I felt like they were a bit time-wasteful ultimately. Sometimes it felt a little unclear when trying to get content answers from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: goated. Great lecturer, funny, his voice is easy to fall asleep to tho. All assignments and midterms are extremely low risk, 200/300 collective points is 100% for hw quizzes discussion attendance etc and u can replace midterm scores. Never taken a chemistry class before and I was crashing out, but it was because I was behind the whole time.

His lectures are engaging and he cares about making sure the class understands the content well. The only issue imo was that throughout the quarter there were a few times he assigned extra video lectures covering entire classes worth of content he didn't have time to cover, which was a lot of work out of class.

He really cares for his students and teaches from the basics so don't worry if you've never taken chem! The material is somewhat difficult to understand sometimes but the si for the course are really good. The  environment of the class was really good so don't be afraid to ask questions. He sometimes gives bonus points for them!

I thought that Professor Stallings' lectures were quite fun and engaging. He always makes it point to clarify all old topics before transitioning to new ones and gives lots of opportunities to ask questions. Beyond that he is also very caring and sweet outside of the classroom as well.

Professor Stallings in my opinion was one of the best professors for Chemistry. He helps break down tougher concepts in chemistry into more digestible portions. One thing I liked about his style but some people might not like is he occasionally goes off topic into a story, but personally it helps break up the monotony of class.

His lectures were a bit fast and unclear for me personally, BUT his grading is the best to me. Also, unfortunately, you need an iPad for his class. He gives skeletal notes, and you're gonna need to fill those out in class and add what he talks about to know what is happening. I'm also not a fan of the constant AI promoting.

He's a great prof who's consistently funny during lectures and I had an easy time understanding the content he was teaching. Homework and quizzes aren't incredibly demanding and exams were difficult but not impossible

Love Stallings!! Lectures were engaging, and he takes the time to clarify anything you ask. Weekly quizzes are low stakes because you can earn those points in other ways. The midterms (2) and final are well-aligned with the quizzes and discussion worksheets, and he allows a cheat sheet. I struggle with chem, but I enjoyed his class!

I love stallings, if you can take him. You won't regret it. His tests are pretty straightforward and easy. It's easy to get an A or B in this class. And he allows cheat sheets on the midterms and FINAL which is a godsend imo. Thank you stallings for being the goat, can't wait to take him next quarter.

Very low stakes weekly homework+quizzes. Midterms are straightforward, and he allows a crib sheet for every midterm. The final (3 crib sheets) was more difficult than either of the midterms, but I highly recommend taking his class. My only complaint is that he provides skeletal notes and sometimes talks way more than what the slides show.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: not a great professor. makes many mistakes during lecture and his tests are nothing like what he says they'll be like

The book wasn't very helpful for this class. Do all of the weekly assigned quizzes, those are most likely to come up on the exams. There are two midterm exams and the first two sections have a replacement option on the final. Lectures are recorded. Overall, Stallings is a great professor!
He was so so nice but lectures didn't make much sense cause of speed however i loved him as a professor and he was an amazing person and professor if he went slower

Make a really good cheat sheet and take notes on all of the lectures and you'll do okay in the class. I think also it would have helped if I had done more supplemental learning on my own, but overall I did fine in the class. You can watch all the lectures online, but don't procrastinate and let them pile up like I did. Minimal homework, no quizzes.

Stallings makes everything easy and digestible to learn. He allows cheat sheets on the 2 midterms and 3 cheat sheets the final. Low stakes tests bc his grading policy replaces the midterm for both grade on the final. Extra credit on final. I never get bored with this guy, so much stories to tell. As always don't let the bears get you :)

Prof. Stallings is an amazing professor for Chem 6A. His lectures are very entertaining and digestible, and he doesn't assume any prior knowledge for this class. Grading is based off of two midterms, a final, and "bucket points" (a combination of homework, discussions, etc) that are very attainable. One cheat sheet for midterms and three for final.

Just study and you'll be good. He makes lectures pretty fun with his humor so it's not too boring. Tests are pretty hard tho, it's very comphrehensive so just be aware that most of the test is based on conceptual stuff.

Hilarious, super nice guy. Multiple choice, grade replacement system, definitely take him! In general, chem is hard but seriously he's a great teacher who makes hard topics easy and is all around just a delight. Love him and I will probably get an A. I will be taking him hopefully in the future!

Professor stallings is genuinely an amazing teacher, the class is relatively chill and goes at an easy pace. My one warning is the tests can sometimes be harder than the homework so you have to make sure you really understand the material, but otherwise definitely worth how early the class is!
He's a great lecturer and seems very approachable, but to get a good grade in his class, you need to study A LOT.

Great for GenChem. Took AP Chem in high school, so mostly review for me. Doesn't explain some concepts too well for someone learning for the first time, but gives good answers when you ask questions. Funny and engaging. Structure of class is great: weekly quizzes are practice for tests, and you can replace midterm grades if you do better on final.

He's great at explaining the main ideas and makes lectures fun with his tangents. He's really encouraging and lets you use a cheat sheet for CHEM 6A, but you still need to study. Do the quizzes and discussion worksheets—the midterms are most like the discussion worksheets.
Good explanations and lectures but the tests and quizzes often were faulty and had some mistakes. Pretty decent for an online class though. He's very nice and approachable!

Chemistry is a tough subject, but Stallings did a great job at explaining concepts and working through problems in lectures. He gives you so many resources, cheat sheets on exams, and the quiz problems will show up on the tests. Yes this class is very difficult but if you put in the work and utilize the resources, you will succeed.

He's really good at explaining the concepts. I understand some people will rate low but that's because chemistry is a hard subject. Don't expect a professor to just gift you an A. He provides so many resources as the exams are identical to the quizzes and discussions problems. If you took AP Chem like me but got a 3, this class is a breeze.

Stallings is a nice prof and is really kind but he is very difficult to get a good grade with. To get an A you have to sacrifice all your free time to studying his class. He tends to say that things wont be on exams but then puts them there anyway. Tough prof to read but if you REALLY give everything you got you can get a good grade. Go to TA OH.

He was chill, but I didn't like his lectures. He'd say topics wouldn't be on the exam when they were, and sometimes included material he never covered. He occasionally did problems wrong on the spot, contradicting past methods. The class was fair and easier than others, but he wasn't my favorite professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Stallings's a good person. He's funny and nice to students. Though he definitely needs some improvement. He flies through important slides and likes to add his own explanations - which did not work for me at all. Also he kept saying things weren't going to be on the exam and yes they were. Homework points are easy, exams can be tricky

Very personable and funny guy but his lectures are not it. He says stuff won't be on the exams but then they are in fact on the exams. Exams are all multiple choice, not super bad and you do get a crib sheet. He mostly just talks through the lecture and gets sidetracked easily…He knows what he's talking about but it doesn't come across sometimes.

Stallings is amazing. He's so funny and just a sweet guy. The class content was decently hard but he's really caring and open to questions and genuinely wants us to do well in the class. The exams were fair imo and he allowed a cheat sheet for them. He curves your total grade at the end.

Honestly, if there were one thing I could do differently, I would go back and attend every lecture, even if it was at 8 am, because as long as you keep up with regular lecture attendance and do not chatGPT every homework, you will do very well. He is very respected in the chemistry department; overall, a fantastic dude. Watch out for bears!

I didn't take chemistry in high school so this class was difficult for me. So if you're like me, set aside at least 6 hours a week extra to read textbook or watch Youtube videos to help. He was generally okay at explaining things in lecture, but sometimes sped through the last slides because time was running out. Exams were fair though.

Great professor, really cares about his students. Extremely clear expectations and tries to make lectures more interesting, very approachable and willing to help. Loves questions and is great at explaining multiple ways. Although doesn't budge on policies as there are many opportunities in the class.

Unfortunately, my grade dropped significantly due to a printing error, and we had to take the final online. I do horrendously on online exams, so it messed up my grade when I had As on the midterms before. Other than that, he makes the hardest class in the series manageable. GO TO lecture and complete your work, you will be well-prepared.

I've had Stallings for 6b and 6c, 6c is the easiest in the chem sequence, and Stallings teaches very well. Slides/notes are very cohesive and easy to understand, and the homework platform is nice. He keeps lectures engaging by sometimes giving us a brain break to talk about something irrelevant or real-world applications. Overall great dude.

VERY GOOD PROFESSOR!
For midterms, you get one cheat sheet. For the final you get 3.
Chem is easy, this professor makes it easier. Teaching really well and understandable.

LITERALLY THE MOST AMAZING CHEMISTRY PROFESSOR EVER. hands down. I wish he taught all of the chem classes, some of the other lectures *cough inorganic chemistry* need to take notes on his teaching style. LOVE LOVE LOVE

Wonderful lecturer who explains concepts well! I understood a lot more about chemistry by listening to his lectures, as he cares a lot about helping students understand the 'why' and 'how' of chemistry. Tests, if you studied, were easy to get an "A" on, as he provided lots of study material. If you take Chem 6B, I can't recommend Stallings enough!

Unfortunately the much harder messed up final this quarter cost me an A which I would have gotten, but otherwise it was a great class. His lectures are super clear and both midterms were some of the best I've had with being reflective of content. Homework and quizzes are pretty light and discussions are mandatory but easy. I'd probably take again.

Excellent and engaging professor. The way he explains concepts is incredibly clear. Homework is short and easy. He also gives weekly quiz questions that are guaranteed to show up on exams, which helps us study. However, he is a bit unorganized since he printed out the wrong exam for the final and ended up giving a much harder online final exam.

Yes, the concerns regarding the final are true. The final was challenging- a lot more than the midterms. Don't let that discourage you. What happened was stupid, but his paper exams (normal ones) are extremely fair and honestly pretty easy if you study and do the homework. Please pay attention to the lecture; it will show up on the exam. Goated guy

He is a nice person but ok as a professor. He sped through his slides and I had to take pics of every slide to take notes. He goes too in-depth on easier topics and glosses over more challenging topics. I felt it was unfair to make the online final harder since he mistakenly printed the wrong exam. The online final screwed over my grade.

I initially liked Stallings, but for finals, they made a mistake by printing the wrong test and decided to make it harder and with only free-response questions. I relied on the grade improvement, expecting similar difficulty, so their approach felt inconsiderate and not in the student's best interest, especially those that are struggling.

Amazing person, but an ok prof. Everyone hypes him up but I don't get it. Very disorganized and expects us to be able to take notes on a slide he spends 30 secs on. His exams focus on very conceptual and abstract topics which means you have to know everything about everything. I studied 15 hrs at min before each exam to finish with an A.

I took his class almost a year ago and he is an amazing professor. I asked him for help about choosing my class because I thought I was ready to take many upper division classes all at once and he advised me to not put certain classes with each other and honestly now that I finished with those classes I am glad that he took the time to talk to me.

Stallings is impressive, both in and outside the class. He understands your struggle and will do anything to help you feel comfortable and ace the class. Chem is not my favorite but Professor Stalling made it fun and interesting. You have to grind hard to help you. WATCH OUT FOR BEARS!!

Love him as a person, but as a prof he is ok. Very disorganized and speeds through slides. He records lectures but privated them on podcasts, and instead manually uploads them to canvas. He sometimes wouldn't post the lecture until after the next lecture. He decided to give us a very hard online final bc he printed the wrong final on exam day.

you can tell that professor stallings genuinely cares about his students and wants them to do good in the class. he tries to make the lectures more entertaining by going on side tracks on unrelated topics to chem. there's mixed opinions on him doing this but i personally like it a lot.

Genuinely, he's such a down-to-earth professor who makes lectures so engaging and fun to go to. Explains concepts well and the material he presents through his quizzes, homework, and the discussions are very similar to exams. Love this dude so much, he's hilarious LOL

If you have the chance to take this professor, do it. His grading system is niche, teaches very efficiently during lectures, and his vibe is overall very heartwarming. In the hardest midterm of the general chem series (according to him), 300+ out of around 480 got an A or a B. Overall amazing and if anyone said otherwise they probs just hate chem.

Bro is the GOAT. You'll love him. The people who left bad ratings are trippen. Only minor issue he skips through the slides fast sometimes so you have to rewatch the lecture. But overall, HE IS THE GOAT

Professor Stallings is the sole reason I like chemistry. He is caring and attentive plus his slides are super organized and really help note taking. If I could give one suggestion is to enroll in his class on the first pass because it runs out really fast. Also, attend office hours and ask ALL your questions! Hope you guys love him as much as I did
Take his class, very easy to get through. Slides are easy to follow, tests are all multiple choice.

Super awesome guy, definitely can get an A if you do the work and try...clearly I did not put in the work but I definitely think I could have done far better if I made a better attempt. Genuinely one of my favorite professors so far, the class not so much. Highly recommend, chem sucks.

Professor Stallings brings an engaging teaching style to CHEM6A. His lectures are informative, and he genuinely wants students to succeed. unstuck ai was a helpful tool for preparing for exams alongside the practice problems.

Did better than average on the midterms, but did horrible on the finals. Stallings made lectures enjoyable, and he went through the material at a reasonable pace. But I will say that the finals consisted of problems we barely touched or seen before, so keep that in mind.

The lectures are held at a moderate pace that isn't difficult to keep up with and can be reviewed online after. The grading consists of both participation and exam scores so don't forget to keep track of participation points. The scores on the midterms can also be replaced by better results on the final so major setbacks can be fixed at the end.

One of the best chemistry profs I've ever had. His lectures are fun and slowly paced. Everything is very standardized – he works with Schurmeier and Leigh and exams are very straightforward (MC). You should fully understand concepts but that's given. Wonderful professor and (probably) your best shot at getting an A (and understanding chemistry too)

Prof. Stallings is a laid back professor who is passionate about what he teaches. The actual class wasn't too challenging, and you don't cover a lot of different chemistry topics in this class. However, each topic is very in depth so Prof. Stallings expects you to have a conceptual understanding. The final is 1-2 levels harder than the midterms.

Honestly one of the best chem teachers out their for UCSD. Really chill, humble, and respectable guy. His lectures are pretty good on the content but will make jokes to gain attention from the students. 2 midterms and a final which come off from the lecture slides and the discussion practices. Recommend to take him for Chem 6 series. Overall great!

Awesome professor! Attendance for the lecture was not mandatory but was for discussion. Really cool guy. He is the best chem professor I could have ever asked for. Best option Choose Him!!! He was so kind, he would send me emails after every midterm I did good on and hype me up and it made me feel great. His midterms reflected what he taught well.

Super clear, tests are straightforward, homework (Edfinity) is very forgiving. Midterms and finals are all MCQs with cheat sheets allowed. A genuinely funny teacher who does care for his students! Quite hard to find outisde of class, but always hangs around at the end to answer any questions. Wants his students to succeed. Watch out for bears!

Content is easier than 6B, but I found it was a lot easier to make little mistakes that would lead to wrong answers. I made so many stupid errors on exam questions and felt that I knew the material well and deserved better results. Ended up clutching the final to get an A. You'll do fine if you practice the same problems over and over days before

Professor Stallings is a really good educator. He brings passion, positivity, and a smile to class every single day. He wants his students to succeed and exemplifies this by doing his best to make his students happy. And yet still some students expect greater handouts. Chemistry is hard for most. Stay accountable, put in work, and don't be a victim

I honestly never really struggled w/ chem. I had taken o chem before this class so I do see why others found this class difficult and timing to be hard on exams. You need to know conceptually what the problems are about and mathematically it will just make things easier do not just memorize this will help you in this class but also in the long run.

Overall, good chem 6c professor, however sometimes for midterms the amount of problems given were too much in the short amount of time to do them, leading to low class average. Goes off topic a lot throughout lectures, not learning the necessary material. Tests are all MCQ, no frq.

Has a fun attitude and gives breaks in class to talk about fun things (i.e. kendrick drake beef), clear outlined class. Sometimes goes a little slow, but that may help some people focus better! Happy to explain concepts over again and understanding.

Honestly Professor Stallings does everything he can to help his students pass by giving a lot of opportunities and extended office hours. As long as you show up to class and engage with the discussion sessions it should be fine.
This man wants his students to succeed. He is the most caring and supportive professor I have ever had. If you have to take any chem class. He is the one to take. 100%

Amazing professor, I recommend to take every general chemistry course with him. This class is super easy to get left behind, but do not procrastinate! 6B is more lecture heavy than 6A and there's a lot more work that needs to be done to ensure that you're prepared for exams. He has a great grading criteria and he cares about his students!

Lectures do not reflect the exams, does not give proper examples in order for you to understand the concept. You have to go to the office hours of his TAs in order to see the answer key instead of just putting it on Canvas. A nice professor and wishes the best for you but he does not teach that well to accommodate for all his students.
Take the practice problems serious as they are like most of his midterm questions. Very kind professor that does want you to do well and loves to help/answers questions.

He's such a great professor that he made me consider changing my major to Chemistry, he's that good. He makes class enjoyable and is super lenient with grading. There's homework and weekly quizzes. Discussion is not mandatory, but super helpful. I highly recommend this professor.
Has many SI sessions but does not provide study guide for tests

Stallings is an amazing professor who is genuinely rooting for you. Though I haven't interacted with him one to one, you can tell he wishes the best for you! He also is a great lecturer and is very engaging. Attendance is not mandatory, and he is one of the best Chemistry teachers you can get! Just make sure you pay attention :-)
He's not boring!!! He makes the class REALLY engaging. Tests and quizzes based on lecture problems, discussion, and homework. I'm not even a chemistry major but if I was.... I would take him again!

awesome professor! gave quick subtle breaks in lecture to relax your mind and was funny. teaching style was clear and engaging. came with prior chem background and he refreshed it and explained topics well. allowed a one sided crib sheet on midterms, weekly quizzes based on topics taught in lecture. posts podcasts of lectures as well

the midterms and quizzes are pretty tough, but learn how to study because it's possible to pass them!! he's great at teaching and his slides are easy to follow. remember to take notes and not to miss any lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Stallings goes at a much slower rate than the other professors so if you took AP Chem its a breeze. He seems to only do 8am or 9am lectures so be ready for that, but lecture attendance isn't mandatory and he does podcasts. Weekly homework assignments and quiz due on friday but its pretty easy. Really nice prof too.

Prof Stallings has great lectures, also uploads them online consistently (has not missed one yet this quarter) that are always very helpful and I usually don't leave the lecture unsure of much. Takes the time during lectures to answer questions. All he wants if for you to actually understand the material and his grading shows that.
CHEM114A in summer is objectively easier but this professor really does not explain things well. The lectures were just confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is literally the worst professor I have ever had at UCSD. If you have any other option please avoid him. He does not care about students at all.

Hands down the best general chemistry teacher at UCSD, His lectures are clear, well executed, and engaging. The class grading system is centered around being at the benefit of the students and he makes everything in your favor of passing the class. He does teaching like no other.
I really enjoyed Professor Stallings' lectures. He was kind, funny, and seemed genuinely invested in our learning experience.
His lectures are boring and don't reflect the exams. He doesn't respond to emails. Exams take up 80% of your grade and are too difficult. Avoid taking him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures prepared me for homework and midterms, quizzes, and midterms, and I never had to read the textbook. I enjoyed his grading scheme. Allowed to have 1 cheat sheet on both midterms and 3 cheat sheets on the final! His has a grade improvement policy where you can replace midterm grades if you do better on that section on the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Stallings is super funny. Def recommend his class. You get cheat sheets for all of the midterms and finals. If you score higher on ur final than ur midterm then the midterm grade gets replaced. Not the easiest class, but he curves the tests and final grades. Overall, really good prof.

Everyone that says you need to put in extra work is insane, this class was basic in material and Stallings was an excellent and active professor. He also made clear what would be on the tests, specifically through his quizzes. Honestly very disappointed in seeing his rating so low, he is very clear an explicit with his words. I'm taking all year.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You need to put in work outside of the class -- can't get around that -- if you want a higher grade. I know it's discouraging to hear that, but you can absolutely do well in this class if you really take into consideration what he recommends, go to supplemental instruction, be honest with yourself when studying (do you actually understand this?) GL

Not an easy class, but with this professor you have a good chance of doing well. Textbook was never explicitly used but was helpful. Lectures were paced perfectly, and professor kept it interesting and interactive. Easy to pass, exams are tough, but a policy allowing to replace exam scores with final makes them forgiving.

For midterms 1 and 2, I received 91 and 96 respectively. But for finals, I received 83. This is because the last bit of material was the hardest, and this guy rushed thru them because he ran out of time. Also, he isn't rly all that caring. I asked him for the discussion problem set answer keys so I could study them, and he replied with just "nope".

Dr. Stallings makes his lectures entertaining and engaging. He is always willing to answer questions, whether inside or outside of class. All of his exams are multiple choice with ample time given. He even allows you to use a cheat sheet during exams. Overall, he made CHEM 6A a great, fairly easy experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Stallings is kind and caring about his students. He always shares study tips at the beginning of every lecture. You will be fine if you attend all of his LE, and DI, do homework and do other class activities. His class has weekly quizzes to review all of the concepts of the week. Sometimes, he will respond to students' questions on Piazza.

It could be a summer session thing but his lectures were extremely content-heavy and he'd test us on things that he didn't even cover during lectures. On the plus side, the exams were open notes. He kept grading questions wrong, but that is a minor complaint. 

He's actually really nice and if you have any questions, his OH is a great place.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Awesome professor! Really cares about his students learning the material and not just cramming for tests. Takes student feedback seriously and implements it well. Lots of opportunities to make up lost exam points. Easy to talk to. Took CHEM 114A during the summer, asynchronous lectures and weekly quizzes. 2 midterms 1 final.

Already some of your grade is based on bucket points such as homework and participation that is super easy to receive. Stallings is a super caring professor who understands us as students and tries his best to work with our busy schedules.

He goes into detail to explain and prompts you to think about why things are the way they are. He connects to previous concepts in the CHEM 6 series and does some refreshers along the way. Homework is kind of hard. Exams are hard ngl. Neat pick: He does speak slowly and answers a LOT of questions during class.
He is pretty fun, but his exams are difficult and requires a lot of studying beforehand.
Seems like a cool guy on the outside, but anyone can read off a PowerPoint slide.

Stallings is one of the nicest profs I've ever met. He personally congratulated all who got an A on his exams, and he makes it clear that he wants you to succeed. Grading scale was lowered a bit, ~91 was an A. Lectures were easy to follow and sufficient enough to learn the material along with the hw. Exams were MC but not impossibly difficult.

Great lecturer who evidently cares about students and is available outside of class. Very understanding and the way he structures his class gives a lot of opportunities to make up for a bad grade/missed assignment/discussion. Spends a lot of time answering questions during lectures which cause us to fall behind but I personally don't mind it.

Dr. Stallings takes his time lecturing to make sure everyone understands the concepts. I did not read the textbook at all and learned all the material from lecture. Discussion problem sets and homework are great practice for exams. Able to replace midterm scores on final. I ended up taking Dr. Stallings for all of the chem 6 series.
Tests reflect material and he lets you make a cheat sheet

Very sweet guy overall. However, the class is graded by few exams, and often we would have to learn videos outside in lecture because he would not cover them all in time (had to learn stuff on my own a week before the final because we did not get to it in class yet were expected to know it). Hard online, but very kind professor.

He's... okay. Very accessible outside of class (office hours 3x/week) but his explanations are very long-winded despite saying very little in terms of content which confused me at times. Online is pretty rough not bc hard questions, but the small margin of error (not sure WHY he had to have such a small margin) really frustrated me. Better IRL!
Homework was really easy and tests were harder than expected. I made a lot of dumb mistakes. He's a nice teacher but gets condescending when the class does badly on a test.

Dr. Stallings is a great lecturer and presents the information in an entertaining way; however, I found his exams to be quite difficult. There are 2 exams (20 multiple choice questions) and a cumulative final (50 multiple choice), so your grade is essentially dependent on 90 multiple choice questions. The class averages were in the mid to high 70s.

Prof Stallings uses a lot of visualisations/metaphors to explain concepts, which worked pretty well for me, but isn't for everyone. Discussions were mandatory. Very available outside of class! Exams were all MCQ but definitely need to work fast when taking the test.

Prof Stallings' lectures are great, the way he explains the content made me not just understand chemistry, but actually start to enjoy it. He shows in several ways that he really cares about students. The tests and content material is extremely difficult, but that can be expected with chemistry. I am taking his class again right now for CHEM 6B.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: I highly recommend you read the textbook. I'm pretty sure if I only read the textbook and skipped every lecture, my grade would be exactly the same. Provides slides for you before lectures, but they are only skeletal, so they don't even have the core details from each topic. Doesn't give answers to discussion worksheets cuz we "wont learn" that way

Prof. Stallings is a good teacher and cares about his students. However, the content in the lecture slides is very compact and it's hard to fully grasp the topics if you don't remember much Chem from high school. The tests were made for you to think and put together things from lectures. From what I've seen he's helpful in his OH, so go to them!

Despite all the other comments about how awful the tests are or how awful his lectures are, I think Stallings is an amazing professor. Heck, he even have his own recipes on canvas. The tests are not easy dont get me wrong, but he is so generous with curves that it pretty much brings up your grade 10% or more.
Fun professor, but sometimes he cannot catch up with the speed of the lectures because of some of his good jokes.

Professor Stallings is an absolutely HILARIOUS professor. If there are no better professors available, definitely take his class. He is very caring of his students and always cracks a joke every 20 minutes to keep the class hooked. His multiple-choice exams are difficult, so study hard as they're heavily based on the homework/discussion papers.

I am relying on grade replacement to save my grade for this class. When introducing us to quantum mechanics, he stated, "If this is the first time you're seeing this content in my class, you're already behind." That didn't vibe well with me and many others. I wish he provided answer keys to discussion worksheets that's somewhat similar to exams.

I am writing to you today 17 minutes after my second midterm and tell me why the midterm ate my ass but not in the good way. These midterms are not based off of homework or discussion even though he said it would be. Absolutely difficult for no reason. Everything is not what it seems. Stay safe out there.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I think hes very funny and keeps the class engaged. You have to put in work for his tests. I don't think you can watch his lectures and do the homework and pass. And his tests are very time crunched so you have to move fast. Its hard, but out of all the chem teachers he's going to be your best bet. Granted I still don't know what my grade will be.

Super fun during lectures, tests really aren't that hard if you are paying attention in lecture and doing the homework. Very light amount of work and tests match the course, they aren't super difficult. All multiple choice and your final can replace all previous tests. Would take again

Professor Stallings is funny sure but he really doesn't care about his students. His exams do not have enough time to complete them and he refused to accomodate for anyone. He also is crazy paranoid about students cheating and will submit you to AIO for technical difficulties occurring on your exam. He teaches poorly and just reads off his slides.

Dr. Stallings is a very great professor not just for his in-depth lectures, but also for his great personality. He constantly wants to ensure that all of his students are doing well, and he goes to great lengths in giving up his time to explain course content and how to study for his class. Tests are short on time but his grading is extremely fair.

This professor told his lecture hall that we would likely not succeed unless we took his class twice. In his words, "If this is the first time you are seeing the material in my lectures, you are behind." I was stunned. No professor should ever, ever treat their class that way. I'm avoiding this teacher at all costs in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This professor told his lecture hall that we would likely not succeed unless we took his class. In his words, "If this is the first time you are seeing the material in my lectures, you are behind." I was stunned. No professor should ever, ever treat their class that way. I'm avoiding this teacher at all costs in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I don't know if it's because he stopped caring in an asynchronous/online environment but his lectures are oversimplified with typos in math problems. His tests have very short unrealistic time frames and only test to see if you can do chem fast, not if you understand. Plus, he doesn't respond to piazza questions because its for discussion credit :(

Dr. Stallings is an average professor in my opinion, especially in the online setting. I feel that he oversimplifies topics; his exam questions are based on the lectures but they feel very formulaic and I'm not actually sure what I'm doing when I'm solving them. I barely scraped by with an A but I wouldn't recommend taking his course.
Would highly recommend Dr. Stallings for CHEM6C. A caring professor who goes out of his way to help his students succeed. Appreciate how accessible he was outside class.

Stallings makes you work for your grade and has high expectations. Very exam heavy. That being said, it makes you learn the material inside out and he has resources to help you do that including discussions, office hours, and more. Lectures were good, I did get lost in the details during live session. Overall solid chem prof and super inspiring!

Prof. Stallings gives clear lectures, so there is literally no need to read the textbook, but make sure you check every detail of lecture slides. The exams are basic, but not forgiving as no partial credits, and he has very high expectations (93 for A). If you have taken AP/IB chem, than take him, otherwise think twice about taking other prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took 6B with him so back with an update. Tbh he's not the problem, its the material that makes these classes hard. As long as u do all the discussion, weekly assessments, and extra problems for each chapter you will ace the midterms. Make sure to go to office hours if you can he's a great guy and more than willing to help you

He was, by far, the best chemistry teacher that I've ever had. Stallings is the most charismatic teacher you'll ever meet. Even if chemistry isn't your strong suit, put in some work in from time to time and you'll be fine. For the final, 80% of it contained very similar problems from past midterms, so it wasn't too bad. Highly recommended.

I love Stallings, I say that with my full chest. Chem has been a huge struggle but he's is the first teacher I've had that made it feel doable. The class isn't easy by any means, but you get what you put in, it's not one of those impossible depressing courses where you feel it doesnt matter how much you study. And he's so nice it makes my morning!

Don't take, just choose the other professor. I took AP CHEM in highschool and was still confused by the way he presented the material. He often confuses himself before he confuses the rest of us actually. He also gets overwhelmed pretty quickly. The tests didn't reflect the material presented in class too. Oddly specific.

I took him after seeing his great ratings, but boy was I in for a rollercoaster. I loved his burger recipe. However, I did NOT love how his test material did not at all reflect his lecture material. He didn't cover a lot of the topics on the exams in his lectures and expected students to study for this class like it's a full-time job.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: No partial credit or curves. Grade is based all on midterms and final. Super difficult tests and you get so confused in lecture. Dont take him.

Difficult class for sure (its chemistry), but if you put in the time and actually study, you will get the grade you deserve. Appreciate the fact that Dr. Stallings is accessible outside of class (even weekends). A caring professor that I hope to have again in the future.
Stallings himself was a super caring professor, but damn he makes you work for your grade. I, myself, like the test heavy structure (about 80% of the grade is exams), but I can see why some hate it.

He's honestly not amazing, not sure why earlier reviews say he is. 80% of your grade is from 3 exams, they're rough and you can study hard for them for two weeks straight and still barely scrape a B. I'm taking him again for 6C tho so I'll let you guys know if he gets any better.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had high expectations for this class because of prior reviews but sadly, I was let down. Stallings is a funny guy, but his Chem class is self-deprecating. His exams consist of all or nothing fill-in-the-black problems, where you MUST have the exact value he inputted, or it will be as if you never even attempted despite having the correct answer

Professor Stallings is a very caring professor, but his tests are very tough and I don't think that they represent a student's understanding of the material. If you get a negative sign wrong or a decimal point wrong it is the same as not answering the question at all. I would not recommend him if you care about your GPA.

He's a kind professor and funny. However, this class was the hardest I have ever taken. I studied my butt off to barely pass. He does not curve and the grade is heavily dependent on three exams. He explains concepts quickly and it becomes confusing. Last quarter I did well in 6A, but this class was a different story. I would try someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This professor had good ratings when I first decided to take the course but I had a terrible experience. Your grade in the class is basically based on 2-3 exams and they're not even fair. Overall, I would never take a course with him again. He doesn't properly prepare you for exams and his examples from dec have nothing to do with the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Really bad experience with this professor. He had great reviews prior to this quarter but omg this quarter, 80% of the grades is dependent on a final! He makes his class unnecessarily difficult when people have other commitments. Wouldn't recommend taking this professor. Save your stress and take a more lenient and caring professor.
No partial credit at all. Class is pretty much based on two exams. Not enough time on exams. Not good grading structure. Nice professor but would not take the class again.

Honestly, stallings was the worst. Didnt care about us, had unnecessarily high expectations, and wouldnt round up grades that were above .5 even though it is usually what is done. Would not recommend, basically ruined chem for me
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Stallings is a great person who cares about his students but he doesn't give partial credit. So many students didn't do well this quarter and he refuses to apply a curve. I studied my butt off and usually get As and Bs. I would not suggest taking Stallings if you care about your GPA.

When it comes to lectures, Dr. Stallings doesn't really know how to example concepts. He usually just reads off the slides and you can tell he comes to class unprepared and disorganized. If you plan to take the MCAT, this class will not prepare you. Look into better UCSD Chemistry professors.

I entered this class, everyone recommending Dr. Stallings, however his class structure is really bad. 80% of your grade depends on 2 midterms and a final. Class is hard. Although he is nice, helpful, and makes lectures a bit easier, his exams were tough. He doesn't curve at all and overall did not enjoy the structure leading to lots of stress.
Probably the most caring professor that I have ever had. Difficult class for sure, but he does everything he can to help you succeed.

To say that I am disappointed is to say the least. Everyone was hyping up the class saying that Dr. Stallings makes chemistry easier but I didn't feel that way. His recorded lectures are essentially him reading off slides with no clear explanation of concepts. Exams are long and rather difficult yet not enough time is given. Really kind guy though

Even though professor Stallings cares about his students, his expectations are too high. In his lectures, he mostly reads off of his slides instead of going in depth. He also quizzes weekly with a short time length which barely gives you the chance to complete all the questions and doesn't award any partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: the sweetest and most caring professor ever. but he has unnecessarily high expectations. the only reason i was able to get a good grade is because i have a strong chemistry background. the way he sets up his grading scale, your grade basically depends on your final (if you want a 93 in the class you need a 93 on the final). his asynchronous lecture

Honestly, the only reason I got an A on our first midterm is because I have a strong Chemistry background. He's not very good at explaining concepts in a dumbed-down version for first-time Chemistry students to understand. Also, he places emphasis on the weirdest thing like using a specific periodic table HE CREATED. Don't recommend overall.
Definitely a tough class, but I appreciate the way Dr. Stallings is always available to help and answer questions. Not the very best lecturer that I have ever had, but definitely the most caring.

Stallings is a (nice) professor. It's best to attend synchronously. He doesn't record during his zoom lectures and his asynchronous videos are really just him reading the slides. His tests are more of a measure of how fast you can do chemistry rather than how well you actually understand a chapter. Probably harder class with the online format.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Nice and funny, but most of all, he's willing to help if you seek it. However, I wouldn't say there's something special about him that makes him a good lecturer. The tests and weekly quizzes have short time limits, and his expectations are unnecessarily high. Unless you're really willing to prioritize chemistry this quarter, do not take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Proffessor Stallings is the GEN CHEM KING!!!! If you can take any of his classes take them. His test are conceptual but he won't throw a curve ball at you. What you learn in his lecutres I guarantee you will seee on his exams. Prof Stallings is super humble, kind and patient. One of the best STEM UCSD profs hands down.

Professor stallings is the absolute best professor Ive ever had in my entire school career. This man cares so much about his students and is so passionate about teaching and actually made me love chem (and I used to hate chem) That alone should tell you how good he is. Very fair grader and super helpful and explains concepts very well!! Take him!!

Dr. Stallings saved my interest in chemistry, his use of incredibly relatable examples to explain concepts of chemistry. Which makes his class not only incredibly easy to understand but also fun to listen to! He also gives you a ton of extra points that you can earn so you never had to worry about not getting a decent grade.

Let me start of by saying I loathe chemistry but Dr. Stallings made it very bearable. His exams are very fair and representative of the material and there's even a chance to replace your Exam scores with the final. He is also very receptive to student feedback and shows genuine concern for your learning. I highly recommend him.

Great professor!! 100% recommend!! He makes chem a lot easier to understand and makes his lectures very concise and simplified. You have many chances to get a good grade in his class and his exams are fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The best professor I have had at UCSD!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: BEST PROF AT UCSD. I hated chemistry for 3 quarters until I had him. He makes lectures engaging and understandable. Very receptive to feedback and his tests are the fairest you'll get. If you get the chance, take him and your view on chem will change. He is v caring and willing to work with students. Seriously, my class had a fan club for him lol

Took Stallings for SS1 and loved it. His lectures are very clear and hes funny which helps me stay focused during those long heavy lectures. Weekly quizes and all 3 exams were very reflective of the material. he pulls the content from lectures so nothing is too unexpected. He cares about his students for sure. Lots of good vibes.

Dr. Stallings was extremely receptive of feedback and wrote his perspective on why he could or couldn't implement students' ideas for the class. He took everyone's thoughts into consideration. The exams were nearly identical to the quizzes and homework sets. Dr. Stallings tends to lighten the mood of his lectures by talking about his dog or cooking

Dr. Stallings makes lectures engaging and is always open to student feedback. The exams are free-response but are very similar to the discussion problems and weekly assessments, so you always know what to expect. He also allows you to replace both midterm scores with the corresponding section on the final. Overall, I definitely recommend him!

Prof Stallings is the best professor I've had at UCSD. Tests EXTREMELY correlate to quizzes and discussion worksheets, almost identical. He prepares you very well for his exams and they are not difficult if you prepare. Grading breakdown is great. He is also very inspirational, funny, and an engaging lecturer. Would 100% recommend, he is amazing.

pretty nice guy, can't run a class. This was the zoomU semester and he did not want to put in any extra effort to accommodate students. Announcements were often vague or last minute, horribly structured tests. Tests were on the hard side. Only take him if your other options are objectively bad and you are confident in ability to teach yourself.

Sweetest Professor ever, hands down. This was his first quarter, and he was amazing at teaching online. I wish I had taken his class in person because his jokes were amazing, showed us his dog often, and even talked about his cooking recipes. He taught the concepts amazingly and made his tests appropriately hard.
Exams were overall representative of what was taught in the lecture. The material was often confusing, however, he was always open to answering questions from students. Attendance is mandatory.

Super chill class and very nice professor. Memory based so I used flash cards to study. Practice questions very similar to exams, and he did have some trick questions on exams but in my opinion they were easy to catch. Discussions had a decent amount of work to do, and attendance for both lecture and discussion was required. Pretty easy A
Great lectures, tests are based only on slides. Has you do some reading of studies outside of class, but overall grading criteria is clear and straightforward. Lectures are engaging and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: 3 tests and a final. Attendance is mandatory, but he talks extremely fast, so you will barely hear everything. Uses clickers for attendance, which is 10% of the grade. Tests are completely made up of trick questions. If only he had straightforwardly asked questions, a lot more students would have succeeded.

This is one of the best professors I've had. His lectures are super organized and easy to follow. He lays out very clearly what will be on exams and gives in-class practice questions that are extremely similar to the exam questions. You will still need to study & memorize but an A is super achievable.

Taught half the class, had really interesting lectures, and explained content well. Lecture and discussion were mandatory and provided good study material. No trick questions on exams but definitely still required a decent amount of studying, and you can drop 1 of the 3 midterms or the final. I found lectures very engaging and loved the topics.

Great professor, tests are straight forward but there are 3 midterms + a final. One is dropped tho. Concepts arent that bad to understand, as long as you participate and try, you will succeed. He is a great prof and has great TAs 10/10 recommend. Also the material is actually interesting unlike other bio classes I've taken.

Course curriculum is very interesting and fun to learn about. Lectures are dense and he talks fast, be prepared to take lots of notes. No curveball exams, but they take a lot of studying to understand overarching concepts. Barton is also just a good guy who cares about his students' engagement with their major and has open office hours at SIO.

Andrew is a great lecturer and i believe covers all his material in detail in lecture time. 70% of your grade is from exams but they were mostly MCQ and pretty simple and straightforward. Attendance is mandatory for lecture and discussion so be prepared. Overall, i would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures follows a format of iclickers and power point that covers the reading assignments for every week. it's quite easy to follow, but there are instances that I forgot to do a reading assignment or a post-lecture quiz question assignment. So keep track of those you'll succeed in his class.

don't know if I took the same class as the kid who gave professor a 2.0 quality rating, but he does explain clicker questions, even for choices that are incorrect. Material on the tests can be easily found on lecture slides, with or without explanation. It is a very memory-based class, concepts are not too difficult to understand.

Professor talks at super speed and rarely includes all text on slides. Usually just includes maps and graphs then talks a ton about them. Hard to keep up with his talking as you are rushing to write down what he says. Doesn't explain clicker questions literally says "This one is right because it's right." Tests aren't too bad though

Adheres strictly to the syllabus and will not allow extra credit or accommodations to the schedule. Exams are not like lectures, rely heavily on true or false questions as well as filling in the blank questions for easy grading on his TAs' parts. My TA power tripped all quarter when it came to late submissions or discussion attendance. Bad.

Not a fun class to sit through as it dragged on forever during some lectures. The only bright spots was the sometimes we would have live performances which were really cool. I did not like the concert reports as I do not enjoy having to go far and spend money to turn in what is homework. Grading is really slow in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is one of the worst classes I've ever taken. There are so many papers and so much reading. If you have no music background you won't stand a chance. This class bored me out of my mind, I learned nothing, and I don't even like jazz anymore. Also, there are kind of a lot of papers, so if you don't like to write, pick an easier UD writing class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Dresser is an expert in music and makes learning about music interesting. I agree with other reviews that without prior experience in music, this class is difficult. However, he does a good job at explaining certain terminologies that are necessary for the class and I really appreciate the work he put into this class during these times.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Both the course description and prof. Dresser stated that this class is for non-music majors and no prior musical experience is required. However, none of the assignments seem like appropriate workload or requirement for non-music majors, and the live lectures are just bunch of students that know Jazz spitting terminologies we don't understand.

Cool prof, nonexistent TAs, unaware of the overwhelming load. I felt like I was taking three 4 unit courses in one. 2 papers, 3+ concert reports, weekly quizzes, 40+ pages of weekly reading and hours of listening, two 90 minute lectures a week. Overall I did enjoy the guest speakers and the material, but the assignments were way too overwhelming.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This man has no concept of what an appropriate workload for already overwhelmed students is. This was a class for non-music majors and he indunated everyone with complex music theory and 20+ pages worth of papers (EXCLUDING MIDTERM AND FINAL). He's kind and passionate but this class was genuinely the worst class I have taken at UCSD.

When he taught the basic musicianship class he made it really difficult. He quizzed us every week on melodic and rythmic dictation, sight singing, pulse fields, and interval ear training. I wouldn't take him for basic musicianship, his expectations are way to high and he doesn't seem to understand that other people have other classes to study for.
He's kinda cute.  Bad time management, but he knows his stuff well and he seems to care about his students.  Passionate about what he teaches.
cool guy, interesting material and a great bassist.  but he left for two weeks during the quarter!  not cool.

Such a good professor...brilliant.  Taught me things I would have never known.  Talented guy, engaging in class, funny.  The class (MUS 15 TECHNO) was really cool and this guy just makes you excited to come to class, even though the class is 3 hours long on Thursday nights!
Totally awesome.  Very experimental.  He's told me things I've never heard before about a topic I know extremely well.  Plus, he's a brilliant bassist, famous.

Although this guy's comments below mine are so thoughtful, I think I'll add some more info.  SUPER EASY for anybody, the profs (there were 3 that quarter) laid out everything on the tests and really short essays.  The foreign guys were a little hard to listen to, but not much to complain about. the class may be totally different next year, though.
Worst class I have ever taken at UCSD.
Insanely brilliant man. No wonder he is leaving to Stanford.

He's an entertaining and knowledgeable lecturer if you choose to go to lecture. One group project, a midterm, and a final. Discussion is mandatory but you just go over papers, which you should read because they help you prepare for the exams. Learn the different methods used and you'll do well. Easy A class as long as you do a little work!
Midterm was very easy, and the average was about 2830. And then he pulled a difficult final exam out of nowhere, and suddenly most of the class are getting B's. Would not recommend.

the midtermfinal consists of answering 4 questions about a primary research article pertaining to a subject we covered in class. He also makes you design your own hypothetical experiments to test a hypothesis, using techniques he covers in lectures. the class is very loosely structured, there is no book, and overall its a pretty easy A.
One of the most student-centric professors at UCSD. Easy class, interesting, you learn some cool material,  overall very enjoyable academic class.   Take him if you can.

Dr. Huberman is a great lecturer. The material can be intimidating (seems to be taught at a graduate level) but his main goal is to invoke scientific curiosity and teach students how to analyze and understand scientific papers. He assigns papers each week for a group to analyze and present during section. Very good practice for the MT and final.

He's like the Justin Timberlake of neuroscience; legit though. He is really knowledgeable, down to earth, lectures are attention holding, really good class. No textbook, readings consist of modern research papers. Recommend.

Dr. Huberman is one of the few exceptional teachers that truly cares about his students' learning. He won't force you to memorize asinine facts -- instead he'll give you the tools to learn neuroscience from research, like an actual neuroscientist does.  He is a gifted, captivating lecturer and great at explaining complex material. Highly recommend!
One of the most passionate and interested professors I have seen. Incredibly smart and very well spoken!
he missed several classes. he switched the date of the midterm last minute. he rarely responded to emails. I wouldn't recommend him as a teacher.

Class consisted most on group work, and attendance was mandatory as there was a quiz at the end of lecture every day. Found her to be VERY picky on her grading criteria. Not the most approachable, so I mostly relied on the TA who I'd recently had as a teacher. She was okay, just not the best.

The professor was okay but not great at explaining concepts and could come off as unapproachable. The class is easy with mostly group work and little outside effort. The final is the main assignment and could've been online. Only take it if you're interested in linguistics.
Probably the worst linguistics professor I've ever had to deal with. Tough grader, won't accommodate to your needs, always dtm.

Grade consists of 4 HW assignments 20%, midterm 30%, and final 50%. Homework graded on completion, lectures were absolutely boring. Cool professor but man hard to stay awake, usually never went the full 3 hours. Both exams were 50 MCQ each, meaning missing even one question would hurt your final grade a lot. Posts study guides for exams, helpful.
We only had 4 HW assignments and they are all graded as either 100%, 85% or 0. Very fair teacher but if you miss anything you're a little screwed

homework assignments were easy, but completely irrelevant to midterm/final. lecture was boring, but if you paid attention, it did help for the exams (heavy studying). asked random questions about what school he attended. also yelled at our TA in front of the class and went on interesting rant where he referred to himself in the 3rd person.

He is actually an AMAZING professor, IDK why people are saying he isnt. When teaching he is def strict but its at our best interest at heart. He is really easy to talk to and always avalible he is really sweet and helpful. As long as you pay attention you are fine the tests are easy. Pay more attention to what he is saying than the slides.

Very easy going and friendly professor. Super old so he has a different generation's mindset but very clear on what to study to do well. Can secure an A on exams if you know the slides well despite not attending lectures. HWs can take a bit of time but graded well and easy to get full on those. Only prof who hands out his number to be accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Worst learning experience taking a MGT course

Professor Dunn is nice but can't teach. The lecture and lecture slides are poorly put together and useless overall. Homework is graded for completion but the HW material itself is also useless and irrelevant to exam material. However, you get a study guide at the end of the course that covers almost the whole final which makes getting an A doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: At least 5+ hours of work every week, with really tough grading since it's definitely gonna take more than 10 hrs to get the A on the assignment. I wouldn't say you can easily learn things from this class since the topic is too broad, so most of the time you would have to learn the assignments by yourself. Not worth it for an elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You must take notes when you attend class to prepare for the exams. Knowing the basics of the study guide is not enough. You have to know everything front and back. There's no curve. 20% hw, 30% midterm, 50% final. provides one extra credit assignment. If you write down everything he says and review it for the exams, you'll at least get a B.

If you are a student who is genuinely interested in learning about the courses topic, you will be disappointed by this professors inability to lecture, create a presentation with any kind of logical organization, and a total incompetence to clarify topics when he is asked questions. He is simply the worst professor at UCSD. Avoid at all costs.

Not too bad, his lectures and homeworks were confusing at times but as long as you show up to class, read his slides and do the homework you will be fine. He doesn't require textbook use and the final was multiple choice, 50 questions. He is pretty funny and approachable too.

Homeworks are sooooooooo time consuming. Lectures are extremely long and boring, but he provides guidlines for the case. No exam for this class. Only six graded cases. The last one is a group project, so make sure you meet new people. Not hard to get an A, but you need to spend a lot of time on the cases. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Boring class, even if you're thinking about going into business or finance. The class is essential and Dunn is a pretty standard professor with a few jokes that make him slightly above par. Did a lecture on surviving the "Trump era" after he was elected though which was pretty cool. Overall, good but not great.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor. Very helpful (even on weekends) and always accesible. Class is a must for anyone thinking of going into finance.
He knows but he doesn't know how to teach.

Interesting dude, awesome professor, clear lecturer, alpha male & an expert in the subject. In regards to exam difficulty, the midterm wasn't as easy as suggested by some of the comments below. There's no curve & you'll have to be fluent in using the financial calculator beforehand. I borrowed one the day of & my grade surely suffered because of it
Homework isn't representative of class material, lectures are boring. It's doable but not fun

Pretty easy class. Likes to relate the class to the real world, so his homework and tests reflect skills you can use to get a job. They are not too difficult, but may be time consuming, so take note and start a little earlier than normal.
