Also, this is the first business class I've taken at UCSD that does not grade on attendance, thank God.

Really enjoyed how real Professor Dunn was- he told you how it was in the real life and focused on material you would actually need to use. Was expecting accounting to be brutal, but he made it simple gave reasonable homework and tests. Always willing to help students in the class and for the future. Loved this class and Professor Dunn!

Great professor, I recommend taking him! Lectures are a little boring, but then again it's accounting. Prof is really helpful, he doesn't snap at people like was stated before. Class usually ends really early and he gives you leads on internships and will even help you with your resume! This guy is awesome! And the tests are easy if you study/do HW

This professor is so nice and so willing to help you not only with homework, but with advice. Clear lectures and helpful homework. Tells you exactly what will be on the exam. Take him! He'll teach you accounting skills you'll actually use.

I don't understand what these people are talking about either. He's very approachable and easy to contact. He let students know what's going to be on the midterm and final. I'd take his other classes too!

I don't know what these people are talking about. I took him for both mgt 5 and 181 (now). His midterms/finals are super easy. He focuses on giving you the skills to get a job in the real world. What else can you want from him? I would only recommend taking econ173a before you take his mgt181. And being an accounting minor def helps

just like the other comment, he tells u before ur exams what's going to be on the test, but so what? it basically covers most materials. since someone from last quarter got caught for cheating, we didnt' have curve. without curve DONT TAKE IT. Even with curve, you have to work you ass off to get an A,final50, midterm30% hw20% good luck format.

He gave us all the answers to the final at the last lecture.  He snaps at people whenever they ask questions and the lectures are unbelievably boring.  But like I said, dude gave us all the answers before the final!

Sort of a sleepy teacher during the lecture. Quizzes + Final are worth an insane 90% of the grade and each quiz is only 5 MCQ and 2 FRQ. There are no practice quizzes/finals either, and no cheat sheet. Homework is just assigned problems from the textbook.

I think he is a better 2C professor than other courses. He is more knowledgeable about topics like fluids, thermo, light, and sound, so he was able to answer questions in ways that made logical sense. His lectures are monotone, but understandable. He didn't overcomplicate the topics beyond being able to use the equations to solve the problems.

This class is graded very heavily on quizzes which are 51 percent of your grade. 4 quizzes and one gets dropped. Each quiz has 9 points with 5 mcqs (1 point each) and 2 frqs (2 points each). The FRQs are fair and there is generous partial credit, but some of the mcq questions seem to be tricking you; very stressful (1 mcq is 11 percent of your quiz

The lack of effort put into this class by the professor compared to any other physics 2 astounding. All he does is assign homework from the book and give quizzes. The professor adds nothing to the learning and is also hard to understand in lecture. You're better off just self studying, but attendance is also mandatory. 10% attendance 90% quiz+final
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Duscan is just a bad teacher. I get how professors want so much but the issue is I only took three classes during the quarter and still struggled to get by. I don't have the ridiculous amount of time to be at most office hours and now I am even getting cut out of my required classes and on the verge being suspended.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I found it very hard to pay attention in his class, even with iClicker for points / attendance. Lecture felt very boring. Grading scheme is clear but curves can only be estimated during finals week when they calculate grades. Gives extra points on quizzes if the average is too low. Overall mediocre lecturer but the class isn't terribly difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Just like how an electron is - and a proton is +, Duscan's is a net zero. His class is almost just like any other math class here, only difference is that the grading is nicer than average. I regret passing his class and should had focused something else less taxing. Anyone BUT Duscan, skip his nonsense and pick someone's worth more of your time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very boring lectures that I didn't get much out of but had to go to because of i-clicker. The quizzes and tests really aren't too bad and are really are just the hw questions with minor changes. The topic itself is hard, but the test are relatively straightforward, but when combined with a sleepy teacher, it gets tough. Heed the poor reviews.
Prepare to tank your grade. The quizzes are brutal

Lazy teaching. No cheat sheet, given formula sheet is confusing and does not always match what has been used in class, no written solutions in class only typed out solutions on lecture slides. Uses textbook generated homework and then draws out test problems making learning complicated. Unclear expectations from what is said in class to tests.

Professor Keres was a really great lecturer; he tried to keep the class engaged with clicker questions and demos.  I think a lot of people forget that he actually asks students to read the book before class and that's why the clicker questions are based on accuracy. The homework and practice problems were all exactly like the exam

The homework was very different from lectures and are super long sometimes. His grading scale was very generous, with quizzes being 60% of our grade. He makes things overly complicated and goes over good examples and then a super difficult one which tends to be almost every homework problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He teaches with the assumption everyone has had ap physics, so don't take the class unless you have
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
(2023)

Grading Policy:
Quizzes 60% (Fridays 9:00-9:50)
Final 25%
Homework 10%
iClickers 5%

Alternative Grading Policy:
Quizzes 60%
Final 30%
Homework 10%

added extra credit for attend. discuss. at end (1.5%)
added a point or two if class did bad on quiz 

quiz: 10mc 2frq
final: 20mc 4frq 

uses same questions shown in lecture and homework
Very hard class!

If this is your first physics class ever DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR'S CLASS. Considering this is an introductory class, the way the prof teaches it, it definitely requires a lot of foundational knowledge/background. The class is very test heavy and weekly exams are pretty difficult, so if you're not a good test taker, this class isn't ideal.

55% from 6-7 quizzes, 25% final, 15% homework, 5% lecture participation. 85+ is an A. Lectures are decent, good idea to watch khan academy though. It took a WHILE to grade quizzes. Quizzes are pretty easy if you have a mediocre understanding of the material material, averages were kind of low but questions weren't tough if you could do homework.

2B is a hard subject but that's not Keres' fault. He uses iClickers and weekly quizzes that are the bulk of your grade. Quizzes are much easier than the homework in my opinion. Lectures have a lot of content to get through but he does a good job showing how things are derived and making jokes in between with occasional demos too.

Take his class if you want:
- Receive your quizzes grades 4 weeks after taking them
- Get your quiz results wrong (even when they are scantrons)
- Have a though time understanding the class
- Want to get clicker points based on correctness instead of participation
- Do not want to practice quizzes
- Suffer through the quarter without a grade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: You never knew what your actual grade was because he took way too long to grade our quizzes, and multiple times, the quizzes were scored wrong due to a scantron error or a human error. The quizzes were very hard but so is the material. Had to learn how to apply certain equations and laws on our own, and he very rarely would provide an example.

This is probably the worst teacher I have ever had, he doesn't go over problems in class step by step, so the students can understand. He likes to go over a bunch of slides really fast and forgets to post the lecture slides before class. He also takes weeks to grade tests, without giving us back the exam or post the answers on canvas.

Extremely test and homework heavy. He doesn't go over a lot of what you need to know in class, so prepare to teach yourself with the textbook. Doesn't excuse quiz/test absences for ANY reason (even COVID) or give makeups. The load from this class is basically the equivalent of 8 credits, so don't take four other courses with this one like me.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took PHYS 2A with professor Keres two times. I went to every lecture, read every section in the textbook, did every practice problem, did the adaptive practice, and went to office hours. I hardly passed. He is not a great professor and does not show a lot of effort in connecting with students or ensuring students' success. I will never recommend.
Very test heavy, hated this class tbh.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Keres is not a good lecturer. I was in an introductory physics class and he skipped over so many conceptual material and did not explain stuff well at all. His tests were really difficult, especially for the material that he covered in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor DK does not seem to care about how the students learn and enjoy the class, but rather makes the grade so test-focused that students are more worried about a letter than how much they actually learned. It would be better to have other options for grading in order to let students see the importance of the process and the collaboration.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not an easy class but a really cool guy and professor. The class is very test-heavy but he provides recommended textbook problems and as long as you are solid on them you can expect to do well on quizzes/exams.

The class definitely requires some effort to do well and understand the concepts, and there's a lot of readings, but if you watch the lecture and study the homework problems and reading quizzes, the tests shouldn't be too bad. A lot of test questions were similar to the homework problems/reading quiz problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Hardly any problems done in lecture. Waste to show up to his virtual lectures because hardly any of the stuff goes over in exam/quizzes. You will be learning everything yourself from the textbook and YouTube videos. Since everything is online, multiple choice/ fill in the blank questions with slight turn in work portion for exams. Class avg C+
The grading scale was unclear, and grading is very slow. The grading weight is very bad, and hes lecture doesnt really help the exams...

I'm sure if we were taught in-person, he would be a much better professor, but it seems he has struggled to make the transition to online learning. He knows his stuff, but he goes really quickly, especially since he tried to fit in more content due to online learning. The quizzes ramped up in difficulty pretty quickly, leaving many to struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst professor ever! Online school is hard bu he makes it harder. He wouldn't released the answers to quizzes so we can study them before the final and the quizzes and exams were very difficult and the time to them was ridiculous.
Easily the best Prof I've had. Lecture was clear. Caring and responsible.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: 7 quizzes, all average 6/12 (95% test category). Adjusted class scale as of right now before the final (85 is an A). He is a good teacher and does great demos, but he moves very fast, and leaves the catching upon you with the use of the textbook. Put in about to 10-12 hrs a week and not getting any results.

Professor Keres is very kind and caring. His class is not that bad if you go over his lectures and make sure you understand the main concepts. He uses Piazza and is quick to respond to any questions. Keres and TA Nathan are a great team. The class itself has an adjusted scale that he doesn't deviate from at the end of the quarter. Overall recommend
Professor Keres is the best professor I have ever met in UCSD. He is willing to help every students problem and is very patient. His test are not hard and I love his teaching.

Amazing Professor. He loves astrophysics and it shines through his lectures. He is a very relaxed professor but likes when people actively participate in lecture and ask questions. The homework was not too difficult and was related to course material. There is a final term paper. I took Keres for Physics 163, too. He and TA Nathan are awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Very interesting material and easy A. What else ?
One of the best physics professors at UCSD, both educational and funny. Quizzes were difficult, but there were four grading weight scales and the course was curved.

Great professor. Lectures are straightforward and informative. Hes the best physics professor I have taken at UCSD. He gives out extra points if the quiz averages are low. Quizzes and exams are very fair.
He was extremely chill and made his class very fun. With that said, your grade is like 85% tests and they were very hard, but at least there was a decent curve at the end.

He is a nice professor who tries to help his students succeed. He gave out 4 quizzes (very brutal), worth 50% of the grade, and a final, which was worth 30% (also brutal) of the grade. The homework, discussions, and in-class questions are worth 20% of the grade. Conclusively, the content is hard, and the quiz averages are low.

Prof Meyertholen provides plenty of resources to succeed. Do the interactive textbook content, it will prepare you for trivial MCQs on the quiz you may otherwise not get. His lecture content is extremely clear and he does not deviate far from it.

He is the teacher you wish you had for every class. He makes E&M really easy to understand and I feel had I taken any other professor I would have been struggling. What makes him amazing as well is how respectful he is and his dedication for students first. In my class the average quizzes weren't great so he would help boost up the scores as well.

Amazing professor: gives pre-lecture videos to help you understand the content (way better than readings). Homework policy is very lenient; gives a lot of extra credit and curves quizzes. If you can try to take him, he made me actually enjoy physics (especially considering how hard 2B material is).

Meyertholen uses a "flipped classroom" style, where you conceptually learn the material before class through his pre-lecture videos and textbook, and then you go through solving problems in class, which I found helpful. While the material is challenging, Meyetholen does a great job of trying to break everything down before integrating all concepts.
my king he's the best
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good professor, one of the best. Hardest part of the course was taking quizzes every other week. In total the quizzes are worth like 50% of your grade. Not bad but some MCQs can tank your score.

Class itself covers very easy concepts you can learn by yourself. Professor is great: he makes lectures interesting and engaging. Only annoying thing is attendance is mandatory so you physically have to be around the lecture hall to receive credit for iclicker.

Before every class you are expected to read a chapter of the textbook or watch the video associated with the chapter as well as due a short PCQ. The PCQ is only two questions and is graded purely based on completion. He does this so that his lecture are based on what the class seems to be struggling with the most. Overall amazing professor!!

SUCH a sweet person! has his funny moments, does brain breaks. wants to get to know class and ppl to participate. made the class super beginner friendly, SO well prepped for tests from course content. homework is light, just a kinda weird schedule. the "quizzes" are actually midterms LOL  great at explaining concepts, tailored learning environment.

Great professor, great class! It was a bit tough at first because I didn't have the background in physics many other students had, but he made it easy to catch up. Pre-lecture videos and clicker questions were super helpful, and his class had a very interactive learning environment overall. Really cares about your learning.

He is absolutely amazing. His lectures are amazing and he gives regrades on quizzes. he also practically lets you know what will be on the quizzes during lectures, so if you go to lectures (which I highly suggest because he is an amazing teacher) you will be set for the class. He has a pretty flexible grading scheme, and is amazing to learn from.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory, but the lectures are at least interesting; he also tries his best to make them engaging. There were 4 quizzes and a final that represented the materials covered in class very well.

He's nice and all, but when it comes to actually teaching, he sucks. He allows us to opt out of any assignment. HW cost $60 and it's only 5% of our grade, so I opt out. He sucks at teaching because he "teaches" us something new everyday that was irrelevant to the last. Tests are totally irrelevant to what we do in lecture. Average Grade: C (2.08)

He gave a quiz every other week (4 quizzes), which came with nice curves ranging from a 4% curve to a 17% curve on quizzes, making the mean about 70%. These quizzes were very fair, it lined up well with his practice quizzes and discussion. Attendance though was mandatory, but it was not too participation intensive. Would take with him again.

I struggled so much I would consistently study to fail quizzes. I liked the flipped lecture format, but during lectures concepts would get more complicated. Practice quizzes were easy compared to quizzes, HW was difficult and didn't reflect content, also looked to people who did better to gauge performance and didnt explain clicker questions well.

Won't lie - physics is really hard. But there are many opportunities to succeed. The homework is a lot harder than the quizzes, but I don't think a lot of people do it (costs $65 to access). Meyertholen's flipped class format is great practice, but you need to add more as needed. Overall, you have to fight hard for a good grade.
I think the average GPA speaks for itself. (2.5 for my section) I had to study for this more than my upper division classes. I'll be seeing this mofo in my nightmares for the next quarter...

I lowkey feel like his quizzes this year are significantly harder than the ones given before. My roommate gave me his quiz from last year to study with. So much easier than what I got. I thought the quizzes were going to be fine, since discussion problems weren't bad. Nah the quiz was significantly more difficult. I DO NOT RECOMMEND! MUST AVOID!!!!

I've never had this much trouble in this class. It's a flipped classroom and there's no room to succeed if you mess up. There's no support for this class, the TAs and Tutors literally gave me the wrong info about a few topics about 4 times.

Andrew Meyertholen is one of the worst professors I have ever had. He does not care about his students or seem to want them to pass. The discussions do not help at all, and despite being passionate about physics, he shows little regard for his students. He shows favoritism.

He is passionate about the subject but not the students. His tests never truly resemble the practice we did and his review sections helped little to none. Did everything he asked for and passing the class was barely manageable. He has used the same product the last 5 years and his grades this quarter show that he cant explain material well. Just no

The professor is quite nice in lectures. The professor gives extra videos before class to watch prior to every lecture, and during lecture, he gives iclicker questions and examples. Though the course is challenging overall.

4 quizzes make up 50% of the grade but you can drop one. final is 30%. he curves them to make them more in line with historical averages. lecture attendance is worth 3% (can't opt out) and lectures are podcasted. he loves physics.

4 quizzes, 50% of the overall grade, being test heavy. He curves each of the quizzes making the average 70%. The problem is that if u get the average, 70%, you will get a C. The good thing is that he gives extra credit if you score over the curved score. Overall he is great, various formulas for grade calculations, he is caring and nice.

Meyertholen really cares about his students, and is very generous with grades. Just do all the practice problems and quizzes he recommends, understand how to do all of them, and the class will be easy. Good lectures as well. I had never taken a physics class in my life before, but the class does not expect any background knowledge.
Amazing prof, great lectures, engaging and not boring at all, work is tough and exams are even tougher good luck freshmen :)

Professor Meyertholen is caring for his students and makes his lectures more engaging. He explains the answers of his in-class questions, which require explanations to help students apply. Students must listen to those and take more time to understand the concepts and the math. His quizzes are difficult, which is why he provides practice quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Meyertholen is a caring professor, and his lectures were clear. They mostly consisted of practice problems  because there are videos you're expected to watch before lecture. The quizzes were difficult, but not impossible, and they're curved. There are 4 quizzes & a final. He explains difficult concepts pretty clearly which I appreciate.

Dr. Meyertholen is clearly well-versed in his field, and did a decent job making difficult concepts easier to understand. He is very funny and everyone seemed to like him in class. Lectures were sometimes confusing and his handwriting is one of the worst I've ever seen. While his class was fun, I had a difficult time with the material.
Dr. Meyertholen is an amazing professor and is hilarious. His quizzes are not too hard and he does curve:) . Make sure you use all the resources he provides because they are really helpful.

I never had a physics background before his class, and he made it very fluid and understandable given that the material is overall difficult. He was very transparent, and always made lecture fun with some of his "brain breaks" and group discussion. He truly cares about his students understanding the material and doing well in class.

Meyertholen really cares about teaching. He explains things in multiple ways to make it easier to understand. He even takes the time to learn the names of students who speak up in class. He is extremely kind and very invested in his class.

One of the best physics professors ever. He simplifies the difficult concepts and makes his lectures engaging. Includes at least five minutes of break where he cracks jokes and lightens the environment. His pre-class videos are the most helpful in understanding content. His quizzes are hard but are fair. Homework is difficult but optional.

I'll be completely honest, he is a funny and caring guy but when it comes to actually teaching, his class is plain bad. He expects his students to read the textbook and watch the videos before class and treats his lecture as a review session. It's easy enough to get grades because of the curve but he doesn't even teach, at all.

Physics is already a hard subject but he makes it even more confusing like when he goes over clicker questions he flies by them and when u review them later, his handwriting sucks. Some questions on the tests are similar to clicker questions (which he uses to grade you on attendance) but he sometimes will ask you a question from past topics. -.-
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Meyertholen was a fun, caring guy and made lectures really interesting. If you have no prior physics knowledge, though, this class will be tough. I took AP Physics and still barely got an A in this class, but you get to drop one quiz out of four and the final was heavily curved. Lectures and discussions were mandatory, you will need an iClicker.

If you can, TAKE HIM! Physics is hard I mean at least for me they were. He makes hard topics understandable and he is very patient. He holds a lot of office hours and he actually wants us to learn. The quizzes are somewhat hard but he curved some. Recommend.

Prof. Physics is one of my favorite professors so far at UCSD. This class is not easy, but he is aware of that and gives students endless opportunities to do well. He always has office hours, disc & si sessions, and genuinely wants to see his students succeed. Barely any homework but a huge part grade is tough quizzes. He always curves though!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Meyertholen really understands how difficult physics can be. Although he does go through the course at a fast pace, he is always accessible in OH. I struggled with physics in high school but now I have a new appreciation for it and a better understanding. Furthermore he loves to take about 5 min of class to wake the class with some jokes.
Professor Meyertholen is a great professor. He is very caring, and is one of the best professors at UCSD. His lectures are also very helpful for note taking.

the class is not the easiest but Professor Meyertholen makes things very clear. Straightforward with his expectations. Exams are similar in difficulty and structure to homework - a huge plus so that exams are less scary. likes to add humor to his lectures which always makes things better.

Was truly one of the better physics professors I've had. The lectures were helpful and the homework only helped build on what we learned in class. Attendance is not mandatory but he does use clicker scores a small portion (around 3%) of the final grade. He also has a great sense of humor which he displays throughout lecture as a comedic relief.

I highly recommend Professor Andrew for taking PHYS 2A and 2B. He teaches good lectures and not that huge amount of homework. Although electricity is hard, he tried his best to teach it in a much easier way. Also he gives big curves which can boost everyone's grade. He is one of the best professor in UCSD.
He is a nice professor, really good at teaching and really understandable. Lectures are very helpful and big curve.

Dr. Andrew is definitely one of the best professor I had at UCSD. Up tp this point he is the only professor who can let me understand physics. Not much mandatory homework but there will be optional practices provided. Phys2B was a though class for me but Andrew is able to make me understand most of the contents. Also huge curves. 100% recommend.

Andrew is really a nice professor, he cares about students really much and is easy to reach out of class. His lecture is clear and attractive. the quiz covers the material during the lecture and is not out of bounds.

ADORE MR. PHYSICS! He definitely understands how hard physics can be and makes sure to add some fun into his lectures to help. He is very accessible outside of class and genuinely wants to see his students succeed. If you have the opportunity to take him, definitely do!

Meyertholen is an amazing professor who creates engaging lectures that often have a slide or two made to give everyone a laugh. His quizzes are a little difficult but if you know the material you should have no problem getting an A. Overall a really great guy and a fun class.

He is the greatest professor in the world. Andrew can always make my day because his lecture is pretty interesting and understandable, and he is pretty patient to explain everything about the physics after the class. If he could teach me through out all of my physics classes, I would transfer my major to physics immediately.

I took 12 APs in high school and failed 2, both are physics. Thought I would never understand E&M but Dr. Andrew explains everything clear. Gives past quizes which are reflective of real quizes. Not much HW but there are many practices availiable both during lectures and on Mastering Physics.
I had some basic knowledge. So, overall my course is smooth.

Quizzes are worth 50% of your grade so beware. He truly does care about his students though and is very accessible outside class for help. I am taking his again next quarter because I liked him so much.

i'm so sad to drop this class b/c i have to focus on my other one but i'm def taking him at a later time. i love his teaching style and he makes lectures so engaging. he also makes students excited to learn and adjusts to make the most of our learning

I love his teaching style. Students need to read the textbook before the class and finish clicker questions (graded by effort). Then, he will mainly give examples and solve them in the class, which is more helpful than using the lecture to teach all knowledge for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Definitely my favorite prof I've had at UCSD so far. Always went out of his way to make lectures engaging and his grading is very fair. Take his class if you have the chance!

Professor Meyertholen is a solid choice! He's funny and will listen and tailer to feedback! Quizzes are worth a lot and contains some tricky questions, but his "re-do" system made them less harsh. Not a lot of homework, but I would highly recommend doing the optional practice. Only thing I hated were the mandatory "study group" style discussions.
A very nice Professor. My blood pressure rises whenever I need to take physics, but Prof. "Hey Physics" made it way lower.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: discussion is mandatory & questions are due before each lecture. mastering physics & quizzes alternate each week, but he uses a 2-stage system where you correct your quizzes and can earn more points. his attitude towards physics and his students what i admire most; he's someone who genuinely wants to help his students succeed and pass the 2 series.
He truly cares about the students. Makes every effort to promote learning. Very accessible. I feel lucky to have taken an introductory course with Prof.M.
He is an incredible professor, everything was very understandable. Attendance is not mandatory for lecture but it is for discussion. I will 100% recommended, he is the best professor I had so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very understanding. Will cater material to the class and listen to feedback. Quizzes and test were representative of the material in lecture

Professor Meyertholen is one of the best professors I've had. He keeps class very lighthearted and he is extremely knowledgeable. He goes above and beyond for his students to help them understand the topics thoroughly. He does assign a lot of work, but it helps immensely with understanding the material. Highly recommend him if you're taking 2B.
great guy, good prof, don't worry if you fail the weekly quizzes, since there is a nice curve. attend section and do all of the homework to the best of your ability, it really helps

Professor Meyertholen is one of the most understanding and caring professors out there. He made many accommodations based on students' needs. His lectures are clear and easy to follow and he does a great job breaking down complicated concepts.
Probably one of the best professors in the Physics department. He gave us enough materials to be prepared for his class. Reading the textbook is recommended to pass his class but it is not needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Meyertholen is a fantastic teacher. His jokes make the lectures a lot more fun to go through, and he explains E&M in a way that is highly intuitive. In light of COVID-19 and BLM protests, he made all the appropriate accommodations and was very understanding. I would strongly recommend that you take him for PHYS 2B should he be available.

Professor Meyertholen really showed us how much he cares about his students throughout the quarter, he also explained everything very well. Weekly quizzes were all based on what he taught us in lectures. Of course, the material is kind of difficult but I believe he did a great job explaining it and we understood everything very well thanks to him.
Have pre-class questions and pre-class lectures, so lectures are clicker questions based and there is limited amount of hw. Great Prof! Super funny and sweet! Definitely take him!

BEST PROFESSOR EVER. EVER. I didn't do well in PHYS 2A and was expecting 2B to be about the same. Meyertholen has interesting lectures and a reasonable amount of work that make it easy to learn. That was the biggest thing for me, as someone who never took physics before college, i feel like im actually LEARNING which is kinda wild. take this class

I went from hating PHYS to loving PHYS in general because of this professor. His lectures were organized and helpful. He explained complicated concepts in PHYS in such a simple way that everyone could understand it. He gave out enough practice quizzes that could prepare you well for the date of the exams. Take him if you want to learn PHYS.
If you pour some time, you would get at least b. Generous curve.

I love Professor Meyertholen! I don't like Physics at all but he made Physics interesting to learn! He made this unusual home quarter amazing and would always listen to student input. He was extremely accommodating. His quizzes were difficult but definitely fair, no surprises, if you watch lectures, attend discussion, and understand the homework.
Best professor EVER!!! He is super sweet and caring to his students. I came to physics 2B expecting to take a fat L but he ended up making the class super fun and bearable! 1000% recommend

He really cares about his students and his lectures are to the point and clear. He also sends out surveys along the quarter to adapt his teaching and answer specific questions about lectures, so it feels like he wants to help everyone out. Overall the topics and the quizzes are still pretty hard, so you have to work a lot for a good grade.
All I have to say is, the curve is lovely and he is funny.
Great prof! He was heavy on us for the first 2 quizzes and then he adjusted his lectures and homework accordingly. Generous curve + interesting and useful lectures  100% take him again.

Great professor overall! If you put in the time and effort, you can be successful in any of his classes since he provides pre-lecture videos and thorough slides that are available online (along w video podcasts so lecture isn't mandatory if you don't need participation credit). Section was mandatory, but definitely beneficial in the end.

I absolutely love Prof Meyertholen. He made E&M feel way easier when everyone in the years above me were telling me it was going to be the hardest lower division class that I take. He made lectures clear and easy to understand, was extremely available to answer questions, and willing to adjust grading scales to help us succeed and do well!

Really nice and also very good at explaining things. He makes PHYS 2B less esoteric and more understandable by connecting it to everyday life. Mandatory discussion attendance, but the worksheets are actually pretty helpful. Homework wasn't mandatory and isn't necessary to do well in the class.

I joined this class feeling very insecure after getting wrecked by physics 2A and I just naturally hated this subject. However, this professor completely changed my mind and made me fall in love with E&M. Not gonna lie, I worked really hard and his exams are pretty challenging, but you will learn a lot. He is just an amazing lecturer no doubt.

This was Dr. Meyertholen's first quarter at UCSD and he was hands down one of the best professors ever. PHYS2B, without a doubt, is a pretty rough course, but Meyertholen makes his lectures down-to-Earth so the concepts are understandable. There is optional homework but I would recommend doing it for extra practice for quizzes. One of the best!!
Professor Meyertholen is a well respected professor.

Professor Meyertholen is one of the best physics professors here, his lectures are very engaging and clear. His pre-lecture videos are truly amazing. His quizzes and test are fair. Take him and he will make you love physics!

you can tell that meyertholen truly cares. even though his final and 4 quizzes (where you drop the lowest one) are difficult, he curves the class fairly to keep the class average reasonable. the material for 2b was still very challenging. he has mandatory iclicker (graded for participation not credit), discussion, and pre-lecture questions.

Came into 2B expecting a really bad time but Meyertholen made it pretty pleasant. He has videos which basically pick out all the important bits from the section and the examples drive home what you need to know for the quizzes which are a good difficulty level.

One of the best professor's I've ever had! Personally I am not good with physics but this guy made it very easy to understand. He really cares about teaching and knows his material very well. Great feedback when asking questions and quizzes are really fair if you put in the work.

Professor Meyertholen is an amazing professor and overall a really caring guy. It was his first quarter at UCSD and he wasnt confused or lost at all and gave great lectures. He posts everything on his course website so it makes it really easy to go back and study. He has mandatory pre class questions (homework) and clicker questions.
Really loved his class. Great sense of humor, and a really good instructor overall.
Such an awesome professor you will not regret taking him !!

He's awesome! He is super funny and nice. He can be very quiet so BE PREPARED TO LISTEN! Otherwise no complaints!!! Weekly quizzes and written assignments, but they are easy as long as you pay attention to lecture and read! The tests are super easy and very similar to the quizzes. Material workload may seem intimidating but they really aren't :)
This professor has changed the way I view the world. His lectures truly changed my way of thinking and perspective on others. I could not recommend him more. He is so funny and I loved his class.

Please take a course taught by Dr. Dykmans. His class was the most enjoyable and eye opening course Ive ever taken! Prof Dymans has a great sense of humor and you can feel his fun personality and passion in his lectures and slides! I learned a lot, laughed a lot and had fun EVERY lecture. Show up, study the slides and you're golden!

Great professor for it being an online course! We were to submit a super easy and short assignment weekly, quizzes were short and simple & test are based off a lot of the requiered readings, quizzes and lecture videos. Overall, super easy course and great professor!

Professor Dykmans is super cool and is a great guy. His course psychology 110 is intro level but was interesting and his lectures and discussions made it fun to both attend and watch. My class was asynchronous but we did have a discussion every week that wasn't mandatory. Overall it was a fun class with a great professor.

He is upfront about grading criteria and provides many opportunities to improve. Material is fun to learn with his media and powerpoints. Prof Dykmans is passionate about the subject and enjoys discussing details with students. Readily available outside of class for questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I cannot recommend Neal enough. He's funny without trying to be, teaches you a lot and really makes them memorable with plenty of videos or photos to supplement concepts. His tests are very fair and he's just a really cool professor in general. Also speaks 5 languages, how insane is that. He also teaches you how to analyze research articles well.

Professor Dykmans is one of my favorite professors!! He teaches in a very memorable, engaging, and interesting way. His lecture style helps me not only learn but actually remember the information. Very clear about expectations for the exams. The textbook is a helpful supplement. Definitely take his class if you can.
Super nice professor with great visuals to accompany his material!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Neal is a great professor who is super knowledgeable about the topics we discuss in class. He provides a lot of real-world examples that make the content more memorable and he loves sharing additional material for people to look at if there's anything in class that sparks further interest. He also is very responsive to students and super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: I took professor Dykman @CSU San Marcos and loved him! He is so passionate about this subject & makes the lectures very enjoyable. He truly cares and wants to see his students succeed. Attendance isnt madatory, but he gives out pop quizzes, and exams are solely based off lecture so it is in your best intrest to attend. Wish I could take him again!

Professor Neal is amazing. He is passionate about the subject matter and isnt the type of professor that believes his subject matter has no errors. He is always telling students to not believe everything they see or hear from the scientific community. Even if you dont need to take any of his classes to graduate, take a class with him.
I miss you. Come back

He's really funny and chill because he lets us use any notes we want during the quizzes/final. He offers us extra credit after every quiz and one homework extension. There are biweekly quizzes and weekly homework. He is a good lecturer and responds quickly on piazza. He also has zoom and recordings of the lectures if you can't make it to class.

My grade was due to a few missing homework assignments, but he gives extensions when asked within a reasonable amount of time. No midterms, just homework due every Sunday. The final was really difficult, however a lot of the homework problem and previous quizzes were on it just reworded or reworked. Allows digital notes and previous quizzes.

He was chill, attendance not mandatory, recorded lectures, and also via zoom. Had 4 quizzes every 2 weeks with 8 questions. Only bad thing is if you literally get 3 question wrong you're screwed. Hw is worth the most, 25%. Final can replace your lowest quiz score. He gave 0.5 bonus points after every quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I literally hate physics and he made me like it. He really went out of his way to make it really applicable to biology and help us understand why we'd ever need to know this. Explained things SO well with the time that he had
It's such a shame that he won't be coming back for the next quarter, cause he's literally the best professor I've ever had.

Same structure as PHYS 1A with Dylan. 8 question quizzes every two weeks with a final "exam" that is the same weight as the bi-weekly quizzes. Homework is due every week, but the load of homework differs week to week. Definitely harder than PHYS 1A, but I'm glad I took it with Dylan!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: GOAT
One of the best teachers at ucsd. He teaches physics super well and is always available out of class to answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved having him! Wish UCSD gave him more classes so we could finish the 1A series with him :(
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Definitely one of the best professors I've had at UCSD so far. He was very good at explaining the material, and made the class extremely accessible (lectures weren't mandatory, and you had the choice of attending lecture in person, on zoom, or just watching the recording). His short piazza response times were super helpful. Take him if you can!
LOVE HIM!!! He's seriously the best, I wish he was teaching 1C as well so I could take his class. 1B is significantly harder than 1A in my opinion, but if you put in the work, you will do well.

The best physics prof ever!!! He makes everything easy to learn and I enjoy it despite being nervous about taking physics in the first place. Very lenient policies and answers Piazza questions in literally 2 minutes. If you have the chance, take his class.

Caring professor and gives very straightforward lectures. The class is based on four quizzes and a final; the final can replace one of the quizzes if you do better. The quizzes are open notes/homework/practice problems, so as long as you do everything, there's no stress.

Professor Gilbert is very caring and amazing! Open note quizzes every other week, and homework is manageable. His response time to questions is amazing, and he answers very thoroughly. The quizzes are based on lecture and homework content, and his tests are designed very clearly. He also podcasts and zooms the lectures, and is very accommodating.

Professor Gilbert is a great Physics instructor! His exams are like practice exams and he even adds in-class questions to the exams. He makes attending class accessible as you can watch it online or in person. Overall, I recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Gilbert is the best! He keeps lectures light-hearted and has a lot of practice problems to make sure students understand different applications of the material. Make sure your notes are thorough and keep track of all equations, you can use them on the quizzes!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Gilbert is the best physics professor, possibly the best professor that I've had at UCSD. His exams are fair, and he also gives a bonus question for a chance to get points back. He responds to questions on Piazza within minutes. His class policies are also very lenient. Definitely take his class if you have the chance to!

Great professor for those who have not taken a physics class prior to PHYS 1A! Homework is due every week on Kudu; each week's amount of homework varies. Grade is made up of four quizzes throughout the quarter instead of midterms, homework due sundays, and a final at the end. You can make your own cheat sheet, and bring whatever you want to tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is great. He does his best to help everyone

The best professor I've ever had, ever, not just for physics. His expectations are clear from the beginning. All of the exams are open notes--you can literally bring your iPad/laptop to class and have thousands of pages of notes if you wanted to. Replies to Piazza questions in under 2 mins, even at 3 AM. Take him. Take him!

Dr Dylan is the gem of physics department at UCSD. He is super accessible outside the class and all his advices are really helpful. I would say whatever he says on the first day of class is really to be implemented to get good scores in his class. He teaches the real way to learn physics rather than memorizing everything.
Gilbert's the GOAT! I am terrible at math, terrible at STEM, but he formats the class in a way that you can still get a good grade. Super understanding dude that you can tell really enjoys physics

Phys 2b was a hard class, but professor Gilbert made it better. He is a very nice and understanding person, and you can tell that he truly cares about his students. I had him for the summer session and even though the class was super fast and quizzes were every week, his examinations were fair. (Super accessible outside of class and huge curve too)

The best lecturer! I came into this class with 0 experience in physics and Dylan made everything so easy to understand. He's super accessible outside of class, answers piazza and emails almost immediately (even on weekends) and his quizzes are reflective of the course content, homework, and practice quizzes. I recommend him to everyone!
Lectures hold your attention, quizzes every two weeks but practice quizzes help a lot. Homework and quizzes are representative of material. Dylan is funny and seems like a very caring professor.

LOML. Open note/open book quizzes (4) and final. Super good at explaining complicated physics concepts and quiz questions are clear and designed to be straightforward and simple. Truly just tests on your understanding of physics concepts, not ability to take a hard test. If you have the option to take Dylan, TAKE HIM. You will not be sorry.

This is a very lecture-heavy class. Has a quiz every other week, homework, and the final. He gives practice quizzes but the level of difficulty is not the same. Homework was easy points as you have unlimited attempts. Overall a great professor, would definitely recommend understanding the concepts and not just memorizing equations for the quizzes.

Solid prof 4 quizzes 15% each. Theyre pretty easy if you listen in lecture and take some notes. There's also .5 point extra cred probs on these which is clutch. Homework is unlimited tries weekly worth 25% grade. Final is 15% unless you drop a bad quiz score then its 30%. Prof is nice and teaches physics very well. lectures make me kinda sleepy tho
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Gilbert literally one of the best professors I've had. Totally chill dude and everything that he teaches is clear. Overall great person and professor.
hes a pie and cares about his students. 10/10
clear lectures, very nice guy, quizzes every two weeks but very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor was absolutely engaged with the class. His exams were reflective of the material learned, and practice quizzes were usually harder than the quizzes themselves. Going to lecture is vital, but he is almost always available on Piazza or in person after lecture for you to ask questions. Taking good notes is highly recommended!

Lectures were amazing and he podcasted them and even had a live zoom link to attend in real time. The grade is 4 quizzes, the final, and homework. He goes slow and you can really learn physics and equations in this class. He allowed notes for the quizzes so we could have all the formulas down.

Taking him at the moment and he has been one of the best professors I have had. Makes physics easy to understand and provides necessary examples. Explains his steps, and lecture may get boring however the material needed to learn is really good. 4 Quizzes, 8 problems and reflected the practice quizzes. Homework is not too hard long.

BORING AF!

Dude just comes up with a powerpoint and doesn't interact with the students. Whole calssroom fell asleep

Very laid-back and chill professor. Explained concepts well and interesting lectures. Biweekly exams were mostly straightforward, but only 7 MC questions. He graded fairly and gave free points / curved two of them.
One exam dropped if it helped + final grades curved slightly to boost us. He also usually replied within minutes on Piazza.
Good lectures but grade is heavily based on quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Caution: the majority of reviews are from bitter or adoring students. Dylan Gilbert may have a monotone voice, but he is quick witted and caring. His lecture style is digestible: he repeats phrases with different wording, he often brings up common misconceptions, etc. His exams reflect LE and HW. 6 scantrons cost me $1.87 after tax. Book+HW: $50 :)

PHYS 2B is definitely challenging, but Dylan makes it so much easier. The lectures are clear and concise especially considering how fast paced the class gets in the summer. Dylan's class policies are incredible, he prioritizes understanding over chasing grades. He is crazy responsive on Piazza (3 min replies), sometimes even at 3am.

Dylan is a great professor! He's very kind and always available to help. He answers questions on Piazza extremely fast and his homework is pretty easy. The homework and practice exams help prepare you for the quizzes but the material covered is still pretty difficult. Going to office hours should help. I highly recommend this professor!

Dylan was a great physics professor! Honestly my favorite one so far! I honestly think the physics department, in general, should restructure the PHYS 1 series because I personally think Kudu is a horrible textbook. Dylan gave you everything you needed for the quizzes. Homework is pretty straightforward if you attend lectures or watch the podcasts.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lazy was the best way to put it. Lectures are monotone and boring. The quizzes are only 7 questions to reflect 2 weeks of material. Hardly reflect the things you learn. The final is 18 questions given the 3 hours to take it. Both quizzes and final require your own scantron. Waste of money to only fill in 7 bubbles.
I love him

Professor Kern is a nice instructor in general. He clearly explains everything and is well known as being fair when it comes to grading and evaluations. His lectures are very detailed and often heavy but very engaging. I loved his class but if you skip class, you will not pass. Overall, very inspirational and cool guy.

Professor Kern is great. When I say that it is a level 5.0 difficulty, I do not mean professor Kern is difficult. I simply mean the class is very challenging and is a very high level class. Need to have a high level understanding of POLS and IR to be successful honestly. You should be a junior or senior to take this class. Great professor!

Dr. Kern is an excellent professor. He is clear and direct which is helpful. However, if you skip class you will not pass. Expects quality work but understands if students are struggling and will help them!

Professor Kern is truly amazing! He really does care about how you do in the class and if you are fully understanding the material. The class is sometimes difficult however, professor Kern makes it up with his cringey political science jokes. Best prof I've ever had! Take him if you have the chance!
Go to the classes and you would be fine. He uses examples from the textbook word for word on exams. He doesn't curve each test, he curves the final grade. Trust me its better that way.

Professor Ebrahimi is one of the best math teachers out there! He does a thorough job explaining the concepts in class, teaches straight out of the book, and he is EXTREMELY generous with grading on quizzes and the final as long what you show is correct. He help you understand what's covered in class. Hw counts too. He curves at the end. Take him!
He is the one that's all I can tell. Funny accent and attitude.
He is the one that's all I can tell. Funny accent and attitude.
A little rusty at first, but improved really well throughout. By now he's taught more classes, he'll be much better by now. Tests were straightforward, as he says. Goes in the right pace.  :)
He's pretty chill. His tests are not hard and very similar to the HW.

Great professor. Explained concepts clearly using interesting examples and youtube videos. Very approachable and nice guy. Two midterms and a final exam. Straight forward tests if you studied the review sheets given out in section. Overall, a highly recommended professor!
He was a good professor! Midterms and final were straightforward and only on the content he lectured in class. Awesome TAs.

For every midterm, he posted study guides, worksheets, chapter summaries and previous exams with answers. His lectures were very fun and engaging and his TAs were very helpful. He's my favorite professor I've had so far!

He is the GREATEST BIO PROFESSOR EVER!!!!! So damn lucky I got his class my first quarter! Very helpful! His class is pretty easy if you review his lectures and review sheets he gives out before every test. If you know whats on the review sheets, you'll pass his test NO DOUBT!Love Dr. Goodale!!!XD I hope yo have him in the future!!!XD

He is very enthusiastic about the class which makes it interesting and enjoyable. Grades fair, with a curve if the median is below 80%. Get points for attending class and using clicker. However, each TA teaches section differently so you may have your quiz before or after discussion. That being the worst part, his class is the best ! Love Dr. Eben

Very nice professor, seems really enthusiastic about teaching. I found his final slightly disorganized, a few questions were unclear. He used clicker questions, but you can still miss a couple lectures and get full participation credit. Very do-able class if you keep up with the material. I like that he stresses the key points frequently.

Extremely knowleagable professor who worked hard  and I really liked the lectures. This is not a class for whimps who do not like to take their work seriously. But if you are really interested in learning and expanding your knowledge about the living world I highly recommend it!

There's a lot of material for this class, and I believe that he actually explained them thoroughly. Midterms are NOT hard. Just long for a 1 hr class. Gives out review sheets for each midterm; know them=easy A.

A friendly professor, but he doesn't seem too knowledgeable. Could be he's nervous in front of a large group. Likes to play games like assigning work right before a three-day weekend and acting smug. Tests are pretty damn hard too, I hope you're ready to love bio. I'd take it with someone else.

This guy seems nice, but he isn't a good professor.  His lectures are really boring and he had a lot of incorrect information on his slides throughout the semester.  Take this class with someone else if you can.

He was ok. Lectures were just him going over research papers that were assigned for the day. Attendance is tracked through a quiz that tested you on the reading. The biggest part of your grade is your research project, and he will not hold back on telling you how bad your project is.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Does not care about students. huge ego
The worst professor I have had at UCSD. Earlence does not seem to care about their students at all.
He is a good professor and his office hours are useful
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: So far the best ECE professor I've had at UCSD. Amazing lecture which prepared me well in the following courses. If you want to get a good grade in his class, besides working your ass off, you have to understand the material well. ALL EXAMS ARE TESTING THE TRUE UNDERSTANDING OF COURSE MATERIAL. BE PREPARED.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hardest class I've ever taken, but great professor who genuinely wants to help you learn the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Ford emphasized the basics for longer than previously, which made the harder portion of the class much easier. His office hours are awesome and are a very good time to get almost one on one problem solving help. He is there to help you understand if you ask.    He has changed his format of teaching the class since 2010, it is better now

The ECE35 curriculum at UCSD is standardized across all professors, and a lot of how you do is just how much you practice, so I can't really say much about his teaching methods. He's a nice guy though. Kind of a warm grandpa type. Very hard to stay awake in lectures
Avoid if possible failed his class in the winter took again in the spring with Xiang got an A+
always late to class!! puts material on exams that are not covered in class. Exam questions are difficult
Very tricky questions....u think you know it then your like wtf. I suggest you take Xiang! His average was much higher

He represents what I hate about a large set of teachers engineering teachers at UCSD. They truly are not considerate or motivating individuals. The trick to this class is to not fall behind the material. Weekly quizzes. Pretty tough labs.

I can understand that he's not a circuits engineer professionally. However, I find it rather annoying that he is unable to finish problems in class. He's consistently late to class. He wanted to challenge us and knowingly gave us a very long exam, too long. He's not too difficult, most of the time.
Not his strong class per se, he's a photonics guy, but taught well enough.

I found that she explained things well enough but was not clear AT ALL what would be graded on the test. I think the fact that our midterm 2 grades were higher than the midterm 1 grades is indicative of that. Grades were about hitting specific keywords, not so much about knowing the concept.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All non-cumulative: 2 midterms, weekly quizzes + readings (hw), and final. Going to 9/14 lectures gives 6% grade boost. It was unclear what she was emphasizing in lecture bc she would explain small details rather than overall picture. My tip: understand ALL diagrams/equations, tests will ask u to draw/interpret them. Exams based on memorization.

Grades are made up of weekly quizzes and 3 exams including finals. Expects "professional" answers on the exams and was basically all FRQ. Takes a very long time to grade exams and doesn't give feedback on time. Attendance is extra credit, so there's that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her exams are nothing like the lectures, really difficult with unclear free-response questions. She deducts points if answers aren't “professional enough,” even when they're correct. Fill-in-the-blanks with no word bank. Overall you'll just stress without learning. Avoid her to protect your GPA and mental health.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you take this professor, expect the syllabus and even the webreg listing to be ignored. She will drastically change her expectations for students with little warning. She even completely changed the format and requirements of the final, after the drop deadlines had already passed.

I took this class to fulfill a GE requirement. Grading relied on attendance, class discussion, and 16 short, one-page papers based on readings, but the criteria were unclear and subjective. Lectures were boring, and discussions often strayed off-topic. Many required books needed to be purchased. Overall, it was an easy and manageable class.

Professor Dubois has an engaging teaching style, though the lack of slides or recordings can make it challenging to follow at times. Attending lectures and using resources like unstuck AI for exam prep are key to success in this class.

Every class was a fight not to fall asleep. I did not learn all that much from her lectures-- she has a characteristic monotone voice that made everything more boring, even if she was fun sometimes. Attendance isn't mandatory, but she doesn't post recordings. Her exams also required good knowledge of the contents of every reading assigned.

Her lectures were boring and monotonous. She didn't use slideshows and read facts from a page, usually in a disorganized manner, and in a monotonous tone. It was hard to stay engaged for whole 80 minute lectures. She focused on the topic of sex more than any other professor I've had, and I suspect most hype she has going for her is due to that.

The obvious cons for Professor Dubois is that she doesn't use PowerPoint or podcasts her lectures, but she lectures in a slow and concise way with outlines and clear transitions to different topics that makes note taking easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Even though Professor Dubois doesn't use slideshows lectures and she doesn't do podcasts, I still got all the information I needed from her lectures, and if you're on the fence because of this, you can sit near the speaker/front and use a voice recorder; although I never needed them. She talks slowly, so it's easy to type what she says.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. DuBois is a great professor. However, she doesn't podcast, record lectures, or upload images. So while attendance isn't mandatory, I'd advise you to go. Your grade is pretty much dependent on your TA. There are no other assignments besides the midterm and final, so your grade is easily broken depending on how you do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Du Bois has really interesting lectures, but because she doesn't use slides they are hard to follow at certain points. There is a lot of material to be familiar with (as with any mmw) and at times what she wants isn't always super clear. She's super passionate about what she teaches and loves if you ask questions and engage with her.

Lectures have a bunch of information but are pretty monotone and boring as the Professor just reads and talks for the most part. Not a lot of information is important or useful. Lectures are not recorded but a midterm review document is shared before the midterm. Lot of information to learn for the exams and not a lot of time to write it in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So funny and so queen! She doesn't talk THAT much about sex to be honest and when she does it is refreshing and fun. Attendance is not mandatory, but do NOT skip because she goes over basically everything in the readings and does not post lectures afterwards. Study guides given for midterm and final was basically everything on the exam. Super easy.

She was hard to follow because she doesn't use slides. she was very nice & funny. Grade was based on discussion, one midterm, and one final. No assignments, the only thing she assigns is readings, which are covered in class. Gives study guides which were almost identical to the exams. Overall was an easy A if you attend lectures and actually study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Dubois is very knowledgeable and knows what she is talking about. Your grade is based on discussion participation, one midterm, and the final. She doesn't use slides so lectures can be hard to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are incredibly boring, no powerpoints, just her faint voice buzzing in the background for an hour and 20 minutes. She spends an ungodly amount of time talking about sex in different cultures/regions. The textbook is NOT a substitute for lecture, attend your sections regularly to have any remote chance of getting a high grade. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: she has made her class harder in comparison to years. i would not take her unless you have to pick between her and chang then take her. Other than that take someone else. She gives exams and other professors give only essays. would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
She hates technology and refuses to podcast her lectures or use slides with bullet points/images. She's not an outstanding lecturer, so you are going to zone out because lectures are just her talking for an hour. 
One good thing is that she doesn't require attendance, and tbh, if you do the readings and don't go to lectures, you'll be fine.

Professor Dubois is the most caring professor and the best MMW professor out of all of them. The best outfit choices, amazing study guides for tests, and had great TAs. She put thought into every lecture and touched on interesting subjects for each time period. Graded on one midterm and final which both have clear study guides and grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dubois is an amazing lecturer! She does not use a powerpoint so you do need to pay attention and attend class. She does go over everything you will need for the midterm and final. Your grade will depend a lot of your TA because they do the grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor DuBois is generally a great lecturer. The midterm and final are writing heavy, but she gives out a good study guide. She does talk a lot about sex and is more critical of some ancient religions than others. Reading can be dull, but it's all covered in the lectures. Your TA will really make or break your experience.

Horrible professor, her lectures did not have podcast recordings or did she use slides. All her lectures were listening to her speak about history and you could barely understand her. Midterm was difficult, a lot of memorization was required of art pictures and vocabulary. The final was easy it was an essay that was graded by TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
This is likely going to be your only option. 
She does not use slides during her lectures. Jumps around different topics. Monotone, dull. No sugarcoating of sex, etc. 
TAs grade everything; I had a great TA. Discussions take attendance, lectures don't. 
Lots of reading, she provides the primary texts/sources, but you have to buy the textbooks.

Great Prof! Easy if starting the MMW series and sets very well with the rest. I recommend Dubois for MMW 11, Balgerg for 12, Murillo for 13, and 14 and 15 (Dr. Grey) during the summer! I passed them with an A or B+ without much effort!
The grading is dependent on your TA. Unfortunately, sometimes the readings did not align with the essays very well.

Her lectures are brutal. She doesn't use slides, she just talks and it's impossible to follow what she is saying for 80 mins. The grade depends COMPLETELY on your TA. The good thing is no tests (compared to chang). Her essay prompts weren't hard. You do have to do the reading and its a lot.

The most boring lectures I've ever been to. It's impossible to stay awake for more than 30 minutes. Her voice is very monotone and talks very fast, not clearly and low in volume. It was a struggle but made my other classes much more enjoyable

duBois is clearly very knowledgable on the topics she is lecturing about, but she doesn't use slides so you really have to pay attention to what she is saying and lectures can often get boring. TA's do all the grading, but there are only 2 critical analyses and a slightly longer final essay. duBois has amazing fashion sense (an added bonus)

Professor DuBois was one of the best professors ever! Although she is very lecture heavy, she was sometimes pretty funny and is always passionate about what she is lecturing about. Although going to lectures is not mandatory, you should go to take notes because they will be important for the papers. The TA's do most of the work grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: TAs do most of the work i had the best one (in my opinion they were very sweet) two critical analysis and a final, duBois was also very sweet I loved how she didn't sugar coat the sex aspect of history, she said it how it was. Clearly very passionate about what she was teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The most solid choice for mmw11. Her essay prompts are the fairest (no tests) and lectures can sometimes be all over the place, but it's ok. It really depends on your TA, mine was harsh, but others were an easy A. I actually read the textbook which helped because it made the essays so much easier to write and I didn't have to cram for them.

Professor DuBois is clearly very knowledgeable, and she often talks about sex in interesting ways. However, I often find myself bored in her class and unable to concentrate for too long. She also talks slowly then quickly. The grades really depend on your TA, and mine assigned lots of hw while others didn't, but overall it wasn't hard to get an A.

She's pretty cool, you can definitely skip lectures and be fine. It all comes down to TAs!! The TAs all grade papers differently, and those are what determine your grade in the class. Easy class as long as you do well on the papers (two midterms and one final).

This professor is the complete opposite of the rigorous MMW I've heard about. A professor that has very interesting outfit choices, with lectures that contain interesting vocabulary about intercourse. We wrote 3 essays the entire quarter, and they weren't really hard at all. Lectures and readings aren't really mandatory. Take class for easy A.

Your grade in the class really depends on how the TA grades your two critical analysis + final. My TA did not read my essay thoroughly, ended up giving me a low score that I had fixed. duBoiss lectures are very lengthy, but she is funny - however, sometimes she starts slurring and I miss out on who exactly or what she is talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: I love her. Her lectures are inspirational and so are a lot of the readings. She made me not hate history anymore. TA's do all of the grading but if you show up to their office hours they go easy on you in my experience. The analysis essays are rough sometimes but you get used to them. Great professor, just pray you get an easy TA.
Final made me angry and frustrated that's all I'll say.

Honestly, she's a really nice professor but like others mentioned, TAs basically do everything. Her lectures are not very interesting and sometimes leaves me confused about what she's talking about. I thought her final exam was a bit unfair.. it was 2 essays "designed to be 3 hrs long" but she asked for detailed citations and 2000 words max

Really hands off and lets your TA take everything, thoroughly enjoys what shes teaching and you can tell how knowledgeable she is from the lectures (which I did watch in 2x speed), wish I had more direct contact with her though :/ CAs are hard at first to figure out what they want but it gets better :,)

If you're taking this online, there's very little work. You'll write a total of 5 analysis essays and write a weekly discussion post. The TA does all the grading so get to know them. You really don't need to read from the textbook. The discussion questions often come from the book she wrote (Longman). Read those texts and you'll pass with an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's honestly an amazing professor; you can really tell she cares about her students success. Her midterms and final are super reasonable as they reflect the content learned in class. Just study off her study guide! She lectures with no slides but pay attention to the pictures at the end! Also - participate in TA, this was what brought me to an A-

I absolutely loved DuBois for MMW 11. Her lectures were awesome, and had a soothing voice that for some reason made me pay attention. She posts study guides for the midterm and final, and has fairly minimal reading. She doesn't podcast, but I wouldn't skip lectures for anything. She really puts her all into her teaching, and you can feel it
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Her lectures were pretty boring and a little bit confusing. She doesn't really explain and develop the ideas very well, just throws a bunch of terms at you. This made studying for the tests more difficult because I had to look everything up. You can get a good grade if you just go to lecture and do the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: old school lecture style, but keeps it interesting. not too much reading and provides an in-depth study guide. Tests are short and sweet, easy a if you study

Prof DuBois is a caring professor who is humorous and easy-going. Her lectures are not the best and can get boring sometimes. Grades are determined by 2 tests (a midterm and a final) and discussion section participation. The tests are not hard if you study for them since she post very detailed study guides a week before.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DuBois's class was easy and I learned a lot. She gives a clear cut study guide for both the midterm and the final which are the outline of the exam. I didn't do a lot of readings, but I attended every lecture and took detailed notes. Lecture is important because some terms that are on the study guide were defined in class, but are not in the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class was graded upon 3 things. The Midterm, Final, and Participation in the discussion section. She gives out a study guide before the midterm and final, and all you really need to do is memorize what is on it and you'll get an A.

Professor DuBois is great. Even though it's a lot of content and it was sometimes hard to pay attention to what she said, her slow pace was really good and made the subject easier to grasp. Her tests were heavily based on the readings. They weren't hard tho, very straight forward and if you read you'll get an A. Office Hours --> she is amazing!
