reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dubois's class is very lecture heavy, however you don't need to go to do well in the class because she gives clear study guides for tests. Lectures can be boring, but interesting if you engage. The final is a lot harder than the midterm, so I suggest studying hard to do well on the midterm so that you have some leeway with the final!

There's alot of say regarding how her tests are easy and such, BUT there are some things you guys should take into account. The classes are all curved so even if you get a professor that is a hard grader, he won't let the class grade average be a D-. Just keep that in mind. Personally, the way she talks didn't suit me at all. Way too slow.

She doesn't use PowerPoints or any visual learning tools during her lecture. She does speaks with a clear voice and always made the lecture engaging. She does makes sexual references but it's all academic. Overall, she's a pretty cool teacher and I wish she teaches MMW 12 too. Definitely will take her again.

Dubois is definitely the easiest MMW11 professor. She doesnt use powerpoint and just talks for the entire class but her lectures are identical to the readings. Her discussion sections are participation based so attendance is mandatory for those but lectures are definitely optional. Exams are straightfoward and follow the study guides closely.

Dubois is a spunky woman. She's really easy, one midterm that's not bad, and the final isn't bad either. Her lectures can be boring but pay attention whenever she mentions a reading because those will be the readings that come up on the test. Her outfits are always on point. She talks about sex a lot too

Lectures seriously lull you to sleep but its important to pay attention because she doesn't have Powerpoint slides or anything. Previous reviews about her talking about sex are accurate, she somehow manages to talk about it every single lecture lol. Midterms and final well represented in her study guides

I am providing this rating because as a student, I was able to provide my experiences I've had in college to her and she said she felt she gained a new insight of how the students feel. She also explained that she would love to get to know her students well, but working in a big classroom is difficult. She is an amazing individual overall.

Prof Dubois is really nice but her lectures consist of her talking upfront with no slides or anything so it can be a little hard to pay attention. Attendance is mandatory because she does pop quizzes to test you on the readings. Graded on an 8-10 page paper that can be written about anything as long as it relates to greek and roman mythology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Learning Greek and Roman mythology was a wonderful journey! Her lectures go over and analyze the required readings, and occasionally she'll have one question pop quizzes to see if you did the reading. Grade was based on a single 8-10 page paper of any topic, as long it was mythology-related. Kind, passionate, and raises many interesting topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: I just love her so much. Prof. duBois is awesome. If you pay attention, you'll learn a lot. She is so knowledgeable in literature. So inspirational. So cute. I wish I can just be like that. Some think she's really weird because she talks about sex A LOT. It's not her fault. It's just what ancient Greece is. PS Her outfits are very nice. Artistic.

Straightforward, doesn't throw curveballs for midterms, and is extremely nice! Lectures can get boring, but she does write all the key terms on the board so as long as you know those and read all the primary source passages(poems/holy texts/etc) you should get a good grade on her tests. You can get away with not reading if you attend lecture.

Professor duBois is a very nice woman. She really does care about her students; just go to her office hours for that. She will help with whatll be on the midterm/final. Just be careful with your TA because they can be very tough graders. Her study guides are explicit and you will have a set of directions of what she wants on the tests.

She's really funny and keeps the lectures interesting. However, you don't really need to attend the lectures to pass the class. The midterm review is extremely similar to the actual midterm. Doesn't assign homework other than the readings. Talks about sex A LOT (but its chill).

DuBois is one of my favorite professors for MMW. Her lecture style is old school, as she stands in the front of the room and talks, but she is a really funny professor and helps the material "come to life". Dubois is VERY clear about what was on the midterm and final. As long as you are willing to study the study guide, it should be an easy A.

Nice professor, but the lectures were very scattered and all over the place. The class consisted of weekly quizzes and a paper on something with mythology which isn't too difficult but if you actually want to learn something I do not recommend.  Left more confused about mythology than I began.

Professor DuBois is a great MMW professor. In lecture she writes key terms on the board and those are pretty much all you need to know to ace the midterm and final. I found her lectures to be interesting and funny.

Grade entirely up to TA, but you're at least guaranteed a B. Lectures are unorganized compared to other professors and it's so easy to fall asleep, but the class is fair. Midterm and final were exactly like study guide, only hard part is IDing passages (you better read), but you can get away with cramming. There's extra credit. Has cool outfits.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Don't go to lectures. She's SO dull. You can ace the class just by reading the pages she assigns,STUDYING the study guides,and attending discussion (mandatory). Grade determined by TA. 1 midterm and 1 final (not cumulative). ALL memorization of the history content. Takes effort to study and read but def. the easiest mmw professor, HANDS DOWN
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Your grades totally depends on your TA, but the exams were fairly easily if you studied the exam guide.    BTW, the extra credit did help your final grade.

Professor DuBois is the BEST professor I've had in UCSD. She is such a nice and classy old lady. We all love her looks! Her level of knowledge is phenomenon. She is respected by all the students. I'm so honored to be her student in MMW 11. Although the lectures are really heavy and require active attention, they are so great by her!
The lectures were overall so boring.. Tests are fair
She's everything I aspire to be as an old woman. Midterm is so easy, final's pretty easy. Just read the readings and attend most of the classes, this should be an easy A.

I really loved her lectures. Her voice was actually good to listen for me lol. Your grade will definitely depend on your TA.  The final was alright. Wasn't as easy as the midterm. For Longman, you can just skip the texts and focus on the passages and you'll be fine. The midterm was just like the study guide. Make sure you pay attention.

It seems like you'd either love or dislike her. I wasn't a big fan of her lectures since she doesn't use powerpoint slides and her voice makes me fall asleep. Her lectures are basically the textbook readings with some added details. Had a lot less readings than my friends in Herbst's. Midterm was easy and final was alright though.

There was a final this quarter. And it kinda sucked cuz it wasn't just like the study guide so make sure you don't piss her off by not going to lecture or something. Your grade depends on your TA (my TA was so harsh :c  ) but in general, everyone hates mmw.
Super easy. Midterms exactly like studyguide. You don't have to show up to class or even do the reading. Regarding grading however, it's really up to which TA you get.
She is so funny and I really enjoy going to her class.

Basically, just do all the reading and its an easy A. She did not even require us to take the final the quarter I took her. She allowed us to base our grade off simply the midterm and discussion participation.
Professor Dubois is one of the best professors that I've had the opportunity to study with.  her scope of knowledge is impressive.

Dr. Dubois is an incredible professor. Her lectures are engaging and the course material is good as well. She will whip you into shape if you fall asleep or are disrespectful in class so make sure to pay attention and participate. She also has been great in helping me get credit for the class after I had to leave to get back surgery.

She is an extremely nice person. Just make sure not to yawn in class or anything like that or she will call you out. It is a little difficult since her lectures were a little dull. But overall, an easy class. I didn't even have to take the final because she made it optional.

I felt a little guilty about having Dubois for MMW while watching the other students have to do real work for the other MMW professors.  Nevertheless, I was extremely pleased to be taught by Dubois because 1) the midterm was very easy if you paid any attention to lectures and 2) the final was optional this quarter.  Mandatory discussions, of course

Professor DuBois is a kind woman who is passionate about MMW. Her lectures might be a little long because of her lulling voice, but you learn a lot from the class. She's very lenient, even making the final optional. Overall, I recommend this professor if you want to get an easy grade while still thoroughly learning the material.

Easiest A you could get at UCSD. Don't show up to class (seriously don't. Most boring lectures I've ever been to).. Just study her study guide WHICH IS EXACTLY THE MIDTERM WORD FOR WORD, and ace it. She let people who were happy with their grades not take the final this year!
She's the best. The midterms are like hugs, and the finals are like kisses.

After taking this class, now I have understood the ridiculously complicated relationships among the Greek gods. She explains the text very well. Here's a suggestion to get an A in this class. First attend her lecture and write down everything subtle. Working hard for the midterm, and use your imagination to analyze the text rationally

Professor duBois is really funny and her lectures are extremely interesting. She's really sassy and her fashion is adorable, especially her Pokemon skirt. She makes lectures fun and enjoyable and points students out when they talk or leave class. Also, her exams are exactly like her study guides. All ERC students should take duBois for mmw 11. :)

I had Prof. DuBois quite a while ago.  She was very funny and eccentric, which made this much more than your average male-centric mythology course. I liked her refreshing approach. (Not sure why people complain about not using PowerPoint. It would drain the life out of this kind of class.)
She was absolutely amazing, and I adored her. She's incredibly passionate and wonderful.
easy and boring.
very good professor. her class was interesting and a very good professor to take.
easy A class, nice to have for your first MMW course. midterm/final are exactly like the study guides
easy A. know her study guide, which is really simple. take her for sure for mmw

Her lectures are usually interesting and easy to follow. She focuses a lot on passages and artwork for tests, not so much 'textbook' though it's helpful to read it to understand the material. I didn't think the tests were too hard, but it also depends on your TA. But overall, I liked her class.

Page is awesome!  Very eccentric but super sweet and passionate about what she is talking about.  Very easy final and midterm - both had study guides.  You don't need to read the T+E, only read the pages she reads out in class and take notes during lecture.  I loved her sex talks!  Helped keep class interesting.

her voice is super boring. her sex related talks do not help her voice . shes nice... jus very monotone. i guess if you like to study and read take her... but she doesnt have powerpoints so goodluck note taking.

I liked Professor duBois, she's an eccentric but compassionate and likeable lady. Her lectures were interesting and her exams were very fair and representative of her lectures and readings. I actually enjoyed this class by the end. duBois has a sharp sense of humor and is very knowledgeable, you just have to give her time to show that.

She really isn't as bad as everyone makes her out to be. Yes there is some "sexual content" but not to the extent of some of these reports. Her tests are completely fair, and she even has study guides that are EXTREMELY helpful! Ppl should really give her more credit for the amount of work she puts into this class and pretty helpful too.

She is very interesting to listen to and keeps you attention on the material. She is also super helpful in class, and outside of class, and very easy to talk to.  Keeps the lectures clear, and test very representative of material she lectures on. Answers any and all questions.

Explains concepts of her lecture quite well.She writes an outline of her lecture before class including terms which are of focus(this comes in handy for the midterm). She doesnt just talk about sex, she teaches the vast views of cultures. It's college,be mature and just learn about different cultures

Her scholarly interest in ancient cultures is apparent. As is her want to get students to think seriously and care what kind of world they live in, where it comes from and how one can change one's own self. I learned that you can even change your mind,think differently about things and actually learn something from antiquity.

This is a grad seminar, and I didn't learn a thing from her. She clearly plays favorite, and you know it when you are not one of them. She also wears very strange clothes. Her lecture are long and repetitive; the only good thing is the class was easy, that's about it..........

i was dissatisfied with this class, i thought i was done with sex ed. in high school but i guess not. she spent most classes talking about sex. extremely monotone voice, which couldn't hold my attention.

The class is straight forward and not at all difficult. All you have to do is pay attention and do the readings. The essay is fun because you get to write on any topic that interests you! The point of learning is to develop our own ideas that interests us. Overall, I recommend this course!

I took Mythology with her. Participation counts, quizzes every thursday, VAGUE, rambles, writes nothing on the board ever despite difficult spellings and fast details. Tests completely random. Hard papers with no prompts whatsoever.

Professor Dubois sometimes seems to go out of the scope of the curriculum material to make borderline anti-semitic comments.  She has a friendly demeanor but some of her comments are unsettling and often quite unfounded.

She totally mails it in - lecturers are more like casual, scattered conversation. I think most of her energy goes toward her books and teaching is just a chance to show off her cool sense of fashion and how witty she can be. Sometimes she does deal with some interesting stuff, but mostly she seems to have a lot of disdain for her classes.
i really learned a lot from her course, especially by attending lecture. she chose interesting topics for discussion and was very obliged to help with any questions.

not very good. I can't tell if she just dislikes teaching, but she's a really lazy lecturerl - doesn't prepare at all - and just talks about whatever she wants without necessarily leading to a point. paper comments are useless and idiosyncratic. take her only if you want to take Intro to Page duBois, since her outfits are interesting, but that's it

Took her twice for the same class. She knows her Gk/Rm myths, but the world myths class was new material for her and I dropped b'c it was boring. She speaks extremely softly, considering the size of her classes and wasn't all that helpful re:paper topics.

She was really nice and helpful, she approaches the material clearly when it comes to be prepared for class. Talks kinda fast so I recommend a tape recorder or laptop, but other wise she presented the material well and her tests are really fair.

I picked Dubois because I heard she was eccentric and based everything on sex. For the first 5 weeks she wore black head to toe, was extremely boring, and made no jokes. Her lectures, however, are extremely to the point. Don't read the Craig book, go to lecture. The passage IDs are a killer.

Great lecturer, gives you an outline at the beginning of class. Tests were based upon the slides she showed in lecture, passage ID's, ID's and essays. This class is only horrible if you have a bad TA. The proffessor is awesome, and she has an intersting sense of style.

Professor duBois is crazy! But in a good way. It was always worth it to go to class just to see what she was wearing that day (one day was plaid head to toe...) her lectures seem difficult since she doesn't use powerpoints or anything, but less reading and easier test than others. Just don't sleep!

She has a bad reputation, but she really isn't bad.  Her lectures are interesting, clear, well thought out, etc. Although some people are bothered by her constant references to sex, it sometimes helps to make the topic more interesting.  Tests are very representative of reading and lecture.

i've had her before & normally she's pretty good but she totally phoned this course in.  needs to rethink her priorities or something because this course was the worst i have taken, undergrad or grad.

What a disappointment this course was.  Seems to think flamboyance and style make up for lack of substance in her courses.  Maybe she's good in other courses, or in person, but by all appearances from this class she does not take her teaching seriously.

She really marches to the beat of her own drum, but if nothing else, go to class to see what she's wearing today. She's quite intelligent and makes some very interesting points about the material. (Not everything is about sex.) She even remembered my name months after the class was over.

She's a marvelous teacher and a marvelous human being.  Cares deeply about her students, makes really helpful and interesting comments, very engaging lectures.  Highly recommended.  Oh, and very cool and sexy.

She's awesome.  Didn't care much for the material, but she does everything possible to make it as painless as possible. She even ended the quarter by taking our class out to dinner-- and she paid! I don't know any prof who would do that.  LOVE HER.

This was the best class I have ever taken! She is a very good lecturer, interesting topics...  Can always relate ANYTHING to sex, which makes it all the more interesting!  Half the fun of the class was going to see what she would be wearing today!  She has some CRAZY style... But I loved the class.

Very witty, funny, and fun. Lectures- bit more complex (than Overton), facts&ideas get linked to other things, which make it hard to follow sometimes. Exams are okay. If you talk to her,she is extremely nice,helpful, and cares so much about your learning.

Her midterm and final tend to be tougher than Overton's and other MMW professors, but if you do the readings, take good notes and study her slides, you'll do super good!! Her lectures may be a bit confusing at first... GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS, she's sonice
she was the worst teacher i've ever had.

Witty, wacky, and wonderful.  She is willing to address any questions students have, and is readily available outside of class.  Midterm exam was very representative of course material.  Paper topics are fun to explore.I'd love to take another class w/her
She sucks and is always going off track to talk about sex
No Comments
very dramatic with retellings of myth...doesn't seem to care about students...

Grades and releases assignments late often. Forces political ideology. Does not allow critical thinking or engagement that does not align with her beliefs.

Pretty easy class if you anticipate and submit what she wants to hear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't know what these other bad reviews are about, maybe some people didn't like that she grounded the course in centering and understanding human rights. She inspired me to think about how I can incorporate Ethnic Studies into my future career. There are 3 major assignments, we go over the readings together in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grades very late and does not give good feedback. The point system easily ruins your overall grade and she leans more to the side of my way is right over yours. Information given is clearly meant to brainwash and fit a political agenda. I wouldn't recommend this class unless you fit a certain political demographic.

Definitely take her. Summer course, attendance easy, 3 essays and one video project, which in person would be a presentation. Not hard, but she easily grades on a point to point basis which makes her more complicated. Lectures great. If you have been writing essays, your good. Connecting directly to each point she wants in prompts = A, good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was my first coding class and the prof made the material easy to understand. We're graded mostly based on problem sets and labs. He has a really useful class website that has all the notes from the lectures to help with them. The problem sets weren't extremely challenging but some problems required a bit of googling.
Dr. Vul is a totally amazing teacher. His enthusiasm, material, and energy keep me interested and I learned a lot. Best class of college so far. I recommend him!!!
I wish I didn't have to keep the comments clean in this section.  Just awful.

The homework sets were pretty hard, but great tools to prepare for midterms and the final. If you work hard in this class, you will get an A. It was a bit hard at times to understand concepts during lecture, but going to his office hours helped A LOT! He is a really nice professor. After taking this class, I understand statistics inside and out.

not a great professor. he was confusing at times. Not so helpful either. The TAs were much more helpful then he was. if it wasn't for section i don't think i would have understood the information as much. I do not recommend him.
Wow, BEST PROFFESOR, she is extremely helpful, she loves the class and it really shows, she encurages you to do better all the time. BEST PROFFESOR. TAKE HER CLASS!!!

Professor Eckles is super funny and believes in her students (sorta like a momma bear and her cub). If only I had time, I definitely could've gotten a B. Nonetheless , she made a UC level class seem fairly easy and straight forward.  Take time to study and you're golden.

This was the first time Dr. Eckles taught this course, and it sucks that she's leaving to teach elsewhere. She was an amazing lecturer, chose really good readings (there were a lot, but it's basically a philosophy class, so of course), and really cared that we were learning. Exams weren't easy but were very fair. No homework, just reading.

Dr. Eckles is one of the best biology professors that I have ever had in my life. She makes learning fun and interesting. Her lectures are very animated and captivating. Be prepared to study her lecture notes though because the exams can be difficult. I wish I could take another class with her. She is really good at explaining difficult concepts.

Dr. Eckles was an AMAZING instructor made bio Lab super fun & interesting. She explains what we are going to do for lab that day and we worked in groups. We have a quiz every time we had lab (super easy 5 questions)you need your notebook for every lecture don't forget it!!! She signs it off easy points. Easy A!!You will love her!(I took her at swc)

Dr. Eckles is amazing! Even though tests are pretty difficult she is an amazing instructor. Teaches very clear and her lectures are fun. She is very knowledgable and I could say one of the best instructors I've ever had. I would definitely recommend her and take future classes with her.

I had Doc Eckles as a prof at my community college, and again this year at USD. BIOL 221 is one of those classes that makes you hate life, but her teaching style and explanations made it a lot easier.  Good review assignments, study guides for exams, etc.  Tests are tough,  but fair.  She tells you what you need to know, you just have to know it.
No readings, engaged and good lecturer, easy to take notes, tests are mostly short-answer and force you to make connections and employ several parts of the course.

Dr. Eckles is BY FAR the best professor I have had during my college career at USD. She is extremely passionate about teaching and it is clearly evident by her enthusiasm in lecture. I learned much more in this class than I had expected to and enjoyed every minute of it. If you have the opportunity, take Dr. Eckles!!!

She's a great professor. I was never bored in any of the lectures. If you do the work that you're suppose to you'll get an A. Lectures aren't mandatory but not all of the information is on the slides she posts up because she'll talk about the topic more in depth during the lecture.

She is one of the best professors I have had in college. She is extremely clear in what she is looking for and shapes the class based off of what the class is interested in rather than a strict structure. Learned a lot.

Eckles is obviously passionate about this subject, but tries her best to present both sides of an issue.  There were two midterms and a final for the class, none of which had anything unexpected on them.  As long as you study your lecture notes, you should be fine.  Discussions are mandatory; there is no textbook which is really nice.

Most inspiration and funny teacher I have ever had. I took the course because it was a requirement but I am so glad but she made it fascinating and she was always prepared for class. Very fast grader and always willing to find time to talk to students.  This teacher is epic

This woman actually likes to teach. She is a fantastic professor and tries her best to be engaging. She cares that we learn, I had forgotten how that felt. Her assignments can be a bit tricky, but there's always a point to them, which is nice. She is hands down one of the best, funniest, most motivated professors I've had at UCSD

No textbook required-save money It's easy for Americans to get a A but not so easy for an international student like me to do so. Recommended taking this as pnp rather than letter. This course is not that scientific oriented but more like a social science course which requires you to remember a lot of information. There is no curve.

Her tests are tough, but Dr Eckles is such a fantastic teacher. Super interesting lectures, lots of fun labs and hands on activities.  She does her best to get the students interested and excited to learn.  Use the study guide because her tests ARE tough! You don't even almost need the books though.  Didn't touch them all semester. Likes pop quizes

Meg is unique relative to most UCSD faculty. She truly cares about her students. I have had a lot of excellent teachers over the years but Meg sits at the top of list. She dedicates an incredible amount of time to each and every student including those who don''t seek out help. Meg is the epitome of an excellent teacher.

I can't express my gratitude to Meg for making this class enjoyable, easier to understand, and worth all of the hard work. She met with me multiple times throughout the quarter, helped me through the material for as long as I needed it, and matched my personal desire to succeed above and beyond in this course. She has an incredible ability to teach

THE BEST Professor at UCSD. She made the ESYS final project easy to approach and really takes the time to help her students create the best work of their college career! Meg Eckles was there for me when I wanted to give up, she encouraged me to keep going and I managed to create a better project than I thought was possible. She is an A+ Professor.

After 4 years at UCSD, she was the only professor who genuinely took a personal interest in the experience of each of her students. It's an incredible shame that few other teachers meet this criterion. Her course material is rigorous, but her grading is fair. She is the epitome of the ideal professor, and  should be the benchmark for all others.

Dr. Eckles is one of the most exemplary professors I have ever had. She challenges students in each class to embrace the course material presented, and is very attentive and reactionary to the students' grasp of concepts. Though an authority figure, she is truly approachable and engaging in her friendly demeanor. The embodiment of an ideal teacher.

amazing teacher! shes very clear and is excellent at explaining subjects. she uses drawings and diagrams that are EXTREMELY helpfull and breaks subjects down into easier parts. very patient, very friendly and approachable with teaching. i always looked foward to going to her class. if all my teachers were like her id enjoy school more
Genuinely cares for her students. Has an upbeat clear lecture style and takes the time to explain difficult concepts. Makes class enjoyable and encourages questions. Take this professor!

This semester Dr. Eckles was teaching at SWC and honestly she made biology so simple to understand. Definitely recommend her, no hw, few assignments. Grades on tests but easy if you just review and memorize her powerpoints. Love her class, she's just so awesome

Dr. Eckles is, without a doubt, one of the most passionate and caring professors on campus. Her love for teaching really comes through and she is always available and willing to help or accomodate students however she can. After five years at UCSD, I can easily say that she is my absolute favorite professor.

she's a cool professor. if you study, you'll get an A for sure. but when you study for the midterm and final, memorize the slides perfectly. also, go to lectures. don't miss any although she does not take any attendance.
She's a really cool professor. You don't really need the textbook but it is helpful. It's only an easy A if you work hard. I really had fun and I would definitely recommend this class.

Very cool teacher. Very easy to relate to and make the subject matter relevant. She facilitates easy note taking and answers questions whenever. Don't really need to read the book. Just go to lecture and take good notes. Choose really good project members because mine screwed me over. Recommended class!

Dr. Eckles is such an engaging and cool professor; I'm happy I took her class and she makes concepts extremely easy to understand. The homework isn't bad with two short papers and a final project along with conventional midterm/final. She incorporates humor into her lectures and overall is a friendly person. Definitely take her if interested!
She's awesome! I absolutely love her. She makes concepts really clear and she's super fair. Her office hours are helpful also. Best professor yet. take her!

Prof Ochoa is a top notch prof. I learned loads and he genuinely cares about the students. I found reading the cases after the lecture to be more helpful because it's tough reading, but he randomly calls on people to answer questions, so if you don't want to be embarrassed read before class. Overall a fantastic experience, not easy though!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: No curves, 70% is the benchmark which I just passed. Only once per year. The reading is so hard!
Worthwhile class, especially  if you have any interest in the environment.

He is really straightforward abt what you need to know. Make sure to attend the review session because he will hint at things he will test on. It was easy for me to get an A but I attended every class (lecture's super impt b/c there is no textbook, you read case law) and kept up with the readings. He also provided snacks like cookies for the final.

Professor West was not the best lecturer. I feel like a lot of the stuff you are actually expected to do in HUM is on your own for this class. He didn't go over any important concepts from the readings. That being said, he had a different format for a final and his lectures are definitely important for that because it's memorization based.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Watts just loves his coins and honestly I'm all for it. On top of that his lectures are super engaging and interesting, and they are online as well so you can review easily. Oral final is easy as long as you pay attention in lecture and study for a few days before. Essays are tough though, but its Revelle Humanities so what can you expect

The oral final was incredibly challenging, requiring extensive memorization based on everything discussed in lectures. The expectations are unrealistic, considering that HUM 2 is a Revelle writing requirement, and most students are STEM majors. The class is boring, too hard, and the information we are forced to learn is so irrelevant.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: People have been lucky due to Covid and protests. AVOID. Misleads you into bribed free labor for wife's charity work; 5 weekend hours chastised and yelled at for HELPING as a VOLUNTEER, then he changed the worth from 2 overall grade points to gradebook points. The best part is the oral exam for a writing class. The irony. You memorize coins. COINS.

If you're taking this class as a Revelle student to improve your writing, find a different professor. Most of his points are discussed verbally with few visuals and his lectures are boring. However, he doesn't develop your writing in any way, and does not provide any writing advice. He will not help you improve at all. Rely on the TA's.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I was not a fan of his essay prompts because they were essentially the same prompt with different texts. Great to practice writing for, but not great if you want significant growth. His lectures were pretty engaging and helpful.

the essays weren't bad, just standard hum essays - if your ta was fair, you got a good grade. lecture isn't mandatory and i went maybe 3 times ever but thank god the final got waived due to the ta strike, because the short answer portion were all niche topics and pictures of sculptures he talked about in class lol
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is one of the only hum professors who actually record lectures and the final was online. His lectures include a good balance of historical context and provide a lot of examples from the text that could be used for the essays. Definitely recommend him!

Easily one of the best professors I've had. The material is interesting by itself, but his way of presenting it makes it infinitely more engaging. Kind of like a history documentary, a good book, or an interesting podcast. The course is very flexible, and the three essays are very reasonable and thought provoking. I'm ECE and I'm a fan.

I had prof Watts for both HIEU 102 and 103 and he's a really great speaker. He knows his stuff really well and will make more modern comparisons so its easier to understand the ancient history. Grading really depends on the TA so you have to be lucky, but the classes are really interesting and I would take him a third time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Cool lectures about history but being the prof for Revelle HUM course, he should at least teach more about how to properly write an essay. The TAs are there but their discussions are really just unstructured and sometimes lecture reviews. Watts makes history interesting but fails to be a great professor for a writing sequence.

Good lectures, all available online. His course focuses on biographies, but we are required by the department to read some texts that are not biographies. Reading them is a huge waste of time, is not even addressed in lectures. I learned a lot from this class about Roman history and became a better writer, but a lot of the class is dependent on TA
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A solid professor I would say, lectures are more history based and information on them are seen in the final. Your grade is dependent on your TA, but overall a pretty understanding professor.

Professor Watts' lectures are very clear and packed with information that is actually useful when writing essays. The grading depends heavily on your TA, as like most HUM classes. Overall he's a great professor and is very lenient when granting extensions for essays.

I hate the HUM series but I loved Professor Watts. Unlike other teachers, he really does care for his students and was considerate bc of COVID + riots. Grade depends on your TA though but lectures were pre-recorded and with outlines provided.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor, cares a lot about the students and it shows
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: My first HUM under quarantine - Watts had pre-recorded lectures and explained well. His essay formats are different, but easy once you get the hang of it after your first essay. Watts was incredibly considerate with COVID.
Went to ask him a question after class and he basically ignored me. Super rude and unprofessional.
He is an awesome professor and is so nice. Wonderful guy. I would take again. If you get this guy, you are set. Awesome teacher overall.

He is actually a good lecturer. Things are clear and the tests are mostly about history, in which he provides study guide. Good learning experience for all kinds of students. But if you are international STEM major devoted to STEM and work in lab, be prepared to not get an A since thats what HUM is.

STEM kid here. Class is basically a history class. Watts posts all of the outlines he'll use in lecture online. Even has podcasts for when you can't make class. As with any HUM class, the essays come down to the TAs and how strict they are. Watts might change up the final, but he makes sure to break down all its parts beforehand. Good stuff.

His lectures are amazing & intellectually stimulating. I am a stem major, so I knew I would not be able to devote a lot of time in Hum. Since his lectures and expectations are very clear for the class, it was perfect for me. All the lectures are podcasted, all notes are posted. All of his papers and finals are based on the lectures & notes. easy A.

Disengaged from the students.  It seems the vapidity of the rich/white/conservative money cult here in San Diego has gotten to him.  He's got two of the three but can't join the club because of his intellect, so he overcompensates in the classroom.  Class is fairly easy though.  Take good notes and you'll be fine for the papers and midterm.

Watts is my favorite professor I've taken. Didn't really do the readings until the midterm and papers were due, but they weren't difficult. He's a great lecturer, he kept me interested in things I thought I would hate; thought there was no way I could care about Roman History but it was my favorite class this quarter. Easy A with decent effort!

Great professor if you're a stem kid like most other Revelle students. Final is very historical-fact based, with a thorough study guide and essay prompt given in advance, making it very easy. Lectures are filled with quotes you can use in your essays, though essays graded by TAs, so grade depends on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The professor is nice, but the class is more like a history class than a humanity class.  The assigned books are long and boring, focusing on biography. Papers are graded harsh. Final has study guide, but there are too many things to take in. And I don't see the point of memorizing the whole historical timeline for the test.
Amazing class. really insightful lectures

Watts was funny and interesting. He teaches hum closer to history but he also gives you all the information you need to pass and to do well on the papers. For the final, he literally gives you every possible thing that could be on it and he is very kind with his papers.
Bombtastic professor. Favorite professor I have had in college. Hope to take him in the future. Definitely a memorable class. Lots of content, but everything is essay based.

Good lecturer, but emphasized historical background details. It felt more like a history class instead of a hum class that should also embody literature and philosophy. He only assigned biographical books, which were often boring and incredibly long. There was only one essay topic for all three essays, which is both good and bad.

This professor has revolutionized hoe medieval and ancient Roman and Byzantine history is taught. Although he is not the easiest grader, he offers much feedback and help for those who truly strive to achieve. He is extremely enthusiastic in regards to Roman and Greek Studies. Keep in mind an easy professor is not the best. Highly recommended

Professor is "Nice";however, class is confusing especially if you are not familiar with Byzantium Empire.Grading is taught! He can crucify your paper easily! Not flexible with grading or papers at ALL, No extra credit. if you are thinking its just a History class, you better think twice before taking his class. It's not like any other history class
bing chilling

Wang was a nice teacher, but I felt he didn't explain the course content well, and led me and other students fairly confused when it came to completing homework and studying for midterms & finals. Rescheduled the discussion in week 1 to a time that conflicted with my other classes. Showed up to OH multiple times and IAs didn't show up.

He truly gave amazing lectures and I love that about him. I hear people having bad experiences with other professors, but he actually made the class enjoyable. Exams were very fair and the staff in ECE 15 did an excellent job at helping students in their studying and PAs. Thank you for a wonderful experience Professor Wang!
He's a strange man but a good teacher. Very intellectual and connected with the literature that he's teaching. A bit odd but overall a nice person.

Such a respected and thoughtful professor. He genuinely wants you to learn without such high stakes or pressure. Goes through lectures fast but they're interesting. Provides great feedback and takes a lot of time responding to students' responses/work. Graded on attendance/participation, Perusall, midterm creative paper, & two short final essays.

Great professor! Graded on attendance, Perusall discussion posts, an analysis paper, & a take-home final. The analysis paper involved expanding on a chosen reading, with helpful feedback provided after the first draft. The final exam consisted of short answer questions on the readings and discussions. Attend lectures and take good notes to do well.

I took his LTWL 101 course on Ancient Egypt.  Kelting is an extremely well-versed individual on all things Egyptian, including history, art/archaeology, mythology, society and even language.  Challenging course with heavy reading required, all fascinating content.  Somewhat fast paced, but very informative
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: very easy class, i stopped going to lecture and wrote all my essays the night of and i passed w an A. get on ur ta's good side fast and the rest will be smooth riding. i skimmed the readings just to get some participation in for DI but other than that u can just pull up some evidence for the essay and not have to read anything else.

The grades in MMW always have to do with your TA, but I loved Kelting. His lecture style was wonderful if you like history, literature, analysis, etc. He speaks quickly and efficiently, and watching lectures back was honestly sort of fun (for the 4 essays we had to write, citing lectures worked well). He is passionate and excited to teach!

Professor Kelting was a very caring Professor who wanted his students to really understand the MMW concepts. I appreciated how he would try to make historical connections to our world now. The papers had a lot to do with his lecture materials so paying attention to them is important even though they can be a little boring.

Long, boring, and convoluted lectures. Half of his lectures are not applicable to the Essays and the prompts are a bit tricky and complex and come with short deadlines. Lectures are mandatory but not needed to be successful, except for the final. But he is a nice guy and interested in the subject he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 4 perusalls + 4 essays, no exams. Discussions are mandatory. Kelting is funny and has interesting lectures, but honestly you don't need to go to them to do well on the writing assignments. Weekly primary source reading -- some are a bit long, but overall reasonable. Grade completely depends on your TA; will be an easy A if you get a good one.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Kelting gives amazing and gravitating lectures that really entertained and interested me. He doesn't give a lot of readings. He's a very nice professor that gives valuable advice. His slides have a lot of notes though so it may be tedious to jot them all down if you're that type of person.

Kelting was a great professor who is very passionate about what teaches. While sometime his recorded lectures went over 80 minutes, he always apologized and made up for it by giving readings that weren't that long. He always introduced readings so you knew what you were reading about (so helpful). I would highly recommend him!

I don't think this quarter was indicative of Kelting's usual teaching style. Because of Omicron, we were completely virtual and asynchronous. Kelting uploaded all the lecture videos at the beginning of the quarter and we had to watch the videos each week and do the readings. Not great. I think in person, he would have been a great professor.

I really can't recommend Professor Kelting. I think his heart is in the right place, but his lectures really didn't feel very applicable to the essays in a lot of instances, and in general, they were quite vague and understated. I really don't believe much would have changed if I had skipped class altogether this quarter. Reading was reasonable.

An interesting lecturer who really cares about students. Gives a lot of advice. Slides are kinda hard to take notes from but you should be focusing on the readings anyway. As usual with MMW, if you're a competent writer, you can do well. Your grade is based completely off major writing assignments and section participation.
Amazing professor. The class was ruined by a shitty TA. Take him if you get the chance, pray you do not get a shitty TA. He's one of the most proficient lecturers I've encountered.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Kelting's material is so nicely organized and on his primary sources he notes where to start/ end reading, where things are unimportant, and gives question for you to think before reading! Readings are doable, about 3-4 a week. He cares a lot about his students, and his lectures are always very engaging. If only he taught more MMW courses!

Professor Kelting so far has been one of my favorite professors, he is extremely caring for his students and for the content that he teaches. He teaches the content so students are able to understand it clearly, he has good essay prompts that make the student improve their writing. He was an amazing teacher and I would highly recommend his class.

Prof. Kelting was an amazing lecturer and really loved what he taught. I think that translated really well into his teaching by really trying to engage his students all the time and successfully did. He’s very understanding and very easy to talk to outside of class. I would totally recommend Prof. Kelting for whatever class he teaches.

Since I took this course fully online and asynchronously, I never got to talk to Professor Kelting but he seems very kind and I enjoyed his lectures. For the 5 MMW essays he made additional videos on advice and to further explain the prompts which was helpful. I also liked the way he organized his online lectures and readings on canvas.

Professor Kelting is a great teacher, he really understands the topics he is discussing and he is very caring. I would recommend him a million times over if I could! There is a lot of reading in this class but the subject is very interesting and he is very good at helping us understand the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Kelting is the best! Grades are based on a midterm project, a final, and participation, but he's very understanding. He's very enthusiastic about what he teaches and although im not a fan of literature, this makes me actually want to go to class. There is quite a bit of reading, but there's a read-aloud feature so I treat it as a podcast.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Kelting is clearly enthusiastic and knowledgeable about the topics discussed in class. He is very approachable. The insights provided in discussion of the readings are instrumental in constructing a well-rounded answer for midterm and final essays. Lecture is a good balance of images and speech.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You can tell from day 1 of the class that he's incredibly knowledgeable about his areas of expertise and is eager to spread that knowledge to his students. He always emphasized the significance of class material during discussions and kept everyone actively engaged with humor and encouragement. Definitely recommend his classes!

A very good natured and knowledgeable professor. Very caring and flexible with his students. Passionate about the subjects he teaches, can easily go on a tangent. It's best to take his classes if you have genuine interest in the subjects and like to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: He's a smart guy (he won a field medal). However, his explanations are not clear which made me learn all the class material through YouTube. Tests are easy, Homework is easy, and the class itself is easy, but he wasn't a great teacher.

Professor Zelmanov lectures enthusiastically over Zoom with his characteristic Russian accent by going over his pre-written notes, pausing regularly for questions, which makes his lectures very fun and enjoyable. However, his proof-first approach to concepts are not the easiest to understand and turns students away to other Math 18 lecturers.

Made an account so that I can warm people not to take a class with Zelmanov. Learning linear algebra from Zelmanov is like trying to learn how to ride a bike purely from dictionary entries. He overcomplicates almost everything, and I find that reading the textbook and just teaching myself is a better alternative than trying to understand him.

Professor Zelmanov's lectures are mostly proofs and not actually useful examples. They're more confusing than helpful, and I basically taught myself everything thru YT and the textbook. Very test heavy and lots of homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's clearly a very smart guy based on his credentials, but teaching a first semester undergraduate course is certainly not his strength. Extremely confusing lectures, me and most others in his class just attended another professor's lectures after the first 2 weeks because of how confusing his lessons were.
be prepared to basically just teach yourself

He's definitely got his own style of teaching, but it worked for me. I liked not turning in homework and open note tests. With some effort, I could follow his lectures fine. He doesn't like it if you're late.
This is a graduate level course. Very few people would be able to teach it with the ease and rigor of Zelmanov. Absolutely excellent!

Thought a Fields Medalist would be a good thing. Turns out it doesn't to a student. He skips around and assumes you know what he means. People in my class barely knew what a bijection was. Not worth it. Take it it with a professor who is organized and will teach you well.

Definitely one of the best math professors at UCSD.  For 102, exams are open book, open notes, and calculators are allowed.  He does an excellent job helping students understand.  Also a very funny guy who makes funny noises :)  Take Zelmanov, you won't regret it!  (another thing is, don't be late to class, he will stop lecturing and glare at you!)
easy tests, nice professor. However, u wont learn a lot.
Too bad I never went to class.  But from the few times that I did, I usually understood what was going on since he did a great job of explaining things.  Too bad he failed me too.  But I deserved it.
explains material well, slowly and clearly.  shows concern for students.

This guy has a Fields Medal, so he does whatever he wants in class.  Which means no homework, open book/open note tests, and no set schedule.  If you ask lots of questions, he covers less material.  And the tests are easy.
How can you not like him? He's so clear about everything. I have nothing to complain. Definitely one of the best math professors in the department.
very easy professor, no homework, open notes/book midterm and final, easiest professor ive had at ucsd
Worst, accent is very difficult since he's from Russia. Don't bother to email him  for question since he's never bother to reply back.

Makes mistake here and there up to the point that I don't even know what I am learning anymore. Also, the test is more complicated then it needs to be even though the class is already hard itself. Plus, he sometimes curves down the scale which doesn't make sense at all

Honestly an easy class. Calculus is fairly simple enough to begin with already, so I liked how the professor tried to explain the concepts on top of doing examples in class. Solid choice in my opinion. I know a majority of the class would disagree, but if you have a good understanding of maths, you'll develop well in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ed really tries his best and I appreciated it. I prefer step-by-step lessons instead of a complex explanation of the topic so I struggled a lot in his class. His study guides are pretty similar to his midterms, but I still had to learn from the SI.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Caring and a cool guy, but he doesn't know what he's doing as a prof just yet. Confusing lectures, waaay too much online homework, never told us what would be on exams. Discussion was the only place that helped me. I failed every exam but the fat curve brought me up to an A every time, so I feel like I passed without learning anything. :/

I went to lecture maybe 7 times max? This prof wasnt too bad, he really tries to teach the concepts instead of step by step. A lot of it was self studying the HW, class didnt help much, he explains things a lot more difficult bc he has a lot of math knowledge. Prepping for exams was hard bc no practice exam + barely a guide. Prepare to go to SI

If this is your first time dealing with these topics, Dewey is definitely not going to help you understand them. He constantly makes mistakes during lecture and students have had to correct him several times. He expects you to read the textbook before class which is equally confusing

As a student from a CSU university nearby crashing class, I have to say this teacher tries to focus on the essence of key concepts. I notice that past students think he makes things complicated, but really, he focuses on explaining the concepts and reasoning instead of just dumbing things down to step-by-step approaches for tests. Solid prof.

A lot of people are gonna roast Dewey but hes probably the most wholesome professor I've had this quarter. Hes not good at explaining concepts at a lower division level, but if you understand the fundamentals then a lot more makes sense. Hes definitely passionate about teaching math and he always responds to students on piazza on time.

Dewey's very smart and knows what he's doing, but he doesn't know how to teach or explain things to other people who don't have the same knowledge in math as he does. He makes things really abstract to the point where everything is just a list of confusing variables. I used to love math but after his class I don't wanna take another math class.

At first I was excited to be taking the next level of calculus since I enjoyed it so much in high school, but after taking Dewey's vector calculus class I hate math. It is not hugely difficult curriculum but the way he lectures makes it even more complicated. The samples are nothing like the actual tests so beware. Prioritize good professors!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I was planning to become a mathematics major, but after taking Dewey's class I have completely reconsidered. His lectures were incredibly difficult to understand and he often over-complicated otherwise relatively simple topics. I survived the class by watching other professors on youtube. Don't take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I didn't get the lectures in the first few weeks but started to understand after. You gotta try your best understand him and you will find out that everything he said makes sense. Homeworks are hard, if they are in difficulty 7-9, tests are just 5-7. So if you know how to do homework problems, you should be fine in tests.

Having professor Dewey's class my first quarter in college was terrible. Throughout the quarter I understood absolutely nothing. His lectures are incredibly difficult and doesn't explain well. Makes lots of mistake during lectures. I'm a math major and after this course I'm afraid to take any math classes again. I hate math now.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class itself, no matter the professor, is difficult. I thought he did a good job explaining the material given and he shows he knows the material well. Definitely go to office hours and you will see how much he cares that you understand the material. Also, going to office hours helped me better understand the material. Would take him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Actually I found Ed is good. He is caring and super cute. The course material is very hard itself, and the first midterm was extremely hard but he gave a good curve.

Horrible lecturer, makes mistakes on his solution keys, in lecture, doesn't give feedback on homework answers so you dont know where you went wrong, and doesnt grade homework until a month after you turned it in, so you dont know if you did it right. Tests are hard with little time allotted. Doesn't respond to piazza or emails consistently.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He is a nice professor but the way that he talks is VERY difficult to understand. He knows the thing he teaches very well but he just doesn't know how to make it easy to understand, which makes linear algebra even harder. Midterms and final are hard, and you have to spend plenty of time trying to figure what he want you to do.

A very dedicated teacher. You can tell he is smart and he knows how to respond to student questions. But he is still difficult nevertheless. Many problems in lecture were easy to follow conceptually but difficult to learn. Learned mostly from online homework and SI Sessions. A lot of vocab and high conceptual tests.

I had to learn mostly outside of class. He seemed like a nice professor but the exams were very difficult and not very straightforward. The most difficult part was interpreting the question and understanding what it was asking you. He answers on piazza but he is not very direct with his responses.

He is a very nice person and he knows A LOT of math but doesn't rally teach the material well. He is very disorganized and his test are ridiculously difficult. They don't reflect the lecture, the homework, or the textbook. His lectures are hard to follow as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: so disorganized, lectures are incredibly hard to follow. exam questions are too wordy so you have no idea what they are asking. doesn't hold review sessions, doesn't make announcements in class to make sure his students are on the same page. he's on piazza very frequently, but beats around the bush in his responses. do NOT take him for this class
Very DISORGANIZED. Lecture hard to follow and often explain a concept in a way that is difficult to understand rather than a simple sentence.

Poorly organized prof and is terrible at explaining concepts. His notes are all messed up. Also he is the only prof that i've met so far that actually curves down. Really need to avoid him, at least on math 18.

Okay class. Lectures hard to follow. Writing on blackboard is light, so hard to see. Midterms were difficult but given a full sheet of notes. Only provides one practice exam. Handwriting is hard to make out.
nice prof
A good professor!

Ed is a nice and caring prof and is always patient to answer questions that student ask. His lecture is clear and logical and well-prepared. The exam is kind of difficult but it's the same for all 20B lectures.
He often makes mistakes during the lecture and there's no slides, but he gives pretty good cutoff.

Lectures are very confusing. He regularly makes mistakes in lecture and is corrected by students. The classes are hard because they're calculus (20B is really hard) but not undoable if you have a decent professor. Dewey assigned 67 homework problems due the night of the second midterm. If you take his class it is better to teach yourself.

He is a caring guy but his lectures are not organized and are tough to follow. If are familiar with the course content then you should be fine. For those who are not, you will be left confused after his lectures(kinda) but you can definitely make up by going to his office hours.
The lectures were hard to follow sometimes.  Do the practice problems in the textbook to be better prepared for the tests given.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a really great guy and makes what he wants to see very clear. That being said, his lectures aren't always easy to follow and the class itself can be deceiving. I had a solid A throughout the class, and the final was absolute hell and my grade went freefalling.  My advice: take a lot of careful notes and do extra tough problems for the final.

I loved Professor Ehrich. Lectures were very informative and she is super sweet. The tests are lecture heavy and she will put things said in her lectures in her exams. She warns you about it though at the beginning of the quarter. She gives you everything you need to prepare for the midterm and final in her class. Attendance is mandatory.

She makes classes engaging. However, the tests are VERY lecture heavy. She will quote herself from past lectures and will quiz you on that. If you know you won't be attending every class, do not take this professor. She doesn't provide a study guide or assignments to prep for the tests, apart from an in class-review session a class prior.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super passionate about marketing, just info you need to know is heavily dependent on her specific lecture examples which can be tough. Projects were all super easy and got As on all of them, just quizzes/tests were tough to know what specifically to study for. Take comprehensive but specific notes and show up to class and you'll honestly do great.

Professor Ehrich was a wonderful professor. I enjoyed going to class and think as long as you attend lectures (they are mandatory anyway) then you'll do well in the class. The group project wasn't too bad and I think as long as you put in effort you'll be fine.
She has a required textbook for this course but I never used it and got an A.

She is a great professor. She explains everything very well and provides real-world examples. As long as you go to class and write notes on her lectures, the tests should be easy. There are no surprises on the exams, everything on it is what she has discussed in class. Reading the textbook is not too neccesary.

Great attitude as a professor. Very helpful and engaging. Loved the way she taught through real-world examples and provided meaningful assignments to students. Provides extra credit, One midterm, two quizzes, and one group project, an elevator pitch  (1 minute personalized pitch) and a 2 minute product presentation (of your choice!) She's VERY KIND

This professor wasn't good. The class relied on four high-pressure exams without helpful practice materials, and the time limits made tricky questions even harder. Assignments were graded strictly with little clarity on how to improve. Overall, the course felt more difficult than necessary, and I wouldn't take it again.

She's teaches what you need to learn in the class, mostly from lecture, not from the book. Her grading criteria is clear and I enjoyed her classes. Go to class and participate. It helps you stay engaged. Would definitely take 103 from her.

This class felt overly strict and uninspiring. Video assignments required staring into the camera the whole time—looking away was considered cheating. Lectures were minimal, and the group project was frustrating since I ended up doing it alone. Expect 5–8 hours weekly, but little real-world application. Her teaching felt very annoyingly strict.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Kristine is the best teacher. She explained marketing in a clear and an easy way. Her class is well organized, and the projects are fun and helpful. If you follow her lectures and do the work, it is easy to get a good grade. She really cares about her students and makes the class interesting. I highly recommend her !

Book doesn't really matter because she explains everything in class. 2 quizzes, a midterm, 2 projects and a final. She keep the lectures quiet interesting because she interacts with students. She is very strict about professional behavior which makes it hard to approach her when you have an issue or want to communicate late work.

Ehrich is a really good lecturer and makes concepts easy to understand. Exams were tough but the projects were easy and interesting. Even though attendance isn't mandatory, I would definitely suggest going to understand the material, and questions on exams will include "from what we discussed in class...". Overall great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She seemed nice and all but the way she structures grading, assignments/projects, and lectures were not my fav. The rubrics for the projects and assignments were extremely vague and hard to navigate through unless you asked 1000 clarifying questions, and the exams and quizzes were pretty confusing.

Lectures were engaging, easy to follow, and brought marketing to life with real-world examples. She's clear about what's important, making it easy to focus. Material isn't easy, but if you attend class, take notes, and study, you'll do great. I got an A by doing just that. I highly recommend her class for an interesting introduction to marketing!

I took her class this winter, and I hate it.
I plan to work in marketing, and I was very excited to learn, but she kills your motivation. The class is all about her. If you expect help or advice, you won't get it. I advise you to choose a professor with more sympathy for their students. You will learn more about the class in the book.

She is super awesome. As someone who hates lectures, hers were actually interesting. She is very caring and easy to talk to. The midterm was very hard, but the quizzes are manageable. I would recommend her class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: People who complain about her have never actually taken a difficult class in their lives. She's an engaged lecturer, all of her guidelines and expectations are very clear from what she says and what's in the syllabus, no false advertising. If you take decent notes during lectures and study for literally an hour before the quizzes you'll be fine.

Dr. Ehrich is the best!! If you are interested in the subject you will have a great time but if it is just a mandatory class you may find it boring. She is super engaging in lecture (mandatory) and her quizzes/ exams accurately reflect the content. Don't expect an easy A, have to put in a few hours of work every week but it is not a heavy load imo.

The negative reviews here don't make any sense to me. Expectations and requirements are clear, the lectures are interesting and worth going to. Exam content reflects exactly what was discussed in lectures and the professor even emphasizes what specific information you should focus on. Great professor!

Professor Ehrich has been one of the best professor I've had. She is caring and charismatic & is always open to talk to students whether it is because they need help or to talk about real life marketing. Lectures are very important bc of the examples she gives but they are so interesting! This class felt faster than most 50 min classes. LOVED!

she is great! i don't know why there are negative reviews about her. She teaches in a very clear and easy-to-understand manner and i would def love to take more classes with her.
her grading and tests are fair and she has extra credit opportunities at the end of the year. she is a great professor overall, and I recommend her.

Definitely avoid unless absolutely required. Exams are tough and you need to attend lectures and take notes to do decently well on the exams since she refers to what she said in her lectures on the exams. Answers are very similar and you need to know exactly what she's looking for so be ready to recall small details. Slides are not enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor is very passionate about the subject. However, the material is useless. I personally didn't learn anything about marketing. It was all about terms memorization
She hardly gave any instructions or guidelines on midterm and final exam. Both were extremely difficult and accounted for a huge portion of overall grades. Avoid at all cost!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

She's amazing, incredibly caring and has awesome lectures. The material is a bit tough, but studying terms and learning how to apply them will help you a lot. If you speak up in class, she would LOVE to hear from you. Such a cool person

Professor Ehrich is amazing. Take notes during lectures, compare lecture notes/slides to the textbook for a deeper understanding, and participate if you want to get a good grade. She's extremely kind and I hope to TA for her at some point. Fun course and she plainly says what she expects of you. The bad ratings are completely out of place.
Ehrich was a very passionate and energetic professor. You could tell she really liked the subject. If you put it enough effort fairly well balanced class.

The exams and quizzes are mostly reflective of the material learned in class but there is always 1-2 questions that are tricky. However, she offers 15 extra credit points which makes up for those questions. Some sort of A is achievable with 2 hours of studying for each exam. She is accessible outside the class and respond to emails very quickly.

Learned so much about business strategy. You get to read cases about companies you know. Much of the class is a group simulation but it is really fun and she helps you a lot. Make sure you get a good group. She likes lots of discussion. Cares about her students. Pay attention during the discussions and you'll know what is on the exams.

Winter 2023. Coursework (out of 890 points): 1 Midterm (250), 1 Final (250), 3 Quiz, drop 1 (100), Syllabus Quiz (50); Product Presentation, Elevator Pitch, Application of Concepts (50 each), Rady Labs (40), Engagement (50),  Extra Credit (10). Everything is very reflective of lecture and textbook summary materials. Spent about 4-5hrs weekly.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved her and the class. Lectures flew by with her style of conversational teaching. I wish so badly I did better on the exams so I could have gotten an A and been her TA.

She loves what she teaches, which makes her lectures fun and engaging. She highly prefers taking notes on paper or tablet, and even posts slides with notes column next to it. As long as you go to lectures, the class would not be difficult to keep up with.
She passionates about marketing.

Imagine having the audacity to tell students not to use laptops or electronics in class. Then proceed to force students to come to class with a laptop to take quizzes and tests (because no one is taking one on their phone lets be honest now). Midterm class average was a 62%, then proceeds to tell the class we aren't studying correctly. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Super tough grader with horrible teaching. Lectures aren't really helping. Doesn't let students take notes using iPad. Electronic devices are not allowed in her class. Would NOT recommend -10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: One of the most boring professors I've ever had. She literally talks to students like they are 2nd graders and tries to micromanage every single detail about the class (like not being able to take electronic notes). Highly would not recommend unless you like falling asleep during class
Very specific projects that require lots of attention to detail
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: doesn't let students take notes on laptops or other electronic devices. we're adults, stop micromanaging us by telling us we can't even take notes how we want to. all style and no substance. class is pretty much just a bunch of business buzzwords strung together. waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Tests are very difficult and timed. Unfair amount of time for tests and you will feel very rushed. She is also bad at communicating and will not allow you to makeup work. 10/10 would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not a good professor.

Great teacher. You truly learn from the class, but how much you learn doesn't get fairly reflected on your grades. Her grading criteria is mehh; it's on the syllabus but it's displayed very weirdly tbh (out of 940 points). TL;DR would recommend if you don't care about getting a grade that is (arguably) less than what you deserve.

She really is a great professor when it comes to a Business / Marketing Undergrad course. Her lectures are interactive, smooth, and apply tons of real-life examples to solidify the content. Her class is also organized, following the textbook closely. She is also personable, remembering you if you participate. Participation enforced in a good way.

She is a hard grader and horrible of teaching class. Her class was not worth to listen because nothing you could learn from it. She just let us to discuss and even no power point to summary those ideas, so you would feel lost. When you took the quizzes and exams, the questions, especially in Markstrat, she asked are not taught in class. Nightmare!

You can notice she likes to teach this class. However, you have to read 1-2 chapters before every class and her lectures consisted of repeating the information in the textbook. I did not like how she would often say, "if you don't get this, go back and read your book again."

Professor Ehrich is the best professor I have taken at UCSD. Don't be afraid to speak up in class because she will never make you feel bad even if you make a mistake. She genuinely cares about her students. The class has a lot of material, but all the tests are fair. Choose your group for the group project wisely. She is amazing!!!!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's okay. Her lectures are discussion-based but attendance is required. She glosses over textbook material, so that kinda forces you to read the hundreds and hundreds of pages due in a short period of time. Exams are all textbook heavy, so make sure you really read and understand the concepts. If you hate reading a lot, don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Absolutely love Ehrich! Engaging, funny, energetic, very caring prof. Lectures are discussion heavy, slides online are helpful, 5 quizzes from textbook material but kinda hard, 2 class presentations are easy, 2 papers are also easy. Great class, definitely recommend!

Reading the book is not required, but its good to be prepared before class. Mandatory attendance via sign-in sheets. Pop quizzes approximately once a week. Knows the material well and explains it in a manner that we can understand it.

One of the BEST professors I've had! She really makes class interesting and creates an environment that fosters a good discussion. Her lectures are really engaging and she's very straightforward about what to expect on exams. This class is what ignited my interest in marketing and it's all thanks to her. HIGHLY recommend

She is one of the best prof's I've had. I honestly looked forward to her lectures as they are very interesting. There is minimal homework and if you have any basic understanding of marketing going into the class, the material shouldn't be hard for you. 2 speaking presentations, 4 pop quizzes, 2 exams, and 2 written assignments. Highly recommend!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures
