reviews.comment: Such an amazing human, I wish that she was my aunt... just maybe not my professor. Don't get me wrong, her lectures are extremely interesting and you can tell she cares a lot about the subject. BUT her tests are entirely based on the textbook, which throws you for a loop, because they have almost nothing to do with the lecture & all the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: She is so funny, really makes your day. However, she is a tough grader, she may look pretty lenient when she lectures though. On the exam, you're expected to know EVERYTHING, every concept, idea, etc. So it's a lot to study for.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the truly amazing Professors at Rady. Vikram
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: very good pro and class was interesting. You MUST participate her lectures and share ur personal experience. 3 Pop quizzes, not easy! 60 MC for Middle term, our average Grade was C for middle term!! u need really understand definitions, dont memorize!  2 presentations and 2 reading assignments. Tough class, tough grade. But you will learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's a funny and engaging prof but tests you on the minor vocabs on tests which can be annoying. listen in class and study the powerpoint and ESPECIALLY THE PICTURES and you should be fine for the tests. class is nonweighted so the hw and projects count just as much as the tests. Shes a good prof but a little sloppy at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: She was really great in class--she kept everyone interested in what she was teaching even when the subject matter could have been very boring.  The class isn''t an easy A but you''ll be okay if you show up do all of the work and go to office hours. I hate going to office hours usually but Jodi was so helpful

I loved having Jodi as my Spanish profesora.  I never felt comfortable speaking in Spanish classes until this one.  Also, the readings made so much more sense with Jodi than other profs.  She is AMAZING in office hours too, so eager to help you with anything.  I feel like I learned so much more about THE WORLD in her class, not just Spanish!
I really liked her, she is always willing to help and is a very understanding TA.
Smoking hot & super cool. Interesting discussions. Pay attention & work hard & you'll do fine. You have to work hard for an A.

Jodi is really nice and understanding. She knows what's it is like to be student. If you need help, she'll help! She's really friendly too! Muir 50 is not an easy A though. Expect a lot of reading and a lot work!

She's a well-known poet in the LGBT arena but she's completely incoherent, a terrible teacher, said there was absolutely "no theme" for our class, made us watch the Kennedy shooting 8 times. She shouldn't be teaching, really.
AMAZING. AMAZING. AMAZING. Made me love poetry when before I'd totally hated it.

Eileen is a poet and I feel it is a previlage to be in her class. She makes learning poetry so fun and exciting. She gives interesting assignments and makes it bareable for non writing students. Defently take her if you have a chance she is great.

I actually think her assignments and ways of explaining things are really great, there are gemstones in her lectures.  I think she's the best thing that could happen to lower div writing courses, but feel a little more reserved about how she handles upper div courses, b/c she tends to conduct more traditional workshops, unlike Springer & Liebegott

Nice, interesting lady, but was unclear as a teacher. Assignments seemed random and she heavily favored post-modernistic poetry.  Just seemed like a "turn any random pile of words in and get an A" kind of class.
Eileen is my mentor and idol!
Interesting lady, but sometimes unclear on assignments.
She has this energy to her-- she is so brilliant.  During lecture, yes, she is a bit unclear, but she always took time to re explain things when someone needed.
No Comments

She is fun and has a lot of spunk.  Although she sometimes has trouble explaining exactly what she wants from you, her assignments are creative and she is very low key and an awesome writer and teacher.

She's cool but she does a flipped classroom thing that I was not a fan of. Just do your work and pray you don't get a bad partner/group for labs and final project bc that WILL ruin your grade. Email her if you have issues bc she is very understanding. The final is a breeze just pay attention to the lecture quizzes bc the questions are the same.

VDE's class will give you a solid understanding of SE concepts and of what to expect in the major. The class is VERY homework heavy and requires setting aside a lot of time to work on assignments and attend office hours. Make sure to choose your teammates wisely for group projects as this can make or break your experience.
The class was heavily group work with a lot of involvement. You'll be working with a lot of classmates on weekly assignments. Not a bad intro to SE.

No tests, but there is about 20-27 hours of work a week which will eat up your weekends. The class is extremely exhausting but "fun", in that in the end you learn a lot about the multiple softwares used by engineers. I would highly recommend only taking two other courses that are easier, because you will be exhausted by the end of every week.

VDE doesn't do tests, so she assigns a TON of homework instead. They're mostly busy work assignments that are meaningless. She does teach well though, and does care about students. The TAs also grade harshly, and often mark points off for arbitrary reasons. Expect about 8 hours of work a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She's a tough lady but you learn exactly what you need.

Her lectures aren't conceptually difficult to understand, but she assigns too much work. Weekly lab reports take hours to complete and are very tedious, especially if your lab partner(s) don't do their part. Aside from that, she's very passionate about what she teaches and is always a great advocate for her students.

There is so much busy work and the homework is graded so harshly, it is impossible to get 100% on an assignment. At least there were a ton of office hours if you had questions and the final group project is somewhat fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not conceptually difficult but work heavy. Too much work for an intro class. Class eats away at time to study for other crucial courses, with weekly lab reports that takes hours, problem sets and quizzes. Quizzes are easy and the final exam is based on quizzes. Choose partners wisely for the design project as doing most of the work is stressful.

This class is a good introduction to the world of structural engineering. VDE is a passionate professor, and the TAs that I interacted with were very helpful. Tons of HW every week, and can take up time from other equally important classes. In addition, grading criteria is very scrutinizing; 100% on HW is very rare. No midterm, just a final.

Cares about the success of her students and is easily accessible via email. Not the best office hours and maybe could be a bit better at explaining some of the more complicated math concepts, but I loved her video lectures. If you take detailed notes with the video lectures and don't rush through them then you'll do well in the class.

Honestly the professor wasn't bad she just leaves a lot of work. It's nothing you can't do but if you leave it last minute it can stack up. Weekly quizzes and online lectures are left to watch. A good 2-3 hours worth of lecture videos a week. Overall she's good but some TAs are tough graders on assignments. Mandatory everything.

VDE herself is not super approachable with questions and her TAs were not super helpful either. There is an unnecessary amount of work for this class and most of the instructions are very vague and unclear. The work is not extremely difficult but it is graded harshly for no reason.

You only go to class once a week (the day of your lab), but in return there is loads of homework. Expect 2-3 hours of homework weekly. In person lecture is pretty useless because the lecture videos VDE uploads cover all the material already, but attendance is mandatory. As long as you put in the time its not too bad, just a lot of busy work.

This class gives me more work than all my other classes combined. Expect to watch lecture videos and complete 2-3 assignments weekly outside of class. Content is not difficult, pretty much just busy work. Choose a good team for your final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The flipped learning along with the group project and homework she gives out adds up to like 15 hours outside of class a week some weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I've now taken three classes with VDE (SE 1, 3, and 103). She is a mediocre lecturer who assigns far too much work, and her lower division classes just poorly designed, focusing too much on vague activities and projects rather than applying engineering concepts. There's no avoiding her if you're SE, so get ready to work and not feel rewarded.
THIS GROUP PROJECT IS THE MOST I'VE EVER DONE IN MY LIFE!!!!! There's not much wiggle room and she has a love for flipped learning which is a real pain when it comes to time. What a waste.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She's not a bad professor, pretty interesting, but assigned so much homework that it does overwhelm other classes. Beware of teaming with lazy people, it will make your life 10 times harder in lab.

Her teaching style is inspiring and amazing. However, her lecture materials are so unorganized and confusing all the time, so definitely having to communicate to make sure ur on the right track. Although workload was a lot, I definitely learned a lot and it helped me prepare for future classes. I got an A- in SE 1 and an A in SE 3 and B+ in SE 103

Flipped classroom DOESN'T WORK. She assigns hours of useless videos made from half a decade ago and just says the same thing during the lectures which she makes mandatory. The labs are helpful but she assigns a lot of useless busy work. Her "reading" quizzes also always have 
unknown material and gives you only ten minutes, even when calcs needed.

Good professor with clear explanations except her graders are hungry to take off any points they can on assignments. Make sure you read the questions carefully as her problems contain lots of text and the actual questions you have to answer are easy to overlook.

You can tell that VDE is a great engineer with a ton of experience. She is accommodating to students' needs. The grading was kind of annoying; points are taken off for the smallest of things. If you participate in class and go to office hours, you'll learn a ton and probably get an A. The main problem was I had to do all the group project work.
Super caring and nice, willing to talk to every student. Work is challenging but good practice for what you need to know.

She does a "flipped classroom" but basically just repeats the material in the lecture. Lots of videos to watch and lots of weekly assignments. She covers a lot of material, and will make you feel like a better engineer in the end, but get ready for heavy workload.

you only have to show up to one lecture which will be the same day as your lab. Pre lecture videos and reading quiz that are fairly easy. Weekly group/partner lab assignment and individual assignment.

This class is A LOT of work. At least 6 hours of homework a week, plus group project work (4+ hours). The class is very fun nonetheless, since you learn a lot of hands on stuff. Homework across several different platforms. However, the information can be really disorganized and inconsistent, so be sure to ask. Lots of extra credit opportunities.

If you like starting assignments early just don't... it has so many mistakes, so if you start you'll have to redo it. She makes mistakes but you cannot. She assigns an unmanageable amount of work and grades super tuff. But it's so conflicting because if you finish her mountain of material. Then, you'll learn more about SE than any other class.

Go on CAPE, you'll see VDE has been teaching this course for years. And yet it was still the most disorganized dumpster fire of a course I have ever taken. It's like she doesn't know what the assignments say until after you read them back to her and point out the errors. Childlike comprehension and communication skills from a professor.
She made sure the lecture space was a very lively and open environment and listened to our suggestions. However there is a lot of work to be done outside of class

I want to take a moment to address the positive reviews on this page. Because I realize as you're scrolling through, it seems like there's a good amount of support for VDE saying she "prepares you for a job/the industry." The only way VDE prepares you for a job is by demonstrating what it's like to have a boss who is completely incompetent.

How this class feels: Imagine going to a store to buy groceries and then a stranger comes up to you saying you can't leave the store until you complete an 1000 food item scavenger hunt and write a paragraph on the nutritional value of each item. She has no business grading resumes and cover letters, especially for those who have jobs already.
People find her class rough because its a lot of work, but at least for SE1, I think its a good way to introduce the major. Its definitely difficult but it also has fun hands on activities.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Unnecessarily strict and picky when it comes to grading. Not an intro class. Deducted excessive amount of points for the smallest of errors.

VDE is a fine professor. If you show up put in the work you should be fine. I took this as a first year transfer and it was by far the easier se class I took that quarter. I recommend her. Her TAs are really chill and helpful when needed.

Everyone who is complaining about VDE is buggin'. They're just first years who take the very first freshman class (SE 1) and hate the workload. I'll be honest, I used to get really mad at her while I was taking her classes because the work was a lot, but when working you realize everything she teaches is imperative to engineering. She cares a lot

Professor is good at giving lectures, speaks very clear and explains. However, I think this class should have prerequisites like Physics 2A, and Math 20B. It is a very tough class for an intro because I haven't learned anything that she is teaching. She also has no mercy for it, she wants perfection. Lots of homework, and tests, definitely a NO.

This course was one of the hardest yet because it isn't structured like a typical college course. It felt like working in the industry and I think that's exactly what they were going for. The professor and her TAs were incredibly helpful

This class has a lot of labs and it will probably be your first time doing this type of lab so it can seem challenging. However VDE makes sure that either she or the TAs are available and ready to help. She is an awesome professor, has a firm grasp of her course material, and makes engineering engaging and fun.

Professor VDE is very knowledgeable in the field of SE. I took her class remotely, and she made all of the grading criteria clear since Day 1. Her pre-recorded lectures are engaging and simple to understand. The weekly lab assignments are a bit of a challenge sometimes, along with the engineering exercises. Put in the effort and you'll get an A.

Horrible. Makes us scanvenge for a bunch of stuff before class starts, so many deadlines to remember (why not just one hw every week due on one day?), avoid at all costs. Also had for se 1 and she was rude to me back then. High maintenance.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Beware this professor! She has super strict guidelines and requirements but never holds herself to those same standards. She constantly posts homework late, full of mistakes, yet never changes the due date or requirements to make up for it. She seemingly has no idea that the average student has 3 other classes apart from hers and drowns you in work

Overall, VDE is a very good professor. She IS a tough grader though, which makes the class difficult at times. Lots of homework, group project required. Lab reports have very specific criteria, but it is possible to get a good grade if you just meet her guidelines. NO textbook, but reading assignments are given. READING QUIZZES IN CLASS!

VDE is a good SE1 professor. Although she throws a lot at you, she takes into account of students who do not have PHYS2A or Statics background and wants her students to do well. The homeworks are straightforward and reflected on the exam. She does reading quizzes and participation via iClicker so attendance matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: VDE Is probably the most caring professor you could have the pleasure of having. A lot of these reviews are very misleading and can be discouraging. Most likely made by students not cut out to be engineers. Practically everyone got an A- or higher in my quarter for SE1. The material is manageable without Statics, and with minimal phys. SHE CARES.
Pls don't, she's more than terribad it's actually hilarious. Too much homework, terrible lecturer, and she doesn't know what she's doing. 0/10 would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She tends to be mirco-managing.  Lectures are mostly examples (which are rushed) and not very useful in explaining the class material.  Exams are fair.  Homework is hard and takes several hours to complete.  (7-9 hours).  Overall do NOT take her class.
Hahahaha do not take her. It's that simple.

The average on each test was below 50%, with a standard deviation of about 20%. She demonstrates no mastery over the material, so don't expect to learn from lecture. It doesn't matter if you read, because her questions are so poorly worded you wont get the answer even if you did read. Avoid her if you're in MAE. I know I won't be taking her again.

Forced students to go to glass because of iclicker counting towards the grade lecture is not interesting at all. She ask lecture guess to read the ppt , she even cancel the class when lecture guess can't come (who is the professor??) barely teach the calculation, but expected student to do calculation on exam never recommend her as professor

I would avoid VDE like she had a very contagious and deadly disease. It is unnecessarily hard and goes over stuff like statics that is beyond a student that hadn't taken 101A or even Phys2A for that matter. Just wait until she's not taking it. a B- in an intro class is pretty ridiculous and I consider myself a pretty hardworking student

She is very good at talking with a clear voice, however she goes way too fast and has no mercy in regards to test. Had to take tests at 8 in the morning while homework was also due at 8. Mastering is terrible and gives way too much homework that are very difficult and takes at least 4+ hours to do. Be prepared to spend a lot of time. Way too fast.

She is very hard and makes each student put a lot of effort for the homework and tests. Took her for dynamics as well and did not pass. Very passionate about teaching however, it is better to ask ta for questions because she usually dismisses the questions or gives vague answers. Goes way too fast and she has no mercy in regards to the cost of books

Way too difficult, it will take you a lot of time. A different assignment every week. I suggest taking easy classes when taking this one. Lectures are easy to understand and exams are easy. But labs and projects will make you hate it.

Considering myself a pretty hardworking student, I have to say this class is kinda stupid.  Remember, this class was supposed to an introductory level for incoming freshman students, but the professor made the class unnecessarily  complicated and vague. Make sure you have taken mechanics and statics before you take this class!
Turned a intro freshman course into a nightmare avoid her at all cost or change your major.

VDE is by far the worst professor I've had while at UCSD. I've only had here for SE1 which I figured wasnt going to be that difficult considering its an intro class for freshman. As a transfer student this class is a ridiculous requirement and to top things off she made this class 10X harder than it needs to be. Switch majors if you can she blows.

Absolutely a condescending professor with a high school teacher attitude. She warped a freshman intro class into a very complicated course with topics ranging from ethics to in-depth solid mechanics problems. There are no pre-reqs but be sure you take Statics before this class.

Good lecturer with a clear audible voice. I recommend taking statics first (or concurrent enrollment) cuz it will make studying for the midterm and final alot easier. For the iclicker questions, try to write down the answer or something cuz they usually appear on her tests.

She is a terrible professor. Half the time I see her before class, she is cramming the lecture. She cannot even answer basic questions. She will try to either give you a bs answer filled with big words or go "thats the way I was taught" and go about her lecture. Makes mistakes all the time. Go to TA's. They are the real professors of her classes.
She has to be one of the best engineering professors here!  She's clear and great at explaining the main concepts. We had quizzes every other week, but beware her final was super hard!

She is a pretty solid professor. Everything in the class is pretty straightforward. There are not many surprises throughout the class and certainly no surprises that can really harm your grade. If you go to class and understand the homework (which is mandatory), you should do well in the class.

She has done her job very well. Be prepared to spend good amount of hours every week for homework. Homework takes time, midterms/quizzes are okay but final is killer. I love her. The best teacher at UCSD by far for me.

Awesome lecturer. She's very clear and uses powerpoint, but doesn't just read off the slides. For SE 1, we had 3 hour lectures, but they always managed to maintain my interest and we got a 10 minute break. I think she explains concepts very well and while the tests were really difficult, they're curved so the class is passable. I recommend her.

Statics: Dr. Van Den Einde is a really good proffesor, probably the best I have taken at UCSD. Her lectures are always helpful and the homework can be a nuisance but the exams are much easier than the homework. The final was tricky, but she does apply a big curve to the final grades. If you can, take her; luckily Im taking her next quarter for 130B

Mechanical Vibrations class. She explains decently but TAs review sessions are great help. I strongly suggest you go to review sessions. Project is awesome and it will give you whole picture of SDOF vibration concept. Textbook she used really sucks. I prefer Fundamentals of Mechanical Vibrations by Kelly. It's a way better textbook.

took her for 101a-c. statics is easy, dynamics and vibs are wayy hard. she used good textbook for 101a-b but for vibs, the book couldn't be worse. for a-b she would do weekly 'quizzes' but they do help in the long run. vib you have 2 midterm, prject, and final. ok prof, recommended i guess. she usually has good TA's.the solution manual= A or B
Awesome professor! Go to class and take notes and you will do fine. Her tests are not tricky.
Great teacher, crystal clear, speaks english well, tests are hard but she helps you a equal amount, really loved her class, if your taking the 130 series make sure you take it with her
4 midterms in one quarter is too much that you may not be able to dig time for other classes. The final was comprehensive and she never said what would be in it!
Loved her! She's caring and helpful, GREAT PROFESSOR.  Her quizzes were alright, really lenient on grading.  Definitely recommend her for the 101 series. *She has great TAs too!
Her quizzes are really fair, but her final is very hard. Don't recommend her at all.

great professor! she teaches you everything you need to know for her quizzes, go to lecture for concept questions she may ask! very nice if you contact her about anything. retake-quiz system is awesome. highly recommend.

Very encouraging and helpful professor.  Her weekly quizzes are fair and reflect her lectures, so make sure you attend each of them.  Her lectures are comprehensible, and I hardly look into the book as my primary learning.

If you stay ahead of everything and really suck up to her you will be fine, but do not be fooled by her fake interest in her students.  She is impossible to communicate with and does not seem to understand problems all the students have.  Wouldn't really recommend her but she is usually the only option for SE classes so good luck.
101A. She is a great professor. Offers quiz retakes for a better grade. If you go to class and do the hw (which is not graded) you will ace this class! Highly recommended!
Teaches very well, tons of good examples. go to class and you will ace it. Actually teaches students, cares about them learning.
Good times in Lelli's class. She is fair and cares about her students.
She is a very nice and funny professor. The class is easy but useful if you really dive in and try to learn from the homework.

About 3 presentations with 1 of them being a group prestation for your final. The HW was based on concepts barely covered in class was done through CODE (python). I had no prior experience to coding, so this was hard to learn on top of figuring out the concepts with this. If you already have a small or any experience in python then it's not so bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Katya is an amazing professor! Took her class, and her lectures were awesome. She gave us lots of extra credit opportunities and gave feedback on assignments all the time (super quickly). Definitely would take her class again if I had the opportunity.
She is an amazing professor. However, in the lab classes a lot of your grade is determined by your TA. The class itself was structured well. The reports were sometimes a lot of work.

Dr.Katya is friendly and caring. I withdrew in week 4 because I bombed her first exam due to poor study habit and not spending enough time for the materials. She offered extra credits thru quizzes, weekly hw, 2 midterms, and a final. I recommend her to everyone
Dr Katya is an amazing professor, and she really cares about her students so if you put in some efforts you can easily do well in her class. She's also just a really nice person in general.

Great professor! She is clear and concise and adds lots of extra credit. Homework is at a medium difficulty. Her grading is a lot more forgiving than most professors and she provides great notes for her class. I would definitely recommend this professor.
Great professor, highly recommend her for MAE 20 and MAE 160. She really cares about the students and does a great job at teaching.
Great professor, straightforward concepts and exams. Plenty of interesting supplemental material, and very accessible outside of class for help. That bad review is out of place
Great prof. Recommend her for both MAE 160 and 20.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! Took her for MAE 20 and 160 and could not recommend Dr. Evdokimenko more. Very clear class and grading criteria. She really cares about the class and our learning.
Very good professor. Good lecturing style (easy to understand). Midterms are comprehensive.  One awful rating makes non sense.

Lots of extra credit opportunities. The way she makes the class structured for the first half of the quarter is extremely easy if you put in the work, concepts on first midterm are just drawing in 3D. Homework picks up a lot for second half of quarter, but some assignments are basically participation points and the hard ones you have 2 weeks.
Really wish she taught more classes.
She is very caring and helpful
Professor Evdokimenko is a great professor. Her course layout is really clear and the homework isnt too difficult. She also always gives feedback on graded assignments. 10/10 would recommend:)

She's really cool, go talk to her in office hours. Great down to earth person. Teaching wise she's good, although her lecture style consisted of reading off slides that were pretty dense. On one hand, its helpful because even if you miss lecture everything is on the slides, but on the other hand, it does get kinda boring. She's into rock climbing!
If you pay extra attention to the hw then the exams should not be too hard. lowest exam was dropped, plus everything on the exams comes from the lecture slides and hw
Truly cares about the students' learning and progress!

Okay, so the people here are being far too harsh. I had Xu Wang the quarter before, and she is miles better than him. For a first time professor, she is honestly pretty good, but yes she could use some improving. Try going to her office hours, as she does try and help.

hooooooooorible lectures, unclear and tough grader. expect hard tests

she was good...i think she is a theorist...easy to understand

should be easy class but unpredictable. review guide out of date = unusable. little effort put into test questions, some questions historically incorrect, many come down to semantics = even if you understand something its still hard. iclickers never figured out = attendance concerns for everybody. barely studied but locked in cls. 2 qz 1 mid 1 finl
Taught pretty good, but kinda a yapper
tell too many stories of personal anecdotes I felt didn't positively effect class.

Super kind and passionate professor, as well as very informative and insightful during her lectures. Quizzes and tests were not difficult as long as you reviewed the lecture slides + she gives extra credit, which helps you out a lot since the class is based on total points.

Very kind and passionate professor with impressive field experience. The material isn't hard and prepares you for other upper div global health classes. Make sure to do the extra credit assignments offered.

great professor and caring. The only disadvantage of her is that she uses a lot of personal analogies in her lectures and it can feel just a bit repetitive. Some of her stories and experiences are really interesting though. Extra credit is offered.

She's nice but her lectures are boring. The class content is really easy and all the concepts are pretty self-explanatory. I love Professor El Wardani. Coming from the Middle East, she is someone whom I could relate to. Besides that, the content in her class was so interesting that I'm planning to minor in Global Health. DO NOT PICK THIS PROFESSOR! She's one of the best professors I've had so far. Her lectures are clear, and she also shares her own experiences related to some topics that I find eye-opening, which helps me learn things faster. Professor Wardani is very caring and inspirational. Her lectures are filled with New research within the world of global health and from experiences she has seen. I would highly encourage you guys to take her class.

BEST PROFESSOR IN DSC DEPT. I've taken a lot of other classes taught by Justin and all of them were perfect! I learned so much from his lecture and he is very good at explaining difficult concepts.

she was such a kind and chill professor. I had mental health issues and she was accommodating and understood when I communicated with her. Her work is super easy, and there were like two essays total. extremely easy and fun class
