As far as her teaching goes, Dr. Troemel is very clear and engaging and she makes sure to go over important material at least twice. 46% of the class has over an A-! Great professor teaching a very interesting subject. 1010 would take again.

Dr. Troemel is the absolute sweetest! :) Her cute sense of humor and quirkiness made an 8 AM bearable and worth going to. The assignments she posts every week are a helpful way to study for the midterm (40%) and final (60%) (her exams are very similar to the questions in the assignments, so make sure to do them!). 5% extra credit with clicker too.
Great teacher! Super nice. Smokin hot!!!

DO her assignments because that is literally the midterm and final. She posts all of her lectures on TED, and she provides 5% extra credit for iclicker. She is very interactive and encourages her students to answer her questions, which is something very few professors do here. I really enjoyed her class, and genetics itself is a fascinating topic.

She is very passionate about her teaching, and did her best to make lectures interesting at 8am. Be sure to always do her assignments, because they are reflective of what will show up on the exams. There is only one midterm and one final, so if you screw up one like I did, it will be difficult to make it up.

Dr. Troemel is absolutely my most favorite professor I've had at UCSD. She is so passionate about the topic and shows that she really cares about her students. Her exams are extremely reasonable if you attend lecture and do her problem sets. She actually makes me excited to go to an 8AM lecture.

Good lecturer. Very friendly and helpful in office hours. Distributes a problem set every week that is solved in discussion section. The test questions are pretty much copied from these sheets, so an A is not hard to obtain. No need to buy any textbook. Would recommend.

She is really boring.  He test questions weren't clear.  She never worked out any problems on the board.  She is not too difficult because genetics isn't too difficult.  I would recommend a different professor if you want to learn more.

She was very helpful. Go to her office hours, and she makes an effort to learn your name. She is very excited about the subject. It was her first time teaching, so it was a bit rocky, but with a couple of years of experience, she will probably be an excellent teacher.
BEST TA!!! Cares about his people, help you prepare. Best TA you can have.

Emre's passion for teaching history is extremely evident-- as a TA, he is so kind and caring towards his students, offering many office hours before midterms and the final. He makes everyone feel welcome and his puppy, Haru, always brightened the mood during early morning discussions. Would absolutely recommend. This guy is like Keanu Reeves Jesus.

Emre is my GOAT. He is the chillest, nicest TA ever and his dog Haru Gaia is such a cutie patootie (he lets us pet her :) ). Everyone can do well if you do your best and talk to Emre. 100,000,000,000,000/10 recommend.

Emre was my TA for MMW 11 - dude is the chillest, nicest, most caring TA I've had so far :D
He had a lot of students, but really did make a very strong effort into getting to know everyone. We

Emre was an amazing TA. Really cares to get the students prepared for the exams and understand the content. Provided helpful resources you can use to study if you take notes on what is done in discussion, but also they're available on Canvas.
This is the best TA I've ever had. Genuinely wants you to do well, gives great feedback, and there are ample opportunities to meet with him for help if you need it. Made MMW so much more digestible.
Great TA outlines what he wants and prepares you for tests well
gives great feedback on papers, chill guy, too nice to be real tbh he feels like a dream!
Literally one of the best TA's ever. Super awesome guy, he really cares about his students

BEST TA ever for MMW! He's a super nice and caring person and if you show up, do the work and try your best, you'll pass this class with a high grade no problem :) Would 1000% like to have this TA again

Genuinely one of my favorite professors. He is extremely funny and explains concepts really well. However, the exams are pretty hard in comparison to the homework and lectures. Synthesis reactions can be hard, especially since there's not really much practice for it, even when you have the homework.

His 8am lecture is like talking in his sleep. The lecture material is like 2+2, but his test is like make a nuclear bomb. The avergae is okay, but the sd is very high. Your classmates are genius. The grade are almost based on your midterms and final. If you want an A-, you must have the avergae+sd.

his lectures weren't even that bad but his midterms and tests were really terribly horrendous. His test avgs were literally 50-60% and he curves the avg to a B-  HW was optional and he gave 10pts extra for finishing midterms early. Ochem is rlly hard but he didnt make it any easier.

Really engaging and funny lectures. Approachable and down-to-earth professor. Highly recommend, especially for the organic chem courses. Your grades will unfortunately just depend on exams, but he's generally a fair grader, and his practice exams prepare you very well for the actual exams. You do need to constantly do practice problems, though.

Very good prof. Tough course material but he made it as easy and entertaining as possible. Super energetic, esp. for an 8AM class. Really learned alot, lectures were very entertaining. Just prepare to put in the work and ride the curve and youll be chilling.
Very difficult class but he's a good professor and teaches well.
Explain concepts and reactions well and provide very useful notes. Awesome lecturer

I was fighting tears during the final after he said we didn't deserve to be in his class if we couldn't do one of the questions. Okay lecturer, but I feel like he didn't prepare us for the exams since they were way harder than the practice ones. I went from loving 41A and scoring very well to failing this final... at least he curves heavily

There are a lot of low ratings (WI25) and I wanted to say he wasn't that bad. You just need to study. The things he says like "weeding out weak links" and people "not belonging" are said in obvious joking manners, but I can see how they rub students the wrong way. He genuinely does care about students and chemistry, but exams can be hard.
The final exam was very bad, nothing like the last winter practice final

Professor made lectures very confusing by bringing up unnecessary topics. Tests were much more difficult compared to practices and gave us hundreds of homework problems that didn't cover the right topics. Also told students they didn't belong in his class during the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor shows clear bias toward certain students. Doesn't believe in fair grading policies with subjective rubric and exams don't cover the content covered in class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a pretty good lecturer but his tests are harsh or maybe I'm just dumb. Final tore me apart and left me questioning everything. He is very caring and sweet though and encourages asking even the simplest of questions.

Good lecturer but very harsh grader. Heard that basically every regrade request to him results in a lower grade for exams which sucks in an exam heavy class. Also made a policy that anyone who finished the exam in half time got EC after too many people complained about time limit. Honestly very demoralizing while taking the exam and kinda hurtful.

used to actually like chem until his class where he penalizes every small error, and grades so harshly. Made me consider changing my major so many times and the grading policies actually made me depressed. This class made me reconsider everything and finding motivation after it was difficult praying for my career and grade now
Funny lectures but harsh 8AM & unclear explanation. Actual Exams are much harder than the practice one.

Theodorakis is a very funny and engaging lecturer. However, HE IS A HARSH AND UNFAIR GRADER. His midterms have barely any partial credit and putting an answer with a slight mistake will earn you the same points as leaving it blank. TIME CONSTRAINTS for midterm 1, and very low averages. BOASTS ABOUT "weeding out weak links"

I personally wasn't a fan of Theodorakis's class. His slides are very wordy and hard to digest at 8 am. 41B is the hardest of the series in my opinion, and having that early morning timeslot does not help. As a professor, he is pretty good and gives good explanations during lecture. His exams are fair, and are likely the easiest I've taken.

Awesome lecturer, explained in great details about the material. ET is really ethusiastic about the material he taught, and managed to make the class humurous in 8am. Exams are much more easier than the other Ochem professors, you can do very well as long as you practice textbook problems. But the grading scale is extremely rigorous, average ~2.65.

The best professor I have ever had. He is the only professor whose class I would willingly go to an 8am lecture and enjoy every single minute of it. He was so hilarious and had such a contagious energy that it was hard NOT to pay attention. But above all else, he is truly a great professor and I can tell he really wants us to learn the material.

Decent lecturer, great slides, but the exams do not look like the slides. He often cooks up his own problems so you're expected to apply the mechanisms. Theodorakis will help you but only if you ask. Funny guy who tried his darnedest to have a lucid class for an 8am lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ochem is definitely hard, but ET puts a lot of emphasis on strategies versus memorization. His ochem methodology is very intuitive, despite it being hard. All this class requires is a lot of effort, and ET helps you a lot through this.

Professor T was awesome. He will make you actually enjoy ochem, which is a really difficult thing to accomplish. Even though it was an 8 am lecture, he always showed up with tons of energy and went through the mechanisms with a lot of details. Attend discussion and SI sections if you want a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: ET is a pretty good prof. He has good slides to study from and is straight to the point about what he wants you to know. He provided past exams for us to look at and tells us some specific concepts that are gonna be on the exam too which was very helpful. HW graded by submission is part of the grade def helps it and he gave EC for failing students

Professor Theodorakis was the nicest professor that u have ever taken. He had amazing slides and explained things extremely well. He assigned graded for completion homework with enough examples to understand the material. That being said, because there is not graded homework and a bunch of busy work assignments your grade comes down to the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor ET is nice and all, but I swear this has been the hardest class I've taken. For the 140A I passed with an A, however I feel like no matter how much I study or how, there is no way this helps with taking the midterms. The class is primarily based on 2 midterms and 1 final with homework assignments. Too difficult.

Prof ET is a great guy. His lecture slides are a great resource to use to study. He basically sums up all of the important concepts and mechanisms for each of the chapters onto the slides which makes it very unnecessary for us to read through the textbook. BUT the tests are RLY HARD. And your grade lies in the 2 midterms and 1 final so GOOD LUCK
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I enjoyed his teaching well enough, he's very lively and it makes the 8am class less tedious. However, I found the course very difficult and if you aren't a great test taker just know the three exams are basically the only things in the grade book. Do LOTS of practice problems and go to DI and you'll be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His slides sum everything up very nicely and his lectures give just enough details about what's going on for you to be able to understand. Completely rational and good at answering questions and making decisions on the spot. Gives everything to you straight and says you exactly what you need to do to pass with full honesty although tricky at times.
Great guy, but horrible at teaching. Its just easier to learn the material by watching The Organic Chemistry Tutor on youtube.

Very nice guy and really cares about your learning. Does review sessions on the weekend before exam which helped a lot, and the previous exams are really good for practicing! Know the concepts well, Bc exams are hard and his questions are unique. Take him if ur ready to work and learn a lot! I feel prepared for the ochem on mcat after his class

The grade is composed of three tests: 2 midterms and 1 final. He gives good notes for us to study and prepare for tests. However, he is not quite accessible through email. Btw, I am not in the US due to the pandemic and have jet lag, so its inconvenient for me to go to his oh.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Theodorakis is very nice and cares about his students. I had a very hard time in this class since grades are based on 2 midterms and the final. I found the lectures very confusing. Honestly the curve and the 400 problems for extra credit helped me pass. If ur good at ochem, take him but if not good luck.

Theodorakis is super understanding and his lectures are honestly pretty fun. He gave our class extra credit options even though it wasn't on the syllabus just because someone asked, which was pretty cool. His exams are definitely difficult, so you'll have to sink in quite a few hours to do well but there's a fat curve at the end of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: VERY HARD TESTS!!!!!!!!!!

I really loved his class. The exams are open-note, but that doesn't mean don't study. The exams are LONG so definitely either know the reagents by heart or condensed cheat sheet readily available. He really appreciates when students participate, and it's a lot more fun when people shout out answers (whether they're right or not).
A man who really knows his chemistry!
I really didn't like him. He's just like every other hands off UCSD professor that makes your whole grade based on a couple heavily weighed, difficult exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Funny guy and seems to care about his students but exams are very difficult and not representative of what is gone over in lecture. Easy mechanisms and reactions are shown in lecture but the level of difficulty on exams is ramped up much higher. His notes he provides are good for studying and provide a good general knowledge of the class.
Explains very easy mechanisms in class but content on exams is extremely hard. Somewhat unorganized in teaching. He's a nice guy who cares about his students but I don't feel prepared at all for 40C
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a caring professor but his exams are super hard. The things he teaches in lecture are nothing like his exams. He really expects you to know your stuff just to pass the class. He doesn't use the whole class time for the midterms and for the final only gives 2 hours. I don't recommend taking this professor!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Truly horrible professor, his tests are nothing like what he teaches at lectures. I have a good understanding of topics, homework questions but still struggle to understand how he manages to create the hardest exams. His practice tests are also nothing like the actual tests. I don't know how he sleeps at night but he made my life a living hell.

He is super funny and approachable. However his tests are VERY HARD!!! Its mostly synthesis which he has never done examples of in class. He only does very simple mechanisms in class but tests you on a much higher level on the midterm. His exams are harder than the previous year midterm he gives you as a practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is super funny, and really cares about his students. His lectures are actually worth attending even though it was 8am as the way he teaches the class grabs student's attention. I strongly recommend it although his tests were harder than you expect.

Overall, Dr. E is awesome. His lectures are always a blast to attend. He discusses what is to be expected from you to help you prepare for the exams. His exams are very representative of his practice exams and content he tells you in class, so no surprises! He's such an approachable and chill professor! Office hours are welcoming and helpful!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Theodorakis is such a great professor! He really cares about his students and their success in his class. Is readily available to help outside of class and does a great job presenting material in a way that is easily understood by students. He is in no way arrogant or intimidating like other chem staff here.

Ochem is not an easy subject in general but he tried to boil down explanations to the best of his ability! He's super funny and I think one of the best ochem profs at UCSD. He doesn't make you learn all the mechanisms but beware of synthesis problems because that'll be the most difficult part (Primarily what you see in 2nd midterm and final)

Maybe it's just me, but I had no trouble understanding what Professor T was saying.  The mechanisms in his notes aren't very difficult, but doing the representative exams and homework will help.  First midterm was easy (to send a signal to weak students), 2nd midterm more difficult (separates A students and B students) and the final is the final.

Theodorakis is a hilarious and well respected professor. He makes Ochem fun and enjoyable! First midterm (super easy) is in week 2/3 to weed out the D's and under students. Second midterm (extremely hard) is in week 7/8 to differentiate between the A and B students. Final is HARD.

My advice to you is stay on top of the homework and go to the review sessions.  He tells you what not to study in the review sessions so you don't waste a lot of time.  Overall he was pretty fair since he didn't make us learn overly complicated mechanisms, but his tests are tough because you have to combine multiple concepts into one mech. problem.

Dr.T is by far the best organic chem professor I've had.  The only downside to his class is the exams are quite difficult but you don't need very many points to simply pass.  Getting a B requires some effort (doing hw) but getting an A depends on natural talent since certain problems require you to think but time is limited.  His lectures are clear

Dr. T is a brilliant man. His knowledge of his field and 140B in particular is beyond measure. His truly understands the material on a level that can answer any question students throw at him. The spacing between midterms was weird (one was week 3, the other week 9!) but was doable. Final was super difficult but he gave us freebies towards the end.

He makes ochem very understandable. Clear and funny lectures,but board problems he did were very general. I wished that he would do more examples on the board, but knowing the general cases is very important too. Otherwise, his tests are similar to his practice exams. Midterm 1 was NMR. Midterm 2 was reactions and 1 mechanism. Final- mechanisms!

This is a very difficult class.  Dr. T is an excellent professor and makes ochem easy to follow.  I did bad in 140A but really improved in this class because Dr. T doesn't test on random stuff.  Instead, the first test is mostly (75% of it) C and H NMR.  Second midterm and final are mostly mechanism and multi-step synthesis. Study practice exams!

Best professor I've had so far at UCSD, and the only one to keep me up during an 8 am. Makes everything in ochem super clear, something the book tends to overcomplicate. His tests may be more complicated than book problems, but it is all very logical and follows usual mechanisms. Just make sure you don't fall behind. If you want to learn, take him.

2 midterms, 1 final. First midterm emphasized on H and C NMR. Second exam and final are all  on mechs. Gives 2 practice exam for every exam and are good representations with good ans keys. No big surprises on the tests and does not test on random things like what whitecell does. Exams are hard-I believe.

A very clear, very informative lecturer. He does have a strong greek accent but it does not get in the way of his explanations. Beware though: his midterms are tough, lots of mechanisms and retro synthesis. Overall he has great sense of humor and is very helpful when you ask him questions.
very helpful professor. He is smart and funny. Made ochem very easy and all of his examples are clear and easy to follow. Best ochem professor eveeerr! :) i recommend him!

Very helpful professor, really loves students. Explained reactions many times so that even if you are lost in a mechanism you can use some common sense to decipher it. However, there is no partial credit on exams which becomes a little unfair when u may only remember part of a mechanism. Overall, great professor and would take him again.

This guy is hilarious and he definitely shows concern for the students' learning. Will answer questions no matter how dumb they are to the class. His teaching style was very clear to me at least. The TA (Ed) never showed up to section (whenever I went) though.

Great lecturer with a sense of humor; explains material and chemical mechanisms very well using a combination of chalk and powerpoint overview. Tends to use the chalkboards on the right, so sit on the right... Exams generously curved; holds review sessions prior to exams. Overal great and entertaining professor!

Fair professor for an overall difficult class (140B). Study his notes and master the old exams and you'll do fine. Tends to skip over some material, but less stuff on exams is fine by me. Here's hoping it doesn't come back to haunt me in 140C. Also, go to TA Ed's section if you can; best chem TA I've ever had at UCSD by far.

Good professor, he reviews his topics multiple times in class for clarity and his midterms/finals are representative of the materials in both his set of notes and his old practice midterms.  I did really bad in 140A but improved in his class.Focus mainly on the notes he provides because it is really helpful! I did not even use the book at all!

Good professor.Always has time for students. Test aren't easy but they are doable.His notes are very helpful and his curve is generous.Problems are usually worth a lot of points, if you do a couple you are bound to pass

I got an A in Perrin, one of the "harder" 140A professors and I thought he was a much better professor than this guy. Theodorakis just didn't have the right teaching style to match his exams. The average wasn't that low because the average student in the class pretty much regurgitated any reagents they could remember from class and get partial.

Everyone stop crying. Dr. T is an awesome teacher. Yes the fake email was funny, what do you expect him to do babysit all of you and tell you it's gonna be okay? Get over it. as far as him as a teacher, T is awesome. And he's hilarious once you get to know him. I'd recommend him over any O chem prof at UCSD.

Agreed, funny guy but lectures consist of the basic mechanism of rxns and moving on. No further examples. Then when you get to the test-even after solving all the book problems-you'll sit there and ask yourself WHERE did he get this from. I'm glad I'm not the only one who felt this way. After having an awesome 140a class I feel behind now in C..

Highly over-rated. Lectures, somewhat entertaining but material presented is nowhere near what is actually tested. Not even doing all of his homework problems would help you on his exams. Office hours are useless, goes on random tangents and starts writing emails while you attempt to ask him a question and end up waiting 5 minutes so he can finish.

He must've been a joke last year if he gave you what's gonna be on the exams. That certainly wasn't the case this year. He's an enjoyable lecturer but his exam questions don't really correlate with book problems so it wasn't very useful doing the homework for M1/M2

omg final open notes. completely useless n super hard. dont understand his accent. teaches from transparency and moves projector screen to write on board then moves screen over the writing. didnt go to class. First half taught by O'Connor - much better. Got an A- only cause evry1 probably failed final. cake for grads. hell for udergrads.

I didn't take his class, but my roommate was taking it at the same time than me and I was using her notes to understand my class! He is along with O'Connor, the best OChem Professor. I ended up skipping mine and going to his instead.

wow.. I LOVEEE this guy!! all you have to do is go to him and ask if "this reaction" is going to be on the test or if "that reaction" is going to be on the test..he will just tell you "yes yes yes" or "no no no".It seems kind of wrong at first..kind of like you're cheating..but he's SOO funny and cool about it..he'll just tell you what to study for

He was a pretty funny professor during class, maybe a little too much. His accent was ok but it was hard to understand especially if your trying to learn all those reactions that we had to learn. His tests were pretty difficult so i would try to avoid if possible. I would take hoeger or ternansky if possible

He's very organized. GO TO THE REVIEW SESSIONS! He tells you EXACTLY what's going to be on the midterm. His office hours are very helpful also, don't be afraid to ask him what's on the test ;) He does have an accent but it's very comprehensible. His final was ridiculously easy and was pretty much all recycled questions from previous midterms

Good professor.  Explained material very well.  The problems we did in class were extremely easy compared to some of the exam questions, but if you and understand the problems from the book, you will be good to go.  He is a fair professor.  I would definitely take him again.
His notes are good for studying. He frivolously assigns hw. Know your reactions. Tests are fair, but difficult.

Dr. Greek was probably my favorite ochem prof. His exams are hard and really focus on details- but he curves it fairly to help give everyone the grade they want. definatley get brian phan as a TA if you can, he gives you problems you wouldnt expect so i was almost overprepared. hats off to the greek stallion!

He is Greek-tastic! He wears clothes that are a little too tight, but he learned me o-chem pretty good. The midterms and final were fair. What made this class was the T.A. Bryan, who was, for lack of a better word, amazing. I'd probably recommend Dr. Theodoropolis.
Material is overwhelming. Need to know a lot of mechanisms for the final. His notes make it seem easy.. but the tests...epecially the final is very hard.

uses old school overhead projector for lectures; impossible to read unless you sit in the front rows. actually told us that the rest of a chapter was not that difficult when he ran out of time to lecture before the midterm, and told us to just read it and figure it out ourselves. take perrin instead if he teaches 140 B, hes a better teacher.
great class, great prof. Just might have to study a bit more for MCATs since it he made it really easy!

His handouts were helpful but the class is challenging. Dont ever buy the molecular model they are like $50 instead I bought an ochemplate which is a fraction of a price at www.ochemplate.com. Very useful tool.
not very effective, but very easy!

very nice guy, doesnt expect you to know too much useless stuff, and the material is pretty hard. You have to go to office hours a lot (TA's office hours help), and lots and lots and lots of stuff to memorize in that class.
great guy... gives handouts that he covers exactly what he teaches, w/ no bs... funny and keeps your attention during lecture... definately take this guy.
Very fun prof! Can explain mechanisms very well.  Very helpful outlines.  Don't need to read book. TAKE HIM!

He posts his chapter outlines online which are very helpful for studying. Its a tough class but if you work at it you can get an A. Exams are challenging but very doable if you studied and know what you're doing.
His test are super hard...so theres a huge curve but still if u dont no your**** WELL...your gonna bomb his test...and i got an A so i no what im talking about

Dr. Theodorakis is the shizzzznit!  This guy is a chemistry wizard and he explains it super well.  Final is short and tough but I still got an A in the class.  I recommend Dr. Theo big time above Dr. Bob, who I took for 140A!
Straight forward exams and interesting lecture.  O Chem is just very difficult, but he is great to take it with.
His tests were difficult, but definitely not impossible.  Really good professor, outlines helped ALOT!
overall good prof...harder than expected though, but tests were fair.  class requires a lot of study time...helpful in office hours, can be funny in lecture.

I totally have favorites and my favorite chem Prof so far was Dr. Bob! Theodorakis was no Dr. Bob; he didn't have such a charming sense of humor and expressed a lot less care in his students' learning. But if all you want is a D in the class, he's the Prof to take!

His test is pretty much based on the book problems, yet challenging!  He likes to mix severals chapters into 1 problem.  I like his online outline, very details and helpful to study.  Memorize as much as u can, then u can make connection from 1 chpt to the next!
This guy was SUPER nice and very helpful.
He really cares about you learning. He's got some quirky things about him, but overall, he's very fair.
His tests were pretty fair and he did a good job telling us exactly what would be covered on the exams.

By far the most interesting upper div bio lab I've ever taken. Concepts are seemingly unrelated to each other but what you're expected to know is very surface level. Got to leave lab early most days. Lab reports are fairly graded, especially if you ask tons of questions during or after lab for guidance. Shoutout to my TA, Brad, the GOAT.

This is my second class with Dr. Grossman and she is amazing! Lectures not mandatory but lab is. One midterm and one final that are similar to weekly problem sets. Opportunities for extra credit. Very caring and understanding professor willing to help you in any way she can. I have recommended her to multiple people; amazing professor!

Amazing professor. I enjoyed her class and her style (although I know others didn't). Her class wasn't difficult compared to other classes/professors but it still requires work because it is a biology class. Her exams were a mixture of MC and FRQ. Second midterm was rough but she acknowledged and adjusted accordingly. Understand the problem sets!!

Nice prof and good at lecturing.Slides are well organized,clear on what you need to know.Attendance not mandatory.I had HARD classes I took with this one,kinda back-burnered it and managed a B.Studied about 2 hours a MT.Hw is a PS weekly and graded for correctness, and 2 MTs and a Final.I knew a lot beforehand tho so it was an easier pass for me.

A bit rough as a lecturer, but clearly explains concepts and how to solve problems. The key to success is really understanding how to solve problems on the problem sets and not just memorizing the answer, though there are some things to memorize. Tests were mostly writing, and similar to problem sets. A fair and do-able class

Attendance for lectures & discussions are optional. Slides are fairly organised. Content is relatively easy. But her practice tests given before each midterm (which only have MCQs) do not reflect the difficulty of her actual midterms (which are FRQ-heavy). Be ready to write a lot during her test (but she will curve if the entire class did poorly).
My brain had to work more in this class compared to my calculus classes but I think I can score at least 200% on the genetics MCAT section now. I just needed to study for 25 hours daily.

She is very good at answering questions and clearing up any confusion w/ the content. Lots of extra credit provided. Exams were well written but difficult and contained a lot of short answer questions in a short amount of time. Make sure you have a thorough understanding of each topic bc a lot of critical thinking is required.

she talks fairly slow in my opinion and her actual exams are nothing like the practice/past exams she gives to study. she also gets stuck a lot during lectures and stops constantly and sometimes even confuses herself. her exams are long and mainly saqs with sub parts to them so get ready to write a lot and fast for the minimum time that is given.

Can't really learn much from the lecture. The contents are not that hard but explained poorly. Had to spend a lot of extra time understanding some of the content. 
The professor is a nice person but probably not the best teacher.
Dr. Grossman is the absolute best. I had a very enjoyable experience in her class and she is highly respected by students. Super approachable and supportive.

I personally felt that she was great at answering questions asked by her students. Is able to approach answers from different angles so students can understand at a deeper level. Not a lot of workload and reasonable due dates. Don't do Friday discussions bc assignments are due Friday and you don't get enough time to fully digest answers.

The content itself is not hard but the midterms are hella long and most are short answer. She gave all multiple choice practice exam but the actual midterm is nothing like that. Mt2 was a nightmare and a lot of people didn't finish it. Imagine 30 questions, most are short answer and some with 2or 3 subquestions…
She doesn't really seem to know what she is talking about a lot of the time, during class she would get confused by herself
What the fk is today's midterm 2? Too long to finish and not like the practice exam at all. Many repeated thins tested.
Very straightforward lectures and lab. Problem sets accurately reflected what we learned and so did the final. 2 lab reports + weekly problem sets. Take Dr. Grossman if you can, you won't regret it!

As long as you know what is on the slides, you will do great in this class. Midterms and the final were extremely representative of the material we learned and fair. She offers lots of extra credit opportunities throughout the quarter. It's a lot of material, but if you learn it, there's no reason not to get an A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her class is not that hard, but only because she is clear about what she wants from you. Follow her lectures and review properly and you'll be fine. Three different extra credit opportunities and you can miss like 6 lectures though at that point you goofed. Be sure to review your exams on gradescope for grading errors.

Shes very sweet! during lecture she can confuse herself and forget many things easily. This class in general is DENSE LOTS OF MEMORIZING. HW straight forward. Exams are all based on memorization from slides half multiple choice and half written.  20 MT1, 20MT2, 30final the rest is based on HW and an essay (not based on correction but effort)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: truly cares about students learning & about the students themselves. make sure you do all of the problem sets as its just like the lab final. she is v knowledgeable & i hope she gets tenured because she truly deserves it. she made so many things clear to me that i never understood in lab. if you can take her you should shes the best

Prof Grossman is super nice and kind overall. I found her problem sets to be a little challenging but not the worst, and lectures were relatively easy to follow. I personally found the exams extremely fair and almost easy having watched most of the lecture content only 2-3 days before each exam. Problem sets were good prep. Overall, definitely rec.

Very accessible and helpful outside of class. No textbook, important information will be on the lecture slides. Problem sets every week are graded harshly but go into office hours before they're due and TA or Prof will help you go over it. Tests are tough and again, graded harshly. iClicker questions every lecture, so make sure to go.

Professor Grossman made concepts super easy, tests were very fair and accurately represented what was taught in lecture material. It's easy to get behind because sometimes the concepts can be straight forward, so make sure to stay up to date with the material. Grossman is very nice and you can tell that she wants her students to succeed.

She is a very caring and nice professor. Though her practice midterms were not the best prep for the actual exams, her problem sets were really good. I got a lot of help from the mandatory discussions so maybe I just had a good TA but her class was fairly easy if you just put in the work and study/memorize. Lectures were very clear too.

Study guides were not like the exams, but the problem sets were. Her exams are a little challenging, but doable. She gives quite a bit of extra credit through extra problems on exams and problem sets. Clicker q's for attendance. Sometimes she would get confused on her material, but overall she was a good prof. She was willing to help with q's too.

Terrible instructor. Problem sets are useless. Her midterms are EXTREMELY hard for no reason. Gets confused about the material that she is supposed to be a pro at during lecture. Her "extra credit" is not even extra credit. Stay away if possible.

Relatively this is not a difficult class. The exam is consistent with the lecture materials. The professor is sometimes confused with the materials and things that are on the lecture slides. 2 midterms and 1 final. Just memorize everything and you'll get an A.

She was a nice professor. Problem sets were very similar to the exams + lots of extra credit. However, also had many issues. Missed multiple online lectures + sometimes forgot to record. Would mix up sections and waste time repeating stuff or talking about irrelevant topics. Also got confused sometimes while explaining and would stop for minutes.

I love this professor! She is so caring and want you to learn and thrive in the class. The problem sets help you to strengthen the knowledge and very similar to the exam. This is my first upper bio course and I enjoy it so much!!!!!

The best bio professor I've had at this school! She is amazing. Was super accommodating with students in COVID scenarios. Has weekly problem sets and post lecture quizzes, all of which are super easy and doable if you watch the lectures. 2 midterms and a final also very easy. Discussion section attendance is mandatory, not lectures through.

Personally, I loved her teaching style. Was able to rewatch recorded lectures. Practice sets every week, relatively similar to midterm and final concepts. Just do the work and watch lectures, dont fall behind and you'll be fine :) IA discussions really helped too, they were mandatory but were graded so boosts ur grade at the end!
Very good professor, clear lectures, fair midterm and final.
Professor grossman's tests were very fair and reflective of the lecture content. The problem sets prepared me well for the exams.

I really enjoyed Dr. Grossman. She is super nice and her problem sets / discussion / lecture do reflect the exams that she puts out. I know people say they don't like her because she "can't answer questions well" but a lot of the time, students as really obscure, specific, irrelevant questions to the course.

She has quiz after every lecture, but almost everytime she cannot finish the material. She can spent 50min going through 5 slides to cover material from the last lecture. Because in the last lecture someone asked a question, she did not know the answer, and she spent 20min googling it and transcribing wikipdia to us. Her lecture is a waste of life.

Friendliest lab professor I've had and was super helpful whenever anyone asked questions or had trouble with their work. We had 8 problem sets with extra credit opportunities and 2 writeups for the class along with lab notebooks. All were generously graded. Pretty easy A, just make sure you're keeping up with the content and putting in the work.

Dr. Grossman took the time to answer every question within reason. Sometimes she would get asked something that was beyond the scope of the class which was annoying but it wasn't her fault. Exams reflected lecture and problem sets nicely so it was easy to study for them. Most people ran out of time on the first exam though. Great Professor!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: As some other reviews mentioned, she is knowledgeable in this area but sometimes has difficulty answering student questions in class. There is graded homework and short quizzes in discussion sections. Exams are multiple choice. She seems to genuinely care about her students and offers some extra credit. Wording on tests can be confusing at times.

Lectures were always pretty interesting and easy to understand. The workload was reasonable and the exams were manageable even if they seemed too long for the amount of time we had. The material was explained well and I felt like the professor really cared about our understanding of it.

She's a good professor. People mention how she doesn't know the answers to some questions students ask, but she'd never test on them. Most questions are straightforward, but some are tricky to read so be aware. IAs help a lot with worksheets in section. The class was pretty fair and she offered EC on tests, worksheets, and for filling out CAPES.

I don't recommend professor Grossman to anyone, she doesn't know anything about the class, kept asking her IAs simple questions that she should have the answer for. She doesn't know the very basic info about genetics. Plus it is all about her final because it is 35%, very heavy and hard material that she didn't cover in class,zero care for students

Lots of dry lectures, multiple problem sets, clickers, and a few extra credit points on sets/exams. Detail oriented exams but still pretty easy. She is clearly uncomfortable with the material (ended a few lectures early because she got confused and could not answer student questions); there's only 1 midterm (rather content heavy). Know all details!

Professor Grossman is nice, but when the PPT turns on the lectures are dull. She doesn't seem very comfortable w/ the material either (someone asks a Q, she says "I'm not sure" and asks the TAs to answer). Exam questions are fair, BUT she tests way too much content in 1 midterm. EC is in the form of exam questions. Should have listened to reviews!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Grossman is such a nice lady, but she is not a very good professor. Going to her mandatory lectures was such a drag, I tried my best at staying awake but she talks so slow that I just could not do it. Her tests are not too hard, everything is on her slides, no additional resources needed.

Professor Grossman was a very nice professor who, for the most part gave a fair midterm and final. While some of the questions asked about very obscure things "which end of the protein is the amino terminus" that she didn't emphasize, most of the class is very doable. Weekly problem sets very much helped. A good TA will help as well.

Grossman is a nice professor with extra credit opportunities. Lectures are rather dull and for structural biochem; she was not comfortable or knowledgeable on the material (she admitted this as well), but definitely cares about student learning. No curves, but does adjust the averages. A good TA helps; there are clickers/problem sets.

PRO: (1) Knowledgeable, passionate and caring professor. (2) Weekly problem sets help reinforce lecture. (3) Interesting material. (4) Lots of office hours. CON: (1) iClickers at each lecture. (2) Sometimes talks too slowly. (3) Tests ask a few questions about very obscure structural features of equally obscure molecules. (4) No practice exams.

Honestly, I didnt enjoy this class whatsoever. We had a sub for most of the midterm information and she had a completely different teaching style than grossman which really threw me off. Grossman also doesnt make lecture that exciting so going to class for me was such a drag. The class itself isnt extremely tuff but it is a lot of info, no curve

The midterm is super easy, average is A. However, the lectures after the midterm are extremely confusing. She talks really slow, and not good at explaining. You would need to study by yourself. The worksheets she provides for discussion are really helpful. Great prof!!

She's great, gives 1 midterm and 1 final, weekly hw, iclicker, and discussion points to boost your grade. Don't listen to the previous comment that said she didn't know anything. She's very knowledgeable in her subject. But several students in this class keep asking irrelevant questions, kind of annoying, waste class time, making us super behind.

Grossman is an awesome person and is super funny and genuinely cares about her students. BUT she is a terrible professor. Maybe its because it was her frist time teaching structural but she didnt know anything, literally was looking up things on google and teaching from wikipedia. Midterm and a final, weekly homework.
Love her. She's the sweetest teacher and is always willing to help.  Exams were straight forward and representative of her lectures.  If you can, take her.

I love Professor Grossman's class! She is very nice and would always help you out whenever you need clarifications on things. Her exams were very straight forward and fair -- really doable! I would recommend her overall.

Professor Grossman did a great job providing thorough explanations of course content. Although she didn't always know all the details of what we were doing, she was always willing to look them up for us. Her enthusiasm for the lab was infectious and her grading very reasonable. All in all, this is one of the easiest labs at UCSD.

Dr. Farley is an amazing professor and person. Lectures not mandatory, EC, problem sets, 3 midterms (one dropped), and a final cumulative exam. She is great at explaining hard concepts and often goes over the previous lecture to help.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor! 3 midterms and a final, all based on problem sets and iclicker questions. Great lectures! She does take a bit of time reviewing past material but I found it to be very helpful to understand the content well. Would highly recommend taking her class! Plus there are many extra credit opportunities.
🐐 Professor.  Exams are based on lecture questions and problem sets with lots of opportunities for extra credit.  She is the best professor I've had at UCSD, would recommend.

Honestly, one of my favorite professors. Her lectures are clear and easy to follow. The problem sets can be a bit long, but they're only assigned once a week and are really helpful for exam preparation.

She structures the class really nicely. Emphasizes understanding of concepts rather than memorizing, so exam questions are never asking you to explain an entire process, etc. Generous extra credits for attending sections + participating (5%). Class is 94% exam and 6% PS completion. Exams are very doable, very similar to things taught class.

Farley was an amazing lecturer! At the beginning of each class she had a recap that helped any confusion. Her exams are very representative of lectures and are based primarily on problem sets, polling questions, and lecture slides. Problem sets are completion based to allow you to understand without the anxiety of getting it wrong.

I honestly thought she was great! The way I honestly got an A was mostly reviewing the problem sets and applying the concepts to it. The weekly quizzes had really easy questions and there would be 1-3 questions you have to be sure about. Besides that, great teacher and I believe she is a solid choice. As long as you listen to her, you're set!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Assigned weekly quizzes which help you stay on track. Problem sets every week were 10 pages long and took forever to complete and the problems wouldn't even resemble what she taught in lecture. In class, would ramble a lot, couldn't answer questions clearly to the point where other students in the class could explain better than the professor.

Her class was so organized and she was such a sweetheart. There were weekly quizzes (one dropped) that tested you on that weeks material. Quizzes were entirely based on her lectures and problem sets which made it very easy to study for. One cumulative final. She was very clear on terminology since mol bio can be jargony sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Unorganized class. Lectures are extremely difficult to follow, had to fully rely on outside resources + textbooks. Quizzes are questions from HW, Final was difficult but well curved.
yutyum tutyu tyu y yuytu
bad teacher

The course material is easy if you have a decent grasp of basic Linear Algebra from lower-div Linear Algebra. worst prof I have ever met. make people take online quiz and exam in person in class with horrible school wifi. his accent makes his words very unclear so it's hard to know what he is talking if you don't sit close enough. lectures are unclear, quiz and exams are not related with his lecture at all. regret i didn't drop before ddl

Vavalis was probably the worst professor I have had so far. Made us take online exams in a classroom in person. UCSD wifi sucks so this made it really stressful. Had a very muffled voice, can barely hear him in lectures. And above all, he is a bad lecturer. Would not recommend him to anyone.
Not very organized, tests are on canvas with no option for partial credit. Can barely understand him in class.
I have never seem any math professor asking for essays before. He is literally the worst professor ever.
Would never take his course again
I relied a lot on the book and doing practice problems for this class, but Vavalis was very helpful during office hours and was always open to questions during class.

Professor Vavalis class is definitely hard to follow, and has to rely on textbook, which makes me feel pretty stressful at the beginning. However, he does have a fair grading scale, so as long as you attend the lecture, take good notes, and read the textbooks, you'll be fine. HAVE A GOOD MENTALITY!

reviews.comment: Lectures are very hard to follow. Professor often skips important steps when solving problems. The class is very unorganized.

Probably one of the worst classes I've taken at UCSD. Having taken courses such as Math31AH with Novak, the level of clarity and mastery over the material from Vavalis is just completely subpar. The course itself is easy in terms of content and work, but lectures were so drawn-out and pointless it hurt.

Super easy A. All quiz questions are from the textbook and homework, super fair. Lectures are a bit confusing, but if you don't understand, just go to his office hours and ask him. Lots of homework though, and only 5 tries for each submission.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Honestly Prof Vavalis deserves much better rating. He respects the students and listens to our advices. The lecture is a little confusing but handleable if you read the textbook.

The Math20D ratings for Professor Vavalis are too low. He is a nice and caring person, and he is a better teacher when students are asking questions. That said, you need to ask questions or attend office hours to pass this class. His quizzes have 1-5 questions and are multiple choice (no partial credit), but they're fair when there aren't typos.

Professor Vavalis doesn't do online lectures very well, but the material he tests on are basic and fair. You can skip the lectures and just study from the book or other online sources and be do perfectly great in that class. He allows you to drop the final and its worth the same as other quizzes, making the class stress free.

His lectures were extremely hard to understand. In fact, I rarely went to his lectures. But it should be an easy A for online classes because he has easy quizzes (you can use online calculators) and your homework worth 40% of the points(a lot of homework though). All you had to do is to watch youtube videos and study the material on your own.

reviews.comment: Made this class extremly easy, most people can get easy A/A+. 99% of hw/quiz are multiple choices, no tests, can drop the final.

After everything goes online, the quizzes and gradings get easier. They are also open book and you can use online calculators. His lectures are not very organized you need to teach yourself. If he keeps this standard and you just want a good grade, it's okay. If you really wanna learn something or try something challenging, then take someone else.

reviews.comment: Worst decision in my life as a student was taking his course. Prof. Vavalis clearly thinks that he is teaching people who are already experts on the subject. Tests are extremely difficult and grading is unclear.

reviews.comment: The worse professor ever in UCSD. There are only 2-3 problems in weekly quizzes but each worth 50 points. You need to get everything correct to get high grades. Also, answer for weekly quizzes are usually wrong because professor always make a calculation error. Whenever you got a question, the only answer that you expect is "that's how it works".

His lectures are confusing, but you get a look at the material and then learn at discussion. Assigns practice problems that are nothing like the tests. Tests are short max 4 questions in 10-13 minutes, all multiple choice, more conceptual than actual solving. There's no partial credit but often makes more answers correct so you get points back.

Comes off initially as a nice and understanding teacher, but that only lasts for the first 2 quizzes. Horrible grading standards, incredibly inconsistent, and attending lectures won't help.

reviews.comment: Even if you did all the suggested problems, you'll probably still fail the quizzes. Thus, trying to increase your luck on multiple-choice problems is the best way to prepare for quizzes/exams.

reviews.comment: Take his class if you want to fail. Lectures are incredibly hard to understand. He skips major steps and teaches like you already know the subject well. The ratings 4 this teacher r too low. He is such a nice guy and cares about your learning. He loves to answer questions, and so you don't feel stupid when asking them or if you are confused. reviews.comment: Please listen to me DO NOT TAKE this professor. He is garbage at teaching, and his quiz and tests are crazy hard and do not reflective anything done in class. If you want to fail feel free to take this professor.

Professor Vavalis' lectures are extremely hard to follow along and he skips major steps when solving example problems, leaving students with more questions than answers. Despite going to lecture, I had to teach myself the material from youtube and the textbook. He also created a piazza but would ignore half the questions.

Lectures aren't the clearest, but Professor Vavalis holds office hours after each lecture. reviews.comment: He's genuinely a nice and caring professor, but he fails to teach the material efficiently. As a result, the class is extremely difficult and confusing. If you actually want to learn, I advise you to avoid his class.

reviews.comment: he is not even familiar with the context. he made a lot of mistakes in class and seldom corrected which made things really confusing. his tests are inefficient in testing students.

Is not helpful at all. Lecture slides skip major steps so to understand I have to go back and try to fill in the gaps myself. He seems like he genuinely wants us to learn, but won't actually teach or help us with the material. Grading scheme is wack. We had weekly quizzes that were 1 multiple choice (difficult) question in 10 min. so 100 or 0. :(

Professor doesn't review material during lecture well. More than half of the time students would be confused on lecture material, he just reads equations off the slides. Only grades on quizzes, midterms, and a final. He doesn't really assign any hw and practice problems in textbook never match his tests. Also gives 1 question 100 point quizzes!

Cant rate much on this professor since I didnt see him in person (since its remote). However besides a few test questions, this instructor made the material very easy to understand thru his lectures and how we got to use excel.

Class is fairly straightforward, Pearson assignments make up the homework, and you have 2 quizzes, midterm, final, and a case study which is group if you want. The quizzes are deceptively easy compared to exams. Study lots. You will be under a lockdown browser/recorded during exams and quizzes, but they let you submit corrections for 1/3 credit.

I took prof engelbergs class remote. He and TAs respond quickly to any questions on piazza. The recorded lectures were asynchronous and help a lot with understanding the homework. We just took our midterm (synchronous) and I found it to be much more difficult than the homeworks due to lack of references. If you take this class, be ready to study!

He was overall an alright professor. Taught what was required, sometimes is confusing in his explanations. Often need to self-study through homework and textbook. Homework often was very difficult. Mandatory discussions. His tests were fair (and much easier) and were based on lecture content.

Many advanced terms beyond knowledge. No podcast, so I learn mostly from other professors(podcasts) Lots of self-study. Bad thing: you gets nothing from lectures Good thing: If you watch podcast and others don't, you are ahead of the game. However, I won't consider it "good" because I am still confused about many concepts, be aware if you take him.

Teaches straight out of the textbook but doesn't go further in depth about it. This class is only bearable because of the other prof co-teaching with him, so the tests aren't as hard and he originally was not going to allow a cheat sheet. No podcasts/online notes too. Despite attending lect, I learned everything from the previous quarter's podcast.

reviews.comment: Lecture attendance was not mandatory but discussion was. Did not learn anything from lectures. Don't waste your time...take this class if your willing to show up for the sake of attendance the leave and go figure out all the concepts from other resources. reviews.comment: Prof. Mackall is a caring teacher who is willing to walk you through the process of solving hard problems. I learned a great deal from him about integrals and such.

The professor is a tad hard to understand when going over concepts. Focused on proving why math worked instead of showing us how to do the math problems. The class was not heavy on examples. reviews.comment: Never take this class. Horrible at explaining concepts and refused to explain difficult example problems during lecture multiple times. He had this superiority complex that made him seem like he wanted to prove he was smarter than the class... He's afraid of bugs too. AVOID AT ALL COSTS (you will cry if you don't)

His first quarter teaching under the quarter system and he adjusted really well to it. The content of the class is tough but he does his best to give us the best understanding. He's hilarious and a relatable professor. Graded on few things (weekly homeworks, midterm, final).

lectures are not that great, he focuses on deriving formulas but doesn't explain well and gets confused often. homework is a reasonable amount, but sometimes doesn't relate to class content. midterm was unreasonably hard, but the final was better. compared to other profs, he is much harder. be prepared to study A LOT. listen to the 1 star reviews.

Class is tough, believe all 1 ratings. No cheat sheet, calculator, recording for lecture, mandatory discussion attendance with professor's quote "I will fail you" if you don't go 3 times, TA careless, 70% grades depend on midterm&final, VERY confusing lecture, lots of self-studying, no answer for midterm. Even professor is a very chill&nice person.
BE AWARE OF 5 RATINGS, THERE WAS A GUY WHO WITHDRAW THE CLASS AND TRIED TO GET BACK AT PPL BY GIVING 5s.

Not great at explaining the material and skips steps a lot. The final was 40% of our grade and the midterm is 30%. We were not allowed a calculator or formula sheet for either exam. The tests themselves are not curved. It is possible that the grade scale of the class may be curved. For example, a 65% may be considered a C. Lectures not recorded

reviews.comment: Take another professor, I would not recommend him. We had no cheat (crib) sheets on tests even though other classes did and still none for the final even after our midterm average was around 65%. Avoid him at all costs. No curves for exams (even though our midterm avg was like a 65%), no recorded lecture, no cheat sheet, no calculator, no study guides, late to lecture sometimes, somewhat of an uncaring attitude towards teaching. Other profs have easier tests with both calculator and a cheat sheet. You'll do decently if you study for eons.

Great teacher, make sure to attend class and discussions as they will show you what you should be studying. The class is not as difficult as some people say if you actually put time into studying and care about what you are doing. There is no cheat sheet on tests, but they are not very difficult in return. 60+ is passing, only need 87 for A-.

He made the class harder than the other sections for Math 20B, did not allow calculators, cheat sheets, or other tools that other teachers of the same course have. The curve is not representative of an average 60% on our midterm.

Never posts discussion worksheets or the discussion answers, no recorded lectures. Not a great teacher either, makes concepts too hard to understand.

Great professor! 

Really like all the lectures, he teaches all the contents in great depth and is great for building a strong foundation for the next 20 series courses

Professor Mackall is an exceptional educator who truly stands out in their field. his lectures are not only informative but also engaging, making complex topics easily understandable. he consistently demonstrate a deep knowledge of the subject matter, coupled with a genuine passion for teaching.
You would definitely like Eoin. he is such a great professor with solid knowledge. If you go to his office hour to ask him question, he is very inspirational, and test is reasonablely okay.
Great class, his discussion is pretty helpful and enjoyable. His test is fairly easy and I would definitely recommand mackall to yall who will take math 20b/math20d

Excellent professor, lectures were really in depth and the grading scheme is really reasonable. The test is a bit difficult but should be manageable if you do all the homework and attend the discussion sessions. Really recommend if you want to build a strong foundation for calculus.
don take his class unless u have to

reviews.comment: Teaches the hardest math class in the series (Math20b) doesn't give us a crib sheet or a calculator. gives bad lectures and doesn't podcast them. Taught myself the entire course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had the latest lecture time so I didn't really like coming in that much but honestly the class was pretty easy to do well in. It's a decent amount of writing and group projects but the prof is very lenient and the course wasn't stressful. Yes the lectures were a tad bit boring but they are built on deep ideas and passion for the subject.

Nice guy, but I'd choose another CCE professor. He assigns way more work than others, including last minute 500 word reflections w/o any notice in class or on canvas. The class had 3 group projects, but directions and rubrics were unclear. You need to yap a lot in essays to avoid getting an incomplete. Lectures are long & boring & no tech allowed
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: CCE 1 as a class is super easy. Sepulveda literally says he won't let anyone get below an A as long as you put in some effort. For an A, you can miss up to 3 classes, and for a B and below, 4.
Really easy grading system (you pick your own grade) but lectures were very slow and boring.

He is very understanding with giving extensions and is very caring. His lectures can get pretty boring and you aren't allowed on devices so you kind of just have to stare at a wall for an hour and a half. He cares a lot about the subject he is talking about, but as a STEM major it's hard to be engaged. Overall super nice though.
This professor was understanding and clearly cared for his students. Some lectures can be boring, but the class is overall very easy.

If he's teaching a course take him! He's exams are lecture based so if u just study lecture and know context well you'll do great and problem set help for extra help, became my favorite class cuz of how funny and great he teaches, truly my shyla

I LOVE PROFESSOR HUI! Lots of EC (optional clicker for up to 2%, SETs 1%), has an amazing grading scheme (3 total NON-cumulative exams; highest exam 40% of grade while other 2 exams are 20% each, and 20% PSETs). BIBC 102 is a lot of memorization and understanding concepts so it may be time consuming, but Hui made this class doable and enjoyable!

He is a great professor with simple exams that mirror the weekly problem sets, practice exams, and iclicker questions. Attendance is extra credit, only need to go to half of the lectures to get it all. 2 Midterms and final is non-culminative.

Great professor overall! Attendance wasn't required, just offered as extra credit. Exams were pretty straightforward, with a mix of true/false, multiple choice, some short responses, and sometimes a bonus question. Lectures were super fun. Take him if you have an option.

I cannot recommend this professor enough, I took structural in the past and ended up taking metabolic for fun but wow, I learned so much in this course from him, probably the most I've ever gotten from a course here at UCSD. He is genuinely passionate about what he teaches and made me laugh every lecture. Biochem could not have been better.

Dr. Hui is a super chill guy! I think this was his first time teaching BIBC102, so he was pretty lenient overall. He does his best to review the metabolic processes that you'll need to know for the exams, and he always makes an effort to communicate with his students. Cool guy overall and really fun to have!

AWESOME PROFESSOR!! Attendance was only for EC. Tests were really fair: T/F questions, multiple choice, some free response, and sometimes a bonus question. There was a bit of memorization, so DON'T wait till the day before to study! His lectures were great & problem sets really helped apply the material. He really wants you to succeed. Take him :)
Definitely take his class if you have the option. Very thorough review sessions before exams. Opportunities for extra credit with attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This professor is a gem! Despite the accent, he knows the material in depth and explains it carefully step by step. I've learned a TON. Tests/HW are extremely easy if you put in a little effort to study, because everything is in the slides and lectures. No trick questions at all. No bs application questions. No textbook. Attendance is not required.
Great professor who has fair exams and clear lectures explaining all information needed to succeed. All around nice guy who offers Ec for attendance and is accessible at all times of the week.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Among all the STEM classes I've taken at UCSD so far, Professor Hui is my favorite professor. His class is not easy, but it provides a fair assessment of the materials he teaches. He is a very interesting and caring professor. I very recommend him if you don't want to have a very easy class, but know you can succeed if you put in the effort.

Professor Hui was easily the best professor I've ever had at UCSD. He tried his best to answer any questions students had about the subject and also held extra office hours late at night before exams. The exams he gave were also a fair assessment and were based strictly on lecture content. Take BIBC 100 with professor Hui if possible :D

I love Dr. Hui! My icon, my Shayla. He is such a great professor, and he genuinely cares about you learning. He made a daunting class like biochem so much more fun and approachable. He also held multiple office hours for us. Weekly problem sets and discussion really helped, and iClickers for EC. Do as he says and you will learn so much and get an A

This is a hard course but he is truly a great professor. He and his team make huge effort in helping you to learn. He also learns students' names, even though this is a huge class. One of the best I have taken here.

Professor Hui is truly an amazing person. He is knowledgeable, smart, and caring. I really wish we had more professors like him! There is one midterm and one final in this class. This is BIOCHEM, so you have to study really hard. He also offers extra credit! He holds office hours, which are really helpful. I really appreciate him!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: one of the most caring professors at ucsd! he is funny, kind, and makes himself available to his students. the material is dense but he allows unlimited cheat sheets on his tests! take him if you can!
Amazing prof. Go deep into topics but interesting lectures. So caring and enthusiastic. Generous on extra credit. Exams similar to HW and study guides. Take him if you can!!!

He is such a nice man and offers a lot of extra credit. On the first day he ripped an apple in half as a hidden talent, and it was really funny. He is so smart and does a great job, but his tests ARE SO HARD. They are directly from the lecture slides, but there is nothing that can prepare you for that. they are open note and are your whole grade.

Weekly HW assignments, a midterm, and a final. Lectures are VERY long and dense, however prof explains the material well. Make sure to attend your discussion section for lots of help with the weekly HW assignment! Midterm and final require knowledge, memeorization & understanding of the lectures. Exams contain a large amount of questions.

Professor Hui is great. He obviously cares for his students and is incredibly receptive to constructive feedback on the course. Lectures are dense in information but Prof. Hui's exams are truly representative of the concepts that are important, not tiny specifics. He also is very helpful in his office hours and pretty funny!

Excellent professor. I really enjoyed his class. The material is tough, but attend lectures and study and you will do well. I didn't use the book. His lecture slides are super helpful. Highly recommend this professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Hui wasn't a hard professor in that he gives you everything you need to succeed. If you study by his lecture objectives and problem sets, you'll do fine in the class. His class is really lecture heavy and he goes kind of quickly through the material, though. Be prepared to do a lot of memorization for his tests!

Prof. Hui's class is very fast paced and information heavy at 70 wordy slides per lecture although he is a nice and funny guy. His midterm was just like his weekly problem sets and a lot of the final questions came from study guides he made. Use the homework and study guides to prepare for tests and be ready to memorize a lot of information.
Professor Hui is okay, but he often lectures too quickly and has a pretty thick accent. He still is a very nice prof, and I would recommend him to anyone who primarily focuses on self-studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I can tell by the comments below that these students probably did not succeed in life. Prof. Luco is very respected in the industry. Once you go to grad school you will notice that these professors do not give away A's like it means nothing. You have to earn it. He was always available to clarify any doubts I had. Great professor.
Luco is a true scholar (one of the few at UCSD) and if you're bright you'll do well in his courses.  Luco is really respected in the field.
Hated this guy. Want not clear. Taught stuff beyond the textbook. Midterms were way more difficult that the hwk. Only thing good was the curve

Extremely poor teacher, not working with students at all.  He was unavailable during the week for help being busy with his "research".  He returned mid-term exams on the last day of class, making adjustments unfeasible.
He just sucks. He can't teach at all. Try everything you can to avoid him. I changed my major because of him!
Can't understand him.  Brags about his son too much.
No Comments
His exams were insane and not anything he even went over. He seems to be a smart guy but can't teach his was out of a paper sack.

This professor was hard, has an accent and doesn't explain things well. Requires a LOT of tedious math work on midterms.  Needs to know differential equations well in order to do well in the class. Overall, this professor sucks.

Took his class at Imperial Valley College, read the book for your enrichment & to strategically maneuver in class through the lazy heard. His knowledge is broad and at times hard to understand -my own ignorance- but, if you read on history, politics, and economics you will be able to establish intellectual conversation and get the A.
Great professor,read your book and you should be fine! Don't expect him to read it for you, and if you have any issue talk to him...he is really friendly!

This class is pretty interesting, but the lectures do not help at all. the lectures are basically interesting political discussions, but not helpful for learning the material. barely attended class but still got an A. I would have gone to class for interesting topics discussed but it was at 9am.

As a caveat, my ratings are based on material assigned and the papers, not the discussion (which though more enjoyable than some posts say, does indeed contribute little to writing a solid paper).  I attended class about once every other session, but read his books, asked for help via e-mail a few times, and got my good grade.
he is one the chillest professors I have ever had, and clearly know things on international relations
what on earth?
I sat in this class and almost everyday thought to myself, "What is going on...?" If you like to talk about politics, it might be fun for you. If you want to learn, take another course.

All the other comments hit the nail on the head. The midterm tested on a book that wasnt assigned to start reading until the week after the midterm. I asked help from an awesome TA who saved my grade. I was completely lost at the "lectures", my notes were random things said by students, and I didnt understand the assignments. He seems nice though.
he wastes your time.

By the amount of comments saying the same thing, students considering taking this professor should understand that HE DOES NOT LECTURE. If you attend class, he wastes your time. And since his classes are filled with "discussions", you are left with absolutely no idea what to focus on in your take home essay exams. Trust us all, do not take him!

For POLI 145C & 142O, Epps' classes are based around discussion, but even if this is not your thing he is very much worth taking.  He gives you the ability to write about what you want for the final, hence it should be about what you know the most.  If you're struggling, just go to him directly.  He is very approachable and helpful outside of class

This professor did not care about the class. He did not teach anything about the subject, would randomly cancel classes and not show up. He would randomly change the dates that assignments were due and would change the requirements. He promoted "class discussions" which had no depth. He put no effort in and had his TAs do all the dirty work.

I went into this class very interested in the topic and learned absolutely nothing! Like the others said, he never lectures. That said, I went to his office hours a couple times and learned more then I did in the class. The TAs graded hard, esp considering that he taught us NOTHING!

It is true, Epps likes his lectures to be more like discussions. At least during International Terrorism, the lectures have virtually no relevance to the midterm and final (both take-home essays). He is very intelligent and personable, and he shows a sense of humor. I recommend him, but don't expect him to be like all of your past professors.

I agree with the last comment. Horrible at lecturing. Basically a giant discussion, where the same few kids spout off their opinions. A nice guy personally, but a near complete waste of time academically.

Not a very good professor or class. He doesnt lecture, so instead you get to hear the opinions of the same 5 people in class every day about topics theyre not fully informed in.  Would be better if the actual professor taught something as opposed to story time from students
Excellent professor.  Don't let any other review sway you.  He really cares.  Is nice.   Learn a great deal

Really chill professor who cares about his students and the material that he's actually teaching. going to class is like going to a big discussion. kinda modeled so that you have to be somewhat a history buff but even if you're not, it's a really good class/ professor to take. pretty easy too
